reviews.comment: Shusterman used to be good (for Chem 32), but for 1A she started doing interactive lectures (where you sit in groups of three and try to teach yourself without any background knowledge or guidance). This class is so frustrating, you're quizzed weekly without being taught. If you want to learn anything, youtube is your only hope. Avoid if possible!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Do NOT take this class unless you already have a strong foundation in chemistry because you will learn absolutely nothing from the interactive format. Its a cute idea sure but Chem is nuanced and technical subject that requires thorough breakdown of material that cannot be achieved by staring blankly at notecards with two other people.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: The worst professor. Shusterman believes interactive lessons are the best way to learn the material, I disagree. I have talked to multiple students and we all agree that we learn nothing during interactive lessons and we are failing this class due to this professor's inability to teach us material. We have to teach ourselves, which is ridiculous.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. S is an amazing lecturer. I am currently enrolled in her Chem 32, which is pre Chem 1A for students who were unable to be exposed to chemistry in high school. her lectures make sense, and you're prepared for exams because homework is a lot more difficult than the exams. Go to office hours, she is super helpful and genuinely cares.

The workload is fair and I loved that there were no post labs after. Once you finished lab for the day you didn't have to worry about more work (except for the prelab quiz and prepping the notebook). The final was hard but she curves the class A LOT. Just remember to write all of your observations down to get full credit.

Well designed course with very reasonable workload. Dr. S gives great lectures and is super nice and helpful in office hours. I learned a lot each lab and really internalized the information well because she made the material so accessible. I dreaded lab in Chem 1AL, but in 3AL I had a pretty awesome experience!

Dr. S is awesome! She's an awesome lecturer and I love the memes that she has at the end of every slideshow! She made 3AL a pleasant and even enjoyable experience. The workload for the course was super reasonable and Dr. S did a great job of teaching content! I'm sad that I won't have her for 3BL over the summer! She's great! (and also super funny)

Love Dr. S! Her office hours are always fun and she cares about students. Welcoming and makes herself accessible. Invites questions. Funny. Clear lectures and very organized and succinct slides. Explains concepts in a very understandable way. Highly recommend! 10/10
Ehhh.. It felt like he was learning the material alongside us. Homework was poorly written, but he seems to care about his students.

The homeworks were kind of poorly written at times, but lectures were engaging and it's cool to see how passionate he is about research and chem/chem E. He clearly cares about his students and is always really energetic in an infectious way, which is refreshing to see at berkeley.

I was impressed by his humility and character. Office hours were fun and relaxed -- a low stakes environment to be wrong and learn from mistakes. I've taken this class before at a different university, but Boettcher took my competence to a much higher level. Very personable, and offers excellent advice.
his teaching style is not good and lectures do not make sense.

Appreciated the good vibes. Speaks fast, but lectures are super clear and breaks down the concepts really well from my perspective. Always available for office hours. Not sure what some of the low ratings are on about, honestly.

Confusing professor and very hectic lecture style. He throws concepts at you and will jump between different lectures within one class. Makes it really hard to follow along and GSIs don't offer much support either.

This class is already difficult enough but he makes it much harder. I go to every class and always come out more confused. He either talks in circles with no substance, or calls things "intuitive" (when it's not at all) and moves on. His lectures are long and his slides don't make sense.
The class is difficult but Prof Faber tries his best to make the material understandable.

2 Problem sets, midterm, and final exam. Attendance is required for both lectures and discussions. Study the lecture slides and section assignments. Grading can be strict for the problem sets. Lectures can be difficult to follow; very self study orientated. Textbook is optional. Class is curved to a B. Recommend taking Ryan Edwards instead.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Genuinely had to teach myself the whole class. Few support resources available and really dull lectures. Didn't release practice final solutions nor final solutions when it came time for regrade requests. Wouldn't recommend.

Doesn't provide a comprehensive answer document to a practice final that includes questions that GSIs don't even know how to solve. Boring, dull lectures full of rambling using unnecessary terminology, deviates from the already lackluster slides, has no structure during lecture, writes with small, messy handwriting that nobody can decipher.

I'm sure he's a nice person and personally helps out people, but his style of teaching is subpar, to say the least. He works totally differently than other professors for course and his teachings are very different from any online material related to econometrics. Too fast, makes mistakes in lectures, and the worst slide maker i've ever seen

This prof isn't good. He talks way to fast and it's hard to keep up when there is so many new concepts being thrown at you. Unluckily, my GSI wasn't helpful either, so I ended up having to learn most of the material myself. Also who posts a practice final without a PDF of the answers? Anyway, if necessary, take this class with another prof.

If you need this class, take it with Edwards or Li; they are both significantly better. Content delivery was dull, lectures were unbearable, problem sets were graded awfully, and exams were hard; for context, I went to every class, and I actually tried, but I hated it. Released a practice final and told us no solutions would be posted. helpful.

One of the best decisions I've made is taking 140 early since econometrics has come up in almost all of my other upper div classes. Beware that the class uses R (problem sets, not on exams), and I wish there had been more support in this area speaking as a non-coder. The lectures are interesting for an econometrics class.
Really enjoyed this class.

Class structure is really simple, centered around a paper each week covering a specific econometric method and/or development concept. Prof Faber is a pretty clear lecturer and highlights important concepts (sometimes he repeats them a bit too much), but overall the class is not that interesting and I expected a lot more imo
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was very interesting and we do read a lot of papers to understand the different econometric research methods. The exams required us to know the questions, research methods, results, and problems Faber mentions during lectures. I recommended taking an intro econometric class first to do the problem sets. Utilize your GSI for help!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This guy is worse than David Beecher, and that is saying something. He comes in completely unprepared for class, and just throws up these nonsensical lecture slides that he has clearly been using since 2014. I don't understand how these half wits keep getting hired at this school. He asks questions that no one answers and it makes class awkward.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This guy stinks. Not only are his lectures dry, off topic and hard to follow, but he provides little to no resources to prepare for tests and problem sets. This class is a rat race to see who is least confused by his terrible teaching style.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great lectures.

Please whatever you do, do not take ECON 171 with Faber. Not only is he condescending and arrogant, but his problem sets are also harder than what is posted on lectures and section notes. One of my classmates visited his office hour and he literally told her to go to sections. He has no interest in wanting students to succeed.

Exams didn't reflect what was taught, confusing fr, ask other students. Lectures often drifted into self-focused anecdotes rather than accounting, with a tone that felt more self-promotional than instructive. The required textbook did not worth its cost. I didn't leave with a solid understanding of the materials, consider this before enrolling.

I had a frustrating experience in this class. The instructor's professionalism and communication fell short of expectations, and the required textbook did not feel worth the cost. Overall, I didn't gain a solid understanding of accounting. Consider this when deciding to enroll.
Haas can do better than this guy.
Pretty cool lectures but the midterm was diabolical, I ended up with a B despite doing pretty well in both final projects and the final exam due to how bad the midterm was

I don't know how I passed this class. Especially knowing that I wasn't given the opportunity to clobber. I also note that attendance, though on the syllabus stated as not mandatory, is MANDATORY. (If you want the unfair advantage in signing a contract to clobber) Haas please reevaluate this courses policies as listed from my peers below.

Dreadful GSI's, terribly written tests, class structure is unfair with some students allowed to clobber their exams. I hope Haas can evaluate the class policies enacted in this course fairly. An absolute joke. And would not recommend to peers

Took UGBA120AA (Intermediate Fin Accounting) with Professor Bell. He's the GOAT. Very funny personality and easy grading. Homework is due every couple of weeks and 2 final projects due at the end of dead week. Bell uses Becker CPA tests for midterms and finals, but usually reuses the practice exams he gives. So, as long as you study that, easy A.

The concepts taught in the class itself are not difficult, but the professor does not teach with the same rigor as the midterm and final. He carries a superiority complex and focuses less on accounting and more on his opinions on social issues. Make sure to review outside of class, the McGraw-Hill is very good practice, also spend time on projects.

Had a surprise contract that you had to show up to class to sign and if you didn't you wouldn't have gotten clobber. Midterm was horrific. Final was easier but i didn't do well and the GSIs were very not present and a bit mean as well. I went to Prof Bell's office hour and he was not welcoming.
a literal joke
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This was one of the most stressful technical courses I've taken. I enrolled to learn practical accounting, but instead dealt with unclear, poorly written (and costly - $80) homework, misaligned exams, and inconsistent grading. Poorly managed overall—I wouldn't recommend this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Bell is collectively known by students as one of the worst professors at Haas. This semester, his midterm was completely different from the massive amounts of homework he assigned every week and not a single person finished on time. He makes students pay for an online textbook to complete homework but wont make any tests relevant to them
RUN WHILE YOU CAN. midterm was brutal, no practice exams at all until the final exam. Please save yourself.

I am a decent student, who puts in the work to study and do well on exams. Professor Bell's midterm was terrible and dropped my grade to the lowest I have ever received. The average on the exam was a 60% with no curve!! The format of exams are not at all reflective of homework and quizzes. Do take this class if you want to be scared for your life!
He's a cool guy that clearly enjoys teaching but in my opinion the exams were very poorly structured and written.
He's horrible. The midterm is nothing like what he taught in class and he took notecards unfairly. The way he decides anything is based on his mood. Do not take this class with him.

Homeworks that do not pertain at all to the midterm which had a ~60% average. Clobbering the midterm with the final only possible if you just happened to show up to one specific, not previously announced day of class to turn in a "contract". Thinks he is god.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His midterm was extremely long and difficult, and ended with with a mean of around 150/250. He makes you purchase an $80+ textbook that connects with the homework and quizzes, which are COMPLETELY IRRELEVANT to the midterm. I wouldn't recommend this class to anyone, and I hope no one makes the same mistake.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: An absolute joke.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He likes to talk about how he was an auditor back in his day, and how he's now a professor at “UC Berkeley Haas”. He likes to make cryptic references to certain students during his lectures. I'm pretty sure most of these reviews are by Mr. Bell himself. All of the people I talked to don't think he's a good teacher. You should avoid him if possible.

If you took accounting in Community College is very similar as you will use McGraw Hill for quizzes and homework weekly. If you get good grades on them you will be fine, the midterm was in person and was curved because the highest score was 148/250 and the final was online. He gives great lectures and goes into great detail explaining topics.

I went into this class absolutely dreading accounting but came out loving the subject. Bell has a great sense of humor and adds that to his slides, he'll make you laugh to the point where you forget you are studying such a dull subject. There is very little homework, I didn't need to spend much time out of class on this class.

Engages class well, sometimes to the point of overdoing the humor. Has easier midterms and is understanding with course policies, however note that the cutoff for an A is a 95%, which is higher than most other classes. Also, keep in mind that there weekly online homework/quiz assignments worth 1% of your grade, so don't forget to complete them!

Great professor who genuinely cares about students. Had group project issues and helped me work out a solution! I learned a lot in the class and was prepared for the midterm and final. Weekly homework and quiz assignments through McGraw Hill, so workload was manageable. His lectures are engaging and very informative. Highly recommend!

Bell is a nice guy who has real-world experience. He will always encourage questions. He tries to involve the class with interactive quizzes as well. The midterm was easier, but the time restriction made it difficult. There are 2 group projects, both if you split work.  2 Weekly McGraw Hill assignments, projects, and 2 tests make up the grade.

Took him for 102A not 102B. Great lecturer who cares about his students and makes class fun to attend. His jokes and personality make coming to class a great time. Always has time for questions and very informative at office hours. Gives good life advice as well.
Prof. Bell was excellent - he somehow made a topic like managerial accounting both educational and entertaining. He is a great lecturer and made the class feel very open. 10/10 recommend.
tests are max 18 multiple choice qs so you basically have to get them all right to keep an A. No extra credit and assigns groups. better than most other 102b professors since he's easier to talk to

Erick Bell is a CPA who worked at KPMG, Deloitte, and has his own consulting firm. If you take him you will be reminded of this every class. The lectures are great to listen to before bed as they will put you to sleep. Graded by 3 tests, 2 projects, and weekly online quizzes.

Prof. Bell has experience at KPMG and as a lecturer at other universities like SF. He's a nice guy and cares about his students success. He is sometimes slow to answer a question and his lecture slides were sourced from the textbook company which made the class fell less authentic to Haas. Overall, he was an ok teacher and your grade will be good
Loved her so much!!! I learned so much and read so many amazing authors I had never read before. Extremely passionate about GWS and loved everything she taught.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She's super nice & u can tell that she truly enjoys what she teaches. Lectures can sometimes feel like they run in circles but it's still worth it to show up. Readings are dense, u don't need to do all of them (just ones for exams/assignments), she explains them all in lecture. Makes a big class feel small, never feels preachy, always realistic.

Great class! The lecture runs a little long at times, but ultimately, the material is extremely interesting, and Prof. Barnes does a great job of explaining difficult concepts. Heavy reading, but it's all talked about in lecture. A really great breadth class for anyone interested.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Super easy class with writing as homework. The reading isn't that necessary honestly because the lectures recap it all. Lectures are boring but it's fine. Easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Not what I expected from gender studies. We spent the entire semester learning about settler colonialism. Nice professor but very repetitive and boring lectures. Unnecessarily picky when grading. Professor is very fearful of AI and is not afraid to accuse people of using it for any reason. Try to find a different class for a breadth or ac.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Loved this class

She's nice and all but there's so much assignments. Attendance is mandatory but if it wasn't I wouldn't show up. Lectures are long and boring. Quizzes and midterms are closed notes & no readings allowed. They can be very specific and ask for certain things she said during lecture. Lecture is recording but you have to request and have a good reason.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The lecture is boring and long, she is repeating same things all the time, if the attendance is not mandatory, I won't go. Be prepared to read a lot!! And you could lose points in the all the assignments for some picky reasons. Closed book in class midterm and some quiz. Try to find other AC classes.
she is so nice and all the test is pretty easy

The class was decently easy and the prof. is definitely enthusiastic about her class. Prof was very into her lectures but they aren't all too entertaining as it is a 2 hour class. Graded off one short analysis "essay," quiz, midterm take-home essay, bigger essay, and final exam. Assignments/quiz are pretty straight-forward def worth a breadth class

Professor Barnes' lectures were a bit disorganized, and never posted the slides before the lecture, even with my accommodations. The readings themselves were very fun and the theoretical concepts were interesting but unfortunately, her teaching style was not as accessible as I hoped it would be.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Prof Barnes is very passionate and knowledgeable in her field. My only critique would be that her lectures are redundant and tangent-heavy, even though they are required! Also, there's a LOT of reading, though if you are taking this class for fun, they should be interesting to you (I actually enjoyed reading them). :)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: professor barnes is very funny and kind! the lectures were repetitive but it allows you to understand the material to its fullest extent since the readings are very dense. however, she goes off on many tangents during lecture. i saw everyone around me begin class ready to take notes and then slowly ended going on their phone

Although this class is heavy in readings, Dr.Barnes does an amazing job at explaining and going into depth on the readings so that it is easier for us to understand. Dr.Barnes is very accessible outside of class and is extremely understanding when it comes to grading. Overall, she is such a sweet and funny professor!
Prof Barnes is the best! The most real/human any of my  UCB professors has been. She is very flexible and communicative. Don't stress her class and if you need help, just ask. Definitely recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: There are 5 quizzes total in the course, as well as an essay split into 3 parts. The quizzes got harder as they went on, but I did fine without taking notes in the class. As long as you have the readings up as you take the quizzes and get your sources on time for the essay, you'll be fine. She also has a 1-day grace period for late assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Barnes is a caring professor who is very passionate about what she teaches and does an excellent job of explaining the content from the readings during lecture. The readings she assigns are enlightening, albeit lengthy at times. Keeping up with the readings is the key to excelling on exams and assignments. I would 100% recommend this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Barnes is clearly very caring and a knowledgeable expert in the field; unfortunately, her lectures are often repetitive and go off on less important tangents. The class was absolutely manageable though, and as long as you keep up with the readings you'll be fine
She's very passionate about what she discusses. She uses iClicker for lectures to mark attendance. She's badass.

Professor Barnes will open your mind to concepts you never knew existed. She brings together biology, feminist theory, and various epistemologies to show new ways of looking at the world and other people in it. She is also funny and delightful and I highly recommend taking any class she teaches.

The class was quite disorganized this semester, and the grading was kind of silly at times because we would lose points for vague reasons. Additionally, the course material is niche in that it is a lot about nature and settler colonialism interacting with it. The class was alright at best, and professor was not the most engaging.

Dr. Barnes is by far one of the best professors I have come across. She's brilliant, kind, and extremely engaging! The topics covered are complex and hard to understand, but she explains them patiently and with wit! She is truly so kind to all of her students, understanding and non judgmental if you're not grasping something.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Barnes is one of the most amazing instructors I've ever had. Just take her classes you won't regret it!

Dr. Barnes is easily my favorite professor I have ever had. She is incredibly intelligent and knows how to break down the material, she can sometimes be a bit scatter brained but by the end you will get the point she is making if you pay attention! Reading matters in her class, but if you don't understand she will break it down very well.
Tok this class P/NP but I just love Barbara. Super nice!!

Dr. Barnes is my favorite professor. She is funny and so REAL with her students. There are times that she must gather her thoughts, and then, BOOM: revelation, manifest critical thinking! Dr. Barnes is also genuinely open to feedback and a gem of a listener, intellectually and emotionally. She thinks WITH her students. We learn from each other.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Prof. Barnes is such a wonderful person and an extremely passionate speaker. I just wanted to make her proud the whole semester and that worked as a powerful motivator! The readings are super intersting.

My favorite Professor at Berkeley. Passionate, kind, understanding, amazing lectures! She's one of the best persons you'll ever meet. Amazing lecturer! I took GWS10 too and she's such a great professor to have when learning basics in GWS. Everyone should take her!!

Prof Barnes is extremely caring, is passionate about her subject and clearly has a strong following of students who love her. Personally, I found her lectures not at all engaging and struggled to pay attention. It was a lot of her talking without any other media or forms of teaching.
Somebody give this woman a raise! She's the best, literally.

Prof. Barnes teaches cutting edge, up to date material. The lectures and readings are amazing. She is personable, authentic, and sincere. Keep up on the readings and bring them to class with you. Try not to leave early because it distracts her and makes her lose her train of thought for a moment. She is compassionate, inclusive, and very caring

Professor Barnes is a real gem. From her jokes to her corkiness to her amazing deconstruction of theory, she's definitely someone to learn from. This was a class that made you work hard for your grade and was extremely rewarding when receiving that high score.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: I'll be taking a third class with Barbara because she is incredible. Read everything and participate, then you'll love it. Don't leave in the middle of her lectures because she will get distracted and lose her place. But don't worry, you will want to stay coz her lectures are amazing and so is she. She also happens to be extremely kind. A++

Barnes is utterly brilliant. Hers is the most inspiring class I'm taking. She is the only reason that I'm glad about my choice of Cal; frankly, she is the best professor I've ever had. She is kind and she is spectacularly clever. Cal: please do something nice for this woman! She is a national treasure and you are extremely lucky to have her.
The most caring and likeable person I've ever met. The personal stories she uses to go with the material help you learn the information. This class was not only educational but inspirational.
At the end of the semester, the girl next to me turned around and said, "I've never been so sad that a class has ended." I agree with her.

I'm currently enrolled in GWS 104 and Barnes is the by far the best professor I've had at Cal. Her syllabus is extremely clever and beautifully thought out; the readings are inspiring and highly thought-provoking. Her lectures are inspiring. I highly recommend this professor.

You cant skip classes but over 4 times during the whole semester or youll be dropped. Lots of reading stuff but lecture was interesting if youre interested in this area Gender Women Studies. There will be a study guide before a week from the exam(exam papers topics are on it) you need to write a long essay and memorize all the stuff before exam

Wonderful lectures. They were absolutely beautiful. She's an amazing speaker. My one complaint is she glared anyone who left early, & while I know we should stay (& I always did), I feel like in college, we shouldn't have to explain why we might need to leave. Other than that, assignments were clear & lecture interesting & thought-provoking.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Fair amount of reading each week, but they're all thought provoking. Lectures are amazing! Very engaging and professor is genuinely interested in hearing the thoughts of students and respectful of all view points. No hw, 3 quizes which she gives you the prompts ahead of time, and 1 research paper that counts as the final.

Dr. Barnes is an amazing lecturer and inspirational speaker. She is passionate about the class and the learning students are supposed to get out of it and her personality is easy to like and admire. GWS10 is reading heavy, but you can get by with skimming the readings and really paying attention in lecture. Great for stimulating critical thinking!

Professor Barnes is easily the favorite professor at CAL. She is such an inspirational speaker who definitely motivated, inspired and taught me to think outside the box. Her lectures are very interesting and fun to listen to. When you visit her during office hours, you can realize how caring and awesome she is. Her lecture is a must!

Professor Barnes is my favorite professor at Berkeley. I have taken 3 of her classes (GWS10, GWS 100AC, Feminist Theory 104). There is a decent amount of reading, but you do what you can, and she really covers it in lecture. Sometimes she is a little all over the place, but I really think it just humanizes her and makes her more approachable.

Left too much space for other people's opinions (that's what discussion is for). Could have gotten way more from lecture if it weren't for that, and there is a LOT to cover. Maybe the most interesting set of readings for any class (diverse, engaging). Final had some extra credit, and the assignments weren't difficult but you had to read most things
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She's awesome and cares deeply about what she's teaching
She is super cool and nice. Reserves a lot of space for students' opinions and questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Respected--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Professor Barnes is an amazing educator. This class changes how you perceive the world and really shows you the value of an education. The texts challenge your point of view and offer completely new ideas. The class was engaging and the workload was fair. If you are truly interested you will definitely get an A, if not... She is so inspiring.

You could definitely feel a strong white feminist vibe in the classroom although Barnes tries to be inclusive. Her lectures usually go off on long tangents and only talks about 1 reading at most in a week. You don't really need to read except for on a couple of articles of your choice to help you with the quizzes and essays.

There is a lot of reading that she does not necessarily go over.  What really matters to her is participation and caring about the subject matter.  Usually half the class is devoted to comments on her lectures both from her and the class.  She is very knowledgeable and passionate about gender studies.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She was often disorganized and late. She micromanaged the class like a high school teacher, taking attendance and scolding people for being on phones. I stopped reading after the first week and still had no trouble writing the essays after reviewing the lecture slides. There are also weekly current event assignments so it's basically 9th grade.

If you do around 75-80% of the readings and pay attention to most of her lectures, you'll be fine. It was a pretty interesting class and Professor Barnes is extremely passionate about the topic. It wasn't my cup of tea, but still, I'd say it's a good class to take! She's clear and concise and makes the information stick to your head!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Ms. Barnes is one of the most incredible professors I've ever had. She wan an incredible orator and graded fairly. As long as you participate and do the readings, you'll do just fine.

This was my least favorite class I have taken at Berkeley. Professor Barnes' lectures were a little all over the place and she was not always clear about what she wanted. I was really excited to take a gender and women's studies class but I will never take one again. I had a pretty strict reader, which made the take home tests a little frustrating.

Barnes is a really good professor and lecturer. She is very knowledgeable and helpful and will take any questions. She also attempted to learn everyone's names in a class of around a hundred. There was a decent amount of work but it was not difficult and she is a fair grader.

I took this course over the summer. It was my one of my first classes at Cal. Barbara Barnes is an excellent speaker, although sometimes a bit scattered. I was quite impressed with her speaking ability. She encourages engagement with the material with writings of personal experience. If you do the reading and participate, you'll do well.

Her brain operates in a fairly scattered way, which is fine, but she ends up repeating herself often, making lectures pretty boring. Her comments are insightful though, she's very willing to help/talk, I enjoyed the assigned reading, and she definitely made it so that if you were willing to put in the work (5 hrs a week) you would get an A!
Not worth it. She's funny and sweet but she's a mess when she lectures. Goes around in circles, runs on tangents, and her lecture slides are not helpful.

This class is not worth it. It's a lower-division level class with way too many expectations, demands, etc. The professor gets frazzled easily, and the structure of lectures are overbearingly long. The GSIs have made it a point that laptops will be monitored. She gets upset if you leave class early. I made a huge mistake taking this class.

I have taken three classes with Professor Barnes: 20, 104, and 140. Professor Barnes is a great person, though I have to admit, she's a bit hit or miss in lecture. If you're not in GWS, I doubt you'll enjoy it much. But, as a GWS major, I appreciated the spaces she left for discussion. She genuinely wants to hear what you have to say in class!

I love Barnes! She is easily my favorite professor that I have had so far at Berkeley. She explained concepts clearly and assigned very interesting readings. In fact, this was the only class that I went to the lectures 100% of the time. She is a very educated woman and I'm happy I got to have her as a professor.

The professor's SO boring. She says the same thing that you read in her reader, so it's really easy to tune her out. I honestly wouldn't bother to come to class if she didn't take attendance. I wish she made Gender Studies more interesting, especially to another woman. Also she's so disorganized. Come to class prepared, we are expected to do that!

She is very insecure and gets flustered all the time. She gets mad and whiney if people leave the class early... in a large college classroom, this is unacceptable and immature. She also repeats herself constantly and talks slowly for dramatic effect, and grades pretty harshly. I would not recommend taking her class, especially if not a GWS major.
I LOVE BARNES! She's such a sweetheart and a very educated woman. I am always interested in what she has to say. Definitely my favorite class I have taken so far.

I've taken four classes with Barnes (20, 50AC, 111, 103) and all were great, but I found 111 especially interesting. Barnes is friendly and validating during class discussions and office hours. Barnes is extremely skilled at explaining difficult readings, even if she repeats herself a few times.

I've taken classes with Barnes before (including GWS 10) and realized that she's not necessarily an "easy A" when it comes to her upperdiv classes.  Compared to 10, she assigns a lot more reading, and grades significantly more harshly on the papers.  I agree though that she is friendly, engaging, humorous, well-knowledgeable, albeit repetitive.

Professor Barnes is amazing! She is very approachable, kind, intelligent, engaging and all around great person and professor. definitely one of the best professors i have had. she is so knowledgable and is a really great lecturer. take her class!!!!!!!!!

Professor Barnes is very passionate about gender and women's studies issues. She is definitely engaging and very welcoming in her office hours. Midterm and final were pretty easy. Go to her office hours if you have questions, and just get to know her. She is amazing!

Charisma is important in lecturers, and Prof. Barnes excels in that department. Introductory course was appropriately easy; coursework and readings were very manageable, midterm was take home, final was provided beforehand. Material was broad in scope. Class was repetitive, especially in the last third of the semester.

Professor Barnes is very friendly, and passionate about GWS.  The class is not hard as long as you set aside time to keep up with the readings.  Midterm and final were both essays, so if you like writing, you will do well.  I recommend this class!

Professor Barnes is extremely passionate about Gender and Women's Studies which made the class interesting and fun! She keeps students engaged in her lectures and makes sure everyone understands the material. Professor Barnes is amazing and I definitely recommend taking this class!
Easy class. She talks a lot and goes on and on about the readings. She can be funny at times. Overall, she is a nice lady and easy to pass if you do all the readings

Nice lady but definitely not the best lecturer. Her class was super easy though and got an A doing basically 6 days of work throughout the semester. Everything that counts for a grade is done at home but 4 absences in lecture hurts your grade. Barely did the readings, or even all the extra credit

This class wasn't too bad, although if youre just trying out GWS, then i would suggest taking GWS14 or 10 instead. The reading is kind of dense and bothersome, but testing was fair. easy easy pop quizzes, a take home final and midterm. Lecture can be boring, but Barnes is super nice and knows her stuff. Overall I'm glad I took the course.

Barbara Barnes is AMAZING. Cares a lot about the students, very engaging and interesting, always eager to help. I took GWS20 and 100AC with her. Grading is generous, although 100AC was huge so most grading was done by readers. Visit her during office hours--so helpful and nice to chat with. Take any class with her, highly recommended!!

She was very interesting and gave an amazing overview of everything that GWS has to offer as a major. I definitely suggest taking GWS 10 with her, she's fun, insightful, and probably the nicest professor you'll have at Cal. I'm planning on minoring in GWS now :)  As far as the quizzes go, just do the reading, it's interesting stuff usually.

Great professor! Lectures were very interesting, she knows what she is talking about, and she is so open to everyone's opinions. Pretty easy to get an A if you do the work; easy pop quizzes if you do the reading, gave out the midterm questions before the midterm, and a take-home essay final. I had an amazing GSI too, which helped :)

Prof Barnes is the****, the person below me got it spot on: the concepts learned are brought up and manifested in SO MANY of your other classes. grade consists of participation, quizzes, 1 MT, 1 Final. VERY manageable. She facilitates class discussions very well. take this class!

Great professor! Its obvious that she knows her stuff. Lots of reading but if you pay attention its easy to catch up on what you missed. All the concepts are extremely useful in other classes too. If you want an A the key is CITE EVERYTHING POSSIBLE and take advantage of extra credit opportunities. I did this and have an A+ in the class

Good material to engage our class in critical voices and prominent theorists, and in the process, is teaching us all to look at mass-produced visual representations in a bigger way. Her lectures inspiring and fully engaging. She is also conscientious, she responded to our midterm evaluation and is adjusting aspects of class to suit us better

she does give a generous amount of A's, but just to remind everybody, she's actually not the one who grades the midterms, well not this year for my class anyway, we have two readers who read them and grades them. extra credit work is a must-do!

I love Professor Barnes.  She encourages class discussion and is open to everyone's opinions.  She made me think of things I wouldn't have otherwise.  Her grading is fair and probably on the generous side, but it's because she makes it clear what she wants and how you should go about midterms and papers.  Definitely recommend.

She is fantastic! Probably my favorite professor I've had at Berkeley. Grading is easy if you do all the work and read for the most part. Lecture is very interesting if you participate, which is a good idea anyways because participation is a significant portion of your grade.
She's nice and her class is easy if you actually do the extra credit, which give you 5% of total grade bump. I didn't do that, so ended up with a B.
This is a wonderful professor who is super intelligent! Sometimes her lectures do get a little boring but for the most part, the whole class talks! Easy grader! A+
Great Professor! Cares a lot about students! Engaging with the course material! Show up and do your work=get a good grade! She is GREAT!
Pretty nice professor. Lectures were often boring but she was very very lenient on grading for papers. Overall....pretty easy class.

Great professor and such a sweet + genuine person - you can tell she is very knowledgable! Class was really interesting and covered a wide range of topics in the field (very nice for an intro class). If you paid attention in lecture, did the work, and understood concepts, not too hard. Would definitely recommend and take one of her classes again!

I really enjoyed the class. Attendance was mandatory as we did short write ups at the end of lecture. Lots of reading assigned but passed the class by just reviewing lecture slides and memorizing main ideas(never did any reading). Professor Brown was always very sweet, understanding and always gave extra credit for our essays. 10/10 recommend!

reviews.comment: Attending lecture was basically just the readings but over again and it gets kinda repetitive a lot of the time.

A little sad to give mid rating since Eliza is nice and approachable, and maybe its because it is her first time teaching this course, her lec is not really organized in a logical way that can be easily followed, which is a lil frustrating for me who likes having a structure. All I can say is that my GSI Minjee saved my life.

GSI determines over all grade! Lectures were helpful but not strict on if the readings were done before hand. 3 Writing assignments, 1 MT and 1 Final. As long as you did the readings you were so chill

reviews.comment: I did really enjoy the content, the professor's lectures were engaging/interesting; however, there are some things I wish I knew. Every lecture is mandatory to attend w/ an in-class assignment. The reading assignments were extensive, with some containing over 60 pages of reading due before each class. In the end, GSI determines final grade.

I totally understand the comments on Prof. Brown's attendance policy, but honestly she was really wanting to be respectful of people's ability to focus, especially during in-class assignments. Every lecture was really interesting! Just skim readings, get the main idea/ argument. I really enjoyed this course, she is a really kind person!

reviews.comment: No homework other than readings that are lowk long. Lecture attendance is mandatory, although if you read the stuff it doesn't really add that much to it. Section and lecture attendance are graded but the big stuff are the writing assignments, final, and midterm. your GSI determines your fate. Mine was a saint so it was nice.

reviews.comment: I don't really like Sociology as a subject, but there were some topics that Professor Brown presented in a really interesting way, so I enjoyed that aspect of the class. Professor Brown always tried to keep the class engaging and ran mock performances at the end of lectures to illustrate certain ideas, which were super cool.

Pretty easy to get an A you dont even have to do any of the readings, essays and tests are graded very leniently, but lecture and discussion section is mandatory and theres 3 lectures and 2 sections a week which is way too much for a intro soc class. lecture is also boring and kind of useless when it comes to learning anything

Professor Brown, while intelligent, is quite a patronizing professor. There is mandatory attendance, and she will often berate students for arriving 2 minutes late in a hall of 300 people. The lectures are also pretty boring, and the readings are numerous and tedious. The class itself is pretty easy, as she offers a lot of extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The passion and vivacity Professor MWBH brings to his field is genuinely inspiring. Anytime I had a question or wanted extra reading on a subject, I knew I could reach out and he would expediently find a time to meet and give a fantastic answer. Understanding of circumstance and rewarding of demonstrated interest, my favourite this semester.
Very sweet and caring about his students and what they are learning. Encourages students' passions and is very responsive. Good selection on syllabus.

Professor Hammed is a wonderful teacher! His passion for the course's content shines in each lecture. Comlit 155 was all about course participation, and deep engagement with the readings; the selection was extremely interesting and carefully curated, and I will think about this class for the rest of my life! 100% recommend taking his classes.

reviews.comment: It was a pleasure taking a class with professor Ben Hammed. Class felt like a breath of fresh air and discussions were something I always looked forward to. reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: MWBH is an excellent professor. I took this class for an upper div humanities breadth but it genuinely became my favorite class. He is outrageously educated and intelligent. He truly knows so much about language and the world. There were two papers in the class, one 5 pager and one 10 pager, very manageable and he grades nicely.

Professor Ben Hammed is very passionate and knowledgeable. He structured the class beautifully, exposing us to different periods of time through diverse works of literature and film that address profound societal issues. He was easily accessible outside of class and was keen on ensuring we understood, discussed, and enjoyed the pieces.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Ben Hammed is an amazing professor who's passionate about the subject.The class is heavily discussion-based so he encourages everyone to speak and be critical thinkers in class. He is also understanding and helpful; you can talk to him outside of class about anything. His class has opened me to a new way of seeing literature and time.

Professor Brilliant truly cares for his students. The work you put into the class reflects in your final grade. Yes, you have to read, and yes, participation matters, but all content is relevant and interesting.

reviews.comment: Really great lecturer, I always looked forward to when he was lecturing in class. He was really passionate about the material and really encouraged students to attend office hours and pursue specific interests in the material.

Genuinely enjoyed his lectures. Mark is a former high school teacher, and you can tell. He has a strong passion for this subject and for teaching students. There's always a line to chat with him about his lectures after class ends.

reviews.comment: He is extremely full of himself and the class is boring. Not generous in the slightest. Should not be teaching students.

u need detailed lecture notes fs, but lecs are hard to understand bc of the way he speaks. i asked him a question after class once & he made me feel so unwelcome. not afraid to share his political views - if he hasn't explicitly, u will have a good idea from the material/readings he focuses on. i watched him call out so many ppl in lec. beware

Professor Brilliant is a very spirited lecturer and always opened class by playing a song. Lecture attendance was taken through iClicker but wasn't part of the final grade due to a technical error. We had our midterms open-book through bCourses. TAKE GOOD LECTURE NOTES, they help a lot with the exams + do the readings (at least skim) for discussion

Brilliant is the best lecturer I've had at Cal so far. He presents his theses effortlessly in class, and his ideas are always well-researched and easy to follow. He provided lecture outlines to prioritize listening and active note-taking, which was an awesome idea. Timed exams will humble you, use time wisely! Weekly readings can be super long.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I cannot voice my gratitude for Professor Brilliant enough. Do not expect an easy class, as you will be doing quite a bit of reading, but his comprehension, passion, and care for the subject make Professor one of the biggest blessings of my college career. I cannot recommend him enough. Amazing lectures, well thought out, USE THE LECTURE OUTLINES!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Genuinely inspiring professor. Every topic and lecture is thoroughly researched and connected to main themes. His thesis and arguments were almost like poetry.

Mark is an amazing lecturer, it's very engaging and I always felt that his class was a great way to start off my day. Only graded on 2 papers and 2 exams, so do your best! Was this the easiest course to take to fulfill an AC requirement? No, but I don't regret taking it at all and would again in a heartbeat. Really enjoyable experience overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Not accessible, arrogant, condescendent.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof. Brilliant is an incredibly knowledgeable and caring professor. His lecture on Proposition 13 is the only time at Cal I have ever seen a class get up and clap after the prof finished. It was that good. His class was pretty standard for the history department and I would 100% take one of his classes again.

Brilliant is a great lecturer and the material he covers in class is well structured and interesting. Just know, if you're like me and history is not your major and you're just filling the AC requirement, this is not an easy course. I enjoyed the class but it was a lot to balance with a full load of other upper div classes for my own major.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Brilliant is truly brilliant. Genuinely passionate prof, very structured class (he makes outlines for you before each lecture). I am a freshman and got an A on the final, so its not as difficult as some comments make it out to be, as long as you pay attention in lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Brilliant is a thoughtful and honest professor. He genuinely enjoys teaching and has a clear and organised lecture style. He also takes care to add elements like period music and film clips into his lectures to make them more engaging. My only complaint would be that he deals with very complicated topics but sometimes does not go into enough nuance

I thought Professor Brilliant was great, his lectures are very clear and he gets to the point. There is a big workload in his class but he lets you know well in advance what he expects for papers and when they are due etc. He also provides great review sheets for the midterm and final, is energetic and has comprehensive and useful lecture outlines.

Best history professor I've had at Cal. Lectures are clear, well organized, and delivered with energy and great enthusiasm for the material. If you're at all interested in postwar American political economy and civil rights don't miss out on a chance to take a class with him! History majors: he'll make you a better historian.
Not a Good teacher in any way

Super defensive about his topic. Be careful when you write your essays to not go against any of his opinions. His lectures are choppy and becomes hard to follow after a while. Not easy to extract the main point out of his lecture.

not so 'brilliant'. his lecturing is pretty good, but he makes a really big deal about phones/sleeping/not paying attention--this isn't high school, relax. also, the course content is useless unless you plan on having an extremely spirited conversation with your friends about "culture" (suffering of minorities) in American history. dont take it.
Gets really irritated when people sleep in his class or are on their phone. He makes a scene and tries to act all tough in front of the students.

I am a US History major and Brilliant is my favorite professor. That being said, I don't recommend anyone taking his class who is not already a history major upperclassman who is at their last stage of history education. Brilliant is really helpful and great to talk to, but he also has extremely high standards that are too high for others

By far my favorite prof at Cal. Brilliant is.. well, brilliant. Lectures are engaging and well researched, always willing to discuss the material in office hours and makes himself avail outside of office hrs if needed. He doesn't accept excuses and has high expectations but he should. Its Cal. If you want your hand held you are at the wrong school

AMAZING CLASS! The topic was great to me, & the lectures were well organized w/ an overriding theme for each class. The class had a direct purpose and Prof. was approachable. The grading is hard, but its easy to know the expectations. Class= in class essay midterm/final,1 15 pg research paper (takes time), 8 books. lots of reading, def. recommend!!

Awesome professor! Take his class- super interesting lectures (played songs and disney movie clips!!) and really presents material without a bias. Talk to him after class to see how he actually feels about it. Gives a detailed outline out every class and assignments are clear. Definitely recommend taking him for American Studies 10!

Professor Brilliant (keep it formal) is inspired and well researched and he expects you to be.  I enjoyed his class, and was fully engaged, but I don't think I'll take him again because of the workload.  Amazing skills to be acquired with him?  Yes!  Will it hurt?  Yes!  Also: don't bother him during office hours.  Wait until after class.
I found his lecturing style to be pretty engaging and not too boring. He is passionate and generally quite interesting. I took American Studies 10 from him and would take another class with him.

This professor could not have been more full of himself. He was useless and his PPTs were garbage. He is a pompous hack who doesn't care about his students. His assignments were completely unclear and useless.

Absolutely awful. I've never had a worse experience in a class in my life. The man is completely full of himself and pushed the other professor, Waldo Martin, aside so he could deliver his garbage power point presentations over and over and over... It's really sad because Professor Martin was funny and engaging and had lived through a great deal of
I found that he was extremely unclear with what he wanted in assignments, but was pretty engaging in seminar.

You have to work in his classes, but the material is interesting and engaging and he is readily available during office hours and open to discussion. He doesn't generally entertain questions in class, but that's because they are large lecture classes and not designed to be interactive. That's why you go to office hours.

Took American Studies 110: Schooling in America...he was an amazing professor, and I learned a LOT. Great class to take if it is offered (special topics in American Studies). He taught it as a seminar. Lots of reading/work, but worth it in the end.

I wouldn't recommend this class.  What I didn't like the most was that he doesn't engage questions.  He gets defensive about them, in fact.  I tried to ask some questions in class, and he just seemed annoyed.
Unfailingly interesting and engaging

I enjoyed Brilliant's lecture sometimes, but overall, his style is basically reading off a powerpoint.  Really boring after awhile.  Most of the time when people asked questions in class he couldn't give them a clear answer, which was frustrating.  Doesn't seem very prepared to grapple with the larger material.
Am I the only one who thinks he's super hot? Huh.

I think he's a great person and he likes what he does, but I hate his class. Bores the heck out of me. If it weren't for the fact that this class can fulfill 3 requirements at once, I wouldn't take it. The grading is not as hard as I thought. I did surprisingly well on the one midterm so it's okay. Your grade is 1 final, 1 midterm, and 1 essay.

Wow--DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR!!  He is extremely unclear, unhelpful and overall a poor professor.  I am a history major and out of all the classes I've taken at Cal, in the major, his was without a doubt the worst.  (I love reading about the material, however his way of teaching and general attitude does not work)

No review or outline for midterm with tons of reading for the course. Definitely a bit of arrogance. when students ask questions it seems  as if he gets defensive. Wish I would have checked here before taking his class. Won't make that mistake again. Hope Cal sends him packing.

Professor Brilliant is amazing!  He is very approachable and helpful to students.  His classes can be difficult as far as reading goes - he's an historian remember, so he's all about text - but he will definitely take the time to clarify or help your understanding.  He's fun to hang out with in office hours and takes a genuine interest in his students.  I don't know why someone thought he sucked- must not have taken the time to get to know him or ask questions.  I highly recommend Brilliant!
One of my favorite professors at cal
worst history professor I've had- very unclear.  Constantly persisting that students need to start assignments, while lacking the proper information needed to begin.  Bad experience taking his class.

Horrible professor- very arrogant, teaches on topics one understands using common sense, yet tries to trick students when testing.  Doesn't outline or review anything on tests...hopefully he'll go back to Stanford--BAD addition to the #1 school...UCB.  Now I can understand why Stanford didn't want him teaching at their school.
Young guy new to Berkeley.  Really enthusiastic about the American West.  Recommend for all history majors.  Easy on the eyes too.
Great lectures!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Morris is organized, and her lectures are engaging. The course has 3 assignments which are based on the course material. Take her class if you want to learn about history and not have to sacrifice your life to get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: i definitely recommend 100D even if you aren't a history major. i took it spring of ‘25 of loved it
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: As a stem Major, this class was a breather for me. You can get away with not reading. But do recommend taking notes as they will help you in the 3 papers wou will be graded on
She doe NOT use Bcourses, assignments, even papers, are submitted printed out on paper in class so don't check canvas for anything with her

I marked that attendance is mandatory but I think she said you could have like 5 unexcused absences. She described it as "your easy class". Her lectures are very engaging and she is very nice but she holds herself in very high regard and makes that clear; I can see why people would find that annoying but she is nice. Office hours are chaotic

She is not tech-savvy at all and attendance is required, her lectures are just her talking so you need to pay attention and they are important. There are readings for the class but if you attend class she will cover it. She is a very nice and informative professor and you will watch movies in class would recommend talking to fulfill AC requirement.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Her grading is very variable, it is hard to get feedback from her. I found her to be unprofessional at times, she is condescending and has a grudge against any engineering/STEM students?
Her office hours were rushed. She was kinda rude to me when I was asking questions. I felt like she did not value me as a student nor my time. Grading also depends solely on the grader.

Prof. Morris is the nicest and most caring professor I've ever had. I would highly recommend her classes (History 100AC and 100D). Make sure you come to class because she takes attendance, and she goes over everything you need to know. The reading is interesting (and not too long), but you can do well in the class without doing all the reading.

Don't go in expecting an organized lecture with slides. The class is more like a group conversation. She is very kind and gives pretty in-depth feedback on essays. Lots of flexibility on what u want to write abt for papers. Learned lots about music! Ask her for some life stories and you won't be disappointed lol

I absolutely LOVED Prof. Morris's class! She is such an engaging lecturer and always takes the time to personally connect with her students. There are 3 papers, but they're mostly free-form and open to creative topics, this was my first upper-div and I got As on all of them. Shes an inspiring person with lots of stories and passion, take her class!

Anyone giving her a bad rating over "not having slides" is clearly not a fan of storytelling. Bonnie's cadence is relaxed, easy to understand, and hilarious. As someone with ADHD, I found it easy to comprehend while still having my attention. She is a yapper, but thats part of the charm. Honestly, look her up on Youtube, she has some fun interviews

Bonnie is such a lovely person and takes the time to get to know each of her students, encouraging to talk about how gender norms influenced their lives. Class is only graded on three things and all the essays are pretty easy. My only issue is she doesn't make slideshows so you have to catch everything she says in the moment and she tends to ramble

Took hist 100d. idk why she has such high ratings. Doesn't use slides and u have to print and staple each paper. she's not tech savvy which is inconvenient tbh. Yapper yet grading criteria is so confusing. Got a B on a paper when I did exactly what she asked. Got marked off for writing "they". Corrected me to "individuals".. are u srs. wouldn't rec

Class is made up of: short paper, midterm, and final. Attendance is taken at lectures, there are lots of readings, some films in class, but no homework. Overall, professor is very interesting and passionate about teaching. Paper is 3 pages MLA, Midterm is 3 in-class essays, and final exam is ~10 short answer questions with a longer in-class essay.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Bonnie is the best! My favorite course this semester. She is incredibly knowledgeable and full of wisdom. She makes lectures really fun. Only graded by a few things. If you take good notes, you should do just fine.

If you go to class, take notes and take a peak at the readings before an assignment, you'll have an A. "Doctor Bon" loves what she teaches and cares for her students. Each 90-minute class usually consists of an hour of lecture plus 30 minutes of open discussion.

Every class felt like a TED talk because she is such an interesting person. If you want to know what class is like, just search up her name on YouTube and watch one of her speeches, it's similar to how she lectures class! But with that said- that's all that class felt like, she uploads nothing online so you have to rely solely on word of mouth

She doesn't use any slideshows for her lectures so it's hard to keep up with what she's saying. She also tends to go back and forth through topics and overall her lectures are hard to follow and unorganized. Her grading criteria is also confusing as well since she doesn't give you an actual percentage.

Best professor I've ever had! Truly passionate about what she teaches! I took History 100D with her, a class on Gay history in America (I selected HIST100AC on here because ratemyprofessor didn't give me another option). Extremely reasonable grader, super engaging lectures, easy to reach out to, and just all around an amazing person to get to know!
Engaging lectures. You do 3 assignments the entire year. Chill class. Morris rocks

Bonnie Morris is the greatest professor ever!! Such a kind woman who cares deeply about what she is teaching. She really makes the class fun, you can totally get by just skimming the readings. Class is one essay, one midterm, and one final. She is very clear on criteria and a fair grader, TAKE THE CLASS!!

3 assignments total in the class, 2 are timed writes. I loved Morris, she was great and I'm so sad I'm not taking a class with her again. Her office hours and after-class talks are so fun. class is split between 1/2 lecture and then QnA. Lots of in-class movies and snacks. The readings aren't required at all. Keeps you updated on the world. Easy A.
She was great and I learned so much. She really wanted students to do well and getting a good grade was doable.
Incredible professor, really supportive and helpful + clearly incredibly knowledgeable.
Fantastic professor. Super easy A, yet I learned a ton. Attendance is mandatory, but you can have a lot of absences. Syllabus is super clear, and professor is reasonable and responsive.

I've taken a few classes from Bonnie, she literally changed my life. Best prof I've ever had if you like feminism or history. She's so so kind, always responds to emails, always sticks to the syllabus and has clear goals. Extremely passionate about not just the topic, but also teaching it. 15/10, sad I'm graduating and won't be able to take more.

Dr Morris knows a lot, however, u literally do not get any resources in this course aside from her talking with no slides during lecture, ya, no slides I said. She just talks for the 2 hours of ur class and u gotta just somehow comprehend it. office hours arent helpful either, sucks bc this class could be so good with a different teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Bonnie Morris taught me a lot about sports history. I didn't read a single thing she assigned and was able to get through midterms and final easily, but a downside is there was only one homework assignment outside of the midterm + final which means you MUST do well on them. Her office hours aren't very helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof Morris is a gem! I generally don't enjoy history but I found every lecture of hers incredibly interesting. She teaches with so much excitement for each topic and always includes discussion in the last 30 minutes (she won't call on people, but that was never needed since so many people had things to say). Super caring and nice too! Love her!

I took her Sports and Gender class. All required material is presented in person, WITHOUT slides, so you MUST attend class (or get notes from someone). She keeps track of attendance. Readings are supplementary, but everything you actually need is from lecture. Paper20% of grade. Midterm40%. Final40%. She's very passionate and caring!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures are sometimes boring, but as long as you do the problem sets, you should be fine. The midterms and final are based on the problem sets.
Good if you enjoy proofs and math heavy economics

He spends a lot of time deriving math expressions in class instead of showing practical examples or problems, and just reads from his slides (which he doesn't project). The problem sets were more useful. The exams were very difficult and 1/3 or 2/5 questions were about proofs.
Mostly self studied everything. Final was almost word for word problem set questions so grinded those. The course content itself is really hard and professor is OK.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: not a good lecturer and the tests are difficult

One of the only econ professors at Berkeley I could understand and comprehend. I think the misconception people have is that he is bad professor but the reality is: the content is hard and he is dry but why are you expecting a college professor to be entertaining. I thought the midterms n finals reflected what was taught and what was in the slides.

Bianchi's lectures are super monotone and he tends to go on long tangents that make it hard to stay engaged. The tests barely reflected what we actually covered in class—our final even had a random proof-style question, and this isn't a math class (discrete math isn't even a prereq). Honestly just a really frustrating experience overall.

I think Prof. Bianchi is not as bad as the other reviewers say. He seems disconnected from the course logistics (he refuses to answer grading questions), but his lectures are fine. However, his course favors pure memorization. I'd suggest taking this class if you can memorize quickly and are comfortable with math (matrices are a plus).
the worst prof i have ever seen. he curved his class to a c, 0 respect for students... do not take a class with him

I don't usually make posts for my professors but this is absolutely the WORST class I have ever taken in all my years of schooling. Not because of the content but because of the professor. Genuinely, the worst professor I have ever had and if I could go back in time, I would never take this class under him even if I was offered a million dollars.

ECON 136 is tough, especially for students without strong math intuition. Bianchi rushes through equations without building understanding, and grades rely solely on tests. Curving based on the top 20 is unfair and should violate department policy; it rewards prior skill, not learning gained.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: he wont even respond to questions about what the scope of the final is and just straight up has ignored everyone's questions asked during finals week on ed. i don't understand how such an uncaring professor is still allowed to teach such a hard class and he makes it seem like its all the student's fault for not being able to do well on the exams

Uncaring and traditional. Lectures are boring and aren't recorded. Your grade is comprised of 2 midterms and a final. The avgs are ~60% curved to a C. He laughs at students concerned with their grade. His course pack to study for exams is 90 pages needing different formulas you have to MEMORIZE; no cheat sheet. Lectures don't prepare you for exams.

His lectures make no sense and are incredibly boring. 2 midterms and 1 final make up your entire grade. In his grading system the top 20 students set the curve, however the top 20 do significantly better (by about 30% raw score) than the rest of the class so the class average is a B- if you're lucky. For us its currently a C. DON'T TAKE HIS CLASS.
He's very unavailable. Selectively responds to questions on Ed, ignoring valid questions about the awful grading scheme. And like others have said, prepare to teach yourself all of the material.
Worst grading scheme I've ever seen, incredibly difficult exams that are based on an unending number of formulas from 70+ practice problems that all require almost complete self-learning

Course is extremely test-heavy and poorly taught.
The professor does a poor job explaining concepts, and you're expected to teach yourself most of the content. If you're not already confident in the subject, prepare to struggle hard.
Inconsiderate

Not easy to sit through. He'll go on and on about something and... I don't even know. Lot of Brawl Stars played this semester. He's a good guy though I'll give him that. I liked talking to him. Good person. Hard to sit through teacher.

AVOID.
literally entire grade is based on 50% midterm 50% final and he is curving the class to a C and refusing to change. avg grade in class has gone down from B+ 3 sems ago to now a C??????
selectively respond to questions asked on ed disc
feels like he's happy to see about half the class failing and hates all his students...
Seriously no words for this professor. When most of the class if not passing or getting barely a passing grade because of his atrocious grading system, he just thinks that it's the students fault.

AVOID! Lectures are 1.5 hrs on a blackboard in a 500 person lecture room. Grades are solely based on exams &he loves testing obscure, untaught math-intensive FRQs that are impossible to prepare for. 

The grade is based on the average of top 20 scores in a 500 person lecture so even if class average is F, if 20 people get A, then you get no curve

Extremely dry lectures that spend an hour and a half doing proofs for formulas that can be memorized. The class is 100% test graded with the exams only test preparation material a 60+ page problem set pdf. He laughed and made jokes about the exam average being low and has little care for his students.
Do yourself a favor and do not take this class or with this professor in general.

This is a professor who doesn't appear to care very much either about teaching or his students. His lectures are almost entirely formula-driven, he makes the final brutal and grades students harshly, is not transparent about his grading policies, and treats engaging with students as a tedious obligation. Probably the driest class I've ever taken.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Terrible professor who genuinely hopes students fail. Based on midterm 1, if you get the median grade you get a C+ and if you get the mean grade you get a C-. Gives this HUGE (i mean nearing 100 pages) packet of problem sets that nobody can finish unless they dedicate their life to this class to practice for the midterms and finals.

Avoid this class at all costs. Lectures contain an overload of content, making it difficult to understand. No homework but your grade relies on 2 midterms and a final. 100 pages+ of practice problems to do on your own pace. Midterm was half multiple choice and half free response. This class will make you not want to go anywhere near finance.

By far the worst lecturer at Cal. Classes are not engaging, proof heavy with many tangents and completely incomprehensible (thankful for the lecture slides and the GSIs, as going to lectures is useless if not counterproductive). There are 6 problem sets, 1 midterm and no exercises or worksheets proper to prepare for exams. Class is self-study.

Absolutely the worst professor at Cal, and one who finds joy in tormenting his students. During my final he gave something that was completely proof based, something neither the midterm no practice finals consisted of. I heard he's moving toward a entirely exam based grading system, and during my final he was laughing seeing how much we struggled
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Bianchi is extremely lecture and test heavy. Make sure to take the first midterm—it's straightforward and reflects the practice tests. The final is completely sandbagged (it's rough).

Terrible teacher and very unkind. Says he will curve generously but then has a brutal curve. Most boring lectures I've had. Grading criteria and bins are not disclosed and suspect and no regrades. Also, he refused to tell me midterm policies because he said them in lecture, turns out they were in his lecture slides but he refused to even say that.

I swear no matter what anyone says about Bianchi you must never take Econ 136 with him. Sure his problem sets are for completion only, but that just means you have to do incredibly well on the midterm and final. And no, you cannot just skip the midterm because he intentionally makes the final undoable
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is absolutely the worst class I have ever taken, bar none. GSI teach better than him. He is just like a machine, coming to class every day just to get paid. In fact, his class is a complete waste of time. It is better to read textbooks and study on your own. I scored in the top 25% in the final exam, but I only got a B+ in the end.
He does not curve this class. I did well on the final and landed myself not even at a B. Furthermore, you must show up to class everyday because his lecture slides are actually useless

Avoid this class at all costs, it will kill any interest you might have in finance. I've had a 4.0 up until taking this class, and this one killed it. Midterm was hard and final was insanely hard. The culmination of micro, calculus, and even linear algebra you have to know for this class makes it ridiculous. Formula and proof heavy for no reason
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very hard exam. test on things never appear in problem set and past exam for 40 points

Created my account just to rate Bianchi. Lots of thing's come to mind but the main point is that none of them are good. No point of even taking the class as there is no support at all. Midterm was fine but the final exam is clobber for 65% of your grade. There are three final practice exams he gives, none of which actually helped for the test.
Boring lectures that don't make sense. Practice exams nothing like the real exam. Don't take for your own sake.
Don't take this guy. You're doing yourself a favor

I had Bianchi for 3 semester in a row, Econometrics, Financial Economics, and then Empirical Asset Pricing. 

He really is a great professor that gets a bad wrap. His courses are definitely hard and math/derivation heavy but it's because he wants people to truly understand what is going on at a deeper level.

Grading curves are VERY fair
