lectures make you want to fall asleep. exams are hard. he is very smart but just doesnt know how to teach. his voice is very monotonic and shows no excitement or passion in his voice when talking about finance subjects. rude when you email him.

Easily the worst professors I've had. There were no lecture slides, recordings, GSIs, discussion, or office hour. All we had were scribe notes, which were full of errors (grammatical, mistakes in the formulas, etc.). Lectures were boring and disorganized. Curve is good though, since no one has any idea what's going on. Overall, not worth it at all.

No Lecture Recording, No Lecture Slides, Lecture Notes written by students that don't know the content or how to use the software and the notes are always late, No GSI, No GSI Office Hours, No Discussions, Can't Teach

Nuff Said

Impossibly hard class with impossibly hard to follow lectures with impossibly hard problem sets. Does not post the solutions to the problem sets and does not help at all in office hours. Would never recommend this class to anyone

Does not explain concepts well, lecture slides often don't even have formulas, sometimes information (definitions of variables) contradicts. Pray your GSI knows their stuff-- mine cancelled almost every section last minute. Assignments are difficult but graded on completion. Worst midterm I have ever taken-- countless formulas and no sheet allowed.

Terrible, had him for Econ 136 and 140. This is the single worst professor I've ever seen. I  took a finance class with a different professor and realized that the topic can actually be taught well. Doesn't know a single thing he teaches, just reads off his notes (which he doesn't understand), no wonder he had no success in his financial career.
HOLY CURVE! But still a really really hard class. Avoid if you can but do not worry if you cannot. The curve will do justice.

The lectures are sometimes hard to follow because they are mainly deriving formulas, but overall I enjoyed the professor's lectures and he always encouraged students to ask questions.  His exams were difficult, but he curves the class.  The main negative part of the course for me is that my discussion section TA was not very helpful.

I took his Econ 140 course in spring 2022 and was surprised by the bad ratings he's received. His version of 140 is a bit dry and overly mathy (although it is Econometrics), but there is adequate section and lecture material to learn from. This class was definitely difficult but if you do the practice exams you should do decent.

One of the worst class at Berkeley. No notes, slides, recording. Graded by only few things and make exams extremely hard. All the nonsense proofs in lectures, no useful stuff, and we get completely different stuff for exams diff from the lectures. Practice finals  useless, final is completely new and different stuff and mess. No structure at all
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Final was extremely hard and midterm was way too long. He's not the worst at teaching, but spends wayyy too much time on proofs. He seems like a nice guy, but he should reconsider how he structures his exams.
really hard exams and unclear summary of content, needs a tons of self-studying on every corner without anyone guiding you

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. RUN! Hardest Economics Elective at Berkeley. This class needs GSIs/sections and lecture notes from the professor. No stupid scribe notes that tend to have a lot of mistakes in em because they are written by students. Save your GPA. Test heavy class that is difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I don't like how he structure the midterm.

he's a nice dude and seems to have a super chill personality but this class is such a slog for very little reward. there's a textbook, but he doesn't really use it (and for once, you wish he would just read the textbook) because he has no slides or notes just writes on the chalkboard for 90 minutes.

Knowledgable. Very clear in his speech and talks in a comfortable speed. Does most of the relevant stuff on the chalkboard, which is beneficial if you pay attention. Spends a bit too much time on proofs. Could benefit from having a bit more subtitles when making deductions and examples to help keep track. Overall very happy with this professor.

problem sets worth 35% of your grade were mostly completion based so that was refreshing. he definitely knows what he's talking about and he's really nice but lectures were really boring and kind of felt like a waste of time. i found a more productive alternative was just reading the textbook.

The professor had no recording for a non-mandatory course. His notes on the board were the same as his slides, making it almost no help for attending class. His exams were long and had a ton of small questions. Even the True False questions were based on calculation, and you would receive no credits for not having a correct explanation. RUN!!!

spends wayyy too much time on proofs when most of the exam is applications. i was so lost in class that I stopped going and did better by just relying on the slides and my gsi instead. the material's not that bad but the lecture was too dry and difficult to follow for me

Took 139 and 140 during my third year. 139 is probably the hardest undergraduate econ class at Berkeley, but 140 as a mandatory course is not that hard. I would even say that Bianchi over-simplifies many things. For example, he always uses Z test, but in many cases the strong assumptions clearly don't meet.

Honestly many accusations are not fair.

This course has a bad rep but it's really not that bad. The lectures can be a little dense but I think econometrics is just really hard to teach in general. Generous grading and Bianchi's office hours are helpful. Definitely attend sections. Only complaint is Bianchi could do a better job of explaining what topics to emphasize for exams studying.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Nice guy, eh teacher. If you skipped every lecture but ran every problem on the past midterms and past finals, you would get an acceptable grade. That kind of sums up the class. Lectures are high level and beyond whats expected on exams, and mastering the bulk of the course comes with repetition. PSets are free points, also.

Bianchi is a cool guy but simply not the best at teaching econometrics and not passionate about the class at all. I think in general it's just a difficult class but I would say GSIs were generous with the grading.

I found the lectures to be overly complex, and to succeed really all you need to do is study the practice equations because what is discussed in the lecture is way more advanced than what you will be tested on. Problem sets were fair, curve was acceptable.

Unclear grading criteria--uses Gradescope but doesn't give accurate feedback on why points were deducted. Also doesn't listen to student feedback throughout the semester. We all wanted more clarity on how proofs were derived but he still kept going at his usual pace.

Tells us the midterm is going to be similar to past midterms, then gives us a midterm twice in long (22 pages) for 90 minutes. It doesnt help that he rambles on in class and lectures are extremely dry.

Spends a lot of time on proofs (20% of tests) instead of applied questions on the material (80% of tests). Nice guy, but lectures are extremely dry and I honestly have no clue what were doing half the time. Midterm this year was WAY too long. I get that there were cheaters last semester but making the midterm hard only punishes honest students
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Though Bianchi is a nice guy and seems like he throws killer BBQs at his place, I genuinely have no idea what he's even lecturing us on and why it matters. We have spent basically every lecture going through notation-heavy proofs, yet every time we ask why we need to know this, he tells us we don't need to.

His teaching style is extremely dry and he's terrible at explaining the material conceptually . You'll be better off just reading the textbook and skipping lecture altogether. Cannot possibly recommend him, even though he's nice.
He really cares about his students, and can be a great resource outside of class too! It also helps that he is not a tough grader at all :)
Tests you on unnecessary materials and reads from slides to lecture.

Bianchi teaches Econometrics which is a really difficult Econ upper div. Some think he's "bad" teacher; however, I think it's b/c the course content itself is really hard to learn AND teach. He does his best to answer questions during class/office hours and really cares about his students/receptive to feedback. He used slides this semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: - He said he would grade generously in this course, he is such a funny guy, 5 stars for that (David E. Card gives by far better grades) - OH useless, take a nap instead - Arbitrary and non accurate grading - By "applied" he means proofs and theory, which he even does not know lol - He does not let you see the final exam, transparency goals

Bianchi gets a bad rep that I think is really undeserved. He's a nice guy, incredibly smart and very helpful in office hours. Doing well on exams requires a good understanding of his lecture notes (though not a perfect understanding) and a good command over the psets and Stata demos he posts. The class is fairly conceptual but also interesting!
Horrible at explaining concepts, handwriting sucks, makes you memorize countless proofs that he tests you on in his exams.

Lots of equations and proofs but the his proofs are not clear. Exams are also not at all like the lectures or the stuff in the book. You get cheat sheets for the exams but honestly the best way to pass is to do practice exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Truly kind and amazing guy. Takes a while to understand his logic, but easy class tbh
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Bianchi is a nice guy, but an awful professor. In class, he just wrote equations on the board. No explanations, no context, just equations and proofs. He's the worst professor I've had at Berkeley. Like said, he's a nice guy and was generous with the midterm grading (because the class did AWFUL) but he just can't teach.

Dont think he knows what hes talking about since hes constantly making mistakes. His idea of teaching proofs is literally to memorize every step and he often goes on unnecessary tangents instead of focusing on more difficult concepts. For such a slow teacher, he is also very impatient with students and lacks basic empathy. Do not recommend.

Bianchi is by far the worst professor I have had at Cal. He is extremely arrogant, does not care about his students, and straight up rude. His grading is easy and he doesnt teach/ test for anything beyond the surface. If you want to take it easy without mandatory attendance, go for it. For anything else that is worth your time, stay away

actually my favorite econ prof at berk. He is so nice and trying so hard to help you. he is very nice and approachable and caring in his office hour. I know ppl say there is too much proof in this class we dont need, but he said he must teach that according to the college requirement and a rigorous teaching process. I really appreciate him.

Classes are boring and filled with unnecessary proofs that not only does he not explain, but then has to correct in the following class. Often its completely unclear what we are even trying to prove. Little structure, a close reading of the textbook is necessary for this class. No notes posted online, no use of slides.

Lectures are straightforward and fun. The class is relatively harder than other Econ classes at Cal, but Stephen is VERY generous about gradings. Loved this class. Just don't miss the class. There's no lecture slide posted on bCourses.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: just read the book

laleh is amazing. if you can take anything with her plz do. im not a soc major but she makes me want to be. she always repeats what you need to know & says it in a super accessible way. take good notes. tells you exactly what concepts to study for midterm & keeps to her word. once in a lifetime prof. just take her!

Incredible, eyeopening class with an incredibly thorough syllabus that carries you from slave patrols to witch hunts, counterinsurgency, and mass surveillance. Laleh is very compassionate and understanding to her students and encourages us to pay our lessons forward out into the world. Coursework is light to standard for sociology courses.

This is the second class I've taken with Dr. Bebehanian. I enjoy the format of her classes a lot, and the building she does leading to a thorough understanding of more complex topics. Readings are tough, and worth it. Good class, great professor.
Best prof I've ever had. Will change your life.

this class was so GOOD! the readings were good and the lectures were great and there was such a sense of community in the class. Even though the topic is heavy it was so inspirational and I looked forward to coming to every class. I'm sad the class is over :-(  She's the best prof I've had at Cal by far

Laleh is one of the best, if not the best lecturer at Cal. Her courses have changed my world view and understanding of our society more than any other class I have taken. Soc 149P and Soc 140 are both fantastic. Lectures and readings are very important, essay style exams. She is phenomenal, absolutely take one of her classes before graduating.

Soc 140 is a hard class, but it is SO worth it. It will change the way you think about our entire society. Professor Laleh is so loved for a reason. She's super smart and her lectures are amazing. One note: if you miss a lecture, you WILL miss a lot so make sure you find someone to get notes from. She's also very nice and easy to talk with.

Reading can get to be a lot but even skimming through helps you understand the topic you'll be covering in class next. Professor Behbehanian is well-respected and popular (all for good reason!) but she can make office hours work despite her being high demand. Attendance is taken every day. She is very accessible via email and lectures amazingly.

I've never met a professor as wonderful and caring as Laleh Behbehanian. She genuinely gives a shit about her students and I would even go as far to say that she loves each and every one of them in her way. Her course content is also life-changing and eye-opening. If you can take one of her courses at Cal before leaving, I highly recommend it.

Professor Behbehanian is so incredibly gifted as a lecturer. She cares deeply about the subject matter of the class and conveys it in a very educational way. She welcomes all questions, concerns, and confusions about the material. Take her class! Any of them! She is a well-known VIP Sociology Professor. We're lucky to have her fr

You can tell Prof Behbehanian is truly caring towards her students and passionate in her profession.  I took her class last semester to fill unit requirements and was pleasantly surprised about how much I learned and enjoyed the content of the course.  She is such a genuinely kind person filled positive energy as well! Would take again, 100x over

Laleh was an amazing professor! Her assigned readings are intentionally shortened and have reading guides. Her lectures review readings and explain well the concepts she wants us to understand. The exams are also take-home, open note and straight forward. Overall, she's a really great professor for learning and doing a good job at it too.

Laleh is amazing! She is by far the best lecturer I've had this semester! Her explanations of concepts from readings are thorough, and she always ensures that everyone follows along and understands the concepts. Her obvious passion and interest in what she teaches made going to lectures so exciting. She is incredibly caring and very equitable.
Amazing professor! Her lectures are so good, and she's so passionate and inspiring!

AMAZING lecturer. Taken 4 of her classes. Sociology of Policing was the best class I've taken in my life. Prepare for light reading. Since you only have to do 9 reading responses throughout the course you don't have to do all the readings, the lectures will make you feel like you did the reading anyway. Heavy content trigger warning.

Laleh was my absolute favorite professor! I took 4 courses with her over my 5 years at Berkeley and I learned so many things in every single one of them. Laleh cares so much about her students and the topics she teaches. Readings are mandatory, but nothing she assigns is filler and she takes the time to create extensive reading guides.

By far the best teacher from my 4 years at Cal - this course changed my life. Laleh's lectures somehow break down complex global systems into understandable concepts that make everything *click.* She teaches with humor, deep caring, and genuine respect for all students, and facilitates meaningful discussions even in a big lecture hall! She is REAL.

Laleh is amazing. Her lectures were terrific, and we had space for discussion. Do the readings because 85% of your grade depends on it. 70% of your total grade relies on two exams (papers). Yikes! It is hard to recover if you underperform on either of the papers. We signed an attendance sheet daily but have yet to receive a grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I absolutely loved Laleh's class. I took SOCIOL 149P as a first-year without knowing it was an upper div. course. Her lectures and content revolutionized the way I conceptualize race and social dynamics in the United States and basically changed my whole outlook on life. Also, highly recommend going to her office hours just to talk!

Haven taken three courses with Behbehanian, the course embodies the meaning of a true sociology class. The lectures are amazing. The reading is dense but manageable if you remain on track. 2 exams, a research paper, and some writing responses. 10/10!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: Taken two of their classes so far. They weave together the material and their passion so well into the lecture that it is honestly a joy to be in class. Behbehanian is one of the best sociology professors at Cal. Make sure to at least skim the readings and show up for lecture. Super approachable and caring during office hours.
Wonderful, inspirational professor. Caring, well spoken, and an admirable woman!

One of the best professors that I've taken at Cal. The lectures worked in parallel to the text, were SUPER FUN and REWARDING to listen to. I thoroughly enjoyed every minute of the class and class discussions. 
The essays were not difficult but still gave us an option to get a better understanding of the text. GREAT OFFICE HOURS too!!

Professor Behbehanian is one of my favorite professors at Cal. She gives very thorough, interesting, and concise lectures that make the mandatory attendance doable. No textbook but an optional course reader for $30 available. Graded based on completing 7 out of 9 reading responses and three exams composed of 2-3 short essay questions.

L is an amazing instructor and very passionate about teaching. The class consisted of a reader where readings were due every Tuesday and Thursday. You have to submit 7 of the 9 reading responses available. The exam questions were difficult but easy if you do the reading/attend lecture. Lots of reading, but great class. I recommend this course.

If you are looking to be challenged in your understanding of police/policing in the world strap in and enjoy this class. Her lectures are engaging the reading is intense but broken into easily digested sections. When you think of sitting in a UC Berkeley lecture Prof. Laleh embodies that experience! Do not miss out on taking her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Laleh was very kind and accomodating. Her lectures were very engaging and she walked through each reading and topic super clearly so that it was easy to understand. Minimal assignments and the grading was very generous as long as you took very close notes during lecture.

Ive taken laleh for two semesters now and I want to take her every semester until I graduate. Amazing lectures that make you love sociology! You cant leave Berkeley without taking one of her classes. Easiest lectures to understand. Idk how she breaks down such complex topics into such easy terms.

The best class and best professor I have ever had. Prof. Behbehanian is incredible-I learned SO much in this class that I will never forget for the rest of my life. She is makes sure all concepts are extremely clear and understandable to everyone. She deeply cares about her students and is so passionate about her work. TAKE A CLASS WITH HER.

I've taken Soc141 (F21) & Soc3AC (F20) w/ Laleh & she is an amazing instructor. Her lectures are super easy to follow & she is really good abt answering questions during lecture & in office hours. The structure of her classes is super easy to follow & honestly its easy to pass if you just pay attention in lecture & submit the reading questions

Amazing class! Homework is pretty light and the reading reviews actually help you learn and are easy points to boost your grade. L is super caring, amazingly kind, and great at breaking things down simply + reinforcing the main idea. I actually felt like I learned something in this class. Would definitely recommend.
She's the best professor here and anywhere

Easily one of my favorite professors at Cal and I'm not even a sociology major. She is charismatic, very clear, and passionate about what she teaches. I've had the honor of taking Soc3AC with her and I intend on taking Soc141 with her as well. Yes you have to read, but it's important content and she will work with you to ensure you understand it !

Professor Behbehanian is one of the best and hardest working professors I've ever encountered at Berkeley. Numerous times she has made space for us to discuss real world issues and how it's impacting us, and she reduces the required readings for the class when she can tell students are struggling. She's no nonsense but cares A LOT about students.

I took professor Behbehanian this semester b/c everybody said she was amazing. I honestly did not enjoy her class, she would get frustrated if you asked more than one clarifying question & when I met with her in office hours she was very condescending. There are a LOT of dense readings & there are only 3 assignments, Exam 1, Exam 2, & Final.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: If you haven't taken her class yet, do it. They fill up fast as heck because she is literally the dream prof. She is a kind and brilliant professor with a firm grasp of sociology. She is truly the best, but PAY ATTENTION and TAKE NOTES because that will be pivotal for your exams. Always attend class. Read! Goto office hours. PS graders kinda tough.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The reading was worth it though. Every topic was relevant to current events. Great discussions. Would recommend to fulfill requirements!
Laleh is an amazing professor. She really cares about what she is teaching, and it shows. Her grading is based on two midterms and one final (cumulative).

To say that Laleh is a great professor is an understatement. Even though I am not a Sociology major, this class was accessible, fascinating, and inspiring to say the least. Be prepared to actively analyze assigned readings and write because your grade depends on it, but Laleh makes the assignments clear and fair. This class is extremely worth it!

Really great and passionate professor, sometimes gets annoyed by certain questions & occasionally rushes through her lectures. I did all of the readings but you're only graded by 3 essays, and the grading rubric is super specific and hard so this was my first B at Cal, but the material was interesting & I loved the discussion in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Laleh is absolutely amazing and deserves all the hype. Hands down my favorite professor at Cal! Her lectures are well organized and inspirational, and as long as you take good notes, you should be set for exams. You can tell that she cares deeply about her students and what she teaches -- her passion is contagious.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Laleh is one of the best professors at Cal, brilliant, and caring. Her Sociology of Policing class is a MUST TAKE for students in any major. You will learn a lot of interesting info and the class environment is extremely supportive as well. I loved having Laleh as a professor so much that I am taking another class with her next semester too.
Oh my god I love Laleh soooooo much she is so caring and respectful and intelligent! Also great with DSP accommodations and very clearly cares about each of her students

An amazing professor! She explains everything so clearly and truly wants you to understand. She doesn't share slides but she outlined her points so well that you will be able to get all the info you need. I learned so much in the course and would recommend it to anyone. It's not a difficult course either. A lot of reading, but she explains it all.

PROFESSOR BEHBHANIAN IS THE BEST THAT BERKELEY HAS TO OFFER. Not only does she actually care about her students (she will take the extra effort to remember your name and SUPPORT YOU), she does a stellar job combining the readings to in-class lectures/the main idea (better than I have seen any other teacher before). Her lectures are LIFE CHANGING!

Laleh is by far the best instructor I've ever had. You will have a great experience no matter what class you take with her. She's an incredible lecturer, extremely knowledgeable, and deeply cares about the topics she teachers. She clearly values each and every one of her students and is once of the sweetest people I've ever met. I love her!!!!!!!!!

Easily the best sociology professor at Cal. This is a no brainer. Super engaging professor, so organized with her content, and also just really sweet, caring, and funny. Her Soc 140 class taught me so much, and I would take it again for fun if I could. Her assignments are pretty rough though (e.g. 4 essays due in a week), but it's worth it
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures--So many papers

reviews.comment: I am taking Sociology 3 AC (during covid-19) and she has been beyond understanding and accommodating. She is very passionate and clear. The class was really fascinating and easy to understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: 100% my favorite class Ive taken at Cal. Laleh is extremely passionate about her work and it shows through in her lectures. I will say that her grading on the take home essay exams is tough, but she is extremely helpful during office hours. I would recommend any of her classes to everyone of all majors :)
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Beware of pop quizzes--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: What a fantastic class! I took SOC140 with Laleh and I didn't regret it a second. She is very accessible outside the lecture, really helpful and just a very nice person. The content was also very interesting and she manages to explain difficult theory in very easy terms. I would definitely take it again!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Beware of pop quizzes--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Inspiring professor that really cares about what she does and the students wellbeing! First semester transfer at Cal and she pushed me to be challenged (reading every day for the Summer session) but also is super clear on what she expects and fair with her grading. Makes class very interesting and everyone is constantly engaged in her lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Laleh is by far my favorite prof at Cal. She has pop quizzes throughout the semester but if you do the reading you will ace all of them. She even drops your lowest quiz scores. Her lectures are insightful and the midterm and final count for a lot but if you actually pay attention you will do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: One of those professors you'll remember years after you've left Cal. Laleh is very clear in her lecture and she is just so inspirational. Make sure to stay on top of the readings as there are (easy) pop quizzes on the readings. The content of the class really challenges you to critically think about the modern state. I would def take Laleh again!

Laleh is probably the best prof. here at Cal. She explains everything in a way that is very easy to understand. The reading is a lot and you will have unexpected pop quizzes throughout the course but they're not hard. If you have a basic understanding of the readings you'll be fine. All exams are take home, 3 short papers for both midterm and final

Words cannot express how amazing of a professor and human being Laleh is. She is a brilliant educator who empathizes with students and connects them to the material. She is passionate about sociology and her lectures are very dynamic and engaging. Her class is structured well and her expectations are made clear from the jump. 100% recommended.

Laleh Is an amazing professor! Her syllabus is clear. This is UC Berkeley an institution that is hard regardless of who is teaching. However, Laleh manages to make her course interesting and engages you with her questions. Available and accommodating. See Laleh in spring! Crybaby below me is in my class and must not be doing well, unfortunately.
She is the BEST professor at UCB. Soc 140 with her is highly recommeded. She will show the real sides of States in the USA.

My favorite professor at Cal. Not only is she a more than effective teacher, she instills a deep passion for social issues in every one of her students. Attendance was mandatory because she gave out pop quizzes regularly & does not post slides online. However, class is always inspiring so that wasn't a problem. Highly recommend any of her classes.

Excellent lecturer who rly did a good job clarifying readings. Readings were long, but they did end up changing my perspective on everyday life. Besides reading, not a very time-consuming class except when papers came around. Just attend lectures, take good notes, and it'll be great. Glad I took her class, and would take another with her in a snap
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: What an amazing professor who's passionate about her work. Even though I'm a stats major, this is the only humanities class (out of 3) that I thought was worth attending this semester (and attendance is mandatory for all 3 of my classes). Elucidates the readings in class lecture, and is very accommodating. Take her 100%
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Behbehanian is amazing! I feel so inspired by her lectures! I love her and her pedagogy so much that I took three classes with her and I want to take more! Shes inspirational.

Laleh has enhanced my experience at Berkeley tenfold. She is so brilliant, patient, passionate, caring, and beautiful - you will want to come to class every time! Do not graduate until you have taken one of her classes. I am so grateful to have been in two of her classes and to learn from such an inspirational woman.

If youre reading this to decide whether to take her or not then STOP WAITING!! Amazon person and lecturer. Is she worth it even if her classes dont fit into your schedule as easily or you have to come on an extra day? YES. She is a prof where you dont just regurgitate information, you actually LEARN and retain. Her classes affect your life
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I took political sociology in summer 2017 and Laleh is amazing! She unpacked this topic in a unique way with various theorists like Tilly and Brown. She is truly invested in her students and made every effort to know students names and be available above and beyond outside of class. "Pop quizzes" were broad enough where you had to try to fail.

I've taken two classes with Laleh so far, and I have to say her classes have made a huge impact on my academic path. SHE IS AMAZING. Super clear, super passionate, super friendly. You will learn so much from taking her classes, and you will do well because it's so easy to stay engaged with the material. I recommend her to everyone I know!

She is clear and passionate! Essential class. Learned so much relevant history, soc theory, and critical thinking. Very easy to be engaged, readings are not too long. A real privilege to learn from a professor this intelligent and dedicated. My best experience at Cal yet, hope to take her again. 15% attendance, reading responses 35%, are easy pts

I love this professor! She is so passionate about what she teaches and really gets the students involved. Her lectures help you analyze the readings (although the reading is pretty easy!) for midterms etc. Midterm and final were both essays  and she had about 7 reading responses throughout the semester. Also grading is very reasonable.

This was the best class I have taken at CAL so far. Prof. Behbehanian is clear and takes her time to ensure that the class understands what she is talking about. I had the class from 5:00-6:30 pm and it was the only class I looked forward to attending. The class is graded on 3 papers and attendance but there is a lot of reading (worth it!)

This is a really great class and Behbehanian is super engaging and down to earth. The lectures aren't overly complicated and the material is relevant and interesting. The class is graded based on three essays. You don't have to read if you go to lecture.

The professor would not choose to stress out her student by taunting readings, but by elaborately-chosen texts, she gives clear-cut analysis and also care how student understand her. The learning quality depends on devotion to texts.
Amazing class - highly recommend! She gives fascinating lectures that make everything crystal clear and connects sociology to real life events which keeps things interesting.... Loved this class!!!
Prof. Laleh completely changed my bias against lecturers. (sorry...) Her Soc 140 is so inspirational. It is hard to believe that she can make political sociology so interesting. highly recommend

Laleh is extremely passionate and excited about her material. She has an engaging lecture style that makes you pay attention and connects the material to recent events. Never dry or boring. My favorite class at Cal so far. TAKE IT IF YOU CAN--it changed my worldview, and the hard work was so worth it. I cannot say enough good things about her.

FANTASTIC! Laleh is the best Sociology lecturer I have ever had. She makes dense and difficult readings crystal clear! Her lectures are engaging, enlightening, and super helpful. She is also very kind, funny, enthusiastic, and accessible during office hours. Her grading is quite fair, and she does an AMAZING job connecting theories to real events!

She is extremely passionate and patient with the class and the students, and actually goes over the assigned reading to make sure everyone understands what the hell they read and also ties it into examples that you can relate to and retain for months to come after. Definately need to take her and visit her office hours. AMAZING!
Awesome class - she keeps it interesting and explains everything clearly...
Best class I have ever taken at Berkeley. She is so smart and makes the class fascinating. Partly because the content is amazing but so is her articulation of it. Highly Recommend.
side tracked very easily, I find it hard to focus on the actual topics covered in class. Exams are good, not too hard.
Quite engaging in lecture, and lenient and accommodating in grading

Odd lecture pacing- can get sidetracked on questions/details but can also be fast & spend little time on a required slide or topic, catching up w day's slides. Weirdly enjoyed going over recording- able to pause 4 notes & enjoy his lectures' fun tone+delivery.
Test Qs can be unclear/ involve topics from one random slide/ HW Q.
Explains content well
The workload is huge for this class and seems more than what's necessary
His lectures are unnecessary to go to. He's a really nice person, but rambles a lot.
Very disorganized class. Do not take if it's not a requirement.

The class is very disorganized. Lectures weren't that helpful, had to rely on discussion sections most of the time to understand what was happening in class. The content for the "quizzes" wasn't covered thoroughly so I had to try learning a lot of the content on my own. The group projects were fine just make sure you get a good group.

Prof Clark was nice, and the class itself was not that bad, but it was very disorganized.  The homework seemed to be nothing like was taught in the lectures and it seemed pretty random a lot of the times.  There were times when the professor did not know how to answer to the homework which was frustrating.

Professor Clark is amazing! His lectures are super interesting and you can tell he cares a lot about what he teaches and his students. He's very accessible outside of class if you ever need help with homework.
Lectures were confusing and unhelpful. Quizzes required assistance from many different people to be able to complete correctly.
(Currently taking class) Clear lectures, nothing made too difficult. Practice exams are highly similar to actual ones, so it was easy for me to do really well on the exams.
Didn't feel like she wanted students to improve. Otherwise, the class seemed okay material-wise
Not a very understanding instructor at all. Almost mean when it comes to students understanding
Lectures didn't cover all topics, so had to read the rest on your own. Gives practice exams that are pretty much the same questions that will appear on the real exams.

Professor Corteel is a good Professor, which means she's a fantastic Professor by Berkeley standards. Honestly this class was very fair (even if you are not a math major). Corteel loves induction so there is a little emphasis on that. Overall if you have the homework down, do the practice exams, and study for the quizzes, you'll do great.

I took Professor Corteel Fall 2023 for Math 55. Overall, I really enjoyed the content in Discrete and found that lectures were not very useful and lacked structure/consistency, but I was lucky I had an amazing GSI (Mitsuki).
Her exams are VERY similar to practice exams, which was nice because I didn't have to study much. Corteel is alsovery funny.

Saw a piazza post of a student explaining how unfair the course was, the final questions were graded unequally, a concise proof is lacking clarity and a detailed proof is also unclear. TAs made their own quiz so many students had easier quizzes than others. We were removed on piazza unable to voice our concerns along that student, how odd is that?

Corteel is not the worst professor Ive had, but also not the absolute best. Shes a solidly dependable choice if you want to take Math 55. In all honesty, youll be fine just using the textbook as your main resource, you can get away with missing most lectures.

Having taken several math courses at Cal, I can say Professor Corteel is superb at teaching and explaining the concepts. I think she can be more accommodating for her students, especially during a global pandemic.

Professor Corteel is amazing! She is caring and very willing to answer questions. The class was not too difficult, and the practice exams solidly matched the actual exams. There were no bad surprises in her class. I really enjoyed her lectures, and she was as clear as a math professor could be at explaining things. Also, she is French!

Early review for people choosing classes for next sem. She always gives a full week from assigning a hw until it's due, usually 15-20 problems. Midterm 1 was straightforward and like the practice test. Average was an 80%. Her lectures are pretty clear and she'll try to answer any questions . Overall a reasonable professor and would recommend
Very bad Professor.

Average Econ class:super long exams (40 pages of pure computations), messy handwriting (hard to keep up with), and concepts that feel more complex than they need to be. Overall, though, not bad. There's a generous curve and pretty reasonable HW. GSI (Anson) was a crashout tho, and made it hard to ask questions (made you feel bad for not knowing).

Lectures were fine, just a bit dry; I wish she gave more interesting real-world examples and such. My section was very useful, but the textbook was not. The p-sets were pretty hard, but not too much work and fairly graded. Very generous exam curve because they're difficult and LONG - the final was something like 40 pages of computational problems.

Lectures were okay, but covered everything you needed to know; recorded. Psets are similar to exams and graded lightly. Exams are long and very computational. Brush up on Calc I. Curve/Bins are undisclosed but must be quite generous. Extra credit through polls, bonus for class participation. Gaubert has a lot of experience in the industry.

Definitely one of the better French econ teachers. Lecture and section are so important for her class. Her lectures can be a little all over the place, but section (go Anson!) really clears up the concepts. A lot of material for exam prep (exam averages around 50%) and curve is thick cuz some people forget its math intensive.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Cecile is a caring professor whose lectures are quite good (definitely attend them). The psets and discussion notes were particularly helpful for exam prep and understanding the material, and there are quite a lot of resources available for students to succeed compared to other math-intensive upperdiv econ classes at Berkeley.
Pretty good class. Good and clear lectures. PSETs are helpful for exams. Exams can be difficult tho

Material is well-covered but still requires study outside of lecture and section. Tests seem to be really easy or really hard and examine understanding over memorization. However, past exams have sometimes been less than helpful in preparation. Professor is a great person and is good at making sure students understand, answering lots of questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: lectures and sections are useless...you have to study everything by yourself

Class is graded pretty generously (20% HW completion, rest is exams. Participation can boost you up one grade so get to know her). Tests seem either really easy or really hard, tend to present material that you've seen before in bizarre ways. Lectures often deal with math/stats concepts but they suck at teaching non-econ concepts.

The professor and GSIs are nice and accessible outside of class (especially David). Most of the students who choose this class are really smart, so beware of that. However, the curve is pretty lenient, with a large percentage getting A's and B's. The problem sets are lengthy, the exams are hard. STUDY! Cramming does not work.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Gaubert is an amazing professor for Econ 101A. Her lectures give you an in -depth understanding of the math involved, builds your interest in the topics (she brings in a little about studies in areas such as behavioral economics) , and her exams have been fair thus far. Take a class with her, you won't regret it!

ECON 101 series, in general, attracts more impressive students so be prepared for that. Gaubert is a good lecturer but holy hell the exams are incredibly difficult. I scored +1 and -1 SDs on the MTs and that final was literally the hardest test I've taken in my entire life. She was a good professor for the class - definitely do past tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Her lectures are solid, and she answers everyone's questions clearly. Plus her accent is quite delightful!

Good professor at what she is teaching. Econ101A isn't necessarily an exciting class, but she does her best to make it engaging. Every lecture covers a lot of ground, so it's important to go to them. A very solid professor and definitely gets the job done.

Very passionate and knowledgeable professor who is truly excited to teach. However, because he does have so much to say, lectures can feel overwhelmed with info and jumbled. Lots of reading, but the course is not difficult. I loved the content so I didn't mind the work, but if you do not care for anthropology, pick a different breadth.

His lectures weren't very entertaining but they were definitely were interesting. Very tech savvy and made sure all the lectures were accessible. Get ready to remember a ton of anthropologists names and what they did!

He writes lectures the night before class, which are disorganized. He changes the syllabus throughout the semester, and made us pay for reading material in the middle of the semester. Pray you have a good GSI to help break down his lectures. But he does care a lot and provides detailed study guides that have prepares you for midterms and finals.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: lectures are hit or miss, sometimes incredibly interesting sometimes he goes on tangents. attendance is technically mandatory but he only enforces it if lots of people dont show up. all exams were extremely easy because he gave study guides that literally told you the questions. there is a project that requires you to conduct anthropology yourself.

He's passionate but his class is a BORE. He took away the free online readings halfway thru and made us pay for it. My GSI seemed lost under his instruction and didn't know how to help us cus he didn't guide them or make a centralized grading system. The course was formatted with unclear instructions and inconsistent exams. Easy A but never again.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Cohen is a decent person made absolutely unbearable by his boring & neurotic teaching. Most course content is based on inconsistent lectures that had nothing to do with readings. The syllabus was changed halfway through the semester after a disasterous midterm, & no written assignments had any rubric provided despite being a majority of the grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: this dude is having an increasingly worsening existential crisis day by day and I have never related to something more. He really cares about what he teaches, sometimes a lot more than what makes sense for students taking a breadth course. But I found that his self deprecation and genuine lack of hope for society makes everything he says memorable

he is a professor who really cares for the material, super passionate—sometimes his lectures drone on quite a bit, and your GSI makes or break your experience. The tests are not hard if you study, however, and he does create really detailed study guides before each exam. not bad for an AC and a breadth, but only if you enjoy humanities
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Cohen is a very good professor. His lectures can be a little tangential, and he clearly has higher priorities than this class, but overall, he is very transparent and interesting to listen to. The readings are probably the dominant course content, and he outlines them very well. Study guides tell you what to study for the exam -- verbatim.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Cohen was my favorite professor by far this sem! Only assignments were 4 in-class essays every few weeks (~1-2pgs) and a final essay (~5 blue book pages). These were very easy and were all based on the readings from the textbook. He does yap a lot and this class works best for independent students, but he is AMAZING! 100% recommend his class!
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Incredibly knowledgeable and caring. Not the kind of person you can talk to because he never really stops talking to let you talk. If you are not an independent student this is not for you, but if you want the time and encouragement to learn how to do research then do it! Take notes during lecture and review later to find the gold in his lectures!

Professor Cohen was delightful! He cares about people & students. We had a lot of really insightful guest speakers and conversations. My only complaint was that he is a bit unorganized as a professor. Kind of all over the place

Prof. Cohen tends to have a lot info thrown at you, talks a lot buuut show up to class, skim the readings, talk to your gsi and you should be fine. Personally didn't find the class that interesting and recommend another class for an AC.

Horrible horrible lecturer. Seems like a respectable and knowledgeable guy , but he just can't lecture without going off tangents. He started taking attendance because no one went to lectures. Lectures are dreadfully long. Just do the study guides he gives for exams. I learned a lot of interesting things from self studying though.
amazing class that changed my entire perspective :)
He's a brilliant person but a horrible professor. I wouldn't bother listening to his lectures as they are incoherent . I recommend focusing on the readings and to listen to your GSI.

don't even bother going to class, he has a voice that puts me asleep and sounds like he's going on and on about irrelevant things. you're best bet is to read the readings and go to the lectures if you can listen to him.

Professor Cohen has a bad rep but he is a great teacher. He teaches anthro3AC which is an AC requirement at Cal, so perhaps not all students are interested in this class and do not put enough effort in. However, he is so passionate. If people actually went to lecture they would realize how great of a professor he really is. He is hilarious.

Lawrence speaks a lot and seems like hes rambling but has brilliant things to say. Its all relevant but take what you must. He really opened my mind. Just sit through it and know it may click later. Above all he really cares about his students which is more than most other professors.

Boring lecturer, not worth it to attend lecture unless you are truly interested in the subject. If you are just taking it for the AC requirement, best resources to do well are GSI's/Section, and posted bcourses summaries of the weekly readings. Nice professor who cares a lot, but unclear on what we needed to know from the lecture slides for tests
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: The readings in this class are everything. I literally learned nothing from lecture; Cohen rambles on and info dumps on his powerpoint. Go to discussion, at least the GSIs know how to communicate the information with undergrads. Readings aren't optional, the midterm and final both test heavily on them. Pretty boring class but changes your worldview
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor is really immature.  He  doesn't understand that come college students have other events which may cause them to leave a bit early during the class and will have no problem making a scene about it! He rambles about lots of useless things that make no sense whatsoever unless you're an anthropologist. Take something else

Material would be more interesting if he knew how to teach without making you fall asleep. I feel bad for him, nobody goes to lecture, but for a reason. Lectures aren't mandatory and people still don't watch the course captures, just do the readings. Boring class, but not hard.
This guy is so bad. I feel like he's knowledgeable but he sucks at teaching the material. Period.
Rambles on in lecture, knowledgeable but you will fall asleep.

Prepare for long random tangents in lecture. We had 3 or 4 versions of the syllabus from him as the semester continued, none of which he followed. Nice guy, kinda funny, but this class was JUST him talking. Grades were mostly from a midterm and a final paper which had NO guidance to it at all. Wouldn't take him again, just too scattered.

Cohen is long-winded, but he says a lot (he's not just listening to himself talk). Don't expect to understand his lectures if you do not do the assigned reading. There are few assignments and his is a tough grader. But if you approach his course with  the intention to actually learn (which is what we're here for) - you will be rewarded.

Cohen is knowledgeable and approachable, but his lectures are consistently 1.5hrs of him rambling. It's not easy to pick out what is relevant and what's a tangent, sometimes he goes off for 20min on something unrelated. We've had 3 syllabi versions and he still doesn't follow it. Prepare to get lost in class and get your grade via long papers.

One of the most compassionate and caring professors at the university, and a bit of a genius to boot. Really willing to work with you, prefers face-to-face to email (a refreshing change). His class changed anthropology for me.

Cohen changed my academic experience completely. He has opened up new worlds and possibilities for the way I think and engage with life. He is a gift, and if you take any of his courses you should go to his office hours. He will answer your questions indirectly through stories and references, complicating your understandings in a beautiful way.
Entertaining but confusing lectures.  Endless reading.  Mandatory section attendance and must keep up with reading. Class appears daunting, but, in the end, grading is straightforward and fair.
Professor Cohen is amazing! I've taken his Anthro 114 class and his Global Sex class. Both are really interesting. As long as you stick with his notes and the readings he emphasizes, you'll be good.

Cohen is brillant. Not an easy course. Incredibly challenging, but he is a fair grader. Don't miss lectures and stay on top of readings. His lectures are very clear, he discusses the readings in detail. Loads of studying, get in a group to spilt up the info, but he gives you a big list of what to focus on.

This is an intriguing and challenging class.  Cohen does a great job of giving a nuanced account of the multiple factors that have influenced anthro thought. He does not just give an overly simplified progression of ideas in history, but shows that the changes don't occur in a vacuum.
Professor Cohen is brilliant.  If you bother paying attention to his lectures then quickly realize they are quite clear in form and insightful in substance.

He is the real thing - a genius. Berkeley is lucky to have him. Take his classes if you want to be immersed in the intellectual traditions of the discipline and beyond - do not take his classes hoping for an easy and formulaic path to an A. He'll talk your ear off, take you more seriously than you take yourself and that's an amazing gift!

studied SO hard for the midterms. got an a because i worked my ass off but more importantly had a brilliant GSI. cohen is brilliant but he cannot lecture, and i went over his powerpoint slides indefinitely, over and over again. you have to if you want a good grade. you have to synthesize across a lot of material, know your stuff, get a study group.

This class was definitely challenging, but it was great. The lectures and readings can be quite overwhelming but I learned SO much. My GSI was incredibly nice. He made the tough material pretty understandable. Overall, great class, professor, and in my case GSI.

Cohen is a genius but he does not know how to lecture. If you ask him a question, he will NEVER answer it with a clear answer. Rather, he goes in circles and never gets to the point. Lots of readings, unsympathetic GSIs, and powerpoint slides with 500 words per page. Complete info overload! Never studied so hard in my life but ended up getting an A

Lawrence is brilliant, funny, approachable and fascinating. He teaches at Ivy League level and doesn't dumb anything down. I loved going to his lectures and personal interactions during office hours were even better. The man's a treasure.

I have mixed feelings about Professor Cohen.  He is obviously a very intelligent man.  However, the man needs to learn how to edit.  We were inundated with so much information during lectures, and some of the information was irrelevant as far as what we actually had to know for exams.  That being said, I did learn a lot in his class.

A seemingly brilliant man, his tangents lend insight to his large bank of knowledge AS WELL AS his inability to lecture. He is horrible at making a point, and can be led astray by any slight theoretical suggestion.  Do the readings and go to section...you'll actually learn something that way. And you'll do well on his tests (which are quite fair).

Cohen is really brilliant. I didn't get to know him, but the small interactions we had were pleasant. It doesn't seem that he's very passionate about lecturing, but maybe just wants to research. Never answers student qs clearly. Goes on tangents constantly!  Generally enjoyed the class, a little theory intense at first, but towards the end more fun

He's a really interesting, dynamic, funny lecturer and a great storyteller. (He made a 3 hour lecture class tolerable.)  He's also very friendly and approachable. Can spiral off from student questions to tangentially related topics, so be prepared to interject and clarify if you ask questions in class.
Hilarious and insightful--an utter genius.

He never made eye contact with us, which is telling of both his lecturing and scholastic styles.  He talks fast, writes indecipherably, and doesn't appreciate alternative viewpoints.  Overall, I found his credibility questionable.

Very lively, animated lecturer. Keeps you interested in class, but sometimes wanders around the point. Great facial expressions, the Jeff Goldblum type. Lots of reading, but they're fun books and a reader that wont kill you. Short answer/essay type exams. Beware stuffy, snobbish GSIs that are obsessed with their own research.
No Comments

Prof. Campbell is amazing! I couldn't recommend him enough. For this being my first introduction into philosophy, he made it extremely engaging and easy to understand, and he's a really funny and enthusiastic lecturer! Grade is dependent on 2 midterms and a final + section participation, but you get the questions beforehand! 100% would recommend!!

John Campbell is a funny lecturer who was so enthusiastic about concepts that it was contagious. However, my experience with Philosophy 3 was mixed because it's graded by two papers and a final, and I didn't know my grades for any of them until they went out on transcripts. It will take a while to wrap your head around the (interesting) readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Grading completely depends upon GSI. Grades revolve around 2 essays, discussion attendance, and one final. Professor is charismatic, engaging, and very knowledgable. Every class is intensely interesting because of his teaching style and enthusiasm for the material.

Such a sweet old man, always excited for class, you can tell his passion. Class is graded on the midterm, 2 papers, a final exam, random discussion posts and attendance in discussion. Easily doable but since the readings are so philosophical you will need time outside of class/discussion to teach yourself the concept fully to write a paper on it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Cannot recommend enough! Such a fun lecturer with a wonderful accent. Short readings every week (posted online) and lectures aren't required/are uploaded online. But I highly suggest attending, as Campbell often brings jokes and anecdotes. And no cold calls. The grade will be composed of two essays. one final, and participation. Interesting course!

John is a literal sweetheart that answers every question. As a stem person with absolutely no interest in philosophy, this was the best class to take: interesting, few readings, all recorded. Idk why people are saying the GSIs were horrible but Scott's worksheets were very helpful and made studying for the final easy. Loved John and Scott.

I would not recommend this professor. I took this class during Fall 2024, and I always waited a very long time receiving a grade for my assignment back. The professor himself and his GSI team are good resources, but slow graders. Now that it's January 2025 and I'm still waiting for my final grade to be posted on CalCentral. Like SERIOUSLY??

Course is unorganized (basically no syllabus) but lectures make up for it. Readings are manageable and generally entertaining. Course quality depends a lot on GSIs, section participation matters a lot. Final study guide is thorough and prof spends a lot of time going over paper and final prompts.

There are only four things that account for your grade in this class. The class is super unorganized in terms of grading, it's been two weeks into break, and grades are still not published and past the deadline. Three of the four things are not graded yet ???????????

It was an interesting class but the GSI's suck apparently and many other people I talked to said the same. I keep getting notifications for a section that I wasn't even in. It's past the grading deadline and there have been no grades on assignments from two months ago
Very unorganized, horrible gsis, was a tough grader
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor He has so much passion for his subject and profession. He's respectful of others perspectives and opinions, always willing to answer questions. He records his lectures and assigns weekly readings, which he explains thoroughly in class. Each Wednesday, he posts a question for participation, gives study-guide of what the final is abt.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: John is one of the best professors at Cal. He's a brilliant person, always willing to help, and his class is one of the most interesting and easiest. I would definitely take it again. The grade is based on 2 essays, the final final, and, of course, participation in section. Scott Blomgren is one of the best GSI on John's teaching team.

ABSOLUTELY LOVED THIS CLASS! full of fun facts about the mind/brain, consciousness. lots of readings assigned, but he clearly goes over them in lecture and is always open to questions, will clearly answer them. papers for finals, midterms were easy (online, open note). even discussion for this class is fire af because content is that good!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Super fun professor, jolly and makes the material engaging. Does a great job of highlighting the nuance and difficulty in studying the mindl. Highly recommend this class under him.

John is a genuinely kind, warm person--I loved attending lecture because he always made them fun (his Scottish accent also makes things easier to listen to). He sometimes veers off course, but he gets the important stuff across. The class itself is graded on 2 essays, an easy online SAQ final, and weekly discussion posts--very reasonable workload!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is a very great person, but his lectures can be very draining most of the time. Discussion sections really helped out with digesting the material, but because it's philo, it still can be quite difficult to understand. Overall, not a bad class, but I had no idea what was going on in that class 90% of the time. Find good people to study with.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof Campbell's lectures are so enjoyable. He is such a jolly man and his Scottish accent makes everything better. Makes me laugh every lecture. The content doesn't really make much sense (that might just b/c it's philos). But, there aren't many assignments so you don't need to have a great understanding. Plus the GSIs help you get the basic pts.
I absolutely loved taking Philos 3. The professor was wonderful and my GSI was also great!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Campbell's lectures can be confusing at times, however, he spends lecture time on discussing the material further if the class is still confused or doesn't understand. He really cares for his student and tries his best for every student to understand the material. He is very helpful in OH and will meet outside of his OH as well. Good Choice.

Professor Campbell has a deep wealth of knowledge but is also incredibly humble! I probably learned just as much dialoguing with him during his office hours as I learned in lectures. You can tell that he genuinely enjoys thoughtfully discussing content from the class. However, as in most other courses, your grade will largely depend on your GSI.

Professor Campbell is phenomenal. His lectures are extremely engaging, he's smart, witty, and very accessible, and is truly passionate about the material. If you put in some effort, you end up with an A, and he's always ready to meet with you and provide detailed feedback about assignments. He also has a contagious laugh and makes classes v lively!

With a new grading/assignment system, many people hated him, but if you reached out to him, he was always there to help. He is now one of my favorite teachers! He would reply to my emails and meet with me day -of to look over my work to make sure they were good and provide feedback. Amazing!!

Campbell is an amazing lecturer but class was very hard to keep up with. The 1.5 hour lectures were discussion heavy with your peers--he will cold call on you, too. I felt like lecture was way too intense in that regard and the material itself was very difficult to understand on the spot. The key to me doing well in this class was recording lecture
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof. encourages students to participate as lecture is often a discussion. This discussion took time to get used to. Discussion focused around biweekly handouts. I strongly encourage you to record lecture and re-listen to them when you have time as content is challenging. Readings, while difficult, only need to be done on the 3 essays assigned.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great guy! Super friendly, funny, and approachable. He's always willing to explain his ideas and debate with his students. As long as you meet your GSI's grading criteria, getting a good grade should be pretty easy. Thoroughly read whichever readings interest you and/or whichever readings you need to write your papers on and you're set.

I fell asleep a lot in his lectures, but when I was awake, he was great! I got an A and I read a total of about 7 of the readings (there are 2-3 a week). I wish I would have taken better lecture notes because he pretty much tells you the answers to the essay prompts. There were two essays and one in-class short essays final.

Textbook is needed if you choose to do the readings. You do not have to attend lecture. He posts the slides online. He goes off on random tangents but is usually entertaining. The papers are graded pretty tough, so if you do not know how to write philosophy papers, it may be difficult. The GSI's are very helpful though.
Hilarious, concise, witty, thoughtful. I'm a graduating senior and yet found Professor Campbell to be the best lecturer I've ever had at Cal throughout my 4 years.
Beautiful lectures, beautiful man
The best professor teach the best subject matter. So approachable, kind, and funny. I literally cannot think of one bad thing to say about him or the class. It's mind blowing. Get it ;)

Amazing professor! Lectures were very entertaining, as well as highly thought-provoking. If you go to his OH he is seriously the nicest guy, takes his time to talk to you and discuss your questions. I was exposed to so many questions I'd never even considered. And on top of all of that, such an easy class. I wish I could have him every semester!

Professor Campbell is absolutely brilliant (and hilarious). The lectures are fascinating, and the class is fairly easy. The only things formally graded are papers and the final (he gives a study guide), so going to section isn't necessary, but I did just because it was so interesting! Philosophy major or not, this class is definitely worth taking.

Professor Campbell does an awesome job in clarifying the readings. Philosophy readings are definitely different from novels; it requires much more focus, time, and effort. But honestly, if you enjoy thinking deeply about all the philosophy material, you'll enjoy this class. If you're whatever about them, well, at least you won't hate them :)
The best professor I have ever had. You can count on laughing every class

amazing sense of (rather self-deprecating) humor; very witty and extremely intelligent with a completely good-natured air (not pretentious or self-important at all). very responsive to student questions. god, i wish i could have him as a professor every semester!

He is a brilliant, funny and likable professor that clearly loves his subject. His lectures are great-I never missed one. He teaches with a wonderful sense of humor, and seems to really care about students and generating real understanding. He can be inscrutable, cloaking in mystery some deep questions and his own actual beliefs. A great professor.

The most interesting professor I've had so far at Berkeley. Go to his lectures! He's very responsive to questions. (so much that it gets a little annoying to listen to all the questions asked during lecture) The grade is 2 essays and 1 final. Make sure to talk to your GSI if you've never written a philosophy paper before.
Intellectual man with the greatest expressions.  Go to class, take notes, talk to your GSI.  Not a hard class about an interesting but a rather obscure topic.

A brilliant and engaging Prof. who makes use of analogies and humor to teach in a fun and entertaining way.  His mild Scottish accent is a nice change and his passion for the topic is infectious.  I will take anything he teaches.
The perfect philosophy professor to have first thing in the morning!

Amazing teacher. My first philosophy class ever but it felt like he and the helpful GSI's eased me into this new field seamlessly. Very intellectual and not pretentious at all. Do the reading because you are interested and not for the grade and you will do fine. Overall, I totally loved this class and recommend it highly. Peace!

Very passionate about his subject, teaches very well, but if you want to do well in this course you're going to have to go to lecture. Discussion is important, but useless if you have a bad GSI. Midterms/final are essays and are graded by the GSI, just an FYI. USE HIS OFFICE HOURS. He is extraordinarily helpful then and open to all questions.

Great, fun professor.  An interesting class if you like the subject.  Personally, philosophy was hard for me to understand. I don't think you can "learn" philosophy, you have to be able to think abstractedly already.  It's possible to write papers off of powerpoints and email GSI's.

Overall, a great, funny professor with a great personality. However, sometimes I felt like he was oversimplifying the material, thus changing what the authors of certain articles were really trying to say; I would have to read the text to really understand. Also, watch out for unfair grading by GSI's. Final was really easy though, and Campbell is l

Absolutely amazing professor. He is an amazing lecturer who encourages questions and answers them completely and with a smile. Quirky is a good way to describe him, his Scottish accent is clutch. Material is a bit tough, but he explains it perfectly in lecture.

Excellent lecturer! Reading almost optional because lectures are so clear. Very receptive to student questions and comments. Take this class it will make you think and the work is manageable. If you are going to take a philosophy this is it, the professor is one of the best teachers I've had.

Campbell has a great sense of humor and his lectures are illuminating and entertaining. This was the first philosophy class I've taken at Berkeley, so it was a little intimidating but this was a really great course and I'd recommend it to anyone!

Sensitive to students, very approachable, humble, great humor. Cool, understandable Scottish accent. A great lecturer. Uses powerpoint (makes available), completely on-topic. Lecture content is organized in a semi-stream-of-thought way; the understanding is in his presentation, not the slides alone, so go to class. Rel. short reader only. Recommend

One of my favorite courses and favorite professors. Best lower div class around next to Fillapenko's Astro C10. Fascinating material, amazing lecturer. Brilliant with a great sense of humor. Highly recommended.

After four years at Cal, I can say that he's one of the best professors I've ever had!  You can tell he loves teaching.  Absolutely fabulous lectures.  He keeps you awake through hard material with quirky comments and his great sense of humor.  I recommend Campbell to anyone who's even thought about taking philosophy.

I love that he takes time out of his lecture to clarify any questions students have.  Lectures can be a bit hard to follow at times because he digresses but the GSI's make up for that.  His accent is very interesting but distracting as well.  Unique!
very nice, funny guy, cute accent. helpful both in and outside of class

Campbell is more than amazing.  He seems to really care about students.  He is always helpful and never condescending.  The material is difficult but facinating. He actually cares what students think and seems to value feedback as to whether or not he is conveying the material in a valuable, clear manner.
Campbell is the best prof I've had at Berkeley. He has this amazing enthusiasm and clarity that he lends to a pretty obscure topic. Certainly a paradigm of a good teacher.
Presents very difficult material in a clear and accessable way. He's very nurturing of his students which is a very rare thing to find at this school. Great in office hours.

J. J. Campbell!  Ah yes... Sweet man, very brilliant, clear lecturer.  Very helpful outside class!  I got a bad GSI who was a tough grader, but still enjoyed the class.  See if you can catch Campbell wandering aimlessly around campus with his big headphones on (classical music?)  Dresses nicely, but wears the same pair of pants everyday (yuck.)
Easy smile, first a foremost.  He is really concerned with the student's comprehension and he keeps it all lighthearted.

One of the best teachers I've ever had.  He makes everything clear and fascinating at the same time.  I found the class easy, but only because he got me so interested in the material.  He's also got a great sense of humor.  Highly recommended.

The reading may be tough at times, but overall the reading load is light and managable. Campbell does a good job of covering the material from the reading in class and his Scottish accent does help to make things more interesting! Lectures may seem long if you're not interested in others' questions.

Cutest Scottish professorly man you will ever see. Great explainer. The reading is interesting but confusingly written; Campbell will help break it down for you and then it becomes easier to break it down for yourself. Funny Scottish expressions. Encourages/tolerates questions of all kinds,accesible

Amazing teacher!  Extremely clear and concise in his lectures, yet also has a wonderful sense of humor and lighthearted nature.  I talked with him after class one time for some clarification, and we ended up talking for 20 minutes or so.  He's wonderful.

You can tell he cares about teaching; his lectures are amazing, and he can convey difficult concepts into simpler terms that are easy to understand. The design of the class in on another level, I really loved the course pack.

He is a nice and funny professor, but the midterms are extremely hard. You are like 8 complex math questions, but only 50 mins to solve. which you don't really have any time to solve the questions. throughly at all. 

Course pack each topic have around 25 questions to practice, each of them takes 30 mins to 1 hour to learn. IMPOSSIBLE TO GO THROUGH

Great storyteller and lecturer. Cool shoes and Scottish accent as well. Class was not difficult, final exam is an essay but the qualitative thinking aspect actually makes u absorb the material better imo. Would recommend this dude to literally anyone. This class made me want to be an econ major, taking 100A with him rn!
jim is an amazing lecturer. material was just really dense

I LOVE Jim. Took him for Econ 1 and 100a—very straightforward professor. Lectures are mostly a review of the course pack, but they are pretty helpful. To do well on midterms, you must do most course pack problems. Final is a normative essay, not too much cramming needed, which I appreciated.

Overall a good professor, his class is very straightforward. He gives the materials you need to succeed in the class, such as the coursepack, practice midterms/finals. It all just depends how much work you put into the class. I didn't put in as much effort in this class due to another class i had, but if you study the coursepack you will be fine.

Campbell is such a fun professor. His lectures were so funny and even relatable, it was so refreshing to see someone who didn't present stuff in the same boring way. His course pack quite literally has everything you need to succeed in the class, so make sure to put some time into it.

LOVE LOVE LOVE Campbell. Took his Econ 1 class and now his Econ 100A as well. Incredibly straightforward, provides you with all the materials you need to succeed (course pack), and his lectures are interesting and effective. Go to lecture, take notes, do the practice problems in the course pack, and you'll end up with the grade you want.
