Jim is an incredible all around teacher who cares about his students and it shows. Course pack is a path to success in his courses. Do the problems and you will succeed. GSI teams are organized and sections are useful, though I skipped most of them. Final is essay. He also plays some niche edm pulls if you show up before class (four tet alt, etc)

My fav professor!! Showing up to class was always worthwhile. I really enjoyed both Econ 1 and 100A because of Jim's entertaining yet highly effective lectures. He does go on the occasional ramble but even those are interesting to hear. Exams test students' ability to think critically using course concepts; he truly cares about teaching economics.
I LOVE JIM! Super inspirational and clearly loves what he teaches and makes it super interesting. You do have to lock in for this class, but it is not too bad.

Jim is one of the best pure educators on campus. You can tell he cares about teaching and gives his students a blueprint for success via course pack. Lectures are engaging and memorable (found myself regurgitating lecture bits on exams and course pack problems). There's a reason why ugba kids opt to take 100A with him instead of the ugba version.
An amazing prof who desires to help his students succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: cool man. show up + do course pack = 36/40 on midterm. i did fall asleep a few times but tbf it is econ 1...hard to be enthusiastic (or conscious) for the lectures sometimes. other than that, i think he really tries to make econ understandable. pretty easy course, also i think he likes pinball...his course pack has many pinball questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is sweet, lecture is clear, he keeps it entertaining. Honestly one of the only lecturers I have trully enjoyed. However, the structure of the class is really poor. Midterms and PS are quantitative, yet the final is essays. It doesnt reflect at all what you learn in the year. Asks you to go on philosophical rants like Smith or Hobbes. Thumbs up.
He keeps the lecture entertaining, everything is good, but the three-exam policy is annoying.

The only thing is that there are 3 midterms which makes this class a little stressful, but the exams were pretty fair. You get one drop as well. He is a pretty good lecturer and I liked that the final exam style is essays rather than MCQs

took this class online over the summer--one midterm and final and both are in person which I think is fair. as long as you spam course pack Qs and visit OHs for further clarification you'll be fine. both prof and GSIs are very willing to help. only thing i found annoying was at least one topic in each exam werent covered in lecture or course pack
Awesome Prof. He genuinely cares about his students. He also has great and interesting insights academically.

his econ1 class is so lit. hes a v good lecturer and entertaining too. as long as you go to lecture, participate in discussion and do the course pack problems its an ezy A. professor campbell's grading system is super clear and is made to help you. if you have some econ knowledge before this class will be chill
The classes are engaging, and it definitely helps if you go to lecture. Having 3 midterms is a bit annoying, but the lowest one is dropped and the final is an essay so it evens out in the end.
He's a nice dude, his lectures were interesting. Exams were fair and the final was straightforward.
He's a good professor, I honestly wish his lectures were a tad faster because sometimes he goes on the same point for too long. But a good teacher overall.

An amazing professor all around. He's funny and very engaging. I recommend going to lectures even though it's not mandatory. You definitely need to study for exams to get an A. Exams focus on understanding rather than memorization. Taking this class actually made me like economics. If you put in the work, it's an easy A.

3 midterms, lowest score is dropped. he brought down the grade cutoffs so thats how I was able to get an A at a 91.83%. genuinely a funny and sexy guy - god I love the Irish. make sure to do all the reading responses and practice essay assignments - it can be the difference between an A and a B. He does not round! Not an econ major but it was fun!!

Campbell's lectures were very interesting and I learned so much in his class. Do the course pack and go to the lectures, and you'll be fine. Great guy wished I had the time to get to know him better and go to office hours.

Best prof I've had at Cal, very passionate about the subject & lectures are interesting, some simple math. Weekly readings that can be interesting & make sure to participate in discussion, that's how I learned the most. Midterms are short but not too bad (lec & course pack problems). Final: in-person essays. Worldly applications, Recommend!

An amazing lecturer and just a solid guy in general. His lectures are very applicable to the real world rather than spitting out word problems without context. Although his lectures are captivating, they do not help you with the midterms, just jam all the course pack problems and you should be okay.

Jim is one of those genuine teachers at Berkeley who puts every effort for his students to understand concepts. Kind, conscientious, and compassionate he reminded of my high school teacher who got me interested in Econ. Thank you for helping me find that joy in learning 🙏🙏.

Great guy, really makes himself accessible to students, even in a class of 500+ kids. BE WARNED: midterms are extremely concept-heavy. I studied like crazy for all of them and only got an A on 1. Final exam (2 essays in 2 hours) will carry your grade + he changes grading bins. Definitely a challenging class that will test you, so put in the work.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: An incredible and insightful lecturer but the lecture content doesn't pertain to the midterms. Do course pack to prep for midterms. Midterms are conceptual, and difficult, but I found them to be graded generously. Final is easy. Lectures are recorded and available online.

Really loved Campbell's intro to econ! His course is extremely organized and he lays out everything you need to succeed at the start of the semester. Use his course pack – I got more than 90% on every exam just be doing the exercises of the weeks included in each midterm. He gives great lectures and the courses is a great survey of econ @ Berkeley!

This is NOT an easy class, but there's a lot of opportunities to boost your grade + it's curved. Lectures aren't really too helpful and I thought this class was too conceptual for me. The coursepack is helpful, but I found that the practice problems and exams were easier than the actual exams themselves. Go to the SLC and grind the coursepack.

Took his class over the summer as a synchronous, online class. Lectures were interesting but not totally comprehensive, his lecture notes tended to include additional studies/data not mentioned in class. The final (essay and written portion) made up 50% of the grade, but homework assignments (reading responses & presentation) were leniently graded.

A terrible professor all around. The lecture material is not helpful to the questions on the midterms. He asks far too conceptual questions for an intro to economics course. The midterms are also graded extremely unfairly. The course pack questions (same as midterm) has no resources or help in how to answer them in a way that would give full credit
Concept HEAVY. Be sure to understand the underlying reason why for each topic. If you are cramming for midterms, skip lectures and go straight to the coursepack.

I took this course over Zoom during the summer; it was hard to stay engaged in class but I attribute that to the medium more than the professor. He was funny and engaging and did a good job of explaining most concepts, although some were still a little unclear (class moved quickly). Tests are more concept than math heavy.

Jim was amazing! I wholeheartedly recommend his classes. I waived Econ 1 with a HS course, and Jim made 100A fully understandable even though the last time I took econ was a year ago. Do the coursepack and pay attention to more abstract ideas he mentions during class for the essay.

Material was way lighter than past macro/microeconomics classes I've taken. Exams were even easier than the material and extremely straightforward. Also curve is generous because there's a bunch of Haas wannabe bozos in this course that bring the test averages down. If you're even semi-locked in then this course is a free A.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Hardest class I've taken, counting upper divs. Intro class but isn't taught like one. Jim's funny but lectures are absolutely useless and tests are unreasonable. We learn basic concepts and practice the course pack problems on our own, which is fair, but the tests q's are all tricks, exceptions, etc. W/o the curve I wouldn't have gotten an A.

Very caring and knowledgeable guy. This class has a lot of content and moves quickly so it's important to keep up with and understand the course pack as much as possible. Don't wait to cram right before the tests. To be honest, I didn't do great on the midterms but there are some other easy assignments and an easier final to make up for it.

Campbell teaches 100A way differently than Econ 1 -- it's a lot of him doing coursepack problems on the screen and answering questions. That is to say, he is the best lecturer I've ever had and I went to every class. He stays after for up to an hour just to talk with students and is really committed to making sure you learn the content. Great guy.
I love Campbell he is literally the best lecturer of all time.

Prof Campbell is actually the goat. His lectures are very engaging and he's just a funny person. It's clear that he loves what he teaches. He also rounds up grades if you're near a cutoff! Absolute tank.

honestly you dont need to go to lecture just study the course pack +  look at the slides on ur own time/ recordings, then gsi OH. he's a great guy but the lectures dont really cover the complexity of the coursepaoc, since most the stuff you need to write to explain, besides the graph. he's super cool if I known course pack was important id take

Campbell is generally great at explaining key concepts, but he often goes way too slow in lecture. His pace prevents him from covering topics in detail, so you essentially have to teach yourself all the material outside of lecture through his infamous "course pack." Be prepared for his horrid, ear-destroying music taste to bookend lecture times.

GOATED. Never took AP Micro/Macro but I was chilling in this class. Do the course pack and ask Chatgpt to explain you stuff that you don't get - its essential to truly understand everything in the course pack.  Awesome prof, tbh wish he taught all my classes. Spend the time = get the good grade. One hw assignment every other week, lightttttt work

Professor Campbell is one of the best professors I've had at Berkeley. I think everyone, Econ major or not, should take his class. He is unbelievably kind, and he breaks concepts down simply and perfectly. His lectures are very thought provoking and enable you to be creative. I truly developed a love for economics by taking this class.
Love Jim. Best professor ever. Lectures are engaging and relevant. Course pack problems are a great way to use active studying. Genuinely changed the way I think about the world.
Best lecturer, love his abstraction of concepts that makes everything very intuitive

Jim is a spectacular lecturer who has very interesting classes. However, (like other people reviewed) the lectures sometimes don't completely pertain to the midterms, so it's important to always keep up with the packet. It's a great introduction to economics though!

Econ 100A is a tough course, but Jim makes lectures fun and engaging. Material is tough, and midterms are quite difficult, but this is compensated by easy final. Jim genuinely cares about his students and is a great professor to learn from
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lectures are really interesting and inspirational. However, the lectures do nothing to prepare you for the midterm exams. He recommends doing previous exam questions from his course pack to study, but every one of the three exams in the fall 2023 semester had curve-ball questions that didn't resemble any of the course pack questions.

study the course pack and make sure to really understand the answers!! not a class you want to fall behind in. lectures are hard to follow, kind of useless. midterms are tough (there are 3), and final is an essay, which helps round out your grade. nice and funny guy
Engaging lecturer, challenging exams. Lectures and readings largely focus on the mechanics of economic models, while exams are geared towards conceptual/mathematical understandings.

Class is made up of: homework assignments, discussion presentation, midterms, and final. No attendance for lectures or discussions, however I would recommend going. Professor is passionate and very helpful/good at teaching material clearly. Some busy work assignments. 3 Total midterms similar to practice problems, and an in-class essay final.

Super down-to-earth dude. Well-organized class and clear presentation of course topics. Prof is usually more than willing to help you out outside of class as long as you ask for it. Amazing guy overall, an awesome introduction to Berkeley. You can really tell that he has a passion for teaching.
Drippiest professor at Cal and all-around great guy. Love that he makes econ approachable and fun. Also tells funny stories, and has an epic sneaker collection.
Don't really need to go to class
He round up my class score from b+ to a-

lectures are okay, but focus too much on problems instead of concepts. Midterms are COMPLETELY different from the practice midterms, don't be fooled. Like why do you test this hard and different for midterms LOL especially your final is completely different, which is just writing essays. You prepare ten hours for midterms and just forget right away

Amazing lectures and if you go to section the material is very easy to understand. Generally a very fair grader and communicates very clearly about grades and what he is expecting for exams and assignments. He's also just a great guy in general

jim is an incredible lecturer, this was one of my favorite classes at cal and i can't wait to take 100A with him next semester. there is no homework, just biweekly papers and a presentation. my midterm scores were about 70-80%, this is without much studying. do the coursepack and you will do fine! the final exam is writing 2 essays on the spot.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Although he is a funny and passionate guy, this has been by far my least favorite class at Cal. I am bad at econ however I tried extremely hard on the midterms and he purposefully graded me harshly. I truly believe that they are trying to do bad. Would not recommend it unless you need to take the class.
Great lecturer and professor, just a strict and harsh grader tbh.

Professor Campbell was great and so so good at teaching. You either get econ or you have no idea what you're doing half of the time. I was the latter. He was an awesome prof, I just absolutely suck at econ.
BOO!
Interesting lectures, exams similar to the practise problems

Campbell's preparation, such as the course pack he assigns, are great to helping one understand the content of the class. In lecture, he goes over concepts slowly in an easy-to-digest manner. The key to succeeding in this class is to do the course pack problems ahead of the midterms. The final is easy, the mean was a 90% (just two written essays).

its not a class you can just cram last minute for but hes rly good at explaining concepts and his lectures and the course pack are rly relevant to exams. hes funny and relatable and clearly very well versed in and passionate about economics

A wonderful man. Infectious enthusiasm. Lectures were all practice problems, which was a little strange structurally, but overall very useful to jump into example questions right away. Loved that he integrated reading responses into the course. Very in-touch w students and what's happening in modern microeconomics. Highly highly recommend.
Best teacher at Cal.

I'm a public health major and this will probably be the only econ class I ever take but it was so fun. I really enjoyed Jim's lectures and I feel that he's an awesome person overall and he actually cares about the society and our future
I took his class first semester, and it's what convinced me to be an Econ major. He makes everything super interesting, and he's pretty lenient with grading.
really good at teaching for sure

I respect other students liking this type of teaching, studying by themselves and then getting tested. 

I personally really don't like these type of classes. This class was mostly about learning bymyself and the lectures were just solving homework sets. 

I rather prefer a proper lecture format. I really cannot get motivated.
Best professor at Cal
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: You will know what to expect in exams if you study the packet. The packet of practice problems will be your best friend. Same questions, different answers type questions. Very engaging and energetic. SUPER excited about the subject. Final exam is fairly easy- write a couple essays from a list of prompts.

Campbell made my freshman year the best. Econ 1a material is honestly light coming from AP econ, but his teaching style covers the game theory and broader implications of the basic material. The lectures are absolutely worth attending in-person. I decided to fit extra econ classes into my schedule just to take more classes from him.

He is humble given how scarily smart he is. The reading response and essay format really align with the course objectives. It would have been easier for me to follow if there was either a traditional lecture format or regular p-sets. There are 3 midterms, 4 reading responses, a presentation, and a sample final + final, but he has a clear rubric.
Jim was a great professor. His lectures are enjoyable and informational. Midterms and finals are very reasonable and allows for students to display how they interact with the lecture material.

Professor Campbell's lectures are great, though it may take a second watch to fully understand. He is also so understanding and was the most accommodating professor during the UAW strike this semester. His final was essay based, while his midterms were more of the stereotypical test structure. All in all, great dude, great professor.

Professor Campbell keeps all of his lectures interesting and actually applicable towards the real world. This class involves biweekly reading responses, 3 midterms (no drops), and a final. You have to do 1 presentation with a partner in the discussion section. Overall this class is a great intro to economy and the Professor is always enjoyable.
Jim is a great prof who truly cares about his students. This policies due to the strike were extremely generous and shows how he prioritizes our learning above all else.

Jim is nice, funny, and loves teaching, which makes lectures bomb. He's young but so so intelligent, it's scary. This makes midterms and the final essay difficult because he knows how to make you think and apply. The rest of your grade is completely GSI-dependent so shop around and find a good one.
Fire professor, Campbell is so engaging and interesting to listen to, he's still very young and knows how to connect well with students

Literally hands down the best professor I've ever had. He is so passionate about what he is teaching and made me passionate about Economics again. He always encourages his students to challenge the current state of society and tries to plan his course to best support his students in doing so. Would highly recommend!

Super nice and fair professor who handled the strike very well. However, I do not think he is the best lecturer and although lectures are somewhat interesting, he leaves all test material to the GSIs. I like how the course is laid out but feel he could better prepare students and made my econ 1 experience quite difficult.

Use the course pack. The course pack that he posts will save your understanding and save your grade. Lecture attendance and discussion attendance were not necessary, keeping up with the material is essential.

This man single-handedly revived my love for Econ. He truly cares for his students and not only lectures amazingly but will drill these concepts into you without you knowing. Assignments and presentations are lightweight, grades exams pretty fairly, wish he taught more classes. By far my favorite professor.

Midterms every 3 weeks get annoying, especially considering the unclear grading criteria. On our last midterm, the class got a mean of 70%. WELL, I GUESS STUDENTS CAN BE ONLY AS GOOD AS THEIR TEACHER... Used to like Econ before him :(
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Midterms almost every 3 weeks - workload can get exhaustive if you fall behind in lecture content. Exams are graded arbitrarily and literally based on how the grader 'feels'. Sometimes the midterms can have really randomly hard questions not reflected in practice problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Genuinely enjoyable human
This teacher makes it fun to learn!

The lectures were VERY content heavy, if you spaced out during a lecture it was difficult to keep up, but he explained the concepts really well and the practice exam and final questions were pretty accurate to the actual exams. The exams were pretty difficult, but I enjoyed the class nonetheless.

Prof is awesome! Highly recommend. Lectures are easy to follow and he is good at answering questions. Be careful: do not underestimate the midterms. They are difficult if you show up overconfident. You can do well if you pay attention and study carefully. Shoutout to the SLC for getting my anime comeback in this class
Professor Campbell is very straightforward. Doing well in the class is easy if you attend lectures, discussions, and study the course pack.
Very nice person and loves to interact with students. Can be a little confusing at times but will clarify if asked during office hours.

Lectures deviate a lot from the slides so it can be difficult to review. Lectures consist of a lot of visuals and real world examples but lack in definitions. Make sure you understand foundational concepts or else you will be lost because he moves quickly. 3 midterms and an essay final which is graded super easy (mean of 88.6%).
Professor Campbell is the best professor I've had at Cal. I highly recommend going to lecture (he's really good at explaining concepts!) and doing the course pack problems. Definitely take his class!

Campbell lectures were awesome. He will stop during lecture to clarify any points that were confusing. Weekly writing assignments and one presentation were both easy. The questions on the exams were similar to his course pack, though he likes to throw a curveball sometimes. He offered a remote option for finals if you got CoVid during finals week.

Campbell is one of the reasons that I am majoring in Economics. I had him for both Econ 1 & 100A, and his lectures are super engaging. Both classes are doable and the exams are fair. I am not a big fan of the Final Exam format (it's 2 essays), but overall, both classes were really fun and interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great professor who actually explained the concepts well and made the class fun
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: One of the best economics professor at Berkeley. His lectures are truly inspirational. Not boring at all. More like a performance! We got to solves the questions together. Hopefully you'll enjoy his lectures as much as I do!

He is a very kind professor, I really enjoyed going to his lectures, plus his accent is nice to listen to lol. Always has fun stories and teaches well. The class is mostly dependent on the GSI tbh, luckily mine was amazing, he's very accessible outside of class even though we had around 600 students. Midterms are a bit difficult but I recommend.

Great lectures, very engaging in class, presents source material relatively accurately, though at times I needed the discussions to clarify it. Not much homework, just a presentation and reading responses which are hard to fail. Mostly graded on 3 midterms and a final, which are easy to prepare for and accurately reflect what is taught. Good prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Campbell is a very fair professor. 1 assignment every week with clear instructions, and 3 midterms. He tries to connect with students during lectures. His exams are quite difficult, and not similar to the course pack provided.

Professor Jim has a very organized format for the class and will always include a joke in his lectures. There are three midterms, but if you look at the coursepack he provides then midterms are pretty easy.

Such a good and captivating speaker. Super reasonable with the content he tests. If you do all the coursepack problems and actually understand the ins and outs, you will do well. Really accommodating with extensions and just overall a good guy!

I LOVE professor Campbell. His lectures are very entertaining and he manages to connect concepts in class to outside material/news often to show the impact of learning economics. He cracks a lot of jokes in class and makes it a fun time for everyone. He has also been the most accommodating professor with DSP!

This class was great and fairly easy although I did have some background in econ. The course pack is your best friend! The midterms are basically the same structure as the course pack and it is a great way to study.
Very simple guidelines to pass class, 5 quizzes and a final essay. Gives solutions to quizzes afterwards as well as past quizzes and practice problems. Put in the work and an A will be easy!
Very good lecturer and person, made economics very interesting

Jim is like a friend to us. His lectures are interesting and he explains concepts clearly. He motivates us to think like real economists rather than students who only pursue good grades. However, admittedly, this class is pretty hard for people that are not super familiar with Econ.

His class is chill and his lecture notes are VERY WELL WRITTEN. I got a 88% only because I was nearly not putting in any effort (due to two other really hard classes I was taking). I did not watch any lectures and barely went to discussions, only read over the lecture slides 3 hours before each midterm. Midterms and final are essay/SAQ based.

Prof Campbell was really engaging throughout his lectures and made sure to tie in the concepts we were learning with the real world. Graded mainly off of 3 midterms and 1 final, I'd recommend one to study a fair amount of practice problems (provided by the prof) before each test  as performing poorly on one can really tank your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This was the best course I've ever taken at Cal. Even with the flaws of his class (sometimes too subjective grading in quizzes, occasional disorganization), he at least tries to be as fair as he can. I learned a LOT from watching his lectures, and I did it all asynchronously. I told him at the end he was the best professor I had. Take him!

had him summer 2020. good lecturer & funny guy but not much beyond that. problem sets were worth the majority of the grade & very difficult. said he would lessen their weight but never did. didnt like how he made it sound like he was sympathetic to students bc of the pandemic and political climate but didnt bother making the class any easier.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class was so much fun! Jim is an amazing, caring, and thoughtful professor. Most importantly, he knows what he's doing. He's great at lecturing and engaging his students, even with an online class. That said, be sure to put in extra work if you want anything above a B. Go to office hours, ask questions and you should be fine.

He's genuinely passionate about econ and wants you to learn. His lectures are SUPER helpful. I didn't have any prior experience whatsoever in econ, but his exams are straightforward. Just re-watch his lectures and do the coursepack problems! Coursepack probs. are just like the real exams. There's also a textbook but IMO don't bother. Take him :)

The material itself is not too difficult, but the class grades WAY TOO HARSHLY. They give very limited time for Quizzes and expect intensely elaborate explanations for all of your answers and if you don't, they would take several percents off even if your answer is correct. There is no rubric either, they just grade based on what they feel "enough"

Professor Campbell is a wonderful lecturer who always throws something in to keep your attention. Hes a very inspirational speaker who wants you to form your own opinions and wont tell you what you should think. He lays excellent groundwork for economics I would highly recommend!

His lectures are super helpful. The only thing I did was watching the lecture recordings before each quiz, and I got near full scores on all quizzes. Simply master his lectures and the class becomes easy.

Professor Campbell explains things clearly and is a very amusing professor. He teaches unconventionally, not using a textbook or traditional lectures and instead opting to teach through practice problems (and he provides a good variety of these). Importantly, for his quizzes, there will be curveballs so it is important to understand the concepts.

Probably the worst lecturer or teacher I've ever had. Completely unclear and annoying teaching style that is all over the place and difficult to follow. He refuses to deliver the content in a straightforward way and insists on haphazardly teaching through example problems, making the actual concepts difficult to understand. Really really bad.

Professor Campbell is a nice person. He is genuinely passionate about what he teaches. However, he breezes through his lectures and is a very tough grader. It may be because I don't have prior experience with econ. but this being an introductory course/pre-req course.. wow.. The average for our most recent midterm was 20/30 (66.67%).
I really loved Professor Campbell. I had him for Econ 1 and Econ 100A and he makes economics so interesting. His tests are definetly a bit tricky but he is also super helpful if you go to OH.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Jim is extremely passionate about econ and yes his quizzes may be tricky, however he really cares about preparing us. He provides all the resources to succeed in the class and has literally handcrafted hundreds of problems to prepare us for quizzes. He genuinely cares a lot and you can see that as he makes himself very available for any questions.
Great prof! Teaches really well!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Caring

reviews.comment: great guy, lectures are easy to understand and is always available for extra help during office hours

Incredibly AWFUL at lecturing. He's pretending to be so chill and act all bro with his students by skipping through important math and explanations regarding more complex concepts. You will not learn A THING (at least anything advance) by going to his lectures.

Pretty good lecturer, but he goes through content very quickly. His lectures are fun and he spends a lot of time explaining the real-life applications of the lecture concepts. His office hours are very helpful for homework/quiz help. The quizzes themselves are not super difficult, but you have to be able to write a lot very quickly.

Campbell is definitely a tough professor who makes you put in the work to succeed, but words cannot describe how nice and genuine he is. He really cares about his students and the content he is teaching and he always makes himself accessible outside of class to his students. He's a visiting professor, so be sure to take a class with him soon!

One of the worst professor to ever be employed by the university. I do not question his education or research, but I have always been questioning his teaching methods. Takes ages to mark homework, curve grades up and down throughout the semester, and extremely anti-capitalism, which I find ironic since he's a naturalised US citizen...
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: An amazing and passionate professor. Great at putting complex topics into simple terms. Tests were straightforward and very similar to previous exams he gave out as practice. Go to office hours if you can because he is genuinely a caring and understanding person. Certainly a strong choice for someone who has little experience with economics.

Clearly a very passionate prof, cares a lot about not just teaching exam material but also about why the material matters and its real world applications. Lectures are clear and understandable, if a bit fast. One con is that his grading criteria was not very clear, and it was not always easy to understand what made an answer good vs just okay.

He assigns very time-constrained quizzes that are worth 45% of your grade, and he loves to be tricky. He doesn't really explain or contextualize anything during lectures and prefers to solve problems at glacial speeds in lieu of actually teaching the material. I wish I had been able to choose either Carson or Olney, who are superior lecturers.
Professor Campbell is charming, engaging, and a very talented lecturer. I never liked economics but I loved his class! Very wholesome vibes.
Overall really great teaching. Lecture material was generally very clear and motivated. I found that despite the fast pace of the course, I was able to get a good grasp of all the material covered.

By the time this professor and his crew of GSIs successfully graded all our quizzes and midterms, Japan would be under the ocean, the United States would have its 100th president, and China would be at war with India. In other words, this guy takes ages to mark a single homework. Truly disappointing. Oh, and somehow this guy hates free market.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I love Professor Campbell as a person and think he's a nice guy. That being said, the structure of this class is absolutely ridiculous. The GSIs in this class take off so many points without explanation and just make up their own grading rubrics. Quizzes are 45% of the grade and even a couple of points can drop your grade an entire letter grade.

One of the best professors and lecturers at Cal. Professor Campbell is incredibly caring, down-to-earth, knowledgeable, and downright hilarious. Quizzes are challenging but reasonable, all the economic concepts covered are interesting and useful, and all of his lectures are funny, enjoyable, engaging, and super relatable. Can't recommend enough!

He gives lecture in a speed of words that makes you feel your brain is working like an engine. He doesn't give us a textbook but he uses a coursepack to make everything clear and neat. I'm curious about how he just runs through some examples to illustrate all the concepts you need to know for the quiz. My favorate professor.

Campbell is sweet, funny, and genuinely cares about his students and the impact he makes. His lectures are entertaining and interesting, and he is very accessible/ happy to answer questions. That said, he gets off topic very easily which can be detrimental since there are less than 2 hrs/wk of lecture. Show up, do the work, and you should get an A.

great guy, really cares about his students + his impact. as long as you put in the work, it is perfectly reasonable for you to do well in the class. if he offered other classes i wouldnt hesitate taking them, probably my favorite professor thus far

Took Econ 1 with him over summer and got an 89.97% but he didn't boost my grade up to an A-. The class was very test heavy and if you failed one test you would probably end up with a C for the whole semester. Might seem like a nice guy but a very tough grader who won't have the empathy to boost you up a bit even if you need the class to declare.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He's a cool guy, but this is definitely a tough class. I kind of wished that my grade wasn't so dependent on 6 rather difficult quizzes that made up 50% of my grade in this class. A quiz drop policy would have been helpful since I did pretty bad on one of the earlier quizzes which pretty much messed up my average for the rest of the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He does not go over concepts at all during lectures. Instead, he makes us watch UCSD videos and do problems in class. He goes over about 1 problem per hour by wasting time on totally irrelevant things. Worst of all, the final gradebin is 3% higher than what he posted before the deadline to change grading options. I am genuinely confused.

Although the grading is a bit tough, Campbell gives you all the resources you need to succeed. Very affable guy and down to Earth; pretty difficult but fair class. Make sure you understand the material before you go into the quiz, as Campbell likes to throw curveballs.

Such a cool and passionate economist! The caveat, of course, is the material: you really have to work for your grade. This class is light on the HW, but don't let that fool you -- you have to read EVERY resource he provides to even get a shot at a good grade. Prepare to dedicate more than the 4 units of work it requires.

Good professor (pretty funny & relatable guy), straightforward lectures. The course pack he created for the semester has all the information you need to do well on the quizzes. However, if you want a deeper understanding of the concepts, watch the virtual/video textbook lectures.

definitely tough to understand conceptually if you don't have any experience with econ coming out of high school; otherwise, prof. Campbell has an amazing personality, explains things effectively, and is very lenient and forgiving in his policies.

I get what he's trying to do in having 6 quizzes as opposed to 2 midterms, but I have never seen my grades suffer like this in classes with the classic midterm set-up. Jim, if you're gonna make quizzes 50%, you need to factor improvement. Would I get a beer with him? In a heartbeat. Would I take his class, again? No.

Prof is a great person and a really nice guy but I would never take him again. Absolutely the hardest class I've ever taken and your grade depends 50% on the quizzes which are EXTREMELY hard. Nothing like you've ever seen before and the material provided is not enough, really feels like you're on your own. He doesn't drop a bad score either, HARSH.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Jim is genuinely one of my favorite professors. I think his quizzes are actually rather straight forward. He explains things in such a way that just watching lectures and doing practice problems before a quiz is enough for me to ace them, and I am by no means an econ whiz. Made me want to double major in econ!

I am currently taking Econ100A with Jim, and it is hard, but really enjoyable. This class is math heavy (not hard, just calc/algebra). Make sure you really UNDERSTAND each topic, as his tests are NOT like practice problems, more applications of your understanding. However, you learn a ton, and he has inspired a love for ECON in me. I RECOMMEND!

Professer Campbell is nice and his lectures are interesting, BUT I WON'T TAKE HIS CLASSES EVER AGAIN. The quizzes are VERY TOUGH and the time limit is EXTREMELY TIGHT. Simply attending his lectures is not enough to get a good score. You have to do plenty of extra work to keep up with the pace. AND THE QUIZZES COUNT 50% TOTAL GRADE. LIKE GEEZ.

I took Econ1 in the summer with no Econ experience and found it pretty straightforward with Campbell. If you understand the concepts and know how to apply them, you won't really need the book and should be good. Campbell is passionate and easy to understand so in terms of lecturer he is a great choice

I really do like Prof. Campbell -- he's young, relatable, and very passionate about what he does. He structures his class in a way that's more theoretical, so he will be difficult if you're a stick-to-the-book type. Quizzes are difficult -- put in the time to really understand the concepts though and you will excel.

Professor Campbell is really nice, but the experience I had in his class with the lengthy assignments, tests, and awful quizzes, I would not take again and would not recommend. It was econ 1 but felt like an upper div. The content was taught in a confusing and difficult way. REALLY tough grader, expect to fail quizzes and be graded harshly.

His GSI's would take off points for not submitting individual pages per question on Gradescope. He grades heavily and doesn't curve the class up. He wouldn't boost up my friend's grade from a B+ (89.9%) to an A-. He also tends to not reply to emails so don't bother emailing him.

Graded on a few problem sets and tests, with some group projects thrown in. Great lecturer, and just generally a nice and chill guy who loves teaching. He doesn't go easy on you though, so put in the time you need to relative to the grade you want.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Misleading attendance policy, forced participation, and busywork assignments.

Prof. Cole was the absolute best!!! She was so kind and genuinely wants her students to learn. She puts in a lot of effort and makes a bunch of time so you can meet with her. I suggest you meet with her 2-4 times for each essay. Choose her as your first option! I learned a lot from her and I would 100% take her class again. 100/10!!
Chisako is a really caring professor. Her critiques make my writing stronger and more developed. I would definitely take another class by her!

She gives amazing feedback and truly cares about helping her students improve. Honestly, I learned far more than I would have expected from an intro to writing class - I genuinely feel like taking her class helped me become a better thinker and writer.
Willing to help out on all your writing and learned new techniques that is easy to learn and is helpful in future assignments.
She taught me about one of my essay as my origional professor went for a therapy. She was really insightful and helped a lot

I took her r1a over the summer. Yes it was a lot of work but if you put the effort in, she will know. She also puts A LOT of effort in as a prof. She gave me so much of her time and I will be forever grateful. It may not reflect in this review but I am a much better writer because of her. If I could take another one of her classes I would. THE BEST

Professor Cole was the best!!! I personally never liked writing and English classes, but she helped me somewhat like it! Her feedback is very crucial and beneficial to make the essay better. If possible, I would recommend going to office hours as much as possible to make the essay better and better.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This is one of the best classes I've taken at Berkeley. The level of personal feedback you get on essays is incredible; sign up for office hours at least twice a week, it'll be worth it. She really cares about each and every student's work, and her advice is deep and pulls out the absolute best. I'd rate 6 stars if I could.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Professor Cole is amazing. She's patient, gives solid feedback, and her generous grading is a bonus. With so many office hours, she's always there to help. Would take her class again, no question.

Chisako is super sweet and caring, one of the most thoughtful professors I think I'll ever have. The in-class activities she assigns are super helpful in completing our projects, and she gives plenty of advice along the way. She also brings in snacks occasionally! Just put the effort in, and make an optional OH meeting and you'll do great!

You can tell she really cares about her students. As long as you get your work done on time, you'll be rewarded for it. The assigned readings and graded essays were not too lengthy, but still challenging. She makes this class fun compared to STEM classes by bringing snacks. If you have Professor Chisako, she genuinely wants you to do well at Cal.

Such an amazing, fair, and kind professor. She cares so much about her students and really wants you to pass and succeed as a writer at Berkeley. She makes you meet with her outside of class, and although it may seem annoying, it is extremely useful. Take her notes and apply them to your essays to ensure your A. She also gave us lots of treats:)
Make sure you show you care and put in effort in essays and writing assignments. Also, try to make meetings for essays to show improvement. Very easy to approach and very nice, highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Norena seems like a very good professor, I simply was extremely bored from the course material. Norena structured the course well, was adaptable to feedback, and gave informative lectures. History 4A is a very surface level course teaching the basics of analyzing sources and creating historical arguments. Good for requirements, but imo, boring.

Norena is incredibly well-spoken and very kind; one of the best professors I've encountered so far and would def take again. The lectures can be really dense with not all info written on the slides so I would try not to skip class. Your grade, however, pretty much depends on how hardcore your GSI is, good luck!

Professor Noreña is so sweet and organized. His lectures were very detailed, and he has a great sense of humor. I strongly recommend taking very detailed notes for both the lectures and the readings since there is a lot of content.

I've realized Ancient Mediterranean history is NOT my thing but Professor Noreña is an amazing professor who is so passionate and knowledgeable about this part of history. His lectures were interesting and I enjoyed certain ones. Also I was fortunate to have an amazing GSI who made the class more enjoyable.

Hes great. He explains really well and is clearly passionate about the topics. The course was awesome and I would highly recommend. The lack of assignments to boost the grade makes this course a sneakily difficult course to get an A in, but you'll do fine. Theres lots of info, but you only need to know the broader pictures.

the prof is literally an angel and one of the most sweetest and well-spoken people ive met here at cal. however, my GSI genuinely sucked sm, no screens & we had to print out all the readings. get lucky w ur gsi bc those 2 hrs sucked the light out of my eyes every week. i repeat, this is not an easy breadth, its a lot of reading and super test heavy
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He was an amazing professor. Many people go on and take his upper Division courses after this one.

He was an amazing lecturer! He was very organized in his presentations and you could follow along really well! Just make sure to take detailed notes as his slides have one or two things on it and he will explain everything else. Lots of readings as well, however, you can kinda get away with not reading them. Depends on the GSI. Take the class!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: HE IS SO AMAZING AND PASSIONATE I WILL MISS THIS COURSE AND HIM SO MUCH

Professor Norena is clearly knowledgeable about Ancient Mediterranean History and his lectures are usually interesting. Your grade is based on participation in discussion, a writing portfolio (in-class essay and term paper), one midterm, and one final. Difficulty depends on your GSI as they grade everything. I recommend this class!

Such an amazing professor! I have never liked history whatsoever but it was always so enjoyable to come to his class. He's a really engaging lecturer and he's clear about outlining the important information needed for exams. AND his fit is always hard. The reading isn't super important, just make sure to come to lecture and take detailed notes.
Great lecturer, very engaging. Lots of reading, but you can get away without reading most of it. 2 essays, 1 midterm, final.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Norena was amazing! He's lectures were very heavy with information but he made it interesting and I enjoyed his sense of humor. Your grade depends on your GSI and for the papers, midterm and final, take very detailed lecture notes. Discussion were long and you have to participate for a good grade. Very reading heavy so plan ahead.

He is a great lecturer! This class is assigned reading heavy, I barely read anything, but I suggest to look ahead into the two essay topics and slowly start your readings to work on the essay- that will be so much easier on time. Your GSI grades all your work. The midterm/final were fine, just take detailed notes in lecture and memorize the terms.

Professor Norena is so passionate and intelligent about history. His lectures were always interesting and respected various opinions. Your grade depends on papers and exams, so study well. Also, there were heavy readings every week that were at times difficult. The 2 hour discussions were tiring, but helpful in understanding readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Norena gives very good lectures, and always has respect for the varying opinions in the field. His positions on topics are well informed, and he loves to give a comprehensive view of the subject matter. Class is graded on a few assignments, so work with your GSI for a decent score. Great class

By far my favorite professor I've had at Berkeley. He is so passionate about his work and he will gladly answer any questions during class. He gives the most interesting lectures out of all the professors I've had at Berkeley. The only thing I did not like was that discussions were 2 hrs long.

His lectures were very engaging and it's obvious that he is extremely knowledgeable and passionate about his work. The class grade is based entirely on papers and essay exams, so if you're a decent writer, it's quite easy to get a high score.

Professor Noreña was such a gem, and was clearly passionate about the subject matter. Lectures were very engaging despite them being 1:20. There were quite a bit of readings, but usually your GSI's would tell you what was important. Midterm and Final could be completed just with detailed lecture knowledge. GSI's were great too.

Prof. Norena manages to make history interesting despite it being a class I thought I was going to fall asleep to most of the time. He is quick witted and makes plenty of jokes during lectures. This class itself is not too hard, just expect to read a bunch. Other than that, I think whether or not you get an A or B, is really dependent on your GSI.

His lectures are informative, entertaining, and easy to follow. Encourages questions and does a great job answering them. He helped restructure the course curriculum and is clearly passionate about the subject. He cares for the students by being very accessible and shifting deadlines to make it easier on us.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Norena is a top-notch professor, somewhat worshiped by Cal History majors. He has a stunning knowledge of Roman History and the ancient world more broadly that he tries to pass on, while still reaching every student at their level. His office hours are an incredible, casual opportunity to explore the topics he teaches in greater depth.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Absolutely incredible, sheer intellectual brilliance coupled with amazing lectures! Clear grading criteria on the essay and final, clearly cares about his students, and made me love History even more. Definitely recommend this class along with 106B.

The loveliest man you'll ever meet. Great sense of humor and made taking classes in the sweltering hot (and very far) North Gate Hall worth it. His lectures are like listening to a documentary! Insanely well articulated (and well dressed). 10/10 would take again - history major here I come.
Seriously he is genius every single time I meet with him during OH he makes me wanna switch to history major just for his class.

Amazing guy. If you're looking for a history class where you'll learn a ton of interesting things and won't fall asleep in lecture, this is the man to look for. There are sizable readings involved, but you can get by. One of my favorite professors - made me want to switch to history!
He is amazing! Such a funny guy. If more people from Pike were like him I would be in a fraternity.

Prof. Norena has very well organized lectures and is very engaging in his presentation of them. There is a lot of reading expected but usually, you can get by if you just take notes during lecture. Test content and grading criteria for tests and papers are very clearly laid out. He's also very good-humored and enthusiastic.

Professor Norena is one of the most intelligent, engaging professors I have had at Cal. Prepare to read a lot, but you should be able to get by if you skip some of them. Incredibly interesting lectures, and fantastic in office hours
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: History 106B with Carlos Norena was the highlight of my year. I had him for History 106B and his enthusiastic, funny, and interesting lectures kept me coming back every day. He is incredibly knowledgable. The readings aren't really necessary to do well in the class, but the lectures are. Tests are all in class essays, with two papers in the year.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof. Norena is the best lecturer I've heard at Cal. His presentations can be very dense with information and most of that is spoken so class is a must. He is very engaging and open to questions outside of class. Best professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Norena is a great professor and a funny guy.

One of my favorite professors at Berkeley. I took his class as a breadth requirement and it has been my favorite class outside of my major by far. Lectures are clear and engaging, he does a good job making them interesting and easy to follow. Very professional. Gladly answers questions. Quite a bit of reading but it never felt without cause.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Norena was great when I took him in Fall 2015. I was a transfer student and starting with his class (which was challenging) made all my other history classes seem a lot easier in comparison. Fantastic lecturer but Prof. Efron (history) is  just as good if not better than Norena. Both are hidden gems.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: He's a great lecturer who can put a lot of important information into that 1.5 hours. He's also very funny and perhaps the most articulate person I have ever met. To do well go to his lectures, take notes and study the book a little. You don't have to do every single reading. Get a good GSI; they grade your papers, participation and quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Norena is a nice guy and knows a bit about most things but he is not a gifted lecturer, he refuses to speak with certainty on much and answers questions for no reason during class that some would see as a godsend but in reality it is just people extrapolating minute time-consuming details or trying to make themselves look intelligent. He's a 1/5.
Such a great guy. His lectures are amazing, and if anything is unclear (unusual), he is very nice in office hours and will make time to explain. Take a class with him if you can!

I took his class because there was an open slot and it was one of the best decisions I've ever made at Cal. The lectures are incredibly interesting and well delivered. They are quite fast and it can be difficult to keep pace, but if you're a decent note taker it's fine, plus Prof. Norena always hangs around after class to answer various questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof. Noreña is undeniably one of the best lecturers at Berkeley. He is very thorough and concise with the info he presents. That being said, classes are densely packed with content and reading is extremely important.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Very entertaning with good sense of humor
An amazing professor. He makes the lectures interesting and clear. I would love to take another class with him.

Professor Norena was an excellent lecturer, probably the best I've had at Berkeley so far. I really wish I didn't have to take it as a class and could take it for fun. However, the lectures were very informative, and he was quite clear on what would be tested. I would definitely take Prof Norena again.

Norena is literally the best professor that I have ever had. His lectures are awesome. Although the class isn't an easy A you can achieve it if you study hard, do the readings, and don't procrastinate too much. Tests/the paper are fair and you know what's expected for an A in advance. I can't recommend 106A and Prof. Norena enough, he is amazing!

He's a great professor! Lectures are very clear and (for the most part) held my interest, though I'm not a history major. Super sweet in office hours - I never felt intimidated because I wasn't clear on the material. The midterm & final are sort of a lot to handle, but expectations are very clear.

Fantastic Professor. I loved every lecture and went to every one. He definitely is an expert on his material, and his lectures are always organized, very thorough, and interesting. He covers through a LOT of information over a short period of time though, so you cannot expect to miss a lecture or dose off in class. Great class and professor.

Such a fantastic professor.  His lectures are dense, but as others have mentioned, he is always clear with the information you are accountable for. But he's not an easy A-for his midterm & final, he gave out around 80 ID's we had to define & only had 5 on the exam. But I totally recommend his classes.

Professor Norena throws a lot of information at you in lecture but he is CRYSTAL clear and always interesting. Every class is so thought-out and organized. His final was a challenge and you can't miss lecture without missing important material but the class was 100% worth it. Take anything he teaches.

Professor Norena's lectures are packed with a lot of details and is very comprehensive. Despite the plethora of dates and people that you need to know, the class is amazing as Norena is funny and articulate just like Cicero. His diction is superb. He uses extended metaphors that relate to physics and biology which captures his points very well.

Absolutely exceptional on every possible scale. One of the most dynamic, engaging, interesting professors I've ever encountered. Inspired me to study ancient history at Berkeley and beyond. So professional - the slicked back hair! Totally adore him.

JUST Amazing professor!! JUST TAKE WHATEVER he teaches. Professor's teaching ability is surely extraordinary and makes you to be really interested. I realized that there can be some error in this site rating, but this guy is REAL!

Professor Norena is THE MOST charismatic, engaging lecturer EVER! I looked forwarded to this class every day (which I'd never done at Berkeley). He was really encouraging and helpful through email or even in person. I loved everything about this class. Lectures were perfectly paced and organized too! I am seriously going to miss this class so much.

This was an absolutely FANTASTIC course. Norena is a really entertaining lecturer who presents the material clearly and passionately. I attended every lecture and really enjoyed the class. If you like History and are interested in Rome at all, take this class! :)
AMAZING, HE IS AMAZING TAKE HIM IF YOU ARE TAKING 4A HE IS THE BEST

I had ZERO interest in ancient history until I took Prof. Norena's class. VERY GIFTED LECTURER (and, easy on the eyes). It's a VERY demanding class (huge amounts of reading) and lectures were jam-packed with details. One of the best classes I've taken. He will become legend at Cal one day. Carefully select your TA, a few have major power trips.

Carlos Norena is an outstanding lecturer. He knows his stuff! There is a good amount of reading and sections are fairly intense and not used to review course material AT ALL. I would recommend the class to history majors but there are much easier classes for those just looking to fulfill breadth. Also- he was a Pike at Cal in the day!
Great lecturer. Interesting and organized. I came out of the class feeling as though I knew a lot more about Roman history in a very structured way.

Quite possibly one of the best professors at Berkeley. Norena is an incredibly engaging lecturer and his organization and powerpoint slides are superb. He is incredibly knowledgeable. Quite a bit of reading, and discussions are centered around primary source documents. Three easy map quizzes(10%) It is necessary to do some work, but it is worth it!

Norena is an awesome professor. If you have any interest whatsoever in history you should take this class. The lectures are engaging and he has this hilarious dry humor that occasionally comes out. Going to class is mandatory as he clears up a lot of things from the textbook. Awesome!!

I enjoyed listening to Norena give lectures during class. He's very engaging, and he's a great speaker. He knows his stuff. However, I'm peeved by the grading in this class. While the material is easy and the midterms aren't difficult at all, the GSI that I have (Amy Russell) is such a difficult grader that I'm looking at getting a B in the class.
Brilliant lecturer, engaging powerpoint slides

I had him in Spring 06. I still cant believe how incredibly awesome he was. he keeps you interested EVERY LECTURE - it is always fascinating. his knowledge of Rome is amazing. one of the two best history lecturers ive ever had. (the other was Gruen.... who retired :(

One of the best professors I have ever had. He has a great depth of knowledge in Roman History and is very easy to approach. He makes himself available to his students and is very helpful. His lectures are fascinating and well organized.

Incredible professor. Very well organized and gives great lectures that make you want to keep coming back, refrains from being too pedantic and dense (something that many professors have forgotten how to do over the years spent in the ivory tower). Easily the best instructor in a department full of great professors.

Extremely well-prepared, engaging, knowledgeable, friendly, helpful, organized, compelling... lectures were seriously a joy. He's everyone's favorite professor... TAKE HIS CLASSES IF YOU CAN! (He's unfortunately not teaching Fall 2007 or Spring 2008... so look for him later!)

Never have I heard such unanimously glowing reviews of a history prof at Cal, which is saying a lot considering the dept. is home to some serious heavyweights. Articulate to the point of surgical precision, knowledgeable & incredibly well-organised in every respect. Flawless. The man is on fire in&out of the classroom & delivers every single time.
No Comments

As long as you attend lecture and take notes your grade is in the bag. Really, he is such a great lecturer, the text is okay but not necessary. Primary source impt for paper and somewhat for midterm/final. Best lecturer at Cal, hands down. Funny (in dorky way, but amusing). Keeps class lively. Wish he could teach other prof how to lecture properly.

Norena has got to be, hands down, the most eloquent, organised, razor-sharp lecturer in the history department at Cal (not to mention best dressed, despite the commendable efforts of the other profs he's been compared to). He is very apprachable; the students even attended his optional discussions on FRIDAY AFTERNOONS. Enough said.

Professor Norena is the most incredible professor I could ever imagine teaching a history class. Not only did he convey all the necessary information with eloquence and grace, he inspired and made me almost consider changing my major to history. Take any class you can get into with the wonderful man.

Great professor. Lectures are very interesting. Attendance is absolutely mandatory. The only difficulty of this class is the incredible amount of information it covers. Keep up with the class and you'll enjoy it. Reading the textbook is not necessary. It just confuses the straight forward explanations Norena gives in class.

Epitomizes "great lecturer." Unbelievably knowledgable, very clear, and funny! 4A is a survey class, so there's not a lot of time to learn about culture and society, but Professor Norena's lectures were still a treat; I never missed one - I enjoyed them so much and I knew I'd fall behind if I did (they're essential if you don't read the textbook).
Lectures clearly, precisely, and beautifully and inserts dry sense of humor at just the right moments. Wonderful professor, couldn't ask for more.

Such a great lecturer, love the sense of humor. For final though, it was a little hard to get 'big picture' ideas from lecture because he goes a lot into the specifics. Best way to study: look up essay topics on Google and just outline them. Worked great. Final asks general questions so you have leeway- can talk about more than one topic.

Skilled lecturer, broad and deep knowledge of Ancient History. Amiable, always on time, always ready, engaging, open for questions, all around a great teacher and person. The pace is fast because of the amount of material covered, but worthwhile. Midterm/final totally fair. Good GSIs.

Lecture is mandatory but the reading (textbook, not primary source) is not. Assigns a lot of reading but really doesn't expect you to read it all. GREAT LECTURER! Funny,thorough. He will tell you when to read the text. Best professor so far. Midterms based a lot on lecture but know the key terms from the powerpts. Primary source only for discussion

Excellent history professor. His lectures are very organized, clear, and informative. He also takes the time to not only present multiple perspectives on key topics, but also provides a wide variety of evidence, whether literary, archaelogical, circumstantial, etc. He is also quite personable and will provide earnest individual assistance. Humor to

Best history professor I've had, and the most eloquent speaker and comprehensible lectures you will ever witness at Cal. Along with fascinating textual evidence and his own interesting analysis, he truly stimulates the students to love the Ancient World. Also a humorous and affable character. Highly recommended for majors and non-majors alike.

Professor Norena's lectures are very well organized and clear. He is exemplary of what a great professor is. He is approachable, friendly, with an undeniable love of and for ancient history and willingness to discuss pretty much anything about it. The tests are a bit challenging, but it helps you become a better writer. Highly recommended.
_Very_ organized professor, _very_ clear lecturer.  A bit pedantic and assigns too much reading, but quite good overall.

I agree that Professor Norena is an excellent teacher. His precise eloquence in presenting history is a treat to listen to. The loud, extended applause at the end of this semester was evidence of his skills as a professor. Cal is indeed lucky to have him!

This is, simply put, the best history class I've ever taken. Norena takes ancient history and makes it vibrant and engaging. If you are even vaguely interested in the topic of Rome (or in fall of '06 the classical world for Hist 4a) take Prof. Norena. He's new and Berkeley is lucky to have him!
one of the best lectures/professors ive ever had. very engaging and clearly enjoys what he is doing. he made a fascinating topic the highlight of my semester.
Covers a lot of material in his lectures but tries hard to make them interesting and revelant every time. Clearly loves teaching history.

Super interesting class with information packed lecture. Three models, 5 quizzes but one is dropped, and two reports make up your grade. Lecture is not mandatory but lab is and his office hours are by appointment.
I would say that David Jaehning is the best teacher within the US Berkely ARCH program. Highly intellectual and really cares for his students.
Professor Jaehning is the best!

He really cares about you! Sometimes his feedbacks arent really that helpful. So you should ask him a lot of questions and hell try his best to help you. Hes really understanding towards his class, And he knows that other classes are demanding as well.
It will be week 12 into the semester, and you won't know what's going on. Avoid at all costs.

You're basically not allowed to get sick in this class because there's no makeup exams, even in serious situations. The professor focuses on his own accomplishments/travels, and lectures don't prepare you for exams. If you care about your GPA and learning, think twice. Many students particularly DSP students drop midway.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He cold-calls at the undergraduate level, which makes the classroom feel tense rather than engaging. Who wants to speak when getting pressured for an answer you don't know? Don often rambles and lacks structure but he's got passion for econ. The education quality of his class felt disappointing for the #1 public uni and especially for Haas.

If you have to take his class, go in with a positive mindset and figure out how to effectively study (many negative reviews may make it feel impossible to do well, but it is not). Try to pay attention in lectures as the current events he brings up are interesting to think about. Overall, he is a nice professor and a good lecturer.

They say an apple a day keeps the doctor away. For him, I'd buy an apple farm so I'd never have to see "Doctor" Hanna again. 

Lectures not relevant to exams. Hostile towards students. Passive-aggressive. Don't take---EVER.
This guys is the worst professor I have ever had, someone please come for his tenure so future students don't have to endure this prof

DO NOT TAKE! His lectures make no sense, super unclear with exam expectations and grading, so unresponsive, said he was going to email course grade matrix the day grades were due and never did. Please take with another prof if possible
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do NOT take 101B. Just wait for 100B with Edwards. Lectures are unhelpful for the exams. Heavily based on memorizing facts.
Fire this guy ASAP.

The exams are 80% of your grade that's not even on lecture slides or textbook, and he won't give any info about it before. After trying to wake up for so many 8am's, he mentioned at the end of class that attendance won't lower your grade (still don't understand how his grading will go). He will pick on people and call them out. Please avoid him.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Most of your grade is made up of exams (80%). He said at the end of the semester that attendance won't lower your grade. The final had so much material I had never seen, and that's after days of studying. He goes on rants and rambles the whole class period. He started to shame people in my 8am for being tired. Do not take him. Avoid at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
You might be thinking to yourself, “I'll just ignore the ratemyprofessor I have to take this class for my bbs”. DO NOT TAKE. Wait until literally anyone else is teaching it. 

Confusing. Miserable. Lectures are hard to follow. Exams have material never covered in class that's worth 80% of your grade. No amount of studying will help you. Genuinely.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Run the other way. I feel like he's prob a nice guy but his lectures are completely useless (and more confusing than just reading the book on your own) and mandatory. He doesn't give you any relevant information about any of the exams either. This class is not at all easy, avoid at all costs tbh.
do not take

His lectures are useless for the exam.Tests are 80% of our grade and having 0 practice exam doesn't make sense. Felt like he was trying to make students' lives miserable on purpose by saying that attendance doesn't matter at the END OF SEMESTER when students were literally FIGHTING for their lives to make it to this 8AM class.
Cold calling on students is not the way to teach.
This guy sucks

hes smart for sure, but he cannot teach. super unclear about what students are expected to know on the exams. makes attendance mandatory but the fact that people STILL dont come despite taking a hit on their grades just shows u how bad sitting in this class is. avoid, made me dislike economics even though i loved it growing up

I'm surprised with how generous the reviews are. Exams (bulk of grade, 2MT, 1 F) focuses on trivial knowledge, incorrect questions, and ambiguous language (luckily curved to a mean of B+). Classes are purely him going on tangents with a slide presentation of screenshots behind him. Attitude towards people with disabilities and Asians.

My first day of class, I was wearing a red shirt, and the prof, in front of the whole class, told me to never come back again wearing red. This just set the tone for the rest of the class. Insanely long homeworks, horrible lectures that oftentimes are just long tangents about his time in the banking world.  Weirdest midterms format. Dont take.

I have never written a review for any professor before in all my years of college, but this is by far the worst professor I have ever had. His lectures are extremely boring and have nothing to do with the actual content of the tests. He likes to just yap to feel important but no one in class really cares. Terrible professor!!

The devil works hard but this man works harder. I went to every class discussion and office hours and i learned nothing. Every time i asked a question he answered with a snarky tangent We had a mentally challenged individual in or class and whenever he asked a question this guy would literally just pick on him and quiz on the spot.

Not a fan of this professor. Lectures are useless compared to the book, speaks more about his experience rather than teaching us material in a digestible way. Way too many long HW assignments for a 3 unit class. Provides no test prep materials and makes the tests very long. Changes final format / syllabus less than a month out from the final.

this class was so incredibly difficult and there was so much work to be done on a weekly basis for a 3 unit class. the professor is also not accommodating to illnesses. that being said, i think if u made the effort, he is a generally a sweet guy who is just doing his best.

Nice guy, but ineffective teacher. Lectures are never finished on time, and slides are shallow. The only way you are able to learn in this class is through the textbook. Tests are similar to the homework. However, homework solutions are always released last minute. Gives you a 20-page test that is difficult to finish on time. Don't take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: No. Don't take Prof. Hanna's class here. No.
Fair and caring prof.

This class was... frustrating. Attendance is a big part of the grade, but the tests are all based on the homeworks and textbooks. The lectures are very boring, and he often gets overly political. Quite a bit of homework. Very generous curves though, if you study the book and hw you will do well.

Prof Hanna's final exam was fair (most problems were from hw or midterms). He requires participation but offers different avenues (Ed posts) to make up for a lack of live participation. His lectures don't involve practice problems but they conceptually reinforce concepts from the textbook. He gives most people at least an A-. Fair and caring prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS AND I DO NOT SAY THIS LIGHTLY!!!!!!!

Donald Hanna, or Don Hanna, is smart, kind, and inquisitive, but his course is rough. Poor communication, inconsistent grading, and overwhelming exams make it a humbling experience for Haas and Economics students alike. Despite a few years of teaching, the course feels unrefined. As I await my final grade, I can only wish future students good luck.

Absolutely do not take it with Don Hanna. Worst Haas professor BY FAR. He is so rude to his students and his GSIs. His last homework assignment was 119 questions which goes to show you how time intensive the class is. His lectures are entirely unhelpful and are mostly just him bragging about his travels and honestly just cause more confusion.

It has been a nightmare attending his class. He always bullshits so much about his experience, not the content related to the class. He has so much homework, personal emotions, and rubrics. Be prepared to grind a lot and good luck :)

You will know what Haas's professor is like after taking this class.
He always fails to finish the lecture on time and even skipped Chapter 20 without realizing.

He decides to change the syllabus on the spot when it was set in stone on paper since the beginning of the semester. He does not care about if his students perform well or not, rather he prays on his students' downfall.
