I truly did believe that UGBA 101B was going to be an interested macro-economics class and was excited to learn more after taking 100A. However, he has a very disorganized course and does not let students know about any homework deadlines. Neither does he provide any review material specifically for exams. Truly don't take with this professor.

This class has got to be a joke. The guy goes on tangents about graphs and unrelated topics to the course. The lectures are never finished so students have to practically self-teach the course. The midterms aren't related to what's taught and is made so people cannot finish on time. The GSI's also don't have a clue about what the Professor expects.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: AVOID DONALD HANNA AT ALL COSTS!!!!!!!!!!!! YOU HAVE BEEN WARNED!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! Taking DONALD HANNA'S class has RUINED my LIFE!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! LECTURES are EXTREMELY IRRELEVANT to EXAMS, yet the GRADE is HEAVILY determined by EXAMS and PARTICIPATION, and he DOESN'T provide any MATERIALS to help STUDY FOR AN EXAM!!!!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Very test-heavy class, also I worry for the man because all he does during lecture is go on random tangents and ramble A LOT. Maybe it's early onset of dementia, or maybe that's just how he lectures but seriously, I don't really know how some of the content is really related to the core idea of the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: he will not announce upcoming midterms OR reminders OR provide midterm prep OR provide midterm study materials OR give guidelines on what the midterm will test OR answer any questions on Ed. Mark your midterms on your calendar bc there are no reminders. Lectures are MANDATORY and GPS tracked but will NOT be on anything on the test.

Awful course logistics and lecture!!!
Never take this class to substitute Econ 100B.

His lectures come off as rambles that are very difficult to decipher. They are not useful for learning course material at all.
TAs/GSIs during his semester seem to have a hard time with concepts, often just saying wrong things.
The exams are incredibly long multiple choice (where each question has multiple answers??). Wouldn't recommend to my ops.

Expected us to know China's GDP growth on the final exam + 6 other obscure data points (ex. US's unemployment rate, nominal GDP last quarter, etc.). How are people supposed to know China's GDP growth? I don't even know the numbers for America. Literally such a ridiculous question and deliberately set-up to confuse students.

Don's lectures are not friendly to students who do not have prior economic knowledge. He doesn't teach concepts well. His lectures are about applying concepts to current events, which is understandable because he has decades of experience in various impactful institutions. The tests are hard and focus on applications as well.

Objectively he is a good lecturer, although there is zero useful content in lectures. He basically teaches current events and how to read a graph, and then throws actual macroeconomics onto the exams. Read the textbook to do well.

Professor Hanna is a brilliant professor, but sometimes his lectures and concepts can be hard digest and understood well enough to do well on exams. The exams are based on hypothetical questions about macro, but are multiple choice. Participate and go to office hours, and he is more than happy to reexplain and go in concepts more in depth.

As others have said, lectures are largely unhelpful in the context of exams, and frankly to learn in general. They are convoluted and difficult to follow, often throwing equations onto slides haphazardly. I do not think the content is inherently difficult but the way he presents it certainly makes it far more difficult to grasp.

Literally does not teach anything useful in class so majority of students self-teach. Final includes math questions that he never goes over in class, are not included in HW, and not explained in the textbook.

A very caring and accommodating professor who you can talk about economics outside of class. You can attend either through in-person discussion or Ed forum, which helps you actively read and interpret articles and graphics on macroeconomics. The exams tended to be much harder than the homework, but the curve was generous.

Dr. Hanna's best lessons stem from his OH where he dives deep into current events and is open to answering any questions that one can think of. I highly recommend getting the textbook for this class and reading the chapters. The class is difficult but rewarding, especially if you are new to the material being taught.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: The professor is Inspirational and teaches the class in connection with the real world. Take this class if you actually want to learn something that will stick with you for a life time!

Very knowledgeable about current events, and overall a really nice guy, but the lectures are abstract, hard to follow, and have little bearing on the exams, which are extremely difficult. This was a very hard intro to macroeconomics class, made harder by not having an in-person GSI this semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Echoing what everyone else has said, but Professor Hanna spends so much of lecture on tangents talking about his personal experiences (which are definitely interesting), but none of it translates to the finals or midterms. I did so poorly on them because I genuinely don't know how you could've studied for it.
Lectures are nothing compared to his hw or midterms. lectures are boring and difficult to follow along. most of the time i dont know whats going on and he expects you to know everything.

He's a good lecturer, but lectures rarely have anything to do with HW/Midterms/Finals. I recommend reading the textbook. Tests are tough. I also enjoyed the anecdotes during the lectures. Wasn't the best econ class I've taken but it's decent.
Bruh. I went from taking econ with the Romers to this. Waste my time SP21

One of the worst professors Ive taken at Haas. The contents of the lectures are way above the level of introductory macroeconomics. The level of the exam is way above the level of the textbooks and have no way of preparing for it. The professor have changed the grading policy mid-semester and did not curve the class with midterm average below 75%.

A great lecturer, but not the best professor. Lectures are always interesting and he's extremely knowledgeable about current events and global macro trends. However, he overcomplicates concepts. Sometimes he forgets that he's teaching intermediate macro to a bunch of haas students. I recommend reading the textbook after lectures.

Very intelligent professor that is extremely well-versed in her field of study. With the assignments, she gives great feedback and is easy to talk to about questions or concerns. She will engage with the classroom, so if you are looking for something more casual maybe this isn't for you! But I very highly recommend her.

Prof. Santana is an inspiring and caring educator. She made her class a safe space for everyone and delivered the content in a straightforward way. I made so many amazing friends in this class. The main work in this class is weekly readings and participation, so make sure to speak up during class. This class was wonderful!

Prof Santana's awesome. Nice and down to earth. She's super insightful but sometimes her smarts a little difficult to process. Doesn't post lec slides or recordings. Really easy class if you just do the work. Paragraph long reflections per week based on readings, final project on whatever you want. 20% of grade is attendance so make sure to go.
Doesn't put much attention to her class.

The class has a take-home midterm and final and a group project that we work on all semester (all graded relatively easy). Prof. Draney is very sweet and her lectures were amazing (can get away without doing the reading if you show up to class). She is clearly very knowledgeable about her field. I came out of the class feeling like I learned a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Draney was sweet but her classes were a repeat of the textbooks we had to read, so it was quite boring. However, the class is super easy and Prof. Draney gives excellent grades.

Took this class at Cal and found it very engaging. It's interactive, with games tied to real-world application. He brings strong energy and creates a supportive environment. Can feel different from a typical lecture, but it leads to high engagement and useful takeaways.
I love this professor. The best!
Doug was the best professor I've had at Berkeley.  Knowledgeable, caring, experienced, and fun!  If you take his class you won't be disappointed.
Dhehe

Professor Leeds really cares about students.  He says it's because he was a student at Berkeley, but I think it's because he's just a good guy.  I LOVED this class, and I think he (and Bill Collinns) were the best of the teaching team. I learned a lot, more than in any other 2-unit class, but the learning was easy and fun.

Doug taught the last 3rd of the course. He is great at feedback and scheduling office hours appointments. Our class was a 2 hour session once a week and I felt that Doug was great at keeping the class engaged for all of the time in each class. He is great at showing how what we learn in class applies to the real world. Highly recommend his courses!
A team-taught course, and all of the profs are good. Prof. Leeds (aka Doug) was the best though. Looking forward to taking his other class this semester.

SOOOO much reading for a 45. I enjoy him as a teacher but I have multiple other classes, expecting this much is kinda insane when compared to other english classes. I also may be biased as I had a particularly hard GSI, so beware!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: pretty easygoing class, the prof. was a great lecturer, super funny and super kind even if i personally wasn't too invested in the material--just make sure to stay on top of readings and be mindful of your essays, GSIs can make or break your grades
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Solid lecturer and really nice professor once the intimidation of the course wears off. Classic Berkeley English professor-- super passionate, super smart, and a course with reading that's well-picked and very valuable to engage with. The reading is only a burden if you put it off-- I did that once or twice and would not recommend it for others.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Respected--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof Duncan is a wonderful lecturer who maybe assigns a little too much reading (but I forgive that). I wish I could take a more specific class with him, he definitely has extensive knowledge about things that we couldn't always get into. Not very much writing but there was a midterm and a final. Read everything even when it feels like too much.

Fantastic professor - I'd love to take more classes with him, because he's just THAT good. I learned so much about Scott and Austen, and was introduced to literature and criticism that I otherwise never would have known about. Incredibly knowledgable, and he is so supportive and kind to his students. It's a pleasure to have been taught by him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Professor Duncan is probably one of the best professors at Berkeley. His lectures are all engaging, and all of the operas that he picked for us to discuss for this semester were so intriguing. He also  provides a lot of support for papers, which helped me grow as a writer. You can tell he genuinely wants all his students to succeed in his class.
Honestly, Ian Duncan was an amazing professor and he really cares about what he lectures about and makes it sound rly engaging
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Duncan is one of the few people I would describe as whimsical! His lectures are engaging and he has a great sense of humor! The inaugural assignments are pass/no pass, prioritizing students to learn. He genuinely wants his students to learn. He cares about his students. If you can, take 45B with him!

Fantastic professor! Lots of readings, but his interpretations of them are fascinating. I often wished that lectures were longer so I could hear more of his thoughts! The exams are straightforward and honestly, a lot simpler than I expected. Grading for papers is dependent on GSI. He's one of the best instructors at Berkeley! Loved his class!

Professor Duncan is passionate about what he teaches and truly cares about his students. His course is not super easy, but it's also not overly difficult. His lectures are extremely interesting. He is also kind and approachable in office hours. I would definitely take a class with him again!

Least favorite English class taken at Berkeley, the readings aren't that interesting. Prof. Duncan assigns SO MANY readings as well (be prepared to not get through all if it!...) Can be detrimental as the midterm and final require you to recognize quotes and state titles and authors. TRY TO READ! The course requires memorization of literary terms.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Duncan is the best and I sincerely enjoyed reading and learning about Stevenson's works (especially the lesser-known ones) and the literary/historical context behind them. He made the class enjoyable and informative! He gave great feedback and was flexible with prompts for writing assignments! I was so lucky to be able to take his class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Duncan is a remarkable lecturer! He animates the lesson with great accents and lots of character! However - he assigns a HUGE reading load for ENGL45B. Somehow by the grace of the Gods I got an A, but I was genuinely stressed due to the accumulative final that covered ALL the works.. even ones covered on the midterm.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Loved his opera and literature class. I felt like a better writer after finishing his course. He puts in so much effort to make his course engaging and mutually productive. Please dont hesitate to take his classes!

Professor Duncan is a true academic, the first and foremost important thing in his courses is to be engaged with the material. Anyone who is "not into" the readings will probably find the class difficult, but if you are interested in the literature then he is a great lecturer to listen to.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Prof. Duncan is welcoming of student ideas during lecture. He clearly has a passion for literature, although the class material can be dull, especially the historical content. I did enjoy the readings (Gulliver's Travels, Robinson Crusoe, etc.); GSIs gave good feedback on the papers. Exams can be difficult and require matching names to quotations.

Ian Duncan is a wonderful professor. He's genuine, clear, and intelligent. While I wasn't a fan of the course itself, ENG 45B, Duncan made the lectures endurable. Honestly, you don't really have to read the books if you go to lectures and take notes on his main ideas. The opposite is also true, if you skip class, reading will help you keep up.

Honestly you can tell he is a smart guy but I could NOT keep myself interested. Some teachers in the English department are so engaging you cannot help but pay attention even if you're not into the material, but for 45B was SO BORED THAT CLASS WAS LITERALLY PAINFUL. I think he is a nice person but would not recommend.

Brilliant professor, but his lectures were too fast and he assigned too much reading. We were not able to accurately or deeply discuss any of the texts, which also made it difficult to finish assignments and discuss in section. Besides that, however, it was hilarious watching him bounce around the classroom. Lots of energy.

I definitely hated this class, but a lot of that had to do with the period & not Duncan himself. He's funny sometimes, but lecture tends to get droll- it was way to easy to fall asleep. My favorite thing about him was his accent while reading Scottish poetry. The reading load was heavy but that's to be expected from an intro English course at Cal.

I created an account on Rate My Professors specifically to leave a review for Professor Duncan. He's the single best professor I've had at Berkeley  prepared, funny, and so brilliant it takes your breath away. I cannot wait to take a class with him again. A lot of reading, but if you take the time to do it, you'll find the lectures fascinating.

Duncan is the nicest teacher I have ever had at Cal, he is always willing to help and challenge you. He ordered everyone coffee and cookies at the final, too. He gives amazing historical and cultural context for everything and is a very fair grader, interested in seeing you improve and succeed. I loved this class, great coverage of the material!

Dry lectures that emphasize history, attendance recorded. Participation a part of grade. Some texts boring, some more interesting. Overall 45B covers a dull period so not worse than I expected. Duncan's clear, fair, and good, but not amazing.

Definitely my least favorite of the 45 series -- almost made me want to give up the English major. Duncan has a cool accent, but that's about it. He provides a lot of historical background, which is nice, but his literary analyses were lackluster. Reading load is ridiculous, and he requires three essays, as well as a final exam.

I had the pleasure of taking Duncan twice: for my thesis course (Comedy) and for Scottish Literature. The man is brilliant but extremely humble. If you treat him with respect, and illustrate interest in his class, he will go out of his way to help you. I have graduated and he still helps me! I have a passion for Romantic Brit Lit thanks to him!

Professor Duncan is incredibly knowledgeable about his subject matter, and fully willing to go above and beyond to assist students in their studies; whether related to his field or not. I am very proud of the essays I completed in his class, and felt that, though difficult, that I earned my grade in his class. He also has a fun, dry sense of humor.

Prof. Duncan's class is interesting and fun; we explored complex ideas without getting too lost in the process. However, he is VERY difficult to please. His class was my first B at Cal; if you're going for an A, maybe avoid his class. Utilize office hours and read very carefully, and you might end up with a B+.

Duncan is an Oxford professor with an endearing British accent. He teaches 45B as a survey course literally since he demands double the reading required by other English courses: analysis tends to be cursory, focused on historical context rather than textual & introduces concepts w/o saying why it matters. IMO: D+ Not a Cal cutting edge professor.

Must add that I wrote the below comment, and am not sure why the rating reads "Good Quality." I gave him a C-, which is "adequate at best." I have only disliked 2 Eng profs in my lifetime school career; this is the 2nd. Anyone who worships this person is telling more about themselves than this performer.

Worship this man? He doesn't know or care who YOU are. Rock star attitude: arrogant, self-absorbed actor, doesn't meet a single eye as he lectures, smug and mocking those who dare ask questions. Yelled at a girl leaving 5 mins early bc she distracted him - What's a prof throwing a tantrum? Not why I major in Eng & pay to attend Berkeley. Prof FAIL.

Professor Duncan is open to all sorts analytical input, but not babble. Very approachable. Very kind. Very attractive. I worship Professor Duncan. He is the best English professor I have had at Cal. So great. A genius.

He made 45B my favorite class this semester despite the fact that it was my least favorite literary time period. He made almost every reading interesting and really tied overall themes together well. He's totally funny and his accent is adorable. Lecture attendance is mandatory, participation is 25%, midterm and final are only worth 30% together.

Professor Duncan was an awesome lecturer. The readings he assigned were pretty boring but he always made them more interesting and made me think there was more to them than I had previously thought. He was passionate, engaging, and his jokes and accent kept me going through the class. I highly recommend him.

Professor Duncan is awesome!  Very approachable and interesting to talk to.  Plus, he actually publishes work, which is pretty amazing for a nice professor.  I definitely recommend taking a class with him - he makes seemingly obscure topics relevant and interesting!

As described below, Duncan is still very accessible. He is very down to earth. He is one of the most acommodating Professors I have had. I got a B+, and I went to 5 of his office hours this semester. With a few more visits and great essay writing an A is possible, but not easy.

He is a publishing super-star, respected in the most elite academic circles. How come he can still manage to be so accessible and unassuming, then? I am not prone to hyperbole, but I think he is one of the best "professionals" I know: he loves his work, he loves his life, and he loves his students. And he does so without ego, and little resistance.

I really liked his insight on several of the readings, he was quite funny at times too. Lectures are extremely important, vocabulary too, exams are based on the excerpts he reads in class and his analysis of them, so take notes.

Not too bad for a prereq, had some good book choices. The poetry was a beast to get through. Do make sure you show up. Otherwise very genial to talk with. He makes visiting his office hours required, though.

Good prof. Makes books I hated in high school newly interesting. Has an awesome accent. Attendance is KEY but he keeps track, so there's incentive to go. Not too hard, but definitely not easy. Good luck!
lectures are very important, take careful notes and write down all terms, interesting lecturer, good insights into material

Prof. Duncan is SO enthusiastic about his lectures that you can't help but be won over. If you take careful notes from lecture (which shouldn't be difficult) and KNOW THE VOCAB, this class should be no problem. DEFINITELY a great professor.
He's the kindest professors that I've ever met.He is always willing to help students. His lecture is so clear and profound. Also, he is super kind and helpful in his office hours!

Good lecturer, excellent at reading passages aloud (getting his Scots on when reading from Burns or anything brogue-y), likes throwing in an occasional pop culture allusion to keep us alert ("Tarantino-esque fountains of blood"), and is fun to talk with. Also he looks like Leonard Maltin!
Great sense of humor and very interesting lectures.
Great lecturer.  Loves his subject, very organized.  He explores complex ideas, but is very clear in their presentation.  Good humor.  Scottish accent.  He's also quite accessible.  Take him for 45B.
Difficult.

This course is very easy. If you are interested in the environment, culture, and technology this is the class for you. A few things you read about are the Acequias, the Japanese Diaspora, Deforestation, and migration along the Sonoran Desert. Dr. Danis is literally the easiest professor to talk to so if you are failing it's Cuz you want to.

Dr Danis is a newer professor who's really hit their stride, I had a great time! Social justice oriented so it's a great choice if you're into that. Weekly reading was around a hundred pages, but if you're into it it's super fun and interesting. Super excited they're at Cal Poly now, if you have the chance to take Dr Danis I'd take it!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This class was pretty good for an online class. It's a super hard class, but the professor did a pretty good job. Group projects were impossible because most people in my group never did the work for the first half of the class, so no one knew what they were doing.

Convoluted teaching methodologies with unclear course content & crazy time commitment. Lectures are useless & don't clarify concepts. Course is self-taught from textbook. Not consistent with communication. Group project feels unattainable and unfairly weighted as well as graded harshly. Would not take again from this professor.

Run. Time commitment much higher than stated in syllabus. Course content is unclear. Lectures do not solidify concepts. Unnecessarily complicated group project that is weighted heavily. Accessibility is mixed and inconsistent. Made worse by bieng a lab online. Should only be taught in person, and not by this professor who lacks teaching ability.

History of Women in Colonial Spanish America was an amazing proseminar that sought to better understand women's history in this region and time period through weekly deep dives into convents, witchcraft, market economies, changing gender roles, and the household. Reading was necessary to understand seminar discussions. Clear syllabus, fair grading.

A wonderful professor brimming with passion and positivity. Truly one of Berkeley's best! He does a really good job infusing the class with energy and getting people talking. The way he discusses the content is also inspiring and totally changed how I see the world. Hopefully, I have a chance to take again.

Great professor, very passionate. Participation matters! Do the reading and you will be fine. In class group activities. 2 writing assignment, weekly discussion post, very chill. Definitely recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: It seemed like the course grading expectations where purposefully designed to be impossible to understand

Very passionate and caring nature that really motivates you. Reading/writing were not originally my strengths, but his clear and actionable steps and feedback helped me improve so much. Participation definitely matters, so make sure to go to class prepared. It helped to skim the readings and take notes of a few points to discuss during class.

One of my favorite professors at Berkeley. Really cares for his students and is really understanding. The content in class was always interesting and essays were really fun to write and not too difficult. Your grade is based on participation (that includes attendance) and 3 essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: More than just an outstanding professor, he is a genuinely kind and empathetic person. Does a great job teaching difficult material. He is also passionate when speaking and I really enjoyed his lectures, especially his tech workplace one. Try to go to his office hours but just know appointments are usually all booked which can be annoying.

Great professor. Took for Data C104, try to get in his discussion section if you can. Tbh I had some schedule conflicts so I didn't go in-person for lectures, but even his discussions are really engaging. Come to class prepared (yes, reading matters!) and open-minded to learning about different perspectives. Super engaging content and delivery.

I took History 100B: The Global Spanish Empire From Resistance to Revolution in SP 24. An amazing professor who values interacting with his students, encourages participation, keeps class entertaining, easily accessible outside of class, and overall a great understanding professor! Do be ready to write critically thorough ideas tho.
In my opinion, hands down the best professor at Berkeley. Is really passionate about the material and gives incredible lectures. Highly recommend going to his exam review sessions.

The Best professor in Berkeley! He genuinely cares about ensuring students truly understand what he's teaching. I feel fortunate to be a part of his discussion section. Only prof who did not judge me at all and I could talk about anything. Joined the class thinking its just another one I will have to bs but ended up learning a lot thanks to him.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Amazing lecturer with gives out extremely interactive lectures. I never had interest in history before I took this class with him. He's also really supportive to students who struggles and provide constructive feedback during office hours.

Prof. Millers was was a great instructor but the actual exam he gave us was insanely unpractical. Keep in mind this exam was the week after spring break so we basically had 2 weeks of straight cram time + a flashcard. Exam was 18 pages
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: Good god, this exam broke my heart and shattered it into a million pieces. Let me say it isn't representative for this section. I like Professor Miller's teaching and the content is doable but the exam was 18 pages, 1 hour 50 mins and no time to check work. Very disappointing and I'll be honest, I don't know about a curve but I wish for one.

Just his teaching's a solid 4/5. However, his exam was unrealistically long--18 pages in 1 hour 50 mins. Some questions had parts up to like o or m (abc style), which each being 0.5-1 point. Allegedly, he finished the exam in 22 mins and the avg (allegedly) was ~56%. Most students didn't even finish the last few pages. Prep well for his test..

Memorization and conceptually heavy, fast lectures, had to rewatch most of them.18 pages in one exam with many subquestions per numbered question. In my objective opinion, amount of questions in the exam were unreasonable for 1 hour and 50 mins. There should be a way to test students' competency w/o making the test unreasonably long and hard.

Prof. M is excellent! Very caring and clear about what we need to do for success. Lucid lectures. Exam is long, but practice exams direct you well. Metabolism unit is very difficult but Prof. M breaks it down in a way that's digestible.

Good prof, BUT exam are beyond what a human can do. Extremely LONG exam (1hr 45min for 18 pages). Lowkey I bet 80% of student either didn't finish the exam OR guessing a lot to finish the exam. BE aware! For us, class was NOT curve, so long exam made it so much harder to get A (curve should be fine--if u A student u will prob get A when curve).

Dr Miller is a caring and amazing professor! I had him for CHEM 135. Despite it being a heavy memorization and conceptual course, he made it fun and easy to follow! I enjoyed attending class and learning the material! He makes sure to engage with all of us!

As someone who hated ochem, I LOVE taking biochem with Miller. It's definitely not an easy class, but he makes the material so enjoyable and easily digestible even for people who didn't do well in past chemistry classes (me). Tests are fair and homework is graded on completion, which gives you time to not stress and fully digest the information!

I apologize for giving Prof Miller a 1 star rating after the first midterm, it was a very emotional rating and doesn't really reflect his ability. Exam 1 was honestly a bit long but definitely the second midterm is very fair.  His lectures are well organized and explain things clearly. HW and Worksheet are graded on completion but def do them!

Prof. Miller was great for the metabolism unit. He is very organized and his lectures are all done via tablet so it makes it easier to learn all of the reaction/structures that you need to know for the midterm. He is also pretty accessible during OH and is generally pretty helpful there. Midterm is very long (15+ pages) but fair.
The king of metabolism. Also personable and understands that we are all in class for different reasons.

He is a good professor, but I hyped him up a lot based off of the previous reviews. He teaches it relatively well, but when I asked him questions, he was a bit vague and did not specify which aspects we needed to know or not know. Other than that, he was very organized. It might just be the content of the class that makes me not like him as much.

Prof. Miller is good, he clearly loves what he does but man, why so many pages in a test? Like, for real!! Nonetheless, he knows what he is doing and you will enjoy his lecture but you still have to study a ton.

Professor Miller was amazing. Super clear lectures and unlike lots of other MCB professors doesnt use PowerPoint. Stresses key themes and shows how they reappear for all the pathways. Test was very fair and similar to practice. Weekly problem sets are optional but should definitely be done. Overall an amazing professor.

Professor Miller truly cares about his students. He taught the Metabolism section of MCB 102, and truly did a phenomenal job, and I really feel like I learned a lot. During this section, we had to transition to online classes due to COVID-19, and through it all, Prof. Miller and all the GSIs were super understanding and accommodating to students.

Miller is the best chemistry prof I have had at Berkeley. He is an excellent teacher who explains clearly and makes sure his students understands. He is super friendly and patient in office hours. His energy and enthusiasm about chemical biology was inspiring. He assigned light amount of homework and very fair exams as well. Highly recommend!

Professor Miller is a real gem out of the many in the Chemistry department. His passion and care for teaching and students really shows during his lectures. Hes kind and patient with students at office hours and his explanations are crystal clear. There are times where he rushes through material but go to office hours to fill in what you missed.

By far my favorite of the three lecturers in MCB 102. His lectures are interactive with annotated slides. I would suggest printing out the slides beforehand to avoid getting bogged down writing out all the chemistry. His section is chemistry mechanism heavy.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Miller is by far the best MCB 102 lecturer. The metabolism section is filled with a lot of information and memorization but he makes it clear and easy to understand in lecture. If you study his slides and do his practice problems you can do well on the midterm.

I had Professor Miller for the metabolism section of MCB 102 and received an A. This guy is legit. You can tell he's passionate about the topics when he ties his research into lecture. In office hours, he is extremely patient with all students. He makes you feel like you're a valued, respected student in his class, which makes you want to succeed.

Such a great guy who cares about the students. Learned a lot from his lectures and problem sets, and loved how you actually learn to analyze and think critically rather than memorization. For tests, he would alter homework problems so you had to apply what you had learned to a new situations. It was still very challenging but do hw and go to GSIs!

One of my favorite professors! He's super nice. He made me enjoy learning about how the chemical mechanisms work in a biological setting. Professor Miller cares a lot about class feedback and adapts accordingly. His midterms were also very fair/lecture based. You're solid if you review the psets and stick close to his very detailed study guides!

He taught the metabolism section of MCB 102 during Spring 2016. Miller was hands-down the best of the three professors that semester. All of his lectures were clear, and his test was very fair. The material was very dense and possibly challenging, but most of us were able to understand it thanks to Miller. Lectures consist of mostly arrow-pushing
Don't need the book at all. Get ready for unclear grading. content was ok.
Also assigns homework due during dead week. Was initially very interested in the topic but this dwindled towards the end.
L crur s well but very misleading on grading. Said he would curve at the end but didn't. Avoid if you care about your grade.
Super awesome and nice teacher. His lectures are very captivating imo and it's clear he cares a lot about the content he teaches and his students.
take him! you won't regret it. just take notes or find someone who takes notes

what do you mean I scored above average in every single exam, I got 100% twice out of 4 exams, I had 100% attendance, I had 100% in RPP, and I got a B+. That is the most ridiculous thing I have ever seen.

He is great for 270A. I took the online version and he was an engaging lecturer. As most online courses go, some classes get a little boring to sit through but most classes were a good watch. The interactive negotiation sessions are interesting. The final essay is easy to write if you pay a fair amount of attention during the course.
Hey get the grades posted on time little man

The reviews don't lie, this professor yaps (talks a lot) and rambles about his slides that could have been explained in a few minutes. You don't actually lead people you just listen to a professor teach you how to lead people without actually doing it. Tests are very ambitious and the study guide doesn't really help much.
Very little support on ambiguous exams. Likely would end up scoring at avg on his own exams (doesn't know what he's talking about)

I have no idea why he is rated so low, he's a phenomenal lecturer and very understanding of the potential stressors students have. Not only was this a super easy class it was very fun coming to lecture and I do think I got some good takeways from it. Only downside is he doesn't put much on the slides so it can be hard to study for exams.

You won't learn anything. Half the things taught are irrelevant. Exam is mostly short answer, test corrections save everyone. The class is just him yapping and people falling asleep. Class is a lot harder then how 105 should be. I suggest another professor.

Kass was actually a really great lecturer and had interesting things to say. Lecture wasn't required so tons of people don't show up, but the times I went it was worthwhile. Exams are totally dependent on the external grader, but the curve is generous.
As a prof, he's one of the most caring and understanding that I've seen in Haas. Had a fun time.

Great lectures, sometimes a yap sess. Slow grading from GSIs. Difficult exams but he offered us test corrections (midterm 1&2) & inflated our grades, make sure you do that. I scored less than 50% on the first exam and still got an A at the end. Final was online. Group project, present on the first day for extra credit. Study hard bc no cheat sheet.

Terrible professor, one of the worst haas classes to take. Doesn't reply to emails, slides are useless, and the exams have random topics you've never discussed. Take a different professor if you can lol
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Nice guy; irresponsive. Extremely disorganized and very unclear grading criteria. Syllabus (including grade breakdown) changes throughout course. Won't be able to estimate grade after final. Interesting content, but can't apply what he teaches about motivation/leadership/organization to the class itself. Lectures are nuanced but not always direct.

His class was highly disorganized, which I didn't enjoy. He is honestly caring and willing to be flexible for his students, but the lack of GSIs slows down the grading process unfortunately. I'd take his class if you are okay with uncertainty in your grade throughout the semester, but maybe it is bc of online?
Prof. Kass rocks. He packs a lot into the summer class, but it's all fascinating. His vocal inflection is great.

Eli is one of the most passionate professors you will take. Hes super smart, loves teaching, and cares about the subject. He is difficult to meet with at times and he doesnt have the best organizational structure to his class but if youre looking for something interesting I would take him.

Dr. N is very passionate about Chemistry, but he isn't the best lecturer. Don't get me wrong, you can learn a lot from him, but his style of teaching often leaves students confused. Be prepared to go to office hours.
Doesn't explain topics well

Dr. Neuscamann is a very nice, intelligent and funny professor. However, his lectures are very theoretical and logic based, and he spends not enough time on explaining and simplifying practical applications of concepts.

Very caring professor, but unfortunately, not as engaging of a lecturer. I understand that he teaches the harder units, but the lectures don't effectively clarify concepts. Very important to be consistent with lectures and touch up on topics outside of class when it is his turn to lecture.

Dr. Neuscamman is somewhat underrated. He's very nice, and he focuses a lot on formula proofs. I found the proofs helpful for understanding the theory behind each concept even though they were hard to follow at times. The exams resemble the practice tests. I used Khan Academy for extra practice.

You can tell he knows a lot about Chemistry, however his teaching style is not for me. He goes on and on, talks really fast, and I can never process what he's saying half the time. I left most of his lectures very confused.

Dr.Neuscamman clearly cares and tries hard but his lectures are difficult to follow, overcomplicating things. The class has many resources including tutoring practically all day every day, as well as him also having office hours. The class has online questions that you have to answer during class and easy biweekly homework assignments.

Super confusing lectures with examples that were unnecessary and required lots of extra knowledge to understand. Went on lots of tangents and rarely finished on time, end of lecture was always rushed. Nice person and clearly very smart.

ngl ur not gonna learn much w him, esp for thermo thats like the main pt of his research so he just overcomplicates it, its def possible to learn the material just watch lectures on 2.0 speed (theyre all recorded and posted which is nice) and then just do all the practice exams and study the dif topics on the exams by watching yt vids
Underrated, he explains pretty good in office hours just know your stuff beforehand.

Really makes an effort to connect simple chemistry in lectures to more abstract concepts which is cool (although slightly confusing first lectures you have him).  Has easier test questions than Dr. S and very friendly, don't worry about learning everything on the slides.

Dr N seems more like a good researcher than a good lecturer. He clearly knows a lot about the topic but doesn't know how to teach it to first-time learners. I had to self-study a LOT more than for Dr S's lectures. Advice: just watch the online recordings in *0.75 speed to get what he's saying.

He uses weird analogies to explain things that sometimes made zero sense to me. Class is organized very well. Can skip lectures and do AKTIV polls from home, lectures are recorded. Exams are difficult but VERY similar to practice exams. Very minimal homework. I never went to office hours. Discussion sessions were mandatory but NOT helpful.

Dr. N is very passionate and knowledgeable, and it shows in his lectures. He explains concepts thoroughly, and his office hours are especially helpful for understanding difficult topics. Sometimes, his lectures go beyond the scope of the exams, but staying engaged and making an effort to understand each concept makes the class very doable.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This man is intelligent and nice, but cannot teach. Thermodynamics went over my head, which is generally an easy topic, because of his lack of explanations and heavy focus on unnecessary concepts. I had to teach myself his units by watching OrganicChemistryTutor since they were relatively harder. Also, he reminds me of Young Sheldon grown up.

Wastes most of lecture deriving equations which you do not need to know how to do at all. Overcomplicates many things in his lectures and it shows if his units test averages being lower than Shusterman despite arguably having easier units. Seems like a chill guy he just does not deliver effective lectures.

His lectures were confusing and he tends to derive equations (in a confusing way) for his lectures (for unit 2, though I think he's better for unit 4). Don't waste your time taking concise notes on all the lectures because you won't be texted conceptually in the exams, just practice w/ hw!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures are super fast, the slides are very dense, and some heavily tested topics are mentioned very briefly. I ended up teaching Unit 4 to myself and it made more sense. However, Dr. N is kind, clearly cares about students, and lectures are recorded. He's passionate but seems better suited for upper-division courses.

Lectures are pretty hard to follow, even more so since he covers the more complex units of the course, but if you can reach him in OH he would be more than happy to answer any questions you have for him.

He's very passionate about the subject matter and explaining things in-depth, but often that made it really confusing to understand the material. Still manageable, but required a bit more work compared to the units that Shusterman taught.
adult version of young sheldon. bad lectures, study yourself.

He is a very smart professor, but it feels that at times he forgets that some of us do not have the same chemical knowledge as he does. His lectures can be confusing and hard to understand, as he tends to teach the more complex units of the class. He also tends to go into a little too in-depth, which can make it hard to grasp the concepts.

His lectures were very difficult to understand, and even lecture recordings didn't help. Asking questions didn't help either because answers were usually equally complicated. Still, he is kind and very willing to help.

I could rewatch his lecture 3 times and still not understand this man was talking about. 50% of the time he spent too much time giving conceptual details than actually helping us learn how to think in the context of solving exam questions. Constantly practicing will help you more than attending his lectures!

I think a lot of the negative reviews come from the fact that the content he teaches is more difficult than the other units. But I do agree that his lectures were definitely more confusing and abstract than they needed to be. Accessible through OH and does care for the success of his students.

Havent taken chem before and it was HARD with him. pretty abstract teaching and convolutes stuff. READ the textbook (technically optional) and go to OH the second you don't understand something. Quizzes are technically participation based

Participation: 5%, HW: 9%, Quizzes: 9%, midterms (3) 17% each, Final: 25% (final can replace lowest midterm)

Dr. N is a nice person, and you can tell he's very passionate about Chem, but in a gen ed class, he can get too broad and too complex with simple topics and leave students unsure of what they were supposed to take away from it. All the content he teaches ends up needing to be heavily reviewed and I found myself rarely understanding it.

Very nice person however, his lectures can often feel overwhelming, not sure if this is because he taught the more difficult units compared to Dr.S or if he was a worse teacher. His voice can get very monotone and make you fall asleep, be ready to do a lot of review for his units as they can be difficult to understand at first

His lectures can often feel too abstract/overwhelming compared to what's actually necessary to know for the course and exams. He tends to overcomplicate concepts compared to Dr. S, however he is often available during office hours in which he typically explains better. The rest of the course staff's helpfulness make up for this.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: he has hard to follow lectures that show a lot of unnecessary material. especially when compared to dr. s, he is overall just worse at teaching chemistry.

Very knowledgable and kind professor. However, he way overcomplicates topics and makes them harder to understand. It's hard to go from Dr S (taught the other half) to him. Since this is gen chem, it's easy to find other resources and homework helps. Tests are difficult just off his teaching but practice tests are very similar to tests.
Lectures go quickly but he knows his stuff
Not great at explaining concepts. Often overcomplicates things. Tests are difficult

an intelligent & kind professor, but his lectures were sometimes difficult to follow & overloaded w/ abstract content not relevant to the course/exams. if you're interested in derivations of formulas then his teaching might be suitable for you, but otherwise i'd recommend taking 1a in the spring w/ just dr s. research seems very cool though!!
nice guy but genuinely a HORRENDOUS teacher. lectures were overly conceptual and needlessly confusing. take this class in the spring to avoid him.
his lectures are super hard to understand, take chem 1a with only drs if you can her lectures are amazing.

genuinely seems like a good person but his teaching style sucks, he overcomplicates concepts ( he dedicated a whole lecture to deriving delta g= delta g not + RTln(Q) which was pointless to the unit 2 test. He could use his time more effectively and explain unit 4 better, also the pond will not throw the rock back at u and yes a pumpkin is orange

Lectures are hard to understand and tests are somewhat irrelevant to his lectures. He might be professional in his field, but his slides and teaching style just make the materials way more difficult to understand than they supposed to be.

dr n and dr s switched off between chem units and honestly while i much preferred dr s's teaching style, i can tell that dr n is genuinely a caring and passionate prof. that being said he often explain things in a very abstract manner, by the end of unit 4 i stopped going to class lol. he's hard to understand but not impossible

I get all the comments about Dr. N, and I definitely had my fair share of difficulties, but that's also the nature of a weeder class. His lectures were on the more conceptual side because the units he teaches require more of a conceptual understanding in comparison to the units Dr. S teaches, and I think he's a really great, passionate professor.

Professor Neuscamman is genuinely not put to be a professor. He is a very intelligent person and knows what he is doing. However, cannot relay any information to a student. His lecture slides are mostly filler stuff you don't even need. I would suggest Neuscamman if I was taking an upper-div. Try to avoid at all costs if you want to learn.

Respectfully, I think he is a good person and he tries his best to explain. Just the thing is, not all smart people are good teachers. He knows a lot and overcomplicates the lecture too much. It's like explaining why the pythagorean theorem works when you can just memorize the equation.
People say that professor Shusterman is better but honestly both of them are great professors. They just say that because the stuff that professor Nuescamman teaches is just harder in general

He is a very passionate and genuine professor that actually cares about chem and his students. His lectures can be hard sometimes but that's just because he has a lot of knowledge. Nevertheless, the class is doable and getting a good grade is possible if you just put in effort.

The bad comments are from those who don't study or pay enough attention during lectures. He's a nice professor who tries to make the lectures as engaging& clear as possible. It is true that the contents covered aren't easy, but are necessary for STEM majors. People shouldn't be complaining about it, and I like him because he genuine and passionate.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: even the GSIs think hes a horrible teacher. his units go over so so so much info but its unclear what we're covering bc his lectures are super scrambled, messy, and make no sense and he has random math and calculus stuff on slides which make everyone super confused
all i can say is ... horrible

His ability to teach is literally zero. He seems very smart and should be working at a lab full time instead of teaching an introductory course. Classes are overly physics based while no one understands the basics, and the test questions and HW questions are super hard and irrelevant to his lectures. I wish Dr. S taught all the units of this course

MY GOD - I don't understand anything from his lectures (and I don't think anyone does). The exams over his units are INSANELY hard and his teaching style is so disconnected and he assumes you understand all the physics and orbital stuff behind whatever he's talking about... genuinely horrible

Known for not getting to the point when he talks about chemistry. Not very good at explaining concepts and adds random parts that don't contribute to the class. More or less just confuses everyone. Highly recommend looking through the slides, textbook and online recources.

Make easy concepts hard, skip harder concepts and say "you just need to memorize without understanding them" He tells you how to memorize and never explain so you understand conceptually. Also, he goes on the lecture as if you memorized everything from the previous slides, when I think he really should refer back and connect the pieces.

He seems very nice and passionate. However, his teaching style is WAY too abstract/physics-heavy for an intro-level course. Feels like everyone is completely lost on what he's lecturing about, and his lectures aren't very related to exams. If you take him, be prepared to spend time outside class learning stuff, bc he doesn't know how to teach.

Very passionate about chemistry, seems like a very good man. Overly theoretical classes with minimal explanation, most of what he teaches is irrelevant to the actual tests. Likes to go on tangents without explaining what is going on or how he derived something.

I took chem1A during the fall and it was co-taught by Dr. N and Dr. S. I definitely preferred Dr. S, but I still thought Dr. N was a good professor. His lectures were a little too abstract and conceptual in my opinion, but he talked a lot about the experimental and physics background behind certain concepts which I thought was very cool.

I took half of chem 1a with Dr. N and the other half with Dr. S. The difference in teaching ability was stark. Dr. N's lectures were so much harder to understand and I found myself rewatching them multiple times after class trying to understand the material. I did significantly worse on the units that were taught by him.

His lectures were unnecessary proofs with the last 10 minutes spent trying to scramble down the take home points that were actually important. The only thing that saved me was going to Schustermans office hour lectures. He needs to do more practice problems in lecture and not rely on the Aktiv homeworks since they aren't 100% course specific.
lectures were hard to understand as a beginner in chem as they were slightly too technical and fast paced, however very passionate about the subject and has some cool demonstrations

I was taught by him and Professor Shusterman but his teaching style was much worse. He obviously was very passionate and knowledgeable but he was almost TOO smart so it made it very hard to learn content that he overcomplicated. Many of the content of his lectures are proofs that aren't necessary to know.

I wish Chem1A didn't switch off between professors, it made it harder to adapt to each teaching style. People I know who took AP Chem in hs did good in the class, those who didn't seemed not to. Great passionate guy, but I'd probably enjoy him more if I had more background knowledge in chem. I felt so lost.

Dr. N is an extremely knowledgeable professor and very helpful outside of class. However, he does tend to overcomplicate many topics. Don't be too intimidated by his lecture slides - you don't need to know everything he says to pass this class (many of his proofs were good to know but unnecessary).
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. N is very passionate and knowledgable about what he's teaching and also super funny. Although he tends to overcomplicate certain concepts, he is accessible on Ed, after class, and in OH (highly recommend going!) where he explains lecture concepts better. It is clear that he enjoys teaching and cares for his students. Exams are also fair.

Both Dr.N and Dr.S taught Chem 1A this semester, and I found myself struggling the most on the units that Dr. N taught. His lectures weren't really helpful for me I felt like slide decks had a lot of info on one slide a it made it harder for me to comprehend the topics. He's really passionate professor but I found myself in office hours a lot.

Don't know why but chem this year had him and Dr. S switch off every other unit to teach. I noticed that for the units he taught, I didn't understand anything. His lectures are confusing, so reading is essential. Doesn't really focus on explaining the confusing concepts during his lectures.

Oftentimes entered lecture confused and walked out of lecture even more confused. However the homework and practice exams really help in understanding what content we need to know. Lecture was often entertaining tho with the demos. Good class, and it all works out in the end!

Not the best lecturer. Often over-complicates concepts that are already difficult to understand. He is definitely still very passionate about chemistry. I was unable to visit his office hours, but my friend did. According to him, Dr. N was a lot more comprehensible during office hours.  Visit his office hours if you do not understand something.

He's a nice guy, caring, and funny (if you understand his humor) but at least for me having limited chemistry experience in high school explained the concepts in a hard to understand way. With recorded lectures and being responsive on Ed discussion it is very very possible to get a good grade!

Dr. N explains concepts well during office hours. His lectures were harder to follow because he would over complicate material. I wish he had explained some things differently, but I recognize he taught harder concepts. Answered questions effectively during and after lectures and was very responsive on Ed Discussion. His dry humor was entertaining.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I felt that he overcomplicated things in lecture and went too much in detail for an intro class.  Would have been better to go straight to the point and give us the formula instead of trying to derive them, such as the formulas for entropy and gibbs free energy.  Other than that, he is a kind person and quick to respond on Ed discussion.
Uses analogies that are somewhat difficult to comprehend. Hard to "lock in" to his lectures as they get repetitive. Responsive online and answers quesitons.

Lectures were hard to follow (contained lots of abstract analogies that kind of went over our heads), I wish he put more emphasis on how to apply concepts to problems during lectures, and he was very condescending during office hours. Good lecturer but overcomplicates everything way too much.
Maybe his personality is fun but that doesn't override that he isn't a good instructor. You can get through the class if you study outside and don't listen to his complicated explanations.

Horrible at explanations.Teaches in a pretentious manner that if I paid attention was somehow starting to confuse me on all the chemistry I already knew well.These are simple concepts and he makes them feel so much harder than they're supposed to. Though, I had a stellar chem prof. before this class and maybe he set my standards too high.

He is a very smart man but does not teach like its an intro class. Goes very quickly and has confusing lectures that you really gotta pay attention to. Giving him the benefit of the doubt he tries to be funny and is good at answering questions so there's that but... he's tough.

His lectures could be a little confusing but he is constantly trying to turn abstract concepts into funny comparisons. He even invited the cal band to class and turned a giant tube of red liquid into golden blue (representing Stanford and Cal). He's really fun. I hate to see how people hate on him just because they don't understand the lecture.
Lectures move very fast. Responsive on Ed discussion. Exams are difficult but the lectures and practice materials are true to the real exam.

He was very friendly. He did move a bit fast, but he did answer questions. His midterms looked super similar to the practice ones. As long as you take time to understand the material you will do well.
An overall good class and professor for learning chem. Exams can be difficult, and homework is reasonably long.
Professor Neuscamman is a solid lecturer. Tough exams though. Make sure to go to office hours. Uses iClicker. Lectures are recorded.
Lectures were very elementary and information was not helpful for difficult midterms and final

Was a mediocre lecturer who forgot we were in an intro course. He would use overly complex language to explain simple concepts, and unless you regularly attended discussion and office hours, it was easy to lose track of the lectures and concepts. Locked grades, and you had no idea what grade you got until the last day. Wouldn't recommend.

He is very passionate about chemistry, but sometimes forgets that this is an introductory course. It's really easy to lose him when he goes through sample problems because he makes them more complicated than they are. I highly suggest attending discussions because that is where I learned all the material.

i enjoyed chem1a with prof. neuscamman. he's not a bad teacher - there's just not much special about his lectures. it's usually engaging enough with his dry humour and his slides but the class does move pretty fast. he did choke a bit on the quantum unit though, had to go to khan academy for that one. the gsis were really helpful too
Chem 1A is a hard class in general, and Neuscamman was a hard teacher. His lectures are straightforward but fairly boring. Not a bad instructor though.

One homework assignment per week (about 20-25 questions usually) and anyone can get 100 percent on it. Most of your grade depends on the three midterms and final, though one midterm grade can be replaced by your final grade. As long as you pay attention during lectures, and attend GSI review sessions (which are recorded), its possible to do well.

Lectures were fast-paced and jam-packed with information. Manageable if you keep up with reading and attend GSI/prof office hours. Past midterms + practice exams were very useful. Prof was caring and reassuring. However, final exam + grade bins were not adjusted enough for difficulty and the GSI strike :(
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Best professor I've had at Berkeley. Clear lectures, easy-to-fair exams, and SO caring inside and outside of class. Looking forward to enrolling in his future classes!
This is the best lecturer and mentor I have ever met.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Great course if you have strong chem background. Lectures moved fast but were well-explained + interesting and recordings are really helpful for review. Do the reading if you want to fill in the gaps, but you don't need it for tests. Prof was kind and very much aware that people stress over the course-- he really tries to make it doable for people.

It is clear that Professor Neuscamman truly cares about his students. The course is well-organized and offers lots of preparation before exams. Advice: attend office hours regularly (hard to get questions answered when it gets busier right before an exam), and focus more on taking detailed notes from lectures rather than the textbook.

He was a great lecturer and all of his lectures show his passion for Chemistry. This is a fun class but it is super fast paced. A mistake that I made is not doing the pre-class assignments even though they were optional. This professor provides everything that you need to succeed in this course. Be sure to do all the work and do not slack off.

Lectures were very concept-heavy and fast-paced; difficult with no background knowledge. I'd highly recommend using the GSI-led review sessions and taking your time on the homework. Textbook is good for supplemental learning. Tests were pretty difficult, acids and bases sucked. Lectures were recorded which was nice for review.

Chem 1A is an amazing class. It is most definitely driven by the student's desire to learn and their effort to understand the concepts and ideas discussed in the course. I had zero Chem knowledge going into the course but I took the time to read the pre-class readings and homework. I recommend you ask questions and do the pre-readings!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I shed several tears for his Chem1A class. However, if you put in the time and study the right things, it will all be worth it. Neuscamman's lectures were fast paced and took a while to adapt to, but he was accessible at OH and friendly. I studied about 15 hours for each midterm and 30 hours for the final. Acid/base & common ions aren't a joke.
I was not a fan of his lectures, but it wasn't bad. Course was really fast-paced and I struggled to keep up in places, but overall as long as you practice problem types a bunch you should be fine

This class is quite tough, especially if you have no previous chem knowledge. The lectures are very fast-paced, and sometimes the professor gets into so many details and forgets about the audience. Get ready to teach yourself as the lectures were of no help, the only thing that was helpful was the practice midterms.

He's an amazing professor, it's just the content is tough (obviously) so it's hard to be able to understand everything if you just rely on the lectures alone. You get what you give, if you reach out for extra help he'll be glad to explain things as many times as you need to understand it. The grading bins are also really nice

Chem 1A is structured well by content, and I feel like I learned a lot in this class, despite not having a strong chemistry background coming in. However, the structure of the midterm and final exams are terrible, as everything was MCQ, with each question being 7 points or none. The curve is 85% for A- and 90% for A, so the bins are semi-generous.

I loved his class! He was really good at explaining the lecture materials and all his lectures went really smooth. He knows what he is talking about, (REALLY WELL), and I all the demos that he did during the class were really helpful as well.

Best chem professor I've had at Berkeley no doubt. CHEM 120A is one of the hardest courses you can take in the degree. Raw score, the average is going to be around 50/100. But this class is not graded on strict bins. This class was very difficut, but this professor made me fall in love with Quantum Mechanics.

Get ready to go to office hours. The lectures are very fast paced and there's little time to understand everything within the hour. Either have a strong basic chem background or attend office hours because the course just moves too fast to depend on the lectures. Prof is very helpful in OH and will walk you through problems
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: prof really knows his chemistry, but fails to remember that his audience are not on the same level. he speaks way too quickly during lectures, making it hard to understand the material. prepare to self study, read annoying chapters, confusing discussion ws, and heavily rely on GSI's. module 2 is miserable! take chem 32, it'll save your brain!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: 1st unit(intro) was fairly easy to understand, and 3rd(thermodynamics) was ok. Yet, 2nd(acid base) and 4th(quantum) were terrible. I had to teach myself literally everything; I learned most of the content via YT videos. Only some students understood these units (and that's only cuz they did a lot of chem b4). Midterm averages range from 65% - 75%.

He's a great professor and lecturer, however, I'd highly recommend reviewing your high school/AP chem content before coming to class. It is very fast paced and you have little time to adjust. Plan on going to office hours. If you don't understand his lectures, you can ask for clarification in OH and it makes all the difference.
His lectures are so horrible, he just reads off many slides. His grading system is also bad. He tries to lighten the mood but it does not help.

I can tell that Neuscamman is really passionate about chemistry and cares a lot about his students. His lectures are well organized, although sometimes it might be hard to follow because the pace is pretty quick. However, there are lots of resources like GSI's and OH's that make up for it. Make sure to stay on top of material and you will be fine.

There are 4 modules in this course, and as of writing this review the class is currently on Module 3 (thermodynamics). After module 2, the lectures become boring and feels convoluted. The professor talks and talks about topics that aren't (personally) interesting and it's a lot more self-teaching. As a lecturer, the professor is not engaging.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Neuscamman is a lovely individual, he loves chemistry and you can tell by his lectures. However, I felt like the time given for the lectures wasn't enough to cover everything, and the level of difficulty of the midterms compared to the lectures was much more difficult. The average for the first two midterms (out of 3) was about C.

His lectures were well organized and interesting. Strong mathematical background helps but I honestly flew blind after taking many years of break from school and made it through. Thoroughly review his lectures and utilize OHs available throughout the week for the problem sets. He is funny & personable in his OH so I strongly recommend showing up.

This was by far the worst class I have taken at UC Berkeley. The lectures were information heavy and they forced a lot of material down your throat. Tests were brutally difficult and unfair. They told the class they would curve it at the end, but never did. I somehow managed a B+ because I studied for about 25 hours for the final. Difficult.

He was a nice enough person, but he is such an expert in the subject that he tends to use a lot of jargon. This was by far the most challenging class I have taken at Berkeley at least conceptually. Make sure you don't memorize equation, but simply know how to use them in their many, many forms.
Professor Neuscamman is very boring. He is not a bad lecturer, but his voice will put your to sleep.

Pretty bad lecturer in that he pushes through material way too quick and mentions a lot of random stuff you don't even need to know which makes it even more confusing, especially during the quantum mechanics unit (the last one). The class is hard, but not unbearable, but you really need to spend your time on it.

His lectures are extremely boring. The tests for this course are extremely hard. The average grade for a midterm was a D. Lectures doesnt help when it comes to studying for this course. If you take this course read of the book instead of focusing on the lectures.

Not a fan of his lectures. Very monotone and put me to sleep. At least his explanations are not horrible. Class is tough! Discussions seemed to be slightly off-tempo with what was being learned in lecture, but they were still very helpful. Tests are hard. Good luck!

I didn't mind Prof Neus.'s lecture style too much, he was a little monotonous but his lectures weren't rushed and paced well. The content was explained decently well, and for CHEM1A the exam questions were fair (but I wouldn't completely rely on the practice exams), instead, I recommend doing a lot of textbook problems until you're comfortable.

His lectures made the most challenging material of the course clear and accessible if you put in the time to review and practice. Exams were challenging but often had similar questions to the ones given in the lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Much preferred Neuscamman's lecturing to Boering. His lectures, despite tackling the most difficult material, were much easier to follow and made me feel like I actually understood things when I left.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Neus. was very organized and knowledgeable in chemistry. He taught alongside Boering for chem 1A, and I liked him a lot better than Boering. Exams were very difficult and the homework (OWL & weekly discussion worksheets) never reflected exam problems. Hard class, so prepare well.

Professor Neuscamman taught alongside Professor Boering and I always found myself looking forward to his lectures. Although this class was difficult, his explanations of concepts (especially during module 4) really clarified many of my doubts (I just wish they reduced the number of live demos). I hope to be in another class he teaches someday!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Neuscamman is the other professor who works with Professor Boering for Chem 1A. He doesn't give as many lectures in class, and if he does, they tend to be very general. However, he is definitely patient and helpful during office hours.

Eric is one of the best professors at Berkeley in terms of organization of lectures. While the material is very difficult to understand, he definitely is great at explaining it. Beware that his midterms aren't that bad but his final is killer. Go to his OH because although he goes a little fast in lecture, he's super patient and nice in OH!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: i absolutely love lectures wit prof. denero. he makes such an effort to answer questions in lecture despite there being so many students and he runs his office hours incredibly efficiently as well. he's so passionate about what he teaches and you can really feel it in his lectures. plus his dog is so cutie and he brings her sometimes!!
Istg he sounds like Mark Rober but he's a pretty chill guy
THE GOAT! THE GOOOAAAATTTT!!!! THE GOOOOOOOOOAAAAAAAAAATTTTTTTTT!!!!!!!!!
Lectures are clear, although the material is hard.

CS 61A has insane exam difficulty and a homework load for an intro CS class. Welcome to Berkeley : ).
Homework/Projects are pretty hard, and there's a lot of them. Lectures are very fast-paced, so study beforehand! DeNero made lectures fun with jokes and a conversational tone, and he's kinda just known for being a cool guy (too many 67 jokes tho).
Previous years tests are gonna seem doable but then you take the actual and John Denero steals your wallet and takes your kids.

My biggest piece of advice is to take practice exams at the time that your exam will be. Exams for my semester were 7-9/10 PM, so teaching myself to be focused late at night was good. Watch the lecture videos, and do a lot of practice exams. Don't be discouraged by low midterm scores, clobber can come in clutch. Also turn in projects early for EC.

Grade bins are super harsh (15/300 pts between A and A-). I didn't attend a single lecture, screwed up on MT2 (scored 80%), forgot to do a dozen homeworks and labs, but somehow recovered my A- to A+ on the final.
Pretty well structured course and ample resources for further learning, though he did not really do any of the lectures which was disappointing. Best advice is to do the practice tests.

CS61A is a hard course, and you really have to put in the work and time if you don't know CS (or lowkey even if you do). The way DeNero has interpreted and executed this introductory computer science is incredible- he has really created a course that, if desired, is the path for so much learning, epiphany points, and academic growth. Great prof.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor DeNero is very passionate about CS61A, which shows through his lecture style. He led great lectures and helped explain things very clearly. The course definitely provides the necessary materials and resources to be successful despite being challenging, even if you don't have prior computer science knowledge.
Tests are challenging and I enjoyed them a lot.
This class was incredibly interesting and fun. All of the course staff are extremely helpful, it makes you really enjoy coding.
He is the goat. Did 6 7 in one of the lectures at the beginning of the course and it became a legendary highlight.

Great professor, but the exams are rough. The class isn't curved so make sure to study and do a lot of past exam problems. Chances are you need to take this class for credit and not for fun, but Denero is a great professor to have.

Professor DeNero is a great lecturer and his passion for CS shows through his efforts in teaching. Midterms are difficult but fair as long as you put in effort and keep on top of your work, grading policy isn't too harsh either. I would recommend attending lectures in person as well as going to as many labs and discussions as possible!

The course was difficult if you did not have any prior understanding of core coding concepts. One issue, though. The exams were quite difficult, with DeNero stating that practice exams would help. The exams scale each semester differently, meaning if one semester did badly, the next semester would get a easier exam. Good guy tho!

I enjoyed the course content of 61A, and DeNero taught very well. I will say that his use of pensieve, an AI grading software developed by old students of his, is lowk corrupt (he pays thousands of extra dollars to the company over using gradescope) and detracts from learning (we don't learn to use github like we would with gradescope).
hard midterms

I went into this class with little interest in CS and came out loving it!! CS61A focuses on restructuring how you logically think. As such, I felt like I came out of this class smarter, both in coding and in general! Also, the class felt fair to me (I'm not cracked at CS).
