Prof. Shagan is the best! The topic is already interesting for History nerds like me, but he made it very interesting. I love how clear and organized he is with his lectures. You can tell he has an outline in his head and it helps you to take notes accordingly. TAKE GOOD NOTES- that's all he tests on. I don't think I opened the text book once.

This professor has a great sense of humor, knows his stuff, and made an already interesting topic fascinating.  I would highly recommend this professor and given the large number of students that stayed in his class the entire semester and the lack of seats from others showing up just to hear him lecture, others would seem to agree.

RUN 
RUN 
RUN
Never post any slides or recording and test questions are all about tiny things mentioned in lecture. Worst prof
no no no no no

Literally mid. He's not the worst but he's not the best either. If you are a solid studier who just needs to get a rec out of the way, just dig your heels in and do it. If you want to actually enjoy the material and do your requirement, he'll bore you.
He's honestly pretty nice. As long as you put in the effort, you should get a good grade. He does assign readings that might come up during a midterm/final so be aware of that.

8 am lectures w/o recordings, unresponsive when GSIs didn't print enough midterms & we still had to take the test in the morning with HALF our time cut, DEDUCTS points (-1) when you get a MCQ wrong on MTs and finals, long readings that are mainly all his own research papers and barely have anything to do with econ concepts. 

DON'T TAKE FOR SANITY
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: 8am 2x a week. No notes posted. No lecture recordings. VERY limited exam review material-1set of practice problems w/ key. no past exams. Unfair grading practices. 50% averages on midterms. GSIs forgot to print 1/2 of the midterms and he wasn't respond to any of their calls. we had to take the full mt with
I cannot believe that my tuition goes to his 500k salary.

This class was insane. Majority of your grade was a midterm and a final (composing 55%). Did not even have practice exams, only one packet of "practice problems" that did not have an answer key and far more difficult than what was taught in lecture or was on the homework. Tests were very difficult. mandatory lectures with no recordings or slides.

The negative reviews are from people who didn't come to class. He's a solid lecturer and there's not too much homework. If you read the textbook and come to lecture, you'll get a good grade. But it is very test-heavy - one midterm and the final is most of your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: i had no econ experience. bro really needs to either post lecture recordings or at least give the slides (he does neither for an 8am). the final had questions that were on topics about lecture. i got an A- without ever going to lecture for the second half of the course and just read the textbook. curve is crazy. he is not a good prof at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASSES. Professor Moretti has A LOT to improve on. Only having a midterm and final (worth 55%) for an intro class is actually crazy. The practice problems were WAY HARDER than the problem sets and he didn't give answer keys. The tests were HARD and the lecture slides weren't posted at all. The class was more stressful than needed!
No class structure. No textbook.  Incoherent. Overall bad prof.
Great at explaining concepts, provides ample examples, and frequently stops to accept questions. Lectures end early so he can talk to students. Weekly problem sets take
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Horrible professor. Doesn't release lecture slides for a mandatory class that is at 8 in the morning. The class is also extremely test heavy and there is not much partial credit. He is one of the worst professors I have had at Berkeley.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor is not responsible and he doesn't care for his students. He doesn't genuinely want to help you to succeed. He never post solutions to practice midterm/final, he ask GSI's to do some of them during review session, which also isn't posted. He only have one office hour, and the location is right outside of the lecture hall.

Okay professor. Doesn't release lecture slides for a mandatory 8am which didn't help increase attendance. went too fast in lecture and was so passive aggressive. Only gave one practice midterm and one practice final, both of which were not like the actual exam, didn't release keys either. HW was nowhere near difficulty of tests. Wouldn't take again
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Mediocre lecturer who often went too fast and finished early. This would've been good if he released his lecture slides for an 8 AM class, but he didn't. He also only released one practice midterm and final, and he did not release an answer key for either, leaving the GSIs with different answers from each other.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class is structured extremely poorly. Enrico acts like a nice guy but I found him to be very passive aggressive and occasionally rude. The class is also extremely test heavy and there is not much partial credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lectures are very interesting; he discusses interesting researches related to topics we learn. And the course is not hard as long as you stay on track. Definitely recommend this course!
One of the worst professors I have had at Berkeley.
The class was structured horribly, the midterm was nothing like the practice exam and was graded on minute details rather than an understanding of the material, and he is extremely rude.

1. He requires mandatory attendance for an 8am class
2. He doesn't post his lecture slides for "better engagement"
3. He gave only one practice midterm that's nothing like the actual midterm. The average was 50%
Overall, his class is very poorly structured. Wouldn't recommend.

Any Econ 1 class will be difficult and content heavy, but Moretti's was slightly easier to get a good grade as opposed to the other. There are problem sets every week worth 10%, one midterm on micro worth 30%, the final is worth 50% and then section is worth 10%. If you grind right before the midterm and final you can get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I thought he was really cool. He always talked to students after class and seemed to really want to help us learn. I was following along with the content until the end, when I fell off because of the GSI strike. The tests are hard. If you do the work (problem sets) and pay attention in lecture, you don't need to read so much.

Good lectures, don't have to read the chapters from the textbook but it's helpful. Moretti's nice, funny, answers questions. Show up to discussions and speak every time to get full points! Problem sets every week for completion credit. Midterm was very hard, abstract, and all about concepts. Heard Campbell's class had their final on completion.

Professor Moretti's Econ 1 class has only 2 important grades - a midterm worth 20% and a final exam worth 50%. I took this class during the GSI strike - Campbell allowed his students to take the midterm home and graded final exam for completion. Moretti offered no extra credit or bonus material even though we had no support. Final had a 65% mean.

Moretti the embodiment of pure hatred. For our final he gave us 46 mc questions on canvas that's worth 50% of our grade. Class average was like a 65% and only one person out of 200 got above 90%. No one got perfect. I would advise other's to stay away from this professor when they take Econ 1 next year.

His policies are awful. Hard multiple choice 46 question final (50% of our grade) when the other class got an auto-A essay. Our midterm avg was a 68 and Campbell's was an 88. Moretti is distinguished/smart/good at answering questions, but those benefits don't outweigh the costs of a grade that'll likely be 10% lower than if you had Campbell.

Nice guy but maybe teaching isn't his thing. New textbook this year but his lecture doesn't help. Just summarizing the book. Final counts for 50% towards your grade, no practice exam, never sent out lecture slides, also there's no recording.

Moretti is by far one of the worst professors I've had at Cal. I enjoyed the Econ 1 material, however he makes learning more difficult for students. His final exam was worth almost half our grade. He also made the final harder than all of the practice exams, and put an insane # of questions for the given time constraint. A horrible professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof Moretti is alright. Seems like he tries to help students out but prof's decision to make a 44 multiple-choice question final exam worth 45% of grade (timed and locks answered questions once completed), was kinda excruciating. a lot of ppl went from solid A's down to B's just because of the final.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This was kind of a meh class; nothing to really complain about but not phenomenal by any means. The final was 45% of our grade which was scary. Enrico seems like a nice guy but its hard to truly know in a class of hundreds. The readings were interesting but lectures were kind of bland. If you did well in AP econ you will probably do well.

The professor answers questions but is kind of boring, but I speak from zoom experience. My GSI was the toughest grader, never got a perfect score on any of the homework, always got like 9.25 out of 10 or something similar. Essays were roughly graded as well, we had two of them. Just super hard to get a good grade, no matter how hard you tried.

not much feedback in this class which makes you really confused about grades. but thankfully the econ 1 textbook reading is relatively easy (definitely easier than reading for AP history) and if you just do the reading you can ace the homework and tests. i never watched lecture and left with an A-
One of my favorite profs ever. If you stayed after lecture to ask a question, he always was willing to talk. Genuinely a great guy, a great teacher, and would take him again.

Lectures are super fast-paced, but the worst part is he doesn't post them online. Therefore, you might fall behind and end up having to read a whole chapter out of the textbook even after listening to his lectures. Other than that, his grading is clear and exams aren't bad.

Very disorganized class with unreasonable policies (e.g. no electronics in lecture to take notes, no webcasts or posted lecture notes). Mandatory attendance is bad enough but his lectures are unhelpful, dry, and he sidetracks a lot. Exams are also very difficult and unfair, grading is also very harsh. Steer clear of this prof if you can.

Moretti is a decent choice for intro econ. He's a nice and approachable guy and has a passion for the subject. His lectures are alright - but do read the book - he loves to pull examples/content for exams. This semester was dicey for all classes in terms of grading due to these circumstances. Reviews from other semesters might be more applicable.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Overall this class was OK. His lectures weren't too complicated but his class is pretty disorganized and not really set up for people to succeed. He likes to answer questions during lecture which helpful. My GSI was great for this class and I always felt supported by her. Enrico is fine to take Econ with but other professors are better.
Doesn't post lecture notes, but an easy and interesting class

IMO his teaching and pace is respectable, stops frequently to allow for questions. But the way he handles logistic procedures is terrible. No regrades allowed, even my own GSI thought my answer was correct. Grade weights changed due to corona, final worth less. HW weight increased, but no drops allowed. 2020 Spring head GSI super cocky, unhelpful.

I can state with confidence that this is the worst econ class ever. 20% of the first midterm asked questions on an article that was sent 2 days before the test in an obscure email. Not only that, but the grading criteria was heavily changed midway through the semester. To any freshmen or sophomores needing an Econ class: Please, PLEASE TAKE ECON 2
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I enjoyed Professor Moretti's lecture style as he was open to answering all questions that he was asked. But the GSI section is where the class fell for me. They are fairly harsh in terms of grading. And while the slides are nice, all of the info is in the book, so be sure to read (as it can give a better grasp on the info from lecture)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: There are many aspects of Moretti's class that make an otherwise simple topic, intro econ, impossible to keep up with. No course capture, no phones in class (can't take pictures of slides) the man speeds through lectures so I often have question marks all over my notebook, and NO REGRADES on hw or exams, even if your GSI majorly messed up grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Did not like this professor at all. Had really strict policies and wasn't very understanding. He did not post lecture slides to encourage in class attendance, but he would always go super fast and did not give us enough time to copy down the notes. He even yelled at us for using our phones even though we were just trying to take pics of the slides.

Midterm was wack, but it's nothing studying and paying attention in discussion can't fix. The textbook is really your best friend; his lectures are frankly boring & not that helpful. However, he does have passion for econ & I feel bad he has to teach Econ1 (I can see the boredom in his eyes). Wholesome man, I love the way he says "zlope".

Lectures often went off the topic about things that weren't really central to the class. The content wasn't too difficult, but the lectures weren't very helpful. Lectures notes are also not posted online.

NEVER take Econ1 with this professor. Horrible lectures, ridiculous course policies(they never release answers for anything, not even for practice tests they give to prep for the actual midterms and finals).

The lecture pace generally drags(Italian accent tho) and reading the text makes me understand better than lectures, though being there still helps. The midterm had an unfairly hard last question that bombed a lot of people. He seemed very helpful to students, but there's definitely not much attractive of his lecture that makes me want to go back.

I really liked Enricos lecture style. He is very clear and always ensures to pause for questions in order to clarify concepts. I never read, but I attended nearly every lecture and discussion section, and I scored way above the mean for the midterm. Its really not as hard as people make it out to be, and Ive never taken an Econ class before this.

Moratti does not teach at all. He just reads off of lecture slides which can be pretty dry. You solely depend on your GSI to basically teach you the concepts besides doing independent reading yourself. You are graded on literally three things : the midterm, a tiny paper, and the final. Be wary of this class if you do not have a background in Econ!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Exams are graded very strictly. One thing that drew me back about Moretti was his accent, it just made lecture slightly more difficult to understand. Lectures weren't particularly useful or helpful and felt lifeless and boring at times.  Exams are above average difficulty, so do lots of practice problems. Go to review sessions and youll be fine.

fair test, but grades very STRICT, get points off for the different wording, etc. but overall very enthusiastic, kind-hearted professor. I actually liked going to his lectures because he is a very nice guy and teaches with passion. Too much work in sectionsdiscussions. Lots of tedious stuff. I wish he just assigned more practice problems.

He lectured on the easiest parts of the reading and didn't really delve into the harder stuff. Used really clear examples that did help clarify. You need to go to lectures to get clicker points, but it's up to you to decide to pay attention. I did because I found the streamlined lecture points to be useful for studying but I had friends didn't

Everyone struggled with time on the midterm. I got slightly below average on the midterm because I didn't budget time well. Still got an A because I did all of the practice problem on the back of each chapter to prepare for the final. A lot of the questions on the final were similar to the book questions.

Lectures straight from the slides. If you do the problem sets and actually read the textbook you'll get an A. Grading criteria is not clear and he did throw a few curveballs on the final. Overall fair professor. He is quick to respond to emails and is available in office hours if you need extra help.

he gives very engaging lectures, stops very often to answer questions. very knowledgeable. tests are not very hard but are VERY strictly graded. definitely go to his lectures, as it's the only way you can write notes down.
Knowledgeable professor, boring class.

His lectures were extremely engaging and thorough, with powerpoint slides and many examples. He spoke slowly and clearly and always offered to answer questions. His midterm was hard but the final was fair. Overall, one of the best and most invested professors I've ever had!
Interesting class but tests almost have nothing to do with textbooks or notes

Took my first econ class at Berkeley w/ Enrico and he was pretty awful. He barely touches on anything in lecture and goes off on tangents, plus his midterms and final are all massive curveballs that no one sees coming. READ THE TEXTBOOK because tests look similar to examples in there and look nothing like the problem sets. Go to lecture if you want
Boring lecture and a lot of people fall asleep and don't come to class

Prior to taking this class, I had heard that Econ 140 was a notoriously difficult class. However, Professor Moretti ensured that this was not the case. He was clear and succinct during lecture, gave very fair (if not a little bit too easy) tests, and provided great examples to illustrate the concepts. I would highly recommend taking his class!
Complete bad ass.  Extremely clear and teaches the class concepts and foundations that are important for later material.  One of the best profs i have had at Cal.
Overall a good class. He focuses a lot on proofs. Very helpful outside of class.

Taught the lower level econometrics class like it was a math class.  Half the final was proofs. If I wanted to take a math class I would've taken calculus; like I need to ever know in the future how to prove heteroskedacity.  AVOID.

I think he taught this like 141.  The midterm was really easy and the final much harder.  Lots of proofs, problem sets totally useless since they involve stata and exams do not.  Book doesn't have a lot of practice problems.  Probably big mistake to take Econ 140 with this kind of prof if you're not good at theory.
long hard problem sets, not enough hard examples in class
Clear lectures and takes the time to answer questions.  Long problem sets.  Tough exams with low means.  Very approachable, agreeable and willing to help in office hours, etc.
Holy bruh. Is this real life
Bad lectures, even worse exams. Tends to use past problems from previous exams so make sure to study those. Avoid if possible.

Professor Ma copies+pastes screenshots from the textbook onto his slides and then does practice problems from the same book. He does not explain the respective material well. I did not go to lecture after midterm 1 because it does not help. I wish I could have had a better dynamics education, because this is the field I'm interested in. Thx Berk.

I believe most reviews on this professor are a bit harsh. His lectures were clear and assignments were fair. They were difficult but everything was doable given the course material, I only struggled at times because I am not that smart. The professor is very caring and approachable. The course was well done and organized.

Exams take up most of your grades, but they're compiled from old exams and homework (60% of my grade were copying down from cheat-sheet). Have to pay for a program ($70-80) for HW that tests you on textbook problems. Boring lecture, most students stop showing up and just study from lecture notes, HW, and past exams. Not helpful outside of classroom

90% of your grade is from exams and 10% is from homework. You're forced to pay $80 to actually do the homework as most of it is online with no opportunity for late work or individual accommodations. Lectures were basically just screenshots from the textbook which did not help reinforce content, it is easier to just read.

Avoid if at all possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: His lectures are useless, its essentially spark notes of the textbook with even worse explanations. Paid homework service, tough grading, and overall lack of beneficial material. Bad instructor, avoid if possible.

The vast majority of students in the class abandoned his lectures and just read the book. His lectures are literally just screenshots of textbook material. Grading was tough and the curve was large: I got a 73% on the final (which was 40% of the grade) and still got an A in the class.

Not only was the lectures horrendous and the grading atrocious, but there were 2 instances in his class in which inappropriate adult content was seen/heard from his computer. Multiple witnesses to this from Fall 2022. I am extremely surprised he is still teaching.

He reads directly from his slides which look copied and pasted from the textbook. His lectures are mostly useless. The textbook he uses isn't the best. Homework requires you to pay for WileyPlus. If you are a DSP student with extensions on assignments, wiley doesn't permit individual extensions and neither does he.

DO NOT TAKE MECENG 104 WITH MA. He is honestly the worst lecturer I have ever had. His lectures are just slideshow presentations of the textbook's example problems. Homework questions do not reflect on the tests. He's played out loud pornographic content during the final. Midterms are incredibly harsh (
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very test heavy and exam-oriented. 45%  final, 25%  midterm 2, 20%  midterm1, 10%  Online Homework (WileyPlus). Attendance is not mandatory. He followed his PowerPoint slide very closely.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: lectures absolutely suck. disorganized and heavy accent. stopped going and read the book myself.

Good lectures. Obviously very knowledgeable about the subject and follows the textbook closely. Even though we transitioned to an online homework system, the problem sets prepared us well for the exams.

He would not exist if not for his textbook. Seems as if someone forced him to teach a class, and somehow the students are at fault. Final is now 45%(instead of 60%), but the lectures are painful to sit through (more or less reads the textbook). Senior year and the worst I've had so far. Avoid at all cost if you can.

He is THE worst professor I ever had in my life. I never found out what he was talking about in lectures. Couldnt even read the blackboard with his terrible and handwriting and because he doest push the chuck. Goes on and off about topic and both discussions and lectures do homework problems from textbook. It is the worst thing you can imagine.

Grading system sucks, but Ma himself is a very average ME professor. Lectures are slow but help with homework. Problem tests are fair and tests represent the hard problems or what is gone over in class. He's no O'Reilly and the 60% final is a big concern, but the material is inherently learn-by-doing and Ma facilitates it well.
Final is 60%. Speaks about unnecessary stuff instead of just doing the problems. Not the best lecturer, but for 104 there is enough in the book and online to get by.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Ma lectures are whimsical and useless. He double penalizes on things that really don't show Dynamics ability. For instance, I lost 80% credit for messing up two unit conversion systems in the Imperial Customary units. He believes that 1 mistake is ok, but two is not, hence 30% for the wrong answer and 50% for wrong units. Curves to B-. AVOID,

Just bad... DEFINITELY has a chip on his shoulder. Overwhelmingly pedantic & wastes time like you wouldn't believe. When people talk about "slogging it out" with a bad professor for an entire semester, this guy is a textbook example. You've been warned.

I don't think I would recommend this professor to anyone. He spends at least 10 minutes every day discussing how his grading system works, and then has the nerve to start an example with five minutes to go and holds us past the hour. Never gives real world examples, because his entire world is based in academia. Take it with someone else if you can

Normally I don't really talk badly about professors, but Ma is truly one of a kind... It's kind of a hit or miss with him, most people don't really like him, but some do. He spends so much time talking about the most irrelevant stuff, if you have the choice, take 104 with Tongue he is definitely the guy for this class. The Final is 60% of the grade
He's pretty good at presenting ideas in a logical way, and is well prepared before lectures. Very nice and patient in answering questions, and quite helpful overall.
The exams are 90% of the grade. The lectures are not that well.
Hard class, couldn't pay attention to his lectures. If you like the straight-out-of-the-book teaching method, take his class. Tests are worth 90% of the class
Fair and consistent.

Prof Ma can seem a little rigid, but he is fair and consistent.  His lectures were pretty standard, but clear and helpful nonetheless.  Homeworks increased in difficulty as the semester progressed.  Exam questions ranged from fair to incredibly difficult.  He likes to give test that "produce a good bell curve"
He's a boring lecturer, but he goes at a good pace and is fair with exams and homework.

Difficult tests and lots of homework, but not unreasonable. Stays to the fundamentals, but often elaborates excessively on a single topic, especially administrative stuff. It may take a while to get used to his accent. The book was pretty helpfull and concise.

This is easily one of the worst professors I have ever had...I quote "I am not a nice guy...if you are looking for a nice guy...you are in the wrong class."  Plus...hte book he uses sucks.  Take it with Tongue if you can because he uses a really good clear reader that is sooooooo much better.

Professor Fang Xu is awesome. She is super knowledgable about her field and loves to facilitate group discussion. I've been super grateful to learn not only from her but from the diverse linguistic perspectives that she encourages to be shared in class. She takes the time to learn every student by name and she's funny too!!

While the course material is interesting, the professor is not lenient at ALL with absences, even with illnesses, considering this is a 3x a week class. The GSI and professor don't communicate, which leads to awful grading. So many presentations and discussions that don't contribute to anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr.Xu is a great lecturer, however, assignment rubrics are not clearly communicated at all. Students who followed her advice would often end up losing points in the process. She claims to be accommodating, but refuses to allow absences due to illness without a doctors note. The reader for this course is cold and clearly dislikes their job.

Fang's lectures are very clear and relevant to the assignments she gives. Readings are mandatory, don't slack in the first few weeks, those are the toughest ones. Grading depends on the GSI's, one GSI was a harsher grader. Discussions help with the denser readings. 3 short papers, 5 in-class quizzes (based on completion), midterm exam, final exam
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Xu is a GEM !!! Take her Language and Identity class. She is such a good lecturer, super interesting topic, good readings, good amount of assignments but not very difficult. She knows so much and is very well-versed. I love her !! Super smart!

Fine professor in terms of teaching, but class was managed very poorly. She only had one assignment in the grade-book before the P/NP deadline and didn't see an issue with that. She also miscommunicated with my GSI multiple times about grading rubrics for essays which cost many their grades.

Fantastic professor - had her for ISF 189 and ISF 100C as well. She is clear about her grading criteria and her lectures are posted online (with audio). Provides excellent feedback and is readily available via email or during office hours. If you follow her assignments closely and revise based on feedback, it is not hard to receive a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Fall 2018 is the first time Dr. Xu has taught ISF 100A, so not sure why students have left reviews with their grades when final grades have not been released yet. Grading on essays is difficult and Dr. Xu has high expectations for tests (you are expected to reference specific details in order to do well).
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: 3 reflections, quizzes, a mid-term and a final. The reflections are not bad but do not wait until the last minute. You're supposed to keep them between 350-400 words but you will not be marked down for going over. Attendance matters in class and in discussion, that was almost 20% of the grade. I recommend skim reading, don't need to read everything

I wish I would've taken this class sooner, I have no idea why I was so scared of it to begin with. Professor Xu structured this class very well. Everything is very clear. The lab assignments may present technical difficulties at times so make sure you do not miss those days. Participation and attendance are a huge help. It is hard not to earn an A
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Gosh I love her. She really grew on me. She is so intelligent! I could not stand reading Marx in the beginning but thankfully the material lightened up. There are reading quizzes but not very difficult, 3 writing reflections, a midterm and a final. Attendance matters! Ask questions and form study groups and you'll at least earn a B.

Laptop use not allowed unless it's lab day and/or you're DSP. This class is very clear & straightforward. Prof Xu encourages participation. Feel free to ask questions and she will gladly answer. The class starts off busy but calms down towards the end. All assignments help you create an end of semester research proposal. Don't worry it's not bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I'm so glad I took research methods with Xu. By far the most organized professor I EVER encountered. I highly suggest having your thesis topic narrowed down as much as possible so u can get the most out of this class & not waste your time. Bring your laptop with you on lab days so you can minimize take home work. Attendance/participation matters!

Professor Xu is a sweetheart. I dreaded this class and it actually got easier, not harder. You start with Marx and then move on to more contemporary philosophers who are much easier to understand. The reading was reasonable and luckily. she lectures so well that you do not have to read word for word. She mixes up the class too (which I like).

Professor Xu is wonderful. ISF 100A is not an easy class because there's a lot of theory and complicated readings but, she will not overwhelm you with reading assignments. Her lecture powerpoints are clear and straightforward. She also incorporates videos and other materials to help you understand the subject matter better.

Professor Xu comes off cold but she is really sweet. Her lectures and grading criteria are very clear. I don't think she is a difficult grader, she is pretty fair. I enjoy attending her office hours, she is always willing to help you understand something but also not a push over either. I highly recommend taking her for research methods.

I took Prof. Farghal for 4A. This class is super easy to get an A in. She isn't the best at lecturing, it's very surface level. But she is very nice, cares about her students, wants you to pass the class. Responds to emails quick as well. Your grade is just based on a couple quizzes and the final.

The best professor. I took her Physics 4A at De Anza. She's probably one of the best professor that gives the easiest gradings. She only have quizzes and finals exam. The quizzes are on mondays. Quiz are super easy. It's only once question and super super easy. Final exam is very manageable with two hours. I finished the exam in one hour. Pick Her!
Super nice teacher would recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Too many "ums" during the lecture. She might need to practice her presentation skills. It's not pleasant to listen to lectures with frequent pauses. Can be more prepared!

The lecture is too long without a clear focus. No emphasis on what to study. Also, I hate group project in an online environment especially we never see our classmates. Group project are good for GSI so they don't have to grade too much but not good for student. However, prof is nice.

Each assignment worth a lot since so little so MUST do well on all. Prof was nice and passionate but lectures were unnecessarily long (and you have to watch since the slides don't have anything on them besides symbols). Responds quickly to e-mails which is great and is willing to clarify all the time.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I had this professor and for our midterm he didn't allow me and a few other students to start the midterm until after 30 minutes (out of 1:30). Every other student was allowed to start. His reasoning was that we didn't come to lecture enough

Prof armero is a great guy but he does not teach the best unfortunately(might have been an off semester as he was dealing with health and personal issues). you could tell he wants students to suceed and really tried to get to know people but it was hard to understand lectures. he curved really hard and gsi eduardo was the goat
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: the exams are very challenging, but if you practice w/ tau beta pi you should survive(though the final is 30% more complicated then the ones on there). he still have a good sense of humor and will answer questions more in depth after class or in OH fairly well. Also sit in front row, he likes front row students a lot.

Nice guy but not good at explaining concepts. Lectures are confusing and do not prepare you for homework or exams. Midterm was fair but final was very challenging. Gives bonus points to students who show up to class and participate.

I don't know why this guy has such a high rating. He is a nice guy, sure, but a bad teacher. He rambles. He is bad at explaining. His tests have material that wasn't on the homework or taught in class. Also, he goes over time. Sometimes he finally stops talking after an hour and a half.

Tries to learn the names of every student in the class. Good shift to online learning Spring 2020. Very funny and will call you out in class. Tests are difficult but follow an exact template he talks about before the test, so you can pinpoint your studying. Likes bicycles.

Profs are supposed to teach the concepts while GSIs teach you to do problems. Armero and GSI Jorge mastered this arrangement. Exams are very reasonable and test the same kind of questions every year. I think he genuinely enjoys teaching. A lot of his bad ratings are from CE130/92 - if you are taking him for CE30/ME85, he's a solid choice.

Hes a CEE prof. alright? So, he covers most concepts with Structural application (bars, columns...). Alright, ok! Hard to understand at times because he has some accents. But, he excellent if you pay attention always. Very into Mr. hinge. Has two projects for extra credit. If you are ME, choose the other Professor unless you cant. More ME stuff.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is not the best at explaining things, so I learned everything from the GSI and book. His lectures didn't seem to be related to the homework or exam problems, so make sure to read the book and do extra practice problems. He notices whether you come to class, so try to ask and answer questions to get participation points.

Not the best professor. Tries to make lectures funny, but cannot explain concepts in simple terms. The book is your best friend. Your time would be best spent doing sample problems from the book instead of going to lecture. However, he does not give much work and his tests are relatively straightforward.

Clear lectures. Tests and midterms were kinda tough, but straightforward and similar to practice ones. Sometimes lectures get boring, but thats the nature of the subject. If you truly understand the concepts, you should have no problem doing well. He's also a pretty funny, approachable guy, definitely recommend his class.

Decent professor. I never thought the material was challenging but the competition was bit stiff. 100% on homework assignments and above-average scores on the midterm and the final was only good for a B. Regardless, I definitely learned a lot from him which is essential for upcoming upper-div ME courses.

This guy was the best professor I have had at Berkeley. His lectures are extremely well organized and crystal clear.  He seems really serious at first but he turned out to be hilarious. This class was a lot of work though, so be prepared.  But he is a fair grader and curved his ridiculously hard final.

He is very good at teaching concepts, you really feel like you understand when he lectures (which are excellent), but HW is on the hard side. Midterms are not bad at all (averages were MT1 73 and MT2 84). His Final was killer though!!! It was sooo hard (for the whole class), but grades are curved so it should be fair. Overall he's great(funny too)!
the stuff he cover in the class is not relate 2 to exam too much, the homework is helpfulless
One of the worst classes I had at Berkeley!

I really enjoyed Armero's class. Study hard and you will get a decent grade. If it is just to satisfy req's, take it with easy profs (although it really shows that students don't get much out of taking their classes, esp with Li).

The tests were very difficult.  I could do all the homework, and try at it for hours and still get zeros on the assignments, it was very discouraging.  His teaching did not at all align to the book and so there was nothing to cross reference.  The lectures were good, but with no additional reference it was hard.

Excellent lecturer, one of the best I've had at Berkeley.  1st exam was moderate, 2nd was difficult, final was next to impossible.  Too bad final is 50% of the grade.  The text used was the worst I've ever seen.  Armero assigns extremely hard HW problems.  I heard Lubliner's class was a joke by comparison.  Explains concepts very well, but tough.
He is alright

Who knew you had to do work for a 1-unit class?! And how disorganized is it possible to be, I think I'm going to fail the class if he keeps losing my stuff. 1-unit classes aren't worth this much effort, take it when someone else is in charge
Exams were very difficult, class average was always in the 50's.
Clear communication, lecture notes are easy to understand. Answers Q's thoughtfully.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: His lectures are great and he is pretty clear when he explains; but there is often not too much text on the slides and he speaks pretty fast, making it hard to write down all of the notes. i recommend recording his voice and going back to understand the experiments as those should be known extensively.

Probably one of the best lecturers in MCB - extremely clear, concise, and organized; loves what he teaches and studies. Extremely helpful in office hours as well. Interesting topics (very heavily neuro-based) are covered, but this course may be drastically different next year since it's still new.

He's amazingly knowledgeble and also super clear about what he expects students to know. His lectures notes are very detailed so don't really need to read textbook. He speaks fast and covers a lot of materials very rapidly in every lecture so it's definitelyt helpful to record them an re-listen.

Agree with everything comment below has to say except that I'd add that he is downright mean in office hours. He morally degrades students.  I literally saw him question a student's attendance in lecture. Jerk
Prof. Feldman is ridiculously smart. In addition, he is crystal clear in his lectures and his tests are very fair.
Amazing Prof 10/10

He is obviously really good at Chemistry but he is not good at teaching students who aren't naturally good at or previously experienced with it. I found his class very difficult as someone who hadn't taken AP Chem in high school. He seemed very snobby, as if someone who didn't understand what he is teaching is dumb.

Toste is a decent professor and a real chemistry whiz, but I noticed pretty early on that teaching doesn't seem to be what he's here for. There were a few occasions when students tried to ask questions and he refused to answer, however he still gave great demos and had a sense of humor!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Chemistry at Cal is challenging in general but Dean is a great professor and makes lectures entertaining and concepts easier to understand. Study hard, do the homework, ask questions, and go to lecture and you will pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Pretty easy class. Two in class lab reports that are just the discussion and post-lab questions in the book. NMR section was really tough, but if you go to office hours the GSI's will answer every confusing question for you. Final was also very easy.
Meh. He's alright, but the lectures weren't very useful. It's a relaxing way to spend a Wednesday afternoon when you have nothing to do.

i foolishly decided to take this class for fun.  turned out that i wasn't as much of an organic chem whiz as i had thought.  i should have put in more effort. no textbook, must attend class and pay attention (class goes by quickly, he's easygoing and fun). easy to be in the mean of the class but must go above and beyond to get an A.

considering he taught us something that had no text to go with it, he did an excellent job. He's brilliant and he's totally approachable and clear. His class is not easy, but it's definitely not because he's a bad teacher.
This guy really really knows his stuff. And he knows how to teach. He gives creative demos to willing volunteers. I like O-Chem more now.
He was pretty straightforward, but he didn't have a book which sucks if you don't go to class.  Don't take his course if you don't plan on paying attention.  His tests were kinda hard too.

I thought he was a great professor. He showed us very interesting aspects of chemistry and tried hard to make things clear. The beginning was rocky but then it got a LOT better. OH are very helpful and he is very approachable.
he was damn difficult...make sure you understand the concepts...his exams are mostly applications of concepts rather than repeating the information...damn i got 0w///3|) on that final
Pretty good
rather annoying
No Comments
Great lecturer, cares a lot but I've never seen a more horrid syllabus in my life.

One of the best lecturers that I have had at Berkeley. Exams are not difficult if you have watched all the lectures and done the HWs. She genuinely cares about making sure students understand and is very accessible on Edstem as well.

If you haven't understood the HWs, you won't be able to derive the linear algebra frqs on the exams.

Prof Ranade's lectures were pretty good, if slightly boring. Her homeworks are exams are killer though, definitely need to prep a lot for them. She is accessible during OH and the staff are helpful though.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Compelling lecturer, great person. But calling on people at random, presumably to see if they are paying attention, in lecture is immature and giving tests that are meant to be taken over the course of 110 minutes in an 80 minute section doesn't make a whole lot of sense.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She is very good at explaining the material and and she is able to answer every student's question with clarity. The discussions are helpful and if you go to lecture and do the homework, the exams are fairly straight forward. My favorite professor so far!!

Early in the course, I found myself disliking professor Ranade. I thought her class was too hard and she didn't run it well. However, being honest, my poor performance was often due to my own lack of effort into the course. I'll admit, the course is challenging, but if you do everything that is asked of you, there is nothing hard about it.
Prof.Ranade's 127 is great. But get ready to work hard as she is like your big sister who expects you to go grad school

Took Ranade for 16A and B, loved her for both. 16B was significantly harder for me, but I was a lot less prepared for it. Go to lectures and take good notes. Discussion helps a ton. She has super organized lectures and exams that are patterned after the homework and discussion.

I LOVED Ranade's lectures. Super well organized, and she was willing to stop the class multiple times to go over confusing parts again. The class gives you so many opportunities to learn the material, from lecture to discussion to homework. However it is challenging, especially for someone new to circuits. The bin shift at the end was great, too

She knows several students who took 16A last semester and she was able to build upon concepts from 16A especially matrices. After an exam, she would have one-on-one talks. Many of the TAs are helpful during homework parties and office hours. The website has a clear grading scheme. This semester, it was lenient because of the pandemic.

Even though the course was a lot more chaotic being online during the pandemic, prof. Ranade really made it a lot easier on us with the staff review sessions before the final, the binshifts, the availability of course staff members for 1-on-1's and check-ins, etc. You can tell she genuinely cares about the students and wants us to do well.

After a year of being forced to take 16A/B, I now regret transferring to UCB. I have no respect for Sahai and Ranade--they force these classes on students to serve themselves. They disrespect circuit analysis to hide what 16A/B really is--a poorly taught intro to ML. At least 90% hate 16A/B, and have no use for it. Wasted two upper divs for me.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof. Ranade is very smart and knows her field, but her lectures are hard to follow at times especially in 16b so go to office hours. The GSI's that taught the discussions are life savers though. HW is REALLY long and sometimes doesn't seem to help.

Professor Ranade's lectures were the best thing about this class (which isn't saying much because this is the worst class I've taken in my entire life). Her lectures are clear and actually helped me understand the concepts more. However, the homework always takes so long (around 10 hours if you do the whole thing) and isn't that useful.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Took this class Spring 2021 and it is difficult class for no reason. Very disorganized and the TAs don't know how to handle the course
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: I took this class my first semester at Cal (Fall 2020) remotely. She gives interesting lectures and test was reasonably easy (very similar to homework). I have to say that 90% of the learning was done through homework and reading the notes. Didn't attend discussion and watched all lectures at 2 times speed. Make sure you understand every note well.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Professor Ranade explained things really clearly. She would always take the time to ask the class how we were feeling with the material and she thoroughly answered questions. Though I did not particularly love EECS16A, I also appreciated how excited Ranande got about the material, or the "magic." Her passion comes through. Exams are hard though.

I don't get why some people are being so negative. I took EECS16A this fall and I thoroughly enjoyed it. The course staff was super helpful on piazza, and the discussion sections were very useful. The class was pretty challenging but at the same time it wasn't overwhelming. I thought prof. Ranade did a great job!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Her class this semester was very time consuming with the homework and preparing for exams. Other than Moses I did not find any resources very helpful.

She is great at explaining concepts by drawing diagrams of circuits and other important concepts. She holds office hours after class and calms down students after the first midterm. Although I didn't have a real in person lab experience, I enjoyed building circuits at home and the software component. Homework and tests are long, but doable.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: EECS 16A was pretty useless but Ranade tried to make it better by having office hours and virtual things. I just found this class very disorganized. There were just  class notes outside her lectures and some useless textbook some clueless TA wrote which didn't help at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Her EECS16A class is a big time commitment. Labs, homework, lectures; all take a solid amount of time. Prof. Ranade seems fully aware of this and every aspect of her class is run really well. She makes sure to really drill in the most important concepts during lecture. Pretty fair grader too. Looking forward to EECS 16B.

Professor Ranade is a really passionate and intelligent educator. Her lectures are very good at explaining concepts and breaking them down into easy to understand parts. She will draw attention to the more important concepts but you should take time to pay attention to lectures and readings or you will feel behind. Homework if hard but important.

The most boring/useless class I've ever taken. The HW/exams are long/tedious and notes/lectures are poor/confusing. She does not write the exams, and the GSI's don't write well-structured exams. They are too many problems, and each question is a one-page essay written for children. Other past exams from other Prof.'s were much more concise.

Her course is structured well, she communicates very clearly (expectations, grades, what to know, etc), and is understanding of students. Her lectures aren't the best as she often takes a long time to explain one concept, but all-in-all the course is a tough, but you'll come out having learnt a lot.

Gireeja is one of the most caring professors I have met at Berkeley. However, she ought to prepare more for her lectures cause she does make quite a few mistakes that can be distracting and derail lecture for several minutes. I also wish she would be more transparent with her grading scheme.
Crystal clear lectures, fair tests, the right amount of homework. Overall a great class and she does a great job of teaching it.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Ranade is super eloquent, clear, and concise. She knows what she's talking about and is always ready to answer peoples questions. I think she's also encouraging. Sometimes lectures would get pretty boring, and I would recommend watching webcast if you prefer fast paced, as she speaks slowly (probably because this class is meant for freshmen).
Amazing and very clear lectures! Prof Ranade is willing to help us outside of the class. She makes ee16a clear and easy for understanding.

Professor Ranade isn't the best lecturer (ironic, since she basically wrote the content of the course). Going in with no linear algebra or circuits experience was tough, but asking a TON of questions in discussion, reading supplemental texts and lecture notes, doing homework diligently, and going to office hours helped me succeed in this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: I learned more about linear algebra and circuits from the notes and the optional texts assigned for the course. Going to lecture is absolutely worthless and the homework is unnecessarily long. You can get perfect scores on all the homework assignments but it all comes down to your performance on tests which are quite lengthy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Lectures are clear, tests are fair, homework is difficult. There is clearly a lot of thought and preparation that goes into each assignment which is nice because they are not easy assignments. Very rarely feel like you're doing busywork.

Most professors in college just regard teaching as job, but don't really care, while professor Ranade is one of the very few who actually cares about how students are doing and really want to make sure that her students are learn something. Perhaps a normal lecturer, but amazing teacher or educator. Remind me of my high school teachers.

Disproportionate amount of work combined with her rushed teaching style makes it hard to learn. Theres hw due on Fridays, self-grades due on Tuesdays, 3 hour lab, and two discussion sections, repeating every week. If you have no prior knowledge of linear algebra, you'll have to spend extra time outside of lecture going over concepts.
Not beginner-friendly, was difficult to understand her explanation of linear algebra

Lecture is boring, dull, and confusing. She also doesn't let you take notes on a tablet/laptop which is annoying since I do that for all my other classes. Hard to understand her mathematical notation and intuition if you have no linear algebra prior experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Great
No. Just no.
didn't learn anything in the architecture curriculum's FIRST foundation studio class.

didn't bother to look both ways when crossing the road when walking to this class she ruined my life. condescending and called her students slow to their faces. doesn't care about you or your work. will always find a way to make your life harder.

least favorite prof. she pretends to care about your health yet piles on the work and laughs about how tired her students seem afterward. not accessible, super vague, no sympathy (my friend had to go to a psych ward and paz gave her so little grace with extensions and did not offer any additional support to a student who was clearly suffering)

Gave no clear grading guidelines, tutorials were super vague, feedback and instructions were always unclear, overall difficult and draining class and professor. Gave an unfeasible amount of work every week.

really fun and passionate lecturer but respectfully what was that midterm. i hope it was fun to write, dr. gibbs. it wasn't fun to take. it wasn't fun at all. i hope you at least giggle when you grade it, maybe then my hour of suffering would be worth it..
Lectures incredibly dense and hard to follow for Gibbs. Try not to fall behind, read the textbook and lecture slides for genetics. Horrific unit. Stay strong u got this. The rest of the class is fun.
Currently pulling hairs out trying to interpret Dr. Gibbs' jumbled lectures.
Undoubtedly passionate, just be ready to pull a lot of extra weight to understand her jumbled lectures. A little unfortunate she is teaching the most dense unit of Bio 1A.
She talks fast and then stumbles over her words and loses track of what she is saying, gets very confusing during lecture so u have to do ur own research to figure out what she meant

Dr Gibbs is nice and caring, but she'd be even better if her lectures weren't chopped. she needs to either slow down or rehearse her lectures because her train of thought is not cohesive. very well might just be a skill issue on my part.
Too many "um" and "uh".. talks fast but not much information, slides are usually explained very briefly

She would only cover 40% of the slides in class yet still expects you to memorize every single detail for the exam. Not a good lecturer especially when genetics is arguably the hardest unit of bio 1A.

Bio1A sucks regardless of who you get. If you get Dr. Gibbs, use her as a resource! One of the most easily approachable professors and she is caring, kind, and great at explaining things in a simplified manner. She is so passionate about microbes, so if u can take gen microbiology with her, you should!

I had to select Bio 1A, but that is not the class I'm reviewing. Prof. Gibbs taught graduate-level Scientific Reasoning (PMB 210), and I'm reviewing for this class. This was an excellent class that discussed how scientific experts can advise and influence business and policy. Excellent discussions and good writing support for the paper. 10/10!

She could never cover all her slides in lecture because they were so long and expected you to finish them on your own. Her lectures weren't important in actually learning the topics. I ended up self-studying this unit using the slides and YouTube. The exam was fair and similar to the practice exams.

Gibbs was very enthusiastic about the subject, but she was not good at teaching it. Her slides were essentially just the textbook and she spent little time explaining anything really. She would often not finish her slides and the exam was very difficult. I had to self study the entire unit from her lack of clarification during lecture.

Beware! She says you don't need the textbook because everything's on the slides, but the slides are a total mess. Half the time I couldn't even tell if I understood English because the way she explains things makes zero sense. She can't explain even the simplest ideas. Unfortunately, she teaches the hardest section in Bio1A.

She packed a lot of things into one lecture but didn't go over them completely. The slides were very disorganized. I can't even get through one lecture recording b/c it's all over the place. I ended up having to use outside resources to understand her unit. Her exam was fair though.

Content was hard and her teaching method made it worse. Always rambled about things that seemed unimportant. She has a lot of energy at 8am which is a good and bad thing. Somehow I did better on the genetics midterm than Doudna's. Her lecturing is awful

Dr. Gibbs is clearly well-versed in her field of work, but is not the best at teaching biology at an introductory level. Her lectures have 63+ slides that are specified to be the "key summary" slides, or slides that would correlate with the important topics taught in lecture. I recommend reading the textbook before lecture and ATTEND OFFICE HOURS.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Gibbs is a great person, however her lectures are crazy long and she speaks way too quickly through them. Doesn't recommend reading the textbook but her slideshows are too hard to understand. Make sure course capture is available.

Dr. Gibbs is a very kind, caring, and engaging professor, but unfortunately she cannot teach. Her lectures often had 60+ slides and the information we were expected to know for the exam was not made clear. Struggles to explain even basic concepts so you will basically have to teach yourself this unit using the textbook. Do NOT fall behind this unit

girl... just when I thought bio 1a was gonna get better. Gibbs is so enthusiastic, smart and you can tell she knows her stuff but her teaching an INTRO to general bio was not the move. She doesn't finish her slides, talks super fast, and expects us to remember things she never went over (even though reading the textbook isn't mandatory).
Spends time rushing through the lecture but expects us to know so many minute details for the midterm. It is practically impossible to keep up with what she says during lecture.
Overpacked and rushed lectures. Poor planning. Hard midterm. I had to self-study almost all of the content. Least fun section of any class I have taken at this school.

Honestly very amazed at how the Spring 2025 staff managed to make every single worst possible choice while running this course. She is enthusiastic about the material but relies heavily on the students to read the material beforehand, because she doesn't get to finish most her lectures. Take when Mike Meighan retires and Lones teaches genetics.

She speaks in 5x speed but gets through less than half the material. It ends up being a game where you are trying to catch important terms and information between the "ums" in her lecture. She is enthusiastic about the material but that does not translate to being a good teacher.
Makes 60-90 slide lectures, gets to about 25 of them each class. So unorganized to the point where even she confuses herself on what lecture we are on. The exam was challenging for no reason.

I liked Dr. Gibbs as a person because I can tell she cares about students. But she was not that great of a teacher. She goes way too fast. She rushed through like 50-60 slides each class and wrote long and confusing exam questions. I'm in a genetics lab and I didn't quite understand what she was asking most of the time.

Dr.Gibbs is a really caring person and wants all of her students to succeed. The genetics unit was fast-paced and dense but she explicitly tells you what you need to know and into how much detail for the exams. Her office hours are a must!
Worst exam questions. Rushes through lectures.

Very very very hard lectures to follow, can't explain topics in a simpler to people completely confused on the subject (like myself). If you miss lecture, make sure to set aside 3 hours to catch up on the 70 slide lecture that makes 0 sense. Hardest midterm I've taken besides math 53 lol. You teach yourself this unit and it's a very hard unit.

Gibbs has more passion than some of the other Bio 1A professors but often talks so fast that she stutters on her words and doesn't fully finish sentences. Her slides are often 60 slides long and she rushes through lecture to try to get them done in time. The lectures feel rushed and therefore unclear

Very difficult to follow and lectures are terrible, she doesn't explain concepts properly and expects us to dedicate a ton of outside time to make up for the material she cannot cover due to poor planning.
Really hard to follow.

Gibbs taught the second unit of Bio 1A, which is probably content wise the toughest. She organized the slides very well and marked which one was important. Go to her office hour because she actually will tell you what she cares about and what you should focus on when studying. She also had Studio Ghibli themed test questions. Super adorable prof!

One of the 3 teachers teaching BIO1A SP'23. Definitely caring. She has lots of lecture slides and outside material for her students to understand the content better. I wouldn't say I enjoyed her section much because of how lecture heavy everything was. Oftentimes her ppts would be over 60 slides and it was overwhelming to study. Overall she's OK.

Professor Gibbs' section was very clear and easy to understand. Although the lectures are dense and fast, she provided many additional resources to supplement the material. Dr. Gibbs is approachable, understanding, and fair, with every question from the midterm being on her lecture slides, and I recommend going to her office hours for help.

Although Professor Gibbs was incredibly passionate and sweet, she was my least favorite of all Bio 1A professors. Her slides were long and not helpful for exams. Her questions are long, wordy, and difficult to understand. Doing well requires relying on AP Bio knowledge and reading the textbook. She does provide a lot of resources and help however.

Although Gibbs is teaching the "hardest" section, I found her having the most useful office hours and PPT where she clearly states the ideas that she wants you to know for the exam. She also works through problems in detail in class and in office hours. Although the course design makes this section a bomb of information, Gibbs really breaks it down

Spoke way too fast, had about 80-90 lecture slides during a 50 minute lecture, 3 times a week, all at 8am. Very hard to follow her lectures because she went so fast. She taught the genetics section and so it was a LOT of content and she could have organized it better so she was not so rushed during lectures. Exams and quizzes were difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: you really need to practice because even with knowing all the information, you won't be able to do well unless you can apply it.  she cares and is more approachable than doudna fs.
She was a terrible lecturer. Very unclear.
Did not enjoy her style of teaching at all. If you're taking Bio 1A with her be very cautious on her section.

LONG presentations she never finished. UNCLEAR grading expectations so basically everyone failed her two quizzes. On the other hand, her slides are clear and the big concepts are tested instead so her midterm was more than fair. She's not the worst and you'll be fine.

Overall reasonably fair with exam/quiz difficulty and she definitely is enthusiastic and passionate about what she teaches. My main complaint would be her slides; half the time she wouldn't be able to finish her 70-80 slide lecture within the hour and table discussion until later, making flow of information excessive and difficult to digest.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Gibbs gave fair exams, unlike Schekman. The lecture concepts were hard to grasp but she taught genetics which is known to be harder. Her lecture slides were good, with emphasis on points to understand. However, her lectures were confusing and she would sometimes contradict or correct herself. She seems very passionate and knowledgeable

Not really sure why her rating is so low, as her portion of the course was one of the easiest. I basically just watched lecture and read the books and ended up with a 96 on the midterm. Her exams are pretty straightforward, and unlike Schekman, there were very few abstract questions. Her lectures kinda sucked but she gives you key slides to study.

Tremendously disorganized. Rushes through slides which only halfway cover textbook material (all of which is fair game for exams), then revisits them a week later in a completely different context. Never had a worse case of deja vu. Avoid if you can

People did not like her and I never really understood why. I just reviewed the "mandatory" slides before the exam and I did well on her exam. I thought her section was the least dense and memorization-heavy section and her test was fair enough. I never went to office hours, and I never read the textbook. Look at the slides before the exam!

Her lectures are extremely disorganized and you never know what youll be tested on. She rambles a lot on info you dont need. She tells you she wont test you on it but SURPRISE its on a quiz. Avoid her if possible.

Dr. Gibbs just came here this semester so her genetics section was naturally a bit disorganized: there were no pre-lecture videos and readings did not always correlate well with lectures. I found her teaching style a bit dry although it seems like she'd be better in person. Sometimes slides she'd labeled as "extra info" showed up on tests

I like her enthusiasm in her lecture material, but her lecture skills ain't it. Idk what it was but her lectures were so dry and garbage I had to resort to studying in the textbook. She literally read straight from her slides and didn't elaborate on any bullet points. Worst professor out of the three imo.
The professor was very passionate about her research and area of study (genetics). READ the book and go to OH if you want to pass.

maybe she's a good researcher but definitely not a good teacher. Very unorganized lectures and slides. Studying by yourself can be much more efficient than listening to her lectures. Doesn't give pre-lecture video records as the syllabus says. Bad timing, always cannot finish what needs to be finished for one lecture.

Professor Gibbs is a new professor who is passionate about her work & teaching. Given it was her first time, she did a wonderful job despite the module being disorganized. However, she's a wonderful person & focuses mainly on lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: She is very enthusiastic about the topics that she lectures about and that makes class somewhat enjoyable. However, the way she runs the class is pretty disorganized. The lecture slides and the readings she assigns sometimes don't correspond to the lecture material and her explanations of topics can sometimes be vague.

As soon as Professor Gibbs took over the Bio1A lectures I felt more inspired than I ever have. She made me love biology because she's so passionate and makes things so interesting. She values students' understanding more than memorized textbook knowledge, and always tells you if you don't need to know something for the exam. She loves her job!
Absolutely unorganized. Doesn't cover material in lecture and expects you to come to class after memorizing material from the textbook. Hated by Bio 1A students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Studying for exams was a pain because you have to memorize so much at once with no cheatsheets, but the class was great! I learned a lot and found it quite eye-opening, and Dr. Presti was a fantastic prof and is so passionate about the material.
Favorite professor here so far. Loved this guy, reminds me of a very friendly elf. Very kind man. Go to lecture and study the concepts and you'll be okay.

Love him! Such a nice guy and great professor to have my first semester. Go to lecture although not mandatory, it'll solidify the concepts for you. Midterms are based on memorization of the key concepts. No final which was nice, the only thing is I had no idea what my final grade was going to be because he doesn't reveal distributions at all

Honestly class is super chill! And professor Presti is very passionate about neuroscience so it makes going to class that much more enjoyable. If you look at the key concepts you will do just fine in the exams. Really interesting class will highly recommend!

LOOK AT THE KEY CONCEPTS!!!! Seriously the only things you need to know are the key concepts and that can get you to an A, grade boundaries were strict (95 for an A) but they round and as long as you submit the homework you get 100 on those. Super interesting class that i think anyone should take, the content changed my POV and is useful to most

The class itself was extremely informative and interesting! Though it's a lot of material to memorize, taking physical notes really helps. There are 3 midterms and no final, and 6 homework assignments that are easy, reflective, and good grade boosts.
super nice teacher and super fun and interesting lectures. midterms directly cover what he says they will

dr presti gives fun hippie grandpa vibes, hes a very intelligent guy and the content was super interesting and unlike anything ive learned before. but go to lectures bc slides are unhelpful and not recorded, midterms require detailed memorization, and lectures were not really structured and felt like presti rambling for an 1hr30mins. not a free A
Absolutely loved this course and he is truly an amazing lecturer! Homework assignments were fun to complete with a small project at the end of the semester.

David E Presti is the best lecturer I have ever had. This was the first class I took at Berkeley. Drugs and the Brain was truly a paradigm-shifting class; you will emerge from it knowing much more than just simple chemistry, botany, and pharmacology. HW/assignments are very meaningful and enjoyable to complete. All majors should take this class.

He truly cares about the wellbeing of his students, not just academically, but mentally. We often would start class with a couple minutes of meditating, or whenever we talk about substance use disorders (the class I took is Drugs & the Brain) he always reviews methods of quitting that are proven to improve success rates. Fascinating class, loved it

I took this during the strike so this class ended up having an easy final and a lot of people passed. His lectures are so interesting and he's a charismatic person. It is a lot of content to memorize though. Overall, this class is very enjoyable if you're able to memorize a lot and find drugs interesting.

Presti's lectures are highly interesting; be sure to diligently take notes for the exams. The exams, although fairly easy, do require knowledge of some small details from lecture. The 6 homework assignments are easy and fun. Don't be afraid to ask questions/attend office hours, as Prof Presti is kind and knowledgeable. One of my fave classes here!
He was what made me consider neuroscience when I hadn't even considered that field before. I adored his class and I would love to have him as a professor again.

You can really tell Prof. Presti loves the subject he teaches. He teaches with a lot of passion and excitement which makes you enjoy his lectures. Exams were fairly easy with it all being online. The textbook he uses is actually written by him and he even brought a real brain to class once.

Such a cool and inspirational guy. Amazing lectures and cool anecdotes. However, the class is not an easy breadth that some may think. Lecture attendance isn't mandatory but slides are usually not posted. Class is heavily weighted on 3 midterms (but no final) and they aren't a cake walk. Homework assignments were fun though.

Presti is endearing in a "fun eccentric grandpa" way, kind, and super knowledgeable about subject matter. Take detailed notes during lecture, as tests (3 midterms, no final) require a good understanding of material and a bit of memorisation, and lecture slides are mostly visual aids to content. Homework is easy/creative, but class isn't a free A.

Fun balance of science and lore. Rushes through a LOT of content really fast and the 3 midterms are quite hard. You won't be able to understand much from the slides alone since they're a jumble of random pictures and words in Comic Sans, so go to lecture. Homework assignments are silly and easy. Interesting class, but not necessarily an easy A.
just an absolute gem
Presti's class is fascinating, with engaging lectures and a friendly demeanor. Prepare for memorization, but the material is worth it. unstuckstudy AI is great for study prep.

YALL SHOULD TAKE THIS CLASS WHENEVER HES TEACHING IT!! He is very chill and funny and he is passionate about the things he teaches. Online midterms and finals were great as well! They are pretty manageable as long as you are familiar with the materials!

The online midterms and final are great. You do have to memorize the entire slides though, so take very detailed notes. I think he's a cool guy in general, and he is clearly passionate ab the subject, but I felt like his lectures aside from drugs and the brain were boring and obvious. I already don't like biopsych, this class didn't help w/ that
LOVE Presti's class! His lectures are so interesting and he's really kind. He even wrote his own textbook.

Presti is so knowledgeable; lectures are engaging and go by fast. Listening to him talk about his encounters with drugs was very intellectually stimulating and very cute in the "this old guy is talking about a bad acid trip" type of way. Overall, very entertaining and I'm looking forward to taking his PSYCHC61 next spring!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took the online class during the summer, very easy tbh, but also very boring. Based on the textbook and everything is memorization based. Literally had to know the smallest details of the textbook to do the quizzes and exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Presti has an ability to inspire like no other teacher, and he cares about teaching enough to actually let students explore what they're interested in, instead of just trying to force his set curriculum onto them. You must take this class if drugs fascinate you! (stay away if you don't care)

Presti is an incredibly inspiring professor. If you're actually interested in the topics he teaches about, you will come to respect what he has done in his field and his passion for his research so much. You'll only think of him as a mediocre teacher if you truly don't care at all about the things he's teaching.

Professor Presti is one of the biggest sweethearts on campus, he seems so invested in his work and that made me happy to go to class every day. In the beginning of the semester, I thought his lectures were a little long (oops I fell asleep a few times), but the information was always super interesting. He reminds me of a cooky old grandpa

Took for breadth and it became my favorite class of the semester! Although the lectures are very long & information-heavy, the topics were super interesting. Lectures are also recorded so it easier to just watch those so I could rewind/follow the transcript. HW is super easy and grading is chill.
