Teacher is very animated and has clear lectures. Two midterm essays (3 pages each) worth 80% of grade and one multiple choice final (50 questions) worth 20% of grade. Highly recommend this class! Useful information.

Just to start, the content of Sociology of Organizations and Institutions may sound dull but is super useful. Linus is very clear during lecture, and is great at answering questions! He provides a lengthy study guide for the final exam, and his powerpoint slides are to the point.

Prof Huang's class on Orgs & Institutions was insightful, and his lectures were engaging. He is very animated, has a sort of ironic humor. My gf sat in on one class and opined that he ought to be a jester in a medieval court. The info is very fascinating, and he keeps lectures alive. Tests are easy. Go to class!

This class was the best. We had two take-home midterms that were essay format and worth 70% of our grade, and then one in-class final that was multiple choice, and worth 30% of our grade. Linus is a great lecturer. He's very animated and interested in the topic. I'm very glad I took this class!

Don''t listen to the crying kids.  I am NOT a Soc major.  ISF no background in Sociology loved the class consider it to be a foundational class with excellent and highly relevant information.  And Dr Linus brings huge energy.  I''m 42 and picky and can confirm 100 that this is a great class to take.

Very enthusiastic lecturer and funny too. If you attend lectures, you will certainly get an A. If you do 50% lectures, 50% reading, you will definitely get an A. It's easiest to just go to class and read summaries of what he assigns. The books are interesting anyways. He also usually offers a final study guide which comprehensively covers the test.
Tests are unnecessarily hard and the grading sucks.  Most of us in class are soc majors too, and nobody likes the tests or the way they are graded.  What a lame Summer experience.
I have to say I was displeased.  The readings and lectures are awesome, but the exams are super hard and no one was happy.  Hate to say it, but avoid this class.  It's not worth the trauma.

I would avoid this class at all costs.  While the material is valuable, the examination process is random and will potentially kill your GPA.  Lots of unhappy students in this class, and we are all Sociology Majors.  Not good.  Not good at all.

Dr Linus is one of the best lecturer's at UC Berkeley.  He is passionate, funny, inspiring, eccentric, available, and very smart.  I would recommend him to every student on campus.  Seriously- he is a must-take for everyone.

His lectures are very entertaining and the readings are very manageable (maybe 50 pgs of reading a week AT THE MOST, but usually much fewer). If you attend lectures, take good notes, and do the take home assignments VERY CAREFULLY, an A should be very attainable. My only complaint is that sometimes the GSIs were a bit subjective with the grading.

Made the class ridiculously hard for some reason. It was not a lot of work.. Until finals. The final was an immense amount to study for and he looked for details in 6 essay questions. Like the take home midterms, the questions were asked in an almost incomprehensible way. throughout the course he wasn't helpful and pretty confusing. Overrated!

one of the best classes i took in berkeley. i think its VERY easy and VERY interesting! the professor is an awesome guy i totally recommend! if you love sports its a great class i learned a lot and if you come to all the classes you dont really have to read although the readings were interesting. not hard at all and actually pretty fun!

Dr. Linus is a great professor. Crystal clear in presenting interesting materials, cares about students, and the readers are quite lenient in grading. Do the reading and take notes, you will be fine. He is also cheerful and values students' opinions. I was not that interested in sociology sports prior to this class, but now I learn a lot from him.

this is soc of sports. fun topic, fun class, cool teacher. dr. linus is a generous grader. for the final & MT, he does not grade u by your poor english if you're ESL. MC quizzes are hard tho. his lectures are exciting. i live in SF and only missed 4 lectures. i wish he touched more on less popular sports like track, gymnastics, etc.

I had Dr. Linus in a 6-week summer course. A lot of reading to do (we ARE cramming 1 semester of stuff into 6 weeks!!) Two take home exams and an in-class MC final. Attendance not mandatory, but we did have 1 pop quiz. Definitely take his class. He's so funny, "smiley," and passionate about the subject.
Easy class, 2 papers, 2 exams.They are all bring home paper and the questions are not tricky. He is nice and will answer everything. He is funny. TAKE HIM FOR SURE

Dr. Huang is just amazing! He is so sweet, he makes you feel engaged and he is definitely a devoted professor. Seriously, I don't understand why does Haveman teaches organizations when there is a "Huang" in the Soc. department. Go Linus Huang!

I love Linus Huang. Give this man tenure immediately. His lectures are clear and engaging and he definitely has the best personality of any professor I've encountered at Cal. I took Soc 110- it's a lot of fun. All tests/assignments are take home, but definitely pay attention in class (not that that's hard with an awesome prof like Dr. Linus)

I didn't think I would like the class considering that I am a science major. But I learned so much that it was extremely surprising. One of the best class I've taken at Cal. Also, Dr. Linus has a great presence during lecture (very entertaining). The class is easy with little to no reading. Highly recommended (took it over summer).
great!

Nice, entertaining professor. Clear and concise lecturer. Topic is useful and relevant to the real world. His exams are fair and pretty easy if you read some and go to lecture. I joined the class because I just needed a random course, but after hearing Huang lecture, I became really interested in the class.

I very much enjoyed Dr. Linus SOC 110 class.  His lectures were fun and he knew how to make some of the more difficult theories comprehensible.  He is a nice guy and isn't strict.  On top of that I found the course content useful in everyday life i.e. I have a new understanding and appreciation for the social organizations that surround our lives.

"Dr. Linus" is a nice enough guy, but I think he is still finding his way as a professor. He seems sincere, has a quirky personality and tries to have fun with it, but something is missing. I just didn't find this class all that enjoyable. It's fairly easy though, I got an A with minimal studying. Take him if you need an easy elective.

Professor Huang was really interesting. He was not the greatest, but he tried his best to make his lectures clear and always tried answering our questions. I went to class every time. His class is easy, take home midterm, three papers and a multiple choice final. take his class.

Middle-of-the-road professor.  Lacked a bit of authority and confidence it seemed.  Hard to get truly interested; he did not really engage the class.  I felt the course  did not warrant much investment.  Course is decent, only assignments were take-home midterm and final.  Take notes, read the lecture slides, and you should get an A.

Incredible professor who has a lot of knowledge and experience with the subject so ask questions if you are interested in the material. Short but dense lectures; doesn't waste time and gets right to the info. There are 3 noncumulative exams (requires long essay portion), but as long as you rewatch the recordings and take notes, you'll do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I appreciated the exam prep periods, as well as the q and a sessions. The slides were helpful and organized.

Prof Hinshaw is by far one of my favorite professors at Cal! I highly recommend Psych 131, the content is very interesting and applicable and he's also very articulate and passionate about the subject. 

You definitely have to know the content for the 2 midterms + 1 final (noncumulative), but exams were fairly made and weren't terribly difficult.
This professor was unethical and I would not recommend

Professor Hinshaw is one of the most inspiring and engaging lecturers at Cal. The classes made me change my career focus, and I got goosebumps all the time hearing how he dissects and interprets these topics. I felt fully immersed in his lectures all the time and studying was no longer for good grades on exams but to fulfill my curiosity. Best prof

Read the book and memorize and you will be fine. It was a bit of a struggle reading his book, because it went on and on, but overall he was a great professor and I learned a lot from him. He was very nice.

Excellent lecturer. I don't think I ever missed a class. Tests are fair measure of your knowledge, just pay attention to the lectures and do the readings (which are interesting!). I read some of his other books outside of class; he's a clear writer as well. Take this course! It pairs excellently with Clinical Psychology and Developmental Psychology

Great professor! I would take another class with him in a heartbeat! Lectures are course captures so you don't really need to go but honestly he's so interesting that I go even at 9 am. His lectures are super clear and as long as you do the readings and pay attention in lecture you will be fine. TAKE THIS CLASS!!!
Tests are a fair representation of testing your knowledge.
LOVED THIS CLASS! Professor Hinshaw is the BEST PROF EVER! Lives up to the hype. Seriously, TAKE THIS CLASS, hands down best class at Cal.

Professor Hinshaw is one of the best professors at Cal. He's funny, brilliant, compelling, and patient. The level of engagement he induces about the lecture material is off the charts. If only he taught more classes--that would be a dream come true.

Professor Hinshaw is simply an amazing person. His class was phenomenal. He is one of the most engaging lecturers I've encountered at Cal and a truly good person. Office hours were such a joy, and I always left with some nugget of wisdom. I wish this class were a year long. I would take any class with this professor! He's one-of-a-kind.

By far my favorite class this semester. I looked forward to attending every single class because Hinshaw's teaching style is incredibly engaging and he makes the material sound even more interesting than it actually is, it's like magic. He is super approachable in office hours and loves to talk to students. Wonderful professor and a great guy.

Hinshaw is FANTASTIC! 131 was my favorite class so far. Never a boring moment in lecture - he's an incredibly engaging speaker and the material is fascinating! If you go to lecture (you'll want to) and study the slides, there's no reason not to get an A. I constantly brought up things I learned here in conversation with friends. TAKE THIS CLASS!!!

TAKE THIS CLASS! Worried about your grade? Take it P/NP. The ONLY class requiring thought during my Berkeley education; material is graduate level but given it is psych it's nothing to worry about. Hinshaw analyzes mental illness from every facet of human experience, arriving at sound conclusions. Exams are curved. Everyone does well on the final.

He was really awesome! Very very clear lectures with organized powerpoint slides, always took questions and answered them thoroughly. His tests were fair and not just MC which meant it was a little easier to BS...Great class though :)

Hinshaw is extremely passionate about the subject he teaches and wants to transmit that passion to his students. His tests are easy and straightforward and his lecture style is unique but interesting. Great great professor!
The best professor I had at Cal. Truly a crystal clear speaker, and you can tell he really cares about the topics. Tests are fair. Wish I could've taken more classes with him.

He is an amazing professor.  Very clear, and very forward.  I took his class on child psychopathology, and I really enjoyed it.  I want to just sit down and have an hour long conversation with him.... <3

Prof. Hinshaw is by far the best prof, I have ever had: he is interesting, smart, REALLY involved and interested in the material himself, he is funny, and seems like a genuine and caring person (just as a side note). If you have to chose one professor to not to miss during your time at CAL, Hinshaw is definitely the one!
He is so nice and so smart. I feel really lucky to have been able to take this class with him. His books are really good too...read them

Professor Hinshaw is very nice and approachable, but I found his class boring and his teaching overrated.  He reads from his powerpoint slides, which makes it useless to go to class, since you can stay home and read them yourself.
Prof Hinshaw is amazing. His lectures are incredibly clear and interesting. He is fair and helpful. I tend to sleep through many of my classes but never this one!

Professor Hinshaw is a genius!! He knows so much nformation, he can answer everything and give examples of studies for EVERYTHING! The midterms are tough since there is so much material, he expects a lot but he's an awesome professor!!
This man is amazing!! He has mountains of information in his mind, and he presents reallly interesting material, his lectures are never boring, take as many classes as you can with him!

By far the best lecturer around... this guy's a mutant... the amount of knowledge he stores in his brain is beyond any normal human capability.  Take any class you can by him... before he leaves for a far better and paying job!
Hinshaw is amazing.  If you have the opportunity, try to get a research job in one of his labs, especially the ADHD lab.  Take as many classes with him as you can!
One of the most interesting course I've had.
One of the best classes I've had.
No Comments
he rocks
Lectures were very confusing and honestly tough to understand.

This review is for HISTORY 137AC, this class met online every other day and involves reading about 100+ pages a week. There are weekly assignments which are not very hard, two essays, and a final, which is composed of 2 small essays and one big essay, all graded by GSIs who grade quite harshly. Not the worst for a summer course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Lectures were good and interesting. Not recorded. A lot of reading which is kind of needed but not super mandatory since you're using them for essays. Essays very vague on what they want so hard to tell if you wrote a good essay or not. Two essays and one midterm and one final are your whole grade.

Many things Hirota says are borderline inaccurate and lowkey diabolical--probably why he doesn't allow lecture recordings. They grade essays based off of criteria not mentioned in the prompts. Do not take as a breadth. EVERYTHING is "strictly prohibited" according to him. So much reading, will make you insane and have unnecessary crash-outs.

Professor Hirota has a unique view on the span of history that is taught in this class, and it was very mind opening, however lectures are unbelievably boring and non-engaging. The GSI's definitely carried this class with engaging with the material.

Lectures were SO interesting for the entire 90 min, held my attention. But, not recorded so showing up is important; lecture slides on their own will not be useful, it's all about what he actually says. Essays were kinda harshly graded, but as long as you take good notes you will understand everything and be very well-prepared for midterm/final.

Professor Hirota was kind of paranoid about cheating so the lectures were not recorded and GSIs were not allowed to clarify study guide terms for the midterm and the final (both are solely based on lectures). Therefore, good note taking is imperative. That being said, this was my favorite class this semester.
Heavy accent with a stutter; made it hard to understand lectures. No recorded lectures; your grade really depends on your GSI. Stephen is a bit of a rambler but grades well

Super passionate about the course which makes him a great teacher. What he said matters more than whats on the lecture slides so TAKE GOOD NOTES! Better sign up for someone like Stephen as your GSI even thoug I didnt have him, he was easy grader fs. LOTS of readings but easy midterm and final!

If you're thinking of taking this class for a breadth, do not take! Unless you really love history or it's your major, it's not worth it. The professor is fine, but the GSIs are harsh, especially on the essays. One advice I'd say if you do take the class is really read the essay prompts and talk to your GSIs a lot so they can see your effort.

Found the international perspective towards US history interesting and clear he is very passionate about topic! Slight accent but friendly.  Your grade is heavily dependent on the 2 Essays and Final and your experience in the class is mostly based on your GSI.  Lecture attendance not mandatory but lecture slides are sparse with actual information.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Hirota gives engaging lectures. Lecture attendance isn't taken and lectures aren't recorded.  Section attendance is mandatory. The course based on lecture material includes weekly quizzes, 2 essays based on weekly readings, 1 midterm exam, and 1 final exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor has a 'secret rubric' which is to indicate AI use, but instead it just marks down your grade over time. Grading as a whole is really unclear and you will get marked down on the citation system used in class which is unique to this class. High emphasis on writing rather than demonstrations that the student understands the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: exams/quizzes are heavily dependent on ur ability to recall the professor's synthetic interpretations of lecture content (not recorded, slides were vague). lectures were sometimes boring but discussions were engaging, reasonable coursework (2 essays/1 mt). interesting course overall but would recommend taking an alternative hs/ac breadth
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Linear, easy to follow lectures and assignments which set me up for the final.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: The class I took was not listed but its HIST 137AC. Took it P/NP. Lecture content objectively is well structured and interesting to listen to. A very satisfying level of content for an upper division course but still a lot of information to cram into a short period (hence the P/NP grade).

Lectures were interesting and engaging. Readings were quick, but the subject matter was intense at times. He teaches history from a global lens that includes multiple perspectives (not from a Eurocentric perspective). GSI was Mario Burrus and you could tell he is passionate about history and teaching. 2 5pg papers, discussion posts, and final

Your experience in this class depends on your GSI. I had Mazdeh, and he's the best GSI I have ever had by far. Hirota's lectures were boring with multiple students falling asleep each class, but they are recorded. Tests were easy take home essays. No homework about 30-40 pages of easy but tedious reading per week with books that tend to ramble.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: (HISTORY 137A) Long lectures that weren't terribly interesting, but some of the readings were really interesting. My GSI Caroline was great and had very clear feedback and expectations. Exams had interesting prompts, weekly reading discussions also had interesting prompts. Overall a 3.5/5 class. Not bad but not inspiring.

Every adult in this country would benefit from Prof Hirota's class, he teaches history: good, bad, and ugly. Prepare to read/write! GSI Mario Burrus was awesome. He gave us a take home final with ample time to prepare and understand expectations. I learned more in this history class than in my entire learning career. Loved it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Your fate in this class heavily depends on your GSI. My GSI, Johnathan Garza, gave very vague and controversial feedback on assignments. What he demanded for an assignment was different from the instructions provided by the professor. Also, the lectures are very long and boring with the professor talking nonstop for two hours.

This class is boring but not too difficult if you do the readings and take good lecture notes. It's not enough to copy the slides; the important info is what the professor says. Midterms and finals were online and open-note. There are also weekly not too challenging quizzes to see if you paid attention in lecture.

Honestly taking APUSH in high school helped me survive this class. I didn't pay much attention in class but survived because of APUSH. Readings are VERY important, especially for discussions (but you can survive without but be smart about it). I loved my GSI, he was tons of help. It was a little difficult to hear the professor in lecture sometimes
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: do not take this class if you value your mental health

I took history 7A as a breadth course and it was one of the most difficult courses that I have taken. Professor Hirota made grading far too difficult, and the midterm and final exams are an insane amount of writing. Definitely would not recommend taking this as a breadth course, it will probably take up more time and effort than your major classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Hirota is an engaging and very knowledgeable lecturer. I'm baffled by his policy to record lectures and then take them down. There is a TON of mandatory reading in this class, so keeping up with it is a priority. Lecture attendance is not mandatory, but section attendance IS, or else you fail the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Hirota incorporated many international and racially diverse perspectives into the course. The lectures are recorded and available for a week, but he republished them all during RRR week. Discussion section is mandatory (some online options) but helped with the readings. Essays/take home tests were on readings and lectures. Overall, a good class.

Professor Hirota is a good professor who gives clear guidelines and enough information and resources to be able to succeed in his class. His previous 1 star reviews are unfair and don't give an accurate account of how he actually is as a professor so take them with a grain of salt.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Frankly, I think he is a great professor. There is a lot of information and the class is lecture-heavy but the Professor is very good at organizing the information in a cohesive manner. I would defo recommend this class to anyone who likes reading and wants to learn more about American history. I would recommend going to lecture/watch them asap.

This class was one of my favorite that I have taken at Cal so far. It taught me to relearn American history in a more worldly, innovative way. Many of the lectures were super interesting and brought up new information that repositioned many of the things I had learned before. Having a good GSI is important though.

The lectures were clear but concise and dense, I wouldn't recommend taking notes by hand but definitely take notes. He doesn't grade anything himself, but gives good expectations and gives a great opportunity to succeed in essays. The weekly quizzes were kinda hard I thought as well, very niche and sometimes misleading questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Organized class, understandable explanations

I thought this class was very interesting. Professor Hirota had very clear expectations when it came to the papers. Lectures were okay, there's usually a lot of content in the lectures and make sure to take notes!!! I liked how the midterm and final exam prompts were provided in advance so that we could prepare for them. Overall, good class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Overall, Professor Hirota was a great professor. While his lectures do have a lot of content, they are easy to follow and overall interesting. I personally believe that the lower ratings are unfair, he was interactive with the class and the grade criteria were made extremely clear throughout the class. I would take the class again if I could.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment:
Professor is a nice person; however, his grading criteria and expectations are beyond any level of understanding. He is a harsh grader. His expectations are unclear. Final is extremely tough. I knew the material from other classes but still struggled with his expectations. It makes the course harder than it is.

Better RUN AWAY or take P/NP.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment:
Positives: Very knowledgeable, clearly an authority in this field.
Negatives: Unreasonably strict, inflexible, uncompromising policies. It's possible to demonstrate a good understanding of the material but receive a poor grade solely due to technicalities. The sentence "you will have no choice" will haunt me.

Good education, unreasonable policies.
Extremely difficult for no reason.

The final for this class was extremely tough. The professor seems to not be able to recognize that most of the students in the class are here for a breadth requirement and are not fully immersed into the topics. Course policies and grading were extremely detailed for no reason and caused further confusion. Unnecessary late submission penalties.
Final papers were auto-failed if they were a more than a half-page short.

The grading for this class is impossible to understand. Hirota has very specific instructions and if you don't follow each perfectly you will not get an A. Also the graders for this class were a mess. Professor Hirota seemed like he wanted to be there less than the students.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Grading is convoluted and seems not tied to syllabus or assignment descriptions. Focus on regurgitating exactly what he said and when he said it (cite lectures by date) rather than course concepts. Incredibly difficult to obtain even a decent grade and grading scale complicated and difficult to follow. Cumulative grades unavailable through semester

Horrible class and a very unfair professor. He shows a complete lack of understanding that this class is simply an american institutions requirement for many of the students, and he creates unreasonable exams. He comes off as very punitive and grading in the class appears to be inconsistent. Overall, a really unpleasant experience.

Peter's lectures make no sense, have nothing to do with the textbook or section activities, and are always closed by a 5-10 minute long motivational speech that is literally unbearable incomprehensible nonsense. Your ability to learn anything in this class will hinge on if your GSI is a good teacher, not on anything that Peter says.

Professor Hurtubise talks very fast, but it makes the class go by quickly. He makes all of his students feel included, even though it is a big lecture. he is very passionate about his subject and grades a total of 3 assignments throughout the semester.

by far the most passionate prof i've had at cal and i always left his lectures inspired. unfortunately the grading is confusing, with vague rubrics and a page limit i found too constrained for the complex prompts. also there are no lecture slides or recordings. i would recommend this course tho esp for ac credit- great guy with good things to say !

Didn't really like teaching style. You're "supposed" to learn Stata but he just assigns YT videos and textbook so unless you do it, you won't learn. Stats part really missing overall. But you do choose a research topic interesting to you and work on that all semester. Grades based on midterm, final, and participation. Both exams relatively easy.

Amazing guy, very inspirational and passionate, but poor format for the class. BCourses is bare, there's no syllabus, and expectations for assignments are, not just unclear, but never stated. There's about two sentences of directions, no rubric, and he barely mentions it in class. Lectures are good and interactive but no slides, no recordings.

Probably best class I've taken. Literally so good. Super engaging lectures. Couple book reports and a take-home essay for final. Books for book reports were so good, i read both, fav and easiest was How Children Succeed. Would read again for pleasure. Overall super inspiring, every lecture made me wanna do something to fix the edu system.
The man, the myth, the legend.
He is incredibly passionate about his course material and has very inspirational lectures. I took this for my AC requirement and was a to get an A without dedicating much time to the class.

Only graded by exams + book report but not difficult at all. Amazing lecturer, course content and readings. I actually wanted to go to lectures for an attendance optional class because I left each class feeling inspired. Participation is very encouraged but he makes a good effort to facilitate good discussions. The readings were interesting as well
Really great lecturer and is very passionate about the subject of teaching.

(Broken into parts because of this stupidly small character limit) I really wanted to like Professor Hurtubise. He's clearly passionate about his work and attempts to rouse his students with inspirational speeches at the end of each lecture. Unfortunately, I found his teaching style offputting. (1/4)
Great professor! Extremely clear on what he expects on the midterm, project, and final. Very inspirational and passionate about the topic. Would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Inspirational--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Best professor ever. Hands down. He puts in so much effort to make his students feel heard, and he is so passionate on the topic! All of the projects are relatively simple, and his entire goal is to help students learn and succeed. Definitely recommend, he's amazing!!

Hurtubise is an amazing lecturer! You can tell he is incredibly passionate about the subject he is teaching. His lectures will never bore you, they will always leave you feeling motivated. He always ends class on an empowering note and starts it with a fun and welcoming icebreaker. Highly recommend this class and lecturer.

Best professor I've ever had. His lectures are amazing-- like inspirational speeches. He has so much knowledge and cares for students/their passions. Every lecture there is an assigned reading. Only assignments are: mid-term, book project, and final. They all base around the readings and are fairly easy. Highly recommend!

Lectures are often incomprehensible, since he's a rambler AND a mumbler. You can ask him the most basic question, and he starts spiraling into a mess of spaghetti for like 5 minutes trying to answer it. Thankfully, his psets and exams are incredible! Challenging, but extremely rewarding. This is a class I actually learned something from.
Lecture content is very different from the recommended textbook. Grading is tough and Exam questions are weird. I spent so much time on this course and struggled to pass it.
Tough profesor

Lectures solely proof based, in fact we spent about a week proving one theorem. Almost no examples shown in class, it was all about proofs. Went so in depth with some of the proofs early in the semester that we didn't even have time to learn important topics like Brownian motion. Did not really follow a textbook. Would not recommend

Lectures are blatantly soporific. Another Cal class where I had to teach myself everything in the last two weeks.. Prof recommended one textbook and spent the rest of the semester basing the class off a different one. Statistics is an applied discipline yet this felt only theoretical. All proofs. Overall 0/5 if i could

Prof doesn't pay much attention to whether the students are learning. The lectures were not of much use, neither were asking questions. Flow of theorems does not follow textbook so need to attend class. But then again you will need to study the textbook yourself for doing assignment if you want to really understand the concepts. Won't recommend.

Professor makes very less effort to make himself understood. Doesn't address questions. Spends excess time on trivial points and leaves out important concepts. Class is not recorded and professor doesn't follow a textbook, so one has to attend every class and take down everything. Reading a textbook will help more than this course.

The lectures are very verbose and pedantic, and not enough attempt is made to be understood. The honors course could have been much better had it not been for the extreme (ridiculous) formalism adopted by the professor to explain and prove very simple theorems. The grading criteria is almost all over the place and very unclear. Don't be surprised.

Unfortunately, I felt as if the material he chose to teach was rather simple. Of course it's one of the "harder" courses as noted by the average minded people. Yet, I noticed a lack of truly difficult deep cutting material. Maybe I'm just...smart
For me, this class was easy. I had no trouble went by breezy. This is because, im a prodigy. To put it quite simply, im a genius, hehehe. Prof. Holmes aint for everyone, but for me, twas breezy.

Lectures were extremely dense and often hard to follow, with explanations that assumed a high level of prior knowledge. Much of the learning felt self-directed, relying on past modules and old Zoom recordings. The professor's tone could be rude, communication was inconsistent, and exams were complex with material barely covered in lecture.

This class is like drinking from a fire hose. We were expected to attend lecture in person AND watch the recorded lectures from last year, plus an additional module. I feel like I would have learned more if we spent more time on fewer topics. Lectures cover a lot but it is not clear what is meant to stick. Holmes clearly knows his stuff though.

Absolutely terrible instruction. It's disappointing because I'm genuinely interested in the topic he was supposed to be teaching. Do not take this class unless you want to spent a significant amount of time in this class and feel like you are still not getting anything out of it. Waste of time.

Lecture sucks, he's too smart and can't talk logically. He give us lots of materials but can't explains all the ideas clearly. He even add new modules and make us watch zoom recording for the old module. Though it's open-book exam, more than half of the content was not covered in the lecture. Please consider thoroughly before enrolling in his class

VERY VERY helpful and sweet! Ian has sufficient knowledge and he's brilliant, the material he brings to class covers the core ideas in Bioinfomatics, and he can bring even more ideas from other subject like machine learning and statistics ! Really enjoy his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Don't take this class unless it's the very last class offered in Berkeley. You will have to spend a considerable amount of time doing the lab assignments, your grades will very likely suffer, and you will learn jack from this class. Please do yourself a favor and learn from my mistake.

Doesn't care if his students get anything out of the class.  All too often, he's the last to arrive to lecture and the first to leave.  This class does very little to peak your interest in computation biology.  He goes over too much material and doesn't expect you to learn any of it.
Pompous, antisocial geek. Thinks he's a superior human being compared to you. Made me lose interest in computational biology.
He is so passive aggressive

Straightforward course and prof does a good job at explaining the material. The exams (3 midterms + 1 final) are based on the slides, not the assigned readings. The written essays are also straightforward and the grading criteria is clear if you attend section and read the rubric.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lectures are posted to BCourses & he had great inflection in his voice. He also gave 5-15 minute breaks halfway through the lectures :) VERY easy class for Freshman- if you are happy with your first 3 midterm scores, you do not need to take the final (or the final can replace a bad midterm). Qua Miller was not good. Transfer out if possible.

very easy class, but also content is very structured/organized and well-paced. grading policy is clear and fair. content itself is interesting, and you learn as much as you want to learn, considering it is an online course. good resources, including lecture videos and flashcards.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Psych 1 online. super good class easy to follow would recommend for an intro psych class.
Interesting class and course material. Gade's an engaging lecturer, just note that class is very exam-based

Frustrating but easy A if you play his games. Beware: (1) mismatch between textbook and lecture slides made studying for exams confusing. (2) exams test for rote memorization on minute details from lectures. (3) NEVER trust a man who can't spell “Gemini” and “Grammarly” on his own syllabus where he threatens to use AI to sniff out AI in your paper

The class is fairly easy, with straightforward papers (graded by GSI) and multiple-choice exams. The lectures can be dry, but Gade is approachable and easy to understand. Be sure to attend your section for additional material and paper information. The papers have clear guidelines and are interesting and easy. Pay attention and you'll be ok!

Requires you to understand what your specific GSI wants to read in terms of grading papers (go to their office hours). Exams were fair enough and almost copy and paste of the slides and there are many opportunities to improve your grade. Very interesting material.
This was a great intro psych course. Gade was an engaging lecturer and I learned a lot. Just memorize everything on the slides and you are guaranteed an A.

Professor Gade was awesome. He made concepts very easy to understand and had engaging lectures. Essays and tests are easy if you follow the rubric/study— a lot of succeeding in this class has to do with knowing what is expected. Come to lecture though, because it isn't recorded and concepts will be on the test!
condescending and makes you hate academia

Very traditional but engaging lecturer. Lectures aren't recorded though so make sure to attend every single one, since some of the material on the exams weren't on the slides. Other than that the exams and papers are pretty straightforward and easy to score high on.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: easy to get full scores on essays, just follow the rubric. mcq is easier than ap sciences & social sciences, except no curves. 5 extra credit bonus points increases your grade by a little less than 2%. interesting topics. engaging lecturer. don't skip all the lectures and cram study like me

Papers are super straightforward and easy to knock out quickly. Lectures were engaging, and he doesn't just read off the slides. Slides are great if you can't attend class, but he shows videos that you'll probably get tested on. 3 midterms (only 50 MCQ each) were chill—some memorization of names/experiments. 5 points RPP bonus helps a lot!

WORST class I've ever take, DON'T take it for breadth.
Horrible, tons of memorization, nothing on the slide, tough grader for papers. Get ready to fail.
Absolutely recommend it if you want to have a hard time!

XBW1, good introductory course, fair class. Do the readings before lecture and do the weekly assignments. 2 exams, 1 midterm 60 min 60 multi choice , 1 Final 90 min 12 short answer. Open note doesn't mean don't prepare. Dr. Gade is fair with grading, gives feedback quickly and responds quickly. Study, do the work and you'll be fine.
Cool dude. Engaging lectures. Fair exams.  Would recommend the class.

Don't skip lecture and if you really want an A make sure you review the lecture slides before class so you aren't going in blind. Take notes on the lectures and connect them to the lecture slides in order to review for the midterms, then you're guaranteed an A. For the papers, don't be extra, just follow the rubric.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Very run-of-the-mill professor, watered down version of AP Psychology. Just take notes on the lectures and you'll be fine. The papers really determine your grade, if you have a difficult GSI can bring down your grade. The other reviews about how he's condescending aren't true, he's very ordinary in his lecture style nothing to discuss.

He was super cool and his lectures were super engaging. This class was easier than high school (non AP) psychology, but some midterm questions were very very specific to the slides. I found that making a cheatsheet (even though you can't use it on the test) helped me study. You can only lose a few points overall to get an A so watch out!

Probably one of the worst professors I've ever had. Many students quit to have another professor because he was so terrible. The exams were entirely questions that were not covered in lectures of the textbook. I have no idea how this guy is even teaching at Berkeley...he's more of a junior college quality and even thats being generous.

only homework for this class was 3 papers, which were easy to score high if you follow all the checkboxes. lectures were easy to follow (they're also recorded). he sometimes skips over information so look over slides before tests. plus rpp extra credit and he drops lowest test grade.

I took his General Psych class through the online Extension program. Recorded lectures are 2-3 hours per week, 1-2 assignments per week, and two tests for the term. First one is open note, but it would be very hard to google the answers. Final was in essay form. He was very quick at responding and his lectures were clear and interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took him through an online general Psych course on the Berkeley Extension. He generally had recorded lectures (2-3 hours per week) with 1-2 assignments per week. Two tests, first one was open note but very short time (so you cant google the answers) and the final was essay responses. Overall his videos were high quality and his feedback good.
Bad teacher

Easy class if you have any prior exposure to high school psychology. Tests are mostly covered in class materials but expect 1 or 2 questions written from REALLY REALLY cornered content on the slide. Generally very generous course: has RPP bonus. The three essays are easy to get top grades depending on your GSI. Not a stressful course.

The GSI's and the professor are all very clear on the content and if you ever have questions, don't be afraid to ask. Classes are engaging and definitely where most of the test answers are going to be. DONT rely on the uploading of the recordings if you are taking the class in person. You WILL fall behind. ATTEND the discussions!

Since I took the online version of this class, all the lectures were recorded. The lectures had been made by a different retired Prof (Dr. Kihlstrom), but Kihlstrom did a great job! I never actually heard much from Dr. Gade, but that didn't make a huge difference. All exams were open notes and could be taken at any time during the assigned day.

Just a doable class overall, really easy to stay above an A- as long as you turn in all your work! Biggest downside for me was the 'two-part final' which was just having the last midterm and final on the same day. Exam questions are also weirdly nit-picky sometimes. Required mindtap textbook also cost a little over $100.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I really liked his way of teaching. The lectures are not filled with tons of information, and he makes his lectures really easy to follow by, in a way, telling more of a story. Together with the many examples he provided, the material was super easy to memorize and I really the topics we discussed.

Professor Gade was very knowledgeable in the subject. Although his lectures were a bit slow, they were easy to follow in general. The tests come straight from the lectures and the 3 papers have a very clear grading criteria. The lowest test score gets dropped, which is also really nice. Overall, very easy class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Gade is very knowledgeable in the subject. Although his lectures are a bit slow, they are easy to follow and the tests come straight from the lectures. There are 3 required papers for the class, and they all have a clear grading criteria. Overall, very eays class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Such a great professor! Very knowledgeable about the subject and gives students clear explanations of important concepts. Exams completely lecture based. Textbook helps but not required. Easy and manageable essays. No other homework. Drops lowest exam grade. Very kind. Overall great class and professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I loved Dr.Gade!! He's such a wonderful professor and I truly learned a lot from him. Textbook not required but very helpful! Go to class!!!!

Prof Gade is an okay professor, he was nice but sometimes kinda snobby LOL. The class was easy, I might be biased since I took AP Psych in highschool and passed, but this was way easier than AP Psych and didn't even cover as many topics, which was surprising, especially for an intro course. Just memorize the lectures really well for exams.

TAKE THIS CLASS!!!! three midterms and one final, three papers. you can get 100% on papers if you follow rubric and tests are all participation. RPP gives you 5 pt extra credit. One exam dropped and final is optional. Gade is an AMAZING lecturer and the content is very interesting. You also don't need to go to lecture to do well.

He really knows what he's talking about and posts lecture slides that are very informative. Towards the end of the semester, we started watching more video clips so don't worry, it's a very chill class.
Professor told me to finish my essay that night after I asked for a two day extension after I had gone to the hospital for mental health problems because of suicidal thoughts

With the amount of options out there. You should avoid taking this proffesor. Don't be like me and ignore ratings. From what I heard. People in the class get failed on purpose not cause of course material. Just cause there needs to be repeats in order for the proffesor class to refill.

Discussions were not helpful for course content, but did facilitate bigoted conversation. An ableist discussion about ADHD meds being allowed for neurotypical people as "smart drugs", a flagrant debate on whether transgender people should be allowed in society, and asking us to argue for or against conversion camps.

Memorize and quizlet for tests.
Focus on the lectures!  Tests are easy if you study the slides and attend class.

Easiest A ever, basically all the material on the midterms and final is taken straight from past midterms and the online resources. As long as you do the weekly discussion posts and the homework modules on time, you're basically guaranteed full credit in every part of the course except the tests. Definitely recommend his class as a GPA booster.
Great lectures, easy exams and papers, just go to class and do the work.  Also, try to get a good GSI, they really matter in this class.

This class was overall pretty manageable. Lots of memorization. I got an 89.9% and when reached out about having my grade rounded or if the class would be curved. I got a simple "No, this class does not round grades." I only needed to get 1 more question correct on the final to get a 90%. Just another reason to hate Berkeley.

Overall I enjoyed Gade's class and he provides extra credit, just memorize memorize memorize!

For an intro course, this was way too hard. Nothing I wote for his discussions were good enough for him. Refused to help or give points back. His weekly assignments were ridiculusly extensive and a lot of information needed to be included. Wouldn't take again.

Lectures recorded. Tries his best to make lectures interactive to better understand concepts. Lectures not super content heavy. All exams multiple choice. grade based on your exam and RPP extra credit.
I think he made the class fun IMHO.  I missed a few classes b/c of PIs and caught up fine because they're posted after.   Get a good GSI though, they help a lot with the papers!

The class was super easy and straightforward. The grading rubric and GSI's make writing papers easy. All tests are multiple-choice and memorization based. Recorded lectures helped when I was too lazy to get out of bed!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very condescending. Class itself was pretty easy, but Gade was not an interesting teacher and was very rude. He talked down on his students and was extremely inflexible.

Tests are pretty simple since they're based on what is discussed in the lecture and discussions. Really great at explaining the concepts and wasn't hard to understand. Great class and great professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Every time he speaks it feels like he's mansplaining. He talks about mental health issues like he's sooo above it, and I think he sucks.

reviews.comment: Class was made up of 4 exams (you get to drop one) and 3 papers, plus optional extra credit. He tests on lecture/discussion content only (breadth not depth of content).

Psych 1 was a very easy class- 3 papers, 3 exams. The papers were graded by GSI's and exams were simple memorization. HOWEVER, I will say that Gade is extremely condescending to his students. reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: I'm so confused by many of these posts.  Going into the class, I assumed this would be a nightmare.  Now I'm planning to major in psychology.  Thanks Prof Gade!

All 3 required essays had clear guidelines and were easy to score highly on. Dr. Gade was difficult to accommodate DSP when still waiting on intake. Wouldn't take again because of the challenge I had in proving my situation.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: as a freshman, this class made transitioning to college less stressful :') topics are so interesting that it makes it very easy to digest the information. readings are optional and there's no hw. only prepare for 3 exams (review lectures & disc) and 3 essays! GSI's also cover intriguing topics. 5 star yummy class. negative reviews took an L ngl
Very disturbed with this Professor. Expects you to memorize everything he says and is very cruel to his students.

I don't know why Gade's ratings are so low, he's great. Lectures and slides are very clear/organized, and he's also quick in responding to emails. There are 3 midterms + a final (but he drops your lowest exam grade), as well as extra credit. Essays are a lot of work, but the criteria is clear, and most GSIs grade pretty leniently and fairly.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This Professor will suck the life out of you .

Gade's course is very well organized and he's very clear and concise in lectures, although not too engaging. His exam questions veryyy specific and the paper prompts can be confusing. My advice is to memorize vocabulary before exams and ask your GSI for help on papers.

I'm nearing the end of the semester and I decided to look up the ratings for Dr Gade.  I'm shocked by many of the comments.  Maybe this is for another class.  Attending lectures this semester has felt like I'm attending a movie.  The information is clear and I really am learning a lot.  I'm not sure what grade I'll get, but I'm very happy.

The course is very organized. All of the lecture slides, modules, and papers are posted ahead of time. You need to study for the 4 exams (50 multiple choices) but if you've taken AP psych it shouldn't be hard. The 3 paper's instructions are all very clear, but your grade depends on your gsi. My favorite class of the semester.

Exams are HARD! Took him over the summer, and had difficulty with the 3 midterms & final. No questions were pulled from the book, so do not waste your time reading. Questions are random nit-picky points from lectures. Assigned 4-5 lectures a week that were all about 2 hours long. Horrendous amount of work. Avoid avoid avoid!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Grading on papers depends on your GSIs, so get to know your GSI! The exams were the worse, hated the time limit for the questions and they were lecture & section content heavy. Sometimes some questions did not even match which made the exams even more difficult.

This needs to be read for future students. Gade was bland and was death by PowerPoint. Always looks for some trivial detail to grade harshly. Exams are based on remember what he said word by word (hour video) on top of being timed means more anxiety. There are better instructors on campus. reviews.comment: It's as if his grading policy is to pick some random line in the paper and mark it down to give the impression, he is reading the paper. Not the greatest option
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed this class. Professor gade is a great professor and he explains things thoroughly. Attendance is not mandatory but exams are all based on lectures so if you want to do good you need to attend lecture. Overall, great class!

Took the class Fall 2021 and it was online the whole semester. Exams are all based on the lectures, so definitely recommend actually going. Also go to the discussion sections because they teach extra stuff that isn't covered in lecture. Had to write 2 papers throughout the semester, but they were pretty easy.
4 exams, lowest one dropped, 3 assignments that are challenging but doable, and he seems to genuinely care about students.  This class wasn't super easy, but I learned a lot.
The test are hard and nowhere near the lecture or the readings. It quite literally makes no sense, would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I don’t understand many of these negative reviews. Was this for a different class?  His lectures are clear, everyone I know is doing very well in the class, and he seems very approachable.  Also, what weekly papers?  People complaining about having to dedicate 5 hours a week to this class need to reassess.

Lack of clarification and condescending attuite towards student shows why most would not recommend him. Insanely hard and prides himself knowing his students are confused and struggling. Feedback is so vague that he leaves 1 sentence on a 1000+ word essay. He is not a good teacher and abuses his tenure. His mindset is why teach when I am tenured?

Gade was a great professor, especially for an intro class like Psych 1. He did well at explaining all lecture topics and answered questions in a helpful way. He was understanding of hardships during the pandemic and did a good job working around the troubles of online learning. Would definitely recommend.

Great professor but his class is a bit rigorous. There are three midterms I believe and two papers, plus a bunch of online homework that you have to buy through Cengage so it's a bit annoying but he is very smart and knows what he's talking about. As long as you pay attention to the lectures and do all the homework, you're solid.

For two mandatory, highly weighted papers: u're not given an example essay so you'll feel underprepared to write it. But, if u follow the instructions and writewhat's in the rubric, u'll get v high marks. Exams: If u write bullet-pointed semi-detailed notes from each lecture, you can just refer back for the exam. not v hard, just quite specific.

reviews.comment: Lecture was recorded; exams were based on lectures. reviews.comment: class structures and grading is tough even on small trivial things. Feedback felt ambitious as he doesn't outline where exactly in the paper needs to be addressed. reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: I thoroughly enjoyed this class. Exams were fairly easy as long as you pay attention in lecture (that's where all the test questions come from, readings are there to supplement but are not that important), and I got an A on the final with barely any studying. He drops your lowest exam grade, and the papers have clear rubrics and are easily graded.

Although lectures were clear, assignments and rubric for papers seemed extremely vague. We were not given any papers as example of what we were expected, the instructions for papers were hard to interpret if you were unable to make it to section, also hard to find the material for certain papers, which carry weight in your final grade.

Online lectures are always recorded, voice isn't monotonous so lectures aren't super boring. Tests are lecture based, so please take lots of notes and re-watch the recordings if you missed information. Textbook is only needed for online Mindtap activities; not needed for midterms though, it's mainly there for clarification. GSI's are also helpful!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: Is not monotone, lectures are interesting. Tends to mumbles and asks for participation which is hard to understand. Mindtap activities as homework weekly

reviews.comment: I really didnt like the mindtap activities but the class was easy enough and my gsi helped a lot. I just wish I could have taken the class in person.

I took "Introduction to Psychology" with Gade as the lecturer in the Fall semester of my freshman year. I will never forget how dismissive & belittling he was to me personally & how uninspired his lectures were. His exams were also heavily based on memorization, not understanding. I'm sad to see not much has changed...

Extreme volume of work. Tight test times (40 minutes for 35 questions in my class). Tests always featured some questions on singular, random lines in the reading. reviews.comment: this class was meh. if you do the assignments you'll pass. midterms and finals are reasonable, and there are a couple short papers in between. i took it p/np because I was struggling mentally that semester, and I passed without taking the final.

The class was good in that it was easy to access lectures, and everything on BCourses was extremely organized. His exams are EXTREMELY lecture-based. reviews.comment: Just finished the class. One of my favorites this semester. The material was very clear and I really liked my GSI. I'm very excited about pursuing a major now.

The worst class I have ever taken. GSIs grade too hard and do not communicate with the students. I would not recommend anyone to take this course.

He's the worst professor in the department. He's snarky to students, a boring lecturer, and an unfair grader. This class has so much interesting material, but he makes it a horrible experience. Every semester you get one of these professors that has to to make his students feel unwanted. he makes snarky remarks and belittles you for no logical reason. Lots of papers and busy work with the book assignments, but this was a very easy class compared to my others last semester! Section and class lectures were clear, but the class did cover more than I expected.

I had a rough semester at Cal. His class was one of the few bright spots. I loved my GSI too. Watching the lectures on my own schedule really helped me get through a lot of things. It's tough to tell how much he cares about students in an online class, but he seemed nice the two times I emailed him and met in office hours.

Lots of papers. Follow rubric and take notes on what your GSI suggests when they talk about formatting and you will ace each paper. Tests are lecture-based. Extra credit gives you a percent boost. Finished with a 101% in this class because of how clear the instruction is, even if it is a lot of work. U can hear his kids in background of lec LOL

he wasn't there in person, just a few recorded lectures so it's hard to tell how great he was. didn't even feel like my professor. pretty easy over online. just focus on the lectures and you'll do great. follow the essay instructions without going too fancy to get full credit

Professor Gades lectures are very informative, engaging and interesting. Midterms and finals are strongly related to lectures so make sure to take good notes. I just saw my final grade in the class. I don't want to offend others, but this seemed like an extremely easy class to me. There was minimal work with exams dropped and tons of extra credit and easy busy work to boost my grade.

Like another review said, I was on the cusp of a grade and immediately emailed him to ask what I could do and he refused to. Class wasn't as fun as I thought it'd be and that's probably because it was online.
he refused to round my 69.9997 to a 70 and I failed the class while doing my first semester of college online during COVID. I also didn't see his face once and all he did was talk over slides.

If you have the option not to take his class, do that!! He's absolutely horrible, not only is his tests EXTREMELY hard but he also tests on things he randomly says in class. reviews.comment: This guy is the worst teacher I have ever had in my life. YOU'VE BEEN WARNED, his assignments are incredibly difficult and the tests require TONS of memorization. If you are planning to take it for a breadth, just don't. There are far easier and more interesting classes out there. Professor Gade is extremely pretentious and insensitive. Prof Gade covers interesting course material that is very easy to digest, and his papers are also easy. reviews.comment: had him during COVID-19 and he said that we were at an advantage compared to other students because we have to stay home? He is the most frustrating teacher I have ever taken as a student. His instructions for assignments are unclear and he becomes insensitive when you ask about a question about it saying... Read the instructions again. Reading something that is unclear does not make it clear. If he does not wish to help students he should not be teaching.

(Covid-19) While in-person lectures, he made lectures interesting and fun. After switch to online, it was frustrating to see that he was not understanding of the challenges that arose. He emailed "don't be jerks. You guys have it easier than other semesters" HUH. There are many students that have lost income, family. Insensitivity !

Mediocre class and professor. It was an introductory course so it wasn't anything great but wasn't bad either. Tests are fair and papers were easy. However, losing a few points on each test adds up pretty quickly and so to keep an A you have to do pretty well on each exam.

Gade's class is quite easy and given that the content is interesting, he does not have to work too hard to keep students engaged. Given that, however, he can get angry if people are not listening to him which can be annoying. If you study for the midterms (which are multiple-choice) and closely follow the essay prompts, you'll get an easy A.

Psychology of Personality had a lot of diverse material. There were 2 major papers at the beginning of the course. Later on, your performance relies heavily on the theory quizzes and discussions. Be careful with that--if you make a mistake on those or leave out material, you take a big hit in the second half of the course. Read the book! It helps.

reviews.comment: I took Cognitive Psychology with him online. I have no experience what he's like in-person, but I know that he's very good at giving clear feedback and provides a ton of resources. reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The criteria to get an A is ridiculous. Your grade is determined by four exams (best three out of four) and three papers that are each worth 60 points. In order to secure an A, you can only lose 20 points altogether! Exams are based on content directly from the slides but can be on very minute details that are loosely related to psychology.

DO! NOT! TAKE! HIS! COURSE! He teaches outdated, inaccurate, and generally well-contested content of his field. His lessons largely perpetrate a lot of ignorance reminiscent of many critiques of the psychology field. It's astounding he even teaches at what is supposed to be a top university. The most irresponsible educator I have seen here.

Great professor! He's nice, humorous and lively. I don't understand why the ratings are so low. The PSYCH 1 class I'm in now is more than reasonable. It's not just a fair class but a class in which you learn life-worthy information. You have to work for every class if you want that A, but unlike some classes in which you simply cannot get that A...

A lot of people give him a hard time for being harsh on students but I found him to be fair, clear and engaging. Not much to say about a Stats class but he's a solid professor, just not my favorite topics :)
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Don't take Psych 101 with him if you can help it. He's an extremely likable guy, but he isn't good at teaching stats. The textbook makes much more sense than he does.
Very boring class but Stats is a dry subject. Gade was ok--somewhat helpful. Probably my least favorite class last semester.
Dr. Gade was always available to help me when I needed it. His class was pretty easy. He seemed really young to be a professor. I think he was a graduate student at Cal.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I would take his class again because it was so easy. Everything was fairly standard and you can probably get away with skipping class if you read the textbook and do well on the tests.

Unclear grading criteria, assignments don't help with the course material  more like a creative writing class. Seems to grade subjectively, with absolutely no feedback on the student's understanding of the subject. No leniency with due dates for family emergencies. Lectures just reiterate the textbook  the instructor bears no educational value.

Psych 1 with Gade is a straight forward class, but won't inspire you deeply. The exams are straight from the lecture slides. Memorize names of important people. He occasionally mansplains and likes to flex the Berkeley title, but is overall a really kind guy and a good professor. If you need a solid/easy pre-req/breadth -- take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Mostly a good prof, and I got an A from him with little effort. It's important to know that Dr. Gade is kind of unforgiving when it comes to little things like mistyping the APA formatting on the paper, so keep a note of that and you'll do fine. The test questions are extremely easy, and he drops your lowest test score as a cherry on top.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Course was content heavy and very general, but Gade made the lectures interesting and engaging. He has a sexy voice too so thats a plus. Hate that its graded by only three tests and three papers, but the final can replace lowest test score. Theres a lot of content, but just memorize & learn lecture slides for exams and youll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: This class is a breadth that's actually an easy A, as long as you go to lecture and section and pay attention. Gade is an interesting lecturer, and gives memorable examples that make all the material easily absorbable and entertaining. Nicest, most thoughtful professor I've had so far. His GSIs are super nice too.

Professor Gade is an efficient, no-nonsense instructor. He drops the lowest of your 4 exams and made us do two papers. The exams are multiple choice so they come back quickly. He performs these really fun activities in class that makes us understand the class better. He can be a little condescending so know what you're talking about.

I honestly studied so much for his social psych class and I just feel like the more I study the worse I do on my exams. His questions are extremely difficult and he makes you feel awful for being 5mins late to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Really not a big fan of this guy, he grades hard on assignments and his tests are extremely difficult. Each test has an overload of information to memorize. There is also a lot of reading and listening to lectures. By far my hardest course and worse grade even though i put most of my time into this class. LOOK FOR A DIFFERENT PROFESSOR.
