reviews.comment: Very tough grader, I reached out to other students in my class and they were receiving bad grades as well. I reached out to the professor and asked for an example of what he wanted for the weekly modules and he was no help at all and could care less. He would also leave me rude comments back on my assignments such as "That was really rough".
Assignments are way to time consuming and in depth for being an INTRO class. Super hard grader as well. All im sayin is this dude needs to chill out.... this is psych 101... its not that deep.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Tests are fair and based directly off of lecture material. Take good and thorough notes. Lectures are pretty slow.
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: he speaks too fast

Awesome professor! Very clear and interesting lectures. Loved his teaching style. Always welcomed questions, even though we were in such a large lecture hall. Had us do some fun interactive activities with the people around us to help us with the material. Take his intro psych class!!

Gade makes lectures painfully boring with his eye-offending slides and tests that cover random and unnecessary details. The papers cover more overall important concepts, but they're pointless in terms of understanding the material of the class. Had another, more engaging, professor taught the class, I'd have been more interested in it.

Long lecture videos, lots and lots of reading. Random test questions. He's really good at responding to emails and questions. I learned a lot, he a good teacher you just have to be very detailed in your writing. He is also a tough grader. You have to be very specific on exactly what he is looking for. You definitely need the textbook.

Gade's lectures are clear and thorough. He really makes an effort to make sure the material is presented in a way that makes sense. Textbook is not required, but helps a lot. Tests are not difficult but are detail-oriented. While attendance is not mandatory, sometimes important videos are shown in class that come up on exams. He's a fair grader.

Gade is a great professor. Focus on the research paper, pay attention in lecture, study & you will do well. He has clear expectations. Office hours are helpful if you'd like clarification on a subject. (a few people have mentioned he can be a bit condescending, so study & avoid stupid questions) Btw- watching the Course Captures to study helps!

This class is pretty easy and he's a decent lecturer, but his grading is very biased. He grades papers so fast that he deducts random points without valid or justified reasons. Sometimes he says you are missing things even though you have clearly included them in your paper. The prompts for the essays are also pretty dumb. I wouldn't recommend him.

He's a good professor with one of the best grading formats. He drops your lowest test score (3 midterms + 1 final-all weighted equally), so you might not have to take the final! His class is pretty heavily based on essays. My GSI graded hard, or else I would have gotten a better grade. Discussion sections are basically another lecture.

Gade is a very eloquent professor. He definitely knows his material very well and presents it to the class in a rather informal (sometimes monotonous) but inviting way. Papers (3 of them) are worth a huge chunk of your grade and the final is optional (only 3 of 4 tests count and they're all weighted equally). Text is unnecessary to get an A.

Gade is great! His grading style is one of the best things ever in that your lowest exam grade (midterm or final, they're weighted equally) is dropped - so before the final, if you're satisfied with your grade, you don't even have to take the final. His lectures are also interesting and the content is not hard.
He doesn't seem to care much about engaging with students, although he is very approachable.

Made psych lectures surprisingly interesting.  I typically get bored/distracted during lectures but he kept my attention for the majority of most lectures.  Psych1 itself is an incredibly easiest class -- the easiest I've taken at Berkeley -- and is completely memorization-based.  But don't underestimate the papers!

The class is a lot of memorization, but if you put in the work, you can pass with an A.  The essays were fine if you followed the rubric and I could've gotten an A if I had followed the rubric on the first essay. Overall, good lecturer and has students participate in psych "games" or experiments for first hand application of material.

I'm terrible at Math and Professor Gade made Statistical data and analysis really interesting. 4 exams, one is dropped. very limited R data work. He really wants you to get it and will go slowly and warns you when things are about to pick up. I loved that he related what you were learning to future classes. Tedious research project but great class

Online class. Was rude when you asked him something. Had to read one chapter per week (which was long) and 2 YouTube videos. hen wrote 6-8 pages worth of notes for assignment. Exam was alright b/c it was open book. Limited extra credit points

Gade is a great instructor and definitely knows what he's talking about. He does a good job making class instructional but also engaging. Sometimes pacing seemed unnecessarily fast, but this class is so ridiculously easy. Just go to class, take good notes (take notes on ppt slides the day before!) do your homework and you'll be set.  Fun & simple.

Meh. Gade had some mood swings. His lectures were relatively clear and well outlined. Powerpoints are posted in the beginning of the course. Very little work in R and one group final paper. One of four tests dropped which saved me and had an excellent GSI. He came off as annoyed sometimes and would make snarky comments; other than that recommended.

Professor Gade is an excellent professor of psychology and his passion is clearly evident in his lectures and sidebar comments which help to get all this material into our long term memory storage. Lectures more important than the text to doing well on the tests, he likes details so pay attention to what's NOT on the deck but in his words.

Professor Gade is an excellent orator who presents the material in an extremely comprehensible fashion. Reading the textbook before attending lecture is also very helpful. Overall, I would definitely consider taking another class with him.

Psych 1 is very easy especially if you've taken AP Psych in high school. Gade makes lectures fun and interesting, definitely a class you want to go to. Tests are straightforward if you study the lecture slides, and papers are not tough if you follow the rubric. Overall a very easy, interesting class! Put in the effort and it's an easy A.

Professor Gade is funny and cute in class, clarifying psychology concepts through interactive examples, videos, and demonstrations. He clearly cares about teaching and his students, but his tests are strangely formatted. He tests mainly on specific details rather than larger concepts.

Gade was a, super hot, especially when he would get really excited about Psych and stuff. Anyway, his lectures were awesome. He was really easy to listen to and made jokes sometimes. He really enjoys Psych. I think there was a little bit of work with the GSI and then a final. The final is all about the slides and in lecture examples so go to class!

he is the definition of engaging and interesting lectures. he has so many good class exercises that make sure you dont fall asleep, so its really easy to find yourself really into the  lecture and time flies. easy-ish midterms. optional final. lots of extra credit points

The course was graded with three midterms and an optional final, in case you missed one of the midterms or you wanted to improve your grade. There aren't assignments for classes, but you will have to work on a review of three different psychology articles during the whole course.
Gade is a really great lecturer-- but I would say that the class seems easier than it actually is. Do the readings! Don't procrastinate!
Excellent professor. He teaches well. Lots of interactions with the class. Exams and papers are straightforward. Forgot to mention he's easy on eyes and looks like Chris Pratt!!
He is an animated teacher and very focused on his lectures. Be ready to stay the entire class! Term paper was a bit rough with closing topics and studies. I will admit this was not my favorite class.
Overall fun class, cute professor, and great lectures. 4 exams with the lowest score dropped, and 3 papers.
Great Professor!

He is really great! Although sometimes the concept is complicated, he can always find a easy way for us to understand. I learned a lot of useful things in this class. One of the best classes I've ever taken.

Professor Gade is just phenomenal. He uses real life examples to make complicated problem fun and easy. He is super helpful in lecture and outside of lecture. I would definitely recommend taking his class.

Gade is an awesome instructor. I took his Psych 101 last fall. Stat. is not easy but he explains everything clearly. You need to go to the lectures because the examples he gave during the lectures really helped us understanding the materials. Test are straightforward. Final project is fun. I wish we can learn more R or SPSS stuff during section tho

His lecturing is okay, but he gets annoyed at people on their phone in a 500 person lecture hall. Exams are not so great, he asks about minutia, not broad concepts, just from his lectures. The multiple choice answers are very vague and subjective.

His quizzes are based on using content learned in class and applying it to examples. One time I had him check on my paper topic and said it was okay. When I turned it in for a double check to see if I wrote my topic correctly, he said it was good. When I received my paper back, he failed me.
Gade is terrific! He's super interesting in class and he is very fair.

Gade teaches an intro to psych class so it's pretty easy. It's not the most exciting class because it is just introductory but he does a great job explaining everything and telling you about potential other classes and even careers you should consider depending on what you find interesting.

He is a cold hearted, unsympathetic professor. All he cares about is his grading curve and his reputation. He will not stick his neck out for any student who needs help or a second chance. He doesn't deserve to be a professor because he doesn't care about his students or teaching those who have higher aspirations.

The class is all regurgitating the information from lecture slides, so it's pretty annoying. I guess overall it was okay, but depended heavily on memorization rather than actually stimulating the mind/ knowing why.

Professor Gade is one of my favourite at Cal, he does a fantastic job at making it understandable! Must attend lecture, slides are online. Some students complain class is too tough, but I would say those are the students who don't attend every lecture/section. Super friendly in office hours, email responses are helpful! I'd highly recommend Gade!!

He is a fantastic lecturer! He inspired me to major in Psychology. His lectures are clear, enjoyable, and interactive. The exams are simple and papers are easy to write. Don't depend much on the book. Just go to lectures, and you'll get an A for sure. Everything is in the slides! Such a fun class! Wish I could take it again!

Constantly makes mistakes in class and students have to correct him. He teaches his own "shortcuts" for how to do problems, not in the book, and if you don't learn them you won't have time to complete the tests. He isn't helpful by email and just makes vague statements instead of answering the questions you ask. Take this class from ANYONE but him!

I loved his lectures! He is very charismatic and gives clear explanations. Went to his office hours and he was helpful. The tests are pretty straightforward as are the papers. Definitely recommend this class even if you are not a psych major and plus he isnt bad looking ;)

I took pysch 1 with Gade and I absolutely loved it. He is interactive, engaging and fun. He tends to talk fast and I recommend to attend every class as you will miss out A LOT if you don't go to even just one class. A lot of the material is from the textbook but he also plays a lot of videos that do appear in the tests. In short, I LOVED IT.
Gade was a wonderful professor and I learned a lot from his class. He is extremely helpful and this class really spurred my interest in psychology. Also the final paper was really fun.

IF YOU HAVE AN INQUISITIVE AND CURIOUS MIND, STAY AWAY. YOU WILL BE FRUSTRATED AND DISENCHANTED. Gade kills your joy for statistics. It's all memorization. Class feels like he is teaching monkeys to remember the formula and then plug it into the test questions. If you want to learn WHY, and MASTER statistics, take anyone BUT GADE.

Prof is very engaging in all of his classes. His assignments aren't too hard but he does expect good work from everyone. Will call you out if you fall asleep. Must go to class everyday to do well. Ask lots of questions and he will gladly answer.

Gade is fairly entertaining while going through the course slides. He tries to make it interesting since the class is at 8am. :( He explains concepts well and takes questions from students. He presents concepts and expectations clearly. Do not sleep in his class as one of my classmates found out. That makes him very upset and he will call you out.
Such a good professor. He is definitely interested in the subject matter and transfers that in his lectures. Psych 1 is a must-take, regardless of major.

Take 101 with Gade! He's a great professor - he makes the dry material at least somewhat engaging for students by using relatable examples, his lectures are very clear and well-organized, and he's young and has energy so class isn't boring. Homework assignments are GREAT practice for exams and can replace a bad score. The exams are fair.

No doubt one of the best professors I ever had. His lectures are clear and to the point. He offers a lot extra credit assignments. Funny and gives great memorable examples. Exams are easy as long as you study class notes and read the textbook. Highly recommend him!

Difficult. He uses a lot of his own shortcuts - which are not in the book - but if you don't master these, there isn't time to complete the tests. I did fine where we followed the book, but I could rarely finish the tests because I did not understand his shortcuts. Also, he TRIED to keep it interesting but it just wasn't.
He is one of the best teachers I have ever had. He is very clear, and never once boring or difficult to listen to during lecture. (Not hard on the eyes either!)
Great Professor - lectures were clear and concise,with detailed slides. Exams primarily on the slides, so many got by without reading the textbook. Sandy Lwi is a wonderful GSI.

The class covered a lot of interesting material and his lectures were very clear. I didn't make much use of the text book, but even though I got a pretty good grade I would recommend at least skimming. Papers were extremely easy, exams a bit harder. He offers extra credit occasionally.

IMO, Psych is probably one of the best classes where anecdotes/class demos/videos really help. And guess what - he likes to use them. a LOT. So yeah, good teaching style for the class. Class itself is pretty easy, to boot. You don't have to read the textbook but it's actually pretty fun.

I'm sitting in lecture right now, actually. Chris says everything like it's an epiphany. It gets old. It was unclear what content was going to be on the midterm. He went to school as a math major to be a math teacher, but he said he didn't like teaching math. So I get the vibe that he's not entirely into the subject he teaches. :(
very good prof, he is a nice person, he explains things clearly and gives you extra credit when it is needed. i enjoyed the stas class very much with him, and he is hot!

To succeed in this class I think one of the most important thing is coming and taking notes. This way you can learn the formulas the way he teaches them. Our class had a problem because he disagreed with the book- so I just stopped reading altogether and did fine.

I'm taking his class this semester and I'd say the course is very interesting and his teaching style is very soothing. He simplifies concepts and the projection of his voice is well suited for multi-cultural students; not to mention he is also pleasant to look at.

I was excited for this class because psychology sounded really interesting. But lectures were sooooo boring. He's a very slow speaker. I actually found the book more interesting! That said, he's very clear and it's a pretty easy course.

I was super excited for the class, loved the textbook, saw the positive reviews for Gade, but I have to say I am now pursuing other majors. A lot of the class is structured around the big names in Psychology, easy as hell essays and exams. He's not a bad teacher by any means, but I've lost any interest I had in psychology as a major.
One of the most interesting, useful, and easy class I have taken at Berkeley. Class demonstrations are fun memorable. The text book is REALLY fun to read. Highly recommended.

This is a great class if you're a non-psych major looking to fulfill one of your recs.  He's only a grad student and unfortunately, I think he's done teaching this class at Berkeley, but maybe he'll come back or the new teachers will be  comparable.  Sad.
Loved, loved, loved him!
He is the GSI for this honors thesis class.  Its a bit disorganized, but he does his job really well.  Great help with projects.
Great teacher.  One of the best that I've had in Berkeley.
Helped out a lot and was very considerate.  This was a tough class to GSI for.

He was not very interested in topic and did not really seem like he ever wanted to be there. Was not impressed by knowledge of the course or his teaching style. Compared to the other GSIs definitely did the least amount of work.
fun, easy, interesting, i actually looked forward to lectures

This teacher doesn'T know ANYTHING.  All he does is rely on the book, and then thinks his students are too dumb too pick anything up for themselves.  The chilipepper on this guy is totally overrated.  Took psych 1 in GPB last spring and he spent his time telling stupid jokes and trying the baby his students.  Take this class for an easy A.

The lectures are very clear and interesting! He presents video clips and use hilarious examples to get his points across. [i.e. the little green men-- you'll get it if you take his class] He posts his lectures up and the exams are clear and easy. BONUS: sooo hot, you'll melt!!! ;-] I wish I was still in his class.
so i totally agree with the first post.. the man is attractive. the class was pretty good too. he was really clear and thorough, you get a lot out of the class. and ... rawr.
He's not a prof. He's currently a graduate student teaching psych. He's young and he is smokey HOT HOT HOT HOT HOT HOT HOT. We need more young, hot instructors at Berkeley!
Not recommended. Poor engagement, low grades, no focus, rambling with huge ego.

Professor Hassner was great and always delivered unbiased lectures. This class was extremely fascinating and the lectures are online but the dedicated class time is used for optional Q & A (you'll do better if you go). It was a lot of reading and clear grading rubrics, if you choose two theories and know them well you'll do just fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I loved this class, and appreciated Hassner's commitment to delivering content with minimal bias, despite having a connection to many of the core issues. He always allowed dissenting opinions and hard questions. This class was made by an open environment that allowed students to express their viewpoints. Great lectures and professor cares.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Really good lectures.  Lots of reading (like, lots).  Big class but not everyone comes to lectures because lectures are recorded so class time is just for questions.  If you come to class you have a good chance to get to know him and argue.  Office hours are good too.  Tough class but rewarding.  Too much reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: By far my favorite class I have taken at Cal! Seems to genuinely care about his students, and go to office hours (he will make coffee and give you life advice). Very well respected, and has a big ego because of it occasionally.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Respected--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Amazing! He is so smart.
His PS124A was the best class I've ever taken in my life. Ask him to show you his card tricks during office hours!
Easy A.  Fun lectures.  Only problem is that it's not easy getting in to the class because of the long waiting list.

Hassner's class is as difficult as political science can get. I do not understand the reviews below, you could have dropped them if you did not like them. Hassner is amazing and inspirational. He is very tough but you learn a lot, and he walks you through everything. Take his classes, and try to get into Britt's sections, he is phenomenal.

Decent lectures but they are prerecorded.  Show up for question now and then to boost your grade.  He cares about participation and you'll do better on exams.  They're easy but asking questions helps.  Britt was an excellent GSI both tough and fair.  Try to get into one of Britt's sections.

PS114B is harder than PS124A and PS191 is even harder (but I scored A's and low A's in all three).  All exams questions are online and there are no pop quizzes so you have to be pretty dumb (or just lazy) to do bad.  Brings in some interesting guest lecturers.  Likes games and props tho some of these are more cute than useful
Generous and kind.  Really, really cares.  Go to his office hours: he will make you tea and will offer great career advice

Professor Hassner is a good lecturer. He cares about his students and wants them to understand the concepts. He will help clarify things more than once. He will also make himself available to students through office hours. However, during lectures he can get a little carried away and become a little condescending, but he is passionate and cares.

Professor Hassner has got to be one of my favorite professors during my college career. He makes history and lecture materials fun to study, and inspires me to want to learn more and actively learn. The professor's lecturing style is incredibly entertaining and well-formatted, whether it is in the QnA sessions or recorded lectures.
He's great.  Puts a lot of effort into clear and fun lectures.  Really cares and not just about class but about you and your career.  Not the easiest class but fair and def not boring.

Stellar man.  Tries hard to be fair and profesional.  No wonder Muslim and Jewish students who are against or for Israel/Palestine sit in the class together.  I guess that's why.  Respect.  Also lectures are fun and exciting.

Such an amazing professor - lectures are fascinating and captivating. He can be intense and the workload is heavy, but I think it's totally worth it to experience a truly lifechanging class on war. Seriously, the class was always a highlight of my week. The grading itself was reasonable too. A must take for any poli sci major at Berkeley.

I learned a lot about war. The first part about history of war is boring, but the second and third parts are enjoyable. The professor is knowledgeable about his topic, and very humble and helpful in office hours. The best thing is that the midterm and final prompts are posted in the beginning of the semester. Lectures are already recorded.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: If you are thin skinned or don't like your views to be challenged, this isn't the course for you. Debate and disagreements are OKAY and ENCOURAGED in this class. Ron pulls no punches and challenges all students to study war as objectively as possible. Awesome in-person lectures and truly engaging material. Only warning: Lots of reading!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Lecture heavy in a course about War in the Middle East. I felt like Prof. Hassner was more biased in this course as compared to 124A. Q+A sessions would often get a little more repetitive and lackluster with Ron often rambling. There is a lot of reading and you are graded on discussion, a quiz, a midterm, and a final. Talk to him in Office hours!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: he is the best professor i've ever had. TAKE HIS CLASSES

Great guy, great class. Super interesting content from beginning to end, though quite a lot of reading and reliance on theories from Part 2 of the class. I liked the structure of the class - asynchronous lecture with live Q and A sessions. I also appreciated how nonbiased Prof. Hassner was and how awesome his office hours were! Would recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Loved Ron (although he sold us out and then scolded /us/ for being close-minded). Never missed a lecture. Expects a lot out of midterms and finals, and you need to be able to write the way he wants. I didn't do well on the second midterm (despite all correct content), but did well on the final by tweaking my structure and writing.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Amazing lectures--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Ron is one of those professors who are super passionate and genuine. His lectures are clear cut and give real-world examples. He is indeed one of the best professors at Berkeley hands down! HE is extremely accessible and is very easy to talk to. He's a professor one can really connect with and bounce questions/ideas off of. 10/10 would recommend .
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: You get what you put in. And Ron knows this. So for the students who just want to get by (and you can get by in this class with an A, if that's all you care about) he offers foundational, clear lectures. BUT for the students who really want to learn, he assigns *excellent* readings and many opportunities to go to office hours. Your choice.

Professor Hassner provides students a great chance to engage with material and his lectures will generally keep your attention and teach you interesting new information. He can also be exceptionally disrespectful to his students and appears not to take them seriously at numerous points in class.

Ron is the best professor Ive ever had, the only class I never miss lecture and always enjoy. He is knowledgeable and funny, and cares deeply about his students. He will make active efforts to get to you know you and make himself available to talk if you just send him an email. He makes questions for midterms and finals available ahead of time!

Prof Hassners War class is incredible and one of my favorites at Cal. I definitely recommend taking it. You learn so much that is applicable outside of the realm of war and IR. Lectures are really engaging and Prof Hassner is very accessible and encourages OH visits. Class is some work but everyone is able to succeed. Offers extra credit!

Much of the material receives superficial attention. Several lecture days were wasted with insipid demonstrations and activities. In addition, I exp unfairly critical grading by my GSI (Alice). Answer structure was far more important than content. His 2 hour final is iniquitous and sets one up for sub-par performance regardless of the study guide.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Whole class is a 25 page paper (which our GSI told us needed to be 30-35 pages).  Hassner is funny but lectures were a complete waste of time and not relevant to your paper (which is 100% of your class grade).

Take Ron's War class. You'll learn a lot. Grading on the midterm and final are fair. Section attendance is worth 20% of the grade. Ron is an amazing prof who is entertaining, caring, and is excellent at explaining concepts. Go to his office hours!! He genuinely cares about each of his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: The class might seem intimidating at first (25 page essay) but really the essay is the entire class. Just don't put it all off until the last week and you'll be chilling. Lectures are not necessarily mandatory, but he does take surprise attendance.
Great guy all around that really enjoys the subject areas he teaches. The test questions options are given to you then he randomly draws which will be on the exam.

Ron is a fantastic Professor. I consider him the Dumbledore of UC Berkeley. He's amazing. Loved his lectures. Easy to talk to. Willing to work with students. His course is invaluable for learning how to take classes here at UC Berkeley. Really enjoyed the topic too! I will be taking 123H with him as well. Can't wait!

BY FAR THE BEST PROFESSOR AT CAL. Hassner is HILARIOUS. His lectures are fun and exciting and he's super cool!!! Don't sleep in class or text, he will throw chalk at you. Also, I recommend you to go to his office hours. He is soo helpful and his office looks so cool

Professor Hassner is BY FAR the most wonderful professor I've had at Cal. I looked forward to his lectures every week and am genuinely sad that I've already taken both of his classes ( PS123H and War!). Interesting lecturer and genuinely cares for his students' well-being.

Hassner expects A LOT out of his students but he holds your hand the entire time. He is funny and because he doesn't grade on lecture material, you can enjoy them without freaking out about memorizing every detail. By far the best class I've taken at Cal.

Professor Hassner is one of the best Professors I have had at Berkeley thus far. You can tell he truly cares about his students and that he creates a 30-page Final Paper to develop our writing skills and allow us to engage in a long-term research project on pretty much a topic of your choosing. I can't wait to take War! with him in the Spring!!!

As others have said, Hassner is interested in and cares about his students, which I found very encouraging - kudos to him for that - Class requires plenty of work. Readings were mostly excellent and lectures clear. Class is definitely a must if you like IR.
Good Professor, but class can be hard.

Great Class, professor gives 3 additional points for writing a film review, so many people got an A in the class. The midterm and final are 2 essays and a few ID questions. The essays needs to include the readings and lecture materials into it. The essay questions often are very vague, you need to ask your GSI to give you an outline for each essay.
Take this class! Hassner is such a genuine person. He wants to help students and encourages you to visit him during OH.  I'm looking forward to enrolling in more classes with him.

He's probably overrated, but still a good professor. Really engaged in students, super nice and helpful. He kinda dumbs it down alot, which has pros&cons. I recommend though, it's a fun class and he's good

Ron Hassner is by far the best professor I have had. EVER. He truly does seem interested in his students. He would stay after class, as long as it was necessary, to answer questions. His lectures are clear and well planned. There really is no reason why you should not get an 'A' in his class as he gives you possible exam questions well in advance.

It's true--Professor Hassner's class on war is the best class in the political science department. Probably the best class at Cal, although that is a bold statement. Incredibly interesting, engaging, and articulate, Hassner has perfected this class over many years and it truly shows.

The best Professor in Cal! One of the most interesting classes offered in Berkeley. You will not want to miss a single lecture, he is very entertaining and you learn an incredible amount of really cool information. Pr. Hassner is very approachable and fun to talk to in his OH. IF you do the readings, there is no reason you shouldn't get an A.

Professor Hassner is the best Political Science lecturer I have ever had at Cal!  If you can get in to the class, TAKE WAR. His lectures are clearly structured, well prepared, and incredibly insightful.  And go to his OH, he is very easy to talk to.  2 midterms + in-class final.  Seems pretty straightforward and easy, I expect to get an A :)

Believe me when I say this, Ron Hassner is quite possibly the best college professor in America. This man should have a shrine dedicated to him. Seriously. Do yourself an intellectual favor and take any one of his courses. You will be captivated for the entire duration.

One of the best professors I ever had! Very knowledgeable, raises interesting questions, yet absolutely clear in the presentation of ideas. Well-designed and continuously improving syllabus, very helpful during paper writing. Discussions could have been more moderated sometimes.

By far the best professor I have had at Cal. I was literally totally engaged for all 90 minutes of each of his lectures. Even if you dont get into the class (it is popular), I highly recommend just sitting in on it. Absolutely fascinating

WAR!! Seriously the best class I have ever taken in my life and Hassner is the best professor I have ever had. He is extremely helpful and loves interaction with students. GO TO HIS OFFICE HOURS HE IS AWESOME! The class isn't hard and it's so interesting you will want to go every lecture.

At times very funny, at times awesomely condescending. He covers very interesting stuff with abundant humor and seems genuinely interested in (most of) his students. I could do without the sophomoric explanations and cartoonish examples in his PP slides though. As usual, really wish I had gone to his OH. Interesting guy.
He is really dedicated to his class and his students!

He is a smart and intellectually engaging person.He knows how to keep the audience focused. He is also very friednly and helpful. He knows 4-5 languages and it is really exciting skill. He is also quite productive in the adacemic life. His courses on "War" and "Internaional Security" will positively blow your mind! Take his courses!You won't regret
He's a great professor- very organized and compelling lectures. Very interesting and engaging, awesome class!

I took this during the spring and it was absolutely difficult and hard.  He gives out 3 midterms and each one consists of 3 essays.  Also, his GSIs are extremely hard.  His lectures are confusing and he only goes out a brief study guide which is pretty much useless  trust me and take my advice.  drop him immediately!

Hassner is an amazing and engaging lecturer. His power points are clear and useful. He really wants students to succeed. Exams are easy; he gives study guides and provides one hour reviews before the exam. Great course! highly recommend it

Hassner is one of the best lecturers at Cal - he's funny, well-informed, exciting and energetic.  He definitely keeps the entire class interested. Topic is awesome and his organization and clarity makes it easy to understand the topic. Definitely don't miss out on this one!

Ron Hassner is an excellent teacher.  He is truly in his element when lecturing, he assigns interesting readings and his class is well balanced bewteen theories of war, history, and current issues.  War! is one of the best classes a student of IR could hope for.

Professor Hassner is brilliant and funny, and makes it apparent in lecture. As a lecturer, you can't get much better than he is. He always has power points, always outlines his lectures, sticks to his outlines, makes his points perfectly clear..... he makes a complex subject interesting and easy to understand.
I think he's overrated, but not too bad.  There's too much "setup" for the main part of the class, and his lectures are so-so.
Awesome Class! Hassner is super fun and I found his lectures to be engaging. Oh yeah, and he is SUPER HOT! His wife just had a baby, and he is super cute!

One of the nicest, genuine professors out there.  Encourages office hours and presses students beyond what they thought they could achieve.  Brilliant, down to earth. A bit theory driven, but none the less interesting.
Extremely smart. Wants students to become better writers and know a lot about the subject of war. He is a great. PS 124A is related to PS 120, but it completely stands on its own.

Great professor, funny and entertaining.  Awesome readings, killer power point presentations (Behold, the power of powerpoint).  Go to his OH--he has cookies and a comfy couch!  He is so witty and charming--I totally had a crush on him.

Prof. Hassner is very knowledgeable, easily approached, and has a good lecturing style. The assigned readings are interesting and relevant. The simulation really brought the class together and made good friends out of strangers. Definitely take this class, even if it's only to participate in the simulation.

Hassner's War! class is one of the best classes I have ever taken here! Hassner is a great lecture...certainly a rising star in the department. The Arms Negotiation is simply amazing. You really get to know the students in the class and the professor in a way that seldom happens here at Cal. Hassner also examines the topic of war in a fair way.

This is best class I have had at Cal. Very interesting topic that is brought to life by Hassner (a top notch prof). Despite being a class of 100 people, it seems quite small and I know many people in the class (from the big arms control simulation, which is really fun). Very organized lectures--Hassner, smart and approachable. TAKE THIS CLASS!!!!

Best class ive ever taken at cal, and one of my favorite professors, if you do not take this class and you are a poli sci major, you have missed out in a major way. He made a class of three hundred people seem small, at the end of the semester i knew every person in the class as well as him and my GSI  ALI is the GSi i had and she is great!

This is without a doubt the best class I ever had at Berkeley. The lectures are clear and concise, the reading is interesting, and the activities are totally fun. Also, Hassner is very approachable. Go to his office hours! Also, take this class. Seriously.

SOMEWHAT CHALLENGING, BUT WORTH IT. YOU KNOW WHAT IS EXPECTED OF  YOU, AND YOU'RE EXPLICITLY GUIDED AS TO HOW YOU NEED TO ACQUIRE YOUR GRADE OF PREFRENCE, NO SUPRISES. YOU'LL BE SORRY WHEN THE CLASS IS OVER.
awesome
War! the class is really good. Prof Hassner has an unmatched enthusiasm for the material that really comes across in lecture.

this treacher is an amazing professor, who is very passionate about his work.. he is so articulat that even the most difficult of points seems very clear when he explains it.. take his classes..seriously
My favorite prof so far, this guy is awesome.  Very inviting, very very intelligent.  Go to his office hours.. take the class, but go to his office hours also.

Amazing professor. Exams are very straightforward and the readings are interesting. Gives you a list of possible exam questions so that there arent any surprises on test day. He is very charismatic and even has an arms control simulation which is a lot of fun. Definitely take him and go to office hours.

One of the best professors ever. Requests that students come and speak to him. Very intelligent, and a great lecturer. Teacher War, so the subject matter is great too. A lot of reading, but what do you expect from Cal?
Very unclear and unwilling to explain topics to students. Wouldn't take again.

Doesn't give clear answers; in fact, after office hours, she leaves students more confused than they already are. I learn more asking AI to explain concepts and textbook examples combined than from her. She says: "textbook will help" for everything, but she doesn't mention herself to support students. She also favors Japanese descent students
very interesting classes, kind professor
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: One of the best Japanese teacher.  She is very clear in her lectures and explains difficult materials well.  She is also a very funny teacher and makes the class very fun.  Very patient in office hour.  Willing to stay overtime to help me understand the readings.

Imagawa sensei is a very funny, happy, sagacious teacher. She is very helpful and creates a healthy comfortable classroom environment. you are expected to learn a memorize a lot of grammar and vocab in the class, so having a teacher like Imagawa sensei is key to doing well.
It's real Stoica... teaching. Guys please, take advantage of your berkeley years. Comments from CMU SCS.

Goes far beyond surface-level operating systems concepts. Instead of just memorizing how virtual memory or scheduling works, you are forced to understand the invariants, failure modes, and performance tradeoffs behind real systems.
Not that engaged
He can't teach at all. Thinks he is too smart for the students.
