got touched
Amazing professor, its great and is a great lecturer, Amazing professor, its great and is a great lecturer
Amazing professor, its great and is a great lecture, Amazing professor, its great and is a great lecturer
Amazing professor, very clear voice and always happy to answer any student questions!
Amazing professor, very clear voice, and always happy to answer any student questions!

Class is a must take but if you can avoid Stoica I would. Droning and mumbling 90 minute lectures, and he forced in some overly complicated scheduling algorithm when we were still learning the basics. Ended up watching lecture videos from years past for most of the term.  On the credit side his homework assignments were interesting.

Told it was going to be hybrid, ended up being remote. Projects were Sisyphean, even in a group of 4. Homeworks and the 3 "Midterms" were just as difficult. Stoica's lectures were dry, confusing, and content-heavy, with no real flow to them (he's def a researcher, not a teacher). Discussion GSI's read off of slides from their gamer chairs via Zoom.
Great professor; highly recommend taking 61B with him.

i loved josh hug. i think i want to become a cs major bc of this class and this man. literally so fun and engaging and i actually think i understood and learned data structures well. please take 61b with hug hes amazing

He's an entertaining lecturer, is up to date with meme humor and has funny, reasonably timed and appropriate side tangents. He talks too fast sometimes and he's better suited for someone who can keep up with a fast paced lecture. Not a fan of how he drastically changed the 61B format this year without giving us a study guide on the new format.
I learn all data structure knowledge from him and get a job at NV.

Although the class has a heavy workload and exams are difficult, I cannot imagine a better intro CS class. Professor Hug prepared us extremely well for basic coding interviews and taught problem-solving and algorithms in a way that stuck with us for a long time. Always grateful for CS61B!

Very nice, understanding, and accommodating professor. Also a fantastic, personable instructor. He explains concepts super well in class and recorded videos. Definitely take a class with him if you can, there's a reason he's a Distinguished Teaching Award winner!

Hug's lectures are amazing!!! I feel like I learn so much after every lecture. The class is fair if you put in the effort, starting projects early & doing practice exams. Hug is very passionate for CS and this was my fav class at Cal so far. ABSOLUTELY TAKE THIS CLASS!!! 🐐🐐🐐

Honestly, he made 61B actually fun, and I loved to watch the youtube videos. For someone who does not know how to code very well he explained concepts super well and made them very digestible. He made 61B not as fearsome as people made it out to be.
Hug is easily the best professor in Berkeley, lowkey not close. Loved 61B, 195, and would take every CS class I could with him if it was possible. My 🐐.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Although my iteration of CS61B was taught by Kao + Yokota, I found myself watching prof Hug's prerecorded lectures a lot and was amazed at how prof Hug was able to explain really hard concepts like it was second nature. I thoroughly enjoyed applying what I learned to assignments and hope one of my future classes will be taught by this guy.
Professor Hug is great! His passion for was definitely prevalent in his lectures. Although the content was a bit challenging, he was able to explain it in such a way that it felt second nature.
Best lecturer I've ever seen. He makes everything so intuitive and builds your knowledge from the ground up with no assumptions, which I needed.

hug exemplifies the qualities of a great professor 4 required, but tedious subject matter. many of the STEM faculty here lack the ability to understand how newcomers may be intimidated by material. however, the empathy hug has cultivated makes 4 engaging & digestible lessons, which over time have created hug a positive, almost fatherly reputation.
Hug is a nice guy. I give him 4 only becasue I do not want people over-and-overate him. I think I would like him more if he is an EE instructor.

CS61B was probably the hardest class I have ever taken. Fortunately, Hug was easily accessible outside of class and the homework was minimal. He was also such a character. Project 3 was overly difficult and the class was too theoretical for me. Discussions and lab sections were pointless.
Great lectures and manageable workload. A lot of engaging projects which didn't feel like a chore to complete.

an amazing lecturer and a genuinely great person. exams are tough, but as long as you watch his lectures, stay on top of work, and maximize your time in discussions, you'll do just fine. clobber is pretty decent.
Absolutely inspirational
One of the best professor I ever had at Cal. Explains concept clearly, makes fairly generous curves, and is very caring for students.
Josh Hug is one of the best professors in Cal. His lectures are inspiring and very useful for preparing the future career in CS. Highly recommended.
Awesome lecture. Explain complicated algorithms from simple, intuitive concepts. The project is also pretty good.
Nice, interesting, patient, fun.

CS10 is an awesome class, and Josh Hug is probably the best lecturer I've had. Course was well structured and accommodating during the pandemic. I'm a non CS-related major, and this class was a great introduction to the subject and isn't too difficult. Grading is fair. No homework, but there are exams, labs, and projects.

Prof hug is a nice guy and funny. However, he made CS195 feel more like an afterthought than anything. He often to forgot to update the course site for assignments and left students clueless. Also, what's the deal with 3 papers? This isn't a humanities course. Not to mention, the grading approach was very sloppy and unclear.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--So many papers

reviews.comment: Hug is a great lecturer and will help with any question any student may have, no matter how big or small. I advise you to at least go to one of his office hours just to get to know him a little bit more outside of class. The tests can be very difficult sometimes, but he acknowledges and gives extra points in compensation. He's great overall!
The immortal best cs professor in my heart

61B is the best I've taken at Berkeley so far. Hug is an amazing lecturer and his style of teaching suits me very well. He usually starts with a problem, the obvious solution, and then makes his way to the optimal solution which I find very effective. Even though you'll probably take this class for a req, try to appreciate how cool the content is.
Hands-down the best CS class I've taken and the best CS professor I've had so far. I learned so much in this class, especially from the projects.

Great class! Lectures are easy to follow and keep your attention. Tests feel a lot more fair than 61A. If you understand the material you will do well, they aren't meant to trick you. Projects are tough, don't procrastinate.
Dude literally saved someone's life during the course. 10/10 would take again.

This class is the hardest one I have taken so far. Lectures are pre-recorded and come to the professor's Q&A sessions. Projects are a lot of work and the TAs are easily accessible in office hours on Discord. The exams are challenging and I didn't do so well on them. Due to the pandemic, your final exam score can replace two midterm scores.

Gives few partial credit and is graded mainly by exams, his 61b is way tougher than Hilfinger's and is much harder than 61A to get an A in. His lectures are great and available on youtube publicly but he's a harsh grader and exams don't reflect understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: At the end of the day Professor Hug is good at teaching. You watch the lecture, you'll know the content, however outside of lecture he's pretty much non-existent and hard to reach. The course itself is tough and very exam-heavy, so while Professor Hug is a happy face to see-- be prepared to work hard in his class.

I don't even attend UC Berkeley, however, I am taking a data structures course at my college which is not great at all. I found Professor Hug's course online(since he posts it online). I can confidently say this course has made me a much better programmer, and wish I had the opportunity to learn from Hug in person. Amazing prof and very passionate
One of the best classes I've taken at Cal thus far.
Good guy!

Josh Hug is one of the best professors I've had at Cal. He's a true gem within the CS/DS departments. I really love how organized his lecture slides are and how he's always eager and prepared for lecture.
Nice course for Data Structure. Lectures are clear and impressive but projects are a little tough.
Great instructor. I attended every single lecture because I enjoy the way he gives lectures.

I took 61B with Hug and now I'm taking Data 100 with him just because he's teaching it. I didn't even want to do data science but Hug is teaching it soo... I can't rave enough about this man. Aside from his glorious lectures, Josh is the most caring person in this cursed land. He lifted me out of depression. Appreciate him while you live.

He puts an incredible amount of work into the class and it shows. He explains difficult topics in an easy to understand way and really wants his students to learn and succeed. The projects can be a lot of work, but they are a great learning experience. The tests are very difficult, but doable. There are lots of resources to do well in the class.

Best frickin CS lecturer I had! He puts in a lot of work into his lectures and it shows. He is very clear in communicating his points and very friendly and approachable outside of class. He understands that students have other classes and commitments and tries to make things easy while still keeping the class effective. 10/10 would recommend.
He is a very nice person and very enthusiastic in what he's teaching. Thank you very much!
He came out of a garbage can on the last day of lecture.

His first time teaching DS100. He's a nice lecturer and nice guy overall, but I think his 61B class is better. Data 100 got very hard last semester. Prof. Perez and Prof. Hug set tough exams with not much good prep material. Lots of math and a new robust introduction to machine learning. Good class and homeworks that are industry relevant.
His lectures are amazing. I went to his office hours every week and my interactions with him were always delightful and super valuable.

The best professor by far that I had at Berkeley. So funny and relatable. I talked to him about lief during OH. GSIs are super nice and amazing. Organized course, but it was difficult. Projects are difficult--plan your code before you implement it. Do all the practice midterms available. Hardest questions are on creating your own data structure.
Josh was wonderful!

Josh Hug is an excellent Professor with infectious charisma and a great lecture style. He is one of the only Professors who I thoroughly enjoyed attending his lecture. He cares tremendously about his students and is very fair. I look forward to taking more classes with him in the future :)

Josh Hug is singlehandedly the greatest professor you can learn from. All you want to do is be bestest of pals with Joshua Hug. He is inspirational, funny, and great at delivering concepts. 10/10 would recommend to a friend.
Hug is pretty friendly to students but I don't really like his lecture style

Hug is absolutely the best. He really cares about his students, which makes him one of the kind in a large university. The tests are really challenging but manageable, and he will seriously consider your regrade requests if you really have a point. Overall, if I were to take 61B again I wouldn't take it without Hug.

Hug is a great professor, gives fun lectures, and the homework and projects he gives out are reasonable. He releases assignments a bit late though, and exams can be very challenging. Despite this, he is an excellent professor overall and can explain material well.
Best professor I've ever had at Cal. Great lecturer, hilarious guy, and realllly cares about the students. He knows 61B is tough and gives all the support he can.
Such a great professor, couldn't recommend more. Not only a genius but hilarious, understanding, fair, and an overall very effective teacher. Don't take 61B without Hug!

Great professor. Really puts incredible effort in TEACHING the material effectively with interactive lectures and demos. Projects are hard but (generally) worthwhile and interesting. Of course, tests are worth a lot of your grade and the class is ultimately challenging but you learn a lot.  Better than 61A. Really recommend.

I took two classes with him and he is absolutely an amazing lecturer. His lectures are not heavy with conceptual/theoretical aspects, his demos are pretty helpful. I have never actually physically been to his lectures, I follow his webcasts and I didn't have a problem so far. In terms of grading midterms are much easier than our own Hilfinger
A great Professor! Definitely recommend taking CS 61B with him.  The class is challenging but he is very supportive and helpful!
Seriously one of the best professors I've ever had

One of the best professors I've had.  I had him for CS61B and CS195, and both were great experiences.  He's very accessible and not intimidating.  Explains things clearly and generally runs his classes very well. Definitely known as one of the cooler professors. (Also, I've heard he's a dank memer)
There is truly nothing negative about the Notorious H.U.G.

He is an incredible Professor. One of the few Professors who actually cares for the people he is teaching in as much as he cares about what he is actually teaching them. He empathizes with students and offers help and alternative routes when he realizes that the students are overwhelmed. It was a pleasure taking the class from him.

Overall I liked Hug's teaching style and laid-back-ness. I found his lectures decently entertaining. Two downsides for me, though, were lack of organization (like getting assignments out on time), and subtle hints of condescension or not caring a lot about the students on an individual basis. But still worth it to take his class!

Hug is a really inspirational teacher. He clearly cares about his students, is easy to talk to, and manages the class very well. He is very receptive and responsive to any feedback from the students, so the class is fair. This semester, however, the large software engineering project, Editor, was extremely difficult. But overall, an amazing prof.

Simply fantastic professor - never a dull moment in his class, teaches the material amazingly well and gives projects that make you bleed, but ones that also teach you a lot more about CS than anything else could (while balancing it all very well for students). Hats off!

Way more interesting than 61A and I highly recommend it. People complain about the projects but honestly those were a cakewalk (the notorious second one took me about a week and the other ones I did it over the weekend). However the exams were hard as hell and since everyone gets 100% on the other stuff they are the deciding factor so good luck.
I wish I could hug Josh Hug :(

Josh is awesome, he's really easy to talk to and super fun. I've been to his office hours many times and he's super helpful. Lectures are interesting and interactive, we have iclicker questions or sometimes guest speakers. He is very flexible and understands when things aren't going as planned, he changed deadlines when issues arose.

Every once in a while there comes that professor that completely changes your perspective on a subject. Josh Hug is one of those professors. He is an amazing lecturer, and layed a great foundation for learning computer science. I come into this class iffy about whether I wanted to do CS but now I am sure I want to make it a part of my life.
so chill.

Josh is one of the finest profs I've had at Cal. Lectures are delivered with wonderful clarity and eloquence, so that even hard materials are easy to follow, understand and process. He's also super funny and so considerate. Devoted to helping students in & out of office hours. I wasn't into CS before but this class is life-changing.
Great professor, one of the best at Cal. Makes even difficult problems and concepts accessible.

Josh is the best professor I've had at Cal. His lectures always seem like he's just talking to you individually, explaining complicated structures like they're nothing. If I could take every CS class with him I totally would. He really cares about his students.

He is super enthusiastic and loves to connect with students at every given opportunity. Although the class is large, he makes himself approachable and available. He's funny and young, too. He knows the material very well, and his projects are hard but doable. In the end, you feel like a more independent programmer and project designer.

The class is hard and time consuming like any other cs class.   But josh definitely makes it enjoyable and manageable.  He also truly cares about his students: he'd be up at 1 in the morning answering piazza posts and helping people on their projects- that's dedication.
Super clear lectures, responds to Piazza + emails, really cool guy. Cares about student experience a lot. Highly recommend taking any class with him. Ask for a hug at the end of the semester lol

An absolutely wonderful professor who is an example of the best Berkeley has to offer. I liked 61A, but I LOVED 61B. Projects are hard but manageable, grading policies are extremely reasonable, and he loves his students. Amazing class (best ever?)

Perhaps the best professor I've had at Cal.  Lectures aren't as dry as previous CS classes I've had as he tries to make the lectures entertaining. Very helpful and responsive to comments or when asking for help. Very open to feedback and suggestions. During projects he made them a lot more bearable by giving quick introduction videos to them. 1010
Josh only joined the faculty a summer ago, but if you want definitive proof that Berkeley's CS department rightfully deserves its place at the top of the universe, take 61B with Hug.

Honestly the best professor that I've had at Cal. He truly cares about his students, is so open to feedback and willing to help his students. He made 61B a little bearable and always made videos to make the projects easier to understand because the skeleton was usually really complicated. Take 61B with Hug!!!!

JHug is the bomb! He's an excellent professor, very clear and willing to help. He'll get to know students individually and hold extra sessions for reviewing for tests. He's a super nice guy and a great CS professor. Would take again
Josh Hug saved me from the wrath of Lord Hilfinger's projects with his videos. Definitely learned a bunch in this class and 1010 would take again!
Josh is amazing and has a true passion for teaching.
Dude is the bomb.

Josh Hug is very entertaining, smart and engaging. You must take his class if you haven't taken EE40. His lecture notes are very clear and straight forward. EE40 with Josh Hug is by far my favorite class I have ever taken in my life. SERIOUSLY.
awesome guy but i'm afraid he's going to give me "the darts."
Bad lecturer, mumbles, can only hear 50% of what he says, lecture content is completely different form the lecture slides, slides filled with so much words but he doesn't go over them

Absolutely atrocious. Ong he had to have taken these slides from somewhere else. There's so many words on the slides that he doesnt go over and so i have no idea how to study for the exam. on top of that, IN GENERAL THERE ARE JUST TOO MANY WORDS. he is super unorganized and boring. the WORST out of the three professors teaching this class.

One of the WOREST prof I ever have. Lectures are SOOOOOOO dry and boring. HE DOESN'T KNOW HOW TO TEACH. He only put tons of facts on the slides and read off his slides. Even the GSI it better than him.

I took this class Spring 24. His lecture material wasn't particularly difficult to grasp and he would let us ask questions during lec. He isn't the most engaging lecturer (kinda dry) and is honestly very soft-spoken. It can be easy to doze off when he's presenting. His exams are really generous though and he's kind/patient. Overall a chill dude.
very enthusiastic professor

Great professor and class. Most lectures were structured around learning a sustainability transition framework and then a case study that fits it. There was one group project. A fair amount of readings, but they were all really interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: class was super chill, you are graded off of two problem sets, a group project, and a final essay. The professor and GSI were great and want you to succeed. definitely recommend this class to anyone interested in the topic

One of the best at Berkeley. A bright light. Provides in depth knowledge and meets students where they are at, which is rare and valuable at an institution where those struggling with personal difficulties and/or disability are often met with a lack of depth, compassion, and support.

If you have the chance to take this new class, I totally recommend it! Prof and teaching team are so kind and want the best for you. The lectures are so interesting and incredibly useful for anyone doing anything remotely environmental. Def one of the classes that'll stick with me!

Alastair has been one of my most favorite professors I've had here! His class is so neatly organized and his personal grading is really fair. He really encourages critical thinking and wants you to learn more than anything. I loved going to his office hours! He is super accommodating and very helpful. Subject might seem intimidating but it's not!

Professor and his whole team work really hard and the amount that the course is interactive is super engaging. If you have any attention deficit then lectures are fast and tough to follow. For assignments I felt like I was missing information or a prereq somehow, could have just been me :/
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This was one of my favorite professors of all time! Amazing lectures, amazingly clear and concise and engaging. Highly highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The class format (GSI delivering lecture with Prof. Iles delivering occasional comments) took some getting used to, but I really enjoyed this class. Prof. Iles is very caring & helpful if you choose to write the research essay/policy intervention for the midterm assignment, and will be flexible with deadlines. Heavy reading/essay workload (3 total)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--Caring

reviews.comment: The lectures are pretty straightforward but there is an amount of reading that is essential in the most part for the midterm and final
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Iles was one of my favorite professors at Berkeley! The class was entirely lecture-based, with the GSI reading off Professor Iles' lecture, and although it sounds a little boring, the material was always extremely interesting. There is a lot of assigned reading, and you'll need to at least skim it in order to keep up.

This class changed what I want to do with my life, it was tremendously influential and very interesting. It will be difficult if you don't have any prior knowledge of environmental issues and how they work, as much of the course is discussing solutions to these problems.

Very good professor. He truly cares about his students. I must say that you will struggle in this class if you don't have a base level understanding of the environment. I did not at all and it was difficult. They say you don't need to have one, but in lecture it can get pretty complicated even though he tries to thoroughly explain some topics.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Environmental Policy, Law, and Management is as dry of a subject as it sounds.  The fact that a GSI reads Iles's lectures with minimal enthusiasm doesn't help (Iles is deaf, but has an effective system to keep this from negatively affecting student learning).  I never went to class, just copied the power points & read about half the articles.
Alastair is a fantastic professor- he is involved with his students' interests and whipsmart.  Take his classes if you can!

This was a great class. Although the three papers and the final exam were pretty time consuming, they were all graded very easily and also pretty enjoyable if you are interested in environmental issues. While the professor unfortunately cannot speak to the class, he puts much effort into writing good lectures and including interesting material.

A great professor- you will learn a ton in his class.  The hearing impairment makes for challenging communication at times, but he has worked out a great system for delivering his lectures with GSIs, and is able to respond to questions and give feedback with a computer.  Thoughtful research assignments.  Overall, a fantastic class.

I came into the class having never taken ESPM and I came out wanting to major in a similar area. The class is heavily dependent on the course reader, having to read about 2 long articles before each lecture.  It was very hard for me to take in the information at lecture due to the way Iles had to have the head GSI read his lectures.

Professor Iles's lectures are well-written.  It is obvious that he puts a lot of effort into preparing them, which I appreciate.  Also, he has a good sense of humor.  This class requires a lot of reading, but it is not too hard.

Alistair is a great and this class is a good introductory course for anyone interested in environmental policy. When it comes to grades, he is generous and understanding. The class might take a while to adjust to since his hearing impairment makes the GSI the actual speaker. Maybe technology will improve the way he teaches. Overall, great class.

Taking Data 104. Does Mursinna know he doesn't have to lecture like a self-aggrandizing TEDTalk speaker all the time? I'm. trying. to. learn. about. Silicon. Valley. but. I. can't. pay. attention. because. he's. talking. like. this. with. the. strangest. vocal. inflections. ever. His cadence of voice is grating.

Lots of reading, but content covered again in lectures. Lectures were super interesting and felt like he was telling a story. Grading sets up students for success. You'll do well if you do the readings (just skim them, he explains further in lecture), go to lectures, and participate in discussion. He made content I usually find boring interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This class is reading heavy but each subject is covered 3 times (in reading, discussion, and lecture). Mursinna's lectures are entertaining, easy to follow, and rarely off topic. This is mainly because he reads off of a script which is off putting at first but I became used to it quickly. Lectures were not recorded and exams were graded easily.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This is a great class! If you show up and immerse yourself in the topic and readings you can get a lot out of it. Mursinna is passionate about what he teaches, and I found his lectures to be very insightful. Class is lecture heavy and reading heavy, but content is interesting and if you pay attention you should do fine. Take this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great course design and lectures! The professor is really well prepared, with clear organization and supplementary materials. Lectures highlight key points that make the readings easier to digest. The course is structured around a theme introduced in the first lecture, which creates a strong throughline that deepens understanding beyond the surface

A good lecturer, but his lectures can be stressful. You're expected to take notes on pretty much everything he says & he is a fast talker. But if you do the weekly readings you honestly don't need to go to the lectures, since attendance isn't required & they tend to go over the same content. I only went to ~1/3rd of the lectures and still did great
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: terribly dry lectures, the worst i have encountered in 3 years here. its overly scripted, sounds like a pretentious youtube video essay. other than that the workload is fine, the exams are fair.

Nice professor. Class has a good amount of reading with weekly responses in discussion. He puts nothing on his slides and reads off his script for the lecture, so you have to pay attention. Overall though, if you do the readings and listen the tests are very predicable and reasonable. Your GSI is what really matters.

Class was overall pretty easy if you completed weekly readings (there are a LOT). He was pretty boring and monotone but it is clear that he wants students to succeed and does his best to set you up for success. GSI's kind of make or break since there are two hour discussions every week that you're trapped in.

Lectures were amazingly delivered. If you attend the lectures and complete the ~60 pgs of readings per week, you'll have everything you need to perform well. The professor is also very considerate of our time and cancels lectures on weeks with midterms. He's also approachable and genuinely wants his students to do well.

This professor simply was not for me. I think it is important to know before taking this class that all of his lectures are him reading from a huge packet of prewritten lecture. So the whole time he is basically looking down at the paper and speaking in the way one writes, not the way one speaks/delivers information. Some may like it, I did not.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great Professor, very intelligent and actually wants his students to learn. Weekly written short quiz but you will always do well if you did the assigned reading. Tests also written but fair. Most reasonable professor I have ever had at Berkeley, unlike many other professors on campus. Great format and he's somehow makes its extremely interesting.

He is a an intimidating person. He is knowledgeable and passionate about what he teaches. No notes on slides, write everything down. Assigns 70 pages of reading a week. Reading quizzes every week. Thoughtful participation affects your grade a lot. Just memorize history well enough and exams will be fine. Grades writing sorta harsh. Daunting class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Great lectures that are very interesting, can tell he is passionate and will make jokes about historical figure. Nothing on the slides so you need to write everything. Quizzes every week and lots of reading 50-75 pages every week, can be hard, final exam before RRR week. Attendance to discussion mandatory. Your grade really depends on your GSI.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Mursinna is always super prepared for lecture and covers all the key points efficiently, but doesn't post recordings (take notes!). Exams don't require much in-depth knowledge; you can get by with just key ideas since specific dates, locations, or people aren't required. Weekly (< 1 pg, easy) timed writings, one 5-7 pg paper, 1 midterm.

Very good professor. Lectures always finished 30 minutes early, and our final exam was two weeks before actual finals which was so nice in the long run. He's very accessible and helpful outside of class, but do note that this class is basically entirely GSI dependent. Also, as a straight man, he's devilishly handsome.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great Class. Make sure to participate cause getting a 92 in participation kept me from getting an A which I would have gotten with just 3 more participation points.

I really enjoyed Professor Mursinna as a teacher; his lectures were very interesting. Even though attendance isn't mandatory you should go to lecture since it isn't recorded and the slides he post don't really have any content on them. Get ready to read 80 pages a week and get tested on the reading every week in section with a reading response.

Decently easy class, but SO much reading per week and mandatory reading reviews every week during section (that makes up most of your grade). Lectures are lowkey not that crucial and it's mostly professor just yapping but also kind of interesting.

This class involved too much reading as a STEM major. Sometimes, the reading took away from my technical classes. The lectures were not mandatory but there were no recordings and hardly any content on slides so you had to listen the entire time, so I missed some information. Can use chat GPT to summarize readings + section helps analyze dense texts
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Lots of reading, with weekly short writings in section based off of readings. Lecture attendance isn't mandatory, but recordings are not available and the lecture slides don't have notes on them, just pictures, so go to lecture. Professor is engaging. Go to class, do the readings, youll be find. Grade largely depends on which GSI you get.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Never went to any of his lectures (he didn't record lecture) and his slides were posted but weren't good at all, each slide had a picture with some words, but I would take the class again. Grade is determined by your GSI, clear rubric layout. Weekly readings, around 50-70 pages, never did it and reading responses every week was doable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Mursinna was a great teacher and his lectures were genuinely interesting. Class is an hour and a half but he really only lectures for an hour. Reading each week is heavy but if you split it up over the week its not bad. The most painful part of this course was the 2 hour long discussions which aren't that helpful in my opinion.

frankly the course is the real problem, not prof. don't take it as a breadth unless its last resort, my gsi was a bum and bro treated this class like our life depended on it, graded way too hard for a breadth. not worth the time and effort, just take another breadth.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One day of the week has a ~10-15 minute warm up question on the assigned readings. Grading was fair, but you do have to be at least somewhat engaged with the material to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Ignacio was an incredible lecturer! I felt like I could engage strongly with the material and he definitely made me think of my role on earth so much differently. The syllabus was a bit messy, but I learned a lot, and formed a great group of friends by attending his field opportunities! DO NOT skip those, they're so fun!!

He's a kind and passionate professor who is constantly questioning the world around him + enjoys conversational lectures. No hw other than 2 tracks to pick from: quizzes throughout the semester or writing for the final. I recommend the writing track, it's not graded harshly and it's more of a way for you to write about what you're interested in.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Class was easy to follow but a little unstructured sometimes. Very accessible.

Very easy class, didn't go to lecture or discussion at all. I chose the quiz track, 3 very manageable quizzes, one microcosm project, one field opportunity project, and that was pretty much it. The instructions were a bit brief for the projects but very doable. Definitely an interesting class if you engage.

Really enjoyable class. Prof liked to make lectures a conversation and encouraged us to share our ideas, even if they were contrary to his own. I chose the writing track which ended up being one 2-3 page, hand written essay, a field opportunity, and microcosm project. Guidelines weren't super clear, but all the assignments were interesting.
Very passionate and knowledgeable professor.

I choose the quiz track and it only requiered 3 quizzes, the semester long project, and field opportunity. Professor Chapela is really cool and passionate about what he teaches. Attendance is not mandatory, and he turns the discussions into field opportunities in the mornings or office hours, very accessble even tho getting an A is easy.

Extremely easy A. Didn't go to any lectures and discussion sections were made into optional office hours, but a really interesting and passionate guy who wants class to be a discussion. You get what you put into it.
ESPM6 is a fascinating course if you attend lectures and engage. You get what you give, and you sometimes have to be patient, but Chapela is an unconventional, exceptional professor.

I'm slightly disappointed because I don't think I could tell you much about what I learned during the course, but he's a really nice guy and super open to conversation/feedback. If you need an easy science breadth definitely go for it

Professor Chapela is a very kind and caring professor. The lectures are not a lecture and instead a non-mandatory discussion. As long as you do the work (4 quizzes/2 papers, microcosm project, and field opportunity) with good effort, you will get an A. He makes sure to not stress grades. I'd recommend for a easy breadth.

What you put in is what you get out. Grades aren't a concern in this class. It's essentially a discussion between Chapela and the class about any biology-related subject matter that either Chapela or the class finds interesting. I found it enriching, but I could see how it may be boring for others. Take for easy A or for philosophical discussion.

Ignacio is the most inspiring professor I've met at Cal. It's an honor to get to speech with him and he's truly the wisest person I have ever met!

As for his classes, they are very much so a "you get out what you put in" situation, but I would highly encourage putting in that work. Doing so, I've learned more than I have in any other class.
Best class at Cal! Take it if you can! I absolutely loved the class.

ESPM 6 is the best way to fulfill the biology breadth requirement. The grade is made by a few easy quizzes, a field opportunity, and a semester-long simple project. Everyone needs to take Ignacio Chapela's class while at Berkeley - an excellent, caring professor.

Ignacio is one of the most inspiring people I have ever met. He inspired me to choose biology as my major concentration. I highly recommend taking if you are interested in learning about biology in a more philosophical manner. You will get out as much as you put in. You can decide to write 2 papers (track 1) or take quizzes to get a grade (track 2)

Prof. Chapela is frankly dope. He's extremely understanding and makes a point of not grading harshly or really even emphasizing grades at all. During my time in ESPM 6 all that was required of me was weekly quizzes and a semester long project which was easy, fun, and engaging. The de-emphasis of grades makes the class/everything much more enjoyable
My favorite Prof on campus. Please go to class if you can! Such a beautiful community and breath of fresh air and truth with Ignacio.
Loved this class and would take anything he teaches again

I'm a terrible student and never attended a singular lecture for this class. But I chose Track 2 where we only had 4 quizzes, a microcosm project, and a field opportunity and that consisted of the whole semester. No final! Quizzes were unbearably easy. Project was interesting as hell. Field opportunity only took me an hour. Great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Inspirational--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Extremely easy A, choose the quiz track. You don't need to go to any lectures but keep in mind you will likely learn nothing. GPA boost, all it is.

Easiest class of my life. Skipped lecture and discussion all semester, aced the super easy online quizzes, and got an A having probably spent 20 minutes a week on this class. Professor Chapela is honestly a super cool guy though, so if you have time go to his office hours and talk to him!

Ignacio is a special professor unlike any other you'll have on campus, he inspires and cares about you PLEASE go to his field days, meet him during office hours, have tea with him,ect. I have taken him for 2 classes and admit some of his lectures can be Off-tangent but any of his field offerings will teach you so much about Berkeley's environment.

This class was so easy. Choose the quiz track!! I didn't go to most lectures and got an A. Lectures did not seem connected to quizzes but would be important for essay track ppl. Just do the study guide very completely and you will be fine. Grading is very generous and he wants you to pass. Its very much, you will get out what you choose to put in.

Although not always clear with communicating and instructions, Ignacio cared about his students, especially during online learning. He was very flexible and accommodating but also passionate about what he taught. The class required minimal effort but was still very engaging and valuable!

I learned not one thing in this class. The two assignments that determined my grade were a midterm & final paper on whatever I wanted really. If you're selecting this from a list of major requirements, select something else. I was really excited for this class but it really let me down. It's pointless attending lec or dis

Ignacio is a really cool guy and super passionate about microbiology! His lectures were engaging and I wish we could've gone out in the field. There are a lot of terms he throws out that are not always defined in the slides which can get confusing. Also, the class structure is a bit disorganized. You won't know where you stand with your grade.

Literally learned nothing (not complaining since I was just taking it for easy A), but it's still pretty insane how disorganized this dude is ... Most tilting thing is probably him saying that there's going to be a "quiz 5 that will be posted" which just never happened ... probably worth it if you're looking for an easy A though ...

Professor Chapela is one of the most interesting persons at Cal. He is willing to share his secrets if you ask--which not many professors who truly are full of themselves are willing to do. He will put in as much effort as you will and is a "door open" kinda guy. He is a legend, but is very humble. Do a quick google search and be inspired!

Easiest class I've taken. Professor cares about you actually understanding and caring about the material, not just learning the stuff. You can do the bare minimum and get an A in the class or you can put in effort and Prof. Chapela is happy to help you explore your interests.
This man is a joy. Plain and simple. This man is a joy. Plain and simple. You take one of Chapela's classes if you want to think a little deeper, dream a little bigger, be a little better.

This class is for happiness! His class is not hard to get A. I chose the "paper track" and I really learned a lot by going to his OH. I also enjoyed the field trips. His lectures were hard to follow, but they were exciting: prof taught me how to view things from a different perspective!

Professor Chapela structures his class into the research and test track. Research track does essays on any environmental biology topic and test track takes bi monthly quizzes. His lecture style is interesting, and sometimes boring/dry for people. But he's a great person to talk to in person. Highly recommend going to office hours to chat.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Interesting professor for sure. This class is all about what you put into it. He lets you choose between a "research track" and "testing track." I chose research and learned so much. Only thing is the lecture just do not have to do with the research at all. Honestly don't choose the testing if you want to actually get something out of this class.
His lectures don't have to do with the quizzes that he give out but you learn things that are important in life

Ignacio is one of the greatest professors I've met here at Cal. It is very worth going to his office hours. He sits down with you and asks what you're truly passionate about and to think about why you are here, more than just trying to get a good grade and paying job. Its easier not to think about but Chapela sees through you and false happiness.
Excellent class, excellent assignments and excellent material. Especially excellent hotness. Very excellent. Recommend the excellence.

ESPM 6 is a ridiculously easy class. No midterms, no final, and your grade is entirely based on a few quizzes that Chapela gives study guides for. Even though lecture is optional, I still made an attempt to go to them. I eventually stopped because Chapela goes off on random tangents, is completely unorganized, and unrelated to quiz material.

Ignacio's class is less structured than most courses out there. However, he gives his students the chance to choose two distinct tracks. An exam or a research paper track. My exam track peers who received an A said the quizzes are relatively easy if you study the day before. I took the research paper track.  Got an A-. No complaints-the man's funny

Ignacio is the man. He is informative, passionate, creative, progressive (part of student-rights protests), and laid-back. He is not only genuinely invested in educating his students, but he also wants his students to learn about the real world and not stress about schoolwork. He expects a lot, but he also encourages you to be at peace with life.

Horribly unstructured class and vague (but passionate) teacher. "participation and attendance"--in class, fieldtrips, etc--are part of the grade, but no attendance is taken. There are 2 essays on ANY topic you want, with no rubric or guidelines. Prof promised inflated grades so I took it for fun, but I ended up with a B--wish I never took it.
interesting subjects and very passionate teacher

I have to agree with the person who said Prof. Chapela is full of himself. And he's not helpful at all; I tried to get help from him three times. He didn't help at all twice out of those three times...
Very helpful to students. Only one midterm paper & final paper. Occassional quizzes (easy if you show up for class). Interesting guy. Not too happy about his style of teaching, but engaging enough.

He is extremeley intelligent and has developed his own class structure where he interacts with the class.  The only problem I had with the class is that I still do not have a grade for the class and half a semester has already passed since I SHOULD have gotten a grade.  No one in the class has a recorded grade yet. Needs priorities!
He thinks he is god. He is also full of himself. I did not like him at all. Arrogant and rude

No books, very very very little HW, and interesting guy.  Spends most of the class interacting with students and talking about current "news."  Grade is based on two papers (70% of grade) and quizzes (20%).  Believes that everybody has the capacity to get an A and wants to help them achieve that!
Don't take her.

The instructor is amazing and gives great lectures! She is clearly very passionate about Egyptology and knows a lot about the subject. I learned so much from the class. Definitely recommend taking a class with her! Most of the grading is based on the papers, so make sure to do good on those. However, she gives a lot of great feedback to help.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great and very caring teacher!

Came into this class with no real interest or knowledge of linguistics but he made all the content super approachable. All tests were take home and graded fairly. Attendance not mandatory, but lectures weren't recorded and there was an drop on my test grades when I skipped lecture. Overall, GREAT teacher and I'm taking another class with him now!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Super engaging lecturer who is clearly very knowledgeable about the subject. All quizzes/tests are take-home. Grading took a while but very interesting and great class overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: As a student who had only taken STEM classes up until this one, i can 100% recommend SPAN 100. The class was very well structured, the professor was very available, and exams/ quizzes were more than fair. Although lecture/ office hours aren't mandatory, I HIGHLY recommend you attend at least the lectures and office hours if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Take home exams, Lecture was super helpful so make sure you attend and you'll be fine. Although not mandatory, OH were so goated. Light class and fun.

Overall a very kind and caring professor. Lectures were clear and engaging. All exams were take-home and very doable as long as you do and understand the homework. Definitely recommend doing the optional homework/reading too. He would also sometimes bring his dogs to class with him. Would definitely take a class with him again!
Justin is fantastic absolutely love his lectures
Very fun teacher! Workload is very minimal... All test/assignments are done at home (1 week to complete). You make sure you pay attention and you will be fine!
Very fun professor! You can tell he is very passionate, and all test/assignments are at home (you have a week to complete it). Good educator but you have to make sure you pay attention!

He is a great professor. I really felt comfortable in his class, especially as a non-native Spanish speaker. He makes the environment very relaxed and he's passionate about the subject matter and made me want to take more Spanish linguistics classes. I'd highly recommend any of his classes. He's a legend.

I have to say that I really enjoy attending class with him. He's very caring and fun professor to be in class with. As for the class, it's not too hard but not too easy either, I guess it's a good balance. Prepare to read the lectures he assigned, so you can understand better the topics. I definitely recommend this class and Dr. Davidson as well

I was avoiding Pro. O'Brien after my faculty-advisor made him sound bad, but he was the only one offering 184. Specs out that he's totally nice and knowledgable. The lectures were now my favorite at Cal.
I wish he taught more classes.

At the start of the semester, everyone hyped up Professor Ng as really good at teaching and said that Professor OBrien was very monotone. While it appeared like that initially, if you went to lecture, it was clear that couldn't be further from the truth. He was great in answering q's but I will say that he caters to the top students in his lectures
They know a lot. Ask a question and you get interesting answers.
He sometimes goes too fast and it gets confusing, but if you go to office hours he'll work with you until you get it. Very patient and he likes graphics a lot.
Mr. O'Brien's lectures get a little repetitive but he always tries to make them engaging, he answers questions and can seem condescending but isn't looking down on you

I think he focuses more on the top students in the class.  For example he will skip basic stuff and focus on big picture.  I liked that a lot but my project partners got frustrated that little details were not covered.  He has really good industry connections and just got an Oscar.

Laziest professor I have ever seen during my four years in Berkeley. Not bother to stop in lecture to make sure students understand the material but keep his monotonic and fast style. Projects are interesting but never changed. Same for midterms. Take class with him if you want to sleep during lectures.

Extremely hands-off prof. Lectures were useless both at understanding material and doing the assignments. The assignments are quite open-ended with little to no information given and involve a monstrous amount of coding as compared to other CS classes. Tests are recycled every year so quite pointless. One of the most unstructured classes ever.
Cool class and he seems good.
Project is monstrous as are the assignments.  Tests is simple if you study old tests.

After taking this class with O'Brien I changed my focus to graphics.  He has worked with me to help get a good internship at DreamWorks.  Most profs are Cal are to busy to talk to you, this guy  actually acts like he cares about the students.
Guy seems to know everything.  Has great industry connections.   Projects are crazy hard but his tops students all get jobs at Pixar and ILM.
boring lectures, expects too much from the students, and is condesending

He gives a bunch of of programing work, but he told us up front  that he would and said that's the only way we'd learn this stuff.  I think he's right.  I've gone to his office for help about 3 times and he's always been willing to make time and help me.
He knows graphics very well.  Total expert.  Students he has taught now work at Pixar and ILM.  He also expects a lot out fo the class so if you're lazy take Barsky instead.

I think he tends to focus on the smarter students.  If you are into graphics he's for you.  He has connections with places like Pixar and ILM.  If you jsut want to get credit and move on go with Barsky.

Monotonous but informative lecture. Has an insane knowledge of the subject and can answer any question. Take the class with him if you are interested in graphics because you will learn anything you are interested in. If you dont have a special interest, it will seem way too broad and dull, however.
Manages to make an interesting topic seem very dull. Came off as really arrogant at first but is very nice towards students' questions and tries to answer them as deeply as possible.
I really like this class.  It is a lot of fun.
lectures are hard to understand, better to take it when Barsky teaches it
No Comments
Very bad lecturer, condescending towards questions, arrogant, questionable research prowess.
Very nice prof, sometimes a little fast but answers questions well.  Much better than Prof Barsky who I dropped.
No Comments
super funny, super well spoken, really sweet :)
Amazing professor!

Ousterhout always explained concepts clearly and thoroughly. Her lectures were always very well paced, and she was great at answering questions. She would also share extra tips on topics that she saw students struggling with in discussion/OH. Exams are very tough, but I would definitely recommend her.
The professor was very passionate during lectures or labs. The exams are evil. Classwork is light and simple
Very good office hours and one on one teaching for students. Always approached student questions with openness, empathy, and clear guidelines. Also incredible overall teacher and lecturer.

Very clear lecturer and great at addressing student questions. Go for those easy EC points by submitting projects early. Entire course staff is super supportive on Ed, they genuinely care about student grades and wellbeing. This is a hard course, prepare to grind all past exams from 2021 by DeNero onwards.

Professor Ousterhout is an amazing professor! I was lucky to have her as my discussion TA, and she genuinely cared that each student understood the material or, if they didn't, that she helped them learn. She is a very accessible and caring professor, and her lectures were clear, helping to reiterate the concepts from the lecture videos.
Really good lectures that are understandable

I believe this was Ousterhout's first semester teaching at Berkeley, and she did amazing teaching 61A! Very engaging lectures, funny questions and comments with Denero at the beginning of the class! Kay Ousterhout was very confident, energetic and helpful with the contents of the course. I seemed to prefer the lectures she taught over Denero :)
Great professor! Talked to her a few times in discussion/lecture; is good at teaching the content. The tests are pretty hard but CS61A is very well supported!

Quizzes and material are mostly common sense, grading is very lax, but the (required!) lectures are spent talking about random irrelevant things, and thus felt like a huge waste of time. Sitting in lecture is incredibly frustrating because the professor goes on extremely irrelevant tangents and cracks unfunny jokes. Free A, though.

This class is one of the most frustrating classes I have ever taken. Not a single valuable piece of information has been taught, and we are literally being tested on her random rants about who knows what during lectures. I do not recommend taking this class or any class by Karen. Good luck.  WOAT

Lectures talk about next to nothing related to the class. Last lecture, she talked about symptoms of menopause. This class is a complete waste of time, and lecture attendance is required but entirely unhelpful. Nobody knows what is happening- not even the GSIs.

This class felt very disorganized, the syllabus was very loosely covered. Lecture were more like discussions but it was very easy to lose track of what was being talked about. Assignment wise the class was very easy to pass and earn points but I don't feel like I learned much.
Very easy A, bunch of opportunities for extra credit. Lectures were hectic, but also informative. A little repetitive at times.

good overview of disability studies. many lectures were off topic discussions about totally random topics. I felt those were a waste of time/money. criteria for assignments was incredibly frustratingly vague ("entertain me!" "half points if you submit sh*tty work full if u do something interesting") but the class was easy and I enjoyed the readings
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: took this in spring of ‘25 and honestly that class was kind of a waste of time, i didn't learn anything except to dread the class and the weekly discussions.

Readings are ridiculously complex, weekly quizzes were ridiculously difficult, and prof is extremely noncommunicative with students and GSIs. Most interesting part of this class was watching my GSI's slow descent into madness.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Honestly really annoying and was doing too much for an AC class. I can tell she's passionate but it's really not that helpful when she just goes out of her way to make the tests difficult. Dont understand why she would do that. But otherwise, it's a lot of work for an AC class and I dont reccomend. Loved my GSI though.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lecture is a waste of time. If you want to hear someone talk about everything without saying anything—take this class! I thought this was going to be an easy A, but this professor did everything possible to make it hard. I would not take this class again it was a waste of time.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: For an AC class, this was def a lot of work so beware. It was her first time teaching 3AC, and there were weekly readings that you need to know for the online quizzes and midterms. Also discussion grade is 60% of your grade which is lowkey crazy

Absolute joke of a class. Grades are based on ability to regurgitate professor's opinions. Lectures are mostly about the professor's personal emotional state. One lecture was her just reciting the poem from the Biden inauguration and talking about the "big orange turd" president. Like what is the point of this?
weird expectations, couldnt ask for extensions at all, wasnt accomodating, lectures were kinda slow and i often felt irritated...

Im not from the States and tbh kinda jealous that students here get someone this cool teaching a breadth course on their culture. Karen is kind, fun, and one of the wisest person I've met. There's a quiz every week and you can choose to take 3 midterms instead of a final. Quizzes are chill if you watch the lectures and spend 2hrs a week on readings

I do not recommend taking this class to fulfill your american cultures requirement. It had an excessive work load with ridiculous expectations of students especially considering it is an AC class. If you don't have a genuine interest in anthropology do not take this course or it will ruin the subject for you, take a class with a different prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Nakamura is my favorite professor at UC Berkeley.  She is very understanding, easy to talk to, and knows the subject well.  She wants all her students to succeed and helps them as much as possible.  Her GSI, Nate, does a fantastic job as well.  Together, they make all their courses fun and easy to learn.

My FAVORITE professor at UC Berkeley. I took this class even though I didn't need it for a major and I LOVED it. Karen makes the class super enjoyable and really cares about her students. Even if you don't have too much of an interest in medical anthropology, her caring and joyful attitude will make you interested and brighten your day.

Professor Karen is awesome and really cares about her students.   She is very understanding and works with you if you have any issues.  She is an easy grader.  Karen is one of my favorite professors at Berkeley.

Very good lecturer, and enjoyed everything I learned. The class could be a little disorganized at times, but both her and the GSI's are so helpful and accommodating. This is one of the most interesting classes I've taken at Berkeley, and If you do the readings and go to lecture you will ace this class.

Professor Nakamura is such a wonderful and caring professor. I always looked forward to attending lecture and getting to know her as a person. Very accommodating and always willing to listen and help. Definitely my favorite professor in the Anthropology department here.

Anthro 115 is the best class I've ever taken (at Cal or otherwise). Prof Nakamura is so understanding and really cares about her students. She does a great job in virtually assigning no work while keeping us engaged in the material. She is the most accommodating professor I've ever had, and I encourage anyone reading this to take her class!

Medical Anthropology has been my favorite class this semester. Karen is one of the nicest professors I've had at Berkeley. Very approachable and class is so fun and interesting. Highly recommend this class to anyone in any major.

Practice tests were always WAY easier than the actual test. Her accent is hard to understand, but her notes are AMAZING. Reading the notes was enough for me to understand all the topics. I took calc in high school but forgot everything before taking her course, so I don't think that made much difference.

Even though I had taken Calc 1 in high school, I felt like I was going backwards being in her class. She explained topics in way that seemed more difficult than they needed to be. Had I not taken calculus in high school, I can guarantee I would've had a grade lower than what I got.
If you do your work, do all the practice midterms and finals. youll be good. I lowkey should have failed but still got a B- so the curve is amazing.

I think Professor Ohm's grading was fair, and the workload was manageable. As long as you go to her lectures and make sure to take the practice tests before the midterms, you will be fine. She is genuinely passionate about the subject, and I can tell she enjoys teaching.

Oh brother you really gotta learn the material on your own time. I feel bad for the ppl who've never previously taken a calc class. I wouldn'tve understood a word she said if I didn't. Just wait and take it with someone else.
hard to understand her accent, explains everything more difficult than it actually is. better off learning the curriculum yourself, don't bother showing up to lecture it will hurt u more than help u

Kind professor, but not an amazing teacher. I found YouTube and my GSIs more helpful than lecture. I went to every lecture and always barely learned anything. She spoke fast, had one small break, didn't give time for you to write or process notes you're taking. Had a strong accent that took getting used to. Overall I didn't get much out of lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lecture's can be a little boring at times and you might have to put in extra work to thoroughly understand the material outside of lectures.
Hard to understand, lecturers were unhelpful. Learned more from watching YouTube

Professor Ohm was a really nice and caring professor. However, the lectures go really fast and I would recommend reading the textbook or attending discussion if you didn't take calc in high school. 

Overall, if you actually attend lecture and discussion sessions, this class is pretty manageable.

Overall, the class was not too bad, good portion of your grade seemed to be based on which GSI you had. There was a whole scandal about some GSIs going over the same questions but just with different numbers before the quizzes
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: genuinely the worst lecturer I have experienced. her accent really isn't an issue; it's that the actual words she is saying don't progress in anything resembling a logical order. while the class itself is well organized (good notes templates and practice exams), she as a professor is incoherent. prior calc experience is required to do well.

I would say my A grade is completely irrelevant to her teaching. I did not attend any of her classes, and I really recommend to only look at her lectures with 2.0X speed. She's talks super slow and does not explain at all. Doing her practice exams is useful, however, so I really recommend practicing a lot before exams and quizzes.

Overall, lectures could get confusing because she'd often run out of time & she wouldn't go over harder problems, but office hours were very helpful. Lots of chances to buffer exam grades (homework, quizzes, etc.), and practice exams pretty similar to actual exams. If you took AP calc classes, you will be fine.

Lectures were really fast and sometimes confusing. I could definitely see it being extremely difficult for people who have never taken calc before. Midterms and finals were basically the same as the practice ones she releases, so make sure to rinse through those until you completely get it. Overall, ok class
Awesome curve. Practice tests are similar to the actual test.

I don't think the low rating reflects the class overall, but there are things to know. Prof. Ohm had generous policies (HW extensions, dropped quizzes, and grading options that favor you). My GSI was very helpful. Lectures weren't great for learning, especially if you're new to calculus, so I recommend self-studying and attending every discussion.

Since I've taken Calc BC before, this review might be skewed. I think her policies were generous; you can drop 2/7 quizzes, and there's a 1-day grace period on hmw. All her practice exams are very similar to midterms/finals in terms of problem type. I probably only showed up to the first 4 lectures and just did hmw/ practice exam for the exams.

I'm surprised Professor Ohm is rated this low. She's chill on attendance. There's a grace period for late homework. Lecture can be confusing, but reading the textbook cleared things up for me. Quizzes weren't like exams, but every exam question strongly resembled one of the practice test questions, so you can use practice exams as question banks.

The class was easy if you took Calc in HS and this is 10x HARDER!! She runs through the material so fast and is hard to understand. GSI's are like 6-7/10 and it's just rly hard to understand the material. Quizzes, were nothing like the Exams, and grading was HARSH and very inconsistent between tests.

Did not take AP Calc in HS - this class was a nightmare. Lectures overcomplicated topics that could easily be explained when self studied. Weekly homeworks assigned were incredibly tedious and rarely helpful as actual practice for exams. Generally felt like the class was taught as though you had at least taken AP Calc.

Professor Ohm seems like a nice person, but her lectures weren't the best. In some areas, she would go very fast and then very slow, making it all the more confusing. Her explanations were roundabout and difficult to understand.

The content of Calculus I isn't difficult. However, the ability of the professor's teaching skills and the unexpected difficulty on tests, which was a lot harder compared to homework problems and quizzes, made the class difficult. The professor herself was nice, though.
Thick accent and lectures are pretty useless as she talks in slow motion. She often overexplains rules with proof that goes on for half the lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: She calculates grades based on two methods and drops a lowest scored quizzes and homeworks, the exams are difficult but similar to practice exams she provides, but her lectures overcomplicated many concepts, which made it confusing and hard to follow along. You will want to self-study a lot.
Can see her passion in math, but definitely not a good teacher. She has a very heavy Korean accent.

I genuinely regret taking this class with her. I had no prior calculus experience, her lectures glossed over important concepts and lacked valuable practice problems, they left me feeling defeated. I ended up using the SLC and various friends to teach me calculus. The final exam was horrendous (especially compared to finals from previous years) 0/5
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: I know her lectures still have a lot of room for improvement, but what I can say is that she truly cares and is doing her best. If anything is unclear, just ask questions after class or ask your GSI. The exams are very similar to the practice tests, so with enough preparation, it's even possible to get 100. I feel bad for her being rated that bad.
Professor is kind but the lectures seemed too unorganized. - someone who never took ap calc, just ap pre calc (so be prepared to cry)

She has a weird way of explaining things, didn't make a lot of sense to me. Took me a min to understand her accent. Homework not super relevant to exams. Significant partial credit given on quizzes and tests was very helpful. Practice tests very helpful but a bit more challenging than actual exams. Find the textbook answer key online to ace the hw!

Prof. Ohm is kind and definitely cares about students; she calculates grades using two methods and gives students the higher score. The exams are difficult but similar to practice exams, (from someone with no previous calculus experience.)

professor ko is a really sweet person, but her lectures make no sense (i went to all). the way she explains things is all over the place though her accent isn't as bad as people make it seem. practice tests for midterms align pretty well but the final was brutal. lenient partial credit and curve. definitely need some calc background to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Homework doesn't match the lectures in difficulty, and you won't understand much if it's your first time taking calc. Practice exams do match finals perfectly, but just skip her lectures and watch KhanAcademy. Curves well and is lenient with partial marking.

Lectures were hard to follow, and she spoke to us in a condescending, childish way instead of getting straight to the point. Exams were extremely difficult, and the course was barely curved. I would strongly recommend avoiding this professor.

Lovely lady.... however, her lectures are really hard to follow. Her tests are very difficult, however I must say her practice tests are similar to what she assigns. 


The course was also disorganized at time especially compared to other courses. I overall did not have a great time in her class and do look forward to taking paulin next semester.
I actually thought about switching majors...

Ko Ohm was very hard to understand in her lectures. A lot of the content was irrelevant towards the exams. The final exam was very brutal. Office hours did not help. Given 3 practice final exams for the final, but the answer keys were adjusted hourly just days before the final exam from students catching errors. This course is very self-taught!

This class is very test heavy however from what I saw partial credit is very lenient. The notes and lectures especially later on get very confusing to look at and understand. In the second half of the semester I basically ended up teaching myself the material and worked with the tutors at the SLC. If your struggling stop by there.
Her English can make it hard to understand lecture sometimes. Probably should have curved the grades more based on low test averages.

Nice person, but not a great fit for Calc 1. Lectures feel basic, then homework and exams are much harder and very fast paced. Many fundamentals are skipped, so I wouldn't recommend it if you didn't take Calc in high school. However, the course is structured and exams match the practice ones. I personally needed a tutor to get through the class.
Very confusing to follow with her. Fast paced lectures, lack of useful explanations while teaching.
lectures did not feel helpful, felt like she rushed them and didn't go over enough problems. the tests are extremely difficult and there are a very strict curve. overall not a great teacher
very hard class

reviews.comment: tests were extremely difficult and not reasonable. lectures were not helpful and she sped through a lot of the content which made it tough to fully understand material

reviews.comment: bad teacher don't take please save yourself

reviews.comment: tough class, curve was not very generous. try to not take this class if you can

reviews.comment: Honestly loved her lectures because she always made me laugh. The lectures are packed with content, she wastes time on insignificant topics then skims over fundamentals. The exams are significantly harder than the homework and quizzes and made them ineffective practice.

Kind professor but ran out of time to finish lectures.  Quizzes are based on homework problems.  Midterms and final exam are manageable as long as you stay on top of the material and complete the provided practice exams, which are very similar to the actual exams.  GSIs are not always helpful, but the tutors at the SLC are a great resource.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you think about taking her class, start becoming religious and pray to God. Her lectures are hard to understand, even as an international student listening to her speak. She also assumes that you would know a lot of the material and glosses over concepts fast.

The lectures were pretty straightforward and fairly easy to follow. Homework could be challenging at times, especially in the later topics, but it was manageable overall. Exams are very similar to the practice exams, and were reasonably difficult but doable. Highly recommend attending discussions especially if you are struggling with the content.

I would honestly recommend that she take more time explaining the material rather than covering a million different topics in one week because of bad pacing. The class was very fast-paced, and the material was often rushed. Many topics were often overcomplicated and/or badly explained, which meant students had to self learn the material.

She's hard to understand in lecture, we got lots of very difficult and irrelevant homework, the quizzes and midterms were way easier than the final. That final was actually disgusting, and after the test material from the rest of the semester, no one was prepared for it, and it's a huge part of the grade.

There is a textbook (free online) that you NEED to read if you want to succeed. Lectures are based around the textbook, so read BEFORE lectures. STUDY practice tests, they are similar to actual tests. 

Grading- HW: 12%  Quizzes: 10% and 20/20/38 midterm/midterm/final OR 28/50 midterm/final (whichever higher)

She's tough. With that being said, the practice exams (for the midterms, esp #2) were almost identical to the actual midterms. Final was pretty heinous but each exam gets boundaries that are around 8-10% higher than the actual grade.Quizzes are fair and very similar to homework. Homework was heavy but def doable and you have a whole week to do it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not an effective lecturer, but she somewhat makes up for it with her impressive course organization. She posts 3 realistic practice exams before any test, and the actual test is on the easier side actually. I will say that you will be teaching yourself the course most of the time, but Stewart makes it easy to do that. The hate is exaggerated!
Just pray. This page won't let me post my true feelings, which says a lot. -  someone who didn't take calculus in hs (only AP pre-calc).

Def a weeder class. Experience should be mandatory but even ppl w/ experience struggled a lot. I went to every lecture, did all HW, went to SLC a lot, but still bombed every quiz and test. They are SUPER lenient with grading, which I appreciate, but the last exams (final) were so hard that it barely mattered. U PM have to teach yourself everything.

reviews.comment: professor ohm is a very sweet lady. however i would rather watch paint dry than go to her lectures. if you have previous knowledge it CAN help, but even so the college level math is different compared to highschool bs. office hours barley help, go to the SLC instead. i unfortunately will have to retake the course in the summer..
