reviews.comment: If I could leave a 0 I could.
I started wondering how a career at McDonald's would work out.

she's a super sweet person and grading is pretty fair. not the best lectures but lots of resources outside of class and imo her tests are basically the practice exams but a bit easier, which is awesome. def reasonable to succeed in her class and esp if u have a bit of calc already under ur belt you'll be fine!!

Lectures are very confusing, she overcomplicates the topics for NO reason so you have to teach yourself, homework is fine, quizzes are decently difficult, midterms are easier versions of the practice exams, but the final was unnecessarily difficult compared to everything else and I went to every lecture.

Lectures are confusing, so you will have to self teach yourself the topics. Quizzes are basically the hardest HW problems so if you understand those problems, you'll do fine.

Midterm and final are basically the same/easier than the practice tests. So just keep on redoing those problems and understanding how to do them, and you'll be fine

If you aren't religious, pick a religion and start praying. She draws hieroglyphics on her ipad and starts giggling to herself when no one understands a single thing she says. Paulin has always been the goat and always will be. If you love yourself do NOT take this class. I would rather switch majors than take this class again.
I don't like the way she teaches the content. It often makes the material more confusing. The exams are much harder than she says they will be. I wish I had waited a semester and not taken her class.

Professor Ohm is a really nice person. I did not go to lectures but I sometimes went to her OH and she explained things nicely. I would take her again. She sometimes gets confused but I think she is too smrt for this course. She should be teavhing a more advanced class

Took BC in highschool and 51 for credit and this class was genuinely awful from day one. Professor   Ohm overcomplicates concepts to the point where they become incomprehensible. I wholeheartedly did not think it could get this bad. DO NOT UNDER ANY CIRCUMSTANCES TAKE THIS CLASS. just wait for paulin to come in.

homework's not that tragic though.

Not sure what all the hate is about to be honest. Her lecture notes are very organized and easy to follow. Two midterms and a final and three practice exams given for each. She ensured to explain the reasoning behind Calculus concepts which helped a lot in my opinion. Only criticism is that sometimes she would sometimes run out of time in lecture.

Attending lecture for me wasn't helpful, but there are a lot of resources to help you do well in this class. Make sure to actually do your homework and go to discussion; if I didn't understand something, I would go to my GSI's office hours. The exams are very similar to the practice exams, so as long as you do well on those you'll be good.

This class was genuinely awful. I've taken calculus before but decided to take this class as a refresher and WOW! I think my understanding of calculus actually REGRESSED. I performed better on tests when I STOPPED going to lectures: that's how bad they were. Do not take this class

Overall, she seems nice and has a good mood everyday, but she is a horrible teacher. She overcomplicates even the simplest of calculus concepts, and her lectures provide no help at all. In addition, her midterm and finals are atrocious as they contain questions that are way harder than the ones seen in lecture or homework.

this was my first exposure to calc, and it felt 10x harder to learn, only went to lectures for the first 2 weeks because it felt like a waste of time. the 1h30 lecture was just her reading off her notes as you fill it along. she seems nice and her accent isn't bad like some people say. hw isn't too bad but the quizzes and exams are so different

Extremely nice person and seems really knowledgeable, unfortunately a terrible professor. I accidentally took calc 1 again when I didnt have to after misreading my ap scores (stupid I know), and being in her class regressed my understanding of math. Tough grader and not enough to be graded on, and the final was absolutely atrocious

Lectures weren't that helpful, she can't help you understand the knowledge points any better than the textbook. You have to already know enough calculus to be able to understand and do well solely from the lectures/textbook/class material.

As someone who took calc 1 in past years, this was 8 time worse. She seems nice but can't teach to save her life. She breaks up simple concepts to the point you don't understand what you're learning and barely covers hard concepts. Exams are also way harder than any quiz question. Only positive is the exams are identical to the practice exams.
prof is such a nice person but horrible lectures that confused everyone. dont do math 51 w her, i did ap calc in hs and I'm still struggling to understand her methods

You will absolutely suffer in this class if you have not taken Calculus prior. Her lectures are not worth going to and you will be probably better off teaching yourself because she over explains even the simplest concepts that get everyone confused. However, her practice exams are a lot like the actual tests so thats a plus I guess.

reviews.comment: This is genuinely the worst class I've ever taken in my life. Every single midterm makes me more and more depressed. This class has taken years off of my life. Prof Ohm is a very nice person but a terrible teacher. Please save yourself and never take Math 51 with Prof Ohm.

i scooter without looking both ways, i genuinely hate math and idk if its this prof but i had no time to comprehend anything. its all so fast paced and test heavy. She doesn't give room for any exam changes and the staff aren't very helpful either, I have no idea what my garde is but probably not good lol
This class was definitely challenging if you didn't take AP calc in high school. It goes pretty fast but the professor is good at explaining things and her lectures are well structured.

Ko Ohm isn't the best choice for math. She's very nice and caring but to be frank I wouldn't suggest her for math. Her lectures difficulty is very simple. Homework is difficult, and the exams are about 9x more difficult than homework. Her teaching style could improve. Try avoiding at all costs if you want to keep your GPA high.

Could not understand what she was teaching and would not have passed this class if I hadn't taken calculus in the past. I learned absolutely nothing. The tests aren't horribly difficult if you already know calculus. You'll have to self-learn everything.
Needlessly complicates concepts that should be simple, do not recommend going to lecture. Content isn't too bad, you just have to self-study.
Not comfortable in teaching the material, tests are really stupid and too much emphasis on homeworks and quizes and has a very very weird accent which is so hard to keep up with.

She seems like a kind person and has an enthusiasm for teaching math. Attendance is not mandatory and she posts lecture recordings. There is a quiz every 2 weeks, 2 midterms, and a final. She ran out of time every lecture and would rush through everything at the end. With her teaching, you basically need to have taken calculus before.

Ko Ohm is a nice person but an AWFUL teacher. Has a pretty heavy accent that makes it very hard to understand her. She makes us forget concepts that we previously learnt in highschool. People don't go to her lectures because it's a waste of time. Good luck if you have her!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class can be quite challenging if you have no prior calculus experience. Overall, Ko Ohm is a kind woman, but she is not an amazing professor. reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Ohm isn't bad, but not ideal for intro Calc 1. Having taken this before helps, but others may be lost without prior Calc 1 exposure. She overcomplicates concepts, and her accent slightly hinders understanding. The course has a lenient grading structure, and she is clearly well-versed in math.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Ko Ohm was very sweet. I went to a lot of her lectures and they weren't horrible. I think if I didn't know calculus before this, I would have struggled more. She has an accent, but it's not bad. Attendance is like completely voluntary which is nice if you want to miss. Overall, I thought she was very kind and fair with both grading and vibes.
so terrible. I took this class in highschool and the way she teaches is so much more complicated than has to be
This class challenges your philosophy on technology. The best professor I've ever had and the best class I've ever taken.

Best Professor on Campus. Readings were relevant and thought-provoking. He changed the way I see myself as an Engineer and my role in transforming the field. He cares a lot about students and very accommodating-- available after class and friendly.

I took Dr. Kadir's class last year and had to come back to commemorate how excellent of a professor he is. Prof Kadir has so much passion, charisma, and thoughtfulness when it comes to teaching, I thoroughly enjoyed going to each and every lecture (not so much the sections held by GSIs). BUT this class has forever changed the way I think.

Probably the most influential class at Berkeley, and Khalid is a wonderful professor who cares deeply about his students. Helps engineers see the world through a less constricted viewpoint. Eye-opening course for many,
Best professor and absolute best class I have taken at Berkeley

Took PE 100 during the summer and while it was intense with the readings and lectures were intense sometimes, I thought Khalid was an amazing lecturer. Khalid cares about his students and the world which was refreshing to see! Graded on participation, the midterm, and the final. DO THE READINGS!!!

His practical project and field trip is a good resume builder and life skill learning experience. Some students were spreading rumors that it wasn't good because it wasn't technical. Wrong, engineering ethics is practical for this day and age. Do both ethics and the engineering you like. He cares about teaching and is constantly improving it. A+

Summer session A: worked really hard in the class even read the two thick course readers and bought the three extra books (total 1500+ pages). Went to every single office hour and i was the only one there. Really tried as hard as I could in the class, went to every lecture and asked lots of questions. Studied more than i slept. I only got a B+ :(

He acts friendly at first glance, and gives the initial impression of a caring and supportive teacher, but question him in any way, or push back against unfair practices, and you will rapidly see the true face of the man.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Can't say enough good things! I had the semester from hell and Kadir was supportive and accommodating the whole way through. Truly passionate and inspiring lecturer who changed the way I view education and the world. Genuinely cares about his students as individuals and their progression. Was also impressed when he used the strike as a learning opp

THE BEST EDUCATOR BERKELEY HAS AND WILL EVER HAVE. 
Khalid's lectures are amazing and unbiased (this is coming from someone who grew up with very conservative values). he makes things easy to understand and is the funny, kind & genuine. I only get out of bed for his lectures.
I'm planning on double majoring in PE just because of Khalid!

Kadir is one of the best professors I've taken at Cal. I've taken PE101 and ENGIN157AC with him. He seriously changed my life and has influenced the way I've seen the world. Take him you don't regret it. The course is a lot but he is accommodating and his GSI's are great. Lectures are very interesting Go to his office hours, he's the best!

Literally the best professor I've had at Berkeley. Khalid's lectures were AMAZING; so interesting, and I always looked forward to them. He's such a great guy too, really cares about his students. I loved this class, grading was a bit tough at times but very manageable if you work hard. Great professor for sure though.

Professor Kadir is a cool guy! He is really helpful when asked for feedback, he picks out great readings that really summarize the GPP minor well, and he's super chill about assignment deadlines. There are quite a few papers assigned but they're short and simple. He is a slow grader though!

Khalid Kadir is the best professor I've ever had. He cares about students, and cares about the lecture material. His course affected my life in more ways than I could have ever imagined, and I'm so grateful that I was able to take a course with him!
I'm a 4th year EECS major, and he might be one of my favorite professors I have had a Cal. The zoom lectures are extremely interactive. He is very knowledgable and is very engaging with students.

Kadir is 100% without a doubt the most amazing professor I have ever had at Cal. He is so knowledgable about everything he teaches and is truly an inspiration. Very few times in my college experience have I looked forward to lectures. He cares about his students and the content of his class so much. I wish I had room to take this class again.

Not really the best professor to take this class with. pretty disorganized imo and he tries really hard to be your friend like telling you that class is mandatory in the syllabus and after everyone shows up says it wasn't mandatory loll. The GSIs for this class dont really seem to give a sh*t tbh and just send u to breakout rooms for 4/5 of thetime

Professor Kadir is by far the best professor I've had at Berkeley. His lectures are so interesting, I don't even consider them work or tiring. He's the most understanding professor I've ever had or heard of and genuinely cares about spreading knowledge. Most importantly, he's mastered what most professors at Berkeley seem to lack: teaching.

Great at lecturing, leading discussions, etc. Presents material in a relatable but still smart way and the course content is relevant and a good different perspective on economics. Very understanding of student needs. Lots of reading, some tedious some easy. Exams themselves are straightforward but the grader (not Kadir) was absurdly picky.

Amazing professor, clear lectures, well organized and thought out. He's very helpful and knowledgable. However, a tough grader. Be prepared to work for your grade in this class, as the average is a B.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Highly recommend!

The fact that he doesn't have a 5/5 is truly a farce. Best professor I've ever had in so many ways. Firstly, really knows his material, well-read and does a great job explaining it. Really felt like I learned something. One of the most caring, kind-hearted guys who's a true homie and is willing to work with you, but not give anything for free.
This man is truly brilliant! He cares for his students and really motivates each student to leave his/her impact on the world. Please take it if you have the chance!

Genuinely cares about and isn't cynical about students which is rare at Berkeley. Very accessible. Our GSI had to miss discussion & he stepped in and taught it himself, the 1st thing he asked us was, "how can I improve?" Readings: super interesting. You actually feel knowledgable leaving this class. Note: PE 100 sucked. PE 101 is amazing &relevant

My favorite professor I have ever had and I am a senior at Cal. He is honestly amazing and absolutely brilliant. Nothing but great things to say about him. TAKE THIS CLASS if you want to laugh and be mind blown about life and the world as we know it!

The most brilliant professor I've had at Berkeley. Professor Khalid is absolutely amazing, and has the most enlightening perspective on topics of political economy. I don't think I will ever meet a better professor. He is kind, thoughtful, puts himself in the shoes of the students, and I dont have a single complaint.

Professor Kadir is by far my favorite professor I've had at Berkeley. His lectures were engaging to the point where I looked forward to attending them, and whenever I spoke with him outside of class he was friendly and helpful. I learned things that are actually relevant to life, not just my major. I definitely recommend taking a class with him!
Definitely the best professor I've had. Just a super enthusiastic lecturer who really seems to care and an approachable person. E157 is fun and easy to do well in.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Best prof at Cal. Genuinely likes his students and talking to them outside of class. He will remember you if you participate and he will still say hi to you years later on campus. He is challenging and makes you think, but still is reasonable about extensions etc. Truly would be sad for Cal if he ever left.

Kadir is a remarkable individual. Outside of class, he responds to concerns or questions via email within the hour. In class, he is one of the best lecturers I've had, conveying information in an interesting, engaging, and relevant way that makes you remember it for the exam. One of those classes where you pay attention closely, and study less.

There's a ton of reading in this class, but if you're a PE major then it's the normal amount. Really engaging lectures and 100% worth going to his office hours to get help or simply talk. One of the most enlightening classes I ever took in Berkeley.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Definitely one of the best professors at Berkeley. Have never written a rating before but he deserves 5.0. His lectures are so entertaining and inspirational and he is truly caring about his students. Being in his class made me so proud to be a student at Berkeley.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Literally the best professor I've ever had. He is so accessible, he makes you think critically, and he is always there to listen to your concerns, or just chat! The readings in his classes are great and you will want to do them. I highly encourage you to get to know him as a person.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: VERY charismatic and engaging lecturer who will leave you with some new perspectives on seeing the world. Exams were also straightforward and focused on applying the readings.

I usually don't rate professors, but Kadir really deserves some recognition for the qualify of preparation he brings to class every lecture. His lectures are not only interesting, but he also understands the workload of being a student and is abundantly fair. I would take any class he offers again if I had the time.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Khalid is a fantastic, engaging lecturer. He asks tough questions but ensures that students feel safe to express their honest opinions. He openly encourages dissent, which makes for some really lively discussions/debates in lecture. There is a good amount of readings, but they are interesting. The community project was a great way to be involved.

Amazing professor! My favorite professor at Cal thus far. His E157 class changed my perspective of the role of engineers in society. There is a lot of reading, but if you put in the time, you gain and learn something from it which at the end of the day is why we are all here. Khalid cares for his students and puts their learning first and foremost.
Lectures were  dull  and felt like Khalid was preaching .

Probably my favorite class at Cal, even though I'm no engineer... Definitely one of the people that contributes to Cal's reputation of being innovative, critical and forward-thinking. SO important in learning to see the bigger picture instead of only the micro impact of our actions!

Khalid made my experience at UC Berkeley worthwhile.  I love how he is able to merge his engineering background into poverty alleviation.  You can't bs or rush his assignments because he KNOWS when you are, which means he also knows your true potential and believes in you.  He gave me a lot of valuable feedback that'll stay with me into my career.

PE 101  was best class I've taken at Cal. You can tell he really cares about his students and lives to educate.  He really changes the way you see the world, see development and underdevelopment, and understand power in general. Kadir is truly inspirational and you must take one of his classes before graduating!

My first review but Kadir is definitely worth it! Such an exceptional professor with amazing GSIs as well. His PE101 class should be mandatory for all students--he is super knowledgable, helpful and transparent and wont trick you on the midterm/exam. Favorite class I've taken at Cal!

He is nice from outside, you can say, but sometimes he gives this odd looks. His lectures were really amazing, I felt like crying when he discussed elections and what we suppose to do as a society. He will inspire you to see "the role of power" like everywhere, even where it is not needed. His exams were fair. I was a great experiance overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Hands down the best class I've taken at Cal. He symbolizes what it means to be a great educator.
Nice professor overall, But be careful when choosing GSI.

The lectures are organized, and they can summarize the thinkers' thoughts perfectly. But he should work on how to lead students to follow his arguments, and the exam questions should allow more room for students to develop their own answers.

I didn't know classes could be this good! Even though class was three hours long (once per week) it was never dull. Lectures were interactive, students were engage, and the professor was open to student ideas unlike any other professor I've ever had. Outstanding class!!!
Good Professor.
You shouldn't graduate from UCB without a class with Khalid! He's balanced, energetic, and makes you want to read and learn more.
Best lecturer ever.

I am now a super senior and I can say he has been the best lecturer I have had to chance to take. I took his GPP intro course. Amazing. My palms would sweat every time I went to lecture because of the excitement and passion he'd put on 'em. Lecture becomes a luxury and not a responsibility. Talk to him. He gave me a letter of rec.

HE IS THE BEST! His lectures are very clear and straightforward! Be prepare to read a lot of different authors and make sure you don't procrastinate. His short answers are very specific and straightforward but there are just too much information. You might get confused between the authors. I would definitely take his classes again in the future!
Khalid is a wonderful teacher and an amazing human being. He's clearly brilliant, and he has such a knack for pushing you to think critically. By far the best professor I've had at Berkeley.

Can the same class and prof be taken in the span of your 4 years at Berkeley, please? Prof. Kadir was the best. He's not just an amazing lecturer, he really, truly cares about his students - seriously. He's brilliant, humble, and has a huge heart. He puts so much passion and hard work into his teaching, it's refreshing. Would recommend to everybody

Probably one of the best professors I've had at Cal. His ethicsAC class changed me as a person in the way only movies promised college would. My only regret would be not take his class before my junior year.
Great guy sooo sweet and extremely intelligent,articulate,real and just and overall great positive person. HIGHLY RECOMMEND!!!

Khalid is a gem. I have so much respect for him. You can tell how much he cares when he gives his lectures, which are fantastic. He urges you to think critically and from all perspectives. I will be forever grateful for how much I learned from him. He has a wonderful teaching style and is also a great guy.

I'm not sure what one of the other reviewers is saying. Khalid Kadir is by far the best professor that I have had at Berkeley. His lectures are interesting and engaging, he always leaves plenty of room for discussion, while presenting all sides of issues. He is also super committed to his students and gives students a ton of time. Highly reccommend

The class was good, and I ended up passing, but it is slightly difficult if you do not keep up with the readings or work. The TA is the one who grades the weekly assignment, so it's really based on their interpretation.

The grading scale is at the highest, 95, which can change your GPA. Very heavily graded on responses and in-text citations are the by far the most important thing for getting a good grade. Great and interesting class material, but the lectures are a bit slow and make the material monotonous.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Broo Professor Ak is the goat. Super easy class for your first year at Berkeley!! He was lowkey funny when he wanted to be. It was literally just weekly readings, taking notes of them, and writing an essay-length discussion post due every Friday. (Tip: the GSI likes it when you don't use any quotations, just paraphrase everything, and ur chillin.)
Great professor, lectures can seem a bit all over the place.

Mostly graded on weekly discussion + midterm&final. Pretty chill, most people barely showed up to class, and submitted stuff late. Fairly easy, but also interesting served as a great backbone for future philosophy (im a philosophy major). Definitely would recommend and if your someone who's on top of their work you'll get an A
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Entire class is graded on repetitive weekly discussion posts and a midterm + final paper, which I'm pretty sure he doesn't read because his GSI has graded every single assignment this semester. Lectures are helpful sometimes, however he doesn't take attendance or track participation so a lot of kids just don't show up. Rather lazy, in my opinion.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Solid teacher, lectures are a little boring but very informative. Midterms and Finals are heavily weighted in this class. Discussion posts are also fairly easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Super great prof and Anthro 1 were both easy and super interesting! I took it as a bio breadth, but I ended up switching my major to Anthro as well. Both prof maher and the TAs are great. Highly recommend, would take the class again!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Loved taking 129D with Professor Maher. Her lectures are well-organized and clear. She's also super responsive to any questions or emails. There is a lot of reading, but they're great resources for assignments. The class was graded on a take-home midterm, take-home final, annotated bibliography, blog, and one group presentation. Take her class!

Lisa is an amazing professor. I will say she does assign a LOT of mandatory reading, but it's manageable. Her class is only graded on 4 major things: a take-home midterm, media assignment, blog/website, & a take-home final. The way she grades is fair. You can tell she genuinely cares for her student's success.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Absolutely fantastic professor! Her lectures are clear and well-delivered, and the content is fascinating. She's also very caring. The class is graded on a take-home midterm + final, plus a few other written assignments -- but she's a fairly easy grader as long as you follow the rubric. Please take Prof. Maher if you can!

Lisa is a great professor for the student that self paces themselves. She's extremely straight forward and gives you a bunch of information (but only what you need). Taken her twice now bc she's chill!
Professor Maher was a great lecturer. Shes super organized and kept you engaged. Her grading was also very fair! Easy and enjoyable course and teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Class was extremely boring, which made the topic difficult to care about or put effort into. Very little opportunity for discussion.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Maher is a really great professor. Anthro 1 had a lot of reading, but it wasn't terrible. Personally, I found some of it interesting. There is no curve, but grading is fair. Many different components go into your grade, so no one thing is extremely impacting. You will be fine if you do the readings and go to lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Anthro 1 is a dry class for many people, plain and simple. Prof. Maher's class has no curve, but do the assignments and you'll do well in that criteria. Exams are easy if you study. Best advice I can give is READ THE BOOK. I got above 100% on the midterm and 95% on the final. So study the book! She is very sweet and caring, and always there to help
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: So I took 128 as my first class ever at Cal. Dr. Maher's lectures, although sometimes dry, were very informative & clear. She really REALLY knows her stuff. The following semester I met with her because I didn't really have any academic direction. Not only did she point me the right way, but she has become a true mentor and has gone above & beyond.
Brilliant professor. Very approachable, and willing to help students who are having difficulties with the course material. Study hard, do the reading,  and you can be in the A range!
Brilliant professor, even if lectures are sometime boring.  Easy to approach and very helpful.  Heavy reading and expectations to know it on the midterm.  Take-home final project.

Brilliant professor! The lectures are clearly laid out and the study guides are excellent. There is a lot of reading - it helps to read and summarize the papers before before that week's lectures whenever possible. Pay close attention to the main points highlighted at the beginning of each Powerpoint and go to review sessions. Exams are very fair.

Maher is the freaking bomb. Her quizes aren't the easiest thing in the world and you for sure need to study your lecture notes above all other things, but its so interesting! I never miss a lecture. She knows her stuff and you can tell how much she loves archaeology. get the pervading concepts, key finds, and their effect and you're good.

The lectures were engaging, and I appreciated the material covered in the course. However, the expectations and grading criteria for exams were not clearly communicated. I found the instructor to be unapproachable and dismissive when clarification was needed about course standards. This made it difficult to understand how to succeed in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: #DONTTAKETHISCLASS.I'm a Legal Studies major and I personally had a difficult time with the first midterm. For me, it felt like the expectations for how to approach the exam only became clearer after the midterm had already happened.

When she tells you its a lot of readings its NOT a joke. DO THE READING and take notes. Look back at your notes weekly and summarize them. Make flashcards for the key terms. DO THE PERUSSAL! Participate in section and in lecture pods. Talk to your podmates outside class(study with them!).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: a ton of work- more than any other LS class but prof did an amazing job and clearly provided all expectations. 50-100 pgs of reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Sangren is great and loves her content. There is A LOT of reading, and she does not hand you an A for doing nothing, so if that's what you want look elsewhere. If you want to learn however, it's a great class, stressful, but fun. It's a good class to push yourself and see what you can handle, especially if you're interested in law school.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Oh nooo, I have to actually show up to class AND do the reading AND turn things in on time?? how will I ever survive?? especially when I'm trying to go to LAW SCHOOL where they definitely don't expect any of that. honestly don't listen to the people whining about it. this class is actually fire.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof. Sangren is incredibly knowledgeable and well-spoken. Her lectures truly give me a greater understanding of the legal institutions and their interplay with society. This course and her other one, 160, are two of the best classes I've ever taken. The readings can be quite long, but they are well chosen and always interesting.

Horrible instructor talks people out of going to law school and does not allow time for questions. If you ask a question in class she makes answers feel rushed. You are not able to yawn in her class or glance at your phone because she deduces points. For not being a professor, she made the class boring and went over time.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Extremely boring and monotone during lectures. Workload is unreasonable, and we have readings before each class, up to three large readings per class. Doesn't give study guides or post-lecture slides and CONSTANTLY goes over time. She gets upset when people get up after she's been talking for 10 extra minutes. Unorganized, rude, and unapproachable.

The worst class taken at Cal. She treats the class like hers is the only one we are taking. Very negative & discouraging, she discouraged everyone from going to law school. Lectures are disorganized, readings were boring. Would not recommend. Also brings in a lot of politics into class lectures, of course one sided and not up for discussion.
coooco professor too much work

She expects you to do the readings and show up to every class. The exams test detailed understanding of the readings. I had a lot going on this semester and wasn't able to focus as much as I wanted to on this class, but she was actually really understanding when I went to her office hours
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment:
The work: necessary lectures and group discussions; weekly reading of 50–100 pages, 3 essays that you choose; 2 tests with a crib sheet

The reward: a greater understanding of the history, structures, and experiences of punishment and oppression that define our society. And practical preparation for law school

This class was so well organized, and the expectations were so clear. Sangren has an amazing ability to explain really complicated concepts in a way that makes sense. She comes off as intimidating, but she's super understanding and relatable. Go to office hours!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Sangren is incredibly articulate and her lectures add a lot to the readings and slides. If you show up and actually listen, you will learn so much! The exams are not difficult as long as you've been attending and doing the readings (which you have to do because there are annotations). Super knowledgeable and thoughtful about the topics she teaches.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Legal Studies 160 is one of the best classes this school has to offer. I don't know why exactly everyone has rated this professor so low, but because of it I went into the class scared. I shouldn't have. Lots of reading, but some of the best you'll find. Super good topics, interesting, i loved this class. Will be taking 184 in the future.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I was worried about taking this class last semester, but it ended up being one of the most rewarding classes I've taken at Berkeley. I learned so much from Professor Sangren. Her lectures are so insightful - definitely go to them.  As long as you put 75% effort into readings, go to lecture, and pay attention, you'll make it out with a good grade.
This course makes students smarter
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I really don't understand professors who make it their mission not to support students. She organizes the class as if she's the only professor you're taking to the extreme and the midterm is genuinely insane. As a 4th year I think she's the worst professor i've taken though the concepts in class could be enjoyable, kind of sad.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: People who have given low ratings are just salty that they actually have to learn. Her class is one of the easiest classes out there because of how she has scaffolded the grades. As long as you're consistently showing up and doing the work, you'll do well in her class. Anyone who says otherwise is honestly just lazy. Also, her dry humor rocks.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I didn't understand why her rating was so low but from the comments it's obvious these people are just salty she has expectations. Yeah she assigns lots of reading (like all legal studies profs) and you actually have to do it and you have to come to class. You also learn a ton about how law and society interact and if you do the work it's an easy A
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS! she expects you to complete so much reading and have then annotated, as if you are not a full-time student who has other classes. She was truly the worst professor I've ever had at UC Berkeley in all my four years. She refused to make the slides or lecture notes available, which made the class even that much more harder.
AVOID her, she is an ELITIST. Also, Lazy herself and harsh on student.

This class was a lot of work but I feel like I learned so much and I actually remember a lot of what I learned. She's super clear about expectations and honestly I feel like it better prepared me for law school than any of my other legal studies classes. Stay organized and put your due dates in your calendar!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Sangren PRESENTED on why her coursework is manageable but it is simply a full-time job. Annotations on readings before each class, complicated papers that take hours and are graded harshly, insanely specific detail in exams, and discussion section is practically led by students and is not helpful. This class caused so much anxiety, not worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Please ignore the good reviews. Expects you in class every day & attendance (participation) is large portion of grade. Assigns annotations every week for 3-4 readings/week (too much!). Extra credit is weekly but barely counts towards grade. Schedules her final exam either super in the morning or super late at night on the last day of finals week.

Great class, great professor, really changed the way I think about the way the legal system interacts with society. Some of the assignments seem tedious at first, but it benefits you in the end because you go into the midterm and final with an excellent understanding of the readings and concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: There were 2 lectures in which she used to show her students (who are almost all pre-law), how becoming a lawyer would lead to alchoholism, failed marriage and depression. She seemed very sour about not becoming a lawyer herself. It was honestly very weird and we were all so confused.

When the whole class complained about how there was too much hw & readings, she used a WHOLE CLASS w SLIDES to speak about how the amount of work she gives is completely valid. She showed us statistics of how doing her homework was possible.

Professor Sangren is amazing. Her class really changed my POV on law and research. Lots of reading, but all of it pretty interesting. The CRMs are super helpful for exams, and exams are not that bad (definitley have to read!). TAKE THIS CLASS!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The reality of this class is that the lectures are very dense people say she is a boring lecturer but the truth is everything she says is something you should write down, she doesn't waste time, and if you pay attention and do 50-page readings which is like twice a week the class is a very doable A. Look at the example papers provided!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I haven't had a professor who I genuinely disliked before her. I've had hard graders, but not someone who is so lazy and incompetent to do anything on her own. She doesn't make lecture slides available, so if by some chance you can't make lecture you're screwed. Instead of uploading grades, she makes you figure it out yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Sangren is like no other professor I've had before. Her passion for teaching radiates. She puts so much thought and intention behind her course design, and as a student, I felt certain she had our best interest in mind and was genuinely trying to make us better thinkers.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Sangren is very elitist and it is ironic that she teaches about inequalities and injustices when her class only serves the students that were raised with the same education that she has. The class readings were interesting but they were extremely long . I would not recommend her class
Amazing class, amazing professor. Lots of work, but you actually retain what you learned. She can come off a little intimidating but is really caring if you go talk to her during office hours

Sangren gives you a lot of opportunities to work for your grade and improve it. Although the work can be a lot, make sure to be organized! Communicate with your GSIs in order to stay in good standing (they are very understandable). My only con was the lectures being orally convoluted and not accessible online/not specific.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I feel as though the instructor was not empathetic or professional. A large portion of the course grade was opaque: participation was not based on a grading scale, and so many of my classmates and I were wondering where we were standing in the course as we entered the final. She also offered extra credit in a way that was wholly inappropriate.

She is a really nice person, but she often speaks in circles and overcomplicates everything. This class has a lot of reading, which as long as you have good time management, you will be okay. However, she often wants extreme details on exams. I would not recommend. The first half of the course is great and interesting, but the second half isn't.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I've taken 2 of her courses (184/160), she is an AMAZING professor. LOTS of reading, about 100 pages per week. She makes you work for your grade, but you benefit. Has clear grading criteria. Sangren genuinely wants every student to succeed and she has a cat, which is a plus!!! Go to office hours/lectures if you want to understand the readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Not a class you can slack off in. There's several hours of reading a week, but it's super interesting and you'll get used to it. Start the reading memos early!
Professor Sangren is great. Very caring, and the class was super interesting

Big portion of grade was dependent on a handful of memos based on that week's readings. The average for those was very low and they did not provide helpful feedback on those or really any assignment. Lecture participation required unless you want to do extra work outside of class
Was not enthusiastic about the course. When I needed help me told me to drop the course and lectures were pretty dull.

Had him for biological psych. He's very accommodating and clearly cares about his students. He's quick to listen to feedback and actually makes changes, which I really appreciated. He's also a strong lecturer and explains things in a way that's easy to follow.

Had him for PSYCH N110 over the summer. Simply the best. Super accommodating and caring prof. Did flipped classroom so you study at your own pace. Online quizzes, midterm and final. Very forgiving and chill guy.

Great lecturer! He's very open-minded and doesn't care so much about grades. He cares whether you have learned materials in his class this intrigue you.
He is very lenient when it comes to tests and exams. I would definitely recommend this course if you are looking for something easier but interesting! Functional Neuroanatomy is great pair forcours
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took this his Psych 2 class, he was my first favorite professor and he's hilarious! Very understanding and caring for student's time and schedules. Also always made sure we were prepared for quizzes and exams. He had very fun experiments for us to do as well. 100% recommend
Really engaging lectures. Very clear. Very good orator. Gives more assignments than some other classes, but cares about the subject and about students understanding the material.

Ryan is a genuine professor who listens to students feedback but it seems like it's his first time teaching a quarter system as the class felt unorganized and overwhelming for deadlines for exams and papers as the deadlines were within the same week and we would wait to receive our grades for a while. Also, rubrics for papers weren't very clear.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Amazing lectures--So many papers

reviews.comment: Great, young professor (UC Davis). He has a dry sense of humor and made me die laughing several times. Very engaging lecturer, but assigned too much work. Two papers, two exams that were not easy, 3 quizzes, weekly web exercises that were very long personality tests. Got the feeling that it was his first time teaching on quarter system.

He was great! Ryan is younger than most professors, meaning that he is a lot less uptight and serious. He talked and taught like we were his friends! No need for a textbook, he has great lecture slides (can be a little long but very interesting). A few quizzes, web exercises and 2 exams. I would highly recommend him. 10/10
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: No comment

He is such an eccentric and likeable person who wears a cardigan every day and lights up, as though you are a genius, every time you ask a question. I loved the focused learning environment--no computers allowed, and he WILL call people out for being on their phones.

Great and fun class that I thought was pretty easy. If you're good at solving puzzles and finding patterns you'll be fine. Weekly HWs are short multi-choice quizzes, there are three midterm exams and a final but the midterms are not too bad. No writing is involved and you don't really need to do the readings.

Very sociable and very friendly, the real life "Indiana Jones" minus the bad parts. A genuine adventurer of the modern age with his trips to the Amazon rain forest to research languages. He is really a cool professor who cares for his students.Also a linguistic anomaly as he is a real life example of complete loss of his first language(Japanese).
Lev made me wish I was pursuing linguistics. Absolutely hilarious and truly knows his stuff. He answers questions incredibly effectively. Groovy ocelots.

I wish I could take Lev for all of my classes. He is so funny and charming and his lectures are genuinely enjoyable. 3 midterms is a lot but it is honestly not bad at all and everything is open note. Copy down the slides and understand them and you could get a 100% in this class. He also gives two attempts for weekly homeworks. Best professor ever!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: lev is a great lecturer and i love his sense of humor. his lectures were boring sometimes. 3 midterms + 1 final which i think is too much. some of the gsis suck in terms of teaching, but you will learn a lot from lev. very passionate and extremely articulate! not fond of him not providing recordings of lectures, and exams were kinda tricky too

One of the best professors I've had at Cal. He's the most adorable professor, with great lectures. He's extremely knowledgeable about the material and makes lectures pretty engaging by taking at least 6-7 questions every class. I find linguistics sooo boring, but he made me want to come to lecture, and actually pay attention.
honestly easier than ling 5 for me. only scored below 95% on one asignment (historical linguistics week). exams were fair, class well organized, professor was nice.

Very passionate about linguistics and made every topic seem so interesting. Great overview of the field, making every concept pretty easy to understand. Always stopped for questions and cared about the students. Many fun stories to share. Homework was very doable, exams were fair, and plenty of support offered. One of my favorite professors ever.

Lectures "required" but doesn't take attendance, if you can self-learn through the slides and take handwritten notes to bring in to exams (3 midterms + final are open note as long as they're handwritten) then you're chilling. Slides are written well and explained better in class but section helped way more.
Really good.

a very interesting class, his research is super cool but the homework was so difficult and due every friday night on gradescope. quizzes are easy, midterms and final were ok but if you don't understand the material from the beginning, it's not gonna get easier. if you want an intro ling class, consider ling 5

Lev is hands down the best professor I've ever had for giving clear explanations of complex topics. The class was hard, but not impossible, and while I was challenged I was not overwhelmed. My only complaints are the GSIs... but Lev is amazing!
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Lev's easily one of my favorite professors. He's an adorable character, shows cute Amazonian animals in class, teaches thoroughly, & cares deeply about our learning. He's transparent about logistics & does anything he can to help. He even hilariously described getting lost in the Amazon basin to make us laugh & calm our nerves before the final (':

Lev is the most clear and thorough lecturer I have ever had. Fair warning: the homework is hard, and the concepts are confusing. The final will turn your mind to mush. Go to office hours - he runs them like mini review sessions in a conference room. And be precise! I lost many points through careless errors or missing material.
Linguistics 100 is fairly easy, interesting, and fun. Lev is a great professor--good at answering questions, clear in explaining things, and I thought his lectures were hilarious.

His class fascinated me through and through but it was a ton of work. His classes are really tough and he can sometimes get ahead of himself in teaching when the class is lost five minutes back but he''s really patient and extremely willing to make sure students understand so long as you ask for the help. Above all he''s a really  fair on grades.

If you're gonna take Linguistics, take it with this guy. He is absolutely hilarious and he tries to make it fun. He is also totally adorable (randomly showing us pictures of amazonian cats)! The homework IS hard. DO NOT THINK THAT YOU CAN DO IT IN AN HOUR. Or two. Mid-terms weren't bad, but that final KILLED me. Still, I'm gonna take 150 with him.

Great lecturer. I find Ling boring, but he made it interesting or at least bearable. Too bad the homework is time-consuming, /hard/ and worth 55% of your grade. Meanwhile the midterms are easy, but worth just 20%. Backwards IMO. A good GSI/study group can make or break you in this class. Ignore the reading, but pay attention in lecture.

Lev's classes are simply a pleasure. He is incredibly engaging and witty, and explains everything quite clearly. I have seen him get overly upset when his bureaucratic decisions are questioned, especially with regard to grading; it's best to bring up such considerations your GSI. His class made me love linguistics and decide to major in it.

Professor Michael is an amazing person.  He is one of the most charismatic teachers at Cal and so friendly.  I did not enjoy the set up of this class though in comparison to Ling 100 taught by him.  Many computer based assignments including blog posts, blog comments, and a wikipedia page. A great deal of dense reading but overall very interesting!

Wonderful professor, extremely helpful, knowledgeable and clear. I would highly recommend going to his office hours even if you don't have trouble in the class, you'll learn all kinds of interesting things and get even more out of the class.

He's very clear and very helpful, and his course is challenging without being overly demanding. Professor Michael listens to his students and is highly aware of our needs. In addition to being a wonderful lecturer, he's also an incredibly pleasant man. One of the best professors at Berkeley.

There are weekly homework assignments and attendance is mandatory, but I found his class to be very clear and informative. He tries to be the best professor he can be, and he's amazing! I liked this professor so much I'm taking Ling 150 with him in the spring!

Excellent educator! For someone so new to teaching (at least that's what I heard) he is remarkably organized and well spoken. His slides tend to be a little verbose, but the language is very clear. This semester was a lot of work, but I also learned a great deal. I have no regrets!

Professor Rosenthal is deeply knowledgeable about so many issues. He has many readings and you should go over them in order to succeed because the midterm is heavily based on that. A large portion of your grade is a group public policy project which is graded very fairly in my opinion. Go to office hours and get to know him he's very interesting.
larry seemed passionate even though i had no idea what he was ever talking about.  lectures were over complicated and confusing. the only things tested were based on the readings.

The class is pretty chill if you keep up with your group's Memo work. The grading is lenient and the midterm average is pretty high, just study up for it. Lectures aren't helpful in my opinion even though you have to go in person. You kinda have to keep up with the textbook and the readings but the problem sets are super easy.

Prof Rosenthal is super smart and knows anything and everything, not to mention he's hilarious. Yeah, he's kinda all over the place, but in a good way. I think it's pretty insulting that some students couldn't be bothered to show up to lecture because they found them "boring." Anyway, I thought the class was great! 10/10

Larry is extremely qualified and has a wealth of background in the field, but his lectures sometimes felt excessively long and monotonous.  Lectures were mandatory, and honestly, I didn't feel that they were particularly helpful in understanding the content, but the class was pretty easy overall.

Incredibly difficult to get through lectures, can't say what I learned from going, or from the class in general. Get someone to give you the attendance access for participation, not worth going after the midterm. The class and assignments themselves are very easy.

im gonna be honest it was really boring. he makes an effort to make things interesting, but genuinely it was so hard to pay attention. i had him in a decal & he was much better so i think it also might just be the fact that pp101 is an intro class.

attend section & find a way to skip out on lecture

i wanted to enjoy this class more than i did. larry seems a decent dude and the class is designed for students to succeed. group projects were very manageable and my gsi was great. only need the pre-midterm readings, final is take home. that being said, the lectures absolutely dragged and the mandatory attendance made this all so much more painful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Rosenthal is a sweetheart and the proudest Golden Bear ever. He talks current politics often, and I personally really appreciated that - at a school historically known for its progressivism, he is a reminder of our roots. Lectures are slow, but the class is interesting, intuitive, and very beginner-friendly. Lucky to have learned with him!

Larry is so sweet but genuinely so hard to pay attention to. Lecture is required and I went to every one, yet gleaned pretty much nothing from them. Readings are pretty short and interesting, do them up until the midterm. Grading on assignments is pretty generous.

Lectures can be long, but the content is engaging. As someone who went on to work in policy research, this class helped me a lot. It is simple, maybe not easy, but simple, to get a good grade in this class. The instructions are clear, and plenty of office hours opportunities if you need them. He also has some good jokes.

larry is such a chill dude but the unfortunate reality is that this class really drags on. i think it wouldnt be so bad if lectures were cut in half lol. my advice: do ALL the required readings up until the midterm, and after that you can ignore the rest of the readings. the rest of the assignments/work are super easy and really not time consuming.

Honestly one of the best and most responsive professors I've had. He talks a lot, and the lectures are mandatory, but you can truly tell he cares about what he teaches and he loves his students. Bombed the midterm but still got an A because everything else was graded pretty leniently. Leniently professor overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: The most difficult thing about this class was the professor's oratory style. He talks like a lawyer because he is one. He talks like an economist, because he is one. He talks like a wonky policy professional, because he is one. It takes some getting use to and can be challenging at first, but there's no question that this class is useful. Take it
No need to study or take notes after the midterm, prof will take anything that could be said in two words and turn it into 1000, but overall it was fine.

Larry is a sweet guy and is very passionate about the subject he teaches. However his lectures are so boring and hard to pay attention to. No final which is nice, but alot of required reading and you have to buy multiple textbooks. Don't take this class if you dont have to.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is a boring lecturer, and sometimes I had no idea what he was even saying. The topics were interesting though (when I did the reading). It is a pretty easy class to pass. Only the midterm really required studying because the final was a group project. My GSI was really good and did most of the grading which made passing easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Kind of a yapper but a very nice guy

The class was fairly easy but the lectures were mandatory and incredibly boring. The professor would drone on about topics and it all wasn't very useful to the course. Most of what you need to know for tests are in the readings. There's just one midterm test and a final group project so it's not that bad.

Larry is just that pub pol character we all have to go through. This class is doable, especially with a good GSI. If you have a political science/econ/theory background you'll especially find the class easy. Boring lectures but attendance is taken. Some writing assignments, a midterm, and final paper/project.
Very interesting class

One of the easiest classes I've taken despite being an upper div. Larry's super chill and his class is very low effort. Midterms are almost exactly like the problem sets you do for homework. Very few assignments, all you have to do is show up to class and it's almost an automatic A. I believe nearly everyone gets a 10/10 on the written final.

Prof. Rosenthal is a kind guy, but not a very good lecturer. Classes seemed to drone on for hours, when the material could be covered in a ten minutes. Probably to be expected for Public Policy at Cal, but was explicitly biased towards Liberal/Progressive politics. Not much critical nuance. BUT, redeeming factor was that it was very very easy.

Larry was a great person overall and obviously cares a lot about the information. However, it felt like at times I learned nothing from his full 1 hour and 30 min lecture. He is very roundabout and focuses on things that don't correlate w/ exams/papers/hw. This class is foundational but doesn't focus very much on the basics in lecture or readings.

He isn't a bad lecturer, but his lectures seemed to go on and on without a point. Gives LOTS of reading, so much so that you don't actually know what to study for the exam. Final project is lots of work. Course wasn't too difficult in itself, but wouldn't recommend taking it for fun. I think he would be better teaching a smaller class.

he's an interesting lecturer, certainly not monotone, but he can be rather round about in delivery. It feels difficult to nail down the "point" he's making per se. A lot of class talks about the reading and doesn't actually talk too much about the readings, which can make things rather difficult to follow.

LARRYYY. God I loved this class. Larry was such an incredible person. I was very lucky because I got to take it over the summer of 2023, where it was about 25 of us in the class. It was very intimate, we got so much time talking together and sharing ideas with Larry. If you take this, which I HIGHLY recommend, make sure you read and can participate

Great lecturer and full of energy, clearly cared about his students and the content he taught, but just kind of hard to follow along. PP101 content was very redundant, I stopped taking notes halfway through the semester

Nice professor but lectures were dry (not his fault, just the intro content) and grading was weird (max is 93?). Nonetheless, it's easy to do well on memos and the econ/quant problem sets (one each; both were surface level). Says there's no curve but there def is one. Midterm easy but review key concepts. Either do lectures OR readings (not both).

Graded on a group project, short writing assignments, take-home final, and midterm. Lectures can get a little daunting and some topics are more engaging than others. He requires readings but they're all pretty quick. The midterm is straight from the study guide.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great Professor! Lectures are interesting and helpful to understanding course work. Hes very caring and understanding to his student, wants to help.

Lectures cover a lot of material. He brings in a few guest speakers for open discussion. Overall, Prof. Rosenthal is a solid teacher. He is very considerate and is friendly in offering any help. GSI's were all super helpful and positive. Workload is very manageable.
best prof at Berkeley!

Hate how he doesn't have a R1B class. LOVE taking his R1A class, super engaging, reading materials are relevant to essay topics, gives good feedback. Class theme, conformity sucks, is really interesting and professor himself is a good example lol. As long as you put in the effort, you get the grade. DEF recommend if ur finding for an r1a course!!

I recommended his course to all of my friends. he is really caring and lectures are great, you are not gonna fall asleep. himself is a great example of iconoclast so it is impossible for his course to be boring. his grading is really generous as long as you do your work.
Coolest prof I've ever met in my life. So supportive, honest and kind to everyone.

Professor Parker was undeniably one of the best professors I have encountered at Cal. Super sweet guy with an inspirational backstory. Feedback is very helpful and to the point. Lectures were always entertaining, and Prof. Parker was very flexible with extensions for essays, along with being easy to get a hold of.

Honestly one of the best professor out there! Lots of readings (mostly short passages) and homework load is very light. He may seem harsh at first but is very caring and willing to help his students. His grading policy is fair and does his best to help his students get an A.

Instructor Parker was amazing!!! He was very helpful and supportive throughout the semester. If you put in the effort, you'll get an A/A+. He also said that he's an "easy grader". I 100% would recommend taking his class if you need to take a R1A course. He was so cool and super funny. 5/5.

Professor Parker definitely comes off intimidating but is one of the sweetest professors at Cal. There is 4 essays throughout the course and not much other homework. For the essays, it may seem he leaves harsh comment on the doc itself but he is the sweetest when you ask for feedback in person. If he sees you trying you will get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: parker is an angel professor. super understanding and nice!

Unprofessional teaching. I was frustrated with the way he criticized assignments. He was hypocritical and trashed students' essays, while still giving the essays' A's. He intruded on students' personal lives and implied I was lying about a medical issue. I'm thankful for the writing skills he taught, but I wouldn't take the class again.

He is by far one of my favorite professors here at Cal! He is a very interesting and unique professor whose background is definitely portrayed in class. He genuinely cares about his students and is very understanding. He provides good feedback on essays and can really help you change your perspective on writing (like he did with me). Amazing!!

as someone who used to be intimidated by english classes, parker taught me how to express myself and appreciate literature. he is an inspiring guy who gives plenty of useful feedback on essays. he's very reasonable when it comes to extensions! i'm definitely a better writer and i've learned so much from his class! take his natural rights course :)
Great professor overall. He teaches in a very interactive way; it is entertaining and educational. He is also very understanding and relatable.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Super nice, funny, and approachable guy. Homework is pretty light and lots of the learning is done in class discussing with your group. Easy A and I still learned a lot.

Instructor Parker took the spot for my favorite educator. He devoted time to educate us on the mechanics of a good essay, gave students a lot of feedback, and amused the class on several one-of-a-kind stories from his life. He taught us that being an iconoclast isn't favored, but needed in our society.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Professor Parker is  cool  the class focuses on a bunch of social issues. Him being an ex-con is interesting, and for sure plays into his personality which always leads to fun conversations. Readings are homework for each class, but nothing heavy. He gives feedback on all papers and is flexible. He can have a tough attitude, but he really cares...

Parker mainly focuses on natural rights and educating girls in developing countries. His up-bringing, ambitions and intriguing life stories makes his class worth the while. You learn new things everyday in his class. However, he seems to be short-tempered and brutally honest with your work, which I love. Overall, great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Hilarious

reviews.comment: (Rating him at SDSU PHYS195). Really does not know how to teach at all. Wouldn't recommend taking him, he picks what he wants to read off the slides and that's all you get taught. Tests are unlike any material you will get from him. I recommend just teaching yourself if you have to enroll in his course. No curves given but a midterm is dropped.

(I'm rating for PHYS 195; it just wasn't an option.) Goes way too fast in lectures on what he's teaching you, then does poll everywhere questions about the materials he barely showed. You MUST GO TO CLASS. He's been hunting down people attending virtually; if u skip, he'll find out. Exams are multiple choice; missing 1 tank's ur grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Reinsch gives solid lectures that make a great addition to what's in the textbook, but due to the content of the course, reading the book is more important to do well in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Professor Reinsch's class was one of the best learning experiences I've had at Cal. The lectures are clear and well-organized, and he's pretty friendly and good-humored. The homework is pretty tough, but if you're willing to put in the time and ask questions when you get stumped you'll have a good time.

At least for Physics 5B, the honors class for intro EM&Optics, Prof Reinsch didn't go through the materials in details, probably because there was too much stuff in this course (the entire EM+ Wave/Physical Optics). Assigned good amount of homework. He mostly summarized the key points of each chapter and compare/contrast some analogous concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class was hard and Prof Anderson had trouble explaining concepts clearly.  I wish I had waited to take the class with another professor.
The lectures were unprepared and difficult to follow.  Students in our class would count how many times he said "or whatever" during a lecture.
cant teach and just wastes time

Horrible professor, he rambles on and on and does not give clear explanations.  Appears to like the sound of his own voice more than actually teaching.  I once asked him a question straight from the book and his answer was completely off.  My advice is to avoid him at all costs!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Anderson is not a great lecturer. He's monotonous, trails off most of his sentences, and goes on a ton of irrelevant tangents. His lectures are pretty easy to understand otherwise especially if you've taken econometrics. If not, you'll have to brush up on statistics. Assignments and exams are tricky so you have to know the research papers well.

The lectures are all very interesting and mostly focus on research studies in the field. Professor Anderson is very understanding and always happy to answer questions. He has very clear expectations and is organized.

The class is pretty easy and interesting overall. Topics are pretty relevant to today's issues like air pollution, increasing healthcare costs, etc. The class is mostly graded by HW assignments (one set every 2-4 weeks) and 1 midterm/final. Lectures aren't mandatory, but you should go for them participation points. Prof is very nice too

Grade: 36% problem sets, 60% tests, 4% attendance. If you watch lectures and pay attention you'll do well in the class. Really interesting material/studies reviewed. I never went to discussion and still did well. Prof Anderson is also very understanding and accessible outside of class.
best professor at Berkeley. would take every class he ever taught. such a kind person to go to for any questions or even just a normal chat

He is so sweet and funny. Your GPA is safe with him. The lectures are very interesting, if you pay attention the midterm and final will be a breeze. Both midterm and final are online; if you pay attention you will finish in one hour if you don't it will take a lot longer and be pretty annoying. But overall a back burner class that is pretty fun!

LOVE this guy, he is super into what he teaches and makes lectures funny, most of the stuff covered is also accessible online for a better understanding, midterm is long but also super flexible and the class is really lenient if you just talk to Professor Matthew bc hes super chill
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: super nice and easy to listen to in lectures - 1 midterm and 1 final and written texts every week but they are manageable. go to lecture and discussion section and you'll do great!
Passionate lecturer, grade is mostly based on listening responses which are easy As. If you go to lecture you will be fine for the midterm. Would definitely recommend!

Professor Mathew was an incredibly funny professor who always made his 1 1/2 hour lectures feel like 30 minutes. Such a fun class to take as a breadth! Open note exams, final is an essay. Although, quite a few 500 word writing assignments which took up a good chunk of time to write almost every week, but graded very nicely. Take this class!

The proudest I've ever felt of an assignment was the final paper in this class. Professor Mathew makes it so that you can write about what YOU are passionate on. So I chose Jazz through an education medium, and went to speak with him about the idea. He had SO MUCH to say. Just off the top of his head, no looking anything up. Insanely intelligent.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Prof. Mathew is the best professor I've ever had. His lectures and assignments were always engaging, even when the topics weren't individually interesting to me. His office hours were frequent and enjoyable as well.
er, maybe it was just like sensory deprivation coming out of covid, but I find this man strangely compelling. a **great** professor

Professor Mathew is absolutely amazing. Every class would make you laugh and at the same time accumulating loads of cultural capital. He is like a born performer on stage, and you can never get tired of his humor.

One of the jewels of the music department, seriously. had no expectations, had idea that this class was going to be such a crazy blast. totally changed my whole outlook. prof. mathew is an amazing pianist as well as being hilarious

Prof. Mathew is one of the best I have ever had the privilege to take a class with. He encourages thoughtful conversations and keeps it real. Wide range of interesting topics surrounding the music of Vienna. My favorite class this semester, and my major is not music. My EECS Professors should take teaching lessons from him.

Professor Mathew is super chill and understands that a lot of people take this class just as a breadth. Class consisted of 1 (small) paragraph a week and you can really talk about whatever you want in these. The midterms and final are take home and very similar to his lecture so as long as you take notes during lecture and you'll get an A
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: he really wants students just to think and do research on their own which seems super relaxed until you have to turn in some really really long papers. but he's super cute and helpful about the papers in OHs, although he's super picky about writing style, and the lectures (if u go to them) are interesting and pretty hilarious
this guy is legend
Professor Mathew appears to be maximally helpful. A lot of times, he contradicts himself on the same points.

Excellent professor with a sharp sense of humour and immense passion about his subject. Made the subject of Western Classical Music very approachable and understandable, with tests that were fairly easy so long as you went to section regularly.

best class I've taken at Berkeley. Didn't even know when I signed up that we'd be going to see some amazing concerts for free, and even meet players from the Vienna philharmonic!! Mathew is a riot: razor sharp and  opinionated, totally changed how I think about classical music. the few times you're bored, it's kinda nice just to watch him... ;)

For the first few lectures, Professor Mathew made me think about Beethoven and composing in a whole different light. For the rest of the course, however, the same messages were repeated over and over again. On the final essay, he constantly contradicted himself when giving advice, which was ambiguous and frustrating.

He is unquestionably one of the best professors I've had at Berkeley. His course was always fascinating, funny, and well presented. His assignments were very straight forward, and in fact rather fun! He grades very well and is just the absolute nicest and most helpful professor at Berkeley.

He's an excellent lecturer, no doubt about it. My issue was the fact that he seemed to heavily dislike me on a personal level. He would  take lines out of my paper and dissect it in front of the class, which was a bit hypocritical considering he ranted about my vocabulary, yet he himself is quite bombastic. Marked me down for illogical reasons too.

In all my years at Cal (and believe me, it's been too many...) I've never had a professor as eloquent or as engaging as Prof. Mathew. Most entertaining lectures I've ever sat through - between the copious wisecracks and pop culture references he gets the course material across very clearly. TAKE HIS CLASSES. :) Ladies, he's kind of a dreamboat.
I don't understand the previous two comments. Professor Mathew doesn't even teach those classes. His Beethoven class (which is still going on) is totally awesome.

Awesome.  Gotta take a class with him if you get a chance.  British accent is entertaining when he's not telling jokes (and they are funny).  Extremely clear; I took no notes but learned more in this class than many other classes.  Only assignments were listening responses and two papers.  Lecture content was never tested; just really fun.
