Dr. Nadeem's UGBA 106 class was one of the best experiences I've had at Berkeley. He connects real-world marketing with strong academic insight, making every lecture meaningful. He genuinely cares about students and fosters critical thinking. Highly recommend this class to anyone interested in marketing!

One of the most engaging and caring professors I've had. If you pay attention, you'll genuinely enjoy his lectures and learn a lot he makes the material feel approachable and relevant. He's often at Café Think after class and is always open to chatting or answering questions. It's refreshing to have a professor who truly cares about his students!!

Prof Nadeem is super chill! I love his classes I've taken ugba 106 and had to take ugba 168b international marketing with him!!! His classes are mostly group projects based and that was fun! The workload is totally doable! Would definitely recommend to ppl :)

Dr. Nadeem is an exceptional professor! He's incredibly kind and genuinely caring, and his passion for teaching shines through in every class. While there are a fair number of group projects and assignments, they're very manageable thanks to his clear expectations and the fact that work is divided among large teams. Definitely take his class!

Professor Nadeem makes the class engaging with discussions, projects, and even a field trip. He's always willing to help and creates a welcoming atmosphere. Definitely take this class - unstuck ai was a game-changer for test prep!

Opportunity to work with a real business which started within a year span and we learnt, how they leveraged marketing, importance of it and the real output of it.

Professor Nadeem is super caring, and his class has a manageable workload. There are 3-4 group projects throughout the semester, and you're with the same team for each project. I really enjoyed this class and recommend any course taught by Professor Nadeem

This is the worst class I have taken in my career. Instructor doesn't have any grasp of the subject material. If anyone asks any question he usually redirects it to other students. UGBA 106 was an amazing class, and Professor Nadeem does an excellent job teaching it. He demonstrates a strong grasp of marketing concepts and genuinely strives to showcase their real-world applications. Overall, I had an incredible experience and highly recommend taking his class.

Professor Nadeem was a highlight of my college career thus far. He made every class memorable, and I came out of it learning so much. It helps that he is also an incredible person who builds a connection with every student in his class.

Second half of the class looked different from the first half due to the above changes. He's a nice human and brought in successful people from all over his network to talk to us which I appreciate.

Dr. Nadeem is such a wonderful professor! He is extremely caring & encouraging, always checks in on his students' well-being, & has an optimistic approach to teaching. Prof Nadeem helps facilitate lively discussions in the class which foster learning. He is kind, compassionate and encourages curiosity.

If you're passionate about exploring the intersection of AI and marketing, I highly recommend taking Professor Nadeem's class! The lectures use highly relevant and recent marketing cases, overall, this has been one of the most rewarding courses I've taken at Haas!

The professor used real world examples and scenarios to explain marketing principles. The professor also introduced to real life leaders to get an insight into everyday modern marketing strategy and role of artificial intelligence in new age market place.

Professor Nadeem is a kind, supportive, and approachable educator who deeply cares about his students' success. He connects theory to practice with real-world examples, making lessons relevant and engaging. His detailed feedback fosters growth, and his passion for AI marketing is backed by strong expertise and recent publications.

Took EMBA 206 course Marketing course. Overall course was very well structured and paced. Prof. Nadeem had a very good balance of theory with and case studies. Learned on 4Ps, PESTAL, SWOT analysis, use of AI in marketing and effect of dynamic pricing on brand equity and customer loyalty. This is a core course.

Professor Nadeem is knowledgable and shares real life examples in marketing that helps us relate with the topics being covered. He is approachable and caring towards his students and focuses on a practical approach by learning from guest speakers he invites to his sessions.

The Marketing course given by Prof. Nadeem isn't extremely challenge, as long as you put enough participation and time into the course. 

If you are interested in Marketing and share real-world questions with Prof Nadeem, I'm thankful that he's willing to share industry insights to help you gain deeper understanding as well as the recent AI trends.

Dr Nadeem is kind, approachable and creates a welcoming environment that makes students feel comfortable seeking help or asking questions. Professor actively encourages student participation during lectures and discussions. He provides timely and constructive feedback on assignments and assessments.

The class atmosphere is great.The professor encouraged everyone to participate in discussions,and I was inspired by the diverse perspectives that were shared.The discussions in class mainly revolved around theory and case studies, which is perfect for beginners.If you enjoy being part of a student-centered learning environment, you will like it.
Professor Nadeem was very passionate about marketing when he taught my class and committed to engaging all of his students as frequently as possible. Participation is key to a good grade!

Professor Nadeem is a great instructor! He is always approachable and willing to help. The course itself is relatively easy to get an A in, provided you put in the effort and stay engaged. Professor Nadeem is genuine and flexible. "It is easy to get an A in my class", but if you want an A (>94.99%), you have to put in a good amount of work. reviews.comment: Professor Nadeem is super engaging and loves active participation, the more you put into class discussions the more you will get out of it. He's really approachable and flexible if you're having difficulty with assignments and is very invested in his students succeeding.

By far my favorite professor at Haas!

one of the best professors at haas, definitely take him for marketing, grading consists of quiz, midterm, and final (all super easy and online), and a couple group presentations that are chill -- definitely go to class and participate, it's important he knows who you are for the participation grade -- show up and you'll for sure get an A

Professor Nadeem is an incredibly friendly and inspiring professor. He does his best to make the class engaging and his efforts are noticeable from his interactions with his students. Professor Nadeem is a great lecturer and 106 is a very engaging class.He also makes sure to integrate different types of learning like presentations, videos, guest speakers, etc- which enhances learning greatly. Professor Nadeem is a personable, passionate, and intelligent source of knowledge. I truly appreciate that he is invested in his students' success and genuinely cares, creating strong positivity and empowerment.

Prof. Nadeem is the most caring professor I've ever had. He wants you to succeed, and gives advice that helps you do well in class + generally in life. Professor Nadeem is a wonderful Professor - personable, engaging, creative, innovative, and genuine. I enjoyed every class of professor Nadeem, his enthusiasm for marketing, teaching, and material made me genuinely excited to come to class and made me like marketing now. I am about to read and study more marketing by myself.

Wow Professor Nadeem, he just totally rocks! When I was very depressed and couldn't fathom making it to most classes, I still went to his class because he is so uplifting and peaceful. Take this professor! Super easy, truly cares about students, and always ready to help.

Professor Nadeem was kind, caring, understanding, and always willing to help. I loved his class because he is an amazing person and professor and allowed a lot of time for insightful class discussion.

Professor Nadeem is an amazing professor. He has genuine care for his students, ensuring that we not only understand the course material, but also feel supported in our learning journey. Professor Nadeem is incredibly kind and understanding. I love Professor Nadeem. He is a great professor and very caring. He has motivated me to do well in school even as I go through tough times. Take him he's the best professor at Haas.

Such a soft-spoken, brilliant man! He is very passionate about the content he teaches and about his students. Very responsive through emails, tons of opportunities to do good in the class, and brings in two interesting guest speakers! Very inspirational, and enriching experience!

Professor Nadeem was a phenomenal marketing instructor, and in my opinion is among the absolute upper echelon of the teaching staff at UC Berkeley Haas school of business. Professor Nadeem's summer course has been an amazing experience. Professor Nadeem is caring, understanding and inspiring. His lessons were engaging and the readings were interesting and useful.

Dr. Nadeem is probably one of my favorites, if not favorite, professors at Cal. He is knowledgeable in what he teaches, understanding, and generous. I am so glad I took this course with him and would do it again in a heartbeat.

Professor Nadeem has been a great teacher. His classes were very interesting and practical. Lectures & group projects combined, lots of readings but good grades. Professor Nadeem is really nice and caring.

His style is definitely geared toward physics students. Made it clear what concepts to nail down, homework was useful. Sometimes made mistakes in lectures but always corrected himself later. Exams were difficult.

Professor H was respected by our 5A class for his in-depth knowledge, detailed lectures, and fun demos. Expect to learn concepts in lecture while most of the applicable material (solving strategies, etc) outside of class though textbook/videos. Tests push your understanding and problems sets are difficult but all interesting if you put in the time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Very sweet person, gives decent lectures and assigns difficult (but enjoyable, interesting, and very well picked) homework problems. I spent around 4 hours a week on them. Midterms and final generally around the lower to middle end of the difficulty of homework problems. Will throw some shade at engineers from time to time. Good accent.

Very sweet guy who was open to a lot of my tangent questions. The lectures were fun but scarcely useful for problem sets and exams (if you read ahead, they're good for indexing the material, but you will mostly learn from the book and discussions). Doesn't quite answer emails, so take any questions to OH. Difficult class but rewarding nonetheless.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lectures don't help for exams. I mostly learned in lab sections or directly from doing homework assignments. Homeworks are each worth so little, labs are easy and worth a bit more, but most of your grade comes from exams. The exams were purely theoretical which I thought was more difficult than anything we worked on in the course.

While his demonstrations during lecture are fun, and he can be quite funny at times, his lectures often spend lots of time on proofs or long examples that don't help much for the midterms. Because lectures weren't super helpful, this class became very GSI dependent as I learned more in discussion section. Prepare to learn some stuff on your own.

AVOID Oskar if possible for physics 7a. His lecture style is not suited for an introductory undergrad course. He may be a funny lecturer, but he DOES NOT cover the content you need to know for exams. The e-textbook and hw sets are the only way to learn in this class with him. Take this class with a professor who actually TEACHES the content!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: run away :)

He consistently had interesting and fun demonstrations in class, at least 1 or 2 every lecture, he was a fun teacher and all the homeworks are from the textbook. His lectures are very example heavy, and the tests were more difficult than the problem sets, but the GSIs will provide resources of good problems to study with. He does regrades on exams.

Decent teacher, but some disconnect between midterms and material covered in lecture. If you've already taken a physics class in high school, it'll be easy to get a good grade (this class is a literal copy and paste of AP Physics C: Mechanics), but a first-timer to physics might have trouble with his teaching style.

Things taught over a 1-hour lecture could've been covered in 5 minutes and didn't help students prepare enough for what came on midterms. His obsession with the iClicker definitely needs to end as no one learns anything from it. He could be more transparent with grading and allow regrades considering his vague rubric system. Mediocre at best.

His lectures teach very basic mechanics, and the required textbook that he told us to buy only goes into concepts slightly more in-depth than he does. His homework however, is incredibly hard compared to what he goes over in class, and is harder than problems given in the textbook.
He's an OK teacher. Nothing horrible, but nothing extraordinary either. His iClicker use and demonstrations certainly helped, but he's still pretty average.

I liked his heavy I-clicker use. It tests you memory of the lecture. He sometimes dumbs down the physics however and does not cover a lot of the harder material. It is rather easy to avoid failure in this class.  I also found the textbook very unhelpful for the general problems sections and sometimes had to use chegg.

Lectures are completely boring and useless. Professor Hallatschek enjoys using iClickers, which are a terrible way to engage students and a waste of your money. Tests are straight forward, but the curve is a very strict bell curve.
He is supposed to be clear but takes basics high school mechanics and instead of clarifying it makes you confused about something you had previously mastered. reading the book is more useful.

Great professor. She really cared about her students and had great resources available. There was a lot of readings in the beginning, as expected in R1A. English is not my strongest subject, but attending office hours really helped. Would recommend!

Genuinely felt like I was not at Berkeley. Easiest English course of my life-time. She does take attendance since she teaches a discussion-style english class however it's not necessarily graded. Lots of collaboration assignments with other students for essay feedback and such but it is so easy.

Incredibly sweet and understanding Prof! Kaya is the best and even though I wasn't very well versed in many topics, she provided helpful insights and expanded my perspective on many topics for the better. If you can take her, def do!

Had Prof. Oakes for Fall 2024 and even though the theme was not necessarily something I was interested in, she made the class super enjoyable. She is very flexible, supportive, and understanding! All her readings were accessible online too. She gave us precise feedback and the opportunity to revise previous essays. Go take her class!!

Prof. Oakes class was a blast! In her Cultural Critique course everything couldn't have been more clear and straight forward. We had two essays worth 40% and 50% of the course grade and discussions posts that were easy and engaging. She also provided extra credit that helped give reassurance we could get whatever grade we aimed for. She's great!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Kaya is an very caring and empathic professor who genuinely cares for students. She is very understanding and supportive of you as an individual, and her classes are actually super interesting and have good discussions. She really puts the effort in on her end to make sure that you are improving at your writing and she is truly kind.

Prof Oakes is an amazing professor. She cares about students especially during the COVID time. If you need an extension, just explain your situation to her and she will understand it. Office hours were really helpful and she would respond to your questions in detail. Workload was not too bad if you follow her steps.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Fun readings and space to grow in writing and awareness on certain issues

The class was based in Music and Social Change, which was really cool! The books we read were okay, but I definitely think there could have been better choices. Other than that, her grading criteria was clear and she gave good feedback on essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Kaya is really awesome! I took her last year both for R1A and R4B. She gives really good feedback and always makes herself available for extra office hours if you need them. I would really recommend taking her if you are interested in reading a lot about political movements, social change and music in relation to protests (how they've changed).
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Friendly, caring, genuine to students. Reasonable grader. My COLWRIT R4B (R&C B requirement) class' theme was Protest Music.  General advice for any R&C class - the reading will be tedious if you don't enjoy the topic, so choose wisely! I've learned how to more effectively use research to support my writing, and how to write for a "larger purpose".
She is awesome. The only criticism is too much reading and not enough writing.

CWR1A seemed intimidating before I entered this class, but she made it very fair and doable. She is very nice, and laid back. Her friendly and positive attitudes make the class go a lot smoother. At the end of the class, I definitely learned a lot and became a better writer.

Kaya is funny, nice, and really intelligent. I was not a huge fan of the readings, but she assigned us interesting essay topics, which made the class fun. The subject was music and social movements, so we were able to write about music that personally interested us. Overall, my writing improved a lot, thanks to Kaya's class!

This class is really helpful and a really good way to brush up on writing skills! Oakes is really good about sticking to the schedule and manages to teach a variety of techniques that are really helpful for every sort of writing. She is very calm, which makes class not intimidating. She is very good at what she does and lets you out early!

If you want a cool way to fulfill your R1B req. this is it! I really enjoyed the prof especially since she was really involved in the subject matter (music), and quite modest about just how knowledgeable and connected she was. very chill, but attendance/reading was definitely not optional.

She's a great teacher. Offers a lot of help on papers. If you take her 3 hour per day course expect to get out early. She grades easily except when it comes to giving above a B+ which is rare. 6 units at a B+ is a great gpa boost!

probably the best teacher i've had here so far. the topic was very interesting and kaya presents the material in a way that even people who aren't familiar with underground music, can understand it and appreciate it. she's very helpful, but is a tough grader. overall, highly recommended.

Kaya is super chill.  The subject matter, music, was really interesting.  She really knows her stuff too and is really helpful.  If you have to fulfill the second half of the R&C requirement, take this class.  It actually made me want to do research!

This teacher is amazing! Beautiful, funny, caring, passionate and FUN. Her books are fun (the music theme is amazing, and I learned so many interesting things!) and it MADE me want to go to my 8am class! I never missed a class! Take it!!!
Great teacher, super laid back. The class was really interesting and it helped me improve my writing a lot.

I have been in American education for 5 years and my English was horrible. She corrected the way i write and the way i see literary works. She regularly have office hours with students and guide them to right direction.

Very cool teacher. She is very nice and helpful. Slowpace pace class, becuase she will no move on to the next topic unless she feels comfortable that all her students understand the material. Lets you out early from class most of the time. I hated writing before the class, and now I don't think its too bad.
The books are very interesting and her teaching is very effective. I don't hate writing anymore, so thank you Kaya
She's effective as a teacher and assigns really good books.

She's fair and goes out of her way to help students. The books are interesting and she makes a 3 hour class go by quicly. She swears often, se be prepared for that, but it's always in a joking way. Cares about your writing and makes an effort to improve it.
No Comments
No Comments
lecture mandatory for the most hard to follow lectures that were essentially just long tangents. very disorganized, took this class for a breadth but wish i had just taken another class later on.

I had a hard time following her speech as she mostly just went on long tangents. I often walked away from class never understanding what she was ever trying to say. Although the topics are interesting, I was not the biggest fan of the execution.

Professor Pandolfo is honestly a very kind professor. Her class is easy to keep up with, but she assigns a lot of readings and not all are necessary. That being said, most of the readings are super interesting and I even bought a few after the class ended for my personal collection. Overall: kind, but VERY reading heavy. 10/10 teaching team though

Professor Pandolfo is brilliant. You will be incredibly inspired by her lectures if you are interested in art, psychoanalysis, and culture in the aftermath of trauma. Some people complained that she was disorganized and difficult to understand, but if you really listen to her lectures and do the readings then this class will change your life.

Lectures are summaries of the reading and hard to follow. She shows up late and expects you to stay 5+ minutes after class ends every single lecture. She is good hearted, but sometimes there are uncomfortable interactions. There are more rewarding anthropology classes offered. Syllabus and due dates were constantly changing and instructions unclear

Her class wasn't that interesting. She tends to go on and on during her lectures without really encouraging her students to share. When they do share insights or ideas, she is usually pretty dismissive - it feels like she doesn't care about your opinion. She talks too much about her own research and expects students to have the "right opinion".
Pandolf really makes you think. Her lectures are incredible. This class changed my life, and I am genuinely freaked out about the ghosts and spirits that lurk in my house now.

I struggled a lot in this class due to lack of organization on the professors part. There was no way to keep up with the syllabus because the readings and deadlines were constantly changing. Lectures were also difficult to follow and often strayed from assigned readings. Shes an intelligent person, but not very approachable for help.

Truly the most disorganized professor I have ever taken a class from. The syllabus was irrelevant from the get-go and was constantly saying she would release prompts or have things graded by a certain time and then never met those deadlines, to an extent that was frankly comical. I can't imagine getting tenure with that kind of organization.

Professor Pandolfo is brilliant but a terrible instructor. Lecture is unstructured and 2 powerpoints explain concepts of 2 from 8 readings. She rambles about issues related to readings but not assigned ones. Her engagement with students is awful and she struggles to use zoom/powerpoint. The GSI is not helpful either. Save your money and skip.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dense readings, that were gone over in lecture in a way that made them more confusing. Didn't grade papers before new ones were due, so there was no way to tell how you are doing. Quick to cut off students or ramble on the subject without answering the question. Talked in run-on sentences used academic vocabulary, was not very open to student input

Her lectures are very poorly organized and she is not a good lecturer at all. Your grade in the class pretty much depends on your GSI. Pandolfo always goes on tangents, but she is a caring and accessible professor. She responds to emails instantly. However, overall you do not learn anything in this class and you have to do a lot of reading for it.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Although her classes were not as well-structured, after the pandemic occurred, she was very considerate of the students. She graded two out of three essays based on completion and cancelled all sections. Very motherly. I liked her as a human being, although unsure as a professor.
Very theoretical and most lectures consisted of unrelated tangents. Late to everything and the readings/assignments were constantly changing.
best professor I have had berkeley!

Rambles on for hours about nothing. I had more serious problems when I was in a class in which I disagreed with what she was "preaching". I questioned her, she grew extremely flustered and a little angry, and her GSI approached me after class to try to get me to understand why her beliefs were correct and mine were wrong. Indoctrination.

The material ranges from being politically interesting to almost absurdly theoretical...a lot is difficult to grasp but she understands that. No one in the class (except for a few) actually understood the readings on their own, so attendance was/is essential. Beware of your GSI--he/she grades everything. We had a bad GSI who botched grades.

Very unstructured and lectures consist of mile-a-minute ramblings...though they are, to be fair, very articulate ramblings. Lots and lots of required reading. Very theoretical. If you don't do the readings, her lectures make no sense the majority of the time. This class may be difficult for students who rely on structure and clarity in lectures.

She allows you to think for yourself. Her classes are not structured and the syllabus is always subject to change. Nonetheless, her classes are very interesting and generates a space for students that permits them to critically think about the various assumptions that we live by. Take her class, its worthwhile and fruitful.

No exams.  Class grade dependent primarily upon two 10 page papers, with some participation and short reponse papers added in.  Lectures are extremely boring and hard to follow.  Syllabus not followed very closely.  Not a fun class to take, but easy grading.

A bit of a diva but extremely articulate. Lectures are basically 1.5 hrs worth of ramblings, the length of which is enough to provoke me to wonder why I'm wasting my life in Anthropology. But she can be "poetic" when she explains concepts in psychological anthro. Her lectures on Freud made me swoon unintentionally.

I had a lot of trouble with the class at first and was frustrated with her lecturing style, however, she is brilliant!!! It just takes a while to get used to but I learned more from one class with her than I have in any of my other classes!!!

Run for your life! One of the worst classes I have ever taken. I would have dropped it immediately but needed it to graduate. Everyone I spoke with in this class had no idea what she was talking about. This class was total drivel. Don't say you haven't been warned.
not worth it!
dull and stupid. waste of everyone's time involved.

Good lecturer, though somewhat disorganized and scattered. Too much assigned reading so didn't explore many of the more interesting readings in-depth - it was like a bird's eyeview on many of the readings. Lectures were scattered at times and expectation for class participation was paradoxical as she didn't really want to engage in discussion.

Professor Pandolfo is obviously quite brilliant, but is less effective as a teacher.  Lectures were very disorganized and not always clear.  Some of the readings were also challenging, but ultimately essay grades were very generous.  She also gave us the opportunity to revise our midterm essay for a better grade.

she's a nice person and the topic is pretty interesting. there was a lot of reading. VERY EASY GRADER though. despite the fact that i nearly did none of the readings and didn't understand any of the material, i still got an A+ (grade is based on 2 essays)

Stefania is very intelligent and her class is interesting. Her course is not very organized though and it is sometimes hard to know where to be in her class as far as the syllabus goes. Otherwise, she is very generous in grading!

Readings assigned were intreesting, but at time difficult. She does a good job of trying to explain all the readings yet her lectures are often boring, and she has no structural format in the way she explains the readings.  Yet I think she is a good teacher and does her best so that all the students understand the readings and pass the class.

She is very interesting, i think, and her lectures, while difficult to follow, are very insightful and fascinating IF you care about the topic.  Reading is valuable, but if you don't do all of it you can still survive.  I love this class and think she deserves a better rating than she has here.
Lectures put me to sleep. I was very worried about my grade in this class, but I still ended up with an A.
She is Hot! I had a crush on her, and made her blush in office hours.
SHE RAMBLES ON AND ON! mainly it's about uesless things not connected to the topic objectives.  everyone in class basically fell asleep, played their ipods, or stared outside the window. big waste.

Pandolfo is very helpful and accessible during office hours, however, she does have a tendency to expect that all students have read anything that she references; i.e. if she says "Jung" in a lecture, you'd better have read everything ever written by Jung, but I think it has more to do with time constraints and her trying to get through her lecture

Nice guy, but there's disconnect between him and course staff. There is barely any helpful communication from them and stuff isnt usually updated on time. Theres also impossible quizzes every week with trick questions.

Professor is good, but the class is not well run at all. Assuming you took science classes in HS, you don't learn much, and there was a bunch of messed up logistics. Lectures/discussions were WAY longer than they needed to be, and similarly there was a lot of work in this class (although all of it was not hard). No tech policy is just ridiculous.
The class teaches you nothing, complete waste of time

Prof Perlmutter was very cool and clearly cared about the material. The class was run absolutely horribly (not the profs' fault) and I would not recommend anyone to take it, at least not as it is now- the discussions and plenary are painfully long and drawn out and the test questions are very confusing. but saul helped make it tolerable

Whatever everyone else said about an easy class, I feel like they took that personally and just made it difficult. The grading this year was bad, & there were not clear rubrics when it came to the projects. The final had so many questions that SO many were confused upon, as the guidelines for studying weren't accurate. I felt so duped w/ the class

Saul is so amazing, I loved the PlayPosits and plenaries. When we were locked in MLK because of the campus threat, he checked up on us. Genuinely wants us to learn and succeed. Also offered to bring our ideas to the White House President's Council meetings. So caring and sweet. Really enjoyed this class.

Saul is the best professor I've ever had. He is truly brilliant, loves teaching, and cares for and holds respect for each of his students individually. He is kind, funny, and fair. He shows true interest in all of the topics he teaches. He will thoroughly consider all of you questions and answer them in an insightful and usually humorous manner.

Class was interesting and Saul was really passionate about teaching the material. As far as the grading, 35% of your grade is homework and participation, which you just need to complete/show up for. Then 20% was quizzes (there are six, all pretty easy, lowest two dropped). The rest is the final and two projects (all not hard with generous grading).

FANTASTIC INDIVIDUAL. The class was wide ranging in scope and co-taught by 2 other Professors but it was one of the most intriguing classes I have taken. The material is on the intersection of philosphy and psychology from a scientific perspective but take this class for the Professors no matter what. An opportunity not to be missed!

As someone who has never liked physics in his life, I quite enjoyed this class. Mathematical portion of this class is high-school level at best. You need to do weekly homework, but you will be rewarded with fun experiments that explain concepts learned in online textbook. Professor is also very enthusiastic! Highly recommended!!!

Professor Perlmutter's passion for science and this subject in particular permeates to  students in the class. This class will not only change the way you think about music, but of the entire field of science . Perlmutter is brilliant, but that doesn't obscure his ability to present concepts clearly. A contemporary Richard Feynman!
Physics and music is a fantastic class.  Professor Perlmutter is extremely enthusiastic and loves to help students understand the material.
A really fun, charming class with a extremely enthusiastic professor. Full of great demonstrations and activities with fairly interesting and not too challenging material.

Took Physics & Music in spring 07- was his 2nd semester teaching ever. Very enthusiastic and spoke more quickly when he got excited so sometimes difficult to follow. He obviously loves teaching which made the class better. Lots of demonstrations and prof and GSIs helpful in answering questions

Awesome teacher, really loves teaching and is a very smart man. "Physics and music" is a really easy class. just go to class and do the homework and there's no way you can't pass. good way to get physic breadth out of the way.

He is very enthusiastic and obviously loves teaching, even though he hasn't taught much because he is a big-shot physicist. Quizzes sometimes tricky, final was easier than quizzes. Go to class, pay attention, and you should do well. He is very helpful and friendly, don't be afraid to approach/ask for help. He loves talking to students.
No Comments

Prof. John is great, he explains concepts very well and is super funny! The two exams were very fair and the weekly homeworks are extremely doable (graded on completion). Every assignment was meant to help you learn. He also offered 3% extra credit at the end of the semester :) Please take him if you can!

It was a joy to take Professor John's class. His lectures are clear and full of fun concept/theory application. The class was very well structured, and the journey through the theoretical shifts in personality psychology was very fun and interesting!

Professor John is one of a kind. He always approaches students with respect, care, and knowledge. He's good at explaining the material and had great real life examples. For the class, it was during the summer, so a lot of material to cover and memorize in 6 weeks, but manageable if you organize your time properly. Take this class, you'll love it!

This class was interesting and chill. Oliver is really enthusiastic and loves to have conversations with students. Do the assignments and you will be able to do well on the tests. Lectures can be super lengthy but most of the test info comes from there. There is also lots of extra credit offered and quiz drops. Overall I really enjoyed the class.

Probably one of my favorite classes in my 4 years here. Chose to take this class relatively last-minute as was the best decision. Prof John is a clear and funny lecturer and has the absolute best GSI team. Exams are straight-forward and fair, material is beyond interesting and applicable.

John was really annoying and bad lecturer but the GSI's were amazing (shoutout Maria!!). The class is boring and lecture slides were basically incomprehensible. Lecture attendance was mandatory too. Pros are that the (2) midterms are only 42% of the final grade and there is no final exam!! Also 4% extra credit offered at the end of the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He's amazing!! Tests are a bit difficult just because they consist of fill in the blank questions that require you to really memorize everything, BUT, he gives so many great real-life examples in his lectures so that makes it easy to remember everything. His lectures are always amazing and he's overall very kind and caring, my fav professor at cal

Take his class if you can!!! He is so knowledgable and passionate about what he teaches. Show up to office hours because he really tries to get to know his students. If you show up, he'll notice and it's fun! The class is really interesting and he is just the absolute best :) He can sometimes go on tangents but they are usually related to material

Prof. John's online summer class for PSYCH 150 was awesome! He was totally engaged during lectures and shared very interesting stories. There were a lot of things to complete but as long as you put effort into them, you'll be fine. I'm not a Psych major, but he made me very interested in the field. I highly recommend his class, he's just amazing!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I loved Prof Oliver's Class! Though there were a lot of things to be complete (articles, web exercises, quizzes etc), they gave you a chance to improve your grade. Not to mention that he is a reputed professor with super interesting lectures and he also cares a lot about his students! Would def recommend to people needing a psych upper div!

One of the best professors at Cal. 150 is the best class to take if you are just interested but not majoring in Psych. By far, my favorite professor. Very accessible through emails and office hours. No Final Exam; two mid-terms. There are weekly readings of the textbook and web exercises but they are fun. You will not regret taking this class!

Prof. John is one of the best professors I've ever had. He genuinely cares about each of his students & wants you to do well. Super great guy to talk to, I went to his OH even if I didn't have questions about the course. I wish he taught more undergrad classes because I'd take every single one. If you have a chance to take his class, do it!!

Super funny, has interesting stories to demonstrate tough concepts, super approachable and super patient. Just skim through the textbook. If you pay attention in his lectures and just go back and read the particular slides youre prepared trust me! Dont underestimate the MCQs tho. Articles really force you to think. Web ex are lengthy. very doable

His class really is easy. Study the slides and you're good. He is so, so, so nice! And he really DOES have a great personality. I wish I could take him again because his personality and stories are so adorable to me! Free text on bcourse. 2 tests total, 3 article questions to answer. Def okay to handle during summer.

Don't believe people who say it's easy A, but yeah reading the book wasn't necessary to pass the tests at all. Web exercises are time consuming. Went in expecting easy A, really have to work for whatever grade I'm getting. Loved him as a lecturer and think that the material is enlightening. Non-psych major.
Oliver P. John... Cool German dude with a great "personality" and hilarious yet effective teaching style :) Do take a class with him!

Professor John is fun . Reading is long and boring, but not needed all the time. The article responses are the longest part. Don't wait until the last minute. You will most likely get an A for effort on these. Tests come from lectures and book, but ask your GSI what is relevant in the book. Use the study guides. Good GPA booster for psych majors.

Prof. John was radiant and colorful. Genuinely kind & goofy. Reading is wordy, LONG, & dry. Course content  history of personality psych. vs real life application. 2 non cumulative tests but HEAVILY weighted. Web exercises & articles saved me. Articles take forever to do. Got our grades SUPER late. Offered extra credit  in the end. I say take it.

This was easily the most boring class I have taken at Cal. Professor John goes over the same material over and over again and feels like a history class. The slides are so horrific, so much info on each one. Would never recommend this to anyone, waste of time class.

Dr. John is a super nice guy and is great to talk to in office hours (definitely visit him there). The class wasn't a good fit for me though. We spent way too much time on the history of personality psych. It's an easy class and Dr. John is great, but I didn't walk out of there feeling like I learned a lot about contemporary research on personality

this class was disappointing - could have been really great and i was initially excited, but i don't think i really learned anything substantial from professor john's lectures. he's a very talented scholar and amazing researcher, but not the best professor in my opinion. he loves teaching but again, didn't learn anything. easy A though.

I love this professor -- and not just because I have an insane crush on him. He's a genuinely good-hearted, kind, and caring professor. His lectures are entertaining, he wants his students to succeed, and he is passionate about personality psychology.
Easiest class I've taken at Cal. 1 midterm and 1 final, no paper. Professor John is engaging and clear, has great slides. Textbook chapters uploaded on bSpace.
took this course over summer. 1/5 of the class got an a+. 1/3 a. 1/3 a-. easiest course i've taken at cal. memorize the slides the night before the exam.

I regret not going to his office hours more. He was a rad dude and wanted to get to know you and help you as much as he could. His lectures are fun and he loves teaching to undergrads. May be confusing at times, but he is always willing to clarify things for you. Highly recommend him.
The best professor I ever met. His lectures are interesting and inspiring. He is helpful and loves chatting with students. I enjoy every lecture! His class is definitely a must-take.

Great teacher, funny lectures, pretty good slides and very engaging. He's an excellent professor and I would recommend him to anybody. Don't underestimate the difficulty of the exams because they're multiple choice.

Sure, the teacher is nice, the lectures are clear, and the material is easy, but this class might be too easy. Because I had lots of other work, I only crammed the day before the midterm/final, did not go to class, and did not read the book, and I got an A+. As much as I like that grade, I don't think it should be that easy to come by.

I've already graduated with a Psych degree but this had to be the best psychology professor I ever had. Engaging, charming, and very easy to understand. The tests were fair and completely matched the lectures.

Took this class over the summer and what a breeze it was. Easiest class I've taken at Cal. Although there were some tedious assignments and group projects, none of it was challenging. Prof John tries to make this class as interesting as possible and wants to give good grades to his students. Highly recommend!!

Really great professor, interesting, funny. I'm a business major and have only taken one psychology class ever before this and still got an A. Print out the lecture notes, go to lecture/section and just sit back and enjoy the ease and peace. Midterm/final are straightforward, just make study guide from topics he gives you to study. A+
He's my IDOL!! I would normally choose to sleep in at 10 o'clock in past years at Cal, but i went to class and actually enjoyed it because of him. Take it!
AMAZING! HILARIOUS! INFORMATIVE!  PALATABLE! The best psych class I've taken yet, not necessarily because of the content, but because Professor John is outright fantastic.  Take it!
I doubt he's using the personality inventories for anything but teaching tools.  He'd have to go through informed consent first in order to use them in his research.

Why am I the only person who hates this course? He is so uninteresting--a horrible lecturer. The textbook is unteresting and boring (he wrote it). Smiles all the time. You have to take all these personality inventories in class that in the end go to his own research. A complete waste of my time. Didn't learn a thing.

There is such a thing as overly-easy. I had classes in my junior high school that was harder than this. He really makes personality psychology uninteresting. If you like an easy A and a superficial, dumbed-down depiction of how psychologists study personality, then this is for you. Fell asleep often, finally stopped attending, and still got an A+.

You'd never think that the same man who wrote our soul-crushingly dry textbook is a lively, hilarious professor. I found lectures a bit scattered but very informative. He provides outlines of what he's going to lecture on. My only suggestion is to make sure you do all those surveys online. I thought I had them all done but I missed one and ended up 1% short of an A. D'oh!
His class is fun and the tests are easy as long as you keep up with the material.
Funny guy. Midterms are straightforward and class is interesting.
This was a pretty easy class, but you still learn a great deal about personality. his lectures were funny but informative, and he was very approachable in office hours. i highly recommend this class
A highly recommended class!  Work load is light, and lectures are interesting!
i like how he applies psychology 150 to simone and his cat chloe
Just a great professor.
Great class and professor! He really cares about students doing well and makes it easier. There are weekly assignments but it's almost fun!!!

Professor John is awesome! He makes the subject really coherent, his lectures are always engaging and funny, he's not all arrogant, totally easy to relate to and wants us to learn and succeed.  2 exams, pretty easy if you read the book and listen in lecture.  he's a great guy, and everyone should take 150 with him!
Awesome teacher, and a lot of fun to talk to in Office Hours. Definitely recommend taking his class or just meeting him!

Why can't all professors be like professor John? He really loves his students and you can tell from your first class with him! He is a great lecturer. The best professor in the Psych department hands down!!
An amazing teacher.  I enjoyed having him as my advisor for my thesis and my life as well.  Very engaging, friendly, sincere, and honest.  I am grateful for having met such a great mentor and friend.
No Comments
Professor John is really interesting.  I always enjoyed going to his class.  It was almost like watching TV.  Hell, I didn't even notice that I was learning.
He is by far one of the best professors at Cal, he makes the material fun and interesting, and is REALLY FUN!
excellent

One of the sweetest, and cutest 'Personalities' I have ever met. He has a silly sense of humor, and interesting stories. Lectures are fun, and almost relaxing. He really knows his stuff, and conveys it in a very enjoyable manner. He is such a friendly pers
Funniest and most interesting teacher in the Psy department.

Great professor!  Enthusiastic.  His lectures were always very interesting.  All of the material was always clearly presented.  If something is unclear, he would always make sure things were clarified.
The BEST psychology professor at berkeley!! Very humble, kind, and fun. A GREAT CLASS!! He is so nice no person can ever hate him. The class is interesting because he is lively and engaging.
MY FAVORITE PROF AT CAL!!!
LOVE HIM. it's all been said already
One of the easiest class I've ever taken at Cal.  He's such an awesome prof and he's so enthusiastic about the subject.

Wow, he's easily one of the best professors I've ever had. He's fun, engaging, and informative. He really brings a passion to the material and always has an anecdote to illustrate it. The class and tests are easy, but mostly because you can't help but pay attention and he's clear with his expectations.

There is no final (just a second midterm), discussion attendance isn't mandatory, 1/3 of your grade based on weekly 1-page write ups of chapter readings and online "exercises." Class is easy--just pay attention to lectures and since he lists what he might test you on, you can get by reading a little
good lecturer, if psych is your thing.
GREAT professor. approachable, clear, and helpful.  Interesting lectures.

One of the kindest professors I have ever had, as well as one of the most effective because he makes his lectures relatable on a personal level. A fresh breath of air to the impersonality and academic snobbery of UC Berkeley.
he's great, and so is the class - very interesting and fun
By far the best/most-fun/easiest professor in the psych dept
such an awesome class.
Friendly instructor who enjoys adding personal ancedotes to make the material more enjoyable
The textbook he wrote for Personality Psychology was pretty good actually. Good Prof

Dr. Bradni Pearce is great, she is very lively and brings alot of joy to each lecture. In this class, it's mostly group work, so hope and pray you get good teammates. The worst part of the class is the GSI, who is an MBA student who grades very harshly. The lectures do get a little long and boring at times, but overall, a great professor!

I really enjoyed UGBA 150 and Dr Pearce. She is really kind and you can tell she loves her job tremendously. I learned a lot in regard to leading teams and the class was worthwhile and a part of the UC Berkeley Changemaker certificate. At times the material can get a little slow and boring, but she picks it back up well.

In UGBA 10X Brandi was a sweet prof, but out of the four professors in this class, her lecture was the least interesting to me. Of course this might be because I am least interested in her topic, but over all the lectures were boring. Also, mandatory attendance for this 8 AM class, which she makes you take selfies in class to prove you attended....
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Brandi seems sweet. Just her lectures were really tough to process at 8 am, especially as a freshman... She often got frustrated by the class's lack of engagement. 

I think her lectures were honestly the least engaging out of the four professors who taught the class

Her class was interesting even though it can get repetitive and boring, however the class was easy and I came out there learning more soft skills. Your grade all depends on your GSI, the prof doesn't grade anything and is only there to lecture and guide you through your group project. Honestly, very minimal work.

Dr. Brandi Pearce was the best professor I have taken here at Berkeley. She is extremely passionate about what she is talking about and I have learned more about working in a team over the past semester than my entire college career. Her lectures can become a little boring sometimes, but most class time is working with teams.

She talks a lot and can get exhausting. I remember one exercise she does with these sticker dots makes you question the true meaning behind it. It was supposed to show us the way bias works in the world but was an exercise in privileged, classicism, and racism.

Very sweet professor, I interact with her frequently outside of class willingly because she's so caring and gives great advice! Lectures can be long and no-tech, but everything she teaches is applicable to the real world. Best piece of advice: "Don't be absent."
She put so much time into creating this course. Class attendance is a must - partner activities every class. Little to no homework outside of class.
He keeps going on and on about how amazing AI is and it is pmo
This course is a little heavy on math and problem solving. The GSI's help alot. The professor is always willing to help and cares alot. The grading is really good too.

Before Midterm you will be crunched with Lab assignments. You will learn excel and linear programming, after MT it gets much easier. Prof. Potts is very caring and flexible and super knowledgeable. GSI's help alot too.

Personally, I was really disappointed in this class. I felt Matthew was a pretty confusing lecturer. He would go back and forth on his definitions and the material for the class was so scattered. You learn something very different from what the weekly assignment would be and you depend so much on the GSI for help since they are the ones teaching...
Very passionate scientist. Respect and appreciation for all roles and ppl at CD. Jokes mediocre at best.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I had him as a guest lecturer and I don't understand how people take his actual classes. Worst lecturer I've seen, so hard to understand and he has powerpoints behind him with basically nothing on them??

Professor Potts barely taught any of the material in labs. Everyone in the class struggled to complete labs and the GSIs were the only ones who got us through. If youre taking this class, prepare to teach yourself everything for the labs and/or go to office hours twice a week.
Really difficult labs that everyone struggled with on material that was rarely taught. Ended up teaching myself excel and majority of the course

Over 60 students in the class and roughly 90% of them were confused with what was going on. Classes were riddled with information that no one could understand, and there was constant confusion between the staff on how to do things in excel. This class is difficult because of how unorganized it was, and I highly recommend that you do NOT take it.
He was very straight forward and made information digestible. Office hours were always helpful to get clarification on the problem sets.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I really liked prof. Potts. He was super helpful during office hours, but I found that his lectures were good enough, so you wouldn't even need to go to office hours to clarify topics. Your mark depends heavily on the problem sets, so I would go to OH for that. Overall, I thought he was an enthusiastic prof that genuinely enjoyed teaching.

Matthew really cares about students and answering any questions- makes environmental science very accessible to everyone as an intro class. He likes to encourage class discussion so find someone you like to sit next to!

You take this class to get an A, not to learn anything. It's unfortunate this is an approved DS course. It makes sense, though, given how smug the prof is. But when you see his "research," you quickly realize he became one for producing endless slop. I encourage you to read his work, going back to 2010s

Class is honestly a mess. Haven't learned anything useful, lectures are boring, course staff is not unresponsive They took the entire semester to grade anything. Its been over two weeks since finals ended and they just released the grades, many of which were incorrect scorings with assignments still not put in. No communication efforts at all.

Disorganized, unclear grading, and inaccessible outside of class. I am just ashamed that this is an approved class that are offered under Cal's Data Science program. It is easy to get an A but I genuinely learned nothing.

Grading was finished around a week before the last day of finals, and they are somehow still not released. He has no transparency or communication around grades. His lectures are just high level summaries that can be found if you ask ChatGPT what a neural network is. Easy class though, just only take it if you want an easy A.
Easy class but you don't really learn much. Also very disorganized

Class has no use in terms of material. Prof is often visibly unprepared for lectures, midterm was dysfunctional, staff didn't bother to use DataHub (assignments were links on bCourses to Google Colabs you had to manually save a copy of) and lab questions were unclear/poorly written. No finals yet they couldn't even submit CalCentral grades on time.

Completely online course with a clear weekly structure. The labs are due each week and are manageable, helping reinforce the material without taking too much time. Lectures are three hours per week and recorded. The instructor explains concepts clearly, and expectations for assignments are straightforward. Final is project-based rather than an exam

don't take this class if you want to learn anything. class content is barely much, no prep sources for midterm, late grading for labs, doesn't answer ed inquiries, no clarity on grade distributions or grading, etc.

A truly worthless class. You learn nearly nothing, and what is taught could be self studied in a couple weeks. The course staff is lazy, and the materials are haphazardly put together. If you want an A, you could take it. If you want to learn something, avoid it. I haven't met anyone who enjoyed this class.
Hes fine like nothing special he dosent hate students or anything but teaching is sooo dry and slow and a waste of time

Prof. Pardos is a cool teacher but if you're in his class you're more likely to interact with the TAs than him. Lots of group projects which can get annoying since everything is online and people can procrastinate but other than that the class isn't bad at all. Pretty chill
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Professor Pardos is a highly qualified professor, unfortunately, he knows this and is consumed by his ego which is super off-putting during lectures. He repeatedly dismisses student questions and makes you feel bad for not understanding the content. If you want an engaging, caring, cool professor, look elsewhere.

In Data144 with Professor Pardos, valuable content was overshadowed by unnecessary sarcasm, hindering engagement. Clearer, more encouraging communication and prompt responses to inquiries could vastly improve the learning environment.
Amazing lecturer would highly recommend! teaches concepts from the ground up, which makes it easy to learn and fully understand the material.

Zi Qiu was genuinely one of the better physics professors I've ever had. Lectures weren't mandatory, but I suggest going to them since he really enforces getting an intuition for the physics. The midterm and final were of reasonable difficulty, so if you understand the lectures and about 75% of the homework, you'll be fine.

Decent lecturer, went deep into deriving equations and explaining concepts, but rarely showed examples. Accent made it difficult to understand at times. Not the most helpful in OH, especially if you come to him with a personal problem. Homework questions taken directly out of textbook, solutions can be found easily. Tests are short, graded fairly.

Great lecturer, good at emphasizing physical intuition over mathematical drudgery (where there is a lot of in mechanics). Don't let an easy midterm food you, he seems to like compensating with a much harder (but still fair) final.

Qiu's lecture's were more or less an overview of the textbook material, but of course with his own take on things. He is a good lecturer, but in order to complete the homework, you definitely need to supplement the lectures with readings, as the homework is usually mostly from the textbook. I recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Respected--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Awful experience! Easy midterm, so he made the final excruciating to compensate. Final qs relied on multivar calc theorems (which hardly remembers at this point, esp since that's not what we were told to study for!) instead of actual class material. Qiu is a great lecturer, but the lack of organization and communication ruined the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This was one of the most frustrating classes. The midterm was ridiculously easy so the class averaged an A after it. The hws were always copied and pasted from the book but were stupidly tedious. To fix the high class average, the final was insanely hard with topics not covered in class. I had a 98 in the class going into the final & ended w/ a B.

Qiu emphasizes physical reasoning above abstract and detailed mathematical calculation. He is great at extracting the physical meaning of formulas and building your intuition. However, this also means he passes over some interesting mathematics. The class is paced very slowly and the work is easy. He could have taught more topics pretty easily.

He is the best professor that I had at Berkeley and I'm not even a physics student. Took 141A and 141B and he just got better and better!! His lectures were so amazing and I loved that he didn't focus purely on formulas but tried to get us to build up our physical intuition for solid state physics. Really wish that I could've taken more w/ him!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: A super easy professor, his class reminded me my days in the community college. The final exam was mostly based on the lecture notes; in other words, the lecture notes were the solution manuals for the final exam problems, no kidding.

A super easy professor, his class reminded me my days in the community college. His final exam was mostly based on his lecture notes; in other words, his lecture notes were the solution manuals for the final exam problems, no kidding.

One of the best professors I've ever had. Explains everything very clearly, the HW only takes a few hours every week or two (7-8 psets/semester), and the tests are easy if you have physical intuition. Really stresses physics but also develops the mathematical formalism.
Loved the professor, Loved the Class. He teaches eerything very clearly, and makes sure no stoned is unturned.

Qiu is neither great nor terrible. Clear lectures, but he cares very little about teaching. Make sure to get a good GSI, the one I had was horrible and that made things a lot harder. Tests are relatively easy, but again this depends on the GSI!
Remarkably clear despite the accent, very intuitive lectures that follow Griffiths closely. Homeworks and tests weren't too difficult.

He's almost too easy; the homework could have been more challenging.  The only other flaw I can prescribe is he follows the book a little too closely.  But, it's a great book, he's a great lecturer and he'll even interject cool little anecdotes into his lectures occasionally.  I highly recommend taking a class from him!!!

I love this man. His lectures are so clear and well given that you doubt Quantum was a difficult subject to begin with. Homework is straight out of Griffiths and exams are fair. I would highly HIGHLY recommend taking the class from him. He also can't pronounce "measurable" but it is adorable.

He's a total G. Good, informative lectures, and he's helpful and nice. The problem sets are painfully challenging, but the tests are straightforward and reasonable. He has a hilarious tendency to say "arrpha" ("alpha"). Awesome subject.

Great professor. Lectures are very organized and clear, explains every step in derivations. Homeworks are also insightful. In OH he will answer all your questions, will help you solve the homework if you show that you have thought about it. Test, not hard and very closely related to homework and lectures. Attend lecture! Used Marion 4th ed.
He's definitely a good teacher. Tests are mostly based off of the lecture and pretty easy if you go to class. Homework problems assigned from the book.
Very fair in grading and workload. I am not Psych major but still found the material digestible. Solid choice for clinical req.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Overall super chill class. Dont need to go to lecture just review all of the notes before exams and you will be fine. Section attendance is mandatory. 50% of your grade is completion only assignments due at the end of the semester. Big research paper to write but can do it on any topic. Very easy way to satisfy clinical psych requirement.

Dr. Zhou is great. The class was easy to follow along with-- hw assignments and exams were directly related to lecture content. Final paper isn't too bad either, as it gives you a lot of freedom to discuss what you'd like. Only one "group" project in section (presentation on a specific article or journal) and it's simple. I def recommend her :)

She is so sweet, has very relevant material to the field of study that is updated as well. Homework and all assignments vary, very lenient on late homeworks but there is a group project in section. Midterm and Final was online and if you pay attention in lecture and write down what she says you can definitely pass with an A.

Prof. Zhou is amazing! She's very kind, has a deep passion for what she does, and obviously wants everyone to succeed :) The 3 exams are very straightforward, the majority of your grade is based on completion/participation, and the final project is pretty open-ended and has clearly outlined criteria. Loved her and loved PSYCH 131!

Lectures are very slow. Lectures recorded and slides posted. Easy A if you take 130 at the same time. Online midterm but in person final- super easy. Attendance not mandatory for lecture but is for discussion. Easy assignments- literally just reading an article and submitting a question you had.

Very sweet professor, you can really tell she's passionate about what she teaches. Her and the staff were very accommodating throughout the whole semester due to the pandemic. As long as you do the study guides provided you should be good for exams!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof Zhou was really great, and PSYCH 131 is by far the best class I've taken in quarantine. The professor and GSIs were very accommodating--you could tell they really wanted us to do our best, which was motivating. Super clear lectures and tests (with material basically straight from the slides), great GSIs, and pretty easy assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She is a very nice person and a great lecturer! I love taking her class. Although there are about 2 readings per week, her exams are mainly based on lecture and section materials, all close-book. Fair grading and no HWs! Recommended!
Great professor, I wish I could take his class again.

I took this professor my first semester at Berkeley, I absolutely loved the way his discussions were set up. It's an easy class because he offers immense support all you have to do is pull your weight by participating in class and submitting essays. Additionally he allows you to resubmit essays for better grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. JDQ really cares about his students. His class was genuinely interesting and easily my favorite course this semester.

took it in the first semester of my freshman year. The best class I have taken here at Berkeley. Much of the advice given helped me through tough times. Learned much more beyond knowledge to write. The most caring professor so far. Didn't think that this would best class experience so far. Just be present. a solid 6/5. Take it.

JDQ is an amazing R1A professor. As long as you participate in his classes (he cares a lot about showing up), hand homework on time, and show thinking in your essays, he is probably going to give you an A. Class gets really chill once you are used to JDQ's teaching style. Love him.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Quattro actually cares if you pass the course or not. He tries his best to help you inside and outside of class time. He is very responsive and definitely not a tough grader. As long as you try hard and take his feedbacks seriously you will receive a decent grade.

He wants you to pass the portfolio evaluation, which is a hard pass or fail for all R1As. Surprised more don't talk about that here. Two weeks of missing class especially early on is grounds for drop, I think, especially if you didn't provide evidence. Covid or not, you can't make that time up on your own. Why bother with the course then? Great.

This is the worse professor to take if you get sick. I had him back during freshman year, got COVID, and after the two weeks in quarantine were over I tried to join class again and got banned from attending in-person classes and was removed from the canvas for no reason even though i did all of the homework while sick. I don't recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: JDQ was one of my most memorable classes at Cal. English is my second language and I didn't have a strong background in writing but I still managed to pass with an A. 6 unit class def helped me in the long run. Loved how engaging his lectures were. Really made me think a lot with the required readings. Thanks for such a memorable class!

This class was honestly one of the most memorable during my time in college. Prof. JDQ's lectures made the readings come alive with color and his teaching gave me inspiration and a sense of freedom in my writing. If you want to hone your skills, enjoy thought provoking lectures, and laugh a lot along the way, I would recommend this course.

Work, but it's the course and it's required.Some aren't prepared for the workload and fall behind and fail the portfolio and then take it personally. If you do the work though and follow JDQ's suggestions, you won't just pass the portfolio, but you might end up writing something you'll actually value. Funny that 28 over the top and one bad apple.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Horrible instructor
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: JDQ is the goat. He may push you in uncomfortable ways but he knows what he's talking about. Trust the guy and you will pass. Not the easiest grader but not impossible by any means. “ you will get the grade you want”. He's awesome to engage with. Be comfortable and open/vulnerable and you will be rewarded. He's a funny prof too. You will enjoy clas

The course starts off hard and ends relatively easy. Though I will definitely take the professor again, wouldn't want to take this class again. Generally good, works pay off. He will make you pass the portfolio, even if you are very bad at writing. Also, note that you will write 5 papers instead of 4, which is the maximum allowed on portfolio (3-4)
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Prof. JDQ changed the way I write entirely. The course revolved around themes of real life, the future, and humanity, we explored various interesting & diverse materials which included short yet deep poems, novels, and a 2013 Oscar-winning film. His engaging prompts encouraged us to reflect deeply and express our personal thoughts and experiences.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He's a genuine, caring professor who wants to help you succeed not just in class, but beyond. His assignments were thought-provoking and often required insight into oneself, with JDQ underlining the sometimes blunt, harsh realities of life. Little did I know this class (which I only took as a requirement) would help me transition into college life.

As an ESL I used to only feel confident expressing myself and writing in my mother language. But prof. JDQ helped me to get more confident writing in English. As long as you put effort into writing you will be able to get an A!

You will write a lot (5 papers plus several response papers), and your writing skills will definitely improve as long as you keep on the right track. Professor De Quattro cares about everyone's performance, so don't hesitate to reach out to him about any of your concerns related to writing or reading. Easy A as long as you take this seriously.
Made writing class an entertaining and engaging class for my first semester. Taking this course would mean writing a lot but it'll genuinely help you grow as a writer. Would definitely recommend.

One of the best things that happened to me at Berkeley in my first year was to have Professor Joe De Quattro as my professor. As long as you follow his instructions and stay engaged in class, you will be just fine. My writing has improved so much, and I feel more confident in writing.

Number one thing about Prof. JDQ is he will help you as much as you are willing to put the effort in. I encourage you to email him because he will help you. Overall, I became more confident in my writing because of it.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: amazing professor! Stick through with it!
He is an incredible professor! Super entertaining and cares about each and every one of his students. Easily the best class I've taken at Berkeley so far. Would highly recommend it!

Super respondent to emails. Attendance is mandatory, but if you give him a heads up, he is very understanding. It's obvious he cares a lot about his students and their success. I highly recommend taking COLWRIT R1A with him. He makes class entertaining and engaging, and has never assigned us any busy work. He's super genuine and overall incredible!

Great professor he's, someone you can definitely joke with but take seriously at the same time. He makes the class very comfortable and shows that he cares about your writing. BEWARE of his emails he loves to spam to the point where you guys are texting. There's a total of 5 papers, you only have 2 weeks to write so attendance is mandatory.
Professor JDQ brings me really good experience in the course! He made me (someone who doesn't write before) become confident and interested in writing and thinking.

Professor De Quattro is genuinely the best writing professor. He cares about his students and their development as writers. He is communicative and always reachable outside class. Highly recommend this class if you lack confidence in writing because you will come out of his class and be comfortable/confident about college-level writing.

I think "simple" might be misleading. Prof. JDQ doesn't assign a lot of busy-work, and cuts through everything to get at the heart of your writing all to enable you to produce work that's sophisticated, complex, and, yes, simply clear and focused. Prof. likes to quote Pound: "fundamental accuracy of statement is the one sole morality of writing".
JDQ is a simple man in his academics. As long as he sees effort, you'll be good. Very few assignments and generally a very enjoyable class. Def recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This man is a godsend he single handedly made me care about writing again after years of just winging my writing assignments. My final portfolio was initially given a NP but he requested a reread while also including additional notes for them and I did eventually get the NP changed to a P. He will not let you fail if you truly care and put in work
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Prof JDQ is the best Professor ever. At first, I was intimidated by his sense of humor but later loved him for it. He may come off as uncaring, but trust me, he is one of the only professor's who truly cares about your development as a writer. As long as you put in the effort, you will get a good grade. As to accessibility, he responds ASAP. GL!

The best professor ever. Professor De Quattro gives very constructive feedbacks to his students. It is an easy A class, but you need to let him see your growth over time and that you actually care. Most importantly, don't be afraid to ask him for help, go to as many OH as possible and annoy him lol.

By far one of my favorite classes at Berkeley, he really takes the time to work with each student to better their skills as a writer. He cares very deeply about his students and wants them to succeed. There were 4-5 essays with an opportunity to fix the essay. Would highly recommend this class.
Prof is very funny and really cares about his students. He is all around great.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: A lot of fun
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor JDQ definitely cares about you in the fact that we wants you to pass the final portfolio. I initially went in feeling bad about my writing abilities but am more confident than ever now. I got C's and B's on most of my papers but passed with an A because of how hard I worked to revise and understand my mistakes. Weekly response, 4 papers
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I do not think Prof. JDQ is insensitive. In the opposite, I feel like he is the most caring professor I have had in Cal. He reads and responds emails quickly and patiently, and gives a lot of help for your essays. He also has a special sense of humor that makes a writing class fun and lively. I highly recommend this class.

He is very passionate and care about his students a lot. Despite he is a little bit insensitive about people's feeling, that is what's great about him; he is not afraid to say something offensive and that often results with sharp and humorous points about different things and most constructive advice that he can give to students.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Prof. JDQ is super fun and definitely makes going to class worthwhile. We had 4 big papers to write and weekly responses to do every week. It sounds like a lot but it completely doable. Try to sure you go to class every day if you can and participate, he likes people who speak up. Doesn't really have office hours but he responds through email fast
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious
