reviews.comment: He is super nice and kind. He is very funny. Stand up guy. He is a very good thinker. His readings were fun and easy and this is coming from a guy who hated reading his whole life. Very good feedback on papers. Only had 4, max 5 page papers in semester. Weekly 1 page free write reflections (sometimes prompted). He made me a better writer.
Made class very engaging by having us do group discussions, group presentations, and peer feedback. Very smart professor knows how to deliver his class materials. Was my favorite class.

Professor Quintero creates such a wonderful learning environment! He effectively shares information while encouraging lots of questions and discussions. The atmosphere in class is incredibly friendly and welcoming—I've built closer connections here than in most of my previous classes. Plus, he presents information in so many fun and different ways.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Weirdly off-putting and unhelpful towards his students, puts on a fake chill vibe but is completely mean behind closed doors. Don't take his class, you'll be draining your eyes from how much work he assigns. Doesn't actually know how to improve kids' writing, just has to prove something bc of his inexperience and his prejudices towards them.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Incredibly, unnecessarily rude. The first day of class, I came up to him afterwards and asked a very normal question (just if there were any writing resources posted for the class). He told me, word for word, "It's really *NOT* that hard, it's pretty straightforward. If you think you struggle then go to the writing center." Like?? What?? MEAN.

Amm is a lovely human being. He is passionate about his discipline, and very kind/understanding towards students. He can be a little boring in lecture but ultimately all papers are (mostly) straight-forward and related to them. The final is also fair, as long as you review carefully and ensure a basic understanding of topics you're good
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: love like a father or a mother

The content was interesting and engaging, but lectures could get long and somewhat confusing. Professor had very interesting things to say, but at times just lectured his opinion. The class had a few assignments throughout the semester and a large final (supposed to handwrite 10+ pages in 3 hours) worth 40% of the class grade.

Provided detailed lectures and had good GSI's to reinforce the learning. The final exam was five essays (hand written) with the rest of the grade coming from multiple papers and one essay throughout the semester. I would take this professor again but would suggest for him to make the final based on the computer.

Dr. Zhou is one of my favorite professors! His extreme clarity in lecture is super helpful for a memorization heavy class. In his unit, it isn't necessary to read the textbook, but important to attend lecture to know what to expect on his midterm exam (BIG part of grade). I did have to set out lots of time to study all the details, but it paid off.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Qiang Zhou was my favorite professor within the MCB 110 course. He was a real gem to take this course from and he was amazing at teaching us about one of the most difficult macromolecules to understand, RNA.

He is a very good lecturer, holds your attention through very complicated topics. Material is very experimental based. Same with his exams, experimental questions testing conceptual knowledge. Definitely one of my favorite professors at Cal. Take him if you have the chance, you'll learn a lot with him, without having to sacrifice grades.

Honestly, best professor I've had at Cal. Lectures were excellent and interesting. Exam was definitly difficult, but I thought it was a great exam. You had to think, but it was totally doable if you understood all his lectures. You need to know both details and concepts really well. I loved  MCB 110. Best class at Cal.
Very cool & funny professor in lecture but his tests are extremely difficult

Great guy with good intention, but fricken hard midterm (expect to be comforted by extremely average 40% and curve).  Takes time to explain everything, puts a lot of time into lectures and ppt slides, which are great for studying (or first read if you missed or slept through lecture)

He is a clear lecturer and the material is quite interesting. He's patient about answering questions in lecture and his slides are really useful. Didn't have to use the book. Personally, not enough practice problems because he only put up two practice exams, no homeworks. his midterm was long and tricky. the average was 77/150!
Really not that hard. Just go over slides. Conceptual learning.  Clear and no fuss teacher.

His exams from the previous years that were given for practice before the midterm were somewhat easy. Yet this year's exam was extremely difficult. Grueling horrible experience during this midterm.Some questions are extremely tricky.He focuses on very specific parts of his lectures.The hardest professor so far.

Friendly and funny professor.Yet AVOID HIM AT ALL COSTS!His exam is long and insane.Some of his questions are taken from nowhere.His midterm was the hardest exam I've ever had in my life.And I studied for it from A to Z, non-stop.Don't take chances,and wait until another professor teaches this course.Zhou's exam is a killer
He takes time to really explain his lectures. His test is quite manageable and also places strong emphasis on laboratory techniques.

Loud and clear lectures! One of the few profs to use powerpoint as a good thing - we had his exact slides in a reader with lots of space for taking notes. Good at fielding questions and good pace. One bad thing was no homework, quizzes, or past exams to study - not much idea on what to expect on the midterm, which was the whole grade of his section
He's hard to understand and often puts you to sleep because of it. His part of the final was easy, but the midterm was really hard

It's not often that Prof. Zhou teaches MCB 102. The course material was actually fairly simple, however, it was difficult to understand Zhou's lectures. For the longest time, I thought he was saying "writing numbers" instead of "writhing num

Although Prof Zhou is fairly clear during lecture, the information presented is overwhelming. His section should be an entire course on its own. This section was insane, but the professor is a nice guy.

He's nice, fairly funny, very helpful, but his test trumps all of that.  He focuses on small details with no partial credit.  The result is that if you don't have mastery of the subject you get nothing for that question.  He's nice but should be avoided.

Poema is really nice. I took Portuguese 50 (the introductory Portuguese class at Berkeley) with her a few years back. So long as you memorize the verb conjugations (use Quizlet for that), you will do fine. The three compositions you have to write are graded more or less generously.

Poema is a wonderful teacher who genuinely cares about her students. She has a way of explaining the material that makes a lot of sense and helps out anyone who might have any doubts. There are a lot of little assignments, but if you stay on top of things you should do just fine.
Poema really cares about her students and was a great instructor; although beware that there are a lot of little assignments you have to be on top of and it's a lot of self-learning.

Professor Eliot is one of the most awesome professors I have ever encountered. He explains everything clearly in his lectures and is super accessible whenever a student has a question to ask him. I have been to his office hours and we talked about some interesting stuff! Definitely a good professor to reach out to and Astron C13 is a great class!!!

Professor Quataert is passionate and knows everything he is teaching inside and out. He is approachable and kind during office hours, always appreciating a good talk. He takes questions throughout the entire lecture, which is helpful. He speaks slowly sometimes though, so watching course captures on 2x speed is a lifesaver. Exams are all lecture.

Professor Quataert does a fantastic job expressing complex scientific concepts in layman terms.  He's friendly during office hours, hw & exams are reasonable, and above all else this was a very compelling class about our origins!
Extremely engaging and knowledgeable about his subject as well as friendly during office hours - only wish he taught more lower division astronomy classes!

40% of the class grade is weekly HW, but it's graded super harshly. Even though it's supposed to be a non-majors class, he gets very technical and tackles some difficult concepts. The midterm was very difficult, and the class wasn't curved. The subject matter was very interesting though.
A great professor. He does a great job of making difficult and complex material comprehensible. I would highly recommend taking his courses if possible.

Amazing lecturer. Inspired me to go into Astrophysics. The class is very fair and well structured. Easily accessible. Very friendly and encouraging to students. The tests and homework are a bit hard but well worth it. Best professor I've ever had.
Amazing.  I have considered having his babies, but unfortunately, I am a man.

Definitely a good class.  His lectures are very clear and his homeworks/tests/lectures all correlate very well.  Class can be a bit time-consuming at times--to do well in this class you will have to know your stuff--there's no way around it.

Great professor. Elucidates everything. While some of the concepts seem basic, some are pretty difficult and he simplifies them greatly. Also very easy to talk to and always tries to answer every question. Though he does have a bad habit of saying "We'll get back to this next time", which is a little frustrating. Great overall
Simply amazing. Easy to talk to during fffice hours.  Explains things very clearly.  Makes an effort to help his students. Aslo, just a great person to be around
Great teacher - seems to always know the answers and makes really hard material seem much easier (though still hard) and extremely interesting

he's a good lecturer and knows what he's talking about, though as an astro major i found the subject matter somewhat boring. tough hw, fair tests. will help students but is awkward to talk with at times.

Amazing Professor.  Actually interesting lectures that I looked forward to. I honestly felt disappointed walking out of class. If you're a physics/math/cs/whatever take this class. It'll make you want to double in Astro.

Absolutely amazing professor! He and the GSI are perfect! I was choosing this course for fun, but finally fell in love with Southeast Asian Art. You can see he is passionate about this topic, and the lecture is so inspiring and interesting! GSI is also very nice, patient, and helpful! Five Star Highly recommended!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I have never taken an art history class so I was worried taking this class. This teacher is so good at explaining things, I would leave every lecture fully understanding the material. There's a good amount of writing and reading but nothing too difficult.

This prof is very chill and caring. His readings are inspirational and interesting to read. All the artworks that appeared on the exam were the ones that he already discussed in class, so pay attention, and you will be fine. This class also has the best GSI I've ever met; he's super helpful and cares a lot about the students.
Prof Ray was an engaging and enthusiastic lecturer. Cares about student opinions and perspectives, and has a good sense of humor.

Prof Ray is so sweet!!! He's genuinely a good person and hes so kind too. He would cancel lectures sometimes if we were tired. The material is also super interesting and he has a very intriguing post colonial lens of thinking about it. This was my first Berkeley humanities class and I rlly enjoyed it.

This class was awesome, highly recommend taking a class with Ray it is graded pretty nicely and you learn a lot of applicable stuff for any museum you visit or just any interaction with S/SE Asian culture. Be sure to go to class because attendance is mandatory and its easy to fall behind as nothing is recorded but everything is based on lecture!!!!
Great prof who is extremely passionate about the course. No need to pay extreme attention in lecture as long as you grasp the general ideas. Make sure you're good at writing before taking.

Overall a great professor. He's very kind and passionate about his teachings. However, since his classes are very lecture heavy and long, it's hard to stay focused and therefore connect his lectures back to the weekly responses. His lectures aren't recorded so if you do miss a lecture it's a ton of reading. But overall, a really amazing professor.

He was a great lecturer but the material wasn't the most captivating... so maybe that's why I found myself not that engaged. In terms of seminars, he was helpful and clear about what needed to get done. You have to do the reading or you won't understand what's happening at all. But its like 150 pages of reading every week which is brutal.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Ray is very chill, approachable, and passionate. His lectures are interesting, but can also feel long since the class is 3hrs. The assignments are cool, all art/experience-based, and as long as you connect it back to the themes, you can argue anything. He's very kind and often would shorten/cancel class if we were tired or had lots of work.

Professor Ray taught how to think about every day "givens" such as the ocean, animals, etc. in completely different perspectives. Lecture is long but enjoyable if you engage with the material - same with the readings: long but really interesting. Additionally, the assignments are very easy - you can almost yap about anything on the essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Sugata is an incredible lecturer who prompts some of the most thought provoking in class discussions in any undergrad course. Discussion section was a little underwhelming compared to lectures. Tests consist of timed essays that aren't difficult but are graded reasonably rigorously. Some readings are a little dry, others are phenomenal.

Professor Sugata taught in such a fun and inspiring way. Lectures can sometimes get boring and confusing, but the topics he touches upon are incredibly interesting, and you simply need to ask and he will keep trying to explain something to you until you understand. He's also super accommodating and understanding. I would really recommend!
very exciting class. he is a gem and I learnt so much. very kind professor
one of the most amazing classes at cal. im glad I took it and now I see ecology very differently

Lectures were pretty strong but sometimes very frenetic or difficult to follow. He likes to make connections to other historical or art historical periods which can sometime seem random or not relevant. I think I would have enjoyed this course more if he lectured more! He's kind, sweet, and funny. His research is super interesting too.

I took art and ecology with this professor and he was so incredibly thoughtful and passionate. I loved hearing his ideas and prospectives and was thoroughly engaged by the class assignments and readings! I highly recommend this course to anymore who is looking to explore and new perspectives and intersections of art and ecology!!

Sugata finds it difficult to structure and organize lectures in a clear manner, so do expect to put in a lot more work independently. Teaching style is very monotonous and lacks a depth of topic understanding, it feels like regurgitation of lecture slides. Overall not very conducive to a good learning environment.

I don't have a background in art history, took this for a breadth, & it was interesting and not super technical. The papers were straightforward, GSI and professor were both very clear & offered great feedback. Lectures are a little on the dense side, but they're manageable once you get used to it. He obviously cares about students & the material.
Fabulous class!
Amazing lecturer with great thoughts and willingness to share. I just love him.
Wonderful professor, great great great!!!!!
Great class! Opened new perspectives on ecology and art

Prof Ray is a very knowledgeable professor and his class brings art and science together . The assignments and papers are interesting and not like typical art history exams ( no slide ids!). His class was very important for me to understand the relation between art and climate change and should be taken by everyone interested in ecology.
Fantastic class
Interesting class with a lot of diverse perspectives. Readings are tough but overall fascinating lectures
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I took her for 173, and would not recommend at all. Lecture is mandatory and she is SO hard to follow. She puts her notes on the board before class starts, and then starts lecturing unclearly. For the amount of effort I try to put into this class, it makes no sense, and then she gives long HWs which you have to teach yourself how to do.
Best professor I have ever met!
bad teaching overall
such an awful teacher, nothing she says makes sense, teaches antiquated concepts in an antiquated style. avoid if you can !!!

While Professor Righter's lectures can be a little chaotic sometimes, she is the most caring professor I've had (she even introduces little games to keep students involved). She is a little old-school, but she makes sure every question is addressed and the course material is quite easy.

She makes sure you understand concepts as long as you reach out for help. 

However, besides she herself wearing a mask her course policies make it very covid unsafe. She does not do course capture even though the building website states the classroom has the functionality, and requires in person exams even though the university doesn't mandate it.
lectures are all over the place
Difficult homework. Very time consuming.

Righter is a very good lecturer, so keep up with her notes and make sure you understand them! She's friendly and very helpful when you ask questions. IEOR 172 starts out pretty manageable but towards the end of the semester gets very tricky to grasp. Exams aren't too bad, pretty straightforward, but require you to think deeper on some questions.

The work is very manageable, and she is super nice. Just talk to her outside of class! No ego, wants students to learn and succeed. Exams are very fair. While I am not the strongest student, I found probability very intuitive. She gives great examples. I wish I could have taken more classes with her...
very helpful, easily approachable, fair exams. RR is amazing. I loved her class.

Reasonable professor, but does not take much interest in teaching the class. Therefore it becomes a bit of a drag. She is not incredibly helpful... Material is manageable if you spend time outside of class.

A grad professor just started teaching undergrad students. Very helpful and available during office hours. Students got to create their own problems which, if she likes it, will be used for the finals.
GOAT. Trust. Not even remotely an environmental science major but still the most interesting class I have taken.

I loved Dr. Rhew. This class wasn't very hard, but a few of the concepts were tricky, and I felt like some of the exam questions were much harder than anything we had learned or extremely specific. Overall he is a great professor and super silly and I loved the class.

This Professor was very fun to watch and very easy to follow along. I could study for a midterm/ final with just the lecture slides, and there was only a few pretty manageable assignments in the class. He cracked jokes and was very passionate, I would recommend paying attention to the lectures and staying on top of things. It was a good class.

Rhew was such a great professor and really cared about what he was teaching. Grade determined by 5 homework assignments, discussion attendance, and midterms/final. Definitely don't underestimate the content because the exams are NOT common sense. Office hours are very helpful. Homework can lower your grade if you're not careful. Rhew is great tho!

I LOVED this class. I am an Econ major, but this was still one of the most transformational courses I've taken here. Robert Rhew is insanely cool. Such a fun person. So fun to talk to. The material was so interesting. Highly recommend this course, even if your major has nothing to do with the field.
Amazing professor just make sure to review notes every time after class and don't undermine those midterms. They are not common sense lol!!

Took his class in the semester with all the strikes. He was accommodating and tried his best to mark everything on time considering the GSIs did play a large part in the marking before the strike. 
A brilliant lecturer, he made class fun despite the size, and the lecture went by fast as he was engaging and funny.

Professor Rhew is an amazing lecturer who is not afraid to crack a joke or two to make the entire auditorium laugh during lectures. He is very friendly and approachable in and outside lecture and always willing to accommodate for any situation you may have.

I'm weak in the field of geography and I took this last year, but Professor Rhew made everything so enjoyable! The lectures were engaging and jokes to keep your attention. Includes labs, midterm, and final. This class is a great way of getting a taste of geography and seeing if it fits you. While I won't pursue geography, this class is great!

Professor Rhew was one of my favorites and was a very engaging and interesting lecturer. Attendance was not mandatory and the coursework was fairly light. I would definitely recommend this class, especially if Robert is teaching!

I've never had a professor more passionate about trying to inspire his students to be interested in the subjects he teaches. The majority of the lectures were interesting, and for the few boring ones, his perfectly timed dad jokes made them bearable. Took this class for a breadth, but for a moment he made me feel like I should pursue envi sci

Intelligent and silly. I thoroughly enjoyed attending Robert Rhew's class. He gives me total dad vibes but in all the best ways. Not terribly difficult at grading and he cares for his student's well-being. Very approachable too. All in all a great Berkeley Professor. 10/10 would take again. Thanks for a great semester Prof. Rhew.

Prof Rhew is the BEST. I can't stress this enough, his class was very easy as long as you participate. Ask questions, get engaged, and you'll get an easy A. More importantly, the class was fascinating, almost entirely teaching about climate change. It still holds up as my favorite class/lecturer. I would take all of Prof Rhew's classes if I could.

A fun professor with a dad-like sense of humor which is honestly the Best type of humor. Very intelligent and willing to re explain anything you need. Very knowledgable in his field. The definition of a quality Berkeley Professor.

If you're interesting in biogeochemistry this class will amaze you. Rob is brilliant and great at making lectures fun by engaging in activities, and not just talking for 1.5 hours straight. Some human geographers my semester struggled... but if you've taken HS chem you'll be fine. The assignments can be tricky, but everything is reasonable
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He made a lot of dad jokes which I didn't really find that funny. He wasn't that great of a professor either. I got a pretty good grade in this class but I mostly attribute that to my GSI. Study the slides and guides the GSIs provide for some exams.
Amazing prof! funny and makes class interesting. Weekly problem sets and 2 midterms, and a final. Would definitely recommend! Also, DON'T GET THE TEXTBOOK
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This guy is hilarious. His enthusiasm is infectious. I don't think the class is an easy A. I didn't miss a single lecture because they are quite information dense. He does ask questions about a single fact he might've mentioned one class. Attend class, take notes diligently and study hard for the tests and exams and you'll do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Rhew is one of the best professors I have ever had at Cal. I took the class as a breadth out of interest since I have never taken anything in this department before. I was intimidated about the workload and difficulty at first but Prof. Rhew made it all better because of his excellent teaching and engaging methods he uses in class.
Rhew's Top 10 Environmental class is incredible; he introduces material in an organized and fun way.  The readings are also amazing.  The homework is time consuming and graded hard.

Rob Rhew is a gift to mankind. Witty, dazzling, and hot as hell, he outshines his teaching counterpart. He'll help you if you need it, and if you do  the  classwork, it's pretty easy to get an A (He literally spells it out for you in his letter slides) Rob Rhew is something else. He is #basedgod
Easy class. Tries to keep the class engaged with "entertaining" lectures. Funny person; I would definitely recommend this professor
Easy and interesting class. A lot of personal opinion is required so as long as you have that, you are all set.

HATED HIM. absolutely awful professor. tests did not reflect lectures at all. worst class i've ever taken at cal. if you're not a science major, avoid this class at all costs. also, he is not funny at all.
Lectures were very entertaining, even if you had no interest in the subject.  Professor Rhew is very funny and very clear.
Extremely entertaining lectures (he certainly tries), lots of jokes both genuine and lame but always amusing. He really gets you interested, great lecturer.
Cute

Rhew is one of my most fav profs at Cal. He's funny & refreshingly enthusiastic! After the stressful lecs of other courses, his class is the only thing that cheers me up. He's an excellent lecturer.It is obvious how hard he tries to make his class fun. He is also very helpful in OH. He doesn't mind   spending extra time to help answer ur questions

He is funny, straightforward, and approachable. He is so nice, and loves helping students. However, he takes a long time going over easy material and he brushes over harder stuff which is on midterms. He lectures STRAIGHT out of the book, so just read it. Midterms are fairly tough you really have to know intricate book+lecture stuff for them.

He is great!! He loves to teach and he is a very funny lecturer. The material is not hard and the tests are very straight forward. The class is not demanding at all. Take it if you want Biology Breadth requirement!

He's is by far one of my favorite professors this semester.  In fact, he makes me like going to class! You can tell he really enjoys teaching and wants you to learn the material, employing all sorts of ways to convey the material.  He really has fun with class.
Very charismatic and clear lecturer, yet the material on his tests are out of the blue and difficult. Don't take this class... It will screw up your GPA.

Prof. Rhew is amazing.  Originally took this class and thought it'd be easy but I thought that it was pretty tough.  However, I LOVED it and think this should be a requirement to graduate- yep, I liked it that much even though it kicked my **s.  Tests are a little tough but you learn a ton.  Awesome stuff.
like everyone says, he's a nice guy & really knows what he's doing. fairly entertaining at times, too. but the level of difficulty of his exams are beyond the level of simplicity of his lectures.

First things first-- he's good looking, a great guy, and a funny guy. He's also extremly informed and knowledgeable. But damn, I find his lectures so-so. Many times, He just reads off the powerpoint word for word, resting on his charisma. Perhaps the material dictates such a teaching style. But still....i dunno....i did horrible on his tests...
This guy is charismatic and funny, but his tests are hard and tricky to study for. Don't take this class unless you are taking it pass/not pass or really into the subject.
He is pretty hard on tests.. no curve so that means you HAVE to take this class Seriously. Good luck, my advice: don't take it unless u have a DEEP DEEP interest or can stay up in lecture.

Rob was awesome! Great sense of humor, enthusiastic about the material and uses interesting analogies to make the concepts easier, very friendly and approachable to students... the class was very chemistry based, which I am not good at, but he has made the experience all the greater.
This prof is super awesome! I loved his jokes and I actually started to like geography. He hands out lecture notes which helps so much when studying for the tests.
By far one of the best teachers here. Great guy, great teacher...who else can make the atmosphere sound so interesting?

i dont' know about you, but this class is not as easy as i thought!!! prof. Rob is nice and all, but the materials are kinda heavy on the chemistry part(very heavily base on chem). exams are fair. very light on homeworks and lots of take-home exams :P

i didn't find this class to be as easy as everyone else did, but prof. rhew made the experience as enjoyable as possible. he has a great sense of humor and he really cares for his students. i would definitely consider taking more classes with him.
Great teacher. Very interesting, has a corny sense of humor, very enthusiastic about teaching. He likes to keep the class involved too, so it's nice.
No Comments
The class is fun and easy.

Not recommended. Professor Rao's teaching style was difficult to follow, and he did not feel supportive when students needed help progressing in the course. Students should be cautious and clearly understand all course policies, as academic integrity concerns are taken very seriously with impersonations.
Super hard exams. Not bad of a guy (quite funny outside of class), but his teaching style is terrible. Made exams super difficult compared to past sem. But overall, meh

I really appreciate Rao's emphasis on intuitive understanding of content and his approach to learning. Contrary to what others say, I thought the lectures were actually pretty useful in solidifying understanding on top of notes. Tests were hard, but grading was fair and TAs were quite responsive.

This class is all learn the material by yourself. Don't even try to understand his lecture, since he just read the slide without explanation and asking you "right?". Suggest learn the probability part from youtube.

Class went over tons of topics really fast which is the typical recipe for a highly challenging course, will require lots of diligence and huge variation in difficulty based on previous experience which is unfortunate, still can learn a lot and generally well designed, prof himself is OK but notes/discussions/hw are the key to learning
be aware he seems to be making exams significantly harder which is wild for an already infamous class

Professor Rao is a great and caring person who genuinely cares about his students. I think most people find his class hard because they do not read the lecture notes ahead of time, which is something he assumes all of his students do. If you read the notes ahead of time and try your best to understand them, then you will succeed in his class.

I don't get it why he makes the exam so many questions and no one can finish. Reading notes before attending classes does help but not too much and usually it takes hours to finish reading. His lectures are just reading out the slides with no explanation.

Worst professor on campus. Is condescending to students and unwilling to help. Lectures are redundant. The only way to pass this class is by watching videos of someone else's teaching. Avoid at all cost.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This professor can't teach. Although he's somewhat comedic, he makes the content harder to understand. So at the end of the day, you're just teaching yourself discrete mathematics.

Rao's teaching style can be hit or miss. Lectures are tough, but the material is manageable with the free textbook and helpful resources like unstuck study. Grit through the challenging assignments, and you'll learn a lot.

Please stay away if you can. He is demeaning toward students and tries to antagonize. 

He has actually falsified his identity in a bate and switch / catfish scheme to push students to admitting things that are not true. He also does not follow university teaching policy. Very scary, yells a lot, makes sexual comments about female students.
Come to lectures having read the notes beforehand, and his lectures will make a lot more sense.
bad teacher
Best professor I had at Berkeley.
Hard to understand

Entertaining lectures, but they're incomprehensible. No clear grading policies and no clear resources to learn. Pretty much just him yapping throughout class and expecting us to pick up something while he's putting no active effort into creating a good learning environment
Great guy but can't teach at all. I was much better off not coming to class.

The class would have survived without him. Lectures were beyond useless as he always told us to just watch DeNero's videos, which you will have to do anyways because he is a terrible lecturer. DeNero is the only reason this class is as organized as it is.

I think Rao is a great guy, but he just can't teach. His explanations are not intuitive and he reads off of slides while skimming through proofs. You will end up relying on discussions/OH/notes to learn the content. His vitamins often have typos, and his problem sets are very hard. Thankfully, his exams are heavily curved.

Professor Rao is an amazing human being first and foremost. Perhaps he may not be the best at lecturing, but whatever lack in that area he has, he makes up for in humaneness and ingenuity. Rao equipped me well to deal with the hurdles that many computer scientists will come to face in their careers as breakthrough artists of technology.

Apathetic but in a good way. Didn't want to teach the class so can't hold much against him. Discussion of programming as a religion is always interesting, and the way he talks about linked lists really calms my nerves. In a word: Overhated.

Started the first 4 lectures of cs170 without our knowledge. Made this the hardest start to a class ever and caused me 3 missed homeworks because I can't even understand the prerequesite knowledge he's "teaching". If you get him, watch 2022's lectures.

Funny guy but his lecturing is some of the worst I've ever seen. I can't understand a single thing this guy teaches in 1.5 hours, and a 20 minute youtube video will explain everything I needed. For cs70, he assumes you've read notes and understood them before coming to lecture, so he can recap (he doesn't help).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Wonderful guy, fun lecturer.
I do not know why he shows up for CS170 lectures and the lectures he was given are not good.
Very bad lectures
I don't like his style.
Bad overall
Homework hard af
Doesn't really care about students.
Weird class type
Just ok
Very funny jokes
Idk what to say
Wooooo
Denero's better

Prof. Rao leans heavily on personal anecdotes, especially about his daughter, rather than focusing on course material. Concerns arise about his depth of knowledge in the subject. Interactions with students often stray into personal matters, raising questions about maintaining a professional and ethical teacher-student relationship.

He doesn't care, and 70's design generally reflects that. The notes have a lot of gaps which means sitting for hours trying to figure out what's going on, when most of the material isn't that complicated = artificial difficulty.

Genuinely a good bloke. People joke about Rao but he's got a heart and he really does care. He went out of his way to make himself accessible to us students (he got us boba!). Rao doesn't lecture like a Youtuber, he lectures like a human. He treats us like humans. Sure he's got his flaws, but I wouldn't have preferred to take 61A with anyone else.

Slow with the tech and not efficient with time but he provides a strong way of thinking regarding programming

Woohoooo

Just gave the starting lecture for 170 and I genuinely could not understand what he was talking about or why. Reminded me of the time I took 70, it was painful. He is just a bad lecturer, cannot follow his thoughts at all. Just his lecture style made it difficult to learn and understand.

Lectures in this class felt redundant, serving as mere summaries for those who had already read the notes. The course seemed more like a do-it-yourself experience, where reading the notes several hundred times was required to fully understand the concepts.Extremely difficult exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: DON'T TAKE HIS CLASS! The professor uses resources and materials from a professor "John Denero". I have had bad experiences understanding his lectures and the example he used wasn't clear. He isn't horrible since he gives enthusiasm and energy to his lecture, but his lecture didn't help me prepare for CS assignments/tests.

I found that understanding the material in Professor Rao's class was challenging. It seemed that there were gaps in the explanations provided, and I believe a more thorough grasp of the subject matter would improve the overall learning experience for students. Constructive feedback and additional clarification could benefit the class.

CS70 with Professor Rao and Tal was a life-changing experience and deeply shifted my perspective on how I interact with difficult concepts. Rao lectures are concise and intuitive - he makes sure you see the forest for the trees. CS70 is transformative: me going from a 3-week-behind desperate student to enjoying proofs is thanks to Professor Rao.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment:
Rao is a great person and an incredible researcher. However, if you do not have math competition(I'm talking about a decent rank in AIME) experience, DO NOT take CS70 without understanding of discrete math. 
His lecturing was awful. The notes are massive amount of text. Rare resources. Literally no one goes to lec. EXTREMELY difficult exams. RUN
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He does not teach.

Spring 2023 here. Rao is an amazing lecturer, his jokes are hilarious and keep you engaged. The only people that find him bad or rate him terribly are people that don't understand his lectures, people that don't pay attention, don't read the notes, and don't know how to learn in general. I actually prefer him over Denero and Hug (both were great).

I took this class over the summer when Rao didnt teach it (it was taught by 3 students who actually knew how to teach and wanted us to succeed). I STRONGLY URGE & ENCOURAGE anyone to take this course during the summer without Rao. Even though it's a math class, the staff and instructors ensure that you understand the material and want you to pass.
Doesnt teach

During the Spring 2023 semester, Professor Rao's CS70 had a heavy workload that exceeded expectations. His lectures lacked engagement, mainly reading off slides, and he struggled to answer questions effectively. Exams were disproportionately difficult, testing topics barely covered. Overall, a disappointing learning experience.

I only went to the first 4 lectures or so and a few more online but I liked his teaching style. Also the exams were fun, loved doing the proofs. The midterm should've had more time because it was a race. The final was well paced. The >73% equals full credit for HW is the best policy bc HW is for practice, not to punish you for missing minor things.

Seemed like a chill dude. Lectured heavily off slides. Cracked jokes and didn't put in a ton of effort. Wasn't the best explainer and wasn't very engaging. Made concepts more challenging than they needed to be. Probably a nice person but was definitely phoning it in.
Excellent professor, wonderful lectures, jokes can vary, but gets the essence of the content across quite well.
You either love him or you hate him. I certainly loved his teaching style and his sense of humour.
Horrible lectures...he basically just reads slides off the screen and is quite boring. I'm glad he only taught discrete math instead of probability or I would suffer more.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Horrible, definitely need a tutor for this class. Worst professor Ive had.

Although Prof. Rao's lecture is fast-paced, I really like his teaching style. His lecture is so hard that you have to read notes multiple times. If you can understand ALL concepts in his lecture slide, you are able to solve most exam-level questions. Overall a very positive experience.

CS70 is a tough but Rao is horrendous (data: massive # poor reviews cf to other UCB CS70 profs)  - error laden slides / mumbles explanations / exams are heavily trick questions / hw impossible and encourages cheating. Worst aspect: uses the classic "you need to learn the material" to obfuscate his lack of motivation and clarity in teaching.
He has no idea how to present the content of the class. Horrible at teaching, ridiculous exams, and his TAs know nothing about the content. Worst professor in CS department

Prior to the class, a student told me, "don't waste your time going to Rao's lectures." Now, I can see why. His slides look like a bunch of random facts, and all he does is read them without any adequate explanation. Too bad for you if you aren't a math-cracked kid. Miserable but Indian gurus from YouTube will be your best friends for the semester.

I've never had a professor explain things more poorly than professor rao. Watching one 90 minute recording of his videos takes me well over 3 hours because he explains things so horribly and glosses over everything. I constantly find myself watching youtube videos to find proper explanations. At least he is funny.

CS70 was by far the most challenging class I've ever taken at Berkeley. The spring 2022 final was absolutely atrocious and significantly harder than previous years. Even with attending both discussions, both CSM sections, both lectures, and office hours 5 days a week spending 10-15 hours on homework per week, barely any of it helped for the final.

Pros: 
- Lenient and cool guy 
- Curved (everyone bombs the tests)

Cons: 
- class has very little support and it doesn't feel like there are resources for your success
- Homework's are extremely difficult
- Discussions are not recorded
- Solutions for tests are not clear
- Lectures are 100% useless and terrible
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Rao is legit one of the best professors at Cal. Nice guy, very accommodating, brilliant at explaining things. CS70 is a hard class but Rao really does right by it.
Hard class and content. Rao is caring tho. Bumped up my grade to the next bin because I was so close��. A pretty decent guy in my book.
This class was hard AF. Prof Rao's lectures and notes were useful for understanding the material.

Very nice person but lectures are fast and rely too much on (kinda confusing) slides. Lecture content similar to the notes. Read notes before coming to lecture. Accessible in OH and Piazza. Exams w/ many short answers & 50% averages. I enjoyed the short answer format because you don't have to come up with algorithms and whatnot unlike other profs.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: CS70 is the hardest class I have taken so far. Professor Rao's lectures are very confusing if you do not have a baseline understanding of the material, but are helpful if you do. Personally, they were the most useful to me after doing the discussions and homeworks. He is a funny and nice person, and I can personally imitate his woohoo quite well.

His lectures can be confusing, but that's because he explores difficult problems that you have to look back at and think about. I found the content of his lectures extremely interesting, although his presentation was a bit dry. Some of the homework questions were ridiculously hard, but most were a good level of challenging and interesting.
This class is ridiculously hard and has unclear grading policies. Homeworks are very long (i spent 10+ hours a week) meanwhile they won't even grade every question. Rao's lectures are not helpful
Very unclear lectures, not easy to follow on the already hard material

I was ROBBED of an A- when he refused to give me an A- when clearly, I am at the border of an A-. I wish he gave some compensation for the Zoom issues that happened during the exams. He refuses to give out the grading bins so that students can ensure that grades are calculated correctly and fairly. This class is the hardest one I have ever taken.

This man should not be allowed to be a Professor, he does not know how to teach. His "lectures" consist of quickly reading off badly formatted slides--completely lazy and useless. The exams are absurdly long, and riddled with typos and errors. Avoid this Professor if possible, because it's probably a much more rewarding class with someone else.

Fall 2020: Doable, but make sure you have a solid background in discrete math or a lot of time to devote/an easy schedule. Class is graded on a curve so your performance is based on your standard deviation from the class mean/z-score. I ended up spending 6+ hrs/week aside from lectures, but some people who got higher grades spent a lot more.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Exams and homework filled with typos, very vague grading policies. You knew how you were performing relative to the mean on exams, but he gave no estimate of where that put you grade-wise. Discussions were not recorded and varied heavily, so it was luck of the draw for the quality of discussion, as you could not watch others. Terrible course.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Not the best lecturer, but definitely one of the most caring and compassionate professors I've had at Cal. He was flexible with course policies. Notes are almost more important than the lectures, and exams are rather difficult though.

Professor Rao seems like a nice person, but personally, I had trouble with the pacing of the class. The course was really fast-paced for me, homework took 10+ hours each week, and exam averages were 50%. Lectures seem like a hit or miss for some people, but reading/understanding the class notes is crucial if you want to pass the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class started out not too bad, lectures aren't helpful but he was at least entertaining in a weird way. The homework was long, difficult, and often had typos/mistakes in the questions. On top of the difficult content, prof was unhelpful and vague, esp with logistical questions about grading or the class.

His lectures were extremely confusing, halfway through the class I gave up and just read the text on my own. He fails at reading the slides for a solid amount of lecture time. His grading policies are extremely unclear and the class seems extremely poorly ran. His only response is "master the material". Which isn't very helpful. Avoid at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: In my experience he's pretty unremarkable, not great but not awful either.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: if you take a class with him after reading these or talking to anyone who took a class with him, your loss of mental well-being and grades, as well as dislike for the subject is only your own fault
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Nice and caring guy, but reuses Sahai's infamous hw's or writes his own which are filled with typos and missing needed info to answer them (doesnt update pdf). Gives exams with reused true/false questions since hes lazy. Worst lecturer of all time (literally reads from the slides), the best advice I can give to anyone is avoid him at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: fall20 He may be knowledgable as a person, but a horrible lecturer. Not only that, but he's not willing to listen to students and to any inconvenience or unfair policies, his answer is "just master the subject." I suggest students to teach themselves all discrete math before taking him. I had to use youtube and other universities' notes to study.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Terrible professor who doesn't understand student issues. Non sympathetic and causes high levels of emotional distress. I strongly recommend you avoid this professor at all cost, for he isn't a good lecturer, nor does he provide any growth to your academic career.
The more he tries to explain something the more confusing it gets. Just read the textbook instead.
Best CS professor at Cal. Took both CS 70 and CS 170 with him. His lectures are very clear so that textbook is not needed. Exams are fair. Would probably take every course Rao teaches in the future!

Rao is likely the worse professor at UC Berkeley. I was expecting way more quality, especially since this Cal is regarded as one of the top institutions in computer science. He might be smart, but he does not know how to teach. Students seem to rely mostly on notes/textbook to survive. He relies on cheese jokes to gain some respect.
Horrible lecturer. Did not understand a thing. If you have the choice, avoid taking a class with Rao at Berkeley.
Very bad lecturer. Usually did not get anything out of lecture. He reads off of his 100+ slides at a rapid pace. However, I can tell that he cares about his students and want us to succeed.

Terrible Lecturer, amazing in office hours. You can read others' opinions on his lecturing, but the few times I did go to office hours - he's amazing. If you have him and are struggling, go to his office hours. He's great when he's not on the podium.

Very poor lecturer. You can tell he is trying and has read the literature, but the way he speaks and delivers material is disjointed and confusing. Also was not amazing at writing test questions. He usually did a pretty good job, but when he made mistakes or wrote poorly worded questions, he refused to allow other valid answers.
He is really bad at giving lectures. Really smart guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: A genuinely nice guy and you can tell he is a genius, but if you are not on his level don't expect to understand a single thing he explains. He is a horrible lecturer who doesn't know how to put what he knows into words, and assumes everyone knows everything. Honestly he should just focus on research and give up teaching.

I took CS70 over the summer, but the lecturers were quite bad so I watched Rao's webcasts on double speed to learn the material. His lectures were quite funny (terrible jokes but he's a cool guy so it was funny). They were a little scattered and fast for some students, but I really enjoyed them. Would def take a class with him in the future!

Good attitude, but painfully awkward jokes and awful at teaching. It's obvious that Rao gives lecture on the fly by literally reading every word off of the slides and getting lost during his own lectures. Teaching is his last priority, so if you take it with Rao don't even go to lecture and just read Sinho/Alvin's notes.

One of my favorite professors, because he genuinely cares about his students. I learned discrete math really deeply and it prepared me well for cs170. Really glad I got to take a class from someone that is brilliant but also compassionate

Nice guy, but lectures are sometimes unclear (he skips a few important steps in math proofs). So, you'll probably have to spend extra time reading the course notes. That being said, he is really nice and somewhat helpful during OH. Exams for this class are tough, but he ends up curving nicely. HW was tough, but 80%+full credit was nice.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Satish is pretty nice and approachable but his lectures are indeed really scattered. The curve is nice though

It is interesting how UC Berkeley has such accredited professors however they are clearly not known for their teaching experience. Professor Rao is a nice, caring and smart but notoriously bad teacher teaching very hard material. In a hard class like this precision in speech is important, which Professor Rao himself confesses to be horrible at.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I've taken both 70 and 270 with him and I've also TAed for him. He's really a sweetheart that deeply cares about his students and being fair. He's a little scatterbrained but ask him questions if you're unclear about something---you'll understand more and he'll slow down. Also, read the notes! (For 70)

Rao explains concepts very well and gives very good examples to strength understanding. Tests are hard but reasonable. Offers test-only option which relieves the stress of the course. Go to lecture, go to discussion, skim through homework, and do some practice exams, and you'll do well.

Rao was genuinely a good person. He was incredibly good at explaining concepts at office hours but his lectures were a little scattered. It was a must to read through the course notes and do a lot of practice just to get lecture to make sense to me. Overall he coherently explained the material (once it already made some sense) and he graded fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: The worst class I've ever taken at this school so far. Not that I don't find the topic interesting, but it's so hard to keep up when the lectures are so horrible. Rao is very knowledgeable of the content, but terrible at teaching it. I hate asking for help, so I never went to office hours, and I was confused the entire semester as a result.
Really great. Really caring.
Love him! Really good at explaining concepts. Has a unique lecturing style (as in makes a lot of stupid jokes) but that helped me not get bored. One of the best math/science professors there is.

Rao is SO CONFUSING in lecture!! He is all over the place and never coherently finishes any of his sentences when he talks. He just is just way too hard to follow. Concepts like these need clear instruction from the teacher!!

Rao's a nice guy, can be humorous & chill. He isn't the greatest instructor though. His lectures lack so much clarity. He has typos and makes mistakes while lecturing/explaining things - confusing. He's nice and willing to help if you go to his office hours though. But overall do not recommend for a course like this. You need a good clear teacher.
Satish is amazing, extremely helpful and devoted and has an awesome personality

This is a difficult course and Rao is not a good professor to teach it. He's scattered in his lectures, goes way too fast through the slides, and he assumes that you know various math concepts before starting the course. If you're comfortable with solving math proofs, you'll do well in this class. If not, take it with another professor if you can.

Rao is a poor lecturer - he can't seem to clearly explain things. He trails off easily and is extremely hard to follow in the first place. Basically, he is all over the place during his proofs and explanations, sometimes skipping essential details altogether. For a class that is so theory-heavy, it sucks a lot to have such a bad instructor.

A scatter-brained lecturer. He is smart but he seems to have a difficult time conveying his thought process and concepts to the class. He will jump around a lot during his math proofs. He will skip steps, goes too fast during critical proofs, or mentally compute/assume things without explaining to us. Class structure is very disorganized, chaotic.
Great instructor - makes me want to learn more theory. Infectious enthusiasm, and cool atitude. hard to follow but the material itself was pretty hard.
Great guy. Funny and help. Maybe a little confusing in lecture though
Great Prof. A little off in lecture but so helpful in office hours

Why this man was allowed to teach a class, I will never know. He had no idea what he was talking about (Harvey always corrected him), and attendance dropped dramatically once he started lecturing. He was completely useless and made the class much more confusing than it had to be.

He taught 61A with Brian Harvey, although it would have been better if he didn't in my opinion.  While I'm sure he's a good teacher in whatever subject he originally taught, he teach the 61A material effectively and when he taught I would have to go and watch Harvey's old web-casted lectures.
Wasn't very clear at the start of the year, but got better as the year went on. Was never very sure about the material he was teaching, which made lectures hard to understand.

Co-taught CS61A with Harvey, but I really wish Rao didn't. Many times he was confused about how something worked and Harvey (sitting in the class) would have to correct him. Very dull and boring lecturer in general, and I ended up watching Harvey's old lectures.
Not a particularly good lecturer. Seemed confused about how Scheme worked. Often corrected by Harvey. I would recommend webcasting Harvey's old lectures instead of attending lecture.
Lectures jumped all over the place.  He simply could not explain a proof clearly, which is a big problem in a proof-based course.
Brilliant Professor. Follows the textbook closely. Helpful in Office Hoursl

Of all my 4 lecturers this year, Rao is by far the most engaging. He integrates occasional jokes into his talking, to which many people seem to take well. Sometimes he fails to explain the connections a particular topic has, and other times he simply assumes we know too much, but overall great prof.

One of the best professors I've had at UC Berkeley. Lectures are engaging and strike a great balance between foundational practice problems and additional context. The grading policy is very fair, scoring above 90% on a midterm problem allows you to skip the corresponding section on the final. Lectures are also recorded and posted online.

Thermodynamics is intimidating. It is quite a lot of material to cover. But Prof. Schutzius takes a very sensible approach to this subject: as long as you keep up with textbook and office hours for example, you will do very well in the course. The course is also structured so that you have many opportunities to catch up. It's fast but a ton of fun!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: buddy had no idea what was going on, neither did I. Got an A, no complaints
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Schutzius is one of the best teachers ive had so far here at Cal. He is super passionate about thermo and is willing to go above and beyond to help students. study hard and Do well on the quizzes bc it can allow u to skip the final. always willing to make sure u understand material. Take him!

The professor teaches well, is passive-aggressive while being funny, and is very forgiving. I only wish he taught more, since he only covers like one or two sections of a chapter during lecture and the rest is self-study. The grading policy is student-friendly and is designed so that almost everyone passes. You have to go above and beyond to fail.

Schutzius is passionate about thermo, but his lectures don't cover the material. You need to learn the material on your own by reading the textbook and/or watching online videos, and then if you go to class, it's just to see him do some long practice problems. Midterms were fairly difficult but fair. The final was exceptionally difficult.

The class was taught with passion but lectures were hard to understand without reading the textbook first. He was doing mostly long practice problems in class and often losses people during the question. Homework was flexible but tests, especially the final, was really hard and also not very related to homework and lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Schutzius is a passionate professor who is great at answering questions. Lectures are mainly practice problems so most actual learning of the concept has to be done by the student reading the textbook outside of class. Tests are difficult and include problems not found in the textbook, so a true mastery of the material is required.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Passionate professor, clearly loves this topic. Lectures are hard to understand, but less of professor's fault and more because thermo is hard. For most people, success in this class will require some combination of discussions, office hours, and textbook. Very fair with exams, assignments, and extensions. Would absolutely take him again.

Schutzius is so passionate about thermo and cares a lot about making the class work for his students. Regardless, thermo is a difficult subject and his lectures were not the most helpful. I relied on discussion/office hours to understand the concepts and do the homework. One midterm and half of the final was take home.

Professor Tugal's biggest strengths as an instructor are that he is incredibly passionate about the content of the material he teaches and he respects his students' interests and curiosity. His lectures are incredibly engaging, and he encourages critical engagement of the texts and never disregards a student or their opinions. Take his classes.

Although attendance wasn't mandatory, lectures were definitely crucial for understanding. As a 5-unit course, readings were intensive and dense, kind of a lot, and hard to understand without guidance. Tugal didn't make people seem small, and it felt like he cared about people's perspectives/ideas. Enjoyed the class.

Lectures are not mandatory, but there were quizzes (~8). Discussion attendance was mandatory. Very passionate about sociology. slides were avail. discussion helped! quizzes were kinda easy/obvious (1 question only). would take again!

Professor Tugal was a great professor! Soc theory is very dense and hard to understand but he was able to provide real world examples that helped break things down or make it more applicable. Midterm and final were take home exams with prompts that were pretty straightforward. What was nice was it seemed like he cared.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I was intimated to take theory. I took both SOC 101 & SOC 102 with Tugal and it was the best decision. Although there is a lot of reading, he summarized the main arguments in lectures & he CARES about his students such as giving expanding reading responses or exams. GSI's were amazing and critical to understanding the material. Structured course.

Very non-partisan when teaching theorists, does a masterful job at pushing forward the concepts from each theorist, and is very passionate. His office hours are so helpful and the material, although difficult, is core to sociology. Be ready to read the works; he gives focus pages and guiding questions to make the reading bearable.

Cihan is an amazing professor who is knowledgeable in his field and caring/accommodating to his students. He made sure everyone was taken care of during the strike and for the rest of the year, he was very accessible and had clear requirements and announcements. His lectures are a bit dense and content heavy but he is a wise and funny lecturer.

He provides a very insightful view of different sociologists without showing much bias. The readings are very well articulated, and the lectures really open your eyes to what the readings are trying to say. Overall, one of the funniest, most intelligent, and most incredible sociology professors that must be taken! Office hours are fun!

He tries to make lectures fun and engaging and seems to be a very caring professor. I personally had very few interactions with him but from what I have seen he loves what he teaches and tries his best to explain concepts. Attendance is not mandatory but you will learn a lot from the lecture since some stuff he explains are not on the slides.

Lots of reading and some are dense but he does a good job of breaking it down. He really cares about his students (constant extensions, cancelled a paper and gave EC opportunity) and always encourages participation and questions. Great to talk to during OH or after class.

Given the structure of the class, I would take him again knowing what I'm in for. He does really care about his students and is very eager to answer any questions. Lots of reading though and some were really complicated.

If you are a student from a marginalized background, Tugal will not be very understanding and he can be very condescending. His lecture slides are very dry and unhelpful for your essays so it's best if you go. His essay prompts were okay but you wish he would make the class more enjoyable especially with such heavy readings.

Attendance for lecture not really mandatory but he explains everything during it, which helps cause his slides don't really make sense if you're copying word for word. Discussion is a must and extremely helpful. He practically gives you the answer for the papers and you just need to find quotes. Readings can be skimmed
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Cihan seems like a nice person but is not a good teacher. His lectures are incredibly confusing and disorganized and the prompts/expectations for the midterm essays are unclear. Would not take again. I
currently taking the class 102, and while he is very nice and funny, the lecture is very confusing and disorganized. Can't keep up . This was a popular complaint in our sections
Lectures are long and nonsensical. He has no organization and it's nearly impossible to follow along. You will not have fun. Sorry

hmm, took 102 last year and while interesting, the professor i dont think does a good job making it easy to understand...a lot of papers too on top of that... hardest class i have taken; maybe he has improved, hopefully for the future students. The GSIs, no complain. Very nice and helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Attendance is not mandatory but if you attend lecture and do the reading you will do well. Tugal is one of the best and most knowledgable professors I had. I took 140 with him as well. Go to office hours, do the reading, ask question, and go to lecture and you will learn so much.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: You really need to stay on top of the readings, ask questions, attend section, and go to office hours if you want to make the most of this class. If you do all the above, you'll learn a lot, leave with new perspectives, and an appreciation for a brilliant professor. but yeah, it's harder than other soc classes
Everything in this class confused me! There is so much reading and he expects you to know your history. Hes a great professor, however, I dont recommend taking this class if youre not into reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Leave class feeling energised and fresh from new insight. Learn a lot if you invest your resources into this course. Just a super nice guy to have a talk with after lectures as well.
He take us as phD students majoring in Russia Study or Middle East Study. Indeed, he is knowledgeable, but so whatif you cannot get what he's talking?
If you love sociology Tugal is the guy. He's passionate and informed
Poorly organized lecture with boring and tedious style. The load of obscure readings would crash your aspiration. In short, hardly learn anything for the whole semester.

This was a way harder class than I had expected (and we're not even halfway through yet!). I wouldn't recommend taking this class with Professor Tugal if you don't have a lot of prior knowledge on historical social revolutions. Heavy readings and lectures, but not necessarily all helpful or substantive at time. Considering taking it p/np.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This class was much harder than it should've been because of a lot of disorganization. Concepts were never fully explained or clarified and I even found a lot of disconnect between lectures and the readings because he taught off the assumption that we already knew material from other classes.

This professor is so disorganized. I wish I had dropped the class when I had the chance like sooo many others did. The readings are very difficult and he has a terrible way of explaining things in lecture, and his PowerPoints are pointless. Hes a nice guy I assume but I wouldnt take another class with him

Class was structured very poorly at first. Did not have a good sense of the theorists until the first midterm. He changed it up and I did learn a lot - mostly because of a good GSI. Your writing will get fine-tuned, readings are long and hard often, and lecture is confusing. Getting a B+ or A- isn't too bad but a solid A is real work
Hardly learnt anything...

Not only did I learn so much Chinese from her that surprisingly stuck with me years later, but I also learned so much that I found helped me in my future teaching career. Super engaging and has a way of making everything stick in your memory. One of my best professors.
Tsai Laoshi was a very intense teacher, and we really flew through the course, but I felt progress nearly every day.  She was well respected and is extremely approachable about anything at all.

reviews.comment: Tsai Lao Shi is one of the best Chinese teachers I've had. She's extremely passionate about teaching and it shows every day with her enthusiastic energy. There's a fair amount of work that has to be put in her class, but if you put in the effort, she has no problem helping.

She is the best professor I've had here. I've never once been bored in her class. She is an incredibly effective lecturer. Tsai Lao Shi is the best teacher I've ever had in my life. Very passionate, very helpful. Never had a bad day with Tsai laoshi. Awesome! Wish I could have more classes with this amazing teacher. Xie xie ni Tsai laoshi.

His lectures were super engaging and organized, and I felt like they really improved my understanding of the course material. reviews.comment: The basis for much of what we were learning was not provided. A lot of photos on the slides and not nearly enough text, making it difficult to go back and study at times unless you write down a lot.

Dr.Doris was the most inquisitive professor I have ever had. She always has lots of genuine questions for the guest lecturers and students. Took mcb65 (Film, Philosophy, and Neuroscience) with her. Organized to be an enjoyable class taken for interest so it was low on workload. Professor Tsao was very personable, passionate, clearly brilliant, and brought in incfedible guest lecturers. One of my favorite classes and professors over my 4 years at Berkeley.

Amazing professor who cares about what he is teaching, he will go on tangents at times but it adds to the class and makes it better lowkey.

reviews.comment: Brilliant man! So caring and passionate. Often went on tangents, but they were fascinating and thrilling. Much more of a seminar than a lecture-heavy class, encourages participation. Really interesting reading list. Two papers, take home midterm and final. Spends lots of time grading but gives incredibly thorough feedback. Highly highly recommend!

This was one of m favorite classes I've taken so far. The class relied heavy on participation. He always made every comment feel like it brought something to the conversation. He often would go on tangents, but it was filled with important information and other context relating to the readings. He was a great professor and highly recommend!

This was by far my favorite class at UC Berkeley. We covered some authors that I would have never read if it wasn't in this course. Edward encourages everyone to participate (more a seminar than a lecture) and always gives brilliant feedback. The movies/books/ songs/secondary readings are really interesting; I was amazed by the sources chosen!

Genuinely one of the top two professors I have ever had at Berkeley. She da goat of ochem, a lot of work but if you do it right u acc learn a lot and she goes above and beyond to teach why reactions occur a certain way so you come out smarter. I didn't really like the way she lectures. I feel like she doesn't really explain what's going on conceptually and instead just tells you how to do it. She gives an insane amount of homework, which sucks, but her grading policies are pretty forgiving.

Her lectures were the most structured ones I've ever seen, and all the work that is assigned is very helpful, even though it sucks. She's intense but she gets the job done well if you keep up. Yeah you really have to keep up.

reviews.comment: I have never had a professor go out of their way to keep a student borderline before. reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: In my experience in 3A, Dr. Robak was a great lecturer who covered a massive amount of topics in the semester very effectively. went into this course scared and came out knowledgable thanks to dr robak's amazing and clear lectures. lectures use lecture notes that are provided beforehand and are followed up by post lecture worksheets. problem sets and practice tests essential to succeed. prob my favorite professor at cal!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: One of my favorite professors so far. reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: If you truly practice and make use of her office hours (she's super patient) and problem sets, you'll gain a lot from this class. If you put in the work, you'll see results. Robak is a fair professor who gives out extra credit when the class average is too low. Class is super doable if you do the worksheets and problem sets. Definitely not as intimidating as people say. Policy to skip final is super nice.

reviews.comment: Dr Robak has a generous grading scheme (many skip the final), so study past exams, homework, etc., and you're cruising at the end of the semester. My only critique is that she usually didn't finish the entire lecture she had planned, and, in turn, worksheets were tough.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: You get what you give from Robak. Make sure you study the previous week's material for the quizzes. Do problem sets for especially difficult material.

Prof. Robak is amazing, and I wish that more teachers were as forgiving and helpful as she is. She gives a lot of work but you only have to do about 70% of it for an A. Definitely recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

AMAZING prof.

Most of the class revolves around mechanisms, similar to the latter half of the Chem 3A class she teaches. Allows cheatsheets during exams which can help a lot. Do well on the midterms and you don't have to take the final. Pretty lenient grading policy.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Robak is truly great at explaining and breaking down concepts, personally I'm not the best test-taker so it was hard in this class but I honestly feel surprised that I did really well in her 3A/3B series. Ochem is a tough weeder course and it will be rough, but for fellow pre-meds anything above a B is solid, so take it easy. Good luck!

Chem 3A is a hard class, but I didn't realize until after how well organized Professor Robak is (especially the lectures).  The GSIs are amazing and there are ones on the side during lectures to answer any questions you have.  All of the office hours were very helpful  Unfortunately I was a few points away from an A- and they would not round up.

Her 3a/3b series was genuinely my favorite class ever. As long as you do the practice, there's no way you fail. Her grade bins are generous, exams are very fair (similar to practice), and she's so caring about students in general. reviews.comment: I honestly was scared to take Robak because of the bad reviews. After taking her class for a year, there's no one I'd rather take OChem with. I struggled with 3A as it was completely new, but 3B with Robak was very interesting. Go to those post-lecture OFFICE HOURS even if you feel lazy. You will thank yourself so much during exams. She offers extra credit for the midterms, which helps a lot. The GSIs are all very nice and helpful. I am gonna miss this class!!!

I had Robak for the 3 series and she was great. Going to lecture matters for participation and learning. She's put in the time to make the course thorough, and all the resources you need are there. Tests are very similar to post-lecture and optional problem sets, so do those and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

I have no idea why ppl dislike her. As long as you put in the effort you will be completely fine. She gives a lot of EC, drops an exam grade (including the final), and lets you use notes on exams!!

Robak is an amazing and caring lecturer. Ochem is a hard course. She makes this class extremely understandable and enjoyable. Her chem 3 series is genuinely one of my favorite classes at berkeley. As long as you do the work (go to office hours!!) it is pretty much certain you can succeed. ochem is hard no matter who you take it with, but her grade bins are pretty generous and there's even extra credit opportunities on top of that that are worth so many pts that they can bump you up almost a letter grade. she makes the class interesting and the material is organized in a good way for long term understanding!
