Feel like Robak gets a lot of hate, but its unfounded. Ochem is a tough subject no matter who is teaching it. You have to stay on top of coursework. reviews.comment: very uncaring about students and assigns more work than is possible for students to successfully complete

reviews.comment: Workload is like 5 unit class. I got 70%-80% on all quizzes, skipped the final, and still got an A. Do post lectures at OH. The GSIs are rly helpful! She's a hard but very fair professor. She grades very fairly with leeway to get points for every questions and has a lot of extra credit assignments to boost up points. It is extremely doable to get an A in her class if you keep up with the lectures, she has pre-lec and post-lec assignments so utilize those to make sure you understand everything.

Although she has tough weekly quizzes in lecture, the way her course and grading criteria is set up makes it so that you can rebound low quiz scores with a better midterm score. Lectures cover much of what you need to know and there is plenty of resources online and in-person. If you do well enough on the midterms you don't have to take the final.

Professor Robak at times can be hard to comprehend in lectures, but you really have to work hard and spend a majority dedicating 15 hours+ to really get the grade you want. I would say there are some curveballs, and it does get better but really it is more or less up to you to figure out the material on your own.
She is a good teacher if you put in the work. No room for slacking off, but generally not difficult if you stay caught up.

This professor has terrible communication skills and lacks empathy or understanding for her students. Professor Robak is one of those professors that does have her perks, you truly have to live and breath Ochem. Grading is intensely harsh!!

The most pleasurable experience in OChem if that is possible. Take the course with Robak if you can.

reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Amazing professor who really cares about her students' success. Plenty of opportunities to gain points and if you have enough after both midterms, you don't have to take the final! Do the post lectures and problem sets, they're so helpful! She made learning ochem so enjoyable and I can't wait to have her for Chem 3B next semester!

Mary Robak is a great lecturer and is pretty funny sometimes. You'll do well in her class if you do her problem sets and attend lectures. She is pretty good and giving extra credit assignments. Would take again! (Just don't look at someone else quiz during the exam or might give you a moment from Matilda where the teacher screams).

Very well structured class. She provides you with so much practice and extra credit, you just need to make sure to do everything that she gives you. Don't fall behind you won't be able to catch up. Love her!!

Dr. Robak is a fantastic ochem professor. She is super considerate of her students and gives out lots of extra credit. Although there is a lot of work, it's all extremely beneficial for succeeding in class, and if you hit the point cap none of it is required anymore. All tests/quizzes draw from assignment material. A very fair prof overall.

I always dreaded the thought of taking organic chemistry but Dr. Robak made this class so amazing that it's my favorite class this semester. Although her quizzes and tests are hard, she gives a LOT of extra credit and makes sure you are prepared (she gives a lot of practice exams and other materials).

Robak cared a lot about the students success. The exams were hard and so were the weekly quizzes. She ended up giving a lot of extra credit opportunities because of this. Attendance not mandatory (except for quizzes). She posts lectures.

Don't take this professor! All the exams she gave were way too hard for us and some of the concepts on the exam were not being taught at all! She does not give partial credit either! She doesn't explain the concepts clearly and is always overloading us with assignments like pre-lecture, post-lecture, and problem sets before and after the lecture.

She expects us to master the concepts right after the lecture with so many assignments due after it. It's easy to fall behind if you're taking other hard STEM classes. The only way to do well in this class is by dedicating all your time to it.

This class is too much work for only being three units. So many things are due both before and after the lecture, so it's easy to fall behind if you're not dedicating a majority of your time to this class. The bins seem a bit unreasonable as well because of capped points and how impossible it may seem to even get a C in the class.

Robak is an okay professor, but by far isn't the best. It can be hard to keep up with the workload if you're taking other technicals, so make sure you balance your class schedule if you decide to take 3A with Robak. You really have to live, love, and breathe Chem 3A if you want to pass in this class.

Dr. Robak is hands-down the best professor at Cal. All of the homework are great and I learned so much from them. Dr. Robak is extremely caring and especially cares about her students. She gives out a lot of opportunities for students to succeed in class, including extra credit opportunities and such. 

Definitely recommend her class.

If you take organic chemistry with anyone, try to take it with her (or Marsden) if at all possible. The lectures are relatively straightforward and exams reflect the lecture content pretty well. Her class also does a good job at preparing you for mcb102 later on.

The most important thing I have to say regarding this class is that if you can take it with another professor, I would try it. Maybe even take it at a community college. Harsh grader. Inexplicable amount of things due each Wednesday. Lecture is heavy. Go to office hours right after lecture.

This lecture and homework are extremely heavy. Avoid this professor if you can, trust me! No curve for her class, too much homework. She even scheduled review session on Saturday... Not worth it all at!

I am taking Chen 3A this semester, the lecture is really heavy. 49 assignments due in 7 weeks ( not include the 3AL assignments). I didn't have any mental issues before this class, and I feel like I need to go to counseling now. All this homework writing is driving me crazy. Avoid this professor!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

Avoid this professor if you can. Not worth it. So nitpicky on every assignment, expectations for students are unreasonable in terms of learning the material and so many assignments every week, can be easy to fall behind. Lectures aren't engaging and are hard to follow as she uses incoherent and hard to follow sentences.

Whoever said Robak was a good professor is lying to you. This class is already so incredibly hard and her lectures are barely helpful. It's like she's mumbling to herself and her sentences aren't even complete and don't make any sense. I recommend looking into outside resources if you have to take 3A with her.

I love prof Robak. Best professor I've had at berk so far. Makes ochem understandable and knows how to teach. She made 3B arguably harder than 3A, but I thoroughly enjoyed both semesters. You can drop one of the three exams, weekly quizzes with drops, lots of homework. Problem sets are crucial for grasping concepts. Cannot recommend her enough

I was shocked by how dry this class was at first, but eventually it turned out to be extremely rewarding! Dr. Robak really pushes you to UNDERSTAND ochem instead of just memorizing it! Very clear and rigorous. A must-take course if you love science/theory, but would be quite tough if you're just trying to pass it for a major.

In the pool of ochem professors, we were lucky enough to have her for both Chem 3A and 3B. Robak is the reason why I don't understand how everyone says organic chemistry is the worst class in your college career. I will miss her and mechanisms

I love maryann. She has taken a beast of a class and made it enjoyable. She has detailed problem sets that actually ensure you master the material, she is always available for help/to answer questions, she understands how frustrating and scary this class is and just genuinely wants her students to do well. I am so sad to leave her. Take her class.

A great professor, and one of the best for the lower division science prereqs. Lectures were so easy to follow and she offers so many opportunities to improve your grade (extra credit on exams). She is super helpful and accommodating to students as well. HIGHLY recommend Chem 3A and 3B with Robak - she makes ochem not as miserable.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Robak was super clutch this semester! Very fair with extra credit/grading rubric depending on class performance on exams, does things in her students' best interest (such as cancelling lecture to give students more time to study for the midterm, might not happen every year tho). Lots of homework but doing them helps a lot with quizzes. Very caring.

very accessible outside of class (always answers students questions on Ed) and she genuinely cares about her students. lots of homework and quizzes but as long as you put in the work, this course is much more doable than other ochem classes + she doesn't limit the amount of As she gives which is nice

Explain concepts concisely and explicitly. Really help us understand the connections between different concepts, and chem makes a lot more sense in this way. There are a lot of homework, and in order to do well, you have to take care of that since homework really helps you practice. Also, there will be a quiz each week, so better be prepared
reviews.rating_tags: Inspirational--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Lovely person, insane amt of work. Eat sleep ad breathe this class

Dr. Robak is an amazing professor. The class isn't curved, there is a point system. She provides lots of recourses in order for students to succeed. Going to GSI office hours is really helpful. She also responds on EdDisccusion (Q and A system) really quick so you can always get clarifications for your work. Definitely take her class!

You have to respect Dr. Robak! She values her students' success a LOT. Yes, her tests are hard. She doesn't really do partial credit the way other profs do. But it's CHEM 3A! It's hard. She adjusted her teaching to make up for GSI absence (on strike)--super respectable. Lots of problem sets. Can drop your final if you did well on the others.

I really enjoyed the lecture format because she provides downloadable templates for use to take notes on so we don't constantly have to draw structures and whatnot. She was very understanding and helpful when students had questions in class. Make sure to practice and do problem sets/practice exams to be successful, but be prepared for a lot of work
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Taking Ochem with Dr. Robak is one of the best things that happened to me (by chance). She is helpful, patient, understanding, and truly thoughtful. She is quite good at explaining difficult concepts, which made ochem so much more enjoyable. I felt very accomplished after the course ended. Get ready for a lot of homework if you want to do well.

Professor Robak was a dream! She is very accommodating and really wants you to understand the material. Lectures were fast at times, but there is a lot of content to learn. She gives plenty of practice problems (DO THEM), and her quizzes and exams were very fair (no curveballs). Make sure you understand the psets, and you will be fine. loved her :)

Dr. Robak is AMAZING at organizing her CHEM 3A class. Although her lectures were hard to follow, she made up for it by providing more than enough resources to fully understand the hard concepts in organic chemistry. Also, she responds within 20-30 minutes for edstem posts and emails during working hours. AMAZING experience with her!

Dr. Robak is super accommodating, generous, caring, and fair (cut out some content, gave ec, allowed drops). Organic chemistry is a difficult class, but if you watch her lectures and solve/understand her problem sets (which prepares you perfectly well for her weekly quizzes and exams), you will be able to do just fine.

If you have to take Ochem, DEFINITELY take it with Professor Robak. She is caring and incredibly down to earth; you can tell she wants her students to succeed, and the entire coursework is clearly designed with that goal in mind. She has lots of resources available for you, so you will basically never be lost as long as you make use of them.

Lecture heavy but no Ochem class is ever easy. A good professor makes a huge huge difference in your quality of learning. She made me actually like chemistry- coming from someone who swore off chemistry.
This woman is my savior. She actually wants her students to pass ochem and not be miserable like every other stem professor. SUCH A G but content is hard tho of course.

Professor Robak was amazing and incredibly caring. Organic chemistry will always be hard but she made it as simple as she could. She provided lots of extra credit and grading was fair and clear. If taking ochem I would definitely choose her!

Ochem is a hard class no matter which professor you take it with, but I liked Robak's style of lectures and the way she explained things. I also appreciated her grading scheme with the opportunity to drop your lowest test score (so the final can only raise your grade if you choose to take it).

OChem is always a considerable time commitment, but Dr. Robak really provided us with all the materials you need to be successful in her class. Her lectures and practice materials were highly organized in both Ochems that I took with her which I really appreciated.

Dr. Robak is a solid teacher and very reasonable with all her tests (no curveballs). She also gave a ton of extra credit throughout the semester to push you into the next grade bin. Overall, yes, the material may be hard but you just have to do all the psets and you will do just fine. She's also really organized and fast on Piazza.

Dr. Robak is literally the reason I changed my MCB specialization to Biochemistry. I struggled really hard in Chem 3A (online course), but when I came into 3B this semester in-person, suddenly the content made complete sense! Dr. Robak goes very in-depth in her lectures and is *extremely* helpful in office hours. Plus, she's very nice!

OChem is extremely difficult for most people no matter the professor, but Robak is SO organized and clear with her lectures and policies. She gives lots of access to practice problems and her OH are great. One of the best professors at Berkeley and 100% best OChem professor you will ever have. Take 3A in the Fall and 3B Spring!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The most organized professor at Cal!! Clear standards and gives extra credit opportunities. She is very fair and accessible through piazza (responds relatively fast). This class is intense and requires lots of studying. But if you do the problem sets and go to review sessions, you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Took both 3A and 3B. Contrary to other reviews, she gives plentiful extra credit, is generous with partial credit on exams, and is a very energetic and interactive lecturer in-person. Does not curve! No textbook required and the only practice required is problem sets she gives, which are similar in difficulty to exams. Tough class, fair professor.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: OChem is hard! You have to keep up every class. Do not fall behind or it will destroy you. Robak explains concepts very well and tells you how to solve problems beyond just concepts. Also, she is very willing to give help and responsive on Piazza. She gives us tons of practice, which are not mandantory but very useful!
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Pros: lots of resources, one midterm replaced by final score, extra credit Cons: sounds like she is reading from a textbook in recorded lectures, requires HUGE amount of self-directed study (going to GSI review sessions is practically required to understand the material), giant time commitment TALK TO SOMEONE WHO HAS TAKEN THE CLASS FOR STRATEGIES
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Organic chemistry is a hard subject alone and requires a lot of devotion in time. Professor Robak's handouts are extremely helpful in understanding course content, and her lectures are explicit in showing novel reactions. She is a very tough grader and does not do bin shifts, but her extra credit options are generous enough.

OChem is extremely difficult, but I really thought Robak had her student's backs - she gave extra credit and was super accessible for questions. To do well in this class: do the problem sets, go to office hours, and do all the EC she gives. She won't change her grading bins at the end of the semester! I'm honestly excited for 3B with her!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Maryann did her best to teach. Her lectures are 3 out of 5 - monotone, somewhat engaging, explains semi-clearly. The class is test heavy with 20% grade coming from hw worksheets. She gives really long problem sets you can practice with. MAKE SURE TO DO THEM and go to worksheet sessions held by GSI, as well as asking ANY questions. NEED TO STUDY!!!!

O-chem will always be a hard class. Robak made learning it so much easier. Grade is dependent on mainly test scores with a point system & no curves. Does give out almost a full bin of EC. My GSI's made the class 100x better. Doesnt give out any averages but all the test are doable & doesnt have any curveballs. Requires outside work like all classes
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Pros-Some extra credit, some HW drops, final clobber OR drop option, spent extra time reviewing material our class tested poorly on, gives review resources Cons-Online lectures werent engaging, seemed thrown together from different semesters, tough exams, no partial credit, no curves, attending GSI sessions is kind of mandatory Misc-No textbook

TBH, anyone who says this is "too much work" or that Robak wasn't caring and had an "average grade" is all cap. 3A is a class that you have to work your ass off in no matter the professor and offered a fair amount of EC which was further adjusted. She cares but I found the recorded lectures to be boring. Otherwise, the resources are there to excel

the only class i have failed my entire life. she seems kind but in order to succeed in this class, you have to do countless hours of outside work (problem sets, worksheets, 1.5hr long lectures) and its impossible to have time and only focus on this class. im so sad.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: While I did not have a class with Robak, my roommate did and I witnessed their suffering daily. Robak offers miniscule extra credit that bumps up the 23% average grade in her uncurved class to 25%. Through their interactions with Robak, students are not encouraged to seek the professor's assistance

Had her for the Chem 3 series during a pandemic, online, and she wasnt super accommodating. Her exams were very hard, and she doesnt curve either. Reused old lecture videos that looked like they were from the 70s. Maybe shes better in person. She does let you submit exams later if you have tech difficulties and we appreciated her for it!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She is a great teacher and really passionate about ochem! 3B with Robak is a bit tough because there is no curve, hardly any bin shifts, and ochem is just naturally difficult. The best way I prepared for exams was doing worksheets without immediately looking at the answer key (test yourself!). She really accommodated students more than most profs.
Pretty terrible prof. Reused old lectures and not accommodating to Covid

GO TO OFFICE HOURS!! She only did asynch this semester so OH cannot be understated if you want to really understand and do well. She teaches tricks and gives advice that drive home lessons. The class's content is naturally hard but she gives LOADS of practice problems. Pro tip: write down all the mechanisms before a midterm & be familiar w/ them

Ridiculous amount of HW that it's practically impossible to finish. Reused previous lectures which were shoddy in quality. Exams were tough as heck. Not very accommodating during the pandemic and was not very lenient with the exam grading. OChem is tough and if you can I would steer clear of her if I could. It it very brutal.

HORRIBLE! If you aren't strong in chem, don't expect her to help you. Doesn't do curves for a class notoriously hard as ochem?? Reuses old lectures and doesn't even put effort into the class. You basically teach yourself. Doesn't reply to emails and is just rude all the time.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Robak really cares about her students and would answer questions in great length and detail on Piazza. She's very kind. Although I personally don't like the module video format of classes, she proved to us that she didn't do it because she's lazy (she actually puts a lot of work into teaching) Also, she gives out a LOT of extra credit.

Clear expectations for what you have to know, expect 2nd midterm to be harder than all other exams in the class. Good professor all around, not amazingly engaging but you can learn the material well with not too much effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Robak was kind and caring during the pandemic, but I did put in most of the effort myself (extra readings and problems) to get an A in the course. As long as you use all of the materials she gives before exams, you'll do fine. I'm currently taking Chem 3B with her as well, and she's been consistent and fair. Looks like I'll end with an A+

Maryann was a good professor. I didn't agree with all of her decisions while teaching during the pandemic, but she really did her best. She seems to genuinely care about student comprehension, which I appreciate.

Ochem is difficult no matter what, but Robak TRIES to make it easier to learn. This class requires effort and work outside of class, but I can't blame that on her. She provides lots of worksheets and some extra credit. The midterms are extremely difficult and are the worst part of the class. If you use the resources, this class isn't impossible.

Honestly, it makes me so sad to see how bad Prof. Robak's reviews were last sem. It was a hard class, but she offered us so many extra resources (multiple daily office hours, review sessions, extra p-sets/readings). If you aren't prepared or willing to put in extra work into a course that is widely-known for being difficult, don't take it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Despite being in a pandemic, she was completely inaccessible and never responded to my emails until the problem was at its worst and even then she refused to help. She constantly complained about her not having enough time and thats why she was reusing past lecture videos... she is the absolute rudest professor (and teacher for that matter) ever..

I would not say Professor Robak is mean or awful. She seems to be very caring and I know a pandemic is especially hard on teachers. However ochem this semester was insanely difficult and I heavily relied on youtube and outside help. I earned a decent grade through LOTS of hard work. It is not impossible but she definitely could make things easier.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Heartless professor especially during a pandemic, offered less extra credit compared to previous years and did not make any accommodations despite a variety of circumstances. Inaccessible, very tough, and bad lecturer.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This teacher made the class very difficult during the pandemic. The class was poorly taught and her videos were clearly reused.

She is literally one of the most heartless people ever. She does not care for her students at all. She did not even try this semester and just reused old videos from her previous semesters that did not teach us at all. Youtube was a better teacher than her. You'd expect her to be more understandable with COVID but no. She just made things harder!

HORRIBLE EXPERIENCE, she didn't even try to teach WELL and her EXAMS WERE THE WORST PART. This class gave me such mental anxiety and really made me depressed the entire semester. WOULD NOT RECOMMEND HER!!!!!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I had high hopes that in a pandemic this professor would have understood how to make the class more accessible for students in these circumstances, but I thought wrong. Her lecture videos didn't even explain the material well and when it came for the exams they were very HARD. If her teaching was better I wouldn't have had a problem with the course

Doesn't respond to emails, makes no attempts to help students, over complicates things, and just sucks as a professor. I didn't learn anything from her (relied on youtube). Previous years stated she gave EC or adjusted grade bins or implemented curves, but this year AMIDST A PANDEMIC, she did nothing even remotely helpful, besides participation EC.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Robak is a caring professor. She's responsive on Piazza and is open to listen to our concerns. But that's about it. Her exams are HORRIBLE (C averages, no curve) and the difficulty is just terrifying. She's reluctant to give points back. In addition, she's bad with emails. There is a little bit of extra credit, but that barely helps your grade.

Fall 2020. I have to say this was quite a tough chemistry class mainly because the content is not really straightforward, so you have to think and what not and OChem in general is quite difficult especially Midterms 2 and 3. Contrary to previous reviews, there are no grade shifts and not much EC. Get ready to learn, because it is relatively tough.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Class was taken during the COVID-19 pandemic but compared to the rest of the professors I had this semester, Robak was the toughest. No curves and didn't shift grade bins (even though averages for midterms were very low), made exams harder than previous years, and made virtual learning VERY difficult. Only tiny amount of extra credit offered too

No curve for the class, even tho the average for the exams were around C's. Has made exams VERY hard but was lenient on quiz times. Sometimes she overcomplicated and lengthened simple concepts instead of getting straight to the point. Maybe this would have been different if it wasn't online.

This semester, she has been very inconsiderate of the pandemic. She made exams harder than past years bc of cheating online, which makes it unfair for those who do not cheat. In previous years, I've heard she lowers grade bins... she didn't do it this year. She makes online learning horrible. I thought she'd be great bc of these reviews...
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I'm not sure if this semester can fairly be used to rate Dr. Robak's teaching, but I just want to say, she definitely DOES NOT make virtual learning easier. Her midterms are way harder than the practice exams in an attempt to catch cheaters. They care more about this than our success. No curves, help, or lowered grade bins this year unlike before.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Her grading is incredibly generous. She makes lecture fun and interactive. Overall she is amazing, and I am very grateful I had her as my professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Doctor Robak is literally my favorite professor at Cal! She always responded to students questions/concerns on Piazza in less than 24 hours and is extremely clear about her expectations + accommodating to students' struggles in this challenging course subject. Bless her heart, she is representative of Cal's finest! DO THE PRACTICE SETS ON TIME.

Professor Robak is a god. Had her for Chem 3A as well and she made Ochem so enjoyable. Chem 3B was definitely more challenging than Chem 3A, and you need to work harder/put in more time, but my learning experience was just as amazing.

Professor Robak is the love of my life! She is incredibly well-spoken, an expert on the subject, super approachable in office hours, and most importantly, very very funny! She understands the struggle of organic chemistry students, so she spices up our midterm with cocaine and viagra synthesis mechanisms. Although course is very hard though...

While the content was difficult and the class moved fairly fast, Dr. Robak does an amazing job of clearly covering the material needed to do well in her class. Lectures are well organized, and the homework sets correspond closely to the lecture. To do well, all that you need to do is pay attention and put in time and effort into the homework.

Amazing professor, concise and clear about information on exams. However there were 3 midterms but other than that she was caring and truly interested in improving her lectures. She always asked for feedback and went over quizzes!

Loved her! All her lectures are recorded, so you can look back on anything you need. Her lectures are truly comprehensive, while still remaining understandable. And if you dont , she is always on piazza or in her office hours trying to make everything work. She sees each student as a person, and wants to help you 11/10! Lots of extra credit too:)

Professor Robak was an amazing professor, especially in clearly presenting topics using OneNote and in creating very helpful problem sets. I was pretty scared for OChem, but it was a lot better than expected. She also was very receptive and friendly with questions. Her office hours were during a class for me, but I heard they were very good also.

Robak is by far one of the best professors I've had. She makes content as difficult as ochem way more approachable and actually pretty fun! Her exams are very fair, and the extra credit opportunities through test corrections were so helpful (both in terms of my understanding of the material and my grade). I recommend going to review sessions.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Amazing Chemistry professor. She loves what she teaches and is always answering clarifying questions. Also, she is very approachable outside of class. Very accommodating and always puts the best interests of her students first. So grateful to have her for Chem 3A!

One of the best professors I have ever had at Cal. Professor Robak genuinely cares about her students and wants them to succeed. Her exams are in direct parallel with her problem sets and she offers ample extra credit. She is always answering questions on Piazza and she takes time to answer questions in lecture if there is confusion.

I think Robak gets more flak than she deserves for 3A. Her class is organized VERY well and she gives a lot of extra credit. Robak's lectures are generally clear and easy to follow. The problem sets are time-consuming but super-useful as they are far harder than the exams and reflect the problems on the midterms and final.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I've taken 3B with her and she is just superb in terms of course organization, lecture content etc. The exams were hard for sure, but she always gave extra credit to make up for all of it! Really really enjoyed taking 3B with her; would highly recommend! Ka (head GSI) was a great great resource as well. Could not have done well without him.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Robak definitely cares about her students and their success. Although the material is rather tough and hence difficult exams, she offers plenty of opportunities and practice problems to learn from mistakes and to improve. She even offered 40 points of extra credit over the course of the semester.

Professor Robak is great - she's incredibly understanding, and definitely wants you to succeed in the class and do well as possible. She offers up to 40 points of extra credit - I nearly failed her second midterm after slacking off, and she was incredibly helpful for the final. Her one midterm drop policy helps a lot. 10/10 would recommend!

Clear lectures and very organized lecture printouts & course materials. Accessible and very helpful in office hours. Sooo much homework, which is optional but essential to do well in the class. Exams were hard but she gave extra credit to compensate. Ochem is an inherently difficult class but she made it less painful! Would recommend Robak!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She's an amazing amazing lecturer and very accessible outside of class. Does a really good job of organizing the material in lectures, homework and past exams. The class is definitely NOT easy, you need to put a decent amount of time and effort and also have a good chem 3A background to do well. She and head GSI do an exceptional job answering ques
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Rather than going through slides or concepts on the board, MaryAnn teaches by providing lecture worksheets with problems that she goes through with you. Like many, I was a hater at first, but gradually realised how useful it is in learning ochem. The tests can be hard but don't worry as if a test was too hard she will give a lot of extra credit!

Every problem that she gives on the exams can be matched with at least one similar problem in either her lecture notes or problem sets, so make sure you do those thoroughly. This class is structured in a way that guides you step by step, not like many classes here at Berkeley where you are left to figure stuff out on your own.

I feel like she could have done a better job at teaching. Her final for Fall 18 should have resembled previous semesters since those were the practice exams she provided us with. Especially not helpful since the class is not curved.

she doesn't curve the class, but this is absolutely NOT because she doesn't care about her students' grades. she in fact cares a lot about her students and their grades and is very clear and accessible in office hours. she places an emphasis on real biomolecules to prepare you for biochemistry and show you how chemistry is relevant.

First 2/3 of the class went pretty well. Midterms were fair. Towards the end of the semester lectures became sloppy and incoherent. Final was very harsh and uncalled for in my opinion, shouldve been the same difficulty as midterms. Not the best professor but also not the worst.

Amazing professor who helps you understand the chemical foundations of biological molecules. LONG problem sets and tough but fair exams. No curve but makes up for it with generous extra credit. Make sure you go to lecture and office hours!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Caring

reviews.comment: Clear and organized. Keep up with the weekly problem sets and you'll do great. Many students dislike her no-curve policy, but her grading is fair and there is enough extra credit that the lack of a curve is not a problem.

Professor Robak teaching method is confusing, lectures are based on worksheets, and she doesnt even curve despite making her tests difficult. The final for Fall 18 did not meet her standards of teaching. She doesnt care about her students, their grades, or future prospects. Avoid at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: She made O-chem bearable, and really tries to go against the competitive nature of Berkeley by making the class uncurved. This can be good and bad. I have a feeling she made the final (Fl' 18) super hard because the class average was too high and she needed to tank everyone. Understands student dilemmas and tries to accommodate. Very approachable!

A lot of people are gonna hate on Robak because of the grade they got, but I barely passed this class and still love her. Is this class extremely difficult? ofcourse, its organic chem at BERKELEY, which has the #1 chemistry department in the nation, its not going to be easy. with that said, Robak gives you the chance to work hard andsucceed
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Robak is probably one of the worst present at Cal. She refuses to curve and makes her tests incredibly hard, theyre not up to par with her lectures at all or the psets/practice tests. I studied everyday for this class and had a B. Her final however, was very difficult so my grade fell from a B to a C. Avoid at all costs if possible.

At first, I didn't really like how she taught with fill in the blank worksheets; however, when webcasting her lectures -- she's a good webcaster. She grew on me over the semester and towards the end she really cared about us. The tests are somewhat hard but fair. You have to be caught up on lectures or else you'll fall behind fast.
She is a great professor and I really enjoyed her teaching. She makes chem so easy. her tests are extremely fair.
She really cares about her students. She is nice even if she doesn't seem like it at first. Stay caught up because falling behind means many nights of stress.

I wish she can teach all my classes. Extremely caring professor and tries her best to rebel against the competitive nature of Berkeley. Her problem sets are really long, but extremely useful and her lecture worksheets help during midterm reviews. Quiz every week to make sure you don't fall behind. Midterms have nice partial credits - tough but fair
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Best professor I had in all of my Chem Career. Assigns long prob sets but they are extremely helpful. She dissects every topic so well. Genuinely cares that we do well. She is like a mom, tough but always looks out for you. If I had her for 3A would have done better and actually understood the material unlike with Pederson. No curve but offers EC!

I took 3B with her and waited 3 semesters to take 3BL with her. She is just that great. Easily one of the BEST professor at Berkeley. Heavy on understanding arrow pushing mechanism (even for the inorganic rxg); thus, you don't have to memorize anything! Her wkst organize the material in a way relies on first principle understanding, not memorizxn
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She was a wonderfully caring and passionate teacher. I highly recommend reviewing the lecture notes after class, because she doesn't read the expository aloud but it helps a lot in organizing your thoughts. There is a lot of (optional) homework, as for any 3A/B class, but it's well worth it since the quizzes can be challenging but fair.

You print out lecture notes and fill them in during lecture which I didn't like because she glosses over certain concepts and because they are printed she goes quickly over some concepts. The problem sets are long and you must do them for the quizzes! Midterm 1 was hard with an incredibly low average. Final exam was brutal. would not take her again

I LOVE PROFESSOR ROBAK!! From the very first day of class you could truly tell she cared greatly about her students. I struggled in 3Aand having her for 3B was a complete 180 in terms of my understanding. Granted it still is a very difficult class but I truly thing she made it much easier and enjoyable for her students. Incredible lecture format!!!

Success tips: If you can understand how she writes/organizes her notes, do iClicker in bed and skip lecture. Each week, spend 4 hours learning/reading from her posted lecture notes, and 8 hours tackling her *2* psets for the week. Practicing mechanisms can become muscle memory (like a jigsaw puzzle) rather than mentally straining. Do hw before quiz
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I made an account here just so I could give my review of Dr. Robak. Overall, she is friendly and approachable. Problem sets way more (annoyingly) redundant than other profs, and exam unfairly tests specific material that rewards you for coincidentally studying the right things, rather than knowledge. Final exam heavy; I went from A to C this week.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Imagine a professor who doesn't curve ORGANIC CHEMISTRY with an average of a 59% on the first exam. This professor is Mary-Ann Robak. She is nothing special. She holds your hand and if you were in elementary school learning fractions, she would be great. We are college students, BERKELEY students. If you want to actually learn chem, dont take her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Robak is easily the worst chem prof I've had at Cal. After having Marsden and Pedersen, I thought my experience in 3B would be similar. NO! Instead of lecturing and going though the steps to actually learn and understand OChem, she gives us worksheets to fill out during lecture instead. BTW there's no curve. Good luck! Avoid her if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: After having had Dr. Pedersen for 3A I thought no Ochem teacher would ever live up to my expectations. This changed immediately after I realized how organized of a teacher Prof. Robak is. She cares much more about her students understanding the material than giving out grades. 100% would take again!

Professor Robak is the best professor I have had at Cal. She genuinely cares about the students and wants them to learn. Her class is built for students to be encouraged and succeed. After a poor experience in Chem 3A, Robak's 3B experience has been so much better than I could have imagined. Her lectures are engaging and she is so organized.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Robak is literally the best STEM professor I've had at Cal. She cares immensely about her students and their learning, and goes above and beyond to be available and teach well. Chem 3A was a pain for me, but Chem 3B has been so understandable and approachable. If you can, definitely take Chem 3B with her!

Professor Robak is one of my favorite professors in my entire time of learning Chemistry. She makes learning Organic Chemistry interesting and engaging. Her exams are fair, all from the Problem Sets. She is also very accessible during office hours, and she knows how to be humorous! Must-take!

Professor Robak is the best professor I've had after 3 semesters at Berkeley. Lectures are clear and highlight the concepts that will be important for the class while leaving room for student inquiry. Problem sets correspond to the material taught in lecture. Exams correspond to the problem sets. Leaving this class with a greater love for chemistry
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: OMG. I feel most grateful to have Professor Robak for OChem. She has turned it into something that is approachable with understanding. With the increasing amount of reagents being thrown at me toward the end of Chem3A, I thought Chem3B will be pure memorization. But no! Her class is heavy on understanding mechanism. I wished I took Chem3A with her.

She uses a tablet, which allows her to be very organized in her diagrams. Great visuals, color coordinated, and applies the dry ochem to real-life examples. Tests are fair. You can leave lecture confidently saying you learned something, unlike Pederson, which left you wondering what just happened.

She forces you to go to lecture with worksheets and clickers (free points), but everything you need to know is in lecture slides posted online, so no textbook is necessary. The exams were much easier than the hard questions in the problem sets (just the basic concepts). She curved the class generously at the end. Would take again - very reasonable!

As far as lecture goes, a really clear lecturer that is willing to go WAY further than obligated to in the form of answering student questions after class, holding extra OH, and PIAZZA (she is piazza jesus). Fair grader--got an A- after getting slightly below an SD on all tests. No homework, just HIGHLY RECOMMENDED psets. Would take again!

Amazing and caring professor. She was very motivating especially after I did terrible in the first midterm and motivated me to turn things around for the second midterm and final. Definitely schedule one-on-one meetings as office hours can get too hectic. I would definitely recommend taking 3B with her and go to every lecture as its easy points.

Robak is a wonderful lecturer. A lot of people thought she was boring but I found her lectures to be very informative and helpful. Participation is required and she uses clicker questions but I found them helpful as well. She did assign prelab questions which were long and sometimes annoying but in the end made the lab much easier.
She is really nice and super helpful. A fan of I-clicker which makes attendance semi mandatory and boosts your grade.
Boring lectures and monotonous voice

PROBLEM SETS. PROBLEM SETS. PROBLEM SETS. Just do the darned problem sets. Online hw was unnecessarily confusing and the stuff on there wasn't tested. She doesn't write her exams so it's best you do the problem sets her GSIs write. Book...is OKAY. I know she's supposedly really nice during OH.

She's a great professor! Super helpful and super kind. Stay on top of the material, and you'll do well. Doesn't deserve any negative feedback. She works hard and knows her stuff extremely well. Definitely worth enrolling in her class

Meek and quiet professor during lecture, but she knows the material well and goes over the material as clear as possible even for students who do not have a Chemistry background. Even more helpful during Office Hours - she will stay overtime to make sure students understand. Cares about students, including trying to fix scheduling problems, etc.

Extremely boring. Her voice is obnoxiously high, and somehow she has zero enthusiasm. She reads off her powerpoint slides and takes her good ole time writing on the board with different colored chalk. But, the class itself was pretty easy: did terribly on the final but the labs weren't too bad. Better than Chem 3BL, that's for sure...

BORING.  The bane of my week.  Somehow Robak made this single hour in the week seem like a relentless eternity.  Lectures weren't really necessary.  Basically her lecture were like an onslaught of boringness.  But if you get a good gsi this class is not only easy, but lab can be fun.  Not difficult but not truly engaging.

Extremely boring professor. It was hard to sit through lecture all the time and over half the class ended up not showing up. She rushes through powerpoint slides and doesn't explain things very clearly. I learned most of the material from the GSI. Really easy class, though.

She explains the concepts clearly in lecture, but is SUPER boring. Has no enthusiasm at all, and after the first lecture barely anyone showed up anymore because of it. Grading is pretty fair for labs and the lab exam, and it's easy to get by just by reading the lab textbook.

Okay the readings are a bit absurd, but you can kinda just skip them and read the slides and/or go to/watch lecture recordings. Prof feels super real and also is a cool guy and tries to keep the lectures engaging but they are 3 hours so it def is a bit of a drag. Last hour is just an 15 min activity and then you can leave tho. One of my favs.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: he is a nice guy and passionate about the subject. knowledgeable too, I like him overall but he seems like OBSESSED with ai and uses it a lot which is off-putting. also the forced class-wide debates are controversial and spooky

He's a very chill guy. put effort into ur hw assignments and study like a week before the midterm and final you'll be guaranteed an A+ (the fact that it's raining extra credit in that class helps a lot too, just do all the in-class assignments and go to all the lectures)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects

reviews.comment: Chill guy easy A+. Also teaches about quite intriguing and curious subjects but the 3 hour lecture can be difficult anyways. Just take it though don't worry at all

lots of easy ec available (if you >5 lectures, do >10 group projects, etc). lectures were long but he splits them up with break and the last hour being groupwork. overall i dont think the concepts covered were particularly hard, and i felt like i barely did anything but still finished with >100%. is very genuine and cares a lot.
Lecture is really long but manageable. The homework do weight a good portion of your grade, and sometimes the hw wasn't even relevant to what we were learning.

uri is a funny guy and always kept it real. i appreciated all the transparency within the course. they can be slow on grading assignments, grade cutoffs are weird (above a 95% is an A), and tests are confusing. takes feedback seriously though and always checks in. class felt really ai heavy. overall, just an okay class experience.

Attendance mandatory for 5 lectures, additional attendance is ec. Pretty passionate about his classes, has dry humor that shows through in the slides; makes his long lectures better. Open to questions and feedback outside of class time. Test-wise, only 1 midterm + 1 final and both were not too bad. Weird grading bins (95+ for an A) but doable.

lots of reading and you need a 99.9% for an a+, but he offers lots of ec that makes it manageable. lecture is worth attending even if exhausting (3 hrs!) i was ill and requested an extension for an assignment and did not get a response for 2 weeks, so don't count on quick comms. fair grader, really interesting content.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: The homework assignments are just utterly ridiculous. Like how am I supposed to look at a massive amount of ridiculous data and make column charts and this chart that chart in excel when I know nothing about Excel? I am a freshman not a corporate slave employee! Ridiculous homework, extremely irritating.

Teaching a 3-hour block is hard, but he tried to make it better with group activities and discussions. Really interesting lectures and content. More of a focus on human behaviour, versus a usual bio-heavy approach to cognitive science.

Lectures are long, but I found the material to be interesting (other people might not have). Can get mundane at times simply bc the session is 3hrs at once. Very flexible with deadlines/submissions for hw if you have valid reasons! Try to speak w him after class if you're interested in what he teaches/go to OH. STUDY FOR TESTS!

Uri wants his students to participate to form an interactive learning environment, and he's a cordial guy. His lecture slides imply this (there's minimal writing, more of a presentation). I recommend going to lecture -- albeit long. Go to OH, talk about cognition with him. Super knowledgeable. MT and final relatively easy. Interesting projects/HW
Even though Intor to cognitive science is hard but he is very flexible for the grade and miss deadline or test as long as you give reasonable reason and write him a email.

Great professor; nice guy. Although there were a lot of delays in grading, the assignments themselves were graded pretty fairly and most of them were finished quick enough. Not that many assignments either, so it wasn't a massive time commitment. Take CogSci 1 with this professor if you can!

Took this class over the summer, and I felt like it was run fully by AI... every email, lecture, and assignment was almost fully written by Chat GPT, and the entire course grading was made up of 60% assignments, 15% midterm, and 25% final. Not a hard class by any means, but honestly wouldn't take it if it weren't fully online.

Content is fairly interesting. It's not hard to do well as long as you show up to class. However, the entire class seemed AI-generated. It's a little disconcerting when AI-generated images are consistently used in lecture slides. Two hour lecture is rough though and unfortunately he is not the most compelling lecturer in the world.

I had him for summer online classes. His lectures were very easy to follow and his midterm and final were also open note. He does pretty much take everything from the textbook and put it on the slides though. I would highly recommend!!!
Very passionate about cognitive science. Truly tries to make lecture engaging. Made me interested in the subject.

For a new lecturer, he is not bad. Glad I took him over the other person most people complained about. He really cares about the subject and tries to make the lectures engaging. Very willing to help you learn if you seek his help. Though he is a tough grader, I think he really cares that you have a solid foundation for CogSci.

He's clearly passionate about the subject. My only criticism would be that some things were sometimes unclear (lack of an exam syllabus, unclear grading criteria), but I think the grading curve took care of any mistakes students may have made from confusion. Test questions were fair & he offered ample extra credit opportunities. Great intro class.

idk if it's because he's a new professor, but his class was extremely disorganized. midterm and final were the length of a quiz, lectures were so boring that ppl would get attendance then leave. never offered any study resources, like a study guide, making this intro class a nightmare. still better than taking it with Meredith tho. he's just ok
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Korisky's lectures are well-prepared and mostly clear, with up-to-date and relevant materials. He adds a bit of humor, which keeps things engaging. The test was tough but fair, and the semester tasks were reasonable. Overall, a good course if you're ready to put in the effort.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Korisky is an inexperienced professor and it shows. He offered no study guide for both midterm and final exam, constantly left students in complete darkness on key info like grading bins, curves test material ect. Tests were horribly worded and vague. Lectures incredibly boring and verbatim from the textbook. Clearly not a good teacher. Avoid.

I do think sometimes the lectures were very repetitive and concepts were overused. At least for history 12 (admittedly lower division), he taught how to study history, especially in the Middle East. I think non-history majors might get more out of his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Very mixed about this professor. On the one hand, very well spoken and gives a lot of good insight on the topic if you have never been educated on it. On the other, lectures can fluctuate wildly from absolutely necessary to attend or a complete waste of time. Quizes were easy, just be prepared to talk about the same thing over and over again.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He has passion but I didn't feel like I got much out of his lectures (he has a very soft voice that put me to sleep at times). Cares about his students and grading was not bad. Shout out to the GSIs, learned the most through weekly section.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Respected

reviews.comment: Makdisi is THE GOAT!!! In a class dealing with such sensitive subject matter, he never failed to offer an open space where students can freely share their ideas and let us come to conclusions ourselves. While the class is long-reading heavy, the important sections are covered in discussion so u should be chilling. Everyone should take this class!!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Makdisi is an incredible historian and I'm grateful to have taken "Palestine and the Palestinians: A Modern History" with him. He assigns engaging readings and is a captivating lecturer. There was a LOT of history to pack in this semester-long class, but Makdisi synthesized immense amounts of information in an understandable format. TAKE THIS CLASS
Gaston never teaches, he just talks to the girls instead.

I am genuinely surprised by the negative sentiment surrounding Sanchez. He was a perfectly normal professor, who explained concepts clearly and seemed to genuinely care about students learning. This course has changed a lot over the years but I think it's in a good place right now. Read notes before lectures, spend time on your quiz cheat sheet.

He is very bad at teaching, he doesn't even know how to explain the concept clearly. Makes the class extremely hard.

DO NOT TAKE
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Sanchez is very kind and he is very accessible outside of class during his office hours. It's really not too much work for a 1 unit class. The exams are not too difficult as well as long as you skim through lecture notes. Great professor and nice class.

He is an easy going person. He teaches basic R code, which is easy content to grasp, step by step. His lectures were boring sometimes but he tries to make it a bit fun here and there. Homework was easy. Exams were easy. The exams just required more memorization of the rules of R code. He's very approachable. Good amount of work for a 1 unit class.
Might be a bit biased because I know some R, but this class was fairly easy and light workload. Decent and nice professor.

Professor Sanchez is an incredible teacher. He is very knowledgable on the material he teaches, and cares a lot about his students. He is extremely approachable, and makes an effort to socialize with students. He is very generous with his time, and can communicate complicated topics in a simplified way. I will always recommend his classes.

Not a STEM major AT ALL (can't memorize anything...) and this class was very easy. Both the midterm and final were online (not sure if that was a one off just for FA '24). Lectures are boring/irrelevant, but Sanchez is a really great guy who will stay with students after his office hours in order to help them finish projects and such.

Professor Trujillo is one of the most caring and helpful lecturers I've had at Cal. He is incredibly accessible outside of class and clearly cares about his students and the course he teaches.

While his lectures aren't the most engaging, he is approachable and easy to talk to, regardless of the topic.
This class is very straightforward. Online midterm and final, projects are simple, just be on time with deadlines and you're fine. The material is pretty easy and just the basics of coding in R.
Best R course in Berkeley. Nice professor nice GSI. HW is a very good practice for this class. Really spend time in Projects, it will be helpful in the future.

His lectures were so dry (I'm sorry) but I learned a lot about programming in R, and this class is def better than stat 20 in terms of teaching coding intuition. Don't slack on hw though, it always takes a little longer than expected and graders are a bit harsh. Projects were pretty lenient. Do not turn in stuff late, that brought me down to A- :(

Lectures are a bit unengaging, but rest of class is good. Workload is very manageable, and pace starts is reasonable, I came in with zero R knowledge of experience. Reasonable late and extension policy as well.

I see a lot of poor reviews about him in the past but this semester was one of my favorite lecturers. I took stat20 and compared to that this was a 10/10 class, teaches everything from the beginning and the class begins to pick up towards the end but all in all not to bad.

This R course is a great learning experience with helpful homework and labs that guide problem-solving approaches. The assignments are meaningful, and the GSI is supportive and willing to help. The course includes three projects, and with an easy midterm, at least 80% of the total score is achievable.
Gaston is a really nice man, I really enjoyed his class, please take it you will learn so much
For a 1 unit class can be a lot of work but assignments are graded very generously. The assignments itself aren't hard. Lectures are pretty boring but they aren't necessary.

He is a nice enough person, but he just wasn't a good lecturer. The class was backloaded and weirdly difficult and time-consuming for a 1-unit class. The structure of the homeworks, worth 65% of the final grade, were really hard to follow; they seem to be written poorly.

Took with STAT131 and first half of this class' material overlapped which helped. Midterm + final tested small details and there weren't resources provided to prepare. Lectures weren't recorded and there usually weren't slides to look back on so it was important to take good notes in lecture. Lots of OH between prof/GSIs for help on projects.
Take STAT133! Fair workload but you can learn really useful skills.

Gaston gets so much hate and it's completely undeserved. I took Stat 133 with him (non-statistics major) and while the class isn't easy, his grading is fair and he's a solid lecturer. Exams are manageable if you study and most of the grade hinges on projects and hw which he gives a solid amount of time on. Overall he's a nice guy, and very helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Stat 133 is a really nice course: it's not a heavy workload class, and I truly learned a lot about R. The professor is really nice. He is always willing to help you even if it's not his office hour times. TAs are also really patient. Highly recommend this course!

Hands down the best professor I have ever had. Clearly cares whether students are learning and will go out of his way to help students who actually want to understand/learn the material. His OH are a game changer for anyone who is having trouble with his classes. Highly recommend.

I had him for 33A/B and while he's a nice guy who will help, the class is poorly run. Also, the instructions on assignments were pretty unclear, the TA was pretentious, and the quiz/exam questions sometimes made 0 sense.

So over-hated on here. Prof Sanchez is a really great dude, always going out of his way to help students on projects, including extending his office hours while the GSIs are on strike. Very helpful during office hours, and decent lectures. No prior coding knowledge is needed.
I like the course structure from easy to hard. Also you can learn everything from his lab and hw assignments, they have really clear instructions.

This was a tolerable class. I showed up to lecture maybe 50% of the time but did all of the readings. You should try hard to not get behind and actually try to play around with the concepts in the labs in your own time to get good at them rather than just doing the bare minimum to finish. Not too much work. Start projects early so you can get help.

I took Stat 133 in its virtual format. There were a lot of assignments (labs, hw, and projects), but there was also a fair amount of extra credit. This class has been incredibly useful for me because I'm heading into a field that uses a lot of R. I suggest taking P/NP if you don't need a letter grade.

This 3-unit class takes up as much time for me as Math 110 (w/Holtz) and Stat 135 combined, both 4-unit classes. Exams don't reflect lectures, homeworks/labs/projects take an absurd amount of time. Unless you are adamant about learning R AND have a lot of free time, don't take this class.

I had the pleasure of taking both Stat 133 and Stat 154 with Gaston, and I never had any trouble in the class in terms of logistics. in Stat 133, Gaston tried really hard to get people to participate and teach effectively. Content-wise, labs, homework, and projects help you learn and they're well organized. I don't understand the hate that he gets.

had gaston for 133, & again for 154. doing another review just for him b/c he's awful. hw was 60% of the entire grade, we were given 0 drops for 8 homeworks. labs were 20% of the grade (completion) w/ 2 drops. final exam was very difficult, mainly multiple choice/truefalse. he doesn't curve anything. grade is dependent on the final & hws. avoid !!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Took both his class for 133 and 154. For Stat 133, I personally didn't have too much trouble, but you definitely have to work for it if you don't have any prior R/coding experience. Lecture isn't too helpful, but the content is all there in labs. Stat154 was great and clear. He does care about students' learning, but grading could be clearer.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Having taken numerous Stats and Math classes at Cal, I honestly don't understand the hatred towards Gaston. While his lectures are unclear, his written material is extremely well-written and useful. The GSIs are great. The homeworks ARE difficult, but also doable - you just have to start early and work at it. Final was very reasonable as well
The final is Nothing match the homework. And the homework dont match the lecture.

gaston is just as bad as my friends and rate my professor says he is. this sem, he decided to do 20% labs, 30% hw, 50% final.. his lectures are absolutely useless as he goes on irrelevant tangents. homework is difficult/graded harshly (took this class as a stats major but w/ no coding exp), so i basically had to learn everything on my own. gl yall

I'm non-stats major who retook this course. Though this class's supposed to be "introductory," if you don't have coding experience or experience of R, you will suffer. This course does not teach you the basics of R in a clear, organized matter. If you MUST take this course, take The Analytics Edge (a free MOOC course from Stanford) beforehand.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This an easy class but hw graded very harshly

The most annoying part of the class is the lack of transparency when it comes to the grading criteria for assignments (you don't know the rubric while doing the assignment). My best advice, then, would be to carefully complete the assignments (be pedantic and explain everything excessively thoroughly) as they can compensate for lower exam scores.

Worst professors Ive had at Cal. Really unfair grading policies, severe lack of resources, lack of empathy in his teaching, doesnt prepare you for exams, grading policies are very unclear, rubrics take points off assignments but dont award you for doing things correctly. My soul feels sucked from this class and I severely regret taking this.

Some people may say this course is easy. Well, it's only true at the beginning of this course. As the course progresses, it would become more difficult. Gaston is a terrible lecturer, at least for stat 133. You need to memorize to prepare for the exam, which is not interesting at all. Labs are mandatory, while lectures are not.

It's very obvious that Gaston has no passion for teaching, and this is shown by lecture attendance and the attitude of his classes towards him. He's known for not putting in effort to his teaching and also has by far the most arbitrary grading criteria ever.

Lecture style is so poor (emphasis on this). Not engaging and goes on unrelated tangents. It states that this class doesn't require prereqs, but as a person with some programming experience, much of the material definitely would be difficult to grasp without some knowledge. His lectures don't seem to correlate at all with labs / homework / exams.
I took his stat 154 class this semester; clear structure; very well organized; homework heavy but it's not strictly graded; so I really enjoyed this class and learned a lot from it. GOOD JOB!

I would say Gaston is the best professor I have taken in Cal. Maybe he is not the right person teaching Stat 133 but he is for stat 154. He explains machine learning concepts very clearly and easy to understand. Down to earth person and to be honest, a tough grader. I definitely will recommend him as Stat 154 professor.

Please do yourself a favor and if you are not a statistics major just take a different class. This class teaches the basics of R and data science. They have classes on R if thats what you want and they have a whole data science major if that's what you want. If you are a statistics major like then just try and get it with a different professor.

When I was about to take the class, rate my professor didnt have a lot of reviews for him so I gambled and signed up. Id rather have gone all in on a 2/7 offsuit blind. Terrible professor, terrible policies, he WILL penalize you for things that are not listed in the syllabus, rubrics, or grading policies. Tests dont reflect the material at all.
Definitely the worst prof I've had throughout my first 2 years at Cal. No transparency in how he grades, no idea on what he's going to put on tests, and no ability to teach.
The WORST prof ever. My first B in my entire life. You will never know what to study and what to expect for exams.

He makes us read an online textbook which doesn't really relate to the things he's teaching in class. Homework and labs are in R (coding), midterms are based on actual math and concepts, which we only practice online and don't practice in real life. Lectures only show examples that are difficult to understand and aren't explained.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He does not cover much material in lecture. Homework does not have much to do with in-class materials. Bad feedback. Mandatory lecture attendance. Would NOT RECOMMEND.
Switched out of Stats major because of this class. Very usefulness lectures and boring lecturing styles plus mandatory attendance at 8am. Your choice

Gaston is one of those people whose merits definitely don't include a teaching talent. His lectures are extremely slow-paced and boring, covering just a fraction of material. He's very disorganized, all over the place with his thoughts. I don't think I've witnessed him answering one question clearly. He hardly communicated or posted any updates.

He is not a good option for this class. Although its 3 units and the assignments do not seem like much work, the grading is vague and inconsistent, costing many points. He also blames any trouble on the students even when its clearly staff fault. I had near 100 in assignments but still got a mediocre grade because of his class is structured.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: One of the worst professors I have ever had. Zero communication and backtracks on topics listed in the syllabus while being extremely strict on other items. Extremely rude and boring lecturer. Do not take this class with professor Sanchez unless you are required too.

Mandatory lectures that are utterly useless. If attendance wasn't mandatory, you could get by without ever attending lecture or doing any reading. Assignments are easy, but points are docked for trivial mistakes even if it's obvious that you understand the content being taught. The class isn't very useful or meaningful, but Sanchez makes it worse
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He doesn't answer online forum questions, assignments have vague requirements, grading is harsher than necessary. Expect to lose substantial points on trivial mistakes irrelevant to the mastery of subject. His lectures are boring at best, explanations are mostly vague. Participation is a strict mandate. Overall, an extremely negative experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: first time ever rating a professor but i had to because he's just that terrible. course is horribly run and overall an extremely negative experience
Literally the worst professor I have ever had. Absolutely useless lectures and a horrible grading scale. He is one of the few people I actively dislike
Gaston is clearly passionate about his area of expertise and his love of the subjects he teaches is contagious. Do whatever you can to take a class with this man.

It's just weird... He looks very nice in person except being a boring lecturer. However, his policy and curve are ridiculous. I can't relate the evil policy and grading with a person who seems to be pretty nice.......

I was surprised by all the negative reviews Prof. Trujillo has, because to me he was perfectly fine. He wasn't leave-a-lasting-impression amazing, but he was nowhere near as bad as some of these reviews would have you believe. I found the class nowhere near as difficult as people had said, and he encouraged and answered any questions people had.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I like his style of lecture. He teaches more of a grad school layout where nearly all of the work is project based--real world application and skills. No tests. Get used to working in groups as your grade is most dependent on your presentations and your group collaboration. Also hws/labs teach you very useful statistical/cs skills.
Very unclear with his rubrics and gives boring assignments. His quizzes focus on  R/RMD syntax rather than actual programming or data processing. Oh, and he also doesn't curve.

Horrible professor. Would spend 50%  of lectures describing random topics likes space travel and rockets. GSIs completely saved the class. Lectures were a waste of time and his tests were decently hard.

This review is for AFRAM 118. I respectfully believe it is time for Dr. Ugo to retire or pivot in his career. He is not tech savvy, so when his lecture slides supposedly did not work at the onset of the semester, he just gave up. Thus, resulting in a highly ineffective lecture style. He is precariously late with grading and poor at giving feedback.

Prof Nwokeji is sweet and very knowledgable but he was all over the place. Always showed up to lecture 20+ min late, never made quiz expectations clear, randomly failed everyone halfway through the semester because people stopped coming to class. He also forgot to show up to our midterm so everyone just left. Easiest A ever but so anxiety-inducing
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He was pretty hard to understand during lectures, but they weren't required to do well in the class. Four assignments the whole year decided your whole grade, so study hard for those. His classes might be boring at times but he is a very happy guy and his class is the easiest A I've taken at Berkeley.
Sweet individual but not the best professor, lectures were a bit confusing. Grading is on an easy scale but he will not help you pass midterms or finals, you just need to know

Most unorganized class I've ever taken. Nothing was ever clear; we had quizzes on the most random content that he never even told us to study, and each quiz was worth up to 15% of our ENTIRE grade. Bro said we had a map quiz and never told us which map??? Then dropped like 7 different maps on the quiz and asked where the olduvai gorge is like what?
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I do not recommend this class at all!!! the GSI never knew what was going on in that class either. Random quizzes. only mentioned about quiz once and never said what to study for!! mind you he mentioned this quiz a day before it was due!!! no format for midterm or final!!  our essays and finals never got graded and they passed the students!!!

This professor is a mess. We had a map quiz when he never taught geography, we had to memorize words in IGBO for a language quiz worth 5% of our grade, our paper and final were never graded so they never went into the gradebook and the GSIs never knew what was going on in the class. This was a horrible class. Dont recommend it.
Dude! Class is so unorganized and lectures put me to sleep (sadly). Nice teacher but lectures are a bit boring. Hope this helps

No instructions on format for midterms until the night before. Randomly gives you language to memorize on tuesday, test on thursday, then its never spoken of again. Grading is unclear and confusing. No instructions given to gsi's so they never can answer a single question. Classes always start late or are cancelled but godforbid you don't show up
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He was a great guy and I feel like I learned a lot in his class. His accent can be hard to understand at times, but you truly do get used to it. I would definitely recommend. I only took this class as a breadth and it was the only one open at this time, but it turned out to be a fun class. Much easier than first depicted.

Prof never called attendance himself but my GSI always did in discussions. Prof says "those who study will pass", that's true. Yes, prof has an accent but tbh it's not too heavy & for the most part I understood him fine. Lectures & readings have similar content. OK at announcing updates for assignments/tests, GSI try to help if issues arise.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Nwokej is very passionate about AAStudies to the point where he can get off track during his lectures and waste all 2 hours, study ahead for the Map Quiz and Language quiz I can't stress that enough, he has a very thick accent so it's hard to understand him even if you sit in the front row of his lectures
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy
