literally said in lecture that he wouldn't want to teach a class where many students get an 'A". This is an intro class, yet there's 200+ pages of readings each week. and nothing is graded yet with our final in 3 days. including our midterm which we took before thanksgiving break and our attendance and participation. Horrible class, GSI was nice.

we have no idea what our grade is going into the final. He hasn't even put in our participation/attendance grade, midterm that was taken before thanksgiving break has not be graded yet. All we have for our 3 hour final, is a list of 200+ terms that we have to memorize, expecting a paragraph with quotes from authors including there names.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. I understand college is suppose to be hard but this is an intro class. 200+ pages of reading weekly + 3 hrs of lecture videos. Weekly quizzes that are on very specific niche irrelevant part. He told us he wouldn't want to teach if every student got an "A" in his class. Have no idea what our grades are going into final.

The midterm essay was just not it. Spent two weeks memorizing a 8 page paper. TRAGIC. & more than 200 pages of reading every week and quizzes every friday on niche stuff barely talked about.
I have a 99/100 but this is only bc i spend 8 hours+reviewing for this damn subject. Fr econ and math 53 I spend max 3 hours per week, but NOT for this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Spends majority of lectures reading from slides but he does take time to make some extra commentary about the material to elaborate on certain topics. Weekly quizzes with lots of highly specific questions, and participation definitely matters in section - my GSI Rachel was awesome and was incredibly helpful in learning the course material!

Very boring with difficult quizzes. Feel completely lost and not knowing my grade since term paper and final are 50% and happening final week. GSI was not very helpful at all either and grades hard. Participate in section is very important. Overall, this teacher is not the best and the 200 word list of key terms isn't really helping either.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Awful Professor! He may be a good professor for grad students but not to undergrad. Tricky and stupid quiz weekly. The weekly readings are heavy too. The final is 17th but we have not received our grade or the physical paper of our midterm that we done before thxgiving. The final exam has no instructions at all but a list of 200 words to remember.

Never take this class, even if you think you can do well in American Politics. This professor expects lots of memorization, assigns hundreds of pages of readings every week and barely unpacks any of them in lecture. You are still expected to do them however as the weekly quizzes often test about them in the most niche ways possible.
Awful. Do not take his class. I have never felt so confused before in a class, and POLISCI 1 is supposed to be a easy intro class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Awful course. Only redeemable thing was my amazing gsi, truly saving me at this moment. He does nothing to help prepare for the final except give a list of 200 terms to look over. Expects us to know every reading AND author for the final with no other information given on what to do. Lectures are boring and just repeat the slides.

genuinely the worst professor i've ever had he literally wants his students to fail. hundreds of pages of reading a week, . expects us to not only memorize IN CONTEXT a 10 page list of key terms but also the authors, titles, and main points of 50 course readings that are all 20+ pages. don't take this class with him i guarantee you will regret it
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: 200+ pages a week, additional lectures to watch outside of class, we don't even have our "midterm" (a paper) grades back to review, we get that back the day of the final. Quizzes on the most random facts to have a "gotcha" on students who don't finish reading. Said he doesn't wanna give A's to students. He is the reason I'm no longer doing polsci

Final is so unrealistic, expects us to memorize 50 different readings with author names, ideas, and title of the articles. Absolutely insane expectations I dont even know if I will pass this class. nobody is learning from memorizing every author's name and viewpoints do not take this class i regret it everyday. does not care about students passing

Deadlines and expectations are never consistent and changed every week.Class randomly switched to sync/async lectures in the mid of the sem and the combined time of both exceeded way past the 1.5 hr alloted for this class. I was intended polisci but I switched this class to pass/fail because I hate it so much and am now no longer doing polisci.

-starting assigning like 2 hours of lectures to watch outside of class in the 3rd week and hasn't stopped
-SO. MANY. READINGS. and all of them are on the final apparently
-the "study guide" for the 3-HOUR final exam (multiple choice, short answer, and an essay) is literally just a 7-page long list of terms. and they've said that's all we're getting
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He does know his stuff, but the quizzes are awfully graded and many times impossible. There was one with infinite attempts and I tried every single answer, both what is in the notes and random and still didn't get a 5/5. Content isn't hard but the quizzes absolutely ruin it. Well-organized, though, although one quiz popped up that wasn't announced.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: consistently makes errors on his quizzes, doesn't care if his students succeed. said in one of the first lectures of the class that he does not want his students to get A's.

This professor is actively trying to make students fail. I have never learned so little about a subject. He even gets his own knowledge checks wrong. He will give you them to study then during lecture say that he got it wrong and still mark you wrong on the test after memorizing answers that he couldn't fix ahead of time. Does not care if you learn
One advice: don't take this class..
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: the quizzes are the worst, they seem more focused on testing if students are doing all the reading and listening to every word of lecture rather than if we're understanding concepts. excessive amount of reading, 100+ pages even AFTER he cut down on the reading. too much content to digest, he doesn't seem to care about if students are succeeding.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: horrible professor - he gives extremely unfair quizzes every week about some offhand thing in the 200 page readings or a one second comment he made in a lecture that we're supposed to remember. not only is there synchronous lectures but you have to watch asynchronous videos and do knowledge checks as well. insane amount of reading. love my gsi tho

Quizzes are incredibly unfair and based on minor details found either in the 80+ pages he assigns weekly or from something he said offhandedly. Lectures are bland, and he makes interesting info boring. Quizzes are also currently one of the only ways to determine your grade, since both the in-class essay and exam (worth 50% total) happen later.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
1. weekly quizzes based on very niche offhanded things he states in passing (not in slides)
2. said quizzes are multiple selection yet does not give partial credit
3. Two chances to attempt quizzes yet you are not allowed to see what you did wrong
4. reads off slides verbatim in a monotoned voice
5. 200+ pages of reading a week
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dont take this professor!! His lectures are dry and hard to listen to, he makes quizzes incredibly hard to do well on and you dont get partial credit for multiple answer questions and you get 2 attempts at each quiz but dont get to see your previous attempt. You have a better chance doing bad in this course than doing well

The real-life examples Professor Van Houweling uses in lecture is super interesting and engaging. Despite the lectures were on Zoom, he made Intro to American Politics very relevant with current politics in 2025 as well as hotly debated public policy issues like health care. I definitely learned a lot!

Horrible class, lectures don't match up to the questions, quizzes are extremely specific, meaning you wont even find them in lectures, it could be the smallest thing he mentioned, and you'll have to remember that for the test, so studying with just the slides is not possible.

Lectures were boring and the professor mostly read off of slides. Lots of reading, but my GSI went over a lot of them (I heard some GSIs don't though). Lots of weird quizzes with highly specific questions. One midterm, term paper, and final. Mostly need to study terms for the midterm/final. Class wasn't super hard but felt dull.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
This course was a lot of fun to take. The professor was always ready to teach and the lectures were easy to follow. 
This being said, a lot of the course is based on reading; I would recommend paying extra close attention to discussions, as they will go into details, as well as going to all the lectures since there are sometimes pop quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: To get a good grade in this class, GO TO DISCUSSION. I hardly learned anything from the Professor himself, but GO TO DISCUSSION, GSI'S ARE YOUR BEST BET. Make sure to get help from your GSI and you will do fine. This class is easy just lots of material and meaningless lectures, and GOING TO DISCUSSION will help you tremendously.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: The worst class I have ever take at UC Berkeley. Professor is so boring and GSIs act like they know everything. They are unwilling to compromise with you and they are honestly sort of jerks. Definitely would not recommend taking a course on the political science department at least if this is an accurate representation.

His lectures were pretty boring for me since at the beginning he mostly read off the slides and just gave minor jabs at them. I think the readings are pretty useful, but if you feel like you've to take HS government/AP US History; then you'll do fine. Make sure to do well on the assignments, since there are only a few of them. Exams are open books.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Van Houweling is straightforward. While it's better to go to class, his lecture slides are clear and posted on bCourses. The papers were tough (this is more of a GSI issue), but if you study the provided key terms, you will be prepared for exams. I never used the textbook. Material focuses on checks and balances/executive power/federalism.

Van Houweling was a boring lecturer. I just copied down lecture slides from the power points he posted online. Was very helpful in always positn resources on bourses so I really liked that.  Going to class isn't really necessary. Readings aren't necessary. Essay prompts for test are pretty easy to guess so  midtermfinals weren't hard.

terrible most boring professor. Evidently hes really good at his research but all he does is read his slides verbatim to the class. No point in doing both the reading and going to lecture because their the same. Essays are a bore and the midterm and final were easy. GSIs were unhelpful too. I'm a pol sci major and he almost made me switch majors.

He's not very interesting, but he's extremely clear as to what's going to be on the Midterms. You don't really have to attend class; you can just read his slides and read the textbook. His class can make you sleepy, but I enjoyed having him because he makes fair exams. He's easygoing and makes the class really easy and straight-forward!

Overall a pretty easy professor. Always clarifies what he means and posts lectures on bspace before class. Not really important to go to lecture because he just reads off the slides. GSI completely decides your grade, so make sure he/she likes you and you participate in discussion.

It was entertaining to go to lecture. Though not required, the Daily Show and Colbert Report made it interesting and fun. He explains things quite well and everything he lectures on is on powerpoints ready for download by the start of class. Extremely organized and a Good professor overall.

I took Congress with V-H and hated it.  He is a really boring professor and tries to make up for it by showing Daily Show Clips (though funny not helpful to understanding the material).  I did learn some interesting concepts but I recommend taking Congress with another professor.  Graded pretty hard, too.  Take Congress with another professor.

While the subject material is interesting, he is not a very captivating lecturer. Clips from The Daily Show and The Colbert Report made class more fun sometimes. To be honest, I skipped half of the classes before spring break and almost all of the classes after spring break. My GSI told me I would have got an A if I were not taking it P/NP ><

SHE IS THE WORST! I would rather have the plague than her. Completely immoral and rude. She laughed at me when I had an asthma attack and kept saying rude comments. She will also threaten you to come to her office hours! AVOID

Pretty good teacher. The class wasn't impossible but it was definitely hard. She lectures well and encourages questions. She was pretty patient with her students and easy to deal with. Would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I did well in the class. However, she is a very mean individual & is often condescending, degrades students. What's the point of having a professor that lacks any empathy/understanding? Yeah, terrible experience. I would say a lot of students in my class complained about her. Unfortunately, not all professors are compassionate and understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: not the most exciting lecturer at times, but clearly cares about his field and is always accessible

Prof Vogel was very nice and knowledgeable about the subject. The final/midterm/essay are based on both readings and lecture but the final is a lot of content esp the questions that could be based on anything covered ever in lecture. I found the grading to be pretty subjective based on GSI and participation accounts for a good chunk of your grade.

Great lectures (graded attendance). He is knowledgeable and very approachable. Readings can get heavy. GSIs were great and helped further understanding. Not many tough assignments. Just keep up on readings. I also recommend OH even just to chat

Lots of reading but honestly most are skippable since its broken down in lecture+section. Grading is GSI dependent. Participation more necessary than other classes. Lecture is dry but attendance is mandatory. Grades max out at 95 but still out of 100 (dumb). 10 bCourses discussions but you had to follow schedule (not sure if this was enforced).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Cool prof that had decently interesting lectures, but the readings and midterm/final were kinda ridiculous. So many readings and authors, and you had to know everything about them for the midterm/final on-demand papers. Wasn't enough time in discussion to go over them all, the rest of the grade is participation and essays that weren't too bad imo
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He's a great professor and the course is interesting. There are so many readings from so many different authors, which gives you a lot of material to use in your essays but it's also overwhelming when it comes to preparing for the final.

Vogel is redeemable compared to the rest of the PS department. Lectures are well constructed & organized, but super dense. more reading than most seminar/thesis classes, & exams are difficult and content heavy, but grading is contingent on your GSI. don't buy the reader, not worth the money def a class for learning, not so much for good grades
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: A MUST! Professor Vogel is one of a handful of professors who actually enjoys teaching and connecting with students. PS 138E was by far the best class I've taken; the content is highly interesting and easily applicable to current events. Assignments are very fair, but you can't get away with not doing readings and paying attention in lectures.

This dude knows his stuff. The course material is based on writings of many theorists and other scholars and can be pretty dense, so be prepared to read a lot and take notes during lecture. There are no traditional tests, just several papers (about 6), but they are graded quite tough. Be prepared to use your brain and really think in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: I highly recommend taking Varieties of Capitalism by Professor Vogel. PS 138E is basically a Poli Econ class. I found this class really interesting and I learned a lot from it. If you want to do well, go to his office hours because that's where he can tell you which parts of the readings to pay attention to. He's really nice and accessible.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: One of the best polisci classes I've taken, still use some theories and cases for other papers! Quite a lot of material, but Vogel is a very engaging lecturer who makes it easier to remember. Very varied assessments ! (media analysis, comparative paper, mid term, participation and debates + exam)

Really nice and helpful guy, but his lectures are painfully boring and monotonous. Exams are pretty tough and heavily based on readings (you're expected to remember 30+ economic theorists by name for exams). Lecture slides aren't much help so BSing this class is damn near impossible. He uses the 2 exams + 1 research paper + participation format.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Passionate and clear professor who tries to know everyone by name and really works hard to explain concepts clearly. His lectures are very information heavy and there's a lot of reading, but he's really methodical when explaining different concepts and ideas. Econ background is recommended, but you don't need to have any to do well in the course!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Hardest class at Cal that I've taken - required to thoroughly know 40+ dense works from economic theorists.  This class was listed as PoliSci but I would not recommend this class unless you are an economics major.  Two 5pg papers, two sets of in-class essays,  one in-class debate, and participation made up our grade.

This class was so much harder than expected. While there is a note that basic macro econ would be helpful, it should be a pre-req because I fell behind very quickly. Most lectures he crams so much dense info WITHOUT notes/board/ppt and it was difficult to stay up to his speed. Not my preferred style of teaching but a knowledgeable guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: A very caring Prof who tries to make somewhat abstract theories comprehensible. Sometimes tries to cover too much material in too short a time. Readings are lengthy and not always easy. Might be better with shorter/fewer readings and more methodical lecturing. Takes questions readily even with 100+ students.

Great Professor, terrible class. This class should be called: "reading Capitalism theory." Most boring class I have ever taken at cal. If there was more original content and the professor and gsi's didn't treat us like children this class could be great. It's too bad.

I was never interested in Japanese Politics, but Vogel made the class incredibly interesting. He's a good lecturer, and Kristie, my GSI, was a fair grader and gave plenty of help. It wasn't a difficult class--go to lecture, skim the readings and get the main ideas, and prep for the midterm and final by outlining. Papers are short and doable.

Lectures are about as engaging as they can get when it comes to talking about political economy from a rather conventional approach. The amount of reading is really the weakest point of this class. Too much redundancy in the readings--you'll find yourself reading three or four authors each stating the same thing and adding nothing substantive.

He's an amazing lecturer! Classes are super engaging. I've never before had debates or such thorough discussions during a lecture class. There's quite alot of readings, though, and the class is not that easy. Still though, if you're interested in political economy, it's a great class

Fantastic professor and course. Prof. Vogel is extremely friendly and approachable, has a talent for synthesizing and explaining difficult concepts, and provides genuine attention to his students. He is an extremely qualified expert in both Japan and Political Economy. Anyone with an interest in Japan owes it to themselves to take his course.

He is very knowledgable and very clear. Be prepared to do A LOT of reading and use it on the final. On the plus side, there aren't a lot of formal assignments. 60% of the grade was the final and the term paper. There was also a midterm (10%) and the rest was class participation and 5 bspace memos (very short, one-paragraph re: readings).
Probably one of the best classes I have taken at Cal. Lots of very dense material, but Vogel makes it worth it! Take if you are interested in comparative political economy!
The best professor I have ever had. Clear, interesting and nice.

Vogel was one of the best professors I had at Berkeley. He explains the material clearly, and is highly approachable. He remembers everyone's name, and is very friendly. Moreover, Vogel is very qualified...he has met with several PM's of Japan, and gives lectures to the state department on USJapan relations

I'll tell you why no one showed up -- the material was very dense. He was a great professor, but I was part of that group that didn't show up too often. If you're genuinely interested in the varieties of capitalism, I encourage you to take this class. If not, you may be in for a long semester.

Vogel was amazing. Best class I've taken at Berkeley. Very interested in his students- remembers names and encourages students to come to office hours. For some reason, only about half the class showed up to class on a regular basis. At any rate, varieties of capitalism with Vogel is certainly on of the best political science offered at Berkeley.

i think he likes listening to himself talk. the material was interesting. be prepared to have tons of japanese students in there, lame essay assignmnents, and a lot of reading. it sounds like vogel is still going through puberty--imagine that for 1.5 hours at a time. he's a nice guy though. it was a mediocre class.

Best class I've taken. The design of the course (readings, lectures, and sequencing) was brilliant. Mark Dallas--great TA. Vogel DOES remember names, which may be bad if you post something stupid on the course discussion board. I don't like to think of my professors as hot, but since it's already been pointed out, I'd have to concur.

He's great w/ Japanese policy/government and covering topics re: new democracies. And yes, he the hottest prof. I've had at Cal. I took two of his classes, partly b/c of the subject matter and partly b/c hes fun to look at.
Vogel is amazingly hot.  I actually recommend you don't take the class because it's easy to become distracted by his looks and forgetful of what he's saying.  With that said, you've been warned!
1) Best looking professor I've had at Cal.   2) Remembers your name (even tho I went to class less than 5 x). 3) Interesting context. 4) Overall, a good class to take (better than BAXXX)
This class is fun! The professor is hot, and he goes through material thoroughly. He's also very smart, and he has a lot to teach his students. Yay!!!
Best Professor I had at Berkeley. Learnes student's names and treats his students like they have ideas that matter.  Enthusiastic about teaching. Take his classes!
gives VERY easy to understand lectures, (almost too easy) makes an effort to get to know and help students- but dresses like and deep down wants to be a wall-street millionaire.
He's a good professor.  One of the few professors that can take dense readings like Marx and clarify with crystal clear lectures.

Great teacher with intriguing insight on issues. The class is enjoyable in many different ways, especially in the later sections (after the midterm). Suggestions - do NOT fall behind in the reading, do ALL the postings on time, and GO TO HIS OFFICE hours. Vogel is friendly, intelligent, fun and HOT!
Learns students names, well-prepared, over-all good person.  Listens to what students have to say. Very helpful.
No Comments

Wonderful guy who genuinely cares about the subject he's teaching. Maybe not the easiest class for a freshman, I put more time into this 2 unit class than Data 8, but I also learned a lot more from it. Office hours are extremely useful, can basically check your answers there. Ample resources to do well if you try.
super fun and easy class. no midterm, no final, only weekly labs and a few projects (formatted as a longer lab). attendance is mandatory but lectures are engaging and interesting

Mandatory attendance but lectures weren't super useful, most learning was through labs. This class is super easy if you've taken Data 100 before or at the same time, but I imagine pretty difficult if you haven't. Serves as good extra practice for Data 100. Labs every week, experimented with computer lab midterm, and NO FINAL only a group project.

Professor Eric is a good lecturer, and Data 88E is a relatively easy class. However, one downside is that attendance is required, meaning students have to go to the lecture hall just for the sake of attendance.
Wonderful.

Data 88E was a nice two-unit course providing a survey of economics and its intersection with Pythonic data science. I found myself learning new things without ever having to work too hard or take focus away from other classes. Van Dusen (+ guest) gives good lectures, and I enjoyed covering a different economic topic every week. Would recommend!

I got a good grade with an R background and going to office hours. I ended up using the textbook a lot and attending GSI office hours to help with the labs and projects (with the goal of finishing the labs in OH).

Take this class if you want to be a research assistant and use economic data and data science. They had great speakers come too!

Professor Wong is a knowledgeable professor. I have to admit that her topic choice is interesting, but her teaching style is somewhat disorganized. When you are trying to refelect of what you learnt, you can't think of a thing. I don't think she cares about the student. She is mean to students and unwilling to provide help with mockery.

Winnie Wong hate will not be tolerated here. Her lectures used the most fun and interesting analogies so it was easy to stay engaged. She's funny in a cynical way, and gives interesting lectures! Her class is reading heavy but interesting, and as long as you read and show up to class the exams aren't really all that bad. Literally bare minimum.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The course is poorly structured, and the professor relies heavily on slides without offering clear explanations. Questions are met with vague answers, and outside guidance is minimal. Exams lack clear focus, and feedback is insufficient, leaving students uncertain about expectations and how to improve.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: prof. wong does great at making an intro class' diverse subjects + readings comprehensive & interlinked. can be strict but put in effort & u will be fine. this semester i had a crisis about my major & went to her OH & she was very patient yet direct with me & got me to the core of the issue in 5 minutes. so well spoken with a dry sense of humor.

prof wong's rating here is fairly unjust. personally, i rlly loved this class and her! if you don't like rhetoric/theory/anticapitalist critique, this class isn't for you. but the reality is her syllabus is pretty standard for rhetor & i LOVED her as a lecturer. she's funny, engaging & makes interesting connections to her own research background.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: class overall doesn't make much sense. Tries to tie things together but fails. A lot of the readings are just word garbage and lecture doesn't clarify. Hard class and a difficult environment overall. Take if you're an intended rhetoric major but if not steer clear.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I wanted to like this course but the professor is very condescending and down right offensive at times. Early on in the semester she told the class we were about bunch of nazis if we couldn't pay attention to a six minute video of awful music. The topics are interesting but not feeling comfy makes it hard to really take an interest in the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Do not take this class. Not very encouraging when prof starts the class by saying she doesn't understand the material, either. Readings are trash, incoherent, same with lectures. A- range is 90-94.99, wtf. She doesn't share lectures but they don't make any sense anyways. Only good part are the GSIs, they're decent. Do not take this!

I personally really liked this class. I thought her lectures were interesting and informative. There was a lot of reading that was required as well as graded annotations, but I found all of the readings to be very interesting. She is a very hard grader, but she makes her expectations pretty clear. I really enjoyed all the papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Prof. Wong is entertaining & engaging. There is a lot of reading & perusall annotations are the worst. Sometimes her instructions for the writing assignments are unclear & it feels like she adjusts the grading criteria per each student. Super interesting class, but tough grader & she has high expectations for an undergrad class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Gave daily graded reading assignments on Perusall. Lectures were informative and engaging with good visual aids. Was dismissive of students' questions sometimes and often gave unconstructive, sometimes mean, criticism.

Her lectures are the most boring things you will ever listen to. The homework is all tedious perusal annotating. Not to mention the fact that she assigns homework over holidays and breaks. She also will tank your grade if you get sick and cannot attend her class. Miss 4 classes and you will be dropped a full letter grade, no joke.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This class is so so so interesting and organized in such a compelling way. Brings up many ideas you wouldn't be introduced to elsewhere. I would definitely recommend. Only issue was we have to use Perusall and read a lot. You have to read to get the most out of the lectures. She is a great (& chic!) professor who pushes students to really think.

I completely hate this class, as it turns something enjoyable into a bore. I wish I knew her absurd grading system, so I could drop. She relies heavily on assistance, mandates pre-class readings/comments. Honestly, I dont think I'm learning a single thing in this class, the content is useless and the excessive readings, including during holidays.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Funny and thought provoking lectures, some stuff factually incorrect or not entirely accurate, liked her until she essentially called my class morons to all of us
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Wong is spectacular. Her lectures are sharp, well-prepared and thought-provoking. While it is one of the harder classes I've taken at Cal, it is the most rewarding by far. But if you're really worried about grades, I suggest PNP-ing the class or auditing it because the material is so interesting you won't want to miss it.

definitely reading heavy and reading content may be complex but there are resources like youtube where you can access broken down versions of the readings which make the class more managable! prof. wong was so kind and i love the way she lectures by tying in the past, present and future within one concept. class is def worth the work! gr8 class!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She always had something negative to say. "This generation doesn't understand music." "The girls in this generation use Halloween as an excuse to be XYZ..." reviews.comment: I love this guy! Great discussions and very little outside work besides reading - so chill! This class (freshman seminar) was my favorite of the semester!

AMERSTD10. Syllabus poorly structured and unorganized. Course had no clear grading rubric; grading done entirely by GSIs and extremely subjective. GSIs were stingy and loved to withhold a 10/10 for every discussion post. Essay (worth 45%) was graded based on an English class and not purely based on history. No way to redeem missed points.

reviews.comment: My favorite class!!! Tons of fun. The seminar felt like a little family getting together and talking about our love for literature. Participating was important and super easy to do. I enjoyed this class so much. Such a refreshment from my other classes. Great professor! Really cares. Nothing but good things to say about this course and professor.

I highly recommend Professor Wagner! He makes class enjoyable with his humor, and gives his students affirmations when we give our impressions of literature and class themes. Though class is usually spent in lecture, Wagner is well-prepared and provides amazing contextual information to support AND ENHANCE one's understanding of course matters.

My favorite professor in Berkeley's English department. Every lecture is insightful and inspirational, classes were always a highlight of my day. He's an incredibly kind and welcoming professor too. You will have to put in the work, but it's very possible to get an A, and definitely worth it to take a class with him. Highly recommend!
Professor Wagner is wonderful. He was passionate and knowledgeable about subjects we discussed in class. Be prepared to read and write a lot!

reviews.comment: This class was great. We read multiple books that pertain to law and lit (all available online). The professor was great, passionate, and insightful. 3 timed reflections about certain passages in the books, close readings to prepare for final essay, the final essay was 14-16 pages (just prepare), and a time final exam essay. The GSI was great too.

I took Prof. Wagner for a Freshman Seminar and he was brilliant. He always had intelligent things to say, was great at facilitating discussion, always willing to talk outside of class, and overall a kind, wonderful professor!

Highly recommend! Professor Wagner is so caring and knowledgeable, and he is one of my favorite professors at Cal! I took three of his classes and loved them all! The grading structure is slightly unusual because it is primarily based on essays for which he provides no prompts- the student is entirely responsible for deciding the topic.

Doesn't get a 5 because the course was disorganized (the syllabus changed about 4 times). Very frustrating. Bryan is very passionate, knowledgeable and will answer any questions you have. Class consisted of a group presentation, 2 essays, and 2 exams(in-class essays). Do 70% of the readings and you will be fine. Essays have no prompts!

Prof. Wagner is both engaging and encouraging. Class discussions are open, just participate. Very knowledgeable, will take the time to explain concepts. He invites arguments and other point of views instead of shutting it down. Take him. He's one of the professors (among many) that know what it was like to not know everything. Helpful. Available.

Professor Wagner has earned his spot as my favorite professor so far at UC Berkeley. Not only is he intelligent, thoughtful and charismatic, gives clear instructions, is a fair grader, and seems to truly care about his students. I would take him again in a heartbeat!

Clear and informative lectures. Fantastic at leading open discussion and pushing students on ideas without calling out mistakes in a mean way. Good feedback before writing but it is hard to read his handwriting on papers.
Brilliant lectures. Really listens to students in discussion and gives good feedback on your ideas. Helpful in office hours.

Humble, kind and open to ideas, even the ones in opposition to him. Readings: doable, don't sweat it. Midterm and final: show up, pay attention to discussions and you'll do great on finals and midterms. Participate in class discussions. Office hours: super helpful. Aside from his good teaching, he is a good person, get to know him.
He was really cool!!!!

Really chill, yet intellectually, engaging class. His lectures were very insightful, precise and you could tell he had a passion for what he was talking about. In the class, we watched films that connected race and ethnicity with American Culture. Just two major papers and a take-home final. He has regular office hours and is willing to help.

Very sweet guy. Lectures are typically insightful, but he likes to devote lots of time to the context of the films, which occasionally got boring. The class overall was very easy - two papers and a very straightforward take-home final. Not a lot of work during the semester - mostly just watching 1 film per week. No textbook!

This class has a ridiculous work load—particularly for a mandatory AC class. He requires 800 words each week, plus two papers and written essay tests. The films he chooses are not necessarily the best available examples, and independent films such as "Night of the Living Dead" and "El Norte" are hardly "Hollywood Films." Avoid this professor.
Wonderful professor. Casual style of teaching. He speaks really well. I would recommend any class of his.
Chooses favorites. He's ok. He's friendly but I don't like his teaching style. Not very professional.

This was the first upper-div English class I took and I couldn't have asked for anything better. Not only is Wagner intelligent, he is also extremely approachable and aware of his students' needs. He encourages discussion and grades essays fairly. The workload is a bit much, but I plan to take another of his classes because he's just that good.

Wagner does his papers differently from every other professor. He's emphasizes creating good questions. In a way, the question is more important than your paper. It's annoying to have to relearn how to write papers, especially in your last semester. Also, you make up your own final. Good professor, but definitely different to everyone else.

One of the best classes I've taken at Cal. Lots of work, but very much worth it. You learn a lot of interesting history too. It is important to talk almost every day in class, so keep that in mind. You pretty much have to keep up with the reading, but it isn't too heavy. Grades fairly, helpful in OH. Wonderful prof and class, highly recommended.

Bryan Wagner is by far the most inspiring professor I have had at Cal. His enthusiasm is infectious and one cannot help, but fall in love with him. The reading and workload are light and the texts he chooses are far more interesting than in any of the other 10 English classes I have taken, although a little depressing. Take him! He grades fairly.

bryan is the best professor i've had in 7 semesters at berkeley.  he's engaging, makes relevant points in discussion, and helps his class really get into the text.  he's also overwhelmingly kind and understanding of stress and other class' assignments and enormously helpful in office hours.  take him if at all possible.

Bryan's a brilliant professor with a passion for literature. He's excellent with stimulating intriguing class discussions and provides relevant information to enhance the material. He's so nice and friendly, especially in office hours. There's a lot of work, but he's helpful with explaining what's expected. Any class with Bryan is an absolute must!

Bryan acts low key, but he is absolutely unbelievably brilliant. There is a mix of lectures and discussion. If you take a class with him, you will learn a ton, but be aware that he expects a lot on papers, including some historical research and background.

brian is one of the best seminar leaders ive ever had the pleasure of learning from. he barely leads anything if the class is engaged..he focuses discussions to make it more clear as to what is being thrown out to be taken in. ask to see his scales of justice dance  it was hilarious. i strongly suggest you take this professor: be ready to have fun.

Bryan is absolutely the best professor ever! He's able to successfully translate his passion for literature to his students. He leads great class discussions and offers valuable insight into the material. And no surprises on tests/papers! He's very helpful and personable in office hours--go talk to him, even if it's just to continuing discussion!
Bryan is, in a word, awesome. Very approachable, great lecturer, great discussion leader. Take his class. You won't regret it.
Bryan is very enthusiastic and makes his discussions interesting by letting the students come up with the topics to debate each day.

I took his senior seminar on Black Vernacular, and thought it was one of the best seminars ever.  The only hard part about his grading is that your grade is based almost entirely on your final research paper.  Not bad though, ended up getting an A- in his class.  Also, he's really personable in office hours-go talk to him!

If you care to break free from the classicks or the modernist hype, take B Wagner's class and get your English degree's perspective widened a bit. Bryan is totally well-read in AF-AM literature and loves the Blues. He digs culture in general and can open up some sightlines to an array of perspective. One thing is certain: BW's class will not suck!

Bryan is my white chocolate brother! He's very understanding and flexible. I was intimidated at first because I fear that all young proffesors are gonna be d*cks because they are so fresh and happy with their career, but Bryan turned out to be one of the coolest professors i've ever taken, EVER!
Actually learned how to make a map here!
Take her version of this course!

This guy makes Chemistry all about Physics essentially and yet he doesn't utilize the blackboard or his writing pen stylus to teach us actual examples on how to solve question.

Ke Xu is a pretty bad lecturer, yes he makes jokes every now and again but his lectures are still long, monotonous, and often overcomplicated. Best advice is to pay attention as much as you can, but review all material online or with GSIs.

Professor Xu's lectures were very intense. Lots of information was packed into lecture and concepts were not explained the best. His midterm and section of the final was extremely difficult compared to the homework and what was explained in lecture.

Lecture were a bit boring and he expected students to memorize multiple equations for his exams. Very concept heavy, you must understand each equation and their relationships to each other. LOTS of different topics in the last section of the class, which made it difficult to keep up with all the content.

Ke Xu is a very cute wholesome man. He tricked me into believing his half of the course would be as manageable as Zuerch's portion of the course. I was WRONG. So bad. Avoid at all costs. You have to know EVERY single detail on all the slides to do well in class. Concept heavy.
Great professor in general. Be prepared for difficult exams.
lectures are super boring. concepts are not incredibly hard, but the lectures dont reflect problem sets and exams. he is funny sometimes tho
