Dr. Zehlia is one of the most amazing professors I've had at UC Berkeley. She is extremely knowledgable in linguistics and culture. If you didn't already know shes a polyglot and is well-traveled. I could relisten to her lectures for fun because she's so enthusiastic and is one of those professors who actually loves what they do. Don't think twice.

The readings are relevant and enlightening and the amount of guest lecturers gives one a diverse knowledge of Applied Linguistics, and she's so receptive to class feedback that any real issues are taken care of before they get serious. She's awesome.

Professor Babaci-Wilhite is an exceptional instructor, she presents herself in a professional manner, but is also friendly and approachable, ready to assist a student if need be. She utilizes academic articles, books, and lectures, all of which are significant and are intended to give the student information they need to succeed. A great course.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Would take again

reviews.comment: Dr. Zehlia Babaci-Wilhite loves to teach and cares for her students.

Dr Babaci-Wilhite led the graduate seminar and assigned a variety of scholarly articles or book chapters that we could download using bCourses. Students had the chance to present their own research and improve their presentations due to her excellent feedback. The best part about the readings were that they were all RECENT research-based findings.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Would take again

reviews.comment: This professor makes interdisciplinary course material useful and discussions enlightening for student learning. She welcomes a diversity of perspectives and encourages everyone to think critically and reflectively about complex, relevant issues. She is genuinely responsive to individual needs and shared interests. An objective, supportive mentor.

This was a wonderful, dynamic course, with just the right balance of lecture, seminar discussion, and student led content. Prof. was always well prepared, full of enthusiasm and great energy, provided access to all the literature, lead great discussions giving real life examples of theory, and was always available for further discussion and help.

The professor was a helpful mediator in the course discussions. As a graduate-level course, I deeply treasured the interdisciplinary perspectives she brought in, which effectively widened our understanding of related fields, as well as context-specific knowledge. The course was also flexibly organized, as participation was welcome at any points.
one of those classes you just look forward to every week. highly recommend

Zook is cool and all but definitely overrated. His essay prompts are convoluted and confusing and are a huge pain to write. the other assignments in class are easy. Its impossible to get in contact with him via email as well. He also has a huge ego because practically everyone worships him as the greatest professor of all time
ZOOK IS THE GOAT.
I genuinely enjoyed this class so much, lectures are engaging and interesting, you do have to attend in person since they aren't recorded but do it!
Amazing Professor. Zook is funny, smart, and very engaging. Best lectures ive had at Berkeley. Class is not too hard at all, and you really learn alot.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Zook's reputation as one of the best Political Science professors at Berkeley is so deserved. I have NEVER enjoyed a PS class this much! The lectures are genuinely so engaging that it's as if he's telling a story, not just teaching. Prof. Zook's class reminded me why I love learning in the first place!

He's a really fun teacher and you can tell that he really enjoys this topic. Unfortunately, he doesn't record the lectures so, even though attendance isn't mandatory, you literally will suffer if you don't go to them. Reading is crucial and there's an 8-page research paper at the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took Prof Zook's seminar on Identity, Diversity, and Social Justice this spring. He encourages participation and will respectfully play Devil's advocate to show students the other side of the argument. His seminar provided a safe space for us to rant abt today's administration and the like. Very personable professor!

Look was an amazing professor, if not he was the best professor I had at Berkeley. I respect his passion and work every class. Even when he lectures he has personal stories of every country he has visited and studied its politics and culture. If you fail this class then thats on you because he was a really easy class to take and very entertaining.

Hands down the best Political Science class at Cal. Can't recommend Professor Zook enough, especially if it's your first semester. The only class where you actually do not want to miss the lectures. Take him!

Although the course felt more like political history instead of a comparative political study, Zook was an incredible lecturer that helped me understand pressing political issues for each of the countries spotlighted in the course. The assignments, which include two incredibly easy online tests and two papers are very simple if you attend lecture.

Professor Zook is phenomenal, and the lectures are so incredible that they will leave you astonished, shaken, and humbled (if not stirred). My only complaint about this course is that it eventually ended, which was a very somber day, to put it bluntly. I strongly encourage EVERYONE (including non-political science majors) to take this course!
The only class that you do not want to end. Seriously.

Darren Zook is an awesome professor, his classes are educational and fun. He knows what he teaches and he is well prepared. Easy to communicate and he is always there to support his students regarding assignments, advise, and letters of recommendation. Best class and professor at UCB.

Professor Zook has been my favorite professor at Cal! His lectures are super engaging and interesting, and not too much reading. There are two large papers, an easy map quiz, and fairly simple final exam (easy if you payed attention in lectures). Overall great class!

The kindest man. Very talented at breaking down complex matters into approachable, interesting content. Ask questions, he likes that! Go to open office hours and engage! Super approachable especially in Open Office hours, very down to earth. Highly recommend, class is amazing and so is he!

Very passionate teacher and engaging during lectures. Class consists of a midterm paper and a final paper. There is also an easy A guaranteed vocab quiz and an online, open-note final where you might have to look over the slides if you didn't attend lecture. There might seem like a lot of reading but you really don't have to keep up with it.

He is such a great professor who cares about his students. The only homework was readings, and exams were online, open notes. He makes the subject fascinating and incorporates humor into his lectures. Definitely recommend him and hope to take another class with him!

Nice guy, passionate about his class. Took his seminar class which had lots of leftist discourse. I had more moderate views on given topics so it sometimes was hard to give my input without sounding like I was constantly disagreeing. Still, all opinion's were respected by professor even when controversial. Show up and participate and you will pass

Zook is, without a doubt, one of the most compassionate, hilarious, and knowledgeable instructors at Cal. I took the class because I met some people at a national park who still remembered the class a decade later. Very very chill grading and one of those class where you will be on the edge of your seat during lecture (esp the Malaysia lectures!)

Hilarious professor, engaging lectures on a boring subject. one midterm paper, one final paper, online multiple choice final, one extremely easy quiz taken for credit. An easy class, with an A guaranteed if you do well on the papers. Take Zookster!

Lectures were nice because they were 50/50 droning/answering questions from the class, where he would show his happy personality. The paper source requirements are awful and he didn't give us an explicit guide. He expects you to be a prospective law student. Test answers are all from lecture and readings so if you miss a couple it's kind of over.

I have taken two classes with Professor Zook and in both classes, I had nearly perfect grades until the grades for the final paper were released which very negatively impacted my grades in the courses.  He releases the grades for the final papers at the end of finals week and then does not respond to any emails surrounding grades.

Zook is by far one of the most engaging lecturers I have had at Cal, and I learned so much in this class. I was genuinely excited to come to class every day. However, assignments were graded EXTREMELY harshly for how good reported grades are, and the class felt more like a history class than political science at times. Doesn't respond to emails.

I won't deny the obvious as this would be unfair. Professor Zook is the best lecturer I have ever had. His classes are talk shows and when my girlfriend came to visit, I brought her to class so that she could see the magic for herself. Yet, I have found grading harsh and I have never managed to get an email answer from him.

Best class I've taken thus far - lectures were inspirational and easily digestible. Lectures were also given as if a soap opera which made it extremely interesting to listen to. Graded on very few things (2 papers, map quiz) so can be as involved/attend as much as you want, and are rewarded for doing so, but not punished for not attending
map quiz(20%),2 papers(30%) and 1 final exam(20%). There is not a lot of reading, as long as you work hard, you can get good grades.

Professor Zook is one of my favorite professors so far at Berkeley! He presents the topics in such an interesting way that sometimes lectures don't feel like 1 hour and 30 mins. He is really funny too and always tries to find a way to make students laugh. Very accommodating and homework and readings arent too bad. Two papers and an online final.

Bro made me believe in good people. He is a phenomenal lecturer; you WILL learn about the topic in class and you will have fun doing so (shock! who knew learning could be fun!!) He is so knowledgeable, understanding, and humble. Will think about this class far beyond my time at Berkeley and to say that his class is a must-take is an understatement.

Professor Zook is by far my favorite professor here at Berkeley. He cares about his students and accommodates with deadlines. Your grade is made up of an online final exam, a midterm essay, and a final essay. His lectures are very engaging and leaves you on a cliff hanger that makes u want to show up to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lectures are super interesting and informative and he's hilarious! He engages with the students and always extends the deadlines for the essays. Theres also only 2 papers, an exam and a map quiz for the course.100% recommend his class, great guy fr !

Zook is an engaging lecturer, very accommodating when it comes to assignments and exams. Clearly passionate about what he teachers and is open to student questions. Readings are light, 1-2 articles/week. Wants students to succeed and not stress. Felt very lucky to take his class in my first semester here at Cal.
Funny and interesting content. Every class should be like this
Fun, charismatic lecturer. Class is very very easy but you learn a lot about the region just by showing up. Would have been nice to have more readings to go in more depth.

Zook is an amazing professor with so much passion for what he teaches! The lectures were interesting and engaging and really taken to a new level because of how much he cares. The material does not go too quickly, there were 2 papers, and the workload was very manageable. Take notes to succeed on the papers! Take this class, it was great!

Light workload, 20-30 pp readings per week, one midterm paper and one final research paper. Lectures are amazing for those who are unfamiliar with SEA. He covers 4 SEA countries in depth each semester, and has recorded bonus lectures for several other countries too. His lectures reshaped my understanding of comparative politics. Take it if you can!

Before this class, I wasn't remotely interested in SE Asia. However, Zook changed that with his hilariously creative approach to teaching. Unfortunately, regarding deadlines, Zook couldn't practice what he preached. Namely when he pushed back against paper extensions while allowing his readers to take their time in grading past the grade deadline.

Zook is so beloved, I was shocked to find he's non-engaging, disorganized, and inaccessible. Don't let his cartoonish voice fool you; lectures are actually dry and dumbed-down--we all felt like kindergarteners. Lectures, readings and assignments have zero correlation. GSIs graded the first paper extremely harshly, and final grades were haphazard.

One of the best professors I've had at Cal! He gave us the prompts/topics for the midterm and final from the start and gave us weeks before each paper was due for "skill-building modules" where he told us exactly what he expected from the paper as well as writing advice. He really wants you to succeed and grades really fairly.

My favorite professor ever, I love all of his classes so much, his lectures are always so interesting and boost my mood for the whole week. I always look forward to them. Third class I took with him, I hope to take more. Also he's definitely the funniest professor at Berkeley, he's always got jokes to tell during lectures.

Favorite professor of all time & the sweetest person on the planet, he makes everything fun and always has jokes and fun stories for every lecture. He always makes sure students know they can come see him (and his extensive collection of imported japanese kitkats) at any time. I always get excited when I have room to take one of his classes.

Great professor that had very interesting, engaging lectures and cared for the wellbeing of his students. Lectures aren't recorded tho, he only gives recordings from 2020 zoom lectures. Grade is only a midterm and a final paper based on readings, very manageable but grading can be kinda tough so try to do ur best on them.

The Zookster is one of a kind! Without a doubt one of the funniest and most enjoyable Professor's I've ever had. Lectures were just as fun and engaging as they were informative. If you show up to lecture, keep up with readings, and put effort into your essays, there's an A waiting for you! Only downside is he wasn't very available for office hours.

A good professor who tries to make the classroom fun - also easiest PoliSci class I've ever taken, a 4-page midterm paper and a 6-page final paper are the only assignments for the whole semester. Interesting content too. However, he rubbed me the wrong way and was difficult to deal with when I got sick, and was super rude during office hours.

I loved this class so much. You can tell he loves what he's teaching about and he's extremely passionate about the topics. Such an inspirational individual who can merge his experiences with the coursework in a humble way.
not the easiest GPA booster class, avoid if you want an easy A but class is super cool and informative!

ily zook. so intellectual and a genuinely good human being. so are his GSIs. paper heavy (grade2 papers, participation in discussions), same structure as AP history DBQs and I thought they ez. OH are AMAZING, definitely go. It's like 10 other ppl all vibing w zook, getting Qs answered & just asking his input on extra unrelated fun topics.

Everything you hear about him is true - amazing professor and a must take for any Poli Sci major at Cal. Lectures are entertaining and inspirational, even if you aren't interested in the topic. To make things even better, his class was the easiest PS class I've ever taken, both in terms of workload and grading. Take his class, you won't regret it!

Professor Zook tried his best to make the lecture videos engaging despite it being completely asynchronous. The content was interesting to learn. He wasn't as transparent with his grading, though, and he probably won't be available via email if you have questions about those. Despite this, the content of his teaching was good.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Zook is one of the best professors I've had during my time at Berkeley! He is not only knowledgable in his field but also very accommodating for students' needs and has a caring heart. He creates a warm environment for students to feel comfortable asking questions or bringing up concerns. Take Global C10A!

Darren Zook was very nice and accommodating this semester. He made changes to his grading policies and was flexible with due dates. I do wish, however, that he would have been more clear with assignment expectations because he made it hard to find out what I needed to improve on. He never returned our last paper so I have no idea what I did wrong.

Prof Zook has been one of my favorite profs at Cal! He is engaged and loves the course material which makes you love it, intern. Lectures are interesting and informative. I had no interest in South East Asia prior to this course and now I'm going there after graduation!

This is my favorite class Ive taken at Berkeley so far. The online lectures are brilliant, both in terms of production and content. I genuinely looked forward to watching them. Readings are short and informative and papers are graded fairly. You will not regret taking 149E with Professor Zook.

Professor Zook is the most compassionate and relatable professor I have had at UC Berkeley to date! While the limited number of assignments can be intimidating (a midterm paper, final exam, and "map quiz" (which is an easy A), his lectures are super engaging! The array of topics you cover sparks good/engaging dialogue that helps you with papers :)
Prof Zook is amazing. He's funny and really knows his stuff. Take him - you won't regret it!

I LOVE Zook! I took Global 10a Sp2019 with him which inspired me to be a GS major. He often teaches through stories and examples that are connected to larger themes (really engaging). Took 10b with him last semester (also great). You're mostly graded on a MC midterm and 2 or 3 essays (based on broad prompts that allow for creativity/exploration).

Zook was a very caring professor and a great lecturer. There were not too many assignments for the course and our grades were based on three assignments. An in-class midterm that was actually very easy and two papers about 6-8 pg's each. Zook does not upload his lectures and does not allow you to use laptops in class, so attendance is necessary.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Loved Zook, wish I could take another one of his classes. Real class act.

Professor Zook had interesting and engaging lectures, however I disliked that he was unclear for the 2nd paper, so a lot of people didnt do well on it and it made it difficult to recover with the final paper. We were graded on only a midterm and two papers. I did well on the midterm and final paper, but the 2nd paper dropped my grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Amazing lectures--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Zook's lectures were really entertaining and made me actually like going to class. The only thing I didn't like about the class was how unclear he was about what he wanted in papers. Besides that, we had one midterm test that was more like a quiz which wasn't horrible, just poorly worded.

Zook engages students and cares a LOT about subject matter, making lecture entertaining and great to attend. There is one midterm and two essays, with fewer readings than most PolSci classes. Didn't like how grading is done on a 5-point scale, so mistakes are costly (i.e. you go from a 90 to an 85). Otherwise, it's a great and one-of-a-kind class!

The class was great until I got my grade back for the midterm essay. I worked so hard on that thing... and I get a C? Each section of the rubric was docked five points and not even explained why. I don't recommend this class if you need to boost your GPA... Zook is hard to reach outside of class and does not respond to emails.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Zook is an awesome lecturer. His stories are super entertaining and he integrates them really well into the material. While the class seems very relaxed, exams and essays are graded pretty tough. Regardless I'd recommend the class to any Cal student.

I was disappointed. I had high hopes based on the hype, but this class is really overrated. Did I get a basic intro to SE Asia out of it? Yes. But I felt this was a very superficial kind of learning experience... it was all easy breezy, jokes, and fun until the essays which were graded SO harshly with little help. I felt kind of duped.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Its scary how different Darren is when you interact with him one on one versus how he portrays himself to be in lecture. In lecture, its all corny jokes and smiles. But one on one, hes awkward, cold, short, and unencouraging. Seeing through the facade made his lectures feel really inauthentic and uncomfortable.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Best prof I've had at Berkeley. Lectures are informative, and engaging and the way he gives them makes the class fun. There is a decent amount of reading, but not too much. The material is very lecture-based and he doesn't post lecture slides online so attendance is HIGHLY recommended, but not mandatory.

Zook is the pop music of UC Berkeley lecturers. Though engaging, his class is extremely easy. This may be great for those taking a breath class, or people who prefer to spend college partying on Wednesday nights, but for a person serious about Global Studies, not so much. At times, Zook seemed more worried about amusing his students than teaching.

Greatest teacher I've ever had. He is wise, but also personable which inspires his whole class to want to learn. He allows students to give their views, then works with them to expand their perspectives on the world. He is funny, quick, and will make sure that you leave each class wanting to think & engage w/ the world. I'll miss this class!

I gave Zook a 5 because he deserves it. He is amazing. His lectures are funny/entertaining. He's extremely knowledgeable. I really looked forward to going to class. BUT I have a bad taste in my mouth from his class because of his readers. They graded so harshly, I couldn't believe it. Ruined my experience. One easy midterm and then two papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The first professor that I write a comment on. Super hilarious!!Be ready to laugh a lot! Zook is very knowledgeable, professional, and interdisciplinary. Lectures are eye-opening and inspiring. A light weekly reading workload. A very easy midterm , more like a 15-minute quiz. No final exam, only a 8-page final paper, which takes time and efforts.

I love this professor! He genuinely cares about how much you learn, no redundant midterms and readings. Talk to him outside of class, he's done a ton of interesting research and is really accessible. Do the readings, they aren't necessary for lecture but will make a huge difference in your discussion participation grade. Wish I could take again!

149E in Hearst Field Annex was hellacious. Pouring sweat listening to a lecture that should take 45 min. not 90. Power points are not available and consist of lazy bullet points that help the lecturer more so than the student. Gsi's were unwelcoming, adversarial, and had a negative vibe. Grading is based off of a vague rubric. Overrated...
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Was incredibly helpful and addressed all discrepancies students had trouble comprehending! Also very well organized when it comes to his lectures, which made them that much more engaging. HIGHLY recommended!

Prof. Zook is a very entertaining lecturer and gives good insight into many of the subjects of the class. However, PS 149E can feel like a shallow dive at times, though that may be a product of the sheer volume of interesting material on each country. First midterm is easy, second can be tough if you begin late as can the final.

My favorite class this semester! Zook is a hilarious and engaging lecturer. I didn't know much about the subject before, but he explains everything so well. I'm taking a class w him next semester b/c he's THAT awesome! Grading is super easy- he just wants you to learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Zook's classes are highly sought after for a reason. He is incredibly knowledgeable and is able to present even the most sobering topics in an interesting, entertaining, or memorable manner. To be honest your GSI makes or breaks your grade for this class. Great class for anyone regardless of their major.
He prefers students to know a little bit of material WELL instead of a lot of material poorly. Very manageable coursework therefore, which made the class really enjoyable.

Amazing professor! one of the most entertaining, engaging, and understanding professor I have met so far. Lectures are amazing and the course load is doable. He is one of those teachers that does not drill you with immense reading and essays, yet you still get to learn so much.

Uncomfortable seating arrangement in class (you still get marked down if you don't attend), GSI grading rubric no one understands and a nice general email at end of semester telling you it's not application of course material that matters, its 15-20 hours of learning how to write a paper. At Soviet Cal you don't mess with agenda, it messes with you

Took pacs 10 at 6pm, do well on your take home essays and final and you will do fine, show up to your discussion because thats where ur attendance grade comes from, amazinggg lecturer will take again !
Zook is amazing and is wonderful for discussing current events. The freshman seminar was very enlightening and basically student led.
Grading based on GSIs. Amazing individual and lecturer!

Professor Zook was amazing; I would love to have him as a professor again. I wasn't too interested in the subject, but he made it interesting, and I never once zoned out during his lectures (which would be incredible even if I was fascinated with the subject). He's witty and kind, and you can tell he's passionate about what he does.

Surprised he's a professor, class doesn't really consist of much learning/material. He tries to be funny/keep the class engaged, but it just comes off as trying too hard in my opinion. The class seems pretty much like a medium for Zook to show off that he's been to a lot of places around the world and not much teaching about human rights.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Zook is a phenomenal professor. His engaging lectures are enlightening and sprinkled with his cute sense of humor. He knows how to balance heavier topics of political corruption with more lighthearted information on civil society. Definitely would take him again. He's amazing. 2 5-page midterms and 1 8-page research paper.

This is my 2nd class I've taken with Zook, after taking PACs 10 last year. He has an energetic and captivating way of teaching. I never wanted to miss his lectures. He has a way of making you learn with realizing you're learning. He'll inspire passion for the subject within you. The first midterm is a trip though because it seems easier than it is.

Loved everything about this course, from his lecture style to his helpfulness in OH. I had no interest in SEA before taking this course, but his lectures always engaged me. Essays are easy A's if you meet with him or the GSI consistently.

The freshman seminar, PACS 24 Diversity and Identity was so incredible. Prof. Zook moderated our weekly discussions with his great wisdom and made the class have an easy workload so we could focus on engaging in great conversations.  This was only a one unit seminar, but I would recommend Zook for any class!
Such an enlightening and inspiring course, and useful even if you aren't a political science/global studies major. Will truly shift your paradigm

Excellent prof, made this class so much more interesting and insightful. Highly recommend anyone to take this class. I am an engineering major, and I still thoroughly enjoyed every lecture. Great guy.
Really passionate about his research! So glad I took this class.

Incredible lecturer, really knows his stuff and so eager to share it with you. Super accessible in office hours. Midterms are fair (no tricks!), and marked quickly. You'll never want to skip a lecture!

Zook is a great lecturer. I have hella respect for him, and he has taught me so much about South Asian political climates. Would highly recommend for anyone who is interested in human rights, cares about the world, and came to Berkeley to learn about change-making! Go ZOOK!

The class was a nice introduction class and relatively interesting. Zook is extremely passionate, but it seemed as though he simplified to include a lot of case studies rather than focus on a select few. Grades dependent on GSIs (2 papers, participation, 1 test), just be straightforward in papers, actually pays off more than being creative.

As long as you show up to lectures, do the small amount of reading, and get your GSI to give you the green light on the thesis for each of the three take home essays, you should get an a good grade in this class while also enjoying the material. Zook's lectures are funny and unique, and he tries to makes your life easier. A must take professor.

While Professor Zook is a hilarious and inspiring teacher, the methods in which he and his GSI's grade is not consistent with what's portrayed in class. He spends much of his class re-assuring students that if they follow directions they'll get good marks. However, after spending over 24 hours on my paper, I received a B- on said paper.

Honestly an easy class, but I'm going to go against the grain a little bit here and say I'm not the biggest fan of Zook's lecturing style. The PS 149 lectures were very much a "pop culture" style of lecturing about each area, with constant cliches mentioned regarding celebrities, music, and VERY oversimplified discussions over political science.

Very interesting class. Overall, Zook was very passionate and provided an excellent look into the world of human rights. While the readings and the lectures were both interesting, the professor never really connected the two. Both essay prompts were vague and it was difficult to get clear guidance.
Great class.

If you expect an easy A in this class, sorry to get your hopes up. I've taken southeast asian politics and international human rights with him.  His lectures are interesting but I wish he would put more content on his slides.  As far as grades go, very hard. Class average is usually a B/ B+ He's very nice and always has office hours.
Would definitely take again

Best part: no tests. Just two midterm essays and a final essay. Professor Zook is like a fun uncle who tells terrible/amazing dad jokes. His lectures are never dull and they are incredibly straightforward, not to mention very interesting. It is possible for anyone to do well and enjoy this class.

This is the class I will think of when I think back on my time at Berkeley. His lecture/readings are so well curated - he uses lecture to give you the historical/cultural/current events context behind the readings so that you are much more equipped to tie them together.

Assigns readings that are gone over by GSIs in discussion sections. Also assigns 3 assignments that require students to relate learned concepts to a given prompt (all 3 are take-home essays including mid-term and final). Gives prompt at least 1 week before the essays are due. GSIs grade your essays, and Zook reviews the essays. No quizzes. Easy.

Hands down my favorite professor at Cal. He is hilarious and really cares about engaging with the class. No exams!!!! Only 3 essay assignments that require significant amounts of research, but are graded fairly.

Zook is an awesome professor! He does tend to give rather opinionated lectures, but it is just because he is passionate about the subject matter. Remember that he doesn't expect you to agree, and you should look into issues and formulate your own opinions! Respect the subject matter and you will be fine and have a great time in class

Great lecturer!! Hes very specific on the material and uses case studies to clarify. Need reader for midterm & final. 3 papers, midterm & final are take home & 1 research paper 10pgs he lets you pick the topic. No section. If your interested in human rights than this is highly recommend & if your thinking of law school. Loved his class!!

Zook is super fun, really interesting material. 3 papers for the whole semester and no section, whoot whoot! Makes topics that can be deadly boring into something you really care about. He's very corny and likes to make jokes, but it really helps the mood of the class. Prob the best class I've taken at cal. Great guy, very enthusiastic.

5-page paper midterm, 8-12 page research paper, &a 5-page final paper. No sections. Zook's a nice guy, makes little corny jokes to alleviate inevitable tension one comes across when talking about human rights issues like genocide, trafficking, etc. That being said, you'lll either love this class, or hate how biased the teacher's opinions are.

I really hated his class because he basically shoved his opinions down your throat the whole lecture. Although he is a likable and funny person, he was constantly forcing his views even though he made a point to say he wouldn't do that.

He's awesome. This is the third class I have taken with him and I like it just as much as I liked PACS 10 my first semester at Cal. HE'S awesome and super approachable, his GSIs.... well they leave room for improvement for sure but it's so worth taking anything he teaches.

Cool guy this professor Zook. His lectures were quite interesting. Focuses on a few countries in Southeast Asia. Assignments are pretty easy, GSIs were mainly concerned with HOW your essays were written, it didn't really seem like they cared about the content. Make sure your thesis can argue something and at the very LEAST you'll get a B+.

Zook is a pretty cool guy...corny...as ever, but cool enough. I didn't think I'd have any interest in this class at all, but! surprisingly it turned out to be my favorite of the semester. The reason was because of how he presents the info. 3 assignments. All Essays. If you write/structure well then that's what the GSIs care about. Give it a shot.

Prof. Zook is the most awesome prof. in Berkeley probably. He is very lenient. He is also extremely passionate about what he teaches about, he's a very confident professor, also he has a lot of background knowledge. DEFINITELY take a class with him! You will not regret it!!!

DARREN ZOOK IS AMAZING! He is so passionate about his field of study. His lectures are interesting, up-to-date, and relevant to todays happenings. If you have the opportunity to take his class..DO IT!
Uses power points well and very entertaining. Received helpful advice and learned a lot. Amazing lecturer

Professor Zook is a fantastic professor and I love his class! Siti is a very nice and helpful GSI, the first thing she taught me is to add a closing sentence for each paragraph and explain how does the para. relate to your thesis. The second thing is to have good transitions so the essays flows perfectly. Must go to OH. I got an A in the class.

Pros: Class is enjoyable, fun, interesting, and uses typical lenses to discuss conflicts. Beyond that lens, it also uses art, history, symbolism, music in politics. Cons:the class is driven by 3 essays focusing more on structure than substance, to which you are not given a rubric.Overall: the class is good, but needs a better system of grading.

Fantastic lecturer! Zook is engaging and funny. PACS 10 is an easy course and not particularly mind-blowing, but it's a good introduction into international relations and surprisingly academic. The reader articles are actually interesting, too. Definitely recommend this professor!

Burma, Singapore, and the Philippines are now some of the most interesting cases in the world. Zook provides you information and you can pretty much write on whatever you want (as long as you justify it to the question he provides, or run it by your GSI as an alternative). I was excited writing my last paper on how religion influenced politics.

Zook's lectures are clear, his lectures are interesting, and he easily connects with his audience. His OH have long lines, but he answers all your questions. Regardless of whether you're a social science or a STEM major, this class is worth taking. Just remember that the GSIs can be a little tough and that winging an essay is not a good idea.

I am not sure whats up with all the negativity on the TA's. I got a pretty low grade, but I earned it because I wrote a poor essays. Its almost 2am and Siti just wrote me back advising on my topic. Give her a break, guys. The class is fair. Plus Zook presents information in a unique manner: art, politics, music. its a refreshing take on the field.

Matt was amazing. He was insightful and really helped me put things together. He responded to emails quickly, was bright, and helped me structure my outlines. Great class, Matt was a great GSI! Really enjoyed it!

This class brought unnecessary drama into my semester with constant passive emails, then "i'm sorry." The professor is intelligent & skilled in lectures. The information is interesting, but he doesnt "deliver" anything.The class doesn't have a focus, its just sort of...information.Focus more on the structure of an essay than what the essay says?

Zook was a lot of fun and classes were full of interesting stuff. Readings were fun, dense, but interesting. Essays were pretty straight forward, GSI? She was pretty bad. But if you ignore her and focus on the class, its a great class. If you focus on her, you will probably not enjoy going. Focus on the class, not the GSI

Lectures are fast but crystal clear. GSI Matt was great. Met with him just because he had a lot to say. But my GSI Siti was more of a deterrence than helpful. I hated turning in work to her because it was so poorly graded. But Zook will meet during office hours and discuss the material in detail if you're up for it.

Southeast Asian class was pretty straight forward. Some readings were dry, most were pretty good.I got stuck with GSI who didn't really know what the hell she was doing. B's on my papers, but the comments were generic and unhelpful. One of the better classes at Cal, but be warned: Siti is terrible and you might be better off switching out.
best lecturer that ive had at berkeley. funny, engaging, clear, and he is very well versed on the subject and impresses his passion upon the students well.

Great class. Siti is a HORRIBLE GSI. If you get her, expect unprofessional feedback and incoherent criticism. Gets angry when student want to meet & snaps at them. Told one girl she had too many questions, told another girl she was not going to do well in this class at this point. GSI does not follow rubric....just  sort of scribbles and complains

Prof. Zooks lectures are very clear, direct, and well organized. I enjoyed it very much! Unfortunately he is big on writing good essays. If you write well, you can expect an A... if not, then oh well.

Zook is a cool guy, but I was a bit disappointed in the class. If you want to get a good grade, you have to write well. It doesn't really matter how much of the info you know. The 3 writing assignments were fairly straight forward. The previous person is correct. He does write passive aggressive e-mails. His GSI's were terrible. Over-all good class

Interesting lectures and course material. Though entertaining, Zook treats his students like children, sending out passive aggressive e-mails on due dates that are generally annoying and unnecessary. Easy class, just know how to write an essay.

ok he is a great lecturer, enthusiastic and his classes are fun. but: i always had the feeling that he never went into ANY depth with any particular topic (contrary to the readings) and there are NO tests, only essays, so i ended up not remembering anything of this class after the semester. could do nothing and still get an A, just write well.
fantastic professor

Zook guaranteed my declaring PACS as my major. His class is entertaining and extremely informative. He is a wealth of information but humble enough to tell you when he doesn't know something.  AND, when he asks you to send him the same question via email, he actually gets back to you! Assignments/Essays are very creative.

This class is very fun. The lectures are structured craftily and appropriately. Zook is an engaging teacher, who wants to absolutely convey varying points of view and solid methods for potential change. Cheerful and funny guy.

Zook's a great professor, no question about it. Very enthusiastic, he will go out of his way to make sure that you are entertained in some way, even if the lecture is covering the driest material. Only lecture, no section (but gsi's do grading). Two papers and a research paper. Make sure you get to know your gsi and what they expect of you!

I loved professor Zook! His lectures were always funny and informative and kept me interested throughout. I never missed a lecture. The lectures were very organized with powerpoints everyday so it was easy to take notes. Grade was based on 3 papers, which was slightly intimidating but the topics were interesting and fun to research.

super great professor, very clear, definitely knows what hes talking about, and very approachable during office hours. i kind of got lost in my discussion section but it was always clearer during lecture (backwards no?). anyways i would take any class with him again

Best Professor at Berkeley. Though I never went to office hrs (b/c there was always a long waiting line) I still felt totally connected to him. He is so down-to-earth, SMART, unpretentious, interesting, entertaining. I learned about methodology but I also learned a lot of random info! Like, about the hidden man behind the Beatles!
He is AMAZING! One of the best classes I ever took. Do take the time and take one of his classes. Definitely worth your time.
Zook rocks! He is the best professor I had this semester! I took the papers seriously and did well. Make sure you pick a good GSI. DO TAKE ZOOK! He's awesome!
Best professor I've ever had! Makes the material interesting and really knows what he's talking about.

Great professor. Engaging and funny lecturer. Well rounded knowledge and clearly presented. The attendance to the lectures is not mandatory; however, the discussion section requires attendance. Had a fabulous GSI as well!

Prof Zook is incredible. The class is super clear and interesting. Even with a GSI that isn't stellar i love this class! Work load is very manageable, 2 papers and a final project with about 40 pgs of reading a week. Def take this class with zook!
Professor Zook is amazing !! he really really knows his stuff and the lectures are incredibly interesting

Zook is a wonderful and engaging lecturer who makes you instantly interested in the material. His humor is spot-on and really makes the lectures fun. Grades are based on take-home midterm, take-home final, and research paper. Please ignore the student who clearly posted 7 times in a row. There have never been pop quizzes, that is a complete lie.

Just need to interject because it's obvious the same disgruntled student has posted the 5 or so most recent reviews. Prof. Zook is an outstanding professor, there are NO pop quizzes, there is only ONE research paper and 2 3-5 pagers. If English is your second language like I'm guessing is the case with this other guy, you may struggle.

Fun lectures filled with cheesy jokes and funny videos. I really liked Professor Zook. Hot GSI is a plus. There is a take home midterm and a final, 5 pages each. One long paper, 12-15 pages which is the hardest part of the entire class. All and all decent class.

Zook is an absolutely amazing professor. His lectures are clear, interesting, and very engaging. Even though the class is big, it still feels like a conversation. I would definitely recommend going to office hours, to ask a specific question or just talk in general. PACS 10 is an awesome class and I would recommend it to anyone interested.

SUCH A GOOD PROFESSOR! I find myself referencing facts from his class in almost every conversation I have now. And it's definitely not hard to get an A if you just attend his lectures (which you'll want to anyways)! Not to mention, extremely helpful in office hours. This is the only class I've ever taken where I didn't want the semester to end.

Professor Zook is, hands down, the best professor I've had at Berkeley. His lectures are clear, relevant, and, interesting, and he's not afraid to veer off course a little in order to provide helpful and fun anecdotes or facts. His style of teaching is engaging and his own personal interest in the subject matter is contagious. Take this class!!!

Professor Zook is the coolest! He's so funny and he is so helpful. I went to his office hours and he is so fun to just chat with. His assignments were pretty easy and the reader was interesting. Get a good GSI!! I had Dan he was awesome and he really likes the Congo!

I took mr Zooks 149 southeast asian politics class during the spring and it was extremely difficult and challenging.  He syallabus is wierd because he assigns more reading and exams during the spring than during the fall,  his idea is that the spring should be more difficult since the students are preparing to graduate and need to be challenged mor

Prof Zook is one of those rare professors at Berkeley whose students come first.  His lectures revolve around the material he believes is most relevant to students and teaches in an accesible manner than allows students to absorb material and retain it for years.  His enthusiasm  made my methodology class the favorite class I took that semester.

his powerpoint lectures are clear and well-paced. hes friendly enough but ive got to say... he never returns emails! who does this guy thinks he is? students should come first and to him they dont. (his office hours always have a long line, so good luck.)

I just LOVE Prof. Zook. I can't imagine Berkeley without him. He is one of the best at CAL. Go to class, listen to his interesting lectures, and surley you will succeed. Essays are fun, and he really helps with everything. Vitally, if you want to go to his office hours, go 30 minutes early, so you can see him. Loved him and his class. Best of all..
Best professor I've had so far.

DEFINITELY take this class!! Zook makes any topic he talks about interesting. He's engaging, funny, nice, and really easy. One 5 page midterm, one 12-15 page research paper, one 5 page final (all take home). There's a lot of choice in the assignments too. He shows music vid clips/short vid clips too which just adds to how interesting and fun he is!
Best professor I have EVER taken by far.
over rated professor.
Many lectures can do without but it's an easy class to get an A.  OK teacher.
very funny like a comedian. fun and easy class.

This guy's amazing. He's engaging and vastly intelligent and you can tell he really knows what he's talking about, and he'll communicate that knowledge in a clear and entertaining manner. His class wasn't too hard but it was really effective. Definitely try to take a class from him sometime before you graduate!
Clear and interesting explanations (and jokes).

He was easily the best professor I have taken so far at Cal. He is engaging, very funny, and informative. He makes you love southeast Asia and instills the passion he has for it in you. You will love this class

HE IS AMAZING!!!!!  I looove Professor Zook.  Incredibly interesting class.  Learned tons about SE Asia.  Inspires a passion for the area that makes you really want to learn.  Gives a total education about the culture, current events, history, area conflicts, etc.  Incredible class!  I wish I could take it again!
I loved this class- The Politics of Music. He did cover a lot, but the world is a big place. Learned about politics, struggle , marginalization. Great class.

Professor Zook is a cool guy who can understand the students pretty well.  Take home essays are always nice and I enjoyed how he added music and film clips to the class.  Speaks reallllllly fast sometimes and it is a bother.  some lectures are pointless as well.  i recommend this class and teacher

Great professor- engaging lectures, clear. Need to take good notes, can do readings selectively because midterms and final are take home--you only need to read what you write about. I did well b/c my GSI liked my writing, but not everyone is so lucky. Go to office hours, get to know Zook, and you'll learn a LOT about SE Asia.
He is a very enthusiastic, intelligent professor. He is a world-traveler. He has a fantastic sense of humor and can relate to students. He's great!

Politics of Music- Like others said, way too much information, I wish the class just focused on a few countries or a few genres and was more focused. Zook is an amazing lecturer, however, and tries to pull it off. The grading in this class, from my experience, is unfair, since its based on your GSI (essays) which is sometimes random and unfair.

I had heard that Zook was a great professor before taking Southeast Asian politics, but I have to say I am truly impressed. Great sense of humor, interesting topics, extremely engaging and thought-provoking, very helpful in office hours, and just a great class in general! Tests are take home and there is no section. can't ask for more than that!

Politics of Music - Tries to be funny and goes off on tangents. Tries to go over WAY too much in not much time, which makes it hard when you want specific info for the midterms. Grading was strict for the info he gave. Brought up questions that I didn't think were that relevant, didn't go into much detail about how music actually affects politics.

"Politics of music."Nice guy. Okay lectures, which got boring and were limited at times. Readings were okay. Class was organized, but tried to do too much in so little time. Grading was arbitrary, lacking reasoning. Overall, class lacked and Zook failed to live up to the hype. Overrated professor!

Interesting class if you want to learn about politics... Bring a lap top because taking handwritten notes is nearly impossible if you want to catch all of his random tangents...jokes are not as funny as people made them out to be. beware of GSI's! They're ridiculously tough for a survey course!

Amazing lecturer. He was extremely entertaining and charismatic, making the material itself interesting. This could have been a boring and unenjoyable class but because of him I loved the class. If you can take any class with him I highly recommend it. He is the best professor I have had at Berkeley so far!
The best professor I ever had. He's interesting and really smart. He's also very easy to approach.
The best professor at UC Berkeley.  It's a shame what has happened.  Save Zook!

He's a dead ringer for Nicholas Cage.  I got an A because my GSI liked my writing style, but not everybody was so lucky.  He is too focused on civil society and seems to be a free market liberal, but other than that he's OK.  Not a spectacular lecturer and definately NOT funny.  Doesnt mention the readings at all, but you need to use them in papers
The best prof. i have had at Cal, inspiring, passionate and interesting. Great lecturer and very accessible.
The best.

Incredible professor.  He deals with intersting and different topics that most poli sci teachers don't touch.  A lot of people take the class for his "easy rep" and those are the same people who get burned and complain about him and say he's overrated.  Everyone should take this guy at least once.
Best professor at Berkeley. It's rare to have such a great professor here. Too bad he keeps getting shafted by the Poli Sci Department....
The best professor at Berkeley.

I absolutely loved this class.  The best class i took through the extension program. His interest was contagious.  The class format became slightly monotonous towards the end but i still highly recommend the class.

I hated this class but it wasn't Zook's fault.  He was very enthusiastic about the material and the readings but I hated it.  The topic of this class was kind of lame and doing the papers was like being dragged from the back of a truck.   Zook's lectures lacked organization and clarity but other than that I just did not like the subject matter.

His unorganized lectures are compensated w/his personality since he's entertaining, but opens up the forum for stupid tangents & questions from the students. This course is really just poli sci. The gags are unbearable & it's hard to keep up with him at times; he is overrated. But the tests are easy if you can write long essays well.

i took two classes w/ him and loved his teaching style. like the previous post said, he really wants to complement the materials that he assigns.  the interweaving of assigned readings and outside materials is great for class and your understanding.

He's the type of lecturer who prefers to complement the reading by bringing forth the humanness of these topics and ideas.  Yeah, the gags can be a distraction, but the point of his interested rhetoric is that this stuff can't be confined just to textbooks.

He is a good lecturer and you will learn a lot if you go to lectures. He is not as entertaining as other students think, but he tries. Doing all the readings is not necessary. There was one midterm, a research paper, and a final.

never respond to emails. nor repeat anything while he talks fast. doesn't matter if u go to class or read or not, becoz if u can write, (which i though i could but i got a B), u r ok. he can tell jokes but not lectures. dum take his class. knowledge and A's are not guaranteed. take-home tests will kill u. expectations will let u down.

In 15 weeks I didn't learn a thing from lecture.  He seems to prefer entertaining his students over teaching them. Although his anecdotes will often arouse laughter, sometimes they border on incensitive satire. The punchline often involves laughing at the difference in another culture.  Not learning about it. Hands down most overrated prof in berk.

I hate comparative politics but Zook actually made lecture fun;he threw candy at the class on Halloween. He makes it clear terrorism is evil but actually explains why people commit terrorism (unlike certain cable news channel). 1 take home MT,1 term paper,1 take home final so three chances to make the grade.
Professor Zook is hilarious, and brilliant.  He brings a positive side to the depressing subject matter of war, violence, and terrorism.
Awesome!!

Has been EVERYWHERE and come back with plenty of stories.  Makes a cheap reader that's short, interesting, and appropriate.  Organizes his class well.  Tells a lot of corny jokes.  Doesn't waste too much time (though he does like random tangents).  Prepares students for all tests well in advance.  Does not grade on a curve.  Wonderful man.

A great professor! Truly knows everything and anything about every country and current events. Keeps class interesting with funny anecdotes and questions. One of the few classes I actually look forward to. Very approachable man, who clarifies anything you ask. Take a class taught by him and be inspired with politics and everything in between!

He is such a great professor, he really knows his stuff.  Plus classes are easy to sit through, not at all boring.  No matter what major you are, you need to take at least one of his classes before you graduate.

Very enthusiastic! This class is probably the only class at Berkeley that I would call "fun." His humor is contagious. Only complaint is that his exams are almost too broad, it's hard to hammer out an "A" answer because it's mostly up to interpretation. Otherwise excellent!

Zook is THE MAN.  Not only does he know everything about every country, he somehow manages to make class funny and himself quite engaging.  You can tell that he loves what he does.  He even showed up late to class a couple of times because he was being interviewed for NBC News!!! I highly recommend him to anyone remotely interested in anything.
Awesome Prof. Really knows his material. one of the few classes that i actually enjoy going to. Each day is something interesting.
The best PS professor at UCB hands down.  Great lecturer and keeps up with current events.

NEVER EVER idealize your profs--reality bites. That said, I think Zook's ideas, while initially appealing, could use more depth, complexity, and relevance. He will benefit from pulling hmself out of his vaccuum of adoring, unquestioning undergrads and engaging in public debates with other profs. Constructive criticism is NECESSARY.

He's left-leaning but that's irrelevant. He's a compelling speaker with a humanitarian compass behind his ideas, hence his appeal. He gave me a B despite my flipping him off by writing godawful, empty, last-minute papers. Not a hard class at all if you're not distracted by other crap. Take Nader too for another good leftist perspective.

Zook is affable and silver-tongued with popular peacenik ideas, but also UTTERLY IRRESPONSIBLE, PARANOID, AND INFANTILE.  However, he's courteous towards 99% of his students. I was an exception. I grudgingly recommend him. He's a good teacher, and I don't want him to lose the popularity his ego so desperately craves. A confounding man.
Awesome and funny and knows what the hell he is doing!
THis professor is awesome, always full of anecdotes and was willing to help clarify all the time. He always kept the class interested and knew what he was talking about.
No Comments
very energetic
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments
I love Professor Zook!
No Comments
Best lecturer ever.

Love love love loved this class. Professor Zook is so amazing and talented that I'm surprised the campus hasn't offered him tenure yet. He is so brilliant that it completely boggles my mind and makes anything he lectures interesting. I highly recommend taking this class no matter what background you have.

Darren Zook is the reason that I chose to go to grad school and become an academic.  He is not only extremely insightful and critical, but he offers a much needed alternative to the methodological orthodoxy in Berkeley's Poli Sci dept!

Professor Zook is my favorite professor at Berkeley. He has very enthusiastic, knowledgeable, and committed. Although he can be a little disorganized, I think he definitely makes up for it with his committment to teaching. I loved every class I took with him and wish I could take more!
Best professor ever.

He has so much knowledge to offer. He is so cool, nice, enthusiastic and interesting. He shows that he is happy to he in the class, and he likes teaching. Sometimes he offers too much information in one lecture, and speaks very fast. One might not catch all of the material or take notes. However, he is a great professor.
A great instructor; energetic, dynamic lectures.  However, he is difficult to get to know on a personal level.

Good lecturer. Obviously passionate about his work. This int'l law course was boring and unusual. Less structured than his other courses. And he had a reader, lawyer Anne Sophie Massa, who was a tough grader. This was not his best course.
Great professor who went out of his way to make sure we understood everything and do well on his exams. His lectures can get slightly boring but it's mostly because of the subject matter.
Awesome awesome awesome. The guy knows how to make the subject matter interesting, even for non PS majors. Take his class.

I took Darren Zook's Southeast Asia course for a few weeks two years ago but didn't complete it, taking time off from school to work instead. When I went back, I jumped at the chance to take it again. He's a dedicated teacher, a talented communicator, and the most colorful, adorable person.
Dr. Zook is an excellent educator: very passionate, very dynamic, and very very funny. His demeanor makes learning a very intimidating topic fun and exciting.

I've heard a lot of wonderful things about Dr. Zook before I took PS 149, so I really wanted to take one of his classes before I graduate.  I'm a junior majoring in Molecular Env. Biology... Dr. Zook makes me wish that I were a freshman again so that I can change my major to Political Science.

Great enthusiasm for his subject, ungodly reserves of energy, ectures are occasionally unfocused, can be all over the place with the anecdotes. HATED the take-home exams format. Seems approachable in class but not very helpful in office hours. Let's just say a little humility doesn't hurt.
great
He is a great teacher, he has the appropriate attitude combined with deep knowledge about the subject.

Zook made summer school fun. Every day in ps2 was like a party. His quirky sense of humor and his obvious enjoyment of his subject matter are two things he has going for him. Zook is definitely one of the best professors I've had at Berkeley.

Zook is really cocky and he does not know how to teach.He hires on crazy-hard readers for his class and doesn't really help students when they have questions.He shares really irrelevant stories in class.He acts all fair in the beginning, but don't fall fo
Best Professor I have had at Cal so far. Very approachable, and very lively in his lectures.
Zook is FREAKING rad!

He's an ok guy, explains things well and seems to be very approachable. Beware his corniness, though, and those students who like to laugh at *every damn thing he says*.  Really, guys, he's not that funny.
The best professor at Cal
All I have to say is that Zook is an amazing professor.

Great professor; he presented the material in a creative, straightforward manner. The class is  easy if you're interested in political science and actually show up to lecture. As always, if you know your stuff (show up to lecture) you'll get an A
Awesome, nice, intelligent
This man is a superb professor! He is extremely knowledgable and interesting. He is fair in grading an tells every student what is on the final/midterms and how to prepare. Highly reccommend
Best prof at Berkeley, no contest
The most interesting Political Science professor on the campus thus far.
One of the best professors I've had.  Very approachable.  Courses are very relevant to today's issues.  Very refreshing to see a professor who still enjoys lecturing AND talking to his students.
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments

The lectures were very fast-paced and hard to keep up with. The material itself is not difficult but it seems complicated during lecture. The midterm/final did not reflect the teachings of the lectures and she would make degrading comments to us during lecture.

Her lectures are quick and can be confusing, but not too difficult to understand (especially if you go to the discussions/read the textbook). She is tough but clearly cares a lot and her notes are very detailed and easy to understand. She offers lots of extra credit (and there's a generous curve). If you put in solid effort, you will be fine!

Her class very structured and organized. She provides all the resources one needs her syllabus. I attended every discussion section and almost every lecture (she does not record lectures). Her GSI team is also amazing and provide great enhancement for learning.

If you don't know the subject she will not teach it to you. She is hard to understand and goes really quickly. She assumes you know more than you do. The only people that do well are the people that are already insanely good at math. Good luck!

Lecture style felt monotone to me, and the course required a lot of homework (expect ~2 hours/day). Class time sometimes drifted into off-topic discussions (e.g., yoga/culture), which made it harder to stay engaged.

So much homework every week, difficult exams, and lectures were extremely confusing. I was not even able to follow along for lectures in which I already knew the content. She spends more time praising herself and the GSIs than she does teaching.
Tons of homework, very fast lectures that were difficult to keep up with, and very difficult exams (including two midterms).
class is challenging but doable. She and the gsi team provided lots of helpful study materials for exams which accurately reflected the content on the actual exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Had to mostly self teach all material and rely on GSIs. Very challenging to follow along during lectures even if you have learned all the content yourself beforehand. Does not release grading criteria. Class is very well organized though.

At first, I really did not like Zvezda.  Her lectures are fast and challenging to understand without proper preparation.  After I started pre-reading and doing homework early, though, the lectures became both entertaining and helpful.  She was very helpful in office hours and is a genuinely kind person.  Be willing to work, but it will be worth it.

Difficult to understand during lectures, which doesn't really matter since she goes through the material so quickly. Lots of unnecessary, advanced, and confusing references, like she's trying to get from point A to B but always finds a way around the world to get there. I can see how she appeals to some students, but not me. Decent extra credit.

Lectures are fast paced, but honestly very enjoyable. Professor is fun to listen to! Would definitely recommend writing notes outside of class, but still go to lecture, this stuff is tough to learn oyo. Lots of opportunities to get help as there were office hours all day. Tests not unreasonable, curve was kind, but know the material!

zvezda is... iconic in her own way. very strict (understandable, given the amount of students), assigns a lot of homework (useful for practice), and you can get lost in the lectures if you don't keep up. this class requires a lot of outside work and practice. you get some quiz and homework drops, and opportunities for extra credit.

I appreciate her passion about Mathematics and effort into making those adorable class notes, but don't understand final median score of 51%, and 12pts lost only because 1 sentence missed. Forgive my confusion in her artwork of lecture and treating our work, but I have to say, she is a good researcher, but definitely not a good professor.

I personally liked Stankova; her lectures can be pretty fast and confusing to follow, but the abundance of practice problems in the homework usually clears things up, and there are plenty of materials to help you succeed in the class. The class is a pretty heavy workload, and exams are graded fairly harshly, but on a curve, and insanely quickly

her lectures are so confusing and the fill-in-the-blank format of her notes is honestly not helpful. self-study is required. however, I will say that the course is super organized and she grades everything very fast with predicted grades included so you always know where you stand in the course. clobber policy was grade and the curve was decent.

Stankova has a way with words that makes even the most simple concepts incomprehensible. Lectures were extremely fast paced and confusing; I had to self-study the entire course. I'm only giving 2 stars instead of 1 because she seems passionate about math and has a clobber policy. But, overall, knocked 10 years off my life.

Lectures are fast and hard to understand plus no course capture. Three 12 problem homework sets a week (time consuming), quizzes on Friday, two midterms, a final, and a little extra credit. Curves everything to a B, without that the averages were about a C/D. Grades super fast, but regrades are rarely granted. Read the syllabus, she will be snarky.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Passionate about math! Leave lecture expecting to have to review the notes and have to get help for hw; try to actually understand the material and do the hw slowly. Dont worry about getting the Berkeley specific textbook-she posts hw problems for chapters not included in that version. she generously provides review packets and sessions.Clobber

I had Professor Stankova for Math 1B, 54 and 110. She provides many resources for you to study like hw solutions, unfilled and filled lecture notes, review sessions, etc. Attendance isn't mandatory but she does have polls which count for extra credit. She also calculates your expected final grade so you know here you stand in the class.
if you want 0 life take this math54 with her

Her lectures were a little confusing especially if you miss a day or zone out or something. Only around 5-6 hours of homework a week, and very generous policies. She drops 4 quizzes and 4 homeworks, and the final exam replaces the midterms if the grade is higher. Lots of EC (9% max). Going to GSI office hours is extremely helpful.

Confusing lectures which was not worth going. But she was very funny and passionate. 

Well structured course. READ THE DARN SYLLABUS. Generous grading policy (clobber, HW drops, quiz drops, cheatsheet allowed, amazing curves). But her and the GSIs were not very available. 

Recommend taking the adjunct or watching SLC topic reviews.
I enjoyed lectures a lot and found the pacing of the class pretty doable. She also is very accessible and I found Math 54 to be a course with a lot of support in general.
Extremely test dependent but somewhat fair grader with usually good exam curves

She's really passionate about math and was a very fun person. Yoga pre-lecture was a blast! However, she lectures way too fast to the point where it's near impossible to keep up even with complete attention. She also tends to skip steps while solving problems saying that we can do it on our own. Had to self-study a lot.

Math 52- goes through content very quickly. You need to stay on pace. Quizzes aren't bad but midterm and final are very difficult. I needed to self study- I did not learn from Stankova because her lectures go way too fast.

Her lectures are extremely difficult to follow, however she is a fair professor. Her exams are pretty difficult but she curves so that if you perform slightly above the average you will receive a high B or an A on that exam.

Context: 16 units, commuting from SF w/ BART, working a part-time job, taking care of sick grandmother. This class wasn't easy, evidenced by my two poor midterm scores: 31.5/80 & 36/80. Stankova however is knowledgeable, well-intending, and while pedantic at times, she is reasonable (grading-wise). You pay to study here, so put in the effort.
Would be a better class if a chimp with a typewriter sat at the front of wheeler
I have taken much of the content previously and still could not understand what her lectures/notes were about. I learned exclusively through chat and youtube
The worst part of my semester wasn't losing my dog, it was dragging myself to campus to listen to her lectures
Some days I would attend lecture, be locked in and following the notes and get 0% on the attendance polls

She thinks she's funny with her ET and yoga stuff when in reality we all have no idea what's happening. Only people succeeding are either spending all day on homework or have already taken calculus 2 in some capacity.
do not do not do not
One lecture's final median was a 64 and the other's was a 51. That discrepancy should tell you all you need to know.

Good if you have a solid foundation and enjoy guided step by steps on the content derivation or problem solving. She had personality which made her lectures more enjoyable. I will say if I had more of a knowledge gap she would have gotten on my nerves with her pace and whimsy. Exams are on the harder end but there's a very fair curve to compensate.

Good grading policy, A rate is pretty high. However, her lecture is a little bit too fast (thats why i only give 4 but not 5), so you may need to use her lecture note to study after lecture. Exam is not difficult. Lots of hw. Have strict rules about sending emails, but it is understandable. Overall a good professor, definitely worth choosing.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
her lecture's are very difficult to understand but if you go to lecture and do the homework alongside chatgpt it'll click. will say in this aspect she sucks though

but her midterms and finals are imo very fair since she posts a study guide with all the concepts you need to know + mock tests and she rescales them up as well, highkey not a bad prof

Her notes are SO confusing to read, and she invents random names for different math techniques. Her accent is not even that bad, but the speed at which she explains stuff makes it SO hard to follow. She's hilarious though, if you get the joke. And I can also tell that she's really passionate about teaching and math in general.

she's a very bad lecturer. just fills in premade notes that are many of us found confusing to read, and she delves into complex topics without giving her students a solid base. this makes lecture an hour of wasted time. shes nice, good curve, and gives extra credit, but VERY harsh with her email/regrade policies.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Her tests are extremely hard and her study guides offer little to no help with the exam material. Her lectures are not helpful at all and make the material more confusing. Her GSI's are the reason people pass the class and she also makes you submit regrade requests for exams BEFORE you get your exam back. Just take the class at CC.
Turn around and run, drop the class while you still can

I agree the lectures seem fast paced, its impossible to take notes, just try to link the concepts.
Otherwise, she is very nice, lots of homework but it helped me to always stay on top of contents. People saying that exams were not fair should have studied more.. Do not skip discussions and stay on top of the course. It is very rewarding by the end.

Students get access to previous midterms/finals, and we regularly do similar problems in the homework, discussion worksheets, and quizzes. However, lectures are convoluted at times, and it's very difficult to catch up once you're behind. Also, a 51% median on the final should indicate poor teaching in a 600-student class.

Homework amounts are ridiculous despite only "being 12 questions long." Her finals are not fair at all and it all depends on the lecture you're placed in. To compare to midterms, the final is so much harder. Her lectures, while organized, is just fill-in-the-blanks and she moves really quickly. Quizzes aren't that bad though.

The amount of Homework she assigns every week is ridiculous. Also, her final does not seem fair at all, it is exponentially more difficult compared to her midterms. But the thing I hate the most is her notes in class, it is just so messy and impossible to follow. AVOID HER
Ts class touched me bro do not take this class with her at all costs

Ridiculous amount of HW each week and final exam difficulty heavily depends on the lecture you're in. Punishes people for regrade requests and has very VERY unhelpful lectures. Despite heavily emphasizing how necessary it is to attend lecture, she goes too fast & emphasizes problems for the “die-hards” more than basic problem/solving.

Ok tbh if I didn't mess around all semester I could've ended with an A. Her test and clobber policy is really nice. Other than that, I didn't learn much in lectures at all, GSIs carried in terms of content. Honestly u can goof around and study the week before the final and still end w a good grade.

Zvezda was overall a pretty good professor. Lectures were pretty alright, she just goes insanely fast (tbh you're prob better off learning from the textbook), her hw assignments are pretty straight forwards and helpful, same goes for her quizzes. Her practice exams and review assignments were really helpful. Overall, not the worst.

Bro shes so cute and funny, but boy, can I not understand her lectures. Maybe I am slow or maybe I am not a math genius like she clearly is. Zvezda is probably really good at upper-division math, but I did not need anything past Math 52. Wait for Paulin if u just need 52, but if not yolo shes kinda a vibe.
Don't do it. Don't do it.

An exceptional, inspirational lecturer who makes learning fun. She ensures mastery of math concepts through consistent homework and offers a generous curve with fair exams. She is highly accessible and provides six dedicated review sessions during the final review week to ensure student success. Highly recommended for anyone wanting to truly learn.

Prof. Stankova is a world-class educator. Her lectures are extremely clear; as long as you pay attention and put in effort. She has a gift for breaking down difficult material into manageable pieces. She is a generous grader with fair exams and truly cares about her students' success. She deserves a much higher rating than she currently has.

Genuinely speaking with his professor is the worst of the worst when it comes to tests as well as the fact she has a vendetta against her own students is insane the discrepancy between final for lecture one and two is absolutely insane

Lowk a diva, which makes me sad I can't recommend her. Lectures are fun, but fast-paced. I spent hours on each HW relearning the content.
Test regrading is annoying, as they have a private "venn diagram rubric" and only send a PDF of solutions. "Frivolous regrade requests" get docked. Very generously curves tests to a median of 82%.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Amazing professor, energetic, humorous, inspiring. Helpful lecture notes, exam packets, practice exams. Everything is super clear in announcements/syllabus. Generous curve, clobber policy, extra credit, drops lowest quizzes/HWs. Yoga & music before class. Some say she goes too fast/off track in lecture which may be true but personally it's not bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Nice person, not a good teacher. She relies only on textual analysis and theory-based explanations, no course capture, and assigns 2-3x the amount of HW as Paulin (the previous professor). Attended lecture for 2 months and felt more confused than helped (common within the class). Learned entirely through SLC topic reviews and old Paulin lectures.
