Great professor, pay attention in class, go to lectures, read the book, do a little more than asked for in terms of examples and you'll do very well.

She is absolutely amazing. If you're taking a math class for a math credit versus to learn, you will not like her. If you want to learn math, there is no better professor. Her experience as a math olympiad gives her a unique problem-based learning approach. She is funny, humble, and extremely intuitive. I loved her class and the way it was taught!

Zvezda is a great professor. I was surprised to see all the terrible reviews for Spring 2014 (currently taking it the same term). She is very clear and reviews the CONCEPTS that will be on the exam. The people that put in the effort (did the homework and studied for exams) got an A. Only 1/3 of the class regularly went to lecture. GO TO LECTURE.
Not helpful, very intimidating. Throws curve balls on exams.... makes 16A a lot harder than it should be/ is with any other professor.
I was really good at math I got a 5 on my calc ap exam she is really a poor quality proffesor who does not teach what will be in her exams
Worst professor at Cal Math Department I have no idea how she got here.
She is a bad lecturer, so boring and makes it to confusing. Her tests are hard and she wants definitions for everything. Regret taking this class so much.

I took this class because of Stankova's great reviews and I HATE it. She's so hard to understand and makes the simplest things complicated. She makes herself unaccessible to students. She writes the tests while the GSIs write quizzes which makes taking the exams extremely difficult as the questions are worded terribly.
She is a hard grader and not helpful cannot understand her accent.
. Her tests are very confusing and she's a tough grader.

Professor Stankova is a crystal clear, very engaging lecturer. Her tests were an appropriate level of difficulty. Unfortunately I found her to be a little intimidating, as she often singles students out during class and asks them to come up to the front.
Not intuitive. Too concentrated on rigor and formality rather than getting the concept across.

There was no homework, so it's up to you to do the problem sets if you need help. She's very enthusiastic, and interacts with the class regularly (don't disturb her while talking). Very explicit with her work, so go to lecture and take detailed notes! Goes into depth and helps you understand the math better. Very fair exams, but still difficult.

She's the best! Very engaging and loves teaching. She's not out to show off how much she knows, like some professors, she actually wants you to learn. I had her for 1A and 1B and I'm going to take 54 with her too!
I really enjoyed her classes but exams were very hard.  I suspect if I had any prior exposure to Calculus (as seemed to be the assumption) I would not have found the material nearly as difficult.
Stankova was great! Lectures were a touch simple, but she made the subject very interesting.

She is a very entertaining lecturer but don't let the high ratings fool you - she is tough. Takes it personally if other students walk out of lecture often, understandable but she will remember once midterms approach (or so it seems). As is par for Cal Math, don't assume the lec/disc. will prepare you at all for exam expectations.

The best teacher I've had. Very helpful, very clear, very understanding. Exams are fairly easy, office hours entertaining.In addition to this great professor, I had a very nice GSI, so the class was one of the best experiences I've had at Cal.

Knowledgeable and engaging instructor overall. This class is pretty easy if you got a 4-5 in BC Calc. Exams are not cummulative. Questions don't have surprises, everything came from HW or lecture. HW is also optional and not graded (so buying the book isn't necessary). Everyone should be able to do well in this class by putting in minimum effort.
Super helpful professor. She makes class fun, unlike some of the other professors in the Math department. She's also extremely engaging and has an awesome accent.

Stankova is awesome. She really made me understand the foundations of calculus much better compared to what I had learn in high school. She is also really entertaining in class. The exams are fair, just keep doing problems as always and look over the notes you take in class.

A wonderful professor with a sparkling personality. Although she has a fairly prominent Bulgarian accent, her English is excellent and she is very clear. As long as you keep up with the minimal amount of work, it should be no problem.
She's energetic and engaging. She thoroughly explains concepts. Midterms are tough but the class is awesome.

Great at explaining concepts and giving examples. Don't think b/c you took Calc in hs that you can take it easy. You will do poorly cause she throws curveballs on the exams and only if you listened to her during lectures, then you'll know what to do. Attend lecture. People who didn't or thought it's just hs calc, were in deep trouble at the end.
never went to class because all she did was redo the examples in the book, so if you understood those, your good! did alot of practice from the book and received an A

Extremely organized and entertaining professor. You can practically copy down her notes from the board, word for word and number for number because her explanations and  examples are so effective. Enjoyed her jokes and her passion in both the subject of math and teaching it. Highly recommended even if her tests are a bit hard.

This class is the best math class out there: engaging, fun, easy, and extremely helpful. Zvezda really knows how to teach through lots of examples and explanations. I felt like I needed to attend lectures because they are making things even clerer than the textbook. She is such an enthusiastic math professor. I highly recommend her class.

Engaging, clear, fun, charming, quirky teacher. Go to class, take notes, do the HW and you should be able to get an A.    This is an easy class and many people who already took Calculus in high school underestimate this class. I did the HW and studied the notes and got better grades than smarter people who did neither. Don't take her too lightly.
fun prof, tests can be a little tricky
A great lecturer. Be prepared to write non-stop while learning via clear examples.

The class really wasn't as hard as everyone says it was.  Although the material was hard, the midterms and tests were very fair and were pretty much exactly what we saw in our homework.  You won't find anything tricky or unexpected on her tests.  She was very amusing and was a good lecturer.
Nice lecturer, but the tests were way too hard. Also, while she claimed that the 2nd midterm would be the hardest test out of all 3 tests, it was actually the easiest (at least for me).

"Zvezda" is a very nice, hard-working, approachable Bulgarian teacher who truly cares about her job. However, this class is not easy and on the exams covered more material than the other Math 1B classes (ex: probability density functions, spring systems...). She is smart, helpful, and it is a good class, but don't expect it to be easy.

She lectured clearly and explained concepts thoroughly. Her tests were challenging. She was pretty friendly and approachable. It was annoying that she was so tight-lipped about her grading policy; for example, she wouldn't let the GSIs talk about grades over email. Overall, I got a lot out of her class, though it was frustrating in the process.

she's a great lecturer, very clear and helpful.  tests are really hard, but fair.  she doesnt collect hw, but make sure you do it.  she's frusterating because she refuses to discuss her grading policy.  there is also a lack of communication with the gsis.

Overrated.  I hated this class with a passion, and her little jokes didn't help.  Tests were NOT easy, she's put a stop to that.  And often she is very UNCLEAR on what she wants for her exams.  She's kind of a dictator, and her jokes really aren't that funny.  Overall, she's decent to take 1B with, but be wary.  She's no walk in the park.

Zvezda is an extremely clear professor. She teaches you everything you need to know about the subject. She is also very willing to help students in office hours. Exams are very fair, but don't just expect a walk in the park. She got word a while back that she was considered easy, so she decided to do away with that reputation. Highly recommended.

She is pretty clear in her lectures and the homework problems are good practice. BUT I felt that the exams were misrepresentative of the hw; I don't think that the hw prepared us-it was too easy. Stankova is a pretty cool professor and geuinely cares. But I got annoyed and tired of her by the end of the semester.

Her lectures are so well organized and she explains the material really well. Her tests honestly are fair because she prepares you for the exams. She also adds some humor to the class with her Bulgarian accent and corny jokes.
She is easier to understand and does a good job at explaining problems in lecture.  Much better than my math 1B.
I had Zvesda for two semesters, and she is great.  Her lectures are clear, organized, and surprisingly stimulating.  Her exams are fair, and straight from lecture.  I 100% recommend this professor.
Very good, definitely take.

She makes math fun and simple. Loved her class, learned lots and got an A+..... Her tests are too hard if u go to lecture and do the practice tests. Her lectures make math seem so easy. If u must take Math1a this is the prof to take it with
Excellent lecturer.  Very clear, very fair.
Excellent teacher. Change to her lecture if possible.
she is amazing. best class i've ever taken. ever.
Zvezda did a great job, and Math 1A was the last math course I actually enjoyed taking at Berkeley.  She is so so much better of a professor than all the other tools in the math department!
I miss her class!
she is an awesome lecturer.  very clear and moves at a good pace.  her tests are fair and she is one of my favorite profs at cal.
She was a great prof and obviously cared about her students even though she pretends to be tough.
pretty funny, very clear

She is so awesome! First math teacher I had at Cal, and I'm thoroughly impressed. Wonderful sense of humor, style, and personality. She makes everything so organized and clear! I didn't even have to read the text to do the h/w problems. Sweet! Hope she teaches more advanced math classes!

darn standova is soooo freaking HOT!!! she's the only reason why i go to the lectures. i LOVE her style... especially her hair!!! im considering cutting my hair like hers but im afraid that im not hot enough for that hair style... i dont even need math 1B yet i took it just so i can stare at her!!!

Awesome!  Even though the material was challenging, lectures were very organized, clear, and filled with examples.  Homework helps!  She's interesting and friendly with a sense of humor.  Best math teacher I've had in a long time.  <3
She was a great teacher!  She gave tons of examples.  Her tests were all way to easy or way to hard so the curve was a little messed...
do hw...that's all the preparation for quizzes/midterms you need...her accent is awesome
Do your homework. She's pretty hot too.
Great teacher, goes through proofs clearly. Study sequences and series a lot though, that was a tough midterm.
SHE IS AMAZING!!!!

In addition to clearly explaining the basics necessary to understand the homework, she goes a step further and explains a few extra "hot shot" problems.  Her lectures are always interesting, and her tests are based on the homework.  Excellent overall.
Nice preofessor, good teacher.  Just picky-as-hell grader. *Grumbles*
A very organized and funny professor.  You'll enjoy her class and jokes.
A very very cute and sexy voice teacher who turn super hard calculus problems into an easy understanding question. One of the finest teacher in Berkeley.
Simply amazing.  Very well-paced with a good sense of humor.

jesus. thank you. thank you. i dont believe in you, but thank you. moses. thank you. thank you. i don't believe in you but thank you. allah, thank you, thank you. i dont believe in you but thank you. GET THE PICTURE?!
i actually Wanted to go to her lectures. and they were at 8am. enough said

Guys, if you have this teacher, you are a lucky **** and you have escaped Berkeley premed math unscathed. This woman is a goddess of clarity, easy exams, and homework that is never collected. I love her, and her name means "Star" in Russian.
god bless this woman!  if you take the SLC adjunct course with her class, it is not so hard. she is so great. i am so jealous that she is now teaching 1b...
wow, she would make the hardest concepts seem so easy... very good instructor! i loved attending lecture... fair exams... approachable!
I like Zveda!  She is cool!
She's interesting and very good at breaking down the material.  In fact, my class petitioned for her to teach 1B too.

The course moves pretty quickly, but she breaks most of the problems down for u into more basic steps. as long as ur willing to work for ur grade, attend the SLC...even if you get a bad GSI, you're bound to do well in t he course.
If you can wake up that early, her lectures are actually worth attending. Makes everything interesting with very fair exams, entertaining lectures. Good teacher!

Her lectures are very clear and concise, and she digresses only to tell funny stories.  She's very witty and intelligent and is quite friendly in office hours.  Her tests are really fair if you attend lecture.

Her lectures were very uninteresting. Never calls on students in the back- sometimes made eye contact with students in the back and then moved to call on someone who just raised their hand in the front, despite waiting in the back for a while. Really unmotivating to engage in lectures.
I loved her lectures and felt smarter after each one.

There was a lot of reading, but it wasn't unmanageable, and her philosophical, analytical lens through which we examined the texts in class was helpful in deep engagement with each text. No reading assignment felt pointless, and each lecture felt important and engaging.

good lecturer, covers a lot of context/background stuff, but for me the discussion sections covered much more of the text itself. There is limited content on the slides so listen in class! There are also reading quizzes every week.
Professor is very stubborn with her beliefs.

I'm only one lecture into her class and she seems fine but there's clearly someone with a vendetta against her on this site who keeps spamming 1/5 reviews so I'd like to balance it out. Go ahead and read the negative reviews under this they're so pretentious and funny. I like the no electronics policy because I do not have a laptop.

Professor Zhang is a wonderful lecturer and incredibly kind. What I appreciated the most about Zhang is her patience and empathy. I loved her lectures, all of them are thoughtful and insightful. She also has a wonderful sense of humor too! Zhang is very approachable, so go to her office hours!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Zhang's class for transfer foundation was an utter disaster. From day one, it became apparent that her idea of helping transfer students was a cruel joke. Instead of providing guidance, she was determined to drown us in a tsunami of assignments, leaving no room for a smooth transition. In conclusion, if you value your sanity, steer clear of Dora.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Her ineptitude extends beyond her failure to support transfer students in the foundation process; it also manifests in her astonishing silence on crucial global issues. When we attempted to delve into an anti-war discourse akin to "Frankenstein in Baghdad," it became painfully apparent that Zhang couldn't even discuss Palestine.

Despite being in a position supposedly dedicated to helping transfer students, she appears blissfully indifferent to their struggles. It's as if she takes pleasure in watching students flounder, all while maintaining an air of indifference.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Nice class with interesting readings but she grades super tough. I normally get As but for her final two papers, I got an 88 and an 89. Other than that, it was a fine class with not too much work or stress.

She never went deeper into the material, she covered so much background about authors that it was boring. She talked about things that never really mattered. She never really engaged the class nor made anything interesting, basically read her notes the whole time. Also my GSI graded very poorly and never gave good feedback so I could improve.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Has detailed lectures that at first impressed me; though I appreciate her willingness to go very in depth in regards to the text, it can be tiresome to listen to someone cover so much content almost uninterrupted for an hour. There are no released/defined "rubrics" for papers, so a great deal of your grade will rest on your GSI's preferences.

This was probably one of my favorite english classes I've ever taken, the book selection was really enjoyable. Her lectures are interesting but not necessary to attend to do well. GSI's definitely were tough graders on the paper so I won't say this is an easy A but if you get help early on your papers and ask for feedback you will be fine.

i went to every single lecture, no absences, took notes, and had no idea how to do the homework or exam. the midterm averages were a 40%, 30%, and i think the final was around the same range. I wouldn't say she's a good professor, but i think she tried to keep lecture engaging and entertaining. would not take again, i hate econ courses.

Je suis d'accord a propos de ce cours. Les sujets sont intéressant, mais les examens ne sont pas justes, parce-que c'est pas possible solveur les exercices sans les connaissances préalables, et ce détail ruine l'objet mathématique.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: While the lectures were clear in the sense that they covered the basics, they did not adequately prepare students for the level of difficulty on homework, practice exams, or the actual exams. Although practice materials are provided, the jump in difficulty between worksheets, homework, and exams is substantial.

Teacher was great at explaining everything, and honestly was one of the more entertaining lecturers I've  had at Berkeley. The curve for the class is fair, and she does give a lot of practice so if you just do all the worksheets and hw, you prob will get an A, just watch out for the algebra since the numbers aren't super nice in this class.
She teaches as if she's at MIT, while ignoring that this is UC Berkeley's classroom.

This class is difficult. Avg for midterm/final is 30 which is because they are quite difficult. She crams so much information into 1.5 hr lecture that it's not possible to keep up in class, but i must say she explains concepts clearly. if you lock in / on top of your work it's doable. if you don't think you're a top student at berkeley, avoid tbh.

Exams are absolutely brutal with averages around 30% even though she curves at the end. Lectures don't prepare you for the exams and while practice exams and problem sets helped for midterms the final was just another level. Homework took hours to complete though was graded fairly. Attendance was also mandatory, but overall avoid at all costs.

Effective and caring lecturer for game theory. Went out of her way to demonstrate concepts with engaging in-class games. The class was way harder and more technical than I expected, but I learned a lot. She was helpful in office hours and generally fair with grading. Exams and homework sets were pretty challenging. I wasn't a fan of the iclicker.
Lectures do not adequately prepare you for tests AT ALL- you basically have to self study everything, which is reflected by how the averages for midterms are 30-50%

I wouldn't say this course is particularly hard if you are a STEM major. My problem is with how much learning you get for the amount of effort you need to give. In other classes tend to help understanding the textbook, here it feels the other way around - lectures are devoid of economic intuition or math proofs, just rushing through equations.

When the average of an exam is 30 out of 100 and the maximum is 80, you can be sure that the fault is with the professor, not the class.

Prof Huang is simply not made out for teaching. She spends way too much time on bureaucratic details, going through slides fast to cover an insane amount of material, leaving even the best students lost.

My tip for those wanting to learn the material: Wait a semester and take it with another professor. Her teaching "strategy" is just to read through slides that basically cover the entire book, not teach how to solve exercises, and then have gigantic problem sets pretty much every week. Wish I could go back and take it with someone else.

Avoid at all costs. 

Lectures are terrible, she basically reads slides and skips the derivations that are covered in exams. Attendance is mandatory. 8 problem sets, each with 15-20 questions. 2 midterms and a final. 

Syllabus is full of weird rules that serve no purpose. 

Huge amount of work for very little learning.

Huang is easily one of the best professors I've had. She is deeply invested in the success of her students. She is strict with her rules which are fair imo. Most of the grade is from 3 exams and 5 problem sets. The resources provided are numerous and thorough. Tests can be a little long but are doable - prep for them well. Participation helps you.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took both 101A and C110 with Professor Huang. Her lectures are interesting and fruitful. I think she is experienced and knows how to combine lectures with exercises to enhance students' understanding of the course and economics. I like her teaching style, which is relaxed yet includes some challenges. Grading is fair if you follow the lectures.

I think people overblow the difficulty of this class and this prof. Lectures were long (3 hour lectures) yet prof Huang somehow lectured nearly the entire time and was fairly engaging. Exams were difficult (scores were low) but its all graded on a curve anyways so raw scores dont matter and it really tested what you learned. Would take again!
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Her slides are great, but practice with the psets/worksheets. Exams were horrid (median: midterm 34%, final 31%), but fair; cheat sheet woud've helped. Grades aren't trackable bc of curves/EC from iClicker polls. 3hr lecture 1x week is so content-heavy she rushed through ques to not be "interrupted." GSI=friend. The math itself isn't difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Would highly recommend this class if you enjoy calculus! Though the lectures were pretty packed with content, they were enjoyable, as Prof. Huang goes through the intuition of each concept instead of handing you formulas to memorize. The exams are relatively difficult, but she curves to a B.

It's a tough class, but she knows her stuff and is really good at lecturing. You can understand economic concepts in a mathematical perspective. Tough grader, VERY tough questions, SOCs are REALLY annoying, but she's accommodating of any circumstances and gives generous grades.

I think Prof. Huang is a great instructor. If you are good at math, interested in Economics, and willing to be challenged, I recommend taking her course. She effectively balances the explanation of economic concepts with mathematical techniques.  She is energetic and makes the 3-hour lecture enjoyable.

Professor Huang is caring and professional. I think she is serious about her lectures. The course itself is challenging to learn compared to the other economics courses. The professor provides annotated notes and other materials to support our study. It is also interesting and enjoyable to have conversations with her and classmates during the OHs.

101A is a difficult course. Professor Huang makes the course materials easier to understand. She explained the contents clearly. The exams are related to the lectures, problem sets, and section exercises, but not the same. I think it's reasonable. I don't think it would be a nightmare if you did something, lol.
Would not recommend for Econ 101A.

The course is well-organized. The professor is passionate about the lectures and her job. The problem sets and SWs are well-designed and help me follow some of the harder content, which is very helpful. Recommend!
A great professor! Her lectures are inspiring, and the problem sets and assignments are well-designed and very helpful for understanding economic concepts and developing problem-solving skills.

The exams are a bit challenging, but I think it's reasonable, considering it's 101A. You can handle the exams if you follow the lectures. The professor explains concepts in a straightforward and understandable way, and her teaching style makes even difficult topics easy to grasp.

Almost worst lectures I have ever took and the worst exam I have ever took. Nothing related to daily problem set and the practice exam. Countless knowledge points needed in the exam was never mentioned before.

I took 101A with professor Huang. She delivered content very clearly and was very passionate in her lectures. The practice she assigned to us was very helpful and practical. The difficulty level was reasonable for 101A students. The professor gave us opportunities to earn extra credit by answering iClicker questions in class.
The professor always prepared excellent lectures for us. The exercises and problem sets are a great support for our study. She is really care the students and always willing to h
The best lectures I have ever had! Good organization. Clear explanation. The professor was always willing to help us even outside her working hours. She is so responsible. Hard exams but fair.

The professor is great! Her lectures are logical and organized. She is the professor who explains things most clearly. She knows a lot about the materials and can give us more. Although the materials are difficult sometimes, it is worth taking this course!

I LOVED this class. It has been the funnest econ course I've taken here. It was very math heavy, whereas 100A taught by Campbell seems to be essay-based, from what I hear. But I loved the math! Professor Huang did a great job going over the material, the resources provided in the class were super helpful, my GSI Jacob Wu was crazy helpful.
The best professor that I've ever had!! I really enjoy her lecture and she is very supportive after class or office hours. I will definitely take her class again!!!

She is a pretty good lecturer who is always patient to teach and explain.  There are various colorful class forms, including watching videos, playing games. There are also five bonus questions with1 point each to help us obtain a better grade. The exams are not that hard if you take class and finish problem sets. Don't be misled! Take the course!

This class was supposed to be non-techincal, requiring no math prereqs but the whole class was math and very difficult to follow. At least once a lecture, she would get tripped up on her own problem. Do not take this class unless you are familiar with game theory and confident you like it enough to teach yourself the applications outside of class.

doesn't explain things super clearly, but her in-class games are fun! i got by from just watching lecture recordings and didn't need to read the textbook. the class is basically all math, but it's not too hard

She is really a good lecturer who really cares about teaching and education. Her course materials are organized, and her lectures are not only interesting but also thoughtful. These people who gave her low scores, are just angry about the hard exam! It's not fair to such a good lecturer! Take the course! Don't be misled by these angry guys.

I'm surprised by the comments here. Overall her teaching is great. She gives great feedback and class notes and really cares about the class. Although she's not the best lecturer I still find the first half of the course engaging.

I have had pretty bad professors in my entire 4 years at Berkeley, but nobody has ever ever been bad enough for me to publicly give them a bad rating. Her lecturing style not only confuses her students but trips her up all the time. If your entire class is based on exams, at least answer students' questions on your discussion platform.

Out of all the classes taken at Cal, this class was the worst. Although I really liked the subject of game theory itself, the lectures and instructions were too poor. I sometimes ended up watching Youtube videos to understand sub-topics since they were much better for me to comprehend.

Professor Huang is super nice and her lectures are engaging and easy to understand. However, the tests were HARD and I'm so stressed about failing this class;(  Probably won't take her class again although I can tell she's  putting a lot of efforts into the class especially during the strike.

She is an amazing lecturer but you need to be motivated to work through problem sets on your own. Problem sets exceed difficulty of exam so if you can do those you will be fine. Class is extremely engaging, with in class game demonstrations. Exam difficulty is not bad. She is also super sweet!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I'm floundering in this class, no support and worried I might not pass. I would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: she is a tough grader :(((((((

Your grade is based ENTIRELY on midterm 1, midterm 2, and the final, using the best of two grading options: 15/15/70 or 30/30/40. Homework is optional. Discussion sections do not have worksheets, they just cover homework problems. First midterm average was ~73%. Second midterm average was literally ~60%. Virtually no support, abysmal communication.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really hard and poorly taught

Please do yourself a favor and do not take game theory with this professor, or any class taught by them. They're very nice I'll give them that.. but the class is way too hard, the lectures are way too bad, and there is no support. Terrible all around.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Pretty intense classes for intermediate microeconomics to finish in the summer. I like her pace because it's very tight and intense, so you can't easily get distracted. Tests are hard, but if you finish all her material (including those does not require to submit), I think you will be great. Highly recommend going to office hours.

This professor is so bad at explaining things. Just throws a ton of stuff on slides and reads from it expecting us to know what is going on. Never properly explains things. Be prepared to be humbled. Your whole grade is just a midterm and final which, are no where near the difficulty of the lecture and optional problem sets. AVOID THIS PROFESSOR.

There's a big difference in the difficulty of the exams relative to the lectures and problem sets. He doesn't teach the fundamentals extensively enough for you to be comfortable with that level of application. The material was enjoyable if you like game theory and math, but weirdly difficult testing was a real letdown.

Fave professor of Bio 1B. His unit (ecology) was the only one where I feel like I really succeeded. I may be a bit biased since I took Environmental Science, but I honestly think his lectures were the least dry of the three profs. It's true that the exams were in-depth, but that is the case for many classes, and his was the easiest of Bio 1B.

This review is specifically for the class; I'll post for other professors as well. With the online transition, this class was made more difficult. Incredibly difficult select all that apply questions, very strict grading scheme, no accommodations made, and a deluge of content. If possible, I would wait till classes resume. Terrible experience.

He is a good lecturer but the exams are extremely difficult, where you need to have a solid and in depth understanding of the topic. Overall good professor and is very knowledgeable and passionate about topic.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof. Ackerly is very straightforward with what he wants the students to know from his lectures. Lectures are pretty easy-going, especially if you have taken Biology before

Professor Ackerly is so sweet and very well educated. He made coming to lectures fun and made what seemed to be a dull subject extremely interesting. You can tell he cares about his students and how well they learn. He teaches in a way that makes sense. Highly recommend.

Professor Ackerly is extremely passionate about ecology, and it shows. He made what can be a relatively dry subject extremely engaging. Overall just a really nice guy. He made Bio 1B much more enjoyable and understandable.

I took the Botanical Gardens freshmen seminar with Professor Ackerly. I really enjoyed the opportunity to take a class outside! It was definitely a unique experience, and I'm so glad that I took this class. I would definitely recommend it.
So approachable and friendly. His lectures are well paced and very interesting! I had no interest in ecology whatsoever, especially after Bio1B, but this class was really worth it to be an IB major.
his seminar on plants in the botanical garden is pretty fun! definitely not difficult, but very interesting and engaging (it's a seminar!). will give you a new appreciation of plants.

One of the best professors I have ever had at Berkeley. Had him for both IB 153 and IB 154 (both were awesome classes).  He goes at a great place and brings in a bunch of interesting case studies examples.
Really nice guy. Doesn't use power point, so he goes at a good pace and uses the board, which is much more interesting than reading off of an overhead. Would recommend the class.

/Very/ easy and interesting class -- go to class and you will be fine. Acker is intelligent and funny, and I always enjoyed his lectures. He's similarly very understanding for specific student circumstances.

He is knowledgeable about the topic but only makes sense when he talks. Go to lecture and listen. Write down everything he says but don't look at the whiteboard. His scrawls are useless! this class has weekly writing assignments, way too many readings, a take-home midterm, and in-class final. It's hard to get an A.

Midterm is Take home, which is nice. Average grade is a B- for it. Class is very interesting, but it was hard for me to be motivated to attend lecture because it was at 8am. Final takes a LOT of preparation. Dont waste dead week. Not as easy A, but definitely as easy pass.

I liked Acker. He was clever, funny, and helped you understand the material *in class*. That said, cutting class was hard because his notes are unhelpful and hard to read and the texts are largely unnecessary. But that said, I miss the fun of being in his class. Undoubtedly, Acker will make you interested in geography.

65% of your grade is the final so you really have to know the material.  Good lecturer but its pretty difficult to get an A. Don't take if your not interested in the material and the three huge readers are pretty pointless except for a little help for the essays

Friendly teacher who knows what he's talking about, but that doesn't mean he knows how to teach. Grades terribly hard and with little substantial reasoning behind it. He requires a lot of reading, often goes on tangents, & doesn't understand how to take notes. The whiteboard consists of random scribbles  & his posted lectures are more like novels.

His experience and passion for SE Asia makes his personal anecdotes both interesting and helpful for understanding. The class can get a bit confusing if you take your notes directly off the board because he is kind of scatter-brained. He's also a difficult grader.

Excellent class. His lectures are well thought out and extremely relevant to current events. He makes a real effort to try to get to know his students. The workload is about average and, although notan easy A, the class is very managable.

Acker is a great professor. The course consists of 1 midterm, 1 final, and 10 short essays. His lectures are well structures and his notes and lectures are available online and on webcast. He has a great personality and makes lectures much more exciting than other professors. I highly recommend taking him if you can.

I took this class in FPF and found that it was the most valuable class there. Acker's research and personal experience in SE Asia makes the class interesting. For As on your papers, be sure to agree with him but contrast with original points to show you've given it thought. Play this game and you too can earn an A in the extension course.

He obviously knows the material well and it is his passion, but his lectures are monotonous and since he posts his lecture notes online (very detailed and word for word), they are not necessary to attend. Way too much reading- 3 huge readers- that were a waste. David is an awesome GSI.

Acker is a great lecturer. I just wish I could stay awake more often because it's very much a current events class. It's entertaining and informative when he talks about his research in Thailand and Laos, when he was researching what we were learning about. Grade consists of 10 papers (you can't get less than a C on them), midterm, and final.

Really good lecturer; weekly papers were annoying and was a little unclear on how to get an A - easy to get a B though. Takehome midterm was a little difficult, but he gave us all the questions that would be on the final beforehand (a lot of preparation). Had a B in the class, but got an A on the final, which boosted me to an A!EC for participation

Many students seem to like Prof. Acker, but I found him extremely dull, boring, and biased. He has extremely messy writing and his notes all on the board are all over the place, plus he tends to mumble. The readers are HUGE and pretty much useless except for homework once a week...so you don't have to read all of the readings.

The best lecturer I've ever had!! His anecdotes are sometimes hilarious. Never slept in class because his lectures are incredibly awesome. On the other hand, the take-home midterm and final require a lot of preparation. But overall, a cool guy and very entertaining lecturer.

Very intriguing professor.  Anecdotes make lecture exciting to attend.  There are ten 1-2page papers due in section that get tedious, but easy to BS.  Midterm is take home and analytical while final is more broad.  Readers are absolutely pointless (stopped reading after first 2 weeks except articles about the essays).  P/NP takes off the pressure.
An apologist for neocolonialism and inequality--i.e., the facts.

Prof Acker had a great sense of humor and I learned a lot of interesting stuff from this class. But being a science major it was definitely more info that you needed to know that I had thought. So maybe for that group I'd recommend taking it P/NP. Don't buy the readers they are a big waste of money.

I have downloaded every lecture of his "Globalization" series because he's truly a great lecturer. He has all the ingredients: an extremely wide knowledge base, very deep analytical thinking, mastery of expression, a well-organized lecture that seems spontaneous-- a very nice sense of humor that verges on gritty if it weren't so intelligent.

Great professor. Some may say he is biased, but he is really just a realist. Always presents both sides of the argument. Goes over a lot of material in each lecture, so I would recommend going. The lectures are very interesting anyway. Final isn't too bad, but requires some prep. Class is definitely easier for those who have had experience in Econ.

Prof. Acker is AMAZING. Take his class if you can. He is very smart and he has seen the world! He knows about everything and presents both sides of the issues. Anybody that says he is biased must have VERY extreme views. He is a very fair grader and is willing to help you out if you need it. Very approachable.

best class I've ever had! a great professor, accessible and helpful, very knowledgeable (especially about east asia). he might be a little bit of a libertarian, but he'll present an issue fairly. and his lecture notes are almost incomprehensible so make sure you listen in class

MY FAVORITE TEACHER. no other comments. Fun class, pretty much about globalization and the PEOPLE of different regions. Very useful information (that i have used for both an english paper and in a marine mammals course here during an exam!) he gives you the question for the final and midterm before and the grade is based on 1 weekly essay (v. easy)
Greatest professor EVER!!!  Not only is he very intellegent, he is also very charismatic and very articulate.  His lecturs are very enlightening, and he is by far the best professor I have ever had.

I enjoyed this class, though he clearly is more conservative. Lectures were interesting and he is very animated but sometimes he is hard to follow.  This class is Rocks for Jocks and isn't that hard in the long run. One research paper and a take home final. This is a good class for science people (like me) who need a breadth.

Clas on globalization.  I liked him because he shares my hatred for communists and leftists.  He also spends like 3 lectures on Comparitive Advantage, which takes maybe 10 minutes to understand.  You have to go to lecture since there's no textbook, but really if you figure out the theme of each lecture you can throw in your own ideas for support.
Really great Professor.  I really enjoyed classes and felt like I learned a lot.
Acker definitly teaches (and grades) with a bias. Readers are uneccesary.

Wonderful man with a huge set of stories that always apply to whatever the topic is.  Has actual feild experiance and is an accomplished theorist (so he is adept at both practical an entirely useless knowledge).  Manages to keep the class under control at all times.
you never ever have to read if you don't want to and who doesn't want that?! he's very clear and the class is organized in a very easy-to-follow way.

It's GEOGRAPHY, for pete's sake, not Theory of Evolution or Law. How many competing viewpoints do you need? Acker's teaching is straightforward and solid, no surprises in the format whatsoever. Nothing special, but this is a good course to take to fulfill your basic science requirements (or Astro 10 with Filippenko).
gives good lecture. go through your notes and u'll do fine in the exams. very easy. DO NOT buy the expensive readers, they're useless. really, trust me.
Lots of material.  The professor didn't offer many different views on the issues.  If you didn't see something the way he saw it you wouldn't pass.
Dont buy the expensive readers, just stay awake in class (sometimes difficult) and take good notes, tests are purely lecture based and very easy
He is an amazing professor. Because of him I am majoring in geography. He is really really good and really really fun

Professor Acker is a great professor.  He outlines exactly what you need to know and doesn't have you read pointless material. His pace was moderate.  Only negative is that he goes through a lot of information during lecture, so try not to miss it!
all you have to do is take good notes and pay attention in class to get an A
Interesting mateiral, but couldn't concentrate in class.  Too much reading, but you don't need it.
I love the professor, he is really helpful and funny

The professor is really ,funny and helpful, you feel like you can really talk to him. The class is pretty easy, and most of the time it's pretty interesting. You really can learn new things. However, he can be confusing (it's hard to take notes cause he jumps from one point to the next)
dont just leave scram
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Flipped lecture style does not work. Videos & Lectures are super slow. In lecture he covers 1 problem, sometimes not even finishing, which is also way easier than the homework & exam questions. Uses Pearson for homework, so buying their program is required. Be ready to teach yourself, especially if you haven't taken physics in a while or at all.
a bit lost

-Lectures are mandatory but cover what was went over in required video lectures and homework, so they're pretty much pointless. They also go over maybe one problem a class. 
-He's very nice and personable, but if you haven't taken a college-level (AP/IB) Physics before I have no idea how you're going to get above a C.
-Rely on textbook for info.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He teaches in a flipped classroom format which is not great imo. The class is way too big for people to be able to work together and solve problems during lecture. Mastering physics is used for homework which is usually slightly harder than a basic plug and chug problem but then the exams are all theoretical with no numbers.

Very cool and friendly guy, but half the lectures are repeating the pre lecture videos (which could be condensed if he edited out the drawing software troubleshooting), and the other half is him getting his algebra corrected by the class. If you have done physics its easy, if you haven't it may be hard, but its mostly obscured middle school math.

You can tell he knows a lot about physics and is very passionate about it, however, he does not know how to teach it. He claims this class is for all levels of students, even if you've never taken physics before. This is not true. If you haven't taken physics before, this is going to take everything out of you and you aren't going to learn at all.

Hardest class I've ever taken and the hardest I've studied. Flipped classroom was ok, but lectures were sometimes not helpful as he would spend too long on problems. And exam questions were always way way WAY harder than the homework/problems we do in class. If you haven't taken AP, going to OH is 1000% necessary to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: RUN!! ESPECIALLY if you have no physics experience. Lee is def the worst teacher I've ever had. His lectures are simultaneously dragged and rushed?? Nothing is actually accomplished but u have to go. Flipped classroom is terrible, weeks behind schedule, and he doesn't communicate with GSIs. Very disorganized course, absurd exams w/ rampant errors

I recommend that anyone taking this class read the textbook instead of attending lecture (do iclicker for attendance anyway), do all of the practice tests that he posts, and you'll be fine. The class is heavily curved. My biggest mistake was wasting time trying to understand the lectures, I started understanding when I stopped going to class.

Cons: choose a different professor. Horrible lecturer's. Lee solves one problem per lecture & often solves it wrong. Flipped classroom videos are horrible and full of rambling, you will be  teaching yourself if you've never taken physics. 
Pros: If you took AP physics you'll be fine. Lee gives the most A's out of all the physics 7A professors.

Prof lee is very understanding and insanely kind, but he cannot teach an intro level physics like physics 7A. He expects students have advanced math skills (linear alg or calc 3) and previous physics skills which should not be needed in an intro level course. Very difficult tests and curve is good but seems random and unfair to some students.

His physics knowledge is way too advanced that he doesn't know how to teach intro physics. All material from pre lecture videos. The lectures are pointless, he just has you do practice problems. I struggled throughout the course and went to friends in 8A for their lecture slides. However, he is super understand and a really nice guy so no hate.

Prof. Lee does care about his students learning and is engaging in lectures/demos, but I did not feel like I learned much in his lectures to the point where I stopped going to class.  I usually learned outside of class during office hours for the hw and the final was very very difficult.  There is a curve in the class though that is applied later.

Horrible professor. He doesn't teach in lectures. He didn't make the final exam; the questions were from the MIT midterm review. He is incompetent in office hours and can't answer almost any students' questions. His demeanor is nice, but it doesn't matter if he can't teach. More focused on his own research than making any form of curriculum at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Bad lectures (flipped classes don't work). Messes up his own example problems, pushes deadlines for work cause he is behind on lectures. Curve is crazy as all the students don't learn. Only ones that get high grades are those that took physics in high school and passed the ap test. Promise this has made a toll on my mental health.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: No physics experience going in. This class was a struggle. Absolutely do not take unless you have taken  AP physics/physics in HS or community college. Should be a prereq for this class.

Flipped classroom is terrible, bad lec videos, would complete MAYBE 1 example in class despite live problem solving being the point of his teaching style. Always extremely behind in content, throwing off literally every assignment deadline and content benchmark. Most unorganized prof Ive had. Insane curves, don't expect to learn anything.

Overall a nice professor but his "flipped" style of learning is pretty unbearable. Videos are slow and monotonous and his homeworks often have subjects not covered in lecture or in videos. Curving is huge, got a 30% which is a C+ for the first midterm, and a 50% which is a B+ in the second midterm. Be prepared to use outside resources for learning.

Please don't take this class with professor lee, take 7 techs if you have to. He doesn't spend time teaching us and his exams are crazy problems we either never see or aren't taught how to deal with the extra factors. Labs are weeks ahead of lecture content. GSI's are lost and barely helpful and they do the best they can.

Adrian Lee wasn't a bad teacher, but everyday going to class I wish a moving vehicle would have done work on me while I was crossing the street so I wouldn't have to class, not because of Adrian Lee but lowkey because of this school.
B.A. from Columbia and PhD at Stanford and Lee still teaches like his highest level of physics knowledge is a high school physics class. Most boring class ever.

This professor is vey disorganized and does not know how to teach. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS if you struggle with physics or have no experience with physics. His flipped classroom is terrible and i haven't learned anything form him but form a professor. Do whatever you can to not take professor Lee

I have physics experience, so this class is pretty meh, but I've seen some glaring issues with this class. Flipped setting makes it hard to get anything out of it. Labs are crazily unbeneficial for such a hands on method of learning in teaching you anything of value for the problems are you expected to solve. This class genuinely needs an overhaul.

He keeps moving homeworks around and it's pissing me off because how hard can it be to just make homework due on the same day every week. Also he sucks at explaining concepts and the reversed lecture format he doesn't even do correctly because he makes us watch video lectures and then instead of doing practice problems he just recaps videos in lec.

If you need a good prof to learn from, don't take him. 

Material is doable with practice (my first physics class ever btw), but his flipped classroom makes it hard to learn—I relied on my GSI and the textbook. Tests are similar to past ones, and the curve is huge (50% = B). Textbook is $60 since it's through Pearson and required for homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The lectures were very boring, and by week 2, almost no one was attending. He teaches how to get formulas but not exactly how to apply them in the same way as the exams. He makes the class do around 50 minutes to an hour of preweek prerecorded videos where he basically does more than he ever will in lectures. All exam grades are done by head GSI.

Absolute garbage class. Skipped every lecture, pre-lecture videos take 1hr+ to watch. Sometimes, 10 - 15 videos to watch before coming to class. Furthermore, he's behind like 2 weeks at a time on course content, labs are actually embarassingly easy. Flipped-classroom has to be the worst idea ever. Midterms are 10x harder than lecture problems.

Chill guy but terrible lecturer. Seems to be very knowledgeable and intelligent but he can't teach. He utilizes a 'Flipped classroom', nice in theory but with how busy college gets, expecting us to watch around 1h before the start of the school week is an insane time commitment bc on weekends we have HW/Lab in addition and other subjects to work on

As nice as he seems, his lectures are boring. He has pre-lecture videos that students are supposed to watch before the start of every week which are difficult to follow and last around 40-60mins. Prof. Lee should realise that we not only have other classes/assignments to do over the weekend.
Don't be fooled by his calm demeanor and cool earrings; Adrian Lee is not a D1 Chiller. He makes concepts way harder than they need to be. You're better off doing random lectures off of youtube.
This professor has refused to sefsefsgsefgsgsgseg
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: AVOID  THIS CLASS IF YOU HAVE NO PHYSICS BACKGROUND EVEN IF YOU DO RUN!!!! Adrian didn't explain concepts at all and I had to rely on online sources like the Ochem tutor and outside resources rather than my own professor or GSI's who are meant to be helpful.
Extremely difficult midterms and finals. Curves are crazy but makes you feel pretty crappy for a while.

The flipped classroom approach in theory is good, however in practice it was truly a struggle especially for someone who is taking physics for the first time. The GSI's aren't very helpful either because there are things that the professor glosses over without explaining and he expects us to know these things from a previous class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I don't understand how this guy has been teaching for so long. He is a disgrace to the school because of how bad at teaching he is. He is more focused on talking about his research than teaching. I have never taken physics before and its week and I don't know what's going on. His flipped classroom is terrible. Worst professor I've taken so far.

As nice as Lee is, is style of teaching is genuinely awful and I feel like I haven't learned anything from him. "Flipped classrooms" do not help in the slightest and Mastering Physics is just a way to get more money out of students.

He does a 'flipped classroom' which pretty much 3-4x amount of time taking notes/watching lectures. He is clearly intelligent and a good physicist, but the classroom dynamic is just awful. This may work for some, but he needs to realize that most students can't contribute 10 hrs a week on just notes/lectures before they can even get to HW/Reviewing

This class is going to be tough no matter who your professor is. I had background in HS so this class was pretty straightforward for me. I struggled with the topics at the end of the semester due to the speed at which we covered it (1-2 weeks for two units). However, if you look at the notes and read the textbook, you should be fine.

Look to take another professor! Professor Lee is a nice guy, but his class is a total trainwreck. Every exam I took had serious mistakes (not corrected until post-exam), GSIs had no clue what they were doing, flipped classroom is terrible, lectures quite confusing, and if you want to talk to the man himself he's probably in Chile doing research.

Avoid Lee unless u already have solid physics background from HS. He does not teach during lectures at all yet attendance will be taken. Everything is taught in his pre-lecture videos but trust me those will be more confusing than a squirrel sitting next to u during ur finals. He expect u to know lots of terms already and does not explain well.

Great guy, an awful teacher, take any other professor. Not a single test average was near passing throughout the semester, curve only gets you so far. The only reason I came out with a decent grade was due to the 2 years of physics I took in HS. All lectures are online videos, actual lectures are him rambling. Would not recommend him at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Difficult lecturer, but study past midterms and it will be fine. It pays to really study for the first midterm so you can get ahead of the curve rather than worrying about your grade for the next midterm and final (there are no drops or clobbers).

Prof. Lee is clearly a brilliant and charismatic person but that does not make him a good teacher. He makes it impossible to feel motivated to do the work necessary to learn the material because the knowledge you need is buried under way too easy labs, tedious homeworks, useless lectures, and outrageously difficult exams. Take Golightly instead.

Prof Lee is a nice person as others have described, but this has no relation to his class whatsoever. Lectures often discussed unrelated topics, and students were severely underprepared for exams. No communication whatsoever (was late to a midterm, leaving students waiting outside for over an hour) and syllabus has anti-student, unclear policies.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Amazing Professor. A very nice person.
Lee was quite a nice and chill person. He has a flipped class, which was a little difficult if it was your first time learning physics.

Adrian is a nice person, an outstanding scholar, but lack of teaching skill. Most important knowledge is in his pre-lecture video(required), and just doing problem solving in class. But we have poll over to let us be in the class, or we will lose attendance. Class should explain the physics knowledge, how they work, and practice should be homework.

Prof Lee was a decent lecturer. Very charismatic, fun, lively with demos; but boring when explaining concepts/proofs. Tests were difficult, he often reused problems so if you didn't write the problem on your cheat sheet, you had a disadvantage. Class is flipped so there are online lectures-- didn't find it helpful. Not an impossibly hard class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: His lectures are pretty fun and entertaining with lots of demos and his personality is great. You'll need to do some self learning for homework since he doesn't cover some things. The whole class is curved so just do your best on exams, but they're not that difficult if you go to lecture, understand demos, and understand homework problems.

Doesn't teach at all. Expected us to already know the material before class by watching his pre-lecture videos, which explained absolutely nothing. Had to spend hours outside of class teaching myself the material because all he did during lecture were practice problems... which he never taught us how to do in the first place.

The median of our final exam was 33%, a testament to Prof. Lee's lazy approach to teaching. All material was taught in pre-recorded homework videos, with follow-up practice in lecture that we never finished due to Prof. Lee's tendency to ramble. My grades improved after I stopped going to lecture because I was able to use my time more productively.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lee is a very nice and caring person overall, but his methodology for classes and exams lacked a bit. His online pre-lectures were nice to introduce the student to the topics, but his actual real-life lectures were hard to keep up at times or he took way too long to explain how to solve a single problem. Also, good luck with rotational motion lol.

The professor is nice, mediocre at explaining concepts and walking through practice problems, but his exams were beyond difficult. He doesn't cover or explain enough, and the difficulty and complexity of problems far exceeded his lecture content. The concepts are basic, but exams are about difficult, complex, and twisty applications of the topics.

Only know him from flipped classroom videos, but Prof Lee was amazing. Lectures were extremely clear and not too long, gave examples with very minimal at home tech, example solutions were worked out clearly. Kudos especially with the weird situation - made my grade possible. Exams were quite theoretical and tough

Fantastic professor! His lectures and demos were fun, but class could sometimes get confusing (as physics often is regardless). He tends to stick textbook problems and old exam questions from other professors on his tests, and the questions themselves are not too difficult. Homework is very manageable. Very smart and reasonable, would take again.
He's a nice person and gives good explanations of concepts, but he seems to focus more on his research than lectures. His lectures are a little unorganized and he uses previous test problems.

Two words - QUESTION REUSER. Professor Lee loves to take level 3 questions from the book and previous test questions for his tests. He usually doesn't write his tests until the day before, so study his past tests. He's a nice guy, but lectures can be meaningless. Be prepared to teach yourself a lot, but that should be expected with any class here.
He reused questions from his previous finals/Yildiz's midterms on his 2nd midterm and his final. Bless that man.

He has very fair assignments. Midterms reflect examples he goes over in lecture, but the final was tough. Overall, I really enjoyed his lectures because he constructs them in an entertaining way. Definitely one of my favorite professors in Berkeley so far!
Not particularly interesting or a spectacular lecturer, but he's a nice guy and loves to talk physics.

Horrible professor. H7C is not supposed to be geometric optics... the treatment of relativity was somewhat old fashioned. Barely had time to cover quantum mechanics in any meaningful sense. Don't recommend for honors courses. Not that you have a choice (still better than non honors course)

I love Lee! He is so cute, friendly, and understanding. As a professor, though, he doesn't do nearly enough example problems, so you have to teach yourself for the homework by reading the textbook, having the solutions manual, etc. Tests were reasonable and the curve was, as departmental guidelines go, 25% As, 45% Bs, 35% Cs. I'd recommend him.

Professor tries pretty hard during lecture to help students understand material by giving easy explanations and trying to make involved demos where he does goofy demonstrations for students to learn.  The tests are okay, (mainly depends on other students because tests are curved).

Great professor! Great attitude towards students and class. Very approachable and friendly during OH. Fairly easy to understand in lecture, although reading the book prior to class is important during harding E and M concepts. Last third of class was rushed. Tests generally okay, but hard to prepare for because there's so much material. recommended

Overall a pretty good professor.  Lectures were very general and gave an overview of the concepts .  This made the problem solving in the homework a bit difficult at times.  Do the homework and practice problems and the tests are straightforward and easy.
his lectures were incredibly helpful and clear.  made 7b as painless as possible

I agree to everyone... he is absolutely fair. So... understand the topic... go to class dude! don't be late. Well lee is pretty good especially on lectures. i know this is bad grammar but well it's engineering.
Shows interest in his subject.
overall a pretty good professor. his lectures are clear and well organized. he's really nice in office hours, and exams are hard but fair.
Like a big, warm, cuddly, physics teaching teddy bear. Entertaining classes, though reading the book is very important to follow him through some of the harder materials.
go lee
extremely friendly and enthusiastic, very approachable, challenging but fair tests, sometimes not great at explaining more difficult material, but overall an awesome professor
Prof Lee is a very enthusiastic lecturer with great examples and clear, easy to follow notes.  He made a potentially difficult class very reasonable and very interesting.

Good lectures and I liked how real world/relevant examples were talked about, but the exams in this class were just bad honestly. The class was not run very well compared to some other classes despite the large GSI team and it didn't help that nobody (the GSIs AND students) seemed like they wanted to be there, we're all just fulfilling reqs.
Very good lecturer and communicates math concepts well. Literally saved this course because the other professor who teaches this class (Rui Wang) is very bad
Much better than Wang, but still did not give any study material for midterms.

She is clearly much better at communicating mathematical concepts than Wang, but still is incredibly vague on the scope of exams. No practice tests were provided to students, and there was no overlap between the homework-style questions and the exam content. The best advice is to get old midterms from older students who already took CHEME130.
Not an easy class but the professor does a very good job making the material understandable. Has funny stories about history of math
This was the best and most useful course I've taken at Berkeley. Very knowledgable prof who knows the the most cutting edge research in AI.

The lectures were well-organized and lecture notes were easy to read and follow after class. The statistics portion of the course was better taught than previous data science courses I took. Exams are not the easiest but fair. Office hours were helpful.
Very clear lecturer, much better than the other prof.
really smart

Incredibly smart and very enthusiastic about the subject. Course was extremely well-organized with clear lectures and lecture notes, especially with how much content the course covers. Created a welcoming environment to ask questions, and is simply one of the smartest and kindest professors I have seen here!

Very knowledgable on the subject and on complex concepts, clear explanation of content, and genuinely wants students to learn. Office hours were really helpful, and could break down hard problems into easy steps.

Confusing and unclear on what will be on the test. "everything is a fair game" that's what she likes to say. hw is heavy and hella hard. grading is unclear. only get 1 example to refer to on lecture to do the hw. lecture is confusing and not organized.
Awful lecturer, broken participation, unclear grading scheme, and unreliable at best for discussing what kind of content would appear on exams.
Very Hard class. Mandatory attendance in the morning rights after another Chemical En
Joint instructor for abovementioned class. Lectures candidly and makes an effort to highlight important parts of the content.

great guy, just a bit scatterbrained, but he does care about his students. short quizzes every few weeks, but no midterm and just three short projects, which is nice. concepts are really interesting if you're into behavioral econ or psych. definitely recommend this class as an elective for econ majors if you want a break from math-heavy classes lol

Daniel is a hot mess... He's incredibly unclear about expectations for assignments and projects. He's all over the place and is constantly asking students to send him email reminders for things he should keep track of himself. He's not funny, and if he loves Stanford so much, he should just go teach there...

Engaging most of the time and can be funny but really struggles with being on top of things. Did not show up to our first day of class and then made us take our final exam outdoors on the last day. Good lecturer but all over the place and super forgetful, + at least one mishap per class is a little crazy
Professor Acland is a unique professor. The persona might surprise you at first, but you'll end up really liking his humour and insights. Would recommend to anyone.

mandatory attendance with clickers, but is very attentive to his students. I think his rigour and straightforwardness might surprise more than one, but the course isn't inherently hard. expectations were set early on, one just has to follow through

Amazing professor. Lectures are clear, interactive and allow students to participate quite a lot. The content is really fascinating and thoroughly presented with good examples and case studies. Great class for anyone interested in public policy, psychology or econ. The teacher is really caring and nice.

Thoughtful professor, engaging and caring about his students. Gets a bad rep, but truly tries to push for understanding as much as possible. Lectures can be fun, and guest lecturers were great – could only recommend to my peers

absolutely bad, everythibg is hard, and he intentionally wants students to suffer

one of the worst professors i have had at berk - he is so disorganized with content and then gets frustrated when you ask him simple questions. incredibly rude and demeaning, esp in OH/emails. his grading is incredibly unclear and confusing, the class is so much work and esp being taught by such a bad teacher worsens it. epitome of yt male

I really enjoyed this class. The exams, lectures, and problem sets all tie really well together, so the content is well organized and easy to follow along. Psets and exams are very fair. Super interesting class and would recommend

Acland is such a nice guy. Detailed lecture notes really help, especially if his teaching style doesn't work for you, and both the tests and the curve are reasonable. You can tell he has genuine interest in the intersection of psych and econ and tries to present the material in an intuitive manner

Problem sets are rather short but very useful in understanding materials. Exams are doable though there is time crunch during midterms. Would definitely take it again!

Super dedicated to students, class well organized. I would highly recommend Dan as a professor!

great instructor, kind man, difficult problem sets/midterms, INSANE final.

worst professor EVER

by far the worst class and professor I've taken at Cal

Midterms fine, and the final was hard, but Prof Aganagic is def one of the most caring profs and will work with you to succeed in the class.

Prof Mina's own lectures often were confusing and riddled with jumps in logic and/or conceptual explanations and proofs, but her GSIs more than made up for it; they were very clear and covered relevant material. Her tests are extremely straightforward and and very fair. She was super caring during COVID and reduced her class difficulty, amazing!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Mina is a very sweet woman, but her lectures are all over the place. It was hard to know what to learn. During COVID, she was super nice and caring. The midterms went back and forth. It was hard to understand what to know for each and what to study. 1/3 of the exams was super hard compare to the other 2/3. These 2/3 were VERY straightforward.

If you have never taken calc before she will definitely be no big help. Self resources like teaching yourself, reading the book and/or taking and adjunct course will save you. Her lectures are not clear. She herself is not great at answering questions or clearing confusion but she is kind and tries.

Was the best professor I could have asked for in these tough times as she kept trying her best to accommodate and changed the class structure multiple times to make sure the students were comfortable and learned the concepts instead of focusing on grades and stuff. Her lectures weren't very clear but she didnt make attendance compulsory so....

She's very flexible and accommodating (in these dire times). Lectures are clear. Tests are super straightforward. Exams were made to count for less of the final grade in the beginning of the semester because everybody made dissatisfied noises on the first day. She shortened the final bc we were assigned a late time. Super nice would recommend.

She is clear in her lectures and in what she expects you to know for the test. Her HWs are Mastering Physics, so could be easy or hard. Her tests can be easier (Midterm 1) or much harder (Final). She does focus on certain topics too much, i.e Geometric optics, and sometimes ends up making a particular topic boring. But overall, solid.

Lectures were borderline useless, and made the material even more confusing. I have professors in Mse who explain quantum better than she does. She's not good at answering questions, and her accent really gets in the way of clarity. The GSI also really dropped the ball on this one. Mina might get 1 out of 5 stars, but the GSI gets 0 out of 5 star

Instead of being the promised introduction to QM and thermo (Bohr model, particle in a box, ideal gases), we spent 80% of our time on upper-division Quantum and the remainder awkwardly covering stat mech. Lectures were incomprehensible, and the GSI did all real work of teaching and writing problems. In sum: a disaster on par with the Hindenburg.

As others pointed out, lectures were absolutely incomprehensible, and if someone asked a question she couldn't answer, she'd get visibly more erratic subsequently. Homework was brutal, midterms and final not so much. But really the worst thing was the unfair grade boundaries (although I'm not sure how responsible she is for that)!

Lectures are extremely confusing, making the textbook your primary instructor. Homework is interesting, but beware if you find a mistake in the solutions - it will be difficult to get it fixed. Exams are also interesting, but are based on deriving material not directly covered in class, and thus very stressful under time pressure.

Do the reading before class; the way she talks is occasionally brilliant if flustered, but the problem is that most of the time her lectures are borderline incomprehensible, unless you already are acquainted with the material. She's friendly and all, but just not great at explaining anything.

She was an amazing Math 1A professor. She was clear about what she wanted you to know and tested you as such. I had a great first math class experience here at Cal because she was willing to take the time to explain concepts and didn't assume you knew everything. (unlike some math professors here)
She is an amazing professor! Her exams are straight forward, resembling much of the homework. She doesnt throw any curve balls. Highly recommend her!!

HW and Qz's are worth only a small percentage. Everything is centered around 2 MT's and a Final. Tests are an accurate reflection of HW and Qz material. GSI are where you will get more intuitive examples, while Prof gives more general, abstract informal proofs, or derivationsexplanations.  Responsive to questions, but GSI is main point of contact

ABSOLUTELY AMAZING. So far the only math class I've taken is 1A, so I have no experience with other profs, but considering all the lukewarm to atrocious reviews other profs have, I feel very blessed to have had Mina. She's a clear lecturer,  gives perfectly straightforward exams, and is quite enthusiastic and charming to boot. Easy A if you study!

Mina is super adorable! She is very organized and all of her notes are uploaded to bcourses after class. Sometimes she can overcomplicate certain topics but overall is very clear. If you took AP Calc AB in high school, this class will be almost entirely review. If you do the homework you will be fine on midterms and the final. Highly recommend her!

Mina is a fine lecturer. She explains concepts clearly and goes over example problems in class that are very similar to those given on the tests. The tests were challenging but by no means overwhelming and if you do the homework you should be well prepared.

In general give clear lectures with good examples; tries to answer all questions.  Quizzes and midterms are relatively fair; the final comes out of left field, however, and is much harder than either of the midterms.
Very hard to follow her lectures. But other than that midterms and final were decent and fair.

Generally explains concepts pretty clearly, and gives lots of examples in class. Her midterms are pretty easy, but that means a lot of people do well, which brings the curve down at the end. Final is a LOT harder than the midterms so watch out. Otherwise she's a pretty good professor
Best math professor ever! She's clear, her tests are very reasonable, and best of all, she doesn't take herself too seriously. If you can take Math 1B with her, DO IT.

Math 1B is apparently the most failed undergraduate course at Berkeley due to intense grading and difficult tests...Prof. Aganagic makes this class completely manageable though! She doesn't try to throw curve balls in her tests and even tells you how to approach every problem. Take Math 1B with her if you can!! You won't regret it.
BEST TEACHER EVER. gave hints on how to solve every problem on the first midterm.

I took this class 4 years ago when I was a freshman. I was doing some scheduling and found myself on this website again and remembered her, and just wanted to take the time to mention that despite her nervous tics and tendency to reach the end of lecture covered in a layer of chalk, she was one of the hottest math professors I have ever had.

Mina isn't teaching this class anymore, but I really liked her. She was kind of nervous and kept dropping the chalk and the eraser, which I found very endearing. Class was early so I skipped out most days, but sometimes I went just to admire her (that pic above doesn't do her justice).  You just need the textbook and your GSI for Math 1A.

Don't take this class if you have never done Calculus.  It's really hard.  She's a sporadic teacher.  Her accent is hard to understand.  She tries really hard, but she's just not a good teacher.  I was in tutoring for this class four days a week, at least.  I eventually took 16A and did much better.

She apparently was nervous and struggled with her explanations at times.However, considering the topics of the class, I think she organized the lectures pretty well, gave very fair and straightforward exams, and showed her passion for teaching.
