Well... The material for Physics 7C was Quantum Mechanics and Relativity. I think she taught it very well and clearly for such a difficult topic. Her tests were really fair. Rather surprised to find such a young professor teaching this subject.. haha.. she's pretty hot... Enjoyed this class a lot!

Went to every lecture, but what helped the most was having the answer key for homework problems. As long as you thoroughly understand all the concepts behind the homework problems, you're set. Class attendance isn't necessary.

If you have taken calculus prior to her Math 1A class, this shouldn't be too difficult. I thought she was a decent lecturer; she goes through lots of examples. She has an accent, but she isn't hard to understand. Mid-terms are straight forward. The final definitely threw some curves, but if you understood the material, you could work through it.

Everything but the final was really easy. The final even wasn't that bad. She just threw a few curves that a lot of the class didn't expect. I didn't get some of them and still pulled off a good grade so don't worry so much about the final. If you know your stuff then it's fine. O yea she sucks at lecturing so you'll have to go to a GSI. Get Jana.

Kind of difficult to understand during lecture because she was always super nervous teaching. Her midterms were pretty hard and the final was ridiculous. If you study hard and use the book alot you should be able to pull an A. Lecture isn't all that helpful, if you have questions go to her OH or GSI's OH.

Good class.  Straightforward tests and material.  Not the best lecturer, but it is worth going to class because Mina is pretty hot.  Brains, beauty, and she's super cool.  She is still young, so I imagine her lecturing skills will improve in the upcoming semesters.
Great professor!  Very willing to clarify things.  The best part, though, is that she is totally cute.  I'm in love.
She is great, very enthusiastic, and generous with the grade curve

Homework and lectures are decent, but what sets this professor apart from others is that the midterms are pretty straightforward and there aren't any "clever tricks" to most problems. However, the final was harder than anticipated. On another note, she is very cute for a physics nut, but that just might be the berkeley-vision taking over the senses

Midterms were very straightforward and like the homework, but she really tried to kill us all with the final. Overall, she needs to improve a bit on her lecturing skills. It seemed she was trying too hard to get our approval. The class is pretty easy, just make sure you don't fall behind, especially when you learn about proofs :/

Easy class, easy midterms...but the final was horrendous. She went out of her way to make it as difficult as possible with at least 5 parts to each question. She posted 3 sample finals online, all of which were straightforward and very similar to the midterms, yet the final was long, complicated, and poorly structured.

It's an easy class if you just do the homework. You don't even really need to go to lecture. My only incentive for going to lecture once in a while was to check out Professor Mina and listen to that cute accent. And she does explain everything well.

easy class - she does a good job of making it seem harder than it is (ESPECIALLY when it comes to delta-epsilon proofs, geez!). if you took any calc or precalc in high school the class will be totally fine regardless of her teaching. lectures are pointless
She is very helpful in office hours.  Midterms and finals are fair.  Lectures can get a bit wordy but still interesting and cover the material well.

If you already know General Calculus, Math 1A with her may be a bit boring, but I know some people who were afraid of the lecture about Delta/Epsilon proofs.  It was enjoyable because she pronounced it "ep-sigh-lawn" but it confused a lot of people.  She needs to work on her explanation skills, but otherwise, she's a good and fair teacher on tests.
supercool

Her exams are _very_ fair. When I took the final, I thought to myself, 'Wow, this exam is really well done!' I couldn't complain if I got a bad grade since the the tests weren't crappy like most physics tests I have taken. She seems to be new to lecturing and stutters a lot tho. Prolly needs more practice and/or confidence.

she's very nice, and she just may be the cutest string theorist EVER.  however, she isn't all that talented at explaining things.  if i didn't already know the material i'd be lost in lecture.  i usually just check her out and wonder if she's married while she's looking cute and defenceless while struggling to finish an ambiguous explanation.

I took Data 8 over the summer, but only watched Professor Adhikari's lectures from Fall 2021 because of how brilliant she is. Not only is she an amazing intellect in Math, Data Science, and Physics, but her control over language is so masterful that she can explain anything in the most intuitive, elegant way. UC Berkeley is so lucky to have her.

Adhikari has pedagogical mind that is so brilliant you only come across it once in a lifetime. Her ability to speak about probability in such an intuitive way is unparalleled by any other professor. She doesn't just teach you probability - she opens your mind and teaches you how to think differently. Pure genius, and a gold standard for professors.
Probably one of my favorite professors in berkeley. She is super knowledgable and a GREAT teacher. Any concept you have questions with she can explain it in a way you can comprehend. GREAT CLASS!!
Very inspirational. You will learn a lot from this class if you attend lecture and read the textbook. Two thumbs up!
Adhikari is a great lecturer and very engaging. The course content is on the harder side, but she explains it clearly.

Lectures are extremely fast-paced, made it hard for my adhd brain to keep up. The textbook is written by Adhikari and is fantastic, homework are really tough. My gsi didn't really seem like they wanted to be there. Adhikari is an absolute master of the topic, and doesn't mess around. Pay attention and turn in your work and you will be good.

Adhikari is an amazing professor - her lectures are super engaging and her textbook is super helpful. The class is challenging but doable with unstuck study and consistent effort. Definitely take this if you can!

Once during a lecture, Adhikari said she thought her students were crazy for telling their friends, "140 is a disaster - please take it!"

We all laughed because it's true.

Adhikari will be teaching 140 for the last time in Fall '24. If you can, take this class with her. Just do exactly as she says and you'll be fine. She's the actual GOAT.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lots of homework

reviews.comment: one of the best classes at Cal. amazing prof, fair tests, but very challenging homework. expect a large time commitment. it will pay off
Good class, prepare to think

By far one of the most inspirational and best classes you will take at Berkeley. Make sure to keep up or it will be near impossible to catch up. Just do what she says word for word and you'll be fine.
Genuinely one of the best professors that I've ever had, she's also written a really good textbook for the course. Overall, would highly recommend this class even though it's a lot of work.
she is amazing. best class ever

absolutely an amazing lecturer and professor. Her lectures are always so illuminating and enlightening. Even if the concepts take a long time to digest, she was able to explain things in the clearest form. hands down one of the best professors I have ever had.

Extremely engaging lecturer and always ready to help students, the textbook that she wrote is really clear too (and even has videos of her explaining concepts). Overall, really great class and gave me a good foundation for future classes
she's a very organized instructor that sets clear guidelines, but the material was extremely difficult with a very high workload; and she was intimidating and didn't seem to take well to questions
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She ignites my interest in math and the importance of math and statistics in data science. Before taking this course, I'm not a big fan of math courses, but this class has been truly transformative for me for my future pursuits. Prof. A has been very fair on HW, and exams and very caring her students.

For a course about randomness, Professor A. is extremely fair. The lectures genuinely teach, the homework labs can be long, but the work can be done if you read the amazing textbook and go to class. Data140 is a hard class, but genuinely worth taking. I'm below average and I haven't finished the course, but I stand by this.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The professor's knowledge of the course is evident in the lectures. Labs, homeworks, and projects aren't too difficult. Having at least a basic knowledge of Python would help, but you don't need any prior knowledge to do well in this course.

Prof. Adhikari is patient and knowledgeable. However, this course is tough for students with no prior coding or stats experience. If you have some experience in both you will do well! If not, expect to attend lots of office hours and labs. Also be prepared to feel super lost and spend hours on homework. Good luck!

Professor Adhikari is a great lecturer who explains new concepts clearly and makes them easy to understand. There are many resources available for students in Data 8 to succeed, and I found it to be very manageable even without extensive prior coding experience.

Data8 is easily with prior coding experience and quite tough without. Office hours and textbooks are AMAZING resources. Adhikari herself is a great, laidback lecturers who is great at relaying concepts. There's a reason Data8 is one of people's favorite classes at Berkeley

She is an amazing professor. As an introductory class for statistics and Python, DATA c8 is not a hard class. However, two professors make it a relaxing and useful course. Much appreciated. Definitely recommend this class to every student who is interested in exploring data science.
Difficult class, great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prob 140 with Professor Adhikari was a life changing class. I learned so much, and she lectures so clearly and so well. Material is quite difficult, but if you work hard you will learn lots and be prepared for any machine learning class you might want to take as a followup. Highly recommend this class. Also go to her office hours! Very nice class.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Data 8 is one of those classes that's spouted as a great class for non-STEM students. What they don't tell you is that most people in it are CS/DS people looking for a GPA boost. So if you're truly a curious non-STEM, it is REALLY HARD. I had 0 coding experience and felt so lost, as much as I tried and went to OH every single week. Just beware...

In the most simplest terms I took this class and then declared the minor immediately after. She doesn't really teach this class anymore but she's an absolutely amazing lecturer. because of her I got into data science and have a job and a minor. Words cannot describe her.

She's literally one of the best lecturers I've had, so good at explaining concepts and so knowledgeable in her field. She's also hilarious and gives great lectures. Made me want to minor is DS. Wish she would teach a full class though instead of having another professor teaching alongside.

Adhikari has a talent for making difficult material digestible, and on top of that she is so organized which makes this class one of the more reasonable ones in my opinion. She's sassy (which I love) and for good reason, and her lectures always capture my attention.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I think she's quite overrated as a professor. She definitely has a talent for clarity, but she is also intimidating, and often doesn't take well to questions.

Every single lecture of hers is a gem. She has a very coherent way of presenting concepts that will make you understand them very intuitively. She also drops jokes occasionally and keeps the class engaged. She is a Berkeley legend and for good reason.

I thought I hated the field of statistics, and then, Professor Adhikari happened. She not only inspires you to work hard, but more importantly, she enables you to develop intuition towards problem solving in a pretty hard class, and helps you see the beauty in what you're learning. The best professor I've had at Berkeley.

One of the hardest but best courses I've taken at Berkeley (this is for Stat140). Insane course load, but I learned so much out of this class. Grading was also incredibly hard but that doesn't make it any less of a great class. Prof Adhikari's lectures were amazing and that made an extremely conceptual class a lot easier.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great lecturer. Best professor Ive had at Berkeley. She can be tough on you some times but she really loves her students and pushes to get the best out of you. Go to lecture, she gives so much insight on material that you cant get from just reading the textbook. Homework was challenging but satisfying when you finally figured it out.
Data 8 was such a great class! Work definitely needs to be put in, but it will pay off. Adhikari is an amazing and entertaining lecturer. Highly recommend.

Ani is amazing not only is she a funny professor but her lectures are worth listening to. Data 8 is very structured and easy to understand and pass if you put the work in. I also went to her for office hours many times and she was great!

I love the lectures that Professor Adhikari delivers, and last but not least, she makes the content really engaging and lively. Having taken Stats 2 beforehand, I didn't feel bored. I felt like I was refreshing and refining knowledge. I definitely recommend this class as an alternate to Stats 2.

Amazing professor. Great lecturer who is very clear and communicates material in an understandable and charismatic way. Also, she is very inspiring in terms of the data science field and encourages students to challenge themselves and try new things outside of their comfort zone. Would definitely take again.
Data 8 is severely overhyped but she was a solid professor

Already well established in data science, Prof. Adhikari commands respect. Her lectures are clearly logical, and she can handle any kind of bizarre questions students might have. Workload is high not because of homework but because you have to do a lot of self-studying (pre-read text, exercises) all on your own, or you'll be VERY lost in lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Love her! She is tough and she will get answers to her questions (you must participate). Her classes are no joke. She knows what she is talking about and she will do everything she can to teach you. She is clear, driven, and focused. She asks tough questions and will make every side of the room participate. Definitely take her class!
She is an expert in the subject and she has the ability to convey it in a clear and focused manner. She is a genius and her lectures reveal her sincerity and diligence towards her profession.

One of the better professors that Ive had at Cal so far. Great lectures in that she explains things very clearly and is very fair when it comes to assignments and tests. Would definitely recommend taking her for Data 8.
OMG I would definitely recommend her if you are about to take stat 134. Her lectures are clear and fun. She's pretty friendly too
I've had her for Data 8 and Prob 140. She is amazing. Very clear lectures, really help you understand the material. She has inspired a love for statistics within me
Best professor at Berkeley. Stat 140 was a difficult class but her lectures were very clear. Going to Office hours helps a lot as well. highly recommend taking a class with her; she's brilliant

There are not enough good things to say about Prof. Adhikari. She's hilarious, knowledgeable, and engaging. Although 134 was an extremely difficult course, Adhikari likes to focus on the overall intuition behind things by providing clear and consistent examples in class to support the logic. She invites questions and encourages participation.

Both she and DeNero did a fantastic job creating a course that would be accessible for everyone. There were some issues with the course logistics, but many of these stem merely from the sheer size of the class (several hundred students). I would highly recommend this course to other students who would like a good introduction to statistics and CS.

The best professor I've had at Berkeley so far. Never before have I had a professor that was SO clear in her lectures and where I didn't have to learn from the textbook at all. She's brilliant and I'm so in awe of her.
the best professor I've ever had at Berkeley

Everyone knows she's great. I'm taking her again next semester. She's brilliant and dry, witty and to the point. Calculated, caring, charismatic, and in her words, "not a softy". She struggled with data8 a little because it's not stats, which she mains. But she is a great teacher and mind. Honestly, the course was easy to bite into and an easy A.

Ani is not a Distinguished Teaching Award recipient for no reason. I took Stat 134 with her in Spring 2016, and her lectures were crystal clear. 134 is conceptually difficult but she and the GSI team were pretty amazing. If you have a chance, take any class taught by her!
One of the best professors at Berkeley. Highly knowledgable, delivers crystal clear lectures, really helpful in OHS and much more. Really loved the class.
She gives excellent and very clear lectures that made stats accessible even to my very non-mathematical brain.

Very knowledgeable and is an amazing lecturer. She explains everything very clearly, and provides insight that is not found in the book. Grading was fairly distributed, mostly A's and B's. Definitely take a class with her if you can.

Took Stats 20 with Adhikari Fall '13. If you have the option to take a class with her, I would 100% recommend it. The way she presented the material was so clear that I was learning without even knowing that I was. She never put up notes from lecture, but attendance, attention, and good notes will take you far with her class. Lucky to have her!
lucky to get her

This was a trio of introductory online courses on statistics, and she was able to explain the subject in a very accessible and simplified way. She uses her voice wonderfully: has a clear pronunciation, stresses the important points, has calmness and humour, and great clarity.
excellent experience
In my top 2 of the best teachers ever!
despite the difficulty of the course,she delivered the lessons with clarity combined with wit and humor! keep up the good work, prof. a!
I love everything about Prof. Ani - she's wonderful teatcher. I love her sense of humor and great voice - pleasant to listen to!
Prof. Adhikari is a great educator. She makes the not so easy subject accessible to almost everyone and she even triggered in me the desire to study further the topic.
My dream professor! Couldn't ask for more. She ultimately rocks my stat world.

Hands down the best professor I've had at Berkeley. I hated statistics coming into this course, but I ended up attending every lecture and enjoying it! Adhikari is humorous, clear, concise and fair. I loved her, take stats with her if you can!

Prof. Adhikari is one of the best professors at UCB. She incorporates humor into her lectures and is very knowledgeable, professional, and friendly. You definitely learn a lot from her class. The quizzes were relatively easy, but the midterm and especially the final were killer... so watch out!
Very clear and precise
She is one of the best professor I have ever had in my life. I will be always grateful for her best teaching..

Wonderful, hilarious professor who is passionate about the subject. Keep up with homework, even if its not mandatory, and midterms and the final were somewhat hard but nevertheless fair. I think that if I spent more time I definitely would have gotten an "easier A".  Study past quizzes and midterms for the final!
Her enthusiasm and clarity makes the learning process enjoyable. She has a real knack for engaging the students, and I feel truly blessed to have been afforded the opportunity of learning from her.
Unusually good
i lover her teaching style
She's a really awesome and friendly professor. She's open to her students and I think that's what makes it easy for knowledge to be exchanged between her and her students
Very enthusiastic and knowledgeable about her subject, a pleasure to learn from.

Adhikari's lectures are crystal clear and really engaging. Hands down, one of the best profs at explaining difficult concepts of any department. She might not look the most approachable, but I have found her to be very helpful and to give really good advise.
I AM IN LOVE WITH HER. Despite being a straight female. This professor is amazing. And kind of terrifying. But mostly just an excellent teacher. SO glad I'm getting to take her class.
The class is competitive but she teaches the materials very well

Fantastic Professor! She expected nothing short of hard work and dedication when it came to homework in her class(HW was very difficult and R heavy). Sometimes she could be rude and wasn't very helpful in OH because she doesnt believe in giving you the answers. Lectures were so amazing i made sure not to miss a single one!
She is not a nice person. A lot people dislike her. Homework is too much. Totally don't recommend her!!!

An amazing lecturer. No one expects stat class to be hard so the low easiness goes without saying. She has depth of knowledge on this field of study, and her examples always highlight the most important aspects of different methods. I went to every lecture, not because I forced myself to, but because it was fun.

Worst professor. She assigns homework from the book, but her tests are not even remotely like the book, she expects you to know equations that are not in the book + doesn't give them to you before hand +5-6 chps a week, terrible professor, but she thinks she's all that because she runs the stat department + people suck up to her all the time!!!!!!

The fundamental concepts for Stats is relatively easy and the class is very slow paced. The only difficult part is that the avg. for the midterm is so high that you can't really miss a problem if you want an A.

She is a great professor! You really  have to keep up, and lectures are highly highly recommended if you want to get an A. She follows the book very closely, but her examples are what will be on the tests. But she really cares about the students and she is funny and entertaining. Take it with her.

Her lectures are very clear and easy to follow. However, make sure you can do the problems outside of class as well. I recommend getting a study-buddy or two (this really helps). She also gives problems that are recommended but not required-do them. I didn't do well in the class because I tried to do all the work on my own and didn't ask for help.

Prof. Adhikari is a really great lecturer, and attending lectures is both mandatory and enjoyable. She makes the course harder than it is, but she makes it really fun and exciting as well. The atmosphere she sets in class is well-disciplined. There's only 1 midterm(you will encounter 1-2 difficult problems), and performing well on it is important.

she has a ton of experience teaching the class so she knows exactly where students usually makes mistakes and will warn you against doing so. she's one of the best professors i've seen at cal. she's impeccably clear, her boardwork is easy to follow, and she even makes funny jokes and tells interesting stories. take this class with her..not purves.

Hands down, one of the best professors here at Berkeley. Super clear during lecture.  Makes what we are learning tangible and practical.  Very logical person, and she can be quite funny.  During some lectures, she walks on water.  She is OG for real!

A very clear professor and well paced.  Although this is "Stat 2", not everyone will end up with an "A".  Beware, the stupid students seem to do better.  The more intelligent ones are too conceited to study and will be careless -- possibly getting the lower grade.

This class is hard, but Adhikari is an awesome professor. You can't really blame her for the difficulty of the course, because she does an excellent job in providing examples. There's plenty of help for the class (OH, SLC) if you choose to use it (and I recommend that you do). You'll get out what you put into the class.

Adhikari is a very helpful professor. She actually cares about students' well-being and tries to be as clear as possible. Still, the class is much more difficult than it seems. A lot of students end up doing worse than expected.

I loved her and this class! She has taught intro stats/this class for over a decade and was clear in her lectures. She always took the time to ask for questions more than once in every lecture. Her exams are fair as long as yuo come to lecture, do the hw, and and the practice problems she posts for exams and quizzes. Don't take anyone else!
Excellent teacher, but I definitely would not have gotten through the class without my high priced tutor.

Professor Adhikari is extremely challenging. This was both good and bad for me. This was one of the hardest classes I have ever taken, and she does not slow down. However, that just meant I had to find ways to keep up. If you're committed and go to her office hours, you'll learn a lot and will be proud of your final grade, no matter what it is.
she is an excellent professor! i just went to class and i wasnt even in it! she applies stats to the physical world! she should win the nobel prize!!!

Professor Adhikari is always thorough and clear in lectures. She gives helpful examples. Attend her office hours if you have trouble with homework and I guarantee that you'll come away with many insights. She has very clear-cut expectations, so just do what she asks and you'll be fine. She also has a wicked sense of humor. Definitely recommended!

She is exceptionally skilled at teaching statistics. Doesn't go too fast, never makes a question seem stupid, writes everything clearly.  Great sense of humor.  Lectures so well, I actually overestimated my understanding of the material.  If you actually do at least some of the optional homework, you should be fine.  I still got a B-.
Still taking class. She is tough, but very good. Fair grading scheme. Good amount of HW. Go to the SLC. Definitely recommended. She has a good sense of humor. Very serious, does not waste your time.

She gives crystal clear lectures which are extremely dry but helpful. Tests are hard, though, because you really need to understand the concepts rather than memorize standard solutions to problems. Make sure you do the homework and do well on her quizzes. Don't stress about the MT since you can drop it (I failed the MT but still got    A grade)
EVERYONE does worse than they expect in this class. Not an easy class. The exams are very hard, though Adhikari is a nice professor and tries to be fair.
Very condescending. Extremely rude during her office hours.

Adhikari is a very practiced teacher. Her lectures are clear, helpful and she won't waste your time. That said, her tests are the devil. Make sure youre getting in the actual percent range of your desired grade (i.e. 90% and above for an a, etc), and dont listen to the stats for the exam because in the end there will NOT be a curve.

Prof Adhikari is a very engaging and clear professor.  However, her tests are pretty tough.  Also, you can learn all the material from the book so whether you go to class or not all depends on which method of learning you like better, lecture or book.

Adhikari gives good lectures and teaches stats well.  Although she teaches well, and makes sure there are no questions during lecture, her tests are not very fair.  She likes to give trick questions and question types that were not covered in class. There is hw that is not turned in, but essential to learn the material. Quizzes as well.

Adhikari is the reason I stayed in school and didn't drop out.  Enthusiastic, passionate, caring, witty, super intelligent, friendly, challenging, clever, funny, and a pleasure to wake up early for an intriguing lecture.
she is very nice, and teaches very well. Even though I did not do well in the class, but i will still suggest take Stat 135 with her. keep in mind that the book is so bad writen.
many trick questions not covered in class. graded on the curve, every point counts.

As always, Adhikari shows her enthusiasm for teaching through her clarity and concern for students. Quizzes are easy; STUDY for the midterm and final, especially the tricky, subtle points she makes in class.  You might learn about 85% from just reading the book, but her lectures are DEFINITELY worth going to. If given the choice, go with Adhikari.
great lectures
best professor I ever had. incredibly clear and concise. You can see she really does care that you learn the materical behind her tough-love attitude. incredibly helpful and sarcastically funny.

Prof Adhikari is the best professor I've had thus far. She is organized, time-efficient, concise, and very clear in explaining concepts. It's because she's experienced in teaching stats, and it shows when she stops to ask if there are any questions. Her quizzes are quite fair, but midterm and final will definitely require a deeper understanding.

This class goes at an easy pace and the professor is very organized and concise in lecture. Her quizzes are fair but her midterm and final killed me. She likes to ask tricky questions that makes u think.

I love this woman!  She is very entertaining and presents the material very clearly.  Tests are CHALLENGING, not tricky.  I would definitely recommend taking Stat 2 with her.  The only problem I had was that the class is only out of 100 points (I still got an A-).  Just do the work and you'll be fine!

Although statistics is crappy overall, she at least has some enthusiasm for it and though it didn't rub off AT ALL, her lectures were tolerable, especially since there were so many numbers involved. If you're going to take Stats at Berkeley, you minus well take it with her.

I think she is a great professor. She is very clear and concise with her teaching. The only downside is the grading.. her quizzes are okay, but midterm is a killer. Despite my bad grade in the class, I still like her and would recommend her.
She's ****...... very arrogant and doesn't care about other people's feeling.

V. good intro stats class.  She is a great professor-great lecturer, v. clear/concise, no-nonsense, good examples, etc.  Quizzes, MT, and Final were all fair.  Class is only out of 100 points...so you're lost if you do poorly on more than 1 quiz (get to drop one) or on the final.   Perfectly manageable if you go to all lectures and keep up.

Adhikari is one of the best. She's VERY clear about what she wants and is sensitive to our needs. Advice: go to lec (it saves time), and understand WHY more so than HOW. FORCE yourself to grasp theory! If you want a good intro course or if you have to take stat 2, def take it from her, but keep up and know that the curve will be high. Good luck!!
Her midterm and finals are not representative of the examples that she gives in class. They are much more difficult. She is a very agressive and sometimes intimidating.

No one knows her material better, nor explains it so thoroughly.  There are lots of tricks to statistics, but Adhikari does her best to teach you those tricks as well as to solve problems just based on the knowledge she gives you.  Incredibly funny too.
Extremely inspiring and energetic woman! Actually got me interested in numbers, which i used to hate!

The truth is she is very type-A and unfriendly in her teaching style. No partial credit is given and the tests are tricky and deceptive. Also yells at students in office hours, unless she takes a liking to you.
Great professor, very clear lectures, easy class.. Just stay on top of things and do the homework.
No Comments

adhikari is actually a really great teacher, but her class sucks because it is basically based on the final, which is very tricky. quizzes are very easy, but the midterm and final are hard and no partial credit screws one over. very discouraging class.

She is really witty and humorous. The midterm is really easy, but the final is extremely tricky. This class depends way tooo much on the final tho, and you really dont know what your grade is going to be until you take the final

She's quite witty, and thorough as a professor, but her lectures can get boring and can discourage people from going. I thought the midterm and final were a little tricky, but I don't like word problems

Professor Adhikari is a very thorough teacher who tells you exactly what she wants from students. She's tough, but good. Her comic relief is hilarious and a great change from the seriousness of her teachings. All in all, she's a very good professor.
one of the best teachers I've ever had

she is a very clear and well-spoken professor, but she expects things to be done a certain way. lectures get long and the midterms are hell. oh, and don't forget to write pounds or percent or units after your answers on quizzes or else it's all wrong. there is no such thing as partial credit.
Clear and Helpful.  Highly recommended.  Much easier than other professors teaching Stat 2.
don't believe her when she says that the midterm will be easy.
A good professor, but speaks too fast sometimes.
she was great.  Her work was simple and didn't give us useful info.  she is so helpful so take advantage of it.

Statistics itself is fairly dull but Adhikari picks interesting examples in lecture and tells the best personal stories which might or might not be related to what we're studying. Wry sense of humor, cool British accent.
i love prof. adhikari!
Excellent teacher
ok professor, not great, not bad
No Comments
great teacher. easy to understand, interesting lectures
very clear explanations
She explains lectures clearly. She doesn't assign too many problems for homework. Reasonable tests.
No Comments
she is an excellent teacher, very thorough.  she has a different sense of humor
No Comments
Gives you a second chance by not counting the midterm if you do well on the final. She's a great teacher!

Professor's lectures are convoluted and difficult to follow. Very egotistical and does not support his students. Have seen him single out students, belittle, demean, and bully. Would not recommend anyone to take his class. I'm surprised he is still allowed to teach after his bullying. A few of his GSIs don't fall far from the tree.

Great professor. Lectures are interesting, but lots of concepts, can get tricky. Good to have some IR background. Other reviews that use the words "mean" and "egotistical" have a grain of truth, but by and large don't listen to those reviews. Ridiculously funny. Knowledgeable, clearly a leading expert in IPE. Lovers of Political Economy must take.

Students that participate often (& voluntarily) are usually the ones cold-called and you always have the option to pass on a question. Lectures are some of the best at Berkeley. It's really not hard to get a good grade if you attend and participate. Changed the way I think about the relationship between politics, institutions, and trade.

Aggarwal was really one of the best lecturers I've ever had. He is always high energy and very engaged. His knowledge is really expansive and he has interesting examples, anecdotes, and stories for everything he teaches. His line of questioning is tough at times, but he doesn't make a big deal of it. He's a funny guy. Highly recommended!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I took Prof. Aggarwal's class in 2011. It was hard then, and I am sure it is still difficult now. I now work in government as a trade policy analyst, and I can tell you that EVERYTHING this man taught me turned out to be true. If you want to work in trade and negotiation, this is the professor to learn from - thick skin is req. in this field.

He ruthlessly cold called for questions that were very confusing, and was not very nice if people got the questions wrong. He expected us to know way more than we were required to + assigned a TON of reading that was hard to retain. My GSI (Phil) also graded hard, with arbitrary points being knocked down because of some adjectives he didn't like.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Worst professor at Berkeley. He may be knowledgable, but he is the most egoistic person I have ever met. Has zero respect for students and does not care about you. He only cares about his "great" works and thinks he is the hottest thing since fire was invented. I quote Vinod "I don't want students emailing me because I am too busy".

Don't take his class, he teaches as if he is teaching a doctorate level. Full of himself. I asked him if he is available to meet me besides his regular office hours because it clashes with my other class. He simply said "email me and i will see if i can even meet you this or may be next week?".  Ridiculous .

One of the best professors I've had at Berkeley. Knows a lot about the subject, but his class is a lot of work. 15 page paper, but felt good to finish and wasn't horrible. Class is good for people who want to be well rounded. The people complaining are probably just the poli sci majors that arent interested being well rounded. The guys professional
He is very disorganized when lecturing and that makes the class much more difficult than otherwise could be.

Overall, a good Professor. He likes to boost his own ego and sometimes makes rude comments, but he's very passionate and makes you want to learn. I'd recommend having a backround in int'l poltics/econ before taking the class. Don't be scared off on the first day-Stick around and you will learn a lot. One of the most informative classes I've taken.

Very into himself, loves to cold call, can be unorganized. Over the semester lectures became clearer (maybe based on feedback?) Good crash course on international relations, trade issues, globalization, etc

I swear Aggarwal has been posting on this site to up his  ratings.  Seriously, how pathetic can you get?  Anyway, if you look at how long his faculty bio is, you can get a rough idea of what a braggart this guy is.  A pretty lousy lecturer, as well, and unreachable in office hours when you're looking for clarification of his ramblings.

Very egotistical; rude mannerisms; pompous; likes to think "the world revolves around him."  Takes himself way too seriously and does not show his students any respect.  Don't bother reading the books that he wrote; you won't learn anything new.  *Trust Me* Do not take any of his classes!  Take someone else!!
Best professor ever!!!  Best at Berkeley everyone should take his class. Your education is not complete without it.  Oh and he is only trying to scare you on the first day.

I don't know what the rest of these ****s are talking about, this class is one of the most informative classes I have ever taken. If you want fluff, then don't take this class, if you like blunt cynicism, which I do, this is for you. I don't know who this Boris guy is, but maybe he's the reason the class was so dysfunctional.

I was first skeptical about taking the course since whoever rated him before gave him a bad rating, but the class was so much fun and the material so fascinating that I stayed. Every one Ispoke with said the same thing and how unfair the last rating was.I have no background in economics yet I am understanding everything very well. HE IS GREAT.

Aggarwal is a very articulate, engaging, egomaniac.  His class was interesting but unorganized.  Boris is  a petty, tyranical little child; unredeemably arrogant, deliberately unhelpful and scornful of undergraduates - kiss the ass above you and**** on the face below you kind of guy.  He wasn't even my GSI, but he still managed to antagonize me.
Very interesting material but horrible lecturer! take 139b instead. This guy is an egomaniac/elitist and unbelievable cocky
Do NOT take this class--this professor is an absolutely terrbile lecturer.
He sucks
Worst Class I have ever taken. He thinks he is a god but really he cant teach to save his life

Interesting lecturer, funny guy.  Speaks very fast though so if you're not use to it, you might have trouble.  One of the GSI's was a pretentious prick and not that useful.  Very detail-oriented, themes and goals are not clearly defined.  Grades are about 70% effort, and 30% crapshoot depending on w
This guy is the devil himself. He lectures AT you and not TO you and is an egomaniac. avoid at all costs.
Unclear objectives, unfriendly, horrible class.  Boris the GSI is a world class pain in the a**.  What a joke.

The workload is heavy and it's very unclear what the goals are. The grad teaching assistants are snippy, ruler rapping despots and it's unclear whether their acting on their own or are under the prof.
it's kind of a joke of her being a professor, zero technical content, and she doesn't know anything,  she is actually racist
It is surprising that she became a professor with such pathetic knowledge levels. She is old and forgetful. What a waste of my time.
claims to be a great professor but in actuality her teaching proves be underwhelming; the class structure is excellent
Very engaging, thought provoking professor. One of the best I had at Cal. Class is very different from other ME classes and very useful
Noting exeptional , nonimaginative vocabulary , solid encyclopedia replay

Professor Smelkowska was one of my favorite professors from last semester. She was very flexible with student concerns and make changes to the course material when needed. She also was a great lecturer and every class went by extremely quick. I would defiantly recommend taking a class with her.

REALLY GREAT R1B OPTION! It is history focused but you get to pick the topic of all your papers. 2 papers and the final research paper. There wasn't too much reading. 10% of your grade is based on participation and attendance. She provides great feedback on drafts and grades extremely fairly and is very accessible outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Agol does not care about teaching. His lectures are hastily prepared, and the homeworks are too easy to learn anything from them.
If you have some background, this course is just AMAZING! His lectures connects everything I know, in a different but thought provoking way. Cant love it more!
Brutally monotonous and simply reads the textbook. Kinder than most, but just not very helpful as a teacher.
He's a terrible terrible lecturer.
Boring lecturer, skipped them after the first two weeks. Quizzes and tests are easy for the most part. Should be an easy A if you keep up with the material on your own.

Lecture is very monotonous and followed the textbook pretty closely for the few I went to. Homework was not graded, and quizzes (20%) were word-for-word homework problems. Midterms and final were quite similar to homework problems. If you do your homework and stay on track, this class will be an easy A.

Contrary to what most reviews here seem to say, Agol is actually a great professor. It's more than clear what he expects you to learnknow. His lectures, though monotonous, are clear. However, they are so clear that they rarely deviate from the material in the book. Instead of going to lecture,  I chose to read the book and speak to my GSI.

His lectures are a complete mess, as they are too theoretical. If you  study a decent amount, though, the midterms are an absolute joke. The final came out of left field though: WAY more difficult than either midterm. I used MIT OCW for lectures instead, and that's my advice to you, as his tests are very much based off the Stewart book.

Prof. Agol runs a structured class. He uses the Stewart textbook and has every lecture set up for one discrete section from the text. This is very useful since if you miss lecture, you know what to go over. Homework follows the same principle. For the most part lecture is a going over the textbook so focus on homework, do that and you'll do well.

Agol is pretty underrated. He's a funny, nice guy and can be very helpful if you ask him questions. Nevertheless, you must work for your grade. My GSI, on the other hand, was neither helpful nor clear.
He basically reads the textbook and actually makes concepts more confusing. Horrendous. Helpful in office hours, though.

Professor Agol is extremely boring. By the second month, almost half the room is gone, and there are many, many seats in the front which are not taken. He's also not very personable or helpful in office hours; he gets to the point and never offers any intuition. If you read the textbook, you'll be fine; he does exactly what the textbook does.
Very boring lectures, but good explanations. Exams are fairly easy if you study.
boring, going to lectures didn't help at all
haven't attended any lectures since the first 2; tests are very easy.

Granted exams are based on hw. But the overall pace of the class and lecturing style are very boring: a clear and loud voice does not imply clarity. The only time a spark of excitement came out from him was on the day of the final.

Good teacher overall if you are interested in the theory. Speaks loudly and clearly and classes are very structured. Shows genuine interest in helping students, although he is a bit rigid in demeanor. Exams were based on homeworks (which he gave answers to) so they were manageable.

Agol definitely isn't an easy prof for math 1A, kind of a pre-med killer, actually. His lectures are boring, but if you follow along with the book, they make more sense. Much more helpful if you approach him after class. Great sense of humor, but you might miss it! READ THE BOOK, redo homework, and you'll be fine.

I wouldn't have minded wakeing up at 8am if it was worth it. Everytime I did go to class it only reminded me of why I never went---because his lectures were worthless! His final was really incomprehensible ...find the volume of this napkin ring. What's a napkin ring?

By far one of the WORST professors I have ever had. He is a snoozefest! Lectures completely pointless because more than half the class can't stay awake through it anyway. Tests are incredibly hard, and unreasonable. Do not take this professor unless you HAVE to, trust me.

He's not interesting. His lectures are pretty much straight out of the textbook. (And you'll probably sleep through them.) You will need to do homework on your own, or you won't do well in the section quizzes. However, I hear he can climb walls "like spiderman".

One of the worst math 1A prof. i have ever seen in my life. Avoid at all cost...his lectures were useless so i didnt attend any of them...and i for sure didnt regret it becuz i would go crazy if i hear his BORING voice again...I compared his midterm with other math 1A prof. during the same semester and it was completely  black and white. His is HAR

Truly a boring lecturer, and that was proven by seeing empty seats every morning. The seats were only fully occupied on midterm and final days. I went to every lecture that semester, and honestly, they were a waste of time. Do the homework, and pray your high school background in Calculus will suffice. Tests were difficult, but definitely do-able.

I can only assume the US military will harness the voice of Ian Agol as a form of psychological torture. Dont bother with his hw; just do loads of old tests before MT/Finals (I did it his way for 2 MTs and got Cs and I did it my way for the final and got an A). Avoid avoid avoid.  He has conditioned me to hate calc, geometry, and napkin rings.

Was not a helpful professor in terms of lectures. Midterms/finals were decent but had some difficult problems. Take advantage of GSI's office hours and discussions because lectures will be pretty much useless.

Umm yeah, u can already probably tell he's as boring as hell from the other comments.  didn't go to any lectures or do any homework, but if you're good at figuring out how to come up with proofs and can solve tough problems on your feet, you'll do fine on the tests.  Unfortunately, this isn't the case with most kids.

This was the worst class ever!!! Agol taught directly from the book and essentially read it to the class during lecture. He also felt the need to write every word that he said on the board which slowed him down even more. The midterms and final were also much more difficult that the practice tests that we were given. AVOID HIM IF YOU CAN.

I'm trying to cut him some slack since it was his first year, but still, this class was ridiculous! Way to hard, and he basically just taught out of the textbook- many people didn't bother going to lecture. Agol is very nice though (although a little awkward). Go to his office hours, and he's happy to help make things more understandable.
Not helpful
monotonous voice. I only attended the first 4 lectures and got 98 for the mid-term. an easy A class.

Lectures are useless and uninteresting. Notes are confusing, hard to follow, and useless when it comes to doing the homework. You don't ever have to show up to class. Read the book, teach yourself, teach each other, go to Office Hours and you should be fine. Neither the lecture, professor, nor the notes are worth the time unfortunately.
no good
Monotonous voice, lecture is straight from the book. Doesn't seem to be interested in teaching the course.
horrible teacher. lectures are often straight from the book. monotonous voice.

His monotonous voice puts me to sleep. He never looks at the class to see if anyone understands him. He's really nice, but basically fails as a teacher. This is his first year teaching math 1A though, so maybe he'll get better =/.

I took her ANTHRO 114 special topics in anthropology course; health and disease in the past. I learned SO MUCH and had amazing discussions with the class. She definitely lectures quickly but her slides are always accessible. Very organized as well :)
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: the class was more, research, discussion, and project-based rather than exam-based. There are two quizzes throughout the semester, that are in place of midterms, and one final project. Really recommend this class, because it promotes understanding and exploring the information on a deeper level rather than just memorizing facts for exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Amazing professor but to get an A+ you need to study study study.
Prof. Agarwal class is very lecture heavy and test heavy. Midterm and final exams impact grade a lot. Her lectures can be boring at times.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Although anthropology is interesting, I found Professor Agarwal's lectures to be not very engaging. I did not read the textbook once and was able to finish with an A+ in the class. Attending lecture played a big part in my final grade though, because basically everything she says in lecture is fair game on tests. Take good notes and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT--So many papers

reviews.comment: I absolutely loved Prof. Agarwal! She was super fun and understanding (Zoom lectures were the same as in person, plus her dog Finnegan!). I only had her exams as open book due to COVID, but they followed the study guide very well and she offered extra credit. Grade is very balanced! Very interesting if you wanna learn about monkeys and forensics!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Agarwal is one of my favorite bio profs at Cal.

Her lecture were great! really funny and interesting if you're into bio anthro, but if you're not you'd probably hate it cuz they're like an hour and a half long. Tests were challenging but fair, and there were lots of assessments and papers and only one midterm. She gives iclicker credit so you've got to go to class. Labs were super cool too!

Easiest BioReq.  You MUST read the Lab book every week in order to keep up. If you don't do your work you will fall behind and very fast. Skip 2 weeks MAX and you're 2hrs of work behind. DO NOT BUY TXTBOOK very worthless exact same material as lab book. 100% on assignments if you just do them. Cannot cram MUST be CONSISTENT. If so its an EASY A!

Professor Agarwal is just great! The lectures were interesting and engaging but could get long if you're not interested in the subject. The discussion sections were where you really began to understand the material because hands on with the bones really makes a difference. The textbook was never used, just get the lab book and that's enough

Good. Not great. Had a habit of sending unnecessarily long study guides filled with highly specific topics to review - don't waste your time. Exams are almost always easier than she makes them seem. Textbook reading is unnecessary - rely on notes and your lab workbook. Friendly professor though, and does her best to help you learn

As an Anthro major this class gave a wide overview that helped me decide that I indeed want to dive into Biological Anthro. Agarwal is very approachable. She was not as intimidating as other professors and genuinely wants students to grasp the material. I enjoyed her mildly funny jokes during lecture. Take her class and don't forget your clicker!

I really like Prof Agarwal! She's funny in lecture and you can tell that she really enjoys the topic she teaches. Her exams are very fair and the research paper is actually pretty fun to write and research! This class pushed me toward the anthro major! Highly recommend!
I really enjoyed this class. Agarwal and Wilkie tag team was very interesting/entertaining. Not much work. One paper, a group presentation, a lab and a final worth only 5% in class.

I really liked Agarwal. I thought her lectures were pretty straightforward. Her exams were pretty difficult due to the fact that you had to know everything, and there was a lot to know. She also made us turn in our paper during dead week, which was lame. Other than that, I felt I learned a lot in her class, and it was fun.

Professor Agarwal is a very nice lady, though her lectures are very dry.  I got an A+ in the class and I managed this by attending every lecture and taking very detailed notes, which was hard to considering her no laptop policy.  The book is COMPLETELY UNNECESSARY.

Don't understand the other commenters but I liked the class. Thought it was interesting but it definitely did get boring at some points. If you attend lecture and do your labs it's not hard to get an A at all. I hardly EVER read and studied last minute but pulled off an A-

Alright so to my comment more legit. I got an A+. Okay, so do not buy the book. It's hella expensive and so pointless. I actually tried to read it but there is so much information that you dont need on the test that it's kind of a waste of time to read. Just complete and memorize the study guides!

Horrible professor! "Study guides" were 6-9 pages and was just a list of everything she lectured on. Lectures are SO boring and last for 1.5 hrs. Dull, boring lecturer and she makes students participate in "quizzes" where she makes you go to the front of the class and asks you random questions from previous lectures. Avoid this class if possible!

Kind of monotonous and dull in her teaching. Has you memorize a crap load of info for the exam and then tests you on more generalized information, so it's kind of tedious. Don't bother buying the book, just get the ASUC lecture notes, guaranteed A, a la me.

The absolute worst class I have ever taken.  Agarwal is couldn't be more dull.  This class consists of an overload of useless information.  Be prepared to memorize every detail about every primate species.  The book is a waste of money.  Focus on the lab workbook and buy ASUC notes (lectures are unbearable).  My advice?  Don't take this class.

Professor is extremely boring. Reads verbatim from the lecture slides and aims the class at a room full of junior high school students. If you are looking for an interesting or inspiring class, look anywhere but here.

Excellent professor, excellent class. Took it over the summer. A bunch of material, but grading was really easy. Tests were not hard at all. Final consisted of repeated questions from the midterm. Labs are really interesting. Got to look at bones...and watch videos of bonobo sex in lecture. She learned everyone's name within 3 class sessions.

She's certainly not the best, but she's good. Her tests are not that bad. If you don't study, don't expect a good grade as with other classes. She does talk fast, and her lectures can be pretty boring; however, she knows what she's talking about and is very approachable. POINT: forget the book, study the lecture notes and lab book and you're good.

contrary to what ppl are saying, i don't think she talks fast. in fact, her speaking voice is very clear and unless you find evolution boring, the material is very interesting. test was fair, focused in a lot of details, but still fair. nothing majorly depended on GSI's grading, which is a big + (took class in summer).

I found her to be extremely boring. she talks way to fast and her powerpoints are bland. It was hard to stay awake in class and with the material not being super enthraling, you need someone to keep it interesting...NOT HER! I would not take another class with her.
she is a truly amazing proff. I loved her class and learned a great deal. I dont understand why people would find her class very difficult. If you go to lecture and read, youll do great.

I'm taking anthro 1 in the summer. Overall, the class is easy! I think it's easier if you take it over the summer. The class is ALL about memorizing the little details. No need to read the book. Just study the lecture notes and the material the GSI goes over. The midterm average for the class was a B-.

DON'T TAKE THIS CLASS!  I fell asleep in every single lecture, literally. She talked too fast and was super, super boring. Ended up taking the class as a P/NP because the midterm screwed me over. Her tests ask for random, minute details in the text!  Waste of time--find some other class to fulfill your biological breadth!

My advice: Do not take her class! She was not good at all! Her lectures were boring and she spoke far too quickly. Granted the material was not ground breaking, I felt as though any of th GSI could have done a far better and more adaquate jod.
Not a very good lecturer, but you can tell she knows her stuff and that she's very interested in anthropology. This course is all about memorization!! GSIs are very important. Pretty easy, overall.

She may not be the best lecturer, but if you ever want help from her outside of class, she REALLY puts in a lot of time. Very approachable during OH. For the tests: definitely group up...they are tricky and but doable if you put some time into looking over your notes and such.

I didn't go to lecture after the 2nd week of class because I couldn't understand what she was saying since she talks so fast. Easiest to get an A is read the black lightning notes. You don't even need to read the textbook or attend lecture.

This was the biggest waste of time of my life.  Her lectures range from so slow and boring that I've fallen asleep, to so fast paced that it's impossible to write everything down.  Entering into this class, i wanted to learn quite a bit about Anthro, but now i think it's a complete joke.

I like the grade distribution for the class - it makes it almost impossible to fail. The material covered in this class is INSANE; she goes into depth about everything that I feel like shouldn't be discussed in an intro class. The tests aren't even that hard, but you are filled with so much info that by the time youre there, you get confused.

She's very nice and helpful if you go to talk to her. And the material is not especially difficult, however there are some ambiguous questions. Overall, she's a good professor. The only problem I have is that she doesn't necessarily communicate well and she talks really fast.

Very helpful, very interested in your thoughts if you were into bio-anthro (esp. skeletal stuff).  Take the time to do the reading, go over your notes and possibly read some outside sources in the recent literature.  This class is difficult, but an A is definitely possible.
she is the worst professor i have ever had.

i agree that don't attack others, there's nothing ashamed about receiving an unjustified grade from an unclear exam. she's nice, but quite stern, according to a gsi. materials were easy, but < half the exam was tricky qs, specialized materials, don't know where to study & what she told us to study, study guide, was not on the exam.

I'm sorry, please don't attack others in your reviews. For your information, I got an A- on the midterm, but I still believe she is very unclear. She occasionally has factual (not interpretive) inconsistencies with the book, especially in describing observed characterstics.Also, she seems to have a chip on her shoulder. She is incredibly defensive.
Very thorough lecture notes. The tests were not hard if you studied! Lots of memorization, but I had a great GSI and the notes were easy to follow.

No! Dude she's good!  These ppl are just bitter b/c they didn't get the grade they wanted.  Just be prepared b/c the subject calls for a lot of memorization.  She's friendly and approachable,  Lectures do occaisionally go fast for note taking, but all the power points are online b4hand, so you can't complain.

Fills the air with senseless verbiage and employs a ridiculous number of unnecessary modifiers to make her sound smart. Seems like she's saying a lot, but most of it has no substance. Probably failed HS English. Doesn't seem to cultivate a broad knowledge base (pronounced "Descartes" phonetically). Deacon is wordy, but enlightening in comparison.
Her voice makes you fall asleep EVERY time.
No Comments

The class is doable, so even though the comments about Agarwal are not so great, the class is definitely passable.  If you do all the questions on the weekly quizzes beforehand, then it's easy to get a perfect score on every quiz, and SLC tutoring is wonderful.  If you can't make it to tutoring, have a friend go and pass the information onto you.
Lectures are well structured and interesting.

Fell asleep during every single lecture. She talks way tooooooo fast so I didn't bother with notes. The only reason I got an A in the class was because I had an awesome GSI. So, I would take this class if you had to, the GSIs make up for the professor.

She'll either put you to sleep with her monotone voice or make you go crazy trying to take notes as she spews out 100 words a minute!  Get black lightning notes or SLC tutoring if you want to survive this class.

Avoid if possible. Conveys massive amounts of information in a way that can only be memorized, like a bad history class. Exams ask for ridiculously specific pieces of information. Her lectures yield about a pg of notes every 20 minutes.

agarwal is not a good professor.  she's probably smart, but she doesn't know biological anthro. her lectures are poorly organized and poorly delivered, and her incorrect use of english often has her making factually incorrect statements.  the midterm had impossible questions with no right answers.

Her style of speaking is incredibly convoluted and difficult to follow. She does not explain the material in a creative way in which we could follow easily. Her lectures are based solely on the power point presentation(she just reads). She has actually given us FALSE information in class before. F-

Professor Agarwal's lectures are to the point and easy to follow since she posts all her notes online beforehand. Her Powerpoint notes are much simpler than Prof. Deacon's in that they list all the main points instead of having whole paragraphs which take a long time to read and write down.

professor agarwal was a new co-professor this semester. she talks very fast and expects you to know a lot of facts that don't seem very important. her lectures aren't nearly as interesting as prof deacon's were, but she sometimes let us out early. the class was interesting, but seek SLC tutoring

The lectures are really boring but the readings are interesting! I went to every class, signed in, didn't pay attention and did work in the back. The class is pretty chill considering I didn't listen during lectures, but make sure to put effort into the essays, they account for a large part of your grade.

Her lectures are boring & sometimes it's really hard to understand what she's saying cause she has this weird accent and talks in monotone. Attendance is mandatory - she takes roll every lecture. The info is valuable but your grade really depends on the readers. I got a good grade cause my reader graded super easy. Lots of unnecessary readings.

Very sweet woman but I found her lectures very boring and lost interest in the class. I went from wanting to minor in this field to losing complete interest in it. Her quizzes are a bit of a joke since you will often find the answers in the first page of the reading.

Prof Agis is extremely kind and has a heart in tune with the material she is teaching. The work she requires students to do for this class was minimal, but the work you do have to do needs to be done well and given a lot of thought if you want to get an A. Also, she takes roll so you have to show up everyday because participation counts.

Love her! She is so knowledgeable and very kind, great to talk to in office hours. The content of this class was interesting and important, should be mandatory for all (easy to get an A if you do the work properly). People tended to talk through class and I was sad for them because professor Agis is so worth listening to.

This class was both interesting and engaging, but also non-demanding, a great class to balance with other more demanding classes. Movies were great, she encouraged discussion and loved to sit back and listen when the class (of ~50) went off on its own. Very compassionate, could tell she really cared about undergrads ideas unlike many profs at cal.

Doesn't grade. Leaves it all to her readers, who grades harshly for grammar. When I went to her the next semester to talk about my grade she said it doesn't matter about the grade I got and to move on. I didn't deserve the grade considering I got B's on the midterms and finals and ended up with a C+. Showed up to every single class and took attenda

This was one class that always engaged me.  Because her dry humor clothed in a quiet voice, it is easy to miss.  Her grading was more than fair, and office hours were a true delight.  The sweatsuit set did not respond to her lectures, and for that reason I would not recommend it to jocks.  Come with an open mind and enjoy!

She takes attendance everyday. She either read straight from her notes which tended to be extremely boring or she would ramble. Not a difficult class but the subject manner is ridiculously repetitive.
She is totally awesome and totally passionate. A very fulfilling learning experience.
SHES VERY HELPFUL AND HER READING ARE VERY INTRESTING SHE IS ALSO ABLE TO LINK HER READINGS TO FILMS WHICH MAKES THE CLASS EVEN MORE ENJOYABLE :D

She's really nice and tries to bring the class into her lectures but not many people respond so she gets a little annoyed. Readings are pretty interesting. GSIs look for a specific type of writing in papers but grades very fair. I would love to take her class again!
Unorganized lectures.

Wonderful woman, reminds me of all of my favorite past teachers. The readings were really interesting (I dunno about the reader material though, never touched that book) and the papers and exams were easy (short take home final!). However, the lectures were pretty dry most of the time. But it's a good breadth class.
She's really very sweet. The class was a little boring but the books assigned were interesting. I really enjoyed the class discussions.

I went through a whole sudoku book in this class.  Very boring lectures, with some boring movies.  To give her credit, she knows what shes talking about, but i still found it very hard to pay attention.  She tries to scare you with hard grading on the first paper, but its not hard to pass the class. P/NP for sure.  She takes attendence every day
Her lectures are so boring, but she seems very knowledgable with the material. I didn't enjoy the class- just overall too boring and confusing.
Very interesting material.  Mostly classes were just her lecturing which could get boring, but she'd say interesting things now and then.  Loved the readings!

everything she discusses in lecture is what you should use for the papers and midterms.  the readings were very interesting, however, she didn't make solid connections to them in lecture.  this class is really EASY, but it wasn't the type of women's studies course i was expecting.

she seemed knowledgeable enough, but the classes weren't coherent and you had no idea where she was going with the information.  the readings were interesting...but she never connected them solidly to anything else in the class (i.e. theories).  i just really hated the class.

teacher is easy, as long as you have an idea of what is going on you can pull of a c if you study before the exam you could pull off a b if you stay on top of it (not too hard) you could pull off an a..she's easy..take it if you can work to get an A

This is an amazing class that covers a lot of ground and gets you thinking and making connections between issues that aren't broached in any other class I've taken at UCB. The professor is really likable and the material she assigns is interesting and varied. The assignments aren't difficult because she doesn't test what you don't know, but how you're thinking about the material.

Her lectures weren't as good as they could have been but I really learned a lot in this class. She kind of rambles in lectures.  A discussion section was really needed but the university wouldn't pay for it!  The readings and papers were great. The movies

Lectures are pretty boring (sleepy), but I did think learning some feminist vocab was useful. Certain readings were good, but most were too pedantic for me. Movies during class were a godsend -- watching and writing about the "**** dentata" of Aliens was hilarious.

prof. agis is very nice. go to office hours! she is very helpful and can help steer you in the right direction for your writing assignments. midterms are easy. just read your notes and the books and go to lecture. this class if fun, interesting, and easy!
boring lectures, requires lots of reading. sometimes I can't understand what she's talking about..but the midterm was really easy

What a fabulous Prof. She really knows what she's talking about. For the person who wrote about her accent, maybe you should get some of that ethnocentric crud out of your ears. She's very easy to understand. Very.

Very easy midterm. 10 IDs and an essay prompt that required you to write only 3 pgs from the point of view of migrant women either working as a nanny/factory worker. very interesting videos and readings but lecture itself can sometimes be a bit borning. Easy class no discussion. two thumbs up!!!!!!!

I really dig her.  Not every single second was mind blowing, but there was at least one moment during every class that in which she would make some really illuminating, stimulating point that would rock my whole day. If you're really thinking, once the class is over, it all makes perfect sense.
she takes some getting used too, at first i was very confused, but now her class is my favorite :)

An interesting topic made completely boring by the teaching style.  She stands at the front of the room and drones on and on while you try to decipher what she's saying through her thick accent. Then there are her attendance policies.... I wouldn't recomend her.
No Comments

She was SO hard.She made us buy a book that SHE wrote on the 1st day.She didn't care if you had ordered it from somewhere else,you had to get it then.She gave no real direction with what she wanted,and she was very judgmental.She questioned my heritage.I've spoken Spanish since I was a child,and she said I she said I wasn't a native speaker.AVOID!!

Talks slowly, is sarcastic, but willing to help out, unclear teaching strategy, an easy class to pass if you know spanish really well - coming straight from span 25, it was a struggle, and... i literally whooped with joy after dropping off my last paper.  grades pretty hard.
AVOID HER AT ALL COSTS. got my worst spanish grade from her, and she was rough on almost everyone.  if you're a native AND have great grammar, you might be better off.

Pretty good teacher, allowed for group work which was great. There were some concerning and off-putting views she talked about when it came to reading certain words out loud. Overall I liked her and felt that I grew as a writer.
She is a great professor, with few assignments and a great grader. She makes us work in groups on fridays which become your good friends throughout the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very clear assignment instructions, the readings are interesting and short. You will be put into a group who will review your assignments through the semester and it's pretty cool. Discussions in class were always fun.

Abrams is a wonderful professor for those getting into creative writing! The class is structured very well to include a mix of reading poems from professionals and students. Her feedback was always immensely helpful, and the small group workshops were a great idea. Having a few students look at my work made a huge difference. Relatively easy A

Professor Abrams is one of the kindest most down-to-earth instructors at Berkeley. I learned so much about Creative Writing and was grateful to have taken her twice for the minor. If you're fortunate to take her for anything, make sure attend office hours, shes one of the best and makes you a better writer!

Protect this woman at all costs! I loved taking her class, it was fun and immersive and really made me a better writer. The exercises were super easy and enjoyable with how they tested ur creativity. She felt like a friend who was always there to give you valuable feedback. If u love creative writing u will love this class. I wish I could tae again
The course is fun and professor Abrams provides great lectures and feedback. Do everything on time with effort and you'll earn an A.

Professor Abrams is one of the kindest most down-to-earth instructors at Cal. Her grading criteria is clear from day one. There are 12 nongraded writing exercises, 25 perusal readings, three poems, one short story, and a final portfolio of your assignments. She provides excellent feedback and is always accessible for office hours. A great person!

A very approachable and engaging professor who will get to know you one-on-one. She is very talented and gives great feedback. English 43A is somewhat of a beginner writing class - other professors teach a much more vigorous and less elementary version of this class, but I highly recommend it for anyone who has only taken 1 or 2 writing classes.
Melanie is an incredible professor - she asks insightful questions that help you come up with your own ideas to fix problems. Has great writing advice and such a fun and helpful class!

She has a well-organized curriculum that brings great results. I went in not knowing much about craft, and left feeling much more confident in my writing, and more aware of my technique. Her class is a great intro to creative writing, and a gateway into writing workshops. Put it this way: if you fail this class, writing is definitely not your forte
One of the most charming teachers I've ever had. She's helpful, interesting, and gives great feedback. I loved her class, and I can't wait to read her first novel.

I took her lower division creative writing course and was very pleased with her as a professor. She's young, funny, and helpful. Her advice is really good, though I've never read any of her writing so I'm not sure what her style is like beyond her teaching. A good teacher- you'll actually enjoy her class.
It made me love creative writing!

Very helpful and cheery teacher. She was  respectful and always gave at least a page (typed) of precise commentary on every story and revision, which was usually very insightful.  Only complaint is that the "rules" for how to write a short story are extremely rigid in this class and sometimes creatively frustrating.
She´s an absolutely wonderful professor -- I would highly recommend this class to anyone who has an interest in delving into the creative writing process!

The nicest and most approachable teacher you'll ever have. She's fun and always cheery, and if you miss class, you'll actually regret it. Plus she's a pretty easy grader if you put in any sort of effort.
Loved her class... completely changed my academic career around. Nice teacher, not so easy of a grader (very particular)-- pay attention to the rules and you will do fine.
She is simple.  She teaches creative writing and is a very easy grader.
GOATED! Caring, and inspirational

Dor and his GSI are very passionate about what they teach but sometimes expect too much detail. Its a good amount of reading but class is pretty engaging with him. To be honest you don't have to attend every class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He's excellent
A very intense professor.

The professor is effective at conveying the material to students, primarily by providing extra worksheets, old exams, and review sheets that help prepare for midterms and the cumulative final. Nevertheless, the course is challenging as there are problem sets every week and lab work to complete. His assignments are similar in difficulty to exams.

Very solid professor & huge polymer nerd. He designs the PSets to be "the hardest version of the questions that you'll see," so the tests don't contain any surprises. Offers generous EC, such as Exam Wrappers (corrections) on tests for +5 bonus points, and is very active on Ed to answer any questions. Lecture slides are very useful and organized.
