very fair psets and exams--lectures can be dense but he's incredible in office hours (he tends to ramble but drops a ton of useful info in there). labs are long but doable. go to prof and GSI OH often and you'll be fine. kind and caring and genuinely wants us to succeed; def don't be afraid of this class (about the same as difficulty as math 53/54)
Clearly cares about his students and the material

Abel is clearly passionate and knowledgable of organic chemistry. My best advice would be to take advantage of the many resources the GSIs provide. Also only about 3 of the labs took the whole 5-hour time period. A 5 credit CoC ochem is not "easy" by any means. Not impossible, but def hard.

Tbh one of the hardest classes I've ever taken. I don't even blame bro for it being THIS hard. He's a chill guy. Lectures this fast (with the ton of contents) expectedly only cover the basic; to really understand be prepared to grind thru his PS with excessive YT/OH/textbook…overall a special muscle memory is required for exams. Sadly no shortcut.

12A is way better now compared to prev years in terms of how demanding it is, but it's still difficult due to how much content there is, the content itself being difficult, and the amount of time spent (especially in lab). Prof Abel clearly isn't out to get his students or make their lives miserable, and I actually enjoyed the lectures/teaching.

Very passionate about his research and great to talk to in office hours. Lectures were mostly basic material that's explained well in the textbook (ok to skip); doing the problem sets which have the most challenging examples is when you learn. Writes a ton of extra practice that is very informative and good exam prep. Incredibly generous curve.

Liked polymers a lot, sometimes wouldn't get through all the content on the slides but gave lots of extra review/practice, made his own problem sets, and designed his own polymer lab (which was very fun!) 
Chill guy who liked to talk

Slides were really good altho his speaking style is more on the monotone side, i'm sure he's actually funny but he speaks too fast for the class to realize and laugh. PLS READ TEXTBOOK it's actually rly helpful (found out during dead week rip) some midterms Qs were literally from the harder section of textbook example problems

Brooks is a decent professor, however, he often yaps for much more than necessary, including during his office hours. This would lead to him not finishing the lectures and giving additional lecture recordings and pushing back assignments. His tests are difficult but they are fair and I learned a lot from them.

Never finishes lectures, quite boring and monotone. PSs were too difficult and didn't really help with the exams. Pretty much relied on the textbook and youtube videos. Hopefully he improves for future classes.

Changed policies and exam weights mid semester. Promised curves and wrappers when averages were low but didn't deliver. Homework was sometimes ridiculously difficult and the 8 AM lecture was rough. But overall, he was a decent prof and we learned a lot of organic chemistry.
Lectures can be meandering, goes off on a lot of tangents, overall decent prof

Having him at 8 AM was rough but that may be the fact that learning ochem that early wasn't for me. Overall ok lecturer and very accessible outside of class. He talks about polymers too much but it's inspiring to see his passion about them. Exams were fair and pretty much similar to the HW. The polymer synthesis lab was fun. GSIs were also goated.

Prof. Abel explains things well and draw out mechanism clearly. However there's a tons of topics to cover so the pace is quite fast actually. Very active on Ed. Hard PS and going to office hours and rev. session really helped, and luckily the GSIs this semesters are fantastic. Exams are hard but doing practice exams and supplemental materials helps
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He's not the most exciting lecturer, but he definitely cares about students. He got rid of iClicker for the 8AM lectures and recorded them, which improved my quality of life drastically this semester. Exams are difficult, but if you understand the HW and lectures, they are quite similar. I feel this class helped build me a solid ochem foundation.

Having him at 8AM was tortuous. His exams are unnecessarily difficult (mean for midterm 3 was 47%). Points from lab + hw will give you a buffer, the curve will also help. He is a slow, mellow speaker, not the worst, but very hypnotizing. He yaps about polymers ALL THE TIME. Exams resemble hw format. Hw is VERY difficult.

Prof. Abel is an ok lecturer. He might be better if he were lecturing on more interesting content but I also feel like there are ways for his lectures to be more engaging. The laboratory final exam was (in my opinion) unnecessarily challenging. Overall, he gets the job done. His section won't be life changing but you'll learn a lot in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Brooks isn't the most interesting lecturer, but that probably has to do with the fact that the chem 12a lab content is not interesting at all instead of his lecturing ability. He decided to add an extra lecture this semester so anything we were expected to do for a certain weeks lab wouldnt be taught until next week, so office hours/gsi's are key
Great professor! Very helpful, caring, interested in students ideas and opinions on whatever topics. Lots of guest lectures. Take his class!!!

Kaicker is an incredibly engaging, brilliant, & thought-provoking professor! He taught me about both South Asian history & ways of thinking about history & politics as well. Readings ~60-90 pages/week) & the website he uses to ensure folks read is convoluted, but if you read & pay attention (easy with his lecture style) everything falls into shape.

Kaicker is by far the greatest lecturer I have ever had: funny, ridiculously smart, extremely passionate, teaches you things you'd never expect to learn in a manner only he could pull off. Readings are challenging but he's super approachable; essays are easy and the course opens your eyes and makes many a CS major consider switching to history.

Professor Kaicker is great! Super interesting class that challenges your preconceived notions of what history really is. Kaicker is a cool guy and a good lecturer; he also checked in during zoom classes which was always appreciated. 70-100 pages a week plus 4 essays. Definitely try to get a class with him if you are at all interested in history!

Professor Kaicker is hands down the best professor I've come across at Berkeley. He is engaging and genuinely wants his students to succeed. Please take his class and speak with him during his office hours. You will thank me for it. He has inspired me to study South Asian History and to think and learn about it thoughtfully.

Professor Kaicker not only changed my view of Indian history but of history in general. Through his reading assignments, he teaches critical reading, ensuring you learn how to dissect a source. His lectures are brilliant even if you're someone far removed from Indian history. He's the best professor I've ever had, and a true mentor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I took History 11 with Kaicker and he was a great lecturer!! Most of his lectures were really inspiring and made me want to take more history classes. But just be warned, lectures are not webcasted, and most of the important information isn't directly on the slides. You really have to listen. I really enjoyed taking this class!

There are only few classes that you look forward to attend and his class is one of them. After math heavy and dry technical lectures, his class and the readings would provide you comfort even if you don't have historian-like intellectual brain power. Take HIST 114B and HIST 39T, please do. - This would be my last rating for a Berkeley professor.

Kaicker is incredibly engaging. In his modern South Asia class ("Gandhi's India") he made historical figures come alive. He's kinda intimidating and he will occasionally randomly call on people about assigned reading, but highly recommend his class if you have an interest in South Asia.
I took this class at Laney College. This class is good for gen ed. A nice professor and assignments due each week are very interesting.
It can be a bit hard to understand him at times. He can be a bit disorganized at times, but it will not heavily effect you. He is very kind and loves conversing.
youre graded on discussion posts that are almost every week but youre only graded on completion. midterm and final are both group projects. Easy class.

This class is pretty easy. If u need to fulfill ur r&c a, this is the class to take. As long as you read the main books that he assigns, you should be good (he only assigned us 2). Weekly reading responses are graded on completion. He's a super great professor who's very passionate about his work, and you get a good overview of famous Indian myths.

Professor Paul is a very interesting person to be taught by. His Global Studies course really enlightened me this semester on many problems with media worldwide as well as new perspectives on issues such as racism, sexism, and classism. The midterm and final are both group projects - choose wisely.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: Amazing professor, amazing human! Take this class. It's lifechanging. You will not only learn Bangla, you will find an amazing community.

Super nice prof. His class was incredibly easy consisting of online discussions (that are fully opinionated and based on completion) along with 2 group projects (basically just a slide deck on a topic of your choice). I'm pretty sure you would have to try to not get an A the class is that easy.
Easiest class Ive taken at Berkeley, super sweet, low effort, but you do learn. Interesting guy and very passionate.
He relied on a program to grade our homework and gave zero for those whose homework didnt pass the program. Other than that he is okay.

He is by far one of the greatest professors I have ever had at Berkeley. He really made the lectures super fascinating and for that reason, I loved going to lecture. Be sure to participate because that's key in that class. Since I took the R5B based on film, we watched interesting movies with lots of social commentary which I loved discussing.

A very inspiring and caring professor, Abhijeet Paul made sure to make classes entertaining and informative, but most importantly he always tailored to what the class wanted to talk about and focus on. He tended to go on philosophical tangents in accordance to the novels that we read, that made this literature class very fascinating.
annoying prof and talked too much, class was boring, and put people to sleep. mandatory attendance sucked, best part of class was when it ended. dont reccomend
First time this professor has taught undergrads, and she is a law professor, which shows. Seems like a smart woman, but not approachable nor a good lecturer. Don't recommend this class.

Assigned quizzes every week that made us look for the smallest detail in the readings. Lectures often contradicted the answers on the quizzes and when this was brought up we were told to resort to the readings instead of the actual lectures. Lectures were very boring and hard to sit through. I felt that my GSI taught better than the professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Awful professor, and even worse of class. waste of time, and is the worst class by far I've taken at Cal. Don't recommend, and the class puts you to sleep! Lots of ranting and gibberish of reading off the slides.

i took her for 119 but i personally loved her style of lecturing! it was easy to follow but I definitely recommend participating because that lowk dropped my grade by a lot lol 

the readings were also pretty interesting for 119
Nice and clear videos, engaging topics, light workload. Definitely recommend
I don't know how I feel about this class. I hate the readings. I don't like the way materials were articulated, her teaching style just wasn't it for me. I hate the final project.

Professor Gail is wonderful!! Her lectures are really engaging and the assignments were never too difficult to do. As long as you put in the work, you will be fine. Attend office hours as you get the help you need to complete the assignments and do well on them! The course ends with a creative final project which was enjoyable to do!

If you're thinking of taking a course taught by Professor de Kosnik, this is your sign to DO IT! She is an incredible instructor who has great passion for materials she teaches. Her lectures are always interesting and easy to follo The workload is pretty light and assignments are very doable. Definitely one of my favorite classes / instructors ever

Just do all the assignments on time (they are super easy) and the extra credit. You can get upto 150% so there is no excuse for not getting an A. Did this online and was by far the easiest class I have ever taken.

I took her online summer class and honestly, I'm so glad that online lectures were modeled like an in class lecture. It felt very face to face which made lecture easy to understand. Her graders give good feedback and her assignment prompts are to the point! Her final is also a creative one that allows you to explore your passion in multi media.

Her lectures are succinct and to-the-point while communicating a ton of relevant information. They were never a drag to watch because I would always learn something new and the readings/references she gave were quite interesting. There's a ton of extra credit (up to a third of your grade), so you can focus on genuinely learning the material.

Abigail De Kosnik should be the shining star for all online classes. The course is clear, concise and to the point. Beyond that, the topic is current and interesting, yet well researched by her. The readings align perfectly with the topic and are accessible to navigate and enjoy! The class works well for independent thinkers. Fun Fun Fun!

This Professor parades her opinion around as if it is fact and punishes those who do not agree with her. It is a sad day when an alleged "academic" will not invite dissent or debate on an obviously multifaceted topic and discipline. Prepare to be brainwashed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: One of the best humanities professor I've had at Berkeley. Knowledgeable and clear lectures. Interesting readings and the take home midterms were easy to do.
Gail had great lectures that highlighted key points from the readings. Readings were pretty easy and the grading was fair.

Easy class that only presents one side to many controversial issues in media. Most of the assigned readings are opinionated blog posts reliant on anecdotes, rather than credible data. You may find that you disagree with the professor and the readings on many issues, but you will be graded down for showing it.

Professor De Kosnik is a well-spoken and knowledgeable person.  She definitely knows her stuff.  I learned a lot in her class and had lots of fun!  My only complaint is that her sense of humor sometimes struck me as offensive.  (The class is Theater 177, Sound Design and Media Theater.)
Very fun to listen to. Has a lot of interesting things to say and lot's of enthusiasm.

There is a softness to him, calm, patient, sincere, that makes you want to listen not because you have to, but because something in you recognizes the truth in what he is saying. He teaches not just with intellect, but with intention, like someone who understands that knowledge is something sacred, not just something to pass.

Prof. Salim is incredible - you can tell he cares deeply about the material he is teaching, this has allowed him to deliver some of the most engaging and thought-provoking lectures. He's also extremely considerate regarding student accommodation and genuinely wants to see his students succeed. I would highly recommend taking a class with him!

It is becoming difficult to find professors teaching about Rumi's poetry that come from the same land of the material being taught themselves. Professor Salim's natural relationship to these topics enables him to guide his students effortlessly through a historical and theoretical lens that I have never encountered before. Please sign yourself up!

Very knowledgeable and engaging teacher with a wonderfully contagious sense of humor! He knows how to run a classroom of diverse students and elicit discussion in an inclusive environment. Highly recommended!

Professor Salim is amazing! He is able to engage the students with the materials and create a welcoming environment within the class. He creates a space where students feel not only intellectually stimulated but also valued and respected and his approachability and genuine interest in his students' perspectives contribute to a sense of community.

One of my favorite classes I've taken at Berkeley! He genuinely cares about his students and the material he's teaching and overall makes the course interesting for everyone. Loved this class and hope he teaches another course soon!!!

AMAZING professor who makes something as difficult as Rumi's poetry approachable for a non-poetry expert. He is very accommodating and engaging in class which is always nice. The material of the class is difficult but he makes sure all his students feel heard in their contributions and always pauses during readings to check our understanding. Love!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This has been my favorite class at Cal! We covered so many texts/themes but it wasn't overwhelming and the connections made between the past & present, layers of meaning, poetics, and language and power were eye-opening. The class was like a healing space for me and I felt supported when I needed extensions. Prof. Salim is witty and very caring.

Prof Salim was a really understanding prof, and worked with us no matter what level we were at. I probably had one of the lowest Farsi proficiencies in the class, yet he was completely understanding. For me this class was a grind because of how long it took me to read compared to my peers (and we read a LOT), but well worth it to practice Farsi.

A wonderful & engaging teacher. He's funny, extremely caring, & supportive of his students/their overall well-being (especially during COVID). He has a gentle yet keen ability to get even the quietest people engaged in discussion & blossom; he truly has a gift with teaching. 10/10 would take any class with Prof. Salim!
Dr. Dernburg is a very smart professor, but she expects you to know everything she does when she doesn't explain much. Her quizzes are so hard.

Her exam's class average was less than 50% because of how confusing and poorly worded it was, while the other two professors who taught the class this semester had an A/B exam average. She was late to her own office hours and sped through her lecture slides. Unfortunately, teaching isn't her priority. Avoid taking the class with her if you can!
Her exam's class average was

In lectures, she went on tangents that were irrelevant to the exam and got through 35 of the 45 slides that she put together for a 50 minute lecture. Even though she didn't cover the last 10 slides, she still called them "fair game for the exam" even though those slides had little context. Her exam tested us on info that was irrelevant to the labs.
The only professor I have taken the time to write a comment about their poor guidance and excellent roasting ability. Eminem has been real quiet since this professor dropped her last single.

The most unfair and nontransparent professor I have come across at my time in Berkeley. Also had her for MCB104, and MCB133L is just as bad. Incredibly tough grader with exams being almost irrelevant to what we were told to study. Does not give good feedback either. It's exhausting and disheartening for students that actually put in the effort.

Genuinely the worse professor, super rude in regrade requests and took away points just for having a long response when this was never mentioned. This professor changed my perspective in the worst way possible about a course I would have otherwise enjoyed.

I don't even know how to describe it :( the quiz for her section was awful! the first prof was so fair but her exam I could have not studied at all and got the same grade cause there was just no course content on it 1) the test was AI generated 2) she COOKEd me in a cauldron 3) The quiz had content from MCB104 which wasn't covered in class.

Was dismissive during office hours and used ChatGPT to answer questions (literally just pulled up on the laptop)
Had a very strict grading rubric and her "quiz" had a much much much lower average (40%) than the other course prof(80%). 
Refused to give any points back for regrade requests, seems very sensitive about being wrong
She was not understanding of her students at all. Lecture felt unorganized. She often contradicted herself while lecturing and then would later realize she made a mistake. It was very hard to follow.

late to her own office hours, no understanding of students at all. wanted people to show up to her lectures that are not even helpful by deleting and not posting course captures. when asked on ed discussion wrote a 7 paragraph essay about why she thinks watching lecture and not attending in person is not the right way to go about learning. horrible
Graded very unfairly, did not follow syllabus

The worst professor I have had at Cal. Rude, condescending, and not "for the students". Made the grading curve approx 10% lower than it has ever historically been, does not respond to emails, changed the syllabus to not provide lecture recording mid-semester (is that even allowed??). Steer clear of Dernburg, no redeeming qualities as a professor.
Made class mandatory 2/3 of the way through which was difficult to handle, took attendance very seriously. Exam was difficult but tested content fairly.

Accessible outside of class and is genuinely knowledgeable and passionate about the subject but is honestly a terrible professor. Lectures are often disorganized and goes into minutiae detail about topics she deems important, unforgiving about attendance, and openly hostile in Ed Discussion. Worst professor I've had during my time at Cal.

Extremely unaccommodating compared to the other 104 professors during this semester & demands lecture attendance even when the syllabus did not require mandatory attendance. Lecture recordings were only offered if you attended that day, no practice exams were offered, no regrade requests, etc. Absolutely awful!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Don't take this professor. She goes on rants in lectures. She was upset about the low turnout during office hours, but she made her office hours during a section's discussion time(mandatory). The final was completely different than the practice questions. If you decide to take her classes and she says not to memorize something, memorize it.
Super unaccomadating. Her exam was completely non representative of her section of the course. Horrible

Demands you show up to lecture - despite it saying it's not mandatory in the syllabus. She is accessible outside of class, but is a poor lecturer who tends to rambles/go off on tangents. She'll claim you don't need to memorize specific examples, but trust me you do. There was no practice exam, reviews, and the problem sets nothing like the exam.

reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: They way she lectures is a bit disorganized, but nevertheless informative. However, her test contains incoherent questions and is very tedious and convoluted to go through.
Unclear presentations, often left class early, canceled office hours, poor instructor.

Very disorganized lecturer; rambles about whatever she wants to talk about on her slides, which were in a really confusing order and could have been organized much better. Also, her problem sets are nothing like the actual exam (no multiple choice). Her section (cell bio) is very memorization-based.

test was hard but still a high average.doesnt cover things in depth but will still want you to know every detail about some things. likes to dumb things down in lec AND ask tricky questions on test-dont underestimate her just cuz she leads you into thinking you understand everything she presents in lec. questions are much trickier than lec stuff

She talks way too fast!! Puts a giant load of information on slides and not only does she speak rapidly, but also changes powerpoint slides too quickly. Plus, her exam was a nightmare (many incoherent questions), and probably the longest and most tedious midterm exam I've ever taken at Berkeley.

Worst of the 3 professors! Refused to post the slides before the lecture when students asked because the sound of turning pages bothers her! What kind of prof is that. She goes too fast and teaches only what interests her, not what we are supposed to be learned. Avoid this prof!

The most unclear teacher out of the three.  However, upon listing to my own recording of the lectures, along with the notes, I could follow along.  Everything makes actually makes sense.  I felt she emphasized too much esoteric material and not enough broad concepts.  The test was pretty long and difficult.  Generally not pleasurable...

The worst ever. Her slides were completely useless. And she just put random stuff on the midterm that she never went over nor was assigned in the readings. That was an impossible midterm. She is also very unclear in her lectures. You can tell she just started teaching. Her test is so freaking unfair. Brought my grade down even more in this class.
STAY AWAY! She tested on content not lectured on and gave incorrect information on powerpoint slides. The slides were useless most of the time.
she will know if youre slacking off!

Overall, she is very knowledgeable in the course and course material, but for an introductory course to Arabic, she is heavily biased towards heritage speakers. As a non-native speaker, if you have neither a strong vocabulary base or understanding of Arabic, please take another professor, you only make your life harder when you take her.
So kind!! She goes above and beyond to make sure everyone understands the content. She grades fairly but effort definitely matters. Truly recommend her.

Amazing professor!! Highly recommend. The "Women in Islam" class is beyond amazing at analyzing women's rights in Islam and Islamic history. Super sweet and caring professor, would highly recommend this class to everyone! No discussion, only 1x class a week, couple presentations and papers!

The class I took was HUM 10 not MELC146! 
He is very clear in making a point in his lectures and goes back to sum up what the main point he was trying to get at. Soft spoken (I don't know if it was the mic or not) so I recommend sitting in the front. He tried making himself available as much as possible as long as you reach out.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment:
graded by 4 things (2 essays, 1 midterm, 1 final)
Can skip class and not do readings cause not emphasized in class.
no homework, essays are 1500-3000 word requirement and exams are 7 easy multiple choice and 1 to 3 short essay questions based on a provided reading

Was genuinely interested in the material, but the presentation of concepts made them hard to grasp and there was little guidance for essays and exams. Prof. Ahmed is kind and intelligent, but he goes on tangents more than he provides a clear lecture structure and exam content isn't clear. Not beginner friendly, take a different course for breadth.

Never wrote a review but came to write one for Prof. Ahmed. Best I've had in my time at Cal. One of the few whose lectures I was genuinely engaged by and actually retained material. He explains complex concepts very clearly. He's an amazing lecturer (not common), pay attention and you will do great on essays and exams. Will be taking him again
His essays are graded insanely hard. I dont know if it is him or just the gsi or a combination of both but wow.

Dr. Ahmed is a very caring and open-minded professor. The class being mainly discussion, he himself stated that every year his beliefs on very basic viewpoints are changed because of what his students bring up in class. His exams and essays are easy if you are capable of displaying basic sentience and he clearly wants his students to do well.

Ahmed is sweet. He's a soft-spoken lecturer which can sometimes make me sleepy, so remind him to adjust the mic. The class and lectures were interesting. You get to analyze a bunch of Quranic texts and have long discussions with peers, then the whole class. The GSI is chill and both offer great feedback. You'll be writing 4 essays. Not bad at all!

One of my favorite professors. He doesn't just teach things as "the way it's always been," he teaches different conflicting perspectives and pushes us to question the status quo. In a 100 person class, he learned everyone's name. There was a lot of reading but tbh you don't have to do all of it. Essays required some effort, exams were easy A's.

A really great professor and if you put forth any effort he will love you. Professor Ahmed is possibly the nicest human being in the Bay Area and he makes a dry subject engaging. NES146 is a self-paced class, so if you wait till the end of the semester to do all your work you're making a mistake though.
Extremely knowledgeable, approachable, kind.  Eye candy too :P

He's a good teacher who really knows the subject well. His class is a mix of lectures and discussions, and he's really open to letting students guide the direction of the lecture with questions. He's a kind, gentle person who puts learning first. I enjoy his class.

He is one of the nicest professors that you'll come across at Cal. He genuinely cares about his students. His class is discussion oriented, which gives a relaxing vibe to the class. Amidst all this, you also manage to learn quite a bit about the Quran and Islam.
Amazing professor.  Brilliant and kind.  I got hooked to this class.

I'm in the Taekwondo sparring class right now, he's hilarious and is a really good teacher, really intense at the beginning but he's really nice and understanding, gives us a lot of breaks, midterm is just a bunch of kicks, blocks, etc. One of my favorite classes at Berkeley imo.

took taekwondo 1 and 2 (self defense). classes start with intense warmup, then a lof of practicing techniques, and working in pairs of groups. also stretching and brief meditation. prof ahn is understanding and funny. however, the class takes more time and is more demanding than other PE classes.

Master Ahn makes taekwondo very approachable and gets you working. He values effort above anything and doesn't care about your prior skill background. Being a kickboxer, many of the moves weren't too difficult but nonetheless still learned something. Since the grade is based on skill execution, it can be harder if you have no background.

Nice guy, fun class, easy to pass if you try a little. Almost fully reliant on attendance + participation due to lack of written/other assignments; classes are sports practices. Sometimes will forget what has/n't been taught, including Korean names of things. If a TA (I was one) is present, will almost always have them run warm ups. Good exercise.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Taekwondo was really fun with Mr. Ahn. Also teaches you some Korean! It was a really great way to let off some steam throughout the semester. He has a way of being serious during class but also being caring and light-hearted. Gets upset when studetns are late to class but there isn't a real punishment for it. just some sit ups, squats and jacks.

Master Ahn is a wonderful martial arts teacher even for those without any experience. I took his introductory Taekwondo class and really appreciated how he pushed his students to do their best, incorporated self defense skills, and used lots of repetition to make sure we had proper technique.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Master Ahn is a very open and approachable coach, he teaches the philosophy of the movements along with really great specific instruction throughout the class. You can make up classes throughout most of the week, so the schedule was semi-flexible. You gotta learn the moved though! Practice! Great workout, great fun, and helped me stay focused.

Master Ahn is a wonderful Taekwondo teacher!  Sometimes he can be difficult to understand, but he has a great heart and he cares about his students and their well-being.  He is willing to work with you if you have a disability, and his knowledge of the subject matter is very strong.  He's passionate about what he does; nothing better than that!
I know I would be better at Taekwondo if I could just understand what he is saying! But other than that, he is a funny awesome teacher who scares me sometimes.

Attendance is a must. Master Ahn will get upset if you do not show up to class. However, he offers ways to make up days you have missed. My suggestion to be consistent, practice, put in effort and make up any absences. Overall, he is a good and friendly instructor.

Master Ahn is a great teacher, and teaches for most of the period (the TAs warm us up).  He is much less harsh than most Tae Kwon Do masters - he sincerely wants us to have fun. This is the perfect "in-between" class.  It is an energy-booster.    The world champion of Tae Kwon Do was my TA for the first couple weeks - it was amazing to watch him!

This class started out fun, but as time went on, there was very little interaction with the instructor, leaving us at the mercy of our less-than-helpful TA. Ahn maybe taught 30 mins of the entire hour. I had a really positive attitude going into the class, and it completely dissipated by the end of the semester.

In class you actually have very little interaction with him as it's the TAs teaching most of the time.  I had amazing TAs and enjoyed the class a lot because of them.  Master Ahn... plays favorites and yelled at the TAs because they let us play a game for warm up.

A very encouraging and great instructor. In this class I got to learn a lot, not only in the class but also outside the class. Taking the belt test was also fun ~~~I heard almost everybody from white belt to yellow belt passes ^^ . Oh, and amazing TA's - Jusin & Christie :)
great taekwondo instructor! very easy A if you try just a lil bit. i enjoyed the class so much that im going back to TA for him  in the fall.

Master Ahn is a great martial artists and a great instructor. In this class the grade doesn't matter, because you benefit from physical and mental training. This class is a great in-between class if u got an hour or so, instead of making yourself go to the rsf.

Master Ahn was not only an incredible instructor, but also an inspiring man. his dedication to the martial art of taekwondo seriously made me want to be a black belt, no matter how hard it may be. Even as one of the only white guys in the class, I had so much fun and recommend taekwondo PE for everyone.

(I ta'd for him 6 times) Grading: top 10 get A's, next 10 get B's, the rest get C's. Top = attendance, enthusiasm, and improvement. BUT, WHO CARES ABOUT THE GRADE!??! IT'S 0.5 UNITS! AND IT'S A MARTIAL ART! YOU LEARN TREMENDOUS AMOUNTS OF KNOWLEDGE, DISCIPLINE, AND YOUR CONFIDENCE SHOOTS THROUGH THE ROOF. Take a tkd class, and if I'm wrong drop it.

I really love this man. He is a really nice, sweet guy. There is a midterm, and I found it hard, but it's a really fun class and he teaches it really well. Because of him I love Tae Kwon Do and I am definitely taking it next semester.
Master Ahn is the best! He is so enthusiastic and energetic. He also has a great sense of humor! Take Tae Kwon Do!
Ahn was an excellent instructor. I have good memories of his classes.

Ahn was a pleasant instructor personally, but he didn't give a clear enough idea of how we were to be graded. Prepare to be surprised. This should have been a relaxing pastime; it ended up being difficult and I had minor injuries camp at times (but that may be due to our demanding TA.)

dr. ahn is clearly very knowledgeable about tae kwan do.  i found his class very challenging and enjoyable.  my main complaint is that my final grade was much lower than i thought.  i recommed taking this class, but you should take it pass/fail, not for a grade.  there are weird grading restrictions on the PE teachers.

M90 will be a bit difficult if you, like me, don't have much of a prior musical background. She goes over stuff quickly so beware of being left behind if you aren't well-versed in what's currently going on. An awesome instructor who taught me tons of theory. This course is not only a theory course but you'll also need to play music (and live, too).

Professor Ahn is a very sweet and supportive person. She can be unclear when it comes to grading expectations, but in general she is very accessible and caring for her students. However, I feel that for students without prior experience with music theory, this may be a very difficult class. I highly encourage attending lectures.

Jean Ahn's teaching is alright, but the class itself is extremely disorganised. It was a mess of harmony + musicianship, mixed with group work. I barely learned anything and dreaded going to class. I wouldn't take a class with her again - she isn't great at explaining and I felt like she thought we were middle schoolers by the way she spoke to us.

I learned a lot in this class because Professor Ahn really emphasizes participation right from the beginning. It can be a little nerve-wracking sometimes but it makes you learn very quickly because you have to practice every day. She also offers a lot of help outside of class and is very supportive and adaptable.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Jean Ahn wastes no time in class. The classes are perfectly paced; they are challenging and she pushes every student to do their best so no matter if you are the best or worst student in the class, you will be challenged and learn a lot. After taking Music 52A with Jean Ahn, I feel like I have made many improvements in training my ear.

She's a talented musician and fair professor. If you've never learned about music theory before (and even if you have) this class is difficult, but if you show up to lectures and pay attention, you'll be able to complete the homework and pass the quizzes. The only thing is she doesn't have a lot of office hours. Create study groups with classmates.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Not gonna lie, I was kind of intimidated of this class bc EVERYONE has to participate (ie singing in front of everyone), but after a couple of weeks I eventually calmed down and really started to appreciate Jean's approach to teaching. She truly cares about helping her students and is super understanding, so the class is a very safe space to learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: did not give us any feedback at all on any of the work submitted during the semester, including the final essay. I suspect he does not even look at it and just gives A- to everyone. lots of weekly work (400 or 800 words long reading responses, 100+ pages of reading per week). made me not want to do the work despite being interested in the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The class was meant to be a seminar/discussion but an overwhelming amount of the time students were either too shy to speak or weren't sure how to answer the questions asked.Questions were difficult to understand. A prior knowledge of the subject is definitely necessary. Spent 10+ hours a week on the class just to understand the gist of materials.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I would not take his class again. They are set up in a way to fail the student. We are not provided with any of our grades until they post it. Extremely, against the Iranians and put differentiation among them and other students to the point that the class becomes discouraging for a student to study.

Professor Diab was very kind and courteous with all of his students, and the readings were intriguing and thought-provoking. The class was meant to be more of an open dialogue, but much of the time it seemed that students were either too shy to speak or weren't sure how to answer the questions asked, making it more lecture-based but still enjoyable
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment:
sp '25 was awful with how the course staff handled the cheating with little to no communication, does not care about the students (mt1 and mt2 on the same night burned me out so bad)
he mumbles & talks fast + accent, hard to understand during lectures, gave prac exams but both the original and the retake mt1 were much harder and very different imo

Pretty hard tests but doable if you study (sell your soul and put in the hours as with any other weeder class). Many ppl made a big deal because we had to retake the exam; lots of complaining on ed discussion but rather than using that time to study for a second chance on the exam they chose to whine and waste time.

Genuinely does not care about the students or their concerns. Have never met such a horrible and insensitive professor, also made the exam retake extremely hard even though we had to take a 3 hour cumulative final.
bruh. like bruh

His exam was difficult because he includes stuff that's barely covered in class, and he made the retake drastically harder. Almost impossible to feel like he cares about the students learning and actually enjoying the content he teaches.
spring 2025 cheating scandal survivor xoxo

Aside from the cheating situation that was poorly handled, he was a meh professor. Heavy accent, forgets to turn on his mic sometimes, speaks very quickly + mumbles a lot (mixed with his accent, it's sometimes impossible to understand). Hard exams, not enough practice. At least he provides practice exams, but still hard.

This man DOES NOT CARE ABOUT HIS STUDENTS. He made us scan our own exams using our phones at the exam. Then he heard about cheating and voided the exam and combined it to make a 3-hour exam with midterm 2+ no cheat sheet. It was so unfair for those who didn't cheat, and doubled our workload to take a final level exam in the middle of the semester

The lectures are ok, but when you get to the exam, you get shocked by what you see. Also, they are very poor at handling issues that happen (such as the cheating situation; they made us retake the exam bc they couldn't catch a few cheaters)
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This man DOES NOT CARE ABOUT HIS STUDENTS. He made us scan our own exams using our phones at the exam. Then he heard about cheating and voided the exam and combined it to make a 3-hour exam with midterm 2+ no cheat sheet. It was so unfair for those who didn't cheat, and doubled our workload to take a final level exam in the middle of the semester.
Awesome professor, great lectures. The class is tough but he teaches it well. Highly recommend

i felt like the exams were much harder than the homework and i could not follow lecture at all. this was also when it was online and it was bad quality overall, so maybe it was better in person. i 100% used my ap physics c knowledge to pass this class, without it i'm not sure if i would have been able to understand past the first few weeks.

He seems like a chill and kind dude outside of class but it was so hard to follow his lectures. He constantly writes on a board the entire time and it gets really boring. Makes you wanna fall asleep. Aside from the dreadful lectures, passing the class is fairly easy I guess and if you put in some effort will get at least a C.

Best lectures I've had. Very efficient time management, excellent and entertaining examples. Had students sit on rolling chairs with fire extinguishers to use as propellant. Walks through derivation of complex formulas well.

A solid prof, clearly knows the material. He stays behind after class to answer student questions. Tests are very hard but there is generous partial credit and a curve. Lectures tend to be very fast and run long, especially once we switched over to Zoom.

I think Yildiz is a very good professor. He goes very quickly during lectures but is very patient and thorough during office hours. Doesn't give a lot of homework, so it's up to you to get in enough practice. Difficult but reasonable midterms.

Firstly, Berkeley time is 9 after the hour every lecture so expect that if you have a walking distance in-between classes. Also be prepared for very challenging midterms. If the homework is a 3 level of difficulty, the mid term will easily be around 13.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Yildiz is a big teddy bear. He really teaches the material well and his lectures are fantastic. The class is definitely hard. The midterm/final can be agonizing, but he is super approachable and will give you what you need to succeed. He's like the grandpa I wish I had. Yildiz makes a class as hard as 7A feel a lot more approachable. Good luck!
The concepts are not a reach, but the exam level problems on the homework are very difficult and take a lot of time. Also the tests are very difficult, but curved.

Really Great Professor, good at lecturing and is very enthusiastic about teaching. He always stays behind after lecture to help students and answer questions, as well as, recommending we come to office hours during difficult topics.  Only drawback: He makes super hard midterms and finals; average is centered around 50%, yet is generously curved.
Best class at Cal! Recommended to all interested in biophysics!
Very enthusiastic!
Pretty good overall, but could be better.  Also the GSIs for this class are kinda terrible, watch out!
Overall a very good professor. Some have criticized him for being a poor lecturer, but I personally liked them. More often than not, they were easier to follow than some parts of the book.

Professor Ahmadi is an outstanding academic who is very erudite. Given his valuable contributions to Persian literary works and the Persian language studies at Cal, he is very competent and ensures that students learn the material in depth. Lastly, he aspires to share his wealth of knowledge with students and he is very genuine.

My academic life was transformed and defined by the presence of Professor Ahmadi at UC Berkeley. He is a scholar of the highest caliber and I have learned so much from him. I did my honors thesis with him and had about 10 classes with him overall. He genuinely cares about his students. I remain grateful for learning so much from him.

A real gem. Hes well-versed in Persian literature and pretty much most other things - history, critical theory, politics, religion. Classes have an active role for students. He calls on you to read, helps with pronunciation, meaning, and ensuring youre absorbing whats being said in the text. Great sense of humor. Texts are readers

This prof is nice, educated, and lenient grader. However, his lecture style's very hard to follow because he goes all over the place (history to history; subject to subject) in 1 day. I slept all his lectures-he takes attendance). There's a take home final! So assignments are only one midterm, one take-home final, and class attendance. Guaranteed A

Very educated professor, seriously learned so much from him. His style of lecture is a bit hard to follow sometimes but all in all I definitely recommend this class-especially for Irani/Afghan students to learn a bit more about their literature's history.

He is a very good teacher. He knows what he is talking about and more. He is so informed on the middle east and he is a great person to go ask a question whether it be about the culture or politics in the middle east. Just do your work, if you need help ask, he will offer his time to see you pass.
If you want to learn about Afghanistan, This is the class. Prof. Ahmadi is an expert on the issue and is very passionate about it.

He is a very nice and approachable person. He is a Fair grader and if he believes you are working hard you will get a good Great. he is a very Knowledgeable and professional person in his field. he truly impacted my perspective towards history and literature.<3amazing person!! just take the class and go to lectures Your life will be rocked! :)
A very nice and down to earth Professor. Helpful and he knows his information. If you study you will get a good grade. I learned so much in his class plus he is the best in his field of study.
He is great. the Best Prof at NES. He knows alot.
he is the best, he knows his material and he is very respectful, if u really want to know farsi lit take a class w him

comes off arrogant inside the class and is the same way outside of class. He's not the most well spoken or interesting professor so if there is another class out there with a different teacher take that one...only take his class if you have NO OTHER OPTION!

he is an ok teacher...he's not one to inspire you or to make you feel like you really learned something but if you want a B take the class...if your striving for that A/A- dont bother...he's very random with grading
Nice, kind, understandable. Don't miss him.
If you want to experience the one of the best instructors in Berkeley, take a class with ShahWali Ahmadi. Class is fun and you learn a lot with no stress. I took NES 162 and Persian 103 with him.
Awesome teacher. Show up to class, pay attention, and do well.

He is an extremely nice guy and very good at what he does. He's funny and engages the students well. He goes off topic sometimes. Don't annoy him, or he'll embarrass you in front of everyone. He's also very political.
The best economic theory course! David managed to both showed the big picture and explained the details extremely well. He also has a great sense of humor. Take whatever course he offers!

Very cool professor! I like it that he's trying very hard to make us understand every detail and also at the same time trying to get us to see the big picture and not get lost in the nitty gritties of the proofs. He is also pretty funny and answers questions very well. His lecture notes are very clear whereas the lecture is less structured.
Ahn explains well.  He's relatively young for a professor which helps him understand our confusion and frustration. He's also pretty funny.

great class.  he has reasonable expectations since its only 3 units.  he usuallly throws in random lectures where he just talks about interesting random things.  very worthwhile if you want to spend 3 hoursa  week learning really cool things with a chill professor take this class.  he's laid back and funny! textbook got low rating cuz we dont have

Eh. If you're Econ, this is the hardest class there is, easily(econometrics is literally a walk in park in comparison). If you're math, this is cake. As for professor Ahn, he's pretty cool: I thought he was very sensitive to student needs and really cares about trying to be a good lecturer. But he didn't provide a book...that's a minus.

This is actually for ASTRON 128, I didn't find it in the Course Code list. Definitely recommend taking this course if you want to do research in the future, very similar to the actual research experience. Professor Parsons is an amazing instructor and really helpful during the office hours. He is one of the best professors I've ever had.

Aaron is an incredible professor. He was very receptive to all our questions (and always down to chat), he cares about his students, and his explanations are uniquely intuition-forward/demo-oriented. Radio Lab gave me so much practical knowledge about research, moreso than any other class at Berkeley. It is a lot of work, but super fun!

Professor Parsons is an amazing instructor who knows the material inside out. The course is demanding, as lab classes are, but the effort pays off. I gained more practical research experience here than in any other class. Even if radio astronomy isn't your main interest, the skills you develop in lab are incredibly valuable and broadly applicable.

Labs are self directed & challenging. Lab manuals are purposely vague. Won't grade anything until the end of the semester, but is accessible outside of class. Participation matters a LOT. Provides no rubric and assigns scores arbitrarily. Go to OH to get lab "cheat codes" that you otherwise would not have figured out.

Aaron is one the best profs I've ever had. Radio lab is challenging, and for sure takes more time than a regular 4-unit course, but I learned so much! He was so supportive and provided many extra resources to the students who were unfamiliar with the material. PS: The course now uses Python, NOT IDL, which makes things 100x easier.

Class is really tough and won't say it's easy to get help to do well in this class. Parsons isn't the most accessible person out of class and you'll have to really rely on yourself and your groupmates to keep yourself afloat. I believe he knows the toughness of the class but what he doesn't know is that the way he conducts the class made it harder.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Aaron is a really nice guy and he genuinely cares about his students. He wants everyone to do well and learn a lot. He is also a very generous grader and he gives a ton of good feedback on lab reports. I gained many valuable skills from this course. The course itself is extremely challenging and work-intensive, but that's just how lab classes are

His lectures are very boring and just a waste of time. He's not approachable and does not help you in office hours IF you get a chance to catch him at office hours because he did not show up multiple times. Basically you're on your own to learn everything. I do NOT recommend taking his class.

This prof is all kinds of bad - lecture is all over the place. Very inaccessible outside of class and sometimes do not come to office hours. Emails are usually ignored. The class is too much work for how many units it's worth, and it's even worse when the prof is just plain unhelpful. Will avoid this prof with a passion from now on.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: The professor encourages students from different backgrounds to share ideas, challenge assumptions, and think like real entrepreneurs rather than just students completing assignments. Feedback on projects is detailed and constructive, which really helps improve both thinking and execution. The workload is quite reasonable.
A very good professor and an inspiring course

Aaron is one of the best professors I've had at Cal. He is very accessible outside of class and always willing to give advice. The curriculum is incredibly well-designed and covers the entire entrepreneurship journey in great detail. If you want to learn how to build your own startup or entrepreneurship in general, take this class!

This entrepreneurship course emphasizes learning by doing, with assignments closely tied to real venture development. Professor McDaniel is clear, patient, and highly engaged with students. His own startup experience and invited speakers add strong real-world perspective to each lecture.

Professor McDaniel's entrepreneurship course is very hands-on and practical, focusing on real startup processes rather than theory. He is patient, supportive, and genuinely cares about students' growth. On the last day of class, he even said his “office hours are for life.” He also brings strong real-world experience and great guest speakers.
Great guy, would invest in him on Shark Tank...
wish there was less random lecture videos to watch

Professor McDaniel's UGBA 195A Entrepreneurship is the most eye-opening and enriching class I've ever attended. He and his speakers offer really detailed advice and feedback that has inspired and given me the confidence to step into the space!

for ugba10 his lecture was literally his book and own opinions.. not applicable for everyone, and goes way too fast because "you have the slides" but also tells us come to every lecture? would not take again, his midterm was also not applying his concepts it was just memorizing?? promoted his book every lecture, would never take again

Far too lecture heavy, does not care too much about students, and tests rarely match what is on the study guide. He also creates slideshows with 50+ slides on them and zooms by without allowing any time to both take notes and comprehend what he is saying.

Aaron is a great professor and always willing to give good feedbacks during office hours. It's one of the classes that fueled me to start my own business. Be prepared to find good "co-founders" going into the class. Not an easy class but really rewarding if you are passionate about entrepreneurship and do the work.

Aaron is a patient and responsible professor. He always inspires students to think from a different point of view. And he invited a lot of guest speakers from different industries with high achievements to tell us their experiences and feelings, I feel motivated and moved.

This class is the most impactful I have had. The combo of informative lectures, inspiring guest speakers, and building a venture yourself with consistent feedback led to a steep learning curve. Now I understand the core of business better, and in the future, if I come across an opportunity, I have the confidence, tools, and knowledge to pursue it.

Professor McDaniel is one of the greatest professors I have met in Berkeley. He is super kind and so helpful and really cares about his students. And you can discuss your questions with him (whether it's related to class materials or learn from his amazing entrepreneurship experience) during his office hours. Definitely recommend his class!!!

Professor McDaniel's class was very inspiring. He has a deep understanding of Entrepreneurship and could clearly describe definitions. The homework was very practical and interesting. We got a deeper understanding of Entrepreneurship with the homework assigned. If you're interested in Entrepreneurship, be sure to take Professor McDaniel's class.

I took Aaron's class last semester and had a blast. Although indeed there was a lot of work, it was a very fulfilling experience. The guest speakers were also all incredible and open. I recommend taking this class if you actually want to learn about being an entrepreneur. If you're taking it just for a grade, then it is not for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: My favorite class I took last semester. Although there are lots of homework, all the works and projects were very practical and made me learn about entrepreneurship effectively. His class is constructed as watching the lectures beforehand so students can ask/discuss questions and details in the classroom. Aaron is very passionate in teaching!

It was undoubtedly the best class I EVER had !!! Aaron is a passionate teacher and dedicated a lot of time and energy for his students. In this class, Aaron teaches you how to create a venture from scratch by using the famous lean-start-up methodology. Students develop a real business mindset that can be also used as an employee of a company.

Aaron is an amazing teacher. Always makes himself available when you need more advices or feedback. He provided us useful insights and connected us to relevant people that helped us for our venture. Very dedicated, and the flip format is very valuable because leaves time in class to provide individual feedback. Best class for aspiring startupers!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: Aaron at first appears to be unapproachable, but is in fact quite a nice guy in his office hours. The class is a heinous one. The GSIs are the reason why you shouldn't take this class. They actually aren't there to do anything, they barely reply to concerns, never offer feedback. They are the real reason why this class is hellish.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: While Aaron seems to be a nice person, this course is structured horribly. In a class of over 150 students, no one seems happy. It's a 2 unit course with a higher workload than any 4 unit course I've ever taken (in various disciplines, I might add). The GSI's are beyond useless and arbitrarily take points off of assignments without telling you why.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: He might be a good person, but definitely not a good teacher. The GSIs he chose is just useless wasted people who send email to students just to forbid them talking about homework with them. Just do something else. The world is beautiful, I regret for taking this terrible class

Aaron McDaniel is my far the worst professor or teacher I have EVER had. He is a pompous guy who's perspectives and ideas are far too complicated. He gives the amount of work for a 5 unit class, but you only get 2 units. The grading of weekly assignments is INCREDIBLY difficult. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. SAVE YOURSELF. YOU WILL REGRET TAKING.

The professor is extremely pretentious and is not qualified to teach the course. One google search for "Aaron McDaniels Shark Tank" and you will see why. His views towards starting a company is extremely fantastical and the work is akin to a 5 unit , when the course is only a 2 unit class.
Not worth it at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: While the class was definitely more work than 2 units, it was undeniably worth it in the end. McDaniel is one of the most passionate, engaging professors I have ever had. Very open to critiques, improvements, and always down to help anyone who takes initiative to ask. The very hands-on nature of the course is challenging, but so rewarding.

The class content was overall impressive. The guest speakers were amazing, as they gave valuable insight on what it means to be an entrepreneur and tips on the resources available to startups. There are no tests, no midterm or final. But its a project orientated class where you have a team updating weekly. I had fun but too much work for 2 unit
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests? Not many

reviews.comment: Although the professor was not so terrible, he designed this class to be an absolute nightmare. For 2 units class, there is so many work that must be done weekly. Also it is super hard to get even passing grade on those weekly assignments. Definitely not recommend to take this class with this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Fisher is definitely knowledgeable in his field but that's really the only positive thing I have to say about him as a professor. He goes off on many side tangents during lecture and if he is angry about something he brings that energy with him to class. Fisher frequently warns us anger is bad for the heart, but he needs to take his own advice.

Professor Fisher is a great lecturer, but his negativity toward psychology research made me question my major. While he preaches compassion and integrity, he lacks these qualities. He shows little compassion for DSP students and doesn't communicate well with GSIs. His belief that "misstatements" are acceptable undermines his message on integrity.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof comes off as chill and funny but tends to be unorganized at times. Test questions were released with minimal time to study and most of the content is taken from lengthy research articles. Most of the time the test questions were far off from what was studied. The good thing is one exam is dropped.

Aaron's is chill but often negative about most things. If he is having a bad day, he takes that energy to class. 4 exams (he gives you the exact questions that will be on the exam). 1 pager assignments due weekly. Lacks class recording posts. Lots of reading articles. He also downplays psychological research a lot, despite him teaching it lol.

The content is interesting and there are lots of extra credit oppurtunities. Certain exam questions are often dropped which boosts the overall exam averages. 4 non cumulative multiple choice exams, 1 drop, and no final so you can skip the last exam if you want. He also gives you the exam questions so you literally know exactly what to study.

I took his class over the summer; he was interested in the material and did a great job relating it to real-world experiences. Very funny professor! His exams were lecture-based and I would advice studying the lectures since some questions were straight out of the slides.

I loved the course content, lectures, and the discussion sections. The second and third tests were a bit hard and worded tricky, but the first and fourth exams should be easy. Read the book that he gives and watch previous lectures in course capture if that's still available.

The class itself was difficult but as long as you put in the work watching every lecture and writing notes it'll be very rewarding. I personally enjoyed the material and thought the class was fairly reasonable.

The class: I am not super familiar with medical terminology and this class was heavily based on empirical studies that seemed kind of randomly strung together BUT The professor: amazing! Remembered every single lecture because of how entertaining he made it, and engaging. Got like a B+ on most tests but with reading responses I got up to an A!

Love him as a human. But the class itself is horrible. The tests are difficult and tricky. His lectures seem to kind of help on some questions, but overall the class was just a pain. I would honestly go back and not take this class. so many people I know dropped the first week of being in the class, I should have followed.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor himself is awesome I really liked his take on health psychology, however, the class itself was painful to be in. The midterms are extremely confusing and tricky, doesn't curve his tests, and bland during lecture. There's no course capture and you gives you extremely tricky questions. Get ready to read and think.

I was honestly scared to take this class because of its material. There is a lot of medical terminology. Prof Fisher is hilarious and makes lecture manageable. I recommend to really pay attention in class & take good notes. The course content is based off a lot of empirical research/studies which he goes over in class. Very interesting class!!!

He's very knowledgable in his field, however, his midterms are extremely confusing even after reading the textbook and attending lectures. There is no course capture, really whack midterm questions, and redundant. The professor is really cool but did not enjoy this class. I would much rather take other psych upper division classes

Ok professor. Digressed so much in lecture the material remained unclear. Unclear multiple choice questions on exams(100% of grade)... a lot of leftist politics had some cringe moments. Mainly, not an MD and didnt seem to know much about the material. After taking the class I still dont know what I actually learned.
He sometimes makes broad statements that overly simplistic, and he can be very dismissive of students when they give an answer he's not expecting.

Honestly Fisher is one of the best professor I have had at UC Berkeley. He is a very kind and compassionate human being. Also had an amazing GSI - Peter. Reading the textbook is helpful and necessary to get an A in this course and attending lecture is always fun as Fisher makes the material fun and interesting to learn with personal  anecdotes.

Wow. Definitely in my top 3 all time favorite professors. The class is constantly laughing, tests are basically lecture-based (text will solidify material), and the material is organized and easy to understand if you pay attention. Aside from that, Dr. Fisher has demonstrated his compassion and humanity again and again. 10/10 Highly Recommended.

Awesome & funny lecturer. Knowledgeable researcher. The future star! It is a perfect psy class for bio/pre-med majors. You will learn a lot from him. But the contents are technical, boring and complex and sometimes he acts dismissively and talks down to students. Mid-terms are challenging, confusing and nitpicking while the final is a breeze.

My favorite professor I've taken at berkeley. His lectures were as interesting as Ted talks and he has a great sense of humor. You feel like you're going to get a worse grade than you do because the tests are challenging, but there are easy ways to make up your grade. I will miss this class!

Personally, I felt that I needed the lectures to help me understand the readings and slides. I was surprised to end up with an A. I thought the class was challenging and I did really badly on the second exam. But he drops the lowest test grade and the final was pretty easy. Great class!

The class itself was super interesting and he tried to make lectures funny but honestly you only need the slides he posts online. Some reading and a short paper, but the class is overall very easy and enjoyable!

Ron was a great, serious teacher. Going to office hours was a great way to get his personal feedback on the reading and my student writing. His written final exam was tough, but fair. Ron Loewinsohn raised the level of my writing and thinking at Berkeley, and for that I am grateful.

Prof. Loewinsohn has impeccable credentials. However, his time in the Ivory Tower has made him unbearably dull. His lectures seem to have remained unchanged since they were written on his typewriter some years ago, and he repeats himself constantly. Don't take his class if you enjoy reading the Beats. Do take this class if you enjoy namedropping.
Ron is a nice guy.  Too many of the lectures wre taken up with dump questions (ie, how did they warm microwave dinners in the fifties?)

Very interesting and engaged.  His last lecture class at Berkeley was unfortunately tainted by incompetent readers, but Loewinsohn's mastery of the subject shined through. His presence will undoubtabley be widely missed.
Great class, great teacher
Nice guy, but his lectures are boring.
Great.  Lots of fun, very interesting.

For someone with such an illustrious carreer, he has no self-esteem. Humors the stupidest questions and wastes obscene amounts of time. I got an A+ on my first paper and a C- on my second. Very hard to figure out which way he's going to go and what he's looking for.
No Comments
very intelligent, but hard-headed.  irritatingly so.

He reads his lectures straight off a piece of paper, which is kind of boring. He does attempt to inject humour into his lectures, which I have to give him credit for. Nice enough guy, but isn't very engaging.

Very nice and humorous. Lectures were very organized and clear. His lectures were mostly summaries of the books, which I thought was sort of pointless, since I read the books as we were supposed to. Grades were made of 2 essays and a final. Also, he was very helpful in Office Hours. Would recommend
okay professor. makes some good points but constantly repeats them subsequent lectures. paper topics pretty straightforward.

Very advanced information but professor is always willing to help. Group work is encouraged on homework. Learned a lot about soils, something I never thought I would have found interesting. Wish there were more field trips

Very thoughtful and nuanced. Takes many perspectives into account and cares about linking lectures to current events. Has a positive outlook which is nice for a change. Lots of slides, make sure to take note of important people and diagrams for midterms. Easy if you study. Title sounds boring but Professor Amundson makes it interesting. Great guy.

Ron was a very nice guy, but his lectures were a bit stale. The topics were somewhat interesting, and the videos he showed were very informative. The readings he assigned were almost useless, since he summarized them in lecture. The tests felt very random when compared to the study guide. Discussions were easy, but boring + attendance is mandatory.
He was a great guy, but very confusing lecturer and hard to tell what will be on the exams. Def go to office hours to ask more because exams are confusing and demanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Took it in my freshman year, I accidentally missed 2 quizzes, but he let me make them up. He can be hard to reach by email, but luckily my GSI that year was helpful. The exams and quizzes were pretty easy and online. Participation in discussion sections matters. Overall, it was an interesting course.
Great professor who clearly cared about his students and the subject he was teaching. Everything taught in the class is very relevant, and Dr. Amundson makes lectures very interesting.

His exams were online and multiple choice, very easy. Lectures are very detailed slides which was really helpful when studying. The readings are not really important as he summarizes the reading in lectures. Discussion homework are based on completion, you can leave early most classes, chill GSIs. Overall very chill professor and class.

as a first semester freshman, this was a nice intro class. lectures were straightforward and easy to follow. a lot of content/memorization involved.

however, tests were a joke. nearly all multiple choice, online, and some questions were difficult to interpret. he was prone to making errors. 

sweet guy and easy class, but could be more organized.

Ron is a deeply knowledgable, clearly accomplished academic in his field. His passion for the subjects which he teaches is abundant. Biosphere was an eye-opening class in many regards, covering the entire history of the universe. Because of the wide subject matter, the course became a bit disorganized.  Test and quiz questions were broad.

I am a freshman majoring in Environmental Science and this was my favorite class this semester. Prof was super passionate about what he was teaching and it made lectures super interesting. Lectures were not mandatory (discussion was) but I went to all of them because I was so interested. If you go to lecture and do the homework you'll do fine.

A bit disorganized--every test and quiz had at least one thing graded wrong. However, I was definitely impressed with the span of the course, as he connected it to lots of interesting topics I didn't expect, and I really felt like I learned a lot and came away with a new perspective. You'll have a jar of mud sitting in your room for a few weeks.

Course is clearly geared for freshmen taking their first college course, anyone else may find parts of the class especially pedantic. Course is easy but poorly organized with mandatory discussion attendance to sit and do practically nothing productive for an hour.
Good professor, sometimes didn't respond to my emails, but clearly knows his stuff.

Lectures were a bit stale and participation is mandatory, taken by different methods each day. Content itself is straightforward and not difficult. Exams were online but taken in person during class time. Professor is hard to reach but I was fortunate to have a great and communicative GSI  Edward Mbewe.

He's a very sweet dude but very unresponsive when it comes to emails and such. Exams were mainly lecture based and attendance is mandatory for discussions (he also has graded polls and pop quizzes in class so it kinda forces you to go to lecture too). ESPM C10 is a very boring course even if it is easy, there's not much interesting content.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The lectures were pretty boring but the course was easy. Just some quizzes throughout the semester, 2 midterms, and a final. Readings were assigned but if you didn't read a page throughout the entire course you would do fine (most people I talked to didn't). Professor wasn't much help responding to emails but the GSI was great.

The class itself was not very hard but Professor Amundson was honestly awful. His slides were always confusing, filled with typos and large chunks of unreadable text, and pretty clearly put together the morning of. 90% of lecture was watching TedTalks (which he then tested on). He's also just a pretty boring lecturer. Nice guy, but really bad prof.

He is a passionate professor who tries his best to have the most engaging class he can. He confronts us with a wide range of material and his activities are very different each week. The grading scale is relatively clear and it isn't too hard to get a good grade. It is the perfect class for non-stem students interested in the environment.

warning! the class is easy enough but the course content is awful. ron made insensitive, offensive comments to myself and other students of color. also a super boring lecturer. avoid this class if possible.

ESPM 2 is designed as an intro to Berkeley, CNR, and the ESPM department. Ron is a great professor and he is clearly very passionate about the things he's teaching. The class is easy. You do need a lot of memorization but there are detailed study guides available before the exams.

Professor made this class terrible.  Lectures were awful - slides felt like they were written ten minutes before, typos, large chunks of text cut directly from books, and no organization at all. The rest of the lecture was watching TED talks. Tests were confusing and inconsistent, prof never responded to emails asking for help. 100% do not take.

Very lecture heavy class! My advice is don't skip, he tests heavily on things said in lecture. A little bit disorganized and difficult to pay attention at times. GSIs are good, and section homework is really straightforward. Two midterms and a final, easy enough if you attend lecture and review the slides.
Lectures were impossible to get through because of how filled with useless information, boring, and scattered they were. Take this class if you want to waste your time and fulfill a bio breadth.

No structure in the overall course/within lectures. Fast-paced lectures, hard to take notes, lecture slides rarely posted on time. Unclear syllabus & grading policies, even as I'm writing this 2 weeks before finals. Lack of communication from the prof to students/GSIs.
