Ron made this supposed-to-be-easy class unnecessarily hard & frustrating. Avoid.

This professor was a blast to have, and cared about the subject. He was a good lecturer, and it was easy to approach him with questions. The class was easy to pick up, and he offered a book, but you didn't need to read it to do well. The homework was simple, and the midterms had straightforward. Try to attend his office hours!
Amundson is clearly very passionate about what he teaches, and this made ESPM2 my favorite class by far.

He is a great professor overall and it is clear that he truly cares for all his students and wants them to learn. He can be a little confusing at times and difficult to know what content in the lectures he actually wants us to know. Luckily, I had a great GSI who I LOVE and made the content more understandable. Small hw assignments each week. Easy!

He is a great professor overall! He sometimes does go off on a tangent, but otherwise, his lectures are pretty clear and he is very amiable toward students. The material is not bad either but sometimes the organization of his class is a little confusing such as when discussion assignments/quizzes are happening, etc.
Clearly passionate if a bit erratic while lecturing
I enjoyed the Professor Amundson's lectures and content. The class itself is very lenient and discussions were engaging. A lot of videos and media are implemented into the slides.

Lectures were a drag and extremely boring and he tended to stray off topic a lot. I had an A all semester and then got covid during dead week/day of the final which led to me performing poorly. Ended the class with a 92.76 and said there was nothing I could do to raise it despite it being because of covid/being extremely fatigued during the final.

Prof. Amundson definitely cares about this subject matter & tries to incorporate current events to add relevancy. Interesting class that covers many diverse topics. Exams were pretty easy overall (2 midterm, 1 final) & you had plenty of time to take them. A decent amount of busy work (9 assignments, near-weekly quizzes) but not difficult.

Very friendly and relatable professor. He cares so deeply about what he does, and about communicating that message to all his students. Only two midterms, a final, and occasional quizzes, and can be taken at any point during the day. Very lightweight class- if I had to study for a midterm, I could put this class on hold for a bit and be fine.

Professor Amundson is genuinely a great professor and will teach you so much about soils. Midterms were fair but straight from his lectures. HW's are easily accessible and he does provide great feedback. Overall if you would like to learn about the different types of soils, Amundson is the BEST.

Professor is very caring and nice! He easily accommodates to student needs. Lectures are dense however, he encourages collaboration on all work. He's very passionate about soils and you do learn a lot! Not a lot of work, a few hw's, midterm (w/ study guide), and a final! Grades very fairly.

I thoroughly enjoyed this course! Amundson is a passionate and organized lecturer who has both a depth and breadth of knowledge in environmental issues. The issues discussed in this course were diverse and felt applicable to the real world. Some annoying busy work (weekly assignments and lecture quizzes), but tests were fair. Not a difficult A
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great prof & interesting lectures. Lots of assignments but not overbearingly hard. The 2 midterms & final exam were very specific which was frustrating but got a study guide for each. Exams were open for a generous amount of time (3 days w/ time limit of 2 hr). Wish I could've done in-person but maybe it would be a heavier workload. Recommended!

Prof. is very caring and accommodating to students' needs. His lectures are interesting and exams are very fair. There are detailed study guides for tests as well. GSIs are wonderful and very approachable. Would definitely recommend this class!

Great teacher. His class is organized and he's passionate about what he teaches. His quizzes/exams are really just his notes. Assignments are easy and simple too. Even in a pandemic, he made the class engaging by bringing in other news about the university, specifically football. He's a cool dude and the GSIs are awesome too.

This prof was super cool and I totally recommend taking this class! Lectures were engaging and course was organized. There's 2 midterms and a final with a weekly homework assignment and some reading. Easy A.

Prof. Amundson's lectures are interesting and line up perfectly with material on tests and quizzes. He takes the time to write thorough study guides before exams. Additionally, he always uploads slides and lecture recordings in a timely manner. Prof. Amundson is a great person and professor, and I highly recommend taking classes with him.

Prof Amundson is wonderful. He is an amazing scientist and it shows when he lectures!! Also, the book he assigns reading from is great. He provides in depth study guides and the homework doesn't feel like busy work. It's a pity I have taken this remotely because it would have been even better in real life.

AWESOME professor. Lectures are both greatly varied and unanimously fascinating. He genuinely cares about his students and has gone to great lengths to accommodate various needs. Very knowledgeable about every aspect of the course, and has personal connections to many of the researchers discussed throughout. Take his class!

Super nice, and the course is well taught as other reviewers said. Only thing to add is that his voice is pretty soft and the sound padding in heart field annex will makes you pretty dang sleepy. But, GSIs cover everything and good communication between them.

Professor Amundson is wonderful! He cares about the students and is a great lecturer. However, there are pop quizzes, though he will often give hints to what days they are + they are open notes. His lectures can get a little crammed with information but mostly they are great and i love the videos he includes in lectures, they really keep it fresh.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Inspirational--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Super kind, chill, reasonable, and cares about students. I had a lot of background knowledge coming into the class, so the content wasn't mindblowing to me. But for someone who has had little exposure to the stuff I can see how it can be quite interesting and can expand your perspective. Ron is a great professor and a great person overall!

Professor Amundson is beyond amazing, and his lectures were times I always looked forward to. He is by far my favorite professor at Cal and have taught me, and I'm sure so many others, so much. He is so well-respected, caring, accessible, and an absolute gem. I would undoubtedly take his class again if I had the chance.

Incredible professor and an amazing human. Lectures are very interesting and informative, and it is clear he is super knowledgable about the subject and passionate about spreading his knowledge. Class is overall pretty chill and he is very accommodating and communicative with students. Readings and his notes are very helpful.

easy class & great intro to current env. issues. some pop quizzes @ end of class, weekly quizzes in discussion sections on readings, 3 short essays (1 personal essay, 2 essays about env issues of your choice). study guides given 4 midterm/final. RON ROX. i luv his videos shown during class/assigned documentaries. some breadths r fulfilled. woke af
reviews.rating_tags: Inspirational--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: really opening class if you attend the lecture, lots of good videos and comedy. also learning how people work with the environment. The professor is a nice person to talk to outside class.

Professor Amundson is honestly the best professor I've had at Cal. His lectures are interesting and present new ways to approach environmental issues that I had never thought of. He mixes funny videos into lectures and discusses current events that are relevant to the course. He's very approachable outside class for help. Take a class with him.

Literally my favorite professor I've had at Cal. Does a fantastic job at introducing students to environmental science. He's one of the reasons I decided to switch into CNR. Super fair tests, interesting discussions, and he loves to put silly videos in his lectures to break it up.

Professor Amundson is beyond fair. He writes out long study guides that contain practically all of the information on the midterms and finals. His lectures are straightforward, and he does a good job of engaging the class. The one downside is he gives random pop quizzes; however, they're given at the end of the lecture and you can use your notes!

Amundson was super organized; all of his slides were posted online and his study guides were essentially bullet points providing answers for the midterm/final. One large project makes up a big part of your grade, but it's not hard to get an A on. No textbook, skipped a lot of class and still faired pretty well.

one of the best professors I've had at Cal.  Really interesting guy and very passionate about what he studies.  The class was super unbiased and really strove to make people aware of environmental issues.  definitely recommend taking this class with him!

I literally only attended class for midterms and the final. I attended all discussion sections, however. The professor provides study guides that are essentially lecture notes and posts his power points online. The tests are not easy, but there are no tricks and the material is all in the study guides. 3 papers, several assignments, 2 midterms

Whoever says Amundson is boring/mean is totally wrong. He's a really nice guy who puts cool pictures in his slide-slows, &shows us things like the Daly Show and DrSuess. Downsides: tests are a little picky and he does indeed have a monotone voice--but he gives us an outline before the test with basically all the answers. Take this class from him!!

Professor Amundson is a very nice fellow - the information is good stuff to know but is also pretty basic and the material on the test seemed to be more specific that most people anticipated(hence the comments below) If you're looking for a mindblowing or exciting class, this isn't it...but I've enjoyed it so far.
Boring professor who has very picky grading and teaches as though he has never taught before...avoid

He is very helpful if you talk to him outside of class and he seemed to be a really nice guy.  Some of his subjects he talked about were a little boring (I am just not really fascinated by soil) but he did add interesting stuff too like Mars.  His voice is a little monotone but he is a fair grader and overall a good teacher.

Prof. had about as much personality as a glass of skim milk. Arrogant too; made it real clear that he didn't want to teach and was way beyond all of us poor students. Really pounded the joy out of my semester.
Birds of a feather flock together. The GSI Jon Sanderman is just as horrible a teacher as the Professor.

homeworks are hard! and graded on accuracy. Lectures are amazing and he is a great teacher. his powerpoint skills are through the roof, hes like a powerpoint wizard. but hes usually pretty busy outside of class.

Hardest BioE class. Prereqs needed. Not accessible outside class. Clear lectures, knowledgeable. Homework is extremely hard so go to OFFICE HOURS. Exams easier than homework. Final is group project that needs effort. Compare answers with classmates or upper-class men. NO CURVES on exams. Exam 1 hardest. Difficulty drop right after. No extra credit
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is a great lecturer and always willing to help, but his course content is rather difficult.  Go to office hours for the homeworks and study hard for the midterms because those will make or break your grade.  Group project is also hard, but you receive relatively well-constructed feedback and if your group is good, you're set.
He's simply the best. Take good notes and you'll be fine. Always available for help.

Aaron is a young guy who is super smart, funny, and helpful. His teaching method is very easy to follow, and he is very helpful and charming in office hours. I would not have done as well in this course if I hadn't taken Aaron because he is amazing at what he does.

This is not an easy course. Thermo is a beast, and he tells you this on the first day.  Attending lectures is helpful because he breaks down the material into essential and non-essential material for exams. I'm not sure how he grades because I was in the bottom half of the class and still got a B-. He's a good guy and I would take him again.

I wasn't excited about taking o-chem over the Summer, but I'm glad I did. Aaron made the class enjoyable and very manageable. He makes the homework very hard and long, but if you can figure out the homework, the quizzes and tests are a breeze. He's also super approachable and determined that everyone can succeed. If you can take his class, DO IT!
Aaron is able to take difficult material and make it easy. He is always willing to help students and always comes in an hour earlier to help us. Take it from me. If you are bad at chem, take him.

Super easy class. Exam questions are directly from the back of the book and variations from class examples. Dr. Lopes can be hard to understand at times, but his effort to make the class enjoyable, interesting, and achievable for everyone makes it worth while. Helpful during office hours.

It was a pleasure taking his class. He was very concise with his lectures and gave very practical advice.  Tests are not as difficult as everyone makes them out to be. He also isn't too bad to look at!

He is a really great guy once you get to know him and is very helpful when you meet with him 1-on-1. Going to lecture was helpful. He went through lecture material way too fast. HARD tests with no curves.
Avoid taking this professor at ALL COST. You will hate yourself (and him) half way through the semester. His tests are difficult and she is not a pleasant person.
Mr. Lopes is an extremely good lab instructor. His expectations are clear and focused. However, he is an extremely tough grader and is very nit-picky on what he wants. Overall, great professor.

One of the best professors at Cal! PS 125 is the perfect intersection of data and politics, with more depth in international relations matters. 2 5-page papers, 4 quizzes, no midterm, UN simulation project, one final paper. Every week is a new, clear subject. She'll take the time to get to know you and help out if you attend OH. Highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Solid choice. Not really anything extraordinary, but is ready to help explain topics of challenging things going around the world. Open to a lot of audience participation, but is still strict.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof. Matanock's Intro to IR class was the reason why I chose to pursue international relations as my speciality within political science. She's extremely qualified and knows what she's talking about. Go to lecture. Her slideshows make the course material easy to understand, and she engages well with questions.

Professor Matanock's class had engaging material. The docked star was because there was no grade rubric posted, so we didn't know what constituted an A versus an A-, and because I personally didn't get much out of lectures. While lectures were interesting (and mandatory), you mainly needed to read the textbook for the midterm and the final.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Matanock is very knowledgeable in her field of study. I really enjoyed the structure of the course, however, I did not enjoy the vagueness of her final and midterm reviews. Overall, it is important to complete all of the readings as they are the foundation for the course material. I found international relations to be very interesting!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I took this as an intended poli sci major, and I'm glad I did. The class is interesting and very relevant. If you read the textbook chapters that coincide with lectures, you'll do great. Tests (no papers) were straightforward and there were no surprises-- she only put concepts on the tests that we read/heard several times. This was a great class.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is the reason why I'm going to graduate with only High Honors instead of Highest Honors and I am going to be mad about it. Loved the class content and especially worthwhile if you're interested in the intersection of economics and law. Beware of a group project worth 20%t (what took me out). Earned an A but curve put me at an A-.

The professor isn't thorough with the concepts and takes time to get to the main idea which just makes the lectures unclear mostly. He can sometimes lose patience and get disrespectful when having to repeat ideas or when students ask questions. Don't take a class with him, unless you have no other options.

Professor Edlin provides many resources for the course and is clear about his expectations and grading. Problem sets are graded on completion. Midterms and final were similar to previous exams and the problem sets. He is happy to answer questions during or after class. Participation matters!
His explanations are clear. Recommend taking it in the future. One of the best econ profs at Cal!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Edlin is an awful teacher. He hosts all lectures on zoom (it's almost 2023), isn't easily accessible, and doesn't seem to care much about the class. Wouldn't recommend!
I think that Professor Edlin is a good professor. He explained concepts clearly, answered questions, and the tests and problem sets were pretty straightforward and not too difficult.

He is bad at explaining simple concepts and enjoy cutting students off when we are answering his questions. His quizzes are quite easy, homework is quite easy too. However, you will not learn much from going to his lecture.

Prof Edlin is among the best in the Econ department. Lectures were through Zoom, and provided after class. Class was curved to benefit the students in the best way. He is very knowledgeable about industrial organizations. He is very passionate and always willing to help and explain things over and over. I highly recommend him.

I really enjoyed Econ 121. The interactive lecture style was one my favorite during my student career. Prof Edlin 's papers are also insightful and well written. I became very interested in the field of industrial organization after reading them and attending the lectures. Learning from Prof. Edlin really motivated me to become an economist.

Edlin is a fantastic professor.  His lectures were pretty engaging and he is a kind, understanding guy if you go to office hours.  The scoring breakdown was weird, where homework and just showing up to class was worth like 50% of the grade.  So if you put decent effort into homework and show up to class, you're halfway there.  Tests are easy too.

His background is in both economics and law, and he's both worked in the White House and started his own company! His lectures are intriguing, though slow, and he is passionate about piquing your curiosity!

This is one of my favorite Econ electives. Industrial Orginizaiton is a very interesting topic. The materials I learned in this class ended up directly relate to my first job. The class is easy if you have a good grasp of micro. He's very willing to talk and often provides ideas for thesis. Overall highly recommend as an elective.

Edlin is, like others have noted, a really nice professor. He clearly cares about his students and the material he teaches. However, his tests can be pretty hard and sometimes don't totally correlate with the problem sets and reading. This isn't too bad since Edlin is a very fair grader. Overall, a cool dude.
Edlin's a really nice guy and lecturer who's usually always available in office hours. Textbook isn't needed so go to every lecture! Tests are also really difficult (calculus-heavy).

This is the best class that I took in Berkeley this semester. Industrial Organization is interesting and the professor explains everything clearly in an enjoyable manner. He personally is also nice and helpful, willing to talk with you about your ideas. The exams are a bit hard, but if you understand the basic models you can easily do it.

Easy class, 100A covered 85% of this course in half the time. However not that easy to get an A because he refuses to give you practice tests / problems so tests are arbitrary. No section which didn't help
avoid

This class was very easy if you have any knowledge of calc. I got an A+ just by using what I learned in Econ 101a a semester earlier (and not going to class after the first 5 weeks). If you know how to maximize profit and minimize cost functions, you will do well with very little work.
THis is the worst/2nd worst professor I have ever taken. Can't explain anything. Problem sets are confusing. MT/FInal are very hard. Say will give a good curve, but lies. Avoid like the plague!!!

I must admit Professor Edlin can be funny at times and engaging. However, he doesn't give you past exams to practice and  study for the midterm. Tests turn out to be hard compare to the prob sets!!!He only included one question similar to the hw in the midterm. Goodluck if you take this class.

His lectures ranged from inspiring to unbearable, and the tests were unpredictable.  Nevertheless, I really enjoyed this class and would take it again in a heartbeat.  And I gotta say, when Edlin's having a good day, he's amazing.
Half questions of the exam will be picked from the problem sets.

Dr. Harish did a wonderful job teaching. He genuinely cares about his students. He was very good about checking in with the class and making sure we were adequately challenged but not overworked during the stress of the pandemic. He is always available to set up a meeting and even finds unique research positions/jobs for those who are interested.

Dynamics is SUPER difficult, so going to OH is a must, and fortunately he's really nice and accommodating there. Lectures are OK, homeworks (which are done in groups) are way harder than lecture material, there's a group project, and the final was insane. But he grades super leniently too. So if you put in the time and effort, it should go well.

It is a challenging class, but with Dr. Harish, you will enjoy it. Go to his office hours start working on your homework as soon as you get it. They need a lot of time and a lot of work. I passed this with (-A); my final exam did not go well due to some lack of enough sleeping at exam night.
Dr. Harish, is one my favorite professors. Dynamics is not an easy class, but if you do your job work hard on homework and go to office hours you will get your desired result.

Took dynamics and vibrations with him. That class is HAAAAARD dude. But not because of the prof. , the topic is just hard. The prof is super nice, and will take extra office hours just to help you. Super clear hand writing. You will suffer, but afterwards you'll feel like an engineering navy SEAL.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Best professor ever. He encourages the use of precedents & makes us borrow books from the library. Extremely smart, understands our projects better than we do & makes them better with every iteration. Cares about everything: from the minutiae of line weights to the way we layout our drawings. So dedicated. So grateful to have had Ajay as my teacher
Ajay taught me to draw and make models. He also taught me to think conceptually about my work and to hold myself to a high standard. He is the best instructor I have ever had.
Hottest professor I've ever had
too good

Best teacher in a architecture studio so far. really focused on pushing your design to absolute resolution.  He is tough and strict but if you follow what he says and put 110% effort, your work will be awesome, He will challenge you to your extremees...be prepared. Comebacks are possible!

Arch 100A By far the most helpful and enjoyable professor I have ever had the honor to have at Cal. He takes the time to help students and goes above and beyond when it comes to teaching. Most def my favorite teacher

Ong is extremely smart, sassy, and knowledgeable. She will always challenge what her students say and every day is a new surprise. Hard work, but definitely worth the challenge. Reading is mandatory, no class textbook, just a reader. Ong is intimidating and can sometimes be rude, but definitely makes you think. Worth taking, if you're up for it.
Absolutely LOVE her cheeky ramblings, style and passion. One of my few favorites at Cal.
Sassy and articulate. Love her!

Ong is doubtlessly a brilliant scholar but a horrible, HORRIBLE professor. Her lectures are disorganized and unfocused. She's disrespectful toward students who are genuinely eager to go over the material and generally dismisses opinions that don't validate her own. I would love this class if Ong didn't teach it.

She is the cutest lady ever and tries really hard but isn't the best lecturer. Regardless, she tells funny jokes and keeps the huge class entertained. Subjects are interesting and if you have a good GSI you'll be fine

I thought she was amusing as hell.  The topics were really interesting, but she's not that good of a lecturer.  However, she is brilliant and the reading material is really cool and there isn't too much of it.  Going to class is where she connected the reading with the terms/ideas.  Good idea to go to class, but isn't necessary.

Lecture are utterly useless and lack any sense at all.  Completely impossible to follow and the taking notes off the power points is simply wasting paper.  Class is overall meaningless and boring.  Guest speakers are no better than Ong either.  Looking for a lecture to nap through guilt-free twice a week?  This is it.
really really boring. do all the readings and pay attention to sections & GSIs.

her train of thought is impossible to follow. powerpoints are useless. the readings can be dense but interesting. i ended up falling in love with anthro. Tip for Success: don't bother takin notes in lecture. get an amazing gsi (like saul mercado). read the intro/conclusion to all the articles (main argument) if in a rush. STUDY IN A GROUP!

Her own research interests are very interesting but they didn't emerge until the latter half of the class. Lectures were boring but she must be given credit for attempting to engage a class of nearly 500. Movies were interesting as were many of the guest speakers. Some were outright boring (Hayden, Williams). GSI experience differed significantly.

She has extremely good intentions and tries to create engaging discussions in a class of 500 (didn't really work) her tests are fair, and its not hard to get a good grade (like a B) but if you want an A be prepared to put in more work and especially impress your GSI since the grading was almost 100% up to them.

Lectures are horrible. Very hard to stay awake. For the most part, they're not helpful. Make sure you do ALL of the reading. Doing that is the only way to get a good grade in the class. The readings for the most part are very interesting and I actually enjoyed doing them and what save the class. Her written work is mind-blowing. Take it!

I wanted to like her but she's really bad. She's impossible to follow in lecture, she talks in a monotone and puts the simplest concepts in language that's nearly impossible to understand.  Mainly focused on Asian Americans - even though there MANY cultures in America. Not a word about Native Americans, etc. 2nd semester - mainly just reading her.

Class was pretty straightfoward. Lectures put me right to sleep so I never went. Only go to lectures when there's a guest speaker or a film.  The second half of the course involves a lot of reading HER published material. Her books and articles are surprisingly more incomprehensible than her.  This class is an easy B/B+. It'll take work for an

When I signed up for this class, I was really excited about taking it, since Anthropology sounded like such a great subject to study! But, after the first day of class, I knew that it was going to be a horrible semester! Professor Ong is very hard to understand, not only because of her accent, but because she never seems to finish her train of thou

Ong is very entertaining, if you care to listen to her sextracurricular activites. Going to lecture is a waste of time. Get a good GSI that can explain the topics. Reading is everything in this class.

She is extremely difficult to understand.  Her lectures are like stream of consciousness. She does not progress from one idea to the next with any sort of pattern.  I would not recommend the class just because of how difficult she is to follow.
This class can be really confusing.  Ong has a lot of good ideas, but she has trouble communicating them to the class.  This makes it hard to follow lectures.

Professor Ong seems to have both a British and a Chinese accent, which, coupled with her ridiculously tangential lecture style, make her lectures almost impossible to follow. The key to success in the class is READING and forming connections between the reading and the broad concepts. So, READ, go to section, and skip lectures.
Lectures are hard to follow. She's hard to understand. I still don't know what the notes mean. Hope you get a good GSI
Amazing professor!

Although her lectures were hard to follow, the organization of the class was okay, and the videos were pretty interesting (beginning of Islam, third gender in Samoa). It's hard to swallow all of the concepts she covers, but it's a decent survey of cultural/social anthro.
not that good

Lectures were useless and always off tangent. I'm not the kind of student who sleeps in class -- I always fell asleep during her lectures.  People only complained about her class.  I only learned anything about Anthropology from my discussion section. I recommend only going to lectures occasionally.
boring, boring, boring -- and SO SNOTTY and disrespectful of her students

Very boring lectures that were rarely relevant. She frequently went off tangent and would talk about being an anthropologist in malaysia and sex. Listening to her was sometimes painful due to her incoherency and made me lose interest in anthropology. The class was fairly easy if you had a good GSI though.

She knows her stuff... but cannot get it across.  Unfortunately, in addition to her thick accent, her tendency to go on tangents and stop in the middle of sentences, phrases make her hard to understand or listen to.

Lectures completely unorganized and you can barely understand her. Assignments are not that hard although time consuming. Class is not all that difficult if you have a good GSI, her lectures are useless.

During the first few weeks of class, she was really engaging and interesting, but very soon, the class turned into a how-to for becoming an anthropologist in Malaysia. All she ever talked about was her fieldwork and frequently went on random tangents not applicable to the text. It was funny how she was able to mention sex in every single lecture.

Her lectures are somewhat difficult to follow and she goes off on tangents a lot, but in general I thought it was a good introduction to anthropology and not too difficult of a class. A good GSI helps a lot, and so does keeping up with readings.

At one point in the semester, half the class wasn't there, and half of the class that was there was asleep. She was hard to follow and rambled on about irrelevant topics. The material was very interesting and the GSI's were really helpful but lectures were a waste of time. She did seem really smart and nice which was a good thing.

Lecture was extremely confusing,made no sense,hard to even take notes and follow. No point in going to lecture. Section is the most important,just read the reader and you'll be fine. Some of the readings were interesting but ONG is just a mess and rambles on and on. GSI's are the most important,attend section.

Rambled in lectures, hard to follow, jumped from one concept to another, hard to connect ideas.  Interesting lecturer, take the class P/NP if you can because trying to get a good grade in that class is frustrating and confusing.

Her class is fun eventhough she does have a tendency to ramble once in a while. You will do great as long as you do the reading and attend section. Overall a really easy class with interesting material to read. Definitely recommend it if you are looking for a class to fill the AC requirement.
HORRRRIBLE Teacher/Lecturer. Fairly easy class if you have a good GSI. Just go to your sections and do the readings. DO NOT ATTEND LECTURE... very pointless.
i ****ing hated this class with a passion. going to lecture is ABSOLUTELY POINTLESS. just stick with the readings-- because listening to her will just confuse you and make you want to die.

Professor Ong is incredibly passionate in her lectures as well as very engaging despite the large lectures. Attendance in lecture isn't as important as your section since the GSI dictates your grade. She write very well, although her lectures are not very clear. Easy introductory course with a great reader. Liked it.

She is brilliant and a wonderful writer. Though her lectures did seem confusing, I thought this class was amazing (especially if you're swamped with technical courses). I enjoyed the style of the class and it's true, a lot of your grade is really based on your GSI. Ong's fair in that she draws her exams from the reading. So read!

the topics in her class interesting, but she makes it hard for you to have any motivation to learn them. her lectures are incredibly boring and disorganized. i never went to lecture, and ended up cram-learning all the themes right before the midterm/final. her writing is clear, focused, and interesting but i wish she was the same in person

I know I'm in the minority on this, but I think this was a great class. I had taken two years of IB soc anthro before, and think this was an exceptionally deep introduction to tons of key ideas and techniques in modern anthro. Ong is not clear but brilliant, and if you listen and read and try hard, you could learn a lot.
Respected in her field, not in the teaching field. Nice person, but random lecturer and often lectures on unrelated and untested subjects. Do not recommend.

Her lectures seem to be disorganized and lacking cohesion. She is respectable in her field but she does not know how to lecture. Although she is no doubt passionate for what does, she does not know how to present anthropology to her students in a clear, understandable manner.

In the beginning, I adored Professor Ong thinking that her reputation meant she would be interesting but I was incredibly mistaken.  Her class is boring, her lectures make no sense,  and your grade is based solely on your GSI.  I've worked very hard and my grade is still MUCH lower than friends who have done no reading or studying. DO NOT TAKE IT!!

Professor Ong, while highly respected in her field, is an absolutely horrible lecturer.  Her class is boring and disorganized.  She rambles on and on, and of course must always mention sex and drugs.  As previously mentioned by other users, amusing at first, but annoying overall.

The most amazing professor ever! She is passionate and dedicated and her lectures are engaging and thought-provoking. All the other boring and ordinary classes that fill my day, at least one class stands out as a class worth going to- a class that lets you think for yourself and that helps you show your creativity. It opens your mind!

Lectures are boring! She goes off into weird tangents and always talks about sex and drugs. Even though it was amusing at first, it gets old. I asked her for help on an assignment and she didn't give me any help! GSI's are just as bad as she is! No help and no proper discussion that stimulates any desire for learning or trying!
Aihwa Ong is a little Asian lady with spunk. She engages a large lecture hall with amusing and informative stories. Passionate.
Fantastic course, and great lecturer.  She engages the class even in a large lecture hall

The subject material for this course is so so interesting yet he manages to make every lecture boring and give a history lesson instead of talking about the actual theories from the reading. He rarely talks about how the theories apply to our world today and lectures are very boring. Most learning comes from the reading and going to discussion.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Prof Karras is one of my favorite professors at Berkeley! I really enjoyed the seminar and it was nice to have a break in my schedule to talk about and hear people's opinions on current events and different topics. I highly recommend!

I absolutely loved this professor. He makes class engaging,is absolutely hilarious, and I would defintely take him again. Take POLECON24 for a great introduction to this subject and for a nice, chill, P/NP class that you'll enjoy.
Prof. Karras was a great seminar leader. He helped introduce the basics of political economy in an accessible way and kept each class engaging.

super boring lectures- ability to make the most interesting political issue dry, expect A LOT of readings but don't necessarily have to read; GSI was better explaining and engaging
assignments are reasonable and midterm/final are writing essay+short answer

I enjoyed most of my classes in IAS at. This was a huge exception. Lectures are boring and this professor's teaching and syllabus is dense, dry, and largely uninspired. Karras fosters an unfriendly class environment. I strongly DO NOT recommend.

The overall class is ok, but get ready to massive readings. The lecture covers LOTS of theories and you are expected to remember all of them. Your grade is depending upon toughness of you GSI. Be careful when you pick you GSI.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Karras is really organized and sets clear expectations about what he wants his students to get out of the class. Lectures are interesting but move quickly so you have to stay on top of things. There are A LOT of readings but you can definitely get by on summaries if you pay attention in class, go to section, and go to office hours before exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I really liked prof Karras and Global 45 as a whole. The course covers a ton of material and moves somewhat fast, but if you watch lectures and go to discussion it is fairly easy to stay on top of the class. If you need a B- to declare your intended major, it should be no issue if you complete all assignment and go to your discussion section.

Excellent professor with impressive knowledge of his field. Was a pleasure to be introduced to political economy in his seminar. Easy PNP course, 3 short essays graded on completion. Good way to get to know people in your first year.

I took his PE100 my junior year, and I found his lectures enjoyable and informative. People find him quite blunt, he's very honest about how he sees theorists and politics, and has a sarcastic humor. Grading isn't difficult, just do well on exams by connecting theorists and key themes together. Reading can help, but his lectures and GSIs help more.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Poor lecturer but easy class. The class material is also very outdated.

Karras is for sure the best professor Ive had in Cal so far. Hes lectures were really inspirational and interesting, making me never want to skip one lecture. His midterm was fair, you have to study for u, but if u know what ur writing, you can get a good grade. Super smart and humorous guy, love him!

Lots of readings and you really have to work to get a good grade, but professor Karras always keeps lecture materials interesting. Also, go to his office hours - he's always willing to help understand the course material.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof. Karras is very knowledgeable, but his lectures can be a bit dry. He's a bit intimidating and arrogant; be sure to come prepared to office hours because they're individual meetings. Don't bother doing the readings- just go off of lectures. I got an A and did about 4% of the readings. It helps to make a comparison chart of all the thinkers.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Easy class but a teacher below par!
What a class!

Although intimidating at first, this professor's interest in the subject matter and engaging lectures make the classes he teaches very enjoyable. It is a lot of reading, however you can get most of the material from the lectures if you pay attention. Section is very helpful as well. Grades participation, so speak up in class!
I have to say this was hands down one of my favorite classes at Cal!

My favorite professor so far at Berkeley! He seems intimidating at first and in lecture, but if you go into office hours he's great-- funny and helpful and really knows his stuff. There's a lot of required reading, he's very serious about no phones/computers in lecture. Overall the tests and essays are challenging but fair.

Best professor I have had at Cal. He seems intimidating at first, but his dry humor will grow on you. I liked the class because he encouraged questions and emphasized critical thinking. The reading for the class was reasonable but there were 3ish longer novels. Enforces the no phone rule VERY seriously. You will get kicked out of class.

The class is fairly easy and not that challenging. He does not allow laptops in class but he should keep in mind that there are students with disabilities who need this medium for note-taking. Otherwise an okay class.

Very dynamic speaker. One of the best classes I've taken at UC Berkeley, made me glad I chose PE as a major. PE 100 is very theoretical but made it interesting. Some people don't like him because he blatantly calls on people who sleep in class. Electronics (laptop, cell phone, etc.) not allowed in class.
He is certainly NOT the best and his teaching content and style are not very good. However, you can get an A in his class very easily.
Wonderful Professor! He engages you in lectures and knows his topics extremely well. Is quirky and has great presence. Also VERY helpful in office hours and interested in his students.

Taking a seminar with Karras is awesome. I can't believe how much he has challenged me. He really takes the time to get me to articulate clearly about my thesis and not be afraid to rethink my assumptions. Yes, he pushes hard and I guess if you are not ready to be pushed you're going to hate it. But if you are you up for it you will learn a lot!

I hate this seminar. It is long and redundant. We receive very few (or no) guidelines for our papers. I think Karras is a nice guy, but, after taking this class, I would warn any and all IAS students not to take the honors seminar,  unless you want an enjoyable year. Wow, I really detest this class.
The guy is a genius. Knows his stuff front to back. Will make you rethink people you thought you knew like Smith and Marx. A lot of reading, but it's worth it!!! One of the best teachers I ever had.

Hands down one of the best professors at Cal.  Amazing class, tons of reading, but the reader and books are all very cheap.  The lectures are both entertaining and engaging, and he truly knows his stuff.  I have used things I learned in his class in almost every other class I have taken in some form or another.

Very good professor. Challenged everyone to question the authors we were reading. This class is a very theoretical class - not a ton of memorization, but there is a TON of reading. Just learn the general theories of the authors and you'll be fine for tests. Be sure to find conflicts between various authors.

Awesome professor. One of the best at Berkeley! If you have a chance to work with him on a thesis, I would take it in a heartbeat. He has wonderful command of methods and has amazing logical clarity in thinking about arguments. Very knowledgeable about many different fields as well.

One of the best Professor at Berkeley (ie in my top two or three). He very much encouraged us to challenge and question the philosophies we studied. Great orator. Very clear, comprehensive and left time at the end of class for debate and discussion. In his last lecture, he nearly brought me to tears as he challenges us to change the world. A class

I love this Professor a lot. He is by far the best that I have ever taken, he is very clear and concise. Though there is quite a lot of reading, if you stick to it and do your half as a student you should end up with an A, I got a B, but I slacked off a bit. Also make sure that you get a really good GSI. All-in-all he was an amazing professor.
HE is by far one the best professors I had here at UC Berkeley, he is absolutely breath taking, I have never been so interested in World History until his class, he is the best lecturer!!!

I loved this class and Karras.  Amazing lectures, don't miss them.  I'd recommend forming a study group to compare notes.  I  only regret not putting more time into this class.  Read the material, and really think about what Karras talks about, he wants you to learn and ask questions.  Highly recommended to everyone.

Karras is an amazing lecturer and he ties historical processes together throughout the course. That's a difficult thing to do considering how much history is covered in such a short amount of time. There's A LOT of reading. Bone up on how to make a good argument. I thought I did great on the midterm but only got a C. Very hard but worth the effort.

A great lecturer. Knows his stuff and has a great insight. Encourages students to see things with insight. A lot of reading though, never quite finish reading and barely got to read the textbook myself. Jarrod Tanny was a great GSI in which helped a lot. He arranged so many office hours just to help us with the paper :)
This man should be President! rocks my socks!

Karras is definitely one of the better professors here. He's very intelligent and witty. Also a very good orator. He's a pretty fast speaker so make sure that you have a friend in the class to compare notes with. I can't stress enough the importance of getting a good GSI if you want a good grade for this class. Overall, a very interesting class.
Fantastic class; learned a lot about the Caribbean that I now use in my grad school research on Latin America at Harvard.  Highly recommend!

This class is such a great introduction to world history. Even though lectures were kind of rambling, there really is no other class that will pull everything together for you like this one. Study the lecture notes VERY carefully for the tests; outside reading was sometimes boring and unnecessar; confer with your GSI on the paper. Karras is amusing

This is my second time around with Karras after PEIS 100. IAS 45 satisfies no reqs but I'm taking it because Karras is the best professor you will ever have in the humanities. His courses will teach you how to really think about social studies concepts and how to make awesome arguments. IAS 45 or PEIS 100 will probably raise your IQ up 20 points.
Really good lecturer.  You can tell he loves the subject matter and likes teaching it a lot.  Very personable and always available for help.  Tough grader, though.

Hard class with lots of reading. Karras is brilliant but fun to listen to. His left-wing spin on things confirms the Marxist bent of the hiring commities at Cal. You will learn about the men who wrote the instruction manuels for world society. Very interesting. He speaks with a "San Francisco accent" if you know what I mean...
One of the best profs I've had here.  If you really want to learn and have that information apply to your major, he'll put it together for you.
Generally a very good lecturer, but he was definitly wrong about several things I happen to know a lot about, which made me wonder what else he was misrepresenting.

Dont let the reaing intimidate you.  This was my favorite class lass semester, and I loved going to section. Dont let the first week fool you. Karras is just weeding out the people that dont want to be there for the first week.  Afterthat, you'll probably realize that he's quite interesting, and really funny.
Karras really engages his students and is always willing to answer questions. Effective teaching style and interesting lectures. As he once said during lecture, he tries to be "karrasmatic!"
Good lecturer. Stimulating class, very engaging

Lectures are always stimulating, he's passionate about what he's teaching. Tests are always essay questions and very hard. Lots of reading but doing them and attending lecture will get you a passing grade.
Karras is one of the best professors I've had. Some students whined about this class being hard. Its not easy. But I've learned more than I have in any other history class in Berkeley.
Awesome class, but hard
Inredible
if you don't have to take the course DON'T DO IT!! if you like history then go on ahead.

Crystal-clear lectures. Lots of reading, but if you go to lectures, you will do well in this class. I don't recommend it for anyone who isn't ready to argue about philosophy, and to defend their arguements.
Great lecturer and very witty. Lots lots lots lots of reading though

Spring 2004 was when I had this class. This was his first time teaching a Hist 153 class. Really good lecturer. On the plus side no discussion classes, but we discuss inside class sometimes. Witty and friendly. Recommended.
Very interesting lecturer - you will never be bored in this class.
A good lecturer, but inaccessible to students.  His "helpfulness" doesn't extend beyond the classroom.
Really clear lectures
He is the goat. Very understanding and caring for his students. Great lectures and practical application-based material. One of the best classes I've taken in my 4 years at Berkeley!

AMAZING teacher. Maintains an online notebook with simply notes and follow-up answers to each of the questions raised in class. 

Homework is laid out to be very approachable. Some assignments are much longer than others.

Reza converts Aerodynamics (literal rocket science) into a fun and easy flight path. Would happily take it again.

Great Enthusiasm, and has a very good teaching style. Homeworks are based more on practical problems rather than theoretical but are easily do able with the straightforward steps and hints provided. GSI goes well along with him.

His lectures are excellent and he has a passion for aerodynamics and teaching. The course however, is undoubtedly difficult and goes over a lot of topics (the entire J Anderson - Aerodynamics textbook). His homeworks get considerably tougher after the first few and the tests are based entirely on the problem sets which are never discussed in class.

His lecture style can sometimes be boring but when it's not boring, you learn a lot of interesting things about aerodynamics. His presentation videos or live demos are really interesting and inspirational. He grades easily but sometimes there can be quite a bit of homework

Keen on answering student's questions. Lectures in a way that invites students to chime in and contribute to the discussion. A little too much time spent on deriving equations for my taste. Exams can be challenging. Homework assignments are fair, and there are mini projects are great learning experiences.->ME 163

ME106 with Reza is the best course I've taken at Berkeley. His lectures are always engaging, and the organization of the course is fire. He starts with the most difficult material and works his way to the easy stuff. By the end of the semester homework is comprised of simple algebra while benefiting from already having developed the intuition.
VERY UNCLEAR GRADING SYSTEM. GIVES THE MAJORITY OF THE CLASS A B-.
The professor has very UNCLEAR grading policies. Not only are the grades he gives unfair and very low, but he does not explain the grading criteria well.

Not a good lecturer! There is no reading/textbook for the class, so each day is mystery as to what is taught. He does not use slides, and only shows us what we can do in MATLAB. Very difficult to take notes as there is no structure to the lecture. What is taught in class is not what is used in homework. Also very not flexible with conflicts.
Best engineering professor I've ever seen. He is inspiring.
Fluid is not an easy subject but Prof Alam did a really good job to transmit the knowledge. Lecture is never boring. His lecture + Munson textbook  everything you need to know for this class.

Best engineering professor I have ever seen. His lecture is very inspiring and you never fall asleep during lecture. I learnt a lot from his fluid mechanics class even I don't get a prefect grade from midterm.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Reza is a great person, and he makes an active effort to make lectures more interesting with various applications and demonstrations. He sometimes spends more time than I'd like answering hypothetical questions that aren't super pertinent to what will be on the homework/tested. Grade is determined almost entirely by two MC midterms and a MC final.

Professor Alam's class is a very light workload if you know what you're doing. His lectures largely cover the simpler aspects of the course, but he does a good job making them interactive and helpful. Discussion sections are essentially GSI office hours and attendance is not required at all. Fun class if you like computers, coding, or math.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Alam is a very good lecturer! The HW is very interesting!

He's really good at giving demonstrations, but sometimes he codes too quickly to follow.  He also can get impatient when people have too many questions, or when no one asks questions.  Overall interesting class, strongly recommend for engineers over CS61A.
He  was awesome!

Alam is a great lecturer. He's really enthusiastic and knows the material very well. This is not, however, an easy class. I would recommend Alam to anyone wanting to take E7, but with a caveat that applies to ALL E7 classes-- be ready for a challenge.

E7 is an extremely difficult class no matter who teaches it when it is sponsored by the ME department. Alam co-taught with O'Connor. Alam was definitely the better teacher. Knows the material inside out and is passionate about coding. I also do research with Alam and can say that he is a very nice guy, dedicated, and helpful; although intense.

He does not hold any office hours and so he is not helpful outside of lectures. He asks questions during class and calls a random student's name to answer (stressful!!!).  He wastes 30min of each class by talking about himself and his research instead of teaching.

He is one of the bests. Lectures are so fun with all the videos and amazing experiments. He video tapes the class so always you can see them on youtube with notes written by students (very helpful). Very friendly, willing to answer questions, very professorial and knowledgeable.
I knew like 75% of the material already and kept coming to lectures because they were so good

I really enjoyed having Professor Pfiffner! She timed her lectures perfectly, but the pace was a bit fast to take notes by hand. She is very kind and open to questions & conversations. The first half of the semester was definitely harder than the second. As long as you pay attention in lecture and find a good group for the projects, you're set.

She is great! She is very caring and kind; hilarious and approachable even in lecture for questions! HWs can be pretty difficult but start early and you will be ok. Make sure to do well on the IPA quiz because I thought it was a tiny little thing and its worth 5% of our total grade, haha. She is great and her GSIs are amazing.

Prof.Pfiffner is one of the best lecturers I've ever had at Berkeley. Many silly anecdotes, case-studies, & encouraging words. I'm no linguistics major but I found this class's overview to be SO interesting & applicable. And the GSIs are amazing (shoutout Franco and Madeleine!!). That said, be ready to memorize (e.g. MUSE IPA table) & learn a lot.
She is such a helpful teacher and engaging lecturer. Her classes are very well structured and the lectures are extremely informative. I couldn't've asked for a better introduction to linguistics.
A great teacher, very easy to learn from. Most linguistic professors complicate topics on purpose, but she makes things easy to understand. She also practices questions during lecture.

I came into this course with prior knowledge, so I only attended lecture maybe 4 times but the course content is very interesting and she does a very good job at teaching it! I do wish i couldve skipped the course but id highly recommend others take it.
The best lecturer, LING100 can feel overwhelming at first but Pfiffner is a wonderful teacher and the GSIs will help you.
Really generous and understanding professor, am considering taking an elective in another linguistics class she is teaching.

I loved this class. Professor Pfiffner is incredible, she always has a great attitude. Lectures were accessible online, graded on one (very straightforward) homework per week, a midterm exam and project, and a final exam and project. Light + fun workload, if you're interested in languages you should definitely take this as a breadth! She's great!

Anyone who has a chance to take a course with Dr. Pfiffner, DO IT!

I'm sad that she isn't teaching LING 100 anymore, but what an absolutely amazing class all around.

Great and engaging lectures, awesome staff, fair grading criteria, etc.

I got a B because I'm a lazy moron, but an A is extremely possible for anyone putting in normal effort.

Really great lecturer and fair grader. There is a lot of work (assignments, group projects, quizzes, etc.) so be prepared. You're allowed to solo the group project if you're one of those types. It's a very demanding class but you'll learn a lot. Her midterm and final exams are easier than homework assignments, which can be quite difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: When you think of Professor Pfiffner, you think about learning, inspirational ideas, great and clear illustrations. If you are more than slighty interested in Linguistics, you should take her course.

Although Professor Pfiffner is very sweet, she has high expectations for what you want to learn. I am not a linguistics major, so I wasn't very interested in the material, so having to do an assignment or quiz every week on top of group projects felt like a lot to me. However, she is fun and caring and teaches the concepts pretty well.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Definitely the best professor you could expect.

Probably one of the most caring professors I've gotten at Berkeley so far. Lots of fun during lectures, and keeps you engaged the entire time. It's very obvious she puts hours of work into the lecture. Assignments aren't bad. With Pfiffner lecturing and the GSI's assistance you'll understand the material. Professor Pfiffner is the best!

Pfiffner is new to Berkeley but one of my favorite professors by far! She is youthful, approachable, and makes the content so fun and easy to learn! I hope I can take future courses with her because I can sense that she can make even tricky topics palatable. She also has lots of fun anecdotes and can have casual chats with students.

Prof. Pfiffner is super sweet and you can tell she really cares about her students. Having casual conversations with the class is normal and a great start to an interactive class. Also if you ask to make a video of something lingustic related to the class, she'll likely approve it for extra credit :)

Professor Pfiffner is super youthful, intelligent, approachable, and accommodating. The class reminds me of the best parts of high school (small, flexible, group projects, in class activities), but is still quite challenging.The format is "flipped": you watch the (short & engaging) lectures at home and then you do interesting activities in class.

*LING 110* Professor Pfiffner is one of my favorite linguistics professors here. She is a great lecturer, very smart, and passionate about what she teaches. The material can be challenging at times and fast-paced. However, she is very well-spoken about topics and checks in often with how we are comprehending. No HW assignments.Exams & small essays
Professor Pfiffner is so sweet! Super approachable, easy to talk to and a very engaging lecturer. She is also very accommodating and understanding.

Professor Ross uses his dark humor in a hilarious way. Great 1 unit class to learn about relevant topics in the world even if you aren't a polsci major. Exam in last week of class just tests if you went to lectures tbh but it's t/f and you just have to pass. Ross has been teaching for forever so knows A LOT. Take this class!

Super funny professor, lots of people think he's mean but he actually cares a lot and is super sweet. His tests are quite difficult though so this class does take a lot of work to pass. That being said he is super supportive and will help you out if you need. You definitely need to have a sense of humor and check your ego at the door every class.
Lowk funny, dont listen to the haters
Kinda mean but in a brat way

Most overhyped class of the century :/ 

Nothing really interesting happened in lecture, didn't really learn much. Exam was true/false, but the questions were insanely specific so generally understanding speakers' views was not enough. Make sure to attend lecture and take good notes because he references specific quotes and details.

Lectures are optional but some terms came up during the final that were discussed in lectures. Bulk of grade is midterm, research paper, and final (the GSIs will tell you the structures of the exams and what you should write to get full credit). Research paper depends on your topic and mood of the grader. The one we had is inconsistent and rude.

Class was pointless and had a no-device policy when it came to notetaking but you can sit in the back. First day of class he kept asking a girl "why do you look like that" when she had a rbf and was just listening to him speak. Hes genuinely rude and the class is uninteresting.

This class is very overhyped. It's an easy course if you need that one extra credit for L&S but that's really about it. He doesn't allow electronics in the class to take notes, but you can sit in the back and he'd never know. He claims to care about "both sides" but he brought in only one speaker that wasn't left-leaning, so it got repetitive.

Pretty interesting guest speakers in class, but professor doesn't allow computers which makes taking notes unnecessarily hard. Entire class grade is dependent on the final test, but it's pretty easy to pass even though questions are specific sometimes. I think it's a good class for the speakers and doesn't require much time investment.

Prof. Ross is one of the best professors I've ever had and his classes always makes my day! He is always hilarious and has that awesome sense of humor. Attendance is not required but I've never missed a class! He cares a lot that everybody learn something from the class. However, if you are too cute you'll be intimidated as he will poke fun.

Hilarious and engaging teacher with an abrasive sense of humor that hides the fact he's actually a big softy. He'll poke fun at people in class so beware if you're sensitive, but he's a genuinely caring person and everything he says is a joke. Brutal tests - the main challenge is issue-spotting, not just memorizing the chapters.

Easiest class I've ever taken. Your P/NP is determined by your final, but you have to lack common sense to fail. I didn't go to a single lecture (optional). Instead, I searched the speaker names on Google and Youtube, learned their beliefs, and made educated guesses. I passed with flying colors.
He mainly just did lectures and his GSI's would take care of writing assignments. He cold calls which is annoying but it keeps you engaged. Keep up with reading assignments to answer his questions!

Alan Ross was an okay teacher considering that the only thing he really did was go over slides. The GSIs did pretty much everything else. If you had a question, chances are you would ask the GSI instead of him. He's a nice guy but you should always be ready because he won't shy away from picking you.

Love Professor Ross's teaching style -- his cold calling keeps a 2 hour afternoon class engaging. He incorporates a lot of real-world examples and has a dry sense of humor. 10-page research paper, but grading was disappointing. I worked really hard in this class and ended with a B+ because I couldn't finish the midterm in time.

Ross is a great teacher and his GSI selection is AMAZING. However, my issue with this class is the READER hired by Ross that grades your research paper. He takes SO LONG to grade them - grades out after finals. Everyone in the class complained that he grades unnecessarily strictly. Take this class for P/NP while you still can and save your GPA.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ross tries to act like a hardass but he is actually one of the most caring professors I've ever had. Do the reading and show up prepared to participate and it will be one of your favorite classes. Especially useful if you're interested in going into business or law but good things to know regardless. I'm extremely glad I signed up for this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: UGBA 107 with Professor Ross will easily go down as one of the best courses I've taken at Cal. He is entertaining, knowledeable, versatile (he is a former lawyer, a passionate ethics intellectual, and current Haas business professor-- doesn't get any better than that), and a great guy. Truly loves his students and makes it known that he does.

Class has literally the easiest content ever, but it makes the curve very hard to get an A. You gain marks for your creativity. Without Ross, the class would be soooo boring; he is the only reason I went to lectures. Sensitive people might get triggered because he makes fun of people, but it brings positive vibes to what would be a boring class.

In PoliSci 179 there is no online communication (no emails he sends out, no syllabus, and no bcourses). However, he is an amazing lecturer!!! Very engaging! Sometimes he is too harsh and calls students out in a rude way. However, I once had my backpack stolen and needed notes. He was very very approachable, understanding, and helping.

I do like Alan Ross, his class is humorous, and you can learn a lot of his class and never fall asleep, I am an exchange student from China, the law is difficult for me, Alan helped me a lot and his class is interesting, if I have a chance, I would like to take his class again

The class is basically graded on only 3 things: midterm, final, research paper. This makes it difficult to get an A in the class. Ross is funny and his lectures are entertaining but he is intimidating if you are sensitive. He makes fun of people so you can't get offended. It was still an easy class you just have to listen & ask questions to ur GSI

Come to class ready. Read the chapters, you really can't skip the reading. Participation is important. His sense of humor can offend the thin-skinned and "snowflakes". Seriously, don't take offense. He is very helpful during office hours and very flexible about OH by appointment. Even if it's not for your major, Business Law is very applicable.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Hilarious

reviews.comment: PS179 was perhaps the biggest disappointment of my collegiate career. I was told that this semester's speakers would be all of the gubernatorial candidates. One person running for Governor came and spoke, and her campaign was a pipe dream. Speakers weren't special people; they just knew or worked for special people. Final was full of trick Q's.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Go to class and take good notes, even during Q&A. Your final grade in the class is determinant on the final and final only sooo
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I liked this class, but got frustrated that he did not grade anything. Most work was done by poorly trained teaching assistants who took 2 months to get back to you and refused to talk about your grade. Ross was wonderful, but very distant from his students.

I don't care for him as a person, he doesn't seem like a very friendly person. There's zero online communication with the class whatsoever, so you have to hear from his mouth when and where the final would be (no syllabus). It's one unit so really low pressure, but the Scantron final (50 q's T/F and multiple choice) asked pretty specific questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed Alan Ross' lectures. At first his cold calling can be intimidating, but you get used to it and it's not that bad after awhile. I learned so much in this class and the content was really interesting.

Its ethics and if it was anyone else that taught it, the entire class would be asleep. Ross is hilarious and a straight-shooter, the type you don't find at Berkeley and the type that can aggravate people who are thin-skinned or can't take a joke. Beware, this class is not graded easily. Easy for a B+, hard for an A-, near impossible for an A.

Alan Ross was an extremely rude professor. He mocked many foreign students and when they didn't know certain things (stupid things like certain type of shirts). Makes inappropriate jokes regarding race and sex while he is teaching about ethics. I felt extremely uneasy attending his class and many of my peers also expressed anger as well.

At first I was intimidated by Ross. He loves cold calling and will ask you questions about your life and ethics on the spot. However, I grew to love him for his real talk during lectures. Just be sure to not take yourself too seriously if you're called on. Practice your writing now - your whole grade is essay based! Also took 194 with him.

Very chill class. 2 hr lecture once a week and 1 hr section. Laid back, relaxed, and Ross is absolutely hilarious. But be warned, the only way you can get an A in this course is if you're an amazing writer. Easy to get a B+ in, but grading criteria is extremely tough. Research paper, midterm, and final are your only assignments but their not a joke
Loved Mr. Ross. He is an EXCELLENT speaker. I have never had a teacher that is better at lecturing than him. He is captivating, funny, witty, and smart. Definitely recommend taking his classes.
Good Business Law course but you really need to work hard on it !

His Poli Sci 179 seminar is advertised as fun and easy based off a final examination. However, the final examination is ridiculous because although it is intended to be based off lectures his questions are stupid and ask particular phrases that a lecturer  has stated or a very specific topic and not the overall general theme and message.

Took his pass/no pass lecture class. The guest speakers were great at times, boring at others but interesting nonetheless. Your grade is completely dependent on the final exam and it's easy as long as you show up to lecture every week and take concise notes. Not too hard, only an hour once a week and Ross himself is pretty funny.

This class affects how I still think about my decisions and values today. Great professor (he's hilarious just take his jokes with a sense of humor). Recommend to students who are non-business majors as well, if it can satisfy any requirement for you take him!

Mr. Ross is an incredible orator. These were the best lectures I've ever attended, I would come to them in my free time. Do not underestimate the difficulty of the research paper or the importance of going to class, it is mandatory for your success (you'd be cheating yourself if you didn't anyways). Expect to be cold-called, so be prepared.

His business speaker class. An absolutely fantastic class with very interesting speakers. The grade is based entirely on the multiple choicetrue-false final. The questions on it are fairly straightforward but definitely harder than you might expect (kind of specific details) so be sure to go to lecture. But he picks on people and is kind of rude.

This was his guest speakers series. Here's the thing. The speakers were great. The final was RIDICULOUS. It asked about the most nit-picky points about the speakers, instead of the actual themes they talked about. You would have to transcribe on a laptop what the speakers were saying. But he doesn't also allow laptops at all.
If you're considering law, I'd definitely take this class. He'll definitely help you figure that out. Witty sense of humor. Class is so much fun, but you do get a lot out of it.

Really enjoyed lectures. He cracks decent jokes throughout and has fun with the students. Allows you to write the paper on a topic of interest. Focus on the paper and don't stress too much about the MT and final. Great experience overall.

I've taken all 4 classes this man has to offer at Cal (ethics, bus law, & the two guest speaker classes). They've all been worthwhile: always gave me a good laugh, mind provoking information, and just generally interesting. You definitely need to be able to take a joke. He's like a friend and very approachable in office hours. HIGHLY RECOMMENDED.
Got to attend every lecture. Only one exam (the final) nothing else due. Easy 1 point class if you attend all the lectures.

Great guy! A little obnoxious but he definitely cares about his students. You just need to be able to take a little humor. He always provides a lot of relevant connections to current events. Very engaging lectures, section just requires quite a bit of participation. Not much work - just one research paper, a midterm, final, and weekly journals
Great course!
Class is lecture only with guest speakers every week. No homework, only a final exam. Show up to the lectures, listen, take notes, review for the final, pass. Pretty simple and easy.

Overall an easy pass, as long as you either attend all the lectures and take decent notes or listen to the podcasts (most are put online afterward) and take notes. However, some speakers can be a hit or miss and I was overall disappointed in the Fall '11 turnout.
half the students never came to a single lecture. two of the lectures weren't podcasted but just listen to everything else the week before the exam and you'll pass.

Easy course; I sat near Professor Ross during lecture, as we listened to our guest speakers, and I took notes only when he wrote down material too. Reviewing for the final can be tricky, especially if you don't/didn't take solid notes. There are podcast to assist in going over everything. Highly recommended to all Cal students, regardless of major.

Go to lecture. It's worth it. Listen to the podcasts before the final to review, and take notes during lecture. No assignments. Reich and Lessig were two of the best speakers among others. Very interesting class. Worth taking every semester.
What a wonderful professor!!!!!
I think the best thing to do is to attend all the lectures, but not bothering to take notes. Then, the weekend before the final, have a marathon of replaying all the webcasts. Easy-peezy final
worthless course. funny to laugh at but not so funny when final exam has nothing to do with course but is a question of how well u can bs for 3 hours.
HOTTIE - I JUST LOVED HIM AT FIRST SIGHT!
Interesting lecturers; test could have obscure details but on the overall, the class is an intellectual time pass in the middle of the week

It's a thought-provoking class and he's great at lecturing. Good amount of humor in class and laid back attitude, but a lot of conviction, particularly on last class. Paper is manageable and tests are blue-book style. GSI does all grading, and grading is subjective, yet seemed fair. A lot of reading, but interesting material.

Ross is a knowledgable teacher with practical experience. Keeps class interesting. Likes to make fun of students, but then again they keep giving him material with which to work. Tests are not easy but not too hard. Was enjoyable overall.

There are audiocasts--so what more could you ask for. SOme speakers werent very good. but there were others that I learned alot from in a short 50mins, and guests provide a different type of learning than regular lecture curriculum. My only comment about the Professor himself is that I found his humor mean

Ross is very intelligent, and extremely knowledgeable about Business and Contract Law. Going to lecture is entertaining, but if your not prepared get ready to be made fun of. Great intro to what Law School is like. This is not an easy class-- if you think you've studied enough, study more!
PS179 - "The extra unit."  Just take the class, it's a good way to spend an hour on wednesday afternoon.

His class is hard but it really prepares you for law school. He always dumbs down the difficult rules to make it easier to understand. Ross is very intelligent and knows his stuff. He lets you know how law operates in the real world. Don't take his insults to <3. Best law professor in berkeley. Never fell asleep and class was always entertaining.

He didn't really teach us anything because all he did in class was to make fun of individual students with really crude humor. Pete the GSI did most of the discussion and teaching and grading that gave us the grade. He grades hard but fair. If you do the readings and follow his guidelines on tests and paper then it's manageable.
Just take the damn class you know you're gonna.
Professor Ross's PolySci 179 class is a pretty good class - it's easy enough to pass the final without much stress - however I didn't enjoy his attempts at "humor" - he's still a big kid

How often do you take a BUSINESS class that makes you reassess the way you view the world you live in? Professor Ross is an entertaining, inspiring lecturer, and I think it's fantastic that business undergrads have to take his class as one of their first courses in Haas. Don't fall asleep or say something stupid if you don't want to be made fun of.
