Like everyone says, a funny guy and a very amusing course. Never had him for a real class, so I don't know what he's like as a teacher. PS 179 was a blast, though. Quick easy credit point for your transcript, some good (or just plain wacky) guest speakers.

He always looks for an opportunity to make a joke.  Is funny but can sometimes be harsh.  The final was surprisingly difficult with precise questions that you wouldn't remember even if you took good notes and paid attention.  He supposedly makes the final harder if the class is rude to the speakers.  Maybe he thought we were rude?

He's an awesome lecturer. Some might find him harsh, but I personally enjoyed his brand of humor. And though the lectures supplement the tests very little, they're very interesting and make you think about ethics/politics a little differently.

Alan Ross is a shame to the Haas Business School.  I wonder how he got in.  He is so lazy, does not prepare a good lecture, in fact, he does not prepare a lecture at all, instead, he spends the entire time telling jokes.  He is a great entertainer, but if you really want to learn, do not take his ethics class.

I love this man. Cute personality...sarcastic in a good way. once he pulled a kid from the class (aka-audience) and tried to find him a date. I would recommend this class to everyone, easy 1 unit p/np!

Very easy course if you can write. Ross is a basically love him or hate him type of a professor - but one thing that he's good at is being entertaining and incorporating humor into lectures. If you're somewhat prudish, you might not like his sense of humor. If you're open-minded, like to laugh, and are interested in politics - you'll love his class

Great teacher! Keeps you thouroughly engaged and exploains the topics in depth. Keeps the class entertating while being informative. I got an A but some people were dissappointed with their grades; this is because you need to be a critical thinker who can think abstractly about any topic, do that and you will get an A.
Funny, animated... but kind of don't understand how he grades presentations and tests.  Put it this way, people probably like him because of his personality not his course or materials.

Indeed, the class was harder than I thought. Much harder, in fact. But I learned a lot from it and I love Ross. He is an amazing professor. Here are the tips that will help you do well: do NOT take his sometimes abrasive remarks personally. In reality, he likes most students, just relax and study hard. He is also extremely empathetic in person.

Yep, it's true: a super-easy course (has anyone ever flunked it?) graded entirely on one short T/F quiz at the end. Guest speakers range from very good to ridiculously bad. Ross is the MC and you can tell he's a frustrated nightclub comedian. He is fairly funny and amiable, if a bit sarcastic. Go ahead and take it: It's an easy 1 unit of credit.

one easy p/np unit. if you have a decent understanding of polisci, u don't necessarily have to go to class. Final is about 25 true/false questions and it takes about 15 minutes to finish. he supposedly makes the final harder than usual if the class is disrespectful to the guest speakers.

The class is hard as hell, make no mistake about it. But Ross is amazing. He will try to scare you with his sharm comments and may single you out for his jokes, but if you tough it out, you will learn a lot. He is great in person. He actually cares about students. He is my favorite professor at Cal. Take him, but study hard for UGBA175.

I thought this class was very boring. As long as you have other friends who go take notes on lectures you dont have to go to class. There is a T/F final. Its not like Ross actually does any teaching...he just finds people to do guest lectures. If you arent interested in Poli Sci you will be bored.
Haha, this guy is crazy for giving T/F final and only needing 60% to pass. Basically, a good test taker can pass without ever going to class.  :)
Great class--easy one unit. Alan Ross is humorous and brings in interesting guest speakers.
easy easy easy :)

I've had all 3 of his classes.  Great classes if you have a sense of humor and a thick skin.  His Business Law class is GREAT prep. for law schol [Currently in my first year].  His teaching method is representative of how they teach in law school.  He is  very nice outside of class.

Prof Ross actually manages to grab your attention and make you think about what's really going on in the world. He lets students have a lot of freedom with the research paper topic (a big plus). He enjoys joking around to keep students on their toes and awake; just don't take it too seriously or personally. The 0 dollars you have to spend on textbooks is a nice plus (he uses a free electronic reader instead). Fun class and worthwhile. Exams are not difficult question-wise, but GSI's do the grading.
Cracks tons of jokes, but just facilitates guest speakers.
No Comments

I can't believe this moron was allowed to teach at the university level.  I can see how 9-year-olds can find an idiot like him funny, but college students?  The man is a complete and total dolt.  The first day of class, when he made fun of several students, I wanted to get up and beat him with a billy club.  Yes, he was that lame and annoying.

Ross was one of the best professors I have had at Berkeley.  I took it over the summer, when the lectures were 2.5 hours long.  But going to lecture was more like going to a show - everytime I went to class, I was prepared to be entertained.  The way he taught the class made a seemingly boring subject matter become very interesting and worthwhile.

gsi rider is a great help. you can get away with not doing the reading. essay exam, understand the basics well. emphasis on balanced arguments. yes, ross pot-shots students like crazy, but fun. cold calls. the class provides a deep and meaningful look into the ethical nature of business and politics. i liked this class a lot, made me reconsider CSR
This is obviously a no brainer class but Ross is a major tool.  Too bad he actually thinks he is funny...
Funny guy, but immature the way he makes fun of students. Set up guest lectures, about half of which were interesting. Easy final.
Aside from the hilarious first day (he takes potshots at students), he lets guest lecturers do the work. Funny guy and easy class though -- final exam is 50 T/F questions.

Probably one of the worst professors I've had in my three years at Berkeley. An egotistical jerk who has nothing better to do with class time than insult students. I wouldn't touch another one of his classes with a ten foot pole.

Roster of speakers was ok this semester. I liked Larry Tramutola's passion and anti-Stanfurd spirit (he's a Stanfurd alum.) I can't bring myself to call Alan Ross "Professor Ross." He's like your bully of an older brother.

I've never heard him lecture either, but he's really funny on the 1st day of class.  The only thing wrong with him is that he doesn't think he has to use a microphone to introduce the guest speakers in Wheeler auditorium, with 700+ students...
He didn't teach this class, just scheduled guest lecturers. He's funny but a jerk to students. The class is pretty easy.

Great professor, even though I've never actually heard him lecture. He just presided over the weekly guest-speaker lectures. Good course or political science junkies like myself. He's really funny too.
In the class I had him for he did not lecture he got guest lecturers every week.  it was pretty cool.
107: Professor Ross is an excellent lecturer, but the reading and tests had speed bumps, I got a B.
No Comments
An annoying Ray Ramano.  Lots of noise, little substance.  Terrible sense of humor...
No Comments
No Comments
The professor was kind and would give funny examples, I found some of the content confusing at times and he isn't always the best explainer but I found the class interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: 16B is pretty easy, just have to study. He would teach very basic problems and then homework would be a lot more difficult, so you would need to look at problems yourself and study.

The Math 125A course taught by this professor had an average grade of C+, with 12 out of 37 students receiving an F and 5 receiving an NP—it was an extremely harsh and, frankly, terrifying academic experience.

For a college calc class, 16B is pretty chill. Lectures were good, homework was doable, you got 10 attempts on the online quizzes. The final and 2 midterms made up the majority of your grade. All three tests weren't too challenging, but he didn't provide much prep material. I would recommend going to the SLC review sessions.
Easiest class ever. There is very little content. The exams were incredibly easy. The curve is insane. Don't waste your time even going to lecture.
Kind of difficult to understand because of accent. He's also more of a logician, so this isn't really up his alley. TAs are very useful in the course.
Not the greatest professor when it comes to explaining concepts. Be ready to teach yourself on more than half of the class content.

Did not enjoy my time in this class. Exams were computationally easy and had a pretty generous curve, but I wish he provided more practice (no practice exams provided, minimal homework). A few GSIs made worksheets, but if it weren't for them, there would be basically no practice sets at all. Lectures were hit-or-miss, but he's funny ig.

easiest math class ive ever taken in my life. midterms were both too easy just actually do the homework and youll ace this class like im deadahh the midterms were easier than the hw just have 2 brain cells and lock in
made a lot of mistakes while explaining concepts, lecture was difficult to understand, basically self studied and wasn't accommodating at all when i was sick...DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS

Professor Moltalban is one of the silliest professors I've had. He has a very calm pace to the class and can take the whole class to solve 2 problems. Hw is really easy if you are integral savvy or took BC or Math AA HL in HS. Lots of resources available for you to study. GSIs are eager to help you. If you're not STEM, take this class.

Lecture is very slow paced and boring most of the time, but actual content is very easy. Not too much homework and quizzes are easy with multiple attempts allowed. Midterms are also not too hard as long as you study and curved very generously (e.g. 20/30 = A, 15/30 = B)

Horrible Professor doesn't communicate well and on top of it all gives the most bummy homework questions that required more than just full understanding of the course. Overall take at a cc if you dont want to waste your whole semester trying.
Class wasn't too difficult. Lectures sometimes got confusing about what was proved vs what was assumed, but he was good with answering questions. Overall nice guy.

This guy lectures very well, and the material is fascinating, but hes not trustworthy. Tested material that he said would not be on the exam and used words on the final that he hasnt defined in class. Didnt even show up to our final so we had no way of asking him questions during the exam. Hes very smart, but not a man of his word. Too risky.

Stand up guy, chill course format. Material gradually gets really hard in this course but set theory is just such an awesme subject and it has motivated me to pursue mathematical logic. Naturally the students in such a class are bright and so the averages were very high on hard tests, but the curve was generous with about an A- average.

funny guy. sometimes gets lost in his own notes during lecture but otherwise not a bad professor. very nice and if you go to class and study a little bit for midterms and the final, you should be fine. curves are very strong for this class lol.

Class is curved to an 85, which makes the tests and section grades a lot more lenient. Seriously try to understand the first chapter on integration as it shows up for the rest of the course. The course is not too hard, just don't expect an A without a little bit of work and studying.

Very chill professor, but can be vague at times. Syllabus doesn't help at all, but this class is literally integration until the end so understand the first chapter he teaches well. I had to self study at times. Midterm 1 was fair, midterm 2 had a low average but he curved generously.

He is not clear what so ever about his criteria. The rubric is allover the place and not consistent at all whatsoever. The 2nd midterm was a sham because he put things on it that he never introduced to us. He does not prepare you adequately for his exams. Be comfortable teaching yourself because his lectures are no help. No partial credit on exams

Nice guy. The first midterm had a relatively high average and because of that, he decided to make the 2nd midterm on material we had never been introduced to. Not only does he inadequately prepare you for his tests, but he isn't clear in his questions so you never know at he's asking. Easy examples that are not reflective of his exams at all.

I took Calc AB/BC in high school so this class was easy. 16B is pretty all over the place in terms of subject materialthere's a calc, stats, trig. He does a lot of examples but he tends to take a long time and ends up missing some of the harder examples that would be more helpful. Midterms pretty ez, but prep lots for the final. Curve saves lives!

This class was super easy. He curved exams towards a B+ and curved section towards an A-. He explained things and problems so thoroughly to the point where things sometimes became redundant and boring. His examples were clear and he exams were super easy. Past exams were much more difficult. Take him for math!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Her lectures are difficult to sit through and she isn't great at describing concepts. Also, you have quizzes graded for accuracy every single class, which is really annoying to study for. The good thing is she does offer EC and grade boosts for hard quizzes. Wouldn't recommend for non DS or CS majors.

If you can avoid this course, definitely avoid it. The worst class I have ever taken anywhere at all. So unless you are a computer science major, stay away if you can. And don't expect grade curve, you will fail. My only hope now is to change to P/NP.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She's just the worst. Do not recommend. This class was a joke and she (and most of her staff) are incompetent. So boring. SO bad at teaching. I didn't learn one useful thing in the class besides not to take a class from Collins again.

Professor Collins is really knowledgeable about the material, and she tries to communicate the goals of the course clearly. The homework wasn't too bad if you attended lecture and/or kept up with the slides, and Professor Collins was always willing to explain something in a new way if a student had questions.

Dr. Collins is the most boring professor I had in my 4 years at Cal. Her lectures aren't engaging at all, and often don't seem too relevant to the class. The GSIs absolutely saved me. Sadly, if you're cog sci with a non-cs focus, this is the class you have to take, so buckle up and prepare to teach yourself the entirety of course material.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Best i never fail anyone

I took her at UCLA but no RMP for her. Imagine having a rich lady tell you that being rich is evil and white people are the problem. UCLA pays this person to talk bad about everyone but herself. That is her class in a nutshell. And she says all of this at a high school level. Take her class at your own risk and not say I didn't warn you.

Roy is DEFINITELY overrated! Just go watch her TED talk and see how much you learn. She gives a one-sided argument without acknowledging important counterarguments even when she knows they exist. She has become the consultant that she criticizes about in Dead Aid since she only criticizes with esoteric, made-up terms without providing a solution.

Didn't learn much. Categorization of development concepts and testing for theoretical terms were excessive and impractical. She's a talented professor, although I feel that I still can't exactly pinpoint what those talents are. She was able to tie in a wide range of disciplines as they related to development.

Didn't learn much. Categorization of development concepts and testing for theoretical terms was excessive and impractical. She's a talented professor, although I feel that I still can't exactly pinpoint what those talents are. She was able to tie in a wide range of disciplines as they related to development.

Huge class, about 500 to 700 students. Good teacher. But not necessarily as amazing as everyone claims for her to be. The class seems like it is very difficult because of all the reading, but a little effort will take you a long way. Used a reader. I got an A-. Overall, a class I would recommend if interested in international development.

Ananya is an amazing lecturer. Every class is interesting. I ended up taking this class P/F because I didn't have enough time or energy to read as much as required for this class. SO MUCH READING! Subject matter is amazing. Tests are kind of hard, but I didn't put a lot of effort into it. Take this class if you get the opportunity!

Global Poverty is inherently an interesting subject & everybody ought to take a class on it. The Idea of the Global Poverty Minor is very cool & hats off to Roy for that. Is she the best Global Poverty teacher I had at Berkeley? No.Is this class the best in terms of expanding your mind? Also no. The focus is rather narrow with a few repeated ideas.

I agree with an earlier comment. Taking GPP 115 - she is a genius. Rehearsed or not, her lectures are gold. She packs a lot of useful & INTERESTING information into the lecture. Great clips shown. An eye-opening class. And it offers real opportunities to those who want to get out into the field of development.

I agree with the comment below. I think it was an interesting class. The lectures were informative and the readings were interesting. However, it is not a breath taking class and the grading in this class is a bit biased. I would recommend this class to everyone for general development.
I learned a lot of interesting things in this class, and Prof Roy really gives you some new ways to look at things. That said, it's really not as amazing as everyone seems to say.

Everybody, and I mean EVERYBODY should take Intro to Global Poverty. It is one of the best classes I've taken at Berkeley; it changes the way you think and will probably change your life. Roy is eloquent and KNOWS HER SHIT. If you don't take advantage of the very important lessons this awesome lady has to teach you, you are seriously missing out.
A shining beacon of genius.

Easy A. Class is not all that it's cracked up to be. It's a great survey course if you haven't taken any int'l development courses. I found it to be disapointingly simple if you have already taken similiar classes. Roy is a good lecturer, but lectures also feel impersonal and rehersed. I'd suggest Poli Sci 126 or Geog 110 instead.

The class itself provides interesting information. Useful in the world of poverty? No. She teaches humility, when she herself is covered with pride and arrogance. Don't believe me? Talk to her yourself. In my opinion she's too "by the book" and doesn't actually want to help the Bottom Billion. She simply studies the poor to make herself look good.

Very interesting professor, and very interesting class, though toward the end it got a bit too theoretical and "academic" (I felt like she would make up phrases just to make simple concepts sound more erudite). Reading was excessively long, but not dense, and she'll tell you all the things she thinks are important, so don't sweat it too much.

I found this site and I can't believe this! I earned a (pretty easy) "A" in her class and I agree w/her politics, but Roy is SUCH a case of The Emperor's New Clothes. All of her lectures can be boiled down to two or possibly three coherent thoughts. The rest is a sort of theater. Life is short, time is valuable, and I don't need to pad mine.

Roy is an amazing orator, captivating her audience with every word. The class is impersonal and hard because there is a ton of people and a large amount of reading (two fat readers!). The class is comprised of: section grade(20%), midterm(25%), one 5pg paper(20%), and a final(35%). Assignments were graded harder than expected. Must attend class.

amazing class, thought provoking, gives you the tools to analyze international issues critically and teaches you how to ask the right questions.  having a great gsi makes a huge difference - i had stefan al, he was wonderful. take this class.

Prof. Roy is an excellent orator. Her lectures are thought provoking & inspiring. The hype around her is a little too much though. She's a great professor like many other professors at Cal. If you can get beyond her arrogance, she is helpful. She's challenging though, and she will definitely push you explore new views. Great class but definitely agree that it's impersonal.

The infamous "Global Poverty" class. Prof Roy is an incredible and engaging lecturer but, since she disallows laptops, you have to write notes concisely and quickly. The material is relevant, fascinating, and well-organized. Roy is passionate about this subject, and it shows -- a "must-take" for anyone looking to make change on any scale.

I was really dissapointed with Roy. She's totally overrated. There are a lot of other great professor a Cal teaching the same thing. Roy's lectures seemed more like speech than instruction. It was very hard to remember anything she said. Also it is near impossible to get an office hours app with her. Overall the class was too big & impersonal.
nice.
i'm naming my first child 'ananya' regardless of their gender.

This class blows my mind daily, and has given me a completely new outlook on economies of space and modernity.  Definitely the best class I have ever taken at Cal. It's a definite must take.  Ananya truly is passionate on the subject of urban theory, and shares her passion with students. (Prof Roy has become my role model for life.)

Ananya is a pretty amazing professor. She covers all sorts of material and has fantastic guest lecturers. The grading is pretty easy and the material is extremeley interesting. Lectures cover a lot of material so be prepared. Enjoyed the class overall.
Amazing professor. This class teaches you about a multitude of topics and presents information in many different formats. Best class I've taken at Berkeley.

Ananya is an incredible teacher. You must take this class if you are interested in social issues. Lectures are incredibly good although they cover a lot of ground. Ananya is very clear, and doesn´t allow laptops, but to make up for that she prepares handouts with all the important info she will cover. Loved the class and Ananya.

Prof. Roy was great, BUT I don't think I was fairly graded by my GSI (there were something like 8 or 9 of them).  I'm not a whiner - I accept my grades, yet this is the only I feel I didn't deserve. I got much higher grades on midterm and paper (not sure about final, but I thought I aced it) yet got the same (unexpected) grade as a friend of mine.

Easily the best class I've taken at Cal so far! Do yourself a big favor and read before lecture as this class will blow your mind(in a good way) often. Definitely not an underrated course. A must for PACS, PubHealth, Econ, Business & PEIS majors.

Key to MT1 is to memorize the lingo. Developmental studies is too much lingo/idealistic activism and not enough practical action. I guess lectures are inspiring if you agree with opinions. Whenever economic concepts are explained for the dev. studies majors there a gaping holes/oversimplifications. Relatively balanced POV is surprisingly good.
Wonderful teacher.

Ananya is one of the best teachers I have ever had. Aside from being an amazing lecturer, she is incredibly accessible and kind. She has helped me apply for grants, decided where and what to study abroad, and recommended other fantastic classes. I cannot recommend her highly enough as a mentor. Don't be shy! She is really really welcoing.

To be clear, Roy is very challenging. She offers an essential perspective on global citizenship in the 21st century, demanding substantial effort from her students. The payoff is certainly worth it, though - she truly is life-changing.

Not only is Ananya an amazing lecturer, but she is also extremely approachable.  If you ever go talk to her, she will remember your name; if you ever email her, you will receive a quick response.  Do not be intimidated by her, because she loves talking with her students.  She is also a great contact for networking.

Her lectures are definitely eloquent and verbose. Couple that with a studied understanding of world issues and her awe-inspiring dedication to global peace, and, hopefully, it creates something that students appreciate. Ananya Roy is incredibly brilliant, and she works damn hard! To the raters saying she is overrated, you missed out, sorry for you.

Fantastic lecturer - not to be missed at Cal. Brilliant, brilliant woman - very personable, interesting. This class is rather difficult - lots of theory. It is commonly taken by only upperclassmen and graduate students, but is open to everyone. If you have the time and effort to offer up, this class WILL change your global outlook.
This teacher/class is sooo overated. Overall pretty boring and not as easy as people think. Be prepared to work your tail off.

Class was absolutely amazing, she is one of those professors that you just cant miss out on. She is very friendly, helpful and patient; but office hours fill up fast. IAS 115 was very well structured, with alot of review sessions, class supplements etc if you like that kind of thing. But if you dont like aesthetic presentations, dont take her class
I'll echo the majority of other respondents here - Roy is an amazing lecturer and this was one of the best classes I've taken at Cal. Don't miss it.

She's a sounds like a good speaker, but that's it. Half of what she says is useless and her speech is filled with colorful words.  Try actually writing down the junk she says and you'll see that she speaks in circles and says very little that has actual meaning.  She quotes stupid literature.  Not that hard of a class though but she should shut up

I know I'm going to get slammed by all you Roy lovers out there, but she is so so so so overrated. I think people are awed by her because she's such a didantic speaker and adds "ization" to the end of every word. Every time I emailed her for anything, I got brief one line responses that were in no way helpful. She's a busy woman, too busy to teach.
A brilliant woman, a brilliant teacher and speaker.  This class was fantastic... I'm addicted to Ananya Roy, and plan on taking many more of her classes before leaving this institution.
great class to have. very inspiring and its an eye-opener

Very eloquent speaker. Fair grader, but difficult class. Learned a lot and very comprehensive. a lot of reading and the readers cost a lot too. However, interesting readings for most part, but the best part are the lectures. one of the best classes ive taken here at cal.

ananya roy is absolutely brilliant.  Every singlge lecture was captivating, and it sounds as though she has spent hours practicing for every one.  Don't graduate cal without taking one of her classes!!
BEST teacher I have had in my life. Ever.

This professor is awesome, and this class is an eye opener. I've never had a teacher so concise and precise in her arguments. I could listen to her all day haha. I think the person who wrote the previous quote must be confused (no offense)
Awful class. Extremely politically slanted. Roy is arrogant. Verry annoying accent. Readings are dull and useless. Worse professor I have had at Cal so far.

Dont be fooled by the subject of city and regional planning, this class covers everything from bums in LA to maquiladoras in Mexico.  Ananya's lectures are more cohesive and awe inspiring than any class at Berkeley.  She even uses The Little Prince quotes in her lectures, who knew that development, urbanization, art, and literature could relate!

Prof. Roy is an amazing lecturer.  She presents the material in a clear and engaging way.  Students actually feel compelled to applaud after every lecture.  Despite her popularity, she is also remarkably friendly and approachable.
Best lecturer I've had at Cal by far. Makes references to The Cure.

Harder than her other classes... this class also is amazing. Cities can be studied from many different ways... she focuses on the angles that are least conventional but most applicable for the world in the 21st century.
Most amazing teacher I have ever had. Anyone who takes her should be prepared to look at the world through different eyes. NO JOKE!
An amazing professor; class is awesome, though difficult because if its range and breadth
The most inspiring and enthralling lecturer I have ever had. You won't WANT to zone out and text message during her lectures!
prof roy is organized, challenging and thought provoking. my favorite class thus far. don’t pass this class up!
Amazing engaging inspiring. Her lectures are like poetry.
She is the best professor I've had at Cal.
very interesting, knew what she was talking about, thought-provoking
No Comments
A brilliant lecturer.  Dr. Roy is engaging, provocative, and inspiring!!  Easily my favorite class at Cal.
Prof. Roy is truly inspiring and encourages student learning in and out of class

[5BL] Worst class ever. Take 7B and don't bother with 5BL if possible, otherwise do your best to avoid Charman. He had no idea what was even on the lab manual and wasted 30 minutes unenthusiastically lecturing about some arcane topic completely unrelated. No proper feedback or grading on any assignments. Doesn't respond to emails, no syllabus.

[5 bl] Very unorganized and unclear. Had very inconsistent due dates and was barely accessible outside class. Created much confusion about grades and assignments because of how unorganized the gradescope and canvas were. That being said, grading was fair and forgiving.
[5bl] what a joke. His bcourses page is a complete mess and he has no clue how to use gradescope. Doesnt teach at all and isnt helpful during lab.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: WHAT EVEN WAS THAT!!!!!!?????

EXTREMELY hard exams (20% avg). 15-20 hrs hw/week. 

Totally worth it tho. Went from a B in 137a, not understanding anything, to having a very decent grasp on quantum. 

Other teachers help you learn. 
Charman makes you a better person. (At the cost of your soul)
He is insanely difficult! Be warned

People saying they like this professor are just trying to sound smart because everybody knows how difficult his class is. His lectures are extremely disorganized, difficult to follow, and assume knowledge of graduate-level math. Seriously, he had us use functional analysis more than once on the homework. Final still hasn't been graded after a month
I LOVE ANDY CHARMAN (this has to be stockholm syndrome lollllll)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This class was actually so insanely difficult but he was just such a good professor...ughhh
Extremely difficult but worth it! He is such a good lecturer and will teach this stuff to you better than you will ever learn it anywhere if you are willing to put in the work

I've taken two classes by Charman so far, and he is one of if not my favorite Professors I've had. Word of advice: the homework requires a ton of time and attention, but you will not get a better full mosaic of whatever subject he teaches. Highly suggest going to every lecture, even the ones too heavy for notes are highly interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Charman is a solid 5CL professor. He is generally helpful, but may expect a little more than is realistic from students.

Professor Charman's class was extremely difficult. and his lectures can be disorganized. A lot of effort is needed to keep up, but effort is certainly rewarded. His grading policies are very generous. He is accommodating if the need arises, and once sent out a poll to change the date of a midterm due to another class's exam being just before his.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Poorly managed course, with a serious emphasis on homework (cannot be understated). Difficulty of homework and exams is cranked up to the maximum, which has a demoralizing effect. While Professor Charman is clearly knowledgeable and willing to teach, he may not be the right teacher for an introductory course like 5A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Overall, Charman is an excellent professor. He exhibits kindness and patience when students approach him during OH with questions. Though the problem sets can be lengthy, the effort is worthwhile. While exams may be challenging, Charman and his GSI are very generous with partial credit. Although 5A is rigorous, hard work is definitely rewarded.

The staff kind of just gave up; practice midterms were given day of, hw solutions and lecture recordings stopped being posted, and the professor fell behind so lecture and hw continued into RRR week. Don't take, save yourself the stress of people who frankly don't care about your experience in the class. Truly an L.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Horrible class. No response to emails. Edstem with no response to any thread. Midterms were rescheduled shortly before their set date. No response to DSP inquiries until the day of the second midterm. Exams and Psets are more difficult than you think. Some problems require math not covered in pre-reqs. The solutions posted are one-liners.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: His lectures were interesting and went in depth on the topic, though it could be hard to follow with the pace he teaches at, though 5B can be a bulky course especially near the end. His tests are very difficult and vary greatly from the homework and practice tests and literally killed me. But overall, he's passionate and a great lecturer!

Really passionate guy who's really approachable during office hours. Besides that, not much good can be said. I personally just stopped going to lecture as fundamental concepts were skimmed over or flat out skipped constantly, so it made more sense just to self study the textbooks. Grading was fine and the curve is really generous.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I could have overlooked the massive amount of homework and poorly administered lectures if it weren't for the sheer mismanagement of the class. When our exam room got double booked, Dr. Charman ran into an empty lecture hall in another building and administered the exam like that. Totally inappropriate and unprofessional behavior.

This class was borderline scandalous in the way that it was administered. Three room changes in rapid order and a two month overdue on final grades. Lectures were poorly organized, homework problems were poorly motivated, and grading/feedback of homework in time for exam preparation was also not afforded.
While this class was very difficult, I definitely felt that I learned a lot more than I would have with a different prof. However, the class was extraordinary stressful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: anyone saying positive things about this man has Stockholm Syndrome, pure and simple. yes, he knows a huge amount, but he assigns so much homework that his TAs have nervous breakdowns halfway through the semester and then gives finals where the average is a 33%. he could've conveyed the same amount of information without stressing everyone else out

Lectures are incoherent, textbooks are useless, homeworks are just pages and pages of exposition, crams several upper division math courses into a very short period of time and teaches like he expects students to already know everything. Nice guy though and obviously very intelligent, extremely difficult assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
If you take 89 with Charman expect to do much of the learning yourself. He's a good guy, really smart, but he does not know how to teach. 

Also the homework is near impossible unless you're getting help

The 'required reading' or the textbook recommended for this course by the department is essentially useless. He expects you to read the optional readings/recommended readings (all of them). Probably the worst math class (apart from CS70) at Berkeley. For context, we finished Fourier series & transforms in 1 lecture, PDEs in 3-5, and Tensors in 2.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He is a good lecturer but will surely suck the soul out of you

This was the class that made me question my life decisions. Charman is a good lecturer and uses a lot of visuals/demos in class, but the homeworks and tests are on a whole other level. On the first day he said he expected us to do the weekly readings three times? Average grade on first midterm was a 44. lowest grade a 2.

I know he's good at physical explanations for a lot of his other classes but because this is a math class he really missed the point of this class: to teach rigorous math that is applicable to physics. His problem sets are just pages upon pages of complicated algebra and didn't really emphasize mathematical problem solving. Tests were awful too...

He obviously has exceptional command over the material he teaches. But writing ten steps in one stroke with no careful derivation or explanation of the steps is no way to teach a mathematical physics class. Textbooks that he recommended were terrible and reflected his rash teaching style, that is, assuming that the students already know everything.

Taught E&M at the level of Griffiths for the introductory class in E&M... however, his presentation on the topics were amazing. HW can take up to 10+ hours and exams are a huge step up in difficulty from HW (48%, 60%, 55% averages for MT 1/2, Final). Jackson/Griffiths problems appear in HWs. I learned a lot and enjoyed it, but wouldn't do it again.

Lectures are great. Big ideas are explained, but he doesn't shy away from the math either. Office hours are regular/accessible. The homework is holistically graded, so if you try your best & put in the time, you'll do well. The exams are difficult, but have interesting problems & if you start prep early and internalize the concepts, you'll be ok.

Lectures were always insightful and helped explain a lot of tough concepts. Homeworks and exams were incredibly brutal but you would learn a lot just by finishing them. Doesn't respond to emails though.

As a lecturer, Charman is amazing. He took the time to explain the math and did not shy away from demonstrations. Even so, his homeworks, graded holistically, were complicated and way too long to be manageable. His tests were devastating and had questions on topics not covered in class or in the textbook. Great guy, tough class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lectures are very dry, and often difficult to follow. The pacing felt rushed at times and then way too slow at others. Never communicated with the GSI's, so discussion sections weren't very helpful. Homework is super time-consuming, and exams are very difficult with not a lot of time. We also never got guidance on what the exams would be on.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Possibly the worst professor I have taken at Cal. Lectures are extremely fast paced, but also very boring and confusing. He assigns ridiculous problem sets that take 20-40 hours a week to complete. He went over 3 TEXTBOOKS worth of material over the semester. Please, if you value your mental health, do not take a class with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Charman gives EXTREMELY long and difficult homeworks. His exams are the hardest I have taken at Berkeley (and I've taken 61C, so that's saying a lot). In lectures he will often quote complicated results without derivation or rush through the math in an incomprehensible way. Good at physical explanations though, and has some interesting insight.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Incredible lecturer, both in content and clarity. Homework and exams are extremely difficult, but are also interesting and informative. If you are willing/have time to put in the work Charman expects, you will learn much more than with other professors. My favorite physics professor so far.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The feeling that you - are handed 20+ problems each week - mandatorily do 10 of them - only get 2 of the ones you do marked -- by a TA who does not have official answers. is the most significant feeling I have ever had while studying physics.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Warning: he is really good at lecturing and explaining. Do go to his office hours regularly to clarify homework problems. His homework are long and really challenging, and his tests get progressively harder, especially the finals. Tips for 5C: do 137A past exams to prepare for quantum problems, and 112 or upper division stat mech for thermo.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I took Charman for 105 and 112. 112 is the hardest class I have ever taken. The homework is three to four time longer than any other class. Exams are 3-4 questions all of which would be hard homework problems. My advice is avoid taking his class unless you are a senior with a good bit of advanced math under your belt.

Its ironic that he teaches statistical mechanics and still pays little attention to individual students learning process. Read this book, do this 20 problems and youll be solid. Is his main message in every weeks announcements. Unless you befriend the GSI/Grader as I did, feedback of any form is nonexistent.
Wonderful Lecture. Explain things quite clear. Extremely difficult exams.

Caring guy and fair tests, but his lectures are pretty terrible.  Writes pretty small, drawings are messy and writing can get kind of illegible at times. Also his lectures aren't structured very well and he does a poor job of connecting concepts. You're better off studying off the book, but you still have to attend lecture because of pop quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Caring

reviews.comment: Charman is a hard professor. His homework is (very) long and his tests can be insane. But if you are looking to become a better physicist, you should take Charman's class. He is fairly good at answering questions and lecturing. His philosophy is to set crazy problems which can be graded leniently on tests. If you are motivated, take Charman's class

Charman wants his students to do well, but he doesn't seem to know how to do it. I understand some people really liked him and that's because they are smart enough to enjoy his extremely hard (but interesting) problems, but if you are not one of these people, Charman is the kind of professor that'll make you rethink about your life.

Probably the worst professor I've ever had. Doesn't teach anything in class and home works and exams are ridiculously hard. He doesn't help you out any if you go to his office hours either. A NO from me.

Professor Charman is one of the hardest professors at this University. As a result, you really learn the material well. His tests are a great chance to demonstrate a solid understanding of the material. Lectures can be a little dry at some points but for the most part he is a good professor.

Much harder than other UC Berkeley physics professors. Long, hard homeworks. He picked terrible GSIs, to the point where we had zero labs graded until after we had completed every single one, and we were getting homeworks graded back after we took the final. Additionally, the GSIs were not very familiar with the material being taught.

Charman is a pretty neat guy in general, but his exams are just ridiculously hard. He's really passionate about physics, though, so I liked his lectures a lot. Do a ton of practice problems whenever you can and expect the craziest scenarios to appear on exams.

Most soporific prof I've come across. Literally proved formulae given in the textbook in his lectures. Didn't teach us how to solve a single sum. Papers had nothing covered in lecture. Has this "holistic" grading technique, which is absolutely unclear and leaves little room for review. Would not recommend at all.

I told some upperclassmen of mine about Charman. Most of them get destroyed by him, myself included. They were also quite surprised he was teaching 7A this semester. Charmander gives out like twice the homework other physics professors give, and they're hard; his tests are extremely difficult, but you'll have survived.
The most existentially difficult class I've ever taken in my life
He's pretty cool. Covers a lot more material than required, but does so well.
Challenging, but you won't leave his class without having learned something, and in my opinion, the difficulty is worth it.

Charman as a professor was not too bad, his lectures were boring, but it was an easy class to get a decent grade in.  I studied for the final the day before and pulled a B from the class. Do the homework, do all the extra credit, and write as much as you can on the midterms and final and you'll be fine.

Really nice guy, cares about students and really wants them to care about physics. He tries to make the exams as fair as possible,w/ 1 MP and 1 practice problem question on each exam. HW is 21% of the grade, and he weights the MTs and the final exams so that your best score carries most weight. They are not v. difficult, doable if you know ur stuff

He brings physics to life with his demos and explanations. Pretty good lecturer in my opinion. Exams are manageable given one problem taken from MasteringP and one problem taken from practice midterm problems. Final was challenging, but I feel that it was a very fair class -- definitely better than my past experience with physics.

Nice, approachable professor. Has high expectations of his students, which is probably why he gave a 40page final exam with 10 pages of multiple choice. Curve is fair, but still tough. You need to know your stuff to do well. Portable TA (alone with divine intervention) helps.

Lectures are not very engaging. Charman went way too fast and kept at a level which was generally above the class. He needs to get a better grasp of the tech capabilities of his students. Tests were ridiculously long and extremely challenging for those who have not done the concepts prior to the course. Quite helpful whenever approached.

Lectures had a lot of unnecessary history in them.  They were fairly good though.  Watch out for the exams though, Charman's a theorist and he comes up with some of the craziest (aka hardest) physics problems ive ever seen for them.

lots of history in lecture, doesn't really help on tests, helpful in OH's.  If charman's lectures start to go south do what i did along with many people in my class, go to Professor Bogg's lecture if he is teaching, do lots of problems, its boring but its how you learn physics, thats really the key to the whole 7 series & btw his tests are way long

Great professor. His lectures were clear, well crafted and interesting. But the best part about his class was the tests he wrote; They were actually interesting to take. He was also really helpful in office hours. He understands physics really well, and does a great job of explaining it.
very good professor: cares a lot about students. curves are nice. portable ta is mandatory to do well on exams.

Charman is a really nice guy.  His curves are really nice, and he is no harder than the other professors.  If you expect physics at Berkeley to be easy, you are still naive.  Do every problem in the portable TA and you will do fine in the class.  All physics professors do proofs in physics, he is no exception.

Charman gives unreasonably long tests that are not similar to any of the homework assignments. His tests seemed harder than other 7a classes. He is helpful during office hours and shows that he does truly care about his students. Nice guy.. but youre not going to get a good grade unless you really know the material (& can solve problems fast!)

Charman is a very friendly, approachable professor. However, as a student taking physics for the first time, I found his lectures very confusing and hard to follow. Tests were very difficult and could never be completed in the given time. I would recommend Charman if you have some experience in physics, and feel like challenging yourself a little.

The curve is really nice.  At least 50% get an A or B.  Tests are not easy, but the curve makes it come out fine.  Use the Portable TA (do all the problems) and only skim the textbook as needed.  He is really nice and cares about his students a lot.

his tests are unrelated to homework problems. if you want to pass his tests, you have to know a lot more than the book teaches. he gives a lot of cheat sheets, but all of them are useless because the book is useless. he seems like a nice guy, but his lectures are usually behind on the homework.

He is very nice and approachable. He is also pretty lenient and understanding. But lectures are very hard to learn from and he fell behind. He is young and still doesnt have much experience, but He is very passionate and his tests are fair, creative, but very annoying. Physics 7a is very structured so dont worry too much... many resources

Charman is a nice guy who understands Physics, but who simply fails to make his lectures worthwhile. His tests are relatively fair but always have one problem that is quite challenging. Overall, a bit frustrating if you expect to learn from the professor.

So Charman always seemed to be behind the other two 7A professors and he always focused on history often leaving the problems for you to figure out on your own.  Helpful in office hours but didn't have time to go to them so I ended up getting hurt on the tests.

Stat33B is a chill class, but he's an odd professor. Every lecture, Massari makes it a point to hate on the programming language and appears to not entirely understand what the code computes and or the syntax. It is clear that he hates what he's teaching and isn't proficient at it either. Not only that, he always runs into problems in lecture.
Andrea is my favorite prof at Berkeley. He managed to explain every concept simple and clear. Just make sure to try to engage in his class.

Horrible class, they don't teach you in class. Seriously. All learning is done on your own, and then you just watch the professor do practice problems, where they make no sense. I got an A because I tried my hardest everyday to stay locked in, and the curve was insane. But a bad teacher, and a bad class layout. Take a different class if you can.
WORST PROFESSOR I HAVE EVER MET, SERIOUSLY. DO NOT TAKE ANY CLASS W THIS PROFESSOR UNLRSS YOU WANT A NIGHTMARE
He tries and is kind but is too unfamiliar with the course content that he often confuses himself and thus only confuses students further in the process.

Middle of the road lecturer, but very caring person. Course itself is REALLY disorganized but he is quite ok. Isn't very proficient in R but is obviously very good at statistics itself. Can give confusing explanations sometimes. Regardless of prof, I would def recommend Data 8 over Stat 20 if you can, the class is better structured.

Prof. Massari can come across as confused at times, but I don't think that impedes the quality of his teaching in any way. Andrea is an extremely caring professor and will always go an extra mile for his students. He's a chill relatable dude who always makes his lectures engaging and knows his stats very well. Also he has great industry experience.

He is simply a poor teacher. The material is not even well known to him and that lack of knowledge translates into his poor teaching. He will ramble during the lectures and eventually even give up trying to explain a concept sometimes. Statistics is not a difficult subject in general but his lack of teaching of R makes the class much worse. Avoid.

Terrible. The only thing he had to do was write the midterm and final questions, yet he still managed to mess that up. Tests did NOT reflect what was taught, and he messed up the grading and had to regrade five times. Did not want to curve the class even though the mean was insanely low. Super unorganized, avoid him at ALL COST.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I'm not rating him badly because I think his class was overly difficult; it included basic coding skills and absolutely didn't have to be as hard as he made it. Disorganized lectures, over-reliance on GSIs, and general lack of understanding of the material to begin with. He knew as much as we did coming in!
horrid, avoid if u can. I went to office hours on my last attempt for a hw assignment and he said "I believe you, you will figure it out"

This professor is so disorganized and arrogant. There were tons of errors on the midterm and final. I thought giving out a clear grading bin was necessary for all classes. This guy refused to give grading bins because 'Students will ask for curves.' He also just answered the questions he wanted to in ed discussion.

I cannot express how awful of a Professor Andrea Massari is. From being extremely disrespectful to students through a lack of responsiveness and rude remarks to providing exams that are completely different from provided materials and textbook content, this class should be avoided at all costs regardless of how much statistics knowledge you have.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: What a complete joke. Very incompetent. The class materials are outdated and have minimal correlation to what is tested on the exams. Provides little to no support. Creates exams that contain many errors. Avoid this guy at all costs.

Course content is outdated/very hard to understand and Professor Massari does nothing to help with this other than a couple office hour sessions per week. Unresponsive to emails and unprofessional. Midterm/final reviews were even more confusing to students.
worst teacher I ever seen
Horrible do not recommend.

Definitely the worst professor out of everyone else. Quiz scores for our section were ~10-20% lower than for other professors' sections no doubt due to the convoluted way in which he teaches content. Lack of clarity and constant ambiguity (i.e. - "it could be this, but sometimes could also be this" even when there is a clearly correct answer)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Adding to the course's disorganization, not only did he sometimes actively feed us incorrect info about course content/logistics, he's a physicist, not a statistician and was "learning R with us", terrible end-of-semester review session in comparison to the other instructors; would recommend literally any of the other STAT20 professors before him.

Professor Massari was a very kind and considerate professor to me and every student in the class. Though he wasn't very proficient in R, he knew and explained statistics concepts very well and was very very engaging. There was never a dull moment in his class and his tests are exactly what is learned in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Stat 20 is kind of an annoying class in general just because there are so many assignments--which are graded pretty meticulously--and lots of notes to read. I found his lecturing to be a little disorganized but Massari is a very nice person, and I honestly enjoyed attending class because you'll get pointers on assignments and can work with others.

He is a solid professor. I didn't really attend all lectures. For stat 20, focus on labs because that's where most of your grade comes from. Don't stress too much about quizzes, they are hard but you get used to them. This class was interesting and a lot of work especially cause i didn't have coding background. But if you can put in work, take it

All he does is complain about us not knowing the material from prereq classes, but he's the one who taught those prereq classes. Doesn't teach in class, just complain about how we will go into the work industry not knowing anything. Wonder how he got his phd, what a joke. I hope all his kids fail in both life and academic.

Avoid if at all possible. I thought all the other reviews were exaggeration, but they're not. Every lecture is him talking about everything but relevant content, and usually only gets through 3 out of 20 slides every day. You need to teach yourself everything, and even then the grading is so disorganized and vague

Professor Anwar teaches a very disorganized course and essentially lets his GSI's run the entire show. Grading is ambiguous and it is difficult to know what expectations are.

Avoid if at all possible.

He is one of the worst prof ever. Doesn't do anything, the GSIs do everything for the class. All he does is show up to lecture and make jokes. Learned nothing from his slides, have to learn everything myself. Unfortunately have to take another class with him next semester, don't know what I did to this school to deserve this…
tough class, but Anwar makes it fun. TAs were super helpful over the summer. Exams very hard so be prepared.

His lectures have nothing to do with the content that is being tested. We are expected to know all this stuff that he doesn't teach without the help of external resources. He has the audacity to say that we cannot use AI.. if he taught it wouldnt be an issue. He tries to be funny and relatable but hes not. He needs to reassess his teaching strategy

Wait to take ME100 until there is a different professor. He genuinely spends all his lecturs rambling and trying to be funny rather than teaching. You are better off just watching youtube videos and going to discussion. Labs and final project are fun but that is not related to him just the labs themselves that you dont need a prof for

Lecture was not great. I didn't go. But the class was well organized and I enjoyed the labs and final project. Midterm one was way too hard but then midterm two was literally homework problems so it balanced out. He was helpful in office hours I just don't know why his lectures are so goofy

He changes his test schedule+setup and syllabus frequently. Most of his class is completely disorganized. His labs have incorrect circuits that lead to retractions of the problems. a professor who is handing out incorrect circuit drawings shouldn't be teaching iot. Hopefully the administration looks into this and the way he treats students.

Overall horrible professor. Teaches absolutely nothing in lecture. Literary wrote "some materials in HW are not covered in lecture, and you are responsible for finding resources to understand it" in HW assignments. Unclear grading, you will likely learn nothing. If you have a choice, don't take this class with Anwar.

Worst class I have ever taken. Lectures are extremely, extremely disorganized, and key concepts are skipped over and not explained well. The whole course staff was in shambles. This really didn't even feel like a class at all. Don't expect to learn much in this class. UC Berkeley please look into this class.

His lectures suck doesn't know how to teach. GSIs actively did not answer questions on ed discussion (There were4 gsis). The final project was also all over the place and rushed! We had to make changes to the project in the last weeks due to late feedback and didn't get feedback from the professor who instead decided to laugh at our group project.

Lectures are kind of like going to a comedian. He is very wise and helpful outside of class, but lectures aren't super helpful to learn the material. Great GSI's and I learned a lot from the labs and final project. If you want to learn in this class you have to take the initiative.
His class progress is slow and does not cover much information. Grading policy is blur(actually never mentioned) and you will never know why you get such grade.

Taking ME100 with Professor Anwar was the perfect introduction to IOT and python. I have used the same microcontrollers in other classes and personal projects now. He has also supported me professionally and sponsored a class for me.
Really funny guy, but get ready to self study-- labs are disorganized and lecture reflects that as well.
Great class, Professor Anwar was very accessible in lab when I took it last spring.

He is a great person, and attending his lectures is entertaining. However, don't attend lectures expecting to learn because he spends most of his time sidetracking on one slide, which means most material is never covered. Prepare to self study, once in a while he drops holy knowledge, but its rare. Labs are EXTREMELEY disorganized.

ME 135 is pretty much an open-lab with a few labs and a very open-ended project. (You get what you put into it)

Should emphasize more computer architecture, low-level programming, etc. 

Micropython and Labview not widely used in industry.

Overall the class was good, just could have been taught in a more relevant way towards industry.

This professor, though kind and hilarious, has taught absolutely nothing in the class. The labs are all in LabVIEW but he doesn't teach this language like other entry level coding classes do. No help is provided for final projects because he also doesn't know. Lectures are so useless and boring so no one shows up. Don't take his class.
He is a caring person but I learnt absolutely nothing from his class. Since this was a total waste of time, I really want to get my tuition back.
HE IS THE BEST TAKE HIM (but other ratings about his lecturing ability are somewhat true) I highly recommend you talk to him or GSI for figuring out how to do assignments and such.

Anwar is a really great guy but man I learned absolutely nothing from lectures. He just sort of rambles for 2.5 hours and then gives HWs on nothing related to what he tried to teach in lecture. Exams are very challenging and extremely vaguely worded, you have no idea what they're asking. Also covered much less than normal ME132 with less depth.

Anwar is the man! He's the most caring professor I've ever had, and has a huge amount of experience and knowledge with electronics. OH are super helpful, definitely go! Lectures could get somewhat confusing at times, but were overall pretty good I'd say. Overall an awesome class and great semester :)
Anwar is a wonderful person and a TERRIBLE lecturer. If you're interested in learning at all, your best hope is the textbook.

Great professor who really cares about his students. Two big projects - one in the beginning of the semester to get you familiar with LabView, and the final project. You can find some of the class's previous projects online - be prepared to work hard. Lectures were professional and LabView was a fun and useful language to learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Anwar never taught me a single thing in E25 and I quickly realized that the lectures were unnecessary. Just go to Lab to get a quick recap of the lecture, turn in your homework, get the new homework assignment, and then peace out of there. Homework is easy A's if you do it, which takes a lot of time. Tests are super hard because you only have 1h.

Very funny guy, but lecture is once a week, and he teaches more 'life lessons' than engineering concepts. Self taught homework. Great guy, but did not get much out of this class. However, is it indeed mandatory for E25, so if you have to take the class, no reason to avoid Anwar.
Tough class w tough materials.  But he's a very flexible and accommodating professor.

This class was very vague, but that is George's teaching style.  He prefers to let you make mistakes and let you realize on your own what you did wrong.  The lecture wasn't very useful. The lab itself was good but the reports always felt pretty unstructured.  Final project was interesting and open ended. A unique teacher for sure.
Anwar is great, love his free range and flexible teaching style. We didn't use the text book much, probably shouldn't have bought it.
Great Prof, great class.  He knows so much about implementing mechanical systems it blows my mind.  Any kind of system.  He's always willing to help, great prof.
George is a great teacher who makes the things he teach clear and understandable. He teachers a minimum of stuff in class so in order to get the most from him, go to office hours!
Project class, lecture was pretty much optional.  Very helpful in lab, especially during final project time.

Best teacher, great person.  Lots of jokes.  This class was a project class, so he lectured, but it wasn't used for much more than the midterm, but all info was useful.  He had a lot of great information about the industry.  This was an awesome class.

People who say this professor is too fast just proves that these students are too slow and didn't deserve to be in UC Berkeley in the 1st place. I enjoy her talking too fast because I am a fast learner.

Very sweet and accessible professor but was fast talker and sometimes hard to understand since she seems to go out of her way to use hard words. The assignments during the year were pretty easy and as long as you are creative with your projects you will do well. Only thing I struggled with was studying for the final exam which is all encompassing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Goldstein is simply brilliant. Each lecture was extremely engaging and packed with provoking ideas. She clearly took immense in selecting each reading for the course- incredible variety and content. Easily the most passionate and inspiring professor- and person- I've had at Berkeley. Truly fantastic

ENG 177A- there is SO much reading, and the final is all FACT based from the materials from the entire semester. If given the chance to take this professor, I'd avoid it. Long lectures with scattered thoughts, makes you feel guilty for not attending an optional field trip the Friday before thanksgiving, and pop quizzes to ensure you read.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Shes nice enough but a little annoying when it comes to how she conducts class. She talks way too fast, I couldnt take notes, seems to go out of her way to use difficult words, and took attendance well into the semester for a lecture with 100+ students. The material was awesome but its a lot and she test you on all of it.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I loved English 45B with Goldstein! Her exams were super fair and allowed me to show what I understood about the topics, which I feel is often not true of many English classes. Her enthusiasm for the topics was inspiring and shone through her engaging lectures. I genuinely had fun coming to class and listening to her speak. She's pretty funny too!

I haven't even finished this class and I don't even care what my grade is because I love Goldstein's lectures so much. It's like watching a TED Talk. She's incredibly enthusiastic and it's contagious, especially for an English major. Her office hours are limited but worth going to just to chat with her about the topics.

Currently teaches at Cornell. Had her for FWS, and she was amazing! Very well prepared and energetic, perhaps too enthusiastic for people who are not genuinely interested in English. Leads great in class discussions because she is very knowledgeable. Also very flexible and understanding.

Great teacher. She's super into the material and she brings an enthusiasm that I haven't seen matched at Cal in my 4 years here. I keep in contact with her and she's just wonderful! She cares a lot about you and is down to help you with essays. She moved to the East Coast but she'll be teaching there!
Very passionate about poetry, very helpful with essays and assignments. Very fun and mellow class to talk about poetry in.

I LOVE LOVE LOVE Amanda! I suggest that everyone take her at least once in their career here at Berkeley. She is one of my only prof. that i am still in contact with because she actually cares about her students and is more than willing to put in the time to help and improve your writing.

She asks a lot from a paper. If you want to get a good grade, you have to, and I mean HAVE TO, go to her office hours and talk with her about your future paper. Attendance is required. You dont have to read everything from the reader, just pick some stories that you would likely to be writing on. It's an easy class if you do what she says.

Very relaxed professor with manageable assignments and a reasonable reading load. Most class time is spent discussing the readings, so it's important to come prepared and complete the assigned chapters. Grading criteria can sometimes be unclear, but she offers helpful guidance and advice both in and out of class.

She assigns a lot of reading, but it is manageable. She does not have a very clear grading criteria. She is very accessible and holds lots of virtual office hours. She has a no-technology policy, but was not too strict about it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very understanding professor. She has clear grading criteria and is very lenient. Easy to do well as long as you complete the work and pay attention in class. Overall great professor.

Such an amazing professor. His class felt like a high school class in the best way possible. Great sense of humor, makes the class feel like a family, and great lectures. We only had like 3 assignments, one take home midterm, and a take home final. Best class and professor I have seen here by far.

Meeting Dr. Loggins and having the pleasure/privilege to take this class (Fall 2024) was truly a one-of-a kind experience! He is unapologetically true to himself and his pedagogy is inspiring as a prospective educator myself. I still find myself returning to the literature posed on the syllabus and the course workload is highly manageable.

Dr. Loggins is a passionate, authentic educator. Each lecture was a mix of structured material and powerful lectures, tying it to the real world. He has a "pull-up" policy, inviting you to bring a family member or friend to the lecture, turning the class into a community. Graded on a few short papers, MT, and the Final paper/presentation. Take it!

Every single second in Ameer's class pays off. This former rapper speaks in such a colloquial and approachable way that sometimes I think he is cooler than me. What he discusses is never in the media. I can guarantee that you will understand what kind of music you consume every day in a totally different light. 1 short paper and 1 final paper.

Professor Loggins is by far the best professor I've ever had. The two hours of class flew by every week because of his passion and dedication for the subject matter. Learning from him was truly eye-opening and it challenged us all to embrace "touchy" subjects with open discourse. If you ever get the chance, take one of his classes!

Had him for C127--Cognitive Neuroscience. He's very passionate and cares a lot about the topics and his students. Lectures can get very dense but he's great at breaking down complex ideas and uses good examples to do so. Also features his kid in his slides which was adorable.

(CogSci C127) Amitai is an amazing lecturer and speaker, and it is clear that he is very passionate and puts a lot of effort into this course. Much of the grade is exams, which were relatively hard, but the questions were fair. GSIs were amazing as well. The class takes hard work, but I highly recommend taking it.

Took COGSCI C127. He genuinely cares about his students and knows his stuff. Expect dense presentations on tricky cog sci topics—needs time to digest. Classes can feel a bit dry, but the material is clear if you pay close attention. Not an easy A—takes effort and passion for test, but he's fair and understanding overall.
this is not an easy class. the content is too much for an introductory course and the level of difficulty of midterms could be high
kind professor easy course

Greg was very knowledgeable and informative. His lectures seemed a bit out of order and move a bit fast since he sprinkles in some facts that aren't related to his tests. I crammed for every midterm and the final and did just fine, but I probably would've done better if I reviewed every day. You're better off reviewing the slides while listening.

Easy class. Took this to fulfill my biological breadth. Attendance isn't mandatory, and everything you need to know is in the slides. My only caveat is that he goes over the slides pretty fast, so I would say just write the notes down in your own time. Got away with an easy A by using Quizlet or Notability AI flashcard questions to review.
The tests are really hard and the lectures can get extrememly boring. Workload is pretty light though, but if you aren't good at biology then definitely do not take this course.
Sweet man, but lecture was boring and a waste of time. Honestly don't know how I didn't fail because I guessed on every midterm & final.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Overall, I thought this class was supposed be an easy A but it was not. I did not have time to give 100% to this class because I had much harder ones. He has 3 midterms and one final which basically make up ur whole grade. I really did enjoy the material but im not the best test taker which really messed me up and gave me a B in the class.

This class is definitely very easy in the sense that all you have to do is memorize a few things and if you start early, you will be able to do it. It's very doable. I will say that I didn't enjoy this class much as although Professor Aponte is a really cool guy, I didn't find him to be a great lecturer as everything taught was very metaphorical.

Really chill professor, really easy class. Lectures are disorganized, but the content is not hard to learn. The discussion assignments take around 30 minutes each (and boost your grade), and the exams only require light to medium studying. Go to class & copy down notes from the slideshow and you're pretty much guaranteed an A.

Hes honestly a good guy and chill professor. I loved my GSI, Lara, so try to get her if you can. I expected this class to have online tests but he changed it last minute. If you try for an A in this class, you'll get an A. But don't take this class as an easy A breadth because you need to study to get an A.

Very chill guy, albeit a little spacey, especially with review sessions. Midterms and final curved so heavily it's hard to do poorly. Section assignments easy. One midterm had some wack ass questions but curved out so no biggie. Easy A.

Went in thinking that this would be an easy A class, that wasn't the case. In my opinion Prof. Greg is sweet and caring person, however, his exams are more harder than I expected, there is no practice test questions, it is really up to you to study on your own.  It is very manageable if you put the time into it.

Professor Aponte is a sweet man; however, his class was disorganized. His exams were difficult and closed-book. Because of the material's density, I often found myself studying for hours. I never felt prepared for his exams, though he provided review sessions (no study guides). Discussion sections were pointless (didn't review in-class material).

I love Greg so much. He brought ridiculous items to lecture (bags of his post doc's child's hair) and if you actually listen to what he's saying it's great. The major issue I have with him is that he crams an incredible amount of information during each lecture so a majority of your time in lecture cramming the notes.

Assignments are easy, which has helped bring my grade up. You never really know what's going to be in the misterms since he's all over the place, or he does application questions, which he doesn't explain. Don't expect to learn anything about nutritional sciences, you basically have to teach yourself.
chillll ahhhh

Please do not take this course with Professor Aponte. His lectures are all over the place and his in-person tests are significantly more confusing and difficult then he makes it out to be in his review sessions. He is a nice guy, not a great professor.
Very confusing. Changing the tests from online to in person after the course starts.

Honestly the easiest class to get an A. But I was a little bit dissapointed because I was so excited to learn about nutritional sciences but the lecture was so boring and attendance was not mandatory so I never went. However, he seems like such a chill guy.

Although this course was easy to get an A in, I do not recommend it. If you need to satisfy a breath, go ahead but the class itself is disappointing. I was excited to learn nutritional science but was let down by the non-mandatory lectures, take-home quizzes, and easy assignments that had almost nothing to do with the course material.

Disappointed because I was excited to learn about what seemed to be interesting materials. Tests are all take home and open-everything, which really discourages learning. Almost nobody attends lectures, so neither did I. While one of the easiest courses to get an A in, would not recommend wasting a semester on this course, take something exciting!

his humor is kind of odd. went to lectures in the beginning but mic is so bad you cant hear. started watching lecture recordings but then stopped bc he spends too much time on easy concepts and brushed over hard concepts. learned like 2 things abt nutrition but still passed

Good instructor if you're taking for a breadth. He makes it clear what material students can expect on a test, and what is additional material for understanding. He lectures decently and the exams are fair (they are currently open-note).
kind of an odd guy but as long as you take notes on the slides you'll be fine
Professor Aponte is a great professor. Very smart in his subject and cares lots about his students. Loves when students ask him questions and are engaged
