If you go to class and take notes, you'll get the grade you want. With that said, I struggled to stay engaged during Aponte's lectures. He is a genius regarding his subjects, though.

There is a lot of freedom to explore topics we are interested in. He emphasizes the importance of critical thinking especially when it comes to science. Very accessible outside of class and very knowledgable in the field.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The lectures were pretty lighthearted and fun. Overall, the class is pretty easy if you go to lectures/rewatch the posted lectures and use the open note policy to your benefit.

Professor Aponte tried to keep his lectures light-hearted to learn and not memorize. He would encourage active recall. Most slides told us what we needed to study for the exam. There was no study guide because of this. If you watched lectures and wrote notes, the exams should be easily passed. Exams are open note and online. Exams were curved.

His lectures often felt all over the place and rushed. There was so much information in each lecture which felt a bit overwhelming. The open note policy is definitely very helpful though but you should try to memorize the general stuff because open note is not always enough. Assignments are pretty easy but most of your grade is made up from exams
Pretty cool guy and knows a lot about nutrition with pretty interesting side tangents from what I thought. If you pay attention and use the open note policy on exams you should easily get an A.

I think he is definitely a nice person and has many interesting things to say, but I found the lectures to be quite boring and hard to pay attention in. The midterms and exams were much more complex than the information presented in lectures which I didn't like. Grades are also heavily determined by midterm and final exam scores too.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: A fun, interactive lecturer with interesting and thoughtful perspectives in the fields of nutrition, personal health, and social media. To be fair, it became a struggle to go to lecture in-person, but I highly recommend it for a better experience.      1 midterm is dropped!

The test were online, multiple choice with a time limit of an hour. Curves are wild (in a good way). He doesn't provide practice exams. Lecture were recorded. There was a lot of content, but the content was easy to understand. Lots of memorization. He's very passionate about teaching his students to make the right nutritional choices.
Cool guy but the midterms are stupidly hard. He evens it out with a large curve though

He's a great professor with a good sense of humor. The exams were based on the lecture slides and he told you what to expect on exams. He also curved very generously. The class is much easier compared to other courses at Cal. Your grade is based on exams and a few assignments that are also quite simple. I would recommend taking the class with him!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Aponte is a super kind and funny guy, and he definitely knows his stuff. The lectures cover a lot of stuff, and it can be hard to keep up (from a bio major). The assignments are easy to get a perfect score on, and exams are curved (like up to 30 pts), so the class is pretty chill if you just watch and take notes on lectures.

Funny professor with a quirky sense of humor. The assignments are reasonable and graded generously. Test material is from the slides and he directly tells you what you should know. Compared to most classes at Cal, this class is relaxing and I think covers some interesting topics, if you're interested in nutrition. I would highly recommend Aponte.

Professor Aponte is one of the most relaxed professors I have had and genuinely cares that you are taking content away from the course rather than struggling to pass. All the content is explained well and assignments are easy to get full credit on. Exams are on everything from the lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is a really nice guy. I began this class as a breath and honestly it turned out so much better. He is really nice and while the material is difficult (I am not a bio or chem major) he curves very very generously. He is also very accessible outside class.

This class was more difficult than I expected given that I took it for a breadth requirement. As a non-stem major, I don't think I would've gotten an A if it weren't for the online format. Aponte tries his best to make sure everyone understands the material and cracks jokes during lecture, but his teaching style was a bit unorganized.

I thought this would be an easy A for my breadth, but it wasn't. Some of the GSIs suck and have no consideration. The lectures were heavy, but the professor was nice and funny. I cannot imagine taking this class in a regular setting with SO MUCH information to know for the tests. The online setting allowed open-note and saved me. Pure memorization.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Due to COVID19, things were modified and graded easier; that being said, everything you needed to know was on the slides he provided online, I can't imagine if COVID never happened I wouldn't still be able to earn an A, as I had an A before COVID. He is accessible during office hours, but his explanations are not as strong. Good breadth class for A

This class is a joke if you've taken high school biology. I barely went to class and exam questions are literally based on his lecture slides which were posted online. Assignments are basically graded on completion as well.

Lectures were course captured and discussion wasn't mandatory. His lectures were boring but he really does try to keep student engaged. If you just watch the lectures online and speed them up and memorize all the material you will be fine. 3 midterms (drop the lowest one) and a final. Also some really easy assignments that are mostly completion.

You can tell he's really trying to get students invested, but the way his lectures are organized make it hard to do so. You don't miss out on much if you don't go to class. 3 midterms + final + some assignments that were easy and mostly completion. Never took AP bio/etc, but tests were ok--just brute force memorization (and curved).
His lectures are very hard to follow and confusing. The concepts are simple, so I am not sure how he makes them seem difficult. Funny sometimes, but I would not recommend.

Took this for that easy A, ended up with a B. Don't take it if you haven't taken any AP BIology or ANthropology during High school or community college. Most importantly, the material wasn't bad, but a lot to take in for the four tests in his class. Remember! 80% of your grade will be based on the tests.

The lectures were dreadful and he often went off on tangents so you didn't know what info to absorb. For midterms and final, you have no clue what exactly you need to study. Do not recommend if you are not a STEM major or haven't taken AP bio or similar. Assignments were easy and you're fortunate if your GSI is good. Rougher class than expected.

Don't take. Most boring prof ever. Very fast-paced too, so impossible to take good notes. The only reason I went to class is bc he doesn't webcast his lectures, but I realize now that going was a waste of time. Just go through all the slides and memorize everything the night before a midterm. Got a healthy A, but feel like I didn't learn anything.
Dope professor, looks out for students

Greg is a good professor. his lectures are boring but his lecture slides are important for the midterm. grading is really clear, not many assignments. he's a really nice professor that will answer any question you ask. he genuinely cares that you succeed and he wants his students to do well in his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: Easy to listen to in lecture. Participation in lecture not necessary. Assignments are straightforward and simple. Three midterms and you drop one. All information you need to know for the midterms and the final are posted on the lecture slides. He also posts his podcasts online! Definitely a good choice to fulfill that bio breath requirement!

Aponte repeatedly claimed in class that NSTX 10 is supposed to be an easy A, but it did not seem that way while taking the class. Lectures are long and include high-level science. Midterms do not match what is taught in class, making it hard to study for. Assignments were all easy to do and took only a few minutes to complete. Good P/NP class
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: He's a nice person, but lectures were very dry and sometimes confusing. The tests were pure memorization and it's easier for people who've taken molecular biology (AP or college course) before. Assignments were pretty easy to complete and having a good GSI is beneficial.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Difficult to understand during lecture but he's honestly really nice & approachable and genuinely wants students to succeed. He puts little tool kit symbols on slides you need to know so just dedicate 1-3 days memorizing the slides. A good GSI will make a huge difference, mine provided detailed study guides that had everything I needed to know

Lecture is pointless but he'll occasionally post videos that he'll ask a question or two about on the exams. He seems nice but I could hardly even comprehend him half the time. All you need to know is on the lecture slides. Not an easy, but not a hard class either.

To be honest, he was boring. Lecture was boring and I did not learn in lecture. I learned from reading the slides on my own time, which were not too great either. People say this class is an easy A, but I would say that if for students who have taken AP Bio or have a Bio background. For me, I spent my time memorizing the slides. Wish I did P/NP.

If you have taken any bio the material in this class is easy. I just made flashcards based on his powerpoints a couple days before midterms and got an A. You should go to weekly discussion and make sure to do all the hw assignments. Overall, the class was a breeze but the professor was incredibly boring and uninteresting so I never went to lecture.

For a bio (or another related) major, this class is easy. As a math major who has not taken a bio class since freshman year of high school, this class was more memorization than I wanted (and a lot more difficult). Slides are useful to study (for the most part), but you also have to go to lecture. Nice guy though.
This class was kinda interesting but the tests were hard. There are homework assignments every other week and discussion is like another lecture every week.

His tests are decently easy, but he is a terrible person. I had a few important questions for him, and he completely gave me the go around and ignored all of my questions. He was rude, and he is not a good lecturer. I had heard this class was fun, but I regret taking it. It was definitely not fun.

Loved this class. Aponte loves teaching it too, and he is obviously passionate about it. He is always there for his students, and keeps the class at a good level of difficulty. You have to study, but not particularly hard. Not a free A like people are led to believe, so don't go into it with that thought or you will regret it.

He's a very caring person, and will answer any questions you have. The problem is many students take this thinking it's an EASY A and are shocked when you have to study for the exams (3 exams, 50 MC questions each, one is dropped). Studying a week before the exam gives you enough time to get an A.

This class is not my favorite. It's nice that the midterms are only on the material that's on the slides, but we have three (one the week before dead week), and also a mandatory final. The lectures are dry and hard to focus on, and the midterms are a bit difficult too--more than you'd expect from a course like this.

I can't believe he hasn't been rated yet. Because all his slides are online ("complete packages" he says, ha!), he speeds through the information and never fully explains basic concepts or how they are interrelated. This problem is especially obvious when he asks the class a question that's met with cricketsand this is a big class.

The semester hasn't ended yet but I LOVE Amy Gurowitz. She is the best professor I've had so far, she knows her stuff and is very funny. I always look forward to this class. Reading heavy and lectures teach you a lot, quizzes are seldom and very simple as long as you do the readings. Take Gurowitz above anyone else, she is the best!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Tough grader, but great professor. Not an easy A class, but definitely not impossible to do well. She cares about student feedback as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment:
I've had her twice and I think she does a really good job on her lectures. She reads off the slides, though, so if you don't want to go in person you don't have to. But i do recommend it & she's super nice in OH

DO THE READINGS!! i credit my A to that
Prof and GSI grade harsh.
Grading scale in this class is genuinely so bad I'm not sure how Gurowitz has a 4 on here. So unforgiving and impossible to do well. Do not take this class or any other Gurowitz classes
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Gurowitz's lectures were very dry/boring, you're better off in a different class. There are 6 quizzes, a midterm paper, and a final research paper. GSI was super tough on grading, would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Gurowitz is approachable and always open to questions, which I appreciated. However, her lectures, though scripted, felt dry, lacking, and unfocused. You could probably do well by keeping up with the readings, even without attending any lectures. The reading quizzes are manageable (I always skimmed), and the two papers are graded fairly.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: very nice professor, lectures are really interesting but tough grader
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Gurowitz can seem intimidating at first but don't be shy! The class is very lecture heavy but luckily she is an interesting lecturer. If you don't plan on attending lectures, don't take the class. Lecture attendance is the only way to succeed.

Awesome class with really engaging lectures, you're graded on three assignments, and its definitely  manageable class. All reading material was very accessible, your happiness in this class is reliant on your GSI. I wouldn't recommend taking the head GSI.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Good and efficient lecturer with a very clear, direct and organised style. However, class is very heavy in reading, and most are long and dull. Lecture recordings are also not released online and the slideshows are pretty basic, which basically makes attendance mandatory.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: great class, great professor!
Took Spring 2024 - take Scott Straus' Genocide course instead. Same topics, better lecturer- more engaging.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Great lecturer, interesting material. In-person midterm heavily based on lectures, so although attendance wasn't mandatory it's worthwhile going. Final was a research paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Puts the GRRR in Gurrowitz. Enjoyed the course very much, and enjoyed her information based lectures. She shows that she cares about her students and does her best to present new material in an organized manner. Participate in section, go to her office hours, and ASK QUESTIONS! Don't have to do all the readings, but would suggest doing some.

Releases recordings of lectures online, so attendance isn't mandatory. Follow the schedule provided in the beginning of the year and you'll be fine. Gurowitz is funny and an efficient lecturer, but it can be difficult to take notes at times. I recommend watching the lectures from the front of class and taking notes later at home w/ the recordings.

Overall one of the better classes I've taken in the PS dept. Gurowitz is clearly so brilliant and well-spoken, but lectures are kind of a repeat of the readings and are history heavy. MT exam early in the sem and 5 "reading responses" which are graded as essays. Final paper is based on a case outside of class, so many people stop attending class.

Professor Gurowitz is a great professor, but what helped me through the course was the GSI assigned to the course as those are the individuals who you'll be interacting with the most. This course was extremely reading heavy so be prepared to read.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Prof. Gurowitz is a fantastic lecturer and I greatly enjoyed PS5 with her. My only complaint is that lecture recordings tend to be inaccessible; if you miss a class you have to rely on a friend's notes. However, the actual course content was digestible and interesting.

This class was well-organized and the professor was great about answering questions. There was a lot of reading (sometimes you can skim). You have to go to lectures - they aren't recorded and the slideshows are pretty basic. It's tough to get an A because it's graded based on three pieces of writing, which felt a bit arbitrary and unclear.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Gurowitz is an amazing lecturer and I really looked forward to her class! Lecture isn't mandatory, but you should definitely still go. There are a lot of readings -- it's manageable, some are skippable/skimmable. Graded on a take-home midterm (5 pg paper), in-class midterm, final, and section participation. Pay attention/go to lecture to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Gurowitz is a spectacle of passion and knowledge, she upholds her craft with some of the highest dignity I've seen in a while. That being said, I do think the readings were often too dense, lengthy, and esoteric at times - especially her quizzes being disproportionally formatted. But her standards will subvert your skills and intellect.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Gurowitz is very accomodating to the needs of students, but dont use this to get out of the readings! There is a lot of reading. lectures can be boring at times but attendance is not mandatory. you HAVE to read for the quizzes but she drops the lowest one. bulk of the grdae is a midterm paper and final semester research project
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: thoroughly enjoyed ps5 with gurowitz; she was especially engaging, and I genuinely looked forward to lecture. lots of reading, but as long as you understand the significance behind each module and its nuances, you should be fine skipping like an article here and there (however i 100% suggest you read the mingst textbook whenever it's assigned)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really liked PS5 with Gurowitz. Lectures were reasonably engaging and the exams are easy as long as you pay attention in lec and do most of the readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: There are a lot of readings but it's not a big deal if you don't do some of them. Her lectures are great. There is a lotttt of course material. Exams are tough to study for since there's so many possible short answer and long essay prompts she could give you. Definitely attend lecture it will solidify the readings, plus she doesn't post recordings
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very knowledgable and good professor. Loootsss of material so not a super easy class. Very reading heavy but don't stress if you don't do them all. Few assignments that are easy to do well on if you study lectures. Exams are in-person short answers and essays which can be challenging. But smart professor who really knows her stuff!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor is a nice person! However the content of her course is dense, and it is nearly impossible to keep up with all the readings. Quiz's were difficult with only two questions that could be based on any minute detail from any of the 90+ pages of reading. Majority of the content was theory based, didn't really see much international content.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed PS124D! Her lectures pack a lot of information in, and she speaks quickly, so be ready to write. I thought her lectures were very organized, and she is very engaging; she lets you know exactly what she wants you to take away from her lectures. If you are interested in international relations, definitely take a class with her!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: there were great gaps of difficulty between GSIs and I was one of the unfortunate ones paired with a GSI that thought they were advising doctoral theses. Which is funny given the borderline-offensive simplicity of the class. Gave ex post facto extra credit which I find quite frustrating. Take something else.

Amy talks really fast and doesn't post her lecture notes or class recording which really sucks if you're sick since she usually just puts up a photo and talks (really fast) about it. Also, doesn't follow DSP protocol for essays. Probably wouldn't have passed without my GSI, who taught us most things in a better way than Amy did.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Readings are 20-45 pages weekly. Attend lecture, you might get extra credit. Reach out to GSI for (5) responses during OH, start research paper (EARLY!), and create a study guide for the exam = A. Lectures can be content heavy and dry sometimes, but slides have everything discussed. Advocacy is key because of more GSI interaction. My GSI was great!

Gurowitz is a great lecturer do not get me wrong. She is very sweet and is very informed on the topic she is teaching. However, if you care about your grade, just do not take this class. The GSIs for this semester are absolutely horrendous, everyone has the same thought. They take points off for no reason, and refuse to provide more feedback.
Professor Amy Gurowitz is great, but her GSI's are random.  The GSI is really what's important at CAL.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lots of reading, but not necessary to read it all. Gurowitz is a great prof, engaging and interesting during lectures, and her office hours are always super helpful. Class is weighted on only a couple of midterms and the final, so study well and you can pass fine. All in all, will look forward to taking a class with her in the future.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Gurowitz has been my favorite PS professor so far. Her lectures are very practical and dense with informative. I strongly encourage students to take PS 5 regardless of their previous knowledge of international relations or history. I learned a lot and left her class with a lot of permanent knowledge. If you're considering taking her class, take it!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Attendance in discussion is mandatory. All you really need to do is attend the lecture and review lecture notes. Grade is based on participation, a take-home essay, an in-class midterm with short answer questions and an essay, and a final timed essay. Essays were straightforward and the GSIs were pretty lenient graders. Skip the reading.

She speaks very fast but her lecture slides are posted on her website, so you can always revisit them. She is understanding; I remember that she moved our first midterm because it was supposed to be the day after Halloween (she knows how college students are). Lots of the grading depends on your GSI and how they grade your midterms.

I overall enjoyed this class and the professor. Attendance isn't mandatory for lecture, but you need to come because there are no recordings, and the test content heavily relates to her lectures. Do the reading; you'll discuss in section! I wish I could've taken POL 5 in a smaller class setting to really soak up the material and ask questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Bored. Needs to go farther in depth on material.
Don't take this class during summer!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took this class as my international studies breath as an EECS major. There was a lot of reading and papers that took weeks to complete. On top of this, the professor grades very unfairly and focuses of a few elements of the paper. I spent over 20-25 hours a week on this class and many late nights.

Lectures didn't allow laptops and Prof. Gurowitz hardly ever used slides or wrote on the board: it was just a lecture for 1.5 hours, but it was easily the most captivating class I've ever taken at Berkeley! Never fell asleep once. Lots of readings, but discussion sections make you think about them in a real world applicable and digestible way.

Amazing class! Lectures were clear (not mandatory attendance) and she is super organized. She always held office hours and would respond to questions via email in a timely manner. Gurowitz is also very funny, and even though attendance wasn't required, I wanted to show up and stay engaged. Highly recommend as an upper division polisci class!

Professor Gurowitz is brilliant and will help you achieve your highest intellectual peak while you are taking her class. However, she can be a bit cold and not very encouraging so it's easy to be demoralized when she gives criticism. If you can push through, though, the final product will be the most successful version of it that it could be.

Professor Gurowitz was one of my first professors and I didn't think too much of the class until I had some HORRIBLE lectures by other professors which made me realize that Professor Gurowitz is extremely organized, straight to the point, and an amazing lecturer. Her bCourses page is organized and I would take her class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: There was way too many readings assigned for each week but her lectures make up for it because you can get the general idea of whats being talked about without having to have read a word. I took this to fulfill breadth so I prioritized my other classes towards the end of the semester.

So much reading, she has some pre-recorded lectures but mostly you're on your own. The GSIs are great but grading criteria is not totally clear. You have 3 midterms and a group presentationdon't take a lot of other reading heavy classes if you take this class, spare yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: First of all I dont know what Amy yall talking about cuz it isnt the one Im taking. Her reading is ridiculous conspired to other psc courses. One midterm with a mediocre prompt 25% of the grade. & reading quizzes. Im total worth 25% too. She always says she hates power points and I wont have time to write down the slides trust.

Very solid professor who handled the transition to online learning very well. Class is graded on 3 midterms which are just 5 page take home essays with super clear instructions, so its not a lot of work and very easy to do well if you base your essays on lecture/readings. The lectures themselves were fascinating too, shes very engaging!

Professor Gurowitz is very knowledgable and makes her lectures funny and relatively easy to understand. Our lectures were asynchronous this semester so I do wish there had been more synchronous opportunities for instruction but overall I would recommend taking a class with her. Class grade was based off of three five-page papers and a group project
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--So many papers

reviews.comment: Very interesting and I like her sense of humor. The 3 midterms were just 3 take-home essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Excellent lectures and great sense of humor! I learned so much taking her class and I recommend any student who wants to major in Poli Sci at Berkeley to take her classes.
Amazing professor. Interesting and kind, especially in OH. Not one of those Professors who tries to make PS classes meaninglessly difficult for the sake of it. Truly there to help students learn.

Reading quizzes and research paper make up the bulk of the work in this class, if you stay engaged you should do fine. Heavy theory section in the beginning, but you'll digest it throughout the course. Gurowitz has amazing insight and knowledge of topics, very approachable, and lectures are dense but rewarding. Ask questions, you won't regret it.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Gurowitz is super sharp and presents material very well. Certain subjects can be dry at times but she does a good job of keeping the class engaged. For 124C specifically, it's very theory-heavy so keep that in mind. Toughest part of the class for me were the reading quizzes, which had very specific questions and were worth 25% of the class grade.

Gurowitz is easily one of the best professors at Cal. Lectures are interesting, and all readings are online. There are several small quizzes about the readings (maybe every 2-3 weeks) and one final research essay that she gives the prompt on the first day of class. Very knowledgable, kind, and totally easy to talk to in office hours! 10/10
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Attendance wasn't mandatory but it's necessary to pass the class. No power-points, talks fast but is a really good speaker. This class is not boring at all, she's a great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She is a great professor, one of the best I've had. She talks really fast and there are no power points but it's manageable. She is very knowledgeable and not boring. You need to attend lecture, tests (2) are mostly based on the lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Hands down the best lecturer I have had so far. Given that I am only a 2nd year, it's a small sample but she is very engaging and the content is interesting! ATTEND LECTURES, the content is on the midterm and final. Understand the main points of the readings and take notes during the lecture! 1 essay, 1 midterm, and 1 final.
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Amy is an amazing professor but I do not recommend any first year students to take this class as it is paper heavy and it is difficult to write on this information as a freshman. But I recommend the class to anyone interested in IR.

Lectures were a very dense 1.5 hours of Amy talking really fast, but she's a really good and entertaining lecturer so I didn't mind. No notes or slides or anything posted, so missing lecture is a really bad idea. Essay on theory wasn't too bad, and the exams were pretty easy as well. Do the reading, and get Deirdre for your GSI, and you'll do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Gurowitz does not use powerpoint for her lectures or any supplements aside from her voice with which she speaks 100 mph. It is tough to learn anything in lecture and I recommend just doing the reading and not bothering with lecture. It was an okay class but I would advise against it.

The first part of the class is dense because it goes over theory, but you use these theories to evaluate later topics. Gurowitz is a dope professor who knows what she's talking about, and the outlines for lectures are followed pretty clearly. Lectures are super helpful, and you MUST attend bc no slides are posted online. No laptops allowed.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof. Gurowitz is very enthusiastic and presents the material in an interesting and organized manner. Very interesting class.
knows her stuff but lecture format was boring and and at times repetitive. it takes a long time for her to get to the point.

Dr. Gurowitz is a great lecturer and is consistently good about addressing questions and comments from the class. She doesn't use powerpoint or allow laptops during lecture so be efficient with your handwritten notes. Definitely make sure to get to know your GSI and their expectations as they will ultimately grade all of your assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This class is graded on section participation, reading quizzes, a take home midterm (based on theories learned) and a 13-15 pg research paper (topic of your choosing, very little limitations). The paper is tough, you need a good GSI to help you with this and you should start early (which I didn't and let's be honest, you won't either).

Great lecturer, one of the best professors I've had at Cal! She really knows her material and is often quite hilarious and witty. Doesn't allow laptops in class and lectures quite fast without powerpoint, so be prepared to write. Also lots of reading with reading quizzes, but the quizzes aren't hard and she drops your lowest score.

Prof. Gurowitz was great. She conveyed the material clearly, and was very open to questions to make sure everyone was on top of it. She has a great sense of humour with occasional witty remarks during lecture. No technology and no slides, so showing up is important.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I loved this class, the material was fascinating once you got through the theory section of the first month. Mingst textbook is definitely unnecessary, but Art and Jervis book really comes in handy when finding examples for midterm and final. Midterm paper and final are graded kind of harshly, especially w/GSI Claire, Joe, or David.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: She is an awesome lecturer. She explains concepts very clearly with lots of examples. DO NOT get Fiona as a GSI as she was extremely rude to many of her students. This class requires that you do a little bit of the reading so you can get a better understanding. However, all readings are not required. Tests are semi hard but you can easily prepare.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Honestly, she's knowledgeable in the field, and her lectures are informative, but the class was probably the most underwhelming polisci class I've taken yet. Her style of lecturing can get boring at times, and I found the grading to be somewhat difficult.  She's a solid instructor though, you'll learn the subject.

Gurowitz is an engaging lecturer and very intelligent. Her lectures are clear and she's very helpful when answering questions. If you choose to take this course, I recommend steering clear of Jessica Ward as a GSI- I had many problems with her, as did several other students in my discussion section. Other than that, I would recommend this course.
Love her
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Gurowitz is very organized and makes an effort to make sure her students understand the content of her lectures. She talks very quickly, so it is best to be prepared to write notes QUICKLY. Also, her head GSI Paul seems to have a bad rep on this site, but he was my GSI and I found him extremely helpful despite being a bit of a tough grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: A good professor who gives you a solid introduction to international political science. Lots of reading, and sometimes lecture was boring, but overall it is a solid class. If you prepare for the timed midterm and final you will do OK. First midterm is an essay and is purposefully graded toughly which is annoying. But overall, she is clear and funny

The first month of this class is heavy political theory, which can get frustrating. After the take home midterm, the classes aren't necessary to attend and concepts get fun. Readings are necessary to pass the quizzes, but the questions are very straight forward. The research paper requires a lot of work, and a good GSI is needed.

Gurowitz is amazingly organized. She doesn't play lecture slides, which is a bummer, but her lectures are clearly outlined and easy to understand. The readings weren't exactly necessary to get a B. Gurowitz is funny in her own way; she makes learning about political theory as entertaining as that can be. I would recommend the class.

Professor Gurowitz, although she does talk very fast, makes an hour and a half class feel like very little time at all. Her wry humor and obvious interest in the subject shines through and demands attention. Concepts are difficult, but if you pay attention and put in a little work (and have a good GSI) you should be fine.

Prof Gurowitz is to the point and gives good lectures. Take good notes in her lectures and you won't really need to do the readings, especially if you have a good GSI. She doesn't waste time and throws in a joke or two every once in a while. The beginning is tough, but if you ask questions and go to office hours you'll be solid for the course.
Not a bad class, a little easy to space out and get lost during lecture. Exams are very much lecture based, keeping up with readings is not ABSOLUTELY necessary.

Professor Gurowitz is awesome; she is down to earth, funny, very intelligent, non-biased, and easy to approach. I went to her office hours a lot and she was always super helpful. The one thing to warn future students about is that she talks SO FAST. If you space out for 5 seconds, you're done. It can make her class unclear.

Gurowitz is an outstanding prof. Lectures are clearly organized (however she doesn't use powerpoint, which I struggled with). Reading and tests/papers were manageable with a full course load. Also, she explains a lot of IR concepts by telling us about interactions/fights she has with her kids, which I thought was really entertaining.

Lectures are extremely long without any break (1.5h, usually made me sleepy). No assignment at all. Only 2 midterms ( one 5 page take-home paper and one in-class I&I+essay) are relatively not difficult. Great and helpful GSIs (you have to rely more on GSIs to get deeper understandings of class materials and what appear on midterms and final.

I did not enjoy this class. You're only tested on the reading and a lot of it. Going to lecture was not necessary, except for quiz days. I felt that this was more of a theory class at times instead of being IR but it gets better at the end of the semester. Professor literally reads from a script when she lectures.

Amazing class! She is a great lecturer. She posts lecture outlines before class. There are 6 mini-quizzes(2 short answer questions) on readings, but she drops the lowest score. The 2 papers are pretty straightforward, and she makes a point to help students choose paper topics early. Course content is dense, but very interesting.

If you are willing and able to put in the reading it is a wonderful class in which I learned a lot, the professor is very insightful and knowledgeable and presents topics from both side. Would definitely recommend this class.

She's amazing, super engaging and funny. Very clear about her expectations of the class and about assignments. The grade breakdown was very fair. If you take this class, TRY YOUR BEST to take it with Paul the GSI, he is the best GSI I have ever had. Would absolutely recommend this class, I'm sad she's not teaching any other upper div classes

Her lectures were great and she was very clear. Her class was very well run and she definitely knows what she is doing. HOWEVER, my GSI was the absolute worst and completely ruined the class for me. Try your hardest to switch sections if you get Paul. He is the worst GSI of all time. Snarky and condescending and the hardest grader. Don't do it

Professor Gurowitz is GREAT. Every lecture was very clear and helpful, and I felt like a learned a LOT about IR by the end of the course. She is excellent, and makes me want to take another course with her in the future. Take PS5 with Gurowitz.
Very clear, organized lectures... lecture and discussion pretty much cover all readings so you don't have to do them (but you need the book for the first paper)

Very clear, organized, and helpful lectures. I always looked forward to attending this class. She does talk fast, so using a laptop to take notes is necessary. Tests are straightforward and not hard if you keep up with lecture. Readings at the beginning of the semester are a bit dense but are important for the first midterm.

She doesn't use technologically enhanced methods for lecture, yet the class could not be more clear and structured. She commands attention and explicitly highlights important information. She is also kind of funny. She knows what she's doing. Reading is a little much, but your GSI should help you sort it out.

Professor Gurowitz is an AWESOME professor. She does talk fast, but if you pay attention, you won't miss anything. Her lectures are very interesting, and her exams are practical. Also, I was lucky that I had a very good gsi (Ryan Phillips).
Good professor, interesting material if you like politics. Many found this class challenging. Bottom line for me: attending lecture is key to getting an A.

Mrs. Gurowitz is very a great lecturer. She does not use power point and does talk fast, but she will not mind repeating herself. She is very approachable, I do not know what that guy was talking about. The reading is intense but very interesting and you learn a lot. I wish I could take it again.

Professor Gurowitz is very knowledgable in her field so you should listen to what she says.  Her lectures go quickly and are packed with material, but she doesnt go over readings very much, so go to section.  The class is a bit tough, but I got a B+ and didnt do a single reading. thake this class!  1 paper and in class midterm and final.

I found this professor very fair.  Yes, she goes over alot of material during lectures, but you will do alright if you are a fast typer and bring a laptop, very efficient at notetaking, or bring a recorder.  Otherwise, not too much work, and guaranteed A if you put some work into the class

Very organized, precise lectures. However, she covers way too much material too fast; it's too much/too fast to follow. There is too much reading that is not fully discussed in class. No helpful exam preparation.

Professor knows her subject area well and can articulate concepts with precision. She's very unapproachable in office hours (if you're a guy at least). Professor tends to shoot down your ideas with a condescending attitude and answers your questions with a high and mighty demeanor. To be honest, she's very overbearing with her personal ideologies.

This class was far too broad, even for an intro class. I felt that the class was far too heavy on the reading, and the reading was never discussed in class. Gurowitz also never gives you any exam preparation ther than telling students to study everything and if you do all of the reading there is quite a lot of material. I spent my entire semester o

She's interesting, and is prolly the only professor who can keep me awake at 9am. But really, this lady drinks too much coffee and her lectures cover so much, that she speaks so quickly over important concepts and has little regard for her poor students trying to take notes. If you can tolerate fast paced lectures, take her.

Professor Gurowitz is very clear and concise - her lectures are extremely well organized. The course covers a lot of topics, and is well structured. She does speak quite fast, so many students find it easier to type rather than to write. The grades are quite difficult, but not too bad, depending on the GSI
Interesting class and great teacher.  Very clear lecture.  I highly recommend this class.

she's definitely a good lecturer, who knows how to keep a class engaged at 9am. Had 1 take home and 1 in class midterm, with an annotated bibliography assignment. One drawback is that she talks wayy too fast and its sometimes hard to keep up, but overall, she's good.

Have to agree with the unapproachable kind of arrogant comment, but you can tell she knows what she is talking about. Very structured lectures easy to follow, talks really fast, fairly interesting but makes you do some useless papers on the readings, that was annoying.
No Comments

I'd like to debunk the myth that she's hot. She was all right at best. But past that her lectures were well structured on the whole, much better than when she let the GSIs lecture. The class was a bit ho hum on the whole. Didn't help me want to be a Poli Sci major.
Very clear, very concise.  Awesome.  Definitely will take another class with her.

Ok class, especially as an introduction to IR.  I went to see her for office hours and she wasn't very approachable.  It is interesting and her teaching methods are good.  She's a little arrogant and actually I didn't think she was all that hot.
A difficult course and hard grade.
s s s sexy is she intelligent and a fantastic lecturerer loved the class and like many before me I have a major crush on this teacher.

great lecturer. very knowledgeable. The material is dense and she doesn't use many visual aids, but for those students interested in politics she gives a refreshing perspective and teaches an extremely interesting and engaging class. Sometimes she's a little hard to approach but she has a lot to offer and I'll be taking more of her classes.
Not only is she hot, but she is really entertaining I would recomend this class for people who are serious about political science.

Very prepared lecturer, but the lack of visual aids and dense historical data makes the class a bit boring, though you'll never have a second to stare off into space because she talks a mile a minute. She's very nice, but isn't the type to tolerate students that fall behind. Take this class if you have a genuine interest and work hard.
great professor
Great lady, intereting course, not too difficult, she clearly explains important keys in the course.

I understood her class. Her teaching style was great. The best book I read in college came from her class. The book was about the Ruwanda genocide. This book is not the most up-lifting book but it was real. I worked hard and did well. I was never bored unlike other political science classes at cal.
No Comments

Fantastic topic presented in a horrible manner. Material is regurgitated from assigned readings. The only reason you would ever have to show up for class is to take the ridiculous pop quizes that may or may not happen on any given day.
No Comments

Immigration and Citizenship class... she definitely knows what she is talking about and is interesting to listen to.  NOTE: she is the fastest speaker in the world so I suggest sharing notes with friends because you will miss half her lecture.  Grading is harsh.

A painful, painful speaking voice. Enough to make you want to drop the class. I did stay however. The topic is fascinating and she covers a vast amount of ground. Her surprise tests were a nuisance and bad for my nerves, personally. Yes, grading is tough.

she is very concerned with grade inflation and thus makes all her gsis grade harshly, do believe she is a good lecturer, and her exams arent that difficult but it really all depends on your gsi..and the amount of A's he or she gives on the first midterm

No don't do it she was my worst professor by far.  She is unhelpful and talks incredibly fast.  She really knows how to make a great subject dull as hell. Oh and did I mention her high pitched nasal sounding voice is too piercing for words.  Ugh..never again with this woman I am telling you.
very witty woman.  she's a great orator and very down to earth.  i recommend taking any class she teaches - whether in the PACS or Poli Sci dep.
amazing orator, loved every lecture.  GSIs for my semester were the best i've ever seen, so all in all it was one of the best classes i've taken.

I didn't think too highly of her. She lectures very well, but her voice is sort of piercing, not a good thing at 930AM. She had pop quizzes in lecture which did not follow the reading. Furthermore, the GSI was unorganized and students used bully tactics. She lectures on theory but it isn't theory.
Gurowitz makes her GSIs grade really hard.  She has very high standards.

Witty, realistic and sensitive to the need of her students.  No surprises here; take good notes and seek help.  She may seem a little harsh, but I think it's only mild cynicism manifested in sarcastic bites.  Teaches in fields you may THINK you know about but really opens them up.

Political Science is not a "science" It is a insult to call it a a "science.  It should be renamed "Politics" or Polital Studies" The true sciences are the Natural Sciences. It's all basically BS session about "politics&
exams are sort of hard, but she is a wonderful teacher. also, very witty.
No Comments
No Comments

Alex is so underrated. Definitely take him if you are really into math; if he hadnt been my GSI I probably would not be a math major. His questions are tough, but he is always available at office hours if you need help, and very willing to offer help. Hes a very nice guy abd dedicated to mentoring as well.
Very difficult class, and homework problems may take hours to complete if you want a thorough understanding.
I am taking this class in the future but I predict it to be hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I took this class for P/NP and for no reason other than to feel more prepared for a calc course at Cal. I understand he moves extremely fast to get through loads of material, but he always seemed bothered when people asked questions since he always glossed over things. And turns out this class was harder than the calc course I took next semester.

really good at explaining material and very willing to help in office hours. Alex is definitely not for the faint of heart but exceptional for truly understanding math. Prepares you well for future math classes.

I took this class to prepare me for calculus, but it confused me even more. He did not do a good job of teaching and almost always seemed to be in a rush or nervous. He blamed the students' lack of studying for not doing well on the midterms - the practice midterms he gave out were nothing like what was on the actual midterm.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Teaches in the most confusing way possible. OH are no help.
Dry lectures. Very boring. Homework doesn't relate to lectures at all. Teaches in the most confusing way possible.

Extremely hard midterms and final. Impossible to even study for. Do not take this class if you don't have to. He overcomplicates simple things like the area of a normal right triangle. Write his "g" like "9" and vice versa. Worksheets are impossible and often are the same level as his exams. Little communication with his GSIs. Although a nice curve

Don't take this class unless you absolutely have to. I would have been better off going right to Calculus. Thought I'd take Pre-Calc as a refresher course, huge mistake. Alex means well but really overcomplicates the material. The midterms are never what we learned in class and the class average floats around a 40% until he curves the grades.

I think Alex had really good intentions and tried to do his best but the course was awful.  The class was 1000x harder than the previous PreCalculus class I had taken.  I felt that I did better on the homework by teaching myself but this got really hard toward the end of the class.  The tests were brutal.

Appleton taught Math 32 (College Precalculus) and made this course 200 times harder than it needed to be. My friends in Calculus couldn't even complete the difficulty of problems he assigned. The curves in the class were so heavy that a 50% turned out to be a B-. Nobody could pass the tests, he was terrible at lecturing, honestly try to stay away.
I didn't think that the professor was that bad.. lectures can be VERY long and confusing at times.. but adjunct and office hours helped. The class is smooth sailing until you get to trig!
Horrible professor, you can't understand what he is saying due to his heavy accent. Wouldn't recommend to take this course if you have no previous knowledge with Trig or Pr-calculus.
Beware, the content on the practice midterms and finals will NOT be on the actual test.

I've taken Nanda's class the past 2 summers to fulfill my reqs, I love her. She is a relatively easy grader, offers any support 24/7 as long as you reach out, but has a thick accent and bad mic quality. She's very caring and genuinely wants to help as much as possible, and is passionate about her work! Better than semester professors.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Nanda is amazing! She cares for her students and is very supportive and accessible even though it was an online course. Grading criteria was a little unclear; she has rubrics but doesn't give super constructive critiques. LOTS of reading and writing. But easy class as long as you don't fall behind (easy to if you do it online, so don't).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She has quite unclear grading criteria and does not communicate exactly what she wants from you so the paper grade ends up reflecting that. It is annoying because I worked hard on the papers I wrote only for her to mark them down. This class needs to be more organized in general.

Professor Apara was such a sweet and loving teacher. However, the number of student presentations that were given took away from the experience as it severely limited the about of time we had to learn from her.

Professor Apara was always cheerful and enthusiastic to see my class after a long day. She answers emails within 10 minutes and is very accessible and lenient if you need help. Honestly, the only downside was that I wanted to be challenged to improve my writing and I didn't feel so, but if you want an easy A for a Breadth I recommend her!

She is a wonderful professor. She is hilarious and super passionate about what she teaches. She gives great feedback and is willing to help her students. The in-class discussions are very helpful and also very fun. You can greatly tell she cares about her students.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Prof. Nanda was probably the easiest teacher i have had at berkeley. She is helpful, caring and fun when you engage and ask questions. You must take the time to get to know her to get on her good side. As long as you read the three books she assigns and engage in her 1 hour lecture, youll be fine. Easy course.

Definately one of my favorite professors.  She has a true passion for her students and the courses that she teaches.  In addition to being extremely passionate about her students, she was also very insightful and had a clear grasp on the books she was teaching.

I absolutely LOVED Professor Nanda! English had never been my favorite subject in high school, but she totally changed that. My essay writing improved so much and the reading was actually interesting. She goes over much of the text in class so if the  reading doesn't make sense, don't sweat it.

She is so nice! This professor just wants everyone to be happy in her class. We had to read three novels, write three essays, write two film responses, and write one research paper. It wasn't that much work. She rarely gives negative feedback in class, though, so sometimes it's difficult to understand what she wants. Great professor overall!
She's a Great Professor. I loved her class and her. You can't help but like her classes and get involved in the material. She makes it so captivating!

She is one of the most fun english professors I have ever had. It is obvious that she loves teaching and bringing her students to understanding the texts we read. She cares about her students, is supportive, and can get anyone excited about english. She doesn't give to much reading and if you do your part you can do well.

Nice lady, TERRIBLE teacher. She never explains what she wants from students, and never gives feedback, even if you ask her for it directly. Grades are definitely arbitrary, but that could work to your advantage. Speak up/suck up to her in class and you will probably do OK. Hard to get an A, but really easy to get a B or C.
very unclear on requirements and due dates, but you gotta love that accent. Grades are sometimes arbitrary. The class is really more of an African-American/minority studies class.

You could go through this entire class by writing essays an hour before they're due, reading online sources. Her "comments" on drafts are non-existent, and she changed our final research paper requirements a dozen times, making the project impossible and infuriating. It's an easy A, and she really cares about her students, but so not worth it.
she's cool

Professor Nanda is the nicest professor at Cal. I took her during the summer, and she gave us Fridays off. Read books that we read in HS (eg Things Fall Apart by Chinua Achebe). Just say anything in class and she'll love you. You get to rewrite all but your final paper, so even f you get a low score, you can improve. I got an A in the class.

nice teacher, but never gives you good feedback on essays. there seems to be no definite grade formula because you turn in two out of four papers at the end of the class, so you don't even know how you did on those, and it doesn't seem like she even reads them from the lack of comments when i got mine back. suck up and you'll get a good grade.

She was so nice, but not helpful. If I have to hear "interpolate your response" or "trope" again, it will be too soon. She was super repetive and never answered my questions. I previously thought of myself as an "English" person, but she hated my style and gave me a low grade.

She is very friendly and caring about students. The only thing I didn't like about the class is that papers were all graded by the GSI, who didn't really tell us how to improve our writing style and the grade we got.

She's so cute! She's really helpful and really funny. She makes sure that you pay attention in class which can be helpful late in the afternoon. As long as you follow her fomula for papers, you should be fine. Plus, you're allowed to revise two out of four of them. The only problem is the research paper at the end. it didn't seem to have a purpose.
Definitely one of the nicest profs i've had since i've been here. She's always in a good mood and smiling. As long as you go to class and do the work you'll be fine.

Love this lady! Highly recommend to take during the summer. I am a science person who doesn't like to write at all. I am not good at it. Like everyone has said she cares about your interpretation of the text and you as a student. Just 3 books. Lectures never boring. She is fun. Listen to what she suggests to fix your rough drafts. Easy A class.

I love Nanda!  She is very nice and truly cares about her students.  Go to her for any help you need she will be sure to take care of you.  She is not an English teacher that forces you to agree with her, she is actually the opposite.  As long as you can support your opinions she will love you.  Highly recommended.
disorganized. i dont think the class followed university curriculum

Always concerned about her students, she is always in a good mood and ready to help everyone and anyone. Probably the nicest woman I've ever met. And even though she loves to have her students return, she is always open to new faces.

She is very dedicated to her teaching, it is clear that she loves the subject and intends on helping the students in every possible ways.  As long as you try hard and show her your efforts, you should do ok
really nice lecturer- truly cares about the students and really funny.. i loved her accent.. picks interesting reading too
Great, great, great!!!
No Comments
Prof. Nanda is reaaaally enthusiastic about teaching.. it's so obvious how much she loves her profession! She's pretty lenient, and always ready to explain anything that anyone finds unclear.

incredibly torturous and boring. prof never entered a single grade into the grade book. the lectures suck, you have to turn in notes for hw. generally a very easy class that you can coast through. but jesus christ
Seems like a great person but is genuinely one of the worst lecturers I have ever met. Class was easy though, and there were a lot of guest lecturers which made it bearable.

Very friendly professor who almost never gives harsh comments. Soft voice may make you fall asleep in a warm afternoon. Well-experienced in her area of knowledge. Please be sure to read the materials before coming to class so that she won't be embarrased when no one answers the reading questions.

While participation is optional you should show up to class! Professor Reaver is an excellent professor who is very well versed in her field. She is approachable and willing to work with you if you find yourself struggling. Definitely have to study for the exams and understand the content but the best thing you can do is just show up to class.

Professor Reaver is nothing short of fantastic! She is down to earth, matter-of-fact, and knowledgable and that really shows in her lectures. Expectations for the class were very clear: three assignments, two midterms, a final, and discussion attendance. This class really got me thinking more about my health and food choices. Highly recommend!

2 quizzes, 1 written assignment and 1 group brochure project. Grading is very generous, despite attendance being optional I suggest attending because it helps a lot with quiz material and it's also just really interesting content that can be applicable to life. Highly recommend!

Prof. Reaver is kind, passionate and interesting. You need to take her class seriously, but it is totally doable if you try. I found it pretty easy. Her assignments are very reasonable in quantity and easy to do. I really liked her lecture content as well!

She's a nice person, but the lectures are really dense. The class has way more chemistry than I was expecting. There's no discussion section, worksheets, or assignments, so it's hard to know what's important. And it's almost all memorization. We're only graded by 3 exams, 1 final, 1 project. Would have preferred more assignments to help the grade.
Great class to take if you need upper div units. 4 assignments in the whole class and they were graded very nicely. she is very nice
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Incredibly knowledgeable and a great lecturer. My only complaint is that the course is packed with SO much detailed information so lectures feel like an overload and it's difficult to predict exactly what you will need to know for tests. However, everything is graded *extremely* generously; there's really no reason to get less than an A+.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: really nice and easy to listen to. 2 tests, 1 paper, and a final project.

When I took this course in Fall 2023, Prof. Reaver only taught one lecture in the entire course. (Most of the lectures were taught by Prof Hellerstein). Regardless, she was a very enthusiastic speaker and answered student questions well. My only potential complaint would be that she talks a little fast, creating a bit of an information overload.

Professor Reaver is definitely knowledgeable in her field. However, it's extremely challenging for an introductory course. There are too many slides and 6 hours of lecture + 1 hour of discussion each week (for a 3 unit course!). Questions are structured to be very cumulative and require that you know the minuscule details. Don't take this!

Quiz questions are things you can't find on textbook or in class lectures. I don't understand why she got to test people on details when it is only a lower division class, meant to be an introductory but she is making it really hard to pass.
She is a very kind and understanding professor. She tries everything to lift the pressure off everyone's shoulders during difficult times.

Professor Shole is a fantastic teacher who makes learning fun and practical. He teaches in a way that helps us understand how things work in real life. She talked to us like friends, asking us questions and listening to our ideas. We learn from each other and celebrate our differences. She inspires us to think for ourselves and discover new things.

Sholeh is a lovely artist who feels very deeply in her work. She does have a tendency to ramble, but our class was discussion heavy and everyone who wanted their voice heard did. I felt very affirmed in my own art practice, and more informed about the global happenings of the world after taking this course. Thanks Sholeh!

Okay lectures, but he talks WAY too fast and tends to get distracted easily. Heavily dependent on readings (the course is basically just a summary of readings), and the content is way more political theory than actual American politics. Participation and attendance are mandatory, and prompts for the midterms and final are released beforehand.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: His teaching style isn't for everyone. His slides are essentially word vomit, and he speaks incredibly fast in a loud monotone voice. He often goes on tangents and presents disconnected thoughts, which makes it difficult to follow a main point. The exams are quite easy, as although he presents his standards as very high, they are really reasonable.

Prof Ashcroft is one of the greats in the ps dept. Exams are intimidating because they require a LOT of prep work. Skim readings, attend lecture and review sessions & ur good. Has a witty & deadpan sense of humor, delivers great lectures, puts much thought and effort into teaching and is super helpful in OH. Challenging but super worth it

Extremely rude and condescending. Genuinely not sure what his problem is. Had him during the summer as a required class for an internship program. Perhaps he felt personally hurt because we weren't taking his class as seriously as he wanted, but realistically, why would we? Very unprofessional in his conduct yet will accuse you of being so.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Great lectures, get ready for British humor and for him to go on random tangents. Midterms are easy, given questions beforehand so do the readings and you'll get a good grade. One of the best professors I have had at Cal.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: the class is dependent solely on the readings, but he gives the questions & exactly what he wants from you for the midterm/final/group project ahead of time so it's easy to prepare. much more conceptual than anticipated & expected for an american politics class, make use of your GSI & discussion section for support!
dont bother asking the professor for extra office hours because he will tell you that it is "beyond the duties" of his contract to offer extra help to struggling students.

Weekly Readings and you discuss them during lecture/discussion (open discussion style). Attendance taken with polleverywhere. You have 2 midterms and final and he gives you all the questions in advance. There was barely any assignments (just one precis, SUPER EASY), and a final podcast group project. As long as you put effort you'll do just fine.

Global 110E is literally just about the EU, and not much else. He is funny, but speaks pretty fast and just yaps. You do have to show up and try to participate in the discussions or do the discussion posts. For the midterms and finals, make sure to do the readings and prepare your answers as he provides you questions beforehand.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I'll be honest: this course is challenging, but Dr. Ashcroft is a fantastic professor with great British humor. This course focuses on political theory regarding American democracy and identity, which was often intriguing to think about. Plus, he introduced us to Jaffa Cakes, a delightful British delicacy! Overall, it was a fun and engaging class.

First half of the course was interesting, second half was filled with boring lectures that dont give any insight into the course material. Spends way too long talking about chatgpt despite no one being able to use it in the course since the tests are in person. Finally, has everyone do a group project during RRR week on top of an in person final.
very heavy lecture slides
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I enjoyed PE 100 with Ashcroft a lot. He's a very practical professor. There were no assignments other than the midterms and final exam and they were reasonable. He can talk fast at times, but is very receptive to feedback. Very flexible policies. If every class was this well structured, I'd cruise through Cal. His sense of humor is also great.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very cool guy with British humor. Worked through a lot of topics related to political economy, good surface-level survey of the field. He's very flexible with things but always presented topics in a balanced approach. Has a lot of opinions but he welcomes a debate which I think is actually more productive to learning. 100% recommend.

Ashcroft is honestly a good lecturer, but be prepared for a LOT OF READING from the textbook and supplemental readings. Exams are majority of grade so study accordingly. Lectures are recorded, which meant attendance declined thru the semester but he ended up giving an incentive to encourage attendance/participation which helped my grade in the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Ashcroft mixes in just the right amount of snarky comments into his lectures to make them funny any interesting to listen to. He frames information well and is clear about what will be on tests and what is expected of students. He does talk super fast though, the class has a lot of readings, and exams are 75% of your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Lectures mainly help the readings, which there were a lot of. Participation and attendance is only necessary in your discussion. if you are having difficulty in understanding the readings then go to the lectures in order to get a better explanation of its interpreted. Not much to grade so focus on ur 2 midterms/ final. not the papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Participation in discussion matters. Professor is really funny in class. Office hours is helpful. He goes through slides really fast in lecture. Information is pretty organized. Typically the highest grade on assignments is around 94-96 (doesn't really distribute A+s).
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Lectures are very information-packed and could get very easily overwhelming, but the course content isn't too difficult and is quite interesting. The professor is informative and helpful, and so are the GSI's — though they do grade very strictly.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: It is important to attend/watch the lectures because it may be difficult to keep up with all the material if you just rely on the slides. A lot of readings but many are interesting & easy to understand. Nothing is curved & overall grade relies on exam grades + participation. Grading from GSI's can be harsh. Overall interesting & valuable class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
I generally enjoyed Ashcroft! His witty british humor and outside perspective on US history is fresh and interesting. My main complaint would be that the lectures often regurgitate the readings, making them a bit dull. 
Most of the class grade is from exams, but they're not bad at all if you know at least half the terms and defs.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof is funny and self-deprecating, speaks fast at times so review lectures. Comprehensive intro to american politics, not just repetition of AP Gov. Very detailed/structured slides, lots of interesting readings. Do them promptly because you will fall behind. Get textbook for free online. Review slides before midterm/final. GSI matters for grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: This class is easier if you have background with APUSH, APHG, or AP Gov. His lectures can be blink and you miss it, but thats remedied since you can always watch the recordings after. My only complaint is that grade is dependent on very few assignments, that being two papers and exams. It isn't horrid, but with harsh grading, it's a bit stressful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: As a political science major, I found this class very interesting and insightful. Professor Ashcroft does an amazing job connecting overarching module themes and hilighting underlying concepts from the readings within lecture. Midterms/Final aren't difficult as long as you follow the assigned readings and attend/follow along with the lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures are pretty helpful. Readings can be quite basic, potentially could be substituted by a solid (SOLID) background in political theory and history. Midterms were somewhat tight for time, but overall very doable. Final was easier.

Professor Ashcraft is super knowledgeable of political theory and the course heavily revolves around it. If you took APUSH and/or AP Gov, you'll do fine in the class. Exams are pretty easy and there is (technically) no homework other than readings. He does ramble in lectures and it gets hard to hear him, so be prepared for that.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Besides being funny having a British guy teach American politics, he provides good insights with his outsider perspective. Lots of brute force memorization, but there's a logic to everything, and he makes it pretty clear which readings are actually important. Lectures can be him just reading off slides but talking to him one-on-one was helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Good spirited guy. Been teaching the class for a while and knows what he's doing. Although you're allowed to argue your own opinion, the class is mostly taught from left-leaning perspectives (especially Unit 4) and the professor would never hesitate to share his. If you were a centrist beforehand, you're likely to leave class hating the right.

Lots of reading especially during summer sessions. Be ready to participate. Clear instructions on midterm and final so if you read, participate, and write well you should be fine. The professor may seem intimidating at first but is really nice and helps you understand the complex readings he assigns.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: get ready to read especially in the summer session
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great lecturer, hilarious and engages well with the readings (there are a LOT). You have to spend a lot of time prepping for midterms/exams though, but it forces you to think critically. Super helpful professor for developing your own political thought processes, just wish exams weren't so high stakes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I've taken a couple classes by Dr. Ashcroft and I really enjoy his sense of humor and his jolly atmosphere. You can usually skim the readings, his lectures are some of the best I have seen, he has a good sense of humor, and I have enjoyed his class. The workload isn't crazy, just ask him what he's looking for in exams and you'll get a good grade.

Lecture attendance is mandatory and be prepared to participate and discuss the readings during lectures. The bulk of the grades are split between 2 midterms, a final, and a group project. Class places heavy emphasis on political theory.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: My semester with him was good all in all. While he may not be the best lecturer which I have had and he sometimes tends to mumble as he alludes to it in class, the content of the course is very well organized. He is also extremely keen to make students have the best experience with him. The grading is very clear and it is easy to get a good grade.

Professor Ashcroft is highly knowledgeable and a great professor. His course (especially in summer) is reading-heavy and fast paced. My biggest recommendation is actively participating in lecture, and attend class every day (the points help come final grade). While the class is chock full of info, the class is entertaining and interesting.
