reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: His tendency to talk quickly combined with his British accent made it hard to hear/understand everything he was saying, but Ashcroft is otherwise an awesome prof. He's extremely understanding, accommodating, & funny! If you understand the lectures/readings, you're fine. Although not a polisci major, I still enjoyed the course!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor, engaging lecturer. Loved his witty comments and lecture was easy to follow along with. Papers and exams were not difficult if you attended lecture & did the readings. Very accommodating with deadlines and hardships. He speaks quickly so be prepared to take good notes. Overall good prof for an intro to polisci course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The guy is absolutely great. He's funny and  informative and very knowledgeable. However, your grade is based on Midterm, Final+participation. I got horribly sick the entire month before deadweek, missed a few days. I literally needed 0.2 points to get an A-. He refused to round it up. I guess the lesson here is: Be very healthy+Be an Extrovert.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Mumbles horribly and constantly trails off quietly at the end of his sentences while lecturing.

He was EXTREMELY helpful and accommodating during the GSI strike and moved exams online/made himself available to help students that weren't receiving GSI help. He is funny and very understanding. He also has a great British accent. Our exams were difficult and closed-note/in-person. Read, attend lecture, and study super hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Ashcroft is a great professor but it can be hard to understand his lectures due to his British accent. It is difficult to keep up with how fast he talks during lectures so I recommend writing down what he is saying and later go back and take notes on the slides. The grade for his class is based on a few assignments so they are crucial.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Warm and funny prof, understanding of special circumstances. Lectures are interesting and well-structured. Do the non-textbook readings and write small summaries if you need them. Talks pretty fast-- which is no issue for recorded lectures, but I liked annotating the slides live and then typing up more complete notes afterwards. Great class!

Class is graded through a midterm, a final, a short paper (1-2 pages), and a larger paper (6-8 pages). Professor Ashcroft is great, he's funny, informative, and his lectures are fun to attend. He can talk a little fast, but he publishes all the lecture materials online so it's easy to follow. Very accessible outside of class!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Ashcroft is an incredible professor that goes above and beyond to accommodate for almost any event, made the required course readings easier after reviewing the schedule himself, and allowed for great conversation in the classroom. Lectures, though based on sometimes difficult texts, were incredibly informative and helpful with readings.
He is a nice guy, and has moved due dates to accommodate, however, the content is very heavy and while he is nice his lectures are impossible to fully grasp bc he talks insanely fast.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Ashcroft is a good lecturer and is never shy to input his British humor in lectures. He talks pretty quick sometimes, but his slides are informative. The final is worth 50% of your grade, so your grade mostly comes down to how well you know the material and how the TA interprets your paper, which kind of gives a gray area. An okay class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Grade based on how TAs grades your midterm (35%) and final (50%!). Prof Ashcroft "standardizes" grades, but it was still unfair because some TAs seemed to be more lenient than others (some scored 100 while the mean was 80). He was accommodating but lectures were frustrating because he mumbles and talks fast. He is knowledgeable and you do learn ig?

I'm in POL 1 right now and this class is so hard. It relies super heavily on your final paper (50%)!!! and relies only on two other things, your section grade and midterm grade. Also, the class is super content heavy and the professor speaks very very fast which doesn't make it easier. If you take this class I wish you luck

Professor Ashcroft is very knowledgeable about the subject matter but made POL 1 a more difficult class than some of my upper-division POL classes. He consistently goes over the allotted lecture time by almost 20-30 minutes, while also speeding through the material. Attendance/ participation is also mandatory. :(
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Richard is truly passionate and inspiring. You can tell he cares about his students and what he teaches. A great course if you don't mind reading. Only comment: tends to make connections and talk very fast, he also mumbles a bit. It can be hard to follow at times. But his door is always open if you need help understanding the material.

Prof Ashcroft was really kind during the pandemic, he adapted the course to benefit students with their at-home learning. I found that he is a harsh grader, because he will deduct a few points sometimes but does not always specify why and how to improve, which can be the difference between an A and an A-. He was accessible and was quite funny.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Ashcroft is very understanding of people's lives and the zoom burnout we have been going through. He split the weekly lecture into synchronous and a recorded lecture. Dates and assignments were all dated to when to turn them in and were not too much. He summarises the articles given to read. Just keep up with the course and you'll do good.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: Prof. Ashcroft is a great lecturer imo, if you like dry British humor you'll love it. Lots of readings but you don't have to do all of them, just need a good understanding of the thinkers you discuss. Grading is super tough but it depends on your GSI, mine sucked. Highly recommend going to office hours throughout the semester to improve.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Wasn't a bad experience, but class was heavy reading and lots of writing. Lectures were somewhat confusing. Would recommend to only read the relevant stuff for the discussion posts and response papers. All else is filler. The grading for this class is also extremely tough. Provides a general rubric for the assignments, but could be more specific.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Class itself was taken online during pandemic. Wasn't a bad experience, but class has heavy reading, load of papers, and many weekly discussions. Would recommend to only read the relevant stuff for the discussion posts and response papers. All else is filler. The grading for this class is also extremely tough and grading criteria is unclear.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I loved this guy/class. GREAT lecturer, but goes off on tangents when a student sidetracks him, but there is (usually) a point. The material is dense/difficult. The papers are graded fairly but harshly. There is no hand holding. You're probably not getting an A. But its one of the best classes I've taken! NO TESTS, graded only on a few short papers
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: While knowledgeable on multiculturalism, Prof. Ashcroft would ramble and could not concisely relay info in lectures, which were dense and lackluster. We'd often run 1-2 lectures behind. There are five papers (incrementally weighted) and attendance is mandatory. Reading, while "required," could be done on concepts you plan to write on. GSI saved me!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: He is knowledgeable about the topic of multiculturalism and you will do well in the class if you make use of his office hours. He can literally sit down with you for an hour to answer your questions about the papers. However, the class is hard and is a lot of work. Also the papers are graded very harshly. Avoid if you want an easy theory class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: Prof Ashcroft's lectures are clear/easy to follow, but they are often just repeating the readings. He has a good, British sense of humor but tends to mumble a lot, so sit near the front if possible. It's pretty easy to get an A -- especially because he posts the (very helpful!) slides online.

I am very disappointed. Having taken this class during the election, I was super excited to learn about American politics as a whole. Yet Prof. Ashcroft was not particularly inspiring, has a tendency to mumble a few words under his breath and relies too much on slides. The one review session where technology failed and he improvised, he was great!

While I attended every lecture and read all of the assigned material, I think the lectures were not very original and basically summarized the readings. If you put in all the work you will achieve a comprehensive understanding of the topic, but you can pass without doing so. I will say, excellent British accent and rather funny sardonic humor.

He is a good professor and gives a very clear idea of what will be on the midterm and final. Go to the review sessions that are very helpful. When I went to office hours, he was very helpful and explained concepts clearly. If you get David as a GSI, switch asap as he ruined the quality of the class.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: Lectures are extremely helpful. Midterm and final are fair and reasonable. Review sessions before the midterm/final help guide your study time! Great class and knowledgeable professor.
Really enjoyed his sharp wit and British sense of humor. A really enjoyable class in my opinion.

Easily one of the best GSIs in  Berkeley. Very well structured sections, sent out questions we were going to address in advance. Extremely helpful in his OH, held extra OH the whole last week of class!!! Very friendly, very knowledgeable, funny and super helpful, cheerful GSI!
No Comments

He was a nice guy, but his lectures are vague and abstract. There was very little of what I could take away from  the disorganized lectures. His essay feedback weren't the best. I had him during the GSI strike semester, and they let me P/NP for my minor. Wouldn't recommend. (I think I would've earned a B, but there's no way of knowing now).

I'm not sure how to feel about this class. Kind professor who is very smart and is a good guy. Class was frustrating and disorganized. It is fun if you understand, but the professor doesn't make it clear what you need to do well. If you have to take it, you'll survive. I have a lot of mixed feelings.

His lecture is abstract and disorganized. He is not a tough guy, but I study almost by myself. It is really hard to focus on and listen to his lecture since he wants to focus on to many points, his lecture then become boring and disorganized. He always hurries to leave in his office hour, and this is my worst experience of office hour at Berkeley.

Very knowledgeable, but maybe too much to the point where he rambles on about material that he is not going to test us on and does not clarify that. Focuses too much on topics not pertaining to the course and does not emphasize test/paper topics enough. Also, incredibly disorganized and his lectures are all over the place.

I don't understand the bad reviews. Yes, his lectures are a little disorganized, but he is a really nice, reasonable guy and truly wants students to do well. Class is definitely abstract, but if you care, you will do well. Definitely one of the most reasonable and kind professors I have had so far.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very intelligent, but his lecture style is nearly incomprehensible. He talks for an hour and a half straight without using any visual aids or notes. There's no textbook or lesson plan for the semester. Always runs out after class. Readings are heavy and difficult. He's a nice enough guy, but this class was so draining.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The lecture was so boring, most of the class you could be doing something else and it always feel like a waste of time. You need to be interested in the topic, do all the reading, and take notes to do well in this class. The essay and quiz are pretty much just interpretations but the grading is pretty lenient.

Once you get it, nothing is hard, I will agree with Professor Ashmore. though this class required readings and lots of unit tests, which indeed force you to study. It's a good idea to go to his office hours and discuss anything you don't understand. It is truly a gift for me to understand traditional Chinese culture.
I should not take this class. No caring or patience.
Boring class and tough grader. Never will suggest anyone taking this course again. REALLY HARSH compared to other professors in same department.
Don't take this class
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: I've had three classes with him: Chinese 155, 110A, and 110B. A lot of students take his classes thinking they are going to be easy As. Guess what? They're not and that is ok! If you learn and respect the material, it is an easy A, if you don't show up or disrespect the material, you fail, simple. Truly a knowledgeable and funny guy, no regrets!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He doesn't care about students at all, I mean at all. He never responded to my emails, and whenever I try to talk to him before or after class, he just says he doesn't have time and just walks away. Also, he is often not there for his office hours. He does not allow us to use pdf textbooks, so everyone has to purchase their own expensive textbooks.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This class is hard. Professor Ashmore indeed doesn't have slides and you have to take notes from his speech. He will not spoon feed you information. He will give you just enough guidance for you to read and figure stuff on your own. You will have to do the readings on time and more than once, and think critically.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Hard grader, attendance in class is necessary. If he doesn't like you, you rae likely to get a low score even if you got correct answers.
Don't let this guy ruin your college life. He shows no caring to students.
very sweet, knowledgeable far outside his subject field.

This is actually only slightly harder than 110A, as the texts get longer and more complicated. As far as teaching/learning Classical Chinese from him, he's still awesome. Very knowledgeable and actively makes sure you understand how to parse the text.

You can tell he's very passionate and knowledgeable about Classical Chinese. When I sat in the first day I knew I had to take this course. He's very talkative but he stays on topic and is very easy to approach in and out of class. The work is only hard if you don't put effort into it. Hopefully I'll be able to take 110B.

Hard grader, attendance in class is necessary. Must do a lot of work for this class to be able to get a good grade, especially essays. Lots of readings and lectures and discussions are mainly regarded to the readings you must do every few days. To succeed, attend lectures and office hours regularly and be prepared for the readings.

I really really like Professor Ashmore. He sometimes spends too much time explaining basic concepts in Literary Chinese, but you can tell that he is genuinely interested and wants everybody to do well. He is super genuine, and I feel like he is a fair grader. Take this class with him if you can!

Don't expect any clarity out of this one-he starts topics without finishing them, focuses a lot of time on irrelevant topics, and, while he talks ALOT and sounds good, he actually says very little. He knows his stuff, but I feel that that he's so into his academic world that it's hard for him to relate to students or clearly express his thoughts.
He knows a lot and very approachable.  Material may be hard, but it is worthy.
Very engaged and knowledgeable.  But he knows so much that he gets frustrated with beginners, and his reactions can be arbitrarily harsh. Assignments are very poorly explained.

He has the tendency to start a topic and without even finishing it, move on to the next.  Yet he really tries.  Although he doesn't teach too well, he is really kind.  Just keep up with the class and be able to translate when he calls on you.  By doing so he'll have a good impression of you and will be more lenient on you when giving out grades.

If you are a non-native speaker of Chinese, then this class will not be easy. A lot of the course you spend time translating, and people who grew up reading this stuff will have a clear advantage. He's also not clear about what or how he wants you write.

This man is an amazing reservoir of Chinese history and literary knowledge.  His glib of speech never fails to impress.  I love him!  He does not explain essay writing too well and expects you to cut the crap before your write it.  Also, you have to be pretty interested in the material to do well.
What the hell does "imaginative" mean when he uses it?  It's kind of unclear, confusing, frusterating.  You have to be really interested in the literature aspect to enjoy this class.
I loved this class.  Prof. Ashmore really has an extensive knowledge of Chinese literature and he was always so lively.

I loved Prof. Ashmore! Not only does he have vast knowledge of Chinese Lit & Language, the guy's got great jokes, can talk about Sesame Street and Classical Chinese Grammar in a single sentence, is incredibly approchable, does great squash moves in class.

He is my least favored professor. His class is ok, sometimes boring. He is not very clear, when I was in his Chinese2B class, we enjoyed the TA (David) better, since David explained things more clearly.

Took his time going through lecture slides to ensure all students understood concepts and was always open to questions. Homework could be challenging but was doable, and all exams were fair. Weekly bCourses quiz that was kind of easy to forget about. Asta was always willing to talk after class about the course or other engineering-related things.

Out of town a lot, so we had two professors for this class. I liked Asta's lectures a lot more, and I wish he taught us more and wasn't out of town so often, but I get it he's very busy. In terms of the class itself, the GSI is pretty meh and the grader (Andrew Sweet) is terrible. I've never had such a bad grader in all my time at Berkeley.

The lectures were engaging and Professor Asta always supplemented it with his own walkthroughs on the chalkboard, which helped tremendously. The material was a little lacking on the ceramics and polymers side, but overall covered everything you need for an intro to materials science.
The best professor I had in Berkley, great sense of humor , write notes,  read books and you will be fine

Had him during the pandemic - he constantly injected humor into each class and even though it was all about genocide it was never overwhelming. He had a good mix of lecture to participation for the class. Requirements were simple- 6 books to read & we were graded on two 6 page papers (25% each), one 10 page paper (40%), and participation (10%)
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Professor Astourian gives you his phone number, yeah, but he wouldn't need to if his lectures were clear! He goes all over the place and only gives us a board full of undefined terms each lecture to help organize things. He was funny, but I constantly felt like I was struggling and failing to understand lecture. Not a fun experience.

He is the funniest professor I've had at Cal and his lectures won't get boring. He is an expert on the topic of genocide and is very easy to talk to if you just want to drop by his OH. He is very accessible - will even give you his phone number; so he gives you a lot of resources to do well. He is not an easy grader but he is fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: He is hilarious but his lectures are very messy and honestly pretty boring. It's hard to stay awake and take notes on everything he says, especially since they're still organized. Still, you can get away with getting an A doing the bare minimum. Readings are long but they're easy to skim to get a general idea

My favorite Professor at Berkeley. This man might just know everything. If you listen, take notes, and do a good amount of the reading you will get an A. He is extremely fair, he tells you exactly what to study so there are no surprises. Astourian should also pursue a career in standup comedy; his sarcastic humor will surly keep you entertained.
Wonderful professor, very funny and helpful.  I loved his class

Tied for the best prof. I have had at Berkeley. He is intelligent and brutally sarcastic. Its also great to have an argument with him. the only downer was the rest of the class. As a discussion format, the class relies heavily on participation, but almost no one participated. You will get what you put into this class.

really funny professor. it was just that the readings for this class were rather dull. it was hard sitting there for this seminar 2 hours every week, but he explains everything and is a really great professor. so the professor is good but maybe take another class by him, but it is not a hard class if you do the readings and attend the lectures.

Some how he will thoroughly cover thousands of years of history, while giving life education. His dry wit makes attending his class particularly amusing and interesting. Flexible about paper dates. He actually reads and comments on student essays and is a critical but a fair grader. I'll just end it with "funniest man in man in the world."
Greatest professor I have ever had! I will definitely be taking him again.
excellent

So freakin' entertaining. Very fair grader. Covers a lot of material in each lecture, which was a bit overwhelmimg as I no background in the subject. But he was always willing to answer questions, and was really nice in giving me an extention for the term paper.

The funniest man I have ever met. Could lecture for half an hour about the most serious of topics (genocide, poverty, Armenian politics) before diverging and talking about how much he liked shish kabob, or how worthless most academics are. What a sarcastic ****. Take a class with him already.
funniest man ever

He was an excellent prof. He forced you to try your hardest, and let you know if your hardest wasn't good enough. His teaching and overall academic style was rare in berkeley, but very much appreciated. His main problem was that he was too intimidating.
he's extremely knowledgable in his field and he's a gem here at berkeley.

Immunology is a very hard and Winoto just makes it harder than ever to me. I have been struggling all the time. You can tell he wants to interact with students and remember everyone's names. But his teaching style and slides could improve to make the hard knowledge more accessible. Problem sets do represent exam, but the exam is harder.

Terrible professor. Couldn't understand him for most of the lectures and he pretends like he's talking to PhD's rather than undergrads. Invades your privacy by watching you on zoom during tests and requires many useless assignments that have nothing to do with the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class will be hard if you do not stay on top of all the lectures. It's not hard because Professor Winoto's difficult; it's hard because immunology is so complex. Go to office hours; he will be the one of the most patient professors who really cares about his students' understanding. Ask questions during class - very willing to answer Q's.

tries to get to know your name! and is very conceptual/experimentally focused, and exams reflect that. like ur asian dad type of guy. he's clear and has good board work but class is just dominated by nervous pre-meds so the atmosphere is kinda 'will this be on the test' a lotta the times

Very confusing and unclear. His lectures are not made for students who have no knowledge of immunology. Midterm wasn't from lecture or textbook material. The only positive thing was that he slows down for students and he repeats himself.

I really liked Winoto! He is very organized and really knows what he's talking about. He holds his students to a really high standard. What he talks about is really complicated, and he does a good job considering the difficulty of the material. I really felt like I was taking an upper division course with him (which was cool)!

Lectures are very organized, good pacing (will go slower if it seems like students are confused). Does not seem all that enthusiastic, but will provide detailed answers to any questions during class or OH. Very conceptual.

I actully liked Winoto. the material wasnt easy, but I went to all the lectures and paid attention, did the readings, went to office hours when i didnt understand and I did great on his section. He was very helpful at office hrs and if you actually cared to listen to his lectures and understand the the topic you would. some ppl just like to whine.

Of the 3 profs who teach 150, he's the hardest to follow and his part of the class will only make sense later, when one of the other profs reviews it, and you'll think 'oh, that makes so much sense!  why couldn't winoto explain it like that?' It's a shame he teaches first, because the other 2/3 are way better but a lot of people dropped before then
Doesn't care about teaching at all - one of the worst teachers I've had.

Very influential figure in the field of architecture, and very knowledgeable about the details and minutiae of hardware systems. Really enjoyed the tie-ins to the current state of research and industry practices!

Lectures are dry, but reasonably gets main points across, although material covered in lecture is only somewhat helpful for exams and homework. Theres a lot of material in this class and some of the test questions test tiny details, so be on the lookout. Lots of projects too.

boring, so so boring. Basically switched from MIPs to RISC-V because he helped make it, thereby inconveniencing all of the students by making us use a language that has exactly 0 online resources in comparison to mips which you could actually google something about and expect an answer. >:(

Humorous lectures, truely cares about the topics. He tells you what questions will appear in the midterm/final in lecture. Also your grades dependent on how well you make your cheatsheet. Generous with partial credit and fairly easy midterms. Final was definitely hard; if the question wasnt on ur cheatsheet, you basically got no points for that.

Great in lectures. Accessible outside of class (office hours, personal meeting set ups). Course itself is generally light (5 homework assignments that are fairly straightforward). Cheat sheet can be used (and is most definitely necessary) for both midterms and final. Must write everything on cheat sheet, but prof goes over all possible questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Horvath gives minimal homework (5 for CE11) but all assignments are fairly dense. Attendance isn't mandatory but I'd emphasize showing up to lecture because he's quite literally gives you questions that will be on the exam as he's reading the slides + lectures aren't recorded. If you do everything right, it should be an easy class.
Really interesting lectures that I learned a lot from. He was always super transparent on what should be on the homeworks + exams. Great class.

great lectures but hard to take away from a class that rewards you on how much time you spend copying lecture notes onto your cheatsheets. homeworks are spread out across the semester and final is worth 40%

The class was elementary as long as you did the work and put every little detail of the lectures in your cheat sheet(s). Although I love “easy A” classes, I cannot say I particularly learned anything, nor did I feel myself utilizing my knowledge during exams. Either the question was on your cheat sheet, or it wasn't; there was no in-between.

Horvath, although a dry lecturer, is an excellent teacher. His midterms and homeworks are straightforward. If you attend class and spend about 2 hours per homework (we had 6 homeworks in total) you will be in a very good position to get a good score. He cares deeply about the environment and possesses a wealth of expertise in environmentalism.

HWs were spread out over the semester well but each took too long and didn't tie directly to (tedious) lecture content. Attendance was mandatory; a few classes, he took 20 minutes of class time to check. Horvath really cares about the material and wants to see his students succeed, but didn't structure the class in a meaningful way to achieve this.

The stuff you learn in lecture and the material in exams and hws are COMPLETELY different but he expects you to know everything like its common sense. The exams were really hard imo even though we could have cheat sheets. Also no extra credit or curves in grading even if the whole class fails an exam. HWs are also pretty hard. Don't recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: There is no transparency with grading, he deleted the canvas as soon as the final ended and then he never contacted the class after that. He never posted the grades for the finals. The lectures are bad and mostly jus

Dont take this class - you can't learn anything. Extremely vague instruction and no assignment guideline but very tough grader. Questioning how can people know his rule when he says "you can choose any format you want". A BIG NO
Dr. Horvath is ok. Not the best prof, but def not the worst. The hws were long and hard, but the tests were A LOT easier than the hws. Just be prepared for long, dry, and extremely boring lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Most overrated professor in Berkeley. I was happy when I heard I had him for CE167, but he simply does not live up to the hype. Maybe it's just the class doesn't really overlap with his interests. He definitely doesn't seem interested. I wouldn't recommend taking CE167 with him. I can't speak for CE11/CE166, where he seems to have better ratings.

This guy doesn't teach you anything and acts like he is on top of the world. Absolute worse professor I have ever had, if I could have given a 0 I would have. No one knows what's going on in that class and he takes pride in it.

This is about the general conduct of this instructor. If you are an incoming student for ECIC or EPM, keep in mind that this guy has a resentment towards students who refuse to take his class. Just take his class and do not offend him......... as his class is not a bad class and taking it spares you a lot of trouble.

Prof. Horvath knows his stuff, and it shows. He also cares about his students. With a lot of repetition between lecture, HW, and tests, he's actively trying to give A's to everyone who puts in effort. He's also genuinely interested in his students, and is most approachable. Tests themselves are long, and your cheat sheet should be packed.
Tests are essentially the same as the homework. Professor likes to reference but not really lecture off of slides. Very funny and nice. Will sometimes scold people for coming in late.
Fantastic professor! Explains everything really well and gives clear guidelines. Homework can be long and challenging but exams are very fair!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Amazing professor and class! He genuinely cares about students and is a great lecturer. He is very transparent with grading. Make sure to attend lectures, not only are they helpful for midterms but you also learn so much valuable & useful information. Homeworks are long but office hours are very helpful!
Great professor. Very engaging lectures. Transparent grading policy.

Awesome Professor!If you ever get the chance to take his class, don't miss out. He knows what he is talking about and shows a great interest in teaching his students. Super helpful and very approachable as well.
Very interesting lectures. Generous Curve

He is a very fair professor who wants you to do well. His midterms are pretty straightforward if you know the material. The homeworks can be kind of tedious but they're totally doable and should help your grade.
You have to love this guy!
Great professor! One of my favorites at Berkeley. He spends a lot of time on his students and gives them lots of attention. He gives great guidance and gives fair homework and exams
No Comments

He was pretty clear in lecture and knew what to emphasize. The homeworks were never explained well,  and I did pretty bad, but there are many oppurtunities to overcome that problem (I didn't opt to go for them). Nonetheless, if you are somewhat dedicated to doing well in the class, you will do well. Horvath is a pretty decent teacher.

Professor Roy is a very knowledgeable professor who genuinely cares for her students and wants to help them with real learning in order to succeed. The class is truly interesting and shifted my perspective every single lecture. While the class and its concepts may come off as difficult at first, it is really helpful and I would 100% recommend.

Professor Roy was excellent. I truly recommend this class to all students. Spellbinding lectures (I never missed a class). She is so passionate and cares so much about her students. I have learned so much in her class; the topics have stuck with me even after the semester has ended. Take any class with her, CDSS 94 AKA CDSS 60, going forward.
loved this class, it sucks it doesn't count towards any data requirements. She teaches all things data and ethics. Only final presentation and short essay midterm. Attendance is mandatory.

lecture was boring to me, she js walks around room, reads from notes, accent is pretty heavy. no assignments except 2 midterms and group project. i never did the readings and studied 1 week before midterms/final and i got an A. not the hardest class, but it felt like a DRAG to attend. gave us questions to tests ahead. she's very passionate and nice

My favorite class at Berkeley so far. Every lecture felt directly connected to real-world issues. Roy is an expert in her field, and the course built strong social science foundations that will be invaluable for drawing insights from data in the future. I highly recommend any class she teaches.

Highly recommend to students, even if they aren't studying anything related to CS, the class is not coding-based. The professor is very passionate about what she teaches, allowing her lectures to be very interesting/engaging.
Amazing class and she prepares you so well for each exam. Would highly recommend.

Arguably the best course I've taken at Berkeley. If you are a CS/DS major, PLEASE TAKE IT. Prof Roy is an amazing lecturer, and does a phenomenal job of connecting Phil/Sociology/Anthro with CS that many students never get the chance to learn. Prof Roy cares deeply for students. One of the few classes I genuinely loved. (Class also goes by CDSS 60)

Professor Roy is a fantastic instructor! Her energy, deep knowledge, and genuine care for students makes the class enjoyable and engaging. She encourages questions, supports creative topics for the panel presentation, and gives clear instructions. I learned a lot and always felt motivated to participate. Highly recommend her anthropology class!

Professor Roy is an invigorating lecture that has the rare ability to take abstract material and make it feel urgent. Easily the most though-provoking courses at Berkeley and should be required for CS/DS majors the way that it connects to debates on human values, AI and technology. She is kind, accessible and genuinely listens to her students.

I could not recommend this class more, and it really speaks to the nature that Berkeley is taking to shape CDSS. Professor Roy is truly such an amazing lecturer and you will leave this class having an even greater passion for computing and science!

Highly recommend Data 94 with Professor Roy. She has a genuine passion for what she teaches, and it shines through in her lectures. She's approachable and encourages students to engage with the material, especially during office hours. The readings are interesting, and overall, the course is very engaging.

HIGHLY recommend this class — covers a great deal about philosophical ideas and its intersection with modern data and ethics. Prof Roy is amazing, loves to chat with students in OH about anything in general! Classes and readings are highly intellectually stimulating and have genuinely inspired me to continue learning philosophy alongside my major!

It's a very easy class. There is only one midterm, which is three short essays you get the questions for before then a partner presentation and the final, which is essays again. It's a very easy but fun class. I can only miss three lectures, but it's not bad. Sometimes, she rambles, but she is a very good professor.

Amazing professor, she taught a lot of real world examples that relate to current society. I know she put in a lot of efforts on preparing good and interactive slides for us. Also all of the class readings are the ones she carefully choose, really inspirational. If you have any personal connections or even the concerns, don't afraid of asking!
She's really nice and easy! I love the discussions we have in class and I would definitely recommend any of her classes.

One of the few classes where you leave the room learning a whole new perspective and 10+ words. Smart prof who has knowledge on branches of NS + HS.

Readings are picked well and MT & Finals are easily doable with a few readings and articulation.

Her only downside is that lect. are not the most interactive & there needs to be more focus on DS.

I highly recommend this class for Data Science, CS, and EECS majors. The course mainly explores the social implications of AI and technology, with readings on topics like gender inequality and vocational science as well. The readings are manageable, and exams (midterm and final) are based on them with questions provided beforehand. Low workload!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She was very clearly passionate about what she was teaching although lectures were almost always really boring (she rambles a lot). Your whole grade is entirely determined by the midterm and final- there's no assignments except 1 presentation. Gave zero feedback on the midterm and no explanation to why you received the grade you did. Overall fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very enjoyable course and lectures! The professor is very passionate and knowledgeable, every lecture was interesting and informative. Also very approachable and informative professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I truly loved this class and found it very inspiring to go through with data sciences!! The professor is truly passionate about the course and really engages with students in lectures. No recordings are offered in class but if you pay attention in lecture or if you simply use the poster slides you will be very prepared. HIGHLY RECOMMEND FOR ALL!!

The professor truly cares for the students and this class is one of a kind. Lectures are mandatory and there are no recordings but as long as you are there you will be fine as the midterm and final are based on readings. Her readings and slides are good supplemental resources for understanding the material, and she takes time in class to help kids.

Professor Roy did an exceptional job of bridging the gap between the social sciences and engineering in the Data 94 course, making complex concepts easy to understand and showing their real-world relevance. Her engaging lessons and thoughtful discussions helped students like me connect data science with real-world social issues.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment:
This class first starts with the evolution of science and then dives into modern technology. It highlights the misuse of data and exploitative techniques big companies use today. 
Arpita Roy is an amazing lecturer, using vivid examples and anecdotes to engage the audience. She seems to genuinely care for her students and their futures in the field.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: As a CS major, we are not used to being exposed to the ethics and/or social aspect of the technical world that we are trying to step into. Her lectures were very interesting and are based on the readings given. The whole class is very worthwhile. She genuinely cares about all her students and motivates us to do better even outside of the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: A wonderful professor and person. Her teachings are dynamic, informative, and clear -- technologies and ideas alike. She cares about her students and genuinely wants to help them.

I took ANTHRO168 to fulfill a requirement and am so happy that I chose this course. Professor Roy is one of the most caring professors I've met at Berkeley, and she is so passionate about what she teaches. The class is very thought-provoking, and exams are not too difficult, as she gives prompts weeks in advance. Love this class!

Dr Roy is an engaging professor with a wealth of knowledge. She connects concepts across the disciplines from stem to the social sciences, allowing us to have a deeper understanding towards the course. Medical ANTHRO was my first course in the discipline of anthropology and I was able to follow every single lecture without having prior knowledge.

Arpita is the most caring teacher I've ever had. She genuinely wants to connect and teach you not only about the subject but about life. Very energetic, provoking lectures as well as lot's of funny anecdotes during class. She purposefully makes exams very easy so that students can focus on the actual learning. Must take for any major.

Class covers a lot of readings & topics. Even though the pace of the content of the class is quite fast, you can simply choose one reading to talk about in your essay. As long as you can articulate and support your argument well, you should get a good grade for your essay and final essay. Amazing lecturer!

Prof Roy is incredibly passionate + caring. Lively discussions in class (she shares touching personal anecdotes) + 1 group presentation. Lectures are less organized, but readings are fantastic, thought-provoking. She is so human and very welcoming in office hours; she makes you feel seen. Anthro 168 has shaped my worldview; my fav class at cal!!

Great R1B class. Graded on a few papers but she has interesting lectures and is very knowledgable and enthusiastic. Is a lenient grader and encourages creativity. Gathers very relevant texts which are not required but help understanding a lot.

Prof. Arpita is a kind of Prof who values the relationship with students, and is accommodating to their questions and personal concerns. Classes are challenging but I highly recommend taking her courses.

The professor really breaks down the concepts in a comprehensive way, delivers absolutely amazing lectures and teaches anthropology in a well-organized and multi-disciplinary nature. her lectures and out-of-class conversations are really mentally stimulating for students from all acadmic backgrounds! highly recommend!

Very good for students of all backgrounds. Really awesome that she lets us have lots of intellectual creativity over our essays. As an EECS major, oftentimes I like to connect the essay topics to things I am learning in Comp Sci and Math, and she loves it when students bring in their own ideas/experiences. Also very approachable in Office Hours!

Professor Roy is a joy!! The course readings are interesting and she encourages participation through presentation projects. I've enjoyed the interdisciplinary nature of the course and would highly recommend it to others.

I wouldn't suggest taking an online course by her if you plan on paying attention because she seemed to be constantly confused about how to work zoom and would depend on the gsi's to give information. Lectures can be unclear sometimes and the kinship project is dumb and pointless. I asked for an extension when my grandma had just passed, said no.

AWFUL. so many things to read, unclear test materials, literally read through her slides that we could never understand for more than a hour for nothing. Not inspiring at all, avoid this class at all cost. the course, GSI, and the professor is a scam. worst course I have ever taken in Berkeley

Probably the worst professor I've had at Berkeley. Had an online class, but didn't know how to use Zoom. Spent 5 hours of lecture just showing us how to draw a family tree. Refused to talk about Palestine and muted a GSI who tried to speak about it, saying, "I want to teach this class again next year." A disappointment to UCB anthro department.

The course syllabus was structured around course readings, lectures, and learning about GSI research in different areas of the world. Arpita attempted to silence a GSI speaking about an important global topic relating to colonization and apartheid which is a major topic in an intro to Anthropology course, especially at Berkeley.

Arpita Roy is a caring instructor. She brought concepts from math, philosophy, literature and physics, which made her lectures so engaging. She made the class so useful with real world examples. Prof.Arpita Roy broke down the material really effectively for easier comprehension. Data Science/EECS majors go take her classes. UCB is lucky to have her

if you are taking for an easy breadth, do not. She was just not meant to ever teach an online class. Her lectures were 5 slides for 80 minutes and extremely hard to follow due to her tangents. If you did not have a good gsi you were screwed. Interesting and enjoyable class if you are interested in anthro, if not steer clear.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I was miserable in this course. I honestly have no idea how I passed. The class was online which is not a good fit for her type of teaching. Most of the lectures were her complaining about it being an online class. The GSI for the course was also not great, but he was the primary reason I passed. Midterm was online but final was in person.
Hilarious grading criteria. She didn't even provide students with enough study guide for exams. Be ready to read the whole reading textbook

I took this class for a breadth requirement, but it was clear that the professor was extremely passionate and highly articulate -- I would definitely recommend her to anyone going into anthropology. Exams were pretty easily graded and entirely based on the readings; lectures were supplementary.

Overall disorganized and unpleasant class. GSIs carried most of it in weekly discussion section. Final exam is an absurd departure from what we have been doing in preparation for it. Textbook was tailored to class, expensive, and not worth the trouble it took to get it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: professor roy is very passionate about anthropology, and this is very clear in the way her class was organized. she's especially good at working with students in stem fields because she has a strong background in physics. overall i liked this class but i will say it was basically nonstop paper writing after the first month

She is an amazing, helpful, smart professor who will always care for her students, listen to them and be very accessible in office hours! Her lectures are amazing, would love to take more of her classes! The final exam thing is not her fault at all, it was a decision made by the registrars office, not her.If anything she's been trying to prepare us
I love Professor Roy's class. She is passionate, engaging, and hilarious. I will definitely be taking more anthropology classes from Roy! She is awesome.

Super passionate lecturer! Content and lectures are very interesting. In regards to the final exam situation, that is generally something that is controlled by the university if you are going off of what is listed on cal central--not Prof. Roy. Likely a last minute change by the university.

Arpita is quite disorganized, and honestly the GSI's are carrying the class right now. There was a sudden shift from an online to in-person exam last minute, and lots of students are having conflicts because of this. Also, her lectures are incredibly unclear, and the only reading and learning I have got so far was from the textbook and GSI's notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Arpita Roy's handling of Anthro3AC was disappointing. Her lecture style was ineffective, and the last-minute switch from an online to an in-person final exam caused significant scheduling conflicts for many students. This lack of organization and clear communication was a major drawback in the course experience. Terrible experience with her.

I've attended several summer classes including this 1. This class was diff b/c we started w/ an almost packed class and few or none dropped. You'll be challenged and blown away by how much she knows. It's a hard class but you will learn SO MUCH that you'd love the subject and the class at the end. She is a fair grader & go to office hours it's fun!

Dr. Roy is fun and funny.  She is required to rush through a lot of information very quickly in the summer.  I think some students don't know that that's a departmental requirement rather than her personal preference.

Professor Roy is an amazing Professor whose passion for Semiotics and Anthropology is unparalleled. She offers a traditional and fundamental approach to Anthropology that is rarely taught, let alone talked about, in other Anthro classes. Even those with much more distinguished Professors. Highly recommend taking her class to round out your Anthro.
Magic, Religion, and Science - love Professor Roy! She is amazingly passionate and dedicated. Wish I could take more classes with her!
She's a lovely lady and an awesome professor. She is very accessible, and has a genuine interest in all her students. It was her class that saved me during my last semester at Cal.

Honestly one of the best, if not the best, professor I have had in 3 years at Cal. Passionate about teaching and genuinely wants students to think critically for themselves. A lot of fun to get to know in office hours. Brilliant intellectually yet down-to-earth as a person. Reasonable exams. Wants students to learn and doesn't care much for grades.

Arpita is adorable, delightful, high energy, friendly, approachable, and scarily smart. She talks as quickly as she thinks, she covers complex topics quickly, but she's always willing to stop and clarify and always available and happy to see students in office hours. One of my favorite profs ever.

The subject matter is esoteric, but Prof Roy chooses her readings and explains things carefully in order for her students to understand. She is caring and thoughtful, and you will rarely ever encounter a professor quite like her. If you don't get Saussure (like I didn't before taking her class), you will after she is done with you.

Arpita is absolutely an amazing professor! She's young, passionate and extremely dynamic.  She is very knowledgeable in so many fields that are pertinent to anthropology and she does a good job of explaining if you don't understand. If you really engage the material and appreciate her liveliness then the class will be enjoyable

Dr. Roy is one of the most exceptional, brilliant, passionate teachers I have had the pleasure of having in my life. She is not afraid to tackle difficult(and interesting) material if it means her students will be enriched from it. She is very effective when it comes to breaking down the material while still leaving room for dialogue in her class's

Dynamic and lively lecturer! She transforms mundane materials, i.e., Peirce, into something more accessible. The course is a nice balance of theoretical semiotics and practical, ethnographic application of theory.

Prof Roy is extremely intelligent (almost intimidatingly so), but at the same time very approachable. Her passion for semiotics is apparent in each of her lectures. She brings to life challenging materials with her sense of humor and engaging approach to teaching.
Very interesting lectures, drawing from all over the place!
Arpita is a very interesting instructor (in a good way) - she talks very quickly, but is more than willing to repeat herself. She's really quirky so it makes class bearable!

I had Arpita as my GSI for Anthro 3 and Anthro 1, and was very excited to be in her upper div Medical Anthro course. Fantastic instructor, amazing course. She's brilliant, so the concepts she discusses are a bit hard to understand at first, but she's very helpful and approachable for clarification. Class is a lot of work, but exams are very fair.

I never thought I'd love this summer class, but WOW I did! Arpita is an absolutely wonderful professor and the material is so interesting & mind blowing! This course definitely makes me want to at least minor in anthro! And an awesome GSI (cough*Michael D'arcy) helps! i assure you this is one course&professor you'll be thankful you had in berkeley!

Tries so hard to artificially engineer rigor into this course, when in reality it is some of the easiest braindead simple concepts just convoluted behind flowery jargony language. Weird rubrics that makes getting an A super subjective. Guy would not survive anything that requires actual brain power. No curves by the way.

Breathtakingly smart, humane and kind and incredibly caring. Even in such a big class, if you attend office hours he will know you as a student and person. Inspirational scholar deeply invested in his work. He includes a huge diversity of readings to engage students with ethical themes in the tech world and beyond. Wish I could take him again.

It's a pretty interesting class but the profs make it difficult for no reason. Make sure to do all the readings and read all the lecture slides because they are looking for particular answers on the midterms/finals. He is a super nice guy though and really smart, but the lectures are very convoluted for rather simple concepts
Extremely low IQ class, all I can do is laugh at him
Does he know what he is talking about?

I loved having Professor Edmundson for Data C104! Im a DS major myself and didnt know anything regarding the contexts and ethics of data. Very insightful lectures as well as readings that opened my eyes to how important it is to have a class like this. Although the reading notes weren't clear rubrics, the class itself is awesome and Ill miss it!

Professor Edmundson is incredibly knowledgable and cares deeply about his students. Data C104 was writing-heavy and conceptually challenging, especially for me as a data science major, but the content was extremely valuable and Edmundson's office hours were incredibly inspiring, comfortable, and helpful. Highly recommend

this class is very annoying as a data science major. it is a large time commitment and lectures are very difficult to follow. i wish the professor knew his audience(mostly STEM majors being forced to take this class) and graded papers a little nicer . the lectures use too much jargon that is hard to remember and understand.

The lecture is hard to follow and he likes to use big words to sound more professional and intelligent but that makes the lecture way harder to understand. Really tough grader and gives way too much reading. Requires reading notes on weekly readings which is a lot.

The biggest pseud I have ever had the displeasure of encountering. Loves using flowery, nonsense terms to make himself sound intelligent and lectures impossible to follow or be engaged in. The amount of reading in the course was borderline unreasonable, and all grading was sketchy and unclear (no rubric, might've just used an RNG idk). Avoid.

Edmundson was a dedicated lecturer who took the detailed and complicated concepts taught in Data C104 and made them easily digestible and understandable. His work in crafting this class is no doubt impactful and is a breadth of fresh air in the hyperfocused industry of data science, computer science, and AI.

(DATA 4AC wasn't an option but that's the class I took, not HISTC184D)
Professor Edmundson is incredible! His content is intriguing, he is highly intelligent and passionate about what he teaches, he is very engaging, and he loves to hear from the unique perspectives of students. He is caring, exciting, inspiring, interesting, and very informative!

Professor Edmundson is a gem. He is truly passionate about both the material and his students. He'll stay after class and talk about HCE or philosophy or just life. He'll legitimately ask you how you're doing in OH. He is among the most empathetic and kind people I've ever had the pleasure to meet. This class actually changed my life thanks to him.
dude was the GOAT. Great lectures. Great content. Would take again.

If there was ever a professor who embodied every single godly attribute a professor could possibly attain, it would be Professor Arman Catterson. What an absolute legend, holy moly bro, this guy is the definition of peak. Genuinely the best prof I've ever had, would 100% take again. He and his class were such an awesome intro to Berkeley.

HE'S THE BEST. He's so funny and he kept a THREE HOUR lecture entertaining. I had NO problems with him and would take his class over and over again. PLEASE IF YOU HAVE THE CHANCE TO TKAE HIS CLASS, DO IT. He's so amazing.

Catterson is like the coding version of jesus christ to me 
ive never had a professor who more earnestly wants you to succeed - you get out of the class what you put in + he is so flexible with quizzes and exams. ASK FOR HELP WHEN YOU NEED IT, its so easy to get lost, you have to be proactive about getting support but its there for you!

We were his first class where he was trying out a "flipped classroom" technique which genuinely made it a lot harder to learn but he put in a lot of effort to help us and I left knowing a TON of info about coding.

Such an amazing professor! Makes statistics and R coding really easy and digestible. He can explain concepts in 30 minutes what other stats classes try to explain in a week. One of the easiest and most effective professors I've ever had in Cal. Definitely take his class.

Such an amazing professor!!! Makes statistics and R code so easy. I took statistics in another class that taught a lot of similar topics and Professor Catterson explained something in 30 minutes that other stats class couldn't teach in a week. He's a really understanding professor and doesn't give much homework. Definitely take his class!
Very awesome, both his class and himself.

Very approachable and friendly, wants to make coding approachable. Great at breaking down complex concepts and assignments, incorporates humor and tons of breaks to make sure the 3 hours is engaging and useful. Very approachable and really wants everyone to get an A and succeed

Professor Catterson is the literal best! Great lecturer, makes coding fun and accessible, super receptive to student feedback, and is insanely witty. The course is incredibly well-structured, and every assignment allows you to practice new skills. I learned so much in 101!

Very kind and helpful professor. The content is manageable as long as you pay attention to deadlines and ask for help as needed. Assignments and grading are very reasonable and nothing in the course should be absolutely draining. Have fun!
So accommodating and walks you through everything needed for the class. Highly recommend
Hands down one of the best professors I've had. Arman makes even the driest topics engaging and fun. The workload is manageable, and unstuck study was a huge help for exam prep. Highly recommend!

I could not say enough good things about Prof. Catterson. This class may seem scary to anybody whose never taken a coding class before (me), but Catterson makes the experience extremely enjoyable. His lectures are engaging, he cracks jokes, and genuinely cares about every student in his class. HIGHLY recommend taking him if you're on the fence.

Prof. Catterson's goated. Definitely the best professors I've ever, and will ever, have had the pleasure of learning from at UCB. Super passionate about this class, genuinely cares for his students, and effectively communicates his smarts. Even with no coding experience, this class was really fun! Don't fall behind, do all the work and you're set.

Love. Him. Actually cares about the students' well being and stress and their learning progress. One of the rare professors where if you put in the effort you will get result. Clear assignments and grading. Very grateful and definitely will take again.

Amazing, accessible and extremely helpful. Understanding of the difficulties we face as UCB students. Lectures were very engaging and funny. He takes the difficulty out of learning a new language, R. I highly recommend him as a professor.

Sweetest professor I have encountered. Geniunely learned so much. For a class that is 3 hours long, I actually looked forward to and enjoyed learning. He cares about his students and makes sure you are retaining information , not just going through the motions. My GSI (Abdullah) was so helpful. The 3 hours is worth it! Live, Laugh, Love Arman

Professor Cat is the best! No doubt, take his class. The most caring professor I have had so far at Berkeley. Professor Cat isn't on his own schedule - He follows what the students need and caters to the collective class difficulties. You'll be doing yourself a disservice by not meeting this rad professor - Thanks for a great semester Cat!

Prof Catt is so amazing and caring. For those who don't like coding, this class is great! He genuinely walks through the code and how to debug. His vibe is immaculate and you can tell that he is a professor because he loves his students. The R exam is straightforward and the final project is manageable. Overall, highly recommend for psych majors.
I loved this professor! i went into the class thinking i hated coding, but now i'm doing a cs minor :) thank you prof. catterson!

He truly deserves the 5/5 he has here. If you can take a class with him, take it!!!!!! He is hilarious and the only professor who doesn't make 3 hour lectures feel like a punishment. You actually learn R without feeling the stress of programming and if you do all the work, you will get a good grade.
Dude is great at his job. Teaches one of the most boring possible topics (not his fault) and makes it one of the most interesting classes.

Dr. Catterson is one of the best professors I'd ever have. His lectures are amazing not just for the content, but because he really engages his audience to the materials he presented. I was hard for me to move to different teaching styles after I took his class. The course is not easy, but he manage to make it as easier as possible. Must take him!!

Amaing professor. Coming from someone thats never coded a day in my life, A.D. really excelled at making folks feel comfortable with the language. I couldn't recommend the class enough! Stay on top of your lab assignments, and go to leture and you'll be just fine. Also, the R exam is so chill.

Although lectures were 3 hours, they never felt that long. He's an amazing professor who is very passionate about what he teaches. He always interacts with the class and what you learn, you can take with you in other psych classes. Take him if you can, you won't regret it! 10/10

Arman is one of the best professors at Cal! He's caring and dedicated to making sure that everyone succeeds. The 3-hour lectures are difficult, but he's hilarious and explains everything so well, it doesn't feel that bad. The labs/quizzes are doable if you go to lecture and don't fall behind. Love him x100, would take him a million times if I could

The content of this course was really heavy and Prof did his best to try and make it understandable. He did his best to make it fun. It was not easy content but between Prof and the GSIs it was manageable. Try not to get behind and it will be ok.

Catterson is very understanding and actually values student feedback. There is one exam it is open note and there are no surprises. I thought I wasn't good at R code but I learned a lot and feel confident about my abilities in it now. Overall amazing class, only downside is 3 hour lecture but if you are good at busywork + go to OH you'll get an A.

One of the best professors at Cal and my personal favorite so far. I was scared about the coding aspect of the course but he described everything super clearly and had so many resources to help you succeed.  Even though the class was 3 hours it went by so fast and the content was engaging. Highly recommend this class to everyone!!

Records all lectures. SOOOO engaging. He really cares about the students and their wellbeing, and really makes the class fun. He loves feedback and teaches the material well. There are many sets of practice tests. Easy class to pass (even for me and I hate stats and coding).

TAKE HIM IF YOU CAN! He is literally so sweet and cares about all of his students. The assignments are actually based on things you learn in class, and the tests also test the knowledge you should have. No surprises. He's one of the best professors at Cal for sure.

This professor is amazing. He took what is likely my least favorite thing to do (programming) and managed to make it fun. While learning programming and stats we're also working on a final project all semester, broken into  manageable chunks, so as long you complete all the assignments on time and follow the prompts you will get an A

He makes an effort to make his lectures as engaging as possible and integrates involvement from students whenever he can. He is super passionate about the subject and super understanding. Materials organized and clear. Single R exam that's open book and can have 1/2 credit if you do corrections

Truly one of the best professors I've ever had at UC Berkeley. Super caring, knows his material, and truly wants his students to succeed. Lectures were interesting and engaging, and set up a class discord and answered and help students whenever someone needed help. If you're going to take psych101, definitely take it with him. You won't regret it

Such a friendly and caring prof. As a psych student who hates computers but had to take psych101, I was very surprised by how genuinely invested I became in this course, and I fully attribute my newfound interest in psych data science to profcat

I LOVE THIS MAN. protect him at all costs. the content is very enjoyable and doable to learn without too much outside class studying if you pay attention in class and follow along with the code! Catterson is the type of professor I wish everyone had - he truly cares about his students AND wants them to learn. 10/10 recommend going to his OH as well

Prof. Cat is truly a gem. He is an inspirational professor, who explains R well and really takes into account students' feedback. Berkeley is lucky to have him teaching this important, foundational class. 
TIPS: stay on top of the lectures, ask GSIs/him for help, and do ur final project in something you're interested in!

AMAZING. Just AMAZING! I am not a fan of math and this is still genuinely the best class I have taken at cal. I have 1 hour lectures that 'feel' longer than this 3 hour class. The professor is such an entertaining lecturer and really takes student feedback seriously. There is also a great sense of community in lecture, super collaborative and fun!
Loved this class! Kinda intimidating at first to recall stats concepts while learning R, but he made the whole learning process easy.

This is the first review I have ever written about a professor- and probably the last. Professor Catterson is amazing and we are so lucky to have him with us at Berkeley. He was so understanding, his policies were incredibly generous and reasonable, and he made an incredibly daunting subject genuinely -fun- to understand.

Such an amazing professor!! Really cares about his class and their understanding of the material. He makes sure that he facilitates his students, and understands that a lot of the content may be difficult. Overall, just a very kind and caring prof, I highly recommend taking him

He's amazing, if you're going to take 101, take it with Catterson. The content is inevitably boring BUT he really tries to make it interesting and he gives us breaks during lectures so we're not overwhelmed. He's very caring and it shows. Once again, if you have to take this class take it with Catterson
Amazing professor!! Always cares about his students and makes accommodations according to our needs. There's assignment every week but grading is easy.

This is a coding class, when some see that they may get scared if you've taken coding classes prior, don't worry then this class is easy for you. If you don't have experience coding show up to lectures. Even though this was a 3-hour lecture Carman made it very enjoyable and made the time go quicker. very easy class
SO SWEET I LOVE THIS GUY!!! class has a fair amount of busy work but it's very easily doable

As a psych major, I was nervous about learning R (exam & project too) but he's able to break things down in such simple and logical ways, I felt set up to succeed. Grateful he routinely reminded us that "done is better than perfect" which I have adopted as a personal mantra (reformed perfectionist). He is a Cal gem & hope they value his work.

I really enjoyed Prof Catterson's class. Lectures were definitely too long and often boring but you can tell he tries to make them entertaining. He is very accommodating and conscious of student experiences. Very lenient with grades and assignments.
Do yourself a favor and take this man's class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: I love Professor Catterson! He was super accommodating and offered lectures in-person, live on zoom, and recorded! The labs, quizzes, and check-ins were super easy automatic grade points. The R-Exam is 110% passable if you write down all lab commands and look at past exam links. There is also a lot of late work extensions w/o penalty if needed.

The most authentic professor ever, Prof Catterson could make my three-hour lecture go by in a blink of an eye. Very supportive and receptive to the class + willing to re-explain concepts in R. An amazing educator and excellent taste in Zoom Waiting Room songs :) Go Prof Cat!

I heard many goods things, but was honestly unimpressed and bored by Catterson. Lectures were slow, empty (could be summarized in 30min), and disorganized. It was super easy, coding was surface level which was disappointing. My GSI made this class interesting, but otherwise not an accurate representation of research or coding in psych.

the best professor ever. so understanding. allows late work, records lectures, quizzes have multiple attempts, gives constant feedback and opportunities to do better, doesnt test hard. the final research paper is worked on throughout the semester so its not overwhelming. he plays frank ocean during class. love him

Take his class! Professor Catterson is hands down one of the best teachers I've had. He has a clear grading criteria and has outlines for everything! So when you are doing your assignments, you are not lost at all. He explains so well! Lecture is long but goes by fast. You will expected to do work obviously, but nothing too hard.

Arman Catterson is by far one of the best professors I've had at UC Berkeley. He set up an entire discord channel with himself included for easy accessibility, he understands students have a lot to juggle with academics and outside life, and he's hilarious. He communicates frequently and clearly, and wants you to LEARN and not just memorize.

Prof Catterson is amazing! He genuinely cares about his students succeeding in his class. He offers lots of flexibility with due dates and is always willing to work with students. Highly recommend taking his class

Professor Catterson is the best professor I've had in three years at Cal. Lectures are hard because they're three hours, but he gives breaks and it's manageable. Our class struggled with labs. He listened to us & improved them. He wants you to succeed and cares about students. Super clear expectations and support through all assignments and tests

Professor Catterson was such an amazing professor and he genuinely cares for his students. The lectures aren't too heavy and the workload isn't overwhelming. Honestly had a lil crush on prof too, he's very charming

best prof Ive ever had so far. DS seems intimidating but Arman makes it so ez. I learned to code in R in stat20 and it was horrible, here it was infinitely better. Also, everything other than quizzes/exams can be turned in late up till end of sem, and Arman+GSIs are super understanding of extenuating circumstances. overall so wholesome and an ez A.

Okay. Arman is probably the best professor I've ever had. He genuinely cares about his students and their learning and it 100% shows. There are no deadlines as long as you turn things in before a certain date at the end of the semester. The material can be hard and confusing but you will have a great support system of GSI's and professor. Take him!

The best class you'll take at Cal. Amazing lectures: made me look forward to a 3 hour class on Friday afternoons. Labs: super helpful so do them when assigned. R exam helps w/ project. Prof gives every opportunity to learn and his policies reflect that. Catterson is an amazing person and professor. Can't say enough about how great this class is.
Was on the class discord. Answered any questions students had and would always make people feel cared for. Absolutely the best class at berk.
What a great professor to have my first semester at Berkeley! Would definitely recommend such an amazing instructor.

He's awesome. A rite of passage for every Cal Psych student. Made computer programming way less scary. One exam mid semester, gave an opportunity to make up points. Homework had very flexible deadlines. Receptive to student feedback. One con: 3 hour lecture Fri afternoon, not his fault, but brutal. But, he makes you want to come.

Such an amazing professor! With everything going on at this time, he is so understanding and caring. You can tell he truly cares about his students. Highly recommend taking him! I've only heard great things from others too. Never coded before and this class ended up being my highest grade this semester! Take him if you can!!

Doctor Catterson is/ was and continues to be a source of knowledge and professionalism that goes far beyond the walls of any college. He is willing to teach listen and guide offer constructive criticism all while teaching in a manner that you cannot forget even if you tried. You will feel inspired every class.

Catterson was the best!! Great lecturer, even though they're 3 hours, he's attentive to students and lets us take breaks. He's super in tune to what student's need and how they're feeling. When we transitioned to online Spring 2020 he was the most caring of all my professors. I learned a lot from him & my GSI and cannot recommend him enough. 11/10!

Prof Catterson was an amazing teacher for intro to learning R. I'd taken a python class before but didn't have much experience coding, and he eased us into everything while challenging us and keeping the information exciting. He's funny, gives great examples in lecture, and super approachable for each student individually! 10/10

Prof Catterson is awesome. I have absolutely no coding background and he made learning R so easy. He is funny, charming, compassionate, and very entertaining. I can't even think of anything to critique about his class. I would absolutely recommend Prof Catterson to anyone. His class was the highlight of my week. Also, his office hours are helpful!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: LOVE Professor Catterson. This is the second class I've taken with him, and he managed to make R and psych research super understandable. Incredibly organized and understanding - few professors at Cal really trust their students the way Catterson does. Coding isn't bad if you have some exp, but even if you don't, the prof is super approachable

Catterson is amazing (took him also for Psych 1 and his teaching style made me want to take Psych 101). Extremely accommodating and caring. Accessible during office hours and through email when stuck on concepts/ coding with R. 3 hr lectures but he makes it engaging. thanks profcat will miss your class

AMAZING professor! He really cares about his students and has to be the best prof I've had. Lectures can get long but he makes it as interesting as possible. Don't fall behind on labs or else things will get confusing! No previous experience with coding is necessary. Lectures aren't strictly mandatory, but I would suggest going to them anyway.
Best Professor I've had since I got here.

Prof Catterson is the most caring prof i've ever had. He is funny and upbeat. Lectures are long, but they're recorded anyways. Class has a lot of material to learn (more like a 5 unit class) but the way he grades is very fair. If you try and do the work, you'll be fine

By far the most accommodating professor during the COVID-19 pandemic. Catterson prioritizes the needs and wellbeing of his students, is hilarious, likable, and real.
