He teaches you how to code in R and write academic papers, all while acknowledging the major pitfalls of institutionalized inequality. Great prof, great guy. Couldn't recommend enough.

Hands down the best professor at Cal! Even though lectures for that class are all taught in one day, his personality and just the way he teaches makes you actually want to go to class. 10/10 would definitely recommend him.

Prof Catterson is down to earth, compassionate, understanding, and a great professor. He genuinely cares about every single student and is constantly trying new ways to effectively teach his courses. I would absolutely recommend him to anyone!

Persian king!!! The sweetest, most compassionate, informative, and amazing professor you could have in the psych department and Berkeley overall! Never have I felt so supported by a professor throughout a normal semester, let alone a pandemic. Lectures are long and so are discussions, but well worth it. Not difficult course material, just tedious.

Prof Catterson is too good to be true. He is extremely patient, HILARIOUS, socially intelligent, & has tons of urgency to help you if you email him. He teaches 3 classes in 1 (R coding, research methods, statistics) & specializes in helping you relax. Ex: He once held office hours on club penguin during COVID-19 pandemic. I demand he gets tenure.

CATTERSON IS THE BEST!! If you get a chance to be in his class, please please take it. He is so organized that the class is super simple to manage even when the course content is a little harder. He cares about how the students are doing and do weekly checks to make sure everyone is on the same page. Catterson deserves an award and more recognition

He has been by far one of the BEST professors I've ever had at Cal. He teaches psychology so well, homework and readings are manageable, and made his lectures very enjoyable. He cared a lot about students' mental health, so he did not make the class that tests heavy. His final exam was basically a compilation of all of the in-class quizzes.

Professor Catterson is an excellent teacher. Presented information well and in interesting ways and was always willing to help make sure you understand the topics. If you study whats on the study guide for the mid-term, you will pass. Pay attention to the check-ins and quizzes. watch the lectures online if you miss class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I was blindsided by how he had hidden check-ins in notes and probably missed all of them, but other than that, I loved all of his lectures (legit gave me some stand-up vibes), and loved how he lets students who are doing well in class tutor students who are struggling instead of taking the final. It was a bit hard for sure, but hella fun too.

Syllabus said mandatory lectures based on online check-ins. Went to all lectures and did them yet didnt receive the credit on attendance. I asked him & he said he had hidden check-ins in lecture notes (never said were mandatory, neither did syllabus)& response was rude when I asked. I also talked to others & many had same problem with attendance
Hard course but he made the material fun!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Catterson genuinely wants you to learn. He gets you to be interested in the content material and WANT to have meaningful discussions. You will NOT be meaninglessly memorizing content in this class. He's extremely approachable, offers a lot of extra credit, and is overall a good guy! Don't miss out on the opportunity to take a class with him!
Great professor who definitely wants his students to succeed! Interesting lectures!

I took Psych 1 with prof caterson and it was such a fun and easy class! No midterm, just semi weekly quizzes that are open note/internet. There is a term project which is just a 5 min video about anything you want & the he gives you a study guide for the final which was extremely helpful!

Literally my favorite professor and favorite class at Cal. Dr. Prof. Catterson is so personable and so good at explaining psychology that I learned like a sponge. He was always prepared and, although he makes you truly work for your grade, you will get out of it what you put in. I loved every activity and every lesson. He makes you think.

One of best classes at cal! The lecture is super long but he made it not so boring and can still be engaging. Easy to understand the materials if you do the readings and OH. Many extra credit opportunities but are competitive to get thou. Final and midterm don't weight as much as other classes do. He is the reason that I keep majoring in Psych!

Dr. C is one of the best professors I've had and makes me excited to be a Psych major. He made the class entertaining even tho we had 3 hours of lecture and was extremely caring about students' understanding of the material. Grading was clearly outlined and lots of extra credit given! If you can, take ANY class with him. He's amazing!
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I love Prof Catterson, this is my second semester taking a class with him and he's proven to be one of the best professors I've had at Cal. Lectures are hilarious (though 3 hours is rough and I skipped class a lot) and he breaks statistics and R down into easily understood and digestible sections. Catterson is the reason I'm a psych major! Thx man

Dr.C is the best teacher at Cal!!! I learned so much from his PSYCH 101 class. I really hate stats and don't like computer programming (you learn how to use R for data analysis in this class) but honestly he made it a breeze! TAKE CATTERSON!!!
Catterson is a gem at UC Berkeley. Dedicated, always willing to help, a great professor, he has it all. I was very fortunate to take Psych 101 with him .
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Engaging, interesting, obviously cares about his students, grades fairly, gives fair exams, weights tests/homework/quizzes fairly. One of my best professors at Cal - so good I had to take him twice! Amazing lecturer and educator for both Psych 1 and Psych 101

Dr. Catterson speaks with passion in all of his lectures and makes it easier for us to translate the information to life outside the classroom. Points for this course was mostly participation/effort. He gives a lot of extra credit. Final project is your own study that you design. I would take a class with him without hesitation!

He is an amazing professor compared to the ones I've taken. He knows what he is taking about and his lectures are really helpful. He makes the class interesting and is really straightforward which is a plus. Grading is easy as long as you do it and he offers easy extra credit and the midterms/final are based on lectures and readings.
One of the best professors I've had at Cal! His lectures are engaging, he's funny and tries to engage the audience. I'm grateful to have had his as my professor.
He's so nice!!! Grades generously and overall a great lecturer! Would take his class again!

He is my favorites teacher ever!!! His class is so much fun, and I learned so much!!! 10/10 would take again!!! Pay attention and take good notes!!! He prints out notes for you but taking notes on what he says really helped:))
He truly cares for his students, and tries his best as a professor. He also has a good sense of humor, and keeps a positive mood for the class. Highly recommend, one of the best teachers Ive had.
He is the best teacher in my life. He is really kind and helps international students well. Strongly recommend to take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: ok LET ME TELL YOU Dr. C is the most caring professor I have ever had. He really wants his students to all succeed. I wish I could take more classes with him!! His lectures were super clear and the subject is difficult but he really guides you through it. He's also really into giving extra credit and understands  what its like to be a student.
Best teacher from all my college years, im a 28 year old man and i approve of this teacher alot. Engaging, cares about his students alot! we need more teachers like this one. f

I didn't have any previous stats experience but he explains everything super well and gives many opportunities to help people understand the theoretical concepts. The coding portion was really understandable; can be a bit confusing but Catterson gets it and really helps everyone out. There are weekly labs but they aren't  graded hard at all.

IF YOU HAVE TO TAKE A RESEARCH METHODS CLASS, THIS IS IT! He made my first semester here at Cal (im a transfer) the best. He learns names, gives extra credit on every exam plus in class, and makes material that is super "scary" accessible so dont worry. Yes, it's coding + stats. But trust me: he's there for you. He's daddy.  I wanna go back lol :(
Fantastic lecturer.  Extremely clear.  Cares for his students and is always willing to help.  A great professor all around.

He's a very entertaining lecturer, makes coding in R and learning stats really easy. Grades things very easily: all of the labs were based on completion and lots of opportunities for extra credit. You can watch the lectures online, you just have to do the linked sign-ins.

Amazing lecturer. i was engaged the entire time. class was slightly disorganized but overall I learned a lot. very R heavy so be prepared to code. he made coding a very enjoyable experience. the take home midterms were really fair also.

I feel so lucky that I chose this class. Not only did I learn A LOT(I may pursue this as my future career, you never know), but also I got to spend this summer with such a cool and nice professor and such a diverse class. He inspired me with all these new knowledge and insightful ideas, and encouraged me to answer questions and ask questions.
reviews.rating_tags: CARES ABOUT STUDENTS--Respected by students--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great professor!
Great lecturer, funny and charismatic, knows how to connect with students.

I took Dr. Prof. Catterson PhD's psych class last summer. Statistics and psychology are dry but  Dr. Cat is very engaged and makes lectures active. (Since most students yes i am are in high school) he explains things again over again if asked. He really cares about our feedback and response. He even started to use Weixin and Youku.

Charming professor. Catterson is funny and engaging. Lectures are not mandatory since he also posts recorded lectures online. For papers, as long as you follow the rubric you'd probably get an A+ for them. Tests are fair, most of the stuff are mentioned in lectures so to be honest reading is optional.

Catterson is awesome. He's so young, and he truly cares. He is a great lecturer. The tests are hard, but they are open notes, computer, everything. You're just not allowed to collaborate. He's very handsome, so I guess that is a plus. Lectures are webcasted. Office hours are great. He takes his time to explain everything to you.
Dr. Catterson is seriously an amazing professor! Take Psych 10 with him - you won't regret it!

Dr Catterson is an amazing professor! He made the class stress free despite the difficulty of the subject and the heavy content of the course. He is so understanding and kind towards his students. He provides extra credit to help your grade and is very flexible about extending the deadlines when the class is falling behind. Strongly recommended.

I first had Daniel as a GSI for Psych c162 last semester so I was very excited when I found out he was the professor for 101! He was great! He was so understanding and considerate of his students. He was willing to changes due dates when he received feedback that we didn't have enough time. Tests were straightforward. Final was take home and easy!

Amazing and very understanding professor. He is very articulate and conveys concepts in a manner that could be easily understand. Given, this is a class heavily based on stats it is really nice to have a professor who doesn't use pompous textbook definitions to explain ideas in stats and r. The book he assigns is pretty good as well as a supplement

Catterson is an amazing teacher, given the context of the class. He encourages students to google their question before asking him in regards to R, but don't worry: he tries to accommodate the students' needs. He's enthusiastic, wants you to participate in class, and lectures are easy to understand. I understood R because of him. HIGHLY recommended

Professor was amazing, was skeptical of statistics and its use in the begging. Seemed like a thing that was super boring. He made it interesting and engaging. Asks really good questions that make you think. Also really approachable, honest, funny, and authentic. Clear passion for teaching.

Daniel has been 1 of the 3 best professors/teachers I've had. He is hilarious, tries to relieve the stress that way, he is knowledgeable and explains things over and over again if you ask him to. He tries very hard to make  personal connection with his students and gives prizes away to those who try hard. He is an absolute must have at UC Berkeley.

I took Psych 10/101 with Catterson and he's awesome! I loved this class and his enthusiasm about psychology and statistics. Not only does he make his lectures fun but they're so helpful when it comes to understanding R. If I had the choice of taking another one of his courses I definitely would!

I took psychology 101 and it was great. Expect a challenge but Professor Catterson is incredible at making course materials accessible to ensure every students success. Probably one of my favorite classes at Berkeley.

Professor Catterson is excellent considering the difficulty and limitations of the class. He understands the needs of his students and is extremely accessible, genuinely caring about helping his students learn and stirring interest in psychology and statistics. Additionally, he's cool, young and hip and gets us students.

Professor Catterson is very VERY good at teaching! He explains everything really clearly and uses great examples. This is the first time the class is using R extensively, so it was quite a bit more difficult than I could handle, but overall it was a great class! I would DEFINITELY recommend him! Class was webcasted, so you don't HAVE to go!

Professor Catterson is a great lecturer and obviously cares a lot about the subject and his students. He is quirky and has a sense of humor, which makes the usually dry subject of statistics and data analysis actually entertaining. Sometimes lectures can get a little confusing, but I really liked taking this class from him. Lots of extra credit.
PSYCH 101 is pretty horrible.  R is difficult.  Catterson makes the best of a bad situation.

He does a great job recapping the material from the previous lecture and relates it to the new material. Read his lecture slides! The conceptual portion of his tests are very straightforward and so are his R portions, as long as you know what code to use for each function.
BEST PROFESSOR REALLY ENGAGING AND MADE THIS CLASS FUN TAKE IT WITH HIM

Dr./Prof. Catterson truly cares about his students.  His classes are entertaining and informative.  He is amusing and makes class fun and interesting for what is a pretty dry subject.  I would take his class again.

I took this class over the summer and had Prof Catterson. I was really worried that I would be totally bored out of my mind during the 3 hour lectures but Prof Catterson was such a great lecturer that this wasn't a problem! His enthusiasm and willingness to listen to student feed back  really made this a worth while class.

Dr. Catterson is an amazing professor! He is extremely flexible and always willing to help his students. I asked him for a letter of recommendation very close to the application deadline, and he was so kind and responsive despite the time pressure. Moreover, during this stressful time,  he inspired me to keep pushing.. wonderful person!

Professor Catterson is a amazing person. Although the material may be hard, he does everything in his power to make it fun and clear. He cares so much; He invites questions all the time during class,  accommodates students with extra office hours, answers emails quickly ( even on the weekends). He has a heart of gold. Simply the best. Thanks Prof.

A.D. Catterson, or the esteemed Dr. Prof. Catterson or more simply Daniel, is a phenomenal instructor & an incredible person. I could not have passed PSYCH110 during a summer term without his help; he went above and beyond to help me & my cohort succeed. He explains concepts well, even R. Andrew Bartnof was my GSI & I highly recommend him also.

A.D. Catterson, or the esteemed Dr. Prof. Catterson or more simply Daniel, is a phenomenal instructor and an incredible person. I could not have passed PSYCH110 during a summer term without his help; he went above and beyond to help me and my cohort succeed. He explains concepts well, even R.  Andrew Bartnof was my GSI and I highly recommend him.

He teaches as if your already an expert in Statistics. His scaffolding technique is all over the place and it honestly lacks structure.  His lecture slides are a joke. Very dry class. Just expect to be confused- the tutors did so much better.
Great humor, friendly enviroment , no text book required, easy to talk to and learn from.

Hands down, one of the best professors I've had! Prof. Catterson is hilarious and I never found his lectures boring. Paid attention every minute of the 2.5hr lecture this summer. Sparked my interest in the overlap between psych and big data; would take his classes again! Expect homework and participate in lecture to get a good grade.

Professor Hedeman is genuinely one of the best professors I have had. He is passionate about teaching and cares about his students. His lectures are great and easy to follow. I would highly recommend!

great lecturer with a clear passion for teaching and for the subject! genuinely cares about students and is willing to advocate for them. homework can be long but is very educational. exams are 24 hour open note, can be a bit long but still reasonable. totally recommend!
One of the nicest professors here, and puts a lot of effort into his teaching! Highly recommend

Professor Hedeman is amazing. I wish I could take every physics class with him. He's super helpful and available to explain in detail during his office hours. He is very caring and accommodating. The homework is time-consuming but very well written and helps to understand what is happening. His exams are also well written and fair. Take his class!
My favorite prof at cal so far. Lectures and HWs were fun, and I felt that I really learned a lot. Super nice as well, and goes out of his way to provide support, with edited videos and notes.
He is amazing, most fun I've ever had taking exams (he has started 24 hour exams for all his classes last I heard, which is just awesome). Suuuuuper nice person too.

Professor Hedeman is a great guy and truly does his best to teach well and help his students. However, I feel that his teaching style was not for me. He would often lead with examples and introduce things in a too abstract way (like vector spaces introduced with shapes on a string). Secondly, he would handwrite lectures, so it was hard to see.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very intelligent. Great communicator. Great at answering questions. Organized and thorough lectures. Helpful in office hours. Tons of resources for material: he posts his lecture notes he uses (which are practically a textbook), what he wrote on the actual whiteboard, recordings of the lecture, homework solutions, and several optional textbooks.

Professor Hedeman is an amazing professor! He is SO clear when explaining quantum mechanics in his lectures and is ALWAYS enthusiastic about the topic. Though his problem sets and exams are long and difficult, I would definitely say they are manageable - start early and plan out your time! Would definitely recommend taking this class with Hedeman!

One of the best professors I've had at Cal. He cares so much about the success of his students and is very accessible. His homework assignments reinforced concepts but were not excessively difficult. Exams were similar to homework assignments. Really take advantage of his online lecture notes!

Professor Hedeman is an excellent lecturer, and one of the most accessible faculty in the entire department. He takes time out of his day to meet with you if you're struggling.. His homeworks are a bit lengthy and often require a lot of writing, but they're usually proportionally worth quite a bit in the breakdown of your final grade.

Professor Hedeman, what can I say? Super cool, really wants to help you learn physics, well-organized. His online notes are so good and comprehensive that you don't need to go to class, but I love how he explains things in lecture. Homeworks are super easy, very straightforward and pretty neat problems! Also amazing on Piazza and exams are fair
He is great

Hands down the best professor I've ever had. Easy A? Um NO. But I've never learned so much during the lecture in any other class. He's very caring and always available to help his students. Highly recommend

Hedeman is an extremely nice person, always makes an effort to be available to help, however his teaching needs some improvement. He doesn't explain concepts very much at all. He also teaches physics like an upper division math class, so if you're not used to proofs or never been exposed, good luck! I am very surprised I passed his class!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: There is no one that compares to Hedeman. He is the best in the department by far. Amazing textbook (he wrote), amazing lectures. The homework is fun, challenging, and you learn a ton. IDC if Siddiqi is teaching and he has a 4.8, NO ONE is better than Hedeman. Hands down, the best teacher you will ever have. The most you will ever learn in a class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Hedeman is a great professor, and QM with him is currently my personal favorite course at Berkeley. What makes his class impressive is that it is so easy to follow and understand, the exams are dirt easy (AND he gives you extra time!) and he has an online repository of week-by-week lecture notes that are as clear as day.   RECOMMENDED!!
he's an expert on the material and explains everything so well

What we went over in class was often not what we were tested on, rather the problems we went over in discussion. I am neither skilled at or interested in econ, and only took it because it was required for my major That being said, professor Auffhammer made it as compelling as it could be, he's an incredibly dynamic and understanding professor.

Max was the funniest prof ever and guides you as many times as you need to understand material. It takes a while to absorb and practice topics on your own, but GSI's were helpful with quick responses. He is a unique prof that is hard to come across and super funny. Grading was harsh imo, but it really made you learn and be prepared for future econ

Professor Max knows how to teach economics to people who do not understand the subject at all. He will go over subjects clearly, and if it does not make sense to you, will answer your questions either in the lecture zoom chat or office hours. He is extremely organized, with a schedule of all reading and quizzes and projects and their dates.

Max was an excellent professor for an intro to my major. He breaks down concepts thoroughly and ties in real-world applications in every lecture. The prof delivers incredible nuance in this complex subject, and conveys the weight of the material very well. Even online, his lectures were engaging and entertaining. Will also give you chocolate.

He's really helpful and is always up to answering questions from students. His lectures are ok, he's a funny guy but his lecture pacing is really bad. Do the readings they're more helpful honestly. He kind of also procrastinates ngl and only gave us our midterm date a week in advance which was def not enough. The final date was always changing too.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: Everything you've heard about Max is true. He's hilarious, knowledgable, passionate, engaging, and overall his personality helps make the lectures more interesting. Problem Sets are okay if you watch/go to lectures. Midterms/final were a bit scary and would've been tough if it wasn't open note (Might only have been open note because it was online).
I would die for him. amazing guy. i love him. hes so cool and awesome!!!

Inspiring professor who is full of interesting stories, ideas, and lectures - made me change my major! Funny, experienced, and great at addressing points of confusion. Max is organized and accessible. Lectures often were easy until I got to an exam, problem set, or section and questions relied heavily on math barely touched on in lecture.

Professor Max is the best professor I've ever had. He is incredibly funny and genuinely wants you to succeed. Exams are not the easiest but if you need help with understanding a concept he is very accessible. I can only recommend.

Professor Max is funny, engaging, and gives great lectures. However, beware of the midterms, as they do not really represent what is emphasized in lecture or section. He will pick niche concepts and decide to make a question about one of them worth 1/4 of your midterm grade.

I'm not exaggerating when I say that Max is one of the most amazing lecturers at Berkeley, if not the best! He's certainly the best one I've had so far. He's just so funny and engaging, and his passion for economics is contagious. His exams are not as friendly to us as he is, though. In summary, top-notch guy and lecturer but poor exam-maker.

I created an account just so I could write this review -- Max is an INCREDIBLE professor and I'm so lucky to have taken this class in the one semester that he taught 100A. His lectures are hilarious -- and he's an incredible professor that truly cares about all his students. As long as you put the work in, show up to lecture/section you'll do well!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Max was an amazing prof! Great lectures because he's just so funny. He does a good job explaining Econ and always answers questions from students immediately. Shout out to GSI Abdou--I didn't have him but he was the best GSI imo. Problem sets are so helpful for practicing the concepts taught in class. So many resources provided for success by Max!!

Max was an excellent professor for an intro to my major. The prof delivers incredible nuance in this complex subject, and conveys the weight of the material very well. Even online, his lectures were engaging and entertaining. Stay on top of readings, and this class is a breeze. Workload was very manageable. Hope to take a class with him in person.

Prof. Max is such considerate guy, and you can tell he's passionate. Very attentive to student needs, whether it's extra clarification of difficult concepts or just his engaging online lectures. Reading the Textbook is recommended, but not necessary to do well. Workload is fair: weekly quizzes, 1 midterm, 3 problem sets, & final.

This man is the reason I am switching my major to political economy. The EPA wanted his help on a report and he is just super impressive and super fun to listen to. The material is really interesting and I really enjoyed the tests since they really made you think and want to understand economics. One of the best professors at Cal.

Just an incredibly kind and caring guy. You can tell he loves teaching and puts in effort to make concepts digestible & econ exciting. Lectures were sometimes hard to follow b/c he talks a little slowly and can go off-topic, but they're recorded so you can always rewatch. Plenty of practice qs/tests. Fair exams. Very responsive to student concerns!
clear speaker and explains confusing subjects rly well, also funny so lectures are light hearted

You can really tell he cares about the subject and student's he's teaching. I took the online intro to econ course and was flabbergasted by how engaging an online class could be. Having a professor who can make a zoom lecture interesting is an extremely good sign and I wish I could take a class of his in person. Very funny, smart, and caring.

Professor Auffhammer was great! He made a real effort to connect with us during and outside of class and office hours, and was so funny that I would often play lectures aloud for my roommates to listen in on. He was very liberal with his time and it was very evident that he cared. Grading was very fair and there were very few assignments.

This class was super fun with Professor Max. Lectures were informative, well-formatted, and sometimes funny with jokes. The content itself was easier in the beginning of the course, and then it gets more complicated in the environmental economics portion. But it you attend office hours and discussions it is easier to understand the math

I loved taking this class! Econ doesn't come easy to me, but Max made it as straightforward as possible. Plenty of office hours and loves helping. This was an online class via zoom, but lectures were recorded and posted later if you could not attend. Grades consisted of weekly online multiple-choice quizzes, 3 problem sets, 1 midterm, and 1 final.

Engaging course and entertaining lecture, almost convinced me to be an EEP major. Section and textbook tend to cover a lot more material than lecture/than is required for tests. Very accessible during office hours. Genuine, caring, and passionate instructor; definitely recommend if you're interested in behavioral sciences.

Max is pretty awesome, he made me enjoy and want to actively engage in a subject I didn't care about initially. He uses a lot of real-world examples and can connect the subject material to it really well. Office Hours, Practice Midterms, and keeping up with the material is the best way to do well in his class.

Max was an amazing professor. Everything you need is taught in his lectures. The only thing is to keep up with lectures and go to his office hours for help because they're actually helpful, especially on problem sets.  He has a genuine passion for his field and his students as well. I truly admire him.

Max was AMAZING!! Serisously the best professor I have had at Cal.  Not only does he make it extremely evident that he is passionate about what he is teaching, but he really shows how much he cares about his students. He is very accessible outside of class and wants to help students learn. Great guy, great class!
TAKE HIS CLASS!! But be sure that you know a little microeconomics because that part of the class will go fast. He is the best professor ever.
Least favorite subject but my favorite professor!

Professor Auffhammer was my favorite professor in Fall 21. He has such a passion for economics, especially environmental economics, which makes all of his lectures really engaging and interesting. He is also accessible outside of class and is very understanding about sickness and disabilities, and overall clearly cares about his students.

Fantastic semester taking envecon C3! Professor Max makes an effort to be personable during lectures and office hours. He is pretty friendly and funny. This class was heavy on midterm and final, but if you understand the quizzes and problem sets it's totally fine. Definitely recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Max is a pleasure; he's a wonderful Prof and makes his lectures entertaining and hilarious. When you sign up for the course, you also subscribe to dad jokes and a good amount of coursework given EEP1 is an intro course. There are weekly quizzes but are easy enough if you follow the lectures. It is clear he has a passion for econ and teaching!

Professor Auffhammer is the funniest professor ive ever had. He clearly cares a lot about economics, especially environmental econ which is his specialty. His lectures are super helpful, there are readings but theyre not necessary if you understand the lecture and take good notes. The problem sets are super helpful.
I LOVE THIS MAN. He is wonderful.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Auffhammer makes lectures very enjoyable with his jokes and stories that makes me not want lecture to end every time. He also tries really hard to make Economics not intimidating and makes it very fun! His exams were pretty difficult, but he adjusted the grade bins very leniently to account for the rigor.

Max is the best professor I've had so far! He is passionate and really cares about students. His exams are extremely fair and the curve is very generous. Problem sets are optional but you should definitely do it. The textbook is pretty useless, just try to understand all of his lecture notes.
Hilarious lectures and intuitive examples. Useful problem sets and online office hours.
Max is the best professor at Cal.

I am so glad I have a chance to study Economics with Max. He only taught 1/3 of the class due to his health condition. I personally started going to lectures after he started to teach. I wish I have a chance to take his class again. His grading is fair, and the content is pretty easy. It's basically Econ1 with math.

Max is one of the best professors I've had at Cal. It's really a pleasure to take 100A with him - he had made every lecture enjoyable, and explained things clearly. He's caring, hilarious, and genuinely wants to help students learn.
It is Berkely's pleasure to have a professor like him

MAX IS AMAZING!! Although he was only able to teach 1/3 of the course due to health reason, his humor and engagement capture every student's heart! If you get a chance, make sure to take his class! Although his tests are about the standard to a difficult level, he always offers a generous curve to the student and truly cares about his students!
I love him.

Max is the definition of what teaching should be like, every lecture is a pleasure to attend. He explains every concept thoroughly and with humor. By far the best professor at Cal, with a great attitude towards life. He explains everything so well that the material is absorbed easily and performance on exams shows. Highly recommend!

Max is the definition of a good professor, his lectures are always engaging and he has a great personality. The best part is that he makes the material comprehensible. His exams are well organized and the class structure is great. Overall one of the best professors at Cal hands down.
Great class, loved his class. He even contributed extra hours each week to do review sessions. Absolutely great professor.
If you want a once in a lifetime experience, take him.

I feel so sad i don't get to take his classes anymore! I wish he still teaches IAS 107. I'm so impressed by his ability to explain economic very  clearly. I wasn't an economic person until i took his class. His lectures, humor, and way of teaching style completely change my perspective on economic! you'll never regret having him as your professor!
BEST PROFESSOR by far at cal. loved his class, love that he love to teach.

I really liked Max. He's funny- most of the time. It wasn't an easy class but he made it interesting. If you pay attention and take lots of notes in class you'll be fine for the exams. Tests are fair.

Auffhammer is one of the best professors I've had at Cal, and I'm a junior. He makes what could be boring or confusing material into funny, engaging, and extremely clear lectures. He explains things very well and obviously cares a lot about his students (and he gives out chocolate) Take this class with him!

By far the best class I've taken at Berkeley (and I'm a senior). I had heard great things about Max before taking the class, but I was still impressed by him! I don't think I ever got bored in his class. He always found a way to make it fun but also very clear. I would highly recommend him as a teacher!

Professor Auffhammer is incredibly funny, witty, clever, generous, and friendly. Case in point: When giving us directions at the final this morning, he stated, "Now, I took this exam yesterday and it took me only 18 minutes!" Everyone started laughing. Attend lectures + take notes + study + get chocolate from Auffhammer = a good grade in the class.

Awesome teacher and class. If you need to do Macro choose this guy. I slept 85% of the days but studied my butt off for the final (which basically determines your grade in the class) got an A- and had fun...HIGHLY RECOMMENDED

If you need to fulfill your Micro/Macro requirements this is the teacher to go. 30% is problem set and attendance, and the problem sets are easy. Midterms were graded fairly, but the entire grade comes down to the final. All material come straight from notes which he posts before class and he's funny
i couldn't believe it, not only did i remember the content after the semester, i caught myself explaining microeconomics to a friend while on winter break. Enough said!

i took both 106 and 107 and i loved coming to lecture. i never missed one, always paid attention and i got a relatively easy A in both classes. pay attention during class and if interested in the topic, you'll do fine. oh and i never bought the textbooks

Max is THE BEST. I wish I could take more classes with him. He's extremely approachable and passionate about teaching. Also, he gives out chocolate, which is an incentive on its own to attend his lecture. He has some off days when his jokes tend to be on the dry side, which can be awkward. But other than that, a must take at Cal
Max is one of the best professors I have had at Cal.  Always interesting and fun.  I never missed a lecture if I could help it.  His classes are a must if you are a political economy major!
Max is the best. Class isn't easy, but he somehow makes upper division microeconomics interesting. Tests are fair, which is good because they are 100% of the grade!
One of the best professors I have ever had at Cal.  Brilliant, clear, funny.  Highly recommended.  Gives out chocolate, as well, and says "The ideah heah" with a bit of a German accent.
Max makes economics fun, if that is possible. I hated economics before this class. He really is a great professor!
Max is absolutely amazing as a professor. He makes economics come to life...really. Oh, and great if you like chocolate!

Max is a fantastic teacher.  He is totally intuitive about whether the class is on top of each topic.  He is always available for any type of help you need.  What I loved was how accessible he was, not aloof like so many professors...just a cool guy who knows his economics inside out.
Great prof, very clear, interactive & entertaining, should be in the top 10.

Excellent professor; presents material in an extremely clear manner, and makes it pretty entertaining/interesting too!  Also super-nice and approachable, one of the best professors I've had at Berkeley, and supposedly the UN's got an interest in him as well
Great professor! Makes material easy and fun. Awesome class. i<3Max
he's a GREAT guy, not to mention LOTS of free chocolates :)
Nice teacher, class was easy. I would've gotten an A but my teammates in my group are liars and told her I did no work.

Prof is alright, but lectures weren't always engaging. In this group project class, I did most of the work, yet my concerns were forgotten. Grading was unfair when others did less work for the same grade. Excessive busy work. The class size is too large for the prof to manage effectively. I recommend other design courses such as info 213.

Prof. Au is one of the best professors I've had at Berkeley! She is super passionate about design and cares for her students. Her assignments and lectures really get you thinking about design in everyday products and life.
She also gives genuine feedback on group projects that can translate over to internships/jobs. Overall I highly recommend!
She is my favorite teacher at Cal. She made learning so fun and interactive (even in an online setting). This semester was a rough one online, but her class made my life so much happier.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor Au is a good professor overall; however, sometimes she struggles to explain material effectively. Because the class is one 3-hour lecture per week, there is a lot of homework. It's not particularly hard, but it is long and you have to put in a lot of work. Once you do though, you will be well rewarded and the grade will be easy.

Prof. Au is very organized and straight-forward. If you are down with group projects, punctual about many small assignments, and come to class every week -- you'll be good to go. She cares about her students and is always open to feedback. I really liked Design Methodology and learned a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Au is very knowledgeable and full of wisdom. Class is a heavy workload but not necessarily difficult. An interesting class! Its a little hard to understand her sometimes though  shes from Hong Kong. The GSIs were also pretty nit picky with grading and seemed like theyd knock off points wherever they could. Forced me to get a makerpass though!

One of the most dedicated professors I've ever had. Lectures can be abstract at times (he wants you to understand the intuition underlying each concept), but he holds tons of office hours and is always helpful. His hwk solutions are very detailed, and his ungraded "check your understanding" quizzes are thoughtfully made to help you succeed.

A little tough in person during lectures, especially if you raise your hand with the wrong answer... But overall it doesn't matter. His exam grading policy seems pretty chill, though MT 1 is still coming up so we'll see. I definitely think if he was an async professor he would be top professors OAT but unfortunately it's not an async class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Good for note-taking since he writes clearly and gives examples for each question. He is a generous grader with a solid curve on midterms and the final and tests are not graded too strictly. There are frequent tests and a heavy homework load, but he is very helpful in office hours, responds quickly to emails, and clearly cares about his students
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: When he speaks or writes anything it's in paragraphs and kind of reminds me of if ben shapiro was a lecturer especially when its 8 am. He does respond quickly to ed posts so thats a plus.

I love Sharma, I has not studied math in a long time but Sharma will always be there during OH  everyday to answer all of my questions. The midterm and the final content is the same with the homework and the practice questions bank with 1-2 a little bit harder questions but nothing too hard, everything has been covered at some point.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
Arun Sharma is very accessible during office hours and online (the man's sleep schedule is fried).
However, I didn't find OH too helpful as he gives very vague and small hints.

Ok lecturer; a bit boring, but he talks/writes in a conversational way, which I liked.

Pretty nice grader; lots of partial credit on problems!

His lecturing style of doing proofs and theorems is confusing initially, so I would recommend reading the textbook before class. You will also learn to solve most problems using examples from the textbook as well. Quizzes every week and two midterms. If you do poorly on one midterm, it's basically wraps for your grade as the final is difficult.

Generally, a great class to take, was very clear in the class instructions from day one, and is one of the most responsive teachers I have had. He responds to all questions in his Ed groups and has tons of extra office hours. It is a very easy class to take if you are self-directed, but be careful if you need extra hand-holding.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is not a great lecturer - learning from the textbook on my own was more helpful. But he is a very fair grader and gave a lot of chances to make up weekly quizes. Its not an easy subject but if you study you'll be fine.

Teaching style was absolutely horrendous. Will go too much into the theory of the mathematics thus not allowing for more in class examples and more thorough explanation of material, blasts through many sections this way. Found myself learning more by simply reading the textbook rather than lecture. Weekly quizzes. GSI can be helpful, worksheets no
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great Professor, cares so much about his class. Super fast response time.

The quizzes are much harder than midterm/final, really make sure you get a good GSI for this course. Class is graded fairly, curves applied when needed, and finals are pretty similar to past exams. Use the textbook, lectures aren't great, but other than that sharma is a great professor. Really study for quizzes, they can very easily tank grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Prof Sharma is caring and willing to help students, via ed or OH. HOWEVER, his teaching style was not for me (lots and lots of writing & proof concepts) and his testing format which banked a lot of points on T/F was frustrating. The weekly quizzes helped with learning & preparing for tests, however the final was difficult and makes/breaks a grade.

He's such a caring professor. He's lectures aren't the best, but accessible outside of class, office hours, emails, and ed posts. Replies to every single ed post very quickly and explains with detail. I recommend going to office hours but if his lecture style isn't for you, you should read the textbook. Sharma's so goated you should totally take it
very understanding
very caring and generous professor. Explanation could be clearer during lectures. A very lenient grader. Has lots of announcements with careful explanations of things. Pretty heavy on the tests.
Lectures can be confusing at times. Very clear and fair on all of his policies, and tests are very doable.

Goes thru lectures very fast, hard to keep up BUT records lectures so you can rewatch them. Super accessible and wants to help. Difficult to an extent but he tries to give you points on exams where he can so isn't too harsh of a grader. Good professor, and a makes little jokes sometimes. Also - I didn't get the textbook and was fine.

the rumors are true, his lectures aren't great, but he clearly cares a lot about his job and his students and making sure we learn. always active on ed to answer questions, office hours multiple days a week, very focused on fairness, just an upstanding guy. i wish everyone in the world was like him

I loved Professor Sharma and Math 54. The homeworks were sometimes pretty hefty but not unmanageable, with a quiz every week relating to the hw. His lectures were always extremely helpful. The first midterm was easy but I felt like mt2 and the final were slightly more challenging than anticipated. I would highly recommend 54 with sharma!

If you're new to a topic.. DON'T TAKE

bad lecturer, tests each week on the homework, final review sheets are so exaggerated and feel more overwhelming than intended for review. But caring and WILL respond to you no matter what (even at midnight...)

take if you don't care about lecture + familiar w/ topic

He's a very nice professor -- hosts lots of OH, responds to EVERYTHING on ED. In general, his lecture style didn't work well for me, it wasn't very straightforward so I ended up self-teaching and learning everything myself. Very kind guy and will answer any questions you have though.

Prof Sharma genuinely cares so much about his students. He explains things very thoroughly, and will always offer deeper explanations or answer any questions. Great teacher, helpful lecture notes, super easygoing and caring. best math teacher I've had.

Professor Sharma is a great professor. Perhaps, most notably through his sheer availability at the SLC or through ED. Some of his lectures were unhelpful/confusing, and I supplemented with the book. Midterms were surprisingly easy, on par with the difficulty of homework, if not easier. Sharma is also pretty funny and his reference sheet IS AMAZING.
He is extremely approachable, and his lectures are often funny and engaging without him trying too hard. He heavily curved the class and was quite understanding of the average on exams.

Professor Sharma is a great professor! He has plenty of office hours for help and responds to Edstem frequently (Even late at night). Homework load is reasonable and he curves exams if needed, providing review sheets and other resources to succeed. Lectures can be hard to follow, but he makes up for it in his dedication to help his students!

Very solid professor. Provides infinite resources and responds to questions on Ed at ungodly hours, but can be a bit hard to follow his lectures sometimes. Very accessible outside of class and creates detailed review papers for exams. Very flexible with homework and wants you to succeed.

Arun Sharma is the kindest, most genuine professor I've had at Berkeley. I've never met a professor who cares so much about his students before. He is so accessible and reliable, and he's a gift and privilege to the students! Thank you Dr. Sharma, for the way you go above and beyond for students is so rare to find in professors of large classes.

Absolute wonderful of a professor, super lenient on homework, responds to Ed at 3am in the morning, and quizzes and homeworks are well practiced / well covered, bonus questions test conceptual topics which is completely reasonable
Lots of homework but very generous with making it up and making up quizzes as well.
Very lenient and considerate for late work/missed quizzes

He was a difficult professor. He was not approachable and asking him questions was intimidating. His questions are not as reflective of the homework as one would be led to believe. Overall, be prepared to rely on yourself to understand the material -- do not count on him to be supportive.
Fantastic and kind professor. I couldn't read the board and he literally changed the way he teaches in order to accomodate me. I have nothing but high praise for him.
He's not a great lecturer, but the exams matched what we learned in homework and relatively easier than other math exams at Berkeley. Very responsive on ed and seems like a nice guy.

Super responsive on Ed and receptive to feedback. I thought the exams were fair relative to other classes I've taken at Berkeley. I don't remember his lectures being very useful and good, but the exams seemed reflective of what we learned in the homework and the practice tests given

I had him for both Math 1B and W54, and I received an A in both classes. He is a great and caring teacher, and I truly enjoyed his class. He gives a lot of supplemental material and responds to students' questions within minutes. His exams may be hard at times, but he prepares you well for them and compensates with good grade bin shifts.

He will respond to your question on EdStem within five minutes in the middle of the night (does he sleep?). I was unable to concentrate in his lectures, so even though I went to class, I had to teach myself all the content via the textbook. The exams are quite difficult, but at least there's a curve.

although u might not be able to tell he truly cares about his students but i just wish his lectures and his teaching style actually helped. strongly recommend seeing him OH as he is a lot more helpful there. the exams were not as bad as the hw and practices he gave us but i wish the daily hw and quizzes reflected the exams just a bit more

Class was pretty standard for a math class. Material is hard and lectures don't really help. Reccommend utilizing office hours and your GSI. Really generous on curves and is always really fair. Practice reviews for midterms/finals were pretty helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Poor, boring lectures. Amazing provision of resources. Office hours basically all day every day. Really lenient on late work (homework, quizzes, tests except for final). Very thorough explanations to all of his actions - curves, grade bins, etc. Always on Ed, answers every question. Most helpful + thorough professor, just didn't like his lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Honestly, great prof. He was extremely fair with his students, which is something you rarely see. His midterms were good and the final was not too shabby, and this is coming from someone who is not that good at math. I would take 54 with him again if I had to.
Awesome professor!
He has so much aura as a professor. The most fat curve and very generous grader. Just be sure to know your content.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Goated professor!!!!!

Professor Sharma cares so much about his students. While his lectures were somewhat hard to follow, You can tell he really wants us to succeed, he is incredibly responsive on Ed Discussion and is super helpful during office hours. Exams were fair. Prepare for weekly quizzes in discussion. Read the textbook. Go to office hours!!!
Very caring professor. Lectures can be hard to follow, and the exam review sheets aren't super helpful. Be prepared to do a lot of self-studying. Goodluck!

Always responds immediately to Ed questions and emails. Very long office hours, so very accessible during the day as well. Lectures are slow, in the sense that he is easy to understand and doesn't just launch information at you in painfully fast speeds. Very nice on grading, and seems very caring. Will be taking again for other math classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Extremely accessible & helpful! If you are unsure about any of the course content or have follow up questions, Prof Sharma is always willing to help either in OH or EdStem.

The tests were also also very fair and well balanced in terms of difficulty.

Sharma's lectures were incredibly difficult to follow; my grade literally improved after I stopped attending and studied with YouTube videos. Sometimes came off rude in office hours. Brutal quizzes, but fair exams. I did appreciate his communication and data analysis w/ curving. Take him if you don't gaf about lecture.

Professor Sharma is so bad at lecturing that even if you read a topic and get some understanding on it, after going to lecture you'll be more confused. I had no idea what was going on most of the semester. I will say Sharma is super responsive online and very communicative, and gave a really good curves though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very accessible - never seen a professor with so many office hours & responds on ed in like 5 mins. Caring and wants students to succeed- my goat. Tbh not the best lecturer, but for 16A should be fine if you've taken calc before or learn with textbook. Flexible grading (test weight % shifting options) and test content is fair with partial credit.

I took him for Math 16A and Math 54 and honestly will say this is the most fair, amazing and caring professor ever. He is extremely generous with his grade bins and honestly lives on Ed. If you can, I would take him. He is super knowledgeable about math and a goated professor

This was my first math class at Berkeley, and it taught me how to learn math the right way and how learning the fundamentals of a concept helps actually learn it. Lectures were hard to follow, but reading the book and practice problems made up for it. Very fair grader, generous curve at the end. Very prompt w responding on Ed (within minutes)

Sharma was by far the most accessible professor I've had so far—especially considering the sheer size of the class—but his lectures are unbearable. You're better off using the textbook to learn linear algebra, and finding another way to learn differential eqs, since the textbook was no help. Very fair grading though, & a fat curve on exams.

Professor Sharma is a great professor. He responds to Ed messages with unimaginable speed and he has many office hours. He provides extensive review packets for the midterms and finals and also worksheets that cover more conceptual aspects of the week's material. All in all Math 54 with professor Sharma was an good experience.

Although his lectures are quite dense and hard to follow, he overall is incredibly organized and easily acecssible outside of class via email or Ed. You can tell he really puts in the effort and cares about his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: One of the most caring professors, like he probably has the lowest Ed response time. Office hours wear also great, and I highly recommend going. Lectures weren't always helpful, but most were worth attending. Many helpful worksheets and resources to do well in the class.

Very fair professor. Lectures are ok, best if you already read the textbook before coming. Weekly quizzes vary in difficulty but overall ok. Midterms overall ok, curves them if they are too hard. The best thing about the class is the amount of resources he provides: study materials, responds instantly on ed/emails, even video guides. 100% recommend

He is a bad lecturer - he basically read straight from the textbook and at that point you might as well just read it. But he makes really fair and not too difficult tests and quizzes. He is super accommodating and places a good curve if it is needed.

I never attended class but was diligent with keeping up with the textbook. Linear algebra is quite intuitive if you don't cram. Sharma was very responsive over email and clearly cares about his students. He even connected with me on Linkedin! I wish I attended his office hours but I never did. My favorite technical course I have taken so far!

This man is an absolute GOAT. Replies quick to EdStems which makes it nice when you need help with HW or have questions about something. Midterms and finals are pretty reflective of the practice worksheet he gives before the tests. THIS MAN CARRYS THE MATH DEPARTMENT.

Professor Sharma is the absolute goat. He's caring and incredibly helpful. The exams and quizzes were fair. The homework was 100% doable. Only giving out around 20ish problems each homework assignment. He posts practice exams which are incredibly helpful (albeit a bit challenging). Overall the best math class I've had here at Berkeley.

The exams were super fair, and the review sheet was really helpful. There were plenty of office hours, and the professor was always helpful and truly cared about students. This class honestly healed my whole semester at Berkeley. An amazing professor!

Sharma has to be one of the most lenient professors at Berkeley. The lectures are recorded, and attendance for lectures or discussions is optional. He lets us make up late homework and quizzes for full credit, and the exams are very straightforward, with good curves. He talks a bit slowly, though, I would recommend watching lectures on 1.4x speed.

The absolute GOAT—nothing but the utmost respect for Prof Sharma. I didn't go to lecture and self studied (which is super doable btw) so I can't speak much on his lectures but he is unequivocally married to the game more than anyone I've ever seen. Most accessible prof ever and lit so understanding too i submitted literally everything so so late.
Hes my goat ifykyk. Hes helpful in office hours and is rly active on ED. Class actually made me learn and understand and everything felt very fair.

Professor Sharma was the most accommodating professor I've had so far! The effort he puts into the class is very apparent; he has office hours for six days of the week, is active on Ed, and responds to emails quickly. He may seem intimidating at first, but go to his office hours and you'll find that he's a super sweet and caring guy! Def recommend.

Not a good lecturer but is super fair. Going to OH and discussion section matters since the exams have some curveballs and it's important to be prepared for anything on his exams and to grasp the concepts. Once diff-eqs hit, I was completely lost and checked out LOL

Sharma the GOAT. Sharma is a very caring professor, always responsive on the ED Discussion, tons of office hours throughout the week. In my opinion, lectures weren't too helpful; honestly, you do most of the learning through reading the textbook and practicing by doing the homework. Tests were fair, and the tests that had lower averages got curved.

GOAT. Sharma is unlike any prof (let alone math prof) I've had at Cal in my 2 years so far. He is manic in terms of how organized and present he is. I don't know when he sleeps. He literally is on Ed (the forum for the class) 24/7. So kind, responsive and accommodating. Super fair course. Just do the weekly homeworks closely and you'll do well.

Sharma's lectures are very fast-paced and hard to follow. This class was very much self-taught; however, he offered a good curve at the end of the semester. There are quizzes every week along with two midterms and one final. The quizzes actually help to keep you on top of the coursework. I wouldn't take him again but he is not terrible.

Super caring prof, always accessible outside of class. Responds in seconds on ED.
The only bad thing is that his lectures aren't good at all :(. 

He doesn't have many resources, but seeing as this was his second semester teaching 54, this is understandable.

Basically is a self-study class, which is pretty difficult with a subject like lin-alg :(
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Anybody on here hating on Sharma have no idea how good they go it. I am not the perfect linear algebra student by any means but I actually ended up liking this class a lot more than I thought. Sharma is INCREDIBLY caring and wants you to succeed. Generous curves, fair grading policies, posts extremely clarifying content, responds within MINUTES

Sharma is cool and super active on ed but one of the WORST lecturers ive had. You'll basically be self-studying the entire course and his grading policy is subpar at best. He also gatekeeps the answer keys for his exam reviews under some weird assumption that its more beneficial to students, releasing it ~2 days before the exam, which really sucks.

Lectures r a bit difficult to understand if u don't love math, but he's the MOST caring/dedicated prof. Responds on ed instantaneously from 8am to 2am, right before hw's due. Holds tons of OH and at late times like 8-11pm before quizzes/deadlines. re-records lost lec vids and records hrs of exam review for us. fair curves if exams r difficult too!
Very difficult to understand and a difficult person to work with.

Best professor in the whole world. I've never met a professor who cares about their students more than Arun Sharma did for us. So accessible, so kind, genuinely the perfect teacher. Goes above and beyond in all aspects for his students. So much love for Prof. Sharma!!!! Thank you for being the best!

An effective professor at teaching Calc 1. However, lectures are fast-paced and there is a quiz every week in discussion. Wasn't too hard of a class and the homework definitely helps with exams. Lectures are not required but discussion is.

Grading is very lenient, generous curves on tests! However, be prepared to self-learn. He is pretty bad at explaining things in a way non-mathematicians can understand. Roughly 4 hours of homework a week, including the time you have to teach yourself everything.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Respected

reviews.comment: Sharma is an exceptional math prof, love how he answers edstem questions immediately no mater the time. Despite his lectures being content heavy and fast paced, it's easy to study your notes with how his lessons are organized. Lots of quizzes, prob once every week or so, and 2 midterms as per usual. GSI matters; do practice problems!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Honestly, his vibe is chill, grading is laid back, and he's easy to reach, but it's almost impossible to understan lectures unless you already know what he's talking about, unless you're a genius. Get ready to self-study the whole course, very disappointed with this class, since I prefer learning through the direct content, but its subpar at best.

The lectures focused more on what not to do than what to do and how to do it. Sharma's notes are challenging to understand and make little sense if you did not attend the lecture. The homework is entirely different from the quizzes and tests, and the worksheets are unhelpful. Be prepared to teach yourself the majority of the course.

Personally disliked his lecture style and how stubborn he was about any changes or improvements requested by his students. All of the visuals of his lecture were projected handwritten details in sharpie that were hard to read and went by too quickly to understand. GSIs described topics far better.
BEST RESIDENTIAL ASSISTANT EVER

Sharma was genuinely such a kind professor. You could really tell that he cared about helping his students succeed (responding to edstem posts at 3 in the morning, tons of office hours). I will say that his lectures felt a bit off topic at times, but he was very generous with curves and I had a great time in his class.

He cares a lot about his students. He explains concepts well and replies to emails in a very timely manner. Simply put, he is the best mathematics professor I've had here in Berkeley. He's extremely caring and flexible when it comes to extensions and such. Love him!

It's 1:37am in Berkeley right now and he's still responding to EVERY single EdStem question in under 5 minutes. There's hundreds of questions coming in everyday and he somehow finds the time to instantly respond to everything. I haven't seen a single TA outside of my discussion section so far because he's absolutely ahead of the curve. God bless

Your experience in this class will depend on your prior experience in calculus. As someone who had not taken calculus before, this was difficult and lectures were bad. I reached out to Sharma many times to seek help and he told me there was nothing I could do. I spent every second on this class and was able to get a B after an amazing curve.

pretty iconic guy. very very very accessible outside of class. he's very technical and has an interesting way of speaking which may take a little bit of getting used to. scans pdfs of the textbook for hw so you don't need to buy a textbook
Material was very easy. All just pre calculus and basic calculus. Lectures are split up very randomly. Unc responds instantly on edstem.

Clearly cares about his students, has office hours 6 days of the week. Also gives good feedback although he completely roasts your work while doing so. But I learned a lot from him. His lectures are a little confusing and you might have to go to the textbook to figure it out. But if you ever have any questions he will make it clear for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I would definitely take a class with Sharma again! As long as you read the textbook, go through the examples, and review solutions for each quiz, you'll get an A. Do the worksheets before each quiz, the midterm reviews, and the final review, because you'll have some problems on the test/quiz that are almost exact. Also the curve was BEAUTIFUL.

Really does care about his students but lectures make no sense and feel very disjointed.  Always responds to Ed posts within an hour so very accessible but just lectures in general were not helpful at all.  Exams were not too difficult though and were quite fair.

The lectures were not that helpful. As someone who went into this class without knowing calculus, I found it hard to keep up with lectures because he tends to explain things as if they were common understanding. This was an average class; you could do well if you put effort into studying. You have to buy a textbook but you can live without it tbh.

Lectures are mid; somewhat circuitutious reasoning and unfinished examples. Positive: lec notes posted daily & instant ED responses till 2am. Fair grading by GSIs. Personally slow at math, hw took 6-8hrs a week. Going to GSI hours and disc (Will fisher is TOP) helps a ton. Weekly quizzes are inconsistent difficulty wise, but curved.

Wasn't best lecturer. Focused too much on background instead of how to solve problems. Examples were often left solved halfway and were rushed. However, he does care as he responds within 5-10 minutes on ED (often misinterpreted questions though) and made hours of final review videos. Quiz every Wednesday discussion GSIs graded terrible.

Kind professor. Rambles on Ed a little but info gets across. Not the best lecturer BUT PLS GO TO LECTURE. I never took calculus in hs, so this class was rough. Homework took me 6+ hrs to complete, struggled on quizzes, exam review sheets, and exams themselves. Midterms had like a 5 pt curve but final curve was a bit heavier. Thank god I passed.

Love Sharma!!! I don't think hes the best at lecturing, but is super nice and accessible w/a TON of office hours and responds to Ed discussion quickly. If u took calc before, class should be pretty easy but if not, u might have to study more on your own. weekly quizzes, 2 midterms, 1 final (no calc use on tests) w/flexible grading scale/drop quiz.

VERY GENEROUS CURVE!
- Sometimes your grade might get curved down based on the the grading of your GSI

- However, I feel like the lecture and notes didn't really help and I was better off self-studying from the Organic Chemistry Tutor.

reviews.comment: If you've NEVER TAKEN CALCULUS and can take 1A with Paulin, I say do it. 16A with Sharma was all self-study, lectures were confusing. Lots of office hours, but not very helpful. Made things harder than needed, like 90 question final review. Gave great extensions and replied to emails late at night, nice guy. I'm very thankful I passed with a C.

Caring and understand his students. Always ready to answer your questions! Replying emails even at 3 am. When you feel stressed for any reason, just ask him for a homework extension and everything will be fine. Healed my state of mind at Berkeley.

Not a math person but he's a very fair prof who cares about his students. Go to his OHs, and come into this class w calculus experience in high school. Lectures helped me avoid pitfalls and I found that he was quite thorough unlike some other reviews say. Work hard and just do the homework problems, make friends in this class to study together!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: lectures don't really help with the material, he usually rambles off about random things. learn to study on your own. only things that determine your grade are the weekly quizzes, 2 midterms, and a final. tests can be hard but the curves are amazing

Professor Sharma really cares about you, like genuinely, he's a good person. It's just that his lectures are insanely difficult to follow. Go to his office hours, you'll actually learn something. Don't fret, his curves are usually very generous -- I thought I was going to get my first ever C, but the cutoffs were very nice I ended with a B.

Curves! But you will have to work for the grade you want. Sharma is very reasonable most of the time. It is clear he cares for his students with how available he is for OH and on ED. Personally, lectures didn't help so I read the textbook and attended SLC review sessions. Also a hilarious guy imo, with his sassy way of talking/typing (compliment)!

Sharma is very caring and accessible outside of class. If you have the patience to self teach yourself the material, then you should be able to get by. reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I struggled in this course for sure, the quizzes and midterms were challenging to a point but very accessible outside of class- on ED and gmail. always had office hours and even stayed till 11 pm just to answer questions. however be ready to learn from the textbook. wouldn't take again but arun definitely cares.
hard tests and quizzes but amazing curve, he is very caring for his students

For a 3-unit math class, this was definitely unnecessarily tough. Review worksheets don't match exam content, and lectures are borderline useless. Many students have taken Calc AB or BC before so you have to work twice as hard to offset the curve if you haven't. Sharma is a very nice professor though, and makes himself very accessible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Honestly wasn't the biggest fan in the beginning but he's extremely accessible outside of class (office hours and ed) and genuinely cares about the success of his students! I found his lectures to be unhelpful but I also had prior knowledge from calc BC so I just used YouTube videos. Grade bins lowered, quizzes curved, regrades answered promptly :)

This was a pretty tough class but the amount of practice made up for it like the review worksheets and the even more extensive answer keys to go with them. They are a good gage of the types of questions we may see on exams and Prof is always active and helping on Ed! Lectures were pretty useless but overall not a bad class.

Wasn't a big fan of Sharma at first, but realized he genuinely cares about students and listens to feedback. His grading is fair, exam prep is thorough, and final reference packet is super generous! He's also very accessible, with late-night/weekend OH and quick Ed responses. His lectures aren't for everyone, but he's a helpful and organized prof!
Great teacher! He listens to his students and

Terrible at teaching during lectures, focuses more on what not to do than what to do. Does not explain his steps. Especially if you didn't take calc before, this is a self-study course. Responds quick on edstem, provides practice worksheets & past quizzes/tests w/ solutions & explanations. Great office hours, overall very accessible. Caring person.

he is very good with responding to questions and is SO active on ed but this class is hard if you have no calc background and don't devote enough time to it! also, he goes SOOOO fast in lectures it can be a little difficult to keep up - do not skip lecture or you will fall behind!

Time consuming/Prepare to teach yourself. Lectures are boring and hard to understand. He does not go in depth how to solve problems.
