take attendance every class, the grading is lenient, funny and clear lecture, bearable readings also, but do go to class with the readings read.

Took this class last year.  Very sweet lady, really cares about her students.  During lecture, goes off on wild tangents and rarely makes it through her own outline.  Coursework is light, but reading is exceptionally dense.  Attendance is 1/3 of your grade.

Nice person, but not a good teacher. Left wing radical feminist that only gives a biased and incoherent view of social theory. Lectures can be mildly interesting, but she is not at all interested in hearing differing viewpoints. As a liberation theologian, she is constantly trying to use her interpretation of the Bible to prove some point.
shes amazing, take her

I had to take this class for ISF & thought I hated philosophy, but Ipsen turned me around. She makes the subject interesting, engaging, applicable to modern life, and fun. Her lectures brighten my day (thought I'd never say that about ANYthing school-related, but she's that good). 1 midterm, 1 final = pretty easy =]
Avaren is the absolute best teacher at Cal. She is very accessible, kind, caring and just simply an awesome person.

Avaren's an amazing teacher.  I've never had a professor so interested in my understanding of the subject.  She goes above and beyond the call of duty, and really, REALLY knows her social theory.  Almost too well, as she can bowl you over with a lot of info if you keep pressing her.  GREAT teacher.  Highly recommended!
Great  Prof.! She has a very interesting way of presenting social theory.  Take her class if you can!

Avaren is one of the most accessible teachers I've ever had.  She' completely available for questions, and even had everyone over to her house after the midterm.  The exams aren't easy but she's an understanding grader, and her lectures are clear with good examples.  She's also super nice and works really hard to make sure that everyone "gets it".

She is a harsh grader, but if you meet with her, she will help a lot, and get you a good grade. I think my writing improved a lot by taking her class. Also, make sure you come to class prepared. She will get mad if you don't have your book or if there is no/very little participation throughout the class. She is pretty particular but fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: stay away from her class and find an easier r1a class. tough grader, feels more like a highschool english class. gets angry if you forget your book or when the class does not want to participate
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: The professor is really nice and adorable. The content was interesting. She gives amazing critiques. Readings can be heavy some weeks. Compared to other R1A classes, there are a lot of essays. The class is pretty difficult though and definitely not an easy A. However, my writing improved so much!!!

I absolutely loved Ms A! Your grade depends on your (around 7) essays, but she basically tells you what you should write if you ask. The readings were pretty short and all incredibly interesting. This class is based around art, so if this interests you I definitely recommend it. If you PARTICIPATE a lot, she will seriously adore you, so talk a lot!

Hard teacher, but VERY helpful. My writing has improved more than I would have ever imagined. We write 4 essays and a final essay. There is a lot of reading, but the books are enjoyable. Go to Ms. A for office hours and she helps writing your essay so much! She is a very smart woman. OH and don't forget to raise your hand a lot in class.
She's a very tough grader and gives A LOT of homework. It is difficult to write exactly as she wants. I discussed my papers with her, yet I still received a pretty bad grade...
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Ms. A is a nice teacher. She's strict on essays meeting certain criteria and her temper swells when the class is silent to her questions, but she's alright. It's unfortunate that she can't take criticism for her teaching and grading style and often holds the fact that she grades papers over your critiques. Sad.
The class is interesting and thought provoking. You definitely have to work hard to get an A. Read the texts before class... Go to office hours. She provides a lot of helpful feedback.

Class itself is interesting and the concepts are cool to deal with, however the essay prompts are tough. You also need to write essays her way. Forget about any sort of writing style you had in the past. She's a tough grader to please. Go to office hours to figure out how she wants her essays done.
showing up on the class everyday ,still get the participation grade On C?the most ridiculous teacher I ever see.
She knows the texts well, but to get a good grade you have to write what she wants you to write. I hated this fact and thus didn't enjoy the class at all.

What a piece of work. English was my favorite subject until I took this class my freshman year. There is no negotiating around her opinions of what your literary interpretations are, and how essays should be structured.  She stifles creativity, yelled at us in French, and often dressed inappropriately (see-through tops) on the job. Unprofessional.

Pretty easy if you get on her good side.  Will tell you how to fix your essays in office hours but just make sure that you write what she wants you to. She has very strong opinions about the material and you will do well if your opinions are the same as hers

Read several art theory essays and three books and watched a film. Grade based on essays: 3 short, 2 long, and 1 extra long final one. You get an optional extra credit one. Try to be as analytical as possible and stay away from summary or the best that you'll get on a paper is somewhere in the B range. Go to office hours to get help if you need it.

An incredible English teacher.  She is very funny and absolutely adorable!  Very endearing personality, and very clear and understanding.  If you can analyze text, like thinking about the "meaning" of things, or are a good writer, this class will be very fun, and is an easy A.

Prof. Angevine really loves English, and therefore, have strong opinions about them. Class isn't too hard if you read books and write 4 essays for class. Easy to talk to, tries to help students improve. Not an easy A, but fun to take if you are interested in literature.
The class isnt too easy. Hard to get an A. There are four 4-6 pages essays based on four novels. Have to be really "analyical" in writing the papers. Go to her office hours would be very helpful.

i agree with everyone. she doesnt like it when you go against what she believes so make sure you write what she says... which usually makes more sense than what other people believe. she is really nice and is approachable. if you dont get whats going on then go to office hours. overall, i enjoyed the class. graded on improvement.

She was not a very fair grader, she basically grades according to how your views align with hers and if they do you can expect a B of better, but if they don't then it is clearly reflected in the grade of the paper regardless of how well it is written. Make sure to get her views if you are in this class for the papers.

The reading material for this class is interesting.  There are only four 4-6 page essays you need to write and she grades on improvement.  This class isn't too easy though because in order to get a good grade, you have to write on her ideas.  Just make sure to go to her office hours and write the way she thinks and you will be fine.
Easy, awesome teacher.  Be sure assignments are done before class...she really hates it.

Though I did very well in this course, I can't say it was enjoyable. Be prepared to write papers concerning HER views on the novels, not your own. For an English class, I expected more creative guidance and less teacher interference. Still, Angevine is extremely intelligent, so atleast a dunce won't be teaching you.
She is a great professor. Office hours and email are the ways to get help on your essays. She responds quick and provides great guidance to your papers. However, I would say this class is difficult.
Excellent teacher, though not that easy
study hard. read ahead. discuss in class. sometimes shes cranky.

Amazing professor. He breaks down the previous reading in his lecture, making it very comprehensible and fostering good class conversation. Clearly very passionate about rhetoric in a way that inspires.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very cool class that involved several fieldwork assignments throughout semester and a capstone from that. Selected readings all tied into course and relevant to fieldwork and capstone. Had to do readings before class (participation grade) but he essentially synthesizes them during lecture. First rhetoric class and would definitely recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This was my second course with Atkinson, and not only was the content material incredibly interesting, relevant, and engaging, but he also brought in guest speakers and made the class very interactive. He is accessible outside of class and provides incredible feedback. If you can take his courses, do it! He is the reason I am a rhetoric major now!
Very interesting lecturer, only a few writing assignments for the semester

Nathan is one of the best professors I have had. He is funny, an engaging lecturer, gives helpful and constructive feedback, and consistently maintains a well-paced course. His readings are incredibly diverse and interesting, and he is flexible with students who need extra help. If you get a chance to be his student, don't miss out on it!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Every time Prof. Atkinson talks, you can tell that he chooses his words specifically and with the intention of furthering your understanding of the material--he's incredibly smart, and if you participate and do the reading he will genuinely help you develop as a scholar and rhetorician.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Cool guy. Class solely analyzes readings. Only 2 written assignments so read & participate! Focuses on how/why ppl say things certain ways in tech, & how in modern media, AI & algorithms can prevent us from seeing diff ways of thinking by showing us info based on prior browsing history. Some readings are really dense which make discussion a bore
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She is a very soft-spoken and down-to-earth person who responds to your questions very quickly and cares about her students and their learning. The lectures are also interesting, covering a wide range of topics that are fun to explore. There was an in-class essay midterm and a take-home final. Overall, it's a pretty light class for breadth.

It was difficult to catch everything she said during lecture. Presentations only had pictures, no words or bulletin points at all. Lectures arent recorded so if you miss something it's hard to catch up. You get 10 points taken off every absent, even if you email before hand. Very unclear and overall unorganized class. Hard to understand the topics
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Gupta is one of the most intelligent and knowledgeable professors that I have had the pleasure of taking. Her courses are built around intense readings, lectures and long discussions. She tends to be soft-spoken in the classroom so make sure to ask the hard questions and really dive into the material. Do that, the class will be unforgettable.

Her PowerPoints were riddled with typos and errors. Lectures were mediocre. She is confrontational with students and is not receptive to student participation. To be honest she is disrespectful to her students and you don't learn much in class.
I am glad I took this class and still go to her for advice. Go to office hours - she is very helpful and accessible

Great class and would recommend, you can definitely tell that she's passionate and knowledgable of the course material. Don't miss lecture, the powerpoints are online, but are mostly made up of images. Hard to catch up if you fall behind on lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: It is a loaded course. You have to learn the subject matter, do a research project, and manage portfolios in addition to homeworks. but it was worthed. Prof. Atamturk is very knowledgeable. Recommended.
Pathetic structure, organization, and teaching. Steer away while you can!
One of the best profs I had at Berkeley!
You will be prepared for about 60% of the material you see on the exam. Good luck.

162 with Atamturk is much more difficult than with other professors but I REALLY enjoyed this class. The material is fun and Atamturk really makes you think. He won't spoon-feed anything to you and that's what I liked about him.
It is a difficult class. But professor explains everything very clearly. I liked him a lot.

He is not helpfull at all. He is just a rude jerk guy. I think the chairmen of the faculty shoulk kick him out of the collage. Every one should know that to be a good insturacture is not enough to know a lot he also should understand people and have a good relation with them.
He does not understand when students struggle.
Very well

He can come off as a real jerk, but he is the best professor I have had at Berkeley. His lectures are great at explaining the material. I never had to crack the book to learn the material because he explained it so clearly.
Easy professor, very helpful, likes all students. Happy to accomodate struggling students in a friendly non-judgemental manner.
he flat out says that he expects you to spend all of your time on his course. wtf!

this guy is a tool. he thinks he knows everything. homework gets hard towards end of the semester, midterm was really long but do-able, the final wasn't too bad, but his grading scheme is very out of wack. try to avoid this guy.

the class seems really easy but professor atamturk can just make it really hardthrough his tests. his tests were not that bad but he really should be giving more time for his tests. ace the homework and come extra early for the tests.
The midterm's average is 65. Very hard midterm but final turns out ok. Math intensive. Project required
Midterm was too long. Final was OK. HW in the beginning is easy but gets much more involving at the end. Most of it you can just read from the book.

He gave intuitive explanations of the material in class and was overall a good professor.  His midterm was long (though not exceedingly difficult) and 4/5ths of his final was manageable.  I'd recommend him.
No Comments

Great professor. Funny, approachable, helpful. Motivated the material with illustrations, brief discussions of applications, and intuitive thinking. Highly recommend him. His tests, although interesting & fair, were on the difficult side.

One of the best professors I've had. Crystal clear explanations; very helpful illustrations of abstract content and methods for thinking about problems. Homework was very helpful. Very well-written tests that were fairly graded. And near the end of the semester he even began making jokes. I give this professor an A+, and would highly recommend him.

Very clear, sharp, on point and engaging. He lectures from the book, or rather explaining the book, which is good when the book itself is so dense/difficult/good.  (This also minimizes the need to take notes.)  He tries to make his tests fairly challenging--sometimes everybody gets crushed.  But upper upper div curves can be more forgiving.

HE'S GREAT! I didn't get the subject at all, but he walked me through everything; really nice and understanding about personal issues. If you have a problem, LET HIM KNOW!! He's always helpful. I couldn't make his office hours, so he would always accommodate, either coming super late at night or on the weekends. Very clear, and nice when grading.

BEST gsi I've had at cal! super helpful & funny! even if i came late he always stayed with me after his OH & helped me with my questions. really cool, and easy to talk to. just be honest with him and tell him if you're confused, and he'll make sure you'll do really well. Tells you what he wants for a perfect A. Highly recommend any course with him!

DON'T LET HIM BE YOUR GSI. Figure out WHO the GSI will be for the class before taking it!! This guy is a jerk. He doesn't care about the students and his grading is completely random. He barely gives ANYONE an A (I talked friends about their grade). AVOID AT ALL COSTS. He's also really anal about everything ie. he's picky about expectations.

He's a hardass. Doesn't really care about the student at all -- just wants you to stop bugging him. Kind of arbitrary grading: he just goes off of his gut feeling in giving you a grade which is not entirely fair. He's very clear in his expectations but I didn't really like him just because he doesn't care for the student much at all.
Very Knowledgeable and approachable. Sometimes can be intimidating, but once you get to know him, he is very cool.
head reader for gregor, not a hardass, do the work and you'll get an A
gregor's head gsi. go to his office hours. tells you what he wants for perfect A. scary to approach, but in emails he's cool

I have never had Atul as a professor but he is more of a professor than the vast majority I had at UC Berkeley. He's an exemplary teacher and mentor and is truly invested in the growth of his students. He doesn't care about the test. He cares about the value and perspective added. I would highly highly recommend.

Atul will not be like any professor you've had before, which will be a great or a horrible thing depending on you, the student. Get ready to be challenged and on top of your game for each class. Don't let the political incorrectness offend and speak up if you disagree. You will be shamed or praised but you will never forget the class or dinners.

Singh is passionate about the subject matter beyond words and knows much about philosophical thought and  historical traces, which are the real drivers of his courses relevance to politics and economics. I did not 'need' this course but I took personal the abrasive manner in which he challenges the students to question our world.
rhetorically magnificent and an intellectual model

Atul's class is one of the best classes that I have taken at UC Berkeley. Although Political Economy 101 was difficult to understand, Atul was helping and caring each student at his best. He tried to connect ancient and modern political economists' idea to the current world economy and politics. I highly recommend this class.

PLEASE DO NOT drop or run away after the first class. Atul might come off as intimidating at first, but you will discover that he's just trying to get you to care about and question the world. He wants you to connect the dots and make sense of the things you see, hear, read and learn. DO NOT use jargon. Be bold in your writing. And dare to know.

This is more than a class but a great journey to open up ur mind and see through things more clearly, "Make Sense of the World", as Atul said. He doesn't care about the grades, but more importantly, he cares a lot about what you think. As long as you are open minded, as long as you dare to know, you will get a lifetime inspiration from this class!

PE 101 lectures with Atul and Ti have easily been the most engaging I've attended at Cal. They teach in a way that helps you make sense of the readings, PE, and the world. They check in with students to gauge their interest & understanding. No memorization & regurgitation here; they care more about your understanding & learning!

Atul is one of the most energetic professors, i have ever met. His lecture is largely based on discussion and he really likes discussing with students. if you have any questions about the contents of the class, he can give you great inspiration to solve the issues. It's wonderful class and it's helpful to understand how the world is going on.

Atul and Ti together makes quite a team. I definitely consider this class as that one class that has influenced me so much in my entire college education. It's challenging in so many ways and you got out of this class realizing education has meant something else to you - not just about chasing grades but really about making sense of the world.
He is very bright and full of knowledge. Very aware of current events and connections to what has occurred in the past. Looks for a deeper connection with his students.
He is a great professor to listen to, even if you are not taking his class. Every class had  a new topic in which he connected to the actual words, not just the textbook world.
Inspiring. Class was a wild ride.

This was one of the best classes I have taken at Cal. Atul Singh not only challenges his students to think critically, but also pushes them to express their ideas clearly. I am a better writer and a better speaker thanks to Atul's class. Atul's lectures are engaging and his peculiar sense of humor is entertaining.

Atul Singh and Ti Ngo are intelligible, engaging, and extremely helpful! The idea of learning is not treated as a mindless duty in this class because we actually talked about "what's going on" and how it does affect every single one of us. Be prepared to listen in lectures, but also, to argue about the issues facing our world, and "ALL THATJAZZ!"

I have attended lectures by at least 50 different professors in various topics but this one is by far the best. Do not take his course in your first semesters or your other courses will become too boring. Most complicated definitions will be explained in the simplest terms. Absolutely no jargon allowed. If "you dare to know" this is the right one.

Hands down, Professor Singh's class is one of the best I've taken at Berkeley. He is a professors who actually cares about teaching in opposite to those who are solely focused on research. Don't be intimidated by Atul's extroverted style, you will see that he is really cool and smart . Also, the GSI Ti Ngo, is one of the best GSI's I've ever had.
Great lecturer like I've never seen before. This guy makes you think instead of read and repeat. I've never learned so much in such a short time!

This class challenged me to rethink my opinions about the world. Prof Singh will push you to critically look at social and political theory. I loved how engaged he was with his students; he makes an effort to get to know everyone and will constantly push you to make the most out of his class. He can be a bit scattered but is good with feedback.

This guy will rock your world. Be prepared to challenge your assumptions and think critically. The professor is very unorthodox but stick with it. You will find this to be the best class you've ever taken. Atul is also happy to discuss career options and grad school with each of his students. If you have the opportunity, take this class!!!

Prof. Atul is an intelligent professor who values your learning experience more than simply giving you a grade. Be prepared to read and participate in class! My reader was a very fair grader and both Prof. Atul and our reader gave great feedback when anyone needed help! Don't be intimidated by his enthusiasm, he's just passionate about teaching!

This is for AFRICAM 159!!
She takes attendance every class, but has not impacted my grade. Grades until the very last week of school, so kind of frustrating when the instructions of the assignments are vague. However, there were not that many assignments. Likes to talk about her experiences a lot, so it can be droning. No office hours.

Absolutely terrible and disorganized. I had to do everything myself with absolutely no help from her. She graded papers late, gave feed back late, so now im spending Christmas writing an essay. There is no clear rubric or criteria, grades are due and she only graded 2 assignments. She is so frustrating and I recommend not wasting your time.

Doesn't grade any work until the end of the semester. Unspecific work. Does nothing in class. Learned nothing. Waste of tuition money. Only 1-2 actual work without instruction. Our final essay's instructions were literally to write about anything around 3-4 pages. Such a waste of time and money.

One of the best classes I've taken at Berkeley but Aya leaves a lot to be desired. The class was so great because of the peers and I highly recommend taking this class yet there were a handful of people in this class that had difficulties and struggles with Aya. She tries to come off somewhat radical but she's honestly kinda phony.

I wouldn't recommend P4P for anyone who is an experienced poet. The guidelines for poetry are strictly enforced, and they produce a fairly juvenile brand of writing. If you're any good at poetry, apply for a workshop. Aya mostly reads off the slides in lecture, and the course doesn't go in depth into the issues of different minorities.

It's a great class, but requires a lot of work for an AC class and is tailored to minorities. If you are a cis-white person, I would not recommend taking this class to fulfill the AC requirement because the assignments ask to write about a lot of personal stuff and oppression and you will struggle. Also does not hold office hours
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Super passionate lecturer, although lectures were oftentimes boring and read directly off a slide. If you simply pay attention in class and do what they tell you to, it's an easy A.
Incredible teacher, incredible class.

Everyone involved with P4P acts like they're so out to fight oppression in all forms, but in reality it's filled with politics.  If you're good the other students try to knock you down on their way to the top in their quest to become famous writers. My STP was manipulative, others harass you to feel powerful.  Aya is fair weather like all the rest.

Like others have said, Aya doesn't really do anything in the class, but from what I understand, she does decide how the class is run. As a warning, the class is a lot of work...way too much in my opinion. If you like poetry, though, it can be fun too.

Aya will be on maternal leave for spring 2010, but this class will still run the same because it's mainly taught by STPs, student teach poets. Overall this class was alot of fun, but the lectures got repetitive and dull near the end. You will hear alot of "isms," but i recommend this class for those who have any interest in poetry.

Aya is one of the absolute best teachers I've ever had. I took P4P spring of 2008 and was in her section. She's hilarious, brilliant, a funny and cool teacher, and really pushes her students to think critically and write really well. I can't recommend her enough. She's low drama and super approachable.
P4P is an amazing class. I highly recommend it. The class is really done by the STPs, and all the STPs are good people.

The course was fairly challenging, but with proper studying success is achievable! There is a lot of content to study before exams but the lowest one was dropped. Professor was great in lectures but a lot of the slide information felt redundant. Nothing was unfair though!

this class is recorded, only required attendance in section. the review made on may 2025 is false. GSIs held outside review sessions & proctoring of exams. straightforward with exam content & practice questions scattered through lectures easy A+

no unprofessional comments made but students talked abt bombing her reviews in the class evaluations :/
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof A is great! but often takes a step back and lets the GSI's run the class. I've never been in a class where it felt that instructors did not want students to succeed. The exams are more difficult then necessary, and unprofessional comments made before the exams make it more stressful. I'd only recommend this course if the structure improves.

i think this class is very interesting.
before taking this class, i've never thought about doing research in personality psychology, but Prof. adyuk makes the class awesome!

Be ready to read at least 2 articles every week-- you will need them to be well-prepared for lectures and weekly discussions (take detailed notes about them, they will appear on the exams). I found her demeanor to be direct-- she spoke so straight forward in the lecture. I thought she was fair, also she does not provide a study guide.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Great psych class Professor is very fair when it comes to assignments. She grades on quizzes and worksheets, the quizzes you can take an unlimited amount of times until you get 100% . Attendance isn't mandatory as she records her lectures

Straightforward, solid psych requirement to take. Often references published studies in lecture and on exams so be prepared to interpret graphs and results (she explains them well though). Overall pay attention in lecture (section is also a really helpful resource too, as they summarize the week's lectures) and you'll do great!

Exams and quizzes were fair. Lectures were clear and comprehensive. Prof Ayduk was super understanding (our first exam had a low average so she let students drop their lowest exam grade). There are weekly quizzes, three exams including the final, and a few extra assignments - as long as you pay attention in lecture and do the work you'll get an A.

Ayduk is a decent lecturer, but the class itself is pretty surface-level. She's good at explaining the material in a clear and coherent manner, and if you read the lecture-relevant articles prior to class, you'll be perfectly prepared for lectures (and the class as a whole). Her office hours are very helpful and she's a very kind person.

Not sure what the amazing reviews are about; I think she's an ok lecturer. She reads off the slides and post the power points online, so you can pretty much skip class. You need to read a lot of empirical articles for this course; which makes it annoying.

She is a great professor. Funny, interesting, and very knowledgeable. The class became more interesting as the semester progressed, mainly because she was more animated during lectures. Definitely recommend this class with her. You will learn a lot about yourself and others.
Go to lecture and pay attention and you will get an easy A. Great professor and wonderful woman.

She is great! She is very knowledgeable and seems very approachable. The tests are not hard if you read & attend lectures. I learned a lot in this. Not only about the subject but also about myself. Her research is interesting. She covers all theorists pretty well, shows she is a reasonable person. Some ppl only like to put their view out. Recommend

Pretty good professor. I came into the class thinking it would be boring but she managed to make it interesting and fun. Tests were very fair. No complaints! Definitely recommend taking this course with her, especially if you are not very interested in Personality Psychology.

This class became more interesting as it progressed. The first test I didn't do well because I didn't realize its all about memorization. Focus on the slides and look over the study guide to see what info you need from the book. Should ensure an A.
The class is well organized but it requires too much memorization. Overall, the class is an easy A class if you can memorize all the slides.
This class was an easy A. It was REALLY boring. She didn't seem interested in the subject and showed little enthusiasm for teaching.

Not very engaging prof but she is very nice. You must study quite a lot for the exams and by a lot, i really mean a lot. There's a lot of memorization for this course, esp of experiments. The topics covered are relatively interesting, but you def don't delve into subjective aspects of your own personality. Overall, study hard and do well.
I thought the class was boring... eventually I changed the grading option to PNP. Got a P but didn't learn anything interesting.

Lectures very straight forward, though attendance is kind of necessary because she goes over a lot of research data that are later on in the midterms. No papers, and midterm grading scale is lenient. Overall, an interesting class with lots of memorization and common sense. Textbook reading wasn't really necessary,midterm based off of lectures.
Personality psych is very easy; all you need to do is memorize the lecture slides. The slides can be densely packed with information though, so lectures may run quite quickly.
Good Professor. This class was relatively unstressful and easy, but it was sort of boring. Prof Ayduk was very approachable and helpful during office hours.
very easy professor. Just memorize her lecture slides and you'll be fine. Only 3 exams, no paper or anything! Ended up with an A+ without going to class =)

I really enjoyed taking Prof. Ayduk's class. She always comes to class well prepared and ready to teach. Her expectations are very clear and her tests are based on what what she covers, no tricks. She also very sweet.

Very clear power point notes available before class. She goes through them fast enough to keep things interesting, but not too fast and will stop to clarify questions. Very sweet and approachable. Fair tests--pretty easy if you study the powerpoints from class. I learned a lot.
Class was interesting....she reads the overheads very fast though....overall...pretty good teacher!
I enjoy every lecture to the max with Dr. Ben-Yishai. She inspires and motivates all of her students in a creative manner.

She was really helpful in office hours-- go to them!! Her class really helped me learn how to write a thesis and essay. She grades on improvement so if you get A's from the start you're making it harder for youself.  the literature and theme she chose was so-so. I think she's in Israel but if she ever comes back, i recommend her class for R1A/B

I really enjoyed this class. 5 papers: 3 original, 2 revised. GO TO OFFICE HOURS. They were SO helpful - she is very receptive, encouraging, insightful. Come with ideas and she will give you so much direction. Grades fairly and on improvement. Work hard on your essays because improvement is key to getting an A.

Doesnt put herself out there for you, doesnt care about your success. A significant number dropped. She presents the material in a bland yet organized way, makes people coming to lectures for participation credit. Run away from her course.

Just a lecturer at Cal. Ridiculously tough grader. Puts hella equations on the board and just expects us to memorize them all. Lets you bring a cheat sheet to tests BUT THERE ARE SO MANY EQUATIONS. I would say the best way to pass this class is to be Chakravartula herself, because no one knows what she's thinking or what is important.

She seems like a nice and caring professor, at first. She is a harsh grader, often taking off half-credit for minor mistakes. I got average on the first midterm, well above average on the second midterm and final, nearly perfect lab score, did all my homework, and ended with a B

At first glance, she seems to be a nice, caring professor. Wrong move, buddy. Although her lectures are clearly organized, she doesn't provide students with notes, and she structures the class so students have no feedback on their performance before exams. Also her tests are graded to give students half credit if they make calculator errors. AVOID

This class was pretty interesting, and i feel like the topics are useful for industry. The tests in the class, however, are tough to prep for. It often comes down to how much you can fit on the cheat sheet. She sometimes puts up equations during class that she doesn't explain, but are on the exams. Individual lab reports can get very tedious.

Chakravartula is the worst professor I have had at UC Berkeley. She made an extremely difficult class even worse. The lectures are a scramble to copy down a million formulas with no  logical derivation and attempt to apply them on an exam. The exams are a culmination of the most random and difficult material from the lectures.
No Comments
Ayla is a very caring person and is always willing to help outside of class.

Ayla is an extremely caring and dedicated teacher. She knows the Turkish language, culture, and people very well, and is enthusiastic about giving her students a good understanding of it. She teaches a well-balanced class, she expends lots of effort, and is always available outside of class to help.

Professor Seraj is incredible. I took her Beginning Video course (Art 012). Very engaging and hands on with the course content. Down to earth and has very inspiring lectures.
Easy grader and allows you to resubmit projects to get a higher grade than the one you got. 10/10 Professor, would take again!

Very interesting lectures, not much guidance but a lot of encouragement when it came to projects. She was not very strict on grading and very understanding when I had to miss a lot of classes due to illness and mental health issues.
Very helpful, funny, and genuine.
I haven't even finished this course yet and I can tell this guy is a great professor. He genuinely cares for his students and wants them to succeed. I'd vote for Babak if he ran for president.

Very interesting lectures that flowed well.  Exams are really hard either in time crunch or just difficulty of material but with clobber policy all hope is not lost.  Definitely would recommend 16a with him because we lays a great foundation for any higher level classes and their thinking.
Babak is genuinely my goat. I don't know what else to say. Nice guy. Good lecture. Learned a lot.

Prof Ayazifar's EE16A was challenging, and I didn't enjoy it much unlike other reviews. The long, late evening lectures made paying attention tricky and prohibited me from attending any clubs. Interacting in lectures felt intimidating, and reviewing material was tedious without a textbook and lecture notes being delayed to post to Ed.
Babak is awesome!

I love Babak! He is a great teacher and one of the best! 16A class is difficult, which is too be expected, but he makes it interesting and engaging. His lectures are also pretty funny and I felt like he truly cared about his students. Would recommend.
Undoubtedly one of the smarter humans.
He's a super funny guy!
Didn't realize how awesome he is (and also JP) until I take other EE classes with other instructors.

Good material, disorganized at first. unclear study material for exams, difficult homeworks and mediocre labs. Grading scheme not transparent, they don't do +'s and -'s. course staff were SUPER lazy. Final wasn't during finals week because (from ta) "people want to leave" what??? why have a dead week if we dont use it. embarrassing for a T3 school.

This class is good, but the lectures did feel sometimes unstructured. The staff notes were much better as a comprehensive study tool when they came out. This class also has a lot of applications so it became interesting towards the end, and JP Tenant had a little more structure in his lecture style so it got easier to follow.

There were a lot of goofy moments in lecture with Babak trying to get people to participate. His lectures are ok but can be hard to follow at times. He cares about student learning and tries to be fun and engaging but he wasn't able to connect with the class super well, unfortunately. He's a good guy but his lecturing style isn't for everyone.

Babak cares about his students. However, his lectures are hard to follow so you may need to do extra review. The class is disorganized with recent changes to teaching only linear algebra, and the HW + labs are too difficult compared to the exams. The grading is unclear since this class is curved, but your z-scores on exams can give you a ballpark.

I believe it has something to do with the course structure a bit disorganised due to the recent reform, I have to admit it'd be impossible for me to follow along lectures let alone those “creative” exams without previous foundations in linear algebra. Very chill guy though; require more studying to really go down his trail of thought.

Organized lectures with barely any accents. The change in curriculum makes this class rly chaotic. GSI sometimes not responsive on Ed. The class is entirely linear algebra. Exams are open book but HARD and TIME-INTENSE. Lectures are not related to exams. Compare homework before submission and attend the discussion.  Labs are not tested on exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Babak is a really sweet professor who genuinely cares for his students! His lectures are engaging and I like that he gives us time to really think about the questions he asks in class. One thing I will say, though, is that his exams were really tough, like some of the hardest exams I've ever taken. But he does curve generously, so there's that.

He is nice as a lecturer and a person. Considering that he is trying to change the whole course curriculum, the course is well-organized and engaging. 16A is a bit slow paced, and it's hard to be unsuccessful in this class unless you don't spend enough time and use your brain power.

Contrary to what others say, I love the class so far. If you pull up to lectures, you will be able to understand all the material as Babak covers everything at a reasonable pace and has excellent explanations. He also covers real-life applications of linear algebra and made me feel like I learned beyond the scope of the class. Highly recommend.

lectures are confusing and easy to forget. He over complicated basic linear algebra so much I stopped going to lectures because I was totally lost. Labs feel chaotic and not connected to the course content at all. He made midterms online and open book, but the class is curved so it became a cheating competition.

Not sure if its bc of the new curriculum but the course is very poorly organized, EDstem is a mess and TA's aren't very helpful. Babak teaches whatever he feels like. Doesn't rlly follow a textbook so it's hard to keep up with content or get help on the internet if you don't understand something from lecture

Funny but restructuring of the EECS16A curriculum is not well done. Lectures are way too fast and have lots of ambiguity, not to mention notation inconsistencies in much of his lecture slides. Also scheduled midterm 1 in such a way that it may be impossible to get to 61A midterm 1 on time.
best prof

Chill dude with fun stories and good lectures. Broke concepts down well. Lectured mostly off of notes he made live on his iPad with Notability. Encouraged participation. Definitely a better lecturer than Rao.

Extremely lovely professor! His lectures are never boring and he pays a lot of attention to how the students are doing. Attending his lectures is quite enough to get a good grasp on the content for probability in CS70. Amazing!
The lecture is amazing! The professor explains all concepts in a simple way. In addition, the professor really cares students - really a great experience at Cal!
I don't have a grandpa. But Babak's lectures are amazing and I treat him as my grandpa.

idk if it's just because my dad and Babak are both bald but I rly saw him as such a father figure, he was supportive, caring, and showed it through his words and lectures! He was a great prof as he rly tries to engage w/ his audience and is a big fan of the socratic method which scared me but his energy was so good that I always attended every lec!

Lectures were a lot of fun. He is caring and genuine! His homeworks were extremely long and you couldn't really start them til the very last second because they were on the current week's material. Test were extremely long and the time given was not enough. A textbook would have been useful bc the only thing we had was our lecture notes.

Babak is one of the kindest, sweetest profs I've had. Moves a bit slow but really explains concepts well and doesn't read off slides. Doesn't completely match the notes but that's fine. 100% recommend.

Babak was great. I learned a lot about probability when he taught the course, and he taught very well. He is very enthusiastic and wants to help his students learn and understand. Keeping up with his lectures is very important since one of the ways he likes to assess student understanding is through them.

Wow, I love this teacher. He taught the probability section of CS70, and although I've always hated probability in the past, he made me love it. I looked forward to lectures and enjoyed the assignments he gave. He was enthusiastic and quite funny sometimes, and you can tell he cares about his students.

This proffessor is amazing and gives great lectures. They were all very fun and easy to enjoy. Except that there is one issue. If you are taking Data 8 make sure you try and get a 93% or higher in order to get an A as this class is based on a curve and not bins. This semester was tough as a lot of people who got an 88-93% range got B's. Good Luck!
Great professor. really cares about his students

Love this professor with all my heart. He makes the class genuinely fun to go to, and lectures beautifully and clearly while maintaining humor all the time. Take him if you can, a true gem who will genuinely care about you as a student and person
Really funny and livens up boring material with his bitmoji

I took cs70 with him in the spring, and he's one of the best profs I've had at Cal. His lectures are solid (not the best, but very good), but more importantly, he cares a TON for his students. He goes out of his way to alleviate student stress and make the class more enjoyable. Also his exams/curves are easier than the other 70 profs

Took 70 with Babak and Anant. Babak was friendly and fun to watch during lecture. He went through concrete examples that were both interesting and useful. He only teaches the basics though so you have to learn more yourself to get to the level of exams. Course notes are great for this though. Would love to take another class with him.

Great guy overall. He encourages student participation and welcomes questions stupid or not. Lectures were well-structured and well-delivered. He clearly cares a lot about students. I hate Math but Babak made it somewhat easier where Prof Sahai did not.

Great guy. I had never taken an EE class before and was able to do well in EE 120, as he taught everything from scratch. All I did for this class were going to lecture, trying to understand the materials from lectures, and doing the homework carefully. Guarantee an easy A.
Confusing lecturer but seems friendly enough.
that is ok
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--So many papers

reviews.comment: The best proffesor

I loved his lectures. He is very funny and the 2 hour lecture never feels long with him. EE120 is like a lot of simple math tricks on a blackboard but he makes sure that they blow your mind - EE120 material is amazing with him. Exams are easier than I thought since I did not do much preparation, except going to all lectures and finishing all hws.

I havent seen such a caring professor ever, he sends reminders to sleep on exam night instead studying, suicide regret comfort note with reflection from his life, etc. So despite being in a big class and may never know him personally, you feel related. Lectures are clear. He was great during OH. EE16A sucks but he is the good part.

Babak is great and really cares that you understand the material. However the EECS department states that you can take this course without taking CS61A first, that is completely not true, if you do not take CS61A or the equivalent python first, the labs will not make any sense. The EECS department needs to re-evaluate their pre-requisites.

His explanations are confusing at times, but eventually makes it clear what is going on (usually after hw is due). Lecturing style is engaging, and calls on people to participate. EE16A overall is not a well-designed class. Homework, discussion, and lecture are not synced up, and the procedures to submit homework is annoying. Tests are reasonable.

Babak is literally the best professor in the world. His lectures are literally amazing and hilarious. He is a very cute and quirky individual. I love how he takes passion in his work and he is very enthusiastic about his teaching. He is funny and hilarious. I really enjoyed his lectures. He is a real gem.

Horrific nightmarish mess of a class. The organisation is lacking, insofar as it is non-existent. It's absolutely unreal how near-to-impossible it is to get a clear answer about *anything*. The administrative component to submitting work and getting information should not be the most challenging part of a course, but here--it is.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: he attempts to make lectures engaging with jokes that usually fall flat and a condescending tone towards students. the guy irks many of his students

Babak really sucks up to his students a lot, so a lot of students will think he is good. But that is quite untrue. He is not really good at explaining concepts and many times will make problems more complicated than they are. He is also not very good in his notation. He can simplify a lot and improve himself that way.

Babak is great, even if I didn't do very well  The class is treated a lot like a maths class, so if you go in with a strong calc ABBC background, you should be safe.  Go to lecture--quizzes happen during lecture, and he doesn't give much warning for when they'll happen.
I found my interest in EE through his lectures.

EE 20 is a hard class. I expected to be tortured in it at first but it turns out that I am completely wrong! Babak makes it such an amazing experience in learning it! And his lecture is the best ever!
When I was preparing for my PhD degree, I have watched the video lectures Prof. B. Ayazifar provided which were extremly helpul and intersted.

Very enthusiastic and approachable. His midterms and quizzes may be harder than Lee's , but is still doable and fair if you try his past midterms a lot. His class ends up giving almost 40% A, including A+/A/A-. I fail the first midterm(below average), but did very well(almost top several) in the next two ones,  thus getting A eventually. Take it.

Very articulate professor that teaches you to analyze -- not just answer -- complex questions. The skills gained from this class far outreach simple signals and systems and apply to hundreds of different problem spaces in science and engineering, and Babak makes you understand it so completely that you will be able to learn other subjects easily.

His lectures are very clear.He seems like a nice professor,makes you feel like he really cares about his students, but if you really need his help,he is too either too lazy or too selfish to help you.Not very organized.Doesn't bother to update his lecture notes. He wastes half the class time reviewing previous lectures while he can cover a lot more
he is one of my best teachers,live long babak.

Babak is an excellent teacher and is worth getting to know. Even though I had him for EE301, it was obvious from his comments and stories that he cares deeply about effective teaching of his EE20 course. Rarely has a professor I've encountered spent so much energy on improving and sharing their teaching methods.

20 was an easy class, and Babak is really helpful. The labs are long, and can be done before going to the section. Discussions were useful, and the only way to study for this class is doing sample problems and previous semester's tests. NEVER READ THE TEXTBOOK!!

Good lecturer, interesting and challenging tests, passable problem sets (they get reused from previous semesters for the most part). Going to discussion is fairly helpful, but the labs are rather tedious.

Difficult class, but also FAR more interesting than 20. Less time is spent on basic math operations and more on actual EE concepts. As with EE 20, pop quizzes and midterms were fairly difficult, but for the most part doable. Homework takes a few hours, but you generally learn from them. DIS were somewhat useful. I didn't go to any OH.

ee20 was tough (im a non-ee major).  Looking back on it though, we really didnt cover much; but thats because the material is very different than other class.  Babak will go out of the way to help you.  Tests and midterms are difficult.  Problem sets are long if you aren't solid on the material. "Schaum's outlines: Signals and Systems" helped a lot

One of the finest professors I've had so far. I thoroughly enjoyed EE20N and I'm taking his EE120 class now. Overall, he is a great professor since he keeps the class lively and in my opinion, he's very clear. For his classes, do make sure that your math skills are up to speed. Math 54 concepts are very useful (I took 54 concurrently with EE20N).

Fairly tough in all aspects of the class - homework, quizzes, labs, exams - but fair. Generous curve and drops assignments from each category except for midterms. Doesn't really hold personal office hours, only with a large group of students working on the homework, so I didn't attend. One of the few professors who makes 1.5 hr lectures bearable.

Beginning of class was fairly easy, but picked up near the end when Fourier series was crammed into 3 weeks. Expects you to learn from the homework which doesn't help much when trying to do them. Office hours often end up only getting to a few problems out of the many on the homework. Useless textbook. Rotating GSI for DIS so not always helpful.

A decent prof and really strives to relate to students.  However, the pace of the course was painfully slow.  If this course was condensed into about 4 weeks, it would have been taught at a reasonable pace.  However, it was an easy A and was moderately interesting.  I hope EE120 is better.

Instructor very overrated; he is OK. He is very funny though and very nice, hands down, but not the best instructor in the department. But, it's the class that's really terrible: it covers NOTHING. The course is absolutely useless and should be removed from the EECS curriculum in favor of a more substantial course.

As good as it gets. Extremely clear and good lecturer, and tells some jokes in class too :) Very accessible professor, will take questions one-on-one after class. Expect to work very very hard, the tests are extremely difficult. Highly recommend that you take MATH 54 before EE20N.
the best you can get, in that no doubt about it, he's got his own style, overall a great guy.

Simply marvelous, very friendly, interest and is just one of the best professors you can find at Cal. Course is very intensive and competitive (because of the junior transfers), make sure you enjoy math manipulation. Overall, one of the best class I have ever taken because Babak is the best. Attend his lectures, man, because the book is useless.

Make sure you have a certain level of math skills before even thinking of taking this class and pay extra attention to the last three weeks and DO STUDY the PAST EXAMS!!! you will find the final has little to do with stuff you learned before the the last midterm. Overall it is a very solid learning experience.
Covered the material very well, especially considering the complexity of the subjects.  Also, with the lack of support from the textbook, his lectures were even more valuable and interesting.

Tends to cram the hardest part of the course (Fourier series) into the last 3 wks of school and tops it off with a killer final. Be sure to do all HW and attend all OH so you don't get screwed. The tradeoff is that we do nothing the first 2 wks. and get 5 min breaks during nearly all lecs. Otherwise, prof is helpful and provides clear explanations.

Fantastic professor, extremely good lecturer, gives hard exams (you learn as much on the final as during the class!) Took him for 20, loved him, took him again for 120. Great guy, office hours is an absolute must. A guy you can hang out with! Truly teaches well.
one of the best teachers in Berkeley; and it's spelled 'BANZAI'!

Hardest Prof. I have ever had at Berkeley... challenged me to the limits and beyond. basically brings out the best of you. otherwise, you fail. extremely helpful and very nice, very clear and very concerned about student's success, but very very hard
This guy has it going on. He's brilliant, articulate, personable, and an excellent lecturer. Truly one of the best. BONZAI!

Babak is a fun professor and all, but when it came down to it the course seemed to move too slow, though that is probably because too many people asked questions wasting lecture time. Because of his emphasis on homework for learning, office hours became even more educational than lecture. Overall, the exams were quite tricky but Babak was upbeat.
Final was hard.

I have had many great professors here at Berkeley and I might have to say Babak (yes this is his first name, he doesn't want you to call him professor) is one of the greatest. He is funny, helpful and unusually clear and I say unusually because EE classes are hard to understand. Office hours are crucial to understanding the material. BONZAI!!!!!!!!

Babak is the best professor I have had at Cal.  His desire for students to really understand the material is reflected in both his lectures and office hours.  He once stayed an hour AFTER his 3 hour office hours to tutor me on convolution (his wife even called to ask why he wasn't home for dinner).  Overall a rad prof and a great guy.

Babak is awesome. He has become a lot clearer and organized than when I took him for EE20 the previous semester. I felt that his lectures have improved significantly while retaining his strange humor.

EE courses are HARD, and it's cuz of how well Babak lectures that I dare to rate easiness at 2. His tests are always fair, seeing as he writes them himself. Hwks help a lot, too. He's one of those rare professors who will go out of his way to help every student who asks for help. Funny and enthusiastic. His office hours are also worth going to.

As always, he explains things very clearly, and tries to give intuitive explanations. He also answered students' questions very well. I would rate him as one of the best profs in EECS. His midterm (MT2) was very straightforward and fair. His problem sets were also carefully constructed. But, I did feel that the final did not demonstrate what I knew

One of the best professors I had for EE. Grading was very fair and pro-student. He also speaks VERY clearly--not that many professors in EECS have better speaking skills (sadly). Only complaint I can think of is the organization of the lectures can be a little better. Won't teach 120 again soon but great professor for students taking 20N.

he does have an uncanny ability to put you to sleep.  he speaks very formally, and not too slowly (most of the time).  very helpful in person.  He asks the class to participate, thus letting wrong answers permeate the room.  will be confusing if you're half awake for his class.

I rated him after reading his final email!He didn't organize the lecture well, especialy the last chapter b/c he's behind. Unfortunately, most parts of the final were given in that chapter. His HWs and tests usually contained stuffs that didn't teach in class. Personaly, he's very helpful. TAs didn't do anything but grading your works strictly!

Babak is one of the most enthusiastic professors I have had. He really enjoys what he does and will go out of his way to accomodate the students. I felt he ran a fair class. However, the class was very difficult, and Babak sometimes treats one person's understanding in lecture as if everyone understands the material. The TA's lacked organization.

This class was hard not because of Babak, but because the material is naturally hard. The book, IMO, is not well written, and does not help much. Fortunately, Babak explains things very well, and with a great attitude. Towards the end of the class, though, I was unable to understand things physically/intuitively; hopefully I'll do OK in EECS120 =)

Funny guy. Tests are pretty hard and the final killed me. But the class was very worthwhile and I had a lot of fun. Oh ya, and his head is REALLY REALLY shiny. I get a decent reflection of the ceiling lights from his head.

He was a good professor, but I would have preferred Professor Lee.  No doubt, I hope he teaches most of 120 next (spring '06) semester instead of that dunce Variya.  Babak also helped write the 120 book (Oppenheim one).  One weakness was a lack of clear organization in his lectures, but apart from that, was one of the better professors of EECS.

His lectures were very entertaining and interesting.  He cares about his students concerns and grades.  His tests were hard but definitely fair.  There was definitely stuff on the final we had never learned to do but if you understood the concepts you could put it all together and get the right answers.
babak rocks as a person. His test are tough because he can pull out some crazy sh*& that we havent learned yet. Just seperating the men from the boys i suppose.

Babak was an extremely good teacher, and was always very enthusiastic to boot. What impressed me most about him though, was that he actually cared about the grades of his students. He genuinely cared about us on that level. Thanks Babak!
It's great having a prof whose dedication to the class shows through.  I'll bet he spent more time making problem sets then any of us spent solving them

Professor's lectures were the best resource; I didn't open the book at all.  Not only is Babak's teaching rigorous and thorough, but also he is very friendly.  The final exam had a near-perfect distribution, and though his exams were challenging, they really did test on material.  Babak assigns grades with extreme attention and care.

An excellent professor! His lectures, although covering complicated topics at times, are very well structured and very clearly taught. He always answers questions too, even the really simple ones, without making anyone feel stupid. His final exam, although very tough, was very fair. It definitely revealed who really knew their stuff and who didn't.
Very good lectures.  Very helpful during office hours. Unlike some other professors, this one is very careful with your grades and keep you constantly updated.

As said before, the first midterm was multiple choice and the final covered mostly things we never learned. You don't really know what to expect from his tests, but he was responsive to students concerns. Ultimately, he was generous with grading, although where you stood in the spectrum was largely dependent on your ability to guess on the tests.

His lectures are a little haphazard, they go all over the place. Worse, the coursebook doesn't even go along with the lectures, and many things are entirely different. The exams are a little strange as well, the first one was mostly all multiple choice, while the final covered topics not taught.
Excellent lectures, answers questions effectively. Fun, engaging, and entertaining during class. One of the best professors I have had.

This professor avoids answering to questions clearly. Sometimes I feel as if he was mocking us. You have to read the book in order to learn the material. You have to teach yourself what is covered in class for the most part.
Clear, articulate, smart with an infectious passion for linguistics. His classes were a pleasure.
A very encouraging and great professor. Gave a great insight to things I never thought before.
he knows too much about linguistics and literarture. it is a pleasure to have him as proffesor

He stands alone!  He is one of the few professors who actually listens to his students and supports them.  He is very personable and charming.  You will learn more than just the standard fare in the course description.  His demeanor and humor make the drudgery of learning a pleasure.  He's an excellent professor!!!
¡Fantástico!  Excelente curso de lingüística con un hombre bastante sabio e inspirador.

He has a tendency to go off on random tangents, but overall this course was very easy, as there was only a midterm, a final presentation, and a final paper.  He does have a wealth of knowledge on linguistics, so if this is a field that is of interest to you, take a class with Azevedo.  You'll get used to his Brazilian Spanish accent soon enough.
He is one of the best.

Super chill, enlightening class. Meditated a lot, had guest speakers, & group discussions. Consists of online discussions & one final paper (Vision Actualization Project), no final. Once a week for 3 hrs, left after 2. 3 units. Highly suggest! Loved it. Unconventional class at Cal, but very self-fulfilling to talk about your vision for the world.

This was a good class to take; I would recommend it. It's only one hour a week, and there are minimal writing assignments. It's a useful class if you need another unit, or if you want to learn about meditation.
Definitely a worthwhile course, regardless of your major.

Meditation was the class that saved me from breaking down completely during this semester. There's just something about having a safe, quiet, and peaceful place to sit and just do nothing that gives a sense of centeredness in your life. It was nice being away from the frazzled Berkeley study life for a while. Definitely going to take it again.

Could have been a good class, but absolutely terrible logistics ruined everything. Azevedo did not stick to the grading breakdown given at the beginning of the semester. Never handed back any graded work until last day of class. Too many guest lectures that hardly even relate to the main theme of the history of nonviolence.
Definitely a worthwhile class. Americ is the most kind-hearted professor. Helped me define many of my beliefs. You'll definitely benefit from it if you have an open mind.

Extraordinary use of student power in dialogue--sat in a circle as opposed to facing the teacher, learned much more in this class than I have in many classes at Cal, was an amazing class--had the opportunity to plan and sketch out a "vision," start putting it into action, obtain peer review, read a few great books and discuss them

Class was mostly student discussion, with Azavedo occasionally chipping in. Only one major assignment (final paper) - I went to go ask questions about it and walked away with less of an idea of what to do than I'd had on the way over. Tried to pass himself off as knowing stuff that he...didn't. Easy class and nice guy, but not a very good teacher.
Mediation is very relaxing. I realized that there isn't a correct way for mediation. I have a lot of anxiety and because of that class it has been tamed

very inspring and spontaneous professor. does not follow a certain rubric so if you want a standardized class and professor, this is not for you or else it is hard to bear. easy, attendance not mandatory.
He really cares about what he's teaching. Class can seem repetitive after awhile as you mostly are just having a class discussion the entire time. Guest speakers are okay. Easy A.
This class will open your mind. Professor challenges your perception in a true Berkeley fashion.

Meditation class was extremely easy. Not at all about the grade, solely about helping you to learn how to meditate and why it is beneficial. Consists of about 15-20 minutes of listening to him talk about something related to meditation, followed by actual meditating. Very kind, gentle, and helpful. Extremely approachable. Recommended.
inspiring professor- highly reccomended!
Horrible and useless! Take this class and waste your life~

Lectures can sometimes be dull. They are not organized; he basically talks about what pops up in his brain. The course will be revised for next semester - it should be easier in terms of coding. Don't take this class unless it's a requirement, or if you want an easy A.

Not sure why he's teaching an engineering course, but he's kind, gentle, friendly, & likeable. He teaches more about the philosophy and role of computers than about how to use them. The class is more or less easy. You need to have a good GSI. I thought the exams sucked though. Mostly memorization.

This is one of the most amazing professors I have had at Cal.  He is inspiring and thought provoking.  The class is taught exactly as a meditation class should be - relatively hands off with just the right amount of guidance, zero stress, and no extra work.  Take this class whether or not you have ever had any interest in meditation.

This is one of the most amazing professors I have had at Cal.  He is inspiring and thought provoking.  The class is taught exactly as a meditation class should be - relatively hands off with just the right amount of guidence, zero stress, and no extra work.  Take this class whether or not you have ever had any interest in meditation.
He seems like he's straight out of the 60's. Very whimsical man and very interesting to listen to. Take this class if you're into philosophy... I came away from it with a new outlook on life.
An amazing, thought provoking, inspired man.  He cares about his students.  Take this class and go to his office hours.  You won't regret it.

Lectures&labs are totally separate. Lectures are random topics about technology, but you need to attend to turn in "lecture participation" (this keeps changing from semester to semester, BTW). Labs are mandatory. I got an A- b/c I missed a few, but labs are hard for the first 1/2 but the 2nd 1/2 is all working on your website, so your GSI matters.

Uh... the class keeps changing in terms of lecture attendance and how it affects your grade. For Spring2007, we had to go to class to turn in "lecture participation" which would give us "participation credit". If you can, take the class at a CC over the summer! Pretty light reading, but required for exams. Lab work has nothing to do with lectures!

this class is really as easy as they say. lectures are pointless but he has implemented lecture participation to get you to go. you learn all the html/javascript stuff in your lab. my gsi was really lenient and laidback. i did the final project website last minute (which you shouldn't do) and did decent. got an A in the class. :)

You can webcast all the lectures. There is a final project in your lab that is easy, you make a website. The three tests do not count very much but are very specfic about certain lectures, certain java script/HTML tags. So you need to know them by heart even though you can use dreamweaver in section. Acevedo is a cool guy, good guest lectures.

I took his seminar, "Time money and love in the age of technology," a non-CS class. Wonderful philosopher. Incredible, thought-provoking discussions, this class was one of the best parts of my week. A rare opportunity and a must for any science major (taught me to breathe, and to truly cherish life instead of confining onself to a textbook).

lectures were definitely useless and irrelevant to the lab work.  the professor focuses on the philosophical values of compu sci thru hubert dreyfus' on the internet(only used for the first two weeks). pick a good gsi, b/c they'll be the one grading you...if you are taking this course as a prereq for haas, you can do it at a CC.

lectures are completely useless, he talks about philosophy and his opinions completely during lecture and they have nothing to do with what you do in lab, its like taking 2 different classes for just 1 credit,
Boring lectures that most people do not go to, not too hard to get an A if you put some work into the labs and make sure your GSI loves your website (final project).
Grades depend completely on GSI, and he's highly philosophical in his lectures. Great for those interested in the field of "Science, technology, philosophy, and society".
He thinks he's a philosophy professor. And your grades depends completely on your gsi.
Engaging presentation, dialogic approach to material.
Helpful and engaging.
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments

i was excited to take this class before actually taking it... but that excitement quickly disappeared after a few lectures and sections. it is unnecessary to have any contact with the professor whatsoever. it's nearly an independent study class. midterm and final took me 10 minutes to complete, including re-checking. easy-A class.
Professor and GSI's teach you nothing. Professor Azevedo is a horrible, hippie-style lecturer who rambles and doesn't say much about anything. Pace of class is slow, and topics are retarded.

horrible class but very easy. horrible= students literally learn HTML/JAVAscript from the book (0% assistance from GSI/Prof) and lecture-material (philosophy of computers) only tested on final. Easy MT's when I took it (2003), but i hear in 2004 it was much harder.
didn't learn much of anything

while there are lots of comments about how the class was bad, i just have to say that this class was EASY.  and yeah, lectures weren't great, but azevedo was really nice.  most of  what the grade is based on is in lab anyway and you DO learn stuff you're actually interested in webpaging.

Teaches you about programming web pages using html and javascript. Lectures can be skipped because they are recorded for web cast. The two midterms are easy because the questions and answers are posted online. If you have an above average knowledge of computers, then you should like the class.

One student commented on taking a class at a community college abnoxiously.  Take a course there to find out what a community college is all about.  Good students always do well despite the incompetency on the side of a professor!!!!!

Worst nightmare. Classes were a mess, nothing was coherent and worst of all: the teacher ranted all lecture on tangents that had little relevancy to what was going on in section. This course needs some help.
No Comments

I learned NOTHING in this class -- lecture was all about hypothetical matters and was extremely redundant. All the tests were extremely subjective and merely asked you to elaborate pre-existed opinions. The final project and labs completely depends on you
Acevedo is great- he's a cool guy and I learned a lot from his lectures. Take this class!

Professor Azevedo is absolutely positively the wishy washiest professor I have ever had.  Take this class at a community college.  Save yourself of building a webpage that they don't even teach you how to do.  2/3 of the class is his bs theory. Terrible.

This class is bullshit. The teachers don't know what they're doing-- they're not even real professors. The grading system is terrible and it takes way too much time for a class where there is very little being taught.The worst Haas requirement-- take cs3.

Dr. Ball was a fantastic profesor that made course material very accessible via bcourses, while also clearly breaking down concepts during lecture. This class required a lot of studying, but there were opportunities for extra credit and very cool class that everyone should take at some point.

Dr. Ball is awesome! This course is not lighthearted though -- definitely took a lot of studying. I made and grinded Anki decks every week. Read the modules before and after lecture. Everything on the midterms and final exam were things covered in lecture or the modules. There were opportunities for extra credit for attendance and quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Prof Ball is so good, she is kind and interesting during her lectures. They do go VERY FAST and it is a lot of material, so maybe only take this if you're interested in physio.

Lectures are not particularly great for learning the material as the course modules yield the same material featured in lectures, except in more depth. The class often had 50-60% average scores on midterms and 60-70% on quizzes. However, Ball does not curve so you must grind out every point to get a desirable grade. # of ppl. w/ A is probably 10%.

If you're taking this for breadth, dont. It has 3 midterms & a final. Quiz/Midterm averages were always a C or D. if you don't know anatomy, this class is nearly impossible. If you have to take it, do P/NP if possible. Ball is nice but this is not an intro class, theres sm content. Seriously, if u aren't stem, dont take this. please. if u are, pray

I was not prepared for the workload this class brought upon me. The lectures just kept going on and on and the information was endless. She is a nice teacher but the class took over my life and the studying was endless.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Interesting class but do not recommend super hard and if you have to take it good luck.

This class has been if not the, hardest classes I've taken in college. I've studied and worked more for this class than for any other, yet I still struggle the most with it. Do not take it unless it's required. I feel bad for anyone taking it as a breadth requirement, because no one is prepared for the amount of work and memorization it demands.

Dr. Ball is a great professor, despite the large amount of material covered in the modules. Exams were difficult, but it is actually doable if you studied a lot. This course helped me a lot when I was learning about the physiology section in BIO 1A (especially the diagrams and some practice problems from Dr. Ball)!

Robin and Gary Firestone taught the course concurrently. Robins teaching was much more dense at least for me to understand. The lecture material is everything on the test but just be prepared for question phrasing that can be confusing. Robin is less approachable in my opinion but still very passionate.

This class was extremely doable. Professor Ball provides modules that you can do before every lecture that are extremely helpful. I never even went to discussion and everything still made sense just based on the lectures and modules. She is one of my favorite professors and I loved this class!

Content itself was not difficult. The amount of content required to memorize for midterms was, but it was easy to study for exams bc of the Canvas modules. I think the low averages (at least on exam 1 and 2) were a result of improper studying. That was NOT the case for Exam 3, though; exam 3 was far too difficult and had too much content.

Don't take this class as a breadth requirement if you think it will be easy since it is supposed to be an intro class. There are 28 modules which are packed with lots of information so very lecture heavy so you must study the slides outside of class or you will fail the midterms and final exam.

don't take for a breadth, the class is difficult and has too much content for an intro 3 unit course. She blamed the students for low midterms scores, the exams used to be online.  lecture attendance is based on iclicker but she has two different grading schemes. content was interesting, just too much of it to learn
