only take this class if you are looking for something to consume your entire life & suck all joy from the world. she changed away from open note tests. she has a personal vendetta against letting students enjoy life. prepare to memorize everything under the sun + the chemical composition of the sun while you're at it. i can't unrecommend this more.

Robin Ball is an amazing professor. She provides her own modules that you can take notes on & rely on. Lectures are engaging & helpful, makes learning physiology fun. Resources provided (i.e worksheets, practice tests, office hours from her & gsi's) are great. Caring person. Amount of HW is reasonable, most time will be spent towards studying.
Don't take for breadth, class is time consuming & exams are difficult  (
not a bad teacher but there is def too much material for an introductory class. medical discussions and homework are rather easy but the exams were not. felt like more than 3 units actually.

Midterms were admittedly quite difficult with relatively low averages, but were not unreasonable, and exams were easy to study for. HW, medical racism discussions, and other assignments (as well as a few extra credit points) made it perfectly achievable to do well in this class. I did quite badly on the final and still got an A overall.

This class was extremely challenging for an "introductory" course. Despite spending a week and a half in advance of a test studying for hours, I still got no more than the average on all tests, never more than a C. The midterms are not curved, and the low score is blamed on our study habits. The lectures and discussions were not helpful, take at CC
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you need a breadth class, don't take this class. Professor assigns little homework but requires you to memorize so much. It's not introductory friendly: poorly averaged exams despite studying for hours and discussions were useless to attend. It's too much effort for a three unit class, couldn't recommend less.

There is so much content for a 3 unit class and prof expects us to memorize everything before exam. It felt pretty hard especially for me and I feel this class will bring my grade down. Previous semesters had class open note which is why this class was easier, but this semester changed to closed note. Just try to study ahead of time, that'll help.

Attendance was mandatory but felt like a waste, as Dr. Ball only skimmed over the content we had to teach ourselves through online modules before class. Despite extensive prep, many of us struggled on midterms, yet Dr. Ball blamed our study habits instead of reflecting on her own shortcomings as an instructor.

Good lecturer, even though she's a bit repetitive from what's on the online lectures due beforehand. Exams are difficult, and carry most of the grade for this course. You could probably do well with easy HW assignments and discussion posts, but it's a loaded class for 3 credits.
Just don't. If you don't have to desperately take this class, steer clear away from it. Take it at a CC with literally anyone else.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Her class is way too fast paced for really dense material. Class is not curved despite the class average on midterms consistently being C's. Overall too much work for a bio breadth avoid if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: she is incredibly smart, but content is hard and tests are hard. Class is not curved and the average is usually pretty low.

Professor Ball is very friendly and passionate. However, her exams in MCB 32 have too much content to learn in such a short turn-around. There are 3 midterms relatively close to each other with no curve, and Professor Ball almost seems to fault the students for not studying enough instead of acknowledging her own failings. Do not take this class.

Huge time consumer. If you're not studying at least 2 weeks prior to exams (which she encourages) then you have a very little chance of getting over a B. Class average hasn't gone above a C for exams. Grade is basically dependent entirely on exams. Ya'll only really have each other. Prof. Ball's chill, but I don't really think she likes to teach.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Look, Dr. Robin Ball is a good person. Outside of class she's nice and approachable, but this is where the good ends for MCB 32. The course used to be online, open note exams. However, now it's closed note, and the exams are very difficult. Please do not take this class and opt for something else if you need to take physiology.

Unengaging, fast-paced lectures which are very surface-level reviews. Discussions are less useful (just study halls to do worksheets, which don't help with exam prep). You'll teach yourself everything in this course with the given modules. NOT AN INTRO-FRIENDLY CLASS. Positive reviews are only because it used to be an open-note, online exam class.

Professor Ball's lectures are clear and easy to follow along. Fill-in notes are given beforehand but also done on chalkboard so its convenient no matter how you take notes. Very little weekly work, most of the class is memorizing a lot of material from the lectures for exams. You don't have to know anything about stem cells beforehand to do well!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Ball teaches efficiently and clearly, and conveys content well. In one on one interactions, she can come off as rude or uncaring, though I would attribute this more to her more dry style as opposed to an actual lack of engagement. This class was overall taught well, with concise notes and clear grading criteria from lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Ball is incredibly knowledgeable about the topics she teaches, but moves through material fast.  She answers questions in class and on Ed thoroughly.  The exams are open note, but you need to know small details from lectures/textbook.  No extra credit, but over 90% of the class received an A/B.  Pay attention to the iClicker questions!
Professor Ball is wonderful! She is always happy to go over concepts with you in office hours and makes lectures fun. MCB32 is incredibly dense, so make sure to make flashcards and draw out concepts!

Prof Ball was pretty good! There was generally a lot of homework with the reversed course setup, but not impossible. All the exams were online and open note. The lectures were also mostly interesting. Two grading schemes for attendance and no attendance.

The professor is fun and makes lectures entertaining. Your grade relies heavily on midterms (3 of them) and the final. All tests are open notes, but the course has a lot of content to digest, so it can be challenging. I learned a lot and it was a fun course overall.

Most overrated professor. Her lectures were a reiteration of the homework so they were useless. A lot of the course grade came down to harshly-graded health social justice topics which only offered a very progressively-biased take and were only tangentially related to health. Weirdly refused to call them "male" and "female" reproductive systems.

Professor Ball was good, overall the class is alot of information and can feel overwhelming at times. Make sure to actually study the modules and don't rely entirely on the open note policy. Overall this class is challenging but doable if you put in the work and study. Lectures can be long and boring but make sure to try and participate.

I honestly love this class. In the past, I had no interest in science whatsoever, but this professor makes you really interested in the topic. The lectures are interesting and not boring and she applies the real world in this class (medical case studies and medical racism). The exams are open notes and taken at home and she had two grading schemes.

Although I do like Dr. Ball, the only thing I didn't appreciate abt her class was the amount of lecture hours each lab would take. Often would be over 2 hours and I'd dread every week. She is (okay) clear abt what she expects on tests. Her quizzes were lowk rough, and obvi study smart abt them (like for calcs). Otherwise, grade dpndnt on GSI!

This class has a lot of work. Her lectures are videos on bcourses and her lecture time is used as a Q&A session. Additionally, there were pages to read, a flowchart to make (that I never used), and a prelab quiz. This was all due before the lecture regardless of your lab time. I wasn't the biggest fan of her teaching style, but she isn't the worst.

If you don't love biology and how cells work with one another and stuff like that do not take this class because learning this stuff when you don't care about it is impossible. If you do like the topic take the class it's very informative and overall very useful for a relevant major other than that stay away from this course!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: as someone w/ no prior knowledge of stem cells, prof. ball made class super engaging! notes are given beforehand, so you only have to fill them in with drawings during lectures. weekly homework consists of articles and a m.c. quiz w/ two attempts. you have to memorize a lot and understand the material for the midterm, but overall amazing course!

Lecture are AMAZING!! Breaks down complicated concepts well so you have a solid foundation in physiology. very passionate about application to real world experiences and makes room for heavy topics such as medical racism. Lectures online, review in lecture time. Uses Iclicker but there were 2 grading schemes (w/ participation and w/o)

Took Sociology 160 Fall 2025. It was a good course; the workload wasn't too much, and it was basically just reading. Some in-class written assignments and the final was a take-home essay; there is a no-electronic policy in class unless DSP accommodations. Professor Jill is very chill, and the class is not difficult. I recommend this class.

very writing heavy, esp. in class, so make sure you know the readings! lectures aren't attendacne mandatory but i highly suggest going since her uploaded slides don't contain ANYTHING (like 2 words per slide) and she does a good job of breaking down some dense readings. pretty tough grading, esp on the in-class responses.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Bakehorn has the most engaging, informative, and enjoyable lectures of any professor I've had. They & their grad-student graders are tough but they give good feedback and provide lots of help along the way. There are no in class tests, but there are lots of short to medium length papers. I would absolutely take a class from Dr. B again.

The good part of this class: the content is useful because it helps you make better decisions in life, especially regarding education.
The negative part of this class: it's essentially a writing class. Someone we've never met graded our paper extremely harshly, and her comments were often conflicting.

Although I liked her class and such, she wasn't very engaging but the material was easy to understand and such. I think overall, she should just work on engagement. Maybe cuz it was a morning class, but like almost half the time she didn't rly look like she was interested in the material she was teaching.

You have to show up to class, her slides do not have everything she talks about in class; so to understand you have to be there. It will be hard if you show up to class without reading, you will feel lost when she is lecturing. She loves participation, questions, and overall interaction in class. She is approachable and understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Though grader, overall her classes are interesting, but she is always contradicting what she says. Especially if you are a DSP student shes not very caring of your accommodations. She seems to give your her own accommodations of what she wants not what your asking. I get her position and respect her, but she should do the same.

I've taken four courses with Professor Bakehorn. Intro to Soc, SOC 167, SOC 139F, and SOC 169F (I'm not even a soc major, just loved her classes so much). Professor Bakehorn is one of the BEST professors here. If you know nothing about sociology and are considering it for fun or an elective, take a class with Professor Bakehorn!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She's genuinely so intelligent. Made me interested in the topics through her lectures alone. Readings can be a bit tough early on, but much easier later in the semester. My reader was a hard grader, but my grade didn't suffer that much.

Professor Bakehorn gave very interesting lectures, and the content of her course was highly qualitative. However, there are a lot of papers based on heavy readings. 

If you're looking for an easy class, that's not the one. But if you want to learn a lot about gender and reconsider your beliefs about it, take it!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: Prof Bakehorn never failed to accommodate students needs whether DSP-related or due to personal circumstances. She puts tons of time and thought into her lectures and clearly presents class material in an engaging way. However, make sure to read the books and attend lecture to get the most of the class.

Professor Bakehorn is one of the best professors I've had at Berkeley. They are organized, accessible, and caring. They were always 100% clear with grading criteria; I knew exactly what was expected of me based on the prompts and provided rubrics. The readings were interesting and applicable to life. I would love to take another class by them.

Loved this class and professor. Was super thoughtful and caring when approaching sensitive topics. I thoroughly enjoyed how they handled misbehavior and support during the strike. Class had weekly assignments and a couple larger papers.

Lectures as so interesting! There are weekly reading assignments but they're pretty easy. Midterms and finals are just made up of those weekly assignments so also pretty easy. Taking Prof. Bakehorn for my second semester because I enjoyed their last class so much.

Professor Bakehorn is one of the best teachers I have had. She truly cares about her students and their well being. I took her class as a breath course and was not familiar with sociological concepts. However, professor Bakehorn is very good at explaining sociological concepts and uses good examples. I would take her again!

Professor Bakehorn was so great. She was very accommodating and actually cared for her students. Content was interesting and clear, and clear grading criteria. Weekly reading responses and a few papers.
Love Prof Bakehorn. Really cares about their students. Lectures are well organized and very interesting. My favorite Soc classes are the ones taught by Bakehorn
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: The readings take some time and requires deep understandings, but they are really interesting! Though some concepts are difficult, Professor Bakehorn breaks down the concept. The lectures are really helpful to engage with/understand the reading materials. One sad thing about this class is the tough tough grading!

Professor Bakehorn is one that is respected and her class is highly interesting. The only downfall about this class is the very HARD GRADING GSI'S. They grade papers like their soul depend on it and that is what held me back from that A. Only 2 papers and a Midterm. The good thing about this class is also the optional final.

Was very back-and-forth with zoom lectures/in-person, and spent a lot of time talking about personal life. Although some may appreciate that, I believe that the amount of money I pay to attend the class means that the focus of the classes should be at least 90% about what we are supposed to learn - that was not the case with this class.

I've taken 2 of Professor Bakehorn's Sociology classes. Let me just say, she is one of the kindest, most understanding professors I've ever had here at Cal. If you're planning on majoring in Sociology or not, I still recommend taking at least one of her classes while you're here at Cal. doing the daily readings is important
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: If you have the chance to take a class with Professor Bakehorn, do it. This is my second course with them at Cal and they are the most intelligent, caring, and insightful professors I have had. They are SO accomodating and understanding of any personal circumstances that are affecting students. I have endless respect for them.

You can tell that Dr. Bakehorn clearly cares about their students. There's a lot of reading in her class, but as long as you do it, you'll be fine. Dr. Bakehorn gives a good amount of time for you to work on essays and midterms. Lectures are very well structured and have little movie and podcast clips to make it more interesting.

Love love love Professor Bakehorn. She's passionate, breaks down complicated concepts really well, and uses simple terms for everyone to understand. Grading heavily depends on your GSI. My reader happened to be particularly harsh, which sucked, but not the Professor's fault. She does regrade your paper if you feel like your grade was unfair.

This class was a great intro to sociology and was what made me want to major in it! Professor Bakehorn was compassionate and thorough in her lectures but the papers could sometimes be dense especially if you have a tough grader so I would recommend showing up to section and engaging. She was very inclusive and adaptable to online learning!

Her lectures are important information for success on quizzes. However not all of the information is covered so some questions on the quiz are difficult so its time for your to guess. Make sure you turn in all of your assignments and your homework/participation grade will save you.

As a freshman, I loved this class! Dr. Bakehorn was very understanding of the whole shift to virtual learning. Her lectures were enjoyable as she was organized and clarified concepts. Although there are a lot of readings, they were all interesting. This class is an easy A as long as you keep up with understanding the readings and their concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof. Bakehorn is an amazing lecturer, super accomodating during the pandemic. She also has a kind heart and I wish her the best always. However, I will say her GSI's/Readers are awful! They grade harshly and they do not give good feedback. The essays are max 5 pages and they grade harshly on things that you can't even fit within the page count!

Amazing lectures. I didn't do the readings but taking thorough lecture notes on concepts + attending discussions helped me get As on my papers. Basically participate and get active in course activities and you will succeed!

Professor Bakehorn is absolutely amazing! She is so caring and was so understanding about the pandemic's effects on us all. Even though the whole course was online and I didn't get to interact with her one-on-one much, I still felt like I was part of the class and its community. The GSIs for this class were awesome too! Definitely recommend!

Professor Bakehorn clearly cares about her students! They make such an effort to make sure the students know they are accessible outside of class for anything (does not have to be class related). She's also really passionate about this topic! Really interesting, but watch out for the graders. She does not grade the papers and has others do it.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Lectures are boring, Bakehorn isn't a great at explaining concepts. Class grade is based on two reading response (essay), midterm (essay), and final (essay). GSI are tough graders and Bakehorn doesn't give much help on any assignments. Class is manageable to do on your own but be prepared to work without any clear direction or guidance.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Bakehorn is literally the most amazing professor Ive had my first semester at Cal. She is just so woke in the ways you wanna be educated. Shes compassionate and really wants to help broaden your knowledge base on  sociology.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--So many papers

reviews.comment: Prof Bakehorn is wonderful! She is funny, caring, and incredibly intelligent. She will answer every question asked. There are weekly quizzes and homework assignments, but they are easy and very manageable. I recommend this class as well as any other class with Prof. Bakehorn!!

Very interesting class and the workload is very minimal, Prof Bakehorn is funny, gets straight to the point and explains concepts very very well. Really recommend this class. Workload is very minimal.

Jill Bakehorn is a passionate, highly intelligent professor. As a person and an instructor, she's spot on. However, this review is mostly @ her readers/GSI's. They grade ridiculously hard-- their expectations are honestly too high? I'd stay clear of Bakehorn's classes in general because of her high-maintenance, horrible grading reader. love u jill
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This was my second time taking a class from Prof Bakehorn (took this one for fun- didn't count towards any GE or major credit). They are a very engaging lecturer and give a thorough overview of current events, relevant topics, etc. I loved the readings as well. They are generally very flexible and they were particularly accommodating during covid.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is incredibly passionate about the content of the course and uses actual pop culture like the Simpsons and LastWeekTonight to make her points. Get ready to read though - she'll do short in-class writing sessions about thoughts on the readings so make sure you at least skim them. Clear grading criteria but you'll still need to work for an A.

Jill is such a wonderful professor. Love their teaching style, they deliver everything in such a clear way that's easy to understand. They are also very stylish and cool. Love going to their office hours and just have casual conversations with them.

She's the best. SUPER organized, understanding of student needs, and provides clear/concise lectures that are also engaging. I love her approach to teaching, and I would recommend taking as many Soc classes with her as you can.

I really enjoyed Prof Bakehorn's lecturing style and content, however it did overlap a lot with the reading (i.e. you don't really need to read, just go to class). You have to go to office hours or really edit and work on your assignments because there's four essays (weighted 20/30/20/30%- in that order) with vague expectations. You'll learn a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: AMAZING LECTURES AND READING MATERIALS! Graders can be tough though! 2 reading responses and 2 take home exams!
2 take home midterms and 2 reading response. Readings and lectures are super interesting and inspirational! Fairly easy assignments! Her lectures are amazing!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Bakehorn made an extremely good first impression on me, and that didn't change the whole semester; she's caring, thoughtful, and receptive to others' opinions and feedback. Her assignments were really interesting and engaging, and her class seemed challenging but fair. I'm taking another class of hers next semester just because of her.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: I really like Professor Bakehorn and the content she teaches in her 160 class. However, the grading in this class is ridiculous. The expectations are unclear and the class is structured to make it nearly impossible to get an A. I would avoid taking her due to the grading criteria, which is a shame because shes a great lecturer.
DON't take her social media class and her reader sucks!

I love Professor Bakehorn but her GSI's/Readers are ridiculous. Some of them will mark you down for ANY little thing. I felt like it was impossible to earn a B let alone an A. I believe in holding students accountable but the readers were difficult to work with and a bit unreasonable. I hope there's more standardization with grading in the future.

The professor is good and her class is clear. The materials are interesting and thought-provoking. The problem is that the GSI is sooo terrible and tough, never give good feedback and guidance of how to improve! Gonna drag down my GPA because of this class.. overwhelmed
Her class really challenges you to think about sexuality in ways that you most likely have not before. The material is fascinating. Prof Bakehorn is passionate and engaging.

I'm not sure why people say she is so hard. I know her graders can be all over the place in terms of grading but Jill is an awesome professor. She is very sweet and I am shocked to see such harsh reviews about her. Get to know your readers so you know what they are looking for. Put in the effort and you'll enjoy her classes.
Extremely hard grader, did not care about students and seemed to constantly be in a horrible mood, she would yell at students for closing the door and her attitude reflected in her teaching

Taking the sociology of gender class was life changing. Thankfully, my reader wasn't very harsh on the papers so I received an A- overall. I recommend going to every class lecture. All assignments are take home and relatively easy but a slightly time consuming. Highly recommend attending office hours. Shes a great professor and I enjoyed her class.

Best professor at Cal. Each lecture was well planned, she went out of her way to make each class interesting by providing videos, music and thought provoking readings. She made sure to make things clear and was really awe inspiring. My reader was a tough grader but gave great feedback. Best class I've had so far. I am inspired...
The lecturer is below par. The class is quite easy.

I have nothing but amazing things to say about Professor Bakehorn. She's sharp, passionate, easy to talk to and super down to earth. My sociology of gender class started off a bit slow but I ended up learning a ton despite having almost no work other than readings. There are two 3 page reading responses and easy midterm/final take home essays.

Loved Professor Bakehorn and learned so much in Soc 135! She really makes you rethink everything you take for granted about sexuality, and I would tell my friends and family about some of the readings because they were so interesting. She always plays music at the beginning of class, has a great sense of sarcastic humor, and is an engaging lecturer

I love Prof Bakehorn & have taken multiple classes w/ her. Soc 167 was my least favorite. I got 7-10% lower on the papers for this class than her others, despite putting the same amount of effort in. It seems she's not as passionate about this topic than her other specialties & it hinders learning exp; grader was an INCREDIBLY harsh & unhelpful.

BEWARE: DO NOT TAKE THIS COURSE WITH THIS PROFESSOR. She is not helpful in office hours, very empathetic, THIS CLASS WILL RUIN YOUR GPA! :( I regret taking this class. She doesn't care, and her graders are just flat out ridiculous. They are not helpful, and grade very harshly - don't provide feedback for why you got the grade you did. DO NOT TAKE!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Not a great class, misleading in that I thought it was a GPA booster but ended up ruining my GPA. The papers are graded extremely harshly and the expectations are unclear and unrealistic. Do not take!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--SO MANY PAPERS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Jill Bakehorn was a decent professor. I'm a sociology student and I thought her lectures were a bit dry and boring. But overall not a terrible class. The readers on the other hand were horrible! Lets just say I got A's in every other class except for this class. The expectations for the papers were unrealistic.

Loved Bakehorn. All her courses are done well.  She crafts her lectures to be very organized so it is very student friendly.  She also uses media which changes things up.  Clear, Concise, caring, detailed and informative.
Inspirational professor. Really cares about this course. Makes the readings easy to understand during lectures. Awesome lecturer, easy to follow and understand. Interesting course overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: This was an amazing class! I am not a sociology major and took this class just for fun and it was exactly that. We had weekly readings and 2 papers plus a final paper that were all doable and interesting. Bakehorn is clear and willing to dive into a number of topics, including controversial ones. I wish I could take this class all over again!

Best professor I had at Cal, hands down! She is an truly amazing lecturer. Always assigns super interesting material. You will have to read a fair amount and write 3 essays. I'm graduating and will miss her lectures! Students take advantage of the opportunity to learn from Prof. Bakehorn!

Jill is a passionate, interesting and engaging lecturer. Her lectures were like church for me. Sociological church! Super thought-provoking, excellent choice in material presented and texts read. Her graders are extremely tough though. She tells you on the first day "you're in the #1 sociology dept. in the country, I expect a lot from you"

Here class is totally based on the opinions and perspectives of other professors that really have no evidence for what they claim. Her material is so ambiguous that it can be interpreted anyway she sees fit. Also, the graders are awful. One will give you an A and then the next will drop you to a B.. IDK how she justified a class based on fluff.

Interesting class, but grading is incredibly arbitrary. Catch one grader you get an A+, next time around you present the same quality of work and you get a flat B. She seriously needs to do something about her graders... Otherwise, would take again.

Professor Bakehorn is one of my favorite professors at Cal. She knows what she's talking about. She's done all the research and keeps everyone updated on current issues pertaining to our course. She is very driven and very well prepared for classes. Wish I could take a class of hers every semester. Bakehorn rocks.

AWESOME professor. Especially in her Sexual Cultures course. I don't know if it was the material or the instructor that made the course more interesting. I definitely recommend anyone take any number of her classes- best and more influential professor at Berkeley (for me) by far.

She's a fairly easy grader and the workload is manageable and SO interesting.  Go to office hours!! My only problem is that in class she spends too much time going over the readings but you can dig in more in office hours and she has more to say
Material is interesting but very abstract and sometimes hard to understand. Bakehorn is a good lecturer and tries to explain effectively, but concepts are very theorized. Tough course to get an A.

She is AMAZING! Very Well-organized and amazing lecturer. I LEARNED SO MUCH in her class. The concepts were sometime really complicated to understand but she was amazing in clarifying and explaining everything. Her classes are not easy at all. You need to attend lecture, take good notes, read all the readings and work hard but TOTALLY WORTH IT

She is super entertaining and gives you the material in an easy to follow manner. She checks in during class and asks if there are questions. She shows video clips that support the readings and what she is discussing (which also helps to keep me focused). Adjusts the course if the class falls too far behind. Easy to get along with.
Jill Bakehorn is one of the greatest lecturers I have ever encountered. She makes everything clear and easy to understand, while also interesting. She listens to her students, too.
It would be great if the class would focus more on applicable theories. Otherwise the class is quite okay and pretty easy.

Prof. Bakehorn is an amazing lecturer. She explains even the most abstract things very clearly & is SUPER helpful in office hours. Readings were not long nor hard & the two reading responses were very straightforward. Her midterm & final were not hard as long as you do her study guides. The SLC study group helps with filling out the study guide! :D

Brilliant lecturer. The topic is not for everyone and is a lot more abstract and theoretical than you might imagine. She is not an easy grader on papers, and really stresses that you show your own understanding/arguments in your own words. 3 reading responses, take home midterm AND final make your grade. She's a pretty nice lady too.

His lectures are alright. The content is mostly verbal and his slides are not very helpful. The content covered in class does not feel thorough at all, but attendance is still mandatory... The best thing to do is self-study if you're already enrolled in his lecture. If not, don't take it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: This is meant for 8B, do not take him. The lectures are so disorganized, the practice midterms always have mistakes in them and the actual midterms too. He doesn't do examples during lecture. I love his passion for physics though.

This is for Physics 8B. An absolutely horrible professor. Lectures unorganized slides and he did no problems in class to help during exams. Practice problems would be "water is wet" and exam would be "calculate the quantum data from within the black hole from interstellar". Mandatory 4 hour discussions too. Avoid at all costs. Good person tho.

Ps this is for physics 8B, but I couldn't select that. He looks to get to know people and is super responsive and welcoming on ed discussion, but he just doesn't know how to make physics clear. Slides are disorganized and he goes too fast and way too technical. Averages on all tests were F's, but he has extra credit and is accommodating

Professor Barsky is one of the best professors I've had. He's what I hope scientists strive to be; curious about science and wants his students to learn. There are always less desirable things in certain classes, and 5BL and 5CL are no different (lots of work), but my experience was significantly better with him as a professor. Highly recommend.
Great to have for 5BL
Really enjoyed having him for 5BL!

The worst professor I've had. He picks clear favorites & you can tell. He makes lots of judgemental, snide remarks & won't take kindly to criticism. Weird hierarchy in class reminiscent of highschool; he makes you feel foolish if you disagree w/ him/don't idolize him as a "fun, cool professor". Subpar lectures. Will avoid all of his future classes.
There was way too much work, but that's probably a problem of the class, not for him. Plus, he gave lots of extensions and even more donuts at the end of the semester.

Amazing 5BL professor! Super kind and caring; willing to give lab extensions when reasonable. Very chill and engaging as a teacher. He is hands on and doesn't hesitate to make things more clear and understandable. 5BL is a demanding lab class, but he makes the experience very enjoyable and it feels as though he really cares for the class.
Dr. B is a goat
Class discussions were genuinely interesting, genuinely one of the most caring professor I've taken. I looked forward to coming to class. A decent amount of work for an r1b but very manageable
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment:
Dr B is the goat. Here are some reasons why:

A) He's down to earth and understanding. Super accommodating for extensions and stuff like that.

B) Gives you great feedback during office hours + for *mandatory* essay revisions (you're guaranteed to get a better grade if you follow his feedback).

C) Only caveat is you have to read A LOT.
Easy to get a good grade and lets you redo essays, but alot of reading

Dr. B is truly one of the most amazing professors I've had here at Berkeley. I wouldn't say that I am the strongest writer, but his input and care made it so that I improved drastically in the time while in his class. His lectures were fascinating, and I enjoyed coming to class everyday. Participate participate participate!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Beckett is very organized, and puts lots of thought and care into lectures and the syllabus. He lets you turn in a rough first draft and gives thorough feedback so you can revise your papers and get a better grade. Lectures have an interesting mix of media and topics, and are never boring. Very nice and accessible for help or feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. B's R1B is probably my favorite English class I've ever taken. The books required for his class are interesting and relevant and make the class interesting. However, there is a lot of reading required but if you like Sci-fi, this class will be fun. His grading is pretty fair, he gives good feedback, and is helpful during office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is a very engaging professor and cares tremendously for his students. When submitting papers, it is evident that he puts time and effort into the comments. He is a tough grader, but that is because he wants the best for his students. If you ask for help, he is more than willing to help.

I would recommend Dr. B to anyone interested in learning more about America's past towards marginalized groups. Not only does your ability to be a writer improve, but you also learn the historical contexts of race, ethnicity, gender. Dr. B. also brought an enjoyable vibe to the class by always encouraging thoughtful discussion.
He will want you to buy books - don't just look at PDFs I wasted money on them. The reading is a lot honestly no need to read all the books just make sure you do read for what you write essays on.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: If you put effort into the class, you will do well. Attending his office hours is really important in developing your essays. Overall, he is a solid professor I would take him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: One of the nicest professors I've come across at Berkeley. Fair grader. But don't let him catch you using ChatGPT....!!! He will catch you right away!
Great professor. Lectures are clear and give good feedback. 10/10 would take again. Fair grader.

The course readings were all accessible, interesting, and relevant to American cities and families over the decades in American history. All of the readings were interesting and discussed in class. I enjoyed this structure because it led to more student participation and a student led discussion at the start of each class.

I enjoyed being in this course and I think it helped me become a better writer. The coursework was not super heavy, but still was useful to my learning. I felt like all of the assignments we did had meaning.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: My instructor provided many resources and very detailed feedback when it came to assignments and/or written work. With this I was able to revise and improve my work with guidance. I found the feedback very useful as it specifically stated what needed to be fixed.

A thoughtful professor with a desire to permeate learning beyond the surface/for grade purposes. Every essay/assignment had a motive and encouraged students to think critically at large–scale. Was rooted in whole improvement as a writer and thinker, not a stickler for the minute errors. Interactive learning with a variety of relevant media.

The class was my favorite this semester. The instructor was exceptionally welcoming and provided one–on–one assistance if needed. They also infused humor into the class, which I appreciated as it made the atmosphere feel less strictly academic. The course content, including readings and papers, was incredibly interesting and engaging.

Dr B grades essays very harshly. However, because of him I became such a great writer! I literally review essays for my friends now. He is so understanding, I recommend going to his office hours and asking for help if necessary. Definitely be prepared to read though because he assigns lots of texts. Overall, I would retake his class, super chill.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment:
Grades essays harshly. You submit a rough draft first, he picks out a few things for you to fix, and he gives a new grade based on what you fixed. But in my experience, even when I fixed everything he pointed out, I still received a poor grade. 
He certainly does not set his expectations clearly enough. 
He gives TOO MUCH reading.
Quite political.

No real practice exams (can never know what to expect), exam info gets released super late, lack of transparency about course logistics, virtually unresponsive on Ed and email, stringent regrade policy, and hyper-specific rubrics so its impossible to get a 100%. GSIs also don't know what professors are expecting, so there's no one to ask for help.
This class was the hardest class ever. The exams were so difficult, zero curve, and felt absolutely hopeless.
Not bad…

She was a pretty okay lecturer; taught by the slides. I got about 80% on the first test because I wasn't fastidious enough about taking notes (the slides were pretty much the guide to the course content), and because I wasn't specific enough about what was actually happening. I think the GSIs did most of the grading, though.

Bautista is one of the worst lecturers I've ever had. Her slides are almost entirely pictures and her descriptions of the images suggest she's just as lost as you are. The organization of lectures is also extremely jumbled and hard to follow. Although nice when talking one-on-one, the course seemed designed to make things as difficult as possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She is a very engaging lecturer, as her slides have a good amount of visuals, and provides good topics outlines to prepare for exams. Her portion of the final, on the other hand, was a bit more challenging than what I anticipated, albeit being given the topic list 2 days before.

Her tone is enthusiastic which makes her lectures easy to pay attention to. The thing to watch out for is her slides are almost all pictures so you have to pay attention during lecture to get the explanations for those pics. Her midterm was mostly pretty easy but had a couple harder conceptual questions. Overall solid professor

Professor Bautista was truly one of the most enthusiastic professors I have ever had here at Cal and she was able to make a subject like physiology very fun for students to learn. She also helped me to be even more interested in neurobiology than I was before.

Prof. Bautista is super nice and excited to teach - she gives good lectures (but not a lot of details are on her slides so be sure to actually attend them and take notes). Her midterm and final section were easy and straightforward and the material is interesting!
helpful outside of class

Mostly just read off the slides, material was pretty simple. I thought final questions were harder than midterm questions for her, which sucked because she hadn't lectured since the beginning of the class. Spent several lectures just on a couple channels.

Taught from lecture slides with book as a supplement. Used a lot of practical / laboratory research examples, so attend lecture. Ended up dropping a lecture and doing one on completely different material because she got behind. Very clear presentation of material, easy midterm, overall a good starting professor for the semester.

Not an engaging lecturer. I felt sort of like I was in high school. She doesn't really go in depth. Test was really easy though. I thought her final questions were harder than her midterm questions though, so watch out for that.

Not a good lecturer nor professor. Exams question are not clear. Office hour not helpful at all. Comparing to the other professors teaching in this course, she seems like she doesn't know how to teach. Not recommended.

She's a decent lecturer, but a poor professor.  The material she teaches is inconsistent, the exam questions are ambiguous, and some answers are completely wrong. Be sure to open up the textbook and check your answers because she makes embarrassing mistakes on the answer key all the time. It really makes you wonder why she even teaches.

She always gave clear lectures, paced the material fairly well.  I was iffy initially about the weekly quiz in lecture but it def. helped in the end because it forced you to look at the material and made studying for the midterm less work.  Prof. Bautista is full of energy for 8am. Would def take a class with her again. Bautista = HOTNESS!!!!!

One of my favorite professors and classes at Berkeley by far! Definitely felt like I graduated having learned some of the most profound lessons in Bajohr's class. He's super approachable and office hours were amazing learning opportunities! Would definitely take more classes with him if I could!

Truly an awesome professor. Totally echo the person that said that this is the kind of professor/class that they came to Berkeley for, I felt the same way! There was a lot of difficult reading but Prof. Bajohr is very helpful and any expectations are made very clear.
Evidently very knowledgeable and passionate about the subject material. Readings were interesting and well-curated. Cool guest speakers. Would recommend!

The kind of class I came to Berkeley for. Best one I've taken, loved the material & readings, liked interdisciplinary aspect. Required reading responses (3/w) but not too much time, help engage with the material. Prof very knowledgeable, loved guest speakers he brought in! Projects/essays were really interesting, out of the box. Changed my life fr.

Bernstein is an awesome lecture and really passionate about the material. However, the class has really a lot of material to cover, and he often doesnt have time to explain how to actually approach problems in class. Also, the class is crosslisted as a grad class, so dont feel discouraged if half the class seems to know the material way better.

Lee is a great person, and you should probably take a lecture with him if you have the chance. Unfortunately, the lecture material and the course material often diverge and it isn't immediately clear as to what he asks of you to know for his assignments and lectures. The class doing well is honestly dependent on the GSI doing well in recitations.
Professor Bernstein gives amazing lectures, and is supportive of his students throughout the course of the semester.

One of the most passionate and inspiring professors I've ever had the pleasure to be taught by. His enthusiasm for the course material is incredible, and his desire to help students is unending. His exams are quite difficult but are curved according to class performance

Few are as passionate or capable as Prof. Bernstein. He pushes students to understand experimental design and the underlying, fundamental physics at work. I have taken a few different Reaction/Radiations Labs, but this was by far the most organized, high-level, and most put together course I have come across. An essential class for any NE major.

Below average professor! She pretends to be nice, but is mean. She will not let you miss anything, even for important reasons, without complaining the next day. At this point, I could have done better.

Inconsiderate/Zero leniency or kindness So many assignments and any one missing can tank your grade. Grading is genuinely harsh. I went to tutoring and SLC and their viewpoints on papers are so different than Professor Kremer's. Take a different R4B. Only benefit is that I trauma-bonded with class members.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: not the worst, she can be nitpicky but otherwise isn't an extremely hard grader. i do agree that her personality is a bit strong at times but as long as you stay on her good side/do what you're asked, you'll get through this class fine--class itself was meh content-wise, personally didn't have any issues with her, complaints are valid though

Prof Kremer assigns a ton of work, but she also gives extremely detailed and individualized feedback to EVERY assignment for ALL of her students. She is there for anything that you need, and is very supportive. Yes, this class is time consuming, but it's worth it if you genuinely want to improve as a writer.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Belinda is an amazing professor!! She is so caring; I was new to poetry but she guided me and the class in a very warm and welcoming way. The course itself was manageable and she was very clear in her instruction. I thought that the exercises she assigned were really interesting and worth my time. I really don't understand the negative reviews!

Does not care about her students. If you have mental health issues DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. She does not care about you. She is extremely condescending when it comes to getting help and thinks she is better than you. I truly and wholeheartedly believe she should not be allowed to teach at Berkeley, or anywhere for that matter.

She micromanages everything we do. Her horrible teaching style would be understandable if I felt I learned something, but that was not true. I can say that I gained nothing. She was good at wasting my time, and she needs to be seriously reevaluated as a teacher. If I could give advice to students taking this class in the future; it would be don't.

Kremer is one of the worst profs I've had. She didn't excuse my absences after being admitted to the HOSPITAL, even though I sent her multiple emails with proof (which almost lowered my grade). She expects this class to be a priority regardless of your major and her feedback is vague and condescending if you don't argue for exactly what she wants.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: as a seminar class, prof. kremer genuinely cares about hearing from each student. she gives a lot of work and has high expectations, but offers plenty of guidance. the projects in this class were engaging, fun, and allowed me to be as creative as i could in my research. contrary to some reviews, i found kremer to be a kind and respectable teacher.

Professor Kremer taught me more than any other teacher I've ever had. The class was insightful and so helpful for my research knowledge and ability. I learned how to conduct research, read between the lines, and work well with others. I would 100% take professor Kremer's class again!

Give A LOT OF WORK LIKE A LOT. She made a lot of snarky comments towards me when my mental health was low and didn't attend her class super consistently. Doesn't seem like she really care about her student.

Arguably one of the worst classes I have experienced throughout my academic career. Minimum of "9 hours of work" outside of class each week with them all being annoying, tedious assignments (more work than my STEM classes). The professor is passive aggressive and missing more than 3 classes drops you by a letter grade. Just take another class...
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I am here to warn the public. This professor is the worst professor I've ever had. Literally have MINIMUM of 9 hours of work outside the class. She acts like this is the only class us students have, it's insane. Also not to mention if you miss class, its over for you. This class made my mental health worse. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS! ITS NOT WORTH IT!

9 hours of work per week outside class is the bare minimum, her workload is not worth the credit. Her feedback can be blunt and condescending. I once got a worse grade than my partner in a project because of my ATTENDANCE even though we turned in the same product. I told her I was struggling mentally and wanted to pass; I was refused help.

Professor Kremer sets high standards for her students, but she also provides the tools and support (office hours, submission feedback) to meet them, provided that you also dedicate time and effort to completing assignments (there is a heavy workload). It'll be hard to succeed if you fall behind on assignments or don't follow directions carefully.
To keep it short: if I wasn't so sure of my passion for English, she would have singlehandedly deterred me from this field altogether.

Genuinely, I have never felt more degraded or belittled by a teacher in my life. She speaks down to me like I am dumb. She makes me feel awful about myself with the way she treats me. She also gives you no time for assignments. For example, for a 2000 word essay draft we had 3 days to do it. I do not recommend to anyone.

She is very difficult and does not accommodate. Her instructions for assignments are unclear and she does not provide the extra support you need. This professor continues to give bad attendance grades even when I arrive 30 minutes early before the class begins.

Honestly was a little challenging but worth it. They're very accessible outside of class and understanding of personal circumstances and I left the class with a great paper. The one-on-one meetings were extremely helpful as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was one of the few classes at Berkeley that has actually helped me grow as a writer. Class was a little challenging at times but necessary because you do learn a lot and get a lot of constructive feedback. It's just like any other class, if you put in the work you will be set.

Colwrit R4B with Professor Kremer was an inspiration. They pushed students to think critically, artistically, and independently. The concepts covered in class, I still think about today. I have visibly grown both as a college-level writer and a researcher, and I feel more prepared for the next four years thanks to their genuine care and guidance.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Inspirational

reviews.comment: The toughest classes I've had, but it was a good experience. Lectures and projects build upon eachother so do your best of your ability from the beginning. Go to office hours. It's a very artistically driven class that relies on you to learn how to correct yourself which will help you with other classes.

I had Prof Kremer for fall'23 and it was a truly unpleasant experience. They are an extremely tough grader, but provide almost no individual feedback making it very difficult to do well. Plus, they are extremely passive aggressive which made attending class everyday stressful . I barely scraped an A- after spending majority of my time on english.

There's definitely a lot of homework that you need to do it before class. The logic she uses is: "This is a 4 unit course and you are expected to do a certain amount of homework outside of class..." But if you come to her office hours (mandatory) during her office hours, she is not a difficult grader. Definitely need to spend time in this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS WITH HER. This is the most regretful decision I ever made. No matter how much I improve my essays, my grade remained the same. Does not give a chance to improve again after you submit once.

She is just the worst at explaining herself. I have to decipher every single assignment she posts because of how poorly written the instructions are. Which is pretty ironic given she's a writing professor. Absolutely hate her class don't take it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: This professor, quite literally, will find any reason to critique and belittle your writing. Very condescending and passive aggressive with such high expectations. Save yourself the exhaustion.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Kremer was probably my fav professor for fall semester. They were really understanding and gave great feedback on the essays we wrote. I dedicated a lot of hours for this class in order to get the grade I got. Get ready to read and write a lot!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: I hated my english classes in high school but this professor changed that. I would highly recommend this professor if you are not looking for an easy A: definitely worthwhile. One on one meetings were great and she always had good feedback. Definitely cares about the students. Definitely a reading heavy class, but doable if you put in the time.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Really tough grader and can't even explain why she gave the grade she gave. HORRIBLE at the feedback and has ridiculously high expectations from freshman just out of high school. Expects you to write like a scholar when you are there to learn. Very condescending and impatient. Go to OH and get disappointed. TAKE AT YOUR OWN RISK!

She's nice, but the workload for 2 summer units was insane. I liked the class, but was v. disappointed when she gave no feedback my final project (70% of grade) beyond reread rubric + past advice. Her feedback on other hw sometimes seemed like she hadn't really read it. She also made us submit proof we'd done evals/visited the pgis that ethical?

I rated her before and don't know why everything has been taken down but for the sake of your mental health DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS WITH HER. Absolutely horrible teacher with nooooo compassion for her students, rude and TERRIBLE at explaining things. She expected us to know everything and then wouldn't help or answer questions. Save yourself!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: IDK why people hate on her so much. Yes the exams are difficult, but they are doable if you put the effort in to study and really pay attention to lecture/take good notes. Lecture was admittedly somewhat dry at times, but compared to some of the other faculty that has taught the 4 series, Prof Bergner is way better because she actually cares.

Fun and games till exam day, dont be deceived her exams are not as nice as her. Final grading bins are also not disclosed, so you don't know what your grade is till the term is over. Lab write ups are long, tedious, and grading on accuracy (and grammar?). Will suffice for your daily dose of melatonin.

Professor Bergner was very good at presenting the information on the slides and kept the class engaging and fun. The slides are very dense with information and do not fully go into detail about the things we are expected to know, so reading the textbook is encouraged.
very calm and soothing voice that cures your insomnia

Her lectures are concise and dense, but it's kind of vocabulary vomit if you're not paying close attention. The midterms she wrote were difficult and left out a few essential equations and constants needed in said midterms, but were overall made known was expected to know. Highly recommend attending GSI office hours and reading the textbook.

This class is boring. Lectures aren't worth it, mostly because the content is elementary, not because of the professor. Be careful about labs, look at rubrics for that, to make sure you don't lose easy points. Attend if you need more fundamentals in chem or want to brush up from, else just skip.

Prof. Bergner's lectures were paced at the right speed and slideshows were engaging. I believe all three midterms were around the same difficulty, and the best way to prepare for them would be to go through all the review resources the GSIs provided. Though reading the textbook is encouraged, reading the chapter summaries were enough for me.

Lectures are okay, and her slides are mostly graphics which is sometimes nice but you need to watch the recording to get the full picture. Exams are fair content wise, but I am not a fan of how mcq-heavy they are (that's just me tho). Overall, very sweet prof and fine for a gen chem course!

It's 'not a weeder class' and there'll be no curves! The one good thing is the midterm drop policy. Only the textbook will actually help you prepare for exams. Her slides are good imo, but her explanations are convoluted. Any valid questions about exams and material, and she will somehow be less helpful than an AI chatbot.

Bergner is an incredibly fair lecturer and exam writer. Her lectures were always clear and easy to follow (though her soothing voice made it difficult to stay awake at times). Go through her chem quizzes to study for exams as her exam questions are around a similar level to them, and do all practice problems available to you!!!!

The class is definitely hard, which is expected for a COC course, but the exams are especially confusing because it's unclear what types of questions will be asked. There are no practice finals or meaningful exam prep, so you're completely on your own when it comes to studying.

Sweet woman but very boring and monotone professor. Fell asleep many times. Very unhelpful lecture slides as they are basically only graphics and you need rewatch the lecture recordings to decode the meanings. Not excited to have her again for Chem 4B.

Bergner is a sweet, amazing professor teaching a hard course. Her lectures are well organized and easy to follow along but require a decent amount of self studying to fully process. Good at answering questions and if you use common sense it's easy to differentiate what's important for tests. The course is hard but she truly makes the most of it.

Decent lectures and very kind. However, since she is a new professor, there really aren't any of her practice tests out there, which makes preparation for tests somewhat difficult. Also, pay attention during her lectures as some things on her lectures are not in the textbook. Also somewhat difficult to reach.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The tests are on completely different levels of difficulty compared to past exams, assignments, her lectures, and practice problems. You don't even know what to study since they were all different. But the lectures are very engaging and interesting. If you don't care about the grades and want to really enjoy chemistry learning, this is the class.
Her exams are quite different than what she teaches in class unfortunately. She does not provide practice exams as well which makes things way more difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dropped chemistry after this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Bergner is a kind but not very inspiring/effective prof. Her lecture slides are unhelpful and mostly just un-annotated figures, and her python lectures covered so much yet so little. Exams mostly tested on rote memorization of esoteric information only briefly touched upon in lectures. Would take with another prof (or transfer out of Chemistry)

Bergner's lectures throughout Chem 4A/B were decently engaging, and she's sweet. However, her lecture content doesn't prepare you well for the midterms-- the best way to study for those is with old exams. The content is difficult, but her slides are very organized. She provided a great welcome to the College of Chemistry.

Hmm. Prof Bergner has okay slides and is extremely intelligent. However, she's not an effective lecturer and didn't provide any practice midterms, so it was really hard to know what to study. Her lectures are extremely monotonous and the recordings are much better because you can actually process what she's saying. Not my favorite at all

The material presented is quite hard, but Bergner does an OK job at explaining and problem sets do somewhat prepare you for the exam. It just happens to be far too many equations to memorize and the poor structuring of the CHEM4 series that makes every professor be their worst selves and thus all seem "chopped".
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor did not organize the course in a structured manner and was quite random with the topics brought up on exams.

What Professor Berger lacks in her lecture slides she makes up with her in class demonstrations, she is a great prof if you are active in class and ready to learn, her midterms can be a little tough but they are all fair for the material she teaches. Overall Bergner is a great prof.
Professor makes very difficult exams and its hard to learn from her as info not on her slides can show up on exams as well.

Don't listen to the deluge of 1-star ratings; a student unfairly review-bombed her. Professor Bergner is a super caring and engaging instructor. She puts lots of effort into her lecture slides; they include lots of visuals & aren't too dense, and her chemquizzes are a great resource for test prep. She's kind, approachable, and knowledgeable.

Overall, Prof. Bergner did a good job at portraying the material; I really liked the way she made her slides. She is not an amazing lecturer but she is easy to listen to and is helpful outside of class. I thought her tests were LOADS fairer compared to Xu's. The practice problems she gave before each exam were super similar and prepared accordingly
New professor so she should give us practice material for the exams she gives as there are no "past" exams to practice from.
I don't know why there are so many good ratings when this teacher cannot teach and just assumes we all knew this like a master before joining Chem 4A.

Chem 4A is not designed properly in the first place and then a professor like Prof Bergner teaches us which is okay if this Prof puts the same stuff on the exams that she teaches us with. As long as your exams replicate what has been taught in class then its okay, if not then its a big NO.
If your taking CHEM 4A with this professor then just drop the class within a week if you don't like her lecture type because this is how she does her lectures for the whole semester.
This professor doesn't know how to teach properly at least for intro to chem.
She is very new to the teaching profession so there should be some improvement in at least giving us the correct material and knowledge to study for her midterms.

Because she's a newer professor, there aren't past exams to practice with, but the practice midterms on owl2v are key for studying. Her portions of the course are more fundamental and less math heavy, so it was easier to truly understand what was going on. However, be prepared qm is hard. Start studying early. The concepts need time to marinate.
Lecture slides contained a lot of irrelevant material as some of the reviews have already said and we would be tested on different topics.

Midterm averages were quite low and standard deviations were quite high so it can't be on the students in this case. It is due to the low teaching standard that this professor has. Go compare the standard deviation with literally any other class and you can see its not as high as it is with this class/prof.
If my high school Chemistry teacher is better at teaching than this professor then there is something seriously wrong.

Not sure why some people rate this professor a 4 or 5 even though she does not have any practice material provided for any of her midterms. Next time for improvement this professor should provide some sort of practice midterm like the other professor or something that is actually similar to what we are tested on the midterms.

I'm not sure why there have been so many negative reviews but Professor Bergner was amazing. Her lectures were articulate and she covered every concept that was required for her midterms. The questions were different from the chemquizzes during lecture but her midterms were far easier than Xu's. Chem 4A just requires a lot of time and practice.

This professor should make sure to teach students how to solve questions that are similar to questions that appear on her midterms otherwise she is setting up students for failure and simply self studying at that point why do we need a professor??
Difficult professor because she should teach easier classes as we need a professor who is experienced in teaching to teach this class.

Professor Bergner is good for only showing how demos work and I feel like she is good in a lab setting, but to understand actual concepts and to answer questions on the exams she does not prepare her students which is what the main part of CHEM 4A is. Just in case you didn't grasp it exams have the "highest" weightage in CHEM 4A.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: How do I say this? Students don't understand chem from this prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: No practice problems were ever taught on the physical chalkboard so instead we just had to learn all of these examples by ourself.
This professor's slides material does not correspond to the actual material tested on the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor does not emphasize the importance of mathematics in this course.
She doesn't give any practice material like the other professor does.

CHEM 4A is supposed to be an intro to chem class for a lot of students yet this professor assumes all students have a really strong background in chemistry. If all of us had an extremely strong background in chemistry why would we take CHEM 4A or be required to take it?

Bergner's class is difficult because Chem 4A is a difficult subject. Her lecture slides are accessible, and there's clearly a lot of thought and effort put into every lecture. She's a great introductory professor for students starting in COC, and def the type of professor you look back on and miss. Chem just requires extra effort on your part!
There's no point in attending this professors lectures as none of her midterms are "based" on the actual content taught rather its based on other outside material.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Jenny Bergner is great lecturer 10/10 I miss her. She makes difficult topics seem very easy and understandable. FAVORITE PROFESSOR AT BERKELEY SO FAR!

excellent lectures, slides are organized really well and aren't just equations/word vomit. she explains concepts thoroughly, so even if you just attend lectures you'll essentially be prepared for the midterms. really passionate and love to teach, go to her office hours if you need extra help and she'll be happy to explain things
Get ready to read the textbook to pass the class with Professor Bergner.
I was a chemistry major now I feel like switching because of this class.
Lecture slides were disorganized and usually covered irrelevant material which was not tested on exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures were thorough, slides were neat and organized, and plenty of resources were made available for students to succeed. Was always a pleasure to be in Bergner's lecture!
Difficult HW sets and Exams compared to what we learn in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Students don't understand chemistry because of this prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Bergner just puts a bunch of conceptual MCQ's on exams which she doesn't even cover and MCQ's are weighted the most technically in exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Literally she cannot teach and goes off about some chemistry facts that are unrelated to exam content or homework content.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The homework type of questions are not even talked about in class or given as examples for us to figure out how to solve, etc. We have to figure out how to solve questions in our own time.

We have to understand the material from supplemental material from outside the class so we cannot perform well on homework's and exams without studying from material like a textbook or online YouTube videos on the concepts. We cannot solely rely on her lecture slides which is quite stressing for students as we have to put in a lot more time.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This professor does not know how to teach exam-level concepts which becomes an obstacle when students take her exams. Exams usually make up most the % of a student's grade so preparing students for the exam is the most important component in my opinion.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I was thinking about switching to mechanical engineering but Bergner's lectures are just so interesting, so I am staying. I love chemistry now. Bergner is so great!

Professor Bergner is owesome! She presents the material in a clear and organized way, and her slides are super helpful, with questions that reinforce the content. The class is challenging, but she genuinely wants her students to succeed and is always ready to help during office hours. Highly recommend attending them if you need extra clarification!
I love Bergner. She's awesome. Reignited my passion chemistry. I was gonna switch to material sciences but she persuaded me back.
Love her experiments. Really lights up my day. This lecture is the source of my happiness, maybe minus the orbitals content.

Professor Bergner goes over some hard content with confidence and detail. She taught the first two units which are fairly hard if you come in with only AP chemistry knowledge. However, it would be intuitive to grasp if you follow her lectures.
Bergner was an awesome professor to start your College of Chemistry journey! She conducts really fun experiments and lectures at the perfect pace and gives substantial practice for midterms.

Beware of the professor! She does not and CANNOT teach. Concepts concept concepts but where is the ACTUAL work? No practice problems in sight so we're basically teaching ourselves. She spends all of 10 seconds on a slide before just moving to the next one — cannot even copy the stuff down. At least she color codes everything nicely.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor doesn't teach basically :(

Prof. Bergner doesn't actually teach much at all. She also gives her exams which are based on some concepts which were not taught or even talked about in lecture and on top of that she is a harsh grader. All you have to do to succeed in the class is really study on your own, but what's the point of a prof. if we are studying our self.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Bergner doesn't actually walk through any examples or questions during class which are similar to what would appear on the homework. In addition these homework questions are also way easier than what appears on exams, so one could imagine if she doesn't teach question types that appear on the homework then how difficult would be an exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Bergner is good if you want to self study the class as her teaching is just basically reading PPT slides during the lecture which doesn't help students learn and we can do that from home as well rather than having to attend the lectures. She also makes exams quite difficult for what has been taught in the class.

The lectures are useless to be honest as she only gives exams based on outside information which she recommends reading. The only thing that could be relatable to what she teaches is sometimes when you have to visually think about something as she performs some demos. TA's also don't teach much they just grade harshly and give comments.

The lectures on some topics were confusing, and you have to read the textbook for clarification. Only concepts and materials covered in lectures appeared on the exams. However, the questions are tricky. Some require you to think outside of the box, which can be particularly difficult under the short time limit for the exam.

Prof. Bergner was definitely my favorite prof. at UC Berkeley so far. Her lectures are very clear and understandable. She was also very approachable during office hours, and I felt very comfortable going. Her tests and section on the final were fair and covered what she went over in class. I wish she could teach more chem classes here.

Professor Bergner was a wonderful lecturer. Her content was organized clearly, her slides were designed for reinforcement with questions, and her office hours were very helpful. Hard class, but she is an amazing professor. Don't be afraid to attend her office hours!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very clear and understandable lectures broken up with interesting demonstrations and class involvement questions. Midterms were hard but doable (though easy compared to the second lecturer), make sure to think conceptually.

Such a positive, charming person to set us off on the journey through chemistry. Loved the demonstrations and cute slide additions (even if her adherence to PPE protocol was questionable at times). Will be missed.

Prof. Bergner only lectured for half the semester, but she left a lasting impression. Her lectures provided new insights to concepts I had seen prior and were accessible to students coming from a large spectrum of chemistry backgrounds. She is wholesome, passionate, insightful, and the reason I had nearly perfect attendance. She'll be missed.
Becky is an awesome professor. All her classes were fun and engaging. Every week she brought snacks for students. 1000% recommend to take her courses!
