She is so caring for her students and it feels as though she gets to know you individually. Her grading is very clear and gives a lot of great advice. Also, the work she gives is not difficult.

Becky Hsu is genuinely one of the best professors I have ever had. She not only pushes you, but also truly wants to see you succeed. Her classes were six hours a week, which sounds like a lot, but I honestly looked forward to them. Even if you don't have to take English, I would recommend taking her class.
Not only a kind and excellent mentor, but also an amazing human being. Love her to bits. 100% recommend taking any courses she teaches— she's a ray of sunshine and a joy to be taught by.

prof Becky is absolutely amazing! she is funny and truly cares for her students, such a sweet teacher. would bring snacks to class too. just make sure you go to lectures, read the materials, do homework on time and take her feedback into account. really enjoyed the course!

Becky is a great professor who truly pushes you to step out of your comfort zone so you can actually grow. You're going to walk out a totally different person than when you first came into the class. The classroom felt more like a community.

Truly one of the best professors I've had so far. She's so caring and truly wants her students to succeed. Checks in during the drafting process for essays and is always willing to help give feedback. Provides you with all reading materials and ensure accessibility to students. As long as you try it shouldn't be hard to succeed in this class.

Becky was an amazing professor who really cared for her students. Becky would always give specific feedback on papers and would walk you through the process. Not too difficult as long as you show up to class since there are in class assignments and they are a big part of your grade, attendance is mandatory.
The best English professor I ever had. She is definitely the professor you want for college writing.
very kind and cares about your writing. spunky, energetic and full of positivity. will gladly adjust schedule to zoom or conference with you
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: There aren't enough kind things to say about Becky. I hated taking English classes for almost my entire life until I took a course with her. She makes you feel welcome in the classroom and will not criticize you for any out-of-pocket ideas/ interpretations of the text, which is what made me more inclined to share in class and keep up with readings
She is such a good prof! She is funny and professional. I indeed learned a lot in her class.

Great wonderful kind. There are a lot of readings and writing assignments but they are very manageable. Becky is very nice and sometimes she brings snacks. There are a few group assignments that are really fun and a few essays. Becky is very accessible outside of class and is super approachable. Great friend and great teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Best professor in Berkeley so far. Very very caring and thoughtful. Trys everything to help you improve.

Dr. Hsu was one of the best professor I have had here at Berkeley. She is the sweetest person and energetic. She is very open on helping her students one on one and never brings anyone down. Her class was always my favorite to go to.

She is the best professor I've ever had. She is so comprehensive and cares about the creative process. Becky gives clear feedback and truly cares that you learn how to write and succeed in class. She gives extra credit and brings snacks (so sweet). Readings are great!
She is so great! Inspiring and professional. Definitely will recommend it.
Hands down best professor ever. I suggest going to office hours for more feedback on papers. She's really understanding, she also gives EXTRA CREDIT and snacks !!!!!!
She truly is an amazing professor - caring, funny, and professional.
Great Professor!

She is super helpful when giving critiques on papers, good feedback. She's reasonable with the amount of work you get. During the online instructional learning she made herself available whenever you needed help.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The semester just started, but I'm already loving his class! Lectures are fun, homework is fair, and it's so clear that he cares about students. I'm excited for the rest of the semester and can't wait to take more of his classes in the future!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The class itself is interesting, but the lectures can be a bit boring. Attendance is mandatory. Professor Porter is super nice, and is clearly very educated and knows a lot about this topic. Easy A; reccomend taking.
Professor Porter's lectures could get unorganized sometimes but the class is very easy overall. The final was open notes.

Professor Porter is an expert in his field and makes it easy for anyone of any major to understand. The course material has ups and downs of interesting and boring at times. His lectures are well put together yet can be boring at times (1.5 hrs). Class is extremely easy, midterm and final were take home with averages in the 90s, (class not curved).

Great prof, although sometimes lectures were a little boring with the amount of info thrown at you, but the content is interesting. attendance is key and mandatory (no recorded lectures). the GSIs are the chillest people and are an extremely valuable resource to succeed in this class. overall, great class, def take if you can

Professor Porter included multiple due dates at the start of the semester on syllabus, but changed them so that they were earlier than initially assigned. I reached out to him online but he was unresponsive. He then refused to acknowledge that he misled the class and failed to give students any extensions. Assignment was worth 40% of our grade.

took this class as an elective, only went to like 2 lectures ever, did all the assignments (i have art hist background) and got an A. i think if i had gone to class i would have gotten an A+ but whatever lol. the reader graded kinda picky but im sure going to OH and asking for feedback would help u improve ur grade if needed.

Very organized and clear professor. If you follow instructions you will get an A in his classes. He is a great lecturer as well. I found his assignments straightforward. He does a mix of assignments graded for participation and others based on how well you actually do. Take his class!

Lectures were pretty clear and easy to follow. At times I felt a little infantilized but I suspect that was because it was a lower division class with mostly freshman. Porter is accessible outside of class and is happy to take a moment to talk after class to clarify things. Lectures encourage class participation. Not too many readings.

He's fine if you're just taking the class for a grade. If you're not, and are genuinely interested in the subject, he can be quite condescending. Doesn't handle disagreements well, and struggles with some prejudices. Overall meh.

Aforementioned comment is very accurate. However, I took the final it does require a great deal of memorization. For example, SAQout of 38 cities, only 8 cities are on the test. Alongside with fill in the blank and unfair, tricky MC questions. The photo IDs was okay, prof chooses 5 out of 20 pictures. Despite the exams, there are two projects&quiz.

The class is very straightforward if you make sure you attend class, as the professor doesn't upload lectures, and there's quite a bit of information not in the textbooks and readings. There's no homework apart from the readings (which aren't that important), only 2 projects and a map quiz, all of which are straightforward and not too difficult.

He gives projects that are meant to boost your grades, and his lectures are fairly straight forward. However, his lectures can be pretty boring if you don't love Near Eastern art and archaeology. If you're taking it to fulfill a breadth, it's a good class to take because it's an easy A, not time consuming at all, and informative.

Ben Porter is an amazing archaeology professor. Displays great breadth of knowledge as well as depth. No textbooks, just a course reader and slides. Encourages participation. Great class if you just need to satisfy a requirement outside your major, but even better if you are serious about studying Near Eastern Archaeology.
Great overall experience will go on to take Telugu 1B in coming semesters.

Deeply kind professor who wants her students to do well. We took a field trip to Fremont where we visited a Tamil school and then got Dosa Hut afterwards. This was at 8 a.m. on a weekend, but most of the class went. Really tells you about how caring she is, fun her class is, and how she creates a community. Could not recommend more.

I took Tamil101A with Professor Bharathy my first semester at Berkeley, and it was the best decision I could have made! I went to Tamil school growing up, so I knew how to read and write, but this helped me get better. We had so many fun projects and assignments! Plus, she's the absolute best and wants nothing more than for us to learn and do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: The sweetest. Super accessible, and will always work with you if you need extra help or extra time. As long as you respect her, and the class, she treats her students so well and doesn't assume any prior knowledge at all.

Professor Bharathy is the absolute best. She is so kind, helpful, and a great instructor! No matter your skill level at Tamil, she makes the class accessible and inclusive for all. She is also very accommodating and wants all her students to succeed. I could not recommend her more if you desire to learn Tamil in college!

She's the best! I really did not understand much Tamil before, but after her class, I feel so much more confident in my speaking. She is really forgiving with academic stuff because she just wants you to succeed! I once failed a quiz so hard that I did not even receive a %. I went to office hours, she taught me the material, and let me retake! Best

She is one of the best teachers I have had at Berkeley so far! Really enjoyed the low stress environment that she provided to be able to learn Tamil really well. Would highly recommend for a really awesome non-judgemental teacher :)

amazing prof with fascinating career history and massive passion for her job. will help you network and connect with people in anything you're interested in. clear grading standards. go to office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Inspirational

reviews.comment: I took this course pass/fail for my breadth requirement because I'm a math major. Lectures are not interesting. Most of class time is spent doing easy group projects. My biggest complaint is that the material on the exam was NEVER discussed in class. There were lots of readings that I never did and I wrote a lot of BS on the final and still passed!

Professor Randhawa's class was very focused and heavily relied on participation. She genuinely cares about her students, so be prepared to work on group projects, attend seminars, and more. Arriving late may result in being called out. Exams were pretty lengthy- all FRQ questions. Overall, great class- I personally found her funny and informative.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Very nice professor but the lectures were very dry and very monotonous and so. much. reading. 1 group presentation, negotiations, papers, midterm, & final. This class called for a lot; if you're looking to take this course for the philosophy breadth requirement & don't have much interest in this subject, I'd consider taking a different class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The subject matter was fascinating and I loved the creative mock peace negotiations, but something about her lectures made it really difficult for me to follow what she was talking about.  She is very genuinely kind and helpful if you need anything but idk I couldn't follow her lectures at all. Also do all the (many) readings very closely.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: You have to be engaged to get a good grade. Midterms require for you to read, and pay attention to lectures. Final was in a similar format- and study guides were provided which were very relevant. Randhawa was very caring and the class was relatively fun to take/participate in.

The class is very engaging and requires much participation, especially in team projects. Attendance is mandatory, reading is also heavy. Midterm was a bit challenging, focusing heavily on readings and class discussions. Final was similar in the format. Even though I got called out for being late once for class, it goes to show how Randhawa cares.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Lectures were a bit monotone but prof is very nice. brought in La Vals for us on the last day! Midterm and final are really based on readings and in class mediation agreement. Had a tough GSI. Gave us a study guide for the midterm and final and questions on the exam were extremely similiar. In order to succeed in this class DO THE READINGS! trust

love her dry humor. did not make students feel bad even when their contributions were questionable. learned some legal & negotiation document formatting skills for this class, but overall content did not require critical thinking. lots of in-class roleplaying. easy topic. fun writing assignments. memorize readings' mediation methods for the exams.

This class was completely dysfunctional. There was a complete lack of lectures or helpful information for the exams which are a large portion of the grade. Uninteresting readings and course content. Barely taught anything just gave activities. Do not recommend taking her if you don't want to waste ur time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: So absolutely awful. I genuinely cant believe she has a high rating. This class seemed super interesting and the material had the potential to be taught in an interesting way. Her lectures are filled with nonsensical information with no relation to tested material. I think she needs help.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Where do I start? Karenjot is by far one of the most disorganized professors I've had in my life. This course, during lecture, is elementary level information. Nothing about the text or what is being asked on the midterm or final is discussed during lecture. The class is meant to psychologically torture you. Do not take unless she changes it up.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Profesor Karen is amazing-- I learned so much in her class. I felt like all of the assignments were very practical, and she did her best to help us succeed. The midterm was definitely challenging, but as long as you really understand the readings, you'll be fine. Assignments included presentations, mock mediations, and papers.

Professor Randhawa is amazing, she really cares and is understanding. There was a textbook but I never read it until the midterm and final came up. She gave a study guide which basically was the final. She is fun and low stress class. Did take attendance.

Great professor. I took her conflict resolutions class and it was very fun! We were put into groups to mediate theoretical conflicts. Really puts you in a situation to practice your resolution skills and how to reach underlying positions.

Karen is an amazing professor and I learned so much this semester. The topics we covered were fascinating and despite the high demands the midterm and final placed on my time/sanity I actually enjoyed writing both of them. It's also essential to read consistently over the course of the semester to do well. I highly recommend her- just work hard!!

Professor Karen is AMAZING!!!! the kindest professor, I was lucky to have her. need to read before class, which is very discussion based. tests are clear, there's a review session befor the midterm and final. but seriously, such a caring, welcoming, encouraging professor 15/10 would recommend!!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: This was my second class with Professor Karen and I loved her just as much as the first time. There are a lot of readings, but I personally found them really interesting. Weekly group assignments, 1 paper, and short essay-style midterm and final. Not a hard class, but you have to put in the work.

Her religious course was not biased and I appreciated how the work we were assigned was graded through a google doc that groups completed together. Her midterm and final format was astounding and very accommodating. I wish I tried harder to receive an A but fell a little short. You read long articles and discuss them so be prepared for 30 pg a week
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I was looking forward to taking this class, but I feel like Karen couldn't have taught it worse. Lectures were unengaging and boring. Assigned way too much work during a pandemic and wasn't very accommodating. Negotiations were fun but she made us roleplay genocide for the first one which was super weird for everyone. Overall not a great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor Karen is the most caring and multidimensional professor I've had at Cal. She is smart and really wants her students to learn. Big McGonagall from Harry Potter vibes and we are HERE FOR IT

Karen is super smart, caring, and an excellent professor. Took Gloabl100P / PACS 100 (intro to peace and conflict) with her and absolutely loved it. Definitely easier if you show up, participate etc., but she also builds in small group activities + simulations that help you engage even if you don't like speaking up in class. 10/10 recommend

I took the class International Conflict Resolution (Global 133) with Karen during the Spring Semester 2020 and very much enjoyed it. The course was super interesting and I definitely learned a lot. It is one of those classes where it is rewarding to participate, especially during the negotiations. Karen is a gem and cares a lot for her students.

Karen is such a brilliant teacher (and person)! Her teaching style is engaging and the in-class exercises challenge you to think on your own. There's quite a lot of reading required but the texts are readable and interesting in their own right, so it doesn't feel like a chore to prepare for class. I would 100% recommend taking a class with Karen!

Karen is very kind and easy to approach, and clearly cares. That being said, she was my least accommodating professor in the face of COVID-19: lectures weren't recorded, multiple readings a week were expected, small group project, essay, final timed exam, and we still had to do Negotiations via zoom. These things are also important.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: This was my favorite class of the semester & the content was really interesting. Prof Karens lecture style takes some getting used to, but shes super accessible and caring. THICK course reader but weekly load isnt too bad  understanding readings is important for midterm & final. One group presentation, individual paper, midterm, & final.
Not very great lectures but class material is interesting. Not my favorite class but it was alright. Karen is a good professor but not the best I've ever had. Standard Berkeley class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Very interesting class and Karen really inspires you to understand the material, case studies, and field of work. Hands down best professor I've had at Cal! Take her!
Great..!

Lots of practical negotiation exercises that are helpful for the exams and mediation work. In class midterm & final, one 8 pg essay, and one group presentation.  The in class midterm and final are pretty hard because you don't get the questions beforehand but she does guide you in a direction to study and grades appropriately.

One in class midterm (essay), one essay (4 pgs), one in class final (essay). 4% extra credit added to our grades just for attending class and participating during in class negotiations. Do all of the reading but the reading is interesting and manageable. The in class negotiations are engaging and are relevant to what is going on in the world.

One in class midterm, one essay (4pgs), one in class final. Professor Bhangoo gave a ton of extra credit and really makes herself available during office hours to help. I highly recommend this professor and am planning to take more classes with her. Definitely do all of the reading, but the reading is pretty minimal compared to other Cal courses!

She's a lively person. Engages the students. It's important to attend lectures, but you could still do well if you missed some. She gives extra credit. Participation was 20% of PACS 10 grade, simply by attending DISCUSION. 3 main assignments for a whole semester, 1 essay (4pgs), 1 Midterm (in class essay), and 1 final essay (8pgs). Got a B+

Karen is such a great professor. She's very receptive to her students. She had us fill out a mid-semester feedback card and read them aloud the next lecture. She's very open about her weaknesses as an instructor and that just makes her a stronger one in my opinion. Lectures are always interesting! She's pretty attractive too, so there's that.

Great professor. She is very engaged with students and you can tell she is genuinely interested in giving helpful and informative lectures. Very welcoming and helpful in office hours--overall one of my favorite professors at Cal!

The reader provided in this class is very dated and very Eurocentric. Major peace and conflict/IR theories are left out and the conflicts in the "Middle East" are reduced to a battle over ideologies and identities. I know it was a lower div class, but this was so reductive that I decided against it as a major. She's a good lecturer and very kind.
She is amazing! Knows the subject well, she's approachable, she's funny.  She gives extra credit and even brought pizza to our last class! She's great.

She is a smart and kind professor, she ordered pizza for us before the test! There is usually one negotiation per class per week, it might be intimidating at first if you don't know anyone, however she is always super nice. I didn't like large group negotiations. Tests are easy and the essay is fun. Material and some lectures can be confusing.

Karen is awesome! Very open and helpful. Ordered us pizza before finals and gave us advice on grad schoolcareers. Wonderful person! Expectations are pretty straightforward. 1 essay, 1 group presentation, midterm, final (both essay-based). Participation matters! Does awesome peace negotiation simulations. Overall, easy class.

I'm an engineering major so it was intimidating at first. I found Karen to be very personable and very easy to talk to as she was eager to help her students. The class dynamic was great as she makes sure we interact with each other. The simulations were awesome! There was a lot of reading, but you won't die if you don't read it. Loved it all.

Professor Bhangoo is amazing!! She's hilarious in class and really engages student. 2 simulationsmandatory attendance as questions will be asked on midterm and final. Go to her office hours & she will clarify any material. Incredibly kind she brought us pizza on the last day of class! She has thorough knowledge and experience in the field.

Loved her class, very clear and precise. Watched videos, break out groups, and role play activities. The midterm and final are all based on her lectures. She is really good at listening to students needs which is hard to find.

Lectures her material graduate style ;) She used few videos of the Syrian revolution, terrorism, genocide in Rwanda, and conducted class simulations of diplomatic negotiation and conflict settlement. Awesome for personal professional advice! You can preview the book on google.

I very much enjoyed his class. He doesn't always give you the books as a file but you can easily find them online or just pay attention in lecture if you can. He really tries to have an engaging conversation about the book for that module. Honestly it's an really easy class and very fun if you pay attention. All exams are also open note too!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Bhandari really knows his stuff, and cares about his students. There have been times after class where we even talked about my own interests such as politics and investing. If you attend his lectures and do the readings you can do really good in his class. He does a great job of getting us to think critically. Take him as an ISF major!

I think people who took ISF 100D spring 25 needs to learn how to be more respectful. Even if you did not enjoy the structure of the class, the topics themselves are very interesting and you are guaranteed to succeed in the class if you pay attention, show up and dont spend the class with your nose in your laptop. Have empathy and be kind, not rude.

no clear grading criteria, no feedback on midterms. hardly gives information about final essay or tests in general until pretty recently before, and then contradicts his online instructions with random things he says dropped in a 2-hour lecture that no one really pays attention to. Wish I could like this class more than the structure allowed me to!

I really like Bhandari - he is genuinely kind and cares, and is very acommodating with students. Knows his marx inside and out.

This semester, he tried an unorthodox lecture style didn't work well - a little unstructured. But near the end of the semester, he gave us a ton of materials that were excellent. Loved this class.

Go to his office hours!

don't doubt the intelligence of professor bhandari, but lack of structure FRUSTRATING. 500 pgs of hard, dense material & when you proceed to go to class (unsure if he will actually take attendance) talks for 2 hrs- does not help understanding. no guidelines for exams until day before & can't even access some of the material we are required to read

The readings and discussions in this class were outstanding. Professor Bhandari selected a variety of readings that were stimulating and challenging, but which we were able to work through together in group discussion in a productive and accessible manner. Highly recommend this course, as well as others from the ISF major.

Professor Bhandari is a brilliant lecturer, who is able to present dense material in an engaging and interesting manner. The readings he assigns are excellent as well. He also shows a consideration for his students and openness to talk outside of class that is rare among professors. Highly recommend the ISF major, which this course is a part of.

Bhandari chose interesting books and navigated political issues cleanly and made people of all viewpoints feel accepted. However, he lectures without any structure and mostly he would just read us parts of the book that interested him. Attendance was required so class sometimes felt a little pointless because of lack of structure.

Professor Bhandari is one of the best professors at UC Berkeley. Instead of planned lectures, Prof B. talked  impromptu but passionately about debatable ideas. He always argued both sides and valued student's comments, making students feel included in contested scholarly debates. Attending his lectures was always illuminating and insightful.

Content was great. As long as you do the readings you will be fine, and TA's were very helpful. Lecture on the other hand was long, fast paced (and professor "won't slow things more down"),and frankly  confusing.Wouldn't recommend course because of how time consuming it is.

Rakesh is a kind and caring professor and perhaps of the most brilliant and knowledgeable professors at Berkeley.  His classes are quite difficult, but only because the material we learn is often complex and dense. Though his teaching style isn't traditional, I find it forces me to be prepared and actually LEARN rather than memorize.

He is very passionate but his lectures are usually unorganized and call for very limited student participation. I'm not sure if he prepares his lectures before hand, but usually class sessions are comprised of him going through the previous night's reading just kinda talking at us. I wish there were more discussions and participation
Professor Bhandari is caring and passionate about interrogating topics alongside students. Take a class with him for thought-provoking discussions.

Amazing amazing course! All exams were open note. Though there is a lot of reading they were all super interesting. Going to lecture is always a plus because he will cover specific things for papers and exams that he tends to post at a way later time on canvas. So you are the type of person that likes knowing things early go to lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great understanding professor. Reading heavy but most of the readings are really interesting even if you aren't completely enthralled by learning about capitalism. Will notice if you are absent. Go to class and he will tell you the questions that are on exams/quizzes. All quizzes are open note and easy if you pay attention. Eye opening class/topic.

Classes are traditional lecture-style but he is more than open to discussion, just won't always initiate it. It's a fun class if you aren't afraid to speak up and voice your opinion, otherwise it could be a little frustrating. Grading is exam-based, just do the reading - there is a lot. He will let you know the exam topics in class, so don't skip.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Bhandari has been the most caring and accommodating professor I have had at Cal since the pandemic began. He always shows passion in the content he teaches and ties the course to real life events, adding great relevance. He consistently expressed his empathy for us students struggling to learn in an online environment. Great guy!
Extremely interesting content. Books are very dense but the prof helps you understand
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Though Bhandari is a great teacher and obviously loves the material, it was always difficult to get him to be specific in exactly what he wanted to write for our papers as well as how it was going to be graded. 2/3rds of the papers had no assignment instructions posted on Bcourses until the day of, and didn't have any rubrics.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: This class inspired me to apply for my Ph.D. The cumulative progression of topics covered in the readings and lectures revealed aspects of myself and the surrounding world hidden in plain sight. In his words, 100B is: "Just ideas everyone should know." Well saidsuch an important class for me. Take Bhandari's classes.

Professor Bhandari's lectures and readings inspire critical and imaginative thinking. The books I read in 100A still inspire thought and conversation in my every-day life. From Marx to Harari, 100A will stick with me forever. Take this class for the requirement; stay for the captivating lectures you won't be able to stop talking about with friends.

Bhandari's lectures are great and the value of interdisciplinarity shines through in his ability to connect seemingly disparate concepts effortlessly. Anyone who takes his class and does the reading will benefit immensely since he is dedicated to ensuring that students become really solid critical thinkers. He is also hella clear about exam content
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This is one of the best classes at Cal and Prof. Bhandari made it that way. His syllabus is comprehensive and equips you to interrogate personal identity thoroughly and rigorously by the course's end. Grading criteria are extremely clear, and his lectures and feedback are exciting and supportive. His courses alone make me wish I were an ISF major.

I have taken five courses with Professor Bhandari over the last few years and he is without a doubt the greatest professor I've had at Cal. It is rare to see someone whose lectures reflect such analytic rigor and clarity and who communicates so compassionately and consistently with students. Expectations are super clear and readings are so edifying

Professor Bhandari is prob the most passionate professor I've ever had. He is super knowledgable and incorporates current events into lectures. I struggled to pay attention in this class because there was no student participation, just lecturing which was really dry. He assigns tons of reading but you don't really need to do it if you go to class.

Professor Bhandari is one of the only Professors that I have had that has made me actually excited to go to class. He consistently makes me question my own preconceived notions about Philosophy and Science's role within society. And, a Professor like him who encourages you to think on your own rather than imitate them is hard to find.

Bhandari can be extremely pretentious, and gets angry when people don't show up to class, despite his class being extremely dry and boring. His slides are terrible -- he essentially just throws unformatted blocks of text onto slides and his lectures are very stream-of-consciousness. Don't take him if you can help it.

Prof Bhandari is one of the nicest professors at Berkeley, he cares a lot about his class and his students. His tests were very fair, as long as you completed the (admittedly heavy) reading. He goes off on tangents sometimes during lecture, which gives you a really comprehensive understanding of the material but may not be everyone's cup of tea.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Bhandari's knowledge is extensive, he's fun, and he fosters stimulating discussions, but he could be better at engaging with concepts and experiences that are less/un- familiar to him. Getting into discussions w/ him and the class, your confidence may depend on whether you're a fast-talking, speedy processing machine.

Prof B has immense knowledge about pretty much every branch of knowledge, from Shakespeare to astronomy and political economy. He is always there for his students, no matter what hardship they might be facing. Able to make very abstract knowledge very relatable. Took 3 classes with him, I'd take 30 more. Take whatever he teaches - you'd learn!

ISF 100A teaches you to think. It gives you the foundation you need to understand how economies, societies, and cultures form and interact. Most importantly, it gives you the ability to see how those universal structures interact with emerging technologies, giving you the ability to study not just what the world was, but also what it will become.

ISF 100G may be the most important class at Berkeley. Every student should have a strong background in issues of values & science, given they will shape the future of humanity. There is no better way to get that background. With Prof. Bhandari, you get to be on the forefront of these issues. Take this course; be a leader in the issues that matter.

Professor Bhandari truly wants to see his students succeed and is genuinely passionate about the material he teaches. Very understanding of personal issues. You will get a LOT out of his class if you put in the work (especially by actually doing the assigned readings). Quirky, makes topics relatable, and tells personal stories.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Bhandari is an instructor that really cares about what he is teaching and wants to see students succeed. His class teaches great foundations while going over contemporary work. A must take!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Don't take him if you don't have to (ie, for a breadth) . That being said Prof Bhandari is a really funny guy. This semester we had 4 midterms and a final, nicely curved. Stick to the study guides GSI's create and you'll be fine. The readings aren't hard, but are tedious.

Rakesh is funny, engaged, and smart as a whip. Although lecture isn't mandatory, I wouldn't suggest missing. He rarely teaches from slides, and when he does they aren't always posted. But why would you want to miss lecture? Rakesh's wit and dark humor is enough to engage even the most uninterested of students.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Amazing class with an amazing professor

In the beginning of the semester, Rakesh said we would be able to talk about the economy better than econ majors. I can say with confidence that he was not lying! Great instructor, lots of reading, but he always tells you what's going to be on the exams anyways.

Professor Rakesh is a fantastic guy. His lecture is very interesting and always caught students think deeply. Even though he will assign a lot of reading, the books are meaningful and sometimes change your attitude toward the world. I will definitely retake his class if I have the chance.

Don't try to read everything Bhandari assigns, you'll be miserable. Assigns too dam much yet realizes you won't read everything. Tells you what's going to be on the test, if he doesn't, please ask in class. He's also open to adjusting grading and assignments based on the classes wants and needs. He curves! Get eBooks so u can search key words.

Great human being, very smart and kind, also extremely hilarious. Found his class extremely interesting & fun. He tells you whats going to be on the test. Assigns quite a bit of reading but just go to lecture, see what he talks about, then read those specific parts and you'll be just fine. I recommend finding study groups to discuss concepts.

Bhandari is a really cool guy. You should be prepared to read quite a bit and write a paper every other week. That said, Bhandari is not a tough grader. Many people complain about his tendency to talk a lot during class (which is true), but his teaching is setup as being mostly discussion based.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Would take again

reviews.comment: Easy grader--can get by without reading much. Makes time for students, holds review sessions, indicates what will be tested, and makes it as easy as possible to do well in the class. Still, his dedication to and understanding of his students is inspirational. He restored my faith in humanity even after the subject matter shook it. Thanks, B

Prof. Bahndari was the best thesis advisor I could've asked for. He gave constructive criticism and helped me develop my research by recommending resources. He also helped me make my research relevant to current issues.

Super approachable. The only professor whose office hours I enjoyed going to, just to chat. This class is kinda wierd, not all the readings are great, but because its 100% discussion based it can actually be a lot of fun. Easy readings, not theoretical per se, easy writing requirements, no in class exams. Great Prof, so-so class. He knows a TON

Such a fun class! He structured it to be entirely discussion oriented, so we listen to lecture just as much as we interact in class. He is so helpful & available to students - kinda rare for UCB profs. He's brilliant, super helpful, is charismatic yet humble. Highly recommend! Basically, you just read a book & write an essay about it over n' over.

I took Bhandari for both ISF 189 and 190, and thought he was a fantastic thesis advisor. He is ridiculously well-read and had ideas for sources for everyone in the class no matter how varied their chosen topics. Really engaging and approachable in office hours, and willing to meet as frequently as you need. Really laid-back overall.
The readings are difficult, but professor Bhandari works with students to make them more understandable. He is very accessible for office hours and seems to genuinely enjoy interacting with students.

Readings were really difficult, but he works hard to make it accessible.  His lectures often go off topic and stray from test material, but are very interesting.  Obviously a very intelligent man.  30% MT 1, 20% MT 2, and 50% final.  His readers could possibly be mental patients, but luckily he is very reasonable.  You'll do well if you try hard.
He is so freaking easy... I can't believe ISF class can be easy like this!!! Take him! Take him! Extremely boring, but easy A
Sometimes talks way too much and doesn't allow for student discussion even though he seeks student discussion.

He is a GREAT Professor, is passionate about informing you about about the issues that face us, and making sure our Berkeley degrees mean something. I don't know what the negative ratings on here are even talking about, he encourages criticism of his views and cares what YOU have to say. He is very clear, will help you get that A if you want it

Professor Bhandari is very knowledgeable in a wide variety of subjects and impressed me with his ability to think on his toes.  He's very opinionated, but he always is able to clearly present his reason for why holds his position.  I thought he was open minded and fair, even though many times I disagreed in principle with his positions.

This was his first time teaching the class, so I consider myself pretty lucky - it was very laidback. He basically said he didn't feel comfortable grading students harshly since it is his first time. Overall he is actually really enthusiastic about the subject, pretty helpful, and does not put much pressure on you to make a great speech or anything

Grading based on a couple essays, a couple midterms and a final. Gives you the questions for midterm and final in advance and literally what to say. To get an A, literally repeat what he says in lectures and in the book. Boring lecturer, fell asleep alot. Wants to give you an A! If screw up papers or tests, can rewrite for higher grades. Easy A

His class is easy, it's all papers and a final. He'll notice if you don't read the books or if you don't come to class. It is not clear how he grades you because it's all up to his judgement. There is no grading guidleines he follows. Lectures were boring, he is clear and easy to understand but one must be a social theory fantatic to like it

Had him for a comp sci class at TCNJ. He flew threw though a lot of the material during lectures and they weren't the clearest, but he is a very lenient grader and will not try to trick you on exams. Overall a good professor and would take the class again with him

Maybe it's because I took the class over the summer, but it seemed like he dumbed down the class until it was no longer useful. Getting 100% on the final wasn't even impressive. His lectures were tedious and unhelpful.

Bart is the best teacher I've had at Berkeley and he's only a grad student!!!!  Lectures are clear and helpful although handwriting a little sloppy.  Tests have reasonable questions similar to homework.  Labs are super short and easy.  Grading scale is fixed so 90% is an A.  Overall, it was a pretty easy and enjoyable class

Ok teacher. The class itself sucks more than Jenna Jameson, but since its a requirement for BioE's, ME's, and Chem E's, there's not much choice. Back to Bart though, he's not bad. He makes it pretty clear what he expects of students, and puts reasonable problems on his tests.
She makes the materials more confusing. Avoid her!
Very clear during lectures. Exams were challenging, but fair.

WARNING! if you do want to learn something but not teaching yourself, avoid her! She does have knowledge, but she doesn't know how to teach. The mid-terms are different story than the homework or even from the bk. Moreover, her hand writings are kind of hard to read; also, she speaks soft.
very clear presentation of topics

Considering that Intro Statistics is a rather dry subject, the professor was fairly clear and interesting. She did speak in a soft voice, but she used a microphone. Homework was helpful in preparing us for the exams. Exams were fair. Overall, a good class and a very nice prof. I would recommend her!

Lectures are pointless. HW was only 20% of grade. She makes the final worth 70% of your grade if you do well, so that's a good chance for you to get a good grade in the class. I personally found the class very challenging as a business student and she was of little help. I would take another professor if I could.

Her lectures are pretty dull and hard to listen (she speaks softly).  Go to section, it's pretty useful, makes HW be 30% of grade.  Her test are not that hard, but her probability one was HARD, just read the book, and go to section and you'll be fine

One of my favorite classes I've ever taken. Gives creative options to all papers, doesn't like finals so gives papers instead (awesome!), beautiful voice, great writer herself, and my absolute favorite book list of all time
She is SO RUDE, especially when you stop by during office hours...doesn't seem interested in students...or teaching...so why is she there? to pay the mortgage I guess...
She tended to lecture nearly the entire time, rather than encouraging class discussions.  However, she does offer a unique perspective (that of a writer) to the materials covered.

I had this teacher years ago but I still tell stories about how bad the workshop experience was.  She let things get really negative.  Students were the ones who stepped in to say the class was being unduly harsh.  I also know people who stopped writing because of her.  I did learn things, but thought the class unnecessarily cruel.

Prof. Blaise (AKA Prof. Mukherjee) was a wonderful creative writing teacher.  She has a lot of experience to share, and she's really, really nice.  Her voice almost put me to sleep though - she's got this story-teller voice with a nice accent and it triggered a naptime response everything I heard it.  Great class.  Take it.

nice prof, kinda hard on grading so i recommend going to office hours. only 2 full essays, 1 being your final that you can rewrite. not too many assignments either, but she is a tough grader, overall she's caring and passionate and often gives extensions and extra credit, just participate and don't skip

Professor Bistue is an excellent and deeply caring professor who genuinely wants to see her students grow as writers. I would recommend her R1A class to anyone who truly wants to become a strong academic writer, but not to those looking for an easy A. She is a tough grader, but she consistently provides thoughtful and detailed feedback.
Great prof, super caring and understanding. Reasonable grading, useful feedback. She is accessible and very willing to help you write and succeed in this class. She deserves a 5/5.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She cares about your success! She provides very helpful feedback and suggestions on essays and allows you to edit your essay based on her feedback for a better grade. Truly believes that anyone can be a great writer.

One of the best professors for R1B. The topic is interesting, readings for most classes but they are fairly short. She genuinely cares about students' ideas, and has great energy. Each class has a short assignment that you complete in groups. 2 essays that she allows revisions on + 1 presentation. Amazing professor and person. Take this class!

Professor Bistue is super caring and makes sure her students are supported. There is a good amount of in-class assignments and homework, but nothing too crazy and is very understanding if we're unable to complete something. She grades essays a bit tough, but overall a great professor.
Very useful feedback on papers, chances to resubmit both papers after feedback is given. Engaging and has a great energy.
She'll make you a better writer. Good instructor and gives you many opportunities to improve your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Bistue was great, I do not have any complaints. She allows revisions of essays, and very helpful feedback. Participation is graded, and there are worksheets in every class, so you cannot skip without taking a grade hit.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Loved her! Her clear rubrics, specific feedback, and accommodating nature made this the most low-stress English class I've ever taken. She's interested in our ideas, gives useful lectures on academic writing technique, and rewards participation and thoughtfulness. 2 essays + 1 presentation (R1B) + graded in-class activities
essay and reading heavy but very nice and friendly
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: Awesome professor. Cares about students, super accommodating, and gives clear and concise feedback w/o grading harshly. Not an unreasonable amount of reading. If you participate in class you're pretty much guaranteed an A.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Honestly she's the best, she's very understanding and would work with you if you need help. I had turned in almost ever paper late but she understood and never took away late points. She makes lectures interesting and is so much fun to talk to!

Great professor! She gave very helpful feedback on all of the essays and assignments, and if you make her corrections you are pretty much good to go grade-wise. The downside of this course was that there was a ton of reading and weekly essay assignments that could be very time consuming sometimes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Bad lecturer. His grading is extremely harsh, ur final grade is basically dependent on 4 questions about magnetism on his final. And then took away the regrade request for the final. U might be failed even if ur overall grade is higher than the passing threshold. Save yourself
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The tests are unreasonably hard, very low averages with unhelpful cheat sheets. The prof is nice and obviously smart but unable to teach their knowledge in a way that helps students learn. I would highly recommend searching for another 7B professor. If you do take this class, the textbook will be your best friend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Don't take physics 7b with him, take it with any other prof that is offered. He is an incredibly slow lecturer and goes on confusing tangents and makes the midterms and exams so hard that the average is usually below 50%. Seems like a nice smart guy but just not a good teacher. Better off just reading textbook than going to class

Really nice guy, but really awful class. Almost impossible to hear, very messy handwriting. Test heavy grading and averages far under the other class. Homework is all calculation based, but tests are theory heavy and the formula sheet is basically useless. Very disorganized and almost zero support material. Labs are easy but not very helpful.

This class made me have my first panic attack (for reference both of my parents passed in high school). So disorganized, no one knows what's going on including the GSIs. Textbook and a good GSI are yours best friend (loved Lia). Discussion problems help with the tests. Also no cheat sheet and the equation sheet gives you nothing.

You can tell he's very passionate about the subject, but his lectures are just never that up to par. It's hard to hear him, and his handwriting is messy. He also only uses the board, which makes it very hard to see. You are better off reading the textbook only. The lectures are not helpful at all. In an 1 hour class, he often goes on tangents too.

Seriously considered changing my major to physics after taking this course. Really good guy, wish I got to know him better. Liked lecture style that introduced physics from a historical perspective, discussing the people responsible for different discoveries.

Flat out terrible. He spent most of lectures rambling on about his accomplishments or his connections to famous scientists/politicians that he wondered why no one was learning. Exams had an average of 40-50 out of 100. His usual course schedule is MWF 11:00pm-12:00pm, so please avoid at all costs if you care about your sanity! Take Lanzara instead
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He doesn't shut up about teaching at Yale and MIT. He's a sweet dude, sure, but you won't learn anything from him. Don't go to lecture it's a waste of time. Just read the textbook and do practice exams and go to any review sessions that your TA holds. Birgeneau is probably the worst professor I've ever had at Berkeley.

He's definitely a nice guy and seems to care about the students, but his lectures aren't extremely helpful and usually I felt like I knew less after the lecture. Most of my learning was through discussions so I'd highly recommend going to discussions as often as you can as that's where you'll actually learn course material
Didn't find lectures very effective, he constantly talked about people he has met, or the history of concepts rather than teaching the material. Get ready to teach yourself material outside of class.

Lecture content was pretty much straight from the book, but he spent a lot of time flexing the people he has met and going over the backstories of physicists that discovered the concepts instead of the concepts themselves. Was not very accommodating for timezone issues in a remote semester. Tests similar to the ones on TPB, make sure you practice.

Robert is a great professor. He is interesting and always fun to talk to; his lectures are engaging and easy to understand. Many of his examples come straight from the textbook, but they are chosen specifically by him. The homework is hard but straight from the textbook; help is not far

Good lecturer and fair grader. Because it's in the physics dept, not a lot is in his control, but his explanations were solid and tests were easy once you figured out what sorts of things he would ask you. Take good notes in lecture, do all the homework (on time or early!), and do practice tests!

Kept the content straightforward, and always sprinkled in cool anecdotes during lecture! (He was the Chancellor of Berkeley for 10 years and is a world-renowned scientist) Really sweet man, and the tests are extremely fair. Definitely take 7B with him while he's still teaching it!

Lectures were okay - always had to read the textbook to understand the material. He tells stories about famous friends during lecture which is pretty cool. Tests are very derivation based (which is good!). ALWAYS practice on his old tests before his exams, EXTREMELY helpful (since they are very similar). If you study & do your work, you will be ok!

Average quality for physics lecturers. His lectures are straight from the bookhe actually gives all of the examples/practice problems in the text. Sometimes assigns MT/final problems from there, which is nice. It's Physics 7B so your prof doesn't really matter. His test difficulty reflects what's on TBP. )Also, he'll probably get a Nobel prize.)

Birgeneau is very accomplished, and lectures are interesting when he throws in life stories. Assigns weekly MasteringPhysics HW which isn't too bad. 2 midterms and a final, all very heavy on theory and derivations. No formula sheet allowed, and the one provided is sparse. You end up having to derive most of the equations not included

This is most likely the best class I'll every take within Berkeley. I took this course as a non-engi major but the lectures are so diverse and interesting. Basically no homework (1 discussion post per week), mid-term, and final. The mid-term and final were reasonable essay+proj. A class that you can actually enjoy learning without being stressed.

Prof is the goat. Class consisted of a guest lecturer discussing a topic every week and tying it back to ethics. The course itself is made up of attendance, discussion posts and a group project. Super fun class, take this!
No HW, amazing guest lectures, no exams. Only a few supplementary assignments, and a final project. Highly recommend.

Karl Van Bibber is the most caring and excellent professor, nay human, I have ever met. He has such a gusto for life and at his age his pure energy is amazing. The seminar was super easy as long as you showed up and listened, and very interesting too. The crowning gem of this class though is Karl himself. I am Karl's #1 fan.

Prof. Van Bibber works hard to continuously improve the Nuclear Engineering Department, and nowhere else are his efforts more evident than in the quality and diversity of course offerings. Van Bibber is a phenomenal lecturer, and his decades of experience become apparent when he takes to the podium.

A great teacher. His test always had one hard abstract problem that would throw a lot of people. He's very very enthusiastic about getting student involved and overall was a great teacher. His explanations were sometimes a little confusing but in the end he'll make sure you know the subject. Make sure you know "conflict of interest"

Homework problems from the book were easy, but the problems he makes up were very conceptual and difficult, and accounted for the most points. He's enthusiastic (goes on physics tangents a lot) and will answer questions thoroughly. Concepts can be confusing since he skims the basics. Exams were very difficult (generous curve) so study the lectures.
Honors is a one of a kind experience and Professor Bimes is a cheerleader every step of the way, very approachable, and gives great feedback.

Professor Bimes is very knowledgeable on her subject. The class was enjoyable, with a heavy emphasis on group discussion. She grades fair. If you are interested in the subject you will be in good hands.

She is a very kind, approachable professor. She is very knowledgeable and passionate about what she teaches. Her slides are HORRIBLE, however. Her lecture structure, in turn, is disorganized and can be hard to follow, as others have mentioned. It is not a hard class, however. Readings are straightforward and exams are practical.

I wrote my honors thesis in political science, of which Professor Bimes was an advisor. I've heard she's normally chill, but we had a few bumps in the road. I think it was due to a lot of variables not necessarily either of our fault. I'd be willing to take a class with her and see how she is in a classroom setting.

Professor Bimes is one of the best professors I've had at Berkeley! She deeply cares about her students and want their success. Her lectures did not necessarily follow the PowerPoints, but taking notes based on her outline is easy. Her lectures, doing the readings, etc help out when it comes to assignments. Your grade reflects the work you put in.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment:
My issues with taking American Presidency:
- she lectured off a prepared outline/notes but I found it difficult to follow her train of thought. Her PowerPoints were terrible and mostly images
- midterm and final were very specific and unnecessarily hard
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Bimes is passionate about what she teaches, and incredibly kind. I feel like it's quite obvious that she's more liberal, but she tries to not let this affect her teaching. She cares about her students and granted class-wide extensions and dropped an extra assignment/quiz after class feedback. Quite a few assignments, but manageable! Take 102!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I am obsessed with Professor Bimes. She is funny, knowledgable, passionate, and deeply cares about her students. Her quirky personality and insights make the class very engaging. Only drawback is there is quite a bit of reading.

Bimes is too biased. Nice lady but not great at public speaking. Her bias against the President was over the top, even for Berkeley. She let one of my classmates, who is a member of Antifa, run many of the class discussions. Not worth it. She assigned too much reading and a final research paper in addition to a final exam.

Prof. Bimes is a great lecturer, and a very caring and sweet human being. The course was interesting and structured well. I felt the exams were graded fairly and weren't too difficult compared to other courses. My GSI (Michael D.) ruined the course for me: very harsh grader on the papers & didn't provide clear feedback.

Professor Bimes is amazing! She advises honors students for their senior thesis and I'm so glad that I got to be in her section. During your first conversation with her, you'd be able to tell right away that she is one of the few professors who actually cares about students. I couldn't have completed my 80-page thesis without Professor's guidance.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--CARES ABOUT STUDENTS--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: If you don't want to devote your LIFE to reading, dont take this class. Theres a 700 page reader, a 200 page book and then another book that you read half the articles out of. Bimes is very nice and helpful. Most of the class believed the grading was pretty harsh for exams. You learn quite a bit about the office though.

I absolutely loved Professor Bimes...she is an awesome teacher. She is very sweet and really knows her stuff. This was by far my favorite class at Berkeley. There is a lot of reading, but the work load isn't too bad and Bimes is really helpful if you just talk to her. Highly suggest this class to anyone interested in politics!

Prof. Bimes is awesome.  I took a junior seminar with her and the class was really fun.  The lecture was just a discussion by the class about a topic for the week. Only drawback is that there is A LOT of reading. But that was offset by the fact that the only real assignment was a big research paper at the end. But she is very nice and very helpful.

She's really nice and approachable, which was great for a seminar class. However, she requires an absurd amount of reading. Even though she's really nice, she has pretty high expectations. But it's a rarity to have a professor that isn't full of him/herself, and you won't have to bare with that BS with Terri. Visit her office hours!

Prof def cares about his course & shares a lot about his research. He is nice & gives great feedback in office hours. He also cares about timeliness—he's willing to give extensions per his syllabus but don't show up late for class or leave early. This class requires some light-moderate reading (for an upperdiv), all materials are on bCourses.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: He is the best professor I've ever had in college! He cares deeply about his students and will devote time outside of class to meet with you and help you understand the material. His enthusiasm for Native American studies really shines through. Take his class! You won't regret it.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He goes off topic so much and has revised our syllabus 5 times to accommodate for how behind he gets. Lots of readings that are very dense. Lecture attendance isn't mandatory but is needed to connect readings for papers. 3 papers in total. Very picky about how he wants papers written so I suggest you run ideas by him in office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Tom is kind, humble, and easy going professor-- he genuinely cares for his students. There is five essays and he is a bit of a tough grader. He is selective with the wording in essays. He gives us detailed feed back on how we can improve on each essay. There is a lot of books that need to be read. He has made me in a better writer I can say.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--So many papers

reviews.comment: Thomas Biolsi is not the most engaging professor & tends to go off on tangents often; however, he is very knowledgeable and is very open to discussion in class. There are 5, 5-paged papers for this class and you are expected to incorporate lecture material & readings into the papers (maximum 6 readings per week). Grading is average.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Fanning is my favorite Haas marketing professor after having taken 3 of his classes. Very caring,  super straight forward with exceptions and assignments, has great projects with clear criteria, and fantastic guest speakers. Would highly recommend all of his classes!

Professor Fanning is definitely one of the best marketing professors here at Berkeley. I learned a lot of really core concepts and he did a great job at bringing in a lot of guest lectures! This class definitely thought me to think creatively. It wasn't as technical as I expected though so if you're looking for that, this isn't the class.
He always does my hair for me.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers--Respected

reviews.comment: I really don't understand the hate for this course. Consumer Insights was by far the best course I've taken in college! The professor is passionate and values perspectives of all backgrounds. The material is a really interesting mix of psychology and marketing. Great for anyone looking to go into consumer insights, UX research, market research, etc

So boring. This is not an engaging class like others said. Also, the grading in this class is ridiculous, the GSI will literally do anything to mark points off, and not give you a full score on anything. The lectures are mandatory, and pointless, though I will say the guest lectures in this class were very good, and helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Boring (mandatory) lectures, uninspiring, few ways to truly engage in the classroom, participation is awarded based on how he feels you participated in class (in which there is no measurable way to define the magnitude of participation, and is subject to his memory), and grading, while mostly fair, could use some more transparency.

Don't this class if you're looking for a course with technical concepts actually rooted in marketing. His lectures are dull and uninspiring with surface-level content that's just common sense. He shows favoritism to the chattiest, so be ready to constantly raise your hand. Grading is subjective, and give details even if instructions say otherwise.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class has mandatory attendance, and you have to participate or else he will lower your grade. The GSI is a tough grader, she will find any reason to deduct points. Also be prepared to sit for the entire lecture and just listen to him rant, honestly you have to be passionate for business in order to actually enjoy his lectures. SO BORING!

I wish I have read the comment for 160 before taking it. The class is dull like what others said, no use of electronics allowed, only him talking for 1 hour and a half with only a few bullet points of notes. Grading is purely subjective if graded by him and disproportional to efforts spent. Not many things you can take away from this class.
Lectures can be a bit boring but overall if you pay attention and put effort into participating you should do fine.

Prof Fanning definitely has useful background experience, but his lectures kind of drone on. Marketing is inherently subjective but I felt like he expected objective answers on exams and assignments, which was frustrating. Abundant use of relevant case studies is the best part of this class.

I don't know why his rate is so low because Fanning is one of the best professors I had while at Berkeley. His Advertising Strategy class is very interesting and fun. His lectures are easy to understand and he gives a lot of very useful advices for you to use in your career, if you plan on working in Marketing. Take it! You won't regret it.

Professor Fanning was a great lecturer. He had always the right examples for each of the topics and showed so many advertisings that were already si familiar making the content make more sense. He is super responsive on email, overall great professor.

I would recommend professor Fanning to anyone. Our whole class loved him and we learned so much! UGBA 165 was so fun and we all can say it was one of our favorite classes at UCB. He also made the online experience way better!
Lectures were unorganized and boring. He does not have slides prepared. Lectures were not that engaging.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Fanning is a really good lecturer. He uses a lot of examples from media (since it was an advertising class) and makes the lecture really entertaining. He also listens to students' thoughts and respects them, which encourages more participation during class. Overall, he is a very caring, thoughtful professor with a qualified background.

Fanning is a decent professor. His explanations are usually good but don't offer much depth beyond what's on the slides. He also tended to lecture for long periods of time, making participation challenging. Grading is clear and generally fair, and revolves mostly around a group presentation and several written assignments.

Would highly advise against taking with Fanning. Lectures are boring and tiresome and provide no insight into the material. Youre better off reading the textbook. Beyond that, he is incredibly quick to shut down any ideas that he doesnt see as correct even though he asserts time and time again that there is no correct answer in marketing.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Bill teaches section & is considered an add-on prof, so he isn't the official lecturer FYI.  Would highly recommend avoiding his section. A bad teacher who values smooth-talkers over insight. In a class that should promote creativity and participation, he rudely shuts down your ideas/comments. Had my phone out ONE time and he lowered my grade...
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed Bilder's cell biology portion. Not only is he a brilliant lecturer who knows how to describe cellular processes with the right words and analogs, but he simplifies the material well. His lectures are straightforward, but his exams require you to think outside the box and draw heavily upon the concepts. Overall, I recommend!

He is a great lecturer and makes the material even more interesting than it is. He only used slides and also showed some short clips to help our understanding. His exam was VERY long and much more complicated than I expected, the over all average was low. But a very interesting class and subject.
Uses chalk!  Teaches the material as a story, focusing on concepts and the way things were discovered as opposed to boring factoids.
No Comments

Biwen was awesome! The tests were very easy, and you get a note sheet. On top of that, she curves the final heavily so even if you bomb it, you'll still get a decent grade. Only 4 hws the whole semester, and they were all quick and easy. Beware of cold calling in class though. Take her if you can.

Made this course a lot easier to understand and you can tell that she really cares about the future of her students. I would 100% take a class with her again. Would give her above a 5 if I could, extremely fair grader and you get cheat sheets on the exams. The grading is exam heavy but she does a great job preparing you for success.

She really tries her best to teach accounting in the simplest, easiest way possible at a (honestly, a little bit too) slow pace. She cold-calls but makes it fun somehow, and she brought in alumni accounting professionals 3-4 times during the semester. Gives out candy and even gift cards for Kahoot. She's also just a super amazing person all around.
Amazing professor, amazing course

Truly wonderful professor -- one of Haas' best. Dr. Zhang cares deeply for all students and rewards those who put in the effort. Her lectures are accessible and consistently engaging. Dr. Zhang's passion is clear in the personality she adds to every single lecture. Amazing experience and a must-take for anyone who wants some accounting experience.
Biwen Zhang is a great professor who explains concepts very clearly and has good preparation content for exams

Biwen is an excellent professor for those who are learning accounting for the first time, she really broke it down as much as she could during lectures. The course was very well run and I took away a lot from this class. 

The only thing I'd gently caution students is that 85% of your grade is determined by your performance in the midterm + final

I really liked prof Biwen. She was very considerate of student needs. Although since a lot of the assignments were graded on completion, out final was very long and pretty challenging. Cheat sheets were allowed which help avoid memorizing too many formulae
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Such a nice and caring professor. Exams are relatively easy as you get a cheat sheet and homework is rare but it can be long. Would definitely recommend her.

Her lectures are very clear and her practice questions during class are very similar to what's on the exam. The exams had generous curves. She is also a very funny and caring professor. As someone who struggles with numbers, she makes accounting easy to understand!

I really enjoyed taking her class. Her powerpoints are great. My only con is that she teaches material very fast. Study guides and practice exams are good. The homework and midterm were easy. The final was challenging and hard but doable. I recommend Biwen for 102A.
She is an expert at explaining financial accounting concepts. Her lectures make the material feel simple and easy to follow.

Biwen is one of the most caring professors I've ever had at my time at Berkeley. As someone who was not excited for financial accounting prior to this course, Biwen made the material digestible, and interesting by showing us real-world applications of our learnings. I cant recommend her enough. She genuinely loves teaching and it shows

Biwen is an amazing accounting professor. She broke down the concepts to where most, if not all, students understood. The homework was easy and the midterm was very easy if you paid attention. The reason I didn't rate her a 5 was because of the final. It was more than you would expect and the average was so much lower than the midterm.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Biwen Zhang is a great person, but her teaching skills are questionable. At times, her instructions can be unclear.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Zhang is extremely caring, in fact, one of the most caring professors I've had at Berkeley. She breaks down the concepts so well and the class is very doable for all levels. I have to admit that after a semester of accounting with her, my knowledge about this field has changed drastically. Overall, she cares so much about her students!!!

Biwen cares a TON about her students. She is newer at Cal and it is sometimes hard to understand her accent but over the course of the semester her lectures have gotten much better. She really wants to help students with interviews, job prep, and everything else. Her teaching can sometimes be slow given how easy the midterm was but she is so nice.

Beyond the logistical adjustments Prof made during finals weeks, the content and her teaching style was engaging and promoted a significant understanding of financial accounting. Professor Zhang cares a lot about her students and attempts to maximize learning by gauging the class' level of understanding at the end of each lecture. Great prof.

I have never had a worse processor at Cal. It was her first semester, but this was unreal. Easily 5 emails a day, changed the final to be completely proctored a week before and then changed the format again the day before. Final itself was weighted 45% with a ridiculous amount of MC and short/long answer questions for an INTRO class. Avoid
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This was Professor Zhang's first semester at CAL. At first, she was nice and cooperative with her students. Everything turned for the worst the last week before finals. On top of her 10 anxiety-filled announcements a day, she thought it would be a great idea to implement a new proctoring software less than a week before the final. Would not recomme

She had the chance to be a good teacher but disappointed in the end. Unable to stand her ground, she tainted the experience by changing the final format days before the exam to a testing program that majority of students had no experience using. She allowed herself to be bullied by the vocal minority of the class. Not considerate of pandemic. Sad.

Biwen is the nicest, most caring professor I have had at Cal. She genuinely wants everyone to succeed and makes that possible with clear grading criteria, practice midterms that are almost identical to the real one, and an encouraging, fun class atmosphere. Genuinely just a really nice and fair professor, take her for accounting!
Hes one of the best profs at Cal. Evidently he really cares about his work and make sure students learn the materials in a more intuitive way than many math and cs profs.

Great and challenging class with thorough problem sets. Strong first principles learning (building key causal and ML algorithms from scratch without packages), followed by applying modern packages to novel datasets (usually policy as per his research/labs). I'm glad I struggled through it as I learned a ton
One of the best classes I've ever taken. The way of teaching was great.
I learned so much from the lectures and the problem sets! The TA's were also awesome, very helpul. The material can be mathy but he's one of the best profs at giving lectures I've seen at Cal!
