I've taken more machine learning classes before but this is definitly the best of all of them
lots of work, but will learn a LOT with this class
Best machine learning class at Berkeley or online, worth fighting to get in to
I had to work a lot on the side because I didn't know Python very good before, but it was worth the extra work, absolutely.

It was refreshing to take a course on machine learning from someone who actually understands the subject well enough to explain it in Plain English! So much better than the typically lecture-the-textbook approach taken by lots of CS profs these days (even at a place like Berkeley!)..
Great class. Doable and interesting,keeps you gripped!!
probly the best of the msim profs, no so easy a grader but learn more important knowledge then in other classes at uw
so much better than the machine learning class i took in cse
Easy to understand, and helpful
Tough but fair. Tries hard.
Cool GSI
he was definitely one of the better gsi's i've had around, though sometimes i would want him to slow down and explain things more.  most useful during office hours
I spend lots of time in office hours, and he was pretty much always round and happy to help.  good gsi and not hard to understand

Josh was always will and able to help.  I didn't know much about the topic before taking the class but he was enthusiastic and now I'm going to try to take more development classes.  I'd highly recommend him as a GSI

Prof Bishop's lectures do tend to feel monotonous at times, but he cares about his students, explained things well, and had many chances to boost grades, ex. having extra credit for attendance, and redoing questions on the exams. There were few homework assignments, and the GSI walked us through the steps to do them. Take chem before this class tho

Professor Bishop's lectures often seemed incoherent and lacked real structure. He often failed to lay foundations for concepts that would later be built upon, leaving students to struggle. Luckily, the creative projects/field trips allowed for easy points that boosted grades. Iclicker was used daily to track both attendance and comprehension.

Prof. Bishop is visibly passionate about what he teaches, but his lectures can be hard to follow; I struggled with the chemistry portion of the class. Exams are very similar to homework assignments, just longer and more cumulative. I took this for a breadth and found it challenging but not impossible.

Not the most entertaining lecturer, but he is very fair with grading and helpful outside of class. I put in average effort and got an A, so I'd say this class is an easy A for a breadth. The creative projects and field trips are easy ways to boost your grade. The textbook was pretty useless tho, as the slides taught me everything I needed to know.

The lectures were pretty slow, but you can tell Prof. Bishop is passionate. I personally suffered from a lack of chemistry foundations, because he just jumped into ocean chemistry without much prep. Also, the assignments rarely covered material that were addressed in class, so there was a lot of self-teaching.

Absolutely one of the most horrible classes I've ever taken at Berkeley. I took this course as a breadth, which I expected to be interesting and easy. This professor made the materials so hard and so boring. I late changed this class to PNP, but honestly just don't take it.

Professor Bishop is clearly very passionate about what he is teaching, and I appreciated his sense of humor during lectures. Lectures slowly, but an easy A. Attendance is mandatory (iClicker), and lectures are recorded. The textbook wasn't very useful, and most of the time the assigned readings weren't addressed in lectures or in exam questions.

The prof is a really sweet PERSON but he is not an entertaining LECTURER (I almost never went to his lectures) So many reddit posts said this is an easy A class but the materials are actually rly confusing and the tests are kinda hard so def do not listen to what people say online. The creative projects + curve def help u boost up ur grade tho

The homeworks seem completely irrelevant to the lectures. Also very math heavy which makes no sense because that did not match the description. I heard this class was easy-- easy to who? I don't know. His lectures are mundane and not clear either. GSI's did not help either :/ Go bears
His lectures can be pretty dry and the mandatory iclicker attendance is tough, but overall its a pretty easy and straightforward class with interesting material. Pretty good choice for a breadth.

I took this for a breadth because I heard it was easy, but let me tell you, I literally don't think I understand this class. He's a nice guy but a bad lecturer and even rewatching course captures, I still don't know what's going on. Tests and homework feel irrelevant to class and the grading is so random. Also no curve. I P/NP the class. DON'T TAKE
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Lectures are extremely boring and monotone, does not cover much relevant information and must read textbook on your own. Markschemes for homework are absolutely ridiculous. Whoever is grading some of these assignments are clearly blind, marking many things as "Did not attempt" when they were clearly attached within the assignment.

All lecture did was give me the name of a concept to go home and teach myself. Lectures messy and unclear, HW has little to no connection to lec and exams are totally separate as well. Dont bother with office hours, he cant seem to understand that hes not clear. Extremely tough grader for how little he teaches us. Course is a nightmare, dont take.

Bishop is a so-so lecture as he can be monotonous and awkward at times. He's a great guy but is not so great at lecturing. Oceans was fine but didn't go over some concepts clearly enough. Not a bad choice for a breadth though.

I looked forward to going to Oceans every day. The material and lectures are interesting and enjoyable. I felt like this class taught me a lot. There are 6 assignments, 3 field trips/creative assignments, and 2 midterms. An average amount of effort will get you an A.

Jim is fairly boring. Oceans was not too bad and I think I could've gotten an A had I put in a little more effort on the midterms. iClickers make attendance mandatory, which is a bummer because the class is recorded and uploaded anyways. He's neutral, not great, and not terrible, either. A fine class to take for a breadth.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: The content of this class was not very difficult but every time Jim spoke in his monotone voice, it fell flat on many ears and caused a lot of students to just have to learn on their own. Especially true for the latter part of this class in which more difficult material was "taught" but it was just more and more confusing with little explanation.

I've never had a lecturer quite as scatterbrained and tangential as Bishop. The grading scale is very forgiving but his lectures border on worthless due to lack of clarity but iClickers make them mandatory. Section is an absolute MUST especially if your GSI is good.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: He's such a bad lecturer I don't understand anything in class
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Prof. Bishop is a nice person and is very enthusiastic about the material, but listening to him can be really exhausting as he often loses his train of thought or doesn't complete sentences. Easy class, but lecture was a drag.

I took Oceans out of pure interest in the topic and P/NP in preparation of the Biology /Physics. Boy, was I wrong. Really easy class for me to pass. Jim "Jimmy" Bishop is a great person. He's a little lackluster in performance when it comes to lectures, but he is truly trying his best to get us interested in his passion, which is what counts.
Best Lecturer Ever at Berkeley!

This semester they changed the class. It was a really fun class and I learned a lot, however I worked my butt off to get an A. If you want to work, this is your class! Professor Bishop always is so excited for his class and is always enthusiastic, but sometimes can be a bit confusing. In all of my classes at Cal this is the class I learned the most

Professor BIshop was very nice and you could tell by listening to him that he absolutely loves what he is doing. But tht aside he does not explain the material very well and sometimes he will give information contradictory to the text book. I highly recommend going to the discussion sections, it is where everything gets sorted out.

Professor Bishop is a nice guy, and he is genuinely interested in getting people excited about the ocean. He's not the most engaging lecturer, and the class logistics were poorly organized. It's not difficult material if you put minimal effort into it. All-in-all, if you have a general interest in the ocean (or science) it's not the worst class.

He has great intentions but he has no idea how difficult his course is; there is a major emphasis on chemistry during the final third of the class and he sort of just expects you to figure it out. The best days were those where Bishop stepped aside and allowed the GSI's to lecture-- about 40% of classes. Most difficult 2 unit class available; avoid

He is a nice person, but a boring lecturer. I found the class a bit too hard for a 2-unit class. Get ready to study a lot if you want to get an A. Best way to get ready for the midterms and a final- attend all lectures and take good notes!
Really scattered lectures. He often just starts talking about something complicated without ever telling you what it is. He only does about a third of the lectures though.

Most boring lectures EVER. Thankfully Prof Rhew is incredibly pedagogical and entertaining to boot and co-teaches this class. Bishop seems to have little interest in teaching but his credentials speak for themselves. He says he seeks feedback, but it doesnt show in his lack-luster lectures. NOT and "easy A".

Such a nice, helpful guy. he even gave me extra office hours. Material is ALOT to memorize but if you put yourself in the mindset that you do not hate the class, it can get pretty intresting. Too much work for a 2 unit class and tests are very detailed. However, I put in alot of effort and if you do too, you should be fine. but dont expect a easy A

Most of the material covered in lecture is what is on the test, & the class is very "memorization oriented" overall, so should be a definitely manageable A. You don't have to read all the readings, just try to read what is explicitly talked about in class and it'll be smoother sailing for your grade.

He's a really nice guy that really tries to help you in office hours; he has a rather monotone voice so it could be hard to stay awake. This class is no longer as easy as everyone says it is;the extra credit went down significantly but it's def A doable if you study. but you really have to study. I liked him more. rhew was condescending in office h

My freshman seminar was interesting, albeit a little slow moving.  He's definitely knowlegable in his field and HELLA Canadian. Though the class wasn't that exciting, the free sailboat ride around the bay was AMAZING. Take the seminar, it's awesome.

103 is difficult but Bishop is the best man to teach it.He will tell you what to study for the midterms;they are no surprise. Homeworks are hard: go to OH. Write down everything he says:its all important and relevant.He is so smart and will present groundbreaking research/news. Very understanding and cares SO much about the well being of students.

Overall, he is an easy teacher. His tests are just memorization. He is also very boring, try to stay awake, and make sure to learn what he tells you in class, especially the topics he does research on, he is really passionate about that carbon cycle and will test you on it any chance he gets.

Bishop has a kind heart and loves to help students. However, he also loves to ramble about material that is irrelevant to the course. He LOVES chemistry and will douse it on you right and left and it will also appear on the midterms. Random stuff from lecture will be on the midterms know it all. Read the book and go to office hours to clarify.

BORING!!! His class is very easy, and he is a nice guy, but he is so monotonous. He likes to brag about his trips over seas and talks about really irrelevant stuff. Try to avoid him, he can make even the most interesting class very boring.
super funny and nice!!

Mr. Bland cares about his students and cares about doing education right. His EDSTEM class was not demanding at all, but participation was important in the two hours of class per week. I would take his class again. Always interactive, some activities more interesting than others. Great guy, easy to talk to.
Great!!

Professor Bland is such a kind and caring instructor. He teaches at a local Berkeley high school and is a Berkeley CalTeach alum, which makes him perfect for teaching this intro CalTeach tutoring course. He was incredibly knowledgeable about the course. He was also understanding of the pandemic's effects on students and was lenient on grading.
Definitely a difficult class, but rewarding. Professor Blum's teaching style made it interesting and worth the effort. Grateful for the experience!

Class was totally doable if you actually study. All in-class exams with lots of Japanese terms to memorize. It's a lot at first, but gets easier when you put in consistent effort. Professor is knowledgeable and explains things well. Grading is detailed and fair. Learned a lot and would recommend if you truly wanna know more about Japan

Honestly, this was the worst class I've ever taken. For the final, we had to know how to answer 100+ terms and 50+ essay questions. It would have been better if the grading wasn't so strict - I need to hit every mark to get a full score.
Never take this class unless you want to get a C, regardless of how hard you work.

great professor if you truly wanna learn something about Buddhism! He's super kind and knowledgeable about Japan and buddhism and easy to talk with. A lot of readings and it will be worthy to do them, if you studied hard following the study guide he gave, you will be fineeeeee and A is not that hard!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: mandatory attendance and expensive printed pdfs, weird jokes about east asian culture unrelated to the contents and sounds condescending all the time, would kill an orphan to avoid taking this his class again.
Engaging and funny professor, even though he mostly just reads off his notes. Can tell that he is very knowledgable and has a lot of insights.

mandatory $55 course reader that is just pdfs he could've posted for free. also scheduled a quiz the day after a holiday. his lectures are fine but he's weird about technology and also will cold call you to make sure you're always paying attention.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Blum is such a knowledgeable person and his lectures are super engaging. There's a lot of readings to do, and his courses span topics that need a good amount of knowledge beforehand, but he makes sure to cover anything you may not know. Expects his students to try, but grades very fairly. I've taken 3 of his classes, and would take more.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Blum is incredibly well knowledged, informative, and engaging. His class was like a history, theology, sociology, and language class all rolled into one. You are expected to do the readings, which are difficult, but he doesn't make you feel down for not knowing stuff. I'm impressed by his knowledge, and I learned a lot in the class.

If you're interested in the topic, the class will be engaging/interesting. He gives out study guides that will over prepare you for the exams, so it's an easy A if you do the work. GSIs are tough graders, but Prof Blum is kind + funny. Lots of reading + writing tho!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: You need to remember this. If you take this prof class, you will take C
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Prof. Blum has long lectures where he mostly reads off a wall of text which makes it quite boring although he is funny. The grading was done by GSIs, but they took off points for unknown reasons and didn't really help you improve besides giving vague advice. This class was honestly my hardest, not an easy A.
amazing at explaining content. lectures apply directly to labs & final exam. well organized w/ good amount of resources & fair grading policy, including dropping lowest lab.

Blackford was great, extremely understanding. She would respond to emails immediately after them being sent and she was always super responsive on ed discussion. She also adjusts her bins at the end so if you're like 1-2 points away from the next letter grade, you can get that grade. Overall great professor and can't wait to take 3BL with her too!

One of the best professors I've had at this school. Teaches clearly and her lectures (+ slides) are so helpful. Really appreciate that she does annotated versions as well so you still get all the notes if you can't make it. Super easy to communicate with through email. Looking forward to taking 3BL with her as well!

I enjoyed chem 3AL and 3BL with professor Blackford. I found her lectures to be pretty helpful for assignments and she also gives extra credit. Only really big downside is her finals are way harder than practice exams and we still had lab + a worksheet the same week as the lab final (for 3AL). Make sure you keep your grade up before the final fr
Teaches like the ochem tutor
literally the sweetest person ever, super nice and kind. her lectures are straightforward and clear and organized. super approachable and literally my favorite professor

The sweetest professor i've ever had, super willing to answer questions and very responsive by email & ed. She's SO SO SO nice and all her materials are rlly organized. Gives practice thats similar to exam. Shes amazing.

This professor is genuinely so sweet and kind. She made each lecture very approachable and her lecture notes/annotations were very helpful. I appreciated that the lab analysis was done in the lab period which dramatically decreased the amount of work I had to do outside of lab.

Dr.Blackford is an amazing prof. Makes lecture engaging and is super approachable when you have a question during office hours or after lecture. The data analysis sheets are reasonable and the prelab quizzes are significantly shorter than 1AL. Her final was a bit harder than the 2 practice exams provided, but it was fair. Overall, highly recommend!

Dr. Blackford is amazing! Her lectures are relevant to labs, and the data analysis sheets were completely doable in lab. Grading can be pretty nit picky on notebook pages, so make sure you record everything. Shes very accessible on Ed and in office hours and is so so kind! One of the best professors I have had the pleasure of taking at Cal :)

Easily the best of the lab professors I've had so far. The lab reports can be nitpicks but it's not any moreso than the other lower div lab classes. She is also the only professor whose lectures are actually relevant to the prefabs and is a GOAT on Ed Discussion. She also lowered the grade bins and I was sure I was gonna have an A- :).

Katie is such an approachable professor, someone truly passionate about teaching. When I was sick she allowed me to do the online lab and she responds quickly through email. If you have any problems whatsoever she will be sure to address them. The final was during the last week of classes and was medium difficulty. Lab reports are graded fairly.
Great lecturer, makes each class engaging

Very sweet person. The lectures are organized and connected to labs. They don't release lab solutions which makes it hard to study. At OH, she and GSIs usually give away data analysis answers. The final exam is on the east side and is similar to previous ones. I miss ~1.5 pts for each lab, 100% on lab worksheets, < 5pts on exam still give me an A.

Shes such a darling. Pretty good lecturer and is very accessible outside of class and answers p-much all student questions. Labs are hard but that's just orgo chem rly but shes a tough-ish grader on data analysis sheets and the final. Very sweet person and I do not regret taking her class but wished I put more effort in the data analysis sheets.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She is so sweet! Since she is on the younger side, she is very understanding and fun to have as a professor. Although the topic of the class can be challenging she makes sure to explain everything very well, and always tests you fairly. I really appreciate the amount of effort she puts in.

Best lab professor I've had-- lectures are really good and layout of class is easy and not too much busywork. Labs themselves can be annoying but that's any ochem class. If you're going to take 3BL, take it with blackford. So sweet and caring! There is one group project but it was not graded harshly lol. OHs can help with worksheets and post lab

Labs were interesting and not very time consuming. Topics introduced were important but not too complex. Exam at the end was somewhat similar to practice exam. Advice: keep up with the concepts introduced in class, they are tested on post-lab analysis, which make up bulk of grade.

Dr.Blackford is a breath of fresh air! She is fair in her grading, exams, and even gives some extra credit for attending lectures. She truly cares about making the material accessible and straightforward to students. Best CHEM 3AL professor!

Lectures directly relate to lab content, prelab quizzes are not very time consuming and only act to prepare you for the section ahead, extremely reachable over emails. Final was more than fair, albeit the lack of past exams to practice with. Good and enthusiastic 3AL instructor who provides you with everything you need to succeed in the course.

Really understanding and fast responses through email. Lectures are straightforward: reflected what she wanted us to know for the assignments and exam. Also, your gsi really makes or breaks the class. Online labs are helpful for speeding through the labs in person. Overall, very manageable class!
Super understanding, helpful lectures, and clear communication of course expectations

Surprised at some of these ratings for Prof. Blackford. Her lectures are extremely straightforward (they are not very engaging, but come on...it's Chem 3AL/3BL). Her best attribute is that she is by far the most easily reachable professor I've had at Berkeley. Answers emails/will answer your Ed Dis. posts almost instantly. Tough grader. Great prof

Her lectures were always easy to follow. However, her grading on some of the data analysis worksheets were a bit harsh and it seemed as if the most of the GSI's didn't know what was going on either. Overall, not a bad prof, but not good either just ok. If you do the work you should be fine.
Very nice and understanding professor. Lectures were helpful for pre-labs but analysis worksheets were graded harshly.
She was clearly new but very kind and dedicated to the students. She was very kind and 3AL ended up being very easy. She was unexpectedly kind and personable for a chemistry professor.
Nice person but horrible professor, and the lab coordinator was horrible too. GSIs did most of the work and made the class enjoyable.
Lectures were a waste of time and her inexperience showed throughout. GSIs were great though!

Katie was cool. 3al is a pretty low stakes class in general, but Katie's policies made it even more relaxed (first time teaching the class). Her assignments had very clear grading criteria and lectures covered everything you needed. She was also available through OH and Ed. Her final exam was a bit harder than previous instructors, but still fair
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Your experience in lab and grade on assignments is very dependent on your GSI (mine was great) but Blackford is really caring if you need an extension or you're having trouble understanding something. The lectures are organized and cover most stuff you need to know. Pre-lab quizzes and data analysis sheets aren't bad either.

First time teaching CHEM3AL. She wasn't a very good lecturer to be honest. The data analysis sheets and pre-lab quizzes we did supposedly were talked abt in lecture but I often had trouble doing them either way. Your GSI is v important b/c most of your grade is dpndnt on how they assess your work. The final was OK. Know your lab techniques is all.

Lectures are easy to follow, content is straightforward. Chem 3AL is a class in which your experience is more heavily determined by your GSI, but Blackford does a good job in providing the necessary content to answer all of the prelab quiz questions and sent prompt emails in the event that she misses anything in lecture. Overall good instructor.

Very nice and helpful when responding to questions on Ed and during office hours! Her lectures were chill and easy to follow, and I liked that she put memes in that were related to the experiments. The final wasn't that bad either as long as you do the practice exams and go back over the slides.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: One of the worst profs I've ever had, I know she's new so don't want to fault her too much but good god what a terrible class. Thank god my GSI was incredible which made up for it since lab was tons of fun. But the class was run so poorly, the lectures were mind-numbingly boring, and don't even get me started on the lab coordinator Ms. Briggs.

I love her but oh do I hate this class...more anxiety-inducing than it needs to be and while I get the philosophy behind her assignments I wish there were fewer of them. However, she's a great professor and was able to recognize there were issues with my lab partner without me ever needing to mention it.

Isabelle is an amazing professor who truly cares about her students. She is very honest and gives very direct feedback. She is not an easy A by any means but she will push you to develop your weaknesses. She makes herself available to students and goes out of her way to make sure you learn and grow, regardless of what your grade is.

Professor Le Blanc is one of the best professors I've had. To put it simple, she is straightforward so there will be no surprises on any exams or materials. She's passionate, Kind and she will never let you fall behind if you don't understand the material. It's a hard class but if you actually care to learn lab techniques and materials, she's got u
Run

One of the best professors I have had in my time at Cal. Genuinely cares for the students and is incredibly knowledgeable about what she does. Make sure to engage in the class and work with your peers. As well, ask the professor questions about the material. Many of the assignments are about independent reflection and clarification.

Numerous grading errors on the final. Lab write-up had arbitrary grading criteria (name on paper was worth points and penalized if forgotten). Nice person and semi-funny lecturer but overall extremely unorganized and obviously poor effort in her lectures (late or digressed from topics frequently). Straightforward class, though I didn't learn much.

I have to say that this class has been my most positive experience in Berkeley. I called Professor Le Blanc a mother figure since she def. has those mom moments. She's caring, professional, personable, and charismatic. Best professor so far; will keep in touch with her past graduation

Prof. Le Blanc was cheerful in lecture and office hours. She was also very funny with cool sound effects (Schloop!) that made learning fun! Super approachable outside of class and willing to explain things in detail. Exam was difficult and made you think and understand concepts.
The Goat of Bio 1B. Amazing lecturer, very passionate about subject material. Taught ecology in a very easy to digest way. Really enjoyed his section of the class.

What everyone else said. He's really great. Good lecture pace, good amount of content, and he was the only prof to provide full practice tests -- he even gave a cumulative review lecture before the final. Office hours were VERY helpful (get ready to have him ask YOU to explain things you're confused about!) Just a really amazing teacher.

He was extremely clear on what is going to be on the test and prepares you well. My biggest recommendation is to make flashcards with every single term. If you memorize all of them, you are pretty much guaranteed a good grade on the midterm and final. I didn't even study for his section on the final and I scored a 95%.

BEST professor out of the 3 for Bio 1B. Lectures were easy to follow and slides were extremely descriptive. Textbook optional. Gave clear information about what you can expect to see on the exams.  Only professor that gave us a practice midterm which was very useful. I wish he taught the whole course instead of splitting it up between 3 professors.

Professor Blonder taught the ecology section when I was in Bio 1B. His lectures were paced well and easy to understand. He gave out a practice midterm and made the actual one easier. He was also the only professor that gave a cumulative lecture before RRR week and not new material. THANK YOU SO MUCH for saving my grade.

All I can say is -- Thank God for this professor. He is single-handedly keeping the entire Bio 1B department alive. He explains the content well, he provides a fair practice midterm, and asks questions that aren't insanely minute and abnormal (compared to the rest of the course). If you don't want your love for biology to shrivel, try to have him!

Lectures are fast-paced and lots of slides, but understandable and interesting. Everything is group-based, and you stick with the same group for the whole semester. There are several small assignments (usually ~2/week), and everything is graded generously by standards (e.g. satisfactory, excellent).

Amazing lecturer, great at explaining concepts. Organized slides with everything you need to know for exams. Provides handouts for each lecture featuring key terms and practice questions, along with a practice midterm at the end of the unit. The midterm was fair and doable, you will end up getting the grade you earned.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very organized slides and handouts. Not the most interesting content though, felt very textbook surface level based. On the flip side, tests were easier. Only professor that provided a practice test which was extremely nice. However, this section had the hardest frqs (still easy, but required understanding the content well in other applications).

Amazing lecturer, great at explaining concepts. Organized slides with everything you need to know. Provides great resources, topic handouts, with key terms and practice questions for each lecture, and a practice midterm. Reasonable difficulty, average on midterm was 85%, me personally I got a 89%.

Really accessible outside of class, and approachable during office hours if you have any questions. Wished I went to office hours earlier, and got to learn a lot beyond the curriculum and application of real world issues! Really inspirational! Go to office hours, highly recommend!!
Great professor! Lectures were engaging and spent much time in office hours clearly explaining any questions whatsoever

Best Bio1B Professor! His slides are incredibly concise yet informative, and his teaching style and speed is optimal for student engagement and understanding. Very thorough explanations and examples made it easy for me to apply this knowledge to the exam. Plus he provides lots of practice problems throughout the lectures!

the best professor out of the three for BIO1B (spring 2024). his slides are very clear and he actually provides lots of support and resources for exams. is very clear about what will and will not be on midterms. sweet and accessible!
Nice lectures. Nice person to talk to. Lots of group work.
Professor Blonder explains all of the concepts very well! It is easy to understand the lectures, and if there are any equation derivations, you are not required to remember them!

Dr. Blonder is very knowledgeable about ecology and explains the concepts in a very straightforward fashion. He says explicitly what's going to be on the exam and his materials match exactly (even down to the questions). On both his final and midterm I got an A with relatively little stress.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Lectures and content are super organized and midterms are fair. Take him for ecology bio1b, I wanna take his other class he's great. Always gave examples to everything/vocab he was talking about unlike Blackman (organismal)

Covered Ecology part of Bio1B. Clear slides and organized. Lectures were interesting and applicable. Learned a lot, but most of the information was intuitive/familiar. Midterm was decent for most people.

Clearly extremely knowledgeable and cares deeply for student engagement. Very forgiving on tests and homework, he even amended our midterm after it was made clear one of the questions was unfair. Also very available outside of class.
In my option, the best lecturer of the 3 in bio1b (ecology section). Fair exams. Connections to the modern world.

He moved through course content super quickly which made things hard to follow. The lectures often talked about different things that were unrelated but only mentioned briefly which was confusing. He also brings up a lot of math in lectures that he told us we did not need to know, but why bring it up in the first place? He is a nice guy tho.

I took him for Ecology (ESPM C153) and he was great! He really cared about our learning, and was very approachable. He is very passionate about teaching and ecology which made me fall in love with the class. I would recommend this class or any that are thought by him!

Professor Blonder is the darling of Bio 1B. All of my friends love him and he is the best question writer and lecturer in the course by far. Wonderful, in-depth, interesting lectures and I looked forward to class despite it being an 8 am! Impressive time management skills and just overall super great.
Prof Blonder really cares about what he teaches and his lectures are engaging and clear. Great professor!

He certainly cares about what he teaches but goes on and on about the mathematical models and political implications of ecology, which are important but often too tedious for an introductory biology class.

Really enjoyed all the discussion about climate change and optional application readings. Prof Blonder's ecology section was my favorite part of Bio1B and the test questions reflected this in my final grades (a saving grace for a rough course). You can tell the guy is really excited about what he's teaching and I'd take him as a prof again.
Very enthusiastic and inspired me to learn.

Lectures are logical and clear with some deeply hidden humor. Difficulty levels of exams are reasonable. Also he frequently answers questions on piazza. Definitely the best prof among the 3 profs who teaches bio 1b. I never liked ecology before, but his lectures made me feel a lot better about it.
Best prof among the three in Bio 1B. He makes ecology fun to learn.

I REALLY LOVE PROFESSOR BLONDER. I WOULD LOVE TO TAKE ANOTHER CLASS WITH HIM AND I WOULD LITERALLY TAKE A BULLET FOR HIM. HE IS MY FAVORITE PROFESSOR OF ALL TIME HERE AT CAL! I thought I was too dumb for Cal STEM classes, but he made me fall in love with studying biology <3 :) I love it!

Prof. Blonder is an intelligent and fascinating professor! His classes are very engaging and it is clear that he is passionate about what he teaches. He is tough on his students, but because he wants to see them grow and learn.

TAKE HIS CLASS! I took his online Hist 2A class online and this is my second time taking one of his classes. I just love how independent it is (great class for people that have to work). Easy assignments, no tests/ exams, EXTRA CREDIT! Responds fast. Overall, great teacher and class, 100% take his class. :)

Took his class at Laney College, online. Amazing! 1 Discussion board w/ responses and 1 essay a week. Very easy. Slow grader. Extra credit! Clear instruction. Don't slack off or you will be behind! But a 10/10 professor and a 10/10 class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: No hard deadlines for anything, lots of extra credit opportunities. However, be aware that you'll have to do a LOT of reading and writing. I took him for History of California at Laney, and we had to write 12 essays in total for his midterm 2 + final. Interesting material, so the reading wasn't too bad. No late penalties, but don't slack off!
I took Blakes history class at Laney College. Super awesome dude and very passionate about what he teaches.
I wish he was staying at UC Berkeley and Laney is lucky to be getting him. One of the best professors I've had and an incredibly nice person. And He is pretty cute!

The class had co-instructors and Blake was the much better one (the other, Alex, was very nervous and disorganized) who ended up doing most of the lectures. Blake's a good lecturer, cute too, and covered tons of stuff, but the highlight of the class were the discussions he ran at the end of every class which were much more interactive and lively.

He wasn't as bad of a professor as his ratings are, but the content he teaches was by far the most difficult of the course. I found it the most interesting, but there is just so much content packed into a few lectures that most people perform poorly on his exams.

He doesn't deserve this low of a rating, IMO. His section is doable, and pedagogically sound, but it's very compact due to the contraints of the course in general. But it all makes sense and the exam questions aren't too heinous if you put in the time and effort to really know every bit of lecture material. His office hours are a godsend.

I recommend before every test rewatching every single lecture of his and writing notes on everything he says (emphasis on everything). On the ORGBIO midterm, I did not study that well, and scored a 45% when the class average was around 60%. Then, during dead week, I rewatched every single lecture and  when I retook the midterm, I scored a 93%.

He is kind and caring to students but rushes through the content WAY too fast.  Never went to lecture in person, and I had to keep rewinding the lecture recording to understand what he was talking about.  Would be a good professor if he slowed down and didn't cover as much material.  Exams were challenging due to the amount of things covered.

Good professor but way too much content. Take advantage of his org bio labs, since they were the most useful labs in the whole course; when you're not actively writing something on the handout, take notes at each station, ask the GSI questions, make sure you understand every step of the lifecycle and every part of the plant. DO HIS TOPIC HANDOUTS.

Organismal Biology is a tough section, but Blackman does a good job explaining everything. To be successful on his midterm and final, it is important to understand how every piece of information connects with each other, attend all the lectures, and go to office hours. I got a 95 on his midterm and a 90 on his section of the final by doing this.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Experiencing his portion of Bio 1B was demoralizing, to say the least. Plenty of students, including myself, had A's in the class until it was time for his midterm and final section. Honestly, I won't put all the blame on him: he was a pretty nice man, just a flawed lecturer with paragraphs on slides. The horribly managed course is the issue.

Tests for his unit of Bio 1B were needlessly hard. Get ready to memorize... like a LOT. Sure the unit has hard concepts, but his lectures were very difficult to follow and the tests, in my opinion, are vocab-heavy for no clear reason. Hope you're excited about fungi!

Pretty decent at explaining concepts. Gives topic handouts with practice mcqs, frqs, and key terms. The problem is, there is a ridiculous amount of content packed in a month that you must learn. Yes, Blackman is decent at explanations in general but not enough for how packed the slides are. Explanations otherwise feel rushed. Avg D each midterm.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Enjoyed this section!...most interesting out of all 3 sections of Bio1B. Understanding and nice professor. If you go through his handouts, keep up with lectures, ask qs on edstem, go to study sleuth, office hours, etc.. the class will not be hard. I ended up with a 100% on his midterm and final. Don't fall behind bc it is content heavy!

Covers WAY too much content in too little time and expects you to know and be able to apply extremely complex concepts to highly difficult application questions after not doing a thorough enough job explaining them. The class average on his midterm was a D, in a 600-person class of mainly premed and bio major Cal students, which says a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Way too much content and he goes over it fast. I skipped most of his lectures on purpose because I was only able to listen, understand, and write down concepts when watching the recordings at a slower speed. He goes over so much and then expects you to remember everything and apply this knowledge to complex application-based exam questions.

So much content. He taught the organismal portion and there were 60 pages of google docs worth of notes, which was twice as much as the 30 pages I wrote each for evolution and ecology. Besides the heavy content, basically anything he said during lecture was fair game. I had to watch over the lectures and couldn't speed it up much.
Too much content in too little time.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Blackman's lectures contain a lot of information but his topic handouts and slides are very helpful in learning the material. He provides key terms and learning outcomes for each lecture which are very useful when studying for the midterm. I focused on the key terms and learning outcomes while studying for his midterm and got a 99%.

Professor Blackman is great. The lectures, however, are horrible. Each lecture is packed with a lot of information and the exam is horrible even if you study so much. The class average was a D- because it was that hard.

He's a nice guy and cares about plant biology, except no one else does. He introduces tons of term each lecture without defining them and expects students to have amazing understanding of each term (even if it's not actually explained). Avgs are in the Ds. This unit brought my grade down from an A to an A-, so beware. My study guide was 30 pgs.

While Professor Blackman had the most material to teach, the supporting topic handouts and lecture notes are easy to read and provide tons of assistance. This ultimately makes it so that while his section is the hardest it is simultaneously the most manageable if you devote enough time to it. His topic handouts in particular are incredibly useful.

Lectures move fast and way too content/memorization heavy, he's not the best at explaining things so I would have to rewatch/relearn myself, exams were hard and unfair for what we're expected to learn so quickly 
I got a 39% on the midterm no curve ;)))

lectures are so packed with information, this section of the class could be its own entire semester course. He introduces 10 new topics per lecture, and then says he's only teaching the basics. Exam questions are essentially based off a tiny detail he mentioned once in lecture, and questions often disregard big picture understandings of concepts

I'm not even kidding when I say his section could be its own class, but he expects us to learn it over a month. The exam is also incredibly hard, and the course average for this exam was a D. He seems like a nice dude, but his exams are horrific, and the material is even worse. Unless he shortens his material or curves his exams, avoid him!!!!

The slides are clear, but there is just so much material covered per lecture, which is really hard to follow. It's all vocabulary, and I had to study way more for this section than the other two units.

Honestly Professor Blackman was very caring towards his students. However; his lectures were quite heavy, which I don't know if that is controllable or not. They were also confusing, I had to rewatch the lectures over and over. The exam was crazy hard too, out of all the sections I studied the most for his, and somehow managed to get the lowest.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Although I know Prof. Blackman means well, there is too much material in the org. bio. section of Bio 1B for his teaching to actually be enjoyable. The lectures almost always ran overtime and were jam-packed with material. I had to self-teach almost everything. Some exam questions were odd, but his exam is manageable if you study a LOT.

Professor Blackman is definitely knowledgeable on his content and you can tell he has passion for it; however, he was not a good lecturer as he relied on reading from the slides, not to mention would not emphasize what would be on the midterm and exam. The phrasing of questions on his exams are very difficult and almost in-understandable. Not good.

A great lecturer with an interesting topic (organismal biology). The downside is mainly with exams and quantity of memorization to accomplish. His midterm def blindsided me (+ the class, going by the average), but at least the final exam can replace it. GL

He is a good lecturer and super knowledgeable, but the material covered in class is a bit overwhelming. There is a lot of new ideas, vocabulary, and life cycles presented in a short amount of time and then expected to be remembered by us. I think this part was a bit unfair, but idk who dictates what he presents, himself or bio1b organizers.

Very involved and caring professor but he is ridiculously bad at question writing. Way too much material is covered and not properly explained during lecture and everyone was appalled by his midterm. He will say something once and then ask a super specific question about it on the test.

He really cares about what he's teaching but he is terrible at teaching. He goes over so much content in one lecture but doesn't explain it in depth/ adequately. His tests are EXTREMELY specific (like, half the content was based on minute details in the required readings) and the avg grade was a D-. Do not recommend unless you wanna be confused lol

i would avoid taking bio 1b with him, he is a really nice person and he is passionate about what he teaches, but he is not good at teaching it. he goes over a lot of information in one lecture and does not explain core concepts like the life cycles very well (my notes for his section was about 20 pages per hour lecture). his test avg was a d-

Professor Blackman is a very mediocre lecturer and although he is passionate about what he taught, he covered far too much information in each lecture. There was a D average on the midterm for his part of the class, reflecting the issue in his teaching. His slides were far longer than the other two sections in the course as well.

Professor Blackman is very passionate about the content he's teaching, and the lectures were fairly engaging. The problem was that the lectures covered FAR too much material than was possible to learn, especially for an intro course. The average was a D on the midterm and final, which says something for a class of mainly premed Cal students.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: AMAZING AND PASSIONATE PROFESSOR
Too much information is presented in each lecture too quickly.
The textbook was a useless waste of $70. That said, the professor is average. His test is hard but at least he curves it.
Amazing professor. Very approachable in office hours and really makes you fall in love with toxicology. Take the class if you can!

This course was interesting, learning about drugs, diet, cancer, toxicology, chemicals, etc. There are 3 main professors, teaching 3 different modules. Each "quiz" for Midterms 1 and 2 and the final were 30-40 ?s. If you studied, looked over the notes, and the GSI's review and practice questions, then this class is easy. The final only had 40 ?s!!

Bjeldanes' lecturing was clear and some of the topics were truly interesting. His "quiz" was the hardest out of all the lecturers. The other lecturers were not as good (some of their powerpoints aren't that clear, so you should go to lecture), but the class as a whole was pretty easy. The final was only like 30 multiple choice questions.

An interesting and funny lecturer, his slides are clear and easy to follow, the midterm is multiple choice, and pulled almost exactly out of his slides. The other NST11 professors are less so, so be careful.

Bjeldanes is dry, boring, and monotonous. He only teaches part of the course (the first and last few weeks), and his teaching style is basically reading off of a powerpoint (which often contained grammatical errors...). If you're taking this to fulfill the BS requirement, it's fine, you don't even need to show up to lecture to pass.

Clear, approachable, and very organized! I highly recommend his toxicology course. Only downside - notes were on powerpoint and had the usual pitfalls - LOTS of info, sometimes verging into boring and overwhelming
Very interesting and fun lecturer. Extremely approachable and the GSIs are extremely helpful. Highly recommend this course.
Really interesting class and his teaching is really effective.
No Comments
Really nice guy! Writes on the board a lot so it is easy to follow.  Tests are very similar to his study questions.

I did not like this professor. She made generalized, broad, and absurd assumptions about the class; for example, at one time, she said, "I knew everyone in this class are liberals." Totally offensive and irrelevant to the course material.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Loved Membership and Migration with her and Song, I would recommend it to any Berkeley student.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Bloemraad is caring and passionate about teaching. Will ask for student perspectives and loves outside information that ties into the course material. Three major essays dictate your grade. Each lecture helps piece ideas together. Reading heavy. I was able to get an A doing less than half the reading, but the readings are incredibly interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Bloemraad takes time to help us understand our readings/concepts. She designed our course very thoughtfully--each reading meaningful to our lessons.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Graded by take home quizzes, several projects, and a comprehensive final based on readings. The projects were straightforward, but a few of them were with groups which was annoying. Quizzes are easy. The final was a LOT of work, but also straightforward. Bloemraad is VERY smart and passionate, and made herself accessible in and out of class.

Bloemraad is a widely-cited expert on topics of immigration & citizenship. Since it was an upper-div class, it was smaller than typical lectures. Doesn't make it heavily-based on the slides. Makes it interactive  by encouraging students of color to share their personal stories. Jolly and sincerely cares about students. Proud to call her a mentor.
Normally teaches upperdiv classes. Fall 2015 was her first semester teaching Soc5. Overall,  she's entertaining and funny. She has a lot of discussions and interactions during lecture.

By far the worst class I have taken here, not because of the course material but for the unrealistic expectations the GSI's as well as the teacher hold for the students. If you aren't working on the projects, sections assignments, or quizzes, you're working on the readings. 3 hours for the final, and over half the class did not finish. AVOID

It's a lot of work and tons of reading, but she is trying her best to get us to understand the readings and make them stick. there are a lot of quizzes and assignments, but it's not oh my god the most difficult thing in the world. She's a good teacher and tries to make such dense boring material interesting. I recommend you take her if anyone.
Just terrible. Final was sooooo long and not anything like the practice exam! Ugh. This class sucks!!!
There are 5 assignments, 5 projects, 7 quizzes, LOTS of reading, and a final... This class is extremely boring and  unnecessarily difficult.

This is the worst class I've ever taken. Ridiculous amounts of assignments, projects, and readings (which are painfully dry & boring). The lectures are long and boring, over half the class stopped attending. The teacher is very clear but she has unreal expectations from students. Only take this class if it is absolutely necessary, otherwise AVOID!

This is the most tedious class I've taken at Berkeley, but if you have to take it, for sure take it with Bloemraad. She speaks very well and is really into the material. She is very nice and understanding, though she makes the tests (especially the final) so incredibly long. At some point you just want to get up and bail.
There is a lot of material to learn and remember, thus making the class a bit difficult.  Aside from that, she is terrific and wants you to do well in the class.

Professor Bloemraad speaks extremely clearly, is very helpful (when you go to office hours), and is knowledgeable about the material.  Soc 5 is pretty dry, however, professor Bloemraad does a good job at making it interesting.  I would definitely take another class with her.

Very clear and helps you understand the most boring stuff. pay attention to her review from the previous class cause thats is the stuff that will be on the final. AND GO TO CLASS... it means a big difference in soc 5.

Man, Soc 5 is the MOST boring class I've ever suffered though, though Bloemraad is pleasant and clear about her lectures. Seriously though, avoid this class unless you've got to take it. Medium use of the reader (share with a friend if you can). There are 5 assignments (easy enough) and a final..

Class is a bit hard but as long as you attend lecture and write down what she puts on the slides you should be fine on the exams.  Readings can be a bit boring and long but overall a really good class. Shes very organized and clear with what she wants.

F06 Professor Bloemraad does a great job of making a dry subject (research methods) as interesting as possible. I loved her selections of readings in the course reader, not only were they interesting, but got the point across as well. I found the assignments helpful to understand and apply what we were learning, and the midterm and final were fair.

Although the lectures and materials are extremely boring, Prof. Bloemraad does her best to make lecture fun. Her lectures are crystal clear. The exams are actually not that hard but there is a lot of memorization. 1 midterm, 1 final, and 4 papers (two with a partner).

Very uptight professor! Material is bland and boring, lectures aren't much better.  Tests are long short/essay answer. 4 papers, which aren't bad.  Reading material will put you to sleep!  Office hours; she continues to lecture, and does not want to be your friend.  Overall, a class that is doable, but no enjoyable.

4 assignments, no more than 4-5 pages in length, and a midterm and final.  Picky/harsh grading on the assignments, but tests were more fair.  Reading is not difficult, nor is the material.  Class can be a little dry, but Bloemraad keeps students engaged by frequently asking for input and discussion during lectures.
OK professor, but the material in this course is unbearably boring and dry. Mini assignments and group work were annoying and not engaging. It killed my desire to be a soc major!
Best Professor I've ever had! A few easy assignments. Most readings very interesting. Involves students in discussion. Very helpful outside of class.

She made Soc. 5 a lot easier and much more interesting than it is. The work is not that difficult but there are a lot of mini-assignments that take time to do. However, they really help in understanding the material. Take soc. 5 with her as she is the best soc.5 instructor.

Horribly long, boring, and usually non-informative lectures. No course book, only a reader of publications. You have to decipher the reader and lectures. for info as the Prof gave none and would ramble about research/publications. Essays harshly graded.
If you are interested in sociology, especially the part about capitalism the you will like Boroka's classes, but is very hard to get a good essay grade

So glad I took this class! I changed my mind last minute about the 190 I wanted to take, been counting my lucky stars all semester. While my friends have been miserable in their 190s, I learned a LOT, and she took the time all semester to also make me a much better writer than before. Best class ever, best Prof ever!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Such a great prof! Classes are always fun, I learn a lot every day, and she makes sure every voice is respected and has room in the classroom. I have no idea how she is so knowledgeable in so many things, but Berkeley Soc is so much richer because of her. Also, she gives GREAT life advice too, just ask and you shall receive! Prof. Bo is golden.

She is a tough grader (this is an upper division course, so don't expect an easy A!), but you will definitely get great feedback! I am very glad I took the course, learned (and learning) a ton from Boroka. She is super easy to talk to, approachable, flexible when it comes to office hours, and insightful when it comes to the material. Best class!

Best GSI I've ever had at Berkeley! Respects your time, super helpful, clear, caring and brilliant. Worked my a** off for her class, but totally worth it as she gave me a great recommendation for work. Owe her so much, highly recommend that you take anything she teaches (as long as you are into the subject of course).

Prof. Bo is a huge asset to Berkeley's Sociology department! She is patient, explains concepts well, listens and encourages great conversations in the classroom. I tend to be more quiet, but in her class, I always feel like I will be heard and that my voice will be appreciated. She will not spoon-feed you with info, so you will have to work hard!

Boroka was my professor in a huge lecture course. Her sections made the programming we had to learn feel manageable, as she would always make sure that everyone understood the code and was able to function on their own before the tests. If not for our hands-on R sections with her, I would have for sure had to drop this class.

Prof Bo is AMAZING! Super approachable, clear, funny, caring, and would always ensure we actually learn in class, knowledge that is useful outside in the job market. She is a hard grader, but follows very clear criteria available to the class. As long as you can follow directions, you will rock both qual and quant methods. She wants us to succeed!
He was great
In just this one class he changed my career trajectory from software to hardware!

This man is the worst profesor ever.

He uses to teach the class in chinese to make ir more challeenging. He is great. He is not great.

He is not the best.
He is the best...oh yes. He is nice He is not nice.

We like jim as He is. But he is too ood
W lecture videos.
Does not teach well. Does not have a welcoming attitude. Was not approachable. Made me question my interest  in hardware.
I learned a ton.  He really loves the subject, and is super-accessible. Just be prepared that he often drifts off the topic and tends to mumble sometimes.

Lectures were near unwatchable. He seems like a nice guy but when you're trying to learn something completely foreign to you its extraordinarily hard to comprehend sentences where every other word is "uhh". Sometimes 5 or 6 times in a row, I'm not joking. Painfully slow and explanations all over the place. Only way from here is up.

Be prepared to do the assignments as if you have not yet gone to lecture. It's likely that he will cover the materials that are necessary for the assignment on the due day, if not one day earlier.  After all, he is nice and always smiling. That makes the class feel better.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Took Analog Circuits class with Bora - hard class, great use of tablet!
Very helpful, goes smoothly form theory to design.  Not an easy teacher, though.
Good prof
Office hours are extremely helpful. Just sit in and talk about whatever you like, it had made me enjoyed chem even more.
Professor Boering is extremely kind and energetic.

Her lectures were engaging, though very dense in information. Exams have thorough cover equation sheets, and I'd say were graded fairly. Love her energy during demos and office hours. Be sure to read the textbook and attend office hours to succeed.

Very bad professor, her lectures are impossible to understand due to random schizophrenic outbursts. Mind numbing and easy class though, again just be careful about labs. Don't attend if you already have strong fundamentals in chem, her lectures add almost nothing to the class, just use the textbook whenever you feel like you ned more.

I really enjoyed her lectures. They were engaging, and her demos were very cool! Her exams are very fair, and I think she does a great job at preparing her students for them. It is also very fun to go to her office hours; she is very eager to help with anything. She encourages curiosity, but is also very clear about what is actually tested!

Boering was absolutely wonderful to have for the second part of Chem 4A with her lectures making it clear how much she cares for the subject. Make sure to attend lecture for the fun demos and office hours for candy and thoughtful responses to any questions you have. Lectures can get a bit disorganized so best just to sit in and listen.

Her exams are especially confusing since there's no clear idea of what types of questions will be asked. Her slides are just examples pulled straight from the textbook, so the lectures feel repetitive, and with zero practice finals or real exam prep, everything is completely on you.

Very energetic professor and nice demos. It was clear that she cares about the subject! Always willing to talk outside of class. Super informative slides and she was always on top of correcting wrong things. Felt that she had fair exams although the portion of the units taught on the final was significantly harder than MT3.

Professor Boering is one of the best professors I've had so far. She cares so much about the subject and that really shines through in her lectures, and the class is organized very clearly where you know what is expected. She is an amazing professor and makes herself so available to give help in office hours
Take CHEM 182!! It is the most interesting class and professor Boering is awesome! She tells the best stories and is so kind!
Best chemistry professor I've ever had!! This is my favorite class I've taken at Berkeley largely due to professor Boering! Take this class!! So interesting and she is amazing!

she is great at explaining concepts at different levels for all students and she always has an excited attitude, clear guidelines for post labs, did a great job preparing us for each lab and each assignment, sometimes goes on tangents during lecture but still gives all necessary info (also makes a point to provide textbook resources for free),

Prof Boering was one of the most fantastic professors I've ever had at Cal - she has an immense joy for the subject and breaks down topics incredibly well. Her lectures are engaging, fun, and educational. 10/10 would recommend taking her class if you at all can!!

Professor Boering Is by far one of the best professors I have learned from at Berkeley. I was intimidated by oral exams at first, but after taking this class not only have my communication skills bettered, but I wish every class had oral exams. I learned so much about atmospheric chemistry through this course and through Professor Boering.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Chem 1A was the first class I took at Berkeley and I didn't appreciate at the time how good of a professor I ended up with. Hard class because of a) the material itself and b) it being my first time in a Berkeley class, but Prof. Boering did a beautiful job of breaking things down and including relevant examples. Great lectures, helpful OH, 10/10.

Professor Boering is one of the only professors at Berkeley who reminds me that there are good professors and good classes that still exist here. The lectures were not only super clear and informative, but they were also engaging and exciting! You can tell she cares a ton about the students and answering their questions and making sure they succeed

taught w/ eric. didn't ever lecture but was available quite often for office hours. difficult class without any background knowledge. you're going to need a lot of help from gsi's and the textbook in order to pass the midterms.

She insists multiple times throughout the semester that the lectures and homework will provide you with all you need, the textbook is just for "additional help". The information (AKA demos) in lecture was never enough to fully grasp any of the concepts, especially with rapid pacing, and I only survived this class thanks to excellent GSIs.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Boering is a good professor for Chemistry 1A. It's clear that she loves chemistry when she teaches. She is encouraging and makes you feel good about exams, even when you feel like you messed up. She is accessible for questions and wants to help.
Terrible professor! Did not teach anything! Get ready to self-study!

This was by far the worst class I have taken at UC Berkeley. The lectures were information heavy and they forced a lot of material down your throat. Tests were brutally difficult and unfair. They told the class they would curve it at the end, but never did. I somehow managed a B+ because I studied for about 25 hours for the final. Difficult.

Prof tends to go off topic and goes pretty fast during lecture. Number one tip: USE THE TEXTBOOK!! Reading before and after lecture really helped my understanding. Definitely a difficult class and the exams were hard. Curves are fairly decent but despite what they say, this is 100% a weeder class.

She was a nice lady, but her tests were not representative of what was taught in all cases. I felt the tests were designed to trip you up and cause trouble. I never got over a B, but still ended up with a B+ in the class, so the curve was decent. Just make sure to keep up and strive for a deeper understanding.

Clearly very passionate about chemistry but not very good at teaching. I found myself getting confused despite having learned what was being taught. Also went from an A to a B because she didn't provide any practice material for the final and ended up flunking it. Don't take this class if you haven't taken HS chem!!!
Also, 3 midterms+final...
if you take her class, just read the book. she's very enthusiastic about chemistry, but doesn't cover that much content. read the book, and you should be fine :). Good Luck!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Boering's lectures did not help me at all, I found myself struggling to understand the content because a lot of it was not taught. Luckily, my GSI taught a majority of it to us, but others weren't so lucky. You have to learn a lot by yourself, it won't be taught. Exams are hard, homework is mediocre, good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Boering is a lively professor and will certainly not bore you. However, she makes bad jokes and the lectures are filled with demos that do very little to help you. This leaves barely any time for her to actually teach anything.
Barely understand her lecture as a student who did not take chem in high school. Lack of logic and important information. You need to go to a lot of office hours to catch up with the class tbh.

I didn't take chem in hs so this class was difficult for me. If you're in my boat, you won't do well just from taking notes on lectures. You really need to redo homework problems, find worksheets from outside sources, etc. Kristie herself was okay, better than Eric, but like Eric she can push through material way too quickly for someone like me
does not efficiently prepare students for exams. lots of self studying

I loved prof Boerings lectures. However, the class is very tough! The homework and discussions are helpful but you still need to have amazing understanding of content to do well on the tests. Good luck!

If you were to solely rely on the course's resources, I can assure you will have an incredibly difficult time doing well on the exams. Unfortunately, you will need to do a lot of independent work and searching of good resources to feel adequately prepared for the exams. Do the SLC, RTP, and practice exams all on your own before ever lookin at keys.

As someone who had to take CHEM1A I thought the class was fair. The lectures are demo-heavy so I recommend having a feel for the material beforehand to better understand. There's weekly HW w/ unlimited attempts and 3 midterms + 1 final. The exams were more or less fair, but you definitely do have to self study, and not rely on only practice tests.

I hated chemistry in high school but I liked this class more than I expected. Boering's lectures are demo-heavy and often rushed but she genuinely wants people to do well and her office hours are extremely helpful. CHEM 1A is a challenging class but has a lot of resources to help you succeed (office hours, tutoring, reviews) if you put in the work.

Boering did so many unnecessary demos during class which were not helpful at all. She also was very rushed during lectures, and was disorganized. Practice exams were much easier than actual exams, and I learned more from an hour discussion with my GSI than I did from attending 3 lectures a week with Boering. Chem 1A is no joke, so be warned.

I hated chem in high school and hadn't studied it in a couple years, but I actually liked this class. There are a few issues however; the lectures are too demo-heavy and we don't solve enough problems, the OWL homework is also weirdly difficult and doesn't reflect exam material. I recommend reading the textbook and solving questions from there.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: As a person shes great. Very genuine and kind. However, lectures, homework, practice problems and practice midterms are not at all helpful for the exams. Her lectures are mostly demos. A lot of what we learn in class is not on any exams. Make sure you are ready for a lot of self teaching or to be taught by YouTube videos ��

As a person shes great. Very genuine and kind. However, lectures, homework, practice problems and practice midterms are not at all helpful for the exams. Her lectures are mostly demos. A lot of what we learn in class is not on any exams. Make sure you are ready for a lot of self teaching

Shes a very nice person and seems genuine but her lectures and hw/practice midterms are not helpful and very different from the actual exams. Be ready to put in a lot of work and self study because you will be teaching yourself a lot of the material.

Get ready for a lot of self-study. The lectures do not prepare you for the midterms or finals. She is the nicest person but when it comes to class, she honestly could have included more practice problems during lectures rather than demos.

This class was unbelievably difficult. Though professor Boeing was a really kind and genuine person, her lectures did not prepare you for exams at all. During class, we mainly watched her do live demos and then on the homework and midterms there would be complicated math and content questions that we had not been taught and had no idea how to do.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Some of the reviews on this page are just blatantly false slander. The average on the first midterm is not an F to a D - on the first it was a C; on the second, a D; and the third, a C+ (with median of B). Compared to other freshman professors like Prof. Christ, Boering's midterms are fair, although the complete lack of partial credit is alarming.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The midterms in this class are an absolute nightmare and the entire class is frustrated/complaining. Nothing this professor teaches in any way prepares you for the midterm. They seem to do "trick" questions which are just ridiculous. The test prep they provide doesn't prepare you for the midterms. Avg midterm grades are D-F. How can this be ok?

Prof. Boering has to be one of the worst professors at UC Berkeley. Lectures, homeworks, discussion worksheets do not prepare for the exams. She has poor teaching style and is not able to convey the class material to her students.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Boering is one of the worst professors for incoming freshmen. Her lectures, homework, discussion worksheets, and even the practice midterms don't correlate to the actual midterms. Lectures have less teaching and more demos for concepts that most students still haven't grasped. Prepare to self-study through the entire course.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: the class material isnt difficult but she doesnt explain any of the concepts and only makes it more confusing. the lectures, assignments, discussion worksheets, and practice midterms will not prepare you for the midterm. there are way too many demos that take up too much lecture time and dont help in understanding any concepts whatsoever.

I believe her current chem1a midterm average grade in her class is a D. The lectures, book, study groups, prep test in NO WAY prepare you for what will be on the midterms. She even puts things on midterms that are taught AFTER the exam. Students are really frustrated and voicing concerns - but it feels like nobody is listening.

tests are way harder than the homework/lecture material. I don't know how they expect anyone to do well in this class unless they've taken a college level chemistry class before. its clear this class is an afterthought for Boering. She;s a nice person, but she doesn't explain concepts well or give sufficient materials to prepare for exams.

I liked her as a person but I did not care for the way her class was structured. It seemed like you have a grasp on the material until you realize you were really insufficiently prepared for midterms. I cannot BELIEVE this class was only 3 credits. Prepare for this to be one of your hardest classes taking up most if not all ur time.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Overall this class is ok. However, the midterm exams are not based on the book, demos, lectures or the practice exam. Most students feel they are failing due to this issue (and honestly some are even thinking of changing their majors). There is no way for us to know what topics will be covered on the exam and how best to study for them.

She wasn't the clearest lecturer, I heard much better things about Professor Toste and Marsden if you get the chance to take Chem 1A with either of them. Study the iClicker questions and the homework questions for exams (which are all multiple choice). This class definitely requires work, but isn't nearly as bad as 3A

The tests are all multiple choice and they tend to be increasingly tricky. Even though I wasn't in her class, I would go to her lectures because she explained concepts in a way that was easy to understand. Some professors will explain concepts with the assumption that students already know a lot of chem, but she was a good introductory lecturer.

The atmosphere freshman seminar Kristie teaches is awesome. She is very accessible and enthusiastic about the material. I highly recommend taking this seminar if you can, it's an easy and interesting unit.

Super enthusiatic and makes the class fun. I was not very interested in Atmosphere chemistry but she made it interesting. What chem class do you ever go on a field trip? We went on 2. No lab reports just oral exams that become pretty easy after the first. Take it if you can.

A very interesting professor. likes chemistry A LOT. likes the "geek world." dresses up for halloween. I used to think that professor stacy was ok but boering is much better. i learn more from her than i learn from stacy and she definitely tries.

Very friendly, approachable, nice, and wants to help her students succeed in the class. Very enthusiastic about the subject that I grew into studying atmospheric chemistry... labs were utterly confusing if you have not had P-chem, but I got a lot of help her and the TAs, and oral exams became kind of fun :-)

He's a great person and really cares about students success and helps out as much as he can with code and troubleshooting but the class is run in such a weird way with beginners basically using AI for everything and the course content not really being new information for ESPM students. You will get an A if you just stick to what he writes.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The concept of this class is really amazing, however it really wasn't geared towards ESPM students, it catered more to the advanced coders. There is very little lecture time on learning Python with very advanced coding projects. You can use AI if you're a beginner, however subsequently I felt the grading was very harsh for beginner coders.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things
