reviews.comment: Very clear and accessible professor. His lecture format is very good for learning the subject because it emphasises the students working on the problems and him going around helping out when needed.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She is a good lecturer but spends a lot of time on proofs and specific problems rather than general solving approaches. The exams are not too difficult but are not at all based off of the homework. Tutors for the class are unable to solve some of the homework problems and GSIs unhelpful. Attendance not mandatory but lectures not posted.

Great lectures. Everything in her class is conceptual/symbolic, so no units or sig figs which is great. Both midterms were pretty doable, final was difficult, ended up just losing my A because of it. Doing textbook problems before exams is how i would study, just do it, GPT what you don't know, and you'll learn it with repetition.

Refusal to release lecture recordings/notes due to the actions of past classes is a huge folly. Bordel is one of the best instructors in the physics department, but for such a heavy subject, she goes way too fast during lecture. Students need better access to the material taught after hours to do well.

Lectures were interesting and covered testable content pretty well. Tests are on the difficult side but still doable. There are grade bins that follow the physics dept standard but no clobber/exam recovery of any kind.

This was the worst professor and class I have ever taken in my life. The course is extremely dissorganised, grade recovery is non-existent. GSIs were not too helpful. Lectures go into too much depth and calculus, completely unrelated to the skills exams require. Homework did not help either.

Absolutely amazing professor. If she taught every single one of my physics classes I would change majors. Very accessible and wants you to walk away from her class not just learning physics but as a better student overall.
GSI very very clutch, otherwise textbook does good job covering material

Very sweet and caring professor with engaging lectures. I looked forward to them even though they were at 8 am. She gave a good conceptual overview and made the content very interesting. Exams were similar to practice ones, and there's lots of practice material. She obviously cares about teaching and student success and gives us lots of advice.

Dr. Bordel's lectures were clear + approachable. Very encouraging of/responsive to questions in class/OH. Exams were fair, similar to previous ones. Also the 7C content is the most interesting of the 7-series IMO (go to lecture). Her digital notes (a lot of cursive writing) were not as clear as the actual lectures, where she used more visuals/demos
Very kind and caring professor. Has informative lectures and answers student questions well. Tests are difficult but there's a generous curve.

prof bordel claims to care about students and genuinely seems like a nice person, yet her lectures are dry, exams have super low averages, and policies are unfair. 

All class material is low effort, and her teaching made me dread physics. The GSIs are super unaccommodating and refuse partial credit like it's coming from their own bank account.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Bordel is a subpar professor for multiple reasons. Her lectures are abysmal. She starts 5 minutes before Berkeley time, which leaves you scribbling furiously to catch up for the rest of lecture because she goes so fast. Her exams are extremely difficult but the curve is not at all generous. I used to be excited about physics, now I dread it.

she seems like a nice lady and that she genuinely cares about her students but this does not reflect in her exams and policies at all. super unforgiving with grading, rarely gives any partial credit, and has 0 clobber policies or accommodations. class policies are needlessly cruel sometimes and grading is very harsh. exam averages are about 45-50%.

Although she seems to be well meaning, the exams are outrageously difficult. Many times I considered not studying for the exam because I knew that what would come would be something unfamiliar (although exam 1 was quite similar to the practice exams). When she posts the exam rubrics they are often difficult to read and partial credit is limited.

Horrible lectures. Incomprehensible. Starts writing on the board before Berkeley time and the whole lecture is a race to keep up with her lightspeed handwriting, not to mention the fact that all she does during lecture is proofs. Her exam averages are awful and are written so poorly that she apologized to the class after scores come out.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you are new to physics, this class is hard. Exams are harder than lectures and exam averages were in the F range (44-47%) which makes a really good curve but I don't really feel like I learned much. Try to stay within/ around average and you should be fine for some form of a B. It's hard but Bordel really cares and is very generous with grading!

bordel is a kind, sweet professor and she is well meaning, but her lectures are boring (but not completely useless, some examples she does are on tests). she writes big on blackboard but still hard to read sometimes so sit near the front.
Just get a high score on the midterms and you will be chilling the entire course because everyone fails the midterms. Easy money. Homework was annoying though.
Great lecturer, goes at a very good pace, very clear and concise. Very nice
I had no previous experience with e&m but Bordel taught it so well that I grew to enjoy the class. She is extremely patient and this is the only class I where I've gone to all of my lectures.

Physics personally absolutely demolished my soul but professor Bordel was a great lecturer and explained concepts well. Tests were super hard and class average in the 50-60 range so curves were huge. My year a 54% overall was a B and 78% was an A. Definitely need to put in lots of hours of work outside of class but I learned a lot!

Professor Bordel was extremely kind and patient with students, always answering all questions during lecture. Lectures emphasize learning and understanding the concepts, homework and discussions are where you have to figure out how to apply them. Exams are tough but if you do all the homework and practice problems you'll be alright.

Really enjoyed this class even though I probably will never use most of what I learned. Bordel explains concepts clearly and most of exams can be studied for from lecture notes-- has clear criteria for what you should know. Go to OHs and reviews. Exams aren't too difficult but definitely need to study. Amazing equation sheet provided! Easy hw

She cares about her students a lot and is very approachable. Her lectures can be quite dry and much more simplistic than the exams. However, if you do the homework problems and all the practice material you'll be good. Exams are super tough averages in the 50% and GSI's are frankly not good at explaining. You really have to trial and error it.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Bordel is good at lecturing! She makes sure that you understand the concept and her going over the examples is understandable. However, the exams are hard, so make sure to study and practice.

Best professor that you can get for undergraduate physics! Her lectures are very clear, straightforward, and reflective of what she will test you on. Very fair exams with dense equation sheets provided. Had her for 7A last summer and loved her teaching style so much that I returned for 7C! Very generous curves too. Highly recommend her courses!

I got a 77.5% on both midterms and a 78% on the final (no physics background): Bordel's questions are pretty fair if u try to conceptually grasp each lecture example. DO THE PRACTICE EXAMS. she is such a sweet human tho and wants the best for everyone. and KNOW THE EQN sheet i got MANY pts for not knowing anything but writing relevant eqns
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Her lectures are enjoyable, she thinks highly of her students (regardless of average class grade), grades leniently, and overall made the class an attainable A if you do thoughtful work.

Going into this course, I had previous physics knowledge which definitely helped a lot. Very fast-paced but understandable. Tests were very hard but taking her previous practice tests definitely helped in the preparation.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Reading only first 5 reviews FOOLED ME. As someone with 0 physics knowledge, this course was HELL. Examples in class? Understandable. Homework? Manageable. Exams? HORRIBLE. Yes, there is a HUGE curve but given the fact that the class average is a whopping 50% on a good day, if she didn't make the cutoff at 22%, probably 80% of the class would fail.

I personally hate physics but Bordel actually made me enjoy physics a teeny bit. 8B is hard but Bordel really breaks down concepts and makes the lectures understandable, even the really difficult concepts like quantum mechanics. The exams were fair in my opinion (curve kind of sucks though). She is the best professor to take the 8 series with.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Honestly easy class considering I never went to her 8am lecture. You cant really fail any physics class at Berkeley. A C- was 22% cutoff. IF i had genuinely tried in her class i would likely had received at least an A.

Bordel gives great lectures and is organized and clear, good at answering questions, and compassionate for students. My gripes with this class are with the overall course organization, communications, and the continually useless lab sections. When everything becomes a thought experiment, how are we seeing the phenomena we need to understand?

I don't like Physics, but Professor Bordel made it bearable. She is a very good lecturer and could make difficult concepts easy to understand. She is kind and you can tell she genuinely cares about her students. The tests were difficult, but they're the same regardless of which professor you have, and practice is provided. Overall great professor.

Had her for 7A & 7B. Kind prof, but fairly dry. Overall the 7 series is unengaging, most ppl who take it are forced by COE requirement. Exams are tough but fair grading. Not a bad choice to take 7 series with, just not super fun / lectures are quite drab. TBH, take 7 series at CC if you can. Will be way better time-wise & GPA wise.

7B is a challenging class but Bordel makes the material accessible. She is an extremely kind person who cares a lot about her students. She gives solid lectures, mostly conceptual/derivations but does examples whenever possible. Exams are difficult but fair, if you take advantage of discussion, practice exams, and office hours.

Caring professor. Lectures are pretty dry/boring, but that's generally true for most intro physics classes. Notes are clear & accessible, tests are fair. Overall, a good professor but not super entertaining/engaging. Fairly good experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor's Bordel's lectures provide explanations for when to use many of the equations that will be tested on, so I strongly recommend attending lectures/watching recordings and taking notes on what she writes. Her exams are quite tough, but doing practice problems from past exams definitely helps.

8A this semester  disaster. The Piazza was full of students, no instructors or GSIs to answer questions we would have. Would take off points for submitting exams a minute or two late because of uploads. Everything else in the course was fair, but the exams were brutal. Also, saw on social media how horrible she was to DSP students. Done, but yikes

Bordel is one of the worst teachers I had at Cal. Do not let the positive reviews fool you. She is very unaccommodating when it comes to DSP students, and just loves seemingly takes joy at waging mass accusals of Academic Misconduct. The exams were tough, but labs, homeworks, and discussions were good. Mentally prepare & study hard. It was rough.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Very, very caring professor. I did not take physics during high school, but she made it bearable, but still challenging. Very sympathetic to the struggles of the student, and I don't blame her for needing to speed through a few lectures because they can be very dense sometimes. All exams are fair, practice exams are very, very important resources.

During online learning, Professor Bordel was understanding and helpful. There's a textbook, but you'll only be tested on what is taught in lecture. Grades are mostly based on the 2 midterms and final exam, but there is a weekly homework assignment and a few labs. Bordel is very caring. The class is hard but you'll do well if you study old midterms.

She is one of the sweetest professors I have ever had at Berkeley. She is especially considerate during these difficult times of online learning. She answers all questions without ever being condescending or rude. Tests are definitely difficult, but her grading is fair. Go to lecture and discussion and do the homework and you should be okay!

Super clear and satisfying lecturer, clear expectations on tests. Discussions weren't the most helpful for material we were tested on. Somewhat confusing because her lectures are so well done it feels like you learn the material, then when you try to apply it you realize you actually didn't.

She's a solid choice for Phy 8A. Her lecture tends to be dry and maybe a little boring but very clear, organised, and straightforward. She's really good at explaining things. If you attend classes, take good notes, and work hard on her example questions and other practice problems assigned during sections, you will do great in this class.

One word to describe Professor Bordel: caring. She has been such an empathetic professor during these difficult times and is always looking out for the wellbeing of her students. While the material is quite difficult, you will always be comforted by Professor Bordel's lectures. GO TO OFFICE HOURS!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: she is the first professor I met who acts like a teacher, like her primary goal is to teach us. she's so caring and constantly lets her students ask any questions they have. the tests are hard but not unreasonable and she gives a lot of partial credit. this class was very hard for me but I shoulda studied harder bc she was stupid lenient w grades

Professor Bordel is one of the best at Berkeley. She clearly cares about her students a lot, she's super nice and easy to talk to. Lectures can get pretty fast-paced, but they're very good and she gives clear explanations. Her exams are fair with respect to class content, even if some problems can get quite difficult. She's who you want for 7B!

Professor Bordel is one of my favorite professors at UC Berkeley. There are assigned readings (free!!) but she really explains the concepts well enough that you don't have to read and she is a really good lecturer! I normally hate physics, but she was really an amazing professor and I learned so much from her class. Definitely recommend for Physics
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Bordel is an extremely caring and wonderful professor, who is incredibly helpful in her office hours. Although her exams are somewhat difficult, if you attend office hours and watch all the lectures, you should be able to attain a strong understanding of the material. I cannot stress how amazing her office hours are!!!

Prof. Bordel is organized and decently easy to understand. However, she often launches into new formulas without giving enough intuition on what the variables actually mean. Her lectures focus more on using clever calculus rather than understanding physics. This being said, her syllabus is probably tightly constrained by the physics department.

One of the greatest professors I had at Berkeley! She really emphasizes conceptual learning and provides clear derivation of equations used. The exams are fair, and are true test of your understanding. If you do everything expected of you (go to lecture, do homework, attend labs), you will do just fine in the class. She is who you want for 8A!

Bordel, while sometimes dreadful to be in class, is a VERY good professor. Her tests were the fairest I've seen at Berkeley, and are strictly variables. She is so accessible outside of class and wants to be there for you. I had to get my surgery my semester I took with her and she was the most accommodating out of any other professor I had.

Prof. Bordel cares so much about her students, is very organized, and runs the class in a very structured and helpful way. Her lectures were always engaging and well thought-out, and she made physics concepts easy to understand. Tests are hard, but doable if you engage with the class. Even though I had her 8 AM, I was motivated to go to lecture!

Bordel's teaching style shows that she cares about her students. Her lectures are very useful & she always makes sure everyone is ok before moving on. She is very approachable and creates a comfortable environment to ask questions. I appreciate how she focuses on making sure students truly understand the material which is evident in her tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: She is nice. She derives formulas and solves past exam questions which I do not prefer to have in the lectures. On the exam you literally sho the work or you do not pass. You have to understand the concepts

Attendance taken by iClicker at random lectures over semester. If you've taken AP Physics, it's a breeze. Bordel is definitely the better of the 8A professors. If you are confused at all during lecture, she will really try to help you understand the concepts! Go to review sessions before midterms.

Very caring and understanding. She was stuck teaching a very tedious course, but still treated us all with lots of respect. I would definitely love to take a full, 4-unit physics course with her. She was also very helpful.

Nice prof but dry lectures. Encourages participation. If you understand the concepts you'll understand her tests. The 1st midterm was easy because I understood it, got killed by the 2nd one because I slacked off, and the final was extremely hard but got an A over the class's average of a D cause I understood the concepts. SO UNDERSTAND CONCEPTS!!!

Oh my god was this the hardest class I've ever taken in my entire life. I'm a bio major, not a physics major, meaning I dont have multivariable calculus just sitting in my back pocket all the time. She zooms through topics in her lecture that you may need a few hours to process on your own. Theres too much content and not enough brain for one sem.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: The lectures weren't that necessary if you are able to get the notes. The textbook was key for understanding how to approach problems. Her explanations are not the clearest, but she does seem like a nice person who is willing to help. DO HER OLD EXAMS AND AS MANY PRACTICE PROBLEMS AS POSSIBLE. If you are able to get those concepts you'll be fine.
her tests are good for practicing. Just for practicing, though

Very nice, but avoid if you can. Dry lectures. Tests are just difficult and at least this semester, the grades were basically at the mercy of some very nitpicky and harsh GSIs. But she runs a very well-organized class otherwise - she's very clear about what material to read, quizzes/hw is reasonable, and the textbook complements class perfectly.

Really a sweet and realistic person but does not really test Bio majors the way she needs to. In office hours she would sometimes not give the assistance I needed even after it was clear that I had no idea how to proceed with a problem... aka the reason why people go to office hours in the first place. Tests were graded EXCEPTIONALLY hard.

Super nice and very helpful, she was always willing to stay after lecture to help me, even about the stupid questions from like 4 weeks ago that I probably should've figured out already. It seems that her tests vary in difficulty from semester to semester.

Bordel seems like a lovely person, but her lectures can be a little confusing. The nature of 8B means that you're doing very math-based material, while attempting to approach them from a conceptual, rather than mathematical, perspective. I think Bordel struggles with this, and often just skipped steps rather than explaining them.
Really cares about her students, always willing to answer questions, great professor.  The class itself is hard material, so if you takes 7B with her be ready.

Bordel was a clear, straightforward lecturer, although lecture could get very boring at times. The material in 7B was tough, and Bordel's tests are relatively reasonable. However, they can be time-consuming and you may need to be inventive on some problems. She's relatively gracious when it comes to grading.

Nice lady who definitely knows her stuff, but lectures can be a bit dull and largely reiterate what's already in the book. Exam grading is a bit strict at times, though the problems are fairly straightforward.

Solid. She's a very clear lecturer, is more than happy to answer questions, and is kind to students. Her primary shortcoming was that the lectures did not nearly cover the material in as much depth/difficulty as the hw and tests. Realistically, you could skip the lectures altogether and just read the textbook.

Terribly confusing professor. She loves to talk a lot about a topic for a long time (just standing there), and her wording makes it hard to follow. She does eventually write things down, but not everything you need. She doesn't let students bring their own notes for exams. She gives a set sheet of formulas that excludes a lot of helpful equations.

She's not the best teacher: doesn't spend a lot of time doing problems, which i feel would be more helpful. Exams are a little out of left field since this was her first year teaching, so doing practice tests by other profs isn't helpful. she is a very nice lady though and is helpful when you ask her specific questions.

she tries really hard. she's a great person but one of those science teachers who has a terrible time COMMUNICATING physics to the class. lectures are confusing, tests are a total toss up. electromagnetism is confusing as it is, take it with a prof who is more straightforward (ie: NOT this one)

She's a really nice person, and extremely helpful when you have questions! I once asked her about sample test problems and she went out of her way to look for ones from previous tests. I've heard compared to other physics professors she's not as difficult, so I would recommend taking Physics 8B with her!

Very passive aggressive, and the grading criteria for lab reports is VERY unclear. She always uses some type of confusing logic to say that the rubric is applied consistently across students, but we can't even see the rubric prior to answering questions.

Very nice professor, easily accessible and responds quickly to emails. CHEM 32 is P/NP, so very chill. A little bit new, but good lectures. Tbh I don't think I needed to take CHEM 32, because CHEM 1A was more intro than expected bc has review at beginning and the lecturer was really good, but CHEM 32 might be helpful if you want to ease into chem?
chill p/np class, and she will prepare you for chem

Class was PNP. Decent professor, Good at answering questions. Quizzes very similar to HW. Biggest complaint would be rushing through lectures/asking questions to students on iclicker before even teaching concepts. Slides seemed somewhat disorganized. But if you're willing to put effort to teach yourself stuff outside of class, pretty easy course.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: inexperienced lecturer, but she genuinely wants to help students learn. her slides are helpful. a good amount of tedious work. although its pass no pass she still gave a final, which i did not love. mandatory attendance and biweekly quizzes which were worth a good amount. if ur deciding between this and chem1a, don't waste your time, take chem1a.

She's a decent lecturer who genuinely cares about ensuring understanding. She can seem nervous at times but is clearly passionate about teaching and will happily answer any questions you might have. Homeworks and quizzes are nothing to worry about if you follow along in class. The textbook is free and only used for short "pre-lecture" assignments.

105 and self-study of converters (or just reading a spec sheet) is much much more useful than this class. The lab TA was generally unhelpful and course staff never responded on Ed (IIRC this was policy, LOL...). Probably one of the more straightforward EE courses though, and the follow-up 113B seems like a genuinely good class. Textbook was good.

Amazing professor. She is really helpful and caring about her students. The only thing is that the dates of quizes are weird. One is on Halloween night, and the other is on the evening before Thanksgiving break. However, this is a very good course in EECS. And I will also take EE113B from Jessica next semester.

She cares a lot about the students and was always reachable by email. Lectures are very clear, HW prepared you for exams. Prof. Boles listened to student feedback throughout the semester and truly did the most to ensure everyone was able to learn. It is clear she really wants her students to succeed. Easily one of the best professors at Berkeley.
This prof was super fun, dont listen to the last guy

On paper, Boos was an amazing professor. He is organized, good at explaining things, and generous with his time. The class was well-structured and conducted, and I enjoyed the demonstrations he gave. However, I was very bored. I am a humanities major, which may have been why, but I found his pace and tone dull. Still, the class is a good breadth!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Awesome professor!! Lectures are clear and engaging with lots of fun demonstrations. He gives ample guidance on HW/exams and he answers messages quickly. Class is crazy well organized and Prof Boos always has his student's learning and wellbeing in mind. Physical science and climate fundamentals in the context of interesting weather phenomenon.

Took this class pass/no pass, which I believe is the route to go if you're a non-science major and just taking this for the physical science breadth. I only really tried on a couple of the homeworks and two of the tests, and still passed. Really cool and funny twinkish man. Cares a lot about how much his students actually understand the material.
The GOAT, just take his class!!

Professor Boos was great. He clearly cares about his students, and has a really kind grading policy. He dropped the 4 lowest homework scores, and curved the class at the end by a couple percent. The lectures are easy to understand as someone with no background in EPS and he does a physical demonstration every class!

10/10 professor. Always went in depth into concepts, explained in terms anybody could understand, & made sure ppl understood before moving on. Content is fascinating, & he had a demonstration every class to keep everyone engaged. Assignments/exams are take home, he gave good feedback & extra credit opportunities. Goat professor and brilliant guy.

Professor Boos was the most organized and effective professor I've had. He has high expectations and makes sure students have the resources to really learn the material. There were a lot of in class demos that help visualize the concepts and he would link concepts to current events. Very approachable professor and fun and fascinating class.
Amazing professor who cares a lot about students' understanding of course material.
Boos is a good lecturer, very organized, and very clear. the class is informative but still accessible to those not familiar with the field
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Boos was a great and engaging professor that was really passionate and enthusiastic about the subject. However, I do believe that his grading system was a bit miscued. He never failed to present material however there was just a lack in explaining and working through problems that would then translate onto the homework.

At first, I was struggling hard in this class. But, Boos is so caring and took the time to help me learn personally and I turned my F into a B. Lectures are easy to understand, homework can be hard but he tries his best to help and half your homeworks will be dropped if you don't do well along with 20% of absences.
Super nice guy who makes the course's concepts very easy to understand
Professor Boos is amazing. He's a great lecturer and truly wants his students to be successful; I would highly recommend taking his class.

Wonderful man, fueled my love for climate science. Cares so much for his students. Genuinely a good person and a good teacher. Makes the class interactive and relevant wherever he can! Highly recommend.

Professor Boos is awesome! He's put a lot of time into making the class very informative but also approachable. I am a non-STEM major with no prior physics or chem coursework and was able to understand all the more technical concepts and do well on tests and homeworks. He does cool demos in every class and is very reasonable with exam curves.

The material is all recorded and lacks clarity, she is very picky about the midterm and final! The office hours were frequently cancelled, and when she was there, she was not very helpful and had a passive aggressive tone.
Very kind and friendly face-to-face. Can come off as a little cold but is genuinely kind. Cares about the subject a lot and is a reasonable grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Interesting lectures where you learn a lot she makes it clear in the beginning what to expect from the class. Very educational and relevant to issues in our world today and I thought that the readings were very interesting. She also makes it clear when office hours happen.

Whenever I had lectures with her, they were always interesting. She does require you to buy a course reader, which is $20. Since we met up once a week, she does make you watch recorded lectures and read. So, if you think you can do it, I recommend taking it.

She's an easy grader when it comes to group projects and essays as long as you follow the rubric. She grades more harshly on the midterm and final which are worth 50% of your grade. She does require you to buy a course reader. Not bad of a class you will pass as long as you keep up with assignments, follow guidelines, and participate.

I enjoyed her class, even if it didn't relate to my major. I learned a lot, and despite the fact that there was a fair bit of homework, it was mainly watching videos with some reading (easy work, just takes time). Her exams also have a BIG focus on that homework, so definitely take notes! She also offered exam prep. sessions, which I found helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Brown was lovely and super funny, but man, she is a tough grader! Expect to read a lot and take notes to memorize for exams. (P.S. If you do plan on taking her exams, she loves it when you include the chapter or page.)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Overall, this was one of the weakest academic classes I have taken and offered little intellectual challenge, functioning largely as an easy A. The requirement to purchase a $20+ course reader was especially frustrating, as the materials consisted of articles freely available online that could have been distributed via bCourses.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I loved her course! I learned so much and I felt that she was very approachable and clear on grading. It was a lovely experience to be her student.

not the most engaging lecturer (difficult in a recorded video tbf) and lots of readings that are 1000% necessary for the exams, but as long as you do them and understand them you can do well. group project can help boost grade since she's a bit strict on exam grading. interesting topics and topical readings, be prepared to buy a course reader.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: It covers a large amount of material and reading, requiring genuine interest in the subject to fully engage. However, the heavy workload made it difficult to retain everything. Be prepared to purchase textbooks and course readers, as PDFs are rarely available. Despite being online, the course is demanding and requires consistent effort to keep up.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great class overall and for pre-law students, since there is cold-calling in class. Very clear on instructions and grades fairly. 2 tests. Gives very specific content for review before midterm and final. 1 Group project, will boost score. Make sure to read and attend class. 2 papers, not excessively long. Offers 1-on-1 feedback through Zoom.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Brown was a fantastic teacher; taking this class was really enlightening. Participation in class discussions is mandatory, only had 1 project and the rest of the work was reading and watching posted lectures. The midterm and final were difficult, but Dr. Brown provides you with the specific topics you will be tested on ahead of time.

Her lectures were very informative and easy to follow however there is a lot of reading and she is a harsh grader. She could have done a better job on giving more clearer instructions. Be specific and write a lot on exams. Ask her questions and clarifications because she tends to take points off of a lot of things.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She is clearly very knowledgeable; however, she is extremely vague with directions and will grade rather harshly if you aren't specific (even though she isn't clear with expectations) and is hard to reach even though everything is online this semester. She did not show up to office hours multiple times leading up to midterms--really frustrating.

The class was really interesting but Brown was inaccessible out of class time. She often was late or didnt show up to office hours and discussion. There were very few assignments so midterm and projects are really important. I do not recommend taking this class online.

She's a great person and I learned so much from this class that I never would have otherwise. Lectures were amazing and loved the guest speaker who came. Super passionate  and really tries to engage the large group of people. However, sometimes seemed as if she had more important things to do. Went to a couple of office hours, wasn't there.
She's amazing! Everyone should take her class.

Focus class on Social Construction of Race, Prison Industrial Complex, and Women of Color. Very passionate about what she is teaching-- its like she's preaching. Grading was based on a Midterm, final, group project, participation, and Research Paper.  Grades fairly, a little harsh though. Uses great texts and media to convey point.

Her lectures were so engaging! To this day, still the best class I have taken at Cal, even though it was during my time at FPF. Her class left me feeling so passionate about many of our society's issues.

Prof. Brown is a great professor. The class was not difficult but there are a lot of readings (interesting readings though!). You have one midterm, an in class final exam and a 10 page final paper. Her lectures were really interesting and she is really passionate about her work

Professor Brown is very passionate and wise. Her approach and the class itself raised awareness and allowed me to dig deep and understand other ethnicity's and cultures. Definitely need to be able to have an open mind in this class. She is interesting and I enjoyed attending lecture especially with speakers. Make sure to read majority of the books!

Incredible. I took her Ethnic Studies class at FPF and wish I could take it over again. Dr Brown is a dynamic, passionate lecturer who is as smart as she is down-to-earth. Absolutely amazing professor, can't recommend her highly enough. Her class requires a lot of reading from various texts, but they are all interesting and insightful books.

Took her for FPF, Fall 2013. Honestly, it has been my favorite class in Berkeley by far and this is only because of Dr. Brown. I came into Cal not really knowing what I wanted to major in, but Dr. Brown's passion for teaching has really inspired me to become an Ethnic Studies major. DEFINITELY take this class. Very eye-opening.

Amazing prof! Took her for FPF & she was super interesting, funny and relatable. I used to hate history, but she made me fall in love with "history" and now I'm minoring in ES. I definitely recommend her class to EVERYONE. Very eye-opening and you will miss this class when you're done. I promise!

Took her class in FPF, it ended up being a good decision, she's very passionate/knowledgeable about the subject. There were 2 midterms, 1 quiz, and a 10 page essay. She grades relatively easy, not focusing as much on writing style than on how much information you've included from readings/lectures. Don't miss the guess speakers - especially Lakota!
A fun professor! i would def. recommend, esp. if u have an interest in politics. :)

Professor Brown was a fun and approachable professor. She was definitely good at engaging students and the class itself was fairly easy. The entire second half of the class consisted of watching videos and listening to guest speakers though so I tended to skip lecture more :P

Dr Brown is a great teacher and resource, esp. in the FPF. She taught us how to take notes, write research papers, use the libraries, and question our world. Lecture important: reviews  readings, has fascinating guest speakers, and presentations. Had many substitutes in this class though-she's got a life too. Easy grader: put tons of info in papers

She is VERY interesting and extremely dedicated to her work. She makes every class fun and it feel more like a conversation than a lecture. The class changed the lives of many of her students and she exposes a whole new way of thinking to her students. Always available and ready to help, down to earth and very friendly!
I really enjoyed the lectures.
Great lectures. Exams were a bit confusing.
one of my fav classes at cal

Braun is a good professor and a good public speaker. I took this class for a GE, so I am biased when I say that it's unfortunately boring. The readings were subpar and often too lengthy for the amount of information received. His grading criteria was not very clear, and the grades given by GSIs varied a lot. Solo projects were incredibly boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Braun was hilarious! I specifically remember how engaging he was with the crowd and I had a blast in his lectures. The work was super manageable as long as you kept up with the readings (which were really cool and relavant). Really good teaching style!
The best lecture & course I've ever took in Berk

Nothing but good things to say. Braun is an amazing lecturer. topics are extremely easy to understand if you pay attention. go to lecture. lots of reading. you must do it to understand what is happening. 
favorite class of the semester.

Braun is my favorite professor at Berkeley so far. I'm not a sociology major but this was my favorite class. He is such an interesting and captivating lecturer and homework is fair. It's a somewhat challenging class but not if you pay attention. Tests are really not bad and u can just pick what you want to talk about on them

I loved this class Professor Braun really connects to modern day concepts and makes lectures enjoyable. I had a great gsi that allowed this class to go well! Though 2nd midterm is definitely more challenging than the first, you have weekly readings, and final is video project. However this breath class is now my major so I recommend!

Fun and a good professor but too broad of a subject. I took this class with the intention of majoring in Sociology but have changed my mind. Maybe because it was a morning class and far away from where I lived but I stopped going to lecture early on. My GSI didn't really seem to care about connecting with us.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The concepts and letures were pretty good. However, the projects were not as fun.... The projects didn't really have a rubric so many felt lost/ didn't fulfill certain reqs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class is super interesting, by far my favorite class I've taken at Cal. Robert is super funny and engaging in his lectures. Lots of readings and pop quizzes in your discussion section. Midterms include a timed written paper and the final a lecture style presentation.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Braun is a really engaging lecturer and the topics were always interesting and easily explained. It wasn't detrimental to miss lectures and the discussions were helpful. Lots of reading, easy quiz every couple of weeks, presentation assignment, and easy-ish midterm/final timed essays.

Braun is a good lecturer. Class is based on readings + lectures with the midterm, final, quizzes, pop quizzes, and project that make up your entire grade. My only gripe with this class (& it's a really big one) is that we're never really provided a rubric on what is expected so grading & feedback on everything was super unclear at times :/
Amazing professor, take his class if you can! One of my best classes in Berkeley, he makes sure people understand the material and is very understanding with his students! Simply brilliant
the final was terrible, need to write an essay of 8-10 paragraphs with 8-12 sentences each in an hour.

Professor Braun has expertise & a brilliant mind, but he didn't seem to grasp that students were struggling with the material in his course on genocide. Readings & lecture were deeply upsetting, but he didn't foster an environment to discuss that before addressing theory. Few assignments with little room for feedback. 1 paper, 1 midterm, 1 final.
LOTS of reading. Tests are HARD! Lecture was interesting but at fast pace.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Robert is really passionate and dedicated. Lectures were interesting and clear. He was really helpful and had a ton of ideas when I went to office hours to discuss my final paper.
Ton of reading but section and lecture make up for it. Learned a ton.
Very accommodating. Cares about students wellbeing in times of crisis.
This was a good class. Lectures and section were well organized. Interesting readings. Pay attention to writing.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: even though i personally find his lectures not the most helpful, the material and readings are very intriguing. the gsi though was probably more helpful than the professor. there's a lot of readings but they're mostly explained by the professor/gsi, but you need to read them for essays or to quote certain things for exams too.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Great professor who cares a lot about students. Lectures were easy to follow and slides were engaging (must go to lecture to understand content). Decent amount of readings but all in all good class and GREAT GSI's (well mine was really great!!) take advantage of office hours for final paper
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: very accomodating. great lectures.
Good intro
very interesting class. Ok reading load. Lectures are very engaging
Professor really cares about teaching. Stands out at Cal. Take his class if you have the chance.
Easy class if you keep going to lectures (which are pretty great). Make sure you understand all concepts discussed by professor.
One of my favorite classes at Cal. Worked very hard but was worth it in the end.
Engaging lectures. Assignments were a bit confusing.
Great class. Learned a ton. Tough grader.

Don't get me wrong--Braun is an amazing lecture. He is a brutal grader and not empathetic at all. There was no clear communication between what he wanted in his essays and what the GSI's were looking for. It was almost impossible to get an A (I get all A's in other upper div classes). He also doesn't follow departmental rules. Wouldn't recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Pros: engaging lectures, very nice and accessible professor and GSIs, interesting content, not too much reading. One of my favorite professors at Cal. Tips: take notes for readings to help with papers and tests (pretty much mandatory to get a decent grade in the class), be able to describe class concepts, GO TO OFFICE HOURS FOR PAPERS.

Although this course was very interesting, Braun's approach was often times demeaning to groups and condescending. Definitely has an air of superiority, and the GSI's for Spring 2019 were incredibly tough graders, never gave any feedback even when prompted, and Braun cares little about the students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof uses prerecorded lectures which likely have been reused throughout the years. GSIs literally do all the work and are confusing in their expectations. The textbook (that she wrote) is mandatory and has confusing graphs. She has done nothing to interact with the class herself directly. She feels very disconnected from her classes.

She is a great lecturer, her course was really organized, expectations and rubrics are clear, content is interesting, it's easy to reach out for help, and it's really easy to get a good grade. You will need her textbook and GSls do most if not all the grading so keep that in mind. The class has honestly been my favorite so far in Berkeley.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Bree was a great professor. She got to know each student individually and support us in achieving personal growth as scientists and as people. This was the most humanistic approach I have seen any professor take to teaching a science course and it was extremely rewarding. You will gain new research skills and meaningful connections.

Took it hoping to learn more about amphibians & conduct meaningful research in the field, ended up wasting my Fridays navel gazing, receiving meandering career advice, and being subjected to extended tarot readings.
Solid teacher, very clear lectures, well organized. Comes across as a nice, fun person as a bonus.

Bree is an amazing professor and I highly recommend to take her class. I had some moments where I was not sure about things but going to office hours really helped me and I did well in the class. The material is interesting and Bree is just amazing! Highly recommended!

Bree is one of the best professors at Cal. She REALLY cares about the students. She goes so far beyond the call of duty for any professor's duties! The class is interesting and she is so enthusiastic and fun. She is funny and bubbly. Always a pleasure to be around. You can ask her any question and she will not make you feel stupid. TAKE THIS CLASS!
Though the class was a little easy, it was only the first semester it was taught. Rosenblum is extremely enthusiastic and happy to answer questions and make the class as enjoyable as possible.

I feel like I learned alot because the lectures were always engaging. She entertains all the questions asked and sometimes it felt like a discussion section. lectures aren't recorded. lots of guest lectures. content material mixed molecular virology and public health

Britt is such an amazing professor. Her lectures are DENSE, but that does not hide the fact that she is extremely passionate and knowledgeable on the topic. Lectures are not recorded, so make sure to record yourself because there is a lot of information, and the course is very memorization heavy. Midterms were tough and all short answer.

Super passionate about virology and it is so evident in lecture. Class material definitely requires time studying and tests are short answer, but the material is laid out very clearly of what you need to know or not. No extra homework and having such a strong professor makes it easier to follow the content and retain! Lots of review too

She is inaccessible, does not communicate well, and does not appear to show any real interest in student experience. Unorganized and poor teacher. Classes are not recorded, presumably to motivate attendance. Exams are completely short answer which dedicates itself to the professors interpretation rather than actual content absorption. Do not take.
meanie pants

Glaunsinger is a personable, effective, and engaging lecturer, which makes her lectures for C114 enjoyable and informative. The grading structure of the class is favorable to students and is clearly put forth in the syllabus. Course is interesting, lectures are informative and discussions provide students with info past base-level content.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I've ever had, she's a wonderful lecturer and she has many guest speakers that do lectures on specific viruses. Make sure to get full credit on all the participation points (quizzes + project) and do well on your first midterm. She has a great policy that favors your higher midterm of the first 2 if you did poorly on one.

Professor Glausinger's passion for Virology can be felt through her teaching style and lectures, makes class extremely interesting to go to and an enriching experience. Each lecture dove into public health of a virus then its molecular bio. Not too much work and tests were tough but fair. Overall one of the best classes I have taken at Berkeley!

My favorite class I've ever taken at Berkeley, definitely because she's an incredible lecturer! Went to office hours and she was always so kind and friendly, willing to answer any and all the questions I had. The class also was pretty reasonable, different than any other class in biology on campus, and 10% of our grade was an art project!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I started to enjoy Professor Salama's class once I realized his teaching style is old-school. He won't hold your hand, and if he thinks you're wrong, he'll let you know-- but that's not a bad thing. His class, more than any other, sharpened me. Show up ready to think critically, engage thoughtfully, and participate meaningfully.

I took Professor Salama's Legalst 145 and 147, and he is one of my favorite professors at Cal. Professor Salama's lectures are clear, engaging, and effective. He can explain complex terms in a logically clear and easily understandable manner. He is approachable and enthusiastic outside of class and genuinely cares about students' personal growth.

Awesome class, probalby the best I took during my time at Cal! Bruno is a fantastic lecturer that takes the time to analyze interesting topics in law & tech & answers questions. Easy grading, 2 term papers (10 pages each), smaller written assignments given by the GSIs, and an in-person oral presentation. Overall, highly recommend this class!

Two term papers each 7-10 pages long. I had a super chill GSI made the class easy. Attendance for the lecture is only mandatory for guest speakers which happens maybe 4 times and other than that you should get an A in this class by not even going to class and writing good term papers. Some weekly homework but seems to be graded on completion.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Meyerhof made the class so interesting I would recommend his class

The Professor is knowledgeable, but the way the course was structured was so we didn't really need to attend lectures except for the content you were going to write about in your papers. The GSI was chill. 2 papers worth 90% of your grade and participation worth 10%. Lots of deep, philosophical approaches for a law and economics class.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Graded by few things--So many papers

reviews.comment: Do your readings, the grading is fair but I don't find this class to be very easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: he's smart but a horrible teacher. we all tanked the first test and then he blamed it on our incompetence not his inability to teach us the relevant material. he's eager to help but gets frustrated easily and doesn't communicate well. also told us on several occasions that a 50% isn't a fail by his standards then proceeded to fail people with 58%
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Bruno is an inspirational professor. He is more than accommodating and goes out of his way to help students succeed during class. Make sure to do the review quizzes and to ask questions during class. The class becomes more difficult if you don't ask questions when you are confused - SO ASK AWAY! Amazing class and amazing professor!

Professor Salama is an excellent teacher. Perhaps his teaching style has changed as he has gained more experience. As of Summer 2020, he's very considerate and supportive. He answers questions in great detail and doesn't mind going over things again and again until everyone understands. I found Law and Econ pretty easy, but still interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: My experience with LS 145 summer online course (due to COVID-19) has been an amazing one. I am a Legal Studies major and econ is a different way of thinking. Prof. Salama is a GREAT professor. Extremely smart, keeps you engaged, really takes his time to make sure ALL students understand, and is honest and caring. His tests are 10 questions now.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: I found Professor Salama's course to be very informative and a useful introduction into an unconventional and thought-provoking analysis of law. The topics he chose to cover were insightful and interesting. He was always available to answer any questions in person or over email. I left the course inspired to learn more about law and economics.

Professor Salama was knowledgeable but not good at divulging that knowledge in any digestible way. His quizzes were confusing, had errors, and he often responded rudely to students who found errors in his quizzes or answer keys. Quizzes were as short as 5 multiple choice questions, so missing one question is very costly to your grade.

Professor is very intelligent and clearly not for everyone, Expect to learn a good deal by yourself and then come to classes to discuss topics. Quizzes are easy but could be longer (only 5 multiple choice questions, so if you miss one, your grade suffers)- maybe 10 or 20 questions would distribute grades more evenly. Professor is very accessible.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: He is a terrible lecturer. I got bored and eventually stopped attending his lectures. I personally didnt have any problems with him but hes very stubborn , not really helpful and even rude with some students.

He has three midterms that are mostly multiple-choice which I don't believe is an accurate way to test students on their knowledge. Very easy class to get an A, but miss one or two questions on the exams and you have a B or a C. He doesn't employ good teaching strategies and was oftentimes rude to students
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Theres 3 midterms, he drops the lowest one. Midterms are worth 80% of your grade. First midterm had 5 multiple choice questions worth 20 points per question. You missed one question? Youre bumped down to a B. Missed 2? C. No partial credit. And hes stubborn about changing the format even the slightest bit. The way he teaches is so confusing.

He's really smart but has no idea how to be a professor. I had him for both Legal Studies 145 and 149 and barely learned anything. 145 was easy because the midterms were similar to the review quizzes, and 149 was easy because it was literally just 2 essays and nothing from lecture actually mattered. However, he expects you to just teach yourself.
The book is posted online by him for free. Our syllabus said theres 3 tests and one of them get dropped. Quizzes are take home and theyre not graded. Its the first day of class but it seems doable
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Prof. Brunet's lectures are boring and she's honestly kind of rude to students who don't immediately give her the "right" answers. Attendance isn't mandatory and she posts slide summaries on bCourses so I stopped going to lecture halfway through the semester. It's a battle to stay awake in there at 11am. Do yourself a favor and take a different AC.

She talks slow so lectures can be tedious to get through. She posts lecture highlights that you can go over but other than that no devices are allowed. Quizzes are hard because of some specific questions, but the final is doable. You can lose max 7-8/100 points for A, but 60% of your grade is based on simple notes, participation, and assignments.
Overall, I liked the class. The material was presented in an interesting way. Exams can be a bit specific, but are still doable. She can seem quite strict but she cares about the topic deeply.

Lightest class I ever took across high school and Berkeley so far. Attendance in the lecture is not required, but it is in the discussion. Quizzes are literally just based on the lecture highlights you can find on Canvas (basically just memorization). Readings are not even that bad; I literally just highlighted random parts for full credit.

Definitely take this class for an easy A. You have to do the bare minimum work that should be expected for any college course- go to lecture and turn in assignments. You don't even have to take notes, as the quizzes and tests are on material explained very thoroughly in class. The lectures are SUPER interesting and fun, I didn't even want to skip.

Unaccommodating to make-up work (even when students have extenuating emergencies). Even my GSI had to apologize on behalf of Carla's overly strict policies. MUSIC 26AC was known as one of the easiest breadths, but the policies have tightened, making it high-maintenance and time-consuming. Do NOT take this course if you're looking for an easy A.

She is literally the worst professor I've had at Berkeley. She takes 1.5 hrs to get through a lecture that someone can get through in 20 minutes. Its music history...like nobody cares abt this subject. Rude professor. A lot of readings. Lecture slides not posted, recordings not posted, no devices in class or in discussion. Take another AC class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: evil she is genuinely the worst do not take her class
Take this class if you want to fall asleep in lectures and write a 4 page essay for the final with no notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Genuinely a terrible person and teacher. She is extremely rude and treats the class as if it were an upper-division Physics class. She also manages to turn everything into a gender-based problem. Carla does not communicate with the GSIs and manages to make the 2nd-easiest class at Berkeley the 3rd hardest.
Fade fade fade she made music boring

Class takes itself way too seriously for what it is. Basically none of what is discussed is interesting. Lectures are unbelievably boring, and a better lecturer could probably get through the 1.5-hour class in 20 minutes. All devices are prohibited in a lecture hall with no writing surfaces. If there are ever to be budget cuts, let it be this
the class was easy enough but lectures were so long and the content wasn't very interesting & participation is mandatory.
Terrible professor. She does not explain anything and treats this intro breadth class like it is an upper division STEM class.
Don't take this class if you just wanna fill the AC requirement. Her quizzes are a bit hard and the GSIs are tough graders but the material is so interesting. Also her lectures are very longgggg

Professor Brunet is a genuinely caring instructor. She may seem stern at first, but once you get to know her, she's very approachable and understanding. She goes out of her way to help students, guiding them to resources online and in person, and even sharing her own materials to support their work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: She is a great professor and enjoys getting to know her students. She helps with our papers well and does not give that many. Fair grader and wants you to succeed.

Music26AC has been one of the worst classes I've taken at Berkeley. For a month straight, Prof. Brunet only provided pre-recorded lectures instead of holding live zoom, making the class less engaging and exciting. Her 3 quizzes and final exam were also IMPOSSIBLE with 30 minutes for 40 questions, including listening ones, which was very unfair.
Very irresponsible, abruptly changes class start times or doesn't even hold class at all. Bad attitude when answering questions and is not enthusiastic about course topics. and
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: 3 quizzes and final. The questions on the quizzes are so obscure. As someone who doesn't have a music background, you're essentially learning a bunch of musical terms on the fly. Sometimes she thinks some musical terms are "obvious". Additionally, participation in discussion is mandatory.
Very irresponsible, abruptly changes class start times or doesn't even hold class at all. Bad attitude when answering questions and is not enthusiastic about course topics.
Course structure was very flexible.

took her MUS101 class at USF. easy class, might be a little harder if you don't have music experience, but prof brunet makes sure everyone is on the same page before moving forward. little homework. highly encouraged to listen to the music given in class. several quizzes throughout the semester on each music historical period.

Professor Brunet is such a great teacher. She knows you have a lot of work outside of class. She always gives extra credit. Not much hw, there are about idk 3 tests only. Very chill teacher and class. She gives caring mom vibes so this made the class very welcoming. Really cares about her students. Definitely take her if you just need credits. :)

This class is very accessible if you have little to no knowledge on music terminology. It's extremely interesting as it discusses Blues emergence to MTV. Make sure to do readings beforehand, attend lecture, and take diligent notes. Professor Brunet's grading is very fair and she is very receptive to feedback. 10/10, one of my favorite Cal classes!

I took Professor Brunet's Music of the Americas class at USF, and I loved it. Her passion and knowledge of the subject made her class super interesting. I especially loved the sections about Brazilian music. Very little homework, and when we did, it was pretty easy. TAKE HER CLASS!

Took her USF Music of the Americas Class. She was very passionate about her subject which made the class really enjoyable. Only a few homework assignments and 2 challenging but doable tests that you will have to study for. Overall was a very fun and interesting class with a wonderful professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I had the pleasure of taking MUSIC 20A as a Summer Session E course with Carla. This was her first time teaching this course, and despite the short 3 week period, she was able to cover alot of material. She assigns couple HW pages, and there are written quizzes and a final 1-on-1 scheduled singing exam. Doesn't always take attendance, but should go

At USF. A few homework assignments based on the readings, 2 short papers, and a group project. She is very helpful & available if you are having trouble understanding the material. Might be a bit difficult if you have no understanding of music, as there are some elements of music theory. Interesting course. Just do the work &review for the 2 exams.

Very disorganized- changes the syllabus abruptly based on 'what comes up from discussion in class'. That makes sense but she needs to know that it's ridiculous to expect us to complete freshly assigned assignments in less than a day. Most of us take more than one class and it is unfair for us when need to reschedule plans because of abrupt changes.

She's Brazilian and provides lots of insight on Brazilian music from a native perspective. Lectures don't just cover the music but also the socioeconomic and cultural roots of each movement. Graded on just a midterm and final, with a bit of homework here and there. She schedules tons of office time and will go out of her way to help you succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: good profesor, great

Frankly, Carlos Bustamante tarnishes his legacy and the very study of biochemistry every time he speaks in Wheeler 150. He lacks a picogram of insight or skill when it comes to teaching, I image toddlers would explain protein structures in far more robust and detailed manners than him. He is a disgrace to the very name of Berkeley, should be sacked
If you aren't religious, pick a religion and pray. I'd recommend recording the lectures in class as he does not post them. GO TO EVERY CLASS.

reviews.comment: he's a funny guy and has a pretty thick accent. that exam was not it though, he would tell us what to memorize but also did not tell us enough.
Out of scope exams, poor lecturer.
Known for extreme exams outside the scope of typical biochem. Much harder than other biochem professors at cal, and poor lecturer.

God-awful lecturer and made pretty unfair exams. By far one of the most frustrating professors I've had the displeasure of getting to know and learn from. Please do yourself a favor and take MCB102 in the Spring.

Terrible teacher. Should never ever be allowed anywhere near a teaching environment again. He does not post recordings just to mess with us and make us memorize a billion things and guess what? On the midterm very little of what he asked us to memorize was on it and instead he included tons of info about his garbage, useless research.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor was actually one of the worst professors I have taken in Berkeley. Absolutely atrocious! He made our exam three pages of his research, which he barely covered. His accent is very hard to understand, and he did not post recordings even though he could have fully understood them. Actually hates students. If you can, AVOID!!!

Carlos made it clear that he doesn't like students, and his teaching was flat-out mean spirited. The class has over 500 people, but only 400 seats in the lecture halls. This means every lecture, students are turned away. While Carlos receives recordings, he refuses to post them out of spite. We had to memorize 50+ structures, none were on the exam.

Bustamante can be difficult to understand at times due to his accent, which makes it even more disappointing that lecture recordings for this class are not posted. However, in a difficult class inherently, Bustamante did a pretty good job in communicating the content, curating fair exams and quizzes, and making detailed and informative slideshows.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I'm an international student so it might be a littttttlllleee(? difficult for me to understand his accent. Overall, this part of the course requires an intensive memorization of structures and stuff. But the quizzes were pretty doable and he gave us a list of what will be on the exam.

He goes fast, and sadly doesn't explain things very well. However, his exams are the same every year, so study the practice exams! This section content-wise isn't bad, but the exam is confusing and not super related to what we learned...so learn how to answer the questions rather than the material. Start reviewing early on, and the curve will help.

Very fast lectures but is also pretty friendly if you get to know him. I'd 100% recommend reading the textbook reading for his section as some of the exam material was not covered in his lectures and it helped me better understand what he was talking about while zooming through them. STUDY IN ADVANCE if you want to succeed! memorization HEAVY
Bustamante is extremely smart and very nice in office hours, but his exams are difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Memorization heavy and not receptive to student feedback.

Lots of information, but very low difficulty concepts so as long as you start reviewing material a ways before the test, you will be solid. I never read a page from the book, but I felt fine on the midterm. Do the problem sets and practice exams to get an understanding of what questions will be asked. Definitely a doable A!

Professor Bustamante taught the first portion of the course and after finishing the course, his material was by far the most difficult. That being said, Bustamante was the best out of the three. The only thing I hated though was the curve. I got 1.1 std above the mean and somehow ended with a B+.

Goes pretty fast in lecture so I had to re-watch lectures and refer to the book. Midterm format was almost exactly like his previous exams. Would recommend staying on top of problem sets and going to office hours so you don't fall behind.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I absolutely loved professor Bustamante. I can see why many students might not like him. He teaches very difficult topics, but he really wants you to learn and have fun with the material. MCB 102 is not an easy class and you definitely have to work for your grade. Go to office hours and asks questions. Exams are based on lecture material.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Bustamante starts off his section for 102 by saying that you need to know everything from the textbook, lecture slides, and things that he mentions during lecture. All you really need to study are his slides--they are concise and well made. Make sure that you record his lecturers, and review them later with the slides. Hardest section for 102.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: His section was the hardest of the three sections of biochemistry. He starts the section saying everything covered in the book are "fair game" but never asked any questions about book material not covered in lecture during the MT. Also, his MT was so difficult the GSIs admitted it to all the students. Study guide is exhaustive and didn't reflect MT
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: The professor talked too much about liberal ideology and tended to delve off into rants about Trump

Class was NOTHING like the course description. I expected to learn about interesting topics from a non-physics perspective, and instead got a repeat of AP Physics. Lecture is incredibly boring and unhelpful since he posts the slides online. Tests were hard to study for. The first midterm was almost all theoretical while the second was math-based.

Professor Bustamante is so knowledgeable about the subject he is able to make something as complicated as quantum mechanics simple to understand. He is a very kind person and willing to help. As a person who took this class not just to fulfill a requirement but for legitimate interest, I really enjoyed his lectures.

great professor. humble, funny, SO smart, and still manages to explain difficult material in a clear, understandable manner. midterm is take-home and final is a paper. brings in really interesting guest lecturers...big names who all come cuz carlos is THE MAN

This class was harder than most r1b equivalents at berkeley, the final was over 50 pages of writing. That being said, the class is graded fairly, albeit harshly, with good feedback (pay attention to this), and you are allowed to research anything you want. If you want a hard class that pushes you but is free in what you can research, take this.

solid class overall, the way she structures the project 3/final was smooth and felt digestible since she breaks it up into parts. Lecture was a bit tedious, we just read over what we needed to do outside of class from the class notes. The first couple of weeks were easy, not much to do just simple assignments.

Excessive amounts of busy work, despite saying constantly that she doesn't like giving our busy work. Get ready to spend the whole class reading over the class notes, that could be read at student's leisure. Very tough grader and doesn't give the most constructive feedback.

Asyn class. Only direct interaction with prof was through comments and one Zoom check-in session for the final speech, but she was extremely caring about my progress and really seemed to appreciate her students. I wish I took an in-person class with her.

Extremely unorganized, does not tell you when assignments are due, spends class time speaking about how she is "kind" and grades papers because she is kind (like isn't that literally her job).

DONT take this class if you need to fulfill ur 2nd R&W requirement, get a different professor. She is unprofessional, passive aggressive, and unhelpful.
Unbelievably unclear with everything

As someone who doesn't write a lot and liked writing to a moderate degree, this class makes me hate writing. I physically get nauseous thinkin about the amount of work I have because of this class; physics is less work. Take r1b or r5b if your major is not writing focused. Thinking bout this class makes me so tired. she a good person though overall

CW11 was an online, asynchronous course. Pretty easy, mostly busy work. I almost never heard from Carmen, always from her co-teacher David. Grading was not clear. I was marked down for not doing things that I did do, but didn't argue because it didn't affect GPA (A vs A+). Course evals due before most of my work was graded, this is honest feedback

Carmen really does care a lot about her students and their success in the class. She is a tough grader, but she is also very fair and gives detailed, timely feedback. Your grade is directly tied into the effort and revisions you put into the work. The research project is very open-ended and she guides you through each step of the research process.

The course has a heavy workload with high standards. Participation is mandatory, she notes every absence, even if you're just two minutes late. She provides detailed feedback. While the class offers an opportunity to learn in-depth, I recommend considering other R4B classes if you're looking for a less demanding workload.

Carmen's instructions for assignments and papers make no sense and she is a very tough grader, which is an unfortunate combination for students trying to succeed in her class. There is a ridiculous amount of busy work for a class that she claims "has zero busy work". She does care about her students but her class is very very frustrating to be in.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very caring and accomodating
She cares about everything about you, except your grade. If you care about your GPA, take something else.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I thought this was a pretty decent and standard R4B class! There is a lot of work, some busy work but each assignment helps you out with your papers. Carmen gives great feedback on your work and is accessible to reach outside of class! I felt like my writing improved a lot but beware she is a harsh grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Unrealistic expectations. A ton of busy work, and just rambles about how much she cares. This class has depressed me and made me feel like a bad writer, and I've taken a good deal of writing classes at Cal. Take an R1b or R5b instead. Don't take this!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: I am extremely depressed when I am taking this class, and I still am because it genuinely makes me think I am a horrible writer. It feels like I am NEVER enough. No matter how many times I revise I always end up with a C grade. It is not my first time taking Berkeley English class and I have never received grades like this in my college career.

I am so grateful to have taken Prof. Butcher's R4B back in my sophomore year. Carmen taught us the basics of researches via library-hopping (from one to another, similar to island-hopping), the tips and tricks in building our portfolio website, and was very lenient with our choice of topics for the essays.

She is the sweetest, can come on a little intense at first, but she's kind, respectful, and cares about you as a student. I've made friends in the class even though it's online and we have talked many times about how much she's healing our parental trauma lol
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This is honestly the worst professor I've had at Berkeley. She treats her students like kindergarteners and most of your time will be spent on busy work.
