Prof seems to care more about how much she cares than her actual students. This class made my writing worse. Insane attendance policies and will call you out if your camera is off  for a second
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Class was solely online and through zoom. Professor grades tough but gives a ton of good feedback + allowed a redo of the 1st essay. She has a ton of office hours so it's easy to get a hold of her, and cared a lot about her students + gave a ton of advice. Final project was a 4k word essay but process felt easy due to previous lead-up assignments.

She provides lots of resources but is an extremely difficult professor. She is an instructor with the mindset of "C" being an average grade. Expect to fail most essays unless you put in long hours. Attendance policy is also very strict, you'll be penalized for being even a few minutes early/late or if your camera ever goes off during class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Carmen was the best professor I ever met in college. She helps me regain confidence as a writer, researcher, and most importantly, as a person. Her class deeply changed my life and she encourages me to express my true self in all circumstances. I wish all professors are like her.

The amt of busy work in this class in the first 3 weeks was lowkey insane LMAO. But, it started to die down after which was a breath of relief. She def cares about her students a lot, and it made me feel very appreciated. It was an online course but she tried her best to incorporate classroom inclusivity. Grading is ok!

Extremely inspirational and energetic professor. Really cares about her students and takes genuine interest in the research that everyone does. She gives extremely good feedback on assignments and is also very accommodating. Definitely worth taking a class with her.

Professor Butcher was extremely considerate about conflicts/issues during class, and she provided lots of opportunities outside of class to meet and discuss work. Her essays were graded a bit tough, but she gave opportunities to revise the first essay and lots of work aside from essays, so if you put in work in the class, you'll get a good grade.

Carmen is a demanding grader but available to students with forgiving office hours. The best way to get a good grade is to take advantage of her OH!! The class was online, and therefore students were only required to do four doable essays. Overall, she's very considerate of all her students and does offer the ability to revise for a better grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She is literally the best English Professor, she really cares for all of her students. Definitely go to all of her office hours and ask a lot of questions and you will definitely get at least a B+! Pay attention and be respectful, she makes classes fun and worth the effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Carmen cares about all her students and wants them to pass. With that being said, she does grade her essays very tough. She has made a better writer and I would recommend that everybody takes one of her classes at least once. Just be prepared to work very hard for a good grade. It is a very rewarding class!

Carmen is an amazing teacher, she always has your best interests in mind and she absolutely loves it when students email her asking for help (not sarcasm). Always ask for help if your struggling, her goal is to help you succeed so you don't have to take that class ever again. I love this teacher!

I took R1A with Butcher and I liked the way she taught but I must be honest, she grades every single paper very harshly! I got F for my first draft essay. Sometimes she is hard to reach because she doesn't stay on campus much. She gives great feedbacks and compliments you for your work but if you don't meet the paper criteria, grade won't change :)
Dr. Butcher is an exceptional and caring teacher. She really wants you to learn. She provides extensive feedback which will help you to improve your writing skills.
Honestly, Dr. Butcher completely killed any confidence I had as a writer. Her harsh grading that runs contrary to what she said in office hours/paper workshops made it feel impossible to succeed.

Dr Butcher was extremely accessible outside of class and you can tell she genuinely cares about her students. However, her extreme strictness of expectations for papers, class attendance, and participation outweighed her caring. There was no transparency about grades at all besides one mid semester check in and grades did not reflect effort at all!

Dr. Butcher is an amazing professor and I highly recommend taking her class! She is super accessible outside of class, gives a ton of feedback for your essays and cares deeply about all of her students. However, her grading is extremely stringent and you really have to work to get an A. She does give revision opportunities for your essays though.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Dr. Butcher's a sweet lady. However, she is a really tough grader, she gave us all F's the first essay we turned in, and an average of D's and low C's on the 2nd essay. She did let us revise our essays (3 essays and 1 personal essay) numerous times. The amount of readings were crazy, and assigned us an essay the first day of class. I did pass thoug

If you have no coding background like I did, this class is going to be very hard as the prof assumes you do despite the prereqs. Rewarding content though to learn even with the poor quality and structuring of the class but now I can proudly say I can code computer simulations!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Unless you're being held at gunpoint, do not take this class. Prerequisites are completely opposite to the ones advertised and the prof is extremely unhelpful and often combative to students. Refuses to elaborate on policy. This class is completely mismanaged with the GSIs not knowing anything because the professor refuses to share it with them.

As a student with coding experience who is used to organized STEM courses, I found this professor's teaching style very difficult to follow. Lectures felt poorly organized, with topics that didn't build on each other, assignments were very time-consuming relative to how clearly the material was taught, which made the course unnecessarily stressful.

Avoid this class at all costs. This professor just changes the syllabus based on his whims and fancies. Changed the final exam format halfway through semester, and added a final project without clarifying how it'd affect grading. Very passive aggressive if you try to ask him questions. Doesn't respond to student concerns. DO NOT take this class.

Often there were typos and other syntax problems that hindered a student from actually solving anything without office hours; which would rarely take place, often without a TA. The professor himself was combative and passive aggressive, especially to those who weren't doing wel. I felt lost throughout this class. don't take!

While many say this is not an introductory class, this was my first experience coding in Python and the class was not particularly difficult if you attended the labs and devoted a couple solid hours every week on the homeworks. Lectures were mostly conceptual and exploratory, a bit of a hit or miss depending on the topic. Would definitely recommend

Love it or hate it. I personally really enjoyed EPS 109, the assignments were interesting & applicable, but the lectures are more of a supplement to the course material which you will learn in your lab section. Difficult but very rewarding to go in without programming experience. Good first upper-div.

Professor could be more accessible.

Didn't weigh our grades in Bcourses as in the syllabus, leading us to believe we had higher grades. Exams (esp. midterm) were not easily completed in the given time. Misleading announcements about exams w/ raw score to letter grade conv., implying a curve, then using raw score for final grade calculation. Spoke to dept. chair about serious change.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Avoid this class if you can!! This class is coding intensive and NOT introductory. My GSI carried me through this class b/c Militzer didn't teach anything relevant or covered on exams/HW. Also he was so passive aggressive to students who weren't doing well in his class :/ Every bad thing you've heard abt this class is true, its not worth it.
tests were too specific on topics not covered during lectures
had fun in class and he's passionate which is good
The lectures do not help with course content nor does it help us with coursework it was mostly the GSIs doing most of the work
He does not teach in a way that helps us understand the coursework and does not teach the class but rather the GSIs do
I would be careful while taking this professor, in terms of how he does not teach relevant things in lectures for our assignments.
Not the best ran class

There is a difference between a researcher and someone who can teach, this professor is a researcher and talks to us as if we are experts in his field of study and teaches irrelevant things for us to do almost all the assignments for the class. I think he is smart, but not qualified to teach.

The professor is very nice but the lectures have nothing to do with the homework and lab material. This is definitely not a "no coding experience class" you need at least E7 or CS61A to take this class. Does not provide us any information to any assignment that will graded
Easy class, easy A, and nice professor.

Burkhard and our GSI were extremely helpful and I'm very grateful that they took time every week to hold office hours for assignments, often times very late. I do want to make clear one thing: the course description labeled the class as "introductory" but in my opinion, this class is VERY coding intensive which felt very overwhelming at times.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I took Prof Militzer's online ASTRON W12 class for the Physical Science breadth requirement. I was good at the physical sciences in high school, but, after flunking out of Chem 1A, I decided to go with Astronomy to fulfill my breadth requirement. Anyway, the class was a lot of work on top of my summer internship, but I did well and learned a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Decent enough. A's require some work, but a B is basically guaranteed
I took EPS 109 with Militzer during Fall 2012. He was extremely helpful and knowledgeable, and I'm glad to have taken the course
Well organized course, fair assignments and grading.  Enjoyed the class, but limited interaction with professor because course was online.

Roland is such a sweetheart who is so knowledgable about earthquakes. If you keep up with the class(easy assignments), it is an easy A and has very useful information on being prepared. It is kind of sad because people take this class for the GPA boost, but he is clearly so passionate about the material he teaches. Highly recommend!

I love professor Burgmann! Although sometimes I do struggle *just a bit!* with staying on track with the lecture because he talks a bit slow, EPS 116 with him was rather enjoyable. The labs could be a bit tough at times but GSI is helpful as well. The field trip was fun although rally cold - lol. He is so kind and funny it was a great experience.

Such an AMAZING professor. Super passionate and sweet and accessible, weekly quizzes/assignments were easy and only had few live lectures but mostly had to attend a section with TA/GSIs only once a week. As long as you study the study guide you'll do fine for the exams. There are few readings and the lectures are straightfoward and chill

Though Professor Burgmann is very kind and passionate about earthquakes, the structure of his class is very bad and I would not recommend to take his course. The grading bins are 95% or higher is an A, which is pretty insane. There are at least 2 quizzes per week, which, although are short, require a great deal of effort and lecture note taking.

Burgmann is a great professor. Lectures were via zoom and recorded in case you couldn't make it. Additionally, the guest lectures made it fun. Around two online quizzes every week and a writing assignment about every other week. Professor is kind and cares. Grading is balanced well and no one area seems to be able to tank grades if you do bad.
Is not accommodating

Fantastic, sweet professor! Prof Burgmann is very caring and passionate about not just the topic, but making sure students understand how they can use what they learn to protect themselves and their loved ones in the event of an earthquake. There wasn't too much work and the staff is caring and lenient. I truly enjoyed this class!
sweetest guy ever and very passionate about earthquakes. genuinely cares a lot abt his students and def one of the best breadths to take

EPS C20 - He is very kind and super easy to get in touch with! Always open to have a conversation and super lenient. You learn a lot in this course. What you learned is shown through the weekly assignments which discussion sections help with. GSIs are also super nice and approachable. Very passionate about course

I took EPS 20 to fulfill my breadth, and I'm glad I took this class with Burgmann. This class is literally an easy A, I can't believe I got an A+ in it. He has students watch pre-recorded lectures and we occasionally have live lectures. If STEM is not your best area, TAKE THIS CLASS!! It is an easy grade to complete your breadth and boost your GPA.
Professor Roland is by far the most amazing, interesting professor I have taken. This class is very informative and easy to pass if you attend lecture and complete the weekly assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Super easy class and really nice professor! Lots of assignments that feel like high school work but are kind of fun to do. I found the lectures interesting and he was really accommodating during covid. Great physical science breadth.

Professor Burgmann was one of my favorite profs! He was really genuine and cared about all of his students. Lectures could get a little boring (1 1/2 hours) but he broke them up with earthquake music videos/other videos. His exams are very fair/easy if you go to class and review slides/major concepts before the exam. He offers good extra credit too

Kinda of just a simple professor. Attempts to make the topic of Earthquakes interesting, but loses luster really quick. You can tell that he is really kind and wants to be there for students, but unfortunately the subject matter is left to be desired.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: What a good guy! You can tell he's passionate about earthquakes and seismology and truly loves what he does, which is incredible and inspiring to see in people these days. He puts in a lot of effort for his students and tries to keep it as interesting as possible and updates with announcements. Thank you for a great class Professor Burgmann!!

Professor Burgmann is one of my favorite professors at UC Berkeley. I love his subtle sense of humor, the way he talks, his accent, and the way he gives lectures. He always makes sure to keep his lectures light and engaging with real-world examples, videos, animation, and demos. Burgmann is also extremely organized and reliable.

Hands down best elective I've had. Has a monotone voice, but is somehow not boring in lectures. Wonderful demos and videos. Solid foundational understanding of how sound and music works from a physical sense. Virtually no math knowledge needed. Short (~5 pages) readings assigned twice a week. Two "group" projects (can be solo). Highly recommend.

The class is manageable, attendance is not mandatory, and homework is easy and graded on completion. If you pay close attention in lecture, you'll do well on the quiz midterms. Lectures have fun demos/practice problems, and Terry often reviews material. There's 1-2 homeworks weekly, 2 projects, 3 midterms, and 1 final, all of which are fairly easy.

i went to maybe 6 classes the whole year, still did pretty well watching the lectures online. it's not very difficult as long as you take it seriously, but there's a lot of elementary level physics that make you want to just breeze past the course content if you already know some stuff. project 1 i got marked down for not enough physics

I took this class not knowing what to expect and I REALLY enjoyed this class! The lectures are super interesting and all of the concepts build on each other which helps with comprehension. Lots of fun demos in class. I attended almost every lecture (they are recorded too) and did well on the quizzes despite the quizzes being pretty hard

Super engaging and encourages questions during the lectures. Cracks a few jokes here and there and provides lots of examples/demos. The lectures are always recorded so you don't always have to go. 3 midterms, 1-2 weekly readings + 2Q quizzes that are completion based only, and then ofc a final.
The in-lecture demos for this class are really cool. It's an easy breadth class. Assignments aren't too difficult. Terry is caring and funny.

I took this class for a breadth requirement expecting it to be relatively easy. However, the lectures tend to be really monotone and boring with hardly anyone showing up. The quiz content was not actually taught in class since everything we "learned" was random video demos with little to no explanation. Quizzes are HARD!!
Really cool in class demos!

I loved this class with Terry. It was an amazing respite to my days of other stresses. I learned so much from it that I still use to this day, whether directly connected to music or not. I remember learning about the stacking of waves of footsteps on a bridge, I remember all the simulations and visual diagrams. I learned SO MUCH. Highly recommend.

Tests are pretty tricky and significantly harder than the homework (hw is graded on completion). The 2 projects give your grade some padding in case you do badly on the tests. Generous grading bins. Demos help you visualize some of the more difficult concepts. Don't fall behind and make sure to deeply understand all concepts & you'll do fine.

Terry clearly cares about this subject and his students. He gives generous curves and is almost always accessible outside of class. He explains tough topics thoroughly & gives fun demos. Homework is SO easy but beware of the quizzes. They are tough and I feel he doesn't prepare you adequately for them. Overall, great prof & a fun class.

Physics classes should have great demos, and Terry pulls out some really awesome demos. An excellent course to introduce broad physical concepts, not just corresponding to music. Course contribution projects were extremely fun to dive into a niche topic.

He's a cool guy and he seems to care a lot about what he teaches. This was meant to be an easy-ish class; while the quizzes and tests could get pretty tricky/difficult, just don't underestimate them and you'll be okay. Easy homework and two major participation projects (they take some effort but are open-ended). SUPER generous grading bins.

had terry for the summer of covid, so learning over zoom was hard but terry was very understanding. his class is not easy and exams can be quite difficult. work hard and do workbook!! terry is a great prof and answers questions thoroughly!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Took this class thinking it was an easy A .wrong. I wouldn't say it's easy. The quizzes are actually kind of hard and tricky sometimes so make sure to actually study for them. Attendance and homework counts towards grade. As an individual, Terry is very kind and caring to students.

Terry was a great professor and the subject matter was fascinating! He was very accessible and fun to talk to during office hours. He even dabbles with hypnotism and showed us some cool tricks during OH. Do the workbook to do well on the tests. Absolute must. My GSI was amazing and I highly recommend going to all discussions. Textbook not helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The lectures tend to be dry and uninspirational although the material is very interesting, which has in part to do with the fact that a different professor designed the class. The homework is very easy (gets graded on completion), but the quizzes are quite difficult! There's a generous curve though; as long as you do the work and try, you get an A.

Took this in the summer. Terry's lectures are extremely clear and examples are really helpful. He's always available for questions after class (checks in office hour room multiple times a day). His tests are not easy, but really fair if you study(Definitely do workbook!). We had another HW system, which helped so much more than masteringphysics.

Pretty good lecturer. I definitely suggest going to lecture because the concepts he explains are very very useful for tests.  Tests are meh. Very tricky at times, requires you to really think. Only bad thing is he doesn't post many practice tests at all. Only one per test. You really gotta force understand why things work in this class to do okay.

Buehler is clear in teachings, goes through trends in formulas, and uses various examples and diagrams.  Always go to his lectures. The tests that he writes are fair and do not use outrageous situations. Just remember to do the mock midterms he posts, review the Mastering Physics, and understand the workbook problems.

I actually had Terry as a GSI while taking Prof Jacobsen's class, and he is definitely one of the best teachers/GSIs I have ever had. He always made sure everyone was on track; he made sure everyone understood the physical concepts, which then made applying them a cinch. I would highly recommend taking him because you will learn A LOT!
Clear lectures, explained difficult concepts at an elementary level.  Multiple choice questions on exams are tricky, designed to set the curve to where he wants it to be.  WOOIIIREE

Lectures are clear but deceptively simple. Prides himself on tripping up students on exams (aims for a 65 average), so doesn't give much information toward exam success in lectures. Homework seems to be unrelated to either lectures or exams.  Book is useless. Has some language/spelling issues.  Makes for unclear,ambiguous questions and answers.
He is a pretty good lecturer. His tests are extremely difficult. He loves to put multiple choice questions which are very tricky. Going to office hours helps a lot for homework.

He is a very difficult teacher.  His lectures consist of blazing through example problems one by one until the class ends.  He really needs to learn more teaching techniques.  Its difficult to keep up with his speed, so come to class prepared!  I would not take his class again.

Buehler loves to put "qualitative" questions on the midterms to separate the normal people from the geniuses. He believes that there can't be a class that's full of geniuses. The non-multiple choice portions were pretty fair. Awesome demos. He's helpful in office hours. The final was hard but you learn a lot and he teaches torque really well.

His lectures are very clear & organized, but are much simplier than what he puts on hw and exam problems- which makes the class hard. He loves conceptuals problems & multiple choice, so you really need to understand the material not just memorize formulas. But he is very helpful in office hours and encourages asking questions.
No Comments
I love his Tommy Bahama wardrobe.  Those silk shirts must be priceless!

Great lecturer, explained everything clearly, has a good sense of humor, neat demos, engaging, fat, bald...exams were fairly difficult. does not rely heavily upon the book, although reading it is still a must. very friendly, helpful prof.

Tests are unreasonably hard but he is a relatively good lecturer.  If you want to read the book and skip the class like you would for a normal physics class forget it take another teacher.  If you want to do well on the test do HIS stuff (questions, past-tests etc).
overall, a great teacher.  his teaching methods definitely worked for me, put things in the most basic and easy to understand terms.  funny.

He did an exceptional job, especially considering the circumstances with which he was handed the class.  It probably helps that he's truly a great teacher.  Like others have said, he emphasizes concepts.  Understand the sample tests he posts!
good.. learning with fun

Book problems weren't really helpful for his tests. Make sure you understand the CONCEPTS! CONCEPTS! CONCEPTS! Don't always just expect to remember the formulas and get an A--he expects more than that. His wording for the exams can be tricky. Try to understand what the problem is stating, figure out the concepts and then think of formulas!
Great professor!!!!
EXCELLENT lecturer, very fair grader, tip: study CONCEPTS & watch out for tricky exam questions!
One of the best professors I've had in my 3 years here. Clear and concise.
Above average lectures considering the material.  Straightforward teaching.  Tests are average.

I LOVE THIS CLASS! By FAR the best professor I've had at Cal(insanely intelligent). They push you to work hard, but it's still easy to do well in the class. They avoid long lectures and encourage discussion and participation. They are funny and genuinely care about the students. I was actually excited to do readings and assignments. 11/10
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Will is an awesome person and prof! This class was fun, engaging, and definitely presented a novel perspective. Lots of reading but super interesting books that could be a leisure-read - the ones that are more avant-garde & difficult are discussed in detail in class. They also provide really helpful guiding questions if you're struggling.

TAKE THIS CLASS. Will's amazing, the readings are interesting, no midterms. Instead, just take-home quizzes or take-home essays(u get to choose between the quiz route or essay route. PARTICIPATE, read like half of each reading, and you're gonna get an A. Great class to fulfill a breadth! 

 French43A was fr my favorite class, maybe ever. Take it!
They're a great professor. Very rigorous literature class and you learn a lot. The grading was strict but fair. Would definitely recommend for anyone who's into literature!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: WILL IS AMAZING. I would send every freshman student to their class if I could. They are such a genuine and caring person and is so helpful in explaining topics that may be confusing. I dropped in to their office hours once and left in TEARS just inspired by how passionate they are. If that isn't enough to convince you, I'm not sure what will.

Will is incredibly understanding (especially when it comes to dsp) and a fantastic lecturer. The books are really interesting and always relevant to class. However they can be fairly judge-y without trying to. Though they would never say so, you can tell when you don't give the interpretation they want, for example.

This was the first tme PS136J was offered at Berk- and I hope it's not the last. This class was an amazing PS expierence for me, and I'm so grateful for the grants that allowed us to have field trips, sewing expirences, poster presentations, guest lectures, and more! Def Reccomend!

Oh my god, the course is 138J. It just started.I honestly thought this class would be good,but in all my years at Berkeley,she's the only professor I'vemet who completely reads off a script for the entire lecture. At this point, it's not even a lecture but a monotonous audiobook recordingor a poem.I guess we'llseehowitgoesuntiltheend, butthisisbad.

I Took her Political Science in fashion class and it was such an amazing course I loved attending it every week, and even though it was a 1 unit class it still opened up my eyes to the political side of the clothes we were in our everyday lives.

From 2016. Cares a lot about the students and has a lot of insider knowledge of the field, especially of interesting construction techniques and issues around Japanese architects. Great site visits and fun group projects that uses the wood and metal shop. Hosts group lunches at the faculty club to get to know her students better, so sign up early!
Worst professor i've had. Grading system is confusing and unnecessary. makes it super hard to get an A in the class. psychological torture
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dana Buntrock takes pleasure in embarrassing her students in front of others, is extremely hierarchical in her teaching approach (she picks favorites, and screw everyone else) and is a miserable person.  It's an incredible negative mark on UC Berkeley that she still teaches there.

Worst professor I've had during my entire college career. She humiliates students in the middle of class, changes class requirements whenever she feels like it, and generally has no regard for student's time, budgets, or safety. Assigned us projects involving power tools during a semester on Zoom, when most of us have never been trained for safety.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Very caring and experienced.
reviews.rating_tags: GROUP PROJECTS--Skip class? You won't pass.--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Dana will use any conflict you have as a chance to learn. You should engage with her, she's a valuable resource.
great instructor !!
Great class, one of the best professors I've ever had.
avoid.
No Comments
No Comments

I'm not sure why there are so many negative reviews for Prof Bunge, this was one of my favorite classes I took at Cal! She is very knowledgeable and passionate about the subject she teaches, and answered all my questions happily. I finished this class with an A, and all of the material you are tested on can be found in her slides. Just study hard!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof Bunge is obviously very knowledgable about neuroscience but that is her only strength as a professor. She is disorganized, glazes past important info, and makes students feel stupid for not having the same expertise she does when they ask questions (her tone is so rude). My GSI was the reason I learned anything. would not recommend.

Professor Bunge obviously loves what she does, and it can be intimidating to attend her lectures because she just knows so much. I'm not a psychology major, and I just put an honest effort into the class, and she (plus the really kind GSIs) made me feel like that effort was worth it. Definitely read the textbook before lecture, though!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Bunge's class was interesting! We had 3 final exam 2-page each essay, 2 short essay question midterms, and 2 tricky MC quizzes. The 1st midterm was a bit rough since the course staff was trying to find out best way to administer it, but 2nd one went much better with also the option to do an EC question. You could also get 4% EC from RPP.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Cannot recommend this class ANY less. She speeds through the lecture + deliberately shames people that ask questions/ clarifications. Grading is unfair & extremely specific when essay questions are vague + confusing. Even mc quizzes have abysmal averages. Do your future self a favor & fill the biopsych req any other way. RUN!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Interesting material that prof was clearly very passionate about. Also very responsive and quickly answers any questions posted online. however, we were not given a lot of time for tests and the prof didn't seem too opened to change. Overall however, a very resilient teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Absolutely horrible professor. Extremely unorganized and everything is constantly up in the air. I have never gotten so many emails with daily changes from one course in my life. Tests are impossible as there is not enough time allocated for them. She is super unprofessional and does not care for students, and has never responded to an email.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Avoid this prof at all costs- worst teacher ever had at cal. Is nice enough to provide textbook though it is very difficult to read because of formatting and structure. Often dismisses students and their needs, claiming to have taught for over 20 years. Lack of any awareness of assignments, tests are extremely fast and unnecessarily difficult.

The worst professor I have had at UC Berkeley (rude!). She often does not explain things clearly, and the lecture is disorganized. You may not get the grade you deserve because her grading policy is not fair.

Class structure/modules are extremely organized, but I agree with the students below. The textbook reading is technically her textbook draft, the exams are very rushed, and she glosses over questions asked in lecture (which leads to even more confusion). Maybe it's different in an in-person semester, but this is not suited well for online.

Lectures are all over the place, she skims seemingly random topics and says "I wish I could go more into depth about this but we're running out of time." Every class is rushed. Prof doesn't know how to answer questions yet boasts about her connections and research which don't get me wrong is cool itself, but I don't think she should be a professor.

Agree with the students below. I do not think this class was adapted well for the online modality. Complex concepts are not explained well in lecture and there is a miscommunication between what material the student should learn themselves.

As previous student mentioned, she seems to be all over the place. She doesn't elaborate in her lecture and basically reads off of the slides. Her study guide was just us writing bunch of random questions about the material. And whenever students ask question during lecture, she is often not sure how to answer them.

I think she is doing a very poor job teaching in the online setting. Her lectures are incredibly scrambled, she goes so fast and glazes over things that she claims should be background info. She tests on complex readings which she doesn't cover at all. The study guide was written by students and she didn't review it until the morning of the exam.

Prof Bunge is very knowledgeable, approachable, and sharp. The class had an experimental feel to it, because she was trying out new exams. That messed me up a little. She was very understanding though and allowed us many different opportunities to help us out.  I like her. She could be more organized, but the material was interesting.

She taught in the style of an "absentee landlord". While busy with conferences and other professional duties, Prof. Bunge was present for maybe half of our lectures, using guest lecturers for the rest. This, is conjunction with offering vague guidelines for exams, papers, and projects, left me with the feeling of being a lab rat in an experiment.
Prof. Bunge did a very nice job presenting cutting edge literature about the developmental brain. It was a treat to attend lecture. She was also very fair with grades, if not a bit too generous.

I thought this was a fairly easy but rather interesting course. Yes, the topics were broad but Prof. Bunge did a good job integrating the material in the last third of the course. Section was not greatly helpful; it was a venue for student presentations the entire semester instead of reviewing material. If you pay attention it's an easy A.

The course material was very interesting, although the topics are broad. Professor Bunge was very helpful during office hours, providing additional explanation about lecture content and answers to any other questions about the material. Recommend the course if you'd like to learn about dev. psych from a broad perspective and read recent studies.

One of my favorite courses at Cal. Bunge was very engaging during lecture and went into detail on many topics, which was great because it really helps you see the big picture. Just go to class and listen closely, it's so interesting it should be easy! Guest lecturers-eh.

This was an extremely interesting class and covered a broad range of topics, all relating to the development of the brain. As long as you attend lectures and take notes, the exams will be pretty straightforward. Reading is not necessary.
one of the best professors in Berkeley!

There were many discrepancies between teacher and GSI about deadlines and requirements, sometimes changing things the week something was due (frustrating if you like to do work ahead of time!) Section never reviewed lecture and we didn't spend more than one lecture on a topic. Far too many topics and far too much work but everything was interesting

Professor Bunge is a great professor, very knowledgable and enthusiastic. The class structure is different from other courses at Cal and requires integrating information from different topics learned in class. It is not difficult; if you are interested in the material you should have no problem with the course.

Yes, the course is challenging, but it's a college level developing brain course- what would you expect? It's true that the slides were not much help, but as long as you're in lecture and paying attention, you should have no problem. I learned most from this course because it wasn't about regurgitating info, it was about thinking critically.

I personally enjoyed this course greatly and it was one of those courses that made me feel that working hard was truly worth it. I don't understand what the raters below are saying as the course was not difficult if you worked hard. It's definitely not an easy A. The empirical studies were what made the class more interesting and easily applicable.

Professor Bunge is extremely knowledgeable and passionate about psychology and neuroscience, which is inspiring. However, I think she would be better off as just a researcher, because her lectures were difficult to follow and switched topics at random, the slides gave little information, and the classes were largely based on previous studies done.

This class was extremely interesting and has inspired me for grad school research! I think this class should be a seminar because it is conducted very much like a grad course. Simply memorizing the material will not suffice- must think critically and read harder articles. Do not take if you don't have a solid background in biological psychology!

Words cannot describe how frustrated I am by this class as a whole. All this class is about is complex empirical studies, even though the professor does not explain everything thoroughly and does not make herself available enough outside of class(you can only sign up to talk to her in 15 min. intervals. The reading is more dense empirical studies.

I am really disappointed with the way this class has turned out. There is no textbook to refer to, and lectures pull material from dozens of empirical studies with absolutely no background information given on the slides, which makes it incredibly frustrating to try to study for exams. We're supposed to write the textbook as a "Wiki Project." Ugh.

She will surprise the class at the end by rewarding one homework assignment as extra credit. Be sure to attend office hours for your presentation and  participate as much as you can even if the questions are dumb. She talks too quickly, but she is very knowledgeable. She has more ratings at the UCD ratemyprofessors.
he is great i loved taking his class

Interesting material and Duncan clearly has a strong grasp of the material but he clearly does not care about student feedback and the course structure is horrid and unfair. There are easier ways to learn these topics without dealing with a professor who is so thoroughly out of touch.

He genuinely cared so deeply about the experience of the students and was constantly offering constructive feedback on the final project. The GSI and him both were regularly available to go over concepts and homework questions in depth. I hadn't taken d100 or d8, but he provides async lectures for the coding concepts which made the class easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Callaway is passionate, caring, and good humored. His OH are great if you go with questions. While the class starts slowly, you should read the textbook to really understand later lectures. ER131 overlaps DATA100 but with much fewer people and a final project. How much you care about your project determines how much you get out of the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: I enjoyed Prehistoric agriculture. Byrne focuses on understanding patterns and the explanations for those trends rather than simply relating facts. This approach makes the course much more intellectually stimulating. For written exams, understand and elaborate on concepts using key examples. Know some archaeological sites and specific domesticates.

I really loved biogeography. I enjoyed all of Byrne's nuanced ideas about past climate and vegetation patterns. Make sure to come to class and pay attention during lectures. Focus  more on understanding the concepts than rote memorization...just know key examples for the exams. Roger Byrne is a great  teacher and a kind person.

Professor Byrne is a boring lecturer who is kind in the sense that he wants his students to do well. I wanted to get an easy A for a breadth and this turned out to be the hardest class of the semester. He makes physical geography way too complicated and beyond the scope of the class. A must NOT take class.

I fell asleep everyday in this class but got an A. So with studying you should pass no problem, but you will have to survive the boredom of 3 hrs of dry lecture a week (if you aren't interested in glaciers and clouds). Labs are easy & tests/quizzes aren't too hard either. The lectures also are a hard to follow... resulting in unpreventable sleep)

A really nice professor. He genuinely wants his students to do well in his class. Midterm had a very generous curve. My only compliants were that he does not tell you what will appear on the exams and that the lectures sometimes seemed a bit disjointed. Other than that, class was pretty good.

Byrne is a real gentleman. He really loves what he does, and he truly cares about his students. One of the rarest types of professors in a school driven only by people who want their name in a journal or win a prize. The school would be a better place with more Byrne's. His lectures were not the most clear, but just follow it really hard.
He's quiet, uses lots of slides about small stuff so bring glasses or sit close.  Pretty good.  Don't really have to go to class to pass.

Byrne is a nice older gentleman who has a genuine passion for his occasionally dry subject matter.  You'll get the most out of this class (biogeography) if you're majoring in this area and have an interest in plant species and the ancient history of climate change.  Tests come from the lecture notes.

Decent teacher, likeable guy. Course was fairly interesting and useful. One annoying tendency: He likes to save main point & important info for very end of lecture, just as students are packing up to leave for next class, then dumps it on them all at once as everyone scrambles to get it down in their notebooks. Pace it, Dude. Pace it.

Byrne is a very smart, knowledgeable man; he looks just like your grandfather would if he went on safari.  he obviously understands and loves the material, but i had a hard time liking it.  the class can be tough, but the first quiz is meant to scare people into pass/fail.

Byrne's classes are easy if you come to class and take notes. His exams are based almost entirely off of lecture material. This is not a class that you can skip class and then catch up by reading the text. If you aren't interested in the subject matter, however, his classes will probably be pretty painful.
OMG..this i hated going to classs...it was soo boring and the professor lectured as though someone though his jokes were funny..DON'T DO IT

First lecture was boring (intro lesson), but everything after that has been super interesting; I'm learning lots in this course. Greg does speak a bit monotonously, but the way he lectures is very engaging and at times funny. His presentation of historical facts makes it seem like I'm listening to someone "spill tea", making me not fall asleep.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: The class was at 8am T,Th. Attendance was not mandatory but there were weekly pop quizzes on the readings, so if you were not at class or showed up late, you would fail the quiz. The assignment for Greg's part of the class was fairly straightforward but the graders were vague sometimes on point deductioins

Expect a lecture going over different buildings in his PowerPoints. He is pretty monotone so its hard to stay awake if its an 8am class. I hated the pop quizzes on the readings because they were so early in class skimming the reading wasn't enough--and they were the only form of attendance. The final "museum exhibition" is time-consuming.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Castillo is a kind and brilliant lecturer. His lectures were extremely interesting and piqued my interest even during the 8 am class! I highly recommend attending his office hours.
He is an amazing lecturer. His class was very interesting. Read, attend and all shall be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Interesting intro class to architecture, urban planning, and environmental design in different places and times. A lot of lecturing from slides but minimal tests/quizzes and so the class time isn't stressful. Case studies are good for an intro lower div but also it's going for breadth rather than depth. Still neat and I found it fun and engaging.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed this class.  Ist half: lectures by Castillo, more historical, graded on several quizzes, responses to guest lectures, and social justice poster midterm.  2nd half: lectures by Pol Matamoros, more theoretical, graded on weekly reading responses and graphic novel final.  Wish 2nd half had preceded 1st.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class is taught alongside a GSI that's equally as boring (Pol Matamoros). Castillo turns really interesting lecture material into the most boring thing ever. 6 attendance checks that you can easily do at home if you log on during the start of class. Grading takes forever. 2 creative plus weekly discussion posts. Final was a 500w reflection.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Castillo is such a good professor! The content he teaches is really interesting and he is really approachable (highly recommend meeting with him in office hours). There are just 4 projects (one for each of the three modules and a final paper). He is a great professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very good!
reviews.rating_tags: Inspirational--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Castillo is a great lecture and speaks very passionately. He's very approachable and easy to talk to. ED4A was a fine class to take, just be prepared for the pop quizzes that appear towards the end of each module.

I adored professor Hesse. I don't know about the other classes that she teaches, but 166B was wild because she just knows literally everything. I had pages of notes every day. I'm not even really interested in more modern or political history but she got me completely hooked. Devastated I probably can't take another class with her. But difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment:
it is hard to catch what is being taught in the lecture
and the lectures are boring
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Hesse is very knowledgeable and inspiring. Her lectures were in depth and my only complaint would be that it is hard to copy the notes down because she goes fast. There are 2 essays, a midterm, and my final was online. The midterm was very difficult from what I remember, but it was a formatting issue and not her fault! I loved this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: While the instructor seems kind and well-intentioned, I found little value in the lectures and discussion sections. Had attendance not been required, I likely would have chosen not to participate in either.

Almost impossible to recover if you missed a day in class as nothing is recorded and the slides were vague. Readings are interesting but pile up very quickly (reading a book + other works in one week). Interesting course and essay questions but grading sometimes felt like a hit or a miss.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Pretty good lecturer. Used slides with minimal text and no textbook so be ready to engage with the lectures and take good notes. Wish there was more structure to the course but otherwise learned a lot.

Amazing professor, lectures are clear and easy to understand. You do need to attend lectures and take notes as important contents are only said in lectures and you won't understand the slides without attending lectures, which are enjoyable if you are intested in the period.

Prof. Hesse is an amazing lecturer. The way her lecturers function is that she provides slides and you take the notes down (this is always the pattern). Be attentive because she teaches somewhat quickly. If you want to pass the class with an A then I recommend understanding her notes more than the books you are assigned; comprehension is key.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I love Prof. Hesse's lectures and her thoughts. The class is very intellectually exciting, and Prof. Hesse's lecture style is a mixture of serious analysis and dark humor, which I find incredibly French. One of my favorite classes at Berkeley.

Hesse is great. Her lectures really manage to make renaissance history interesting, surprisingly. The class layout is super clear; two lectures a week, readings to go with it, a 250 word discussion post along with discussion once a week. Sometimes the readings were difficult but my GSI was great and was very helpful in getting us to understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She teaches well and is very good at grading
She is great and her lectures are super easy to understand. She distills information down in a super easy to understand way.

Loved her, she is genuinely one of the best professors I have had at berkeley. Her lectures make sense, it's very applying heavy and less proof based, and her tests were very manageable. Highly recommend if you have to take math 53

Exams and quizzes were very similar to the textbook problems.  If you do the homework , the tests should be super easy.  Provided practice tests that were very similar to the actual tests. You can self teach the material by reading the textbook, watching videos online, or using her detailed lecture notes. Gave super easy 20% EC on midterm 2.
The GOAT!!!

Solid choice for 53! Weekly quizzes were fairly easy and homework is graded off of completion. The practice tests were very similar to the actual tests, which made studying easier. Straightforward lecture notes and overall very organized class. Includes fun animal pictures in the notes :)

Failed math 53 with Norman, took it with Prof Canic and I feel like i genuinely came to understand the most difficult topics like divergence/stokes/green because of how well she would simplify things and would have very clear notes on. Exams were very fair, practice exams were accurate. one of my favorite professors so far. very caring

Generally considered the best for Math 53, your grade is mainly determined by tests (3 exams = 80%) but they are very similar to textbook problems, her lectures are alright but the course itself is very self teachable if you find the right resources :)
Great professor!

Professor Canic was fantastic and explained concepts clearly with really well-written notes and was very caring! Exams were very reasonable and gave extra credit! Please take her some of the ratings on here are not valid.

Canic is the best! A lot of homework but it helps with tests. Really cares about students and the topic she teaches. Tests are fairly simple if you come to class/read notes(which are very good) and complete homework. Take Canic!

Suncica Canic is the absolute sweetest, most caring, and interesting professor at UC Berkeley. Her lectures always made sense and she would make sure that the class didn't have questions before moving on. Math 53 in general is difficult but she makes it so much more enjoyable to learn.
Very competent instructor. Great lecture notes and straightforward exams. Generally she's considered the best for 53

Rushed through the arguably hardest parts of the course in Stokes/Greens/Divergence theorems at the end and made them a large part of the final. Your experience in this course is very dependent on whoever ends up as your GSI. She's okay at teaching the content when she's there, although it definitely looks like she'd rather be somewhere else...

Decent prof. Lectures were weren't too helpful, but homework assignments were well-designed to help students master the material. Easy exams, but grade bins were quite high as a result, making it difficult to get a good grade. Also can be quite rude and passive aggressive when responding to questions during lecture.

Sshe does not know how to lecture at all. She just reads from the textbook and explains nothing. From past reviews I expected her to be somewhat easy but the test averages were around 70% so I'm not sure why so many people claimed that her tests were easy. Anyways if you take this class expect to teach yourself 100% of the material.

Prof Canic is a decent lecturer. Material best learned through both textbook and lecture recording. Weekly high volume HW graded by completion not correctness. 

However, exams are too easy: mean is low 70s but SD is ~20, so distribution is bimodal. Getting an A requires not making silly mistakes. My overall 94 was likely close to cutoff for A-.

Lectures weren't very helpful: you're much better off reading the textbook. Quite a lot of homework but it prepares you well. Weekly discussion quizzes are fairly straightforward if you're on top of the material. Midterms and final are the majority of your grade. Overall not a bad choice for 53

Lectures covered content more or less and she always stopped to answer any questions. Not many resources outside of class but going to discussion section frequently was helpful. Midterm 1 and the Final were very difficult (64% and 59% mean respectively) but Midterm 2 was fine. LOTS of homework at the start of the semester but got better later on.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Fair final and midterms that account for most of your grade. There is quite a bit of homework, but it is very helpful -- the tests and quizzes shouldn't be too difficult if you stay on top of the homework. The lectures I thought weren't that helpful, reading the textbook is more helpful than going to lecture, which is pretty slow.
Mediocre lecturer, would just slowly go through practice problems without really explaining the concepts in depth. Also tests were too easy.

Canic is super hands off, she basically just lectures and the head GSI handles everything else. Lectures are standard and she goes through proofs and examples but doesn't really explain in depth. Still would say the best 53 prof though. She's nice and will always stop for questions as well.

She lectures very slow but that's not necessarily a bad thing. Midterms were so easy. Final was hard. There was no Edstem or communication platform whatsoever. If you had questions, you either had to email the head GSI (pretty sure he always had an influx of emails) or ask her right after lecture. Otherwise, not bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Does not update the grade until the end of the semester. Everything is so unorganized. Every single lecture recording is titled lecture 2 except lecture 1.(Again she need to learn organization) She is good lecturer, as long as you don't fall asleep... which is very difficult. You only need to turn in you homework once a week which is good.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor! Amazing lecture notes and straightforward exams!

Can't lecture to save her life! Progresses at a snail's pace through even the simplest example problems in class, fixating on insignificant details while glossing over important definitions and theorems. Ambiguous grading criteria and displays passive-aggressive behavior towards students. Awful professor! Definitely wouldn't recommend.

Prof Canic has good lectures and she's a good person, but she's test heavy with tests that don't even match with the difficulty of homework. She either made our mean score or her other section's around 60/100 and rotates it around sections. She also doesn't give clear final grading guidelines even though most people are expecting a C-.
Canic is a good professor. Her midterms are short and straightforward. Her lectures are very informative and follow the textbook pretty closely. Likes to prioritize understanding.
Love her as a person, and she is sometimes silly, HOWEVER she makes learning so difficult. Her lectures aren't useful when none of her notes/problems are done live.

Not the most entertaining lecturer, but she cares about her students. Exams were same level as homework problems, so I'd say they were pretty fair. She posts all her lecture notes which are clear and easy to understand. By all means, she's definitely not a bad professor.
Not an accommodating professor, I had an emergency and she still gave me a 0 on the final! Unbelievable!

Canic is a good professor, but too easy. Her tests are very short and straightforward, but this causes the gradebin cutoffs to be high with a very big STD, with lower AVGs. Despite this, her lectures are very informative and teach proofs to help provide an intuitive understanding. Although, her class can put you to sleep if you're already tired.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Worst professor I've ever had. Tests are 6 questions each and are worth three quarters of your grade. Going to lecture is pointless, as she slowly goes through proofs rather than showing us how to actually approach her problems. She was inaccessible outside of lecture and was randomly rude over email. She kinda just does whatever she wants. :/

She doesn't care about her students and won't even reply to emails after a certain point regarding grade issues. She just does what she wants. I've never posted here before but she gave me the worst experience I've ever had at berkeley by just ignoring me when I had problems.

I never go back and leave reviews, but for this one I needed to. She assigned way too much homework, and her lectures were so disorganized. Her practice tests were nothing like the real deal, and her grading criteria was ruthless. I was a B+ calculus student before this, and this class has absolutely taken a toll on me. Save yourself and avoid.

She explains concepts through examples in detail, and her notes are well-organized. Homework took a long time to finish, but it did help you prepare for the exams a lot. The practice exams she provided reflected the difficulty of the actual exams. This course with her is easy as long as you understand questions on hw and practice exams imo.
I really do love and appreciate Canic. I think Professor Canic is awesome. She has awesome notes and reasonable tests.

Canic's lecture made challenging concepts easy to understand and she solved a lot of practice problems. She is a caring person but her exams were extremely difficult (practice exams were very misleading). Be prepared to work hard in this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I really liked Prof. Canic. Her lectures made difficult concepts approachable. She explains things in a simple manner, straightforwardly, and thoroughly. I cannot ask more for a math professor. Her lecture content is well-organized (posts lecture notes that serve as an outline), and she always includes example questions that are important to know.

Toughest grader ever. Tests vary drastically in difficulty. Untruthful about the difficulty. Release trivial practice then an insane exam. Unclear rubrics. Graphing problems require computer level precision. Missing nonessential steps cost you 50% of a question, and yet A cutoff is absurdly high. and much more much worse (StopDueToWordLimit) AVOID!

too much homework, graded by completion. the lectures often had unclear explanations, and I lost focus often. the homework really didn't support the course, and the final exam was absolutely nothing like the midterms/practice final. i was a B+ calculus student before this, and this course was absolutely demoralising.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Canic's teaching style was unfortunately not for me, I really struggled to pay attention. Tests were worth 80% and the tons of homework (60-70 problems) were only worth 10% of our grade. The part that made this class unreasonably difficult was her insisting on NOT curving. In a pandemic. Borderline cruel in my opinion.

Canic is extremely straightforward with her lectures, other than random animal pics which she includes as transitions. Midterms were almost the exact same as homework problems given, but the final was rough. Quizzes in class vary in difficulty greatly based on which GSI you have. Overall, pretty easy if you try.

The exams were a bit tricky but the homework and quizzes really prepare you well. Her lectures are easy to follow and she does a really good job publishing the recordings and notes on time in case you miss the lecture or want to revisit them. The class was really fast paced but you're gonna get a fast paced class with any multi class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Lectures followed the book very closely, given live and recordings posted. Exams were a bit tricky but the grading was generous. Really caring professor. If you learn math through thorough explanations and lots of examples then she is the prof for you. She also has emojis and pictures of animals dispersed throughout her lecture notes which is fun!

Decent professor for Math 53. Its not an easy class but she made it manageable - homework was heavy but graded P/NP. Shes new at Berkeley, so she was still getting used to the pace of class here. Tried not to rush but she had to towards the end. MT2 and final were almost the same as practice exams though, A was 95%.

Decent lectures, but monotonous and goes too slowly at times. You're better off reading the textbook and lecture notes (which are directly copied from the book) instead of attending. Exams for MATH53 F2019 were ridiculously easy (i.e. same as practice with different numbers). Caring and nice, but needs to work on organizing courses better.

She's an alright lecturer, and can be funny at times. As with any other math class, most learning will occur in discussion, so make sure you get a competent GSI. She writes easy exams which resulted in a horrible curve. In future semesters, she will probably write harder ones.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Grade really depended on you showing up and as long as you did that you'd basically know everything for the midterm. you'll also be super well prepared by the sandbox activities. lectures are fun and interesting! definitely one of the best professors at Cal!

Not my typical style of preferred teaching but cant deny the easiness of the course. Things may likely change as she switched up her style recently. Class material was in person and only on paper. Exams were based on logical thinking on what we went over in lecture. Lectures tended to drag but overall professor was kind and caring

I LOVE PROF KIDD !!! no homework, show up to class, take the midterms (took me avg 15-30 min easiest midterms i've ever taken and is based on the sandbox activities) if i could propose to a prof i would propose to her.

Prof Kidd is the kindest professor! Her lectures are clear and engaging, and her work is inspirational. No HW, readings or finals. 3 exams. Pay attention in class and section and you will excel. She inspires her students to pursue research and helps students get information of future work in the field of psychology. I highly recommend this class!

prob the sweetest prof at ucb. she is very caring and preps students for gradschool stuff. however, sometimes it was difficult to understand some of her concepts. experimental confounds. look that up b4 u get into her class lol. otherwise, this class is so interesting, and there is no hw! only like a lecture question during lecture

I loved Prof. Kidd. She really taught me how to critically think and not blindly trust everything around me. I loved her lectures and how helpful she was about navigating academia. The grading policy was a little messy this semester (it worked out in the end) but it was obvious how much she cared for her students. She is a true inspiration!

I'm usually a straight-A student, but this class has affected my grades. The lectures did not adequately teach us how to conduct research, which was necessary for the assignments. Communication is lacking. They often promise to email us but fail to do so in a timely manner, if at all. The long wait leaves no opportunity for improvement.

The professor says that the class is designed so that students don't get stressed, but they are very harsh on grading. Sixty percent of your grade depends on assignments that are graded quite harshly. The rubrics are very unclear, and absences aren't excused, even in cases of emergency.

Although this class seems easy at first with a simple grading basis, assignments are graded really harsh and grades for the assignment are available only a month after the deadline. The GSIs are really hard to get a hold of as well.

Professor Kidd is the nicest professor I've ever had. She truly cares about what she does and she is extremely accommodating. The exams were optional that you can do for extra credit. There were no additional readings outside of class. Super straightforward weekly assignments that you can do as long as you go to class.

Easy material, no textbook needed and no readings outside class. One of my most laid back classes at Cal. Celeste is an extremely caring professor and great to talk to outside of class. I would take another class with her in a heartbeat.
Awesome professor, easy class, cares about what she does

Took ESPM 131. The lectures were filled with information that was not tested which I personally dislike. She's a nice professor I just didn't think the exams were very fair. Exams are also extremely long and are almost all paragraph responses required. Points are marked off for missing small details which would be fine if given more time.

pro pallud is great! clearly very passionate about soils and knows a lot about them. really encourages student qstns. spring '24 was behind in lectures for the entire sem but she cut some material out for the final, bless. heavy on the paying attn in class LMAO. tests are tricky and hmwk is a bit challenging (graded a bit harshly by TA).

Professor Pallud is extremely knowledgeable and I highly recommend this class for ESPM students as well as students looking for an elective outside their major. Homeworks are very doable but still are somewhat challenging and rewarding. Tests are based on lectures and readings. Expectations are clear and you will learn a lot about soils!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Pallud knows a lot about soil and will give you a great introduction to the topic. The lectures are very text-heavy so make sure that you take notes, but if you have questions she always takes time to make sure students understand. GSI did most of the grading. Very understanding and knowledgeable.

I took romanticism with Professor Langan, and it was tough. However, she was more than happy to give me extra time after class or during office hours to clear up any questions I had, and she was always willing to help with my essays. My advice would be to just participate in class and try to connect with the professor as much as possible.

Definitely a professor that's not for everyone. I loved her class and the readings, but the lectures can meander. I found that there was always an interesting takeaway to her lectures, though, if I stayed focused all the way through. She offers extra credit-- I would highly recommend taking up the offer; it's fun and rewarding.

Her lectures were a chore to attend. They felt disorganized and boring. What should have been a really interesting class became my least favorite class. You can tell she's really passionate about the subject though.

Professor Langan's brilliant mind will transform the way you approach life & literature. Out with the trite, trodden road of binaries, poetics, and relatability. Philosophy-heavy, her lectures introduce new ways of knowing and conceptualizing language. Show up to class & definitely attend OH. She makes it a point to get to know you personally.

interesting class but assignment guidelines were convoluted and hard to understand. claimed course was built to be accessible but was resistant to granting extensions even when listed on DSP letter. i submitted all assignments, got a high B and an A on midterm and final, but still only got a B in the class. glad i took it but would not take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Assignments so convoluted even the TA admitted they couldn't understand them. Didn't post discussion post or attendence grades on Canvas. I thought I had a strong A but I received an A- and its a mystery as to why. Doesn't respond to emails, extremely critical and condescending. Lectures are a bore, unaccomodating and passive aggressive. Horrible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I haShe was defintily a teacher where it was "Her way or the Highway." Inaccesible outside of class. I  found it odd how in a class on Disability her lecutre slides, assingment critera, and prompts, were extremely poor. It was a long block of text. This class should have been super interesting, but her style of eaching made it a bad experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: WORST Professor. Lecture's were so boring because she read off of slides that were diorganized and cluttured. Inaccescible outside of class, and an abhorrent attendence policy. Strict with grading and was often incredibly discouraging and negative. Horrible all around. I got an A in this class out of sheer luck but would not recommend or take again
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The class was disorganized from start to finish. The opposite of online-savy, the slides were often hard to read and cluttered with large text blocks in small font. Lots of readings that were out-of-date and inconsequential to the course subject. I wouldn't recommend this professor to my worst enemy.

Professor Langan is challenging, but it motivated to critically think more about the text. I loved the readings and I fell in love with Romanticism. Her lectures are a bit disorganized and unfinished, but they changed the way I look at the readings. Difficult with grading but visit her at OH where she gives good feedback. Take her for a challenge!

Prof. Langan was very kind and easily accessible outside of class. Due to seminar style of class there weren't really set lectures and mostly student discussions, but Langan always had interesting insights to direct conversations. Very helpful in OH, I found papers were graded fairly and if you need help go to her!

Enjoyed taking a small seminar-style class with her. Reading was often light, especially for an English class. Student contribution to discussions could get dry, but the professor always had lots to add. She's funny and so energetic, as well as kind and understanding of extenuating circumstances. She's eager to help with essays, go to office hours!

Skimmed most of the material and did well. Lots of EC opportunities but I didn't take them. Attendance is mandatory but no homework: optional presentation, 2 small writing assignments, 2 papers (1 final). As long as you write it ahead of time and get feedback(albeit harsh), you'll do well. She is also a fun lecturer, and very understanding.

She is very knowledgeable in Romantic poetry but she tried to make that genre fit into a class on disability studies and it did not work. I can't speak for her as a prof in her area of study but would not recommend this class with her as the instructor. I wish we read more authors with disabilities... in a class on disability. Bad experience.

My favorite professor at Cal.  She's not "easy" and is more interested in leading you to the water than she is in telling you how to drink, but the experience was great.  I had her for the Honors Thesis and for 45B and loved both classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: A kind and wonderful professor, but hard. Very hard. Lectures are disorganized. She tries to squeeze in 5 hours of material into an hour and a half. It's helpful to see her in office hours. She'll take the time to make sure you understand the material. Essays are graded hard, but if you see her beforehand you can get a clear idea on criteria.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I loved her class! Prof. Langan is brilliant and I thought her lectures were thorough and helpful. (She posts her powerpoints online for the final so that's extremely helpful!) She is accessible and gives great feedback. Make sure you try to keep up with the reading and do the reading responses!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Lectures are impenetrably incomprehensible with a tenuous connection to any specific literary texts.  Her presentation makes Fredric Jameson appear a model of clarity and concision.  Extremely condescending to students, in all interactions, and her grading is brutal and punishing.  Brilliant but certifiable--take her only if it is unavoidable!

She's very funny and humorous and tries to make her lectures engaging, but they're extremely dense and difficult to keep us. Her PowerPoints are extremely dense and difficult to keep up with taking notes (and I take notes on a laptop). The reading assignments are long, dense, and also very difficult to keep up with. Her grading is brutal.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I didn't mind her at first but greatly disliked her after a Danish girl got yelled at and embarrassed for asking a question about affirmative action. She asked "is that where if there's a tie, they pick the minority?" And Langan began raising her voice and  insinuating that girl was a racist. It was so wrong. Not becoming of an educator.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: There are times when the assignments can be confusing as hell but she is very willing to help. I read a LOT in her class but I throughly enjoyed it ALL and will probably be keeping on my bookshelf for years to come. All in all great professor who has much to offer, that may tangle in lecture sometimes, but lead you to be a better thinker and writer

This one day she walked into lecture and started reading Lamia, by Keats. In the middle, when she gets to the part about shedding her snake skin, Prof Langan was reading aloud and literally started unbuttoning her dress. She took it off (thankfully there was another one underneath)and then proceeded to show us her bra. Brilliant, but insane

Lectures were extremely confusing and abstract. Would rarely engage the students during lecture: instead, she literally read off of an essay she probably wrote the night before. Great ideas but presented poorly and hard to grasp. Never actually got around to the point of lecture until about the halfway mark, then would almost always run out of time

Had Langan years ago for both 121 and a 150 senior seminar in transatlantic romanticism.  She was brilliant, helpful, and funny--and also more than willing to admit what she didn't know (which wasn't much!).  In 150, she was open to student ideas and happy to explain her own.  In 121, there's little opportunity to question her.  Go to office hours.

I'm angry about this class. Her lectures were almost entirely useless far too often, owing to the sort of post-structuralist style which she imperfectly employs, leaving the student with too few handles to grasp. The student, of course, will be graded as though he or she should have grasped her lectures with perfect clarity.

Very brilliant, VERY scattered. Never finished lectures on time & left me feeling like there was so much more she would never get to cover. Do the reading before class & come to every class or your grade will suffer. Lots of assessments--3 short papers, 1 long paper, final--but final + final paper pretty much determines grade. Not enough novels!
