Prof. Langan was delightful and engaging in her lectures. I found myself struggling a bit to keep up with her rushed pace in class, but all material was intriguing and thought provoking. She usually ran out of time at the end, but this just proves her brilliance, exuberance. intimidating, but very helpful in OHs. demanding, but worthwhile

very strange lady. lectures sometimes boring and extremely abstract and hard to follow. I left the class more curious about the poets we covered than knowledgeable of them, which may  or may not be a positive.
My biggest gripe about this professor is that her lectures rarely featured close readings, just a lot generalities that were never convincingly anchored to the text(s). Caveat emptor.

Had Prof Langan for English Honors several years ago.  Critical theory.  If you really wish to take advantage of this class, you had best do intensive reading of critical theory well before you take her class, or (like others here have pointed out) you will surely be lost trying to follow her lectures.  Take the class and explore!

When I first started her class I was completely lost. Her lecture style is intense and often hard to follow. However, I found that in office hours she is more than willing to explain things in depth to make sure you really get what she is saying.
Lectures were interesting and engaging.  Tests/papers representative of what was discussed in class.

While I will admit that Prof. Langan is brilliant, however it's like she lectures out of a lit theory book written in a language only she understands. Works for some, not for me. Never got a response to the email I sent asking to set up a time outside of her office hours to talk about what I didn't get. She seemed really nice just not helpful.
The most passionate teacher I have yet encountered. Challenging, brilliant, and witty.

She is brilliant, true, but entirely incomprehensible.  I felt like I needed a dictionary beside me through all of her lectures, in order to gloss every other word.  Rather boring, as well.  Probably better in upper div classes.

Langan is truly brillant. She has so many interesting ideas that sometimes it's hard to keep up in class.She is very helpful during office hours, and overall I learned so much and I would recommend people to take her!
Langan is the BEST OF ALL
Langan is brilliant

Like clockwork, Prof Langan blew my mind 5 times every week.  I'm not sure why some of the naysayers took a lit class (especially Romantics), but Langan is the perfect professor to teach the era...she's as crazy-brilliant as any of those guys were, and she can actually put it all together.
Of all the many brilliant professors that I have encountered throughout my academic career, she was by far the most brilliant.
One of my favorite classes and professors. She sparked my love of Romantic Lit I retain to this day.

She brings the subject matter to life.  I really liked her, but the class was difficult, so if youre just looking for an easy A this is not the right class for you.  She is however a great resourse and if you are willing to put in the work you'll do okay.
super smart and fun!

I dropped the class because of her.. her thought patterns are erratic, and her " revelations" are expressed in a long stream of thought right when all of us are rushing to get to our next class. Plus, she entertains moronic answers way too much.

She's a very energetic and brilliant professor. Her lectures are always so full of content that it's hard not to get a cramp in your hand from taking rapid notes, but you WANT to write down what she's saying because she has much expertise to share. Also her passion for the material is encouraging.

Prof. Langan knows there isn't one answer out there. Her lecture style is based on asking the right questions and often the conclusions she comes up with are abstract ideas. She is the 1st prof. ive had that tries to incorporate/ understand students perspectives during lecture. She's got zero Ego.
Extremely boring, abstract and unclear lectures. Bring coffee if you want to stay awake. If I were grading a paper she wrote, I would scribble "Clarify!" all over it.

She even describes herself a cross between a grandmother and Big Bird. Ridiuculous "formalist" lectures are a waste of time. Like reading 1K+ Bleak House by Dickens to spend two weeks talking about the names of the characters. Don't take at all costs.
Professor Langan is brilliant, but very demanding.  Her style of teaching is not for everyone, but she is a very dedicated teacher who is always willing to help her students.
No Comments
the worst. pretntious, boring, sadistic.
Abstract, unclear and boring lectures.  Ditzy professor.
very unclear, rambling lectures with showy literary theory put in. save your money.
This class is so boring, you are sure to fall asleep... eventually, you will stop going

Despite other reviews, I enjoyed this class and Prof Saravia; she's a very kind and knowledgable professor.  Her lecture style may not be everyone's favorite but she gives a substantial amount of material/practice problems to review and records her lectures as well.  I did not find this course very hard whereas I thought other econ upper-divs were
Pretty bad at lecturing but much better during office hours and clearly knows her stuff. Class was decently easy as long as you understand all concepts discussed.

This class was bad in so many ways. First of all, the professor was extremely confusing in her lectures and did not explain things well. Secondly, there is no curve, even though the average on the first midterm was a D. Thirdly, almost your entire grade is based on exams. I've never had a class where so much of my grade is based on exams. Beware.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor is rough. Not a great lecturer, she understands the course material but has a difficult time teaching it. Also one of the GSI was not very involved. Attendance is graded. Difficult exams, get ready for the GPA drop taking this course.

Poor class organization comes to mind, for it seemed there was no coordination GSI and professor. Five planned problem sets turned to four after time ran out, the midterm took over a month to grade, and there has been a terribly confusing and disorganized b-courses page to find review material. I'd never recommend this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: It took almost two months for our first midterm to be graded and over a month for our second midterm to be graded. They released the grades one day after the final P/NP deadline. The grades are not inputted into bCourses (only on Gradescope) so you don't know your grade in the class. The professor is very confusing and unorganized. Don't take this.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class is so difficult and exams are majority of ur grade. Exam scores don't come out till dead week so even if you are doing bad in the class you cannot drop before the final so you will fail the class. Exams are graded tough. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS AT ANY COST
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was extremely difficult and the grading policy was very confusing/strange. Over 80% of your grade is made up of exams. While we haven't taken the final yet, the midterms were extremely difficult and graded harshly. The professor did not explain clearly and the topics way were more confusing than they needed to be. It was unfair.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Extremely difficult to follow lectures but there is mandatory attendance (never heard of this in an econ class). Tests are a higher percentage of the grade than other econ classes and they are extremely difficult. Doesn't release grade bins so difficult to gauge performance. Honestly this class feels unfair.

I could tell Professor Saravia knew what she was talking about but I don't think she really knew how to teach efficiently. Her lectures were very hard to follow and she would lose her train of thought very often, which confused a lot of students. The class was almost based entirely on exams and there were no real assignments. Would not take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: lecture slides were tough to understand... prof just read the slides and wrote the problems on the board, a lot of students said they didn't understand what she was trying to convey. Midterm is very hard, 80% of the grades are from exams

Lectures were interesting and introduced me to a few topics I had never heard of. Midterm was straightforward if you studied well and in advance for it because there is A LOT of content. I felt there could have been less coding assignments but it was still manageable and the GSI responded quickly. Takes time to learn everyone's names!!

Sure she's fine but as a professor? You're better off taking another course. GSI was also not good and lacked being a leader for the coding assignments. Cecilia gave boring lectures & hypothetical analytical questions to which she expected perfect responses. Overall, do not take this class. Midterm, Final, Coding, and group project? Ha, stay away.

Take literally any other Political Science course. The information presented throughout lectures is redundant, resulting in a halt in the consumption of any new knowledge since Week 5 of the course. There are 5 CODING assignments assigned throughout the semester ???, a midterm that left me questioning my sanity, a group project, and a final exam.

Dr. Mo It's actually a good proffessor. However, do not expect an easy course, if you want to learn and  have the opportunity to connect with other people in the field than take her class; but if not than don't complain about her being a bad proffessor. *Heavy load work * Readings * Group projects

I would not recommend this course; very data-heavy for some reason and has unreasonable expectations for what students are capable of. Exams are in person with no notes allowed. Truly take any other political science course at Berkeley and save the stress.

Professor Mo is an OK instructor but the forced participation made this class a bit weird. Also, the class is WAY too hypothetical and unlikely to be applied in real life, so I felt like this class is quite useless. But as a general Ed class would suffice.

While we cover a vast amount of writings within the seminar, Prof Giscombe is great at explaining topics and facilitating discussions that are relevant to what we've read. He's very easy to approach and clearly knows what he's talking about, while also being funny. Do the readings, ask questions, and you will do great!
Really great guy. Learned a lot in his class.
Very sweet guy. Knows a lot about poetry and literature, but he's also very willing to chat about other things, even in class. I learned quite a bit about poetry and thoroughly enjoyed the class.

His teaching has greatly improved my writing because he allowed me to think differently and helped expand my creative vision whenever we reviewed my work. His classes focus on discussion which allowed my work to be critiqued by many people rather than just one which I found helped avoid biases. He's immensely kind and accessible outside of class.

Professor Giscombe was amazing at teaching me how to improve my writing without being bias. Creative writing is difficult to teach, yet he had a great teaching method by asking me questions about my incomplete works that inspired the writer in me rather than making his own suggestions that dull creativity.

He was one of my favorite teachers at Berkeley, really taught me how to think differently and encouraged me more than anyone else had. I recommend him highly and suggest taking advantage of office hours!

As a person, he is lovely. As a teacher, I found him interesting, but often biased and unclear about his expectations of our work. Work is reviewed workshop style, which isn't for the faint at heart. He randomly changes the syllabus and frequently doesn't let you know due dates/readings until the day before. Huge confusion on grading criteria.

Ultimately a waste of time.  Class was scattered - or "free form" - to the point of being incoherent, and feedback on essays was of little help.  (Much of it amounted to whether or not he liked the essay.)  He is so into his own aesthetic preferences that he does not seem open to anything outside of that.  Would not take again.

Great guy to hang around with, lots of interesting anecdotes.  But when he's leading a workshop or reading your poetry, you'll find he has a definite aesthetic bias, which he'll try to thrust upon you.  After a while, it can get annoying.
Commentary on poems isn't very helpful.  Has his own poetic gospel he tries to force on his students.  Not much order to his lectures.  Really nice guy, though.

Giscombe is great. Teaching style is loose, which is most complimentary to a discussion style class. Provides very helpful constructive criticism on written work, and genuinely cares about his students. Glad this guy is at Berkeley, he's an original and an asset to the school for his intellectual vibrancy.

Great guy, fun to talk to.  Fosters an inviting atmosphere for discussion.  Has a good sense for what works and what doesn't in a poem.  In his verse class, he talks more about reading poems than writing poems, which bothered me.  Also, the class was *extremely* scattered.

IIf you want to take a class where you learn absolutely nothing and are just confused the whole time, then she is your best option. She is the worst professor I have taken in my entire educational career. Please, whatever you do, steer away from her. She is completely unprofessional and does not care about her students.
Have a good relationship with her, she is very knowledgeable, but you have to ask her questions. Very nice person!

Celia is an amazing professor. I learned so much from her and the class was taught very well. It is also very easy to communicate with her. On a personal side note, if you are interested in social justice, she is a great to her talk. She drops gems of knowledge every single class, to the point where you don't want to miss a class.

Class is pretty straightforward. She might come across as a "mess", but she actually just has a really open curriculum so the students create the class. Not meant for students who are assimilated in academia and expect everything to be given to them.

Celia is one of the best professor's I've ever had. She dedicates time to students on an individual level, and cares deeply for our spiritual, mental, and physical health. While some may be frustrated with her style, it is usually those that are used to a more rigid, hierarchical structure. She is all about communal learning. She changed my life.

AVOID LIKE THE PLAGUE! Celia's teaching style is a mess. The woman was everywhere and yet we went no where in the class. The class meetings consisted of random tangents and ramblings that were hard to follow and irrelevant to the class materials. Readings were never discussed and assignments were never clear. The whole class was a headache. AYYYYYY

The professor himself is very nice and loves to teach has a good heart. BUT the GSI is insane hard with the exams. Two tests so far that are so heavy and not enough time to answer all questions. He does a review 2 days before the test, so you have little time. So, math heavy it is more of a math class. If I have to retake, won't choose him.
very nice person

This review is for UGBA 104, but there is no option to put that. This class is very Excel-dependent. There is homework every week, and at times it is difficult; tests are on paper, even though all the homework and stuff we learned in class was online. There is no practice exam, so you are guessing what you have to do and know for the exams. curves

by far one of the best professors at haas for core classes. very fair and clear about what he expects students to know. his slides are just *chefs kiss* for reviewing because he puts *everything* on there

prof has carried me in three classes thus far: as a gsi in microecon, as my current prof in 104, and in his youtube videos for macro. amazing
Really great class, the lectures are concise and to the point. Need a lot of background knowledge. i highly recommend this professor.

Actually I took the UGBA96 course and Cholera was a fantastic professor who really wanted us students to learn something new and were willing to help out our questions.He encouraged us to dig deeper into the programing and use data anaylysis in real business issues.Thanks so much for preparing wonderful class! Nicest professor I've ever met!

This course is about Data and Decisions and Professor Kunal is very good at this subject! He is patient and introduces basic concepts little by little from life examples. He will mix a lot of humor and happy elements in the class to make everyone learn more actively. Besides, He often asks us about our situation to adjust the speed of the lecture.

I go to his GSI discussions to learn better and work on practice problems to prepare for the exams. He is so kind and takes time to explain things that are confusing. He also creates YouTube videos for us on the textbook chapters, it is very useful and he went above and beyond expectations. I'm planning to take his UGBA 104 lecture in Fall!

I really love his discussion sessions for microeconomics. Definitely a caring and knowledgeable lecturer, really informed of the subject. Will be taking his UGBA 104 next semester, and I am really looking forward to it.
Greatest of All Time physics prof, wish I was locked in enough to fully benefit from his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor lectures very well, and presents the concepts in a way that deliberately builds up intuition. He provides an abundance of external resources as well as posting recorded lectures. His homework sets are didactic and not time-consuming, and his exams are designed to tests your knowledge rather than your ability to calculate

Chien-i is the best lecturer I have ever had (no glaze). Very clear on what to expect on exams, and grading is fair. Homework is light with a weekly extended deadline with plenty of optional problems for those that want more  practice. Amazing lecture notes, I never even opened the textbook. If I could give 6/5 rating I would, I miss u so much king

Chien-I is a great professor! He doesn't give too much work but assigns many optional problems if you want more practice. He's a good lecturer, doesn't go too fast or slow, and answers questions well. His tests are hard but are of the fairest I've ever taken. They cover things that you would expect to be tested on and his grading is generous. :)

Great lecturer, genuinely interested in topics. Did rush through lecture, but provided lecture notes (very helpful, study those). Also read griffths if you have time (didn't read it but heard it was helpful). Late policy on hw w/no deductions, only 3 hw problems/wk (more if u want to practice). Exams are hard bc its physics, study *derivations*

Deserves his praise. His lectures felt a little rushed and he scrambled to get through all the content, but his lecture notes were very accessible and genuinely the best notes I've read. His grading was a little harsh but it is physics. Great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of the most engaging profs I've had so far. However, he seems to fall behind schedule quite frequently and the end of class/semester is rushed. He provides his own lecture notes; be sure to read and understand/memorize them to do well on exams. Only assigns 3 HW problems weekly but provides plenty of additional practice problems to study from.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: I had him for 137A and liked it a lot, but 110A was definitely less fun, though still good. This might be because I don't find EM interesting, but I felt like a fair amount of the intuition in the latter half of the class was lost, and everything just became math at a point. Still really great person and overall good lecturer as well.

Not a bad professor, but I have some issues. He makes mistakes in derivations at times, lectures are poorly paced (often rushing the bulk of content in the last 5-10 minutes), and exams are notably harder than the practice ones he gives & sometimes include topics he specifically tells us not to worry about knowing (virtual images on the final...)

Nice guy but exams are hard. Heavy on derivations that would be cool as HW problems but not so much in a timed environment. It's over for you if you don't perform well on the final worth over 40% of your grade. The practice exams he gave out were also a lot easier than the actual ones. HW is helpful and the late policy is chill. Just read griffiths
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great lecturer! Very easy to understand and clearly knows a lot about the material. Textbook does not follow the class to a tee but he gives you the sections he covers in class. Has a grace period of 4 days on homework and hw load is overall very reasonable. 1 midterm and final were hard but expected for the level of the class.
He's honestly not very good at teaching but his classes are straightforward. You know what you're getting with him and self-studying outside of class helps!

I've taken 3 classes with him at this point. He has a tendency to write exam that are incredibly confusing, either because the topic is very advanced/briefly covered, or because the question was worded poorly. Strangely, his exam questions pre-2024 were much more straightforward.
Very mediocre
🐐 Undisputed GOAT of the Physics Department.

The exams were fine, but having homework be 30% of your grade is a bit unfair. Missing a homework is equivalent to losing 10% on an exam, since I imagine that the homework average is now close to 100% with chatgpt.

Amazing prof! I took his 137A over the summer. He approaches QM from a pretty theoretical angle and really works to build up the linear algebra and classical mechanics formalism needed to understand what makes QM special. His lecture notes were amazingly detailed and neat, honestly better than the textbook. HW was short and easy, and so were exams.

Very good lectures, the teaching style is very well structured and clear. The exams tested a lot on derivations of topics. The professor is friendly and helpful with very fast response rate. And the notes that professor wrote really made a lot of the materials/topics much easier to understand.
Chien-I is a wonderful instructor! His lectures and lecture notes are organized in a very CLEAR manner. His tests are hard, and be prepared to write mathematical derivations for physics purposes.

Chien-I is abundantly clear about his expectations for his students. Lectures and accompanying course notes are very easy to follow, which helps with the difficulty of the course. Exams are fair and taken directly from lecture and course notes.

Great lecturer, short and (usually) quick hw. One of the few professors in the department who is transparent with grading and releases histograms. Very fair exams as well. Only complaint is that the section on spin and angular momentum was pretty rushed, so less time could be spent on classical mechanics, even though it was good for intuition.

I don't know why he got bad reviews! I'm an EECS major graduating this Fall, never took QM before, and he made me love physics. His lectures are clear, rigorous, and inspiring. One of the smartest and kindest professors I've ever had. I would commute daily from Sacramento for 9:40am class out of pure love for his lectures never didthatforanyother.
Probably one of the worst physics profs here

As a rising junior in physics at Berkeley, I just wanted to point out Chien-I's 112 was one of the most well-taught physics classes I've ever had. Lectures were mostly clear. Thermodynamics and stat mech as it is formulated in undergrad textbooks is hard to stand, but that's really not the fault of the professor.

This professor actually makes tests so that the questions are so much harder to process and understand what they are even asking for. It uses many, many complex terms that 99% of anybody would not know the definition of only for it to not matter within the context of the problem. Be careful with this class.

He's a good professor, got sidelined a bit by thermo, but covered everything pretty well. His written notes are great for review and its clear he put effort into them. This was his first time teaching 112, so he had some hiccups, but given his track record, he will definitely get better. Notwithstanding, he was a good lecturer and a fair examiner.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took 110A and 112 with him and loved both classes. I like that he focuses on derivations because it helped me connect physics with the math. His exams are reasonable, again focused on derivations, and the homework is so doable but the class isn't easy so I feel like I learned. He's extremely helpful during office hours and fun to talk to as well.
Just a bad lecturer. Very disappointing class

I took many classes with him and I really enjoyed his classes. Yes the classes weren't easy well because its Berkeley Physics, but you actually learn in this class. Yes he goes derivations mostly, but i think its helpful because it really helps to understand how to approach the problems. He is great lecturer and you learn a lot of math too
I usually don't leave reviews on here but this class was actually so bad

His lecturing style was so bad, he just rambled the whole time, no structure, hard to understand the material. We barely covered stat mech since most of the semester was spent on thermo, and the computational assignments were terrible.
This was actually the worst physics class i have ever taken here! Have taken him before tho and he's usually not this awful
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Sloppy, disorganized, poor lectures and horribly designed computational assignments. Course structure was also very poor, as all relevant stat mech was rushed in last 3 weeks of the semester with most of the semester spent on classical thermo? Do not to take him for 112!

Prof. Chiang focuses mostly on proofs. His exams are mostly inline with the homework. Do the extra homework problems as they will probably assist with the exam, sometimes parts show up. The computational ( computer computation) part of the course was horrible. Parts of the assignments instructions were not clear at times, and not put together well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures were mediocre, very math heavy with little to no insight. But easy homework and chill exams if you like memorization
Very abstract teaching style, which made it very hard for me to understand the topic in the first half. Other than that, amazing lectures, HWs are useful, and tests are fair. Good class.

Great and passionate professor. The only reason he isn't getting a higher rating is because he gave the worst designed final exam I have ever seen. 5 of the 6 problems were connected, making it extremely difficult to skip ahead if you get stuck. His lectures are extremely computation heavy but it really helps in understanding the math.
All the classic things he is known for (3 problem psets, heavy derivation on exams) were a breath of fresh air and made the course super manageable. Good lectures, even better lecture notes.
Great guy!!!!
Professor Chiang is a phenomenal lecturer and assigns a good amount of homework. His tests are fair and he shares wonderful lecture notes that elaborate on lectures done in class.

Great lecturer: records lectures and posts detailed lecture notes for things not in the textbook. Has regularly scheduled office hours. Cheerful w/ good sense of humor. Psets have just 3 required and some optional problems. Insists students know the "why" beyond how to do problems, so exams are derivation-focused. Teaches all the math at sem start.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: One of the nicest professors I've ever had. Homeworks are maybe too short and lectures can be disorganized, and his exams are very difficult. Final included topics we hadn't had practice problems on.

Chiang is a great professor that is generous with partial credit on tests and is super accessible during office hours. However, that is balanced out by how the tests are quite difficult, a major factor being how he requires you to know derivations unlike a lot of other physics professors (At least from what I've heard from my Physics 7B professor).

Genuinely wants the best for students & is a generously fair grader. Tests are extremely proof-heavy, requiring high math skill/intuition, but application-based questions are easier than other professors. Will give a very solid foundation, but IMO emphasis on concepts over application may be too much for a class designed for non-physics majors.

Chien-I has amazing boardwork and truly goes out of his way to support students. Be warned though, his class tends to be more proof/math/derivation heavy than what most people are used to. Overall very enjoyable.

He seems like a super nice person and a very fair grader, but I mostly pieced together the material myself from high school physics notes and the textbook since the lectures were pretty boring and sometimes unclear.
Very caring about students. Strongly lays emphasis on derivations. Read the lecture notes and solve the problem sets carefully. Questions on exams are similar to those.

Prof. Chiang is good at structuring lectures. His class is more proof/derivation heavy than some other professors but I think that it's ultimately a helpful framework. His tests are reasonable and he has a really great attitude towards learning.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very good Professor, I had never taken physics before and he made the concepts very accessible. Lectures were easy to follow, clearly organized, and mostly helpful, found myself looking at notes more than the textbook. Very understanding and, towards the end of the semester, easy with grades. Very nice person.

Professor Chiang is very approachable. He explains the course concepts very clearly and expects students to know the equations (helpful in understanding the foundation of physics). The difficulties of his tests match those of the assigned homework and optional practice problems. You can get a good grade if you put effort into his class.
nice professor, good teaching energy. only thing to beware of is very heavy emphasis on proofs/derivations, especially on tests so make sure you have them down. otherwise, very nice guy.

Great professor, really makes sure you understand the fundamentals in any field of physics. Exams are always either variations of homework problems or textbook examples, or otherwise inspired by them. Really nice guy, pretty caring and accessible outside of class too.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Absolutely amazing professor; lectures are extremely clear and his board-work is amazing. Publishes his lecture notes which are detailed and explain all concepts clearly. Homework isn't too long but very useful in understanding the concept and there are many optional problems. Exams are tough but fair and the curve is forgiving.

Most difficult class I've ever taken, but that likely has more to do with the nature of the material than the professor. The class was HEAVILY curved because of the difficulty of his exams. But he's a fair grader. If math isn't your strong suit, look elsewhere. The entire class is algebra and trigonometry manipulations.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He is everything you need in a professor. He is organized and clear about what he requires in the class. The tests emphasized material from the lecture notes, which are very helpful.

While 110A is hell, it is not because of Chien-I. He really cares about the students and tries to make our lives easier. His lectures are crystal clear. The content however is very hard and challenging. No matter the professor, this class is not for the feint of heart - but Chien-I makes it a little bit better.
His lectures are clear, useful, and interesting. He is down-to-earth and fair with grading and tests. What more to ask for?

Prof. Chien is a really nice professor. He responds quickly and thoroughly to emails and his office hours are great. Physics is difficult regardless of the professor, but Prof. Chien clearly tries to make the subject as clear as possible. His note packets are especially useful. He is very lenient with MasteringPhysics which is a big plus.

Lectures aren't super useful, but he follows Griffiths very very closely. Problem sets are short and don't teach much if you don't do extra textbook problems. Exams are almost more focused on random math than course content. Unclear grading criteria. Might've been different if it was in-person, but I wouldn't retake the class I got this semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof. Chen made the very daunting Organic Chemistry II one of my favorite classes at Cal. His lectures were lucid and he is extremely encouraging and supportive when answering questions. I would be delighted to have him as my professor for any chemistry class again.
Good lecturer, but definitely wrote tough exams!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Had such an awesome experience and made me actually like chemistry. Connects well with students and makes sure you're understanding the material. Best class at Berkeley so far!
Had him for 3b/3bl. Very clear lectures that are easy to understand and puts in a LOTTT of effort to help students succeed. Really willing to answer questions and made me like organic chemistry!

Leo is one of the best professors I've ever had at Berkeley. Super engaging and really helpful. He was also generous with grading as needed, so as long as you consistently went to office hours, did problem sets, and worked through post-lecture WSs, you were set. Sometimes exam questions could be quite difficult/weird, though, so keep that in mind.

Great professor. His exams were fair. Just do the work he asks you to do. Do the optional problem sets in addition to PLWS. Professor was very generous with participation credit and plws assignment credit. Only got around half of the plws credit and attended only half the lectures, but still got full participation credit. Extra credit available too
Really strong knowledge, good at guiding you on how to solve problems! Pretty good grade distribution and very willing to help students.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Clear explanations, patient teacher, and covered a lot of content in a concise way, even though he's not an official lecturer that I know of. Would recommend

one of the worst professors i have ever had at Berkeley. does not listen to students and had to rely on the GSIs to teach me. he would have GSIs teach us sometimes in class and it made way more sense when they did. it was his first semester teaching and i wish i didn't take it this summer and just waited for robak or marsden.
Good lectures, writes confusing exam questions
He is not an honest man.

Professor Citrin is a wonderful man.  He has amazing things to say and really cares about his students.  He is funny and very knowledgeable.  However his lectures were at 9:30 am and his voice always lulled me to sleep so it was hard to focus.  He is incredibly intelligent but not very animated so it's a little bit difficult to stay engaged.

Very boring lectures with a lot of material and no explanation as to what was actually required to know. Lots of reading and dependence on the GSI. 10 page essay at the end of the semester. Without a passion for government, this class is rough.
I never went to class because he drones on about topics that you aren't even tested on. The GSI was the one that actually taught us anything.

Professor Citrin is one of the nicest professors I have encountered. He really loves American politics and will help his students any way he can. He assigns a lot of reading, but his tests and essay prompts are very straightforward. I enjoyed the class, however it  was a little dull at times, especially if you took  AP Government in high school.
Great prof. Knows the material. High standards, but willing to help.

Lectures were long and somewhat confusing with overly lengthy and poorly organized powerpoints. Definitely learned a lot about American politics but felt it was in a very haphazard way. Assigns way too much reading for a lower div class, a lot of which is unnecessary. Midterm was alright, final was very difficult. GSI graded pretty tough.
Boring lectures and essays are graded really hardly. The final was very hard and focused a lot on boring lectures that no one went to.
He does not allow laptops. Look through the slides, the tests are mostly based on them. Books weren't used that much and learn the terms made up by him...
Most disorganized person I have ever met, lecture slides terrible, and the tests are based off them completely

Boring class. Lectures were a slog to get through, poorly organized, and often did not proceed in tandem with the assigned readings (which were totally necessary because lectures were so unsatisfactory). Very dry overall, discussion was really helpful, so getting a good GSI is key. Take it for the PS major requirement I guess, but otherwise not.
Cool Professor; the class is dry though.

Actually pretty funny professor. He is obviously experienced and very knowledgeable on the subject he teaches. Honestly not a very difficult class if you do the readings. The sections that he assign are mandatory, but the lectures are not.

This class is full of non-sense. You will learn what you already know. The materials and the Citrin's terms(named after him) is just made-up terms. totally not worth of taking..  don't waste your units..
Considering the course being pretty common sense, it was a hard class.  You learn about obvious materials made x100 harder.
Very organized. Expectations are clear. Easy to understand what needs to be done to understand the material and do well in the class. Tests and papers are very reasonable.

One of the greats! Took both Poli Psych & Public Opinion with him.  Brands himself as the cranky Andy Rooney type in lecture, but he's really a sweet man and goes out of way to help you if you get to know him 1 on 1. Lectures are perfect balance of funny personal anecdotes & substantive material. Interesting research papers, grading can be tough.

Interesting class but I still recommend sitting in the front to catch everything he says. A little boring. A lot of students thought it was an in-depth AP Gov class. For those of us who didn't take AP Gov, you'll have to play a bit of catch up. 2 big papers. Exams (essay-style) based off readings (good!) AND lecture. Citrin posts slides online.

One of the best teachers I've ever had! Funniest prof by far. Love this man. Made me love the boring subject of politics and really made me see things in a different way. Thank you Citrin! Citrin's law applied before taking his class!

Good: his lectures were pretty entertaining. Not: PS1 might be a different deal but PS164 was strangely difficult. The concepts weren't that hard, but the structure of assignments was really unclear. There was no rubric ahead of time. If you don't say certain "buzz words" on exams, you can get a zero on a question, even if the explanation is right.
Funny, entertaining professor. A little cranky at times, but even that can be kind of hilarious. Tests have a lot of writing. But by the end, you really learn a lot.

So he doesn't use PowerPoint. Big deal. His lectures are interesting and his anecdotes bring the subject to life. Either really good or really bad; definitely slept through a few lectures. Interesting guy. If Clint Eastwood got a PhD, he'd be Citrin. Reading and understanding the book will get you an A, but go to lecture if only for the stories.

He doesn't use powerpoint in his lectures and tends to ramble. He did use an overhead projector to put up some information. Unfortunately, as soon as he put one page up, he would pull it down 30 seconds later, so you couldn't copy it. It was so frustrating! My GSI is the only reason I got an A. She explained everything he confused me about.
Doesn't use powerpoint and just rambles on and on. Its hard to tell what's important and what isn't.

Although he can come off as a little dry at times since he has a nearly flat tone of voice, his lectures are hilarious and interesting. He has a great, sarcastic wit that he threads throughout his lectures. He also tells you almost exactly what he'll test you on the midterm, and gives you a good outline of what the final will look like.

Citrin may know his stuff, but he's not for everyone. To me, he came off as an ass, picking on his students and belittling those who asked for visual aid instead of dry straight-up lecturing. He has a sense of humor, but his lectures were often disorganized and many people stopped attending. A good GSI was essential to my success in this class.

His lectures could be hard to follow because he wasn't always organized and he has a bizarre cadence of speech. Sometimes he said hilarious things and he had cute stories about fighting "the man." The course reader was interesting, but I gave up on the text book after the first week and still got a low A. Having a good GSI is crucial.

Citrin likes to ramble and hates powerpoints. You have to listen intently or else you will miss out which is really hard since all you want to do is sleep through the dry material.  He is a genius and is a great professor, but the content of the course is not for everyone.

Professor Citrin is very intelligent with a sarcastic sense of humor that is very enjoyable. However, lecture is very dull and tedious. He often rambles on (his stories are interesting) with powerpoints he lets you see for about 5 seconds. No laptops so good luck getting everything down. Nice man though and really seems to care about his students.

I love psychology and I love politics, but Citrin really kind of killed it for me.  The readings were super interesting (READ THEM!) but Citrin spends most of his lectures summarizing them and making jokes.  I guess lecture is helpful to understanding the concepts, but I felt like I learned more in section than in lecture (get Matt as your GSI).
Good professor. Flat out told you the questions on the midterm and final. Lectures were boring. Helps to have a fun GSI - (Angelo Gonzales - Amazing). Reading was almost immaterial to the class

Good class, but I felt he based a lot of his teaching on what Huntington thinks. GSI's all seemed great and worked hard for you. You might cry from laughter the first lecture. But through the semester I was only awake when he was telling interesting stories... his lessons were boring for the most part.  Also, all examples involved peanut butter.

Really great class, I learned a lot and enjoyed taking this class. The professor was really straight-forward about what was on the midterm/final but only your GSI  grades your papers, midterm and final and determines your participation grade-- which can leave room to subjectivity. A good, moderately easy class.

Pretty good professor. It can be difficult to pay attention to his lectures and hard to pick out what is important, but he does a quality job of laying out the basics of the American political system. Somehow the class is both boring and funny.
He tries to find the best way to explain all the consepts. He uses the humor to make the class fun, to understand better the material, and to pay more attention to class.

Great professor. He was very knowledgeable about the subject material. He has a lot of amusing anecdotes and witty comments; you could tell he is a seasoned lecturer. Grading for papers in the class (graded by GSIs but he reads some of the papers for grade control) is a bit tough, but very fair. Do not let him catch you talking or coming in late!
do not be late to this class!!! he will make a mockery of you. very enjoyable and worthwhile class :)TONS of readiner-- but you don't have to do all of it!

A great intro to Poli Sci. Lectures are entertaining and very well-organized. Make sure you understand how each concept relates to the larger themes of the course. Citrin outlined the midterm and the final, making them relatively easy and straight forward. His cynical humor is unmatched. I'm now seriously considering being a Poli Sci major!

First off, to the guy who wrote that he has sloppy writing on the chalkboard, there's no chalkboard in Wheeler.  Second, aside from having to use a microphone to talk to the people who were too claustrophobic to sit in the front, his speech was understandable.  He had a good sense of humor, and although the class was a little hardcore, he engaged u
Great professor! Loved his humor and outlined the midterm/final ahead of time.

Omg, best teacher ever! Whoever wrote the comment below mine is an idiot and should have paid attention in class. Citrin's class is not too difficult but it will be if you don't pay attention. He is also easy to talk to. He is hilarious and awesome!
This guy is a ****.  The whole semester I could barely understand what he was saying or read his writing on the chalkboard.  I don't get why everybody loves him.

Hilarious and cynical old man, really knows the material and solidified my choice this major. Gets a bit repetitive towards the end of each class, but his jokes are worth it. Pretty much spells out the midterm material and makes it totally worth going to class. Likes to shout, mock mass comm majors/tardy students, omniscient in NCAA football.

Prof Citrin's clarity really depends on how much sleep he's had the night before and how much he had to drink that day, but this guy knows what he's talking about. He's wonderfully cynical, yet very understanding. The midterm is very straightforward (he tells you what the topics will be EXACTLY) and his essays aren't terrible.

In general a pretty interesting guy. He has his on days and his off days, but he knows what he's talking about. The material is pretty interesting, and he tries to liven in with anecdotes and stories. If you want to take this class, take Citrin. He's a pretty good guy. GSI makes a big difference, though.

Funny professor who clearly outlines the different views on voting behavior and participation. Class is very straight forward with 2 five-page essays, 1 term paper, midterm and final.But he jokingly admits he has a fragile ego so do not read the Daily Cal in class. He embarrased some guy and it was kind of akward. Overall, great professor.

Very knowledgable professor, an asset to the Political Science department. Very prepared/funny/engaging and thoroughly prepares students for exams. And in response to previous posts, he doesn't take too kindly to students showing up late and disturbing his large lecture halls, but he's very kind in office hours and in general.
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments
love citrin. one of the best professors in the ps dept. despite some disorganization, he's really a wonderful guy and great teacher.

Citrin is a great, funny professor! It's true that grading really depends on your GSIs and they can be a bit biased sometimes... but if you talk to Citrin and you have legitimate reasons as to why you want a higher grade, he definitely works with you. He wears a face and acts as if he doesn't care about you but he does! He wants you to succeed.

can be a little unorganized during lecture...his teaching style may be a little bit of a turn off to some students, but if you're interested in the material anyway, it won't make a difference. Midterms and final were fair, as were the papers, but I think that depends more on the GSI's grading style.

I don't see why a lot of people give Citrin good ratings.  He has some good jokes, but he is a bitter old man who doesn't care about his students. The class isn't very hard, but not very easy either. He is a turn off for political science. He may be better than some, but Janos I've heard is good.
If you attend class and get all the lectures, midterm and final should be NO PROBLEM. Has a bit of a temper sometimes, but his lectures give solid information.

funny guy. gives you a very good idea of what is going to be on the test before you actually go to take it. Lectures tended to go longer than scheduled and start late...A fair amount of reading required.

Rambling, messy lecture style, condescending, big and fragile ego (show up late to class and you'll see the mild quaking in the facial muscles!). You won't learn much of great value or depth from taking his class, and he is not receptive to crticism and with questions. Don't bother taking him.
Excellent Professor! Met with him several times in office hours, very encouraging. Looks just like my dad.
This professor is hella cool!
great class, highly recommended.
very intelligent and humorous.  incorporates great stories with lecture. very easy and fair methods of testing

I really liked Professor Citrin..he made Poli Sci as amusing as possible with his stories about drinking and I love the way he poked fun at people! His lectures are straight from the readings and although they may lack a little organization, it's still not hard to understand!
great teacher - funny intelligent and informative.  definitely recommend PS1.

I've taken two classes with him, and I love him!  He's such a riot, and a really great teacher.  Doing well on midterm and final very easy if you attend class...he makes sure you know what is important.  I'd HIGHLY recommend him.

I don't know about the gambling problems...but my GSI keeps telling me stories about drinking...but nonetheless, on top of a very intellegent and systematic style of teaching, he's follows an organized outline...so that makes it easier for you to follow.

this guy is one of the funniest teachers i've ever had! i don't know if he's different during summer sessions, which is when i had him, but he's hugely entertaining while he does actually teach.  the gsi also led pretty productive sessions.

often peppered his disorderly lectures with banter about midday gambling and drinking, as well as facts about how important he is. condescending and hostile toward those who harbor "progressive" political views of any sort.

He has a very funny cynical type of personality.  However his lectures didn't feel very organized, so that could be frustrating while taking notes.  The class got more boring as the semester progressed
No Comments
Witty personality, but very boring voice. Pretty easy and straightforward class. I would reccomend him.

lectures rambling; in reality an economics course; scattered, confusing, dull reading (eg: 70 pages on shipping container history); prepare for two courses' worth of work: learning his cryptic standards and the vastly different, equally unachievable, gsi standards. prof allows gsi team to remain negligent and disorganized.

Prof is passionate and genuine. Tech-free class. Lectures can be boring/confusing. Three midterms are most of the grade and test if you actually understand the authors' arguments, specific details, and can make connections. Do the readings & know ur GSI's expectations. Offered EC. Pretty hard class but learned a lot.

The class is overall SUPER reading heavy (~100 pages per week), and tests are based on them. His lectures aren't always relevant to the readings but (depends on GSI) readings will be gone over extensively in discussion. 3 midterms, no final. Lots of work but I found the readings helpful in understanding economic/societal pressures and changes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Lectures are very dry and they are not recorded. They are often unrelated to what is on the test. The course title "Globalization" doesn't really fit what the course is about. There is a very large amount of weekly reading. Professor does not allow any devices. GSI can make or break your experience in the class, as they are the ones grading exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Chari is very passionate & experienced. Lectures are mostly reading from slides and they are NOT recorded. No laptops/devices are allowed; notes must be handwritten in a notebook. Somewhat heavy weekly readings that are due before discussion section. TIP: ask your GSI what they're looking for on midterms, since your GSI grades all your work.

took class first semester freshman year, having read some of the older rate my prof's, was pretty deceiving. gsi's are awesome, but the lectures are very different week to week. midterms were graded pretty oddly, and you don't see worksheet answers. ended with an a+ bc of the extra credit essay, which is up to 5 whole points.reading heavy

So much reading!!! Lectures are also pretty boring but professor is very passionate and kind. 
There are 5 worksheets 10 questions each and 3 midterms that decide your grade. Do the readings properly, go to office hours, and just do more practice for midterm questions and worksheet questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Be prepare to listen and connect cross lectures, the key point is about connections between all the materials. is intelectually heavy but really interesting if u reach the point of a good understanding of the Chari Method. He is a great lecturer, can be confusing but really approachable through OH or after lectures. Take the class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: an incredible lecturer

I took G123 Postcolonial, it was a very reading intensive course and discussion at a pretty academic/high level. He will expect a decent amount of effort and thought in your work--he wants you to think deeply about abstract concepts that are related to media that is postcolonial. Tough but great content. He's empathetic and funny.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Even though there is only one meeting per week for GEOG C100 it is still an inspiring course. I absolutely love the interdisciplinary components of this course! The only thing is that sometimes the prompt for homework is a little vague but the projects for sure inspire creativity.
Didn't get much from his lectures. Would often bring up things discussed in past lectures without adding much complexity. Maybe is better in geography classes.

I took art and ecology with this professor and he was super passionate and dedicated to sharing his expertise and knowledge! His research outside of class was impactful to learn about and he really cared about his students and their success! Highly Recommend art and ecology!

Sharad is lovely, kind and very funny. Took this class over summer and loved it. Was a bit all over the place when compressed, but covered v. interesting topics. Reading was manageable since not all was required, but def do the required ones (they add a lot to lecture). I walked away feeling like I had learned tons despite the class's breadth.

Lectures are somewhat boring but Professor Chari uses lots of diagrams to explain things well. I found his readings to be lengthy but quite interesting, and you can pretty much just skim them. The 2 quizzes were pretty straightforward if you attend section and there were no required essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The subject of Globalization was interesting, yet Prof Chari was a very boring professor, I admit to falling asleep several times. He has slides and also creates diagrams that make complicated concepts easier. Pretty straightforward and easy if you take notes and attend discussion.

Absolute legend. Love this guy. Some students are scared of him, but if you just take the effort to go ask questions or engage more in the class past just going to lecture and doing homework, he's actually very approachable and clearly cares a lot about students. You can tell he genuinely loves teaching and chemical engineering.
He is very passionate about the material; it's just a hard class with a pretty unforgiving curve.

You can tell by his age and demeanor that if he weren't passionate about the success of his students, he would be retired by now. The course is very difficult (B- average), but going to all lectures and discussions makes it do-able. Radke is respected and adored by many students for good reason.

Dr. Radke is witty, passionate about chemical engineering, and shows a great deal of care to his students. Lectures tend to stray off the material and Dr. Radke has a habit of going on tangents, but these are oftentimes attempts by him to integrate real-world, everyday engineering concepts into the lectures. Very well-liked by the class.
Not a good lecturer and lecture notes are disorganized, starts in one place and ends somewhere completely different with no connection between them. This course made me hate chemical engineering

This class is very technical and attention to detail is paramount when completing homework problems and exams. Both are quite difficult and need long hours of studying. Quizzes, although unannounced, are sparse and based on conceptual understanding (i.e. easy). If you don't understand something, then ask for clarification and Prof. Radke will help.

Attendance was mandatory because of (open note) pop quizzes, but they were not harshly graded and were effectively for completion if you had the notes with you. Dr. Radke is a very kind and understanding human being who really believes in his students. He even went out of his way to tutor struggling students like me outside of office hours.

Dr. Radke is a brilliant scientist and moreover possesses extraordinary pedagogical common sense. The logic of the material at hand is clearly and efficiently articulated and always accompanied by a wholesome, warm concern for his students' understanding and praxis of the material. Go to office hours always!
Love this guy

Radke is a real scientist. He's blunt, clear, and is quite the performer during lecture. Spend a little time with him and you realize he's also quite witty and wise. He's a good a teacher for sure, no doubt about it. Although his tests may be difficult, you will learn a lot from him. He's not unreasonable, far from it. He's extremely logical.

Its all about the math. If your into differential equns, then great, but I'm not sure how much it relates to engineering ???? Very different from my first CH ENG class, and it seems less related to working as an engineer. Prof. Rakde is enthusiastic and tries very hard to get his points across.

Exams are pretty tough for this class. He is also not such a friendly guy either, its hard to approach him for help without him going crazy. I think for the exams its important to rely heavily on the notes as opposed to studying the textbook, and do previous exams to time yourself.
Great professor. Said he wasn't teaching this course anymore, so there is zero purpose in writing this review.

He definitely knows his stuff, so the lecture notes are beyond helpful for the homework and tests. He's really intimidating though. Midterms are hard, but not impossible. The homework, thought, is impossible sometimes. Definitely necessary to work with other people on the homework, otherwise you'll spend HOURS getting frustrated with yourself.

Sort of a love/hate relationship with this guy. He's a little obnoxious sometimes, but overall knows his stuff and is enthusiastic. Go to lecture- he teaches lots of things that aren't in the book, and has occasional quizzes. Tests are hard, open-book, doesn't help. HW takes hours, work with people!

Very good teacher! Be sure to always show up to lecture so you don't miss quizzes plus extra material not covered anywhere in the book. Tests were pretty hard, but were open-book and open-note (won't help you if you don't know the material inside and out). Be sure to give yourself plenty of time to do the homework!
I feel that he is very good at teaching

Radke is a beast. He moves through lecture fast and can be hard to follow so you gotta stay sharp. Problem sets can take 5+ hours, definitely go to gsi office hours. Tests are difficult as well. Overall he is an excellent prof and definitely knows his stuff.

Radke can be intimidating, but he is a very good professor.  He doesn't teach from the book so you have to go to class.  DON'T go to his office hours if you do not like to be put down.  GSI office hours were very helpful: you should always go to them.

I had Radke for 140 and 150B.  At first I totally had him, but now I like him.  His lecture notes are important!  If you can follow his lecture notes you can do well in the class.  The class is really hard and problem sets take forever (10+ hours).  YOu must go to office hours if you want to well in the class. GO TO OFFICE HOURS!  Don't read

Lectures are much easier to understand and more important than the textbook. Regularly reviewing and understanding notes could be sufficient. Hone skills using hw, and come to the test with an agile mind. Sometimes the test is too long and a lot of people don't finish. He said he'd curve the class for 2.7 GPA average. Office hours usually helpful.

Prof REALLY cares & wants you to learn, maybe a bit too much in fact as it often causes him to seem frustrated if students aren't understanding (and he yells!)  He can be rather intimidating.  GO TO OFFICE HOURS IF YOU WANT TO PASS THIS CLASS!  It's a difficult class but if you put in the effort you can really learn a ton.

Office hours are almost required if you want to do well. He is incredibly helpful there and you learn a lot. Tests are incredibly hard though. The mean score for every midterm we took was below 50%. Overall I'd say he's a good professor who can teach you a lot; but he's very hard.

Great professor, very clear but also moves very fast.  If you miss a beat it's hard to catch up.  The work and tests were relatively hard, have to go to OH almost every week.  Overall very good professor.
Awesome lecturer, very good at making things easy to understand.

he's an awesome professor.. very dedicated and actually caresa bout his students... absolutely amazing... i like him and he made class very interesting. didnt fall asleep even though class was at eight in the morning.

Class was  ridiculous far as difficulty. Hardest class I've ever had in my life. Homework took 10 hours and the entire semester I had no clue what was going on. The teacher is very helpful at office hours and does care about understanding. But he needs to have more office hours to actually help students.
Absolutely worst class I've taken at Cal. Made me change my major..

Dr. Radke is an excellent ChemE professor. His lectures are well-organized and easy to follow for the most part. However, he always wants students to go to his OH's for help, but seems to be in a rush to get you in and out. His personality tends to be rather arrogant, and at times can be a jerk. Other than that, it's a good class. Work very hard!!!

CJR is an amazing professor-he truly inspires students to work harder by avoiding all simplifications and assumptions,and often derives many of the equations used.His hws are challenging,but cement the fundamentals of ChE forever.Definitely recommend going to OH,hes very helpful and guides students through problems as they solve them themselves!
Awesome teacher.  TAKE HIS COURSE IF HE IS TEACHING.  HW is quite difficult but tests are fair and test your understanding, not how much grunt work you've put in.

One of the most caring and passionate professors I've encountered at Berkeley.  Make sure you go to office hours; you learn just as much as in the classroom.  Tests are fair but material is quite difficult.

he might seem mean and harsh...but he is definitely very very caring for his students...midterms & final were reasonable...strong advice to read your lecture notes before ur exams...they will definitely help...PS: HW were hard...u have to go to office hour...

I think he is the most passionate chemical professor in the department.  You will never fall asleep in his class.  The homeworks are difficult and the tests are a bit easier than the homeworks, I thought. 140 and 150A are both not easy classes, but at least he makes them interesting.
No Comments
No Comments
I think he is one of the best engineering professor in berkeley!

Clara is such a wonderful professor and person in general. She cares deeply about the subject and is a leading researcher in the field! She brought guest speakers who authored the class readings, which was neat. She's very approachable and is a great resource for anyone interested in food systems or ecology. I learned so much in this course. 100/10
Came to RMP just to rate such an exceptional professor at Cal! Sophisticated lectures and meaningful student-led discussions...

Prof. Nicholls is an asset to students interested in environmental ecology. The class is mostly student led discussion, so be prepared to participate and have fun doing so! Her class enables students to develop their voice and their personal interest in aspects of rural development. Highly recommended class and straight forward grading & open OH.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Class is led seminar style, very biased left but I thought the readings were very interesting although sometimes a bit repetitive. She is really great in office hours and really cares about her students. I really learned a lot about the topic and found it really easy to get engaged. Definitely not a class for people who don't like speaking in class

Clara is very intelligent, passionate, and friendly.  This course has been one of my favorites this semester. We have many key thinkers/writers/activists as guest speakers regularly.  Students have opportunities to lead the class. Highly recommended.

Clara is a superb teacher and her class, sustainable rural development of latin america, is a really great class, though unfortunately overtly biased leftward.  It is taught seminar style and class format is a mixture of lecture and discussion led by Clara, students, and guest speakers.   Clara cares for her students and is a great contact too.

Clélia is my favorite prof at Berkeley! She's really sweet, knowledgeable, and genuinely wants everyone to succeed and improve their Portuguese. We barely had any homework and I loved the class discussions, content, and how she organized the participation. HIGHLY RECOMMEND!
She is an amazing professor with so much knowledge She is also kind and accessible. WOLD DEFF RECCOMEND HER

Took Portuguese 103 with Clelia and it was so laid back, fun, and not too much work! Clelia gives a TON of feedback on your assignments and is so attentive. Clelia encourages you to speak Portuguese, even if you make mistakes it's okay! Overall I enjoyed this class and I loved having Clelia as my prof :)
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: You can tell Professor Clelia enjoys teaching Portuguese. She's always very enthusiastic during class and tries to make the learning experience as dynamic and immersive as possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Clelia cares most about using Portuguese well. She constantly encourages natural conversation throughout the class and takes every student where they are and helps them build their knowledge and fix mistakes over the semester. She tailors the lecture content based on the needs of the students & you can tell she's passionate and cares about students

A genuine soul; a genuine teacher. She is extremely knowledgeable about language/linguistics in general and has a passion for Brazilian culture. I loved that she added various media to her curriculum. I studied with her from 2000-2002 at UC Berekely, so I imagine that advances in technology have added even more to her classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Clelia is AMAZING!! Super upbeat, organized, keeps it interesting--this class is NEVER BORING-and she is patient and helpful.This doesn't mean she is a pushover, you really have to do the work AND stay away from sounding like you're speaking Spanish! Port speakers hate that more than anything; you get points taken off! Take her class!! No regrets!!

Clélia is one of the best professors I have had while at Berkeley. Her manner of teaching is well paced and clear. If you do the work and come to class you will learn a lot and get a good grade. I am very excited for the possibility of having her again for Portuguese 103.
One of my favorite professors, I am from Argentina and we got a long very well (both of us are soccer fanatics), very approachable and the type of prof. that you go out to have a beer with.

Clelia is such a great woman and professor. Finally a teacher that feels like a real person. She's interested, interesting, and her classes are fun. I'm already learning twice as much as my last Portuguese class, and the semester isn't even over! And... good Brazilian movies for homework? It could be worse!

Clelia is amazing. I had a different teacher for my first Portuguese class, and now having her, she's changed my opinion entirely. She's encouraging, sweet, enthusiastic, and incredibly knowledgeable on the language and how to teach it. Great teacher. Highly recommended.
She is awesome. I had her for 101B and 102. Tons of fun.
Clelia is a wonderful teacher.
Clelia is energetic and often funny. She's a lot of fun and a great teacher. No busy work, tests are fair.
Had her for 101A, 102, and 103. Clear, enthusiastic, caring, helpful. Head of the language program. Will help you learn and love the Portuguese language!

This class is so boring. Don't need to do the readings at all u can lowkey just ChatGPT them and understand the main points. Do not need to pay attention in lecture at all but would participate in discussion. Really really boring class

Professor Talwalker's class was an overall positive and highly developmental experience, I learned SO much across the semester. The assignments are straightforward and you are set up for success if willing to put in the effort for it. Course work can be a lot, but you do genuinely see a difference in knowledge as time progresses. Highly reccomend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Talwalker is a nice and genuinely caring professor. Class is readings, which start long but by mid semester are like 10 pages, then write 1-2 paragraphs on the reading, for credit. then, lecture where we take the terms of the reading and create a deeper discussion. midterms/final have cheat sheet, relatively easy. recommend! lecture is slow but eh
Great professor. Sometimes slightly mundane lectures, but if you listen she has great insights. I learned so much through this class.

If you are not interested in understanding how the most influential thinkers over the centuries (Locke, Hegel, Marx, Polayani, Keynes etc) have shaped our recent political and economic systems then don't take this class. There is a mandatory attendance policy but I would have not attended class as much as I did without it. You get what you put in!

I understand the complaints about the reading - but Talwalker shouldn't be rated so low because of it. It's a challenging class but I learned SO MUCH and was exposed to so many different perspectives that prompted critical thinking. She also goes through each author in class and provides Q's to guide the readings, so just focus on reviewing those.

The number of readings is over the top. GSI even said "it's like a form of punishment." Lecture's mandatory, & 90% of class doing other things due to disengaging lectures. They're recorded, but only provided when ur sick, u get 5 sick days. 2nd midterm was day b4 thanksgiving, grade comes out during RRR. 2 midterms, 10 reading notes, & final. GL.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Took PE 100 with Clare and thought it was a decent class! Lectures can be quite boring sometimes because the material is dense and attendance is mandatory. Your grade largely depends on your GSI and participation is worth 15% of your grade. Just do the readings, go to class, and participate in section and you'll do well in the class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: You can tell she really cares about the subjects she teaches, but her lectures are incredibly boring. Grading heavily relies on your GSI not her. Lots of readings. She made me dread going to class...
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: The course covers a wide range of topics in regards to orgs and ethics through readings and in-class discussions. Prof. Talwalker is very organized, understanding, and caring; however, she is firm on her expectations when it comes to work that's turned in. The course is as hard as you make it, just do the readings and participate in the seminar.

My friends had warned me beforehand about the class but I had to take it. It includes three hours of boring lectures each week, but the worst part about the class is the harsh grading, which seems unjustified. Unless you use the tone that the GSI/professor prefers, you will be penalized. Additionally, the class is very politically biased.

Fantastic professor. Lots of readings but they're interesting. Lecture is a little dry but she's great at making the material relevant and getting students to engage. She's also very kind and approachable. Exams and papers are definitely fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: By taking classical political economic theory with Prof. Talwalker, people were able to read a wide range of early modern political and economic theories(ists) that are widely read across disciplines, which opens up the possibility for them to understand things across different disciplines. Graded on reading memos and two essay-based exams.

Grades are highly dependent on GSIs. Zero feedback, grades were not transparent (the only assignment we know the grade of is Midterm 1, 20% of our total), and the grading process took way too long. Though lots of really interesting readings are assigned, test questions rely on regurgitating interpretations relayed from pretty dry lectures.

Although the class is very much enjoyable and engaging, she lectures quite slowly and I'm very convinced she doesn't realize there are only 24 hours in a day with the amount of reading that's assigned. Can def find alternatives for most readings and I HIGHLY recommend not missing section.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Rating for global 121, not global 10b. Nice professor. Expects a lot for a breadth class. Class had a very one-sided political view that was unwelcoming to non "politically correct" persepectives

Great class and great professor. You get to learn about different ideologies and challenges to them. She provides a safe space to critique and talk about different thinkers in an open and intellectual way.

This was a 3 hour class in the evening so it was rough sometimes, but Prof Talwalker always engaged the class and was good at making students comfortable sharing. She even let us play with zoom filters during class and tried them herself. There was a good amount of weekly reading and writing; this class is not an easy A, but Prof was great
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: This class is the class where nobody gets 100% because it is not perfection. Every week there are 2 LOOOOng articles to read, which would be the foundation of your reading note. What I liked about her was that our finals were relatively shorter compared to other classes. It's a lower-division class, she grades harder than my upper-division courses.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She's a great teacher, expands so much in class. You read about two to three extensive readings each week and then make a reading note. The material is extraordinary. However, the reader can make or break your grade. The grading system is so bad and confusing. Reader grade notes and professor grades midterm and final. You learn a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: A LOT of reading every week but prof covers the material well so definitely go to lecture and take notes. Also very approachable and tries her best to keep students engaged. Essays and exams can be a bit challenging but study guides are pretty clear.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Talwalker is really knowledgeable and tries her best to make boring material interesting. She expects A LOT of her students (about 250 pages of reading a week), but she explains the material well in lectures. The tests were all essay based and though challenging, were not insanely difficult. Overall, I would recommend her as a teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Talwalker was so wonderful in GPP105, especially when we had to transition online this semester. She is an understanding person who always wants student feedback on the activities we do so that they can improve! No tests in this class, just a few essays that build off of each other. I learned a lot and am more prepared for this minor!

Clare was an okay professor. She is clear in what she expects from the class, but she is extremely vague in her lectures. Till this day I cannot tell you what I learned in one sentence because she really hopped with her material. Take her if you are a theoretical thinker.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great professor and lecturer. Interesting material presented in an easily understandable way. Tons of reading is assigned but I did literally none of it and did fine. She covers the readings very well in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I don't get why people say you have to write what she wants. Your GSI grades your papers not Talwalker.
