The subject matter is dry but she genuinely tries to add anecdotes to keep 17th century political theory interesting. I think from all those teaching PE 100 - she's the best you can take. Class is not easy - you're at Berkeley. Try harder.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The worst professor at Cal. If you don't think/believe what she wants you to think/believe then you won't do good in her class. Just say what she says and write what she thinks and you will be in good shape. Dry, dull and boring lectures.

This is the second class I've taken with her, and while it was a little more difficult in terms of grading the overall experience was great! Her lectures are a little dry but she tries her best to convey what she thinks are the most pertinent parts of readings. There is a lot of readings in both of her classes though so be prepared to read a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Talwalker is an amazing, brilliant woman but the lectures were a bit dry and the course material seemed a bit random. She takes an economic anthropology approach to this into global studies class. There are A LOT of readings and the take-home paper midterms are all pretty tough.

Clare is one of my favorite professors at Cal. I really liked her class (IAS 150, Globalization in India) and went to her office hours frequently. She really cares about student success and takes the time to engage with you, even requiring that you go discuss an essay topic in her office hours before you turn in the draft outline.

Her boring lectures told you everything you needed to know about the readings so you don't have to do them, just remember her main points and regurgitate it on the tests. She claims she wants your ideas/interpretations, but really, you just have to reword her beliefs and you'll pass.  Stopped going to class because it wasn't thought provoking.
Her lectures were clear and planned out. They had a logical flow and really helped with some of the more dense readings. She lectures slowly and repeats info, so it's fairly easy to take notes.
Superb class and professor. I had not thought this way about human rights before. Really eye-opening.

Clare seems checked out and disinterested in her students and teaching. Out of the six papers we wrote, she only graded 3. She didn't even turn grades in on time. She had the students discuss readings and workshop papers each week and barely even lectured. She didn't even come through on what she promised - feedback for our research proposal.
Prof Talwalker is amazing! Will take all her classes!

Prof. Talwalker is an excellent professor. She is very approachable, has a dry wit, and delivers very clear lectures. She really forces her students to think in critical ways about their place in the world. Most of all, she is extremely smart but does not make you feel dumb. I'd love to take more classes with her.

Among all the Professors I've had, Prof Talwalker is the most dedicated to her students. She is very approachable both in and outside of class. Her passion for her work really comes through in her teaching. I'd recommend her hands down.

The most down to earth, funny, smart, most interesting professor I've ever had. Super supportive, took her class during the summer with about 12 other students and had the best experience. Would HIGHLY recommend her

I freakin love professor Talkwalker. She is kind, caring, compassionate, and really helpful toward students. Although she is not the most interesting lecturer, the material is interesting and she really breaks it down well for students. I really enjoyed her class, and I wish more professors were as kind and approachable as professor Talwalker.

Really nice teacher with a great grasp of the material. I had no interest in this class and no prior knowledge of Internation Studies but Prof. Talkwalker really helped me 'get' the class. Interesting readings and informative lectures. Three reflection papers, one midterm, and a final 'shadow report' project.

This class is one of the better ones I have had at Berkeley. Professor Talwalker worked very hard to make difficult materials accessible and relevant to my long term interest in NGO work. Her teaching style is not flashy but neither is it dumbed down.

While her lecturing style was very dry and boring I think she is a fascinatingly smart woman that challenges students to really conceptualize the theories and readings into the appropriate context. She is also very accessible and helpful during office hours. The graders for this class, however, were unnecessarily nit picky and difficult.

This class is absolutely dry and terribly boring. If I don't bring a laptop to class, I don't know how I would be able to stay awake. The woman is smart, yes, but has managed to turn human rights into a boring topic. Difficult to understand because she uses abstract terms and words.

This woman is a total failure!  The course was extremely easy and extremely boring.  Her reader was filled with out-of-date, non-academic material and her lecturing style was totally unsophisticated.  Worst Berkeley class to date...No exaggeration.

I've only been to two of her classes during a shopping period at the beginning of this semester and I was sorely disappointed. I'm sure the material she covers is great, but honestly you can't tell because she's so boring you drift off. I counted 17 people who walked out before I myself took the liberty (and I never do this!)
Smart, helpful & interesting!
No Comments
No Comments
she is incredibly helpful in office hours! she is a great lady and a great teacher
He has so much aura!! Best professor!!

Clark is an amazing professor. He managed to completely redesign EECS16B into a great class. I really appreciate how he made himself very accessible outside of class and was genuinely receptive to feedback from the students. He listens to and cares for students and it shows in the quality of his teaching. He also shredded Metallica in class. Legend

Ppl usually don't come to lectures. I find it difficult to follow his teaching style. Notes are chaotic. Exams are easier compared to homework and lectures. The lab takes way too much time and the instructions are unclear. Make sure to study labs for exams. The class is on circuit design with no LA. PHYS 7B can be helpful before taking the class.
Great professor! He uses webcast to upload every lecture, which is helpful!

Professor Nguyen is extremely knowledgeable in the MEMS area, which means he explains every concept very clearly, but sometimes the details can be overwhelming. He is very approachable and also very helpful during office hours. His homeworks are okay, but his tests are pretty difficult (but still fair). Definitely go to his lectures! Great prof!

Clark's class on MEMS was a good technical overview of the subject. He taught it in a way such that an EE with little prior knowledge of mechanical engineering could follow along and succeed in the class. He does a good job teaching the basics. He can be a little hard to follow at times, but he has good lecture notes, albeit a little disorganized.
I am in her French 1 class (I was only given the choice for selecting either French 2 or 3). She is unbelievably caring.

Claire is so personable and I love this lady. She is really understanding and funny and grades fairly easily. But attendance is really important because it affects your grade quite a bit if you miss enough.
Caring, knowledgeable professor. Really kind as a person. Encourages you when you make mistakes. Clear feedback for assignments. 100% recommend

Professor Tourmen is a fantastic French teacher. I have taken class from her two semesters in a row and my French has improved immensely. She really cares about all of her students and truly wants us to learn the language. She is very accessible and always gives thorough feedback. Plus, she has the warmest demeanor that makes class a pleasure.

Really solid choice for a French teacher. Lectures are good- everyone attends ours for the most part, you'd definitely be fine if you skipped a few tho. Super nice with the grading and assignments- even though they're standard in the department she helps out with extensions etc. Textbook used 1-2 exercises per week,u prolly could get away w/out one

THE GOAT!! I'm not even done with this class yet but I love it. Great lectures, entertaining, and Professor Coppola is super nice and really cares about students. He's easy to talk to, great at answering questions, super involved, super smart, and passionate. I would take this class a million more times. Couldn't recommend him enough. So fun!

I took Film 45, not Film R1B. I found the class very enjoyable, in large part due to Professor Coppola. He was always engaged with the class, would ask how we were as we walked in, and always tried to keep up with current shows and movies. He structured the course around readings, so be prepared to read a lot or you'll be lost. Very nice guy!
I took film 45. Legend. Amazing class discussions. Really well-spoken and engaging professor. Up to date with current events. Enjoyed that class thoroughly.

NOTE: I took film 45, not R1B
Coppola is a good teacher. He has an engaging way of speaking, I like how he bounces off student answers. I wish we watched more films in class as opposed to random TV Show episodes. I thought some of the content in the class was like too easy, like no duh, shallow analysis. But the hegemony lectures were good.

Friendly and encouraging. Interesting questions on tech. Cares about topics & students. Identity politics, but expected & fit well enough. Participation points, lenient grading, helpful. Casual writing class.
Discussion, not textbook: do the (small enough) readings+films, attend, put in effort to participate&discuss, & you won't need to worry much.

This class tries to take the concept of social justice and ridiculously morph it into some sort of rigorous, systematic science, which is in line with how the Public Health department frankly takes themselves too seriously at times. Easy class to do well in, only due to Corburn's skills of pedagogy.

I did not think I would be really immersed into the material (PH major was a mistake for me) but Corburn's method of delivery makes you want to tune in. There's a lot of MC but they're very easy (perhaps too easy) to the point where a high-schooler could do them. I honestly might've preferred taking this class in-person and I love online now.

He made most of the coursework online and very very very reasonable in difficulty. Definitely passionate about what he teaches but like the other reviews I wish he had in person lectures because they seemed really interesting.

I didn't interact with Professor Corburn as everything was asynchronous and remote. He seems very knowledgeable and all assignments were relevant and interesting. Without the professor, the GSIs helped connect the class and the material. I wish I got to interact with the professor more. Grade is mostly from MC and wasn't too hard personally.

Coburn seemed to do as little of his job as possible. Not a single real lecture, just short, edited down recordings of previous semesters' lecture. If you like auto-graded multiple choice, that's literally all this class is -- hw, quizzes, everything. If you're like me and suck at MC, you're gonna feel cheated out of an easy A.
Considering we were in a pandemic, he was very flexible and the work was lengthy but not too bad. Definitely recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Corburn was a great professor and interesting lecturer. Make sure you go to class because he does use iclicker for attendance. The class depends on the quality of your GSI. Do not procrastinate on the homework assignments, and know the key concepts for the midterm.
Awesome! Take this class

Amazing professor! I had him for c116 and he was the best. made class easy to understand, and was easy to come to for questions! I went to OH a lot and loved the GSI, she explained everything really well! He teaches really clearly and focuses on application and bigger picture messages! would take this class again

Easily the most interesting class I've taken. Prof Coates is a great lecturer and is very helpful at OH. He's an expert on what he's teaching and gives a great history of the field for the papers discussed. Tests are straight forward and questions come directly from what is emphasized during lecture (ie: if there's 10 slides on it, study it!)

There are several issues with this class that I feel future students should be aware of before taking it. 1) ITS NOT CURVED: so everyone could get a C and the semester I took it 88% got a C or B-. 2) The GSI controls everything.He not only grades the hw and exams he also gets a lot of lecture time.If the GSI is a certain Cameron then please avoid

Lectures consisted of her reading instructions for assignments (which was on bcourses) or for instance going over how to write a works cited. Lectures were monotonous and not always engaging. Consists of small group projects more or less every week. She is very caring and kind but does not teach you how to improve your writing skills whatsoever.

Ms. Coleman is very kind, but I feel she is not very engaging. the class time is spent either with her reading off of the board very slowly and monotonously OR by breaking us up into small groups and writing out answers to questions, then reading them to the class. Overall, I feel that I did not improve any skills taking this class.

A whole 1hour and 30 mins lecture was used to explain how to write an annotated bibliography which was completely unnecessary considering all the information was on b-courses and she was just reading off of the assignment instructions

Attendance is mandatory. 70% of class time is group presentation. Sometimes no technology is allowed. Grading system is inconstant, during class when she went over my essay she said it was excellent and no changes needed to be made but she gave me a 64% for that essay with is confusing. And a lot of writing assignments in general outside of class.

She is exceptional. Engaging lectures fostered love for poetry & broadened perspectives. Clear explanations & calm demeanor aided learning; grasped American history well. Goes above & beyond, offering help outside class. Timely, constructive writing feedback focused on growth, not just grades. Truly dedicated & supportive; highly recommend!"

Loved this english class. She gives a lot of feedback on your essays that you can resubmit for more points. She is very sweet and replies to emails very quick. I would 100% recommend taking this class for R1A. Attendance is taken and mandatory if you don't want to take an additional final at the end of the course.

Really sweet Professor. Definitely my favorite Professor this semester. 3 major essays with 1 final portfolio project. She allows for revisions on all essays which is very helpful. She cares about her students. However, make sure you go to class because if you miss more than 2 classes you have to take an in class final! 100% recommend Ms.Coleman
Very good teacher and has very informative annotations. She also allows for revisions which is very helpful!

Very knowledgeable and cares a lot about her students. She gives great feedback on writing, especially on the major essays, and is reasonably flexible on deadlines. With that said, make sure to show up to lecture, because if you miss three classes you will need to write an in-class final!

Had him for Chinese 7A. Mark's a cutie. Lecture slides often have dense chunks of writing and he has a dense lecturing style which makes him a bit hard to follow. Readings were interesting, though lengthy.  
Ripe plums are falling/ Now there are only five/ May a fine lover come for me/ While there is still time

Favorite prof ever. Extremely knowledgeable and respectful. Cares a lot and is super friendly. Nerdy in the best way. 2 midterms, final, 2 papers graded by GSI who was also very knowledgable and friendly. Take good notes and tests will be fine (open note). An extreme amount of reading and I honestly didn't do most of it and did well so whatever
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Mark is a lovely guy. He's funny, relatable, and fair. His lectures can drag a bit sometimes - he's an incredibly knowledgeable man, but a little awkward (in a good way!). You'll need to write several papers, but his grading is fair and feedback is plentiful. Office hours are easy to access, and he'll leave you loving both the sheep and the ritual.

As an EALC major student, mark is currently one of my favourite professors under our school department. He is caring, humorous(kinda cold jokes sometimes smh), and knowledgable. You can tell he is really passionate about his teaching and research and you will definitely learn a lot from him. He is a fair grader and his class is highly recommended.

Caring professor who really encourages students to come to office hours. Says "um" quite a bit but you can see he is quite passionate and knowledgeable about the subject. Be prepared to write quite a bit because you need to write 4 papers which isn't too bad though. Study guide for midterm and final preps you well. Midterm review lecture was fun!

He is a true intellectual. He is very well-read, knowledgable on his topics (early Chinese history, history of thought). He is caring and kind. He is also a fair grader - however, he gives limited feedbacks and not always accessible outside class (he does point out which areas you need improvements in your paper, though).

The lectures can be a little hard to sit through but they are actually interesting and the professor does actually care for the subject. He is very very approachable and knowledgeable. The class itself is pretty easy and fair.
the worst class I ever took in my academic life. he is the most boring professor

Greig is a really great and caring lecturer. He doesn't take breaks which can make things feel like they drag on for a while, but overall the class was good. There were readings and reading responses every week but exams were open book. Had a pop quiz, was going to have more but he decided to change it to a time capsule project, which was nice.

Suberb facilitator of very inspiring and stimulating discussion. It is a few years since I took these classes and still refer to them. It actually changed the way I approached critical theory. Ive studied at many institutions and Prof Cryslers courses were easily the best.
Wonderful and enthusiastic. Really encourages critical thinking and debate. Ties in his own research to lectures which is great. Very approachable.

Greig is a good prof, he sometimes rambles on a bit but he loves feedback and is happy to clear up anything you don?t understand. The content is useful and the sections and very stimulating. Easy midterm and final. Pop quizzes are too easy. The most work are the weekly reading responses.

If you are looking for an easy class and if you are not interested in working hard, you shouldn't even be in berkeley. He is a great professor for those who are keen and interested in learning, dull for those who could not be bothered.
lousy prof

Professor is very dull, and not very helpful. If you were interested in the topic before taking this class, your interest will disappear after taking this class. Besides professor doesn't care how many students attend the class, or whether students understand what is aspected of them. In all very bad experience.

i took this class many years ago...but know this about greig...he is a brilliant, dedicated and genuine professor.  i have no idea why "difficulty" seems here a negative thing.  greig's classes are amazing because they are challenging and provocative.
No Comments

She's nice enough but literally did not grade ANYTHING until we got our final grades back. You will be swimming in homework during RRR week, and she doesn't really give adequate feedback. Throughout the course, it was extremely difficult to tell what was due, and when, and where, and what our grade would be. Take another R4B.

WAY TOO MUCH HOMEWORK. 3 essays due during finals week. (For some reason RMP won't let me say 1 of them was a 10-15 page r*search p*per.) I still do not have a single grade in that class (meaning I don't know what I got on any assignment nor do I know my final grade) and grades were due 4 days ago.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Made a person cry while giving feedback in front of everyone. Had to work throughout RRR week to start and finish the final essays that we hardly got any good feedback.
Made someone cry in class by giving

She gives amazing feedback, and everything is great, she is really nice and caring, you will definitely pass if you follow her rules. The only downside is that you would be doing 4 essays during dead week. Do the revision of the essay as fast as you can whenever you get the drafts feedback.

Teri Crisp is a caring professor that truly cares about her class more than anything else. She also gives great feedback on essays which helps you to become a more efficient writer. The only thing that was a downside was when she crammed 2 essays at the end of the class for the final portfolio.

She really cares about her students and wants you to succeed in the class and in general improve your writing. The only thing I would say is that having do all 3 essays during RRR week is brutal. I did enjoy the class other than the way she organized it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Prof. Teri need to reorganize her course, so we are no longer dealing with 3 big essays in the RRR week.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Crisp gives good feedback, I am grateful for how she has helped me improve my writing skills. However, I didn't love having mandatory class sessions during dead week. Would not take her again for a six-unit course --I don't think I have ever worked harder for an A in my life-- but she is caring and wants the best for her students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: If the class had been structured better, it would have been great. The last few weeks of the semester were quite crammed, which was exhausting and can have collateral damage on other classes if you don't manage your time properly.

A kind but frustrating teacher. Day to day classwork will have you wondering if you're in college or not. The main thing you are graded on is class participation and a collection of 3 essays. Doesn't seem like too much work until you find yourself doing all 3 essays during dead week because of how she structures the class. This class is draining

The class starts off pretty slow, then escalates very quickly. Not an easy A, need to put in hard work. PARTICIPATION REALLY MATTERS, so show her you care. And very good at spotting bs, so try not to. She will develop you as a writer, but if youre looking for an easy A, this is not the class.
very interesting class

AMAZING PROF also had cohen for american studies 102 (equally amazing, also got an A, but attendance mando) he is the reason i am an american studies major he is by far the best teacher i've had. lots of reading but so worth it
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: What a character! Very informative though, and long but good reading list. Only two essays and a midterm and final (timed write style).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Cohen's lectures were genuinely some of the most eye-opening things I've ever heard in my life. I'm not sure if he's teaching AFAM27AC anymore, but definitely take a class with him. He's super super knowledgable, and his lectures are actually really fun and interesting to sit through. Insanely goated prof.

If you want to get an A, YOU MUST do the readings. However, lectures are so enjoyable, and I found myself happy that I chose to go to class. He assigns actually interesting readings. Just get the general concept and some useful knowledge for midterms, and you will be fine. Such a passionate professor, and this really radiates in his lectures!

Super educated and knows how to relate history to modern day. It is a lot of reading but section does a good job at understanding them and he is willing to take questions during class. Books are recommended to be bought but all the PDF's of them are provided for free.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Probably my favorite lecture: super engaging and passionate, readings very interesting but long. Grade entirely depends on the GSI - no standard system of grading. Attendance is mandatory, classes not recorded or put online, but lectures are very engaging either way. Would take class again for Prof Cohen alone.
One of my favorite professors of all time, I was always excited to go to his lectures and overall he was a really cool and genuine guy. Recommend 100%.

Great professor. I graduated in 2023, took Racial Capitalism class with him. Super interesting lectures, generous grading, funny and caring, and the guy knows his stuff. Best books I've read were assigned in this class.

Took this class while on Summer 2025. Overall, this class went pretty well for me. I found lectures were interesting, readings were OK (quite too much), and most importantly, grading was generous. Just do what the Professor and the GSIs ask you to do, and I believe you'll do well. Don't be late in submitting your assignments!
The concepts can be tough and reading is very important but Cohen is amazing as a professor and as a person. Love his classes and he is great.

AC27 was my favorite class I have taken at Berkeley, and I say this as a biochemistry major who initially only took this class to meet L&S requirements. Incredibly passionate/engaging and quite funny- if I have time in my schedule I would take another one of his classes just for the fun of it.

Professor tends to use very complex language and explanations, which can make it difficult to grasp core ideas. + frequent disconnect between lecture & an explicit explanation of difficult material. At times unrelated/non-essential material become the focus of lectures. 2 exams & 1 final paper. However, Cohen is very enthusiastic and engaging
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I've had. His class changed my worldview and his lectures are amazing. 10/10 would recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Cohen is the best professor I have encountered so far. His lectures are full of so much interesting information and he is very passionate about his work. The class is graded based on race theories and a few great books - so it is very easy to succeed if you keep up with the readings and understand the theories. Please take this class!
He is the best professor and lecturer I've ever had in my life. Easy class. Probably the easiest class I've taken at Berkeley.

Very good lecturer that captivates attention. Grading system is a bit flawed inherently as it is graded by your GSI and there is no standard system, meaning it's up to the luck of draw as to which GSI you get. Participation for discussion required, sometimes overly biased but overall a great course. Reading heavy in the second half.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I would take this class again for the lectures alone. Professor Cohen is fantastic! The harder part was my discussion- attendance is mandatory and it was difficult to figure out what my GSI expected. If you ever get a chance to speak with Professor Cohen, he is very wise and has a great sense of humor! Ask him for book recommendations.

goated af i love cohen's class. engaging lectures, great accompanying readings, the midterm is just an in-class essay, and the final is a group project. i originally took this as a gpa booster but it's genuinely an amazing class. attendance is taken but you can miss a lecture or two without penalty. especially easy class if you're a marxist :)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: By far the best professor I've had at Berkeley. You can tell Cohen really cares about his students and his lectures are incredibly engaging. There is a lot of reading for this class but it's not that bad and exams were fairly easy. I 100% recommend this class and this professor!!!

The professor's extreme bias stifled any diverse perspectives, making it clear he believed only his views were valid. His dismissive attitude toward differing opinions created a hostile and uncomfortable environment, ultimately forcing me to stop attending. This class lacks respect for open discussion; I strongly discourage anyone from taking it.
best professor i've had at cal!!

Professor Cohen uses his charisma as a lecturer to make his classroom an echo chamber of his extreme political views. He doesn't allow for disagreement and debate even when he is demonstrably wrong. Your grade is based on how your GSI grades your papers and exams. You will learn more ideology than history.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. MMC is obviously very passionate about this topic and it bleeds well into his lectures. Attendance isn't mandatory, but you will benefit more from attending lectures and taking notes.

Prof. MMC is one of my favorite professors ever! His lectures are so interesting and engaging, I promise you will never be bored. Definitely my easiest class at Cal. Midterm and Final exam and two papers make up majority of your grade. It would be difficult to get lower than a B+. Def recommend for AC credit and you will learn a lot!

Professor Cohen is one of my favorite professors I have had at Berkeley so far. He is a very engaging lecturer, is consistently engaged in current events, and is very knowledgeable in his field. He emphasizes what is important for exams during lectures and writes fair exams despite no curve. Highly recommend it for the AC requirement!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Cohen was an amazing professor and lecturer. He was incredibly engaging and I managed to stay focused for the whole 1.5-hour lecture most of the time. He is funny, intelligent, passionate, articulate, and simply one of the best professors. I highly recommend this AC class, it was pretty easy if you do the readings and do the papers.
He's the best professor and course Ive taken here at UCB. Don't listen to the other raters. He makes lectures fun to go to, I attended them all and they aren't mandatory. Take if you want an easy A.

Dr. Cohen was an amazing professor! Each lecture was incredibly engaging with his ability to talk to the class, his occasional humor, and clear lecturing. I always looked forward to going to his lectures despite them being very important towards exams. The class was very heavy on reading and writing but his lectures are well worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Cohen was an amazing lecturer. The class is not difficult if you go to lecture (midterm was mostly lecture material). Kind of a lot of reading but it's manageable. There are two papers, one midterm and one final. Cohen made the final a take-home essay. He's a really chill, funny, knowledgeable, and passionate guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really cool guy. Interesting lectures, felt more like a fun podcast than a class. Wasn't too much work or too difficult. I hope I can take another class with him!
Professor Cohen is incredibly intelligent, articulate, and very funny. His lectures were optional but I always went because they were so engaging. Easy class, great GSIs. Highly recommend.

Dr. Cohen is a spectacular lecturer and his class was my favorite of the semester. He is lively, engages with students often, and makes difficult concepts relatively simple to grasp. Class grade was based on weekly discussion posts, two papers, and a group project. I definitely recommend taking a class with Dr. Cohen!!

Not only is this guy a straight up living legend, he is EXTREMELY passionate about teaching. He always starts the lecture with whats happening in the world then covers the lectures. Literally show up, take notes and you pass. Im not a good memorizer but his tests were extremely doable and he really makes sure you understand the material!

Dr. Cohen is one of the best professors I have had, if not the best. His class was eye-opening and inspiring. He is a natural speaker with excellent lectures. I hope to take another one of his classes in the future.

Cohen is my favorite professor so far. His lectures are so interesting. Attendance isn't mandatory but recommended because papers and exams focus on lectures and readings. Syllabus timeline goes by quickly so don't slack off on readings. Other than that, he has a clear grading guideline and expectation. Definitely will not regret taking his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: One of the best professor's I've had at Cal during my four years here! He is very engaging in lecture and was one of the courses I looked forward to the most! He implements theory and current news into his lectures. Very accessible during office hours. Assignments are not too difficult if you attend office hours.
Great professor. Took his WWII class. Loved his lectures and he assigned good books to read. Tests were fair and well graded. Would recommend him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Class is graded by 4 things (2 Papers, 1 Midterm, 1 Final). His lectures are pretty interesting and inspirational, however they can be a bit long. Overall solid choice.
Two Exams, Two Papers. Exam 1  25%, Paper 1  10% ; Exam 2  35%, Final Paper  30%. However, beware of the curve as will you only get an "A" if you get more than 95%.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He is a great teacher, his classes are fun and he is really laid back. The class is low work only 2 essays and 2 tests all year, this being said if you don't do well on one thing you get screwed over because there's not much that's going in the grade book. He sets up the class so that if you show up to class and movie night you will pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Prof Cohen is an incredible, fascinating, intelligent lecturer. He really makes you think, and I greatly enjoyed coming to class every week. While I originally took this class just for AC credit, I still found myself engaged and interested in the subject matter. Take a class with him if you can  you won't regret it.

I love this guy. He consistently blows my mind with amazing lectures. The end of this semester is the second class I've taken with him and I have to say every moment, every assignment is so worth it. This guy is truly the treasure of UCB.
Super great lecturer, by far one of the best professors I've had. He really makes you think but keeps class interesting to the point where you genuinely hate missing.

He is VERY liberal. Not much other than lecture notes, but a lot is expected from your writings. Grade definitely depends on your GSI. He's very opinionated, but definitely offers an interesting perspective on minorities and race. Do not take if you are not good at interpreting texts and doing analysis. Description of class does not match actual.

Prof. Cohen has undoubtedly shaped the way I critically think about race, the world and myself to this day. While this class was on the intersection of film and race, he seamlessly related our course material to today, w humor. Few professors have made a profound impact on who I am and Prof. Cohen is def one of them. Don't leave w/o taking him.

He's a great lecturer and clearly intelligent, although very opinionated. The class was awful (but easy) and you have no idea what grade you'll get till the last week of class, but at least he made lectures slightly more interesting.

Professor Cohen hurts his students by convincing them to be angry cry babies and the younger generations eat it up! It was very simple to pass this class, just pretend to be as outraged by every tiny "micro-aggression" as he is (or maybe you actually are the type of person who is offended by everything). I got an A by going along with his BS!

This class has a lot of reading, but they are all very interesting. his lectures were amazing in my opinion and changed how i view race. very entertaining and you can see that he really cares about what he is teaching. the gsi's grade the essays and exams though, so youre grade depends on them entirely. def want to take another class with him!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Cohen is the best lecturer I've encountered at UC Berkeley.  He challenges his students' notions of the world and forced us all to face uncomfortable facts about the United States and humanity as a whole.  Don't skip the lectures.  You'll be missing out.

Prof Cohen is a great lecturer! He is really cares about the subject matter. He is quite biased though so prepare for very strong opinions you might disagree with. Best advice: go to GSI's office hours and get help! Mine was amazingly helpful. Just do the stuff he asks for (like readings) and you'll be fine.

I'm an engineering major, so I'm not used to my grades being based mostly on opinions.  I can't believe a world class university really has professors that teach and grade with such outright political bias. He has a right to an opinion, but ruining my GPA because I disagree is just wrong.
One of the most engaging and charismatic lecturers I've encountered. He blows my mind every time and I truly enjoy attending his class.

I took a couple of classes with Michael back in 08/09 and he was by far the most engaging professor while I was at CAL.  Here I am years later, a professor myself and I came here to remember those who inspired me.  He is also a wonderful advocate of student parents!!!
Excellent professor. I'm so glad I got to take one of his classes during my time at Cal.

I took his WWII class my first semester at Cal, and could not be more grateful to have had the opportunity to work with him. He is by far the most magnificent orator I have yet encountered in a professor. He is approachable, and charismatic, and takes a sincere interest in his students.
Amazing Professor.

Professor Cohen is extremely intelligent and passionate about history and current social issues. His lectures are engaging and interesting, and he picked amazing books to read for his WWII class. The tests and assignments were very fair and he gives a lot of extra credit, so I think anyone who takes this class can get a good grade and learn a lot!

Great class, very interesting material. However, Cohen kind of crapped out in the last month of the semester. He seemed far more interested in the Occupy movement than our class. Classes were canceled and the final book- the best in the class- was never even discussed. We were given little feedback on the two papers that made up our grade.

The guy has charisma in the classroom, I will give him that.  But he's also arrogant, doesn't allow for dissent, and uses his authority and classroom as a bully pulpit for his political views.  I'd rather have a teacher than a preacher.  Lectures also seemed to lack any coherent organization.

I've taken multiple classes with him so far and every single one was interesting. Yes, he's opinionated and to some he may seem preachy, but his passion is what makes him so engaging. The readings are somewhat dull and necessary, but his lectures more than make up for them. He's extremely knowledgeable and very helpful during office hours.

This guy is nuts. Not in a bad way. He's super enthusiastic and usually goes overboard with his speech-like lectures. However, felt that he didn't really allow room for dissent or opinions in lecture and spent every minute pushing his own. Damn this guy is smart. I'm intimidated. Also, doesn't seem to be really involved with the rest of the class.

This professor is amazing.  He is charismatic, articulate, passionate, and absolutely on top of his game.  He has a thoughtful and very through answer for any question you ask, and lectures are so interesting and informative.  He also deeply cares about the educational process, and about his students.
Hottest professor at Cal hands down. What a Beauty...

MIchael Cohen is a dreamy dreamboat from heaven.  Seriously,  If you wanted to be educated and not just spit out on the other side of the meat grinder, this is your chance. This a refresher in truth.  So much more than what I thought U.C. fees would buy. Every once in awhile there is a raging beauty from which your gaze cannot be averted from.
Best professor ever!!!! He is awesome, interesting, and a genius. He will really make you think, and probably about stuff you never thought of before. This class is super amazing too

Amazing professor, very interesting and fun class. he definitely made me think of the world in a different way for a couples months. but now i am stuck with horrible profs who are decreasing my iq by the second...
Such a great professor! Keeps lectures SUPER interesting and yet still gets his points across quite clearly. And he's super hot, too bad he's married ;(

I am not an american studies major and i do not enjoy history at all, but Cohen made the subject incredibly interesting for me. There's a lot of reading but it's really interesting. I highly recommend that you take one of his classes because he's an incredible lecturer
I only wish all of my professor had been this amazing. I wish I could have taken more courses with him.

Amazing lecturer! Very liberal with many radical views but it was also interesting to see American history from a much different perspective. He pushed his agenda pretty hard during the strike (for it) and he's either a Marxist or an anarchist, possibly both. Very passionate, I would recommend taking his class!

Very interesting guy, definitely has some radical opinions, but presented in an intelligent and insightful way. I don't necessarily agree with everything he says, but its difficult not to due to how charasmatic he is. I signed up for this class to handle my AC req, but its turned out to be one of the most interesting classes Ive taken here at Cal

I don't pay thousands of dollars in tuition to hear this mislead fool spout his opinions in what should be a lecture.  The course is almost done, and I'm sure I wont get too high a grade because the last major paper I went against his garbage political propaganda. This college has a huge problem if they let this guy lecture.
very smart guy

Okay, I admit that he does not always present the most objective views (leans towards socialism), but honestly, he knows how to keep the class interesting! He incorporates different types of media into his lectures, and references pop culture into his slides. 2 short essays and 1 midterm and final. Readings were a bit boring, but movies were cool.

I remember this class being the most biased and uneducational waste of time I've ever endured.  All of these good ratings are from ignorant kids who simple absorb whatever propaganda this charismatic charlatan shovels out.  This class is like reading a Socialist newspaper!
Very energetic and enthusiastic!

Very well prepared. Lectures are like a planned speech. Slides illustrate his points. Shows lots of film clips and the weekly movies are thought provoking. Reading is mid-level. He interprets everything from a Marxist perspective and regularly interjects Marxist phrases and key words into his speech - Funny coming from an Ivy Leaguer.
awesome professor. straightforward and intelligent.

really intelligent, passionate professor. lectures are very intense and packed with information - a very different perspective than you get in a high school history class. he's very liberal and opinionated. lots of reading and hard work, but it's a very doable class and very worth it.

Obviously puts a lot of effort into each lecture, revealing his passion and intelligence. He's funny, clever, absolutely hates cell phones going off in class, and can be somewhat intimidating. The readings can be a bit daunting, but a general knowledge of the topics discussed should suffice when writing the essays or taking the midterm and final.
Great Professor and class. There is alot of work involved but it is well worth it. Hard A but an easy B.

This professor is amazing. I came to every class, which is really surprising for me. He makes you see a whole different side of American culture and questions the stereotypes we've created about the past. I had so much fun listening to him and there's not that much work

Great professor. Lectures are interesting and well organized (and extremely well prepared). Sometimes puts too much information into lectures and he talks really fast, but if you pay attention, you'll be fine. Clearly very passionate about his subject and takes his job lecturing a lower div class very seriously (which enhances his lectures).

Inspiring. He lectures concisely, passionately, and humorously.  The amount of effort he puts into preparing his lectures and the gravity with which he treats the topics is evident.  He will challenge you in a way that makes you respect and appreciate his intelligent insights and beyond-reproach dedication.

I absolutely LOVED this professor.  You pick you your pencil & go nonstop until the end of class.  He was so insightful, passionate, brilliant, and well-organized (although very liberal and opinionated) that I never considered missing a lecture. Increadibly inspirational.  Great reading. I would highly recommend him.

I took professor Chang in the fall 2024 and spring 2025, and she has hands down been my favorite professor. She has helped me with my public speaking skills, before taking her class I was extremely shy, but after her classes my ability to speak in front of people has gotten better. She is also very understanding if you have an issue or a concern.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Had a fantastic experience in class with Dr. Chang. Super engaging lecturer that genuinely cares about students. Half the class was a history of Silicon Valley with the other half being a group research project on a startup of your choice. Groups were randomly assigned but don't think there were many issues.
Overall, could not recommend more.

Professor Chang is one of my favorite professors at Berkeley, and I loved this class with her! I would highly recommend her, she made the course extremely relevant to current day and related our theories to the news. Readings were not unreasonable and grading was fair. Participate and go to class because her lectures are always fantastic!!

Professor Chang is hands down one of my favorite professors. She is caring towards her students and pushes them out of their comfort zones. She is great at engaging with her students during class and outside of class. She has given me advice as well as helped me become a better student.

Hands down one of my favorite professors. She is not only a great speaker, but she is also very actively engaged and inspirational. She truly values participation from everyone, creating an environment open to dialogue and discourse on current events. Show up and actively engage!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I took her class on Global China. It's very conversation-based and participatory, which makes sense because so many students have personal experiences that are valuable for the material. She asks a lot of questions and seems to genuinely want to know what we think.

Professor Chang is amazing, she truly cares about her students and gets to know them. She is strict about homework; you can't go over the word limit or get points off. Go to her office hours if you need help or just to talk she will listen to you, she truly is an amazing professor.

Really appreciate it if she would focus on teaching the material > projecting her own political views on what the future state should be. 

References are frankly out of date, inapplicable to the real world. 

Advice: less of your own political views.

Lectures are welcoming, participatory, she memorizes names, warm. But, lectures are simplistic, and even as someone who agrees with her stance, she is very biased and soap-boxy in presenting economic perspectives. Doesn't substantiate counter arguments enough. Online exams, clear grading criteria, group project replaces term paper.

Prof Chang is incredible, she is a true educator. She has very unapologetic views, but challenges students to critically think and challenge the world around us. I wish I could take the class again, each lecture is so packed and leaves me with so many thoughts
Very prejudiced, stubborn. tough grader, she only listens to the opinions she wants to hear and doesn't accept any other opinions.

She's extremely biased. I don't think her course is either taught or managed poorly but after PE100 I expected so much more. I don't need to know what the professor's opinions are I just need to know what the arguments of the authors were and understand where they're coming from. However she would straw man those she disagreed with.
Discussion-based lectures; encouraged students meeting each other, and successfully had students become closer together within context of class. Material was interesting, but not overwhelming
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I've had. Lectures are not just a repeat of readings; they expand upon content and discuss current real-world issues relevant to course topics. Professor creates super welcoming environment. Class participation is encouraged often, but not in a stressful way. Good class discussions. Make sure to do the readings!!

Professor Chang's class provided so many different perspectives throughout her lectures! She truly gets to know each of her students. I would recommend her class to anymore looking for a lot of group discussion and an interactive course. There is a weekly assignment each week that includes readings as well.

I got an A in this class, it's not hard. 

Professor Chang is picky, and not compassionate when students are sick. On assignments, going even 5 words above/below the word count causes point-deduction. I once had a high fever and asked for a paper extension. Professor's response was 'no', and that I'd get a grade penalty if I didn't submit on time.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is my favorite professor!  I love her teaching style, so engaging and inspirational, and I feel excited to share my feelings about China and India in class. She gives me good advice on my future plans, she is so caring and amazing! I love her so much! It is mot so hard to get good grade in her class, you won't regret to choose her class!

Dr. Chang's class is one of my favorite courses I've ever taken at Berkeley. I learned so much! The course is very discussion based and she is very open to hearing about everyone's individual experiences and input. One of the few professors that will get to know you. I would definitely reccomend her.

She goes on tangents and puts up huge blocks of text on her slides but Chang is a solid professor overall. She does a really good job of tackling a subject that no one is going to agree on. If you can, go to office hours. She cares so much about her students and genuinely wants them to succeed.

Prof CCC is the best professor I have met in Berkeley. She is really caring and helpful. Besides she is also really curious to guide us to explore the meaning and the future. When the last class ends, most of the students want to have a hug her, because she is so nice and the lecture, homework, readings, and tests are really easy.

polecon 100 with karras was one of my favorite classes that I've taken in berkeley so this has been a serious letdown. the class seems disproportionately focused on points and writing quality rather than the application of theory. lost points on the midterm for going over 5 words over a 350 word limit. if you write 360 words, you're losing points.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of the worst class Ive taken in Berkeley.

This is a larger class, so less one-on-one time with the prof. I participated more in section and managed to get an A+ with good papers. Prof really likes succinct work, so be INTENTIONAL with every sentence you write. She is also great to talk to in smaller settings so I encourage going to office hours!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Professor Chang is one of my favorite professors. She is caring, kind, and engaging, esp. in smaller classes. She remembers people's names and anecdotes and shares her own. She creates a learning environment where you aren't afraid to ask questions and dig deeper. She grades fairly, but can be harsh. Do your reading and participate for good grades.

I was nervous going into the class, but Professor Chang has been one of my best profs at Cal. There was a lot of reading involved & short (2-3 question) quizzes just to make sure you actually read; I failed a lot of these but still got an A-. People say grading was tough, but I found she was fair (a few 1 pg responses to readings through the sem).
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Gives great lectures, and consistently engages with the class. She encourages student input and participation at every stage. Political Economy is such an important subject and Professor Chang conveys that.

Although professor Chang has the best intentions, her lectures are extremely biased toward her hyper-liberal ideologies. Her perspective is limited to her narrow conception of the current political climate, and it is clear that she does not have the proper education to combat or support her opinions that are the foundation of many of her lectures.

-Participation is essential so take the class only if you're really interested. -She is amazing to listen to and discuss topics with! -She was genuine and nice and her stories were very enjoyable and interesting!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Her class was interesting & she is great to discuss lecture materials and current events, but her grading is somewhat biased. She would grade me very harshly and ask whether I was inserting my own ideas and opinions into a book report we did, but I had gotten the material right from the book and showed it to her. You have to accommodate her style.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She is amazing. I took two classes with her, and so far, she is one of the best professors I know. Her feedback is very helpful, and she cares about each student. Her instruction is extremely clear. I recommend going to office hour.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: I had Professor Chang for both PS 144 and IAS 150. She is very, very picky when it comes to grading, so make sure to read her instructions carefully.  If she says to stick to the 500 word limit, you better stick to it! Overall an awesome professor.
She's a terrific professor, but she grades tooooooooooo hard.

Chang is a kind and compassionate woman. She apologized more often than a professor should for sharing opinions that some of her students did not supports. College level students should not be offended by the concept of a professor with an actual opinion on politics. Aside from that, reading was a bit extreme,  but course work was standard.

Very enthusiastic and extremely knowledgeable. open minded and allows varied opinions to discuss points. She is opinionated but even in disagreement she makes sure everyone feels welcome to discuss. I chose cal because of professors like her. One issue is the essay promts are EXTREMELY vague which can hurt grade if not on the same page with the gsi

Pretty cool, enthusiastic. Originally had an A, but she decided to 'curve' my participation grade down from 100% to about 80%? Her rationale? She doesn't want too many As in her class, because she thinks Bs are 'good' to toughen you up. Make your syllabus harder so that curves are actually justified.

Professor Chang is fantastic! She's a very engaging lecturer, and you can tell she's really enthusiastic about both teaching and the course material. The class is well structured, and she's open minded and asking students to jump in with their opinions. It's a little reading-heavy, but definitely worth taking!

Professor Chang is a great professor! She always appeared enthusiastic. Her class was well-organized. Slideshows were posted after the class. I prefer them to be posted prior to each lecture . She is very helpful outside of the class. Overall, great professor! English is my third language, my writing has improved a lot after taking her class.

This was a great class. I left with a greater understanding of how the history of China and India shaped the economic and political landscape of both countries today. It was a lot of work, but Dr. Chang was nothing but helpful.

Professor Chang is the best! :) She is incredibly knowledgeable and really makes an effort to know her students by their name! Very organized, prepared, and engaging! Be sure to visit her in office hours!!

Professor Chang is an awesome professor. The class is really difficult, however, & in order to achieve you need to go to class regularly, read every assignment, & put in a lot of effort. She gives out very few A's so you HAVE TO go to office hours & ask questions because the readings can be difficult. Also, she's very eager to help & so passionate!

Great class! I noticed a dramatic increase in my organization, research and writing skills upon completion of the course. I have already enrolled in Dr. Chang’s ASN 150: “Emerging Giants, China and India,” for the next semester and look forward to spending another semester  learning from her and about these rising super powers in Asia.

Dr. Crystal Chang is one of the most helpful and enthusiastic professors I have had the pleasure of learning from. She always keeps office hours and returns emails.she enjoys seeing her students writing skills improve while learning the course material. Asian Studies 10 is an introductory course that covers a wide variety of topics in Asia.

very difficult to get a good grade. "B" is considered a great grade, very few A's handed out. grading gets harder as the year progresses. must pay strict attention to lectures and reading to get a good grade. teacher is unforgiving but extremely passionate about the subject.

Professor Chang is an enthusiastic and great lecturer who is very open to discussion in class.This class definitely offers a comprehensive overview of comparative politics and is graded generously. I loved the course and the professor! Definitely recommend taking her class if you are interested in nice intro to comparative politics!

She had a bad habit of playing pundit, making inaccurate statements, and saying, "I'm not an expert!" Even tangents should be factual when students consider you an authority. If you don't want to fact check tangents, don't go on tangents. Lectures just went over the readings, which were way too long. The midterm and final were take-home.

I think it may have been her first time teaching it but this class was not well structured. My GSI was very helpful though and the material was overall pretty good, though she would go over some things for too long and fail to focus on more important things. Readings are somewhat necessary and tests, while difficult, are graded pretty forgivingly.

Very interesting class and passionate professor. Speaks quickly and doesn't share his slides so you need to pay attention but exams are open note. He prefers handwritten notes and staying off screens in class but allows printed notes for exams. Participate in the image analysis exercises in class: he's very encouraging towards all contributions.

Amazing class. Lectures always interesting and diverse topics. 3 big projects, midterm, final. Midterm and final both very open ended (in good way) and open book. Reading load not too heavy and you can cherry pick. Attendance not mandatory but you miss out on notes. He doesn't use text slides (just images). He's invested in teaching so talk to him!

Incredible lecturer. When he opened the class talking about railroads I was ready to be bored out of my mind, but it was way more interesting than lectures in topics I care about. 

If you don't care about humanities classes, I would not take Dr. Craghead's class. He is a lax grader for people who clearly care about the class, but not if you don't.

Really great + interesting class that provides a comprehensive overview of American landscapes and their component parts through cultural geography, architecture, and history. Reading heavy and grade comes down to midterm, final, and 3 papers/projects but instructions are clear. Prof knows his content really well and has a down to earth vibe.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really enjoyed the class! No homework but you do have projects that ain't to much of a burden.
This professor gives zero guidelines or directions on his papers but expects them to be done his way

My favorite professor I've had so far. Lectures are very engaging and bring lots of information. Professor Craghead is also a super genuine and caring person and really wants to see students do well. The class is steered more towards art and culture, so don't expect it to just be another history class. No weekly/daily homework is great too!

He is a great professor who has really fun/open-ended assignments. Easy class, however, going to lectures is essential if you want to get a good grade (he does not post the slides). No homework for the class. Only 3 straightforward assignments. The class has a Midterm and final which are somewhat hard (made easier by open-book and open-note policy)

Professor Craghead's class about U.S. culture in the 1930s was a great accompaniment to my historical studies of the era. The lectures were engaging, and the coursework consisted of an online midterm and final which were fairly graded, and the other assignments allow students to combine creativity and thoughtful analysis.

I found that Professor Craghead's intro course to American Studies was a great way to start thinking about all the factors that shaped American culture in the twentieth century. The lectures were all entertaining and offered insights that I was able to use in other areas of my studies.

Nice and occasionally relatable and funny dude that encourages discussion and questions, but I found it hard to enjoy the subject matter: movements in architecture, crafts, etc. I chalk that up to personal preference, though. Aside from that, my main issues were that he talks a bit fast in lecture and that assignment grade weights were unclear.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Seems like a nice guy but I would not recommend. Unclear grading by very few things. Maybe it's my fault expecting it to be more history oriented, because this class was definitely rooted in art and culture (which would be fine if easy A, but it's not). Interesting at times but I often wondered if any of this information would be useful in life
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: "Making in America" has very interesting content from suburbia, to company towns, burning man, and American film. There is a ton of reading that makes up most of the midterm and final. Grading and expectations can be confusing. Wants you to engage with the material and challenge it, while simultaneously coming to the same conclusions he has.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Very funny and engaging, though I personally found 137B to be pretty hard (partly my fault for slacking). Lectures helped build intuition but didn't always feel that useful. Tests were weird, I don't know if I like his style of giving a bunch of problems but letting you skip all the computation. Would take him again just for the personality tbh!

My only problem with professor Crommie is that I couldnt take him for every physics class. I had him for 141A and 137b, 141A is a monster of a class but he makes it so interesting and doesnt leave out any important details. I think other professors should really learn from this guy, he is very special. Team Crommie!!
Prof. Crommie is great. Lectures are super insightful and entertaining. Really does a good job of making Quantum Mechanics tractable, and motivates his lectures with experiments.

Lectures were understandable and well-paced. Crommie is great at providing physical insight and making the math easy to follow. Encourages student participation but isn't good at answering piazza questions. Homeworks and exams were pretty standard for a physics class.

He's the only professor I've met in the Physics department so far that seems to take his job as a professor and instructor of students seriously. He's committed to his students learning and it really shows in his lectures. He goes above and beyond to teach the material in a way that supplements the book not quotes it. This helps with intuition.
Decent professor. But never seen somebody so messy on the board... like jolts stuff all over the place. Hard to follow

Amazing Professor. He gives very intuitive explanations and he's very funny, quirky, relatable, and nice. He wants to help students. Doesn't throw any curveballs either. Only minor complaints were lack of practice material and tedious HW assignments at times, though that could have been because of the GSI.

I seriously cannot believe how great this guy is. Please, please, please take him! Youll be doing yourself a disservice by picking someone else. Go to every office hour! Youll learn more and seeing from Crommies lectures, repetition is key to learning physics. Hes not trying to trick you, hes there to help you learn. I was very afraid of

Hes legitimately the best Professor I have had at Cal, and Ive had experience with a lot of them in the physics department. Im the type of person that finds it difficult to pay attention during lecture and I learn from reading the book, but with Crommie, it was completely the oppositeI learned everything just watching him lecture. Caring guy 2.

His lectures are very intuitive, I was afraid of 137B because it was a tough class, but he made course materials easy to understand; it was even hard not to follow his steps during his lectures. Also, he gives us many hints for homework problems during office hours. For me, he was the best teacher so far.

Professor Crommie tends to be disorganised in lecture, although the topics covered by the course are very interesting. Be ready to read in not just the required course textbook, but many other textbooks, if you truly want to understand and do well in the class. Exams are a lot more difficult than homework and lecture examples.

really straightforward professor when it comes to the material at hand, but very witty in the way he delivers it to the class. really easy going and lenient. Just learn the material and you will get an A.
He is very clear; good at explaining things intuitively. He is also very funny and quirky.
One of the best common sense explainers, he tries to make everything very intuitive despite the non intuitive nature of the subject. one of the best teachers ive had.

He is funny and clear most of the time in lecture. I really enjoyed his class even though both the homework and exams are pretty difficult. I recommend him if you really enjoy physics and want to understand the material well. But like I said, his class is a little tough in my opinion.
Mike's a really helpful, straightforward and articulate guy.  Looking forward to another class with him.

Really quirky and funny. He will make the abstract world of QM very friendly and happy.  I enjoyed going to lecture. The homeworks are somewhat difficult but the tests are straightforward and you don't have to evaluate integrals. Crommie will make you love physics!

I signed up to this website just so I could rate this guy. He's totally amazing and FUNNY FUNNY FUNNY. Very entertaining lectures and clear explanations. Homework was pretty rigorous and midterm and final are fair. Generous curve. If you can take a class with him, I recommend it. I myself am looking forward to someday in the future have him again.
His lectures are great! He makes them interesting and funny.

First of all, this class is pointless, and should be abolished. He does not do a good job of choosing text books, or homework assignments, usually lectures are written at 2 am the night before the class. Nice guy, and helpful in office hours, but boardwork needs to improve.

Incredibly kind and caring professor, wish he could teach every CivE class! Cruz only taught labs for CE60 this semester but I learned more from him than the lecturer. Very engaging and tends to build relationships with his classes over time.
Professor Cruz is the best!!

Cruz is an amazing professor! He deeply cares about his students and makes you love the topic of the class, despite how boring it may initially seem. He focuses heavily on learning, so midterms are take home and unlimited attempts. Labs are super fun and worthwhile even though the lab reports can be a lot of work. I highly recommend!

I took him in fall 2021. So far most friendly professor I found in Berkeley. He will make you love concrete. After our class got C in first mid, He made rest of exams multiple choice and drop our mid. I still misses him and visit his lab sometimes. Labs are super fun and you will make friends. You should take this class even if not in engineering.

Professor Carlos has such a cheerful attitude and genuine passion for his area of study that you can't help but enjoy learning about seemingly, and deceivingly, mundane topics such as the type of rocks you use to make concrete. The workload was concise and to the point. I also never thought I'd be excited for concrete to dry just to crush it.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Prof. Carlos is amazing! His lectures are extremely engaging, and helps you understand the material much more than the textbook (go to class!). The labs and accompanying lab reports can be long but aside from that, the class is reasonable. HW weekly, but it isn't too much. Carlos is very passionate about materials and makes the class very fun. :)

Best professor I've had at Berkeley so far! Professor Carlos is very accommodating + friendly. Tests are fair and short: all q's are taken from lecture content. Labs are hands-on + v interesting. Professors like Carlos at Berkeley are rare--he is both very knowledgeable on his subject and very good at explaining it. Would take again 100%

Cruz really cares about his students. He is so funny, helpful in office hours, and his lectures are engaging and help with understanding of the material. tests are fair and just enough hw for extra practice. labs are long but fun! Cruz is a King he is so sweet!!!!! Best prof ive had at Cal so far

A truly wonderful professor. Always smiling and exuding a warm vibe. Super clear and easy to follow instruction, highly accessible, and truly cares that her students do well. You wont regret taking her.

I could not recommend Cristina more! She is so caring and attentive as a professor, and consistently gives great feedback. 
She's a really kind grader, and will often give you points for effort if she can tell you understand
Professoressa Farronato is a really really nice person and an amazing instructor. Totally recommend her classes!

Professor Mora will do more than teach you- she will inspire and really educate you. Even on uncomfortable topics, Professor Mora emphasizes the importance of education, plus she makes every lecture exciting and worth attending. Regularly reading-based in-class quizzes keep you on your toes, so attendance is mandatory.

Professor Mora is the definition of a success story and always provides the class with material and motivation so we too can become one. She's so smart, funny, and a great resource. If you're looking for inspiration on being an absolute boss in Sociology- she's your girl to model after. Take her class!
Professor Mora is super passionate about her work and the class was really inspiring, even if sad at times (because of the content). Learned a lot through the class and would highly recommend.

I took her CHICANO C144L course which is a Chicanx-Sociology hybrid class. She was very relatable and inspirational. Highly recommend this course, especially if you're from SoCal. Readings are rough and sort of boring, but if you skim them you'll be okay.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I actually took her CHICANO C144L which is a Chicanx and Sociology hybrid class and it did not disappoint. Her lectures and the material she taught was all breathtaking. Every single Lecture and Reading assignment did not disappoint in being interesting. The information she teaches is 100% worth while and I would definitely take this class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: First review I've ever written because Prof mora is amazing! During covid, she was extremely generous and caring and made a huge effort to help students succeed during these tough times. The content is really interesting too! The class itself is easy as long as you take notes and do the readings. Mora is super sweet and helpful! 100% recommend her!

Her class is hard to follow but not hard to get an A in, because she gives you all of the exam questions before each midterm which are 3- each 30% of your grade. If you get a good study group together its super easy to do well in the class with little effort. Super dry readings and horrible, bare slides but interesting material and a fairly easy A!
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Good researcher. Readings mostly from top journals such as AJS or ASR. Sound preparation for Socio major who wants to go to graduate school. (Ivester, for example, focuses on empirical side) However, hard for non-major who happens to be interested in culture or wants to fulfill Arts/Literature Breadth in terms of both content and grading.

This class sucked. I thought it would be such an interesting topic but her lectures were terrible. I came to every class and still got a D because who ever was my reader graded harshly. Readings were not talked about in lecture much but were heavy on exam. WORST prof at CAL i have had although she is nice, her class stinks.

Super fun and amazing!! I loved this course so much and I felt that it was really well structured and just overall super informative. Craig Miller is one of my favorite professors here at Cal and I highly recommend!! He helps with all questions and takes the time to help his students succeed. I feel that he genuinely cares for his students.

A bit monotone but he makes the material he teaches actually interesting and applicable to medicine/bio. He always has a slide that lists all the key concepts from the lecture, and those are really pretty much all you need to know. His section isn't much memorization and is mostly conceptual, which I appreciated. Good professor all around

I thought I would hate this section but he actually did a pretty good job of making the subject interesting and easy to study. Recorded lectures, knew them backwards and forwards, and aced the exam. Pretty dry in lecture but I feel like I actually understand genomics!

He is a very nice person and very much willing to help, but his part of class "genomics" was the hardest for me. He speaks too fast and if English is your second language, may God help you. I recorded his lectures and tried to listen to him at home to understand him. The average of the class was high for his exam, so maybe it's me and my English!

Professor Miller is the nicest professor I have ever had. He is adorable. Many people complain that he's monotonous during lecture, but he is extremely helpful during office hours. He will stay in office hours as long as there are questions and will often stay for HOURS. I love this man.

Professor Cutler was an exceptional individual who genuinely prioritized teaching. Throughout each lecture, his commitment to the subject matter was evident as he actively engaged with students, asking for their thoughts on the assigned readings. We had a few quizzes, collaborative efforts were allowed, and only two essays were required.

few discussions and quizzes, and there's only 2 essays to do. everything is based on the readings/what we learned in class. our grade depends on what we think we deserve which is amazing! he's hilarious and truly one of the best professors in the English department. take a class with him if you can!

[For ENG 37] Prof. Cutler is an amazing, caring professor who clearly cares about everything he has hand-picked to teach. He feels like a friend telling you about something cool he learned about in class, and his constant re-centering around historic and cultural relevance is on point. Occasional quizzes in class and attendance mandatory.

Professor Cutler is new to Berkeley, and he is kind and smart. He incorporates many things into grades (quizzes, a group project, papers, attendance). Your grade relies too much on the pretentious reader; I got an A- on the first paper and he said the paper is amazing but you still get an A- because no one is perfect and I'm nitpicky like that

Really nice, interesting professor. Very kind and respectful. His grading is fair but my experience with his GSI was pretty bad. The GSI graded super harshly and had a bad attitude when the professor called them out on it after seeing their feedback on my paper. Cutler himself tho is wonderful. 4 papers + group project, manageable reading schedule
