Took Professor Crockett with GSI Jenny this spring for Leibniz. The material is challenging but Jenny and Crockett are kind and super cool. The goal is for you to actually go out into the world and be able to speak on the material. Graded by 3 papers and 1 final. Definitely an upper division class to add if you actually want to "learn something"
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This is my second time taking a class with Professor Crockett, and I can't recommend his classes enough! He provides handouts at the beginning of each class, which is extremely helpful. The content is very dense, but Professor Crockett is extremely helpful in office hours, which I highly recommend going to if you want to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Interesting lecturer. He would explain the readings in a thorough and comprehensive way that made even the most difficult concepts easy to grasp. Very organized notes and lectures. He was careful to present the material with as little bias as possible as it dealt with religion. Our grade consisted of participation, 3 papers, and a final exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Crockett was an excellent professor and did a great job making the content interesting and approachable for the class

Dr. Crockett lectured for this course on modern philosophy which is his area of research. He was enthusiastic and lucid with his explanations and thanks to that I got a lot out of his class, even though it was a condensed summer format. The GSI for the class wasn't very good, but I suppose Dr. Crockett couldn't really have done anything about that.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: perfectly swell guy

Took Prof. Crockett's class on Environmental Ethics. As a seminar, the usual week would include two 10-page readings, one before each class, and three papers over the semester (4, 4, 10 pages). Crockett is incredibly kind, listens attentively even over the 1.5 hour discussion, and open for office hours. Not a lot of feedback on papers though.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Great professor. Took him for Proseminar on Race. He did his best to handle an admittedly hot-button issue in as unbiased a manner as possible. Huge amounts of reading though, so make sure you budget time for the course. Attendance is mandatory though, since it is a seminar. Professor was very kind and patient, and very accessible. A must-take
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Crockett is a clear, knowledgeable lecturer, and an incredibly kind, gracious person. As always, the university is taking advantage of the adjunct, making him teach 2-3 courses every semester, for peanuts I'm sure. But he keeps it up and seems to genuinely love teaching and care about his students.

Professor Crockett is the best philosophy professor I've ever had. Presents the material in such a clear and easy way to understand and also connects it with examples that really get the point across. Such a kind person and really accessible with office hours. Grade is based on GSI and she was really amazing as well! 3 papers + final
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Rough . Not as progressive as I was hoping- It was my last hope for the philosophy major, I realized I wouldnt find what I wanted in this course, or from philosophy in general. Inaccessible language (which was ironic) and conversations were bogged down by the terminology. Not too difficult of a class, though. There's that.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Content was interesting, but readings really dense. Lectures are super dry for a class on contemporary ethical issues. Wished that lecture would be more interesting, connected to real world applications, and less focused on consequentialism. He is nice and has many office hours slots. How well you do depends on your GSI, and mine was great.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Crockett is the kindest professor I have met in my academic career. He is genuinely interested in student's questions and encourages participation. He stays after class to answer questions and opens up his office hours to all who enter. His class requires a lot of reading, but you want to engage with him in the material (you will get more out)
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Prof. Crockett is great, but its not my type of learning. Heavily lecture based. Hardly any homework. He knows the material well, but I wont take again bcuz of how the class works. I want more homework in order for me to be motivated to do the readings. Lectures were quite dull at times imo but its great if you want a simple, specific class.
Hands down the best professor that I have ever had. The nicest guy in the world -- a real gem.

I wasnt sure what to expect when it came to my first philosophy class, but I can say without a doubt that Crockett made my first philos class quite enjoyable. His lectures are thorough and dissect the important parts of the readings, so just skim them the night before. The 3 papers are all graded by the GSI, and the final study guide is clutch.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Three essays and a final. That's it. He just sits in his office for like two hours a day, twice a week waiting for students to pop in. If you don't get something, just ask him. The essays are only hard if you don't go to class or don't talk to him AT ALL, EVER. You do have to read, though. If you don't, you won't pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is very knowledgeable but his lectures can be incredibly slow, boring, and seem random at some points. Your grade in class heavily relies on your GSI. You will have three essays and a final test. He gives you a good study guide for the final. I would say avoid the class if your not a physiology major as you will have to put in A LOT of time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: 3 take home papers and one final exam. If you don't understand something, make sure to consult him during office hours and he'll make a lot of clear analogies.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Amazing professor! His lectures are extremely helpful because he goes over the readings in great detail and breaks it down step by step so its easy to comprehend. The material is complicated but he makes it really easy to follow along! Straightforward grading with a few take home essays & a final exam. Really accessible outside of class as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof. Crockett's lectures were dry and lackluster for a course on ethnicity, race, and citizenship. Lectures reiterated premises and arguments found in readings and rarely touched on application to the real world. Otherwise, he is pretty clear and willing to answer questions while engaging with students in lecture. Graded on 3 essays and a final.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I don't usually write about professors' personal traits, but I think it's worth mentioning that Prof. Crockett is a great person. He goes above and beyond to help students all the time and seems to really care about them. Someone should give him an award or something (seriously).
The nicest guy on the planet. His classes are difficult, but he is helpful and approachable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Hilarious

reviews.comment: One of the best philosopher professor I ever have! His lecture may seem hard to grasp at first (b/c of all the terms), but TAKE DOWN HIS LECTURE WORD FOR WORD. Then, his lectures become REALLY CLEAR. Much clearer than the reading itself! Readings are the original text translated; IMHO, a summary would have been better for this intro class
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is really knowledgeable and his lectures do a great job breaking down the dense material from readings. Do the readings! At least skim them and get a general idea of what to expect. You don't have to fully understand the reading though because it can be difficult. There are three midterm essays and he gives out a study guide for the final!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I've heard he's "one of the better philosophy teachers @ UCB," which is a scary enough prospect. Clearly, I'm accustomed to much bwtter teaching styles bc it's as if he was speaking a foreign language I didn't understand. I chalked it up to that he knows so much that it's hard for him to simlify complex ideas into everyday terms. I didn't like him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: My favorite professor in the Philosophy department at UC Berkeley thus far. Spinoza was an extremely tough class for me, but Prof Crockett really helped
Perfect lectures, really interesting and explain things clearly.

Professor Crockett is a great professor. Since this is a lower-division course, it isn't very difficult. The grading is clear. While enough information is on the slides for the assignments (papers), you should come to class. Crockett breaks the information down during lectures, and it's tough to do the final without the additional info in lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Very clear, calm and accessible professor. Philosophical concepts can be hard to grasp, but Tim breaks it down in a nice and thorough way. His lectures are so clear and to the point that even if you don't do the readings you'll probably find his lectures sufficient (it's a very reading-heavy course).
calm & clear style. interested in your point of view and cares a lot about students. loved going to his class.

Professor Crockett is one of the nicest professors.  Lectures can be very slow, but mostly due to him being committed to clarity. Final was exactly as expected given his final prep. If you don't go to lecture, his lecture notes are clear enough.  I missed 7 our of 24 of the lectures which was fine.  I wouldn't miss much more than that.
Overall average class. Crockett has pretty dry lectures, so the notes are vital. Spinoza is naturally a very confusing philosopher, so Crockett has that to deal with. Reading the book is essential.

Crockett is probably the best lecturer in the phil dept. Unlike some profs, he is very methodical with his lectures, walks you step-by-step through the arguments, and uses the board a lot to map out ideas, making even the most complex ideas easy. As others have noted, make sure to go to lecture because he explains many things not in the reading.

Crockett is clear and responsive in lecture, and fun to talk to in OH. He cares about his students. He even brings the list with student names and photos to learn names. He also offers plenty of OH throughout the semester. The only thing to complain is his lectures can be dry and you might lose interest at some point. Try recording the lectures.
humor professor and always glad to answer the questions!

It's amazing how he balances giving a detailed rundown of every modern philosopher's beliefs, counter-arguments, and having time for students to ask questions. He really takes his time, too, in answering these questions to the best of his abilities. He has office hours if you need help on his papers, which can be enlightening. GO TO CLASS.

You can tell he cares about getting the material across to his students. He takes the dense, confusing material and does his best to simplify it. Expect a lot of reading and writing 3 take home tests. Final was fairly simple and straightforward. I recommend this Professor!

3 papers and an in-class final centered around lectures. You can do the reading at home, but ideas presented by Prof, including  interpretations of certain passages, are essential knowledge for success on papers. So, lectures are mandatory in spirit. Extremely responsive to Q's and is sincerely invested in student understanding. Amazing Prof.
Such a sweet Professor, loved my summer Berkeley experience because of him!
He was honestly amazing one of the best classes I have taken. He truly cares for you and you will enjoy this class

Such a sweetheart. You can tell he is incredibly passionate about the things he teaches about. Class assignments are incredibly easy and straightforward. We even took a field trip to his house where he showcased his vintage poster collection and fed us bagels. I would 100% take again.

Professor Cuffey was great. Lectures were sometimes slow and made me tired. He has a course reader ($15) that he bases his material off of. His midterm and his final were very straightforward and nothing we did not expect. Overall, great professor. And yes, he is also quite funny.

Professor Cuffey is undoubtedly my favorite teacher, and his GEOG 140A course stands out as the most enjoyable class I've taken. His extensive knowledge, enthusiasm, and genuine care for students truly set him apart. While his jokes may not leave you in stitches, they certainly bring a smile to your face and brighten your day.
Definitely recommend. Lectures are hilarious and engaging. He makes the class fun and is great wt working with students

I had him for 140A and 140B and he is simply the best. He's super down to earth, a great lecturer, and challenges you intellectually without making you feel pressured. I was a social concentration so I didn't care about the science stuff at all at first, but he actually made me like the content. Also, he's super funny. Recommend him highly.

Cuffey is a great professor. very nice and engaging in lectures and definitely very knowledgeable. Make sure to prep for the tests but the exams do seem pretty fair though, mostly multiple-choice and all stuff he covered in lecture. Just take detailed notes and enjoy the ride! I highly recommend taking a class from Cuffey, 100% would take it again.

Prof Cuffey is a fun, knowledgable instructor. Works hard to ensure students understand  and uses humor to make class enjoyable. Okay with laptops and photos of diagrams for later review. Uses self-made handbook for note taking which is helpful and many photo slides to further concepts. Tests can be tough, so take good notes and you'll learn a lot!

I love physical geography and this is the best class I have taken since I transferred to UCB. Prof. Kurt is humorous. It helps me stay awake in class. I don't mean the class is boring but it is tough so it requires a lot of energy and focus during class. Sit in the front and take detail notes. Put a lot of markings on your map. Don't skip class!!!!

Professor Cuffey is extremely knowledgeable and gives fun lectures. I always looked forward to going to class. Only three graded assignments. not too bad if you just put in some time and study. really excited to take 140B with him next semester!

Kurt Cuffey is by far my favorite professor at Cal. Deeply knowledgeable and passionate about both teaching and the subject matter, his lectures are easygoing, hilarious, and inspiring. He is held in very high regard by all his students, and for good measure. Take his class, you won't regret it.

If you are at Cal, and you love physical Earth science, and you do not take Kurt Cuffey's class, you are wasting your time there. He is the most incredible professor I have ever had and is respected and held in very high regard by all. You won't want to miss lecture, but go to his office hrs! Best best A+++!!!

Cuffey is one of the best professors I had at Cal. He has an easygoing style of lecturing that is both enlightening and entertaining--he's really funny! You need to go to class otherwise its easy to get behind. And know specific exs of landforms he talks about on the US map the class requires for tests. Not an easy class but not hard if you study.
Kurt Cuffey is the by far the best professor I ever had at Berkeley. He is interesting, challenging and very funny. He is inspiring and really wants his students to understand what he is teaching.
Great Professor, great course! I highly recommend taking a class with Cuffey even if you are not a geog student.
Show up, laugh at his jokes (won't be hard), study, and get an A. No need for textbooks as only lecture material is on exams.
Great teacher, many funny comments and very interesting... lots of Extra Credit opportunity

Took Geog 40, 140A/B and 141 with Kurt. He's a great professor, plain and simple. Easily my favorite while at Cal. His courses were the most interesting and he's clear with what he discusses. Great for the Geography majors to those just looking to fill a requirement.

Great teacher and a great guy. Cuffey posesses a deep understanding understanding of the earth's interrelated physical processes and imparts his knowledge to you in a note-friendly, easy to follow format. My favorite instructor at Berkeley.
Kurt is an amazing teacher.  He explains material very well and takes student learning seriously.  He has a great sense of humor, which makes class go by quickly.  I would recommend hands donw.
No Comments
She was not good.

Her notes were beautiful and I really like her blazers. Tests were difficult, but fair. I wish she made her lectures more personal, but it was probably due to the dense nature of the material. I suggest reading the txtbook before the lecture. Labs and hw are a decent chunk of the grade so don't slack. Really enjoyed this class :)

Tanja gives extremely clear lectures, especially important since quantum chemistry your first semester can be really difficult. The problem sets were relevant, and both midterms in her half of the class were hard, but fair. Many people said her office hours were extremely helpful, but I personally didn't go to them.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: At first many students including myself were caught off guard by the fast paced and dense lectures, but after the first few I really came to appreciate how well she knew her stuff and explained tough concepts. Assignments were really interesting  and challenging but helped me learn. Tests were fair.
Lectures are fast paced and dense, but she does a fantastic job of explaining concepts. Office hours are very helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Very engaging lectures. She covers tough stuff, but I always walked out feeling informed and curious to learn more.  Tests follow exactly what she covers in lecture, so the textbook is just a supplement. Labs and homework are all from the GSI team, but she does her personal part very well. Bonus: Cool demos.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Tanja is one of the best professors at Cal. She explains abstract, convoluted concepts very well. Her exams are tough, but as long as you pay attention to the class and review materials well, you are OK. Her office hour is really helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: It's a hard topic but Cuk tries (unsuccessfully) to explain concepts in the large lecture; go to her office hours and it's a lot more helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Tough exams that cover mostly obscure topics from lecture, confusing explanations that seem as if they were made up on the spot. Tanja has a cute accent and refers to electrons as "little guys." Lab for this class is absolutely brutal, expect to spend four hours in lab per week and at least 10 on pre/post lab write-ups.

She's very inexperienced with teaching. Lecture materials are not as well organized and are from mostly places other than the course textbook. She only writes with chalk and the class is very fast-paced and hard to follow.
Lectures were hard to understand, homework was very helpful, tests were somewhat difficult but fair

CS162 is one of the hardest cs classes but its my favorite by far because of Culler. No one goes to his office hours so I basically got private tutoring two days a week. He also often asked how I thought certain homeworks/projects/exams were and how they could be improved and seemed to take my feedback seriously. Overall a very caring guy :)

Doesn't seem to care about teaching at the undergrad level. I had a doctor's appointment and missed the lecture before the midterm, so I missed directions to memorize the section number (five digit code) to write on the exam. I wrote the time and TA's name instead. He marked me down an entire letter grade on the exam despite my TA trying to help.
A reasonably good lecturer, but the labs were always more helpful.  I think he would've done better if he had more than, like, 12 lectures per semester.

Do not take the lab format of this class and do not take it from Culler.  Wait for Dan Garcia to teach it.  Culler only gave 10 lectures and wasn't clear at all.  The only students who did well watched Garcia's webcasts and skipped class, seriously!

Culler is not a good lecturer or interesting speaker despite his high HKN ratings. Midterms 1/2 were pretty easy, but midterm 3 was very difficult. Lectures have no format/organization, avoid Culler and try to take CS150 with Katz if you can. Culler (or his staff) also has many problems with course logistics (for example, getting hw solutions out).
doesn't know anything. he would look at his notes the entire lecture and made the material so so uninteresting and confusing. ugh and i love art history but this class was a DUD

One of the worst GSI in the department. He has his favorite students and the students he likes to torment for no reason. Also he is absolutely no help in understanding the material - doesn't talk clearly and often told us different things from what was said in class.
great prof
With surgical focus, he stared at me and said "I'm willing to reach out, get into your head"
Meh. Matt's okay. His discussions did not aid me in understanding the lecture. It doesn't help that the course itself is incredibly boring and humdrum, but what can you do.

You know, Matt was super nice for this class. He was always willing to help, and if you actually just TALK to him he's pretty chill. He's even nice about essays. Basically he's just a chill dude. Always willing to meet for office hours and talk about the material.
Very helpful teacher and interesting lecturer.

One of the nicest and most caring people in UCB music department. The material is hard and somewhat boring but he managed to make it interesting. He is not focused and loses clarity during lecture  but my overall experience was very good. Too bad he does not teach in Cal anymore!

Sean is the most caring prof I've had at Cal. He is very knowledgeable and passionate. He is straightforward with the class for when we need to step it up which is great because I want my teachers to push me to be better. He is great in OH, going above and beyond to help in any way. Lastly, he is funny and has a great singing voice. Thanks Sean!
Sean is an excellent instructor and my favorite GSI. Take his class!

Sean was probably one of the most articulate, entertaining, and intellectual GSI's I've had the pleasure of taking a class from. He occasionally strays from lecture topics, which are quite clear and interesting, to discuss personal topics and current events (which is a reason to not skip class). Take his class, you won't regret it!

Prior to taking the class, I honestly was not anticipating much and was hoping for the class to be a easy A. However, Sean really delivers the material in an interesting and engaging way. I definitely spent more effort in this class than I anticipated. However, I felt that I actually learned something in the end.

When rating Sean, thou shalt rate him 5, no more, no less. 5 shall be the rating thou shalt give, and the rating thou shalt give will be 5. Thou shalt not rate him 6, nor shall thou rate him 4, except that thou then proceed to 5. 7 is right out. Thanks for the great semester Sean!

AMAZING!  He genuinely cares about his students and wants them to succeed.  Very approachable during office hours. Great sense of humor.  He helped us all enjoy and appreciate the music.  Definitely take a class with him if you have the chance.

You'll be lucky if you get him as your teacher..why you ask? because he is the best thing ever. he has a fabulous teaching style, sense of humor(we cried from laughter severl times), and he knows absolutely everything. seriously...he loves music, and teaching. You'll know everything about musicianship after...

sean is a great teacher! his sections are extremely entertaining and informative, and he takes great pride in seeing his students succeed. is very approachable and helpful in office hours and is genuinely dedicated to his studies and his teaching. highly recommend!!

Sean was the most helpful and approachable GSI that I have ever had. He is very clear with his explanations and is eager to help whenever he can. You can tell that he is very passionate about what he teaches and that make being in his class even more enjoyable.

Really great class. Inspired by teacher and material. Challenging, but interesting and engaging. Prof Cudahy was very accessible for help, and obviously wanted her students to thrive and grow in their writing/analysis abilities. One of the best Ive taken at Berkeley.
I absolutely loved this class. It's what inspired me to declare my major. With papers, you write once, get it back, revise it, and turn it in for the actual grade= very good.
You will write four 6-10 page papers. As long as you do the majority of the 25-50 pages of reading per class you will be peachy.Small class=good

This is the worst teacher I've ever encountered at Berkeley. He is VERY unsure of himself and seems extremely nervous and awkward in front of the class. As a result, his teaching is very disorganized and difficult to understand. I learned absolutely NOTHING in his class. He should never be allowed to teach again.

Although he is a graduate student, I do not feel that he should have taught harmony. He was very unsure of himself, and made getting an absolute answer nearly impossible. If it wasn't for the monday group lectures, I'm not sure I would have learned much.
Out of the music 20a teachers, daniel is by FAR the best, he is very funny and will help you individually alot if you need it

Loved taking class with Tita Chat! She made the material very easy to understand, and I feel like my Filipino definitely improved! It may be a bit tough for people who have never had any exposure to the language, but if you've heard a lot of Filipino growing up this class will be an easy A.

such a wonderful and caring professor! such a chill and entertaining class! even if you're not fluent in the language, you can easily pass the class with an A. one thing is that textbook is required 99% of the lectures and take advantage of her review sheets, they'll definitely help you out on the quizzes/midterm/final exam.

Tita Chat was a great professor. She deeply cares for her students and their success, and made herself easily available outside of class for outside help. The class itself requires a lot of verbal participation in order to better understand the material. 10/10, would recommend this class to anyone who wants to take a fun and relatively easy class.

She is a great professor who only wants the best for her students when it comes to learning Filipino. She's a bit difficult to get in touch with outside of class, but use her for help as much as you can because she is funny and informational. You do need to attend class because that is your grade and gives you answers to exams.

I am sure she is a nice person but she just reads off the slides and it doesn't help that she is the one teaching the hardest unit of the class too. Many typos in her exams and some questions had to be redacted from hers. Her section of labs were the worst and her midterm averages were the lowest.
Lecture confusing af, and a lot of typos on her slides
Lectures are very confusing. I go to every lecture but am still confused.

The lecture and slides lack coherence and organization. A systematic exploration of large-scale evolutionary trends is notably absent. As someone with a background in biology Olympiads, although I have no trouble understanding her lecture, I'm still disappointed by the overall quality of the lectures, which caused confusion in many of my classmates

1/3 professors that taught BIO1B for Fall 2022 semester. She taught the plants/organismal biology section. Wasn't super respected by a lot of my peers for her odd teaching style and difficult exams. I thought she was fine. The average grade for the plants section midterm was low, and her test questions were oddly specific. Study well for her exams.

Looy's lectures are interesting, especially when she talks about her field of study (paleobotany). Be prepared to know lots of specifics for her exam. The exam itself had some questions we did not go over in the lecture at all and had to be re-graded for everyone several times. However, this was also due to other confounding factors this semester.

I loved Paleobotany. I learned a lot about the Earth's history through the lens of plant evolution. Lectures and powerpoints were clear, the textbook was accessible, and labs were sometimes difficult, but the GSI was there to guide. If you're into plant morphology and learning about ancient climates, you will enjoy.

She is an amazing professor! Very caring, very intelligent, and very sweet. She is open during office hours and curved our course as our reader was a very harsh grader!! One of the sweetest professors I've had. Course is heavy in reading but she encourages discussion of readings in course to deepen understanding.

I love her. Her lectures are clear and concise, she packs a lot of material into the lectures, but it's easy to keep up with. Curved EVERYTHING, which was great. Gave extra credit for participation. She was super accessible outside of class and was really helpful with everything. I wish I could take her again.
Amazing! A little difficult if you do not keep up with the readings but other than that, great! Curves a lot as well as offering extra credit to participate.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She is inspiring and interesting and so kind. Loved the class and learned a lot. Do the reading, and participate in your section. GSI was fair grader and interesting! Class discussions are interesting because the class has students from so many different backgrounds.
This Professor is so clear and organized that you could fall asleep in class and understand what she's trying to teach you. Plus, she's engaging and emphasizes discussion in an open class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The class itself is super interesting, but I personally don't like how she reads off her notes most of the time rather than lecturing off the top of her head, lectures get boring like that. But she is knowledgeable and encourages conversation in class. Super friendly and very approachable. 1 paper 1 final and 5 weekly reading responses.

wonderful concepts, super knowledgeable, and helpful, she wants you to get an A, but yes there is a lot of reading so READ! highlight concepts and remember authors names/ positions..she uses a reader $50...she expects you to have a perspective on all this as well and be able to give examples to defend your position

Prof. Fox is great in the sense that she is very knowledgable. However, I was only taking this class as breadth, not for interest or major requirement. That being said, I wouldn't pick this class if I had other options; there are easier breadth courses if you want an easy A. This class requires too much work and the material, to me, is SO boring.

Prof Fox is great at explaining concepts from readings. Gives a lot of examples (videos, graphs, images) and brings in things that are currently happening. A lot of key terms for midterm and final, but she gives them all in a study sheet. Also gives exact questions that will be on the final.

Dr. Fox is fantastic. She only assigns relevant, illuminating readings; gives useful feedback & lecture material; & has dedicated her life to understanding the complexities of U.S. social welfare policies. She's brilliant; inspiring; accessible; down to earth; & an indispensable resource in every way - for both the U.S. as a whole & my own ed.!
Just don't take it. No one cares
Very disorganized class, does not respond to emails, don't take the class with her.
She seems like a nice lady, but the class is not good. Projects have nothing to do with what you learn, very disorganized. Do not join this class.

He makes it easy to get up at 7:30am three days a week to learn about stat mech; need I say more? He writes his own lecture notes and problem sets, both of which involve all sorts of interesting questions & applications.

He is among the best, if not the best professor in the Physics department. If you have a chance to take a class with him, do it.

I took 161 with Professor Kasen and truly, one of the most amazing professors I have ever had. If I could rate him a 10/5, I would. If I could rate him a 100/5, I would. If I could somehow give him a Nobel Prize for being the best professor, I would. He really loves what he teaches and you can tell he genuinely wants everyone to succeed. Incredible

C161 isn't appearing on the courses he's taught so I'm reviewing that. Prof. Kasen is the best physics professor I've had at Cal. He really puts effort into helping you learn though lectures and homework assignments. Office hours are super helpful and conversations can go in all sorts of fun directions.

Dan Kasen is straight up the best professor in the physics department. His lectures are easy to follow & it never gets too complicated, he explains math super well. He writes HWs entirely by himself  it's guided and super helpful for learning, and never gets too tedious. He's great & nice in OH if needed. Exams are super fair, nothing unexpected.

I love him so much! Best professor at Berkeley. Attend office hours when you can, he's a real gem outside of class too. Goes way into depth when answering questions, amazing lectures, and fair tests. Homework guides you through problems really well and provides context for what we're learning. Doesn't really use the textbook much, so go to lecture!

It's not even halfway through the semester, but I already know this is going to be the best class I have ever taken. He is AMAZING at writing homework that helps you learn as you do it, and his lectures make perfect sense. Asking a question? He answers it precisely and in a way that is super easy to understand. TAKE DAN KASEN WHENEVER POSSIBLE!

Oh my god. Dan is the best professor I've ever had. Seriously. He's super laid back which makes you feel like physics is not overly complicated, he breaks things down so simply so that you can understand everything (without even having to read the book, yet I do anyways just in case), he's super smart, and he's HILARIOUS. He's the whole package.
Amazing. He actually breaks down the concepts of quantum mechanics so that you actually remember there's physics to the math.

Dan is the best. So lovable and such a great teacher! I was actually sad when I had to miss one of his lectures. Definitely go to his office hours because he's really helpful and super fun to talk to about everything. His tests are fair and doing the homeworks thoroughly is useful. (Also read his comments on the homework because they're hilarious!)

EPS 50 is a very dense, memorization-heavy intro to geology course with small margins for error, so if you want a fun or 'easy' physical science breadth, I would recommend looking elsewhere. For those who need it for their major, good luck!

That said, he presents the content well, so you should probably go to lecture if you take his class.

I loved Prof Shuster. Not only was EPS 124 super interesting, but he was always ready to help whenever I had questions. He made time for one on one office hours as well! Be sure to attend discussion section because he walks you through problem sets. FYI it was also my first upper division so I didn't know what to expect, but I am so glad I took it!

Great professor for EPS 50; he explains concepts well and his labs are engaging. Super accessible in office hours; and very passionate about Earth Science. Classes have occasional pop quizzes for attendance credit. My only complaint is that some of the exam questions did not feel relevant to the material, but felt more like random trivia.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Same as the previous reviewer, my main complaint with the class was that the MCQ portion of exams always felt like obscure trivia that the professor had only mentioned once during lecture. There seemed to be poor communication between the professor and GSIs, as review sessions for exams were often confusing. Otherwise, content was interesting.

Hard material but I learned a lot in this class and Shuster was super helpful in office hours when I struggled with homework. Lots of slides but there's some overlap between lectures. After taking EPS131 I understand thermo way more than when I took an entire class on it. Huge range of topics, so there's bound to be one you'll be interested in

Professor Shuster lectures can seem a bit dry at times but you can tell he cares about his students and he encourages people to ask questions. This class was perfect for me because I needed exposure to different earth science topics to see what I'm specifically into. Do well on the labs because they're time consuming and grade heavy!

The professor was always reachable (email, office hours), and was willing to help. The lectures were dense, but was high quality. Homework was difficult but helpful, and the tests followed lecture and homework.

One of those profs who likes to hear himself talk, is monotone and dry, and rarely finishes on time. Slides are good, but he did skip some he didn't know, then told us to review it for the exams. Exams asked us about obscure facts and values not overarching concepts.  Felt like waste of what this class could be with a better professor.

Disregard the previous comment, this student is clearly bitter and is providing misinformation. He does not babble, in fact his lectures are incredibly meaningful and relevant. Power points are very long, but all the information is there.  Test is comparable to reading and lecture. Lots of work in this class, especially labs. I have an 84% so far.

If you are looking for a nice Physical Science Breadth, like I was, do NOT take this class. Although the professor is accessible and kind, his lectures are just him babbling about random sh*t that has somewhat to do with what he is meaning to teach. The test will be on the readings and not on his lectures :/
He aite. JK! I suck at Physical Sciences, but he makes it bearable. Disccuses stuff on class that will not be on midterm.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: One of my fave economics classes at UC Berk was econ 140 with Professor Damien Pouzo.

This was the class I was most scared about, but Prof Pouzo was pretty good. You really have to lock in tho. It helped me to do ALL problem sets since the midterms and final directly reflected those (Some even are the same ones). 90% of the grade is midterms and finals, which is a lot, but still doable.
notice how similar the 5 star ratings sound?
Big lack of communication, his teaching style isn't great, exams were disorganized, bad grading system no curve apparently?

The professor gave amazing lectures for this class. And, the average scores for the midterms and final exam were in the high 80s, so the grading was very fair. I learned a lot from this class, and the GSIs were very helpful. This professor is great!
Professor Pouzo was extremely passionate about his class and was engaged with students. He was very knowledgeable on the subject as well. Would take one of his classes again!

Saying this as someone who got an A only because I'm a DS major who had taken other overlapping classes: this was one of the worst classes I've taken. No structure. Prof did not prepare for lectures. Exams drew from PS's that had no solutions. HALF the syllabus was rushed in ONE week and the "cumulative" final tested that latter half exclusively.

Course design was a disaster. 90% of grade is 3 exams. Practice problems appeared word for word on exams, but practice problem answers were not released and were difficult to get out of GSI OH. Good luck if you have mandatory class during OH like me. Frequent grading errors (be ready to regrade request) and some questions answer keys were incorrect

Extremely disorganized class. Learning objectives were very unclear; no solution set was given with the practice problems (had to learn from ChatGPT). I felt that exam grading was unfairly technical. Lectures dragged on for days about very simple concepts yet rushed over parts that actually needed explaining. Demian is a nice & caring guy though.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: disorganized class. professor is not online answering anything. 90% of grade is based off three exams. Will not give you answers to problem sets. Poorly written final exam, and not cumulative as expected. My gsi had no idea what was going on the entire semester. Did not go over r studio at all even though thats where the hw is.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Demian is a great professor. He is amazing at giving lectures. The topics in the first two midterms (for example univariate and multivariate regression) were the foundations of the final exam material. So the final exam was extremely fair, and easy if you understood what was explained in lecture. This class is very important, and also fun.

Without a curve or clobber policy, your grade relies entirely on three high-stakes tests (25/25/40), and there is zero curve or policy to help your grade. Despite being told the final would be cumulative, it focused almost exclusively on the final handout. The professor is totally MIA on Ed Discussion. Extremely misleading and disorganized. 1/5.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
The exam was explicitly said to be cumulative, and students wasted hours studying the concepts.
The final focused almost entirely on highly specific content from Handout 11. That is not what a cumulative exam implies, and it is misleading. 
The most deceitful class I've taken at Cal. Midterms were fine, but the state of the final is inexcusable.

I have never seen this. Professor respond to a single student question or even acknowledge anything on Ed despite the numerous attempt many students have made every single month about class policy/feedback!!! 90% exam weighted, no midterm drops or clobber or curve. Says final will be cumulative multiple times, then makes the final only on Unit 11..
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The worst professor ever. In the course, we covered 11 chapters, chapters 1-5 were on midterm 1. 6-10 on midterm 2, and chapter 11 was left for the final. We were told the final would be cumulative but we were tested entirely on chapter 11. Exams are very difficult and the grading structure is 90% exams (25%each midterm 40%final) and 10% homework.

Lectures were full of proofs and he didn't give any practice problems. Gave many past exams to practice but the catch was not attaching any answers, and you could not find them online. Problem sets throughout the semester that were easy and graded on completion. Get help from GSIs and OH. Prof proved very smart, but content is very difficult.

Demian is a really nice guy. Tests are 70% straight from previous years exams so use those to study. Grading is very generous and you get a lot of partial credit even if your solution doesn't make sense. Homework is light and usually very easy; don't use it to study. Lectures are clear and well-motivated, so I really enjoyed them. Good class 10/10
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: His lectures are slow and a little hard to understand but his PowerPoints are very good so use those to study. His problem sets are very hard but they are helpful and they aren't graded so they shouldn't be a burden
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Pouzo's lectures are proof heavy but if you read the textbook beforehand to get the general concept, the proofs provide a deeper understanding into the concept. The exams are fair and are similar to past exams. Some questions were exactly the same as past years! The catch is that the solutions are not shared so you have to go to OH.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Pouzo is in readable knowledgeable about econometrics. Going to lectures is a must, as most of the advanced part of the material is taught there. He gives plenty of practice exams. Stat 134 is helpful, but I got the grade I got with just stat 20. If you want to do well, read the book before lecture.

Very hard course. Stat 134 should be a hard pre-req because the course demands a strong understanding of probability and Prof. Pouzo expects prior knowledge. Course is heavy on proofs so strong math background would be good. I had neither so I naturally struggled. Luckily, GSI office hours saved me. Lectures are fast-paced and content packed.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This class was my favorite class I took in FPF at Berkeley. Professor Leigh has a very engaging teaching style and the content of the course really changed my perspective on many things. His rubric and grading is clear---as long as you do the work the way he wants you will get an A! I recommend taking this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Outdated and waste of time

One of my favorite professors I've had! He provided all necessary material information in an engaging and straightforward way. I always looked forward to lectures, every week was interesting. Your grade is based on weekly written assignments, 2 midterms, and a final so be sure to do your best. I recommend taking this class if you have the chance!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I loved this professor, no need to buy books he gives you all assigned reading. It is very clear how to succeed in this course. Conversations with him are amazing and I learned a lot in his class. Go to his office hours to get to know him if you can. He really cares about his students. I cannot recommend him enough.

He's one of the most amazing professors I've encountered here. You can tell he really cares about the success of his students. He provides great feedback and has the patience to discuss every student's questions and ideas, whether that's in class or in office hours. If you have the chance to take a class with him, I highly recommend it.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Incredible professor who really cares. Provides detailed feedback, and has really engaging lectures.

Lots of reading, but sometimes there are films instead. Very clear and organized class structure and genuinely seems to value student opinions and perspectives. dont be too afraid to participate in large group discussions either. You really have to do the readings though, otherwise you will not perform very well in the class
Prof. Leigh is an incredible incredible professor. Very passionate about education and his students success. Always a happy place in his class.

Prof Leigh is AWESOME!! Best class I've ever taken. Every lecture was fascinating and interactive, readings were interesting, and discussions engaging. He really cares about the material and his students. It's not an easy class, you will read and write tons, but 100% worth it to come out with a deeper understanding of the world around you. Take it!

He has a passion for history that is inspirational and contagious. Lectures are interactive and discussion-based. He's a very understanding professor and is happy to make time to help you during office hours.
His lectures were incredibly engaging and interesting. While you had to

Professor leigh is really knowledgable, fun and engaging. The grading is mostly on reflections, so the readings are absolutely crucial to do, and aren't too bad. Professor Leigh's passion for teaching is clearly conveyed through the attention he gives every student. He chooses interesting material to cover in class, and encourages discussion amongst our peers. I would highly recommend Devin for anyone consider taking his class.

Professor Leigh is one of the best professors I've ever had the honor of learning from at Cal. Proffesor Devin Leigh is full of passion and his interest in the subjects covered definitely shines through during lectures. The course deals with current events and conflicts. BEST HISTORY TEACHER EVER. He is a really engaging lecturer and I love his teaching, he genuinely love his topic and he is such a caring guy. Professor Delay was one of my favorite teachers thus far! He made me want to become a history major and his lectures were always filled with really interesting stories. I never missed a single one and if you can take his class, you should!

I rarely write ratemyprofessors but Dan Garcia is an absolute gem. His exams are quite difficult however and the class is also insanely project-heavy.
A's for All? More like A's for None!

The “A's for everyone” model felt like a poor fit for a CS class in my experience. It was stressful since small point losses mattered a lot. I found some exams unclear or ambiguous, with high score variation. There is a small curve at the end, but earning an A+ felt extremely difficult.

My grade went from A to B after the exam (4.0->3.0). Then he decided to give everyone 5 points for the final to account for the difficulty but it was definitely not enough to bring the final average to 65% per the course syllabus, (55-> 58%). The midterm also had a low average. Don't take him if you care about grades. “A's for all” was a scam
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Garcia is an enthusiastic lecturer, but lectures were not deep enough to match exam difficulty. The Fa25 semester ran as a test run for Dan's “A's for Everyone” initiative, and it just didn't pan out well (exams averaged below 65, extra points didn't bring the avg up to a 65, yet bins remained the same). Beware if you care about your GPA.

Professor Dan's lectures are passionate and engaging, but their depth and breadth do not match the difficulty of the homework and exams. Very enthusiastic and you will learn tons of interesting things. 61C is tough & time consuming + exams are HARD. If grades are important to you then beware...

Dan throws out a lot of "As for All" nonsense to make you hopeful about passing the class, but he wont pull through with that. Dan Garcia is enthusiastic, however his "A's for all" policy is one of the worst things I have heard. Very bad professor
Dan Garcia might be the greatest living lecturer. That's really all that needs to be said. If you have the honor to take a class with him, please do it.

Overall, Garcia's 61C is fun and very polished (perfectly structured projects)!

Professor Garcia's A's for All policy is in theory a wonderful system but unfortunately hard to implement due to the sheer amount of things you're graded on. The clobber policy encourages learning but the midterms and postterm are still insanely difficult. The labs are oftentimes really long and many extensions were needed just to complete them.

Professor Garcia's A's for All policy is a wonderful system that is unfortunately still slightly lacking. The clobber encourages learning throughout the course but the midterms and postterm are difficult beyond belief. In addition, the sheer amount of assignments given during labs are oftentimes overwhelming and many needed numerous extensions.
My favourite professor so far

Easily the best teacher I've ever had. He is always super excited every morning and very passionate about the lecture material. His lectures will make you enjoy the content as well. Do not hesitate to take classes taught by him! I would give him 6/5 if I could.

Prof Garcia clearly pours his heart into his job, and he made the class focused on growth, not competition. He implemented an A's for All policy that, of its many perks, lets you retake tests multiple times, which helped me improve my understanding of the material rather than focus on immediate perfection. He's also very supportive & enthusiastic!

Passionate, digestible lectures, although his pace is often very fast. He deeply cares about student success and is a really fun guy, even if the class didn't have much energy. The class is very well organized. The projects can be quite challenging so give yourself enough time to work through them so you don't fall behind. Also, go to lecture! :D

As someone with no CS experience, this class always made me stress and anxious about the projects and labs. The “A's for all” policy is not that helpful if you're confused with the material, I constantly went to office hours but still very confused. Professor Dan is very passionate but just talks really fast, only way you learn is by labs.
Very nice professor! passionate about class!!!

I took this class with absolutely no CS experience and loved every minute of it. He is so knowledgeable and makes every lecture so fun. I learned so many topics and am now considering switching majors cause of this class. There is no way you can not get an A - he literally has an "As for all" grading policy. BEST PROFESSOR AT BERKELEY I SWEAR.

Professor Garcia's lectures are engaging, but the pace can be challenging. Utilize unstuckstudy and the free textbook to supplement and solidify your understanding. Stay focused, and you'll find the projects rewarding.

The best! Full of energy! 
It was also awesome to finally learn about how computers work :) 
Also, Dan really cares about his students understanding the material and succeeding. He's awesome.
just talks fast and doesn't explain things well

I took CS10 with Dan Garcia in Fall 2022. He is an amazing professor and probably why I decided to do CS. He made CS accessible for everyone like me who had no coding experience before. He is so passionate about teaching and he probably shaped my future path. He also cares about equity in CS and truly cares about his students. My fav prof at Cal.

Dan is very caring for all of his students and he makes the lectures very engaging. He provides great resources in which to learn from and fosters collaboration/community building between students of CS10.

One of the best CS professors. If you do not have a technical background but want to take an intro CS class, I 100% recommend CS10 with him!! He is clearly very passionate about the subject and about teaching. There is very little python (last few weeks) but I definitely feel comfortable with Snap! and basic coding after taking this class.

Dan is very passionate about the subject, but in my opinion, he is not good at teaching the material. I had trouble understanding him since he talks way too fast in lecture and rushes important topics. I had to watch other semesters lectures and look for other resources online to learn the material. Honestly, he made me dislike the material.

The class was difficult, especially the projects, which were long, and the exams.  I didn't find the lectures useful.  The professor talks so fast that it's hard to follow what he's talking about, and he adds lots of unnecessary analogies.  He tries to make the lectures entertaining, but I couldn't relate to the references he made.

One of my favorite professors at Berkeley.  His lectures are uniquely entertaining - he is super passionate about both the material and his students.  61C is known to be jam-packed with information - he struck the perfect balance between going through material and receiving questions.  I feel very fortunate to have been able to take 61C with him.

His lectures presented the concepts easily (for the most part) but never connected to the impossible labs. The labs themselves were a mess. Only two lab sections were offered, meaning they were large and chaotic. I couldn't hear the GSI over everyone else talking and didn't get the help I needed. Discussions were from 8-10 pm in person

GOAT (Greatest of All Time) Extremely Accommodating & Understanding. 

He does not assume any previous knowledge & will explain himself for however long it takes you to achieve "Mastery Learning". And if you're already good at his class, he will make you even better. 

He'll do everything it takes to get you an "A" in his class. No one comes close.
take his class
Gives great lectures!

Likely my favorite professor. Enthusiastic and fascinating lectures, like a performance. They feel slower in the recordings: go to lecture. Content is dense but HW helps. Friendly and available for questions after class. Only complaint is that he rushes questions during lecture. Projects vary in difficulty later on; a partner would probably help.

He doesnt explain anything thoroughly in the lectures. He talks way too fast and almost noonne pays attention in the lectures. The Labs are the main way to learn which sucks. If you are not a social person goodluck trying to finish the projects because you need a partner This class is horrible for commuters too and people online, horrible class
lectures make no sense

Worst professor ever. He would frequently digress to random topics and use strange metaphors to demonstrate some point (often not related to this course) and goes over the important parts super fast. (No time! No time!) Then how come he spends so much time talking about stuff not helpful for this class? Quote my friend, is he a rapper or something?
Lectures are so hard to understand, go over topics too fast.

For those starting in compsci or students just interested in the subject, this is the class for you! Prof. Dan is so passionate, and his lectures were always something I looked forward to. The exams in this class aren't easy but you get retakes, and the grading policies are geared to helping you succeed. One of my favorite professors!

Extremely energetic professor, making lectures interesting and active. Also extremely fun. Cares a lot about students by having an extremely generous extension policy for assignments. Interesting assignments and tough exams.
Amazing professor. He brings enthusiasm to every lecture and clearly explains how he arrives at his answers. I greatly preferred Dan's lectures over Justin's.
His energy is unmatched. I was not so interested in computer architecture towards the beginning of the class, but the way he presents it makes it extremely interesting. 10/10 would recommend.

Amazing professor. His lectures are extremely interesting and engaging. I think attending lectures is enough for your studies because of how great the lectures are. He is also really close with the students and has a really perspective on education.

dan  himself was the best prof at berkeley!! the GSIs however were not. loved learning the content but felt like the GSIs didnt want to help me learn and got frustrated if i didnt get a concept(not at all Dans fault) dan made evrything accessible, was kind, and was avalible at most times if you needed it !truly kind, caring,  and compassionate
I really love his teaching style. The lecture is awesome!

Dan Garcia is a wonderful professor. He brings an energy to his class that I've never seen from an instructor before. The course was challenging but fair, and a very good introduction to coding principles. The A's for All policy helped alleviate the stress of the class, but I think it could promote procrastination as well.

Amazing lecturer. You can tell that he really enjoys teaching this class. He also made it a goal to decrease the difficulty of the class by giving easier tests. 100% worked, averages were high. I took 61C with him during the strike, and he was very accommodating and listened to students needs. 10/10 professor!
Dan is one of the best professors at Cal and definitely the best teaching CS 61C. He gives amazing amazing lectures, and it's really worth it to take his class.

Dan himself is an amazing professor, but I would warn against people who take this class for an easy A. Material is difficult and there is a heavy workload. Exams were unnecessarily challenging. Even though I had perfect scores on projects, homeworks, and labs almost everyone in the class including me bombed the midterm and final.

Dan designed a great class for the 0-experienced. Learn fundamentals with beginner-friendly Snap and hone basic skills with Python. Labs & sections are very helpful and worth 100% efforts. Exams & projects are challenging but meaningful, accommodating, and with clear instructions. Lectures could've been better if with slower pace and more details.
Best professor ever. Gave us exams that tested knowledge rather than memory.

Professor Garcia, aka 'Dan the Man,' has a reputation for making classes lively and enthusiastic- compelling students to attend. CS-10 was structured extremely efficiently in that each student received personal attention, with 1-1 tutoring available. There were multiple EC opportunities and office hours slots to get help on assignments. Perfection!

This class is what made me want to be a CS major. Dan really cares about his students and the class. If you've never taken a CS class but have any sort of interest, I highly recommend CS10. It can be difficult, but if you put the effort in, it will be worth it. There are also lots of EC opportunities and many chances to get an A.

Doesn't really teach in class but labs are hard if you've never coded before. Like really hard and when it gets to Python they were impossible for me. I got like a 25% on the final. But lots of extra credit opportunities.

I loved this class! It was such a great introduction to coding and computer science in general, and there were so many opportunities to get an A (extra credit, a clobber policy for midterms, etc) that it was easy to focus on just learning CS.

He is passionate about CS and shares his excitement with the class. Lectures are always interesting and entertaining. However, he is not the best CS lecturer as he tends to quickly run through the slides without fully explaining things. Projects and homework can be time-consuming and frustrating, but teach you a lot.

Dan is a good lecturer and extremely enthusiastic. However, the content from lecture is rarely on the exams. CS1O is a cs principles course, and is not the best bridge towards CS61A. With that in mind, you do learn a lot about the general ideas behind computing.
Garcia is an amazing instructor with a one of a kind charisma. And I want to remark upon his rap during the last lecture. It was the best Hamilton parody I have ever heard.

Dan is such a hilarious and talented guy. He is very caring for his students, and do not intentionally makes the exams extremely difficult. I would say that his exams are definitely on the cs61a level, but he says if you can get an A in percentage he will give you an A, regardless of the grade caps. Love him!

Don't be fooled by his enthusiasm or high CS10 reviews, Garcia is not a good 61C lecturer. He basically just rushes through slides as fast as possible. I would have rather he slowed down going over topics rather than coming up with elaborate analogies. Watch the other professors' webcast - they go at a pace you can still follow given the material.
Dan is a wonderful professor. Very caring and enthusiastic. He motivates his students and grades fairly. He made my first cs class a great experience.

Dan Garcia is an extremely inspiring professor who goes out of his way to motivate struggling students and give them chances to recover. He implemented the ability to clobber earlier midterm scores with a higher final exam score, made exams very familiar to what he taught in lecture, and shifted grade bins downward to boost peoples final grades.

I love Dan Garcia. He is a professor that truly care about his students and trying to provide as many as opportunities for his students in his CS61A community. At Berkeley EECS department, they strive to prevent students from declaring CS, but Dan is the one that truly love his students and help his students getting into this major. LoveDan loveCS

This is a professor that truly cares about students. He not only inspire everyone in his class but he also give good grades. He is also very very passionate during lecture and you can see that he really love cs.

Professor Garcia's an incredible CS educator whose care for students shines through his fun lectures and pro-student course policies. While the content for CS61A is highly standardized, Dan's enthusiasm made a difference in getting through this tough course.

Dan is a great professor. Very enthusiastic every single day. His love for CS is truly inspiring. He's very funny and although 61a is very very tough, having him made lectures something I looked forward to.

Dan is an amazing professor who is extremely enthusiastic and quirky. He introduced several course policies to 61A that were really beneficial to students. Although he's great at explaining concepts, his time management is not the best so lecture material is not always covered very well. Lectures also often have a lot of tangents and fluff.
Amazing professor, very passionate, explains things well.
Amazing professor!!
Amazing Professor!

TAKE CS10! If you don't know anythign about programming before coming to Cal, I highly recommend taking CS10(in the fall of freshman year if you can). You might just reconsider your whole life(or at least major). Dan is just awesome and the class is easy. You can learn a lot if you put in effort, I've can wade into the world of Python on my own now

I knew nothing about CS when I came to Berkeley, and CS10 made me fall in love with programming. Dan is great, truly cares about his students, and is big on making CS accessible for all. Contrary to some students' beliefs that CS10 is a "joke" class, I truly felt I learned a lot and it prepared me well for success in CS61a and CS61b.

Dan Garcia is a great professor and I enjoyed taking CS10 with him. However, CS10 itself is a waste of time. You only start doing Python in the last 3 weeks of the semester and spend the rest of the time working in a language called Snap. If you are a complete novice when it comes to computers then CS10 is for you. Else, save time and just take 61A

Dan's lectures are poor; he uses stock metaphors which skim surfaces and inadequately explain the actual course material. He's too busy and "doesn't have time" to answer questions: i.e. has little regard for his 61C students. Be prepared to read the textbook, ask questions online, and grok low(er)-level software libraries/concepts on your own.

Dan is a great lecturer and nice guy. He goes out of his way to make sure as many students enjoy, learn from, and pass his class. He's also exceedingly funny and open in office hours, he and the GSI's are always around to help out. Few tests, plenty of resources to study given, plenty of feedback and extra credit opportunities.

His class seems like a total waste of my time if I want to learn programming, which was my goal. It negatively inspired me to not take more CS classes at Berkeley. I often program for work in C and python, confirming his class was total waste of time. He is bad at lecturing and doesn't communicate CS concepts well/at all. Projectslame

Dan is the absolute best. He cares more than any professor I've ever had. He was integral in the creation of this class. Lectures are more big picture, lab is where you learn, and there is a ton of extra credit if you still aren't doing so hot.

Most enthusiastic professor ever who made me fall in love with CS. Take CS10 if you're even remotely considering studying CS. Go to his lectures and office hours for sure  he goes over exam problems and it's a great opportunity to get to know him. Bottomline: Dan's great!!

Dan Garcia is AMAZING! CS10 is honestly one of the best classes you can take: you will learn a lot, especially from lectures. The class has a nice pace and you never have to worry about your grade, because there is so much extra credit and opportunities to prove that you learned. Overall an amazing professor and I would recommend 100%!
CS 10 has completely changed my view on computing and programming. Dan is energetic and bound to broaden your horizon. Highly recommend.
Dan is a very good lecturer. He is clearly very excited to be teaching the material. Though he sometimes talks very quickly, he is probably the best lecturer in the cs61 series.
funny, makes the subject very interesting.

Absolutely amazing lecturer, one of my favorites at Cal. I took more computer science than I had planned here just to attend another class with him. He has some great insights on computer science and can really broaden your horizons. I know his technical classes are harder, but CS10 with Garcia is definitely a class I would recommend to anyone.
One of the best lecturers at Berkeley and probably in the world.

Really unprepared, course materials aren't relevant to exam, and exam was poorly made (he accidentally put an impossible problem then proceeded to not give partial credit to people to spent most of the exam on it) would  definitely not recommend
His lectures were very engaging and he always brought in interesting guest lecturers! He is very passionate and excited and friendly, and his exams are very fair. Great experience!!
This guy is amazing for CS10. He will get you to love computer science, I promise.

Dan is the most fun professor I've ever had. He is very engaged, clearly cares about his students, and realizes that most of us are taking more than just his class. Reasonable homework and projects - you need to know your stuff, but in the end it's totally doable. After 61b with Hilfinger it's pretty easy.
MY FAVORITE <3 he is a great and engaging lecturer.

This class is great, in my opinion. There were many things to do in the class, but it (almost) always felt satisfying and fun. On top of that, you can learn topics like recursion and higher order functions in a safe environment before going on to harder classes like CS61A.

I had no CS background so it was NOT an easy class for me. Tons of work. But he's an awesome professor and so organized! EVERYTHING was online. He cares about students more than any professor I've had. The grading policies helped a lot— I freaked out when I got a D on the first exam but I still got an A in the class. He's fair.

while this is definitely a hard class if you're mathematically challenged, it's helpful if you intend to work on the internet or work with computers. It's also a great way to learn about computer's place in our life and the evolution of technology

Professor Garcia is EXTREMELY enthusiastic about Computer Science, which was encouraging. The class was a lot of work and rather time-consuming, but I had a lot of fun with it. It's a great class for students with no programming experience that just want to try it out. I would definitely recommend this class!
Awesome professors, super enthusiastic about computer science.

Professor Garcia made me LOVE programming and even switching from a chemical engineering major to computer science! This class is a lot of fun, and I learned a lot. Even non-majors should take this, though it definitely is the TAs who are the most helpful, due to being there in labs and discussion for help with projects.

Dan tried hard to make CS10 fun, but in my opinion, too much time was spent on building "energy" and hype and not enough on concepts like recursion. You will only interact with the GSIs in this class - Dan seems accessible at first, but you'll find that he's quite aloof. The exams are difficult but all of the points are made up in projects.

Take CS 10 with Dan Garcia! It introduces computing to everyone, even people like me who have no prior CS experience. Lectures were a mix of social aspects (internet privacy issues, etc) and lab concepts (recursion, higher-order functions). It helps to have an analytical or math-ie mind, but if that's not your strong point no worries--Dan's amazing

this review was from wen the class was 1st taught: most enthusiastic professor ive had! hes always willing to help too. however his exams are WAY too complex compared to what we did in lab/projects/hw. wen the mean for the exams is an F, you know you're not preparing students as well as you should be. otherwise AMAZING class. recommend to all!
One of the most enthusiastic and fair teachers at UCB, tries to make lectures as entertaining as possible and is very responsive to the class as a whole.

This was the most time consuming class I took my freshman year. He is fun but the class is way harder than he leads you to believe. If you have no programming experience, the class is a definite challenge, though not entirely impossible. Do all the homework and ace all the projects and quizzes because the midterm and final are ridiculous.

Organized but overly dense and sometimes incorrect lectures. Discussion pretty unhelpful. Homeworks and projects are all GSI-controlled; they usually take a long time and are sometimes unfairly graded. Tests are difficult and confusing, often only loosely based on lecture material. Garcia is also the most unresponsive professor I've had here.

He is an excellent teacher.  I had no problems with him.  However, I'm just not a computer science kind of guy, so I had a hard time with this class.  Expect to stay up quite late at night doing the projects.  GET STARTED ON THEM IMMEDIATELY. I can't stress that enough haha.  Also, MAKE SURE YOU GET THE CONCEPTS. The final is KILLER so be prepared.

Garcia is very into CS - his energy makes lecture worthwhile. Final was difficult compared to midterm. Class itself wasn't particularly hard and Dan is very friendly and easy to relate to. I'd say he is a great guy.
Good lecturer, tests aren't too bad it you're fairly intelligent. Had an overall good experience with him.

This prof is outstanding.  Best lecturer I've ever had, by far. Also, the class itself is amazing. Tons of very interesting material is covered. The only negative: as in every lower-div CS class I've taken, the project grades rely heavily on the autograders, leading to low grades for minor mistakes. Otherwise perfect!

CS61C with Dan Garcia is certainly a fully packed learning experience. A lot of material is covered and the exams are not trivial. However, I also got an A with little studying aside from the final; skip buying the textbooks as the lecture PowerPoints are very sufficient. All in all, good course, recommended.

Good lectures, interesting personality, and shows CG clips before class. Like most CS classes, projects take some time. The midterm is challenging, but doable. There is a nice policy where you can overwrite your midterm grade if you do well on the final.

cs61c was definitely a good experience for me. Lecture was always exciting, but occasionally got off topic and ran out of time. I didn't find the concepts in lecture too difficult, and didn't read much out of the main book, but lots of reading out of the C book. projects really long and hard, but prof was nice: regrades, Slip days, dropped low hw

One of my best and favorite Professor, even though I didn't get that good of a grade. I kind of messed up on the final big time. Knew the stuff, but just made too many mistake on final. Very Clear in lecture and lecture is very fun. Office hours are very helpful.
No Comments

Passionate about the subject and overall a good professor. However, his exams kill. Make sure you understand EVERY little concept that he goes over; even if he says only 1 word about it, there might be a full problem on this thing on exams. hw/proj/lab are OK, but they wont help you on the finals. Otherwise, a good lecturer

One great professor!  I was looking forward to his lectures because he is so much fun.  He will try his best to explain something if you don't understand it.  Yes, he speaks kind of fast but I was always able to follow him.  I highly recomend this class to anyone interested in computer science.

Possibly the best professor I will ever have. There was nothing ever boring about him or the curriculum. Not only is he a smart guy, he really knows how to make students feel appreciated (if you participate). If you ever have a chance to take a class of his, DO IT!
He has so much passion for the subject, it's almost impossible not to find his lectures interesting.  It has been a lot of fun.  Awesome prof.

Not only is he difficult, he is a very bad lecturer. He speaks way too fast, and uses only PowerPoint. Never once did he write something on the blackboard. Sure, he has enthusiasm for the class, but the assignments and workload are just ridiculous. He tries to cram way too many subjects in the class.
Has a lot of passion for his subject.  I really like this class.
Fantastic professor.
Very clear and consice on all lectures. Interesting and entertaining lectures (He won't put you to sleep). Very difficult exams, but worthwhile homeworks and projects.
he is truely interested in the subject.
No Comments
No Comments
Whatever he's smoking, the rest of the world should get some.  Very passionate about what he does.

More interested in meeting "cut quotas" for the department, meaning he's not really interested in teaching Computer Science as he is in eliminating enough people so that they will not get into the major (CS).

Took the class in spring 2005. He is an interesting and funny professor and lectures are not too bad. But exams are very very difficult and projects also a little hard. The exams don't really allow for you to showing understanding. Overall a very hard class.
Good class and very interesting, but exams do not permit students to show what they know.
