Worst professor I've ever had in my college years.  Like the other reviews, do not believe what he promises in lectures.  He does not like to interact with students either.
Great teacher.  lecture is fun and interesting.
Lecture was definitely entertaining... but almost worthless.  He didn't go into enough depth on anything in the second half of the course.  Tests were hard, sure, but otherwise grading was light.
Great instructor, teaches very well and clearly. However, his exams are extremely difficult and the class is hard to do well in as a result.
he's pretty funny and tries to make the lectures more interesting. i dont know if he was making the tests, but they were easy.
He explains well. He's very funny.
Taking his exam is probably the worst thing you ever want to do.  Also, don't trust what he promises during lectures!!!!
very helpful, really wants everyone to learn the info
The best instructor - a little bit hard, but is very interesting and has cool assignments!
easy course, cute comics/cartoons at the beginning of lectures... not that i ever went. he made the tests pretty hard, considering it's just cs3. but still easy for good programmers.
Before you take his class make sure if he will keep his promises. He gave closed books midterm and final against what he has promised at the beginning--open books tests!

if ur smart the class is easy...but he makes the tests unnecessarily difficult and nit-picky. People seem to enjoy his enthusiasm but i thought it was overdone and a little cheesy. Either you'll love him or you'll hate him.
Great professor. Enthusiastic and fun. Hard tests though.
funny and very energetic in lecture, but difficult and tricky tests.
He's easy.  Computer Science 3 is easy anyways so lectures are pointless.
The most entertaining professor,funny and energetic in his show off lecture. wast ur time and ur money.
floop!
Very fun and energetic both in class and out.  Be wary of taking his exams, though..
He's energetic, but it's hard to follow him sometimes because he goes through the slides too fast. He doesn't pause & give people the time to think about the material.
The most entertaing professor I've had here.
No Comments
he's good and energetic
No Comments
His lectures were practically useless. The only thing that helped were the labs and discussions. His tests are tricky, but definitely doable.
It says lecture is mandatory but it isn't really. The lectures and readings are interesting so I recommend you show up. He is a really nice professor.

Amazing introductory class for QGIS. Took it with zero previous experience & it was very manageable & interesting. Awesome GSIs & the final project is just making your own map, but there's lots of support and time for completing it. Lectures were mostly whole class discussion of the readings. Attend lab so quizzes are easier!

The class was easy, especially since I had pervious gis knowledge but I would say it would be easy to someone completely new at it too. The grading consisted of 5 reading reflections, 5 quizzes on gis activities, a final map, and a final essay. The lectures were not very helpful and often a bit boring, but the lab section more than makes up for it.

Professor Barrera's lectures are more often than not based on the readings. There are lab assignments, 5 quizzes that are really easy if you attend lab, and a couple of voice recording assignments on the readings (which you don't really have to do if they aren't for an assignment although you will need to reference them in your final essay).
Amazing instructor, was nervous at first for taking a swim class but it really is an entry level class. Doesn't judge and is very encouraging and chill. 10/10 recommend.
He's a great professor and super chill. He's very funny and won't judge you at all. He wants everyone to do their best. I would 100% recommend him to anyone who takes a phys ed class.

Super down to earth and chill guy, wants his class to be fun. Wants to develop close relationships with all of his students, regardless of whether or not they are super skilled in the class. Has a lot of funky games as well to encourage bonding. Also very accommodating and doesn't make fun of people who are struggling
Fun PE classes that I looked forward to every week! Had him for Swim 2.

Matthew Denham is the best teacher I've ever had. His class is fun, and he always makes sure not to challenge people to the point where they don't want to try anymore. He's super helpful, and extremely understanding in all situations. Taking his class is a nice way to get through the week, and I would recommend that everyone should take his course.

If you need an outlet from school and a great way to meet new people and get some good exercise, take Mr. Denham's PE classes. He is the most enthusiastic and friendly teacher, and he creates a very positive environment for the students, so that it doesn't feel like a mandatory class and more like a fun activity outside of school. The BEST teacher!
Best professor at berkeley !!

Professor Baldua is an amazing lecturer, and he was so inspiring that it caused my brain to develop a second wrinkle! He is so effective in his explanations I highly suggest anyone interested in engineering to take this class!

audited in the course. amazing lecturer. after his lecture, I really want to transfer to aerospace engeering.

this isn't said lightly as a gender studies student.

Professor Baldua taught an amazing class that served as a perfect introductory course to the NewSpace industry. I personally enjoyed the guest speakers a lot and found the course to be very enganging and the actual projects to be enjoyable.
Learnt a lot.
Really cared about both students and topics.
We had really cool guest speakers and the professor was easy to talk to as well as eager to help
Very good professor
Not very organized. Avoid at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Great projects and informative lectures.
Best lecturer at Cal!
Best Professor I have ever taken at Berkeley. His extra credit assignments were a bit weird, however.
Amazing class, would take it again!
she is extremely nice and well educated and so helpful her test is easy, she is so smart and try to never  miss her because its can effect your grade
smart, funny. i liked her class.
she was organized and funny and young.

dr. dhillon was a little nervous at first, but it was evident she was very knowledgable and had the makes of a great instructor. she was quite brilliant with a deep understanding of the material my advice would be to just not be tentative and show what she knew rather than being shy.
A very clear professor. She was funny and sincere about helping students and providing mentorship and guidance. i wish i could take more classes from her.
Very helpful in office hours!

It was her first time teaching when I took her class and it was fine. Definitely more relaxed personality than Dr.Head-Gordon. She herself took Chem 4A (and aced it) so she knows what she is talking about. Hopefully a teacher that will improve over time.

In-class quizzes were either too easy or plain weird and convoluted. Midterm wasn't too bad, although her part of the final was kind of painful. Lectures were pretty much from the book and not too helpful. Had a unique sense of humor... Had lots of demos (some were too basic). Didn't take a lot from the lectures themselves. It WAS her first time...
Physics 8A online was alright. His lecture videos were not the most clear and were more so focused on examples rather than teaching the type of problem. The curve was not the best for this class.

Deweese was great for the online Physics 8A! He genuinely loves Physics and brings that passion into his lectures. I used to hate physics because I had a series of awful teachers, but Deweese explains the material in a digestible way + fun drawings. Hard class regardless, but great prof.

Really hard class no matter the prof, but Deweese made lectures interesting and easy to listen to, even though he would make mistakes and get tripped up sometimes. Exams are tough and homework takes a while.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
He's a super sweet guy, and very approachable in and out of class. Made mistakes occasionally in lecture and would have to redo a big portion of the problem. Exams were fair enough but on the difficult side. 5A is tough no matter what professor you have, you'll be fine with him (probably), but it won't be fun.

He's a cutie patootie though! Love!!!

Deweese is an incredibly sweet guy and a talented artist as well but his lectures aren't too helpful. He basically goes over the textbook content but makes it more confusing cause he gets lost sometimes :/
Love his enthusiasm but not the best prof for 5A
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: DeWeese is a nice guy and all, but he is not a very good teacher. This is made even worse by the fact that PHYS5A is an absurdly difficult course. You will likely have to self-teach most of the material. I have genuinely never struggled in a course as much as I have in PHYS5A, and I feel that it is mostly because of how DeWeese teaches.

Very lenient grading, but partially because the grading system itself is lenient in curving. Some questions sounds like trick questions that deduct a few points in exams but still easy in general regardless of time constraints. ExpertTA hws are basically free full grades. If you took AP Physics before, this course is basically lecture-free

Prof. DeWeese was a very nice guy, but his teaching was not good. It baffles me how one could prepare lecture notes and then proceed to get confused about every example they do, confusing everyone else. Going to the lecture would genuinely hurt your physics knowledge (not an exaggeration). The tests were relatively fair and like practice tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Though occasionally tripped up by an error while lecturing, Deweese is a great teacher. He clearly cares about his students and is easily approachable. Homework is very tough and time consuming, but tests are fair.

Physics is just difficult in general for me but Deweese was a nice guy, stays behind for you. His lectures can get confusing at times but he will try to answer them. Homework every week (~10 questions), 2 midterms, and 1 final. His exams are hard but very similar to the practice exams he posts. Great artist too.

DeWeese is a smart and funny guy, however, his lectures are very disorganized. Rather than have prepared lecture notes, he would derive stuff for the first time in class and would waste a lot of time just trying to figure out where his mistake was. I would only recommend taking one of his classes if you already have a strong background in physics.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I'm conflicted with Professor Deweese. On one hand he was incredibly hilarious and knowledgable and lectures were enjoyable, but sometimes they were hard to follow. Wish he had slides in his lectures. Tests were hit or miss. Was very lenient on giving partial credit but it was hard to earn full credit. Overall Deweese is a good choice for physics

Prof. DeWeese is one of the best professors I've had- his lectures really drive the physics concepts, and he is an amazing artist as well and has a great sense of humor! He provides a lot of practice exams, and the exam grading is fair The homework assignments can take time but they really solidify your understanding.

He is an incredible artist with a great sense of humor and very entertaining lectures/demos. I enjoyed the lectures because attendance isn't necessary but if you go it helps you be engaged. The midterms are really fair and it is literally possible to cram the day of the midterm and make a B+ because he posts a lot of previous exams.

If you dont have a physics background, good luck. His lectures are incomprehensible and impossible if you dont know physics. He did little to transition the class to Zoom during lockdown and posted videos from several years prior that had faulty audio. I had to access the other sections lectures to attempt learning. Dont take his section please

His lectures are extremely hard to follow, since his writing is messy and he seems to confuse himself a lot. I had to do a lot of self studying to learn the material because of his poor teaching, but overall his exams are pretty fair.

DeWeese is very nice and accessible, but if you have no physics background then good luck. Physics is probably the most difficult class I have taken. He is very unorganized in his lectures, but the demos really helped me grasp the concepts. He curves the class and rarely fails students which is nice to know. Be ready to do a lot of self teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Deweese is a great guy and had some good demos and examples at times. However, I personally found it hard to follow along and stay focused during his lectures as he talks very fast and has messy and small handwriting that was hard to read.

Honestly, the professor is a great guy and really wants his students to succeed. But, the homework assignments already take up loads of time and you are expected to do countless problems other than the homework (to succeed on exams-80% of grade). Overall, a really interesting class, just requires numerous hours and LOTS self-studying!

Lectures sometimes felt sparatic, would sometimes go off on tangents. Lectures even got behind schedule as we got towards the end. Did learn some material through lectures. Exams were pretty/very difficult, but there is always one question that feels way harder than the others. Homework is taken from the textbook. Funny, passionate and an artist!

His lectures are slow, redundant and not helpful at all for 5A class. He is trying to improve his course obviously, but the reality does not work like that. His tests are wired and far from the assignments. He makes his own test problems, which makes the test a little bit far from the usual assignments he chooses from the book. Anyways, selfstudied

Okay, Michael Deweese is a great guy and his style of lecture is fairly good. He is usually a 7A and 8A teacher and it kinda shows. The 5 series is for Physics Majors not engineers or MCB majors. Try cramming Einstein's theory of special relativity into 1 lecture and then having it on a final! His lectures are straight from text, so self.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Really sweet and great guy. Always happy to stay after class. Will slow down in lecture if asked.

His lectures are really poor. He does not care to explain any of what he writes on the chalkboards, and he just assumed everything is obvious. On top of that his handwriting is very messy, and makes the class even more challenging. Definitely would enjoy physics if I had a different professor.

In a 1.5 hr lecture, only 15 mins is actually useful (e.g. demos, equation derived). Prof was not engaging at all and goes into long derivations/solves 2 problems during the time, which wasn't useful to understanding the physics. So, you'll need to get a conceptual understanding elsewhere. Exams are ok, but it's curved.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: It's difficult to follow Deweese during lecture if you don't have previous physics knowledge or if you don't read the book. He goes through a few long physics examples during lecture and derives relevant equations on the fly. Tests are long/difficult but generous in partial credit and seem to test a wider scope of material than other professors.

His lectures are absolutely useless. He teaches you the bare minimum, yet his homework and tests expect that you have a complete understanding of each topic. Take this guy's class if you'd like to spend hours teaching yourself from the book.

Lectures were interesting, but more of a complement to the reading. He went over theories and derivations often, which made the book material more clear. I went to lecture only about half of the time. Test questions were similar (sometimes identical!) to homework and practice problems.
DeWeese has amazing drawing skills, and is a fairly nice professor. Homework is the usual MasteringPhysics fare, and the exams were pretty tough too, with quite a few tricky questions in each exam.

It was so hard to get any feedback from this class. Even though they emphasized the importance of written homework at the beginning of semester and made it mandatory for us to work on them every week, they ended up not grading any of those. Tests were tough, but they were interesting and I liked them.
least favorite class of semester, so much to memorize for broad tests

Tests are brutal. Spends the entirety of lecture going over long derivations which you really don't need to know. Having a good GSI or reading the text is crucial to getting a decent grade in this class.

He's a nice guy and helpful in office hours but his lectures are confusing. It was his first time teaching 7A and he had trouble connecting concepts. Often long derivations in lecture, but exam questions often similar to lecture examples.  His class was a real struggle, but exams were fair. His drawings are amazing-- he's quite a talented artist.

Lectures are sooo boring and pointless. He fills them with derivations that never appear again. I remember one lecture he got through ONE problem in and hour and a half. Tests are fair for the most part, but you have to work on your own and read the textbook if you want a good grade.

Professor Deweese is approachable and wants students to succeed. He makes the class a suitable difficulty level, since most people taking it are not physics majors. He makes lecture interesting with jokes and demos, and his tests are fair. Do practice midterms, don't worry too much about understanding everything on mastering physics.

As always, getting a good GSI is crucial in Physics. Shop around the first week of classes. The exams are so straightforward that everyone nails them, so be sure to know all of the concepts. Seemed like a nice guy, which always helps. He did fail to proofread one midterm adequately, which led to some confusion, but he was apologetic about it.
His lectures are useless, but his tests are SUPER FAIR. The reading he assigns always correlates nicely with Mastering Physics. Go to lab, read the book, and do Mastering Physics, you'll get an A.
Lectures are useless. If you have a good GSI then it is all a lot easier. Mastering Physics is usually way more complicated then actual test questions. Use practice midterms/finals!

He only goes through boring derivations so lecture is worthless : he does no examples in class. If you know your mastering physics then you can do well on the midterms/final. Heavily curved I got a 92 and received a B. Just read the textbook on your own, class is a waste of time. He loves magnetism so make sure you know that. Very nice and clear!

Tests are very fair. Mastering Physics was the hardest part but make friends with someone from BSP and ask for the "Mastering Physics Tutorial" that some guy wrote a few yrs back. Without that I would not have known how to do the homework assignments. Whoever that wrote it (drareg whoever you are) - THANK YOU!!!!!
Good professor. FInal was fair! study adn do well. mastering physics is the worst part of course.
His practice exams DO NOT prepare you for the exams. They were MUCH easier than the actual tests. His lectures are not very helpful, as he is all over the place. Be sure to read the book.

Deweese is a really funny guy. His lectures are a bit hard to follow, so read the book beforehand. He is still a great teacher. His tests are also fair. Great teacher. I would definitely recommend him.

Quirky. Nice. Sometimes he's all over the place during lecture, but he knows his stuff.  Tests are fair. Labs are easy. The online homework can be annoying and are often harder than his tests. Better than Jacobsen for 8A from what I hear.

Lecture is worthless. Just read the book, take notes, understand major concepts, and do the homework. He doesn't trick you on tests, so that complicated problem you're trying to figure out isn't worth it. Given that people in 8b, aren't physics majors and probably taking it to fulfill a requirement, he makes the class difficulty appropriate

In short he is an awful lecturer. Given time, he will be great no doubt but he does not know how to teach us basic physics concepts. Teaching physics is really difficult and i guess it comes with experience, do mastering physics and get help from OH and youl be ok I did not go to a single lecture and I am doing well in the class, his exams are fair

Awesome and nice guy.  The midterms and final are straightforward and are based off the lectures, which is really a simplified version of the textbook.  Lectures aren't mandatory, but he does clarify concepts and equations.  The hardest part of the class was Mastering Physics.

His lectures are usually difficult to follow & he's absentminded at times, but some days are much better than others. Although not always effective, DeWeese is very willing to help his students during office hours & he is INCREDIBLY patient! He is nice, approachable & easy to talk to. If you do the HW, read the book, & attend OH, you'll be fine.

Deweese is a good teacher in that he is caring towards his students and always willing to clarify and answer questions. His teaching style is okay, can be a little dry at times, but he does get the concepts across. You should read the textbook and doing the homework helps too. His tests are really fair, no tricks. Just study and you'll do fine.

DeWeese = pure awesomeness! Very smart, nice, helpful, cares about his students and very humble! I never had a physics class before and the tests were doable!Get to have cheat sheet for each midterm and final!Office hours were always helpful!
this guy is awesome because unlike other classes in cal if you work hard you will get an A, your hard work pays off in his course, his exams are fair, not easy but fair

Deweese is an excellent professor for it being his first year. reading the book and and homework help significantly. getting an A is very possible, and i bet going to office hours and class aren't a bad idea! :) his research is very interesting and he is one of the few professors that share a genuine concern for his students!!!! :)
He wasn't very interesting, a bit absentminded. His lectures were useless except for the demos, those helped a lot
kinda easy. final was a bit tricky, but it was pretty easy overall. He needs to work on his teaching skills. Give him time... I'm sure he'll be better later.

Reading the textbook and doing Mastering Physics (online homework) are most important.      Lectures included a lot of demos, which I felt could reinforce the material but not  allow you to completely learn it.  Exams were mostly problem solving (not too conceptual).

First time teaching, so he was inexperienced in the beginning. But he improved a lot towards the end. Very nice man, the nicest professor I ever had. He cares about his students, and even though he is unclear at times, he is a pretty good lecturer. Also, his midterms are very easy but his final can get a little tricky. Overall, thumbs up.

This was his first time teaching so you have to keep that in mind. I think he was really trying to get used to teaching in a college environment. He is nice, approchable, and tried to keep students engaged. I think once he gets used to teaching at a university level, he'll be an awesome teacher so don't hesitate to take physics with him.

He has a great personality and is actually pretty funny. Besides the occasional jokes, his lectures are boring, because they are so hard to follow. He's pretty unorganized, isn't all that great at explaining, and doesn't spend time on concepts that need to be explained. However, his midterms were pretty straightforward and relatively easy.

He is inexperienced, and it shows. He spends a lot of time on demos, and sometimes gets flustered. However, that being said, he is extremely enthusiastic and wants it to be fun for his students. His midterms are relatively easy, and the text good enough to learn what he doesn't cover well in lecture

Deweese is a first year professor and it is quite noticeable in his teaching, however he is really nice and the homework and the book are great teaching tools....he allows you to have cheat sheet and for never having taken physics, the first midterm seemed easy compared to the other class. there is no curve, so everyone is pretty friendly!!!!!

He is a nice guy but he is very inexperienced and does not know how to teach effectively, lectures are pretty useless and you need to teach everything to yourself to get a descent grade, but still .... very nice guy but he shouldn't teach .. yet
Horrible teaching. Does not know what he's doing on the board. Confusing textbook, confusing homework, confusing lectures. Straight up horrible.

A very enthusiastic professor who emphasizes the beauty in what he's teaching. The perfect professor for a first abstract mathematics class. His tests reward those who work hard, not those who've already done lots of high level stuff and just get by (tests lots of theorems). He motivates everything. Gave me the confidence to continue in math.
Truly the worst professor in my life
Worst professor ever. Totally a mistake for choosing this professor.
OMG, worst professor in my entire life and it was completely a mistake for taking him. Hugely discouraged my motivation for learning stats.

Unclear and disorganized. Wants you to understand things that aren't explained in class. Seems helpful and kind on the facade, not really on a personal level, quite condescending. Incomprehensible grading criteria. It's an interesting and a completely doable class, just take it with someone else who knows better.

Good textbook (Axler). I don't like the grading (integers from 1-10). Messes up sometimes. Good in office hours, and overall a good instructor, though the class is a bit unorthodox compared to other 110 classes. sexy french accent tho
Great professor!

extremely BAD professor. French accent, can't explain the material well, and always makes mistakes during his prove (students have to correct him all the time). His grading system sucks! The textbook was not that bad, but he makes us memorizing EVERY theorem and proposition!!!
amazing

Professor Dherin taught Math 110 very well - his French accent can sometimes be difficult to understand, but he covers the whole course in reasonable depth and finishes early, leaving the last four or five classes for questions - a well taught class

I was really excited about this course. Sadly it taught me nothing and even included homework that seemed pretty irrelevant and a waste of my time :( Big "project" throughout the semester which again, taught me very little that I could have learned on my own time.
He made interesting topic terribly boring....

Allowed to bring every material to the exam including computers. However, there is essentially no partial credit when your answer is wrong even though almost all the work is right. Don't go to his office hours because every time I go there it seems like he has more important things to do than dealing with undergrads. Not the worst class in ME tho.
Sit in front, study his notes and you'll do fine.

Awful!  Avoid at all costs!  While he seemingly is easy based on the low amount of work, his tests are brutal and cover nothing he says in lecture.  His lectures are minimal with him getting sidetracked easily answering stupid off topic questions.
The class is pretty easy and he doesn't use a textbook.  HW approximately every other week and occasional quizzes

I took Penny's photography classes back in the summer and fall of 1977. She had a great interest in her students progress and encouraged them to achieve their personal goals. She worked with her students quite often on her own time. She even had her class over at her house for a turkey dinner (she cooked) as we photographed each other. Thanks Penny

Penny was an excellent teacher who pushed my slide photography classmates and me to take great photos and to think about an image as being part of a bigger compostion over time. She had interesting stories and though a bit disorganized at times, I learned a lot about composition, filters, and reflections.

she didn't act like she hated men in my class. she was more like a guide than an instructor, more like a facilitator than a lecturer.it was a color slide photography class, and she really brought out the creativity in people.

I don't get the animosity toward Dr. Wang. She's an awesome professor. She's super knowledgeable, approachable, and teaches some of the most engaging classes I've had at Cal. The material is interesting, relatable to everyday life, and I really liked the variety of class activities. I learned a lot in her class!!!

Took her for PS124W and it was her first semester teaching at Berkeley and it showed. She's really nice and caring, even changed grades/due dates to accommodate students, but this class was disorganized and confusing at times. The GSI and the professor were not 100% aligned on grading or even rubrics for projects worth 25%+ of the grade.

The prof was really nice, but her class is unorganized. She cancelled 3 classes and had another 3 taught by librarians; it's like she didn't want to teach. There was no actual course content, it was lowkey just yapping. Easy A, but you don't learn and it's frustrating how unorganized and unclear the assignments are. Wtf is a conversational exam!

Nayak was a great and passionate lecturer who broke down complex topics in a simple and eloquent manner. She also specified what reading was relevant on slides which enhanced studying. Exams were difficult but she also posted what topics are going to be covered. Cheat sheet allowed on exam.

Her lectures provided tons of examples and how to approach them, and she was a great lecturer, providing visual elements through the chalkboard and much more. She was approachable and kind. Her section had a fair exam, and I do feel her personal notes assisted in studying.
Very clear lectures with extra practice problems. She is very kind and has useful annotated slides ontop of the practice problems. Definitely one of my favorite professors from Cal.
Absolutely GOATED professor. I loved her, and highly recommend!!
Negrin is a truly passionate and brilliant professor who cares deeply about her students. Could not recommend enough!

Very chill professor who is clearly passionate about her work, and has interesting lectures. She assigns a lot of reading (you can skim them, but I found most to be engaging), and the grade consists of 3 papers and 4 reading responses. She does tend to go on tangents a lot and get off track when answering questions, but still engaging overall.
goat professor

there were 3 straightforward papers and 4 reading responses. and if anything comes up, just talk to her about it. she's super chill and awesome. i loved everything we read and i found them to be foundational texts that I continued to reference in my classes I took later on

Professor Negrin is very passionate about her topic which creates an engaging lecture albeit long. Has extra credit opportunities but for minimal points. Only 3 graded written assignments and small discussion assignments. The final project is really interesting and you have freedom to choose your format. Grade booster class honestly, def recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Super nice but is hand-wavy. Spends most of class discussing her research with a specific indigenous tribe in Mexico--everything comes back to that constantly. Heavy focus on "natural" systems--this is not a class that is a survey of political environmental movements. Not super organized. However, it's an easy class and has chill and fun lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Diana is a wonderful lecturer who keeps class content incredibly down to earth and digestible. In class discussions augmented her lectures to make an interesting, tight knit class environment. There are many small-medium assignments but she has clear criteria and gives you enough time to complete them, and most are unique and engaging.

Really great class at surveying key issues in environmental politics/EJ with global case studies. Material tends to represent Latin America more than other regions. Moderate reading, no tests, minimal homework; grade is mostly one big case study that is very manageable. Prof is a really cool person with a lot of good irl experience to draw from.

Professor Negrin is amazing! She always made class very interesting and engaging, and encouraged students to speak on their own experiences and ideas. You can tell how passionate and knowledgeable she is on the topic during lectures. The class mostly consisted of weekly readings -- some were long but they were all still interesting. 110% recommend!

Professor Da Silva is one of the most genuine, compassionate, and kind professors I've had. She is able to lecture and conduct class conversations around incredibly heavy content, while still imparting students with hope and positivity that a better future is possible. She doesn't bombard students with work, and offers an amazing class playlist!

Diana is really sweet! She really cares about her students' learning so she doesn't make her classes stressful. She assigned a lot of reading, but would always go over it in class. Class assignments consisted of 2 short midterm essays and a final project. Attendance was mandatory.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: So many classes at Cal can be too stressful to enjoy and actually learn. Not Border Geographies with Professor Negrin Da Silvas. She uses many mediums of teaching to immerse students in the realities that she is teaching. 100% would take this class again!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: amazing lecturer who fully understood concepts and was able to connect concepts and in class learning with current world issues. the readings were very helpful and she did well at explaining their importance and connecting the reading to overall class by the end of the semester
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Overall, an exciting & intriguing class with lots of cool guest speakers, but co-taught & instructors often gave confusing &/or contradictory feedback, making it hard to iterate on group design assignments. It's evident that Digeo cares deeply for the class & students; however, despite corrective efforts, grading criteria were incredibly unclear

Instructor Diego cares for his students; he often checks for understanding and emails extra resources. Almost the entire course was based around one harshly-graded (but not difficult) group project, a slideshow presentation. We receive very positive feedback in class, but extremely low grades later on; assignment expectations were not very clear.

Had so many bad professors for SED leading up to Diego, where he was the professor that was dedicated, engaging, and grounded.
He structured the class around real-world work that made the capstone feel impactful. Though he brings so much to the table, it is important to be proactive in keeping him up to date on your work and team for a good grade.

He cared deeply about his students and took into consideration their opinions of his students! His passion can be seen clearly through his lectures, assignments, and feedback. He gives specific and good feedback on assignments, and I greatly appreciate his efforts to make the class enjoyable.

Good project in theory, but difficult to execute. We were assigned a project in East Palo Alto (~2.5 hours away). Throughout the project, we were given positive feedback, so we assumed we needed minor improvement. However, once we submitted our final project, we were graded harshly. There was a lack of organization and communication.

Diego is a passionate/dedicated instructor who deeply cares about his students and their success. Diego gave us structured guidance but also the flexibility to explore the needs of our different projects. He went out of his way to make himself available for feedback/support and challenged us to think about our work in new and unconventional ways.

Diego is a caring, dedicated, and knowledgeable professor. I truly enjoyed his class and appreciated his guidance throughout our capstone project. He connected us with real companies and gave us a clear sense of what to expect in our future careers. He truly cares about his students. I strongly recommend him.
Diego was very supportive of the group and provided detailed feedback throughout our project. He cares alot about his students and their success.

Diego was a dedicated/ caring teacher and supported us through our capstone project. He communicated effectively and gave great comments for us to integrate into our work. He is a critical thinker and supports thinking outside of the box and innovation. I learned a lot and would definitely recommend!
Diego put great effort into supporting the success of our group project! He was a huge help in achieving our goals for our capstone class

Diego came to UC Davis to teach LDA 141. It was obvious that he cared and wanted us to do well, but the class was incredibly disorganized, misleading, and exhausting. He rambled constantly, was terrible at communicating information, assigned busywork unrelated to projects, and mislabeled a ton of points as extra credit that he assigned arbitrarily.

Diego is a great person and a super nice guy that cares about his students wellbeing. But, he is very confusing, this could have been due to a language barrier but seems like it is just difficult for him to articulate his thoughts. He gave conflicting instructions and unclear feedback to students. Very hard to understand objectives and assignments.

I enjoyed this class and the professor. There are some amazing guest speakers from high up careers in marking and PR which is great. The only thing I did not like was how heavy the workload was on the group project. The requirements to me required a lot more than what a 2 unit class should require. But Diane is great and I learned a lot.

You do have to do some work, a lot of homework and a lot of group projects but the hw is pretty easy. Gives good feedback and wants to get to know her students she requires we all do ONE office hour appointment. I really like her though. Only had one exam (the final) and she told us what would be on it in her review session, she's nice.

it was o,, not great. It felt passive, at the end we had to take a big test but we didn't necessarily follow a curriculum so I was upset that the class was not  more organized so I can prepare for a test. We didn't follow a textbook or anything.  I can't say I learned anything. it felt superficial and not organized.
Fantastic teacher! Super relatable and kind, I highly reccomend her!!!!!!!
Great class! It was great working with real clients and presenting to the CEOs.

Clearly doesn't know how to make final exams that are feasible for students (especially with the final exam being worth 40%). It seems like he includes "interesting" topics that are rarely discussed in class out of pure amusement for himself.

Makes the final, which is worth about 40% of your overall grade, the hardest thing you have ever taken or done in the class. He will take the smallest topic or detail that is briefly mentioned and create an entire problem out of it that is worth 25% of the final. He needs to learn how to be fair to his students.

Exams are difficult but not the worst, but the material on the final is the hardest and midterm 2 was also pretty hard. Exams were similar to practice exams. Some hw involved matlab so going to OH really helps to figure out what functions to use and how to debug your code. He will sit with you until you understand the material. Great professor!

I took MATH 217 with him at Michigan and while his quizzes were harder than most sections, he dropped a significant amount of your lowest grades at the end of the semester so the grades were about the same as the other sections. He is very nice and is always smiling and laughing. Great professor and I definitely recommend taking 217 with him!

His Chinese accent is sometimes unclear during lecture. However, he makes up for it by providing quality typeset lecture notes that can basically replace the textbook (I studied out of just the notes). The only thing I did not enjoy about his class were the somewhat excessive difficulties of his exams, as compared to other professors this spring.

Prof Ding is hands down the best math prof I have taken a course with. His lectures are clear and easy to understand, and his notes are amazing (super organized + clear). I hardly had to use the textbook thanks to his notes. He is also very friendly and approachable in office hours. The course is hard simply due to the nature of the subject.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The best lectures I have had! The professor cared a lot about the student experience in class and put a lot of effort into class. In addition to the lectures and textbook (Ross), he provided his own notes as well. His lectures, notes, and the textbook all provided unique perspectives on the content. Highest of quality, highly suggest!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class was quite difficult, coming from STAT 135, and his lectures are hardly understandable. However, go to lab sections and stay on top of the textbook materia,l and you'll do fine
Absolute unit of a professor! He's smart, sharp, and you're in for a treat taking the class with him. My one concern is his naming convention. Variables names in his book are stacked!!

Peng seems awesome!  I think he'd be great in a grad level stats class. He is really nice and passionate. I feel like he's maybe not a match for data102 though because he tends to go a bit more into theory rather than stay on track with what's in scope. I feel like i miss a lot of what he lectures about due to the fact that I struggle with proofs.

He's a really intelligent guy and clearly knowledgeable about causal inference, but hard to follow. I feel like his lectures require a level of mathematical maturity beyond the prereqs or scope of the class. I read the textbook and brush up on topics beforehand, but leave his lectures confused. I've heard that he's a nice guy in person.
Lectures are full of jargon and nearly incomprehensible unless you have extremely strong mathematical maturity with a mastery of probability.

Peng is a good professor if you ask him questions specifically about the topic, but the way he lectures requires lots of statistical maturity, and his lectures often go into complex proofs rather than explanations in comparison to Ramesh's easy to follow along slides. If there were slides for every lecture, the class would be easier to understand.
Prof. Ding is an amazing instructor. His class is very well-organized and inspiring. Coming from a background in econometrics, I feel I can still learn a lot from the class.

Super clear and well organized. He is very nice and is willing to help students with the course materials and research projects. He did a lot of frontier research projects on causal inference, which is another plus. I will definitely recommend his courses.

This class was a big leap coming off of 134/5 in terms of difficulty: I put a lot of time into trying to understand notation/various concepts the professor assumed we already knew. He also lectures very quickly, tho he'll stop to answer questions. The lecture notes were super helpful. Homeworks were very algebra heavy. Overall an interesting course
Amazing Prof. Very caring and interesting. One of my favorites at Berkeley!

NO.1 FAN OF POPOVIC! Feels like my intellectual level has been improved by 10 times after attending his class for one semester. Although it's a literature class, he would always bring in history and philosophy into the discussion. In terms of grading he's chill, but if you DO want to learn and participate in class you'd better do all the readings.
Must take. Great professor. Take all his classes, he will inspire you.

Easily one of the best professors in the department, if not the university. A classic educator, more emphasis placed on discussion, synthesis, analysis, and understanding than on points and grades. Definitely a must-take.

Took SLAVIC 39N - not sure why it isn't in the dropdown. The only assignments are weekly discussion boards & ex cred. No midterm or final. Even though the class meets once a week for 2 hours, Professor Popovic makes every meeting interesting! He is knowledgeable and enthusiastic about his subject. As long as you do the discussions, it's an easy A.

I literally made an account just to rate Djordje. HE IS THE BEST!!!!!!!! I've never had a more understanding or supportive teacher. He is charmingly long-winded and will work to make the class work for you. Though there is much reading to do, he gives incredible insight while allowing for your own interpretation. TAKE CLASS WITH HIM!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: genuinely this man is so deeply unhelpful responding to any emails. In office hours he can barely help you. lectures are so deeply not engaging. Doesn't seem to have any vested interest in his students' wellbeing or learning.
One of the best. And we can't forget how cute he is.
super hot. thats it, ur welcome.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Cool guy
Thanks to Ethan, I succeeded at getting a B-. In no-time, I will be pursuing a PhD in applied mathematics!

Ethan was such a great professor this semester. His lectures were incredibly clear and straightforward. However, the best part of his class was him entertaining us. His personality and looks are a 10/10. Most definitely recommend taking his class;)
Amazing instructor who tries to get us excited about the beauty of mathematics. Plus, super friggin hot - this man is a total specimen and I would do anything to be his forever.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Hard professor but fair, genuine and legitimately cared about his students. Get ready to work.

He is a very nice professor and very understanding. I had him during the pandemic (when everything was online) and he was probably my only STEM professor that cared about the well being of his students. Although he does take awhile to grade, everything that is on his tests he has covered before. He doesnt try to throw hard balls or trick anyone.
He seemed to care a lot more than most of my other professors, especially online. Sometimes he would grade assignments slowly, but he was always fair. He seems super smart

A smart and nice professor. I received my first "not A" grade in math in his class at Berkeley, so this class is the hardest from my perspective. But his lectures are pretty interesting! The most interesting class I have ever had online. Would take again for p/np not for graded and simply enjoy his lectures :P

Dmiry is nice and smart but a terrible teacher/communicator. He writes unintelligibly. He never responds to emails or Piazza questions. He took 50 days to grade my midterm in a class of 24 students. He makes at least half a dozen mistakes every lecture. He lectured during RRR week (against university policy) because he "forgot RRR week existed."

He always spend lots of time to present useless stuff. Problem set is not related to his lecture. Even his GSI did a better teach job than himself. DO NOT waste your precious time in CAL to take his class. totally USELESS .

Lectures are filled with hundreds of half relevent behavioral experiments, psets are difficult because technical problems are never gone over in class. Got an A in 100A/100B/ Stats20 and yet my GPA was tanked by this class. Went into the final with a 94 and came out with a B, despite mastering every pset. Whole grading process is a black box.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Hes terrible, unclear, and unhelpful. His problem sets are even more useless than him. Take someone else unless you are interested in bringing down your GPA for fun.

Terrible. This class used to have an A- average, but I'm pretty sure he curved it to a B/B- for an upper division Econ class at Cal, which usually curves to a B+. His grading criteria was super confusing, and I felt really unprepared. Also, he didn't release final exam grades. No regrade requests. He obviously doesn't care about his students.

Dear Dr. Doudna,

Your field needs to get to classification systems, founded on common principles, so science can develop over time. An example of this, is developing work from constant STEM principles for a strong solution or frame. Start with the most stable laws like physics (math), versus chemistry (fluctuate).
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: The class is not curved so good luck soldiers. Very difficult to fail this class but also very difficult to get an A. Doudna is not bad at teaching but it is clear she is only teaching because its required. Focuses more heavily on crispr and random genetic testing stuff in tests even though it was not covered.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is completed wack but just know that if you don't like bio 1a. You are gonna see doudna's name EVERYWHERE on campus no matter where you look.

If you love bio, you'll love this class. Most lectures are interesting but occasionally go on a tangent. Really enjoyable, but keep going to lecture or you will fall behind quickly because there are 3 lectures a week. She encourages us to read from the textbook at night after lectures, I wish I did that...

I know that Doudna is an extremely well accomplished biochemist but with that being said she should NOT be teaching a general bio class. Her lectures were dense and seemed like she should have been talking to students who were WELL into their bio career already. Her teaching was just not for me. Get ready to sit there and be lost.
She's a nice person! Her lectures are straight from the book and her exam is pretty much straight recall. If you don't know the book you're going to do awful

Professor Doudna uses the textbook A LOT. Most of her slides, graphics, and questions come directly from the Campbell textbook. To really understand her section in Bio1A, you need an adequate Chemistry background.
Exam questions are tricky.

She's a good lecturer in that she's organized and well spoken but she doesn't engage the students that well. I went to all the lectures but it felt no different from watching them online. Read the textbook chapter before and after, lectures alone won't cut it.
Obviously more focused on her research than teaching. Smart person but poor lecturer in terms of pacing (never finished her slides in time) and organization. Not a great teacher.

One of the 3 teachers teaching BIO1A SP'23. Yes, she earned a Nobel Prize. But no, she cannot teach. That very much is obvious and no hate to her. Had to use lots of outside material to even get an inch about what was expected in the midterm and final. Pay very close attention to her lectures as well. Her questions are very.. specific.
Not the worst but not the best. Her lectures are clear and helpful, but the exam questions are difficult and test on material very briefly mentioned in the lecture.

Very average professor. Cared more about her research than students, exams were hard and lectures were boring. Not many questions on quizzes/exams were taken from lecture but were instead taken from one small minute detail in the textbook (or from a very tiny written sentence on one of her slides). Not the most interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Good researcher.
Straightforward class, but heavy content.

Biochem was very dry for me, and Doudna, although illustrious, did not help. I fell asleep in lecture often. At the same time, midterm was not bad and even though I only studied the day before, I got an A-. It's the easiest unit, even though it's probably the most boring. Read the book, iClicker questions are hard, but overall easiest unit.
This is a hard class. Lots of information presented. Doudna is well organized and clear in her demands, albeit a bit dry.
Good instructor and class
Went completely by the book, but straightforward material as long as you follow her lecture slides with the textbook.

Forget about masteringphysics or masteringchemistry, the newly implemented Aplia site they're using has questions that are not difficult, but screw you over for the stupidest things.  If you missed a question, a point is taken off.  The questions care so much more about naming and labeling than anything conceptual, and there are no retries.

For those who have a strong foundation in the basics of biology (basic biochemistry, cell structure, the first ten-ish chapters of AP Bio if you took it), I recommend getting an extra hour of sleep three times a week and just watching her webcast. It's not that she's a bad professor, but more this is information you already know and need refreshing

She used many questions from the book, but she was good at emphasizing some key concepts. The exam had too many questions for an hour long, though, and some were really hard. However, the academic coordinator did this, not her. She was ok in office hours, but not extremely helpful. I would look forward to having her for MCB 102.
Very helpful in office hours. Easy to get a good grade if you take good notes and listen in lecture.

Taught amino acid/protein component. Very clear lectures. Makes material understandable. The test is fair. She emphasizes concepts rather than dull memorization. Gives weekly practice questions. For comparison, her portion was easier than Bio 1A material.

Her lectures were very clear and organized and she made the material interesting and understandeable. Her test was also really fair, and actually easier than I had expected. You still need to read the book(throughout the class) but she is definitely one of the better mcb professors.

i actually really liked her teaching for mcb 102. i thought she was very clear and to the point. although i did find it helpful to read through the asuc lecture notes (former black lightning notes)for some of the lessons, since some stuff you cannot find in the book. her test was pretty reasonable.

Only lectures with ppt. I love it, other ppl hate it. There is a LOT of material. The lectures are 1.5 hrs, so my brain was fried at the end of ea lecture. Very clear lecturing style and I enjoyed the anecdotes. The class is very research oriented. Knows her stuff and answers questions well. No book. Study off the ppts and practice questions.
She does not put any effort into her lectures. She is not enthusiastic about teaching science or at least it seems.
too much reading and things that were on her slides that she didnt cover because it seemed like extra details ended up on the test.  not a fun portion for bio 1a.

Her lectures weren't interesting at all b/c she only reads off her powerpoint slides during lecture, and has no sense of humor to make the learning experience more fun. Her exams are also very irritating. She asked several q's on the exam that we barely covered and several that were very tricky.
the most boring class i've taken here at cal.  she has a really boring voice too.  MC tests.

Clearly addicted to powerpoint. One lecture her computer wasn't working and just ended up reading off the notes. People with printed out slides were ok, but everyone else was lost. As a personal chalkboard enthusiast, I didn't enjoy her lectures.
Her lectures are interesting, but she reads off powerpoint notes which can be a bit hard to follow at times.  Definetly try to do the reading before lecture to keep up.

I've found that your opinion of him will depend on which GSI you had. I had a GSI that was super confusing so Prof Livdan's lectures were really beneficial to me. The class was the hardest I've taken at Haas but manageable. Frustrating b/c we had access to so many past exams that were all similar, yet our actual exams were really different.

Prof Livdan is hilarious and very knowledgeable. Def go to his office hours, leverage the chance to get to know him and for him to know you better. I was able to apply many concepts to the real finance world after class. It's not easy A tho! Def lots of work!

DON'T TAKE THIS PROFESSOR IF YOU HAVE ANOTHER OPTION. I don't know why this professor has been the only option for the past seven years for UGBA 103. It's said that ugba 103 is one of the hardest classes at Haas. But the concepts themselves are not too hard. It is just because the PROFESSOR is so confusing. The way he explained thing is so confused

Livdan is a great professor who is approachable and caring. That being said you will have to work for an A in this class, but to get a B is pretty easy. The mean on the exams was like 54%. So its hard, but if you study the old exams and pay attention in discussions youll be good to go.

Like others have said, he is a good professor in terms of breaking down concepts and formulas and keeping all course material applicable to the real world. What I learned in this class helped me immensely in banking interviews. Definitely take it if you are interested in doing any valuation-type jobs. Practice tests are everything!!

Dmitry is really accessible to students and wants to help you learn. If you pay attention in class and do all of the practice tests it's really straightforward. Some of the cases are a little hard but really interesting
hes funny and good at teaching
Professor Livdan really cares about his students and really tries to create a welcoming environment where all students can feel comfortable asking questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dmitry is a super great guy and entertaining lecturer. He explains concepts pretty well and does a great job of clarifying when asked. The class overall is pretty easy as long as you practice.
easy class, livdan is super funny
Not great, but then again it's finance - if he really knew what he was talking out, he wouldn't be teaching.

Professor Livdan's current rating is undeservingly low. Someone below said fill up your cheatsheet, but tests are open-note, and he provides many practice tests so that you're well prepared. I will say that I had a great GSI for this course, which improved my understanding when he occasionally made material more complicated than it should be.

Dmitry definitely makes you work hard in this class. However, I think his expectations are reasonable considering that Haas is one of the best undergraduate business programs in the world. To pass the midterm make sure you read the book and practice a lot. To ace the final study directly from the previous exams (you'll identify the pattern). GL!

This is my most difficult class at Haas. The regular course work is not too difficult, 4 homework assignments and 3 case studies. However, I do not feel I was prepared for the midterm and final. None of what he goes over in lecture will help you on the tests and he makes them unreasonably difficult. Get ready to fill up your cheatsheet...
just focus on his slides and understand it, focus on the practice exam, you will get an easy A. Professor also reply super fast with emails.

I struggled so hard in 103 and I honestly don't think the concepts were hard, Livdan just doesn't teach them well. He's very unclear and throws out formulas without really explaining them. Tests are open note but way harder than practice tests - even with notes they're hard to understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: This class was frustrating because I was really looking forward to learning finance. However, I ended up just learning everything from the book, which I could have done on my own. Even though he's very knowledgable, he just speeds through stuff as if we know the material like he does, and it just starts becoming a waste of time.
He is very humorous yet charismatic. One of the best professor I took at CAL. He made me wanting to pursit finance as a career.

Awesome teacher, pretty entertaining. You will do good if you do the work ON TIME, work to understand concepts, what you don't understand see the teacher about, read the book or the slides (book has good explanations) and PRACTICE! not your regular "leave everything till last minute" class. Mandatory discussions attend. most of grade based on tests

Class was enjoyable. Dmitry has a great personality and contrary to previous posts, I felt he was very reasonable with his expectations. He must have paid attention to his semester reviews because he took it pretty easy on us with the exams.
Doesn't really follow the text and the homework is pretty useless. He makes up his own curriculum which really high level and then tests you on it. Difficult class.
Dr. Livdan knows his stuff, but the class moves too fast, and he can't tell when we're struggling. Tests seemed to come out of nowhere.
Don't take. Too hard! Lots of supplements from his MBA class. Even if you like finance.... this is not the class for you

Very difficult! Nice man who does his best to help, but if anything that makes it worse because he doesn't realize we're all suffering! :( Take with Opp in a later semester if possible. My hardest Haas class by far (and im a Math double)

If you dont go to class, its very very hard to get a good grade. Goes really fast on lectures. If I didnt practice what had been taught in class that day, so essentially you need to keep up every week, i was confused from then on. He kind of expects you to know about finance already.
Lectures were hard to follow. Livdan's a funny guy with a comical Russian accent, but not a great teacher. Very difficult final. Killed my GPA. Definitely was my hardest Haas class
Easiest A+ I have gotten at Berkeley. Curve was huge
He teaches as all students are PhDs. This should give you a clue if you want to take his class.He is a nice guy, but being a nice guy won't help anyone. The hardest class ever at Haas.

I agree with the rater below that Livdan DOES care about his students. If you approach him for help, he tries his best to be helpful and the graders seemed lenient. But the material was far too theoretical and difficult to grasp.. this class was truly frustrating. You put effort in and don't see results. Livdan is a nice, funny, sweet man though.
Despite all the negative postings, Professor Livdan does care about his students and wants them to be successful. However, the way he teaches the class is atypical for Haas.
Agree to previous comments. Livdan's Finance class is very hard!
Very HARD! What's more to say...?

The worst class I've ever taken at Haas!  It's more of a professor issue than a course although his materials are bad either, MBA for undergrad. Don't take Livdan if you want to learn & maintain your GPA!
True, MBA level for undergrads but it's good to be pushed beyond our comfort zone sometimes. It's really hard so hoping for curve to help GPA.  No grades yet but crossing fingers that I don't fail :(

His lectures and exams are way above and beyond the book he assigned (MBA lvl). However, his class is manageable if you keep catching up with the lectures and put MUCH effort. This is what you should expect from #4 Best Finance Undergrad Program. Many people skipped class, didn't know wtf going on in class, and freaked out 2 weeks before the exams.

HARDEST CLASS OF ALL TIME. I have a 3.9 Haas GPA and I'm sitting here wondering if I'm going to fail the final today. Honestly, avoid this guy at all costs. The tests and practice material are ridiculously hard and like nothing in the book, final is going to be you looking at 500 formulas on your cheat sheet and praying something clicks.

Yes, he's a very nice man but the course is really hard for an introduction. In a way undergrads are lucky to be exposed to MBA-level of finance but this could ruin our GPA. Funny & entertaining lectures though ("Is it clear to everyone?") If we put in more effort, we could maybe absorb more? He's undeniably intelligent though; he knows his stuff!

Unless you want to learn a pile of theoretical crap then avoid Livdan. Hes a nice guy, but his lectures are mostly derivations, his exams are nothing like the homework, and the final topics are out of his MBA class material, not the text book. If you are an engineer or math major take with Livdan, otherwise avoid.

Hardest class I have ever taken at Berkeley. He is a nice man, but he cannot teach to save his life. He gives us material at the MBA level and his tests are 3 long questions which are far more difficult than anything done in class or for homework. Abort mission! Intro to Finance should not be this difficult.

He is very nice man with boring jokes and heavy Russian accent. Midterm and final are at MBA level. Matter fact, all his practice tests are from his MBA class. This is a 4 unit class. Do not ruin your grade. Avoid him with all costs.
Tests are very hard and do not reflect what he goes though in lectures.

Just a wonderful professor. Has an incredible breadth of knowledge about critical development around the world. In GPP 150, a discussion-based class, he's always willing to engage with students' ideas, often leading the class to valuable tangential concepts. Students always feel comfortable sharing questions & thoughts & how they're doing.

Great professor, very passionate about his subject. Attendance is a huge factor for success in this class, but assignments are graded fairly overall. Topics are extremely interesting, so would 100% recommend taking this class.

Professor Doll is a profoundly inspiring and compassionate lecturer whose course radiates humanity and hope. His approach to sensitive topics and his willingness to show his own humanness made the experience transformative. This class reshaped my perspective and should be a required course. I'm deeply grateful for his guidance and lasting impact.

I have never learned/cared about anything as much as I do GPP 115. Lectures are great.  The most important class anyone could take, it gives a lot of perspective. If you lack empathy/care for others, you won't enjoy, but you're prob shallow/boring and should get over yourself. I love this class and prof doll, and I'm sad it's over. 100% recommend

Prof. Doll is a very good lecturer and is clearly very knowledgeable on the topics covered in class. His lectures are interesting, and he explains things in a way that gives his opinion while still being able to let you develop your own. His slides don't contain much information, so attendance is important because 90% of the info comes from him.

Genuinely one of the most knowledgeable and caring profs I've had in some time. It is an accelerated course if you take it during the summer, so a lot of work is to be expected. Readings are interesting and complement the lecture well. This class is so good for your academic career, but also just to grow as a person. 11/10 would recommend!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Final exam, 1 midterm, 3 analytic film reviews (1k words), 10 reading reflections. Avoid this class for a breath or gpa booster, etc. It is NOT an easy class. Exam qs are given beforehand. Course is at times too chaotic; too many scholars to understand; lecture slides are essentially an extension of Doll's incomplete thoughts and unorganized
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Doll is an amazing and kind professor who is very flexible and understanding of student concerns and circumstances. Lectures are information-dense, but very interesting. I always left class rethinking perspectives around the world. You have to study for the midterms and finals, but you get the questions ahead of time. Highly recommend.

Prof. Doll is a super sweet guy who is always open to meeting up and talking. His lectures are informative and make you think deeply about the topics. The midterm and final are pretty tough, but he gives you the questions ahead of time, so you just need to study. He's a great guy; I learned a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He was an amazing professor who taught the course very well. One of my favorite classes ever. This class made me really think deeply about world poverty. Professor Doll was very kind and accommodating to some life events I had towards the end of the semester. Lots and lots of readings highly recommend using ChatGPT to understand material.

Extremely accommodating and understanding professor that is extremely passionate about his work.  You leave lecture rethinking the world. There is a lot of reading but it is all very interesting (especially Hickel). The class is rewarding but not an easy A. Class is extremely applicable, highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Drummond was a mixed bag when I took this class. I enjoyed his no-nonsense teaching style, and witty humor. However, class felt disorganized. Often, he would go on side tangents, and article feedback was limited to just occasional, brief critiques in lecture. Class sometimes ended super early. I felt like I learned more from the GSI, Emily.

Taking this graduate course and visiting San Quentin every Sunday was truly a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity—one that has reshaped my passions and career goals. Not only is Drummond an incredible advocate for criminal justice reform, but he is also an amazing mentor. If you get any opportunity to work with him, don't waste it. He has made history.

I took a seminar with Prof. Drummond about memes in the media studies department. I enjoyed his "hip" knowledge of pop culture and healthy skepticism of the media, despite being a journalist. I would take a proper class with him, given the chance. He is very invested in the bay area community, which is cool.

Go back to stat 20 please. First half of the semester was great, grading fast, lectures were helpful, and then idk what happened but everything fell apart. Quizzes (50% of your grade) weren't graded till after the final, leaving you confused on where you stand in the class. Just not how an upper div programming class should have been run.
No score distributions + heavy workload for a 3-unit class…

Bray is a great teacher and I loved his class, but the class assignments are structured to stress you out. Quizzes are 50% of your grade and are extremely hard. Plus, you have projects every other week, problem sets every week. You will suffer a lot but ps and projects are p/np so that's a plus. I can't keep up with class anymore after mid-term.

STAT133 used to be about projects and learning R. Prof. Bray offers a course all about looking nice, but filled with memorization. There are 7 "quizzes" worth 50% of your grade that are an hour long each. This is the worst path a prof can take to battle gen. AI. One look at other programming classes and the prof. would've made a better curriculum.

nice & chill guy but lowk class is a mess itself. quizzes are 50% of the grade and occur every two weeks, there's a group quiz and individual quiz and get averaged together for your official grade, meanwhile the final is 30% so beware of that. quizzes r pretty hard w/ the material given bcs it can be pretty different from hws.
just don't do it...

FOR STAT133*
His first semester teaching stat 133. sweet guy, passionate about data science, showed us tools for future use.  no midterm, but there is constant heavily graded quizzes (two, one individual and one group) every other week for the whole semester so it's like constantly having a midterm anyway. Could be more organized in assignments.

Love him! His teaching style is organized and easy to follow/note down. The content isn't difficult and his class is interesting. It was easier spring of 25, lost the gsi and never had lab(we didn't code much). You do a semester long group project where you have full creativity. He's great to talk to and his exams are based on lecture (don't skip!)
Very straightforward, engaging lectures, organization could have been improved.

It's very easy to follow and understand his lectures. But you're absolutely skrewed if you consistently miss lectures. I think he's genuinely a good teacher, with his attitude, demonstrations etc... But the lectures aren't recorded, and they barely give you any material to study from. We had a few quizzes, labs and a final. No midterms.

The professor understands the content very well, but this class assigns a bit too much work outside of class. The labs are pretty time-consuming. The content isn't too bad and the quizzes are fairly easy as long as you understand the notes thoroughly. There are a lot of resources for help (eg. Ed was helpful in labs). You should attend class.

Very good professor. The new class structure is very engaging. Love the coding aspect of the class. Hadn't written a line of code before this class in my life. Go to group tutoring, and it will save you hours of work. Read the lecture notes and go to lectures. Very engaging lectures. The professor is very nice and plans his lectures very well.

Professor Bray is an amazing lecturer who cares about his students.  Taking stat 20 with him has been one of my favorite classes.  He responds quickly to students' questions and explains the material well.

Greta guy! He made stats very fun, and I truly enjoyed him! He was in my top two Professors at UC Berkeley, and he wrote me a wonderful letter of recommendation for law school. His class is somewhat hard, as the labs are very, very tough. Make sure to work with friends. The exams are somewhat hard, but just study labs and lecture slides.

Andrew was such a great professor for stat 20, he was super caring and understanding. Make sure to stay on track and understand the stat part well and you will do well in class. Go to homework parties and participate in class from day 1!! It will help you A LOT I promise.

Great introductory course to coding. Yes, R is difficult at times but found the GSIs and Bray to be very helpful. The course is well structured and adapted to the class' needs (I took this class the first ever semester he taught stat 20). A very rewarding, interesting, and engaging class. Bray chooses interesting data sets and real world problems.

Professor Bray was great for Stat 20. He explains concepts really well and always answered student questions with precision. He has a good personality which facilitates his teaching so it's easier to learn and it also allows you to get to know him.

Professor Bray I love you. I'm so glad he replaced the previous stat 20 professors because I heard they were horrible and hell for people trying to declare econ. You can tell Prof spent sm time and effort curating his course to be informational but not too advanced. I learned so much about R and if you put in effort, you can't fail.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: As someone who has never taken any statistics classes before, I really enjoyed how he taught it because it made it very easy to understand and learn. The labs were a bit hard sometimes, but the GSIs and Prof Bray were always active on Edstem and were quick to answer and questions. Would recommend if you have to take a stats class!

As someone horrible with stats and math in general, this class was tough. It's not reflective of Bray, but he gives many resources for you to survive. Unfortunately, GSI does make or break your experience, but make sure to go to office hours and homework parties! It'll help make the work a lot more digestable. Study the stats more than you do R
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Easy class that introduces basic statistics. Do the labs and pay attention to small details and the exams were very generous.

The class lectures were easy to follow, and since they were posted online you didn't have to go to class all the time. The labs didn't really pertain to the lectures too much as they were about coding, and sometimes the problem sets would come out really late, but overall the class wasn't too hard to follow.

Prof Bray is great, contrary to what some have said. Nice guy, even talked to me about his experience in the statistics/ds world outside of academia. The course is not confusing. Many have issues with coding, especially in R. I had to help half the lab on the first day. People tend to rant when they don't get the grade they want, keep that in mind.

I loved Bray's class. I've never taken stats before and struggle with math but his lectures really simplify the content for me. There is a lot of support for assignments, especially if you go to all of the labs and lectures. Bray is helpful in office hours and I felt like the exam and assignment grading was generous.

Is a new teacher at berkeley and sucks at giving a clear plan to the course. Doesnt know when his own assignments and quizzes are due and the course staff is practically incompetent under his leadership
Just a bad teacher who has no idea what he is doing, doesn't know how to run course staff. Inconsistent graders
Loved going to Prof Bray's class, he incorporated so many interesting stories to explain one stat concept. Thoroughly enjoyed this class, put the effort in and be interested, you'll get an A.

Professor Bray is a new teacher in Berkeley, I can tell he is trying so hard to teach his class, and he wants to cover everything from the textbook. Honestly, I don't want to judge his teaching way; I hate this class so much is because of his stupid gsi. The gsi has no idea about the class content and only reads the PowerPoint.

A really great person and professor who cares about his students. I found his lectures engaging and loved the labs we did. He was one of the first professors I had at Berkeley and was my favorite. The class isn't always the easiest, but there's lots of support from staff, so I ended up doing fine.

As a preface, I am not someone who is good at math. I tried to take Stat 20 over the summer with another professor but dropped out. But in this class I understand the material because the prof is amazing. The professor is organized, and all the course sites used are very helpful. Lots of resources (ED, study sessions, gsi vids)
