Prof Bray is hands down the best professor Ive had at Cal. He cares about students and it shows. Has quiz/exam retakes where questions parallel those on the original and the better score is used. Listens to students feedback on difficulty. Office hours and Piazza answers very helpful. Wants you to succeed

This was a great class. R is a little confusing at first but he does a great job teaching it, and spent extra time going over things that he knew people were confused about. Very interesting, real-world topics for the lectures, labs, and problem sets.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He's clearly passionate about Japan, but I could never pay attention during lecture. Thankfully, he records all of them so they are available to view later. There's a lot of required readings, but I think doing half of them is more than enough to get an A. Overall, a pretty decent class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lots of reading. Few assignments graded by GSIs. Prof is very passionate about Japan, though it is difficult to follow during lecture. Readings are dense and often hard to understand. Gives study guide before midterm/final which are very helpful. I really struggled in this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Caring and extremely knowledgeable professor who is very passionate. The class is dense, as the prof. crams in a lot of info and themes about Japan both socially and structurally. Although lectures and readings were mostly dull, the class material was very interesting at times, and exams were very chill if you prepared. Learned a lot about Japan.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: super long lectures, always ran the clock even though he was out of things to say. so much reading and writing. hard rubrics, gsi grades incredibly harshly (not sure if its coordinated or not). exam prompts are given in advance but incredibly dense, honestly wish i p/np or dropped it, just not worth the time commitment.

Professor Barshay is clearly very knowledgeable and passionate about Japanese history, but lectures often feel disorganized, tangential, and mentally draining. There are also lots of readings, most of which are quite dense. Grading largely depends on GSI, but for an intro class, it felt like there was an overbearing amount of information to learn.

Great professor. Super interesting lectures and is pretty funny. Engaging and is  good at making overarching connections. That being said, so much reading.  not sure if the grades are more contingent on him or the GSIs, but definitely not the easiest grading-- lots of papers that are harshly scored. Wish there were more chances to improve
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: If you want an “easy A” professor, this is it. However, if you decide to go to the lectures, get ready for long tangents on meaningless topics, get behind in the course, and a weird repetition of the same old themes in every lecture; staying awake is a struggle. I do not believe I did the readings once in this course, and it was hardly necessary.

Clearly an expert and super intelligent. Lectures are full of details (with little on the slides), so expect to pay attention if you want thorough notes. Grade ofc depends on your GSI but is mainly made up of the midterm, final,& 5 reading reports. Expect 100-300pgs of reading every week. Somehow not as difficult as expected, though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: Very knowledgable/excited about Japanese history (especially Christianity in Japan). Gives long lectures, very detailed but somewhat disorganized/limited info on slides. But lectures are recorded/easy to review, slides are uploaded, & he is very easy to talk to/answers questions kindly. Longterm professor at Berkeley, well-respected in his field.

Prof. Barshay was incredibly knowledgeable of his field and offered a new perspective to an otherwise colloquial topic, WWII. I loved the merging of expertise and lecturing with Prof. Connelly -- the two complemented each other well. Looking to take another course by Barshay in the Spring.

Professor Barshay is very knowledgeable when it comes to history of modern japan. Lectures were exhaustive with limited chances for participation. Graded on two papers, a midterm and a final (writing-intensive). Successful writings and exams require close reading of course readers and other assigned text.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --So many papers

reviews.comment: Took a history seminar in Spring 2020 with Prof Barshay and it was really interesting. We went through a series of books about Japan and analyzed Japanese history through these books. Each week, a two person group would present on a book. We ended up not getting through all the books because of covid. The final paper was changed to book reflections

I had Barshay almost 27 years ago for the lower division Japanese history and also one of my 103s. He's a good historian and a top notch *teacher* -- really cared about getting us all to think about the material. Occasionally, he'd bring in irrelevant current politics, but whatever. Good guy.

Professor Barshay is simply brilliant, a real gem in any historical studies. It was a pleasure being in class listening to him lecture and analyze complex historical events-he breaks them down layer by layer while simultaneously attaching these to those of the past. I'd highly recommend taking a class with him, you wont be disappointed.

Prof. Barshay is a good professor overall, having a well structured and informative course that assigned a fair amount of readings. That said, his lectures have something to be desired. They are still informative and useful, but because he improvises his lectures they can go all over the place, and it can be hard to know what to take note of.

His lectures are somewhat hard to follow, but he is extremely knowledgeable in his field. He gives are study guides before exams and stick to them. He says that there is no point to surprise students in exams and he means it.

Professor Barshay's lectures were a joy to attend. The way he analytically picks everything apart to show you the deeper connections in history is very engaging. Be prepared to do a lot of reading though, averaging around 100 pages a week. If you keep up with the reading schedule and attend all the lectures, you'll do just fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I've taken 100u/119/103 with Barsh. Incredibly knowledgeable & refreshingly honest with material outside his breadth. He brings a unique perspective to Japanese intellectual history that I really appreciate. His ability to tie events & thoughts processes in Japan to the rest of the world is just impressive. He's an extremely valuable source at Cal.
The professor is a good and clear lecturer. However, some of the readings assigned were quite outdated, and only a few selective historical perspectives were presented.

Took two of his classes, another one is 100U on World War II. Will take 118 too. LECTURE HAS STYLE. His way of guiding your thinking is exceptional and makes me fall for history. Tests are predictable (ID, short answer, essay, all in his review sheet). He said there's no point to surprise you and he meant it, which again makes learning enjoyable.

Best of all the classes I took this past year at Berkeley, my 1st year of college. Brilliant, knowledgable, thorough, articulate, down to earth. Took this during the 6-week summer session, so it went by very fast. I must say, it was the 1st class I was not looking forward to ending. (Prior to this, no interest in history - now might be my major).

i took the course in summer; course materials are interesting; his films really help you get the big picture of Japan; his lecture can sometimes be dry and hard to follow, tho. overall a very good class and you do learn a lot from it
Professor was nice but the lectures were a bit dry.  Overall, you learn a lot about Japan and the films he shows-- as well as the readings he assigns-- are really informative.

I also took Barsh for a 103 seminar. He's probably the best professor I've had at Berkeley/at all. He is clearly committed to undergrad edu and takes time to synthesize and represent a lifetime of learning to students, even in low. div survey courses. His reading selections are wonderfully insightful, and you finish feeling you had accomplished som
Amazing person and instructor.

Professor Barshay is a very nice, knowledgeable professor. His lectures are a bit confusing, but if you read the textbook, then you should get a good understanding of the material. The class itself is really interested and I would definitely recommend it as a way to satisfy one's History Breadth Req.

friendly guy who knows his stuff and is passionate about it; lectures can get monotonous and his lectures r disorganized; spends a lot of time on pre-WW2 history (barely any time on WW2 which was a disappointment); section extremely helpful; reading assignments can be heavy; 1 midterm that wasn't bad and 1 essay; final is tough.

Professor Barshay's a nice guy, but his lectures were SO boring!! On top of that, they were disorganized & hard to follow. If you signed up for the class b/c you like history/think Japan is interesting, think again & reconsider what you're expecting from this course. It could be an easy A depending on your GSI, but it's not worth the boredom.
Class was relatively easy, readers for this course were really bad.  Inconsistent in grading.  The midterm was considerably easier than the final so don't be fooled.
He's smart, clear, and a pretty nice guy. The course material (20th Century Japan) was pretty interesting as well. I would recommend this professor, and this class in particular.

Great great prof. He was extremely knowledgeable about the subject matter and managed to keep a 2.5 hour class engaging. Also very nice and approachable. The readings were interesting and the grading and assignments were straightforward and fair. I left this class feeling like I had learned so much!

Very helpful and nice. Always cheerful. Stingy on the breaks that we had (not even 10 minutes for a 2.5 hr class), but at least his class was interesting so time went by fast. assignments were fair and I loved the readings. I loved the movies we watched especially the one on Tora-San. He is funny too and very knowledable about Japan. I recommend;)

prof is extremely knowledgeable, friendly, gives reasonable assignments, grading is fair and quick. watched some great films. we had a ton of reading to do, but it was manageable and sometimes even fun. lectures could feel long sometimes (summer class, 2.5hrs a day), but rich. good professor, good class.
No Comments

Interesting lectures though not very exciting. Lots of reading. Final is reasonably easy. Papers were actually stimulating to write. His topics are broad so they allow for individual interpretation and he helps you work on your writing style. Overall, he offers a really good course and you learn an amazing amount of new material.

Boring?  Tons of reading?  Easy?  None of these are true.  The classes were stimulating, the reading was reasonable, and the exams were challenging (but not ridiculously hard).  Take one of his classes.

A good professor though there is nothing spectacular. He really knows his stuff but the lectures can be very boring. The midterm he gave was  easy, but his final was much more harder. Tons of reading but I guess like most classes, it also depends on what your GSI is like.
Very interesting lecturer, creates interest for students.

Pretty chill class, the content was very interesting. Smallest upper div I've taken. Lecture can get a little dry but honestly they're very easy to digest (esp if you did the readings). Data component is not hard at all given PS 3 and it is intuitive. Relevant to both American and comparative politics in my opinion.

Little is great. Let's be real, the difficulty is a 5/5 because he actually expects you to learn and grow (the audacity!) If you're looking for an easy ride, this ain't it. But if you're looking for a professor who will push you to be your absolute best and support you every step of the way, then sign right up for the Little league – they're major!

Prof. is super nice, but the class is *extremely* dry. Drones on for two hours each lecture, making it impossible to pay attention. If you have already taken Data 8 and any kind of statistics class before, the content will be a breeze... otherwise, it will be really difficult because he speeds through everything. Would not recommend it.

Honestly, after hearing a lot of horror stories about PS3, I was relieved this class was much like any other. I have no background in coding and actually came to like it quite a bit. Prof Little and the GSI's were always available for questions and make use of the free tutoring provided on campus.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This class was fair, while, the class is based on coding/group projects the structure of the course was better. The Professor & GSIs had lots of office hours which helped me understanding the material better. Ive never coded in my life, but I spoke up and got tutoring. You have to work hard in this class, but ask questions and youll do fine!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: A little confused by how low most people scored him. Not a perfectly run class and struggled a bit to listen to student struggles during the pandemic. However, the entire class structure was changed drastically and very helpfully in order to make sure students weren't overworked.

Why is the class so heavily based on coding when this is political science? Not only does he do an awful job at teaching you how to code, then the entire class is based on python. If I had wanted to learn how to code I would have done a CS major.

This guy teaches poorly by focusing too much time on pointless things and skimming over what actually matters. His problem sets have nothing to do with the mock ones he does in class. Only took this class because it was mandatory for PS major. Rethink your choice of taking him unless you ABSOLUTELY have to

He did not have a syllabus on how he was going to grade us until we asked for it two weeks before the end of the semester! His videos give no help at all as it pertains to what is going to be on the problem sets and none of the class material is actually useful when it comes to having to do the work that is assigned.

The material for this class is challenging in the tedious and annoying kind of way not the rewarding kind of way. Prof Little is very nice and sympathetic to students concerns and feedback but boy are his lectures tough to follow. Pretty disjointed and confusing. This class did not translate well to online only, but Prof Little doesn't deserve 1.7.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Prof Little is a nice guy and brilliant in his field. However, being good at a subject doesn't always translate into being good at teaching it. His class lacks organization, good lesson planning, and clear lectures/learning objectives. If he's reading this, my advice is to give up and just teach from a book. For students, I would avoid his class.

Super kind and compassionate professor. He knew that many of his students were intimidated by the subject material, but he was very encouraging to us. He was also receptive to feedback from the class on his teaching style. His office hours were helpful too. Overall- I would say that PS3 is tough, but he makes it bearable. You'll be fine <3 I was
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: A lot of people complain about this class and professor but I actually think he does a good job. Hardly anyone shows up to lecture. If you don't show up you're not going to do well. Professor Little is very accessible outside of class and he offers a fair amount of extra credit. Show up, pay attention, attend discussion, go to office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: If you skip lecture,which a lot of people did, you wont do well, but it does lower the curve so.. He is actually a good professor and will clear things up if you ask him about it. The discussion sections are also extremely helpful so if you go to both you should be fine. The R part of the class is also easy just put in the effort and dont skip.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: He assumes everyone has a basic understanding of stats, which isn't true. From the 2nd week onwards I was perpetually lost. He's super unclear during lecture, and eventually I found it more useful to skip lecture and use that time to understand the textbook and his slides independently. Make sure you have a good GSI, that'll make the difference.

His lecture ability is nonexistent; he speaks far too quickly, slurs his words, and speeds through the complex material (like R, which was not taught in previous semesters of PS3). The online resources and PPTs are inanely unorganized  even the titles to PowerPoints dont follow a uniform format. And extremely difficult exams. Do not take him...

This professor is by far the most challenging person that I have come across during my time at Berkeley. The problem sets and tests are not what ruin you, but rather his ability to speed through important concepts while dragging on explanations of useless ones . If he teaches PS3 again and you have to take it, PRAY for an amazing GSI.

This man manages to teach the lectures backwards, so that everything makes sense in hindsight. The lectures are confusing, dull, and made me want to bang my head on the desk. Instead I spent the time on my phone, teaching myself concepts from the internet. Pray for a good GSI, because they will be the reason you get through this class.

Professor Little does not know how to effectively manage a class of the size necessary for teaching PS 3. He is not an educator and it shows in his teaching. He is regularly dismissive of student concerns and questions which primarily come from his own disorganized and unimpactful lectures. If he teaches this class again, rely on your GSI.

I truly regret taking PS3 with Little. Because the course is mandatory lower div PS requirement, it felt unreasonable for him to introduce concepts such as RStudio and Swirl for students who literally are just taking the class to graduate. Additionally, he is abysmal at lecturing and moves either glacially or far too quickly.

Little is a solid professor. He is very nice and accessible to his students, he also takes feedback VERY seriously. The class is hard by nature, which is not his fault. I'm pretty average and not great at quantitative stuff but had NO problems with this class. If you put in a little extra work and attend every class, you'll be fine!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Little is not clear at all. Unlike previous classes of PS 3, he makes his students code using R statistical software. He often trips over himself and leaves many of us confused and lost. There are many topics he covers which dont make sense for a lower division PS research methods course. Would not recommend. Thank u, next.

I am a graduating senior, and have never faced a more incompetent teacher in all of my time in school. The man somehow maintains the dryness of academic language while stripping it of all of its depth and nuance. He constantly contradicts himself, befuddles his math, and spends hours talking without saying anything poignant or relevant.

I'm sorry but this man was not ready to be a professor. He committed so many errors, it was sad. He even confessed that it's "hard to do algebra with these many people staring at you." He has a loud voice but he mumbles a lot and his writing is hard to understand. His textbook was $150+ and the worst textbook I had seen in 4 years.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Super unorganized professor that would often confuse himself during lectures. Handwriting was very ineligible, and signs would often be switched. Textbook essentially useless too (don't buy it). Not a hard topic given the amount of practice he provides, he's just such a bad professor. Very smart and passionate about the topic. Horrid teacher.
Terrible Professor, harsh grading

He doesn't post any slides, and it was extremely hard to follow him. His handwriting is near incomprehensible (just writes on the blackboard-good luck seeing it from the upper aisle). The midterm was ridiculously hard-many people had to take this for P/NP credit. We weren't ready for the psets (adequately prepped), and he made last minute edits.
reviews.rating_tags: Tests? Not many--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Class was an absolute disaster as mentioned by the other comment. Disorganized and lacked structure in the contents of the course. Little has little clue what he is trying to teach in any given lecture. What a waste of a semester.

Worst professor. Makes many mistakes in lecture and laughs when you point them out ("it's a 50/50 chance I'll write the equation correctly!"). Posts lecture slides online with caveat "Use at your own risk." Very disorganized and seems confused about his own material. Practice midterm totally different from harder actual midterm. Don't take him!
Great lectures and really easy and accessible material! Definitely the coursework is manageable and intriguing. Definitely should take it.

Prof. Leong is one of the most caring, thoughtful, and understanding professors I've ever had. Very encouraging, insightful, and skilled at overseeing and adding to student discussion without intervening. A self-graded class where you genuinely wanted to try and that I took a lot away from. Thank you Prof. Leong!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I loved taking Prof. Leong's class, as he had some exciting and insightful things to say about the readings. This class made me really love the short story form and refined my close reading skills. The class discussions were also really engaging and enjoyable, and his facilitation of it made it even more enjoyable.

He was so easy. Everyone either got A or A+. He spent a lot of time making a grade calculator for us to figure out our grade. Had so much buffer credit opportunities that you could literally ditch the final if you had enough points in the class. Didn't read a single book. I want him to teach more classes so I can collect those A's.
had him for asamst 20c. super nice and lenient with grading.

Prof. Leong provides enough extra credit that anyone should be able to get a perfect grade in the class. There are weekly readings, discussion posts, and meetings with a group. There's also a simple group presentation to the class. The midterm and final are easy and it's possible to get enough extra credit not to do the final.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor Leong was a really engaging professor and he maintained a dynamic class setting that flowed nicely. I really enjoyed class discussion, and how he encouraged participation. Essay feedback was very constructive and essay assignments were also well-paced throughout the semester. The books were also very interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: I had the pleasure of taking Professor Leong this spring and he is amazing! He is a well-rounded, knowledgable individual who facilitates the most complex of class discussions. His contributions were so helpful in shaping my understanding of the assigned texts. Not to mention, his sense of humor is refreshing! He is full of smiles. I could go on.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Maybe this was because we were online for this semester, but I was annoyed by how often the schedule for this class changed weekly; sometimes we would have class at 5 or 5:30 or 6 and bc he wouldn't reuse the same zoom link for all lectures, it felt hectic. Other than that, he's a really good-hearted prof and I would recommend! Class was p easy!

Professor Leong changed how I see the Asian American cultures in America. I enjoyed most of the assigned readings. The homework is very manageable. A few of the oral histories and more lengthy readings are difficult to trawl through, but are just as vital as watching the assigned "Like a G6" (yes, the song) three times to prepare for class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Demanding workload: no in class pop quizzes and no midterm. Final was in class, and definitely grueling. However, Professor Leong even made Robert Penn Warren enjoyable to read insert: applause. He layers his lectures with tons of info, and is super accessible if youre ever confused about material in class. A wonderful professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Wonderful, well spoken professor with extremely diverse and interesting readings and meaningful discussions. We were expected to read about two or three things per class. One oral exam, midterm paper, and final paper. Allowed up to three absences. Feedback was extremely substantive and meaningful.

The Asian-American Lit/Culture course is a substantially easy course, but I've actually learned so much from taking this class. I took it to satisfy the Arts and Lit breadth and am so glad that I took this class, and it's an easy A. The professor is very understanding, funny, cares about his students & is so passionate about what he teaches. 10/10

"Garrett the merciful" is how I would describe this professor. I have made so many mistakes and missed a lot of classes but Garrett was willing to work with me and give me more chances than I deserve. I think  this is an example how how a professor should be. Thank you Professor Garrett!

The weekly hw is time consuming and challenging. Attendance is taken during lectures. We had 4 midterms and a final with no cheat sheets allowed. Lectures are not recorded. Partial clobber as one of the midterms was dropped and replaced with the average of the other exams. I should've taken this class during summer school.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Garrett's graders are so nit-picky it gets frustrating to say the least. The content is bearable since it's interesting and the lectures are sometimes fun to attend. However, it doesn't justify having FOUR WHOLE MIDTERMS and a cumulative final, especially since this course in the past has not been nearly as difficult.
Terrible professor. His classes make no sense and are paced absolutely insanely. I don't recommend taking classes with him. AVOID!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I don't know about other people. But I had a terrible time with this course. Many tasks were not meaningful nor helpful in understanding this language. I was very happy with the grade but the course...Just try something else before you take this.
Really awesome to study Yurok with him.
Really amazing professor. Super knowledgeable and passionate. Can be tough, but always fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I rarely went to lecture but as long as you understand the concepts you should be fine. He always gives opportunities to make up for missed grades and he's very understanding! As long as you're doing the homework, you should be fine and you might not even have to take the exam if you get full marks on the homework.

While I felt Professor Garrett's lectures to be quite interesting, I felt that the class was so fast paced it made it difficult for me to learn. It is also mostly impossible to accurately predict your grade throughout the semester. His point grading system is not awful, has it's pros and cons. Would recommend to those not deterred by heavy reading!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Class was interesting, very informative and I feel well prepared for further study in the field of linguistics. I was able to do well by just attending lecture, keeping up with readings, and attending the optional exam review before every midterm. Be warned that it's borderline impossible to figure out your grade while taking the class.

Best instructor I had in all my years at Berkeley as a Linguistics major. I took Ling 100, 130, and two other additional classes with Professor Garrett. He certainly has a dry sense of humor, and likes rewarding students with cupcakes on occasion. A bit twisted. "That's a good question" usually means "I'm not really sure what the answer is."

Everyone told me that Professor Garret's lectures would be the most entertaining class of the semester. I was pretty disappointed. The lectures become monotonous after a while, with a boring emphasis on the technicality. The homeworks are hard, but the exams are fair and not too challenging.

Amazing lecturer really; nothing more I can say. The homework was extremely difficult (he expected you to spend 10 hours a week on it), but rewarding. But surprisingly, the exams were relatively easy so it kinda balanced out!

In Andrew's classes, you are not expected to simply know the material, but you must use every little piece of knowledge you've internalized to solve challenging, complex problems, and then make solid arguments for why you've solved it that way. He is incredibly smart, unabashedly nerdy, and has an awesome sense of humor.
Knowledgeable and has a sense of humor. Lectures are well organized.

Most effective lecturer I've had yet at Berkeley. He's so funny, so topical - I'm someone who can often get bored or sleepy in lecture environments, but I was rapt every single day. He has so much love for Linguistics and for us and it really shines. He's got a dry sense of humor, so if you're down for it then you'll really find him a riot.

Sure, the class is hard, but definitely worth it. Garrett knows what he's talking about, and even if he is intimidating, he means well (and is a genius so who really cares?). Go to office hours, go to lectures, go to section, and you'll be fine.

Garrett is tough, but it is worth it. Although he is intimidating, his lectures are clear and it is obvious he is a genius. Homeworks every week are super challenging, but come out to 55% of the final grade, and the end curve was magical.

I had Andrew long ago when I was a grad student at UT-Austin. I took historical ling and Indo-European ling. His assignments were tough, but I learned so much doing them. He is a fantastic teacher and scholar who I remember fondly to this day. I still tell people about him and his amazing assignments. Berkeley students are very lucky to have him!
Great, intelligent, funny  professor. Extremely hard weekly homeworks. Oh but his grade curves are amazing. (;

Great professor! I definitely recommend him! Lectures are very important, make sure to attend them all. Not an easy class, but if you work hard, you'll get a good grade. Homework assignments are difficult (get ready to spend 4-8 hours per homework; 1 homework per week), but they prepare you for midterms and a final.

garrett is adorable and unintentionally hilarious. he's a great teacher.  the homeworks are very hard, and shouldn't be left for the night before!  great class, but work will be required!  you can get a good grade as long as you put work into the homework assignments.
okay so i am not sure why no one else mentioned how hard this class is. i loved garrett, suprisingly funny, but the actual class killed me.
Garrett is the schit fools! He is knows Yurok inside and out. Take him for any class. He is genius, kind, helpful and so much more. Unlike many professors he is a real "teacher".

He teaches really well. He's probably one of the best lecturers in the Ling Dept! The homework he assigns are a bit tedious, but nevertheless it's doable. And I believe he was very generous when it comes to the grade cut-offs. He knows that the class is challenging. And did I mention he's so adorable. I want a mini-Garrett plush doll! :)

Fantastic lecturer and hilarious guy -- he clearly put effort into preparing the course handouts and lectures (warning: the handouts are useless unless you go to class and follow what he's saying). I really liked that he would present conflicting theories without injecting his opinions into them so much. I HIGHLY recommend taking a course with him.

Smart and funny professor, his class is a great intro to the field.  Homework grading is nitpicky and annoying but tests are straightforward and fair.  By the end of the course you'll be sick of Native American languages, but really well-prepared for other Ling classes.
Great professor: very funny, clear, helpful, and didn't underestimate our intelligence by dumbing down his presentation. Hard assignments but straight-foward tests.
He's a very effective lecturer, and even in an upper div. survey course, he introduces a number of sophisticated ideas/theories that prove to be greatly useful in other ling. courses.

TAKE THIS CLASS if you are serious about learning about language change.  He is the ideal teacher - lectures and handouts complement the textbook perfectly without repeating it.  Assignments, though they will kick your a--, are unbelievably helpful in teaching you the material.  Yeah, AG is on the geeky side, but what an adorable geek!
Funny and available to help you if you need it. Covered too much difficult material for a survey class.

Though Garrett is amusing at first, his lectures slip into a monotonous continuum rather quickly.  This class is probably much more enjoyable for Linguistics majors—I found myself preferring to do the crosswords almost every lecture.  =/
Very amusing teacher (dry sense of humor, as someone said earlier).  Tests are easy if you have a decent understanding of the material.

I wish we didn't have to comment on the hot part.. but, anyhow, one of the best professors I ever had.  I'm in med school now and still find myself refrencing J. Campbell and Garret's handouts.  Great class, great subject and overall amazing teaching skills and data presentation by Dr. Andrew Garret.  I feel lucky to have had him as a professor.  He completely changed my view of language change and its correlation with e.g. demographics and time.  Most importantly, I gained analysis skills I still use today

he is funny in this own way. his handouts are impressive, tests are fair, grading system is good for students, and his lectures can be fun (taking that i don't like the subject very much, i enjoyed most of his lectures)
Very sharp professor. Lectures are interesting, organized, and remarkably understandable. His dry sense of humor adds to the fun.
No Comments
Worst class ive taken
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He pushes students more than other professors—something that is annoying for the uninspired but terrific for the curious. There are weekly assignments and readings, and lectures are packed with interesting material. If you are interested in the topic, this is an amazing comprehensive overview presented and executed pretty well.

He's so interesting and kind, really engaging lectures and fascinating course material. I would sit in the front and ask questions, during and after lecture if you can, and take good notes. Write down everything he says and study them, with the charts, and read the textbook, then you'll be fine. Totally would take again.

weird dude. if you're not an anthro major, his lectures will be a bit of a snooze. midterm average was low but most people made it up by scoring better on the final. Questions were definitely nitpicky and the study guide he provides is kinda wack - better off ignoring it and creating your own. Amazing GSIs though!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Prof Kim was really cool! He explained things pretty clearly, and had some funny anecdotes to go along with his teaching. The exams are very fair, and a lot of your grade is just section attendance/completion points for homework. The GSIs are really helpful, and I learned a lot from them as well. Overall, a solid class :)

Prof Kim is one of my fave Anthro Professors at Berkeley! Smart guy. Really funny/genuine instructor who wants the best for his students. Very accessible outside of lecture. I enjoyed seminar (~ 8 people, in-depth readings/discussions), but I will always rec his psychoneuroendocrinology (PNE) class. Accessible to STEM + non-STEM folk alike. 10/10.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed this class!!

Professor Kim is engaging and funny. He cares about his students and is really willing to mentor/ give guidance when approached. If you get a chance to take his Psychoneurendocrinology class, do it. Never thought I would learn so much about how stress affects our body in the short and long term.
I would avoid taking his classes if possible.

reviews.comment: rough.....

reviews.comment: Professor Kim is the most caring and intentional professors I have encountered at Berkeley. He cares about his students more than any professor I have ever met. I took it as a breadth P/NP and found it very fun and interesting! 10/10 recommend him in general

Creates last-minute assignments and schedules mandatory classes outside of the syllabus/class schedule. The syllabus is unclear on the expectations of key assignments. He is accommodating (with notice) & the class material is interesting, but the class structure often wastes time. Lectures frequently eat into Berkeley time/following classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: taught lecture material wrong, final/midterm were unbelievably hard and when we all averaged at an F, he did not curve the class! do not take this class!

Great lecturer! Concepts were clear and always illustrated by multiple examples. Great pacing. Such fun course content (loved primates)! As long as you make a primate chart and a hominid chart to study for the midterm and final, they are very doable.
Professor Kim is incredibly intelligent and is a good lecturer. However, the mid-term and the final were very difficult, the average being 65%. I would not take this unless it is a major requirement

he's really hot. get a front row seat for the full experience. also a good, funny, + engaging teacher. cancelled lecture like 5 times and the tests were tough but the homework was pretty low-maintenance.
guy cant teach. useless slides, boring lectures. says "um" between every few words. studying for exams is tedious and memorization based. 0/10
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Dulai is approachable and encourages questions, but is extremely unorganized. Exams were all cumulative with the final in particular being unfair.The material tested was content he said wouldn't be included.He crammed 130+ slides in the last lecture, made distasteful "jokes" and told students to use AI when asked a question. Wouldn't recommend.

Lecture is boring even though he tries to make jokes that comes off as insensitive to many students.Exams are cumulative so that makes it hard to know what to study for. Do not take everything he said literal. He said there was no questions on the stuff we didnt learn about but it was there on the final exam. But my GSI pulled thru.
kind person, but unorganized

I received better answers to my questions from GSIs. Sometimes she starts a thought a doesn't finish it bc there's sm material to go through. Exams are okay. Group work for the data skills project is incredibly annoying

She doesn't care about students learning, but simply punishes students for making small errors. Rather than allowing students to learn from their mistakes and explaining commonly missed questions, she doesn't explain concepts well and is hardly accessible outside of class.

The exams were incredibly long and unbearable. It's split into two parts, one timed and one take-home. The last exam was about 24 pages long. Even though you're given a whole day to do it, it was still frustrating to do. I wish the lectures showed more examples of what was on the exam.

Lack-luster professor. Lectures were not adequately explained and explanations given were inconsistent and incoherent. Many "ums" and unfinished explanations. The last exam and assignment were not even graded. Overall, easy class, though.

Not a great professor. She pre-recorded all her lectures from years ago and basically posts the same material from 3-4 years ago. Not a good professor. She is not available to meet. The GSIs are also disorganized and always gave different answers on the data project. This is not a good course and waste of money...

Terrible. Recorded lectures that were FOUR YEARS OLD. Did not even do the bare minimum with giving lectures. I paid $2000 for this class and this professor basically treats this class like a YouTube channel....NOT WORTH IT. She should not teach because she does not even do her job

Professor records all her lectures and pre-records them 75% of the time. It seems nice but she does not offer a lot of opportunity to reach her. So it feels like taking a YouTube course while you are paying thousands of dollars expecting an active lecturing and learning from a professor. If you want to learn, don't take  this class.

Dufour is clear and concise in lectures and her slides are clear and informative to the point that lecture attendance is not necessary for students with any slight inclination towards coding/statistics. While this class might feel different to mcb/pbhlth students due to its different content, it is graded fairly and the prof/GSIs are accessible.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: It is ridiculous how many STUDENTS find mistakes in questions and answer keys for labs, quizzes, and exams. Our Ed discussion is filled with student corrections. The exams are too long for the given period. The content is over-complicated and disorganized, avoid if you actually want to learn and not have to teach yourself due to disorganization :(

Definitely would not recommend--the entire course is very disorganized, the examples given tend to be very unclear, and all three exams were full of typos and required extra clarification. The way this material was presented felt overly complex, only take this course if you absolutely have to..

As long as you have friends in this class, you'll do great. For lab, they go through and cover the correct answer for every question. Also, all the exams and quizzes are online, and I just used the slides as they have good examples and are laid out explicitly. The only downside of this course was that the quizzes were due Saturday at noon.

had to do a lot of self-studying to understand the material. Weekly quizzes based on concepts covered in lectures, and homework were optional. Very easy group project, and numerous extra credit opportunities. Labs are very easy. Overall, the subject was heavily overcomplicated and confusing as a result of ( what felt like) unorganized lectures.

Very clear expectations, and everything is handed to you. Exams are not bad at all, weekly labs for all/non, optional hw for practice, and a group project very easy to complete. Mi Suk is sweet and knows the material well, GSIs are super active and there are resources for you to get help! More stats than data8 but similar in terms of structure.

Although it is true that she lectures straight off the slides, Mi-Suk knows the content very well, the class is organized, and expectations are clear so if you put in the work, you'll do just fine. The content is applicable and interesting, but not particularly inspirational (kinda what comes with an intro stats class)
horrible

I took her in Spring 2021! She was super sweet and I really liked going to lecture. Most information are on the slides (which are really clear), but lecture helps keep up with the content and understand the material faster. Class was also super accommodating to pandemic restrictions. Midterms, quizzes, and the project were very fair.

Profs lectures were not really useful. I could get the same information by reading the slides. So in terms of lecturing, she is not the best. Grading was also incredibly late (dont know if the group projects were ever graded). But, I will say that she was very responsive to changing the class bc of the pandemic, which other profs didnt try to do.

Mi Suk is an awful lecturer. She reads the slides out loud without contributing any extra information. She says "um" every five seconds and clearly doesn't prepare before her lectures. She fails to answer questions in even the most remotely helpful way and she seems to struggle with the material herself. Worst professor I've ever had.
Clearly cares more about research than teaching. Lectures in a monotone, like she's reading notes out loud. Somehow answers questions without providing explanations. Still, an easy A.

Could be an interesting class, but mi suk made the tests way too long for the short hour provided. Lecture, lab, and discussion all seemed like separate classes, and the class as whole was a bit disorganized. Learning R was the best part, though this part could be taught a lot better

I loved this class - set me up well for more advanced biochemistry courses and research. John is a caring professor who places real intention and effort to help us succeed. I highly recommend going to office hours and interacting on edstem. I missed a large portion of lectures due to family issues and was able to catch up thanks to their help.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Clearly just doesn't put effort into teaching. Tests are MCQ and you self-grade the homework to make it as easy as possible for him. Treats last 20 minutes of lecture like office hours because he runs out of things to talk about. Slides are mostly screenshots from textbooks. Picks tricky MCQs and gives no prep materials to deflate grade average.

I can't follow his lectures. He actively responded to EdStem questions, mocked students for asking stupid or already explained questions. For biochem part of the class, read the lecture slides as the bible for exam prep. The ochem part is just 3A. Homework is graded on completion. The biochem exams r based by lecture. NO MERCY IN GIVING NO CURVES.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Extremely willing to help students learn and encourages all questions during class. Lectures are interesting and he breaks down difficult topics with simple analogies. Exams are reflective of content covered in lecture (no surprises) and it's a great class to take alongside chem 3b. Also willing to meet 1 on 1 after the semester to discuss exam!

He's really willing to answer all questions without judgement and remembers student names in this large class after 1 interaction which is pretty nice lol. Very fair exams and grading is pretty generous! He breaks down concepts in a way easy to understand and still makes the content interesting & relevant to bioengineering.

Professor Dueber was a little shaky in the first part of the course (ochem), but he really excels (and knows his stuff!) at the biology/bioengineering material, and was fantastic for the second part. He genuinely wants students to excel, and is passionate about the material. Overall great experience with him + he gave out candy at the final!

Fair professor, adds points/drops hard q's from exams. Rlly open to questions, caring, easy going. 
Exams are identical or nearly identical questions from practice exams/iclicker in lecture/info on slides so it's easy to succeed if you just pay attention. Wants the best for his students and makes lecture interesting with real world applications!

BioE 11 itself is graded mainly on exams which can be frustrating, but overall I learned in the class.  Prof. Dueber makes a consistent effort to know his students and even memorizes their names!  This makes the large class feel much smaller.  If you go to class and office hours (the TAs are also amazing) then you will succeed in the class.

2 of the reviews are 1/5 because the professor gave everyone full points on a question from the midterm (my class). It's not curved so this only helps people. He's been very upbeat and caring in every class and has made an effort to learn everyone's names. I've honestly loved his lectures and homework is very light while still being very helpful.

Dr. Dueber does not deserve the disrespect he receives from his students - most being a result of clear misunderstandings. Many confuse his upfront manner with being "unprofessional," and it is easy to tell whose egos are threatened. I appreciate his drive to ensure that his students are learning and his great effort to connect with his students.

Pretty fair professor, very clear grade bins and questions are pretty fair on exams. Responsive on ed and very willing to answer questions in class! Only thing is that hw content for the bio portion of this class is a little diff than what's taught in class, but it's graded on completion anyways.

John Dueber is quite literally the worst professor I've ever had at Berkeley. I do not believe that teaching is the profession for this man, and I highly suggest avoiding a class with him at all costs. He doesn't teach the material well, and it sometimes seems like he doesn't even know it himself. He's also incredibly unprofessional at times.

he's pretty nice! he is really active on edstem so you can always have your question answered outside of class, and it is probably one of the most helpful edstems ive ever been in. and the exams are quite fair so far.
I hated this professor!

reviews.comment: Just a waste of time I actually could not with this prof

reviews.comment: This guy did not initiate my learning in any way. He was if anything a poverty professor. Actually this guy is terrible, today her reviews a comment from here in class and he essentially says ‘nah you good' but in reality he needs to check and assess how he handles the class because they is not acceptable for any UC BERKELEY staff.

Prof. Dueber is a goated instructor. He's inspired me to think beyond the curriculum and has always been available to patiently answer my questions. He's taken a vested interest in my development as a student, which is rare for instructors at large institutions. I would 100% recommend.
Thank you for killing my passion :)

Completely unprofessional. A student on exam got a question blatantly wrong due to false assumptions, and he dropped the question when they emailed to "justify" their wrong answer. When students pointed out that this question was gone over in lecture, he became very dismissive of the fact that his favoring of one student was harmful to the class.

Since attendance was required (+ participation was encouraged) it would seem that he cares for students but when it comes to the final, neither a practice final or a review session was held (wasn't held SIMPLY because evaluations

Not helpful at all. He said he'd offer a review session if 70% of the class did the course evaluations. We ended up reaching ~50%, so he didn't post any review materials for the final. Heavy focus on memorization (why do we have to memorize the pka's and structures of all the amino acids?)
He took "go girl give us nothing" too seriously.
The grading was inconsistent and resources were limited. :(
Delightful class. Lectures were interesting and informative. I highly recommend this professor!
very passionate. learned a lot!

Incredible professor. Kind, extraordinarily approachable, and knows how to get the most out of you. Gets you to think about asking the right questions, not chasing the "right" answer. Could not ask for better.

Gaspard is a very friendly professor and his class was well-organized. He always encourages participation with open discussions and questions in class and really wants his students to succeed. He is extremely knowledgeable and enthusiastic about astronomy, and I really enjoyed learning so much in this course!

Dr. Duchene is an amazing instructor! One of the best ones I've had at Berkeley. He's a really fair grader, even towards the lenient side (given that you do the work). Lectures are insanely clear. Super approachable and friendly. The class is definitely not an "easy A," but attending lectures and doing all of the required work is all that's needed.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Macrae is just a great professor and super kind and helpful. There are weekly quizzes instead of midterms and it is content heavy but just go to lectures and listen and take notes. Review your notes the night before the quiz and you'll get an easy A. This class was low effort for me and that's what I did. The most you will do is reading.

Professor MacRae was clearly very passionate about Ancient Roman studies and he's very caring and reasonable with his quizzes (and there's no midterm). Sections were just (pretty boring) reading  but GSIs go over them decently well and they were pretty thematic heavy. Lectures were broad but interesting, and there's an emphasis on themes.

Macrae was a great professor. The course itself got a little boring at times but mostly an interesting class and easy to digest material. There's weekly quizzes in lecture but other than that, lecture isn't mandatory. Everything is basically graded by GSIs and you will have to read weekly texts which appear on quizzes. No midterm btw. Great class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof Macrae seemed very passionate about the content in lectures. There is no midterm but weekly quizzes. However, there was a final paper AND a long final exam was A LOT so prepare for that. There is a TON of content so don't get behind. Grades depend on which GSI you get. Grades were rarely updated. Overall interesting breadth course.

Macrae is a kind, engaging, and very fair professor. Communicates exam formatting and exam scope very clearly and provides good preparatory resources. Exam grading and grade bins were a bit unclear, and lecture notes and other study resources weren't provided so going to lecture was crucial. Very accomodating to DSP and other student needs.
I took AGRS 28 and it was honestly a pretty easy and chill class. The lectures and readings were interesting if you like Greek myths, and the tests were simple as well. Great breadth course to take!

SA often brought up so TW! cried a lot bc didnt realize how deep wed get into it:(. still loved the course/prof, lecture felt effortless bc topics were 10/10. sad abt my grade bc im assuming participation grade sucked(A on all exams, B+ final proj) even tho most gave up on the readings & only ppl who spoke in section were me & maybe 5 others lol(:
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I think it was a very easy and straightforward class. Make sure you go to lectures/watch lectures since they will help for the exams, and better understanding of the topics.  I'd recommend making a friend in that class so you can chat about the lectures/stay awake. The exams are not that hard, just review for an hour, and you're good.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
This professor is a kind soul, and passionate about what he's teaching. The lectures were boring at times but I took it for a breadth. He throws in a lot of dad jokes during his lectures, and is very through in his responses and help. 
Note: Find a lecture buddy. Have to attend/watch lectures to pass exams, all the questions are from there.

Great class. Lectures can be a bit dull sometimes, but some are super interesting. Just pay attention to what he says and do the section readings and you'll be good. Exams are not too difficult and graded pretty easily. If you're into greek mythology, definitely take this class.
Always very kind and happy to explain things in office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: great prof. would recommend

Great professor,I recommend this class.. Lots of reading which I didn't always do and still got by. Exams entirely based off of lecture (not slides but what he says) and section readings. He also read and gave feedback on everyone's final projects (like 200 or something students) which says a lot about a prof
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof Macrae was one of my favorites during the semester; he made the content so interesting and organized. Lectures weren't mandatory, but he did random attendance checks every now and then. He does post lecture slides but most of the information you get is from actually hearing him speak. Lots of reading, but they're interesting!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. MacRae is a great teacher; he explains concepts well in lecture & assigns interesting readings. He truly cares about his students & is passionate about the course material. The exams are based off of passages from readings & handouts, as well as handout keywords. The myth telling project is fun & straightforward as long as you think ahead.

Professor Macrae's course material is very interesting but his lectures are a bit boring. He assigns a lot of readings and they are necessary to participate in section and for exams. I hardly went to his lectures because I prioritized other classes and I still passed with a decent grade. Knowing key terms and readings are essential for exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Macrae a good lecturer and makes the topic of Classical Mythology very interesting. However, I thought the class had an usually large amount of reading, and this is coming from a history major. Most of the problems I had were due to the GSI's and not Macrae himself.  Would definitely recommend if your into mythology or ancient history in general.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Very knowledgeable, but lecture can be dull sometimes. He does bring in good multimedia throughout. Accessible during OH. HEAVY on memorization of a ton of Greek figures. The two main textbooks are a waste of money, but the section readings are absolutely mandatory and come up a lot on the two midterms/final. Final mythtelling project 35% of grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Douskey is a super engaging and hilarious lecturer, and really supportive and accessible at office hours. Informal lab reports are a big part of your grade (60%), so make sure to go to the awesome GSI for questions!

She's a pretty good instructor and explains things well, especially if you're taking 1A in tandem. However, pre-lab quizzes and lab reports take a fair amount of time if you really want to get a good score. Ask the GSIs as many questions as possible when you're confused, sometimes they'll just tell you what they'll be grading for on the reports.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Too much work for a two unit class. Had hidden rubric items. lab reports took forever. lab exam is carbon copy of practice exams. Lectures not helpfull. Prelabs and Lab reports are hard without GSI help. Overall class is not hard to get an A in, its just a lot of busy work. Took Fall 2024
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She is a good lecturer and very kind. Her lectures are not very related to the lab work needed. Hours of work spent per week on pre-lab work/quizzes and lab reports that are graded harshly under guidelines that we're not told of. The labs themselves aren't very difficult but its random if you get a gsi who'll tell you what's needed for your report.

So much work for only 2 units. Grading rigorous, some questions were graded in a way where you could get negative points. Grading was unclear, rubric was very specific, but not released until after the fact. Different GSIs had different policies and opinions, so scores varied. Lectures were fine.

Should have been more than 2 units the labs took so many hours, rubric not provided beforehand so you always got points taken away for stuff you didnt know you had to write, gsi's office hours always packed. Lectures made no sense and didn't help for final studying. However final was very similar to practice finals and grading on it was lenient.

prof douskey is a great lecturer, even though the lectures don't really match the labs. if you actually prepare your lab notebook, write down your data and complete your work on time, this should be a pretty easy class. some gsi's can be harsh graders so go to office hours if you want to clarify anything!

Funny lectures and lab final is identical to past exams (which she gives you).  Some of the prelab work feels tedious but it doesn't actually take that long.  Class depends on lab GSI as they're the one you actually spend the most time with.

Should be more than 2 units based on the amount of time it took to complete the lab reports. Not all labs are 3hrs. She's alright, but lectures weren't super helpful so it depends on your GSI. Labs are fine, but very strict grading criteria. Gives good resources for the final and it looks like the old exams, but explanation grading is confusing.

This class soaked up way too much time for 2 units. The grading on lab reports were often unclear. I found that the lectures didn't help at all. The grading is pretty lenient but be aware it takes up more time than you'd expect. I often found myself stressing about lab reports.
Very kind professor! It is only reasonable that she couldn't cover every procedure during her lectures. But she is overall very helpful!
Her lectures did not relate to the pre lab content and I ended up having to look most things up.

Labs are based off her book of lab manuals you are required to buy or print. Sometimes directions are unclear but GSI's help. Lectures are mandatory but don't help with anything. Also on the lab reports and final, grading criteria is very unclear and you will be marked down for not including information the question didn't ask.

Lowkey this class shaved off 2 years of my lifespan but Douskey seems like a good person! VERY tedious grading for lab reports. My GSI Zakir Talpur was the goat, he's genuinely kind and tried his best to help despite the chaos that comes with an overcrowded lab.

Curve was also very generous! Got curved up from an 88.86% -> 90% at the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Douskey is kind of hit or miss. Some lectures were very helpful for lab, especially when she went over procedures. Other times she went on tangents and often didn't finish the slides. Labs are fine, but lab reports can be harsh with unclear grading. However, she's funny and warm, and the final is very similar to the practice finals.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Her lectures weren't the best, her notes were unclear, and most of the time, the lecture was irrelevant to what was actually happening in the lab. The lab reports were long and time-consuming. There is no rubric provided for the reports, but they are graded fairly. My GSI was Kevin Miura, and he was the best. Highly recommend!
Her lectures were usually unrelated to the actual lab, but she is a caring professor and her grading system is very fair.

Lab reports were lots of unnecessary work and graded harshly. Doing the labs themselves weren't that bad since the expectations were clear and easy to follow along, GSIs are understanding and wanna leave as badly as you do. Final was just a copy and paste of the final practice exams she gives so just study those and you're guaranteed to do well.

Professor Douskey's structure for lab isn't the greatest. Her lab report style is weird and there's no rubric so you genuinely don't know what you have to do to get full points on a lab. I remember being docked for not writing a specific word (I didn't see anywhere that we had to). Her emphasis on green chemistry truly doesn't prepare you for 1A.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment:
So much work. I basically lived inside the GSI OH room and did prelabs and lab write ups in there, begging GSI's to tell me the criteria because it made no sense. So much reading (2/3 hrs) for prelabs, mandatory lecture attendance. Only things that saved me was my GSI. 

Grading- prelab quizzes: 10%  Participation: 5%, Lab reports 60%, final: 25%
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment:
She is a great professor, and I don't understand why people are complaining. She is very approachable during office hours. I think all this criticism comes from the fact that this is the first lab class many students take at Berkeley, and they aren't prepared for the rigor
P.S. Don't submit your lab report without going to at least one office hour

Overall grade is mainly based off lab reports and those are pretty hard. Make sure to gain advice and help from GSIs by going to office hours. Final is similar to practice tests. This class will take up a lot of your time even though it is a 2 credit course so make sure to manage your time!

Lectures weren't that good, the lab manual is all you really need to understand what's going to happen during lab. The lab reports were fine but there was no rubric which sucked, they're also just sometimes lengthy and time-consuming. The final exam was pretty much the same as the practice exams provided. Overall, not the hardest class just tedious
Kind professor on the outside, but quite uncaring and unsupportive when adjustments need to be made.

Very unclear grading criteria, and the GSI is a make or break. I second the comment below about Josh Dillen being unhelpful and rude during office hours and lab, but I had a great experience with Haisley, Zakir, and Nick! Most of them are great:)

The lectures are a waste of time, but the lab reports are graded pretty fairly and its a pretty easy A if you do the work and go to office hours. I have to say the GSI makes or breaks the class. My GSI was Josh Dillen and he was quite rude and condescending, but other GSIs were super nice (Keith was incredible)

Funny professor but lectures aren't that helpful towards the lab. This class has a lot of busywork for a 2 unit class and it felt more time consuming than my 4 unit classes. Final was easy if you knew what was going on in the labs and VERY similar to practice tests given.
Overall, the professor is not as bad as other ratings suggest imo. Even though it could be a lot of work for a 2-unit class, I found it to be manageable and the final seemed pretty fair.

I don't know why people are complaining so much about this class, the only con I'd give was it was a lot of work for a 2 unit class, but besides that the professor was really funny, nice and engaging if you actually made an effort to talk to her or ask her questions. The final is also extremely light and earlier than most finals.

labs are very straightforward and simple, but lab lecture is not taught very well. if you are not enrolled in chem 1a at the same time, it may be challenging becuase i forgot most of chem1a content and prof douskey didnt explain the concepts well enough for me to do well on final exam, so i had to self study it all again.

If you're taking her for Chem 1AL, be prepared that it's a lot of work for no reason. SO much busy work. During lectures she's really disorganized, goes over time every class, and uses iClicker so you can't leave early. I didn't like her as a prof, but it really depends on your GSI. The lab exam is just like practice exams and is very fair.

lectures were such a drag and not very pertinent either to the lab, postlab report. final is a breeze if you do all the practice matierial because the content does not vary much between years. GSI makes or breaks this class, but most of the GSIs are great

This professor is nice, but the biggest problem I had with her was her disorganization. The syllabus was extremely hard to find, and she does not make it clear what she expects in assignments, resulting in lost points. It is also very work-heavy. The class wasn't too hard, necessarily, and the final is very similar to the practice tests she posts.

Douskey's lectures were pretty irrelevant to the labs themselves, but she seems like a nice person overall! Lab rubrics weren't clear at all, its pretty common to get points off for minor things that were not specified beforehand, and there's lots of busy work. Labs+prelab quizzes took forever and were very tedious as well....

Way too much work for a 2-unit course. Lectures require attendance but are barely related to the labs. Finals exam is similar to the past papers but had many traps in the questions. The professor seems like a nice person but gives unappealing lectures. She tends to mumble and not project her voice, not to mention she also goes on many tangents.
A huge portion of the grade came simply from iClicker, which was a bit ridiculous. The exams were poorly written.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She was okay, just that there was so much busy work for no reason. Pre-lectures and labs did not have to be that tedious, and I spent way more time than I should have on assignments. Other than that, she's okay, and her lab exam was really easy.
Practice exams look really similar to the real thing, spend time focusing on broad concepts/lab applications. Engaging lectures and really helpful during office hours
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Douskey was a funny and efficient lecturer, but sometimes the lecture content was not really related or necessary for the lab that week. The actual labs were an unbelievable amount of work for how little units Chem1AL gives but still very doable. My lab GSI Nick was truly amazing and the best GSI I think I will ever have in my college career.

Go to lectures, do the iClicker, and pay attention in lab, and you will be more than okay! This 5 is really for my GSI Li Teh and my teacher scholar Riya. I doubt I would have done as well in this class without asking them so many questions every lab, and I am so thankful for the time and effort they put in to helping me and answering my questions.

I would honestly rate this class a 5 if lectures were not mandatory and there wasn't an emphasis on "green chemistry". Half of lab reports are hypothetical questions and lecture is useless if you spend 15 minutes reading the lab manual. Lab exam is  the same as practice exams and reports are fair  once you learn what your gsi wants to see.

It is unfortunate that STEM majors must take Chem1AL as they will have to take this course. The lectures are loosely related to the the lab reports and participation seems to be arbitrarily given or removed because the professor cannot accurately measure it. Thankfully the final exam is exactly like the practices so it isn't hard to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Took chem 1AL last semester and Dr. Douskey was great. She was sweet and approachable, but Im really giving this course a 5 because of Nick Watanabe. Genuienly one of the best GSIs ive ever had at Berkeley and helped me and many other students feel like we understood what was actually going on in the lab and lab reports. Truly amazing and dedicated

lectures can be a little hard to pay attention to but she has a nice sense of humor. lecture attendance for 1al was mandatory (used iclicker). made it clear what she wanted in lab reports. very approachable

Prof. Douskey made 1AL's expectations very clear and her lectures covered general topics associated with the lab as well as some of the procedure. Attendance is mandatory and she uses polls during her lectures to track participation. She's got a good sense of humor and makes lab less intimidating.

Attendance is mandatory, she uses iclicker. The lectures are a waste of time. She's not a bad lecturer but the content she teaches you is not helpful for the pre-lab quiz or post-lab report. The final is the exact same as the practice exam she gives. The class is only difficult because of the busy work you have to do.

I love Dr. Douskey. It clearly shows that she is passionate about education. I will say her lectures don't have any relevancy to the actual labs. The grading of this class depends all on your GSI. The practice final exams ARE CARBON COPYS to the Final Exam you will get. Also the class isn't hard just a bunch of busy work (like srsly a ton).

Lab lectures weren't the most useful and grading criteria was a bit unclear. However she's a nice professor and overall the class was pretty manageable. Lab exam was identical to exams from previous years.

Lectures were engaging and she is accessible outside of class especially in office hours. She stayed behind often to answer questions and it is clear that she cares for her students. Although the prelab quiz and lab reports were time consuming and often ambiguous, they are doable.The final exam was fair and similar to the plentiful practice given.

Lectures were not helpful for doing the lab but attendance was mandatory.  Pre lab quizzes were tedious but easy. Lab reports were time consuming and graded pretty harshly.  Final exam was easy and basically the same as practice exams.

Dr. Douskey is sweet and cares about her student. Has a solid curriculum. Lectures often felt irrelevant to lab reports and prelab quizzes. Reports were tedious and strictly graded, but GSIs were helpful. Reports took up to 8 hours a week. The final was true to practice exams. This class is not hard, just requires a lot of work outside of class.

Easy class but very time-consuming. Lab reports can take hours and are graded harshly, if you submit anything out of order you receive an automatic zero. Pre-lab quizzes can be very lengthy and are often just time-consuming busy-work, but not too difficult. If you put effort into lab reports and study well for the final you can easily get an a.

Lectures were mandatory because of iClicker but not helpful. You don't need to pay attention and you'll still be fine in lab. Lab reports were tedious and long. Final was almost exactly the same as practice tests. Overall, doable class but mostly busy work from the lab reports and ended up putting more time into Chem1AL than Chem1A because of it.

Way too much work that is graded way too hard for a 2 unit intro class. Lab reports are so long with pointless questions and are graded according to inconsistent, arbitrary and unspecified guidelines where the only advice they give you is "be more detailed" and when you submit it there is hidden criteria that is mentioned absolutely no where else.
She is rude when you ask for help and want an accommodation. The opposite of caring and understanding. Do not recommend.

Lectures are hit-or-miss, but the GSI's office hours are super helpful. Labs are graded strictly, so read the rubrics carefully. Unstuckstudy AI made prepping for the final a breeze. Overall, it's a lot of work for a 2-unit class.

She such a nice and sweet professor. However, Pre-Labs and Lab Reports took up so much time and energy. Most of the final grade relied on the final exam, so if you did bad on final exam you were done for. As long as you did practice exam you should be able to get a b at least because I did not attend any lecture.

Professor Douskey's lectures do not cover what is on the pre-lab or the lab assignment. However, the labs entirely depend on how good is your GSI. Lab reports are graded strictly, and some of the lab reports are long (especially the last lab). The final exam somewhat matches the practice exams.

Her lectures are pretty irrelevant to the actual content, she's just cracking jokes the entire time. Will depend on your GSI. Labs are graded very subjectively and vaguely, they're not easy at all. Final matches practice exams pretty well. Overall pretty unremarkable.

Weird and sometime snot relevant lectures but definitely mandatory because of iClicker.  The class itself wasn't too bad as long as you have a good gsi.  Final was also not bad just not a terribly enjoyable class.  Lab reports were easy but like busy work.
Her lectures were kinda boring but she and the classes resources I found to be pretty accessible, especially with prompt responses. This class was a lot of work but ultimately pretty good.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: lecture could be boring sometimes because it was either exactly what was in the prelab or didn't help for the prelab quizzes at all. rubrics on lab assessments were pretty picky, so make sure to read the questions on lab reports carefully and answer every part of the question. this class takes a lot of time for being 2 units.

Lectures are semi related to labs, but you don't need to go to understand the lab. You do a pre-lab quiz before every lab and have to pass it in order to attend lab. Just read the lab manual in order to pass the quiz. Lectures mostly have to do with the stuff on the final. Had an A before the final, and ended with a C, so study for the final.

She was a very kind and funny professor. However, the lectures did not really help with the lab. GSI's office hours helped the most as they are very knowledgeable. There is so much work despite it being a 2 credit class. There are lab reports weekly which are so time consuming. You do learn a lot of lab skills though.

Nice professor! Appreciate how she conducts lectures, fairly easy to understand. The downside is that ATTENDANCE IS MANDATORY (taken via iClicker...which has a lot of connectivity issues). Class is a lot of work (Pre-Labs and Lab Reports are VERY TIME CONSUMING). THE FINAL DETERMINES YOUR GRADE! Recommend taking with Chem 1A simultaneously!
